You're supposed to be graded on how well you use scrum principles, but sometimes we lost points due to our code being incorrect, which was frustrating. Other than that, no real problems. SWE is gonna be group projects, so just prepare for that.

Professor Dobbs is knowledgeable of the industry, he has a drive to ensure all students leave his class with an understanding of how to work together as a software development team, to include tracking of milestones and the use of AGILE and Scrum principles.  He is dedicated to the student's success; I had no communication issues with him.

For ITCS 4155:

Professor Dobbs is a great instructor that has been in the industry and is very knowledgable about what he teaches. He is very flexible in how you do the semester-long project and gives good opportunities to work with actual companies as well!

You're better off learning by yourself than relying on Dobbs to teach. He doesn't teach at all. Assignments are confusing. He provides links to the website of whatever program is being used but those are not useful to a beginner. Each assignment weighs heavy but the only good thing is you get to make your grades up towards the end of the semester.

You are expected to teach yourself almost all topics in the course, which can be really complex. I would only recommend this class to someone who already has a good understanding of JavaScript, MongoDB, React, etc. Instructor is also unwilling to help settle issue within groups, such as group members not contributing.

Do not take this professor if you do not have previous knowledge of software development tools. I.E. MongoDB, REACT, java script, setting up databases and setting up webservers. He offers no lectures on the information and gives very little supplemental reading. You are expected to learn complex topics in a week or less on your own.

He doesn't teach anything, super vague with instructions and grading criteria. He doesn't do any lectures or assignments, just projects. He gives you answers for all the projects except the final one (which is 30% of the grade). He doesn't give you any instructions or provide any help. You are expected to know everything before you take this class.
Homework assignments are long, tedious, and don't really teach you anything.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! 

If you can wait another semester to take it or you have a second option take that and don't look back. 

His homework is extremely complicated (even his TAs get confused), he doesn't go over any of the coding in class - just rambles about unrelated stuff

This is easily the worst professor/class I have ever had at UNCC

Nice man. Terrible class. This was by far one of the worst and hardest classes I have ever taken. The material in this class is so unnecessary and so confusing. Instructions are unclear and confusing. This class is basically in a foreign language.

Professor Wartell is an awful professor, he left the class a halfway through the semester and had another professor teach his class. He had no TA and had trouble trying to grade our first assignments. We never received any of our grades for the assignments until we had to bombard the TA of the other professor for grades. This class is unnecessary

Very easy orientation class. Good lectures and brought in numerous speakers. Class grading criteria is very clear and simple to follow. Not really any tests and not many assignments too. Great teacher would recommend.

I took ITSC 2600 (Computing Professionals) as a transfer class. Professor Slane is very kind and understanding. There's one weekly reflection and occasional assignments. Guest speakers visit weekly and share useful resources and advice for student success. She also responds to emails quickly. Easy class with a good teacher who cares about students.

Ms. Slane's class is a great class to come in for 50 minutes to relax and listen to speakers from the multiple departments here on campus and from companies. Yes, sometimes the lectures can be boring, but for only 50 minutes they're not too bad. The work itself is easy, but make sure to do the assignments, so that you're not stuck with a B like me.

Lectures were basically ppl coming from different departments and talking. Attendance was taken thru pollev. Homework was light work, occasional discussion post or reflection. Had a final group project that we had plenty of time to work on and was fairly easy to do. Professor was nice and seemed to care about her students and their success.
She is the nicest teacher ever, and her class is very easy. Class can be a little boring, but only 50 mins.

ITSC 1600 is an easy course. The class mainly consists of different presenters from student organizations, companies, campus resources, etc. There are some interesting/useful lectures, but a majority of them are quite boring. The assignments are not based on any of the lectures but are relatively simple. Attendance was 10%, and there was no final.

Dr. Slane is an amazing professor, however 1600 is just a boring class. She brings in guest speakers who inform us on various topics relating to resources/possibilities within the school and in the workforce. It's an easy class, and it's great for freshmen to learn what their future could potentially hold going into comp sci here at Charlotte.

I took her class first semester of 2024. Her lectures are really good introduction to Computer Science. She brings in a lot of outside people to talk and you learn a lot about their opinions and they give you advice. Great class for freshman in CS. She also is very understanding and her assignments are short and easy, other than the last long essay
Great Teacher! Super nice

Very introductory class that offers many resources, but it's very boring and at the end of the day you can't take away much. Her TA's do a lot of the grading work but she is accessible outside of class and truly cares about you. Lots of guest speakers and filler assignments.

Everyone gets an A if they do the work. The lectures can be boring if you have no interest in the presenter's topic (attendance is taken). The hardest part is a short research paper you write regarding an ethical issue in technology/computing at the very end.
This class is very easy and pretty much everyone can get an A if they do all the assignments. But I felt this class is pretty boring and not really useful.

The class is a waste of time but Slane does really care about her students and I wouldn't mind taking a class taught by her as long as it's not 1600 again. The class seems to be for straight out of high school students which is not me. It was annoying when recruiters came in for a whole class because I already have a job. Slane is great, class isnt
good professor, super easy class.

Lectures consist almost entirely of guest speakers and the assignments are unrelated to these presentations. Polleverywhere is used for attendance, which is part of the final grade. The assignments are straightforward and simple but Slane is very strict with deadlines. Not very accommodating when it comes to personal circumstances / getting sick.

By far the easiest class I have taken at UNC Charlotte. It was very self-directed and self-taught but the content wasn't challenging. Because everything was online (including test + final) and attendance was not taken you could easily pass this class with an A without ever showing up.

Professor Jugan is easy-going, straightforward, and informative. Attendance is optional and he even takes the courtesy of recording the lectures. This course has few assignments that aren't difficult at all, but it still feels like I learned a lot. A big plus of professor Jugan is that he's easy to reach outside of class!

I took this class on Zoom, attendance is optional and lectures are recorded. This is a project based course, you get to decide what you make. Since you decide, he doesn't give much guidance but is available for questions during class or office hours. There is very minimal work with this class, it's an easy technical elective.

Professor Jugan is a really good professor. He helps you understand the concept of unity and how to code a game from scratch. He is a leineit grader and he is very helpful. We had 4 homework assignments that stacked each time and we had the final game to present as our final.

He's a good choice for intro to AI. Super knowledgeable in the games industry and talks a lot about his experience. The study guides he provides are extremely helpful for the midterm and the final. There are 3 projects in the course. Attend class or watch the class recordings to get good insight on how to do them.

I would highly recommend taking Prof. Jugan if you need a CS elective. All of the milestone requirements throughout the semester are very manageable. There's one final project due, he just tells you to keep it small.

This is THE ELECTIVE CLASS TO TAKE! Super easy, only graded by 10 things, the lowest of which gets dropped. Quiz answers are provided on his posted lecture slides and can be retaken if it wasn't 100% the first time. The final project is easy and he grades things really loosely. Finished this course with a 100% grade! Prof is super funny too, bonus!

10/10. Funny and charismatic and very light workload. He's great at explaining things. He makes the class as painless as possible. Take him as many times as you can. The low-pressure assignments, light workload, and interesting lectures make this class a breath of fresh air. Doesn't try to trick students.-

Don't recommend at all, especially online. Lectures are near incomprehensible and very difficult to follow, and usually never line up with the projects you are working on. You are expected to be good at C# and Unity, or have AI do all the coding. Midterm was set up to be near impossible. Not nearly enough time to complete any of it.

No clear instructions, difficulty in communication, terrible grading, no teaching, 0 understanding. 
You won't learn anything, arbitrary grading, no clear rubric followed while grading assignments. You will waste your time, better take difficult class than wasting your time on this. If the university is listening, please get rid of such classes.
An easy A at the cost of your sanity

I've taken Dr. Benedict for data mining and data visualizations, and she was my advising professor for my senior capstone project. Never in my life have I had a professor more relatable and understanding. Her classes have motivated me to change my career path towards data analytics, and as a student I could not recommend her enough.

She is very relaxed, no attendance. Her class felt like a youtube tutorial, there is very little content and everything can be easily found online for free. She speaks for about 15 minutes over some AI generated slides or the TAs will have a code demo, and the rest of the class you do whatever. This class was a waste of time and money.

She's young and fresh out of grad school, which means that she's really chill and understanding. It seems like she cares, but she doesn't actually have much control over the structure of the course. Typically generates assignments with AI. It seems like she's typically busy and doesn't devote much to the class. New to teaching and too slow.
Great for 2214, would recommend if you want a relaxed professor overall, go with graduate students over professors.

I've taken data structures under two other professors and she is by far the best.  If you get the chance this is the professor you want to teach you data structures if you truly want to understand what you're learning!

If you're taking 2214, take it with Aileen. She didn't design the class, but she listens to students, extends deadlines, and answers questions. When I took it, it was her first time teaching, and she didn't fully know the material, but she admitted that and did her best to find answers. She is by far one of the best professors I have had in CS.

I took ITSC 2214, which was a difficult class—but not because of her. She did her best to help us understand the material and was always open during office hours. The class is challenging because of the content, which is prepared by another professor, but she made it more enjoyable and less stressful. 100/100!

ITSC2214 had a large learning curve, but with ITSC1213 now teaching VSCode and WebCat(coding software/programs), it shouldn't be as much. She didn't have control over the coursework as it was chosen by the department, but she was very sweet and helpful with questions. She truly cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed.

4 projects. Discussion posts and multiple attempt quizzes. In person option has zoom for when you are sick or when you really don't feel like coming to class. No tests. She makes this class so much more focused on learning and coding than tests. GOAT prof
Great professor, always available for any questions and all assignments are manageable & clear. She's also easy to contact and is very understanding!
She's a great professor. I think this was her first sem teaching Machine Learning, but I learned a lot and she offers a lot of chances for students to do well and is very accessible outside of class.

Aileen is one of the best professors here. She is passionate about her work and genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. She is willing to answer any questions and spend extra time with you if you need it.

Aileen Benedict might be one of the greatest prof I've ever had. She a genuine kind person that wants her students to pass. She gives the freedom to work with any dataset for your projects & she assigns the projects & structures the class in a way where you can have a portfolio showcasing your work so you can use it later throughout your career.

The best professor I've ever had. Very relaxed on deadlines and allows you to re-submit any assignment you got a bad grade on. There are 4 projects and a final project, the lowest project grade gets replaced with the highest. Very accessible and always willing to help. You pick the topic for the projects and they really help to build a portfolio.

Aileen is the best! You will have 4 Projects to do, but you can pick the topic for each of them! She is often willing to move back deadlines and help students out. Very responsive in the Discord server. The projects can be a lot of work to do well, but if you do them right, they can be very fun! If you work hard this can be the best class you take.

She's the best! She's truly understands the student experience and wants to help us learn comfortably. There are 4 projects and one final project and no tests! There are unlimited attempts for all of the quizzes/non-project assignments. You learn python and it's a great class for the beginning part of your comp sci major.

He teaches material that can only be found in his research, making it extremely difficult to study for his tests. Additionally, he requires you to complete a project using software from 2007. Grades are based on 2 tests and 1 project. I think the content of this class needs to be updated to the modern era.

Dr. Ras is very knowledgeable and very kind to students. Unfortunately he is just not a good lecturer. Students used to pack the room when his TA showed up for exam reviews. He is accessible during office hours and will give you a chance to make up for mistakes if you participate regularly. Only 2-3 exams will make up your entire grade.

The Prof. was absent the entire semester. I feel like the TAs ran the class most of the time. The material was not too difficult to learn. If you don't have a good team, you will have to work extra hard to get an A. The class is writing intensive. You don't do front-end design in this class but you learn how/why you should design in certain ways.

I took 3 classes with him and his teaching is amazing. He's really good at explaining complex topics in a simple way with real-world examples. His classes and even recorded lectures are engaging. He encourages participation, invites industry speakers, and is very kind and supportive during class and exams. He is my favorite professor in uncc.

The professor receives more criticism than deserved. He is very knowledgeable about the material and has a great sense of humor that makes lectures engaging. He encourages students to ask questions and is happy to clarify concepts. The class is enjoyable and rewarding if you stay focused and put in the effort.

Overall class is on visual optics using AI. Homework and projects are all coded in Python. He gives plenty of extra credit, and chances to make up grades. Bonus points were on almost all quizes, and the ability to re-do assignments were always available. No final, but a final group project is assigned
Just avoid the class. Dr Das is knowledgeable but has weird sense of humor and god complex attitude.

A profoundly confusing structure that meets homework wholly unrelated to what's taught in class. If you have taken Intro to ML get ready to relearn it for half the course instead of what you signed up for. The class has no actual rigor and can easily be completed, but don't expect to actually get the intuition behind the topic from the classroom.

Amazing professor that really enjoys teaching students. He really cares about students understanding what he is teaching and makes complex topics really easy to understand. Above all he is really knowledgeable in computer vision and knows well beyond the course work. If you he the chance to take his class ignore all other reviews and go for it!
The professor thinks he is funny but he is not. Will not take this class again.
One of the greatest professor I had in UNC Charlotte.
If I ever have to take another class with him, I think I'll paint myself on the ceiling!
Who even appointed him as a professor, we should meet that person. Poor attitude towards students, I wish someone else taught the class. Not emphatic at all.
Worst professor in the history of UNC Charlotte, should not be allowed on campus. Entire attitude is wrong.

I wish I could have dropped the class in the first week. Professor forces you to use jupyter and the instructions are inherently unclear on how to use it. Hes a funny guy, but this class is extremely confusing and you basically have to teach yourself. For an elective course, it feels like a core course.

you are going to have to know how to do all of the homework with no resources.would rather you fail than get outside help. hours are always full where u cannot even meet with him .half the kids dropped the class in the first week. about 70 percent of the class got in trouble for 'plagiarism' which was them all getting help. in my senior yr btw.

I'm a senior with a 3.8 GPA and had to drop this class because he was such an awful professor. You have to teach yourself a lot of content, it is mixed undergrad and grad students all learning the same stuff, and he takes pride in students struggling in his course. First day of class he showed his 2.1 rating on here and laughed.

I would beware ITCS 4152 and especially this professor, the pre req are not just matricies and data structures. The homework assignments are through jupyter and python heavy. He gives slides but no back code at all. You have to try to find resources to understand how to even complete the assignments. Please do not take this class it is horrible
Amazing professor. All his classes are great. Take the foundational models course. Truly enjoyed it.

Dr. Zhang is very knowledgeable and a great professor. Definitely recommend taking any of his classes. Just finished the first foundational model course offered in NC. Highly recommend for anyone interested in computer science, or applying foundational models to another research field.

Had the class do a closed-note pop quiz with no prior notice, then cancelled the final project and replaced it with a math quiz based on the results of said pop quiz. You'll be shocked to know that students will tend to perform poorly on pop quizzes when given no indication that pop quizzes will be given. Just one of numerous issues.

If you want to actually learn ML, I would advise against this professor. He admits that he makes the class very easy so that students don't fail, with no exams or in-person quizzes, and labs that are basically fill-in-the-blank with no thinking required. He doesn't lecture very well and doesn't really understand how to answer questions.

He's a great professor. The class is very manageable as long as you keep up with the labs and the capstone project. The best part is that he uploads all the lab assignments at once, so you can work on them at your own pace instead of waiting week by week. Overall, very organized and easy to follow, and you'll do well if you put in the effort.
I really enjoyed taking this class, Lectures, assignments and labs were super straight forward and all the content of the lectures were on canvas day 1 of class so you can go at your own pace
Well paced assignments that keep you involved, good lectures. Not overly difficult, well balanced class.

Dr. Zhang is very knowledgeable and I think did a great job at teaching lots of the basics for the machine learning models he went over. The assignments have been very straightforward with the instructions being clear to understand. Although he did have an accent, I never found him hard to understand.

Dr. Zhang has been a great professor. His lecture notes are informative and break down the goals, intent, and equations into intuitive pieces. 

Labs assignments are long but were really helpful for understanding how to apply techniques. 

Accent is thick, but I find that he speaks clearly and at a speed that allows you to fill the blanks.

This class is exactly what is it, an intro to machine learning. His labs are straight forward and he is always willing to help you with errors in your code. 

10/10
Professor has very strong academically background, which provides student a wide range of techniques and advanced approaches.

1. I took this on 2025 fall semester
2. 5156 intro to ML
3. easy to understand
4. It's good for basic level, but if you want to study more about ML, please take 6000 something ML class.
5. Summary : Easy to understand, good course for student with no having knowledge about ML.

Good bless you.

I saw several bad ratings above from the Spring 2024 semester (I'm in the same class). It seems he really pissed someone off with the tough in-class quiz, haha. 

The professor is, in fact, nice, willing to help, and knowledgeable. Generous in grading.  Has an Asian accent, which is still understandable to me and many of my friends.

This is one of the worst classes I've taken. For one, most people I talked to including myself could not understand a word he said because his accent was too thick. Other than that, he changed the syllabus on multiple things through the semester. ex: he told us he won't take attendance, then changed that halfway through with no announcement.

This class is difficult. If you're interested in ML, you'll learn a LOT and have fun. If you're not interested, you'll have a hard time. His notes and labs are dense but they cover almost everything you need to know about each model. Class is structured in a way that some models have concepts built on previous ones, so reach out if you get stuck.

Heavy accent, really boring lectures, idk about other people but I thought the assignments were super difficult, they're done in jupyter notebook and if you get stuck on one part you can't finish it at all, screwed me over for multiple labs. His only saving grace is that he's actually pretty nice and willing to help outside class if you ask.
bro is the king of yapping, most poorly ran class i've ever been in, it was a joke

One of the worst course experiences I have ever had. It was so unorganized and basically run by the TAs. The teacher would come run a Pol everywhere quiz and leave or lecture in a super monotone hard to understand or comprehend voice than leave and have a TA do a lab or something. My final grade was also suited incorrectly and had to get it fixed.

I swear every positive review was written by him. Professor consistently posts materials last minute, didn't teach/lecture until after midterms when whole class complained, only give quizzes and yaps over them. Extra credit and open book open note means you can get an easy A, but he does not care about this class at all. Grades come out super late.

He does not cover any material in class, just posts a PowerPoint that you are expected to review before class for the in class quiz. Extremely disorganized and often does not post material in a time for students to review. The TAs did most of the actual teaching in this class.

We learned more from a TA during one zoom call than we did with the professor. He would be in class for the quiz and then leave before we started doing assignments. He would leave a TA's in charge and gave her no instructions. He posted the solution to the practice tests the day of the test leaving us no time to understand how to do the problems.

Assignments outside of class are extremely easy, while the in class quizzes take hours to complete and there were only 45 seconds for each question, with quizzes being worth 20%. Midterms often had questions that were not in the videos or slides. Professor is boring during lectures, stays on concepts for way too long, and is difficult to understand

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR. Class is extremely disorganized with frequent absences from Pu, delayed material postings (posted Friday/Sat night and supposed to be read Monday, etc), and prolonged, repetitive rambling during sessions. The substitute teacher was more effective in delivering lessons. Extra credit & tests being open-note is only saving grace

Hard to understand professor! Gives random grades on poll everywhere quizzes! It's about how fast you answer the questions not what place you're in.  Tests are not from learned material! safer to take anyone else for this class.

MANY opportunities for extra credit, mostly based on how good your projects are. The course is project heavy, with three presentations on your dashboards. There's a decent amount of homework toward the beginning but less as the semester goes on. Dr. Yang is lenient when grading projects, gives great feedback, and she's very caring. No tests.

This class is a lot; the difficulty rating is more for the class than Fu. Do not underestimate it, regardless of professor. Fu isn't great, but is knowledgeable and will assist students. But he does not respond to emails, is sometimes unprepared for lectures, difficult to understand via Zoom, and has office hours only once outside of class days.

Can be a lot of homework in my opinion. Not coming from a cybersecurity background made this class a little more intimidating and I think that 3200 should be the only pre req for this class to prepare students. I do think this is a useful class. Lectures could've been more engaging or maybe 1 session could've been a lab session instead.

This class is extremely hard the projects suck. You aren't given a lot of information to go off of so your doing tons of research. He uses HTB for homework and as your learning resource. Do not procrastinate in this class your grade will reflect it. However, he will push back deadlines because he knows the class is hard.

The work can be difficult so it's recommended to start on assignments early, but definitely one of the most useful class you can take. Professor Fu is very passionate about cybersecurity and caring regarding students. He also extends deadlines as necessary so students can get work done on time.

Dr. Fu is a caring and generous professor who wants his students to succeed. He's willing to work with you if you put in the effort. A minor drawback of his class is that some assignment instructions reused from past semesters can be outdated, and new assignments may feel a bit experimental. Overall, his class is fair, enjoyable, and worth taking.

This course was one of my hardest classes I had taken. He knew the class was struggling and decided to switch his teaching methods around to make sure students can succeed in this class. He also is very open to extending deadlines so students can do well on them! One of the best professors I've had and is very caring!

This is a hard class. Probably the hardest class and pain for the cyber security concentration. You better not have a Mac for this class because the VM will not work on there. The professor is good at helping students no matter what time.

Material is hard. Uses Hackthebox as textbook. He teaches and goes over the projects (5) and 1 final and midterm. Gives a lot of extra cred and will curve final and midterm. He will always give extensions if students need it. Extremely receptive to student feedback and always listens to the students. If you need help on the project, he gives hints

10/10 communicator. You can reach this guy at all times of the day. Ask anything anytime and he will respond in a minute. If he is busy he will say so and then tell you he will respond asap. Extremely clear when you ask questions. He will explain everything and listens to his students every time. If project needs more time, ask and you receive.

What a GOAT. we have 5 projects and he said we were allowed to resubmit even after grades near the end. Extensions based on student feedback. We have a textbook and it was quite difficult like the class and so was the midterm and final but everything is open notes. Content is extremely difficult but professor tries to make it as easy as possible.

The class itself is INCREDIBLY DIFFICULT, however I don't think this is because of Dr. Fu. He actually tried incredibly hard to help out all of the students, would give extra guidance on projects, and was also very understanding if you had any personal/life issues happen. But the course itself (based on Dr. Chu's material), is really difficult.

Terrible, just terrible, the hardest class I've taken at this University. The amount of work for all of the projects given is ridiculous. Have known others who have taken this course with other professors and the work load was less than half.
She will never respond to her emails, doesn't care about her students and you will not learn anything from her class. NEVER TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES
Awesome class, the professor and TA's walk everyone through the class with weekly checkpoints and essentially ensure a good grade. Lots of group work and class is discussion based.
Easy A, essentially just show up to class, but other than that she's a really good teacher.

Dr. Johnson is personable and intentional. She gives great feedback and inspires you (furthered by her own extreme endeavors in life). The course is easy as long as you participate in classes and do the assignments, but besides that, class with her is so rewarding that even if there were lots of difficult assignments it would be worth it. 10/10

The professor is extremely energetic, fun, and understanding. There is prep work before each class that takes no more than 30 minutes to finish, and a semester-long project. You will do frequent group assignments. This class was fun, and felt like talking with some friends more than an actual lecture. I cannot recommend her enough.

Well-organized and well-planned course, assignments felt well-spaced and clearly explained. All of the material covered important skills; nothing felt like it was just there to fill a time slot. 

The only point of criticism I have is that she could have been clearer/more specific with feedback on assignments.

Dr. Johnson is an incredible professor. You will learn a lot by taking any of her classes. She does everything to help you succeed. There were group projects, they were fun and easy. When taking her CTCM class, she heavily emphasizes the communication part. Also, be ready to be cold-called! An amazing professor that I would definitely take again.

Liz Johnson is my favorite professor at this school. She is amazing at teaching critical thinking skills and cares for her students. She gives you everything you need to succeed and more. We had two graduate students in class to help us with writing our papers and making presentations. Take her, you'd be doing yourself a disservice if you didn't!
Amazing Professor. Definitely would have her as a professor again.

One of the best professors here. Helped me publish my article. Honestly amazing and even though she rambles a lot she truly respects and admires her students. I learned a lot from her and had an amazing time this last semester.

Great prof if you're taking this for the gen ed credit. Homework and assignment guidelines can be weird at times, but as long as you follow directions and show up to class, you'll be fine. Lectures are entertaining and there's a lot of class engagement.

Objectively one of the best teachers of all time. Very engaging in the classroom; will meet you where you're at; cares strongly about ethics; has extensive experience in a variety of fields, and always interested to hear students' own perspectives; provides insightful feedback; exudes a contagious professional & positive attitude.

If you genuinely want to stand out and improve your confidence in your comp sci career, you have to take her. She will push you to improve but you grow so much as a result. Public speaking is so much easier now. There is a research paper, a final presentation, and group projects.

Hands down the best professor I have had at this school. You can tell she truly cares about the success of her students. If you have to take ITSC 3688 try your best to get in her class. Her class is very easy because if you turn in the weekly assignments you most likely get an A. She made the semester very enjoyable.
I took his course . Biggest mistake I have ever done

Srinivas cares about students understanding of and engagement with the content, however the Mob- Robotics content is a lot of long equations and math, and while the concepts aren't terrible, you will probably feel lost a lot. Be ready for pop quizzes. He is an understanding and reasonable professor, so always ask questions

I enjoyed the Analysis of Algorithms course under professor Akella. 

Most assignments were using pen & paper with the intent of writing good pseudocode/ expressing the solution well. That allowed for better focus on the intuition of algorithm analysis without getting caught up in language semantics.
oh yes Srinivas akella is the best!!!!!!

Entire class is confused. Total of 3 grace days for late assignments. That means if you submit one assignment 3 days late, you've used all your grace days, for the ENTIRE semester. The very first assignment had a mistake, forcing people to use their grace days. Pop quizzes count towards grade. Very tough homework. Bad accent. Lessons aren't helpful
I LOVE SRINIVAS AKELLA HE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR AT UNC CHARLOTTE
classes are long but very confusing, not really sure what he wants. Ambiguous concepts and unclear instructions. avoid it.

Overall if you can learn through powerpoints and know all 150 slides and the codes in c++ on the test...which is 60% of your grade... no notes,no study guide,no openbooks and the "Q&A" days he hosts to answer questions about the test just leads back to the powerpoints.... you will probably pass... otherwise you will fail...

Erik Saule is an awesome dude. Don't get me wrong. But OH MY GOD this class will eat you alive if you are not prepared for it. You will pretty much have to teach yourself everything and the tests are abosolutely brutal. His 3160 class is alos completely different than other professors who offer the same exact course. DO NOT take his section.

Definitely worth getting to know him during office hours. Tests were 50% of grade, no study guide or information about the tests given. He is SUPER knowledgeable about the subject, but you don't code at all in class, just learn concepts. Tests on paper, closed book, coding on paper that was a first. Lenient grader-ish, but you need to put in effort

Very boring required class. Come to class and do the assignments and you'll most likely get an A. 5-page paper and 5-minute presentation at the end of the semester. Strejc is fine, minus a few cringey jokes here and there.

Nothing to do in the lecture, just listen to the lecture and the important dates, and we have to write a research paper for misterm and the final exam same thing research paper, and then make a video about of research paper easy A.

This class is 90% guest speakers who provide little to no benefit. That being said, Prof. Strejc does a good job with the class overall. It's an easy A so long as you attend and do the work. There are clear guidelines on rubrics and he reminds you of deadlines. The resume and LinkedIn assignments are helpful.

Very easy A. I regret not having done everything. Do all assignments in time. Professor Strejc is a very caring instructor. However, I would've wished attendance was not necessary. The class is not worth having to be in class for. Not much is required to be learned. Very few assignments. Anyone can get an A. Take it soon if you need it.

A large portion of the coursework is Khan Academy which can very quickly pile up.There's a course long project of making a website but the assignment instructions are to simply have ai do the coding. Lentient deadlines have been my saving grace in this class

Professor is very easy to learn from and is understanding with work. If you make an effort to do your best in the class and are able to pick up basic concepts and apply it, you will do well. Would take class again!

Professor was truly caring and supportive! Be weary of the fact that you will have to put in time and effort in regards to assignments, extra credits, and projects. Attention to detail is primal...he offers many opportunities and platforms to communicate any concerns and to stay engaged which definitely helps.3##

Course is a lot of work from week to week but as long as you follow what is required of you, it is simple. Professor is easy to work with and continually provides feedback and help to bring up grades.
Lots of busy work but plenty of time to make things up

Coming from a serious graphic design background at a community college, I was worried about the transition to a more technical course. However, Professor von Briesen's deep knowledge of web development and his inspirational teaching style made this my favorite class of the semester. It's rare to find a professor who is a technical expert.

He is an amazing professor who truly wants his students to succeed. He takes time during and after class to explain material step by step. His repetition helps with understanding. The course has a lot of material, but extra credit helps. He and the TAs are very responsive and supportive.
Lot of work given but lot of extra credit also and not much penalities.

Fair and useful class. The start was a little confusing, but once I got settled in it was easier to follow. Grading was fair, late work policy was reasonable, lectures helped with assignments, and the TAs were nice and helpful. Overall, I liked the class.
Make sure you do your Khan Academy work and you will be fine
Asynchronous class with a heavy workload, so stay on top of it! The TAs are awesome and very quick to help if you fall behind. Overall, a solid course if you have good time management."

This course was online and asynchronous for me. It did include a good amount of assignments, but it was manageable. It could be challenging at times but I am finishing this class with more knowledge than when I started. Others complain that its confusing/loaded, but just find a routine and its not complicated. Also hes very lenient with due dates.

D.I. is a very nice guy, although his mandatory online lectures are lacking in real educational content, and assignment instructions can sometimes be overcomplicated or convoluted. That said, I would take another one of his courses, given that it's a little more advanced.

Taking ITSC1110 with Briesen was a frustrating academic nightmare. He outsources teaching to Khan Academy, and his lectures only add to the confusion. The organization is a disaster requiring constant Canvas grade audits. Demeaning busywork and forced weekly logs waste working adults' time. Avoid this professor and class at all costs!

As of now this class is easy but it is a lot of participation assignments that isn't well organized. attendance is also weird in this class because it says that is non mandatory when picking this class but he takes points off if you don't participate in the Wednesday afternoon zoom meeting, also the niner link is very annoying and pointless.

He was a good teacher, he didn't care about attendance but he did give a bunch of workload. He was always in a good and high energy while teaching. I think that it's a trade-off of not caring about attendance but the work load is going to be heavy. Overall it was not bad, I liked the guy!

Professor was overall very unorganized, as well as negligent to NinerLink, which he requires usage of for credit. The class is solely on Khan Academy, and overall, very easy. If you like structure and organization, don't take this class, but if you want an easy A, take this class.

One of the worst classes/professors I have ever had. The workload is often way larger than the content justifies, often requiring hours of work to show proficiency in basic concepts. More than half of the work I did in this class was reading his convoluted instructions, where he tried to be very detailed, but ended up contradicting himself.

This is a pick-your-poison course. The class itself will suck no matter the teacher due to the workload, so choose the best, and the best is D.I. Briesen. The lectures are optional and recorded. Grading rubric is EXTREMELY clear (don't go above and beyond, it's all graded by TAs). The professor is relaxed. Workload is equivalent to 2 classes.

Be warned, most of your time will be taken up with the FreeCodeCamp assignments, which are some of the most mind-numbing work I've ever had to do in college. Some assignments have up to 500 individual steps to complete. If you want to spend 7+ hours a week on a single ad-ridden assignment on top of your normal college workload, then sign up.

Tom Moyer's class was very straightforward and manageable. The course focused on building and hardening IT infrastructure in a VM, with clear step-by-step documents. Attendance was flexible, and class time mostly reviewed the docs or helped students. Easier if you have IT background, but still doable. I'd take it again.
He missed many lectures, does not post slides on canvas. Grading was easy, just a few assignments he gave multiple extensions for. If you're familiar with linux/self-hosting this is an easy A.

The class was heavy on labs, but he gave ample time to do the work( usually 2 weeks), including most of the first class session in which he introduced the lab, and all of the next session.  He was available for in person help although you were allowed to leave if you didn't want or need it.  You could finish it in one session if you stayed.

Missed a lot of classes and usually just announced he'd posted the homework assignment. Assignments were usually posted later than he'd stated and there were 5 short assignments in total. Don't take if you actually want to learn, do take if you already know the material and want an easy 3 credit hours.

He didn't host class for the last month of the semester. I understand he had things going on but he did not post anything on Canvas to make up for it. I know some people would be happy about not having class but when you're paying to learn and WANT to learn it's disappointing.

Moyer is a great professor. Class was required to attend via a sign in sheet, and he doesn't lecture during class, but rather walks through the all the assignments live with explanations for every step, essentially showing you how to complete the assignment. Class only had 5 assignments and a quiz.

I think this semester was a off for him. He had a medical issue and was in pain most of the semester, so was unresponsive to some inquires. Class time was used as Q&A for the assignments we had to do, attendance was mandatory for 2 classes, then he stopped. Had to communicate through CampusWire. Most assignments didn't get graded until finals week.

Doesn't waste anyone's time and is super flexible on due dates. Assignments are clear and instructions are easy to follow. Feedback is good and he's really knowledgeable. Busy a lot though so his TA's answer most questions but with the instructions we're given its no problem and work is simple but tedious. Some assignments are a little free-form.

Took this course for capstone. Moyer knows what he is talking about and he is awesome. Be prepared to do the same kind of hands on lab work from ITIS 3246. Brush up on your linux command line, networking concepts like TCP/IP, know how to configure firewall, and configure selinux security policies. He grades leniently. He wants you to learn.
Great class, great professor! Really team heavy assignments. A lot of material for a good grade is accessible and the audio feature on the book made it quite easy to study for midterm and the final

The class is 3 hours long and he lectures for majority of it from slides. He's a really nice professor and wants you to engage. The class is similar to human centered design and software engineering so a lot of the concepts have been heard throughout the CS department at UNCC.
Very nice. Complex concepts made accessible. Really fun and hands on assignments. Beware acronyms.

Professor Peterman is very nice, accessible outside of class, and understanding. The group project was rough due to unhelpful group members, but the class overall was great. Homework is light. Just one activity per week. There's only a midterm and final, and he provides study guides for both.

All the weekly assignments are group based, and they are quite easy. The only individual assignments are the textbook questions, final paper, and exams. The 3 hr lectures are quite long, however we usually get out 30 min to an hour early.

Hours of long and boring lecture that consists of him just reading straight off the slides. The assignments are not hard at all and as long as you do the group assignments, it is a 100. However, he grades the final project and paper. He is an extremely harsh and picky grader.
Amazing teacher and very knowledgable. Expects student engagement but only if you volunteer. Top 3 instructors here in Comp Sci.

A 3-hour session that's spent leaning against a desk and reading word-for-word what was read in the weekly readings... yet attendance is mandatory :(. Beyond the dreadful classes, my biggest gripe is his snarky replies via email, which students would be scolded for. Respect is a two-way street, even if I am the student and you are the professor!

Professor Peterman knows his stuff, he works in Identity Management and teaches night classes. The work is very minimal, one chapter with a quiz and a short assignment per week. The only downside to him having a full-time job is he doesn't post the quizzes until the day of. Despite it being a 3 hour class, we would always get out early

Group project that lasts throughout the semester but is pretty simple. Tests were a little difficult, but follow study guide and you'll be fine. The topics/lectures were kind of boring, but he attempts to make them fun. Weekly readings that can take up some time, but were fairly easy. He is a pretty easy grader that wants his students to succeed.

Nice to have someone who actually does CyberSecurity for a living teaching a class. Class tracks to the Security+ certification but there are caveats. Lots of great stories and modern topics to discuss. Make sure you read before class or lectures get a little boring. He cares a ton, which is great. Would definitely take in another class.

He is a nice professor. The lecture can be a bit boring, but it's due to the nature of this course, which has a lot of new terms and abstract concepts. There are weekly group assignments(fairly easy), one group project, two exams (midterm and final), and a research paper. I don't think he grades harshly, but the two tests were quite challenging.

Professor Peterman is an amazing guy. Lectures were super long and boring however, and he realizes it. Most days we would end early, and every class consisted of a powerpoint lecture based on the textbook. There were chapter quizzes every week that are open note with two tries, as well as a midterm and final.

There was no option for ITIS 3200. Hes an amazing professor but his lectures are VERY VERY boring. The assignments are very easy. 1 midterm and 1 final. Great and caring professor but cannot keep a class entertained.

He uses slides to lecture, but does his best to skim them and correlate them to real-world situations. A very kind teacher who cares about his students and supplements additional real-world news into classes before lectures.

This was the worst class I took in 4 years. The professor seems to care, but the class is unnecessarily hard. The Hack The Box textbook is required even though it is barely used until the end, and the projects have unclear instructions and do not even run properly on Mac.

HTB access required early on but not granted until mid-semester due to a TA issue. TAs rarely respond to emails, office hours at 8:15 are unreliable, and Canvas messaging shows an empty directory making it impossible to contact the professor directly. He is personable but the lack of accessible support has made this course unnecessarily difficult
Does not use Canvas for grading so if you think you have an A at the end, think again. There was a 10 point variance between his calculation and Canvas.

Class is alright, but formatted very poorly. Relied heavily on TAs who did absolutely nothing to help students. Would avoid responding to emails and give zero help on projects. HTB was a nightmare since TAs managed it ($300 for it btw). The professor feels tired and overwhelmed, but does really care about students. He tries his best to teach.

Class is disorganized and no help is available for projects.  Lectures don't teach anything you haven't already learned.  Grading criteria not clear and not all assignments, including grad student term paper, are included in syllabus.  Class is basically self-learning.

I really like Proffesor's Severs way of grading, its not that often seen. the homeworks were short but effective, you could realistically do them in less than an hour, in addition to that he rewarded participation by giving extra credit point to those who asked interesting questions, or those who helped others understad topics.

Dr Sever was an amazing Professor to have. His course was not very difficult but he seemed to really care for his students and wanted them to succeed. If you do not care for his course and are not committed then don't expect as much help. I really enjoyed the group project we had throughout the semester and learning different development styles.

Instructions for certain assignments were unclear and had to be explained in class multiple times. I wish the lectures were more interactive or that half of the period was dedicated to working on the project instead because it is hard to focus for a 2+ hour long class. I wish the lectures were more engaging too.

This professor appeared to be very lazy. He imported all of the assignments and didn't give clear instructions. Despite unclear instructions, himself and the TA's were constantly threatening to throw academic integrity violations at us. Don't recommend taking him for 6112 as it's just a bunch of busy work and you don't really learn anything!

He actually teaches, which is rare for CS professors here. Lectures are pretty good. Main complaints: keeps grade calculation disabled all semester; unclear on bonus points and attendance policy; midterm is full of obscure multiple choice questions buried in hundreds of slides. Overall okay. Don't choose Go for your group project.

Midterm=easy, based on the textbook chapter and slides and a few parce trees. Tons of extra credit opportunities. Most complainers=too lazy to take advantage. Parce trees take some getting used to, but he can't control content. He explains it well though. Group project=low expectations so if you stress yourself doing more, that was your decision.

The class was very well organized. We had a clear breakdown on what to do week by week. There is a group project which is either a paper or programming assignment. If you have a good group it is not bad. Assignments were not too hard as his lectures taught the material. Same with the quizzes. Really nice guy and good TA's. I would recommend him!

Dr. Sever is very laid back. I learned a lot from the assignments and lecture slides by challenging myself to understand software development. The group assignment was very easy and fun to work on together. The class is disorganized in canvas with no lectures or book materials even though that is needed for the tests. It's still an EASY A.

Most mundane lecturer ever. His 3hr lectures will put you to sleep. Pick a good group for the group project. Research a programming language beforehand because your group will have to write 200 lines of code that demonstrate its functionality. It can be anything like a game. Other than that, easy class. Midterm sucks tho. Final is optional.

This professor is hard to follow during lectures. It is very lecture heavy and covers abstract concepts that are hard. Also, it is a 3 hours class so it is a drag. 
Make sure to pick a good group for the group project at the end. 

Midterm is hard and final exam is optional. 
Overall this class is mid and a waste of my time.
Dr Sever is an amazing professor. His grading rubrics is very clear. He gives extra marks for attendance, class interactions and answering questions asked in class.

I've had Ali twice now (5102 and 6112), and both times the classes have been easy and I didn't particularly learn anything, but Ali is great to take in person. He is pretty funny and will give extra credit for just coming to class. The group projects are very easy and the TAs are also pretty good. If you want an easier course, take Professor Sever.
The best professor.

Now read this carefully, I didn't take her for a class at UNCC. I took her for a class at CPCC (CTI110). Exams are a huge part of your grade, but you get multiple attempts to retake them and get your highest score, and you can just use the textbook since the answers are in there. She also provides extra credit!

Honestly, this class was such a breeze. Everything was straight forward and all the assignments were clear. Textbook can be found for free and tests are open note. Plus, SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT. It was amazing. She missed a few classes, but TAs handled it so I was happy. Plus, she was really nice. I would take this class again for sure.
Didn't learn a single thing in this class but it's a very easy A. The class was supposed to be in person but she didn't show up 95% of the time. Just do your assignments and you will be set.

There is little to no actual instruction in this course and you will need to read the textbook to learn anything. The syllabus is copy pasted from other semesters and the assignments have incorrect instructions due to the professor not taking the time to update anything from years past. Easy A, but a waste of time.

Thayer is easily the worst instructor I've ever encountered. His lectures are unhelpful and poorly organized, leaving students more lost than when they started. He has no patience for questions and sends you off to a TA. He doesn't understand his own course content and is quite hostile if you ask about it. Labs have unclear/vague instructions.

Dr. Thayer is kind and very organized and it is very clear he enjoys teaching this class. The class has a lot of homework assignments (most of which are due within 48 hours, although there is a flexible late policy). You are allowed unlimited notes on the tests which make up 65% of your grade. There are small quizzes a couple times a week in class.

He drop grades for some assignments and a project. final was optional and replaced your lowest tests if you did better on that than the average of your tests. TAs were good and lots office hours for course, but the grading can get complicated especially participation. mostly self guided learning before class but he goes over them in class anyways

I got an A taking him for ITSC2214 last sem, and A now taking him for ITSC 3146. Super nice. Homework has a 2 day grace periodw/no penalty, & his tests are open notes as many as you want. I slacked off in this class but would clutch just in time for the tests and he even had an optional final that only helps you (which pulled me to an A).

The course lays a heavy load of complicated content but as long as you show up and apply yourself you can easily get a good grade in this course. Thayer is super understanding of the rigor so almost every assignment has a 2 day grace period and even if you miss that he has a system that allows you to make up a limited number of assignments missed.

I don't understand such high rating! The course is poorly designed. While the course is supposed to teach you OOP design, the expectation is that you know C# and design concepts from day 1, and start coding on day 2. While prof. is knowledgeable, the lectures are pretty much vague. Be prepared to do a lot of self study.

Second course I have taken with Prof. Thayer, and he was just as great was he was last time. Does a good job explaining things and will always help you when you're stuck. There are multiple unit tests that make up a big part of your grade but they are fairly easy. The prep-work and attendance are mandatory and graded.

Professor Matt Thayer is one of the best at UNCC. He's caring, helpful, and explains Data Structures in a clear and simple way. I never thought I'd get an A in a computer science course, but I did—thanks to him. Take his class, you won't regret it!

Thayer is easily the worst instructor I've ever encountered. His lectures are useless and poorly organized, leaving students more lost than when they started. He has no patience for questions and sends you off to a TA. He doesn't understand his own course content and is quite hostile if you ask about it. Labs have unclear/vague instructions.

Not understanding the high ratings I see. Gives way too much homework and expects it all to be done in a ridiculously quick fashion. He hasn't created the class himself he just reads off slides from another professor and has the TA's answer questions during class. Complex concepts with a lot of work load and very quick pace, seriously good luck

First 2 exams are the hardest of the class, but are some of the most important. First 1/2 of semester is C++ last half is networking and a little bit more of C++. The assignments aren't difficult but tedious. Pollev quiz and pre videos before classes. Ask for exam review slides as they are very helpful for exams. Exams are open notes too.

Definitely take Thayer for this course. He was enthusiastic to teach the course which made it easier to learn. Poll-everywhere quizzes would be done at the start of each week based on the prep work that was due the night before. The content of this class was a bit harder than most and there was a decent bit of homework but Thayer manages it well.

It was a flipped classroom involving groups which can be hit or miss but Professor Thayer was very communicative and provided ample feedback and resources needed to learn. He always seemed excited to teach which is also a plus. A lot of homework but they were fairly easy and participation is a big part of this class.

Instructor was very nice & showed genuine care for our learning. Knowledgeable. Lots of pre-class-time assignments (videos & quiz) but they actually prepared us for class pollevs & weekly assignments. lightweight teams which wasn't bad. Communication was great. Study material was EXTREMLY helpful. we could upload notes to use during tests too.

ITSC 3146.Would have poll-ev for beginning and end of class which is fine but it's the fact that we would get points off our attendance for answering the questions wrong despite it being new material?? He assigned lots of homework, some were incredibly hard and confusing with no clear instructions. Few of TAs didn't even know what they were doing.
Chill; good speaker; shows care for his students.
Prof. Thayer did a great job of preparing us for the exams and communicating the course content effectively. I always felt prepared for every assignment that was given.
Great teacher, explains the concepts clearly and simply. Accessible outside of class.

Loved the class structure, and her teaching is the best I've had in the CS department. Class is somewhat hard, but just do the work and study for the tests. Tests 1&2 are harder, whereas 3&4 are easier. Offers make up exam for the final exam that allows you to recover a lot of missed points.

If you take ITSC 3146 with her, watch the video lectures carefully, as all key information is covered there. She explains concepts very clearly. Attend every lecture since polls are used for attendance. Tests are based on the exercises and modules. I would take her class again..

The course jumps to C++ directly from (ITSC - 2181). You will basically not have any introduction to C++, but you are expected to work on exercise and labs straight up. While there are some recorded videos in the module section, professor does not teach during an hour and 15 minutes class. Also, PollEv quizzes would hurt your grades.

The professor is kind, but the class is absolutely miserable. Code is hardly taught during the course, you'll be tested on it anyways. Test study guides are vague, oftentimes you will find out the questions on the tests aren't intuitive to what you've been learning. Test scores are locked and hidden, hard to learn from mistakes.

We jumped from c to c++ directly. She didn't teach, we were supposed to learn and know it during the first week itself. Test 1 and 2 is c++ heavy and hard, test 3 is easy and test 4 was hard. She does pollev for credit everyday, attendance matters!!! No extra credit!!!

Believe me, this is the review you want to read. Harini's tests are way too hard and worth ~45% of your grade, despite what she says. The first two tests are C++ heavy, but she doesn't teach it and you're left to learn it on your own. She's vague about what's on tests, and her study guides barely help. Not a great teaching style.

Incredibly well-structured class taught by a very knowledgeable professor. Dr. Ramaprasad demonstrates the full benefits of flipped learning and her course perfectly blends theory with hands-on practice. It feels like a course that prioritizes learning beyond all else, and she is beyond understanding and caring about student success.

She's a great professor and you'll learn a lot. Also, this is the only class she typically teaches, and it's clear she puts the effort in. She explains things well and she seems to choose her TAs well. However, you have to put the effort in because even though tests are open-note, they really challenge your understanding of the material.

One of the best professors I have taken in CCI.  Her lecture videos were very useful.  There are a lot of tests in the class, but each test only covers 2-3 weeks of material.  It was an easier class with not a lot of homework.  The instructor and here TAs were always available in class to answer any questions when we worked on assignments.

Dr. Ramaprasad is a great teacher. Her lecture videos are great and make everything easy to understand. The class itself is pretty easy, and becomes even easier after the first two tests. Most of the course content is conceptual stuff and there's only a bit of C++ programming at the beginning of the semester.

C++ heavy at the beginning of the semester. Last half was all labs using Wireshark. All of the assignments were very manageable. She gives you two days after the due date to submit without a late penalty. You'll be working with a group for the entire semester, so make sure you pick a good one on the first day. TAs were nice and helpful.

She is the most disrespectful person I have ever encountered. Her teaching method is good, and she understands her topic, but as a person, she has no idea how to communicate with her students. If you take her class, be prepared to be yelled at over little issues.

Dr. Harini is one of the best professors I had in computer science so far. She really cares a lot about her students. I really liked her classroom structure a lot with the pre-lecture recorded videos. The beginning of the course was quite difficult with there being a lot of C++ assignments but the networking part of the course was a lot easier.

I took 3146 with Dr Harini, and I really enjoyed the class. The material is well-structured, her TAs and her know what they doing and always there to help. In the first half of the semester you have a lot of homework ( mostly coding) so be ready for that. However, second half of the semester is pretty chill. I would definitely take her again.

Professor Ramaprasad is passionate about teaching and cares about her students. She lets you use the classroom PowerPoint during tests and before class you have to watch the content videos to understand the lectures. She uses PollEv to take attendance, I would recommend going to class. The material was fun to learn, we used VirtualBox to do hw.

Great prof, very knowledgeable and really cares about helping her students do well! Lots of homework but mostly simple/small assignments that really did help me understand the material better. Clear, fair grading scale. If you understand the assignments tests aren't too bad. Is pretty strict about attendance but it's not a huge % of your grade.

Professor Ramaprasad is a great professor. The class involves coding initially that can be difficult but the latter part of the course doesnt have coding which gets easier. The TAs had review sessions which helped as well as the tests allowing electronic open-note. Use your team your given and collaborate on the hw and a study guide!

Great lecturer and provides all the tools you need to succeed. She is very accessible and responds quickly when messaged on CampusWire. There are poll everywhere quizzes 1-2 times per week you'll want to come to class for, but all the other assignments and material is very straightforward.
typa teachers they hire in tel-aviv. do not take her for Computer Ethics.
She is a fulltime elementary teacher doing this part time. That will tell you everything

called a student a hypocrite on the first day. first, she asked every person what they think the worst technology is with the most impact. most people said AI. Then asked our concentrations, half the room with AI, Gaming, and Robotics of course. told us on first day that ethics is not about opinion, then proceeds to interject her own opinion

Would rate her 3 stars, everyone looks at 1stars first; Price is not a though grader. She is however very vague about group projects, which is very difficult to coordinate group projects because nobody knows what to do. 2 group projects with same ppl entire semester, doesn't make you aware that you can switch groups if your uncomfortable w/ ppl.
The best professor I've ever had for a class. Be ready for a lot of group work and presentations. Genuinely cares about her students, and I would take her again in a heartbeat if I could.

I can see how her class can be frustrating to many, because it forces you to come out of your comfort zone. The presentations were frustrating because the topics are so broad, but it allows you to get creative. Her rubrics and instructions are very vague, this definitely needs improvement. The 4 ethics papers are based on fictional articles.

This class focuses on group presentations and essays. The Canvas setup was unfortunately disorganized, making it hard to find assignments. Luckily, the instructor is open to feedback and improving. It's laid-back, covering topics outside of the usual CS courses. Mostly discussion boards and some quizzes. Do the work, show up, and you'll get an A!

She is a nice lady and as long as you do the work you should get an A. The essays can be hard and a bit time consuming but all the other assignments are easy and don't take too much time. She is a fair grader for the presentations. Overall I would recommend her!

if she likes you, you'll get an A if not she will grade you hardly. she is Karin but sweet. Sweet "Karin". over all i got B she is cool but when it comes to grading she is biased sort of. like i said above.

Two papers, two group projects, weekly forum responses, and 8 (pretty easy) reviews you do in groups. The work is not hard, but it needs to be quality. You have to ask questions and have thorough group discussions to get a good grade. She cares about your depth of thought and rewards good ethical reasoning above all.

She's a nice lady but her instructions for the essays are so messy and unclear. The prompts she gives you are incredibly vague and her instructions as to what she expects in your paper are so confusing. She has "guides" in her website to help but the description she gives for each paragraph will contradict what she has written in another guide.

Loved this professor. She is super nice, funny, and laidback. This class has two 35-minute presentations, but it's in a group so individually it's only like 6 minutes each. There are 4 papers, around 2,000 words each but she grades very leniently. If you participate and do the work you'll get an A. Plus, she gives time to work on stuff in class.

The professor explains concepts really well and genuinely cares about his students. He's clear about expectations, assignments, and how exams are conducted. The in-class activities helped a lot with understanding the material, which is also useful in later semesters. Be ready to study and practice consistently.
Nice guy, who cannot teach if his life depended on it. Smiles a lot, but is soooo hard. Means well , but cannot relate to us as students. Avoid!

So far, he is the best professor at UNCC. He genuinely cares about his students, and his lectures are engaging. Although he is a tough grader, his teaching is equally good, However, you have to be attentive in class and practice at home. I would any day take his class again if given a choice.

Dr. Chandra is a nice guy, but totally incapable to teach anything. He rambles about unrelated topics, talks about examples that has nothing to do with the content, and sometimes meaningless.  But he tries really hard and means well. Unfortunately his exam is totally unrelated to what he teaches and it hurts your grade.  If you can , stay away..
The class is difficult but she is a good professor and is willing to help you outside of class

The professor isn't that bad. It's her first time teaching, and 3146 is a hard class. It's a flipped classroom, so if you stay on top of the lectures at home, you'll be fine. It's a hard class in general, but I wouldn't avoid her. Meeting with the TAs and going to her office hours will help you a ton!

She cannot teach anything beyond her slides. I'm pretty sure she uses AI to make them because she looks like a teary-eyed puppy when a student asks a question she can't answer and looks to the TAs for assistance.

She is difficult to read. There are times when she would come in prepared to teach but the moment you ask a question, she defers to the TAs and that was highly disappointing. All of the contents of this class came from other professors courses and the moment there was review, she would say "let me confirm and let you know through Ninerlink" baddddd

a very caring woman who wants her students to succeed. stay on top of your assignments and you will be fine. Dr. Striplin is an excellent teacher and simply teaches a hard class. I've have never had to study or get a tutor in my entire life, until this class. Whatever you get on your first exam/test will set you for the rest of the semester. Just know if you need this class, you have to study literally every day. The test are very hard if you dont study and understand how to do practice problems. Shes a nice lady but thats about it.

Considering that most people registering for CHEM 1203 are Nursing majors, there is unfortunately nothing you can do about having Dr. Striplin for it. As is this course isn't hard enough, her teaching style and lack of explanation just makes it even more impossible. She's completely unaccessible outside of class, and has no sympathy.
She is very hard to follow in class, she jumps from topic to topic and lectures feel disorganized. Awful class would not take again but she's not a bad person.

She makes the exams so difficult that it looks like everything you studied wasn't even on there and even if you do all the work and get 100 you will still fail if you do bad on the exams. The way she teaches is so confusing and she makes it more complicated then what is it. Ive had to teach myself everything in that class.

All the work is self taught. She tries but makes no sense when teaching. She goes from subject to subject with no transition. I taught myself everything. There is a ton of reading and a ton of assignments that are only worth 20% of your final grade.

Dr. Striplin is a kind professor! She does move quickly, but she will help you if you just ask! Utilize videos, worksheets, and office hours. Striplin is a great professor. super helpful and provides loads of recourses to learn. anyone talking bad about Striplin didn't put in the work. the course is difficult yes but the resources are there. read the chapters, watch videos, do practice problems, get a tutor, talk to Stiplin if you're stumped. the course is sweet and so is Striplin.

Yeah so she's a little coo-coo but after having her for both 1203 & 1204, she's actually grown on me a lot. She's super sweet & funny but not great instructor-wise. Striplin's not AS BAD as these reviews have made her seem. I think she's an ok person but it's her teaching style that SUCKS. As a nursing student they let you know they are trying to make you fail. So expect it to be hard, read the book and make sure she knows who you are.

AMAZING person, mid teacher. She's very kind and intelligent but does struggle to stay on topic and to show us the connections. GO TO OFFICE HOURS, she is helpful there. Very lecture heavy and the lectures didn't really help me. Textbook heavy. Little to no extra credit. Very test heavy, if you bomb one your in trouble. Someone said everyone failed 1203, but that is not true!! I was intimidated by this class because I had never taken Chemistry in high school, but it turned out to be not that terrible. Go to lectures, take decent notes, do ALEKS, read the textbook, and study a week before exams. Go to the PAL sessions; I heard it helps. XOXO, you'll be fine.

Made me miserable, changed my major, and ruined my freshman year and first semester are Charlotte. Everyone in the class is trying to survive. Honestly she is a really nice professor and would even say hi outside of class however, the lectures are all over the place. Looking back at notes would leave me so confused she never quite finished a thought.

She knows what she is talking about, however this course is rigorous. If you are a pre-nursing student that struggles with chemistry I would recommend taking Gen Chem. Very nice lady but class is extremely difficult and you will most of the time end up having to teach to yourself. CHEM 1204 is very test heavy and almost no chances for extra credit. Awful professor and expects us to know the material like we have been studying chemistry for our whole lives. Dr. Striplin is a good professor; it's just that her class is hard. Come prepared for her lectures by doing the chapter readings and taking good notes, you shouldn't be lost on her exams. Professor Striplin will not teach you the material, she expects you to know it before you go to class. The tests are nothing like ALEKS work, which you will spend literally ALL of your time on. She was a very tough professor. I learned more from the textbooks and YouTube tutoring than from her lectures. If I didn't have to take chem 1204, I would have dropped this course. This class was awful. Coming in as a freshman this course made me wonder if college was for me. This class was a rollercoaster honestly it is doable but it is very hard. You only have 3 main grades which are test grades. So do not take it lightly and study hard from the first test itself. This class quite literally ruined my first semester at Charlotte and if I were an incoming freshman again I would just choose to take this class at a community college and transfer it over because this class taught me absolutely nothing and just made me feel stupid. Dr. Striplin knows her material, but CANNOT teach it at all. I've taken this class before, and while I wanted a refresher, I've never struggled more. Professor Striplin is a hard professor she bounces all over the place. If you intend on majoring in nursing take chem 1251 and not this course. If youre a nursing major and want to succeed, A fulfill your chemistry courses at a CC or B be ready to commit your life and soul to chemistry. Dr. Striplin is a smart but fast-paced professor. The class is challenging, but going to lectures and using resources like unstuck AI can help. Stay on top of the work and you'll do well.

She  bounces all over the place. Be prepared to be stressed to the max if you have other classes. She does not put her grades in canvas. She is the reason I am transferring! Dr. Striplin is the ONLY professor who teaches this chem so regardless you're going to have to take her. Dr. Striplin has forgotten what it's like for the material to be new. She teaches in a manner that assumes you either already know chemistry or will immediately understand, which is not the experience for the vast majority of students.

Dr. Striplin is a good lecturer. However, this class is really hard and a lot of the things you are tested on aren't in the textbook and look different in the homework. Dr.Striplin is such a nice person, but her class is SO HARD. It isn't her fault that there is so much material to cover, but she is so intelligent that she overteaches. chemistry is hard no matter which professor you have. Dr. Striplin was fair and caring.

Dr. Striplin is honestly a very nice and caring person. I had her over the 5 week summer course. The course is very difficult but she tries her best to make the material more understanding. Dr. Striplin is a very kind person. She was definitely easier to understand in this course and I learned a lot! Dr. Striplin is honestly a great professor. Her class is very difficult however if you pay attention during lectures and do the homework, you will do fine. Dr. Striplin is a very funny person and she really does care about her students success. The class is definitely difficult and very time consuming. As long as you read the chapters and do all the homework you should be fine. I used the tutoring services and that was extremely helpful. 
Very nice person, but very tough class.
Professor taught really fast and is hard to understand because she goes on rants. The test looks nothing like the homework.

Prof. Striplin herself is not bad I just think its the classes she teach. Chem 1203/1204 are awful, be prepared to teach yourself a lot of the material and take heavy notes and do a lot of homework.
