Professor Striplin overall is not a bad professor. Do your reading, homework, and come to class prepared. She moves very quickly during lectures so it is best to not take detailed notes. Striplin is caring and will help when asked for help. Make the textbook your bestie, do the book drop, STUDY, make friends, and help each other out. Very smart and passionate about what she does. All I will say is that you have to be dedicated to succeed in her class, but what is a chemistry course without dedication right?

Chem 1252 is a challenging course, but Mrs. Michaels makes getting a C or higher achievable. As long as you watch the PCA videos and attend the lectures, you will pass the course. Very good at explaining difficult concepts, takes time to answer questions. Provides a lot of resources for studying, if you put in the work your grade will reflect that. Assignments (including in-class work, ALEKS, and pre-class) only account for 30% of the overall grade, while exams make up the remaining 70%. That wouldn't be as concerning if the average exam score weren't consistently around 63%.

She is a great professor for CHEM 1251. She is good at explaining material. There is quite a lot of work for this class, but if you go to class and pay attention, it is easy to complete. I hate chem. I don't mind labs just because they're easy, but this lab was kinda hard. I had the TA for the lab and he was okay kinda shy. Mrs. Michael is a great professor and she strives to make her lectures engaging even with difficult topics. She does not post lectures on canvas so you do have to attend in order to get info. 4 exams and then final at the end. Final exam will replace your lowest exam grade.

her lectures and notes are very informative. for this class, i've had to study COUNTLESS hours in order to get an A on an exam. just know chem 1251 is one of those weed out classes, so if you want to stay in the class, you have to go out of your way to really use the material given to you; practice exams, problem sets, and chapter objective lists!!

Professor Michael is a great lecturer who makes chemistry much more understandable. Her lectures cover the material well, and using resources like unstuck AI along with the textbook really helped me succeed in this challenging course.

The best professor I have had this semester! Truly one of my favorite professors! I didn't even need to read the textbook because her lectures cover everything you need to know. Mrs. Michael is an amazing professor. She understands that the class is challenging and tries her best to make everything easy to understand. Great Professor. She thoroughly explains all of the information but the course is test heavy. I averaged a B on my exams using the practice exams and the resources that she provided. Professor Michael is an amazing lecturer who explains things very clearly. She gives a lot of practice problems in class that are similar to the ones on the tests. I see lots of positive reviews but most of the people in class were struggling. This class was hell and made me want to die (I had it at 8 am monday, wednesdays, and fridays). Dr. Michael wasn't bad but the exams are very difficult (not like class). Do yourself a favor & take this course elsewhere, the chem department sucks here (it's on probation)

4 regular exams & they're worth 50% of your grade. Homework doesn't move it up a lot and final is 20% of your grade. Lowest exam grade is dropped but exams are tough. This course is not easy and requires a lot of studying. Honestly, it sucked the life out of me and made me rethink my entire life.

Mrs. Michael does a good job of explaining the material in class that can be confusing in the book. Be prepared to write a lot as some lectures have loads of info in them. She gives really good lectures that help the textbook make a lot more sense. EASILY the best prof for 1251. Stands out as a great teacher and nice prof in a department that isn't so great as a whole. Attendance is part of the grade and you will struggle if you skip lecture.

Chemistry gets a bad rap here but she's a really good professor. Only prof worth taking for 1251 imo

IMO, She is the best professor for CHEM1251. She's a great lecturer and gives clear explanations and notes. She takes attendance in class through learning-catalytics. Tests can be difficult, they are designed by the department not her, but if you properly prepare it's not too bad.

Honestly, she is a decent chem professor. Definitely have to show up to class or else or kinda f****. But the assignment she gives out isn't that bad can be difficult here and there for sure. If you're premed or not a chem major, please don't take this class its nearly impossible to get an A. 90% of your grade is based on exams/quizzes and theres no free response ever, not even the final exam. Just don't take him if chem is not your strong suit.

Being completely honest this class is a bit difficult but Dr. Horger makes the class a bit more tolerable as he does alot of examples in class. My favorite German Jewish proffesor of all time. We spent more time talking about cost of material in lab, than the actual material but I dont remember being asked about the cost of material on quizzes and exams. Something must be wrong.

Ms. Black is genuinely a light of joy in the chemistry department. She is very empathetic of peoples lives and loves to make one-on-one connections. Lecture is guided notes with PollEverywhere for attendance. ALEKS homework can be frustrating but she is very helpful in office hours. Gives good resourced to prep for exams, and grades very fast!

Do the homework, Learn the content, pay attention in lectures, and practice. You will be successful. Most people are salty, but she is amazing. Very well and soft spoken. I never thought I would do well in Chemistry; she is why I did well.

She is the best professor ever. Her teaching style is so thoughtful and you are able to learn content very well. The tests are difficult but as long as you use your resources and do everything she recommends, you will be okay. A lot of people don't understand that CHEM requires the student to practice and learn to be successful.

She expected you to know everything on your own, barely taught. The study material is nothing like the test. Unbearably boring to get through the lectures. She moves at a fast pace and doesn't explain her work only writes down what happens in her head.

The tests weigh so much that the other assignments won't make any significant change in your final grade. She does not allow any make-ups and she takes a long time to email back. Don't take her if you have a choice.
I would not recommend this professor to anyone. She is by far the worst professor I've had at UNCC. I hear a lot of people say prof Outlaw is much better.

Nightmare.
Most folks fail the first time they take this class. Then, they take it at a cpcc over the summer. She will wash you out of your major. Go to office hours, where she re-teaches everything. Exams are difficult because she requires you to know more than she teaches. Exam questions are "gotchas". She regularly uses 3 text books.

General Chemistry 2 with Dr. Asala is challenging, but using helpful tools like Unstuck study alongside the textbook and practice materials can make a big difference. Her teaching style takes some adjusting, but office hours are a lifesaver.
You can expect a lot of homework, so it's important to study and really understand the subject. Otherwise, you won't get much out of the course.

Hardly responds to emails, grades late,+ NOT UNDERSTANDING. Required to do ALL pages of 25+ chem questions each week and grades it on 3 random questions. Couldn't get access to an assignment after emailing her many times so I called aleks and it was because SHE DIDNT OPEN IT. I turned it in but she NEVER GRADED IT after I emailed 2+ times.

If you really push yourself you can do well. Her grading system is horrible. It also takes a very long time for her to actually put in grades. She did give extra credit which was very kind and she seems like a sweet professor. However, I was basically teaching myself the material for this class.

You will be given a worksheet with anywhere from 20-50 questions expected to do all of them. You will only be graded on 3 randomly selected questions. Grading also takes an extremely long time. There is no materials to learn outside of the textbook. Basically, don't take this professor for an online class it's been awful.

Assignments are graded at a very slow rate by TAs, and many of the weekly assignments are advanced chemistry with little or no help/explanation from the professor so you have to figure it out on your own or learn from outside sources. I switched from 1251 because this class was "easier" yet received an even lower grade than I had before switching.

Horrific experience! Her definition of active learning is not teaching then throwing a worksheet at us and telling us to work as a group as she walks around to each table and struggles to explain how to do the worksheet when she could've just lectured the whole class at once.

Dr.Asala is very nice (but sassy sometimes) but is so smart that she fails to see what students get confused about & struggles to actually teach. You're expected to do a LOT outside of class & come knowing the material. Best advice is to go to her office hours, do lots of practice problems, read the textbook, & watch videos. This class is VERY hard

Honest Review; Asala herself is a GREAT professor and person and she cares alot, the chemistry department itself is whats horrible. Asala provided many great resources such as problem sets, practice exams, and videos. Its a EXTREMELY tough subject but not impossible. You'll do fine if you master all practice materials given although tests were hard

I enjoyed having Dr. Asala as my professor. General Chemistry 2 is not an easy course and you have to study on your own time. She posts pre-class and post-class videos which are helpful. The lectures were not bad but sometimes they were all over the place, confusing me.

Garbage professor expects you to come to class already knowing the material from the videos that she posts and is then unhelpful when questions are asked. Exams are worth 50% of your grade and the highest class average on an exam was 66%. Knows what shes talking about but is completely unable to teach.

Like many have said, there is a lot to be done in this course. It is quite insane if you have to take this class with any other general ed class. I am a senior and only had this class as a "hard final" and it was a struggle to get through. I hope this professor comes to terms with herself and not think that 16 years of teaching gets you this.
the whole department is horrible

I advise you to please do not take this course unless you have no other classes associated with chemistry. She gives out so much homework and expects you to know the material when you come to class. She makes you watch a lot of videos before class and after when she can just teach the subject in the class. Tests are 50% of your grade as well.

If you do bad on any of the tests your likelihood of failing skyrockets. She begged my class not to "drop" her class because "it will get better," and like an idiot I listened, I struggled terribly. Now I have an F on my transcript.   I was present for every class and did every homework. If not for this class I would have graduated magna cum laude.

Dr. Asala is a great but tough professor. My advice: attend her office hours and work out SO MANY practice problems. Her office hours are more like problem sessions. A few students attend and you can ask individual questions and she works them out on the whiteboard. It's not an easy A, but it's gen chem 2. That's expected. You can work for one.

Dr. Asala is a wonderful, thoughtful, hardworking professor, has lots of office hours every week and stays over time to continue answering questions. Don't get me wrong, chem 2 is VERY DIFFICULT. This class requires a ton of studying no matter who you take, but I highly recommend taking Dr. Asala because she really cares!

You are expected to watch several 20-40 minute long lecture videos before and after class. There are graded pre-class, in-class, and post-class assignments. Big homework assignments due each Friday. Even if you keep up and utilize all resources, exams are extraordinarily difficult. No grades are dropped.

I don't understand how this prof has such a high rating. This class is horrible; DO NOT TAKE IT! Spams you with videos for pre-class and post-class assessments. Would be fine... if here lectures were even remotely passable. But she doesn't explain anything and just gives you a flood of practice questions. And the test are entirely different too.

Despite what many say she's not all that bad. Yes it's hard to understand her sometimes. But as long as you try you can get an A/B for sure. If you miss one day that's a zero for lab so don't miss. She will help you if she can tell you're trying. I got a B in chem so not a chem wizard for context!

Rabinovich is truly one of the sweetest and most caring people. She is one of the first professors I've had where I can genuinely tell she wants her to students to succeed. However, this class isn't a walk in the park, pre labs are long but very helpful. Definitely stay on top of things and attendance matters! Everyone I've asked adores her!

I've had a very wishy-washy experience with her. She can be quite mean/intimidating online but she's a lot nicer in person. Quizzes, worksheets & prelabs are the entirety of your grade & there's no extra credit so lock in! She's also a slow grader + tends to nitpick a lot but she's willing to help those who genuinely try so reach and ask questions.

This class requires you to be present and listen well. The pre-lab assignments tend to be long at times, but it is EXTREMELY beneficial as it will help you understand the material. Professor rabinovich is very nice and she seriously wants you to succeed so trust the process. She is the reason I got an A in both CHEM 1203 and 1204 labs.

1204L: Prof. Rabinovich is kind and helpful. The course is a little more challenging than 1203L—read all module content and do pre-labs. I missed two quizzes, so stay on top of those. Her accent is fine once you adjust. Most important: attendance matters—no show = no worksheet or quiz!

Mrs. Monica was a great lab professor for CHEM 1203L! Now don't get me wrong there was a lot of work for the pre-labs, but she was always helpful if you had any questions and even gave some extra credit for accuracy during the lab. I'd take her over Dr. Striplin any day.

This class was a BREEZE compared to the actual lecture. As long as you may attention in class and follow directions, you'll get at least a B. Also SHOW UP TO THE LAB because it's a big part of your overall grade. She's so sweet as well and very helpful.

I have her for CHEM 1203L and do not freak out. Very nice and is understanding in various situations. Go to class, pay attention in1203 lecture class, and read 1203's textbook. However I always felt rushed with the quizzes that I had 20 min to do. Regardless, stay on top of your lecture class to do well in this lab.
Absolutely waste. Plz don't take her class and don't waste your time. It will literally make you lose your love for chemistry
She is quite honestly the worst teacher ive ever had, I recommend taking it at a community college.

Do not take lab with this professor! The material we are tested on has nothing to do with what we have learned and the quizzes get up to 30 questions including questions that involve math and you are given just 20 mins to complete and they are worth 5 points. The class in itself it set up for students to fail. She does not respond to any emails
this is acc for chem 1251 Lab but it wasnt an option for some reason BUT DONT TAKE HER!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! warning you now.

She's amazing, she is the moment, and her labs and work are so easy. There is a lot of work, but it is the same amount of work in each lab. Compared to TAs who teach the other labs, her grading style is much more lenient.
Very helpful if you go to office hours or need help during class. She wants her students to pass. Pre labs can take a long time.

Mrs. Monica has a very aggressive teaching style, accepting only her criteria to the solution and will blast students in class who are approaching the answer in a different way. She demands harsh amounts of work on prelab HW and will not accept late work AT ALL. She teaches the lab intro for too long and it cuts into the lab submission. GOODLUCK.
Please please please do not take her. Will destroy any type of motivation you have. Was a big waste of time and money. Take it at a community college.

He is very relatable, fair, amazing lecturer. He constantly goes out of his way to bring in fascinating, slightly off-topic examples that really broaden your perspective on biochemistry and biology in general. Overall, an outstanding professor. We as students do not deserve him. Anybody who says otherwise is just a GPA-obsessed crybaby.

Don't take his class unless it's your only one. He expects full-time study, but most of us have other classes and jobs. His exams are brutal and cover random points that barely made sense in lecture. I pulled all-nighters just to keep up with his PDFs. Three exams worth 90% of the grade should've been red flag from the start. Insane.

Overall, I loved this class! Dr Troutman was really engaging and made lectures interesting. He's always willing to help and explain any concept that you are stuck on. The only way to succeed in this course is to show up to every lecture, read through all of his pdfs and attend recitation.Very cool guy once you get to know him!

One of the best professors I've had in college. He teaches what he finds relevant and interesting, which keeps the course engaging without taking away from its quality. The class consists of 3 exams spaced a month out from each other so staying on top of the material is essential. Would've been cool if our semester was longer for this class.

Dr. Troutman's lectures are more engaging than all my other science courses. He's passionate and an excellent lecturer, I've told him that before. I wish classes were longer. The course is tough but doable; study everything and don't just show up, be ready to learn. Exams are tough but if I changed my studying variation a bit I would've landed an A

Dr. Troutman is BY FAR the best professor I have ever had while attending UNC Charlotte. He genuinely wants his students to succeed, and his office hours are very helpful. I really enjoyed this course, and taking it with Dr.Troutman has made it even more enjoyable. TAKE THIS COURSE!!!!!! DO IT

troutman's lectures were engaging and he enjoyed talking about biochemistry. you CANNOT get a good grade by skipping class, or sitting in the back barely engaging with the content since he mentions important topics in class! cramming for his exams also doesn't work, so make his class a priority! a great experience for a class meant to be a weedout!

Dr. Troutman is a wonderful professor at UNC Charlotte, especially for biochemistry 1. While the material is not easy, he provides concise lecture PDF documents, quizzes, slides, review sessions, and sample exams. If you study, you can pass! It's not the easiest, but if you try you can do it. Don't skip lecture or the reviews! Also: theres a curve!

Dr. Troutman makes you care about the content. Attend lecture and annotate slides as he goes along, it's necessary.  He tells you what to focus on, just make note. He has pdfs with detailed and relevant info, I didn't open my textbook once. Dedicate time to study/review outside of class, the content is dense and fast. 90% exams, 10% Canvas quizzes.

I have taken so many chemistry and biology classes here at UNC Charlotte and I can confidently say this was one of those classes that I had so much trouble studying for. Material that was “not something to worry about right now” ended up appearing on the exams. It made the course feel unpredictable and much harder than it needed to be.

Cool guy, but I really do wish he would change how his course is set up. He has so much potential to be one of the best professors on our campus. He doesn't provide specific study guides to prepare us for exams. While he does provide all of his notes, this isn't helpful when there are only three exams, each covering an excessive amount of material.

Professor Troutman is a very good lecturer.  Attendance is optional, but if you miss a class you will fall behind quickly.  He posts good lecture notes which quiz and test questions come from those so they are good to read over.  Read his questions very carefully as he can give you very tricky ones.

Dr. Troutman is a great professor. He tells you exactly what to know and what will be on the exam. He also has lecture notes written in Canvas that outline what he goes over in lecture (but you should attend lecture for application) He is funny and truly wants to challenge students to not only memorize, but learn and apply.

Biochem with Troutman was the most interesting and intellectually fulfilling class I took in my entire undergrad- but it was also one of the most difficult. He tends to teach specific material that may be difficult to find external resources for, so attend every class and record every lecture and make sure you know how to apply the material.

Qz count a lot, know material beforehand. Based exams almost solely on lecture notes - you'll be tested on all of it - exams can be tricky, take your time, study old exams. Recitation helpful - great TA. Textbook/youtube good supplement. 2nd half semester picked up fast. Req's lots of effort for A. Great  lectures, you'll learn a lot.

Troutman has potential but his exams were needlessly difficult and questions often made no sense. Exam averages were in the 50s and 60s and barely ever curved. It's almost like they're trying to make graduating seniors fail on purpose. Study the study guides like the back of your hand and be prepared to do the work, this class is no joke.

Say goodbye to your social life because you will spend all your time studying for your class. Troutman will make you work for your grade. Miss class? You're cooked. His exams are pretty long but he gives practice exams that are helpful for studying. The final is optional if you're happy with your great. Great professor, just a rigorous course.

3.5/5 stars. Dr. Troutman is a nice guy and he is good at explaining things in an understandable way in his lectures. Make sure to take good notes because he might put something on the exam he only briefly mentioned in class. Also some of the multiple choice questions he writes just don't make sense and one option is always none/all of the above.

You will have four tests, weekly quizzes, and a final, no other grades.  He sometimes curves, but there's no guarantee.  You want to be studying this class lowkey all the time.  I don't recommend cramming a few days before, there is just too much material.  Sometimes the test questions are right off the practice exams so do those.  Tough class.

Awesome professor for biochem. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but it does help if you attend since he basically told us what we needed to know in class and he made post-lecture questions w/ answers that we'll need for the exam. Super chill in person too, study the post-lecture q's and you're golden. Final is optional if you're happy with your grade.

This class made me want to reconsider being a chemistry major. He teaches the course like he's talking to people who know about the topics already. The assignments are unbearable, and he hated answering questions. There were also hardly any slides from lecture, he just talks the whole time.

Ms Rabinovich isn't bad, its the TAs that could use some improvement. I knew more about the material covered in lab than my TA did. Ms R seems intimidating, but is nice once you talk to her or email her. She comes across as passive-aggressive in emails but I think that's just how she writes. The pre-labs sucked, but they did make labs a bit easier.

The lab has a lot of tedious prelab assignments, but the professor breaks down the material well if you attend class. Use unstuckstudy and other resources to ace the quizzes. Avoid missing labs - attendance is mandatory.

Some of the prelabs were ridiculously long, we weren't allowed to print them out and had to write the questions by hand. A lot of the quizzes were hard for no reason and weighed a lot. I recommend taking it with Punnya, she was very helpful and not a harsh grader, avoid taking it with the actual professor. Extra credit opportunities available.

It started after the add/drop deadline or I would have dropped it.  Grading is harsh, with 50% of the prelab for every question wrong and a supposed letter grade deduction for absences. Despite being 1 credit hour, pre-labs took anywhere from 2 hours to 9 hours to do. Hope for a good TA, or you will struggle. This class is designed to fail you.

Not great, but she's the only instructor for 1251L. She didn't respond to emails and was rude to students the few times she came into our lab session. The TAs use her grading system, which is harsh. Pre-labs are tedious but helpful in the long run. Labs later in the semester had extra credit opportunities. Don't miss class.

Rabinovich was my Chemistry Lab coordinator and Sara Salamat was my TA and it was pretty bad. At first I thought I was going to have to change classes in anyway but the more you do the labs the more you get a hang of the class. Outside of your resources there is quiet literally no help given and there was a lot of verbal negativity towards students

No make up labs, but if you miss one lab your grade will drop by a letter grade. But good attendance does not affect your grade in any way. Very rude and disrespectful to students. Has yelled at students before. Pre-labs are generally 11-17 questions, but most of the questions have multiple parts. You have to print out your own lab sheets.

Class has ALOT of homework and you got to know what you are doing. You have to be on your A game in lab. If you get Rabinovich herself, she is a very good teacher so long as you care about the subject. Follow every rule to the T and you will do well.
I'm not even done with this god forsaken class yet and I can already tell you never even think about clicking this ladies name.

I had Prof Rabinovich herself as the lab instructor & not the TAs. She spent a lot of time reviewing what we should know from lecture but it's not bad bc she ends up telling you answers to most of the questions on the worksheet you have to do. Quizzes after lab were sometimes hard but doable. Pretty lenient grading on prelabs and worksheets tho.

She spends an excessive amount of time explaining how to do it. You also aren't allowed to miss a single day of class or your grade will drop 10 points. So even if something comes up good luck. For the previous semester the students were allowed to miss a class and have their lowest grades dropped but not anymore.

I had the professor herself for the lab. Personally, she's kinda so-so, not the best but not the worst I've seen at UNCC. You're not able to skip the lab at all or else you end up failing so SHOW UP. The class itself and the quiz/assignments she gives out isn't bad. I wouldn't ask her questions, she comes off kinda harsh and made me feel goofy af.

Honestly, this class isn't bad at all. She has the TA drop the 2 lowest pre-labs, 2 lowest experiments, and the 2 lowest quizzes. It's not difficult to get an A in this course. Make sure you do well on the quizzes though.

First off I did not even know my professors name. I have never seen her. The TA teaches everything in this course. The TA even does all the grading. The material is not hard but you have to pay attention to the little details. I wouldn't give the professor the credit. The TA does everything for her.

For a 1 credit class she gives wayyy too much work. 
For pre labs we would have to write out the ENTIRE lab procedures, introductions and all this garbage "in our own words". There is absolutely no reason for doing this, its pointless busy work and it would take a long time. Professors like this are awful and ruin learning for students

This was by far the worst professor I have ever taken. She wasted one of my days waiting for a zoom I scheduled with her. There are many stories I could tell from the partial class that I took. She is extremely mean to all students and makes nasty comments. The course is extremely unorganized and the grading is insane. Do not take her classes.

I didn't actually have this professor cause I took this Chem lab a semester apart from the Chem class, but my instructor was very awesome. Adam was a great instructor and helped out the students whenever they had questions.

Please if you can avoid this professor... AVOID them! This was one of the most difficult classes I had to take this semester and I'm surprised I got the grade I did. I have accommodations for assignments and she ignored them until she finally listened to my advisors. There are so many things I could say so just don't take her class!

Rabinovich is the rudest, obnoxious, and most annoying professor. Her labs are confusing and have little to no instruction. The TAs are unprepared and don't know what we are expected to do.  Be prepared for quiz questions that you weren't prepared for. Unfortunately, if you're Bio, Chem, Nursing, and need this class you're stuck with her. Good luck

TERRIBLE. My TA and her were absolutely awful. I got a 79.87% in the class and she refused to round it up to a B. she said "there is nothing to do" no extra credit no help nothing. absolutely ridiculous. They ruined my gpa for what? Also, takes points off literally for fun. If you have this class I will be praying.

Personally struggled in the class most of semester bc of the amt of content u need to learn but as a professor she did a good job teaching it. Fair in grading and easy to talk to after class, its just a tough course in general but its not because of her. I def think that if I had a bad prof my grade wouldve been worse so I would take her if u can.

Dr White is an awesome professor. She explained stuff pretty well and was always willing to answer any question that comes her way. The test could be pretty difficult since each unit stacks on each other. Attend class everyday and try to utilize her office hours. Do these 2 things and you should pass her class with ease!

Took Dr. White for CHEM 1251, she's very kind, patient, and makes chemistry easier to understand. If you don't understand, she's willing to further explain things and offers additional support through office hours. She's passionate about teaching and wants you to succeed, 100% recommend her.

Professor White has been the best Chemistry professor I've had here. She clearly states what you'll need to know for exams. Exams are fairly average if you give yourself ample time to study. Pre class assessments due before each class and a homework at the end of each week.

Dr. White is an amazing lady and she really wants people to understand the material she teaches. An issue with her however is that some of the explanations she gives are more confusing than they have to be for a certain topic or way to do things. She is very knowledgeable but I think sometimes she forgets you don't have a PhD too.

Be fully prepared to take notes twice as fast during the last 10 minutes of class, because she has a bad habit of speeding up to get through slides. Other than that. Dr. White is an excellent professor who is very accessible out of class and very much knows her stuff. Chemistry is hard, but Dr. White treats everyone with respect.

A solid choice for a Chemistry professor. She uses in-class polling so you must come to class. If I had applied myself to this class, I could have gotten an A. Do the reading guides before class and listen to lectures. Use "aktiv" as a practice tool. She drops the lowest test. Do the practice exams. An hour of practice a day will give you an A.

Dr. White is probably one of the best chemistry professors I've ever had. She gives relevant classwork and homework that will help with the exams. It is very lecture heavy but it's because there is a lot of material to go through. She is also very helpful if you do not understand a topic. Would definitely take her again!

Professor White is very sweet however if you do really good on all assignments and not so good on exams good luck! Exams are weighted almost 50% of your grade and roughly 4 questions on the exams are worth over 50% while the rest of the questions are multiple choice.

Dr. White is super nice, but her class is incredibly hard. The textbook was free online, but it wasn't the best. She offers plenty of office hours, but she tends to be confusing in her explanations sometimes. The exams are worth 50% of your grade, so try to get good grades on those. Overall, she's a good teacher but this class is VERY hard.

Professor white gives very good lectures.  She always makes time before and after class for people to ask her specific questions about the lecture.  She posts practice tests before every exam and if you do these her exams will be fairly easy.  I really liked her class and I think she makes chemistry fairly easy to understand.  Great professor.

If you want to genuienly enjoy chemistry, then this is the class for you. If you just need to get through CHEM1251, do not take it.

The professor's mode of delivering lectures is highly confusing if you are not used to it, but once you get the hang of it, you're fine. 

Great guy, just expect to put in work for your grade. Fair but difficult class

Professor schemedake was a great professor. He is the head of the chem department and has taught this class so many times. His PowerPoints are kinda messy so you have to pay attention to what he says and writes. The class is hard, but he tries to help you learn. If you want to pass, you NEED to do countless problems, go to office hours, and a tutor

PollEverywhere questions on new material you aren't fully familiar with were used for attendance. If you got it wrong, you get half credit. So you could attend everyday, but your attendance grade could reflect half of that. You'll also have to teach yourself the material for the PCA quiz before class. Otherwise, he is generally thorough and helpful

PollEverywheres graded on accuracy. Assignments due before every class that you have to teach yourself on. Lectures just consist of a powerpoint with pictures on it and he rushes through explaining how/why to do things. Have to pay for ALEKS where the assignments look nothing like the tests. Basically taught myself the whole course.

You better do good on the tests or your grade will plummet, the homework barely improves your grade but it will drop it, if you do bad. You'll have a Pre-Class assessment before the class on stuff you don't know so you'll have to basically teach yourself. He doesn't explain anything at all, literally just expects us to know it.

Pre-class assessments before almost every class and cumulative exams. For me, personally I got through the class using the PCA's and my notes from the textbook. As far as the actual lectures go, he just repeats the material on the PCA. With your notes on hand you can fortunately/unfortunately tune him out mostly.

I finished the class with an A. He's a cool person but I did not like him... He can be very snarky and rude at times. Overall, an okay professor especially for chemistry. I just don't respond to attitudes very well.
Dr. Cao is an amazing professor. His courses do take a lot of effort and studying, but are extremely interesting. He truly cares about what he is teaching, and his lectures make that evident.

Often participation quizzes to show readiness for the days material. Graded inconsistently, have to get every key word to barely receive partial credit. 25% quizzes, 75% exams. Exams are free response, mind-bending, and hard, but doable if you commit 100% of your energy to the course. Good person, class makes it hard to appreciate him though.

The topics are given very broadly and he wants you to spend OUTRAGEOUS amounts of time diving deeper into the topics on your own. There are pop quizzes, so show up. The test are written response, and no multiple choose! Don't take if you have more than 4 classes! Also, he says read the book, but also says don't memorize the book…
A lot of work and boring

Don't know why this is even considered a biology lab. You do maybe 2-3 labs actually related to what you're learning in lecture. Didn't receive the grade I wanted because he wasn't willing to accept the fact that we accidentally submitted the wrong document with PROOF that we did it in class and submitted it IN CLASS.

For a one credit lab, you get graded ridiculously harshly. Everything is busy work and even if your questions only require a two sentence answer, be prepared to write a paragraph FOR EVERYTHING or be prepared to get a bad grade. TA was very passive aggressive and for a lab, you have to make your own project. You only actually get to do like 2 labs.

This is quite literally the most ridiculous class I have ever taken. ZERO point in the difficulty level, much less for a 1 credit hour class. Honestly shame on UNCC for even continuing to have this class the way it is because there is absolutely no reason for it to be 8-20 hours of work a week. No experiments only lectures and projects.
IM TWEAKING HE IS NOT GOOD AT ALL

His classes are demanding and not for the faint-hearted, but deeply rewarding. He pushes students to think more critically and creatively, enabling them to learn concepts in entirely new ways. Honest, direct, tough-love style, but he genuinely cares. Put in real effort and perseverance, and he'll go out of his way to support you. Amazing professor.

I literally transferred from this school 3 years ago and I still come back to remind everyone that Dr. Cao is the worst prof ive ever seen. He is so rude. He called me STUPID in office hours TO MY FACE... The class is organized terribly. It invents demons because ur groupmates are terrible. He also reads these reviews (weird). Awful guy.

Our lab was basically run by a TA the whole semester, so never saw Dr. Cao. Labs were more like "busy work" worksheets, a debate about stuff like climate change, and a huge group project where you design a experiment, write about it, and present. Weekly quizzes were on LockDown, super detailed + timed (10 Q in 10 min...yeah, good luck).

Bio2 lab- prelab quiz timed and lockdown browser,1 in-class assignment, which is supposed to be submitted at the end of lab, and 1 you work on at home to submit before the next lab. Lots of group projects, but there is a form for each assignment in case someone in the group is not participating, so you won't be penalized if you did your part.

Ridiculous amount of work and the projects are a complete waste of time. Quizzes are difficult and he gives a lot of reading for them. TA's didn't know what they were doing and it was an inorganized shitshow every class. One experiment and nothing but busy work. I would rather stick by balls in boiling water every week than come to this lab.

Had him for Evo and Field Ent

His lecture exams are hard because he wants you to actually understand the why's and how's, and his test questions reflect that. So read the textbook and try to understand each topic, engage in the discussion, and go to office hours if need be.

Super nice prof, lots of homework to cushion the exam grades. 4 exams + final, the lowest exam will be replaced by the final. There's a lot of information for A&P but she provides extra credit opportunities and a lot of extra resources. She wants to see you succeed!

Dr. S has 3 exams, and the final exam is optional if you are happy with your grade. She also provides Kahoots for each topic you talk about in class. There is not a lot of work to do outside if you get it done during class. It is a "needy" course compared to my other classes.
super nice teacher! Has three exams total in an optional final, which can replace your lowest test grade. She gives kahoots for every exam and the questions on her test are exactly like the kahoots.

She's a great teacher, very kind, and the classwork is easy to follow. Light homework load outside of class and good study materials provided. Participation is graded on Poll Everywhere, so attendance is important. The textbook is online with pre-class readings.

I love Dr.S! Had her for principles of bio as well, and she structures all her classes somewhat the same. Does pollev every lecture for attendance grade, but doesn't count off points if you get a question wrong. Very intelligent, and you can tell she is passionate about teaching. Her exams are lockdown with multiple choice and 1-3 free responses.

A&P is not easy and is very information-heavy. Dr. S explained everything very well, and notes/review questions were very helpful in preparing for the exams. Study your notes at least every other day! Attend in person as poll-ev's are taken for attendance grades, and it's vital to hear her explanations about the topics if you want to do good!

Love this Professor, easy to get along with and her tests were reasonable. If you utilize her practice quizzes and look back over her lecture slides then you should end with a B minimum. I would take her for majority of my Bio classes if I had the choice!
AMAZING! So easy. Never studied. Finished with a 97. 10/10 would recommend. You do have to go to class tho :(

TAKE HERRRR PLSSSSSSS. She is literally the best science professor at Charlotte. Great lectures and fun classes! Her case studies are really interesting and she will give prizes like gift cards!! If you put in the work you should be fine. No final exams or final presentations.

Dr. S was a very nice and caring professor. On Mondays you have lecture and Wednesday's an in class activity that is graded. Only 3 assessments (not difficult) and an optional final. This course covers a LOT on content but it is not hard to get a good grade if you turn things in and attend class! Attendance is graded on poll everywhere. Recommend!
Best Bio teacher, caring, kind, and optional final!

The professor uses polls everywhere for attendance and participation points. Class is very simple and easy to pass as long as you do the work! The professor takes her time with the students and explains the material very well would recommend it!!
This professor knows what they are talking about. The accent can throw you off at times but overall very good lectures. 10/10 professor.

I took her for this semester and she's a good professor, but it's a big workloads to pass this class. She's nice, but she does talk pretty fast and there is a lot of information to know. The exams are tough I'm not gonna lie. The homework assignments usually 30min -1hr long. The labs are easy I passed with an A.

It is obvious she wants her students to succeed! She takes the time to meet with us outside of class to discuss ways we can improve our grades. The exams coincide with her notes and lectures perfectly. Anatomy is a tough course, but feeling like your teacher is on your side makes all the difference. I'm so glad I get to take from her again!

She was nice, however, if you want to get a good grade on the exams you need to reteach yourself with her slides. I recommend reading her slides and using the Kahoots she provides with the module. (DONT just do the Kahoots, it doesn't have everything that will be on the test)

Dr. Somayaji is honestly one of the best professors out there. You have four tests; the final is optional and can replace the lowest test grade. You have a lecture one day and do an activity with the lecture's content during the class. Reading quizzes on canvas. You work on a very simple project throughout the semester. Very easy going and funny.

Amazing professor, one of my favorites ive had at UNCC so far. Class is very manageable. The class is broken down with three unit tests, an optional final exam (replaces lowest score), weekly at home reading quizzes through Canvas, in class activities, and attendance (drops a bunch of abesneses). So nice, gives easy to fill out outlines.

I took her summer course and it was a lot of information to know in 5 weeks so a lot of effort is required. However, it is definitely possible to pass as she was an awesome professor that wants you to succeed in this course. I recommend focusing on the practice quizzes and on the MypollEV questions on the lecture slides!!

Dr. S was awesome. Took her pathophysiology class and it was super easy. Expected a 4000 level class to be hard but this was basically a completion grade. No exams, just case studies and a few projects. She is very caring, learns everyone's name, and understands that life happens outside of class. I would certainly take her again!

Theres lots of homework and attendance is required, but the textbook is free and she makes class enjoyable. You can tell she truly cares about her course and her students. Always reachable outside of class.

Dr. S is a great professor. She's very caring and sweet, and will learn your name even in a 150+ person class. The course itself is very fast-paced and information heavy, but she does her best to make it easier. 2274 attendance was mandatory and graded on PollEverywhere (with location on). Do the practice quizzes to study for tests!!!
Honestly I loved Dr. S and her class. She is easy to understand and teaches very good. I would recommend to anyone who takes bio 1101. Also her TA was amazing and helpful!

Dr. S is a great teacher who genuinely wants her students to succeed. Anatomy is a hard class but her class is doable. Tests account for 80% of your grade, but you can do well if you study her lecture slides and outline. There's not a lot of homework and doing the practice quizzes is the best way to prepare for her exams.
She is clear about what she expects, the tests are just very hard and are a big part of your grade. She is caring though and even with 200 students she will learn your name.

This course is very easy; I took it to fulfill a gen ed requirement. Class is structured w lecture and then class activity. Not a lot of work load at all. Just study the notes and you will be fine on tests. And Dr. S is very sweet! Not a bio major but if I were, I would take classes w her.

Her accent is very heavy... almost to the point where it's hard to pay attention to her lectures. Her exams are very difficult. I went to class almost every day and still ended up with a C. Meh professor.
Thick accent and activities are sometimes unrelated to topic material but showing up to class, paying attention, and engaging in activities will result in a good grade.

Dr. Somayaji is an amazing professor! She is knowledgeable and passionate about her field of study and does what she can to help students learn and become better students. Class was an easy A. Topic assessments and reading quizzes were open note and there was no final exam, just a guided 6-part project throughout the semester that was really easy.

Dr.S is amazing! She is so kind and understanding, she genuinely cares for her students. Lectures are long, but they're very detailed and she is clear about what's going to be tested. Study the outlines and do the practice quizzes, they are so helpful. A lot of material to know, but her exam questions are straightforward and easy to understand
You can tell she's passionate about the subject and actually wants us to learn. Very encouraging and easy to understand during lectures. Would definitely recommend to all of my friends.

Took this class in Fall 2024. Exams are challenging, but if you study the powerpoint slides and follow the note outlines you'll be fine. Reviewing homework questions also helps as sometimes they will appear again on the test albeit reworded. Review sessions with TA are also helpful. Be careful though, because it is a lot of information to memorize.
She is not polite and caring. and doesn't let us to ask the questions in the class.

She's friendly and approachable, but not an effective teacher. The course relied heavily on lectures, and the exams were based on her PowerPoint presentations. The chapter outlined notes she provided were essential for my success.

Take her class if you're a good tester. Outside of this class she is an incredible resource and person, and she's incredibly kind. Unfortunately, the tests are effectively 50 trick questions and there is no way to get extra credit or test corrections for her class,. If you're going try this class under her, only use the PPTs and go to lectures.

Don't worry, Bullock's inability to concisely summarize material in lectures is coupled with her insanely detailed and nightmare inducing exams. This would be less annoying if her exams were based on the textbook, but they're not- and they're also nothing like the homework assignments. Avoid.

very passionate teacher, but tests are very tricky like they're made for you to fail, with very small and sometimes irrelevant details posing as questions. you need to absorb everything in the textbook and her slides to get an A in her class. i wouldn't recommend taking any other difficult classes if you are taking this class with her.

I really liked MRS. BULLOCK she did tell you extra things to know for exams. But it just seems like the exams were set up to trick you with 50 questions. She would say certain things you won't need to remember on the test but they ended up being on the exam. You really need to attend class and study hard if you want an A or B. She is very caring.

The professor is pretty average. Lectures are prerecorded online. If you want to get an A in this class over the summer it has to be your LIFE. Treated it like a full time job and that's how I made the A. Insane amount of memorization and some exam topics are not in the lecture or textbook. Take it if you have to, but be ready to put in the work.

I took this prof. Summer one online cell biology class. 

I felt that that class moved very quickly, due to the fact that it is a summer 5 week class. 

I typically had one piece of homework a night and the time it took me ranged from 30 minutes to an hour. 

Tests are pretty difficult, 50 questions with lockdown browser.
DO NOT TAKE IN THE SUMMER. Does not drop exams and its a lot of information to take in for the weekly exams. Study guide is not much help either.

Dr. Bullock's class wasn't terrible, but it wasn't great either. There was a lot of busy work that was time-consuming and her lectures were dry and boring. The busy work was mostly graded by completion thankfully, but her tests were kind of hard and she asked some things that we never went over in class. Not an easy A

Nicest professor but she cannot teach. Her lectures are boring and she talks way too much. Not very engaging and will watch over your shoulder at notes. Her exams sometimes asked too much detail but were otherwise manageable. Didn't require textbook. Shes a solid option for the course but I'm sure there are better. Don't expect to gain from lecture

Dr. Bullock is AWESOME!!! I would recommend taking her for any class you can. She knows so much and does an amazing job at explaining things. She also really cares about her students and really works to get to know you. She's one of the best professors I've ever had.
It is clear that Dr. Bullock loves cell biology and loves teaching it.  She is a wonderful lecturer and I really enjoyed her class.

I enjoyed Dr. Bullock's class this summer. I am not a Biology major so some of the topics were a little confusing for me but if you study the PowerPoints you should be fine. She gives extra credit based on scores so if the highest grade was 88 she will give 12 extra points if you complete the test corrections

The class was pretty easy to understand and grasp if you come to lectures and do the post lecture work. Assignments that weren't exams were commonly graded for completion. One group project that lasted 4-5 weeks where you could finish it in 3 days. Lenient when it comes to short answer and longer questions in exams.

Having a professor that enjoys their job makes a difference. This was one of the easiest science classes I have taken here. It helps a lot to go to lectures because info she gives will most likely come up on tests. Tests were 60%, but she sent out really helpful study guides. She also gives small assignments to help your grade.

I would not recommend her to anyone. She will give 0s for any late work no matter how late. Her instructions are not always clear. I reached out ahead of time to try and reschedule an exam and she was not flexible. Her grading is really harsh and there's a lot of work.

Dr. Wells is a lovely professor! She's very accessible and responds to emails so fast with good feedback. While she is a bit of a tough grader, it's not a problem because she follows her rubrics to a T. If you have everything in the rubric down, you'll do well on her assignments. Also don't submit work late!!! She doesn't accept late work!!!
Dr. Wells makes her online classes incredibly engaging. Not only was the content interesting, but her video lecture with quizzes also helped to absorb the content.

Overall, she is a nice person, but her late work policy is ridiculous and unforgiving. She accepts no late work, even if you submit 5 minutes after the deadline. She claims she cannot make exceptions to accept late work, but there would be no need for an exception if she didn't have a crazy policy. Don't take if you work or have a busy schedule

This professor honestly isn't very good. She often makes mistakes using technology (in an online class) and I just didn't get much out of the two courses I took with her. If you have a genuine interest in learning biology then I would take another professor's class.
She is a great professor. There is a group project over the course of the semester but very easy.  This class is truly light work!!

Dr. Wells is a fantastic professor. Come to class prepared each day having done your reading and assignments and you'll do great in her courses. She is passionate about conservation and is a great biologist. Highly recommend her classes.

Dr. Wells overall was a good professor. Very easy to reach via email, and was helpful with in her responses. She does make you do a group project with 3-4 people, but its split up throughout the semester so it really wasn't bad. If you do the work you'll succeed in her class.

Semester-long group project but its chunked out so not that bad. Grading on it is insane though with unhelpful rubric. Classwork was minimal and easy. Exams were chill, you could study the night before and be more than prepared. Just be ready to get tons of points docked off at the beginning stages of the project.

Ever heard of the song Work by Rihanna? Well you better get ready to "work work work work work" because this class is slammed with busy work. Very kind professor but just an insane amount of work each week. Need to be able to know how to record a podcast to pass...

Exams aren't hard if you do the study guides. Lecture notes have great visuals and are easy to follow. The projects are an easy A if you put solid work into it. She is super easy to reach via email and is so easy to work with- she will accommodate you and do her best to help you do your best. Can't wait to take her again for conservation bio!

This was a poorly managed course with a grading metric that the professor refused to define. To get a perfect score on anything, you must mention a specific thing on her mind that isn't in the rubric. Asking her to clarify is pointless because she thinks scheduling a meeting for her office hours would be special treatment.
Decent teacher and she teaches decent subjects, but her grading is insane. The course pacing is the worst and her online exams are on Friday when due midnight when you literarily have other classes.

Dr. Wells is a real nice lady. The class isn't particularly difficult as it's most of the stuff you've learned earlier in life. The exams used lockdown browser with the camera but weren't hard. The TA offered review sessions which were very helpful for exams. Not my favorite material but I'd take Dr. Wells again!

BIO 3144 with Professor Prosser had interesting content, but communication was slow, and grading felt inconsistent. Exams were tough, but the TA's review sessions helped. You need to do all readings and buy the textbook to succeed. Overall, I learned a lot, but the course could improve in fairness and support.
Dr. Wells is 10/10. She comments back on all student assignments. Organized canvas page, quick grader, fast email responces.
Nice person but Disorganized asl when it comes to being a professor. takes random points off.
She is a very tough grader. I took this class (bio 5244) as a summer class and it was so much work. She is very picky but gives good feedback.
Lectures are great and she gives study guides for her exams which are super helpful.

Great person but horrendous professor, takes points off randomly, very disorganized and shows no remorse towards unprecedented circumstances. She had it out for me this semester for no logical reason. DON'T TAKE SCI. WRITING WITH HER! I would rather retake three writing intensive labs at the same time than take that poor excuse of a class again.

She's great! Literally no complaints. Exams are open-ended written questions on case studies but you can work together in groups on them. Her note guides are very helpful to know what will be tested on. If you fail this class you literally just aren't trying or need to change your major. I hardly studied and got above a 95 on all exams.

She's really easy to talk to and nice. Will re-explain things if you ask. Her lectures are boringly mind-numbing BUT the class is easy-- no tests except the final, just reading guides, learning catalytics (like poll everywhere), weekly chapter quizzes as HW and worksheets graded on accuracy. If you need an easy bio prof Harris is the way to go.
Not understanding gives no grace to students. It doesn't take much to be understanding and personable. But she ain't got that
The class was easy. Her TA mainly ran the class so I can't really rate her as a professor.
She is a great teacher, who is helpful and understanding. The material in this class is tough and extensive, however she offers many resources and grades very graciously.

Professor Harris is incredibly kind and an excellent teacher. She makes biology simple and clear, even for students who don't love the subject. There are 4 exams and a final; ours were open notes, but that may change. Homework is straightforward, and her expectations are clear. Overall, a very good and fair class.

Class was run by TA's. 2 assessments, both worth 25% of grade and use Respondus browser. Labs due Sunday. 3 writing assignments, each worth 5% and are short. TA's were chill. Entirely solo work. Labs are fairly clear. Extra credit questions on assessments.

Mrs. Harris was so kind and made us feel cared for. With all due respect, I will say the lectures she gave can be boring, and this class requires studying, as although the reading guides may help, you have to know the content well enough to answer any question on an exam, and exams are pretty much the only thing that can bring your grade up.
bro her test so mid. ass teacher. She doesn't know how to teach. monotone asf. lame as hell

She was very kind and understanding when it came to submitting things late or being absent. All her exams are open note, which is useful but the questions are worded in a way that you still need knowledge and understanding of the topics. She gives extra credit opportunities on every single exam and is an easy grader.

Mrs. Harris' lectures are incredibly boring. Her tests are open notes and gives a study guide to fill out but they only help to answer a few questions on the test. I would not take a class with her ever again and I wish I took this class with a different professor and online. Choose someone else
So unhelpful. I asked for help and all I got was "are you studying?"

Very boring lectures; however, while attendance is not mandatory, not going will probably result in failing the class. Tests are very hard, and while open note, the given notes are not at all comparable. In class assignments including essays do nothing for you grade so fail the test you are essentially screwed. Learning catalytics are also crucial.

Professor Harris was very kind. Relevant lectures that summarize the textbook, open-note (printed only) tests + provided study guides that are extremely useful and relevant to the test (you'll likely see the same questions). My only complaint is that the four exams that make up your final grade are heavily weighted (40%), so you'll need to do well.

Mrs. Harris was a very good professor. This was a hard class when taking it, but she gives you chapter outlines to use for notes. I recommend filling these out before lecture and going to the PAL sessions. She is a nice test grader and will give you partial points on free response questions on exams

I loved Mrs. Harris. She always made us aware of her email and office hours in case we needed something outside of class. Her lectures could be confusing but she is thorough with any questions she is asked. She was lenient with grading where credit was due. She was great at public speaking and always made us feel cared for.

I loved having Professor Harris for BIO2120. Honestly, if you read the textbook and do her reading guides for each chapter as you read, you should do fine in her class. Her tests cover everything that is said in class and there are no surprises. I recommend going to PAL sessions for this course as well. They were helpful and helped me succeed.

she is such a great professor, ATTEND the review sessions she would legit tell us what was on the test, she is very sweet and explains stuff really well. the test are case studies, but she gives you so much resources to practice, study and you'll do perfectly fine in this class

Mrs. Harris is very nice. Her lectures can be a bit boring at times, but if you go you'll definitely get something out of it. The first two exams were easy and then the last two were harder. The third one in particular was really hard. Study and you'll do fine!

The first two tests were a 2/4 hard to me, but the last 2 were super easy. studying and reteaching yourself at home, and attending PAL sessions, and applying things will help you on the test. And do the chapter quizzes. She uses some questions from the chapter quizzes on the test. Especially on the last 2 tests.

If you feel like you aren't learning anything in this class, READ THE TEXTBOOKS while doing the chapter reviews at the same time, and attend PAL sessions. This is how I was able to do well on her tests and understand things. There are also application questions, you won't find all the things you studied for on the test. STUDY and watch yt videos!

She is sweet and easy to work with, but there is SO much information for the hard tests. Its hard to studying for them as some material isn't even mentioned, its annoying.Also, I feel like we are tasked to critically think on the tests. If you don't do well on the first test, Goodluck lol. But, there is a lot of things in the gradebook to balance.

The class itself isn't hard, and the lectures are very well said. She doesn't move fast, and will answer any question given. But, the test are hard, they are graded 40%, so if you do poorly, it will absolutely show in your grade. Attend the PAL sessions as they help a lot. I would recommend this class if BIO2120 is required, she is very very nice.

Mrs. Harris is awesome, I loved her class. That being said, it is a difficult. Her exams are all short answer questions based off of case studies that are impossible to understand if you don't put in the work with the reading guides and textbook readings. Attendance is mandatory and that ends up counting for almost 20% of the final grade.

Mrs. Harris was the best! Exams are rather frequent and they're all written response on paper, but go to lecture and do the note guides and you'll be perfectly fine. She's very caring and sweet, and she'll clarify anything you need during lecture/office hours. The course itself is not that difficult, and the material is very interesting. Take her!

She wasn't bad. Weekly pre-class activity and chapter quizzes, Access Pearson is used almost every day and her tests have a lot of application questions. Her lectures weren't bad, she didn't make you feel bad for not knowing something. Final project on a genetic disorder due at the end of the semester. Overall, I would recommend.

Ms. Harris is overall not terrible. It may take you a few weeks to get used to her teaching style and grading criteria as she is kind of a tough grader. Do the learning guides and use the case studies in the book and you will be very prepared for her exams. Go to class as she does in class things that count for a big portion of your grade.

The class is textbook and lecture-heavy but she provides the PowerPoints and a reading guide so it is very clear what she expects you to remember for the tests. Scheduled multiple review sessions for every test. It is clear Professor Harris wants you to succeed and if you do the work you can easily get a good grade. Expect frequent free writes

Biology 1 - Overall a solid professor, the work stays consistent with pre-class activities and chapter quizzes that happen every week, no pop quizzes, very nice professor, her tests are pretty hard and make you study a lot of the minor details. The tests are 40% and the final is 10%, there is also a final project/poster about researching a disease.

The class itself is relatively simple. You have to put in the work, but you can get an A. Make sure you pay attention in class, you have to answer questions in class that end up being a large portion of your grade. As far as Mrs. Harris is concerned, she is willing to work you and has solid lectures. Take her if you want to learn.

The course content is not very hard. There is not a lot of homework but attendance is mandatory and is taken by learning catalytics. Her tests are doable but are sometimes confusing and her grading is subjective. You will do fine if you attend class and study the reading and note guides. Not all of the content is discussed in class.

The tests were hard and takes a bit to figure out what to study. She sometimes tests on random, small details in the notes/lecture. But you can ask her any question and she is so ready to help you understand. her PowerPoints aren't the best & should attend class. She is very caring & interactive with the class.

I absolutely loved Professor Harris.  I was nervous going into this class because I didn't know what to expect. The PowerPoints in class are extremely helpful if you pay attention and engage with the material. She is a very visual teacher which I love. She was very helpful when you had questions. Go to class! It made all of the difference.

The TA that taught my class was Janki, she was a very sweet girl. There's a quiz in the beginning of each class 3-4 questions. The material was easy and her teaching was concise. There wasn't any homework (unless you didn't finish something in class). The final is a presentation, which was easy, just cant use flashcards.

Amazing lecturer and gives activities in class to understand the material. A lot of homework tho, but honestly it helps your grade. Attendance was mandatory but you can miss 3 days. Exams were straight from the learning objectives so make sure you study those, there were 3 exams. Final was optional if you were happy with your grade. Sweet professor

Class was fairly simple, lectures helped understand concepts a bit more indepth. Easy homework, but exams are 60% (there's 3). The study concepts she gives are basically the questions on exams. There is a textbook, but it wasn't used and when it was needed she supplied the pages. Pollev questions for attendance.

Took 3144 w/her and loved her!!There are 3 exams not including the final exam which is optional. There was also a group project which will be presented at the end of the course. Very interactive class and tests were fair. Tests consisted of multiple choice and free response questions but you should be good to go if you study the chapter objectives

Dr. Wisner was an amazing professor! I loved going to her lectures, and she made the info really easy to understand. There are pollev questions in every class. The exams were not terrible, the final exam is optional if you're happy with your grade. I would def take her again!!

She is great. Just finished a summer course with her and it was amazing. Easy class and she was the best. Gives fun projects, interests you in her class. She really loves what she teaches and it shows. Overall, great professor. Would take again.

I had Wisner for recitation on Friday's and she was always very sweet! However, for the lab the TA grades and teaches everything. This lab is very fun if you end up with good groups/partners. Very heavy on group projects/papers and many of these projects overlapped each other so it made it a bit difficult. Weekly lab quizzes.
Prof. Wisner is great! She cares about her students in her class and after graduation. I also had a great TA!

100% of your grade is from exams. He changed the dates of his exams a month into the semester. After telling all the students to plan accordingly. Online test can only be taken during class time. There are no makeup tests under any circumstances. Most questions are written response, but he will take off points for defining additional terms.

This class was TOUGH. Lockdown +webcam for exams which you wouldve barely passed had you been allowed to have open notes. Going to class helps in his exams but his classes are boring. Seems like he lost his passion for teaches and now just does it for a paycheck. It is possible to get a B but no shot you'll get an A. Only grades are exams.
Tough grader, would not take again

WORST PROFESSOR EVER! SAVE YOURSELF AND DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS! I am a straight-A student and this professor basically ruined my chances of getting into a grad school because of how strict he is with his rules and is not easy-going or understanding at all.

Powerpoints = Confusing
Tests = Confusing wording
No calculator/paper (Dihybrid cross/chi square is impossible) 
4 Exams, Optional final, but better hope you get the final cuz it cant be dropped
Monotone and boring
Little care for students
Snarky/Pretentious comments in emails and announcements
Document which explains "how to success", all lies.

Steck only grades on 4 exams. The class averages were between 66-68 per exam. One exam is dropped. You have to be a good test taker to do well and study his slides and go over the textbook. Boring lecturer and reads straight from the powerpoints.

Todd Steck absolutely sucks as a professor. This is by far the most boring class I have taken yet. Lectures are "death by PowerPoint" where he just reads off the slides in a monotone voice and is awful at giving examples for the information. He has no enthusiasm and is pretensious. Don't take him if UNCC decides to pay for a decent professor.

All of these bad reviews are not accurate at all. Dr. Steck is very clear with the material, I literally went of the PPTs and practice questions. Made an A on every exam. I took Steck in the fall and my brother took him in the spring. Not a hard class.

He teaches a genetic class and does not allow a calculator or paper. The only thing provided for exams is a notepad online and doing dihybrid crosses are next to impossible. Also, the math for chi-square needs squaring which the calculator that's provided does not have; this would not be a big deal if you could keep track of your steps on paper

The class isn't really hard, it just feels kind of dry and unengaging. Your grade mostly comes from quizzes and exams, and the exams are pretty tough. Some people get A's, but I ended up failing. The professor is really nice though and if you ask for help and stay consistent he will help you. If you do are well in his class ask for research.

He's difficult to understand during lecture and rambles. If you ask a question, he'll just repeat what he said previously and won't try to explain it differently. Graded by 4 exams (22% each)&pollev, No final. Very difficult to succeed if you don't do well on an exam because there is no hw/extra credit to bring up your grade. No responses to email

He has a very heavy accent, making it harder to understand. His class is based on exams only of 300+ slides, he has no hw no projects, just exams and pollev. He does not answer questions, and even if you participate, he will let you know you are wrong. His reviews are not helpful either. I would not recommend taking him.

Amazing lectures on virology, very informative and up too date with current events. A fair lecturer as well with the tests not being to hard as you are allowed a cheat sheet to work with. I would recommend taking his class heavily, and you will easily get an A.

This is the third class I've taken with Valery, he might be one of the best professors in biology.  He doesn't give HW or Projects or Papers or group work; just 4 exams and attendance which is taken with PollEv and graded for accuracy.  He allows a cheat sheet on exams.  Build this sheet from his lecture slides and you'll do fine.  10/10 for Valery
You can barely understand him, he rambles during every lecture and doesn't answer questions. The tests are based on about 300ish slides and they are not easy. DO NOT TAKE HIM

Dr. G is one of the best biology lecturers.  Grading is done with 4 exams and Attendance.  Attendance is done with pollev--graded for accuracy, but the questions are usually something he talked about 3 minutes ago.  Make your study guide based off his slides and the pollev questions and you're set.

If I could reverse time, I would have taken something else. Even though he is a professor, it is pretty evident he is built for research as he cannot engage a class full of 120 students. Professor Valery gives very enthusiastic lectures which I found interesting.  There are only a few grades in the class though, four tests and participation.  He allows a cheat sheet for tests.  Make your cheat sheet directly from the slides and pollev questions and you should be okay.

He's one of the best professors I've had at UNCC. He REALLY knows his stuff. He's really good at making things understandable. His tests aren't too difficult at all. He's a lenient grader. Virology class was way better than expected. I loved his class. Attendance was mandatory but it was not a problem bc of how great his lectures were. Tests and quizzes were online. Lab TAs taught all of the material. Labs were difficult to understand in a group setting, in addition to the post-lab questions. Easy class. She's just extra. The labs don't correspond with what we are doing in the lecture. Papers didn't help understand the material. Decent amount of work and it seemed unnecessary. Easy A though. Just follow the rubrics
Dr. Pass is so sweet and caring. She always looks out for the best for her students and will always work with you no matter what. You can tell she loves teaching and cares about all of her students.

Make sure to be at every class, if you miss a lab you will have to make it up for an hour-long one. The midterm is very easy, however the final is challenging. SO MANY PAPERS FOR A 1 CREDIT HOUR CLASS. I had a great TA and she was able to help us with everything but still. The amount of work for this lab is ridiculous.
Never responds to emails and doesn't even teach.

She doesn't even teach the classes the TA's do. So it really depends on who you get but mine didn't teach that well and your grade is basically made up of your midterm and final (each 50% of grade). You'll have homework and easy projects but they don't bring up your grade at all.

we don't ever meet Dr. Pass because one of her TA's teaches it instead. it's super hard and graded by basically the difficult midterm and final which are each half your grade. other assignments and projects are easy but do nothing to your grade. don't take her.

Dr. Pass doesn't even teach the class but her TA's do (or some type of grad student i think). We never even met Dr. Pass. The projects are easy but don't count that much so it's based on midterm and final which are hard. don't take her
Dr. Chi is great. He's very funny and engaging. The class is very easy. There is so much extra credit. I never read the textbook and got an A on every test.

Dr. Chi is a great professor. Very clear that he enjoys what he does. TBH only got an A in the class because of the extra credit. He is a really funny person and incredibly knowledgeable, but if you wanna meet him personally it gets really serious. Dr. Chi is a really caring professor and very funny! He gives lots of bonus points, the final is not cumulative, and the homework and paper assignments are pretty easy! The class is hard but Dr. Chi makes it worth it. He is incredibly knowledgable, funny, and caring and really makes sure you understand the material. Attendance isn't mandatory but really helps with learning for the exams.

Personally, I learned nothing from Dr. Chi. His lectures were BAD! However, he sets up his students for success by his course format. Dr. Chi is an amazing professor who I highly recommend. He is really kind and funny. You can tell he really wants his students to do well. The tests are hard so I recommend not taking extensive notes during class and just listening. Then go home and look at the PowerPoint again. If you can take him..DO IT! Lots of extra credit too.

I would not recommend this professor. She is unable to grade assignments. Tonight she made a threat if you don't email me about a missing grade by tonight I'll give you a 0. She posted this at 4pm. Group discussions that had to be presented, or an individual presentation/group presentation each week. Dr. Ferdous makes what could be a really neat class awful. The tests are EXTREMELY information heavy and you basically have to memorize everything on the slide sets to do good on the exams. This course was more difficult than it needed to be bc of this professor. She seemed to want to help when the entire class was struggling, but made it feel condescending. This course was challenging due to a lack of communication, as emails often went unanswered. It's a pretty easy class if you aren't lazy about studying and watching the lectures. Tests are pretty straightforward if you know how to apply the material. A hard course because of this professor. The average for the 1st exam was a 50, she refuses to take any accountability for this.
