Dr. Ferdous was very responsive and cares for her students. The class is mainly group assignments so pick your group carefully. As long as you keep up with the assignments and study for the assessments, it should be an easy A.
Weekly quizzes and homework with a group. Tests are 50% of your grade and come from the lectures posted online. Class is fairly easy as long as you keep up.

Very kind Professor who will understand and care if you have questions. DEFINITELY test-heavy as tests are worth 50% of the total grade, so make sure you study and read the lectures. Other than that, amazing class!

The professor is accommodating, caring and understanding. There are weekly group projects, assignments (due on Wednesdays) and Exams taken with Lock Down browser (due on Sunday's.) Dr. Ferdous is very nice and caring. The lectures are a bit hard to follow due to having lots of information and big, scientific words and some of the test are difficult but it is very manageable. This course had only four exams, which focused on small details. DO NOT TAKE 3166 in person with this professor! Only graded on exams and exams are difficult! Does not email back promptly. Please dont be dumb and take this class for credit with him. Reg

The grade is 100% based on exams with no study guides. He did provide extra credit for attending weekly review sessions, and a few practice quizzes. It is hard to understand what he is saying, and the lectures are not paced well or very helpful.

Professor is so unengaging and shows little care about the class. He doesn't teach, he just talks. 4 exams make up your entire grade (and they are extremely difficult and specific). hes not open note anymore :(

Online. 5 Exams, final is mandatory. All open note and open book. You cannot fail this class. Easy A, take him!!!!!!

Your only assignments in this class are tests but they are open note and most of the answers are right in his powerpoint. He also offers 2 extra credit sessions a week where you can get up to 5 points added to your final grade. If you are going to take genetics I would take it with him.
Great professor. Exams will be your only grades for the class though. His power points are easy to understand and he offers optional review sessions two times a week. Take him if you can.

Very receptive of class feedback and it is a bio class, come to class and don't leave early. She is such a wonderful person! Prof Lassiter is SO RECEPTIVE of class feedback. After the class did bad on one of the exams, she changed teaching method & genuinely helped my grade & made me motivated to learn bio a lot more. This teacher is the best she is so helpful and will listen to your questions and genuinely wants to help do better. She gives so much extra credit because she wants to help your grade. This class is a class where you have to teach yourself.

Such a kind woman! She responds to emails quick! (30m-1day). Very lecture heavy, takes up a lot of time. Dr. L is super fun and kind and wants you to learn. As a lecturer for general biology, she's very detailed oriented. The material is somewhat difficult, especially for a bio I course. I had Dr. L for two classes and enjoyed them. Attendance is not mandatory; sometimes she gives quizzes that can only be taken in class. She goes through slides quickly. lovely quick to respond

TERRIBLE TEACHER!! she only reads from the slides during her lectures. does not explain how to complete the hw assignments. gets annoyed when we ask questions. has 1 hour of office hours/ week, and sometimes she won't be in her office then and will not notify anyone. does not give any support to full online classes. Does not have a schedule- just posted all the homework and assignments on the first day of classes and made them all due on 3 different dates. The course seemed interesting, but I ended up dropping/withdrawing. Seemed fun until she graded homework. such a fun class and great professor. goes over a LOT of topics, from all of arthropoda, to apiculture and med-vet. exams are straightforward with 20-30 ec available for memorizing families. hw is drawing NC insects, and grades fairly. very flexible, engaging lectures, and a professor committed to getting students interested in the world of insects

I absolutely recommend this class. Dr. Stellwagen is a very passionate professor. As much as I hate bugs, I loved this course and became fond of bugs. You can definitely tell that she cares about her students, providing fast responses and useful feedback on class assignments. Can be a tough grader. Exam format was different from the norm and challenging, but overall interesting class.

The professor was great. Engaging, encouraged questions, treated everyone with respect, challenged the way we thinked and provided timely feedback. I enjoyed the course content and learned a lot from this class!

She's amazing. Take her if you can!!!!

Dr. Johnson is kind and very enthusiastic w/ a dry sense of humor. Be aware that this class is extremely dense in material. To be successful, attend every class, do the reading beforehand, & don't procrastinate studying for exams! This class is fun but requires work!

Doing well in the class almost impossible.

Loved the topics explored in the class! Lecture-heavy, exams are about 70-80% written response. very strict. I withdrew from this class in the first two weeks due to insane work load. 19 page bio lab, 4 quizzes (which each have 6 study plan quizzes before you can attempt them) and an exam all due. we had assignments due before our first class meeting so many started the course with an F :')

I took this class with this professor without knowing anything about her since there was no rating on rate my professor but I would not recommend taking her. Neelakantan is... alright. Two 50 min meetings weekly, ranging from 15-25 minutes worth of time of true "lecture". Majority of time spent doing monotonous group discussions that are worthless. Mr.Saravanan Neelakantan does not participate in student's lives at all. He doesn't warn about exams in advance. Grades assignments are very late. The exams are very different from what is in the manual.

Had her for Invertebrate Zoology, not General Zoology (BIOL-3231). 4 Credit hours, lots of extra credit. Made a subject I found hard to find interest in, interesting! Highly recommend for any Bio Major!

No cumulative final, he fourth exam acted as the final, which was great. The lab was definitely my favorite part. It's just one section but super hands-on, way more than any labs I've done before. I got really good practice with microscopes, dissections, and anatomy skills.

I've taken a couple of classes with her, and she is honestly one of the best professors I've had so far. Dr. Acosta is committed to engaging students, whether it be looking at live specimens in lab, or providing study guides. She explained everything well and prepared us well for the exams. Exams were straight from the lecture slides. One of the easier professors for biology, tests are based on lectures with helpful study guides/study slides to help guide you. She is one of my favorite professors! her slides are very helpful. her exams are not hard at all. she is very understanding when you miss an assignment. very sweet! if you want to pass take herr!
Very sweet. One of my favorite professors. She keeps the lectures straight to the point and if very respectful to everyone!
Professor Acosta is very good at teaching. She is very knowledgeable and kind. Definitely take her class!

she is the best! it was a pretty easy class, she releases the module for each week around sunday night, everything is due at the end of the week. the beginning of the class was group assignments which kinda sucked for an online class because everyone is hard to reach. exams are lockdown but no camera. LOVE HER.
I LOVE HER!!! She is so sweet and caring. You can tell she loves what she does. Textbook reading and 2 textbook assignments per week. 5 exams with lockdown browser. Responds super fast as well!

Really nice professor. Class had pearson homework, pearson quizes, and reading textbook checkoff's. Very easy and basically everything was just participation. Some canvas assignments here or there and also really easy, maybe 5 overall throughout the semester. 5 Exams, all online, lockdown no webcam and no time limit. Responds fast and super caring.

Ms. Kabir's biology class was the most interesting and perfectly rigorous course I've taken at UNCC so far. 10/10 ive had her three times three different level courses for bio she is amazing and understanding and is easy

Very easy A however don't expect to learn too much just by online videos unless async is your thing. Videos are dated from during COVID times. I took the online summer asych course with Dr. Kabir. there was a LOT of work, including chapter quizzes, and Mastering homework. Tests were weekly and an optional final. She was very responsive and helpful. some of the lowest grades are dropped. the summer term is really fast paced.

2 of the tests were easy the other 2 were much harder but she is great answers emails fast and wants you to pass. Some of the work especially the pack back felt like busy work but hey if one busy work assignment is the worst thing she is a pretty good professor. twice she didnt open the tests till 3 hours after she said lol but still had time.
Kabir held an easily accessible class that was also easily followable. She is responsive in Emails and is very sociable. Would recommend to anyone looking to knock out a science class.

I loved this class. She is extremely caring and wants you to succeed. You do work in a group the entire semester, but you get to choose your groups. Her test were not difficult and you had one assignment and one quiz a week. I recommend taking this class.
she is the best in the world. she always answers emails quick, respectful, give us lots of time, fun projects, and always helps everyone in need

Easy class but content wise, I would recommend you take her only if you already have credit for bio and are retaking it for pre-med, unless you are good with async classes. Lecture videos no less than 1.5hr long and paired with weekly quiz and/or assignment. Definitely easy A. Sometimes hard to understand. Videos are from 2021 (she reuses them).

Very understanding and efficient professor. I was nervous about taking biology online, but this class has been pretty easy. Very quick to respond to emails or any issues you may have, very clear grading criteria and online exams. As long as you participate and try you'll end up with an A or a B.
She is the best and cares, always right and she is pretty!

Pretty easy class, there was usually only 1 or 2 easy assignments a week along with a 5 question quiz on the lecture material. Exams are all lock down browser and some required camera to be on. very understanding. lectures are straight forward. easy class. uses lockdown browser and had 1 on camera. there was 4 exams and you can either opt out of the final if youre ok with your grade or take it and drop the lowest. group projects are easy and you can pick your group

Weekly quiz and group assignment, but you can request the people you want to be in your group. Quizzes and assignments are all fairly quick and simple. There are also four tests and then the final, but the final is optional. Plus, Professor Kabir answers emails fairly quickly. Overall, she is a great professor and very understanding.

This class was asynchronus, so you pretty much teach yourself. However, Dr. Kabir is a very understanding professor and responds quickly to emails. Weekly group assignments and individual quiz. The test were not difficult and included a few bonus questiions. Overall, a decently easy course for Bio.
Ms. Kabir is a very friendly person, and a great professor to have during my first semester of college. Her class was not stressful and she gave out study guides for all her tests.
cares more about water than teaching

Dr. Clinton is a really nice lady but not the best professor. I graduate tomorrow and the last two exams from February and April still have not been grader so be prepared to get your grades at the last minute.

Dr. Clinton assigns a lot of work over breaks/class cancellations. Her lectures are engaging-ish and she provides resources to find internships/research, but she is tough when it comes to grading, especially on writing assignments. Luckily I'm only taking ESCI 1501 as a Gen-Ed.

I took her for Environmental Dilemma. Her lectures are very long and boring. Rambles on a lot and says the word "um" all the time. She doesnt personally grade any assignments she gives she has her TA grade everything so what you get is based off her opinion not the professors and takes FOREVER to grade things so wont know your grade til last day.

He is a nice guy. But very hard headed. he doesnt move tests around at all even if you were hit by a plane with proof. Also extremely smart, however falls short of realizing that when you introduce lockdown browser + monitor you need to give more time to your students to set it up before exams. But again. Hard headed.

Tomida is a doll, he's very passionate about science and you can tell he enjoys the mentorship associated with teaching as a professor at the university level. He tries hard & is very sweet. It can be hard to follow his lectures sometimes because English is not his first language, but he designs his lecture slides with extra detail to compensate.

Dr. Tomida is a really sweet professor. This class was fully online, with 30-60 question homeworks due every week. Tests were difficult was very doable if you read the textbook and manage to follow his lectures. The class itself is taught as Human Physiology rather than Animal Physiology. He offers grade replacement on the final, and extra credit.
Professor Tomida is very passionate about his work, and cares a lot about his students. He's always there if you need help, and was pretty good with lectures too.

If you actually want to learn I suggest taking this course with another professor. I personally struggled studying for this course as I did not know what to expect on the exams. He did specify certain things but for the most part you kind of just have to read the textbook and hope you study the right things. He's very sweet but his teaching style..
Very kind and caring.

Tests were very straight forward. You can tell he cares a lot about his students and the topics he teaches. I have enjoyed him so much I am taking another class with him. Tests were not difficult if you did the homework and just studied the homework and his poll everywhere's. Attendance taken via poll ev. Very happy and upbeat professor!
She is the nicest professor I have ever seen in my college life
She was cool. I didn't have a problem with her. The tests are hard if you don't try or study though.

Loved her lectures, she was funny and made it not boring. The assignments and overall class is organized really well, literally every week will be the same routine so you know what to expect. Notes and assignments were light and straightforward. 3 tests total the whole semester with an optional final.

I loved her class. There are 3 assessments and one optional final exam that replaces your lowest assessment score. The assignments were very easy and she pulls the test questions from the notes you take. She also published the slides after class.

absolutely love her class so much. she's so kind, funny, and really cares about her students. i personally got what i got because i'm not the best student in anything STEM related. the TA i had was also extremely kind and i loved her so much!!! if ur in psych, def take her class if u didn't take AP Bio in high school, or didn't get the credit!!!

I took this class online, and it was definitely an easy A! The textbook is online and completely free; they are relatively short chapters, and most of intro biology is just memorization. The assignments are also really easy, typically a short quiz and activity based on the chapter. She rounds up .5 and up for letter grades which is also a plus!

I really enjoyed her class, she was very responsive to questions and the grading is very lenient. There is no reason to fail this class if you just do the work. If you are in a major that needs a couple science credits and want to take an easy A then this would be a great one. My only recommendation is to attend the lectures.

Such a good class regardless of major. Attendance not mandatory but you should still try and make it to each class. She's super funny, engaging, & not boring at all. You'll get an a as long as you go to class, actually pay attention, and actually do the assignments (which are also very easy if you're paying attention in class).
The professor is really good at explaining the material and the assignments are super easy and informative.

I loved Mrs. Suptela. She knows her stuff and she is a great teacher with the way she explains it. I took it Tuesdays and Thursdays for an 1.15 hrs and I think that was perfect. Tuesdays she taught the entire time and then Thursday she would give a lecture then we had an activity. Test are on lockdown browser, but just study vocab and you're fine.

Current freshman taking this. I LOVEEEEEE Dr. Sam, she's so sweet and honestly so amazing. literally would LOVE to take another class with her. We have 3 tests and a optional final exam. Tests are so easy. It's genuinely difficult to fail this course and attendance isn't mandatory for her.
Very caring and explains things very well. Not homework-heavy and the workload is extremely manageable.

Dr. Sam is a green-haired, Immunology PhD-holding BADDIE with a killer dry sense of humor. HIGHLY recommend this class to any Bio majors who have previously taken or enjoyed Micro or Immunology. I'm a huge micro nerd so of course I loved epidemiology, but I also appreciated that this class (although reading & material heavy) is designed to be fun!

Dr. Sam was an incredible professor who cares about students' wellbeing along with the course mastery. Pick your seats wisely, as group projects/activities make up most of your grade. She made the class even extremely enjoyable, and doesn't have class on Fridays. She is smart and willing to help whenever needed. TAKE HER CLASS!

One of the best classes offered at UNCC. She goes into a lot of detail if you prompt her to and is very knowledgeable about the subjects. There are 2 tests which are based on the lectures and readings. The readings are 3 very interesting books, no textbook.

Loved Dr. Suptela. Shes funny, interesting, and actually knows what she is talking about. Course work is light if you struggle in this class you might as well drop out. Her lectures are great and she gives good assignments that actually allow you to apply your knowledge to real-world stuff. Loved her definitely take the class if you can!
Easy class, she explained everything really well and was funny too. I never really paid attention because I don't care about bio but still managed to keep a good grade all semester.

You do not need to buy the text book for the class from the library, she provides an online version of it for free. She is very knowledgeable in her filed of study and the class is easy to follow. The assignments she givs are not difficult and she does not assign an excessive amount of work.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Great lectures, does an amazing job of teaching the content. One day was a lecture the other day is an activity day. You do the activity in class so you can ask any questions. Exams are all multiple choice and super clear. Highly recommend.
Dr. Sam is one of the best bio professors. Her engaging lectures, clear explanations, and helpful TAs make this class a breeze. I'd recommend Unstuck study alongside the textbook for easy A prep.

Its a biology class so tests are obviously worth a lot.Her tests are simple and the lectures cover everything you will need to learn. Would have probably gotten a higher grade if I studied a little more. She gives a lot of extra credit.

she's so kind and willing to work with you. she offers a lot of extra credit and really likes to connect with her students! Her classes were only lectures, Online lock down browser webcam tests. Take her she's great!

For a class that was very boring content-wise, she made it a lot better & broke down complex concept into digestible pieces. Use plenty of flashcards to study and make study guides for tests (submitting them gives you extra credit). The tests can be difficult but not unbearable.

Tests were very easy and the lectures were very simple and condensed. There was a group project for my class but it was easy as long as you and your group stay on top of things. She loves to have conversations with the class about random things which made a fun environment. Also gives extra credit each test. I have zero complaints about her!

Took her lab not class. She is one of the best teachers I've had in my whole life. MAGNIFICENT!! So kind and caring, genuinely a ray of sunshine. Accessible outside of class and communicates well. She's so nice and was really helpful to me in the lab and personally. She really cares about her students. ABSOLUTELY RECCOMEND!!!

Exams were easy just study the powerpoint. She was barely accessible outside of class and I would not get a response until a week later. She does not give clear feedback for the grade she gives on assignments/projects and instructions would not be clear. She also said to be in class for some participation activities but they were ONE point each.

I LOVE her. she was super helpful when needing help with grades or questions about the material. provides study guides for each exam that were very helpful. Super sweet and passionate about the material. I would 10/10 take her again. Attendance not mandatory but helpful. lectures posted.

Prof. cox was a good teacher. It's a simple class that doesn't go into much detail. It is PowerPoint heavy but super simple and easy tests, opportunity for extra credit with a study guide submission. She is friendly, we took attendance twice within the whole semester. Must take tests in person!

took her gen bio 2 course online over the summer. 3-4 lectures each week with an exam at the end of the week. exams are easy if you just take notes on her lectures and review them. extra credit given for submitting your own study guides. very easy final project, and overall doable course given the fast pacing.

Took her class online during the summer, and it was very straightforward. You'll be graded on 5 tests (including a final exam), weekly discussions, and a final presentation. She gives out extra credit for the tests, and none of them are difficult if you read the textbook and take notes.

Extremely easy professor. Took two classes with her, 2130 online and 3273 in person. One easy packback writing assignment every week graded by AI. She also gives a few scientific article summary assignments on packback over the course of the semester which are graded a bit more strictly. Easy tests, just study the powerpoints and you will be fine.

She's a wonderful professor. I found her class quite interesting in content. Everything on the exams is in the exams. The final exam was cumulative. I have no Idea if this helps future students, but she does not seem to change anything. Her exams are fairly easy. The only thing I didn't like from this class were the deep dives.

MC is a great professor. Exams are entirely based on the lectures. Her class allowed me to succeed and learn without killing myself reading and studying. 10/10.

Her lectures are the main thing you'll need to focus on, as all of the exams come from the power points and not from the textbook. She does require five papers over the course of the semester, but they weren't bad, and she gave lots of feedback. Lots of extra credit opportunities. You can tell she really does care, and wants everyone to succeed.

Professor MC is clearly passionate about what she teaches and is great at explaining difficult concepts. She offers lots of extra credit throughout the course, and I found her to be very organized and professional. There is a lot of writing, but I found the grading to be fair. No curveballs on the tests, just study the PowerPoints.

Dr. Cox does take attendance for 5%.  There were 3 exams (not too hard) and a final.  She uses PackBack for articles (not hard, but annoying) and there were 5 short essays on stressors in birds.  She has copies of her recorded lectures which she shared with me and that helped me a lot.  I liked this class and would take her again.

Professor hardly seemed prepared, exhibiting multiple spelling errors in canvas announcements and even on exams. Almost forgot this was a science class given there were a ton of writing assignments. She made lecture Packback deep dives due the same week as the lab writing assignments!!! Lecture material was interesting only due to animal pics!

took this online and the homework and quiz was simple and the same every week. we only had one project near the end of the semester and it was very simple. 100% asynch. Tests are all mutliple choice and a few matching. not bad but require studying

Took her asynchronous animal phys. class. Exams weren't hard but they had many grammar mistakes. She also used Packback which was super annoying. AI graded the "deep dive" assignments. Lots of writing and busy work in this class. I can't say I learned much. Wouldn't take again.

The class is completely asynchronous, which I didn't mind. As someone who doesn't prefer animal biology, I liked having it this way. Exams were locked down with camera, quizzes were fine. He's very passionate about what he is teaching and does a great job doing so. You'll have 2 big projects which are relatively easy but his grading criteria isn't that clear, but the TA is very helpful.

He is a pretty cool professor, and he is always willing to help. Although his grading criteria are a little confusing, do not be afraid to ask him, he will tell you what he is looking for. His lectures are entertaining, and he is easily accessible through his email. He likes participation, and he makes lectures engaging and interesting.
I thought he would get better as the class went on!
I don't think a single person in our class enjoyed this instructor or class structure.
He is nice but this class was pointless, as I didn't learn anything and he does not teach anything substantial. Could have been an elective.

The instructor was not fully involved in the course or its students. Assignments and modules were sometimes opened late. grading was extremely harsh and only done by the TA. Professor never responded to emails, and any questions that were answered were redirected to the TA.
He's very chill and his assignments are pretty easy if you pay attention and show up. He does talk about bugs a lot especially ticks so if you don't like looking at bugs don't take his class!
Lectures are easy, with few quizzes, but they are easy. Group projects are easy, but be prepared just to be safe, and sometimes grades assignments late.

He's my absolute favorite professor and i'll always recommend taking a class with him if you can. However he does give vague instructions for assignments so you gotta be annoying and ask for more detail on what he wants. He's always willing to take a look and guide you to success!

I took CTCM 2350 as it was a required credit. Instructions for projects are extremely vague, yet grades were very harsh. Super easy class. CTCM 2350. I took this class for one of my gen eds. He gives good feedback and we have like 1 assignment every 3 months. Work on projects throughout the year. final exam is also a project

One of my favorite professors, very nice and cares about what he teachers, honestly a really easy class but he often doesn't make assignments super clear, so you don't know exactly what to do but just put in effort and show understanding that is all he cares about. Very funny and accomplished professor as well.

Very nice and smart professor. I enjoyed going to his class, and learned some pretty cool things. He grades more effort based, but it sometimes is hard to find what hes looking for so make sure you ask questions. overall he is a very intelligent, funny, and kind person.

Took him for an LBST credit, MAJOR chunk of his grade comes from attendance.

Tough on the grading side as he doesn't really give you an outline or grading sheet for the writing assignments, he just gives you random feedback and expects you to know what he means.

Final project is a paper / presentation with absolutely no outline given

Professor Vieira is a solid professor. Class mostly consisted of a short lecture or video then a class discussion. We only really had weekly reading assignments and a group project. He was alright. I took him for a fully asynchronous class over the summer. It was really only the TA that sent out the course emails and did discussions with. There were no tests just one weekly written assignment that was graded hard but if you followed the rubric well enough you get a decent grade. Wasn't awful by any means.

The professor explains things clearly and teaches well. The class had some group-based assignments  and attendance mattered so its important to pick the best group mates for the class but overall do take the class and you'll get an A!
shes a great teacher and very understanding would definitely take her again !

My issue is not with the professor herself, she's communicative and her criteria is concise and clear. My only complaint is her course relying heavily around group projects and the way she handles freeloading group mates. This class is very straightforward and I'd definitely recommend it. The only thing that can make it difficult is choosing the wrong people to work with. Your group is extremely important because the three-part group project counts as both your midterm and final. Being grouped with slackers can seriously affect your grade.

I love geneen. i took her back in summer and i finished the 5 week course in 2 weeks. it's important that u find a great group partner because my partner and I were on the same tracks finishing this course in 2weeks. if i could take her again i would. just read and do your work, easiest A.

She's just ok. Nothing special. Doesn't reply to emails and her brightspace is extremely confusing. She definitely picks and chooses who she likes even if you've done nothing wrong. SHE IS REALLY GOOD! Course load is not overwhelming and if you participate and do your work.. you should end off with an A!

This was a very easy class overall. The tests were completed online, and the textbook was provided online as well, which made things convenient. There were group projects every week, but as long as you had reliable group members, the workload could be spread out evenly. Overall, I would definitely take this class again.

I took this class online and it was really easy. The test were lockdown browser but they didn't require webcam. There was definitely a lot of homework but everything was due the Monday of the next week.

All grades are either mostly multiple-choice quizzes/tests or group project worksheets all based on the online textbook. The assignments aren't very difficult, but there's so many it takes hours each week. I don't feel like I learned much from this class, and it wasn't fun, but Bio majors need to take it. Worth if you're familiar with microbio.

Please don't take this lady's course. The class is easy, but the professor is cold, unhelpful, dismissive, and frankly EVIL. She doesn't support students dealing with illness, religious absences, or group issues. You're on your own, even when others don't do their part. You WILL struggle, not with the content but the lack of compassion.

She says that you aren't given a grade, you earn one. I think that's accurate. If you keep track of your assignments and soak in the info, you're pretty good. She's good at explaining things with analogies so there's other ways to help the info sink in.
Professor Geneen's class is veryyy easy. There are weekly group projects but they are easy, especially since you have 3 other group members. Just do the work and you will get an A
Was a very easy class just do the work that is assigned and you'll be set.
100% recommend Ms. Jones. Responds fasts to emails and very accessible outside of class. No zooms or tests! Quizzes are easy if you read the textbook and group work is heavy.

This is an online class, but group work is involved. You are assigned 1-2 quizzes and a group assignment each week. My group divided the questions equally and completed them on time. She posts lectures, but I never had to watch them. A super easy A, and she is very understanding about late work.

Professor Jones was very flexible when it came to course assignments, knowledgeable in her lectures, and had a late assignment policy that was fair. Even though I never interacted with her in person, she is very respectful and there to help students that need help. Be prepared for group projects / activities if you take her class.

I took bio1110 fully online with Jones. She is clear about expectations. There are weekly quizzes on a chapter or two and an assessment. There are group assignments every week or biweekly with the same group throughout the semester. Group final project instead of final exam. Easy A class if you put in little effort.
Didn't have a lot of communication but she is great! This is group based so if you don't like that this isn't the class for you but overall this is an easy A class if you put in the work/effort.

My class was completely online but I loved this professor! She was very understanding and answered quickly. I would take any class that I could with her being the professor. The class does have a group component but its on average around 1 group assignment, and your final is a 3 part group project!

I feel as if she is actually one of the best professor at this school as she does care about everyone in her class. Her lectures are pretty boring to sit through so i wouldnt say that attendance is mandatory but she does offer extra credit as in class assignments so that was nice. Her exams are completely based off the slides she lectures on.

Class is taught by TAs. You are not provided access to her slideshows on Canvas; instead, you have access to learning manuals, which are a bit different. You also cannot take photos of her slideshows during lab. This can make studying for tests a bit confusing. You have to pay attention in labs in order to do well.

One of the best bio professors.  Explains things very well.  Gives study guides which cover all the test material.  HW assignments are not too demanding.  You get some occasional group projects but they aren't too bad.  Any class you can get with her I absolutely would.

Professor Walsh, did a great job with Ecology. Lectures were clear, assignments were easy, and the final was optional. You do have a semester long group assignment, but she breaks it up into parts throughout the semester so it's really easy in the end. There is also a weekly discussion but other than that there wasn't much work for this class.

Dr. Walsh is great.  You get weekly discussion post assignments or an occasional HW assignment online--not hard.  You get a study guide about one week before an exam.  All of the exam questions are right off the study guide.  You can fill it in and memorize that for an easy A on each test.  Stuff she teaches is often actually useful irl too.

Professor Walsh is an amazing professor.  She knows everything about plants and explains it really well.  She provides you with a study guide before each exam; you just complete the study guide and the exam is easy.  A few group projects and HW assignments are given but these aren't hard and she is fairly lenient grader.  10/10 professor.

I took her summer course and it was a little difficult since I was also taking other classes but to be honest I would only study the day before and would pass the exams. The study guides were pretty helpful but did not include everything that would be on the exams. She did have in class assignments/Hw and E.C offered. Overall, I would recommend!!

I have her for General botany lab and lecture and had her previously for ecology. She's an amazing professor overall, she's very kind and caring and is willing to accommodate for in class participation grades if you had something going on. I would definitely recommend her over and over

shes a very sweet teacher, however, shes very lecture heavy. she posts all of her lectures online and just reads off the powerpoint, so you can very well teach urself. after the first week 90% of the class stopped showing up so you could literally just teach yourself. but she is super sweet and caring, however, i probably could've taught myself

Walsh is a good professor. The material is a lot so you should review them every day. The study guides helped out a lot with the tests. The final is optional. (It won't let me put it but I took BIOL 2273 lecture with him) An amazing professor; his lectures focused on the powerpoints that were very detailed. Very receptive to feedback. Gives practice exams mirroring actual exams. This class is very hard and requires a lot of studying outside of class but he made the lectures good to prepare you.

Super chill guy, clearly wants everyone to succeed. Allows you to bring a note sheet for exams and do corrections for half-points. Honestly, while I appreciate this class not adding a huge load, I thought it was a little too easy. He's a new professor though, so I think he'll figure out the right balance in the future.

It was a pretty easy class given he has a lot of leniencies when it comes to grading, but his teaching style probably isn't for you if you can't learn with just PowerPoint slides reading off information. In order to do well in this class, you have to study a lot and use materials outside of the lectures.

This class is super manageable, there is hardly any homework and the bonus of being able to bring a page of notes to exams. Just wants his students to do well and is one of the most flexible and supportive instructors I've had at UNCC!
She is a harsh grader, doesn't respond to emails, and expects you to know everything, so when you ask her a question, she makes you feel like you should already know it.
Very harsh grader and did not give clear feedback on grading. Overall was a funny professor

Don't walk RUN to a new Cell Biology professor. Donna had an attitude when people in class asked questions like they were inferior to her. Dr. Goodenow was very nice! The way she structured her course around a game provided great opportunity for students who want to learn more or just need this course for the credit. The class was pretty much quizzes, no tests. There was packbacks that were tedious to complete. Only thing hard was the paper that had a hard rubric.

I actually liked the quizzes and how we basically had two opportunities to get a good grade. Overall, it was a lot of work but possible to pass.

This class is not easy, and there is a lot of information covered in a single semester. Her syllabus is changed and is a very different setup. What I will say is that she gives many chances to pass the class now as long as you fully apply yourself. I will say that you cannot pass the class on your notes alone, much more ways of studying is needed.

I would not suggest taking this professor. The class has a point system. She says the class is like a "game." Her lectures are hard to follow. Every chapter has a quiz, using a lockdown browser/ webcam, which is around 20 quizzes. Save yourself the trouble and take someone else. DO NOT RECOMMEND!

Donna is a good professor the test are lockdown browser w/ camera but the exams are open notes. If you start off strong you should be able to get through the course just stay on top of assignments. Bullock > Donna
Just save yourself the headache and take it with another professor.

Dr. Goodenow does power point lectures based on the reading of the chapters that will be on the test.  Attendance isn't mandatory, but you get extra credit for showing up.  Tests were open-note open-book, just take good notes (with page numbers) and you'll do great.  Also gives extra credit projects at the end.

6 open note "mini" exams, no final. The Lecture PowerPoint was hard to follow. She spins a wheel for extra credit based on if you answered the pollev for that day. She seems like a really sweet professor and is caring, but she's really hard to follow. However, If I were to take this course again, I would choose another professor.

There were 7 mini-exams that were take-home with lockdown/webcam, but they were open note so they weren't that bad. Dr. Goodenow was open to class feedback and gave extra credit on tests if you came to class. There were 7 easy homework assignments that had unlimited attempts. Although the class is test heavy, its really not as bad as some say.

Posted very long lectures. Lectures consisted of her reading off textbook slides with occasional example. Participation was done by taking a quiz on the lecture video. This class was challenging, especially the seven mini-exams. There were 7 mini exams throughout the whole semester and the exams were not mini. Usually 40-45 questions for each exam. Felt like she just read off the slides in class and didn't learn much. Exams where not easy and went based off of things she says in lecture and whats in the lecture slides.

The tests were very difficult. She is very passionate and caring. You will learn a lot, but you have to put in the work. Lectures were often posted late, and the schedule frequently became confusing. Overall, though I feel most of  the difficulty came from the course being online. I had to teach myself a lot of the concepts.

Very disorganized. Our grades through canvas have not been accurate all semester and we have had to calculate them ourselves. Lectures are super long. Test questions are "application questions" and none are similar to the ones done on homeworks or in lectures.

very long readings and teaches slides made by textbook company. 2-3 chapters per lecture and tests dont cover what is learned .tests are heavy and constantly changes her plans for course and tests. very unorganized, homework is on MyLabMastering and based on accuracy. final exam grade replaces lowest exam grade.

Dr. Song's class was one of the hardest I had in college. But I highly appreciate her and the other guest lecturers for giving such an interesting overview of systems biology. Didier has an incredibly thick French accent (haw haw oui oui) so it's hard to understand what he's saying regarding the information heavy material. Chill guy, and very respectful to everyone. He is sweet but his lectures were so boring. Like honestly boring. However, the tests are chill and I liked some of the topics he taught. BIOL 4601: I actually loved this guy as a professor. He is so passionate about research and all he wants is his students to succeed. Dr.Dreau is a sweet guy. Attendance is mandatory and I suggest paying attention to the homework assignments as they are similar to the test. She's the absolute worst. Her test material never matches the lectures or the textbook. She's extremely boring to listen to as well, which makes things that much worse. She is the reason I switched my major. She is uninsipirational and soul crushing. She thinks she makes sense but she doesn't.

I took her BIO-1110 online and it was one of the easiest course yet at UNCC. I'm not sure if she really did much ( all feedback/announcements  was from the TA). The every week was a weekly group project, quiz , and test(lock down browser).The final exam was a group project that took maybe 2 hours.

just attend zoom meetings for test reviews as tests are based off of them. not hard to get a B
PRAY TO GOD YOU PASS THIS COURSE!!!! Thats what I can say in 7 words. Good luck and you will need it.
Would have given a 2 but he rounded my D to a C so he's not so bad. Not the best at teaching either. Brutal final and expect to see "GOOD LUCK" written everywhere.

Made it clear what was expected of us. Tests were fair and were similar to the practice problems, study with those. Topic tests are difficult but doable. Explained things well to the class. I thought the student instructors were helpful as well. Class goes fast though, as long as you don't fall behind and practice semi-regularly you'll be ok.

Professor does a good job of lecturing; however a great deal of the lecture is recorded after class time has already concluded. Grading structure tries to help you out overall; with partial credit on most of the exams and lots of overall grades.

I'm not giving a 5 because that'd mean perfection; a 4 is the next best thing. People rate this class harshly, but it's just not an "easy A"—you have to do the work. Mr. Gerardy is incredibly patient and gives more chances than students probably deserve. He is a smart man who leads a great team. Highly recommend if you're willing to try.

Lectures online through zoom however they are hard to follow as this guy has the worst handwriting ever. the workshops and study halls are were you're really going to learn and understand the material. Exams sometimes take +2 weeks to get back.  The TA's are great and actually help so reach out to them

Gerardy is a kind guy; he genuinely wants to help but can go off on tangents. The content is difficult, the size of the class is big. Have a strong trig/algebra background before this class. If this class is the only option for you, PLEASE go to study halls and office hours. Him and his TAs are very kind and helpful and want you to succeed.
Get ready for a bunch of homework. The tests have random things on them. If you're not religious, find one and start praying.

This class had very many assignments. The grading criteria was very confusing. The class is test heavy. The professor himself is very good, nice, and he is a very good teacher. The professor gives every student time even with hundreds of students if you ask for help.

Worst of the worst. Attendance is mandatory. Group work. Placement test on the first day of class, which is graded and we haven't even learned anything yet. Rambles too long for a simple topic and gets off topic.

Very passionate and is great at explaining things in multiple ways if you don't understand. Knows the content very well and it's hard to do bad in his class. Grades fairly. Offers SO MUCH extra credit at the end of the semester, you just have to put in the effort. I finished his class with a 100. Final was worth 100 out of 112 possible.

Gerardy is a sweet guy- he's very personable, nerdy, & a bit quirky. Most physics courses require a lot of outside study time, and this one is no exception. It's best to stay on top of things, DO NOT fall behind on lecture & post-lecture material or you'll regret it. Try and avoid taking other time consuming courses w/ this one (orgo, genetics)

I can't read his handwriting ever, he rambles forever about random stuff, we are required to purchase a textbook which features incorrect answers/typos/offers no space to write. Our exams are extremely hard, and the first one which you take first day of class counts for credit… despite not being taught any of the information yet… Take someone else.

The online format is annoying for a subject like physics however in person workshop helps. Make sure to go in during study hall before exams as this is the only time you'll be able to ask for help in person directly with Dr. G. He explains very well (especially in person) so you must be willing to ask. Gives enough resources for success; use them!

Pretty good lecturer, and he records himself doing the entire workbook. If you can do all the workbook problems, you'll do good on exams. Pretty helpful during workshops too. Definitely refresh on sin/cos/tan in degrees, angles, and moving variables around. Decent amount of extra credit available.

He does a great job making a tough class as manageable as possible. He drops a good number of assignments and offers plenty of extra credit. The workbook has some errors, but that's not on him. I just wish he were teaching PHYS 1102, too.

Extremely slow paced, simply just spits information at you and tests you on a different language of topic for the exams. There is easy, weekly homework assignments. Lecture is requires as PollEverywhere takes attendance. Dont waste time going to exam review, no help given at all.

Has to be one of the worse professors I've had. He is terrible at explaining the subject and just rambles on about topics. He reads straight from a workbook that is required you buy because he grades completion of the pages. In the workbook itself half the answers are wrong and the questions have typos so you cant even use the booklet to study.

Gerardy is a personable guy. The schedule is weird but adaptable. You're given a workbook and everything is in it. He explains things well, but it's a hard class. It's manipulating word problems. Quiz every week, exam every 2. Equation sheet is given. He posts recordings of all lectures! Extra credit for every module- treat it like weekly homework!

The structure of PHYS1101 is very annoying. Workbook checks and weekly workshops which makes it feel like high school. Slow-paced online lectures, but they're recorded and posted online. If you do all the work, it's not too bad, but you might have to use youtube to learn. I wish this was just a regular lecture class.

allows regrading on tests. very understanding let me make up week 2 homework around the end of the semester for full credit. Allowed 6 points extra credit on the final. The only bad thing is the placement exam you take in week one of the class is 7% of your grade.

I enjoyed Dr. Gerardy as a professor. I found him to be very helpful and He took the time to explain every problem you had. I think the selection of TA's was phenomenal. I thought they too were very helpful. He does give a lot of extra credit so I would take advantage of that! 10/10 professor!

Dr. Gerardy was really great in workshops for PHYS 1101, he explained concepts arguably better than they were explained in lecture and he made difficult concepts a little easier by giving us real life examples. Physics is a very difficult course, but Dr. Gerardy made it a little easier to understand.

Currently taking 3220 and learning more from YouTube than this guy's lectures. Everyone who's taken Linear Algebra agrees that the way he teaches the subjects is weird, and that's not even a prerequisite for the class. In addition he teaches to the blackboard while body-blocking, once was an hour late and made a point about refusing to apologize

she was overall very sweet and the class was pretty easy. it felt more like a gpa booster than a good class for if you liked astronomy. I think the lab really aids in the experience considering its a fully asynchronous class. her lectures are alright and watching the videos are for a grade. overall she gives a lot of extra credit at the end

I didnt like that we had to purchase the book just to do Homeworks since there's no reading but her lecture videos are required for attendance.The project instructions made it seem that you could work independently but thats not the case, therefore most people will work on something they have no interest of. Overall good/caring professor.

Very unorganized canvas page, to the point where major assignments can be overlooked, and her video lectures are not the easiest to understand. I would recommend referencing the textbook over her for the work in the class. Class overall wasn't that hard, just seemed lazily put together, but she's very nice and generous with extra credit

EXTREMELY unorganized professor, assignment descriptions make little to no sense, group work is required in a fully asynchronous class, attendance was taking for watching the videos which had a constant noise in the background that gave me a headache, the syllabus is a mess, her answers to questions are incomplete most of the time.

Dr. PA is a nice professor. She seems to care about her students, and for the most part responded in a timely manner; which I respected. My only issue was the short time frame for our tests, as they were online so I expected them to be open for more than one day. Overall, though, she was sweet and the topics we learned were interesting.
Won't take again of there are other options to choose

Professor uses WebAssign for assignments and uses a paid online textbook. Tests are loosely based off of the hw. There is a final project at the end where you make a video answering an astronomy question you have. The recorded lectures are okay, it is hard to understand sometimes because she has an accent.

This professor has NO IDEA how to use Canvas properly. Tests would be locked after taking them, making you unable to figure out what you got wrong/how to improve. Same assignments had multiple due dates and you wouldn't know which one was right. The study guides she gave hardly covered the content on the tests. She's nice, but this class was awful.

On the first day of class, this professor will tell you that if you are uncomfortable or do not wish to be in class to learn, nothing will be held against you. All the professor does is talk quietly, never answers emails and grades unfairly, and also take away study guides without warning. Stay on top and don't be afraid to send emails!

Dr. Porras is so nice I feel bad saying this but her lectures are awful. She speaks so fast and without clarity, and the powerpoints she posts are unhelpful as it's only pictures. She locks homework assignments and there are NO extensions unless there was a genuine emergency. She's very sweet but I don't think I'd take her again

Did not use canvas so I didn't know my grade most of the time. He tries to explain things the best he can. Don't miss class because somethings get confusing. I used Radiology Tutorials on Youtube to understand the class.

Great guy, I thought he was super funny. Lots of great guest speakers, one of which inspired where I want to go in my career. The only hard part is the final project, which was hard because we had to research a physics topic and I don't know that much about physics yet lol

Dr. Fried is a condescending, disrespectful, empathy lacking individual. Picks on students in workshop, does not respond well to feed back, and is a nuisance to the learning environment. He needs to be removed from all physics departmental positions. Ruins peoples passions of grades and any motivation to succeed in their academic careers.
The class itself is difficult but he does his best to break it down and is very understanding if you need extra assistance or accommodations for any reason.

This class was hard! He rambles during most of his lectures, but he knows his stuff. The quizzes weren't horribly hard but did require lots of studying. He was a lenient grader and drops lowest grade in each category. He was always willing to answer questions and enjoyed participation. Brought real materials into class to demonstrate.

Dr. Fried was one of my first professors my freshman year & right off the bat you can tell how much he wants his students to succeed. This was a freshman seminar class so it was more abstract, but he gives great feedback and is very encouraging.

If you DO NOT have to take molecular biology, do not. This course was absolutely horrible. Class consist of just lecturing from the book, reading of the slides word for word. Very boring. And the exams are absolutely hard! He does not provide a clear understanding on what will be on the exam when more than 5-6 chapters are being covered.

Dr. Fried was very caring. he offered help outside of class if requested. physics in medicine was a difficult course. very lecture heavy, taking clean, organized notes is a must, as well as studying regularly. he wanted his students to pass and most of our assessments were curved. this is a class you must attend.

The lectures were extremely ponderous and pointless feeling, many people leave halfway through. Definitely would recommend skipping them and self-studying. Tests were fair, homework would sometimes be quite long. He is a nice guy but unfortunately myself and many others decided that we were better off teaching ourselves.

Lectures are not mandatory, but the Friday recitations are. To sum up my experience, I could not make it through a single lecture without falling asleep, which I never do. I would only reccomend taking this class if you can self study

He is a nice guy, but he makes physics so hard. The practice tests are nothing like the actual exams and I genuinely don't know how people do well in his class. The TAs are amazing, very passionate about physics, and so is Dr. Heindl, but he is very monotonous and it's easy to get lost in class.

Mr Heindl is a great professor. Always shows up with a positive attitude and even is humorous during technical difficulties. Replying to other ratings: lectures can get boring but Heindl does what he has to do: teach. His lecture notes are more than enough to understand a topic. 1 day is lecture, the second is practice problems.

In all honesty he's a good professor, the only harp on him goes to the difficulty of the class unfortunately. He genuinely wants to help people understand it, he typically has one day of lecture and the other with practice problems. I would 100% take him again over the other two available physics professors if I had the choice.
Just talks a lot during lectures and youll get lost everytime. I stopped going to lectures after a few weeks to save myself the time.

Prof. Heindl's lectures are not mandatory and sometimes felt confusing and disorganized, but I believe that he really cares about his students and he was always willing to answer questions or re-explain. If you are good at self study I would absolutely recommend Prof. Heindl, however if you need more structure this may not be the class for you.

Lectures were slow and attendance wasn't required. In class, he worked through problems much harder than those on the tests, which could feel intimidating. Weekly quizzes and unit tests were manageable, but the final was very difficult. He was nice and listened to student feedback

If it wasn't for the online lecture material from other profs, I wouldn't have passed. Lectures are basically pointless because it was a large class and he would stop to answer every question instead of office hours. He didn't explain important topics in detail but would spend the entire class on minute details that weren't ever brought up again.

Lectures are confusing and disorganized, skip them and use the time to study. He asked for student feedback on his teaching and applied some of it, which was good. No homework, weekly quizzes, and a couple exams with practice exams provided. If you study and work hard on quizzes, you will do well.

I took quantum mechanics with Dr. P. It is an incredibly difficult subject but he structured the class very well and so it was hard, but not frustrating. He made sure to teach the subject matter before the homework was due and went light on us the week before any exam so we could prepare.

Marco is hilarious! He makes his lectures feel engaging and encourages us to use our voices without fear of being wrong. The content can be a little hard to grasp, but Marco is willing to help you as much as possible. If you're anything like me, he sees skills in you that you definitely don't see in yourself.

This course revolved around a group project that was extremely poorly done. Grading criteria was unclear and contradictory. It used randomly-generated data which of course had no actual correlations. Tried to grade everybody off the average of a few groups' presentations. 7-page barely-related report due at the end.

THIS DUDE IS GOATED; EASY CLASS + GENUINELY CARES

CHARISMATIC, FUNNY, INTELLIGENT

GENUINELY WHAT EVERY PROFESSOR SHOULD ASPIRE TO BE

USES TEXTBOOK BUT NOT REALLY NEEDED. EVER. 

VERY SIMPLE QUIZZES, JUST PAY ATTENTION AND YOU CANNOT GET A B. I HAVE THE UTMOST RESPECT FOR HIM AS A MENTOR BUT MORE IMPORTANTLY AS A GREAT FRIEND.

Marco is a super great guy and one of my favorite professors I've had at UNCC. He is extremely personable and just wants to create connections with his students. He is always willing to talk and help anyone out. He even went out of his way to email me restaurant recommendations for my and my girlfriend to go. Marcos Awesome.

Professor Scipioni is a kind and funny person, but his classes are not very easy to follow along in, as he often goes off topic. Class structure is not good at all, and quiz dates are often changed in class. Lots of AI usage, especially when coding. He would often tell us to just use Copilot to do the code for us, which was not helpful at all.

This lecture requires a solid base in Python and statistics. Though some parts felt rushed, it gave a clear overview of data science. Following the project instructions helped me understand how things really work and taught me many new concepts. The good thing is they are helpful and caring.

Lectures were disjointed, surface-level, and frequently rambled off-topic. Most lessons and assignments were ai-generated. Very little is actually taught, especially if you already took the intros to STAT or ITSC. Late to class several times. Marco's responses to students were typically unhelpful. This is the worst course I have taken so far. Avoid

Professor Scipioni may completely understand the material, but he fails to teach it. His communication outside of class is typically incorrect and he changes quiz dates and topics at will without telling students. He has no schedule for the class, goes off topic, and assigns quizzes for students to learn what he ran out of time to teach.

Marco is fantastic, I've had him for 1000 & 2000 DS courses, long lectures but we got breaks. Helpful, only issue is lack of homework. If you missed a hw assignment or two it tanks your grade, final group project but still great professor. Definitely take him
Great professor. Funny and engaging. Workload is manageable, it's mostly readings and coding assignments.

P/F 
Dr. Scipioni was an overall good professor. Very funny, well-spoken, and respectful. There will be homework every week but nothing too serious that you cant knock out in an hour or less. The only thing that's keeping him from a 5 is lack of personal connection. I don't blame him, since there are about 50 people in this class. Highly recommend!

I like Dr. Scipioni a lot. He's very friendly, funny, and really knows his stuff. He was a great professor in my Data Science class. My only irks are that he chose to break up the groups for the group project halfway through the course, and I really liked my original group. I wish he had not done that, but I liked him and would take him again.

This professor made the class fun. We didn't have to read a textbook and there was very little homework. The labs were easy to do and fun! The lectures were posted beforehand and all examples were worked through thoroughly! The midterm and final were really nice too! He gave us the practice exams which really helped! Also responds quickly to emails

I did not interact with Prof. Silwal however the TA was the only reason why i passed, I highly recommend Elias Frusher as a TA if you get the chance, so much extra credit and he was very friend and knowledgable on how to run the lab! It's hard to find a good TA that knows what theyre doing!
His lab manual is hard to understand and some questions are unclear within the lab manual, but he recruits great TAs who help us understand it. Easy A as long as you attend lab and actually try!

Professor Silwal is super adorable. I took Physics Lab so I did not really interact with him, the TA ran the class. Physics Lab I is super easy though just put in effort to learn during your lab time! Have fun!

Umesh Silwal is a kind hearted man who cares for his students and his labs are easy A as long as you attend the labs. I took it over summer, and the lab did not even have a final exam which was amazing. This professor has the potential of teaching actual physics classes like 2101, 2102 compared to useless idiots like leilabady and yildrim aktas

Physics lab manual rarely made coherent sense, but with guidance and a good TA you'll be fine. Make sure you understand lecture first half of semester as lab relies heavily on the material. Towards the end the lab is ahead of the lecture. Easy pre-lab quizzes, and an easy final exam during the last lab.

It was an easy class—it was pretty easy to get a 90 on each lab. The pre-lab quizzes were also rather easy and only took around 20 minutes or so. One lab was dropped from the final grade, and the final wasn't too hard. Overall, it was a pretty easy class with a good TA.

His lab isn't hard but its written pretty poorly. Instructions are clear and even the TAs don't understand what is asked. The lab final was way harder than any of the work we did in the lab. Lowest lab is dropped. Prelabs were easy. Overall everyone should do well. Labs do take most of the time.

Phys 2 Lab was easy to get an A in but took up so much time. Labs sometimes took up to three and a half hours, the lab instructions were written very poorly so half of the time no one knew what they were doing, and the equipment was always broken and never worked.
easiest lab class ever. prelab usually takes 5-10 minutes. You can get at least a 90 on each lab very easily.

Dr. Silwal makes Nuclear Physics fun and engaging. Each topic was explained well and dumbed down enough that those outside the major could participate in class. It was pretty broad class so be on the lookout for an advance nuclear physics class that he may develop in the future. The class was graded by 2 midterms, a final, and some homework.

He majorly messes up on problems very often in the lectures. You genuinely have no idea if you are solving things correctly, and neither does he. Solved exam reviews were consistently wrong and conflicted with other ones that the TAs did. To sum things up: 90% of our grade is on content he can't even get right. Just No! Don't take it at UNCC!

One thing if you want to get an A in this class: read the textbook word by word and understand all of practice problems. Email your TA if you don't understand something. Lectures are kind of useless except for the midterm reviews. He always tries to make formulas look complicated in which they could be as simple as plugging in the numbers

Take Lielabady. All classes for Physics 2 have to take the same test in the same room at the same time, and all of the homework assignments are the same. With this in mind, the test average for Aktas's class was over 20 points lower than that of Lielabady. His visuals all look like chicken scratch, and he is reluctant to answer questions in class.

Absolutely the worst professor I've ever had. Unengaging lectures, hard to understand and he delegates everything to clueless TA's. His class structure is also brutal. Your entire grade pretty much rides on the tests as the homework isn't worth anyting. Good luck on those tests too as the formula sheet is shorter than Danny DeVito. Please avoid him

Physics sucks, there is no way around that. That being said, Dr. Allen breaks down the material very well. She drops grades from each category. The class is extremely test heavy with a placement exam worth 9%, 4 midterm exams worth 36% (total), and the final exam (25%). The class is very doable if you do not fall behind the material

Dr. Allen is great! The guided notebook and lectures made everything very easy to understand. Honestly the class itself is not that hard if you know what equation you're supposed to use from the equation sheet and which numbers go into which variable.

Prof Allen made physics sooo easy. I was worried that I wouldn't be able to grasp the material because of the stigma around physics courses, but I really understood it! She does a great job of explaining and is patient when answering questions. I would take her over and over again if I could, she really sets you up for success.

Dr. Allen is a very sweet lady! You can tell she cares a lot about the subject she teaches and she wants her students to do well in it so she is more than happy to explain things and is passionate. However, the physics department grades the placement exam you take which makes absolutely no sense. The tests are also nothing like the practice ones.

Dr.Allen is good at explaining concepts but I wish she focused more on different problems we would see on exams instead of taking up all of our lecture time talking about the theory/science behind everything. Physics is a hard class but as long as you study, go to workshop, and do the homework and extra credit you should be okay.

Love Dr. Allen. She explains very difficult concepts with ease. Offered lots of extra credit and dropped lowest of every grading category. This class requires lots of time outside of class but is manageable. Study, ask questions, and do every practice problem offered. No reason to fail this course at all. Dr. G in workshop is also very good!

I absolutely loved professor Allen. She was very caring and did not care at all to go over things and answer questions. I never felt that I was asking a dumb question. The class is not hard to pass as long as you do the work. We fill out a workbook on lectures that is 5% of your grade. There is also a lot of opportunity for extra credit.

Her lectures are her working through the workbook and solving the problems in them. If you pay attention and do your homework, you will get an "A" in this class. There are review expos on the Friday before the exams. I wouldn't take those too seriously because they are often much more difficult than the exams themselves. Review the practice exams.

Its really hard NOT to pass this class unless youre not doing any of the work lol. Dr Allen was such a sweet professor and gave so many resources like extra credit, practice problems, and practice exams that were just like the actual exams. Obviously studying is mandatory for this class but honestly just show up to lectures and youre straight

AMAZING professor, HARD class. Always do homework and do well on those exams. Best way to learn is practice after every module and ask questions. So much material to go over, lots of busy work like lecture warmups, online homework, workbook checks, participation, attendance, weekly quizzes, but they help! Lots of dropped grades and extra credit.
very nice professor!!!! MATH HEAVY BEWARE!!!

Love Dr. Allen. She has very detailed presentations that she creates in OneNote. She spends a little bit of time talking through theory and then works through practice problems. Poll questions for attendance. Webassign homework is pretty annoying and useless. Lecture and workshop are where you learn the content. Put the work in and you'll be fine.
final exam replaces lowest score and gets entered again on its own. makes your grade go down instead of up.

I love Angela Allen. Honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. Of course people are not going to like the class or struggle, it's a college physics class. The material is not going to be easy. There are going to be tough times out there. But the work fits just right for the class, and she understands that. She is passionate and cares.

The professor goes over the lectures. However, she will skip over lots of things. Often times, it is very easy to loose her when she is going in her lectures. I had to teach all of the material to myself because her style didn't work for me.

13 Homework assignments, 0 graded by the time the final exam showed up. He does return your exam grades quick but actual exams only can be accessed in his office during office hours. Extremely boring lectures and is always behind schedule to the point that we had 2 exams on the final week of classes with the final while still missing 2 more exams.

Poor time management; consistently late and holds students past class. Lectures are repetitive with scattered notes. Feedback is nonexistent, with homework remaining ungraded for months. Assignments have short 3-day turnarounds. Grading is heavily weighted on exams (85%), and the professor speaks very quietly. Some online material is available.

Really nice professor, but can be boring at times. Asks a lot of questions during class to try an keep it engaging though. Assigns lots of homework, sometimes with 2-3 days till its due. Exams were fair and I never looked at them after the fact but im sure he's a lenient grader. He also came to my job and tipped me good, so he's my goat.

Tests aren't super hard. Beaman is a terrible teacher, so prepare to teach the course yourself. He runs over time on every class and comes to each class late. He doesn't really care about students doing well or understanding the course. He strictly abides by his syllabus and doesn't round. Personally would never take another class with him.

Beaman's Dynamics is interesting. He is probably the easiest Dynamics professor at the school. But on the other hand, his lectures were a snoozer. I thought his tests were very reasonable and on the easier side which is great. The homework was annoying, as he would randomly post them and have them due in 3 days. Take for 3121, but idk about 3122.

Always late to lecture and holds everyone up 5 minutes after every time. Extremely boring to sit through where you might fall asleep.  Randomly assigns homework's without warning. Exams are fair and graded decently but you cant access your exams unless you go to his office hours where he'll watch you down like a hawk for looking at your exam.

I would describe this class as disorderly. He often showed up 5 minutes late, assignments created Thurs/Fri and expected to be turned in by Monday, and held over class period. As I am writing this, not a single one of my HW assignments has been graded besides ones from the online program RealizeIt. Tests were fair. Overall, left much to be desired.

If you can stay awake long enough to process what he's saying, you'll learn a lot. Brevity is his arch nemesis. Generally caring and understanding of circumstances. Frequently late to class and ALWAYS went at least 2-5 minutes over. Allowed extra time on exams as necessary. 
Took several classes with him, would not take more.

At the start of the class, the pace may feel slow, but trust me, it's for your benefit. The professor approaches teaching as if you haven't taken any related courses before, which is fantastic, especially if you've had less-than-ideal professors in the past. I highly recommend taking his class—he's great at what he does!

A good guy, caring and understanding. Lectures can be tedious and always go ~5 minutes over, but subjects are explained thoroughly. Occasional attendance quiz (graded on your name being written). Assigns a good amount of homework but chooses good examples to practice. Takes hw questions from the textbook (get the right version or ask a friend!)
Beaman is a great lecturer, and he does a good job of explaining the course material.

If you want a professor who rambles incoherently about unrelated topics for 45 minutes, then keeps you 10 minutes late every class period, this is your guy. Excessive amounts of online homework, he lets online software do all the teaching, and never returns exams on anything remotely resembling a timely basis.

Dr. Beaman assigned two tests during the year worth 60% and had a comprehensive final worth another 30%. He also does not allow the use of a graphing calculator. Tests are pretty similar to the homework problems.
You get what you put in for her class. The tests so far have been based on what we do in class.

Professor Smith is genuinely one of the greatest professors I have ever had. She is very transparent about expectations, grading, and what to expect on quizzes and tests. She genuinely cares about her students and by the end of the semester will have everyone's name memorized. I would highly recommend taking Professor Smith.

I'm currently taking MEGR 2141, and I have nothing but great things to say about Dr. Smith. She genuinely cares about how well the class is learning, always willing to answer questions, and takes the time to walk around and give individual help. Good energy, clear lessons, welcoming environment to participate. 10/10 would recommend.

Tough class but lecture was pretty easy to follow along, homework and additional study materials were all focused and helpful. If you were confused, she was good about going more into detail, and she's accessible outside of class.

Dr. Smith is the goat, if you have yet to take Statics you need to take it with her. All her presentations were thorough and comprehensible, which definitely helps in a class that can be challenging at times. She also made extra lecture videos which were extremely helpful, especially for practice. Great resources and the best professor I've had.
Very caring professor. spends a lot of time making videos and finding practice problems for studying. The best way I could describe this professor is that she is extremely fair yet challenging.

I loved this class she made it bearable and she was always open to helping us be better. The class is long about two hours but she tried to make it shorter now the class is ENGR1301 though for all freshman coming in Fall '25. She is also lowkey funny which I love and there are 5 tests in the class so a test was like every 2-3 wks. So study!

She is genuinely a great professor. Her lectures are designed for you to understand. She is more than happy to clarify things if you have questions. the quizzes and exams made up a large part of the grade but as long as you understand the material you should be fine. She is pretty forgiving on tiny errors on exams and quizzes. Overall GOAT.

This professor was the best I've had. When she missed class, she would post a lecture video. Always extremely helpful during the lecture. She always provided so many examples so we were always prepared for quizzes and tests. I've taken her twice for both MEGR 1100, and MEGR 2141. I would definitely take her if you get the chance.

Attendance is really important, is not like attendances everyday, the teacher gives out random in class assigment, and you don't know if you did not go in person. And this class teach stuff thats rally easy, bascilly high school stuff nothing is new, but somehow attdency is important, and no phone. NOT recommend, do not ever select this teacher.

This professor is great. She is very clear in her lectures and doesn't make you feel stupid for asking a question or to go over something again. She is very understanding and kind. The tests and quizzes are straightforward and similar to the examples given in class. You will do good in the class as long as you keep up and know trig pretty well.
One of the best professors I have ever had.
