Great professor. Very knowledgable. The final exam is optional. He gives pop quizzes and attendance occasionally but they're pretty straightforward and good practice. His lecture notes are very thorough, textbook isn't required. He is very helpful if you have a question both during and outside of class.

Dr. Wolek is a really nice guy, but he expects you to know a lot of stuff that I had forgotten about from physics. many people got A's and B's, but there was still a significant amount that failed. Going to his office hours were helpful despite me still having to retake the class.

Great Professor. You will regret asking stupid questions. If you don't do the homework you will struggle a lot. If you can do the homework you can do well on the test. He doesn't give much time on test though. He also tends to have mistakes in the homework. Lectures are entertaining but its not critical to attend if you just want to pass.

Dr. Schmid is extremely knowledgeable in machine elements. The other ratings are correct in saying he is a tough professor and the material is tough. However, if you put a considerable amount of effort into his class, you will be fine. Study the homework and handouts he provides and it won't be too bad. He is sarcastically funny and has good jokes.

Dr Schmid is one tough Professor but the man is hilarious, knows his stuff, and does his best to make everyone succeed. I personally wish I could take another class with him as it is quite an experience. Dr. Schmid is a lot harder than Dr. Tipton but if you are interested in truly learning about machine elements, his class is great for it.

Dr. Chen is a decent lecturer and a great teacher. He does have an accent, though it never prevented me from grasping what he was saying. The class is fairly difficult and the lectures alone may not always help you to fully grasp a concept. When things are not so far so good go to his office hours, during them I felt that Chen really shined.

He is a very good person and a thorough teacher. Some lecture material would get lost in his accent or the sheer length of lectures, but he usually reviewed it. Chen is very passionate about the material and explains it in a good way, you just have to be good at taking tests since those are basically the whole grade.

Dr. Chen was enthusiastic about the content, but sometimes his heavy accent got in the way of understanding lectures. He knows his content but he struggles with leading a class through it; the occasional example problem was always voluntary and only a few people ended up working them in front of the class throughout the semester.

Dr. Tipton is good professor, and you shouldn't have any issues taking his classes. He tells you all the topics that will be covered on the exams and offers multiple extra credit opportunities. He can get lost during lectures sometimes though and the class can be unorganized.

Not too bad by engineering class standards. He gives lots of random extra credit if you show up to class. He goes over what will be on the exam in class before. Lots of concepts/material, but the math is fairly easy. The difficult part is the large volume of material you need to remember for exams, but nothing individually is very difficult

Roger Tipton's MEGR 3173 offers a highly automated pedagogical experience. The curriculum displays a distinct algorithmic consistency as every presentation and exam appears synthesized by external logic rather than manual effort. With minimal oversight and flexible exam integrity, this course is optimized for those seeking a detached instructor.
brother gave me attitude when I asked for an extension on homework after my cat died.

Overall, I think Dr. Tipton was a great professor. Lectures mostly consisted of 30 minutes of reading from slides and 20 minutes of math problems. Lots of extra credit opportunities. The final grade is very exam test heavy. The only thing I would change is the format of tests, as there is a lot of material to learn, having notes would be helpful.
Tipton is a nice professor but he has changed his exams. They are no longer open notes. He will give you the topics that will be on the exam, so his exams are a little bit more difficult.

Tipton is a cool guy. The slides are boring but to be fair, they are Dr. Hodgins slides I believe, not Tipton's. For the tests, it is open note, all you need to do is "CTRL F" on the slides and you should be alright. The homework + group project was the most interesting part of the class. Shouldn't have much trouble passing the class if you try.

Good person, not a great professor. Lectures involved him clicking through hundreds of slides and briefly touching on topics. Expect the tests to contain the most niche material touched on in class and HW to be irrelevant to the questions on the exams. Tests are online in the classroom. A group project as well.
Great professor overall. Tests were open notes with the class presentation slides available during the tests. Would definitely take a class again with Dr. Roger Tipton.

3122 is a hard course as it is, but Professor Ghasemi made it easy by assigning homework and exams through an online software which he also provided support about during his lectures. He was also the type of professor to provide supportive feedback and comments directly to students individually. Not sure why he is rated so low to be quite honest.

Homework, tests, and final are online and open note. Everything is pretty similar to homework and class examples. Very easy to just never go to class and just teach yourself the material by doing the homework.

His very first sentence wasn't welcome to heat transfer but rather "Despite what you may have heard, I'm not Voldemort."  95% exam weighting so don't mess up lol. Take in the summer with Dr Vrikkas if you can but if you have to take it with Lee, I would recommend watching John Biddle's heat transfer playlist on yt. Only reason I passed.

Heat Transfer is hard in itself, but he doesn't make it any easier. Lectures involved multiple sections a class with MAYBE 1 example per section. His lessons consisted of the theory behind the equations and how they were derived (when its given in the textbook), not on uses or applications. Tests were open note, but most of the class still failed.

Grade is not on a normal scale, its based off the median course grade, so you never know what you truly have. Barely does examples and gives homework to "challenge you" but then grades it on accuracy, with hw averages being in the 50s. Tests are open note and are similar to his practice tests just with some tweaks, averages are still in the 40-60s.

I feel as if Professor Joyee has gotten better over the years based on these past reviews. Her teaching style is not too great, and she does tend to whisper while explaining practice problems which could insinuate a lack of true understanding of the subject. Overall the exams were pretty easy, and the TA was very helpful as well.
The lectures really aren't at all helpful but attendance is mandatory so expect to teach yourself

All the machine shop teachers are great. Lectures can take up most of the lab time, so expect to come back on Friday or Saturday to finish parts. Very easy to make a 100 on the lab if you just finish your parts on time and correctly. I really enjoyed this class even though it's so time consuming.

Mr. Dalton is a good teacher who will help whenever you have questions. He would tend to talk the entire length of the lab section (especially the first few weeks) so I had to use a lot of makeup time to get parts done. Be kind, show up on time, get your parts checked before they're due, and you'll be fine. Showing you care matters a lot.

This is a tough class because almost all the machines are new material. you'll definitely mess up a lot, but dalton answers every single question and it's important to him that you understand the material. he's always able to check parts ahead of time and guide you.

The GOAT of the machine shop! He's very nice, and does not want to fail you. You can probably email him and work something out with him if the machine shop hours in Sophomore Design aren't cutting the time needed to make your parts. He's very nice, and very flexible, and a good lecturer.

A great professor, you either get a 100 or a 0 on every assignment depending on if your parts are within tolerance or not. He will precheck parts before they are due and clearly shows every step in the machining process before you get to machine yours.

Professor Dalton is very helpful overall. He only gives either a 100 or a 0 if you make any minor mistakes on your parts. He gives you the opportunity to submit one week late for a 50. Its's best to have him pre check your parts in advance. My only gripe is that he once told me in a rather mean tone "I'm not checking anything else, it's past 5pm."

This is the best professor I have ever had at UNC Charlotte.  This professor really cares about his student's academics and will provide many examples, detailed answers to questions, and many opportunities to earn extra credit.  My only complaint is that he seems to be very busy and is hard to find outside of class.

This is one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC Charlotte.  He really cares about student success.  He takes the time to really break things down and explain it in a way that students can understand it.  He's very knowledgeable  in a range of engineering topics.  I love how his class has projects.

She was an awesome teacher and does a great job with her lectures. Her exam problems are similar to lecture and homework problems.  Attend every lecture, pay attention and follow along, do all homework problems, and practice redoing lecture, homework, and quiz problems within a few nights before the exams and you can easily get an A.

Dr. Marjan Molavi-Zarandi was a great professor. I was considering dropping the class but I am glad I didn't. The TAs grade the Hw but she grades the Exams but she gives a lot of credit. She requires the textbook but I was able to find a pdf file of it. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you miss a she posts the lecture slides. She gives quizzes.
She is fantastic, and one of the best professors I've had at the university. She cares about and emphasizes learning over memorization, and has a true passion for teaching.

Don't buy the textbook, she gives you everything you need. Very caring and genuine professor, is always willing to tweak lectures/material/dates if you kindly ask. Her powerpoints are not as effective as her lectures so I would suggest no skipping. 2 tests at 20% each but we were allowed formula sheets and problems were similar to hw/quizzes.

A great professor who puts a lot of thought into his slides and lectures. He relates the components and methods you learn in the class to his work in the car simulation industry. Take good notes and go over his slides before tests and quizzes. Be aware that the multiple-choice questions will be more complex than the math!

Professor Stover is great. The homeworks are easy as long as you follow his slides and examples, which he goes over in class and posts on Canvas. His lectures are a little hard to stay focused, but it's because of how much material he has to cover in a 50-minute class.

Not a bad professor overall but I took AP Computer Science in high school and hated it. As I came into this class, I found it quite difficult because I was already sick of coding (loops are the worst part). His programming exams are quite awful as you basically need to memorize code. He he does allow equation sheets on his numerical methods exams.

Computational Methods is a tough class if you're going in without any programming/scripting knowledge, and that's most students. Dr. Stover understands this and will go out of his way to help you IF YOU ASK HIM FOR HELP. He also allows a hand-written note sheet for exams, which is a life saver. Great professor.
Not all professors are equally effective at teaching; despite a clear understanding of the material, the instructional approach in this course makes it difficult for students to grasp key concepts.

He encourages everyone to get A's. His grading scheme was tough consisting of one mid term worth 40% of your grade, a final exam worth 50% and homework worth 10%, but he was very generous with grading the exams and gives lots of credit. He was helpful if you came to his office hours and he asked for feedback on how he can improve the class.

Not a bad professor, but his class was one test worth 40%, HW 10%, and final 50%. He was very leneint in grading the test and homeworks weren't difficult. Does a decent amount of examples and bases his lectures off the textbook.

Integrated Energy Systems was mostly project based, with few lectures on the actual material and limited reference material on Canvas. The final exam felt disconnected from what was emphasized during the semester. Dr. Hall is nice, but the course structure and communication does not align well with university standard.
Course structure did not exist. Professors instructions would contradict assignment details and rubrics constantly. Final exam included material that was never introduced in lecture.

My second professor for Thermodynamics and he was wayy better at explaining the problems. He always tried to help us out if we didn't understand, and we could do 2 or 3 short documents on different topics of thermodynamics for up to 10% extra-credit. I would definitely take another class with Dr. Zhu.
If you have no motion, you have no power. Some projects take a very long time to complete, but I learned a lot in this class, like how many times SolidWorks can crash on my laptop.

This class was very difficult and enjoyable simultaneously. Some projects take 15+ hours, so be prepared to dedicate lots of time to this class. The TAs are very helpful, and you definitely need to start projects early because you will 100% have questions to ask them. Dr. Fagan is also very approachable and clearly knowledgeable on what he teaches.

Fagan is the only professor you can take so I will offer you a word of advise. Attend all the lectures, they are early but you will get brownie points if you answer questions. Start assignments ASAP, they get out of hand quickly and usually take 6-12 hours a week. This class is a lot of work, but isn't hard, if you've made it this far you can do it

Honestly, Dr. Fagan was a great teacher to have, but there are a few things to be concerned about. The assignment descriptions are very vague. I wished that there was more information and constraints provided for each assignment. The TAs will not respond to your questions half the time, and the other half will be after a few days later.

Hes a great professor, very work-heavy work but graded fairly and honestly with some grace. Honestly this class is more about doing work and learning how to be an engineer rather than actually learning a material if that makes sense. Machine Shop portion is time consuming but a very valuable skill (Dr. Fagan does not teach Machine Shop).

Honestly the GOAT. He's super cool despite how much homework he gives. I will say though, I learned more about being an engineer from this class than I have from any combination of previous ones combined. Also the 3D lab is easy.

Fagan is an stellar teacher, who is tragically teaching one of the most intensive classes you'll have. The lectures are quite interesting (if you can stand being up early). The 8-12 hours of work a week is true; however, the substance of which is important, and overall, I had a fun time doing it. He also teaches the 3D lab section of this class.

Most important takeaway is that Terence Fagan is a very beautiful man with great intellect(sorry for the glaze). So many projects, I didn't sleep one day a week pretty regularly and machine shop is made me feel like a child during the industrial revolution. I hope he reads this review in class. But start projects early for the love of god. Please-

going into megr 2156 i was scared because all i heard was that the work load was insane. if you just do the projects when they are assigned then this is one of the easiest classes i have ever taken. the projects are cad heavy but thats what we are used to as mechanical engineers, the 3d lab was insanely fun and challenged creativity, fagan kills it

Fagan isn't a bad instructor but an 8AM lecture can make it feel so. Assignments can and will take time (Averaged 10 hours minimum for 90s+ on each assignment.) You'll get what you put in for this class. Only reason I finished with a B is because of my own mistake in the lab portion of this class but that isn't ran by Fagan.
Fagan's lectures were ok. All of his tests were multiple choice, and you can bring all the notes you want, however, the tests are full of extremely specific and trick questions.

A professor you get out of what you put in. Decent lectures, expects students to ask questions. Crazy amount of homework for 2156 (at least 5-10 hours a week), especially for 2 credit hours... Highly recommend keeping up with EPAs, most of midterm and final questions come from them. Do the work and you'll be fine.

Dr. Fagan has a great personality, and his lectures are interesting and engaging. Sometimes test content feels quite different from what is covered in class, so independent study is recommended, but I would still call it fair. Weekly projects take A LOT OF TIME, especially for a 2 credit course. Plan accordingly for 5-7 hours of homework weekly.
Super cool professor, study hard for the tests and you will be totally fine

Dr. Fagan was an amazing teacher of sophomore design. I had a lot of fun in his class with printing things. He is very relaxed and acceptable. Although with his lab, there is a lot of work that will be pushed. Almost 6-8 hours a week with lab and projects. I found fun in the projects and that has allowed for an easy-ish semester.
Lmao get Fagan'd

Dr. Fagan is a great person and cares about you as a student and is very knowledgeable in engineering. However, the curriculum is quite a heavy load. The lecture portion and the assignments pertaining to it are a drag. He also instructs the 3D printing lab and the curriculum for that is quite easy going.

Still remember he mentioned his rating on RMP beginning of the semester :D
Be sure to attend class, lots of information for the slides were presented verbally, and the exam are based on txtbk, slides and homework. It's open notes, and you can print anything you want and bring them to the exam (including the final). Yet, the exams were still hard.

Sometimes the TAs grade assignment incorrectly, be sure to ask Dr. Fagan for clear explanations. Make sure you finish the exam preps on canvas, most of the questions from midterm and final are from exam preps. We got extra credits by joining the ASME meeting (added to midterm)
Does not teach the material that is on the tests, vaguely goes over topics, no example problems, typos in everything, horrible lecture slides and no material to go over outside of class.

Could be a more interesting class, but it's just listening to him read off slides every class. Easy A either way, one hw every week and a take-home midterm and final. I did appreciate that it's over Zoom since its later on a Friday though.
Just get it over with. One assignment a week and one lecture. I watched South Park during lecture and it was like a try not to laugh challenge.

This guy makes me wanna rip my hair out. Boring lectures where he doesn't take a breath when talking and goes on and on to the point where it just sounds like noise halfway through the semester. Get one tolerance wrong and your grade goes to a 40. One 55-minute class a week and 4-6 CAD assignments due on the next day.

Dr Raquet himself seems like a nice dude but he instructs his TA's to grade very harshly and with no mercy for the most part. This class should not be a 2 credit hour class. The rubric/grading criteria is super unclear AND stuff gets graded super late so you have no Idea if you've been doing the work right. Still should be a pretty easy B I'd say.

This class has a ton of homework but I thought it was fun. He is a very tough grader and you don't get your assignments graded until the end of the semester so you don't actually know your grade. The lectures are pretty useless not gonna lie but the lab was important for homework.

This class had a lot of homework, but online resources and tools like unstuckstudy were helpful for staying on top of it. The lectures weren't the most engaging, but the labs were useful for learning CAD. Overall, the class was manageable with some effort.

Lectures were posted on Canvas for extra help if you need to look back on a topic. He takes points off for the smallest things for 3d modeling on creo, so attention to detail really matters. Knowledge of HTML and CAD helps for the final (group) project. Hope you get a good group and you'll be fine.

Dr. Raquet made this class very hard. 
The program we used, Creo Parametric, was awful. Very hard to understand how to develop the CAD. The only way I survived this class was by going to the TA office hours. If you go to the office hours, you will pass. He also forgot to grade things and I had to remind him several times.

Has great lectures and videos to understand the CAD program used. There is lots of homework each week, but it's usually a few easy cad models, drawing practice, and a hand drawing of some sort. He isn't very accessible out of class, nor understanding/accepting of any issues that arise with assignments or their submission.

easiest class of my life, even with no CAD background the hw only takes aroun one-two hours a week if you go to TA office hours. GO TO TA OFFICE HOURS! It makes life 10x easier. Professor is an interesting character, but if you do bare minimal you can easily get an A.

Grading in this class rewards thoroughness and attention to detail. The lab sessions are helpful for learning CAD, but I found the lectures to be fairly random with content that wasn't often applied in class. Grades came in late without much feedback. CAD and HTML familiarity will make this class easy. Expect the occasional paper.
Good guy and understanding but until grading

I didn't start seeing grades until the last week of classes because there's only a few TAs and a crazy amount of assignments. He also creates assignments that randomly involve html coding (to make a website) and essays ...for a CAD class. If you know about CAD beforehand, you'll do fine. If not, prepare to spend your entire day in a mosaic lab

Harsh and unclear grading. 1 wrong tolerance and you get a 50. I think so at least as theres zero comments on any form of web homework from him. Takes months to grade homework, says to treat this class like a job but he cant do his. Wasteful lectures (we had one on 3d printers with no follow up assigment/lecture). Worst professor Ive had.

Professor Raquet was a nice professor and was knowledgeable. However, he did not really have clear grading criteria, I learned more from online resources and TAs than I did from him specifically. He gave a TON of HW and would make it all due on Thursdays. I learned a lot, I just don't think his lectures are the right way of teaching even with lab.

Dr. Raquet is smart and I learned a lot in 1202, but it mostly was because of the TA's.  The lectures were hard to learn from. There was a good amount of homework but it was manageable. Because of so much homework, the graders had difficulty keeping up.

I learned a lot in ENGR 1202, however, most of that knowledge was gained from online resources given to us, NOT Dr. Raquet's teaching. 3-4 large assignments are given per week, which is manageable if you use your time wisely, however, the graders could not keep up with this work. Grading is very harsh, and the criteria are not clearly explained.

Overall I enjoyed this class and professor. He does assign a lot of homework a week but most of the assignments can be completed in about 30 minutes each. I also feel that most of the assignments are relevant to the major and applicable to the engineering major.
Everyone else's reviews pretty much sum my experience. GO NINERS!

Raquet is a cool guy and tries his best to get back to you abt concerns. Only thing I disliked was the homework, bc the graders were very overcritical, forget one tolerance and your grade tanks, something like that. It also takes a long time to grade the homework, so its hard to determine your final grade. Graded on mostly hw +  final group project

I would give him zero stars if I could. Dr. Raquet is a horrible professor. He uses Creo which is the worst CAD software ever. He also has a dumb grading system and gives you NEGATIVE points on 3D CAD drawings you worked hard on. Overall, this professor should be avoided at all costs.

Lectures were pointless but mandatory for attendance. Feedback on the (many) assignments was practically non-existant and the grades wouldn't even come back for over a month. He also went over the material super fast and wouldn't go back over anything, so if you got lost then you were basically screwed.

He is an okay professor. He is very nice and helpful, but his teaching style is not the best since he just skims over practice problems in class. The two exams are only 15% each, but the final being 40% of your grade is the worst part of this class. The TA was extremely helpful and clearly tried to give all the partial credit he could on exams.

One of the worst professors to take for solids. Mumbles constantly and made me want to ignore him in class. Rode the line of being just in depth enough to sound smart, but not enough actually to teach the class. His final is 40% of the class, so going into the final with a 80% and still failing is how it went for me and most of my friends.

Don't listen to the reviews saying hes not that bad. Hes so bad be prepared to just have to learn everything yourself. He cant teach anything and you can barely understand what he says most of the time.

Less than half the class shows up for lectures and those are the people who are giving him bad reviews. His class is challenging because the material is, if you don't care about learning and want to skip through with an easy grade then don't take him. He genuinely wants you to pass and provided plenty of opportunity for extra credit on corrections.

I was horrified to take this class because of the reviews but it was not that bad. I am quite confident that most people who struggled did not do the homework or go to class/pay attention consistently. Exam questions were not tricky or complicated but tested conceptual understanding. I'd say half are from hw. He gave extra credit near the end.
NOT RECOMMENDED.
worst teacher ever!!!!!!!!

He is a really bad teacher. He doesn't know how to teach or communicate. He seems to be nice, but he instantly changes whenever you ask him questions. Has a strong accent. He is very proud that the class he taught from the last semester had a failure rate of 50% and 1 "A" student. Avoid at all costs!!!

Zheng's lectures are very difficult to follow and his office hours are not helpful. exams are difficult and he gives no curves at all. He can give extra credit for the tests but it happened once for us. Final is 40% of your grade so your grade tank really easily. He is generous with partial credit and allows your final to replace your total grade.
His field of research is not high demand out there. Reconsider before taking a class with him, maybe you don't waste your time, energy and money like what I did!

Txtbk is the most important source of the course, make sure you read and practice with the example problems. The exams are decent if you understand the concepts and the way to approach the answer (not the same compare to txtbk). You can bring your HANDWRITTEN formula sheet to exam, and you can even ask him for the formula if you worded it correctly

Worked rapidly through problems to the point where students couldn't keep up. All example problems were written, not typed, onto the lecture slides, so notes often looked as neat as when you try to sign your name on a tablet with your finger. Lecture slides were posted but the professor consistently skipped several steps on every problem he posted.

I like him as a person, he is super sweet! His class was interesting at times and the homework was always pretty interesting. The only gripe I have is that the assignment guidelines were never clear on what he wanted. However, he was a pretty easy grader even on the midterm and final - so I can't be too mad about it.

Though attendance isn't mandatory, without it, it is unlikely you will do well. The teacher isn't very good at explaining concepts and is at times difficult to understand due to the accent. The homework was a chore. Felt as if I understood the concepts until it was time for the tests. The final exam could replace the overall grade if needed.

All the labs are taught/graded by TA's, and nothing is graded until the last week of classes, so you have no idea what your grade is going into the final. Have to take the final exam using lab data you don't even know is correct or not. Labs themselves are not too difficult if you have a good TA.

This class was the worst, terrible instructions that are outdated and hard to read. He doesn't even teach the class, the TAs do all the work. After the second week we all knew this class was going to suck. Problem is you can't avoid him, the class is mandatory and he is the only one who "teaches" it!!!!!
I was miserable taking his the Labs he oversees.  He never answers emails on timely, if ever. His assignments are not organized well, confusing, and basically busy work. Didn't learn anything.

ECGR 2161 Basic Electrical 

Terrible Professor. I have never met this professor because he never shows up to labs. He has teaching assistants do all of his lectures and all of his grading even though none of them seem to be on the same page. There is a prelab, lab, and a post lab. This is a 1 credit hour lab that takes 10+ hours. Who hired him?

Worst professor Ive ever had. Got all A's except this class and it took up the most time. Nothing was graded besides the first lab until the last week of class. Nor any of the the 40% of your grade that was technical writing assignments. You receive no feedback so you cannot improve. multiple documents have contradictory instructions. Fire him asap

I'm 80% sure Hodgins actually died years ago and they still put his name on the course. No one I've ever talked to, including the lab TAs, has ever met him. If he is still alive he should be fired for this disgrace of a lab. The instructions are out of date and completely wrong from the actual experiments. Your grades depend on if the TA is nice.

This lab is really unorganized. The lab guides are a complete mess, hard to read and hard to follow. For some reason they are all formatted differently and you have to read it a few times just to figure out what you're supposed to do. Also, be ready to spend a few days working on a single post lab because the instructions are not clear at all.

In one word. Terrible. Somehow this guy is still a professor despite the distaster show for MEGR labs. Lab guides are vague, lengthy, and sometimes inaccurate. I spent on average 10-12 hrs a week doing JUST pre lab write up and data analysis (which can involve typing in hundreds of data points). There are no rubrics for papers either.
Probably the best professor in the program, genuinely amazing at teaching and cares about his students. He has a ton of experience and you can tell he knows what he is talking about.

This professor is hard, but if you stick with it, it'll be so worth it, and he will teach you more than you think. He is amazing, very nice, and truly wants the best for you. Do not give up, and he will make this the best class for you.

Dr. Brizendine is a professor who will make you learn the content of his course. You will learn best by showing up to class, being attentive, going to office hours, and practicing problems. This is a class that you will have to put time into. The more practice, the better your results.

Attendance is not mandatory and homework is hardly graded. Show up, participate and do the assigned practice problems or you will not pass. He goes over all the content extremely well during lectures, but the TA, Eddie, is also a great resource. Take the first weeks seriously and show up to office hours and this class will be much easier.

U have to for sure go to class and pay attention, as well as work on it outside of class, but the professor is very caring, whether you pass or not, but in the end, it's about how hard you're willing to work for it. I would definitely go to the TA for help because he is a great resource.

Dr. Brizendine is a great professor. His class is difficult, but if you pay attention you will succeed. He is a funny guy as well, always had a story to go with something. He wants you to succeed, and will stay late after lectures to ensure you understand. Overall, he is a great guy, but you will be challenged. Definitely would take him again.

Dr. El-Ghannam clearly knows what he is doing and is passionate about the topics he covers. Unfortunately, he given extraordinal dry slide lectures and his tests barely have partial credit. However, as long as you study the equations given, you should be fine. Would take again.

I thought professor El-Ghannam was a decent professor for the majority of my experience. Some units had hundreds of lecture slides to go through, and only about 5 questions on the test. He gave minimal to zero partial credit on test questions. While somewhat strict, he will make sure that you learn the material well. Office hours were important.

Extremely immature and unprofessional with emotional maturity equivalent to that of a third grade pyromaniac without a father figure. You can't ask him a single question without a genuine top tier crash-out. Not bad at teaching but desperately needs a therapist.

Is a very moody person. If he is having a bad day he goes off on students, acts annoyed with people when they get an answer incorrect. Makes you not want to answer questions in class. Test got easier over time,  similar to hws. However, I would not take him again because just reads off slides and could test you on anything from 300+slides.

Avoid this professor. Reads off the slides the whole time. Grading is very rough; he changed 1s test grades multiple times because he "didn't like the TA's grading". Test 1 grades were failing and he blamed students. He can be very moody and can yell at students for no reason and it happened multiple times throughout the semester.

He is one of the worst professors I have had. Reads off the slides the whole time. If he makes a mistake, he blames it on you. Grading is very rough; he changed one of my test grades four times because he "didn't like the TA's grading". He can be very moody and can yell at students for no reason. Doesn't respond to emails. Tests are unpredictable.

Do not take. Doesn't believe in partial credit and will expect you to know all 11 lectures, which are 50+ slides for the test. It is very moody and will yell at students for wrong answers. Here is your best advice: take this class online during the summer with her! All you need to do is read the textbook and sorta listen to her lectures. Really just pay attention to the stuff in her lectures that aren't in the textbook. Such an easy A. Make sure you do every packback and the quizzes. Quizzes are easy if you spend 20 min studying.

I have taken Mrs Gaultney for both research methods and senior seminar. Many say her canvas is unorganized, but give her the benefit of the doubt as she's older and is retiring soon. She is extremely knowledgeable about psychology and has done a lot of research on sleep. Her classes are fairly easy as long as you attend the lectures and read.

This class is as writing intensive as it gets. You will be writing a lot, conducting your own research, and basically writing your own journal article. Gaultney was sweet, but her Canvas is unorganized and confusing. The weekly assignments get confusing too but she does not grade them harshly. Attendance is graded and be prepared to use statistics!

The class itself is easy and it is nice that there isn't weekly homework. The only things that are graded are the exams and a few simple assignments. But the Powerpoints are horrendous. Going through the slides is a must, but they are often 80 slides with a 1-2 minute audio on each one. And she speaks so slowly and monotone. Would not recommend.

she had a rude tone every time I emailed her, and also CHANGED the syllabus in the MIDDLE of the semester. she had an "extra credit cap" for the course (odd). I missed ONE critical thinking question and many others missed the same one, but DIDN'T let us redo it, even though the syllabus implied she'd give us an extension.

Even though I got an A in the class I think that some of her policies were annoying. I did all the extra credit assignments and she took away 7 of my extra credit points because she said I reached the limit. Overall, if you just read the textbook and do the practice quizzes you should be fine on the exams.

While the class is kind of assignment heavy, if you put in the time, utilize the study guides, the extra credit assignments, and the unlimited quiz attempts, you'll do great. She gave me so many resources to build on and I honestly could've gotten an A if I didn't slack. She's great!! :)

I took this class fully online, and as long as you keep up with the weekly chapter readings, it is easy to do well on the exams. There are many extra credit opportunities, and she drops your lowest exam score. She is very understanding and kind. I highly recommend taking a class with her.

Amazing prof all around! Caring & knowledgeable. Enough extra credit to bump up a grade. Studying is a must. Study guides were not helpful, they were just the lectures in question form. My advice: handwrite all the lectures & study those for exams. Dr Levens is willing to listen and adjusts her approaches so material is easier to understand.

She is so scatterbrained it makes it impossible to follow along and learn in class lectures, where she reads off slides. Exams are hard, so much memorization,33 page study guides when fully answered. Yes there is lots of extra credit but your only allowed so much at the end. If you have to take the class fine but take time and prepare to study.

I have both taken and been a TA for Levens's B&B class, and Levens is great. There is no reason for you not to get an A; she offers up to 30 points extra credit, drops your lowest exam and your lowest writing assignment, and the TAs always hold in-person review sessions for upcoming exams. She is a tad scatterbrained, but brilliant and kind.

Dr. Levens is a great professor.  I took her course over the summer and am just finishing TA'ing for it.  She grades tough and the material is hard but she really does try her best to make it approachable to students.  Take her class over any of the other professors for B&B, and being her TA was a pleasure.  I would take her course again.
Overall this class gets a bad wrap, you just need to study for it.  Its a lot of information, come to class!

She is extremely intelligent, but I think she has a lot of stressful things going on in her personal life. She stumbles around her words a lot and it makes it a bit difficult to grasp important bits during lectures, but I know she is doing the best she can. I wish nothing but the best for her & her family. I think she should move to online courses!

Felt much more challenging than a 2000-level course. Dr. Levens is super passionate, intelligent, and kind. Unfortunately, teaching complex material is not her calling. I recommend relying on your textbook if you take this class. Her lectures are confusing and boring. Tests are memorization-heavy. Don't skip out on the reading like I did!!

Don't take this class. It is completely unproductive and unmotivating. She assigns everything at the last minute including the Final Portfolio which is approximately 12-20 pages long and only gave my class a week to complete it. She is unreasonable and all over the place. Half of the time she rants about stuff that is not pertaining to class. RUN.

Sara always forgets to prepare for class and needs reminders to turn in assignments. The course requires reading empirical articles, writing response papers (which are important for grading), and making social media posts, all due the next day. It's stressful to rely on her to turn in the assignments on time, which can make learning frustrating

Unprepared for class. Unclear instructions. Tends to ramble and sidetracked. Required to read 2 empirical articles, write response papers, comment, and do separate assignments. Due by the next day. Assignments took 6 hrs. Lacks understanding & compassion. Prefers quantity over quality. High expectations of students but does not meet them herself.

PSYC2113 is a hard course but Dr. Levens is a great professors. She is very knowledgeable and explains complex topics in a simple way. She also gives lots of extra credit. Class is very straight forward so long as you read the textbook, watch her lectures, take the quizzes, and study for the tests.

This class is hard and so are the tests. Dr. Levens gives study guides and tries to accommodate people if an emergency pops up. Do the extra credit it will boost your grade a lot. While the class is hard I recommend taking Dr. Levens for this class if possible.

An all-around wonderful professor! Her lectures are clear and understandable. She makes an effort to make the content as relevant as possible and takes time to explain. Very kind. Gives study guides and lots of assignments, but drops the lowest scores

Amazing professor. She is extremely helpful and responsive. Her lectures are very interesting and she always makes them relevant to our lives. Tough tests but she gives study guides that if you study really help. She also gives a lot of extra credit.

She is an incredible professor- her lectures are extremely organized and help so much for the tests. If you go to class everyday and stay up to date on assignments you are guaranteed to pass. She is very helpful and responds to emails in less than a week. She won't baby the class and can be a harsh grader, but it genuinely helped me to grow.

Her tests were extremely hard and the study guides were 40-50 page google docs, some of the information or topics not even being on the test. We met once a week and would often go off topic in class. You have to try extremely hard to get an A and I just barely made enough credit on the final to pull through. First exam average was like a 50%

I had a class with her for PSYC 2113, we would only meet once a week, and even then, she would cancel classes often. Her study guides would be 3 pages or even longer, but many would still fail the test. She seems nice, and when we did have lectures, I would enjoy them and learn many facts, but overall, I would not ever take a class with her again.

Dr. Berzins is a lovely woman. Her class however was one of the most dreadful ones i've had. We only had it once a week and most weeks she would cancel. The test material didn't match with the lecture most of the time, not to mention they're worth 60% of your grade. Plan on studying for days on end if you want to pass. You do get test cheat sheets!

She was okay. She seemed like she didn't care much for my class. The class was very independent. Many people in my class barely passed. She assigned weekly quizzes that you had to read 1 or 2 chapters for. The textbook is very hard to understand, which is what most of your teaching comes from bc she hardly lectures. She did give exam study guides.

I took Dr.Berzins for 2113 as well, and both classes were extremely hard, but she is so supportive and genuinely wants nothing more than for her students to succeed. she went above and beyond helping me in both classes throughout the semester. she gives insane extra credit opportunities throughout the whole course too!!

This class is difficult and requires a lot of reading, but she gives you lots opportunities to earn points outside of tests. We were allowed to take cheat sheets to the last 2 exams, and she creates exhaustive study guides for each test that the whole class can fill-out together. If you take brain/behavior with her you will pass.

Dr.Berzins did a fantastic job of setting the class up for success. If you read the assigned reading and stay on top of this class she takes a really difficult subject and makes it really easy. Lots of chances for extra credit and the materials were easy to follow.

This is for both Social Psych + Brain and behavior Pysch. Overall, I wouldn't recommend her at all. Her lecture style is unpleasant. Her lecture slides consist of some words and rambles for a few minutes so you don't know what's important and what's not. She wasn't there as often as she could have, Her exams are HARD, class averaging barely a 70.

Most stressful class I had, not only weekly homework, "weeklies"  and assignment's for a 20+ page literary review, then random days where we sometimes learned stuff, her teaching style wasn't for me. If you do the work on time then you will do fine but you definitely have to try and put in the work. no tests or quizzes tho. Final is open note.

She was kind and offered many extra credit opportunities. However, her lectures didn't match up to the content she wanted us to learn, neither of which  fully matched up to the study guides (often ~40 pages long), and all of which didn't match up to the exams. The assignments give a good background but aren't very useful.
Awful, terrible, how could she... (she overcomplicates everything and it honestly doesn't help at all). We all bombed the first test.

Class was once a week and she was never there. She lectures well if you forget about the content on the tests. Everything taught in class is not reflected on the tests. This class isn't hard because of the content its hard because of the lack of continuity between test and coursework. Take this class with someone else.

I found the lectures to be interesting as she's straight forward in explaining the content, and she's very clear about her expectations in general. She provides a study guide before each exam that I found very helpful. Overall I'd recommend because you can tell she really cares about what she's teaching.

Favorite professor I've ever had. She's incredibly clear about what she expects from her students, and she inspired me to seek a career in a similar field. She posts every slide on Canvas, is prompt with responding to emails, and gives very cohesive study guides before tests. If you do the reading and take notes, you'll be fine.

Very lecture heavy. You have to go to class to get a good grade. 4 exams, no final, weekly hw on the readings, occasional journal prompt hw. You have to read a lot in the hw. Her tests are very hard, class avg is a C. She does provide a study guide w/ feedback, but you have to study a lot to get a A or B on the tests. Take 2130 with someone else.

Overall a fine course, the material just gets really similar and hard to differentiate apart from other "theories" and definitions. Berzins lectures fine, but is slightly disorganized and often goes off the powerpoint to the point where she's going back and forth between 20 slides. Attendance is not required, however, you gain points going to class

Despite being a nice person, Berzins is not a good professor. She was absent every other week, and barely taught anything during her lectures. Tests are bad measures of what we learn in the week, and her TAs are incompetent. I have gotten all A's in every other class, I spend over 25 hours studying for tests in this class and still do poorly.

Dr. Berzins is a nice woman but I think she's a little overwhelmed and too busy to be a professor. She comes to class sick and unmotivated to teach. Her teaching style is talking and making us do activities that are useless because it's only like one question about the activity that took almost all of class. I regret taking her for TWO classes :(

This professors classes were one face to face and one asynchronous class. I signed up for this class because I wanted to take it in person and believed it was the best option. Though, we only met in person and actually had a lecture twice six weeks in. I think she is a brilliant person, but seemed busy with other more important things than class.

Objectively, her tests are a not good measure of the way these social psychology concepts are taught/exist. The questions are often ambiguous, she doesn't allow you to ask any questions so "she is impartial" which I think is silly. If majority of the class gets specific questions wrong, it is illogical to attribute to the students' misunderstanding

This class is hard, but Dr. Berzins did a phenomenal job preparing us for it. She made sure we had plenty of time to prepare for the literature review paper. She set a timeline through the semester, requiring us to finish an outline and 2 drafts for a grade. There are extra credit opportunities for the paper and exam. Plenty of resources. Take her!

The class is hard but Dr. Berzins makes sure that her students are prepared to succeed. Provided detailed study guides and was always accessible via email or through office hours. You NEED to do the readings and study for exams, or else you will struggle. If you want to pass brain & behavior, take it with Dr. Berzins.

Great lectures and provided countless opportunities for grades other than exams. Provided study guides that she helped fill out if the class struggled with certain concepts. She is clearly extremely passionate about what she teaches which makes lectures fun. Super accessible outside of class and very respectful! Highly recommend any of her classes.

I loved Dr. Berzins class. The material is challenging but she does a great job explaining it. You MUST study for exams but other grades are provided for some cushion. You will do good just GO TO CLASS and try your best. She is very understanding so ask questions and use TA's.
I couldn't rate her for social psychology for some reason but that is what I took.  The content was difficult but she was great at explaining the content and is extremely knowledgeable in the field.

Dr. Berzins is a new professor and I loved her class. This course in challenging in general and she did a great job making it easier to understand. You will cover a lot of material, be prepared to and and take advantage of TA's and tutoring center. She by far seems like this best option for this course. STUDY for Exams

I enjoyed this class. I'm not good with anything about the brain, so I did find tests very hard even though I studied. He drops your lowest test grade, including the final, which is great. He does random polls everywhere for an attendance grade and drops your lowest five. Lectures weren't boring, and I didn't mind the class at all. I recommend him!

Good teacher really enjoyed his class. Tests aren't hard as long as you study enough. Gives extra credit. Knows what he's talking about and lectures aren't boring. Lets you out of class early some days.

I took this class for credit as an elective but had a fun time during his classes. His lectures were enjoyable and took attendance by using PollEverywhere which also made it engaging. Chill, Friendly, Understanding person. Answers his emails fairly quickly. I recommend!

McMains is an awesome professor! I found his test to be very straight forward as long as you take notes and actually come to class which is simple! He gave very interesting lectures that made coming to class worth it and spoke about personal experiences as well. He's a very welcoming professor and was funny. His study guides were also the best.

The material was relatively hard, unless you have some biology background. Dr. McMains is very knowledgable about the material he teaches, easy to access outside of class, and will gladly answer questions. He has study guides for 5 total exams which are great to use to follow along during his lectures. Other workload done via Revel.

Professor McMains made taking this class so bearable. He uses slides to give all the information needed for his tests, and his lectures are very engaging. He also gives out the test study guides right after the previous test, so you have them while you are learning this material. I highly recommend taking his psych class; he is a great professor.

Dr. Mcmains is a great professor and is very knowledgable in the field of Psychology. I am not sure if this is a course thing, or just what he does as a professor... but this course is extremely exam heavy. Exams count for the majority of your grade. If you are a bad exam taker, I would not recommend this class. They are very hard tests.

This was a class that required studying, but he was an amazing professor. He clearly knows and loves psychology. He sends out "Study Guides", but they are just topics that will be on the exam, so you should know how to describe all of them. The tests are not easy, but they are simple. They are also each 60 questions. He drops 4 attendance grades.

I did drop his class since it wasn't the best fit for me. Even with this happening, he was super accommodating and caring for my situation going above and beyond recommending new classes I could take even from other professors. Absolute amazing guy I would highly recommend taking his classes. Even friends say he's amazing to work with.

he is a good teacher. Make sure to study everything on the slides and you should be good for the tests. U have to do a mini assignment before every chapter but it is easy and u can work ur way up to 100. The 2 journal assignments r also easy. Study in advance for the tests. the second sentence will be the key to ur success. He does drop 1 exam.

He is truly one of the best professors I have ever had. He is passionate about psychology and engages the class in fun activities and questions which helped me to truly understand the materials. I recommend him.

My favorite lecture professor by far. His lectures are great and he includes amazing explanations to all the information needed. Additionally, he tells you exactly whats going to be on the exams. The exams are difficult, but your grade doesn't heavily rely on them. Extra credit is offered along with plenty of time to get all your work done.

I took Dr. McMains for PSYC 1101 my freshman year. Dr. McMains has engaging lectures and a good sense of humor. Tests are the majority of your grade, but as long as you go to class and study, you'll be fine! Highly recommend this course and especially Dr. McMains!

I loved this class, harder material but the way he teaches forces you to pay attention. miss classes you WILL fall behind-the slides only show the vocab not the definition so you cant go back if you miss something he says. Study guides literally show exactly what will be on the exam, exams are fairly easy if you study. Absolutely recommend.

I did not care for this class. I am an A-B student and I found his test very difficult. They are very wordy and hard to understand. The test are a major weight to your grade, however the lowest test grade is dropped. Only one homework assignment a week, but it can be hard. I enjoyed most of his lectures, just be prepared for difficult test.

Great guy! Clearly knowledgeable. Tests are hard but not difficult as long as you know the material. Easy A if you put in a proportionate amount of work to the three credits. (For me, like 2-3 hrs/week). Just go to class and take notes and you'll be fine. He posts the exam study guides way in advance (usually like 2-2.5 weeks). Would take him again
Makes the lectures fun and entertaining. Easy at least A or B if you do the work and listen to him. Best professor I have had at Charlotte.

One of my favorite professors in the dept. Very organized lectures/slides, I truly looked forward to going to class. Fast pace and the material is dense but, McMains is sensitive to more difficult topics and doesn't "fly through". Very responsive and also publishes a study guide for the exam so you know what to expect. Heavily recommend him.

He makes it very easy to get a good grade. His lectures are very interesting and enjoyable. Although attendance isn't necessarily mandatory, there is participation graded in class, but you'll find yourself looking forward to class. He gives study guides before the tests which make it very easy to study what's on the test and get a good grade.

Despite the dense material, he is excellent at explaining abstract and difficult concepts and making them relatable and interesting. Attendance is not mandatory, but lectures are very worthwhile and you will fall behind if you miss them. It is mostly based on a few exams, but he gives a study guide for each.
His lectures are fun and interactive. He is really sweet and understanding, you can tell he is passionate about what he is teaching.

Dr. Gadaire is passionate and well-versed in his subject, and he provided me with valuable information for opportunities when I expressed an interest in this subject. Be ready to understand your material entirely and apply it to scenarios in and outside of class. This class is easy and Dr. Gadaire is approachable when experiencing difficulties.

Professor Gadaire himself is a really good professor who is incredibly kind and caring. However most of the actual work in the class was just textbook assignments that felt very much like busy work to me. The tests were not extremely hard but you definitely have to study. Overall a good experience.

This professor cares a lot, it seems. He just has no control over the classroom. Many classes were drowned out by people talking over him. If he gained a bit more control over the room, I think he would be an excellent professor. Be ready to read because there are 2 chapters per week, usually. But the actual tests aren't too hard.

He's honestly a 3.7, but the class was a lot.  Attendance is taken every day through polls. You have to read an entire assigned chapter reading or two in just a week, with graded questions. He also did not mention, nor did the syllabus, until the day before exam 1, that exams are multiple choice, 3 short essays, AND fill-in-the-blank.

We had lab homework every week and a semester long project as the final. I always recieved minor points off of all the labs (always 9.6 or 9.8 out of 10 points) and I would have to ask him in class why I recieved that grade. Overall, understanding professor and attendence was not graded but you will not pass without attending.

Dr. Gadaire very clearly cared about doing his best for his students. The material itself was difficult to learn but actually coming to class really helped me grasp the concepts. He made things fun when in class and helped us when we needed it. If I could take another one of his classes I 100% would.

I really liked this class as Dr. Ravyts as a professor. The tests are literally just the lecture slides so as long as you attend and take notes, you will pass. One paper and one group assignment, pretty slight class and he grades well.

The class is based around conducting a research project, which can be stressful to cram into one semester. However, Dr. Ravyts is a relatively generous grader and makes sure everyone understands the concepts. Be aware that the coursework is concentrated towards the end of the semester.

Dr. Ravyts is such a great professor and would recommend him to anyone. pretty lecture heavy class but his exams are simple and straightforward. You must take 3 out of the 4 exams given and the lowest grade gets dropped! No assignments other than a group debate and 3 pg paper towards the end of this semester. Loved this class and def recommend!
Very lecture heavy class, graded on 3 tests, a paper and a debate. However, tests were easy if you listened to the lecture. Ravyts was super kind and had interesting lectures.

Dr. Ravyts is a good professor and taught a really interesting class. Grades do depend on 3 tests, but if you attend class, take notes, and study you will be fine. The class isn't very difficult. I enjoyed his class a lot and would take another one from him again

Professor Ravyts was a really nice guy! My only complaint is that the majority of your grade depends on the three exams, and sometimes they consist of topics that weren't in the study guide. Besides that, it was a pretty easy class if you made sure to either pay attention to the lectures or review the slides afterward.
Dr. Lyerly is a great professor who makes it clear that she is here for the students. She is accessible outside of class hours and works hard to make sure everyone succeeds in her course.

A lot of the material is explained during the weekly lectures that you do for homework. Lectures feel extremely simple. The tests are unit reflections which are pretty easy; you only do 3 during the semester.
Expectations are super clear kinda odd due dates for things no tests
Take this class if you want an IDF agent teaching you.

lowkey was a good class if you dont wanna pull up to lectures so much. attendance wasnt mandatory, she grades the discussion posts and multiple choice assignments based on completion. its good if youre consistent. she is strict and doesnt give any extensions/extra credit tho. she doesnt really respond to emails and makes her syllabus extra clear.

There is literally no reason to go to her lectures. Everything is explained online and she adds nothing to the material, only repeating what you already learned on your own time. There are no tests and no final exam so there's no reason to even remember any material unless you are in the lab. Due dates for homework are all over the place.

Dr. Lyerly was a very difficult professor. She has no room for forgiveness and seems to have a disregard for her students. The class assignments are very easy because they are online assignments graded by a computer, but the things that she grades, expect a much lower grade than you think, with little to no feedback.

Honestly, she wasn't as bad as the reviews make her seem. She makes her grading criteria and expectations for the class very clear in the syllabus so idk why so many people complain about that. All of her assignments can be done online and all in one day as well. Very easy class!
Very strict with grading policy. She can be kind of passive aggressive, especially through email. I would say she is an organized professor but could ease up on the grading policy for sure.

Extremely strict with deadlines and won't offer extra credit or curves, so you have to stay perfect the whole semester. Honestly, she often came across as rude and dismissive in my experience, which made communicating with her pretty frustrating.

Absolutely not necessary to attend her lectures. Everything was online and all that was done in the lecture was reinforce the material learned online, but there were no tests or a final, so there was no point in remembering anything you learned. Just get all the online work done and you can forget about this class for the rest of your week.

The strictest and least supportive professor I've ever had. Grading feels inconsistent with the rubric, feedback is minimal, and asking questions often feels unwelcome. The class material is fine, but the environment she creates is discouraging. I won't even recommend my worst enemy to take her class.

This was an incredibly easy class. I was very nervous before taking her class because of the previous reviews on here but I was pleasantly surprised. She's a fair grader and gives good feedback; also, she has a VERY strict late work policy. But as long as you stay on top of the work and don't get lazy, you shouldn't get anything less than an A+.

Psych 1101 was the easiest class I've taken in my life. Most of the people complaining about Dr. Lyerly have poor time management skills. The other psych classes might be different, but the only way to fail 1101 is if you forget to do the work or are just lazy. The Unit reflections can be tricky. I did well, but if you're unsure go to office hours.

Dr. Lyerly is unwilling to work with you on anything. I had to email her multiple times because of mistakes in rubric grading and feedback. I only managed a B because of how hard I had to work for this class. I had a lot of extenuating circumstances and disabilities that she refused to work with me on. Disappointed by the quality of this course.

I don't know why she has low grading but she is so easy with homework and quizzes. It's an easy A with her and never found it difficult. You do have to read but it's a few pages and no finals or midterms only reflection paper. She has TA's that helps a lot. Totally recommend

I can't believe she has such low ratings! Dr. Lyerly is very caring and checked in multiple times throughout the semester. This class is HARD. Quizzes are open note/open book, and I felt she was fair with her grading. The first writing assignment I didn't feel the instructions were very clear, and feedback could have been better.

Took online. Very easy class just do the work on time and don't procrastinate. Assignment criteria is very clear. No tests, just 200-300 word unit reflections that are super easy. If you do the work how she wants it, its an easy class

She teaches psychology well, but her grading system needs some work. Her class has no final exam, but she assigns unit reflection papers that needs a specific criteria to get a good grade. Participation is also necessary to pass the class.

The only reason I scraped by in this class with a B- is because I'm on Ritalin and studied day in and day out. After a plethora of screaming, crying, hair pulling head bashing mental breakdowns, I still averaged 60s on the exams. I don't even blame the TA's for being unhelpful, they were working with SCRAPS.

The class itself is really interesting despite her best efforts w/ dry & boring lectures

There's a study guide for each quiz.  She says everything on the quiz is from the SG but there were multiple times we had questions that were no where on the SG.  *****She doesn't hand back quizzes or feedback so you have no clue what areas to improve on.*****

I did not enjoy having her as a professor. The material itself is not difficult to digest for this class, however she makes no effort outside of sloppy slideshows to teach. It is clear she does not immerse herself in the material and has no interest making her lectures interesting. She also gives no feedback for group discussions and grades harshly

Not sure what's up with the rating but she was a very good professor, as long as you read the text book you're good. She provides a guide for when taking notes which is useful for when studying for the final. My only problem is the lack of feedback when grading quizzes and in person activities. She doesn't tell you why points were taken.
Little communication and not available outside of class. Wouldn't suggest taking anything by her
Just don't take her. She's very passive aggressive and she has no clear grading criteria EVER. She just randomly grades stuff how she wants to and she made this course difficult for no reason.

Do not take her she is very condescending when she gives feedback for assignments. She makes assignments complicated for no reason. Simple assignments like a discussion post is over complicated by her. She has also never been clear on grading in her class taking large amount of points off for silly things, and questions if you read the material.

I am not sure why there are so many low reviews. I took Critical Thinking About Research (course code has changed). The class required a lot of work, but all of the RM classes typically do. She made the grading outline clear and gave great feedback. I did well on it because of the meetings I had with her, and she was very nice.

This is a really easy online class. The exams are open book, and you can use handwritten notes, which makes them much less stressful. The assignments are simple and do not take long to complete. I would absolutely recommend taking a class with her.

Complete lack of professionalism. Appalled by her poor ability to regulate her own emotions. It's clear that she's extremely anxious and rigid. She becomes easily distressed and frequently projects her emotions toward students. It's SO disappointing to see such negative patterns of teaching endorsed by prior students who have taken her classes.

An easy online class. As long as you do the assignments, you'll earn your points. She drops the lowest grades for a few of them. Both exams are open book and she gives you each chapter's study guide to download, print, and fill in the blanks. You can take your own notes, but the study guides and open book are enough to pass the exams.

Dr. Godly-Reynolds is an angel not only as a person, but a professor as well! These reviews are likely from people who are upset she didn't give them more extensions on her already established and fair deadlines. She has extremely forgiving grading, and there is absolutely no reason you can't make an A with her. I absolutely adore her.

I took lifespan development asynchronously and actually enjoyed it. I've had Dr. Godly-Reynolds twice before, this being my best experience as she was helpful and kind. Lots of homework assignments, but they're super easy and quick. The 2 exams aren't too bad, as I got a 90 on the first and a 96 on the second. I would take again!

This professor is ridiculous. 197 assignments, no communication, and barely responds to emails. For Exams, the study guides are 7 pages each per chapter; only handwritten or printed is allowed. Midterm/final is are lockdown browser with the camera. She gives busy work, avoids helping, and redirects issues to tech support. Why even be a professor?

Since this was online I didn't have a lot of interaction with her, but when I did she was helpful. Her lectures do seem to just repeat what you read in the book for the most part, but I like that she provides them. Tests are on lockdown browser.
