If you want a class that has different activities and the weeks are not the same, this is not the class for you. Our grades consist of a weekly 50 question quiz, packbacks, and one weekly Pearson chapter.
All MindTap and Canvas quizzes. He does not teach anything at all. It's wild to me to pay so much for a class where there are no lectures, and most comments are from the TA. Avoid all classes by him.

It feels insane that I have to pay money for a class I have to teach myself and the professor has basically no involvement in. No lectures. Just reading assignments, discussion assignments, and a 50 question quiz every single week. Would not recommend unless you want to teach yourself and read a LOT.

Stephen Russell does not give any lecture materials. He provides the textbook, and you have to teach yourself by reading a chapter per week, and then he gives you a 50-question exam that is all application questions. There is no lecture, no PowerPoints, and no notes. You are teaching yourself all the material.

IDK why his rating is so bad. This is my third class with Dr. Russell. Everything is at your own pace. Read the textbook, do the mindtap + pack back and your grade is fine. The only complaint would be the 50 q quizzes, but your two lowest get dropped.

Every week you will have a 50 Q quiz about that weeks chapter which gets annoying but you have all week to do it so its not bad. Clear grading criteria and lots of grades so there is room to make a few mistakes. Overall it is a lot of reading but not hard if you try.

you have to read the textbook from cover to cover if you want an A. there's no teaching from Dr. Russell, if you want a self-directed class (with due dates), this will work for you. a chapter per week with lockdown quizzes. if you are not able to fully learn and teach yourself on your own and start assignments before due date, don't take with him.

This class was really easy, however you barely learn anything. It's an online course, the professor is very disengaged with the class. If you need an easy A take this class, but don't if you want to learn anything. There are weekly Cengage and tests, with PackBacks every 2 weeks. I learned almost nothing in this class, so take that as you will.

This class is really not too bad. Do expect to take a 50 Q quiz due every friday but you can work at your own pace and its not as bad as it sounds. As long as you read before you will be fine. My class is fully online so its not too demanding. I have learned a lot and you have a lot of grades so it provides some cushion if you do bad on one test.

I really liked the info for this class because I thought it was interesting, but if I knew the entire course was going to be reading a textbook and teaching myself, I wouldn't have spent the money to take this class, especially knowing that it goes towards paying him (to do nothing). This will be an easy class if you retain textbook info well

Easy A class but he can be a little picky on assignments. Very few grades and class is not very engaging either. Attendance wasn't required. Would still highly recommend him over other professors though

This class was not engaging and had little to do with psychology, despite being a psych course. I don't reccommend it generally, but it was pretty easy overall. VERY FEW grades, so do well on the tests which are open note! Lectures are boring and not necessarily helpful. Projects are kinda fun.

Best research professor ever! Teaches about the origin & importance of the scientific method of inquiry, which was a breath of fresh air after the mind-numbing experience I had with RM 1. Assignments are fairly easy; open-note weekly quizzes & 3-4 papers throughout the semester. Doesn't take late work so keep up w/ due dates. Highly recommend!!

Took Dr.Reeve for my capstone course. Genuinely one of the nicest professors I've ever had. I firmly believe that one of the most foundational parts of the course is class participation, and that can be difficult when you have a class full of people who aren't chatty. But he always stayed after class and is available for office hours as well.

what an amazing professor. I beg you take his course instead of research methods-- which was a nightmare. Attendance isn't mandatory, few grades but well prepared for them and his lectures are thought provoking and very personable. A true gem for the psychology department and I wish he taught more courses.
Very sweet, I didn't show up for the past few weeks and was completely okay with it. This Professor is awesome to talk to and actually teaches you stuff!

Charlie was an awesome professor! I took his Critical Thinking about Research course and it was a breeze. He's super laid back and understands where students are coming from. No required textbook. He won't accept late work for any reason. Vry few assignments. A quiz every week, a few tests, and 2 writing small assignments. DON'T miss due dates.
I absolutely loved this class and this professor. he is so sweet and passionate about what he is teaching. he does not use traditional methods which is nice. i felt supported.

He is an amazing professor! I took his seminar and he presented materials and perspectives that opened my eyes to the world. This was so important because I am graduating. This is the best professor/best class I have had in my 4 years attending UNCC.
She is a wonderful person, but from an administrative standpoint, it wasn't easy being in her class. She did not prepare us for exams, and her TA did most of the stuff for us.

Really compassionate and understanding. Never ends class early. Very few assignments, but they're worth a lot and she rarely mentions them, so it's easy to miss things. Tests must be scheduled at the testing center, which is annoying. Attendance is optional, but TAs take roll at the start, and you should still check the slides.

Professor Crowe was pretty alright! I don't have any complaints besides just being a little bored in class. I found enjoyment in learning the content, but I stopped going to lectures for a while. Her class isn't very difficult as long as you put in time, and she's very sweet and willing to help and answer questions whenever.
She only gave surface-level information, and it seemed as if she wasn't really knowledgeable about the topics discussed in class.

I didnt think this professor was super knowledgeable on the subject because lectures were a lot of her reading from the book. exams werent bas and you get a note card. 2 assignments dropped and optional final. its an ok class kinda boring.

She is a very kind and chill professor. Class is easy, assignments and tests are easy. Everything you need will be on Canvas, and she's great at emailing people back. You also get good feedback from her and the TA's.

Dr. Crowe-Taylor's class was very enjoyable. She is am incredibly kind and caring woman and it is clear she wants all of her students to succeed. Her assignments are not always the most fun, but they are not crazy hard. She also allows you to bring a notecard to exams.

Chill and easy class, attendance isn't taken and I skipped it fairly often. 1 hw every 2 weeks which are reading questions. 3 exams + cumulative final, but final is optional if you have taken all 3 exams. You can bring an index card with notes to exams (in person, lockdown browser). Exams are MCQS and T/F. Not much need to do the textbook readings.

super fun teacher. had women and genders studies with her. i skipped a lot because it was an 8am but i wish i hadn't because i like her teaching style. I learned a lot and still got a good grade from skipping. would take again

You don't need the textbook, but she claims you do. I never opened it and got an A. I went to class everyday for the attendance grade, but did homework for other classes and put in earphones. For tests, I went through her powerpoints and made flashcards, studied those, and scored well. She lets you bring in a 4x6 notecard cheat sheet each test.

She was a pretty nice professor! There are weekly packback discussions graded, so I encourage doing them all. Three total exams based on the lecture material, so it's a lot of info to know, but you are allowed a cheat sheet notecard. Attendance is mandatory and affects your grade, which is the only annoying part. Be ready to talk in groups!
Overall very easy class just go. 4 exams and you can bring a notecard. Very kind, attendance mandatory. Overall great professor easy class.

Her teaching is scrambled- it's hard to keep up with what she expects us to know. She often says "Oh wait I guess we didn't talk about that" so you are probably missing a lot of info on the exams bc she doesn't keep up with what she has taught each class. Very unprofessional, even made derogatory comments about religion (while in the classroom).

She was a favorite of mine! Her class was very easy weekly assignment, 4 exams (the lowest grade was dropped) and a paper. Since you are graded by so little it is kind of stressful but the class is great to take and you learn a lot.

Sweet lady, horrible professor. Her lectures are not engaging, she often says "wait did we not talk about this?" and her lecturing is very unorganized. Very boring, which makes it difficult to be motivated. Some of the things she teaches about also seem to be biased opinions, which make it an unhealthy learning environment to me.

My class was 2126: Great professor and class, not many grades but she helps you prepare for exams. You get 4 absences and after that your grade is affected but not by too much, just go and listen and participate and its great.

She's very sweet and her exams are based off of her slides. Attendance is not mandatory but if you show up she will boost your final grade at the end of the semester. No final exam, only 3rd regular exam on last few chapters. Easy A class.

You really don't need to go to class to do well, just make sure you complete the weekly assignments and peer reviews on time and read through the ppts before each test.  I stopped showing up part way through the semester bc she's kind of boring and made As on all 3 tests, just use your best judgment. It didn't really feel like I learned anything

This review is for PSYC 2155: Psyc Approaches to Diversity. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you show up she rounds up your grade at the end! Exams are pretty straight forward and are taken in class. Her lecture notes are easy to understand and she makes the class interesting. She is always there to help you out as well! Easy A class.

Super easy A. Weekly discussion boards & response to classmate, 3 exams (not cumulative), short lit. review paper, extra credit opportunities. Lectures/powerpoints hold all the info you'll need. Textbook could be helpful but I just used her pwp's and was fine. Save ur money. TA's were on top of it and helpful. Overall, Professor is sweet!

Dr. Buch and her TA's were amazing this semester! They all gave such great feedback and are so caring. The class itself is very easy and I got an 100% just by completing my assignments with thought. This class is more for us so they are always so willing to help and answer any questions. 10/10 class and professor!

Dr. Kim is SO sweet and really cares about students! She's a wealth of campus resources, building them into the modules. Weekly discussions, no exams, and one final career paper. Don't know what to do with a psych degree? This course clearly defines career paths for you.  If you have a tough course load, take this class to balance it out. Easy A.

Professor Buch cares so much about her students and this course in particular helped me advance my personal career.  She gives so many real world opportunities and her assignments are always relevant to our career.

LOVED Dr.Buch! She is the sweetest professor I have ever had, and she really cares about her students. I recommend taking this class if you are going into psychology because she has a lot of good advice and prepares you very well. This was an easy class, too!

LOVE Dr. Kim. She is a treasure to learn from. Weekly assignments some based on the textbook, your resume, your LinkedIn profile, helpful uses of AI (ChatGPT), graduate school information, elevator pitch, and final career paper. Overall, such an easy but VERY useful course. Such great feedback always!!! Highly recommend you take her!

Dr. Buch is such a sweetheart and really cares about the well-being and success of her students. The course itself (PSYC 3001) was easy and the hw took me about 45 minutes to an hour (maximum) each week.

We had to write a short paper each week reflecting on the weekly chapter. This was a 'career ready' type of psychology course, and I found it gave me a ton of direction for where I want to go in my academic career. There are really no wrong answers in this class, and Dr. Kim is a sweetheart. She cares so much about everyone and you can really tell.

I absolutely loved this class and this professor. One of the most helpful classes I have ever taken. I would recommend that every psych student take this class. I learned a lot of helpful information and got a better understanding of my career path and the possibilities that follow.
Dr. Kim is a delight! This is great if you don't know what you want to do with your psych degree! She grades easy and gives feedback, while giving awesome insight and resources! I loved this class.

Such an amazing professor! Please don't hesitate to sign up for her class. Assignments were graded by TA's, however, she still cared enough to look at them and leave excellent feedback. This class truly helped me to understand what I want to do with my degree because of the assignments and her lectures. Easy A!!!!

Turn in all the assignments and it is impossible to fail this class. I'm not proud but I showed up to only four classes, turned in half the assignments late, and still got an A. She does everything she can to make sure you succeed. She gives 10/10s for all assignments, including the final paper if you turn them in, and takes 1 point per late day.
this is for my transfer psych class. supppperrr nice prof. she has us do a paper each Friday but they are very easy and to the point.

The sweetest professor who just wants you to succeed! I transferred here this semester and this course made me feel prepared for what UNCC has to offer. She is knowledgeable, responsive, so caring and kind.. take her if you can!!

I forgot what class this was but it was a psych class in 2020 online she is so loving and it was the easiest class I've ever taken. She talked about wanting to get approval to take the whole class up to her family's lodge for a weekend with covid going on. never happened but a super fun class I'm having her again this semester so excited!

She was so caring and amazing. She was easily reachable outside of class and had clear grading for every assignment. Attendance was mandatory but very considerate to accommodating for personal situations. 10/10 would recommend.
Weekly assignments that take ~20-30 minutes to do. Attendance is mandatory but it is a pretty chill environment and she truly cares for the students.

Overall good professor, is a grad student so is relatable. Communication is important as well. Lectures can get lengthy at times, but she's passionate. Relatively few grades, almost lost a whole letter grade for forgetting to submit a quiz worth 10 points. Pretty lax grader, as long as you put effort in.
Lectures are a bit hard to follow just because she can be a bit mundane, but overall this is a good class. She's a lenient grader so if you do the work and participate you should do well.
very easy class, light on grading, exams were online, does take attendance everyclass for a grade

I highly recommend taking Professor Bourque she did a great job at teaching this course. Attendance is mandatory and is done as an exit slip at the end of class. The class consisted of writing assignments + textbook readings + exams. She is very understanding as she is a PhD student, and she gives extra credit. I would take her again!

The class itself was boring but the way of teaching was just monotone and not captivating. It was hard to pay attention because all the lectures are reading off a PowerPoint. Wish there were more hands-on or interactive parts to the class. Grading changes based on the day for papers and attendance is mandatory. Quizzes are online, tests in person.

She is a very boring teacher but she is nice, we are constantly going over boring PowerPoints pretty much everyday. This is her first class but she needs to tweak some things such as making it more interactive. It's hard to pay attention to her continuously going over PowerPoints, if there was if there was a more hands on approach I'd be attentive.

The content itself was pretty easy. She assigned weekly quizzes and assignments. She offers online lectures. I found her exams to be very hard to understand. I knew the content, but consistently got Bs and Cs because her questions are confusing. When half the class failed exams, she blamed it on us for not trying enough. She did offer a lot of EC.

This was a fully online class, but you had to go to campus at scheduled times for exams. Not a fan of that. Professor Lori is SO nice though and genuinely cares about her students. Her grading is very clear and fair, and she's always happy to help. Highly recommend.

The class was ok to me. Normally I am a straight A student and I will be barely scraping by with a B. I used flashcards and learned that way by memerizing pretty much. Shes a nice teacher I reached out a few times and she responded quickly. I think the material itself is whats difficult but its extremely test heavy and 3 other assignments a week.

Dr. Wallendael taught a class of 300 and managed it very well. We met once a week so every class covered something different and Dr. Wallendael always had something engaging/ interactive. You have to read especially if it's your first psychology class. The class is test heavy and the tests are challenging so set aside time to study. Recommend.

I didn't have any grievances with her, but that's mostly because this course was entirely self-taught for me. You MUST read every page of every chapter of the textbook while taking notes and making flashcards if you want to get an A. Those who do not are the ones who fail. Truly.

I had a huge lecture hall and she was so boring. The assignments were easy during the week and not too heavy, but the exams were HORRIBLE, I never got over a 64 and my friends all faield them too. They are not anything like the homework or textbooks were assigned. I am so glad I am not a psych major.
she doesn't care about you, she won't help you in any kind of way, she would NOT forgive anything or be understanding of any situation and her exams are NEVERRRR like her hw or notes :)

By far one of the strictest professors I have ever had. Lowest exam, Inquizitive and Workbook grades are dropped which is nice, but she has no empathy for her students whatsoever. I don't recommend if you don't have good time management. Tests are extremely tricky, I studied for our final for three weeks and only received a 64. Not recommended.

It was a pretty easy class if you read the on line textbook and studied a little. Attendance was mandatory but I did not pay attention or learn during class. I mostly learned by reading the textbook and taking notes outside of class b\y myself.

Good professor, but incredibly hard. You have to read, or else you will fail. Exams are 50 questions long, have to be taken in the testing center, and are worth half your grade—very heavily weighted. You could do poorly on homework, ace the exams, and pass with a B. Very fast-paced class with too much information at once. She gives good feedback.

Anybody who says that her class is hard is not telling the truth. If you read the textbook and do the assignments, it's the easiest A. Since it is an asynchronous class, you have to do things at your own pace, which is probably why people rate her so low because they don't properly manage their time correctly. This class is NOT horribly difficult!
PSYC2101 with Professor Lori is no easy A, but dedication pays off. Quizlet and unstuck AI were lifesavers for test prep - don't rely too much on the textbook alone.
NO!NO!NO! difficult tests.
Quite literally, so unhelpful, so unkind, and terribly difficult exams.
Hard exams, passive-aggressive, mean.

Dr. Wallendael seems thoroughly uninterested in helping her students learn or complete her unnecessarily tedious workload. She is not only a difficult grader, but her multiple-choice test questions are also vaguely worded trick questions. This class is solely taught through a textbook, be sure to read!

Dr. Lori's class isn't a easy, but it's manageable with effort. Dedication is key!! Watching lecture notes helped more than the book,making Quizlet for each of the weekly quizes helps with test,and having a class GC helped. Assignments due early in the week. Tests have around 50 questions, one open-ended. Don't use AI,chegg etc.she will know!

For the PSYC 4103 capstone, Dr. Wallendael is the best instructor! Although this class was a little difficult, she does a good job of outlining the key ideas for each topic. If someone wants to take Research Methods, History, & Systems of Psychology (capstone), I would suggest having her as their instructor. She's very sweet and caring.

I thought the class was pretty easy. As long as you read the chapter and study the concepts, you should be ok. As far as the cheating allegations, I think as long as you do not use outside sources or even Grammarly, you should be fine. This is not a class you can just get by without putting in the work, and if you need help, she is willing to help!
She was alright, not the best. I only passed this class because of

Overall the class was fine. Only reason I didn't give her a 5 is because of her overly strict attendance policy that I felt was unnecessary. Her class is relatively easy to get an A in so long as you keep up with the assignments. The only ones that can be a bit tough are the tests where sometimes the questions are phrased in very confusing ways.

Professor Wallendael makes this course more difficult than it should be for an entry level Psych class. I frequently spent more time studying for these exams than for the exams within my major classes. Most of the exam averages in this course are lows D's of high F's. The questions are vague and need to be expanded upon. Kind but misguided prof

Inquizitive is a terrible resource; requires you to read a lot for a single question and can be very time consuming. More students received an F on each test over As, Bs, Cs, and Ds. TAs graded workbooks very tough at the beginning of the sem, but provide good feedback. Professor is accessible. This class is certainly for those fully dedicated.

Dr. Wallendael would probably be the best teacher for PSYC research methods. She makes the class a lot easier to understand and will help you the best she can in order to succeed in the course. I would recommend having her as a teacher again

Provided several examples and clear explanations for topics in class. Dr. Zendels challenged us and encouraged us to practice research skills because, after all, we are college students in a 3000-level class and should be expected to be challenged! Sadly, he is no longer a professor at Charlotte anymore, I would have taken a class with him again.

Dr. Zendels was nice and had a younger, fresh outlook on the class. I did much better in this class than PSYC 1101. The lecture was super long compared to other classes, but not too bad. I liked the activities he arranged. There are several extra credit opportunities, so TAKE THEM. Quizzes are easy once you get the hang of it, pay attention.

I really liked Dr. Zendels. Though his class is boring, he is a cool guy. He doesn't give a lot of assignments and gives extra credit often. He also provides clear and good feedback on assignments. He tries to make the class interesting sometimes, so I would take him!
Philip is an okay professor. He is a grad student. His class is not super engaging and it lacks some level of fun. Its lecture heavy. Overall though not a hard class.

Phillip is easy to follow and makes Psychology easy to understand. He often cuts through a lot of the psychology attitude/mumbo-jumbo and tells things as they are. I highly recommend taking him alongside PSYC 1101.

You don't need to remember anything from AP Psych to succeed since he'll teach it again. Discussion boards every other week, a quiz every week, rarely any extra assignments. You write a final paper and do a final presentation. Tip: Take notes before class and then add what he says about it in class and you'll do great. Nice guy and I recommend him.
Best online class! You have to do the reading and assignments but grading is very fair! Easy A

Professor Murphy was very nice, but I wouldn't recommend taking this course online. Her instructions for certain assignments weren't very clear, so sometimes it was hard to complete them. There were also lots of assignments due all at once, so a majority of my submissions were late. She does give full credit for late work until a certain extent!

I took this class over the summer and I will say that it is not that hard of a class. If you take this professor, be ready to read and catch on fast.  Now when it comes to email communication I had a hard time getting in contact with her.  So I will say that if you are reliant on emailing your professors for help, this is not the right professor!

Dr. West provided recorded lectures that reviewed what was in the textbook. A majority of the learning is based on reading but I did learn a lot from this class. The only grades were tests and chapter quizzes.

Dr. West does not know how to communicate with her students. Many of us sent her multiple emails and did not get a response for months, only when we brought attention to it in our class groupme. She is not on top of things, she sometimes posts assignments the day they are due, even when the syllabus says when it is supposed to be available.

She's a good professor who obviously cares but her course lacks structure. Theres often no feedback on assignments, no clear grading criteria or lectures at all. The lecture part was nice, we would often just talk of real world issues in the class which was refreshing but it's juts stressful not having grades in until the end of the semester.

Mary is a great professor. She tailors her courses in a way that promotes real learning and understanding as well as a school-life balance. I've had her for two classes now, and she never gives her students more than they can handle. She's also very quick to respond to emails. She's kind of a slow grader, but she cares deeply about what she does.

there are a ton of assignments in this class, 5 exams and two final projects towards the end. Super sweet teacher but you just need to make sure you pay attention in her class you have to be dedicated in this course to learn everything! I would take her again

Dr. McKenzie is a passionate professor who fosters engaging class discussions. While grading can be slow, the class is manageable with active participation. unstuck study was a helpful study tool alongside the readings.

Really good professor teaching an interesting subject she is obviously passionate about. Class periods were all about free discussion of topics both presented in the material covered that week and in the news that related to it. The only drag was that grading was pretty slow for the big project we did all semester.
Good professor, only bad thing is she uses the lockdown browser.

Hybrid course. Dr. McKenzie is clearly passionate about her work but spends most of the lecture talking about her own experiences and beliefs, most of which rarely touch the topics in the textbook. Doesn't take attendance and you basically teach yourself at home. HUGE writing assignments and classwork assignments (which you can also do on your own)

He is a good teacher that really cares about what he does. He is super down to earth and genuinly a good person. His class is very reading heavy, but the books are on real life issues that are very informative and not a pain to read.

I participated in Prof Fitzgerald's study abroad program. He gives students space to contextualize and research ideas. He provides insight and feedback when needed to help guide students toward a clearer understanding. He is a wonderful and challenging professor

very harsh and subjective grader, which can be tough since his attendance assignments are a 5-minute time to handwrite an in-depth response to a basic and simple question from 7-9 chapters of a book, and half his tests are free-response. tests include sporadic content from videos to books to lectures. use his  extra credit to your advantage!

Pay attention in class, show up. The tests are based on the lectures and this makes it easier to succeed. This is a very lecture heavy class, sometimes he can get confusing but will reword if you ask him too. There was also many opportunities for extra credit! Very reading heavy class as well, pop quizzes on the readings as well. Make sure you read

I genuinely did not like this class at all. The exams barely covered the lectures and you had to study very hard and study extra material. You had to find everything through modules and I wish he put an assignment tabs. The amount of work you had to put into the assignments were definitely worth more than 5 points. Did not like this class at all.

Loved this class! I learned a lot through the lectures, discussions, and reading materials. Professor Fitzgerald explained the material perfectly and was very flexible when asked to change something, even if it was projects, reading, discussions, etc. The TAs were extremely nice as well. Very clear grading criteria. Get ready to read.

While Dr. Fitzgerald is very smart and passionate, he is a researcher, not a professor. He assigns an unreasonable amount of reading that are overall unneeded for what we are doing in class. He also believes that everyone in his class will be getting a graduate degree in sociology and that's the only valid path post undergrad, which is unhelpful.

Great professor, always made sure to keep the class engaged and was very open to just about any feedback. Might be a little difficult to get used to the readings, but I personally found them to be really interesting.

Professor Fitzgerald is a great professor. He is so understanding but does have pop quizzes on the reading. The test are fairly easy if you understand the material. He gives good lectures but sometimes he rambles on so it can get a bit confusing

Dr. Fitzgerald is overall a good professor. Three books are given throughout the semester and pop quizzes follow every reading. His lectures can be confusing and he does get slightly flustered with some questions. He gives several extra credit opportunities throughout the semester and is open to feedback. Put in a little effort and you will be fine

Very caring, really loved him as a person. Clear and fair grading, and also very open to feedback and criticism. Lots of reading, 3 books over the semester, but I enjoyed them for the most part. Sometimes, his lectures can get overwhelming; he tends to be a bit erratic when covering multiple topics. Overall easy A if you do the work and readings.

Dr. Fitzgerald has an inflated ego and assigns so much reading for no reason, and the books he assigns aren't engaging and are hard to follow. He's very intelligent, but he's hard to keep up with in lectures because he touches on five different topics in one minute. Do not take this class if you don't absolutely love sociology, you will hate it.
You'll do good if you do the reading. Love his teaching and would take another class with him!!

I like Dr. Fitzgerald as a person, but didn't care for his class too much. Ethics was not interesting to me, so it was hard to pay attention in class, especially since his lectures were very talkative. I would only take his class if it were a class that I was very interested in and passionate about.

I loved prof Fitz. He made class fun & really directed the course for his students. He'll change things if they don't work for his class. No textbooks, but required regular books (like $10 each, we had 3) I would recommend him and 2211 to everyone I know because he's the embodiment of what a great teacher looks like. Really cares about his students

Dr. Fitzgerald is one of the best professors I've ever had. As long as you complete the assignments on time, you'll have no problem getting a good grade in his class. He is also very open to meeting outside of class and provides meaningful feedback when it comes to essays and writing assignments!

Dr. Stearns was great- the class had clear grading, easy to make an A; only reason I've left off a single star is the TA. When I took 1511, the TA accused students of AI use on a few assignments after claiming to have left the country for good, evading backlash and throwing the situation on the new TA. Would take again.

Stearns was great. The class was light. Attendance/participation made up most grades other than the final group project. Lectures were interesting if you actually care about the subject. Just show up to class, participate, do the readings and you'll be good.
She's excellent, fav professor of the semester. Her class was an easy A and she just yaps but shes really funny.

I personally felt like the class was all over the place. There was NO proper structure whatsoever & she spoke in circles, often contradicting herself. It wasn't bad overall but I just didn't fancy her as a professor and HATED the group work we had to do (groups were assigned randomly). I constantly asked myself: "What even is this class?"
Very manageable class… easy grader

Dr. Stearns is also an enjoyable person to talk to and learn from! This class is easy and revolves around a semester long project in which you will present at the end of the sem. My advice is to show up to class (she does allow up to 5 absences), do the assigned reading, and make sure all of your work is turned in on time. I would take her again!
Easy class to get an A in. Show up and do the reading. Only tests were on Fridays, and related to the readings.

Great professor! I have never taken a sociology course but she made it very interesting. Not many assignments so if you show up and complete the work you should pass with an easy A. Friday group sessions are extremely easy too.

Dr. Stearns was a very nice and understanding professor. All she asked was to come to class and complete what little work was assigned. You have 4 free skips in this class. The main assignment was a group project that she gives 5 weeks to complete. Easy class if you are needing a themes course.
I can't imagine anyone having a problem with Dr. Stearns. She was clear about her policies, and it's impossible not to get an A if you attend class—possibly the easiest class I'll take here.
This professor is very nice and her class is overall easy. There are very few assignments throughout the semester and one group project at the end rather than a final.

Great class, lots of group projects so prepare, but you are able to give feedback on members. There is alot of room for creativity in projects as well as learning curves. the first project was graded leniently and the second harder as we have learned more. Tests are not bad but READ the BOOK.

Would have us doing group presentations but used our technical difficulties against us since we are timed. Mind you, he already had access, it was his computer acting up. Cares about his students. He moves very quickly through content, but he is receptive to feedback so make sure you vocalize any concerns you may have. Mandatory group projects.

Lecture heavy, and he's fast. Can be hard to get info he says that isn't on the slide. He doesn't tell you when there will be in class assignments, even tho attendance isn't taken. Gives tests solely based on his study guides, so just do those and you'll be fine. SOCY 1511

Professor Overton did a great job. He's a fast lecturer but does a great job contextualizing the material. Tests are huge in the class but he provides relevant study materials and goes over the material in the week leading up to the test. He does a great job making the course valuable but "easy".

One of the best professors I have ever had! His assignments are very easy and all he really cares about is participation and attendance. He was a great professor. Very laidback and easy to talk to. Don't talk over him during class. Group activities and projects were fun and actually taught me something.
The workload's no easy-A. But the guy offers pretty reasonabl ways to recover your grade. Classes are fairly interactive. I always found him eager to offer help. Friendly and approachable too.

At first, we had a few pop quizzes on the chapters at the beginning, but eventually, we just stopped doing them. Love her. You can tell she truly loves teaching and Socy. Lectures can be a little tough to follow but she always asks if everyone understands before moving on. quantitative. She made sure that we understood the material before moving on.  Many teachers move on regardless of whether i get it.  I finally feel like I understand statistics.
She was an amazing teacher and graded fairly. She is understanding if you need help or can not make class. She tries to be very interactive with her students and is well respected.

For quant analysis. The class was very easy. This class was pretty much movies, one big presentation, and small debates. Some homework/project can have unclear instructions which made everyone confused.

Took this class fully online but I could tell Dr. Y cares about her students. Not too many assignments, just quizzes each week based on the readings/videos. super great professor, she's really sweet and responds to emails super fast. There were quizzes, 3 papers and 2 exams in this course but I found it to be super interesting. You do need to pay attention though since you're graded by so little assignment wise. Would 100% take her again

Dr. Yavorsky is very understanding. There is one book you get to choose from a list she has to do your paper on. I suggest getting a head start before classes start if you want to get a head start. There is also readings for each class so read at least two days before going to class.

Dr. Yavorsky has easily been my favorite professor I've taken at Charlotte thusfar. She's incredibly caring and respected, and is very knowledgable and passionate about the subject that she teaches. I absolutely loved this class!! I am a biology student so this was my first time taking a sociology class at uncc and I loved it! Dr. Jason is a very nice woman but is tough. She gives feedback on assignments but doesn't always make it super clear what she wants you to do.

Amazing professor, I have her for 3155 & 4112 and I enjoy her classes so much. She is one of my favorite professors I have had here - the discussions are fun! The hardest part of the course is preparing for pop quizzes and the papers. Kronberg is both a nice and informative professor. She has really good lectures, and explains topics very clearly; she definitely knows the material. Dr. Kronberg is awesome. Passionate about the subject and clearly cares for her students. no. not cool. she's a lazy professor and makes you spend time doing her job outside of class.
The best professor ever! Super nice and if you attend class you will have no problem getting a good grade.

This class is extremely easy. Tests are open note and you can take them at home. Barely any homework. Prof. Langley is very chill and gives good lecture, he does get side tracked a lot though.

Frankly, not a great prof. He very seldom taught us about sociology, and more often spoke about his life experiences and daughters (Who were usually in the classroom). Professor Bossick is a pretty good professor. His lectures are straightforward and so are his tests and quizzes.
honestly overall really liked this class. his slide shows overall made sense and the quizzes match the material

-- Yes, he's tough. But I can definitely say I'm learning a lot!

Amazing teacher, super caring and easy class.
