Such an easy class. Everything is open note which is including reading quizzes, midterm, and the final. Very easy A, the only thing is she was such a mean person who never really taught anything either.

Dr. Miller places an emphasis on interacting/connecting with the text. She has a heavy emphasis on accessibility making the class more comfortable. The textbook can be rented online for less than $30. She is respectful of name pronunciation and chosen pronouns.

While she may not be to everyone's taste because her classes are very lecture heavy, I always personally found the consistency to be nice. There are a few quizzes and tests throughout the semester, but you get multiple attempts for both so it shouldn't be too hard. A lot of information from the tests is in the text book so be sure to read it.
There was a lot of reading in the textbook for this class but she's a very easygoing teacher. All of my assignments were online and I had unlimited attempts to take them.

The class work is the same structure every week so if you like consistency this class is for you. Chapter knowledge quizzes, discussion posts, academic reflections, and reading logs. Apart from the most boring class work I've done the information is pretty interesting.

This is one of the worst educators Ive dealt with EVER. The lack of professionalism and respect for her students is what gets me. Accused me of not using the textbook (w/ no proof) for a quiz that I got a 100% on. Verbally degraded me and picked a literal fight with me. Dropped it 1 week into the course. Waste of time, money and energy. RUN AWAY.

Super chill class, would recommend prof if you have a heavy workload and need a break. Three tests, all v easy and online, three discussion forums, which if you participate in, there's a chance he'll drop your worst test score. Boring lectures sometimes but pay enough attention to slides and you can easily get an A. Barely uses TB tho, don't buy it

Professor was kind and willing to work with me if I had issues with an assignment. Homework consists of discussion responses to a video he posts weekly, but you only have to do 5 over the course of the semester. The 3 tests and semester paper determine the majority of your grade. Lectures were long and boring, but attendance isn't mandatory.

I never used the textbook. He tends to be very boring, he will read off the slides and then go on a tangent. He never took attendance but he includes a lot of things that he said in class on the test and you won't be able to find them on the slides. The only grades are the test. We did discussion posts but they were not graded.
Do not take this professor, if you care about your grades. the exam questions are not based on the actual PowerPoint but based on his opinion. So don't take him

I don't know why so many people rate this professor so poorly. Most of the assignments are opinion-based. As long as you read the textbook, you will be fine for her tests. Her tests are things that are mostly common sense. Keep up with the chapters from week-to-week and you will easily get an A in this class.

Took her asynchronously, she outlined the whole curriculum in the syllabus down to the day, which was very helpful. The weekly assignments weren't too bad as a majority of them were your opinion. My problem came with her tests, which were based on the most specific details in her own textbook, or based on obscure statistics. Overall I'd avoid her.

She is a tough grader but as long as you follow what you are supposed to do, you will be fine. Her lectures were not very engaging but they are straight forward. I would recommend her if you plan on doing the work.

This teacher is very strict and assigns insane amounts of work for a general ed class. She assigns a lot of readings for quizzes that make no sense. Attendance is mandatory, and you can not be late. She won't let you even go to the bathroom during class and makes you keep your phone and computer in your backpack. Do not take her unless you must.
do not take any of her classes, such a harsh grader, lectures make zero sense and very participation heavy with speaking in front of the class. also doesn't grade until end of semester

There were extensive reading assignments each week, sometimes an entire text of 40 pages but no less than 15. While I didn't mind the reading itself, the assessments felt mismatched. The tests were only three questions, and in some cases, they honed in on small details that you could miss unless you thoroughly understood the reading.

Dr. Flint gives different readings every week that are ~9 pages long and they are very boring. There are some pop quizzes every now and then, so it's better if you show up to class. There is also group work and study groups that meet on certain days. Overall, it's harder to fail than it is to pass, but I personally strongly disliked the class.

Not a very good teacher, her lectures were boring and confusing, if you miss one reading you are screwed. Readings are super lengthy and boring, her quizzes were confusing and if you didnt read the reading intensely the questions wont make sense

More difficult and time-consuming than my regular classes. Boring lectures and 40+ page readings given every week with occasional random quizzes that were difficult to do well on. Slides were never uploaded to Canvas despite grading us on our class notes. Weekly breakout sessions on Fridays that didn't help much. Wouldn't recommend to anyone ever.

The class was quite boring and the professor taught mainly from PowerPoints that were not uploaded to Canvas. She requires her students to take in-class notes in groups which are then later graded. LOTS of outside reading and pop quizzes this professor also uses packback weekly. I would not recommend it but it's not overly hard.

Overall I learned some really interesting things in this class HOWEVER, this is extremely heavy on readings (20-40 pages) for 5 question pop quizzes. She also doesn't believe in making incorrect answer choices so all the choices could be right but only one is actually right, these were my down fall. Weekly breakout sessions.

I had to take this as a freshman intro class, and it was my hardest class. The readings are extremely time-consuming and can be up to 5 each week. The lectures are just talking through slides, and you are graded on notes. Unless this class is related to your major, I do not recommend taking it.

Frankly insane class for a freshman to he expected to take. Flint is a nice person outside of class but her lessons are absolutely brutal. Long boring lectures that somehow still give you no time to write notes in time and 40 page readings for homework with random pop quizzes sprinkled in. There's a reason she's been getting 1 stars for 20 years!!!
In general is passive aggressive about absences, confusing phrasing for a lot of the work. On your own learning style But can gain some stuff from her experience.

There are long readings for every week, which will occasionally have pop quizzes on. Pop quizzes are difficult to get a good grade on even if you do the readings. There are graded notebook checks, checking for all lectures and readings. Tough grader and will change the instructions for assignments multiple times after they've already been assigned.

Overall, I enjoyed having Dr. Flint. She is very reading-heavy, you have to take thorough notes because she grades note-taking and even has notebook checks. She does drop reading pop quizzes that can impact your grade but as long as you have a general idea about what you read you should be good. She is accessible and helps you when needed.

She maybe a very nice person in real life but she is a very difficult professor to work with. She gave out excessive readings, time limited quizzes, and don't get me started on the projects and how nit picky she is about them. This class was supposed to help you get warmed up to college but instead this course only made it harder for us freshman.

Avoid. Dr. Flint is nice, but she's an awful professor. I took her 1502 elective class and the workload was excessive with several 30+ page readings weekly along with pop quizzes and lengthy writing assignments. The lecture slides are wordy and she moves too quickly. She nitpicks your assignments and the grading system she uses makes no sense.

DO NOT TAKE. This class involves lengthy reading of 45+ page PDF's every week for in class pop quizzes. The teacher takes offense to when no one cares for the boring topics that she rambles about. The lectures are sporadic and random just like the grading scale. Reading quizzes were graded heavier than essays. Grading is harsh and she says IDEARS.

I took this prof for HIST1502, this course was meant to be an introductory elective for freshmen, and is meant to be simple in of itself. Professor Flint has created every single method possible to ensure failure in her class. This week alone we had 60+ pages of reading for a short notice quiz, and she grades extremely harsh on papers & activities

Dr.Flint was the absolute worst professor. She knew nothing about the material she was teaching. Her grading is ridiculous, all of her grading was insanely nitpicking, she does not give 100s. Her lectures and readings were so out of touch and elitist. The work load was not insane but the assignment had very odd and not specific rubrics.

Stay away. She gives an insane amount of work for an ELECTIVE class and lectures meaninglessly. She calls out random students who aren't paying full attention and gets offended when no one is as interested in the boring subject matter as she is. Nothing she talks about or assigns makes sense and there's no reason I need to read 149 pages weekly.

Beware!! Do not sign up for any class that has her as a professor. Lectures make no sense, she jumps all over the place and talks about random stuff not even relating to class. Grading is insanely harsh and she does not do extra credit and is not empathetic whatsoever.

One of the worst professors I have had this semester. Her lectures are extremely boring and the homework is beyond extensive. There are very unnecessary assignments and probably the longest readings I have ever done in my life. Please do not take this class even if you think you are "passionate" about the subject. WORST PROFESSOR EVER.

Dr. Dupre is a very kind professor; he is approachable and is willing to explain things from the lecture. Lectures are not the most interesting, but he does make an effort for students to participate. The assignments in this class are all writing, and he is a tough grader. If you are like me and aren't the best at writing, good luck in this course.

His class was honestly pretty easy. There is a lot of reading, but that's expected in a history course. Make sure you pay attention and take good notes because the only assignments are exams, but they're relatively easy.

Dr. Dupre is super respectful and always willing to help his students when they are stuck and confused about something. He does require a bit of writing but it should not be an issue if you get it done on time. Other than that, he's a good professor.

Professor Dupre was very nice and knowledgeable. He only teaches through lectures and class discussions, so taking notes and participating will help you do good. Grades on 6 pop quizzes that he bases off readings he gives you, 3 exams, and a final paper. Attendance is required but overall great class and great professor.

Dr. Dupre gave me hope in history again after having a terrible and harsh professor the semester before. He's extremely smart, he's super friendly, and makes an effort to get to know his students. He's easy to talk to and never makes you feel embarrassed for asking even the most simple questions in meetings with him. Attendance is key though!

Professor Dupre was one of my favorites! Great lectures, make sure to take lots of notes. Pop quizzes are usually on documents that he assigned to read before. He let us bring a flashcard with notes for the exams, which was really helpful. Be ready to write papers and read long documents. Overall, great professor and course.
He was hard to pay attention to, very boring. almost everyone I know had a d.

Dr. Dupre is a good professor, and I enjoyed this class. He is a tough grader but is very clear with his feedback and offers a lot of office hours and opportunities to get help. I also appreciated his meetings throughout the semester to make sure nobody fell behind. A difficult grader but a great professor and a nice person.

This is the first time I have written one of these for a professor. And I highly recommend him for HIST-4000. He gives clear and concise feedback. He will also work with you in order for you to pass or succeed in your field of study. Just communicate with him, because he will communicate with you :)

Don't do it. Takes participation seriously, understanding the readings are important, in-class pop quizzes are considered "quick and short (lies)." Definitely contradicts himself when grading. Says he wants a short essay that is straight to the point (of course) but you get your paper back and says you don't have enough information?? Yeah, no.
super critical, dont take his class

The class is lecture heavy, these lectures are kinda boring and it feels like youre shamed for not alreading knowing historical topics weve never learned. Class participation is really big. Weekly readings that he will assign sometimes at 5pm and its due the next day at 10am. Essay tests that are graded more citical then most english teachers.

Commuters with busy schedules do not take his in-person classes. Dr. Ferdinando requires you to schedule in-person meetings with TAs before every test and group project, and attendance is mandatory for a grade. These meetings are outside class hours, and I had to miss work to attend—super inconsiderate of students' schedules.

Does not provide good feedback keeps telling us to refer to the information without specifying what is wrong with the writing. A lot of reading initially. Does not post lecture slides on canvas. You will be in a group. He maybe needs to be more socially aware.  Although the final project is only two paragraphs.
All tests are in person essays, never left his class without multiple wrist cramps.

Dr. Ferdinando is the worst grader I've ever had, this is probably the first History class ever that I've received a grade lower than A-. Get ready to read your textbook, because whatever you don't include in your quizzes or essays that isn't properly cited in your textbook will deducted an entire letter grade. Nothing is perfect to him.

Dr. Ferdinando is AMAZING!! By far one of my favorite professors. He gives excellent constructive criticism and genuinely wants his students to succeed and know the content. He released exam questions beforehand, and allowed you to bring a note sheet. If you can take him, DO!! HIST1160 (I took it in Fall '24) was my 1st of 3 classes taken with him.

I had 1512 course! He was very knowledgeable and during his lectures you need to take notes & PAY ATTENTION otherwise the exams and Term IDs will be hard to do.Very accessible out of class & has the drop policy.He will know if you use AI- and doc off loads of points. Show up, take notes, & participant in discussions for extra points! Good luck

Kind and humble professor who's willing to help. All exam topics and essay prompts were given in advance, and note sheets were allowed. Minimal homework. You must do the readings to prep for discussions, but grading was unfair—based on if he picked you to speak. Lectures were dull, and exams graded strictly.

He is a very unfair grader, I have always tried hard in school but he refused to give 100s even if it was deserved. I attended every class and he still managed to add negative help to my papers. I spent at least 4 hours creating a paper and 5 hours fixing it and still managed a 70. Not to mention HE GRADED A DRAFT PAPER AS 10% OF OUR FINAL GRADE!

If you follow all the criteria on assignments and it's clear you put effort into your work, you are sure to get a good grade. No tests taken in this class, only online quizzes with 3-4 written response questions. You write an essay as your final. If you have good attendance he'll curve your final grade (he bumped my grade up from a B to an A).
Lots of lecture readings, homework but easy grader and easy class if u do read

Tough grader in the sense that he looks for very specific things, he tells you what they are you just have to figure out how to answer them. He gives good feedback on just about every graded assignment, he'll tell you what you did right or wrong, so it's easy to improve if you pay attention. I probably wouldn't take him for an elective.

Dr. F is a great professor but if you are looking for an easy class, this is NOT the class for you. Each week you will be expected to read 40-70 pages of the assigned textbook. Dr. F is also very specific on grading, you will get paragraphs worth of feedback and tough grades. Lastly, be ready to buy Microsoft Word and PowerPoint for this class. GL!

Dr. Ferdinando does a good job of making this class relate to non-history majors. He understands that not everyone cares about historical stuff, so he makes an effort to constantly connect this class to other stuff that's important to future non-history careers. He is a tough grader, but he is approachable for help if you need it.

Dr. Ferdinando is very knowledgeable about what he teaches and he tries to keep everything engaging. I enjoyed this class, but he is a tough grader so be prepared. He drops the lowest assignments and is accessible outside of class.
Lots of reading and extensive discussion. Lots of feedback to see improvement but is a tough grader

Dr. Ferdinando is obviously very well-educated and he cares deeply about his subject. That being said, he is an extremely critical grader and there is a lot of outside work to be done to be able to keep up with the class. Certainly helps students get prepared for further academia, but for my sake I hope I never have to take a similar class again.
Nothing is ever good enough for this man.

Dr. Ferdinando is a top professor if you're looking for a good 2600/3600 professor. He does an excellent job teaching the methodology skills needed for the final paper and is always available for questions after class or in office hours if you don't understand. He also gives good feedback on papers through comments and clarifies them at meetings.

Dr. Ferdinando is really helpful when it comes to writing. He has a clear rubric for every assignment and gives really helpful feedback for writing assignments. His class is really boring though, & attendance matters. Make sure not to procrastinate on the hard writing assignments. But I would not suggest taking him unless you really have to.

Dr. Ferdinando was a fantastic professor for HIST 2600. Despite the class itself being pretty daunting, he makes everything clear at the start of the semester, he's easy to work with, very approachable, and is a great storyteller, his lectures always had me invested. I loved Dr. Ferdinando and would take a class of his again.

Dr Cameron was great this semester! His lectures were pretty engaging to me, and the five-question comprehension quizzes afterwards were extremely simple. Weekly DBs, but they weren't difficult at all. The midterm and final are oral exams, but attending the review sessions and taking notes on the lecture will definitely prepare you!

This was an asynchronous class and a normal week would look like two quizzes due at 5pm on Mon/Wed then a discussion post due Fri. Lectures can be long and you have to actually pay attention and take notes since the quizzes are based off of them. My least favorite part about this class was the oral exam for mid term and final.

I was a senior in college, working on 2 publications, 2 jobs, and 18 credit hours. Cameron showed no sympathy and instead lectured me on time management after giving none for assignments submitted 1 hour after the due time at 5 PM. Very disrespectful in his response, and genuinely surprised that he is allowed to serve as a department chair.

Professor Cameron is a very chill, laid back professor with extensive knowledge in his field. I found his lectures interesting, and was impressed that he seems to be able to remember historical details with great accuracy, just off the dome. Almost all grades will be quizzes and tests, so make sure to read the textbook and attend class lectures.
Dr. Cameron could teach every single class in the History department and I'd eat them up.

This class is LONG. There are a series of readings you must complete, usually a 200ish-page book every week, followed by an in-class quiz to make sure you did the readings. I recommend doing the readings. There is also a final paper, but it is only 12 pages that you start working on in the middle of the semester. I would try taking another section.

Gives reading quizzes about once a week on a chapter reading. Usually about 30 pages so start EARLY! The quizzes are very say though, just do the reading and you will be fine. Besides that, just lectures and a midterm and final. Lectures are great, he is a very nice and easy-going professor. He cares too, will let students retake always. TAKE HIM!

He was a great professor and made the class very interesting. The class consisted mostly of quizzes, long readings, and the midterm. He is very nice, will answer your questions, and would frequently cancel class. Overall, he is a great professor, and it's an interesting class!
Easy going class. Quizzes every day but if you read the chapter it was super easy. It was an 8 week class so everything went fast but just stay on top of it and you'll pass.

Overall just a great professor. She really prioritizes learning instead of worrying about grades. She doesn't give you tests as well, just a few routine assignments and readings. Also, a very interesting class, probably one of the ones I've learned the most in. Highly recommend!

I loved her. Her teaching style was amazing and very interactive. I feel she is very passionate about her subject and even could make someone who is not and never has been a history buff enjoy it completely. She even pardoned the third test. No one I ever knew did that. She was always my best professor. Life-changing exp. Take her always! The GOAT!

Dr. Frat loves what she teaches and it shows in lectures. I only took this course for the graduation requirement but she made it bearable. Mostly busy work but very easy to pass. I do honestly feel like for an American Democracy course we spent half of it in the Middle East lol. You don't NEED the course reader, just borrow from a classmate
10/10 would take a class of hers again

very good class, she worked hard to make it a discussion class, even with about 50 students.  Learned everyone's name.   A fair amount of reading,  many times class time was small group discussion that was then summarized for whole class

Wonderful professor! I added this course last minute and I'm grateful that I did. Prof. Frat is an incredible lecturer and makes difficult topics much easier to understand. She calls on people a lot but she never makes you feel stupid and you are allowed to pass if you're too shy.

Dr. Frat is a stellar professor and person, and I'm sad the class is over! Her lectures were always interesting and engaging, and she treated sensitive material with lots of care. You can tell she loves and takes her job seriously. She is a very generous and understanding professor & I hope to take another class from her in the future.

Favorite professor at UNCC. I've taken all her courses. Down to Earth, funny, caring, and gives good feedback. Explains what she wants well and helps you to achieve what she expects. W Professor. If she is available as a History Maj Class (3600,4000,4600) get her you won't be disappointed. Took 3600 and 4003 with her, true shame I couldn't do 4600.
She's awesome. She's really interested in what she teaches and wants to teach you about it.

Very nice person and a caring professor. She is very helpful in feedback and accessible outside of class. She is a very difficult grader though. You really need all of your stuff in strict Chicago style otherwise she WILL catch it. Aside from that her class was interesting. Towards the end, it began to drag though.

As a professor, she is very caring, helpful and genuienly nice. Understands that some students have other stuff going on so she extends deadline and such. Her lectures were boring though and the content wasn't interesting for me. I don't recommend it if you're not into Middle eastern history like me. Took it only because I had to.

I took LBST 2301. Textbooks were referenced but I never needed to use mine. Great teacher with a fun personality who genuinely cares about improving your skills and knowledge. She does like to take up the whole class time but if you go to class and apply her advice to your writing, you will earn a good grade with very little issues.
chill professor will work with you but course load hevaing and boring lectures
Just show up and do the work and you will end with an A

Didn't show up for 1st 2 weeks of class. Only gives 5 grades total. Did not update grades the entire semester. Whole class was him blabbing about Roman Sewers in Jerusalem and trying to recruit students as laborers for his digs, which I heard is not a great experience. Got the vibe he kinda only teaches because he has to the fund his digs. L Class

He can barely finish a sentence unless he reads directly from his presentation. He won't provide any grades on Canvas, he briefly gives feedback at midterm. He doesn't allow email communication, instead, we have to write a canvas notification directly to him, and he rarely responds. He constantly cuts students off because they're "not loud enough."

Professor Gibson is a pretty good dude overall, but, he has some issues regarding him and the way he structures his course. Very little classwork overall but there is a 20-page final worth 50% of your grade

CONS: Worst Canvas user I've ever seen, only grade feedback is at the midterm and final, kinda boring lecture, takes attendance, + pop quizzes

This class was interesting and he is knowledgeable about the subject but he never gives feedback or returns grades on any assignments. You turn in papers and do not know if you are doing them right until he messages you about your midterm and final grades for the class. A 20 page paper for a 3000 level course is also ridiculous.

SO BORING! The class is just him rambling and telling you that he can't post the notes due to copyright issues so good luck catching up, also beware of pop quizzes. He says the textbook isn't required but then has textbook questions in the pop quiz. He never post work and when he does the instructions are vague and emails are even more vague.

Insanely repetitive and boring - you will spend five classes listening to him go over instructions over the final presentation and group project. He could have avoided all that if he sent out one rubric, but instead he'll just ramble about for 6 classes. Be prepared to be taught as if you were in the fifth grade - very frustrating.

Professor Dennison makes lecture very interesting and likes to engage with the class, but does not force anyone to participate. He seems very caring and all lectures align well with what is on tests. Weekly work is quick and easy. Just do the work, come to class and passing is very easy. I would recommend this course to others.
Amazing professor! I genuinely enjoyed taking his class, as long as you're present, do the readings and assignments, and engage he's absolutely amazing! 100% would take again!
Makes the history lecture interesting and he makes it great. He's great and sometimes makes jokes. I would recommend.

Dr. Lockton is an AMAZING prof! He makes the lectures interesting! Group and individual assignments  are majority of the class. Midterm and final are hand written and are easy if you pay attention in class. I am not a WGST nor HIST major, took this class as an extra and LOVED it! HIGHLY recommend! Dr. Lockton is a really understand and nice prof!
Bro is so awesome there's virtually no homework outside of a few written responses throughout the semester and the in-class essay exams are super easy. Would happily take again
He gave out a whole letter grade worth of extra credit, he is the goat but study hard for the tests as they were pretty difficult compared to what he was teaching us.

Class is mostly just lectures; it's very laid back though. You have no homework, and attendance is taken, but just show up on days when you do group projects, since there really aren't that many assignments so the few that there are weigh a lot. They're not difficult at all though. Overall, a pretty good class.

Lockton is very knowledgeable and passionate about history- his lectures are amazing. He will lecture for ~30 minutes and you have small group discussions for ~20 minutes. He assigns readings outside of class, but you can get away with not doing them. A good chunk of your grade is doing group assignments in class, so make friends early in the class

He's in the perfect field! Man will TALK about the subject/s with passion. His lectures are funny and honestly his Midterms were not bad at all. As long as you put in some solid notes (like actually paying attention) and look over them, you'll pass! Most Important Thing to Remember: High Anxiety, Low Capability. All of his teachings will revolve it

Professor Lockton is a decent professor. His tests are complicated. All on paper and he has answer choices like "All of the above" or "B and C" so basically all of the above minus one. I didn't like it because it made the tests even more confusing then they already were. Wouldn't take again and wouldn't recommend. Very disappointing class.

Great professor great class, things were graded pretty late because of his workload but the class was enjoyable. attendance wasn't counted but assignments were done in class only, easy class, and would take him again. Make sure you show up on the days there is group/ individual work or you'll miss all the assignments

An easy A, but he takes FOREVER to grade, so beware of that! His tests and assignments are straight from the lecture and powerpoint if you pay attention because it is easy to fall behind since there aren't many assignments and you are expected to retain information for the assignments and test given.

Interesting class at some points, but the lectures were extremely dull most of the time. He will require group discussions on the questions he just answered, which was counterproductive. Group assignments make up most of your grade. He offered extra credit for the final exam. It's an alright class, but it could be much better.

The class could be interesting since it talks about witchcraft, astrology, and magic. But Prof Lockton has a really boring and repetitive presentation style. The coursework is easy and nonexistent. But it's a game of paying attention cause the class is boring. Group projects determine a significant amount of course grade. Good easy class though.

He will work with you and what you have going on. He is very direct with what he wants in essays, assignment and projects. He is engaging during class and does his best to ensure participation and is easy to ask questions and is open to them. I would easily take him again if i were to retake the class

Took this course as an elective & I'm glad I did because Dr. Lockton is a treasure! Course content is intriguing: British marketing/advertising/capitalism via ceramics, paintings, etc. Fairly easy grader-2 midterms & 1 final, lecture/group asgmts, group participation grade, final essay, & extra credit (ceramics @ the Mint Museum Randolph) TAKE HIM!

Professor Lockton isn't a bad professor, I just personally thought the class was boring and his lectures didn't exactly help with that. Aside from that, the class is pretty easy as long as you listen in class or look at the powerpoint, especially for tests. He does do a couple unannounced group assignments to encourage attendance.

Dr. Lockton is an exceptional professor. He makes you do commentaries and he tries to open your mind and fully understand the topic. He listens you carefully while you are talking about the topic and you can just feel that he cares what you are saying just like a friend. I wish I could take him every single semester. He is just the best.

Class is very easy and fun if you enjoy the subject matter. Just show up, pay attention to lectures and you will do just fine. Exams are a piece of cake if paid attention or skimmed over the powerpoints beforehand. People who write poor reviews about this professor did neither which is funny. Easy A

We are graded on unannounced group assignments which was annoying and he graded slowly. However, he always gave us the prompts for the exams. Even if they were confusing, at least we knew what to study. Plan on having to print out primary sources from the slides for exams. Also, he doesn't give ANY announcements or due dates for most assignments.

You have to go to class because in-class group assignments are unannounced. You don't really need to pay attention to the lectures though. He is very cringey it is physically painful, but I can get a lot of work done for other classes during lecture. Really slow with grading but if you follow instructions you'll do well.

I would totally take this class again. It was very easy, and I truly liked it. If you like western history, or history in general, you'll like this class. Even if attendance is not mandatory, I recommend you assist (most of the time at least). That is the easiest way to get an A in this class. He is very nice too.

Benny benny benny where do I begin. You're an amazing teacher but also mental. Like straight up mental. But MAN he cares about teaching more than anyone I've ever met. Class was pretty hard but he will always work with you. Great guy, kinda hard class, lots of reading, but learned a ton. 8/10
all over the place, lectures were a bore, attendance was mandatory but you could miss up to 5 days. kinda weird about peoples names, constantly made jokes and mispronounced mine

Took this class for CTCM 2530. It was US food history and overall Dr. Andres was very funny and reasonable. I can tell he truly cares about his students and wants the best for their degree. There was an absurd amount of workload though, but that was because it was a half semester class. Overall a very nice guy, and very inspirational and funny.

He's super energetic about all the topics. He comes off a liiittle crazy, but it's just his way of teaching. He allows 6 absences before taking off points,had 3 books to read, weekly quizzes, and only reason my grade was a C is bc I slacked off at the end as it was a pretty heavy workload. He's a great teacher overall if you're up for a challenge

When you take the course Professor Andres is hilarious. When in class he has a habit of putting in sounds and jokes when he needs time to think so if you're the type not to like wasted time, you may not like him. Other than that his assignments are easy, the quizzes are home quizzes, but the midterm was handwritten so be ready.

Dr. Andres is one of the best professors the history department has to offer. He is passionate about his subject, makes lectures entertaining, and is a very cool and nice guy. The workload is not hard as there's an open note midterm and final, weekly open book quizzes, a term paper on a required book, and four discussions on assigned articles.

Very traditional professor, does not like technology. Zero memorization on any tests or quizzes, so it makes it very easy to pass the class. There is a decent amount of reading involved, and the VAST majority of the grade for this class is writing-based. No multiple choice. Very passionate about what he's teaching and overall an interesting class.
So incredibly funny, yet also very smart. Good overall teacher, made it easy to get up in the morning for his 8am.

Lectures are interesting and informative, though he sometimes tends to ramble. Weekly quizzes however they are open book and on just one chapter, ~30 pages, midterm and final are moderately difficult but with proper studying are a breeze. 2 essays/papers through the semester weren't too hard. Overall, great class to satisfy a theme requirement.

Proffesor Andres was  one of my most exciting professors I had this semester. He seems a little off the rails at first but its because he has such a passion for history and how it affected people. I learned so much during this class. There is a lot of work for a general education class, but its worth it

Im not sure if Dr. Andres changed his courses recently but my semester with him was awesome. No in class testing or quizzes-- they are on Inquizitive which is a 100 if you put in the effort. There are 2 big papers in the course and for the midterm/final, he lets you use a cheat sheet. I found his lectures entertaining and he's funny.

Where to start, He often uses racial slurs and is purposely sexist to students. Don't expect your grades to ever go in and be prepare for boring stories about himself. He won't put in grades if you request and hides behind his TA by saying grades aren't his problem. If you want to maintain knowledge don't take!!!

DONT. I took him for my HIST1161 and when I tell you he never stayed on topic... I feel like I learned nothing from this class. He thinks he's hilarious, which he isn't. If you can avoid him and take someone else I would. Somewhat easy class, It was just a waste of mine and everyones time.

I took Dr. Andres years ago and he was wonderful! He is an amazing connection to have if you want to pursue history. He can get off track during lectures, but he has your best interest and wants you to succeed.

In short, Benny Andres is a good professor with some issues.

He likes telling personal stories and discussion assignments, which lead him to be behind in the lectures.

Book quizzes are easy and don't prepare you for the difficulty spike that is the midterm and final exam.

But he has been very helpful to me in a lot of areas.

He's ok.

Horrible teacher, horrible experience. Did nothing but tell students they were going to fail or are hopeless if they don't meet his expectations, acts like you're stupid, offered little to no constructive feedback on anything, never graded anything until the final months of the semester, tried to fail almost entire class, uses class time rambling.

Dr. Andres is patient and informative. The feedback he provides pushes you to grow academically. His approach is not aggressive. He doesn't throw his accolades his your face, very down-to-earth and approachable. He's consistent with his expectations and understands when things in life happen (just don't take advantage). Definitely knows his stuff.

Where to begin. It takes about a month and a half to receive any sort of grade. He often uses racial slurs and offensive language in class. The majority of his lectures are about him and not history. He also does not provide clear grading criteria and gives out F's like it is candy. If you are taking this class to learn CHOOSE SOMEONE ELSE.
Would not take again

Dr. Andres was very compassionate and caring about each and every student in his class. You will have a lot of quizzes in this class but they are open book. He also offers a lot of extra credit so if you do the work you can easily get a good grade!
I took him for American Democracy. Very nice guy, but a very boring class if history isn't your thing. There are only 3 assignments for the whole class, but as long as you study they are very easy.
His voice is boring enough to put you to sleep, but the class is easy.

Dr. Wilson is a great professor: He conveys the lecture material so remarkably that people who hate history can appreciate. He's very flexible and reachable outside of class and gave our class options for our essay prompts. The main homework: Reading and taking notes on primary sources and textbook chapters and then in class discussing.

TAKE HIM!
THE best history professor at UNCC! If you need history classes, take them with Professor Lansen!
Long essays, and a couple tedious group projects, but he is always willing to help and genuinely cares about you doing well.

Dr. Lansen was an outstanding professor! I highly recommend his classes. He keeps the class engaged with energetic lectures that he is passionate about. He makes witty jokes, and his class is something I looked foward too. You do read 4 books, but the tests are not very difficult.

I do feel like he's a very funny and genuine person, but his grading is TERRIBLE. He makes things super hard for no reason and his slides are bare and empty. It will literally just be a picture and one word with zero explanation. He will also mention something one time, not put it on the study guide and the entire test will be based off that thing.
He's a nice guy, and some lectures are entertaining. He is so all over the place, making the material hard to understand. There really is no structure.
Great Professor!

This was a very interesting class that I enjoyed. Only two assignments per week, and no exams for summer. You just have to go above and beyond for the assignments, really explain everything in detail and you will get an A. His rubric was the same for every assignment, so I emailed him with questions and he always got back to me fast. Easy class

Nice online summer class to take. Mr. Lansen was a solid professor. No quizzes or tests, just two critical thinking/writing assignments per week. If you are a decent writer and put in any sort of effort, you will get an A. Did this class while having a full-time job. It's not difficult and it's lowkey interesting.

The professor teaches well and has clear expertise in the subject matters he discusses in class. However, your emails will collect cobwebs and he teaches CTCM 2530 like a senior course rather than a progression from WRDS 1103/1104 (its intended role). I did not understand I was signing up for the Hardcore mode section for this gen. education class.

Professor Lansen is a great professor, however my main problem is he is a very very tough grader. I took this class because it focuses on the Holocaust however many of the papers and exams are very hard and he. grades them very harshly. I would take him again because he's a great professor but be ready to work super hard for a bad grade.

Dr. Lansen is SOOOO good. He is hilarious and likes to incorporate humor into his lessons. He makes the class very engaging, which some history professors sometimes have a hard time doing. You have four assignments and tests throughout the semester, which will help you as they apply to creating assignments as a teacher or for the Praxis. 10000/10

He is a great teacher. Lectures are interesting and fun, he has you talk with others in class to form your own opinions about history rather than force ideas on students. Assignments are easy and tests are too if you take notes and skim through the book. He also makes a great syllabus. Very funny too. 10/10 professor.

Dr. Lansen is so kind and caring! He had us read 4 books and watch 3 movies throughout the semester, however, he gives us ample time for everything. He wants to meet with students to help them do as best as they can, so meet with him, especially before the final paper is due. He does not do extra credit, however, he gives extensions!

Professor Lansen is a hilarious and engaging lecturer. While the class has a heavy workload, his teaching methods and feedback make it worthwhile. Unstuckstudy AI was a great study aid alongside the required readings.

I had Dr. Lansen a few years back as a freshman in his Learning Community. He is still one of the most inspiring, understanding, caring, incredible professors I've ever had-- even four years later. He is incredibly knowledgeable about his field and makes that knowledge accessible. If you can take Dr. Lansen for anything, please do. He's amazing.

Funniest professor I've had by far. The jokes he cracks in class are hilarious and he is a really outgoing guy. The class itself mainly comprised of note-taking because is an easier class nonetheless. best guy for your 1502 requirement.

The most interesting history teacher you will ever have the oppuritunity to take. He taught me how to study for harder tests through teaching methods. tells you exactly how the tests will be but make sure you study the terms like you need to know whats going on, he relates the lectures to easier things to help you understand and he is so hilarious.

Best teacher I've had in college so far, his lectures are interesting and he's a funny guy. Lots of reading and about 4 tests a semester but if you put in effort and study a couple days ahead you'll do good on tests. Highly recommend going to office hours at least once and he'll be happy to help if your wondering what you can do better on tests.

This class is easily my favorite history class I've ever taken. Dr. Lansen's lectures are funny and engaging. The class can be difficult, and there are quite a few books to read for the course. He grades semi-harshly, but gives really good feedback so that you can improve your test grades. This class made me love history!!

Dr. Lansen is one of the funniest professors I have taken and has very interesting lectures. He is a semi-harsh grader but fair with his grades. Multiple books are required to do well in the course but they're all good reads even if you aren't a reader. Pay attention in class and take diligent notes because they will be needed for the midterm+final

Dr. Higham pushes you to be a better student, she makes sure you understand the content and can apply it for the exams and papers. Make sure to take notes during her lecture! She's challenging with a lot of reading and work to prepare for class but if you put in the time and effort, you will succeed.

Dr. Higham was the best history class anyone could take. You want to make sure you're taking notes because her slides only have a couple of words on them. When she says she's your textbook. She means it. I'd make sure in that class you do every single reading because she will call on people, she enjoys class participation that is a big thing.

Dr. Higham is a great professor overall and willing to work with you if you have any troubles. However, she is strict with her grading, quite challenging when you aren't a history major. I thought this course was going to be an easy A, but I struggled immensely, hard work pays off though!

This was a very challenging course for me this semester, don't expect it to be an easy gen-ed. Be prepared to spend days even hours on all of her assignments. There is no extra credit given, you will have learn to improve your writing and critical thinking skills over the semester.

Awesome professor, there is a lot of reading but you can tell she loves what she teaches. This translates to engaging and interesting lectures. She is swift to respond to emails and is always helpful.

Professor was always willing to meet during office hours to assist with your papers. All of the lectures will give you the information you'll need to study for your midterm and final. Has a weekly assignment that helps boost your grade. She has a good sense of humor, is caring towards her students, and heavily knows the information she teaches.

Professor Higham is extremely effective at teaching, and getting the most out of her students. While the class was difficult at times, I found the course to be very fulfilling and I am now a far better writer.

Dr. Higham is my favorite professor I've had at UNC Charlotte. I had her for 1160 and chose to take her course again. She is so passionate about her subject and cares about her students. Be prepared to come to class and work hard. She will make you a better student.
2600 can be a tough class, but Dr. Higham makes sure to give feedback and help you every step of the way. Definitely the best professor to take for this class.
Loved her! She kept class interesting. Definitely worth the shot.

AMAZING!!! I would retake her if I could. She gave lots of clear feedback and was ALWAYS willing to help/work with you. She gave lots of great advice and is super funny. Definitely recommend her for 2600, she prepares you very well!!

I took her class Spring 2022. Dr. Higham was a fantastic professor, and was very detailed with what exactly she expects from you in my experience. She always answered my emails in an incredibly timely fashion. She graded fairly, and the assignments helped prepare you for the final paper, and made time management more helpful.

Professor Higham makes this class sooo interesting. This was by far my favorite class this semester. She has very open communication, clear grading, and is always willing to help her students. If you can take her class, TAKE IT. Make sure you do the reading before class :).
Very good communication if you reach out to ask about an assignment or something you don't fully understand.

Absolutely amazing professor. I had her last spring and it was online because of COVID but the community she created in the class will be something I will never forget. Take her at some point in your academic path if you can!
exams are 90% of the grade and barely responds to emails. Not a lot of work just the exams are essays.

This class is mostly lecture-based and the professor talks a lot, which can feel boring if you're not into history. There are three essay exams and a final makeup exam that might help or hurt your grade. He's a tough grader and rarely replies to emails. Attendance counts at the end, with two drops. The project is 25% of your grade—take it seriously

Best history teacher i've had, Makes his own slides and specializes in specific stores/events instead of making you memorize an entire century. Very interactive with class and encourages all answers instead of one specific right answer. Limited HW and exams are essays, you have one page of notes you can bring. Passionate guy and great prof.

He just kind of spits information and rants at you for the entire class. It's kind of entertaining? The material is super boring but his passion is through the roof. He's a bit off-putting but seems like a genuinely nice guy. If you're a history nerd, you'll like him. If you're not, I wouldn't recommend his class.
Class was easy but very boring. 60% of grade comes from exams. Takes months to grade things. Would recommend getting a different professor.

Super kind and will work with you through any issues. If you pay attention and take notes, you'll do great. If you don't, you'll have absolutely no idea what's going on. All of the exams are essays, but the prompts are always relevant to lectures and easy to understand.

The descriptions he gives for projects and papers are very confusing, he also doesn't use a rubric for grading so it makes doing the assignments correctly, difficult. Not many graded assignments so attendance is a big part of your grade. The lecture is kind of boring, and he tends to ramble, but he is nice.

Dr. Klehr is a pretty good professor, I never found his class or work difficult. This was the second time I've had him. His lectures can be a little boring at times, and he does stutter/stumble over his words a fair bit, but he's honestly really nice and super understanding. He offers a ton of extra credit, and he's not a very harsh grader.

beware the exams are worth 60% of the grade and he does not grade lightly. If you don't answer the exam question exactly how he wants you to then gabriel will not hesitate to give you an awful grade, instantly failing you lmao. class has hardly any structure, minimal class materials, so if you fail to take good notes you are screwed on the exams.
Great professor and super easy!  Tests were not difficult if you took good notes during lectures.  Will work with you if you miss time or assignments.

Klehr is a decent professor but his classes are boring. This is the second class I've had with him and every class is slideshows or he's talking to himself because no one in the class knows what's going on.
I wasn't a fan of the class but he wasn't a bad professor.

Really amazing professor, not sure why people are complaining that the class is boring when it's a history class. Really nice and caring professor, he is somewhat of a tough grader but all the assignments are easy so if you put in no effort you can get a B+ or A-. Take it with him if you want to learn and have an easy fly by class.

Not a super hard professor, has some specificities in his grading for big assignments and exams. The class is mostly exams, a few assignments, and attendance. His lectures are where you get most of your information, but he is hard to hear sometimes and pauses a lot. He is very sweet and accessible outside of class.

literally the most boring professor, should have taken someone else. review quizzes are pointless, takes attendance for a grade and speaks all class long clicking through google slides. hes awkward, doesnt reply to emails for a few days, gets his own grading schedule mixed up, and the exams are graded tough if you are doing well in the class.
Easiest class I've ever taken. Homework was once in a blue moon, tests were easy and fair, and lectures were entertaining and engaging.

Solid professor, the man is pretty kind & not super strict. He took attendance every day but he allows 3 absences before it becomes points off. Course content was boring but there's not much homework & he's not too harsh with late grades & extensions. Exams are essays that you can do with a decent understanding. Decent feedback on essays as well.

Professor Klehr can be a bit boring and the homework and exam questions are sometimes a little unclear. He also takes quite a long time to grade assignments and takes attendance nearly every class. That being said the class is interesting and he knows what he is talking about. He also is very quick to respond to emails and a nice guy.
Made my life difficult!! Did not want to give 100 to anybody.
Called my mother in a fit of tears regarding this class and she had to convince me not to drop out of the history program.

Dr. Haynes is a great professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable and encouraging. That being said, you MUST be fully committed to her classes. If you do not show up to class, complete your work on time, attend her office hours, and participate in class, you will not pass. She is a very tough grader with high expectations.
Assignments are easy but require a lot of writing. Need to attend small group discussions to maintain your grade . Tough grader and runs over time.

Terrible. Her teaching style was to have us recreate the French Rev via an in-class play. So for a solid 8 weeks, we taught ourselves. Also, she assigns you a person to be so if you are assigned a rich person you are screwed. Textbooks were crappy. The online version is unusable so it has to be the physical copy. Interesting topic bad professor.
I said a long time ago that this professor was a good professor, but not a good undergraduate professor. I was correct, she is a great graduate professor.

This class was too difficult for a level-1000 class, as a history major. Her slides are just pictures, so if you miss class get the notes from someone because the TAs won't give you notes. Only takes attendance for MWF on Friday, in discussion sections. Lots of unnecessary work, two textbooks, one of them being one she edited, avoid if possible.

girl dont do it im literally so done w her. its the night of the final. she CHANGES the study guide and original test directions. all of the time. she is careless. and annoying. I'm about to have my gpa drop bc she cant seem to understand this is a 2,000 level a$$ course. she is always doing the most and I cant !!!!!!!! do not take this class.

She demands way too much for a 2,000-level course. Tests consist of three essays worth of writing expected to be done in 75 minutes. Grades harshly on primary source analysis papers. NEVER gives out a 100. I ESPECIALLY hated the 1848 unit, which was a group project. I was stuck with a lazy group, which tanked by grade. She's a nice person though.

Great professor, but not suited for 100 or 200 level courses. Grades way too harshly with barely any feedback. No textbook, but 4 history books used for multiple assignments. Group project sucks and she won't give you credit based on how much you did, even if you show receipts. Interesting course but steer clear if you don't want to overwork.

She knows what she's talking about and she talks about the material well but she is asking way way way too much for this level of class and is more often than not unreasonably harsh. 

I'm not done with the class yet, so I can say this. If you want the challenge of your life - take her. If not - it's probably best you avoid her.

Nice person though

SHE IS NEVER CLEAR ABOUT WHAT SHE WANTS ON HER EXAMS LIKE IT GENUINELY NEVER MAKES SENSE. For example, in her study guide, she literally states this: identify five people but make sure you know six because there won't be all eight on the exam..then WHY MAKE US STUDY ALL EIGHT JUST PUT THE ONES YOU'RE PUTTING ON THE TEST ON THE STUDY GUIDE?

I wasn't the biggest fan of this class, but I wouldn't say I hated it. There are a lot of assignments and she grades way too harshly for a 1100 course. You also have to buy the $80 revel textbook for the quiz assignments. I would suggest taking another course if you're looking for a good introductory history class.
Dr. Massino is an extremely caring professor. You can tell she enjoys what she does. Some topics were difficult, but she is a very fair grader.
Very very very lecture heavy. Please take good notes as there are a lot of quizzes

Brilliant, passionate, and creates a safe, fun class. Lots of participation, Packback weekly, quizzes every other week (you can redo for 100% credit). Workload is heavy but doable if you attend and study. Lots of essays. Great vibes, easy to make friends. Attendance graded, becomes optional. Never ends class early, talks the ENTIRE class.
You can really see how much she cares for the things she teaches and is very willing to help if needed.
if you want an easy 1502 class, avoid this one like the plague.

This professor is very kind. She cares a lot about her students and wants everybody to succeed. I took a HIST1502 class over the summer, and most of the assignments were manageable to do and I have received good grades on all of the assignments. However, she doesn't post feedback on some writing assignments but still she is a great professor.

Professor Massino has been extremely helpful to me throughout this course. I struggled quite a bit this semester, with some personal issues and she has ensured my success. Not only this, her lectures are easy to engage in and she moves at a good pace. She is very engaging with her students and is passionate about her work. She is so amazing.
Dr. Massino is an all around amazing professor, whose classes I've taken with her have been very enjoyable. Easy to comprehend and the course work is simple to tackle, yet requires dedication.
Really enjoyed Dr. Massino's class. She is a fantastic professor who cares deeply about the success of each of her students. I would 100% take another one of her classes!

Jill has a tendency to grade like the courses are 4xxx level classes. She quizzes you on parts of her lecture that are being skimmed over by her but not on the powerpoint. Blatantly she is just not very reasonable.

Dr. Massino was amazing. Her lectures can be lengthy, but that is where you get the majority of your information for your notes from. Her lectures were not required attendance, but they were urged. The group project portion was all that was mandatory. Dr. Massino is very understanding about absences and trouble with group projects, I adore her.

This class was more work than I expected but I feel like I learned a ton! Dr. Massino's lectures are informative and her assignments push you to think beyond the course material and make connections to current issues. She is really passionate about history and also a very nice person. Would definitely take a class with her again.

To describe Professor Massino in four words: professional, compassionate, intellectual, and fair. For this class specifically, discussions were peer led with limited input from Professor Massino, except when to guide the discussion in a direction that was thought provoking. Her instruction method was clear, concise, and digestible.

Attendance is important- 5 absences and you fail (allegedly); he doesn't update participation grades at all so keep track of it yourself. His lectures are helpful, so it's worth it to show up. 3 essays are your tests for the semester. A tough grader on essays and gives no helpful feedback, maybe a few words tops if he leaves any comments at all.

I took Sabol for an elective class. He seems very knowledgeable, but if you're looking for an easy credit class, do NOT take his class. Attendance is mandatory as per the syllabus, 5 total unexcused absences results in a failing grade in the class. There is 2 exams in forms of 2000-2500 word essays, and he WILL assign homework during this time.

Professor Sabol is very educated on the topic and is very passionate about his lectures. His grading is questionable. I am not 100% sure he went over some of my assignments before grading them. He also does not give any sort of feedback. Assingments aren't very hard though if you do your readinds you will be okay.

Dr. Sabol is a chill professor however he does expect you to do your work and you really have to pay attention to his lectures and you may want to ask questions because that's what he prefers as he says he doesn't like to ramble on and on, just be prepared to do a ton of writing and try to be thorough as you can, he is accommodating if necessary.

Dr. Sabol is a very knowledgeable professor and will go into great detail about the events in the Cold War. His lectures gave a lot of useful info for exams, and he will answer any questions you have. You have 3 essay exams, 5 summaries, and some discussion posts. As long as you pay attention, you should do well in the class.

Sabol is obviously a very well informed man on all things history and often times he has extra conversations to add onto the class. His lectures are clear he can be funny. Grading is tough and require  lots of reading through documents to be able to finish assignments.

had to drop his class cause he did not give me feedback on any assignments. I asked for feedback on them, He said he would send me an email. I asked sent him multiple emails, but he never responded to me. The worst part is I got a 5/10 on the first summary and a 9/10 on the second summary. I didn't change how I did my work, but he graded different

The professor is engaging, but the workload is heavy. Lots of essays and exams - Unstuck study proved a great study aid to manage the content. Overall, a challenging class, but doable with consistent effort.

Best teacher I've had so far at UNCC. I took his Cold War History 1502 class and he turned the Cold War history topic into something enjoyable even for those not crazy into the topic. He places great emphasis on his essays and takes them very seriously and also doesn't give any feedback on them. Pretty light on homework too (besides the essays)

I have had Dr. Sabol twice now. He doesn't demand attendance but the more you attend the better. You usually write anywhere from 2-3 papers along with small reading assignments/questions. Lectures are fun and you can tell he knows a lot about history, and in moments that he doesn't, he willingly admits it. He seems like a really chill guy.

If you're bad at writing, don't take this class. Weekly writing assignments of 2 pages, 3 papers of 10 pages, and 3 open answer tests that he grades extremely hard. The papers and assignments are graded easily IF you follow the criteria. If you do one thing wrong on the rubric, you could get a 0 on a test. Mostly just rambles in lectures.

Makes the elective class most difficult. Gives like 8-10 pages of essay for exams which is worth 100 points and gives 10 HW assignement which is worth 5 points each. Math doesn't make sense. DON'T TAKE HIM

Super chill dude, he's really funny and understanding, he'll likely give you an extension or whatever you need if you ask politely. The class is pretty easy, just don't fall behind on assignments, there's not that many and tests are weighted very heavily. I only got a C because I missed 2 assignments at the beginning of the semester.

Professor Sabol is an alright professor, he is very passionate about the lectures he gives which are great but if you think this is an easy LBST class you are WRONG. He is super lecture-heavy and rarely posts slides, his essay topics are straightforward but have no specific rubric. Also, be prepared to read 20-30 pages+ for the abstract article.

Professor Sabol is pretty cool and has interesting lectures, but your mainly graded on abstracts, essays, and the exams. There are only a few of each of these so not many opportunities to raise your grade. Lectures can feel long as the information isn't posted online, but just keep on track and don't fall behind.

Charismatic, fun to listen to his lectures. Old school in the best way. Not the quickest grader and doesn't leave a whole lot of feedback. Overall enjoyable class and interesting subjects. Would recommend.

He's a nice enough guy, and he makes his lectures at least some what interesting, but there is an essay due almost every week. He does a weird thing where everything is due at noon instead of 11:59 or the start of class so you should try and get all work done the day before. Tests are also essay heavy, so just be prepared for that.

I took Dr. Sabol's class to coincide with a paper I was writing about Afghanistan for another class. Don't get me wrong - he assigns a lot. I did multiple upon multiple papers that took up a ton of time. But I've never met a professor who's so willing to work with you if you just reach out to him.

As long as you go into Dr. Perry's WWI class with an interest in the subject matter, you will love this class and her lectures . Exams are not difficult, but be prepared to write nonstop for the entire time given. Grading is incredibly slow; I often waited close to a month for my exams and assignments to be returned to me, though feedback was great

She's a really good lecturer, and she is very passionate about what she teaches. She takes WEEKS to grade anything. Never expect it to come back quickly, no matter what it is you submitted. Class has a LOT of writing, but I didn't mind it so that's up to you. Wow does she grade slow.

Class is so interesting (ww1) and fun! assignments are fair and grading is also fair. Tests are difficult because its all open essay questions, so if you are not prepared or did not pay attention you will fail. As long as you pay attention and try you will easily pass the class, and if you give good effort and work with the proff you will get an A+

Dr. Perry is my favorite professor at UNC Charlotte. I have taken her for HIST 3600 and HIST 4000, and I could go on and on about how wonderful she is. Her feedback is very specific (but not degrading), she scaffolds her assignments so you're not overwhelmed, and she genuinely wants to see everyone succeed. I wish we had more profs like Dr. Perry!

Dr. Perry is genuinely a really good professor as well as a person. She doesn't want to see anyone fail her class or get behind but that doesn't mean she will make it easy for someone. If you show up to class and do the work it's a great class. Dr. Perry gives tons of feedback on work and is always open to meeting with you to talk more about it.

She was so nice! Gave great feedback on my assignments and papers. Very helpful, as well. Attendance is important if you want to do well as it is a lecture heavy class. But if you take good notes and do the reading then you'll be all good. Overall I liked the class, interesting material too.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL!!!!!!! she does not give good feedback or help you at all!!!! She also does not answer emails. And she does just enough to say to higher up people that she did this and this. She also berated me in front of the class and i did not want to attend her class at all! She made me cry a few times. Overall DON'T TAKE HER!

50% of our grade was just 2 assignments (a paper and the final), the slides only have a couple words on them so if you miss a lecture, it can be hard to catch up. Reading will help you, however the tests are INSANE. You have one class period to do 5 short answer questions and an essay question. She does give you a notecard to use but its stressful

While I do think that Professor Perry is a good teacher and is very excited by european history, she 10000% over estimates the workload she thinks her students can handle in this course. Over spring break we had 26 quizzes on pearson revel due and they weren't even opened until the monday during break and closed that sunday. Attendance is important

The topic is great, but the structure is failing students. With only eight grades total, there's no room for error or feedback. If you take this class, please be prepared to do a lot of self-review and unless changes are made to how many grades there are, do your very best to never miss an assignment.
I would not recommend this course to anyone.

She is a very nice person and is a person you would love outside of her class. However, her grading policy and the way that the class is structured is very confusing and she sometimes does not respond to her emails. The way that she wants things formatted is big in her class. It is very test based with only a few assignments truly worth it.
