Great teacher! Attendance wasn't mandatory during Monday and Wednesday classes, but Friday classes (the writing consultations) were mandatory. He does not give out any tests/quizzes. The only assignments are journal entries (4) and 2 essays which you have a month in advance to prepare for.

Professor Johnson is a good professor. He does not give out any tests/quizzes. The only assignments really are journal entires (4) and 2 big essays. I feel that with this, he can be a bit of a tough grader with our writing. During the lecture, it could go off-topic sometimes. Other than that, Johnson is a pretty good professor.

Dr. Johnson was AMAZING!!! He really cares about you and teaches very well. No tests and two essays. He is also very passionate and knowledgeable about what he does. Don't hesitate to take on of his classes if you get the chance.

Professor Johnson was a good professor. His class was mostly all lectures, and he had a tendency to ramble but it was never off-topic. Utilize the information he gives you for papers and ask for help when you need it, and you will succeed.

I loved this class with Dr. Johnson. He didn't give busy work. He only gave about six assignments the whole semester which were all essays. Four of them are really easy and opinion based and the other two are research paper. He gives you all the information you need and all the help he can give. I highly recommend this class.

He's really nice, but he barely does notes and doesn't prepare us for exams that well. Low-stakes writing is on random days and exams are all FRQs, no MCQs. You have to rely on the list of vocab words to study for the exams. However, there are a lot of extra credit opportunities where you go to lectures and write paragraphs about them.

Once again, Dr. T. provided me with a wonderful experience in learning about Victorian Britain! I loved the course content & the structure: Discussion, primary sources & movies. He gave great feedback on my papers which really improved my writing! Easy A but lots of reading, 3 papers including the final (60%) and attendance and participation (40%).

He is a great teacher with great TAs. Don't skip! It will drop your grade because attendance and participation are so important. Ask the TAs for help on the essays. There are random pop quizzes, but if you read, then you should be good. Make sure you schedule out the readings well because it is a lot. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Prof. Thorshiem has become one of my favorite professors here at Charlotte. I really enjoyed his format:  Lecture and take questions. The only problem was that he's too harsh of a grader on essays, but will discuss the grade. He tried to recruit me to be a history major. Looks like it worked because I'm taking HIST 3104 with him this coming fall!

Third time I've had him. If you're not a history major he can be tough, but he's always willing to help with writing or understanding outside of class. He's really helped me become a better writer and is very passionate about the subject.

Dr.T teaches difficult classes. I was in a 3000 lvl HIST class. Although his class is difficult, he helps students and actually cares. At the end of the semester his listens to what he can do better. Hard class with lots of work taught by one of the most caring, kind, and respected professors at UNCC. He made a difficult class easier. 10/10 person.

little to no homework throughout the entire semester. Just 3 essays (including the final) that are about 4 different books you will have to read (or not). Good if you can write bad if you cant-picky about grammar. Attendance mandatory. it really effects the grade. The class itself was boring as it had little to do with the book or papers you read.

Dr. Goldfield is a great historian and advisor but not a good teacher. His lectures had no connections and he did not teach us any methodology despite this being a methodology course. He also had no or very vague instructions for assignments, never posted any grades in the gradebook, and his feedback was hit or miss or nonexistent.

If you want to pass, take this course. If you want to learn History, don't. You don't have time to learn anything with the workload he gives you. His lectures are okay, but it doesn't coincide with what he gives you in the test, which you have to study by yourself through the book. He is good with history, but not quite with teaching.

This class was moderately insufferable. The TA did all of the work and emailed very unprofessionally, as if our conversation was texting. I would not recommend this professor to anyone. On the first day of class he said "I can tell where all of you are from based on what you look like, but I can't say the same for the black people." Out of touch.

Prof Goldfield is clearly very knowledgeable about history, and his optional lectures are actually very interesting as he centers on the history of politics. The homework system was atrocious. Expensive online textbook with way too much reading, many quizzes and essays that werent even reviewed. If you dont do well on midterm you wont get an A.

Dr. Goldfield is a very interesting professor. His lectures are engaging if you pay attention, and he is really nice. Just don't leave in the middle of his class (which should be a given, since attendance isn't even mandatory). Be respectful to him and he'll be respectful to you. My only problem was an issue with grades not being available.

Do not take this professor! The only good thing about him is that attendance is not mandatory and most things are done online. He has not graded things from the beginning of the semester and it is week 14. I would have an A in this class if he would put in grades.

He is a good/easy professor for an LBST. Lectures are very boring. You have chapters essays to write but you can bullshit them and do fine, same with the tests. Tests are papers done in class 1 mid-term and final. TA's do all the grading by letters. Very easy class to take if you have a busy semester, just stay on top of the work and due dates.

Very dull lectures but a great professor. As long as you complete the assignments by the due date, you are guaranteed an A. The midterm and final were both in essay format however, he ended up making the final optional when the University revised the exam schedule. Overall, easy LBST to knock out. 10/10 recommend.

Very easy class. However, there are essays every two weeks that are very tedious. Really just busy work. Most of the assignments are just busy work. If you do them, you'll do great on the midterm and final.

This class was amazing, Professor Rieman was a helpful and caring instructor. Most of the class is papers, but Dr. Rieman is very lenient with grading and provides great feedback. She is very respectful to her students and wishes the best for all of them. As long as you read the rubrics and submit the work on time, this class is an easy A.

As for grading, attendance was 20% of the grade and the rest were based off of five essays. She's a fairly easy essay grader. Essay grades were not fully based on the final essay, so it is easier to get higher essay grades. She is always very helpful when asking for help on assignments. Overall, Dr. Rieman is a very caring and amazing professor.

Professor Rieman was amazing. She was very caring and would do anything to help her students succeed. Instructions for papers were clearly outlined and the grading was fair and easy. Would definitely recommend for WRDS 1103 as she made me enjoy writing which I never thought I would do.

Dr. Rieman is an amazing professor. Very lenient and understanding, and laid back when it comes to deadlines and assignments as long as you're dedicated to the class. She was very accommodating when I missed multiple classes due to an injury, and gave extensions. Easy A in the class as long as you're consistent with your work. Definitely take her.

I really enjoyed Dr. Riemans Class, she is a very sweet lady. Dr. Rieman is not too hard on grading there is a lot of reading, that I didn't do, but I still got a pretty good grade. There are quite a few essays to be ready to write. The lectures are pretty laid back and we had some fun conversations in class. overall I really enjoyed Dr. Rieman

WRDS1104 isn't an easy class because it's 4 credit hours, but Dr. Rieman makes it much easier. Her grading criteria is so detailed and clear that as long as you hit everything on the rubric, you should be getting at least 85s on papers. As long as you read the textbook and participate you should be fine, and she gives extensions if you ask.

Dr. Rieman is incredibly sweet and obviously cares about her students. Grading is mainly based on a complete/incomplete because she wants them to focus on improvement and not their grades. Just be sure to always follow her grading rubric. Her class is only "difficult" if you don't expect to write in a writing course.

She's totally great and I'd take her again!  (but I think she left; like many of our best professors, she was part-time.). If she comes back, you should take any class you can with her. Inspiring, cares about her students, and her courses are all very interesting.

She is a very sweet woman, I actually had her for HIST2002. She is very kind and accessible outside of class, her instructions are incredibly clear. Her lectures can sometimes be a bit confusing. She shows a lot of media in class, and gives many opportunities to find sources for our final paper, which I really appreciate.

She was alright, the lectures were long and didn't really follow a PowerPoint. Class consisted of discussion boards, a paper, map quiz, midterm, and final: a good mix. Gave review sessions + Offered extra credit, also she was easy to reach. I would take her again, not a bad professor. Only thing, her lectures were hard to follow and a little boring
She tells you what to focus on for the tests and brings exactly what was discussed during class. She is a bit of a tough grader but I definitely recommend.

You watch a lot of interesting documentaries and videos in class. Attendance is mandatory and is graded by polleverywhere. If you have a 94 or higher by the end of the semester, you do not have to take her final exam. She's nice but awkward, and the way she talks leads you to have no idea if she is actually asking the class a question or not.

Very good professor I loved the stories we read and very good lectures.. She really had interesting topics I would definitely take her again!! I passed with an easy A as long as you show up and do the work and pay attention its an easy A and shes very nice and willing to help at all cost!!

Doesnt really have any structure to his course. Assignments are confusing / vague. Grading is completely subjective - if he doesn't agree with an opinion in your paper it will reflect in the grade. Has ideas on how papers are supposed to be written that contradict every other course I have taken. Half the class dropped after the first day
He did not cancel class after active shooter alert. He did not send an email about the situation either.

He's mean and sometimes even yells at students when his expectations are not met(his expectations are unobtainable) His lectures are always hard to sit through and he never gives answers to the questions he wants us to know the answer to and just rambles on while telling us we are wrong at every turn throughout a class discussion without guidance.

Very rude to students when they asked questions. Directions on assignments are very unclear. I switched out of his African American History class to another professors and it was much more easier and learned probably more than I would have in his class.

There is no reason why an Arts and Society film class most people take as a gen ed should be this hard. Such a harsh grader and for what, sorry to break it to you but no one actually cares. I tried and I still got a C, I just needed 3 more credits this semester and my gpa tanked.

Great Lectures. She tried hard to make class fun with a variety of in-class assignments / work. She can be slow to respond to email, but her responses are always helpful and detailed. I enjoyed the class!
She makes the class incredibly difficult, almost as if she gets pleasure out of making questions really complicated. Take another professor if possible.

It's asynchronous online class. She didn't reach out to us very often, but I found her to be easy to reach via email - and willing to excuse assignments or grant extensions when necessary.  I have learned a lot from her this year!!
An incredibly talented and skilled educator. Loved the way she structured and she taught me that I wasn't stupid, that I could learn to take detailed.

She is not a terrible teacher. In fact I thoroughly enjoyed her lectures. My only complaint about her was how she did not respond to emails very well and the fact that her tests are all written response. However, that being said they are also open note so as long as you take notes during class you will be fine.
Took three months to reply to my email.

She gives out lazy work and grades super rough. I always followed the instructions but nothing was ever good for her. I would try to email her for guidance but she always responded with a few sentences that didn't help at all. My advice, take a different class unless you want to work your hardest to only receive a bad grade.

Professor Deem is a very tough grader. I did everything the assignment said and never seemed to get about a C or low B. Discussions have to be exactly to her standards and essays are long. Only good thing is quiz answers are on quizlet. I would not suggest taking this class.

Class was asynchronous online, so all materials were in Canvas. Much of it was just bulks of unnecessary information. She takes FOREVER to grade and also grades extremely tough with no feedback at all. Never seems to respond to her emails. This is ridiculously horrible for it to be a GenEd course, so I recommend taking another professor!

Made what was supposed to be a fun and relatively easy class into the worst one I've ever had. Seems incredibly unsympathetic to any issues students may face. She said she wouldn't give study guides because it makes "lazy" students only to then focus her tests on things no one knew to study for, no multiple choice to all short response and essays.

Dr. Soliz taught this class that way the I believe a general education class should be taught.  We did not have a lot of homework, and she understood that most of the class were not history majors; however, she worked hard to share her passion for Latin American history, and I learned a lot in the class!

She is the best professor I have had during my 4 years at UNCC and made me think about taking a master's degree in History in the future. She made history no longer boring but interesting, wonderful, and inspiring.
Professor Soliz will call on you most days in the lecture hall so be prepared before starting class

She emphasizes learning skills within the history discipline through papers and presentations, meaning she is a little tougher when grading. She is very caring and passionate, although she does go slightly fast. Extremely understanding and funny. I would recommend her if you care about Latin American History and enjoy engaging lectures.

You're graded by little in this class but they're not difficult. Mainly working on projects with others in the class, the grading policy is pretty clear. She does give out feedback for each project you present in front of the class. Her feedback can come off as harsh but it's just her way of making sure you know what she's expecting.

I highly recommend Dr. Soliz, she is great in every way. She keeps the class interesting, she is reasonable about assignments, she cares about her students and will help if you ask. And overall she's a very nice person who is an expert but does not intimidate you or overwhelm you with her own knowledge.

Professor Soliz is one of the kindest and most intelligent professors I have ever had. She is an amazing teacher that cares about her students. For the LBST you only have to read a few things in the beginning, go to class to take notes and then she will pretty much warn you of an upcoming short quiz and then the other half is writing one paper.

Be prepared to read! We read several books and some weren't available for free or easily online so I struggled to find/buy a book for 1 assignment. She gives harsh feedback so be prepared! Half-done assignments & lazy participation are not going to cut it. Sometimes you have no idea what she expects for a good grade because instructions are vague.
She is very nice, can be hard to understand at times. There are no tests only a few quizzes and if you pay attention during lecture you will be fine
Professor Tabitha is the best! Her class is easy and enjoyable and she respond to every email I send immediately!

Took her course on Irish history, and it was wonderful all around. She's very engaging and open to discussion from just about anyone, so I recommend her if you like to actually talk about history and culture. The assignments were fairly easy so overall the class was a fun experience in which I felt like I had a voice. Would take again.
Extremely easy. Never attended class. It's a busy work class, do the assignments on time and you should get a high A.
The best Professor I have had my first year of college and that speaks a lot. Would definitely take again just listen in on class videos, zoom calls and do the research she assigns.

Favorite professor, I've had. Very caring and down to earth. Her class was extremely interesting. Very knowledgeable in her subject. She did not make the course overly difficult. The course felt very streamlined, we got the info we needed without the useless fluff many professors are notorious for giving.

Professor Wood is great! Her class was very interesting and fun. Not a lot of work, there are a few quizzes but they are easy. A movie response paper and the movie was interesting. She is very understanding and overall a great professor!

Incredibly caring and understanding. Great teacher with engaging lectures. Has movie assignments and gives different options other than papers. Gives wonderful feedback and is an easy grader who helps you in any area you may need. No tests and good extra credit provided. Understands that students are human and things happen!

I absolutely love Professor Wood she is one of the best Professors I have had. She is super understanding and doesn't make the class hard at all I feel like I learned a lot from her this semester and I wish she could teach all my classes.
Only had 4 quizzes, paper/video, and discussion posts.
Professor Wood is one of my favorite professors I've ever had! She responds to emails quickly and is always willing to help outside of class/zoom hours.

Loved this class and Professor Wood! Would love to take this class again or any class by her! Clear instructions and not many assignments which is great to balance with other classes. Also is very caring, well-meaning, and listens to every student she has.

Professor Wood is hands down one of the most caring history professors at UNCC. I took her Irish History class and loved it! Assignments include four quizzes and a couple of papers throughout the semester. They are fairly easy since they're open notes. Her lectures are interesting in that they keep up with current events in Ireland as well. 10/10!

If I could take another class with Professor Wood, I would in a heartbeat. She wants nothing more than to see her students succeed, both professionally and personally. Professor Wood is passionate about the material she presents. I will truly miss this class.

Professor Wood is the single most caring professor I have ever had. Work is graded by open-note quizzes, movie responses, and a final paper. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you don't attend class, you must respond to one discussion post each week. She is super understanding and will always work with you if you ask. Definitely recommend!

TAKE THIS CLASS!! Professor Wood has by far been the best professor I have ever had. I never really cared about European history or Irish history but she made me care. I learned so much and I looked forward to her class every week. She is one of those teachers that is more worried about you learning than grades. She really cares about her students,

Mrs. Wood was an extremely good professor and very lenient about grading since she understands most students take this class because they have to. If you have any reasoning behind why you can't get something done she is very caring and understanding about it, she is a professor that genuinely cares about her students more than the work.
Amazing
AMAZING PROFESSOR. TAKE HER. The best LBST class you will have and you will actually want to attend the class. Such a caring professor who is extremely understanding.

Mrs. Wood is such a nice and caring professor! While Irish history is a tough subject to learn, she is fully aware of it and tries her best to make it easier for everyone. She always explains everything very well, and goes over the open notes quizzes to make sure no one suffered. Another thing I love is that she will extend dates if you are busy.
Prof. Wood is the most caring woman ever. Open note quizzes once every month was the only assignment if you showed up to the zoom meetings. Final was a three page paper. TAKE THIS CLASS!

She talked a lot in general about other things besides the course, but no one seemed to mind. We had a 7 pm to 10 pm course and we were all tired. Got out early every night, and she did in fact give us a whole verbal study guide for the final. She won't give you a physical one. Also let us choose some quiz types, had 2-3 options.

This was one of the hardest classes i've taken this semester and I had chem and bio. She grades way too harshly, and doesn't explain why she graded the way she did. I emailed her 3x about my grade and she only answered one and didn't reply to my follow up. Unless you type out word for word what she was looking for you won't get better than a C

To begin, I enjoy history and the content being taught in 2102 but wow.... this is one of the harder courses I have taken at UNCC. Professor Deem seems very nice but when it comes to grading assignments she's probably one of the harshest professors I've had. I really believe you could write your discussion posts at a doctoral level and still no 100

I would classify this as level 3. Her M class is 3 hrs long and it's hard to learn when she talks for 3 hrs straight. Some of the activities are interesting but her exams/quizzes are difficult. You can't even find the notes from the lecture on Canvas to study, and quiz questions are complicated. If you want to save yourself from stress, avoid this.

She is passionate about and does a good job teaching history but the class has overly difficult assignments. The weekly quizzes are open book but it is still difficult to find answers to questions. There was also no study guide for the midterm. At least assignments were weighted more than exams and assignments that are not quizzes are easy.

Prof does a pretty good job at responding to issues with late assignments. They use my favorite style of teaching history which is explaing it like a story. Important dates and stats are provided for context but most of what you are tested on will be over the significance and impact of historical events which she does a good job at emphasizing.

I quite enjoyed this class. Professor Deem is a fantastic and entertaining lecturer. It is a test heavy, lecture heavy class and she can be a bit slow to return grades on the few tests and assignments we do. However, the class is very interesting and fun and well worth the time spent.

If you have even an ounce of respect for yourself.....do not take this class. Be prepared to spend so much time and effort on assignment's....just to fail anyways. This professor expects you to have the super power of mind-reading and has high expectations for the little effort she puts into delivering them.

She will talk for the entire class and claims at the beginning of the semester she will never keep you all of class but she most definitely will. If you dont read her books, you wont know what to write about on the discussions and she thinks shes funny but she isnt at all. If youre not actually into history, dont take this class
Too many writing assignments. Grades too harshly. Overall disliked the course. Please do not take if you do not like to write about history!

I would avoid Professor Deem if possible. Grades assignments like they're for a graduate course, and won't provide good feedback on why you received a poor grade. She can take weeks to a month to grade assignments. She is often unresponsive to email, making it all the more difficult to discuss grading or feedback. Long and boring assignments.
Amazing professor. Probably one of the nicest professors I have ever taken. He teaches really well and is a super considerate guy.
Professor Melton was an amazing teacher. Always helped out if we had to miss class and made sure we would be caught up if we missed class. He was a really easy grader and never over loaded us.

I had Mr. Melton in high school and now in college. 100% would take him every chance you can. I finished with a 100 in both classes, and it's never been overwhelming. A few discussion posts, one midterm (which you help construct) and an easy group project as the final. You will get an A if you do the work, which is relatively minimal. A+ Professor.

Professor Melton is an incredibly understanding guy, he not only understands the workload we might have for other classes but also just life in general. He gets what it is like being a college student and tries his best to make these classes work as stress-free as possible while still teaching you things.
Super easy class you just have to show up. Mr. Melton is super laid back and understanding.
What a professor, he was so helpful in every way the course was easy and explained very well 10/10 defiantly a great time.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had.  Tyler, unlike most professors, actually explained the slideshow content in detail and helped us understand. He is very considerate and chill. The class is not writing heavy, just one discussion post at the end of each week. The final was a group project, not a test. It was a great class overall.

Goforth made inappropriate comments in class and spent the majority of lectures discussing past students or reminiscing about his younger days. His tests have very little to do with the course and contain numerous grammatical errors. The way he spoke to us led a girl in my class to start an investigation

The class itself is not bad, just very boring. The professor is not terrible either, just very dry. Even as someone who enjoys most branches of history this was a slog to get through. For homework you have a reading and discussion board posts/responses, takes an hour max. Very strict on attendance.

People either love or really hate him. His class isn't an easy A, don't take it if you want to coast through. He can be brutal. He's always up for a debate and he's really fun to talk to. If you want an actual teacher who loves the subject he's teaching and will be honest with you no matter what, take his class.
Constantly changes the syllabus and is very unclear on grading. Did not learn anything all semester. DO NOT TAKE

RUN.  All he did, all semester, was talk badly about past students (and some current from other classes) and ramble on about his personal life or how things were for him when he was in school. We only had about 2-3 classes that he actually taught what the course was about. Took 4 WEEKS to go over the syllabus alone.

He seems like a cool guy, outside of class. As a teacher he is not good. He spent half of the semester ranting about things past students did to make him angry, and didn't start actually teaching anything until after midterm. He also talks to all of us like he knows everything and we know nothing. If you mess up, don't even try to reason with him.

Professor Goforth was really bad.  He treated us like children rather than as adults.  He also overhyped his class a ton.  His class was super easy, but he made it as if it was the hardest class we would take.  He also only allowed 4 unexcused absences, which I thought was ridiculous for an 8 am.  And he was super indirect and made no sense.

Overall Hugh Goforth is not a good professor. We had 3 lectures the entire semester that made sense and gave insight for the topic discussed. The rest of the semester was filled with ramblings and rants. He takes long to grade papers and gives confusing feedback. Sometimes he will talk about politics and religion for the entire class.

Attendance is required and if you come in 5 minutes late your probably going to miss the attendance poll. I hardly learned anything from lectures, a huge waste of time. Can ramble on trying to explain very simple ideas for 5 minutes I have no idea why. Awful weekly discussion questions that most of us bullshit. Same with the reading. Waste of time.
I think something has happened to this poor old man where he has now lost his mind. He makes no sense at all, sounds like he's completely lost it upstairs. Probably needs to retire soon.
He is insane. Run away.

Weekly assignments are easy, it is just a discussion post. But OMG he does NOT teach, he rambles on in class about absolutely nothing. He is such a difficult grader on papers and all he talked about in class after we submitted it was how poorly we all did and basically everything he hates about papers students write.

He was quiet at the start, and seemed to want students to pass. Halfway in the course he began to call students out and became passive aggressive, with a tone and attitude change. Will stare at you like an owl until you say something, BUT grades quickly. I feel that this is our education and $$, if we don't want to pay attention, leave us alone lol

Dr. Knoll is a new teacher so I will cut him some slack. He really is a sweet person, he just seems very timid. He tries to make his class interesting which I really appreciated, but it was so hard for him to do when he was so quiet and seemed so unsure about his next sentence. The work was fairly easy, but definitely sit in the front to hear.

Honestly, Travis isn't a bad teacher, he tries to be enthusiastic and animated while teaching, but Western History was just a boring topic. All there is is 5 question quiz/reading peer post for grades, which make the in-person lectures pointless, midterm is EZ!!!!, and readings are long. Find a partner to read with outside of class! Easy A tho

Most pointless in-person class ever. The only grades are a weekly five-question quiz based on 2 absurdly long passages and a weekly discussion post about 3 key concepts from the same documents. On the day of the midterm, he literally said "this is the only day that it is mandatory to come to class". His slide font is small and he speaks very quiet.

Before I begin, I need to give some credit to Professor Knoll as it was his first-semester teaching. That said, this was by far the most tedious and pointless class to attend in person. Your grade is based solely on reading comprehension-based quizzes taken outside of class. He does give lectures in class, but, he mumbles making it hard to hear.

Prof. Warlick was an excellent professor. Lecture heavy with lots of readings, but easy responses and tests made for an easy course. Although the lectures can be long, he keeps them interesting and fun. Attendance is required, however, I was excited to attend the lectures. Prof. Warlick opened my eyes to a new way of understanding our past.

Excellent Professor. He gives high-quality lectures that cover literally all the topics you need for the course, just be sure to take notes. There are required readings before class, but they are pretty easy to get through, and there are only about 4 pop quizzes based on the readings. Ended with a 103.4, an easy class because of a good teacher.

Very good Professor, very good lectures. His Lectures are very well planed out. He is a fast talker but you will get everything you need down in your notes. He is very funny and he isn't a hard grader, he makes sure you get the grade you deserve. few assignments but easy to get a 100 on all of them, other than tests. make sure to read before class.

Amazing Professor! He knows what he is talking about and can keep the class' attention. It has one big group project that is super easy if you get paired with the right people. I never did any reading and only took notes on the lecture, ended with a 98. Easy A class for your LBST requirement.
Hes a harsh grader, however hes knowledgeable of his field and gives good feedback

Attendance is mandatory and very few assignments, if you screw up on a paper your done the rest of the semester getting your grade back up. Very liberal course as well uses Chicago style to write in and if you don't write in that style you will be knocked hard on grading. Former lawyer so take that as you will, would not recommend to anyone.

If you absolutely have no choice but to take him then do it. He is a very tough grader and his instructors for assignments are unclear . He has a smart mouth when you ask him questions and emails back slow . The accent is a little tough to understand and takes some time to get use to . Also gives random pop quizzes

Terrible professor. I'm a straight-A student (literally a 4.0 GPA), showed up for every single class, participated, and tried my best in his class. Even though I managed to get an A, Dr. Ogundiran was extremely rude, mean-spirited, and arrogant towards me. Even belittled me when I'd visit his office for extra help. Very unprofessional. Don't take!

I liked this class. Professor was relaxed and very nice. You can tell she's passionate about history and really knows the material. No attendance policy and late work was taken at no penalty. I have never been a history person, but I learned a lot and looked forward to going to class.

Prof. Linker's class itself was kind of boring, she mostly just reads off of her slides. But she is super flexible with due dates on all assignments. There were a few writing assignments, which she grades leniently. The midterm and final were both open note. Super easy class.

(Spring 2019) This was the worst class I've ever taken. She had a psychotic break in the middle of the semester, yelling and screaming, threatening to fail us all and then quit. The history department chair had to stand in for a few days. 0/10 avoid her classes at all costs.

Mckinely. His research paper was given with plenty of notice, despite that it was one of the hardest I have ever written. The midterm and final were 5 essays that you had the class period to write (One big, 4 small). Awful. After the midterm we huddled outside and mourned our grades. His lectures were just group recaps of the reading, so READ.

Changed my previous rating as I did end up with an A instead of a B. Not a bad professor if you're a self-learner or confident in the material. 60% of grade is from exams which are pretty dense. The semester project is group work, but weekly homework is solo.

Worst class ever. There are 3 tests that are 20% of your grade no study guides. She's amazing if you READ the textbook and participate in class, even if you're struggling with the material. She mainly cares about diligence, and half of the class looks like they're ready to skip, which doesn't help. Her office hours were amazing!

This is one of the worst classes I've ever taken. If you don't have previous knowledge of literally anything discussed in class, you will struggle. I really enjoyed taking a class with Dr. Crisanti, she is very accessible outside of class, responsive to emails, and supportive during office hours. Dr. Pereira is a great professor who is funny and passionate about what he teaches. He does not teach in class and the tests are very heavily weighted. Class is a waste of time because he just has you do group work and two presentations. He seems to have a good understanding of the material but that is not at all useful because he doesn't teach or offer outside help.

Initially, I was going to take this course in person, but then he told us we'd always have to do group work because he "didn't feel like teaching," and I switched to online that same day. Would not recommend him as a professor.

Could not stand this class. The topics are interesting but you have to read every new chapter before the week begins. There is no lecture at all so you have to teach yourself almost all of the material necessary to know for the class. There are only three tests the entire semester so if you do bad they knock down your grade A LOT. Do not recommend.

Get ready to read and not learn in class. You have to read the textbook to pass the class. Videos he makes are no good, no teaching in class. Tests are 40 percent of grade. Quizzes don't help for studying.

1150 International Studies; assignments? Easy. Exams? Ridiculous. Lockdown browser/video recording required. Take this course in person. Both the TA and professor were difficult to reach and were not clear on both grading expectations and instructions for assignments. Would absolutely never take again.

Way too hard for an intro POLS class. Tests are lockdown browser, camera on, no notes etc, and make up a huge part of your grade. So hard for no reason, no flexibility or understanding when it came to assignments and expect to spend at least 10+ hours a week just on this class. Szmer is not a bad professor. He is witty and knowledgeable.
Test Review

The tests were online and open book just not the final. Lectures were funny and I understood what he was talking about. Attendance wasn't mandatory but provides extra credit for attending. He drops the lowest quiz scores.

Pretty good class! If you actually like American history and learning about the gist of how our government works, you will like this class. GO TO CLASS!! From what I can tell, more participation = more attendance credit. He is funny and thorough during his lectures. Easy A because he gives out test questions during his lectures.
Loved having this diva as a professor this semester.

Professor Szmer is a cool guy. The lectures are long and, at least to me, a bit boring, but if you enjoy politics and history, you'll likely find them interesting. I recommend attending every class because he gives extra credit attendance quizzes, which really helped me earn an A. Do the quizzes and tests, and you'll pass. The final is in person.

GO TO CLASS. You get extra credit by going, and you can literally watch TV, but know that the course is so lecture and textbook-heavy. All tests are online and open, not the final, which is in-person with a cheat sheet front and back, so that helps, but overall he knows what he's talking about and makes the lectures funny

His class is extremely lecture-heavy, but he makes them interactive, and he knows what he is talking about. Attendance is not mandatory, but you can get extra credit if you come to class. Literally my favorite professor

Prof. Szmer is a great professor that teaches American Politics really well. He engages with the class and always welcomes questions. All the tests and quizzes are online, besides the final. He's a good teacher and makes jokes where her can in lectures. I had a hard time following the lectures in correspondence with the quizzes and tests. He just went over the general info in lectures. He is very straight forward, sarcastic, and funny. all tests are online, final is in person. one reading quiz every week is the only work other than tests. tests and quizzes are open book. you get one full printer paper page for the final, front/back and typed. he is a very smart man and really knows what hes teaching.

Mostly graded on textbook quizzes and exams. Attendance is not mandatory but his lectures are funny and have a lot of the info for tests! He also often gave test answers in class to encourage attendance. Honestly, the only reason I got a B was because I got lazy lol, this is not a difficult class

Szmer's class is challenging, but engaging. Attend lectures and read the textbook - it's essential for tests. Unstuck study was a lifesaver for exam prep. Overall, a rewarding course if you're willing to put in the work.

Szmer is hilarious first of all, but he's also a great professor. He cares about you learning the material, especially if you're aspiring to go to law school. His lectures are always engaging too. Attendance isn't required, but he does do pop quizzes and there aren't many other grades in the course so keep that in mind. Definitely a great professor

Definitely not Napoleon. Just show up to class and read the textbook. The lectures can be entertaining if you interact with them. If you do your part in the work, you will get an A or B with no issue. Don't wear Alabama merch to his class though as he is a Georgia fan.

He values us actually learning the content over grades, he makes sure we get good grades so that we focus on learning, his lectures are fun and interactive without forcing us to talk and he makes it very interesting and he is very passionate. I found Professor Szmer to be extremely interesting and more than reasonable. I do not want to go to law school, just wanted to learn more about law and the legal system and I found this course very helpful!

If you are planning on going to law school take this class with this professor. The class is test heavy but the professor prepares you well for the exams if you go to class. Lectures are very interesting

Jason was a good professor, but I do not think I could pay attention in a class with just him. He is lecture heavy and it can be a little difficult to remain engaged. Only graded by a few things so make sure you show up to class and do well. Not sure why he has good reviews. Lectures aren't engaging and can be confusing. I'm coming back to rate professor Windett as a senior now, although I was a first semester freshman when I had him. He was a great professor, but also a really nice and sincere man overall. Very chill guy. He plays music at the beginning of every class and we rate the song through Poll Everywhere and that's how he takes attendance. He was very kind as well. You don't really need to read like he says too. Most information tested on is on slides or gone over in class. Does good review sessions for only two test (midterm and final). Find a buddy to complete unit quizzes. Not many assignments. Just show up to class ready to listen to Bruce Springsteen

Would take a class with Dr. Windett again. Going to class matters, and he will show statistics on grades compared to your attendance. Dr. Windett is a cool guy. Lecture-based with supplementary readings, everything is uploaded into Canvas. Showing up to class is most of the work. Exams are basically your entire grade. About 70% worth so beware if you're not a good test taker beware. 2 tests (final and midterm) and 5 point quizzes that will absolutely make or break your grade. No assignments, no homework. Attendance taken randomly throughout semester for a grade, so definitely attend class. The lectures are fun and interesting, but can drag on sometimes which he tries his best not to do. Attendance was randomly taken throughout the semester. TEACHER: Nice but very openly expresses a conservative bias which seeps into teaching

Super fun guy and I learned a lot (about both foreign policy and other random things). He would get off topic a lot but I personally found these stories a ton of fun. This was my favorite poli sci prof. so far I loved the dude! Dr. Matthews is the best
Great guy, fun class, loves to start debates.

Class with Dr. Matthews is an easy pass, but don't really expect to learn anything. There's a textbook he says you'll use but you'll never use it. Attendance is mandatory, and the grade is tough if you don't show up. Other than that, grading is clear and assignments too shes a very good teacher and is very understanding would recommend her

Great teacher, easy class. Fun at times and interesting. She seems to actually care about what she teaches and was good at making things engaging. The attendance policy was a bit rough, apart from that, great class.
She is amazing! Cares about her students and the material would definitely take CTCM 2530 with her again!

I absolutely loved this class! She's very passionate about what she teaches, and the course overall was very informative/interesting. She only assigns readings and 3 papers, which are fairly easy. I loved Dr. Khoury's class. She is very passionate about her course and it shows. Dr. Khoury is my favorite professor I've ever had. The lectures were interesting and provoked deeper thinking about global issues. I have taken 3 of her classes and highly recommended any course she is teaching. The class had 4 assignments and the work was very manageable.

Absolute sweetheart, and super understanding when it comes to absences/emergencies. Professor Khoury is kind and respects everyone regardless of their opinions and ideologies. She does say it is a discussion-heavy class, but she lectures quite a bit and it gets boring sometimes. She's a great teacher. I had her for International human rights. Mostly class discussions, one bigger project throughout the semester but nothing too challenging. Most of class we didn't stay on topic because human rights is so broad. If you need a filler class take this one.

Dr. Khoury is an amazing professor! She makes the content we read engaging in class through open discussions. Her lectures are also very insightful and interesting to listen to. Gives many readings and videos for each week, but you definitely don't need to read and watch them all to respond to the discussions. Professor Khoury is a very kind professor. The class is not as informative or interesting as I would've liked. If you enjoy discussions, this is the class for you. I am not fond of discussion-only courses so I did not like this class as much as I thought I would. Recommend if you like to talk, do not take if you prefer lectures.

Weekly discussion boards and 3 essays throughout the semester. Most of the readings were from the textbooks assigned or online readings she posted. She never gave a clear "standard" rubric for the essays or discussion boards, so you never really knew in what to improve. Never/rarely gave 100s.

Overall, I learned a good amount in her class. She assigns a lot of reading, but I never did any of it and I was fine. We had to write three papers for her class and most of class time was spent just having discussions rather than a lecture. It was a pretty easy class.
She so sweet lol. I mean her class can be easy it just depends on what course and what level. But she's genuine and collaborative and I really love that in a professor.

Easy class overall. Isn't too bad for an LBST. Your grade depends on tests and a final presentation. My only problem was that she rambles on and on during class so I don't know what to study for tests. She gives you a giant study guide but you can't cram for it the night before.

Dr. Khoury was one of my favorite professors this semester. There's textbook readings assigned but I never did any and was perfectly fine. Take her!!!

Dr. Khoury really cares about her students and wants you to do well in her class. Each week a chapter from the book assigned, and class is primarily a lecture and discussion. Major project was group podcast which is large portion of grade. Overall, great class, and a relatively easy LBST if you do the work and show up to class (attendance counts).

Dr.Miller is one of the best professors I have had. He is an engaging lecturer who is dynamic with his timing and information. It is easy to get an A.

Dr. Miller's classes are absolutely phenomenal. Yes, it's almost entirely lectures, but they're some of the most enjoyable lectures I've sat through in the 3.5 years I've attended this school. Dr. Miller is both funny and knowledgeable, plus very approachable outside of class. It's a shame he only teaches two classes, and I've taken both!

I really enjoyed this professor. Usually, those big 100+ people lectures are boring, but he was pretty funny, and made me want to attend his lectures. Assignments were easy an exams were online. Lectures were entertaining, not much assignments. just one essay and final
I've taken Dr. Miller multiple times at UNCC. He is hilarious, helpful, and accessible by email if you ever need anything.

I'm taking his class right now; HE IS SO FUNNY!! His classes are hilarious and so informative. He is so open to answering questions and making sure we understand the topic clearly. I would SO recommend this class. He is super energetic and very helpful if you need. Assignments are fairly easy. 10/10

Dr. Miller is one of the most energetic and enthusiastic professors that I've had here at UNCC. He knows a lot about the topics he teaches and always has answers to questions. Most of the homework will be Packback questions and reflections, but they are easy. I'd reccomend taking his class!
I love Dr. Miller. Everyone loves Dr. Miller. Take his course. His lectures are so entertaining, you find yourself surprised every time the clock indicates class is over.

I adore Dr. Miller. He's extraordinarily intelligent, but he's not pompous. He's a real sweetheart; he's very understanding about absences. Dr. Miller is the best teacher I have had at my time at UNC Charlotte. He always comes to class ready to teach and crack some jokes along the way. Take his course!

The reviews speak for themselves. Dr. Miller is hilarious and passionate about what he teaches, and he makes normally dry-sounding lectures like exchage rates and trade policy hilarious and interesting to listen to. I looked forward to his class every day, and strongly recommend that you take him at least once if you have the chance!
Dr. Miller is a great professor.  The class is lecture style with weekly quizzes which are easy and weekly packbacks which are also very easy.  I loved this class and I love this professor.

10/10, amazing professor. I've taken his courses for 3 years. Only drawback is that he speaks in a very advanced way. Dr. Miller is an amazing teacher. I recommend taking a class with him. He uses PackBack and quizzes mostly, which neither are difficult.
Professor Miller was very engaging with his material and always knew the topic at hand. Expert in his field and was always able to answer any questions you needed answers to.

You need a professor like Dr. Miller in your life. You will feel smarter after taking his class; he is the kind of professor that could explain calculus to a toddler. The requirements for everything are objective and precise- what you see is what you get. There's not too much work, but tests are almost everything in this class (the tests are fair).

Professor Miller is one of the best instructors I have had in my time at UNC Charlotte. Every single one of his lectures was incredibly interesting, he spoke loud and clear always and was never monotone, and he was hilarious, keeping the entire class engaged. The class itself isn't that hard, and if you put the effort into it, you should do well.

I have taken many classes with Dr. Miller, all of them have been really great. This class was a little harder to understand because of how philosophical it was but even if I did not understand the concepts deeply, his assignments were heavily based on you taking a stance and being able to support it with evidence so you can still do well.

Professor Miller is a great teacher. Only three essays throughout the course and weekly quizzes/packbacks. He seems to use packback in most of the courses he teaches. This is the first class of his that I have taken completely online and I honestly recommend taking him in person instead of online so you can know how funny he is.

Dr. Miller is the MAN. He's a great teacher and a great dude. I loved his class, extremely informative and he made it all so easy to understand. Every time I see him out of class I say hello. He is friendly, understanding, and a very clear grader. He has set deadlines, and his work is not too hard.

I was forced to take this class due to there not being many classes available . He NEVER stops talking about the books he writes and if you want a good grade on his test ( which make up your entire grade) you have to buy it and reference it to get a good grade.

Whoever decided to give this man, a self-proclaimed Luddite, an online-only course is cruel. He's knowledgeable, but rambles a ton about his book and predictions he got wrong. Online class. Every class consisted of at least 2 lectures. Randomly assigned group topics that consist of a powerpoint presentation that the group shares on a specific date and a 4 page paper. 3 tests that are all essay formatted exams and you have to read his books as textbooks.

Don't expect anything that makes logical sense in this class. Rubrics don't provide a substantial reference to correlate to his exams. He keeps pushing you to buy his book by referring to it at least twice a lecture. Communication outside of lectures can be inconsistent and unreliable.

I do not recommend taking this class for any individual that enjoys just a small bit of clarity and coherence in their lives. Took an online class with him, and he was very difficult to understand he also wouldn't stop talking about his book, I dropped the class because I couldn't learn or understand him.

He is not too difficult but if you have ADHD or struggle to listen I would suggest another class. I have personally had a hard time focusing. He takes 3 tests for a grade and that's it. You also have to do a group project that is random. Its not been my favorite class but its okay
Only mf I know who drops your grade after all exams are in lol not even worth showing up to the boring lectures. get your sleep kings

Very unclear grading criteria.  You had to answer her questions exactly as she herself would.  My mind felt terribly constrainedd by her rigidity.  Did not respond to emails.  Very slow in grading.  A frustrating, pointless experience.
Engaging lectures, all tests and quizzes are online outside of classroom, posts lecture slides, open note exams, very nice lady.
Like all my peers' reviews previous. She should improve more about her teaching styles, engagement, and material.

A lot of reading and independent work in the online class. Not terrible, but no interaction with other students at all. She is very nice and incites meaningful discussions, but there were little things about this course that made it more difficult than it had to be. Attendance is mandatory and you get no leeway. My class was a hybrid course. We had homework due Tuesday, and sometimes Thursday at 9am, which is such a weird and random due date time. She never responded to my emails, even though I provided her with the prompt that she asked for for emailing her.
I took this class online, and it was great. The lectures were great, but you could still do well even if you didn't go. She also offers up to 8% extra credit.
Pretty easy overall and good online class to take as the slides are easy to look over and answer quiz and exam questions with, as they are all open note.

Dr. Dai was an amazing prof, I loved her. Super easy, gives a lot of EC, and is really understanding. Tests are open-note online (no lockdown browser). Dr./Prof. Dai is great, not to mention, super nice, I also appreciate her availability regarding office hours, and of course, her willingness to answer questions. I wish more post secondary educators were like her, she truly wants us (students) to succeed, I'll always view her as a role model.
She is so sweet however, her lectures make absolutely no sense. I never went to her class because the material was easier to understand if i taught myself.

Tests and assignments are worth a TON, they are open book and notes, but it is not as easy as just using an AI or googling. Less than 7 assignments a year, so you cannot miss any. Attendance is not mandatory, so you don't need to go to class, and you can treat it like an online course, but you cannot get behind.

A little difficult of a class in itself but professor laid everything out extremely well and made sure students were able to get any help needed when needed. Would recommend this professor to everyone. She is wonderful.

love the professor, indifferent toward the class. the tests are open note and open textbook and open google, but that doesn't help that much. you really have to attend the lectures. but basically no assignments and basically no effort required, just participation
Yes. Yes. Yes. Take her class.

Dr. Dai is an outstanding professor who really cares about her students. I have listened to her handle disrespectful students with class and grace. Amazing professor, I have taken many classes with her. Her rate my professor score should be 5/5. Anyone who gives her anything lower honestly lacks common sense. She is the gold standard of a professor.
Dr. Dai is a professor that I wish taught higher-level classes. Her class is easy to get an A in as long as you attend the lectures/labs and do the quizzes.
