Don't listen to people who put bad reviews about him. They didn't put the effort or just goofed around the class. He's the best teacher ever. Please take him

Let me start off with that I was absolutely miserable in this class. The grade system is not based on completion but on effort. It sounds good on paper but for example you completed a "bundle D"  (these could be 600 word posts) that you didn't get a 100% on, you would automatically fail have a D for the entire semester if you don't use a token.

Prof. B. uses a grading system that is intended to filter out students at levels of effort. As long as you show up & do assignments to a sufficient degree of quality (at times allowing re-do's) you are guaranteed an A. He also encourages unbiased in-class discussion encouraging students to think deeper. 350 ch. can't convey how great Prof. B. is.

the grading system is actually aids, its based on a bundle system and if you miss one assignment per say on the B bundle, you can't get above a c in the class. so your canvas grade could say 89.9 like mine but nah I missed one assignment and boom I get a permanent C. L class do not take unless you want to have anger take you over.

unclear grading criteria that will make you repeat assignments multiple times(on assignments that already take upwards of an hour) don't take this dude unless you want to deal with an annoying high pitched voice that makes you do writing assignments for 4 hours every monday

The course was very difficult to comprehend and grasp onto the material as none of his notes were as helpful as they should have been. His grading system didn't make any sense to me in my personal opinion as it's not traditional. If you're looking for a math credit and need a Philosophy Deductive Logic course, please do not sign up for this one!

Could not choose PHIL3251 but I took that. Totally unclear grading, my group members didn't do anything and I got no compensation. Insulted me and told me I 'didn't try hard enough' when I asked for an extra credit opportunity to make up for my group members. I'm a double major psych/phil and this is the only non-A I've gotten between both majors.

This class was asynchronous and super easy. He is an extremely caring professor who has a token system where you can redeem a token to exempt yourself from an assignment. The work is super easy and you meet once a week to do an easy group assignment but all of the online work is super simple.

Please, please, please listen to the reviews. Avoid this professor at all costs. Your grade is entirely made up of your 'group mates' determining whether or not you were helpful in class. He also assigns confusing work and makes you do it all outside of class and then won't give you any information on what you did wrong.

At the time, I was an RA, participating in two research projects & completing an intense internship. After the drop/add, I had a fairly shocking family matter come to light-I asked to drop late since this was an extra class. Answer=nope. GPA went from 3.8 to 3.57. He loves to hear himself talk, but the lectures do not relate to the work/tests.

Dr. Sullivan was a super great professor! The class was interesting, but the books were very boring. There are pop quizzes and for Friday classes participation and attendance is graded, can only miss 2 classes. There was no work to do outside of class, but if you like reading older texts, this is a class for you!

Dr. Sullivan was a super great teacher who cared about her students. She would give a lot of pop quizzes, but they are pretty much common sense and super easy if you do the readings. The TAs are also wonderful and super helpful.

dont miss classes like i did or you might end up missing a quiz. participation isnt mandatory but there are risks like missing a pop quiz. overall she's a very engaging and funny professor. took her super early in the morning but was still able to pay attention because of how engaging her lectures are. doesnt allow make ups.
Her course was very interesting, and the tests were very simple. The workshops helped a lot. I would recommend this as a fun theme course.

Professor Sullivan is great and I would highly recommend her class. There were pop quizzes 1-2 times a week on the reading but they're only 3 questions and super simple and basic (don't rlly have to do the reading). She goes over everything in detail and makes it easy to understand. Get an automatic 50 on exams just for showing up.

Easiest class and professor I've ever taken. Graded on 4 tests (80%) and attendance (20%). Attendance was only taken 1x per week on discussion days (I never showed and still got a B). The tests are 12 questions, 50 points for showing up, and 5 per easy multiple choice questions for a total of 110 points, you can get two wrong and still get 100.
I had him for American democracy and it was the easiest an ever. he wants his students to do well and this is an incredibly easy course. take him!

I would not recommend this class to my worst enemy. I am a straight A student and received a C in this class. It's a textbook-heavy class, but his textbook doesn't help. I don't think he would be a bad professor for an in-person class, but he is not suited to be an online professor. This class was a nightmare.

He's very nice and wants to help you. Good professor, it was the content that was really hard to grasp. Just make sure you keep up with the deadlines and do NOT procrastinate. My main criticism is the ridiculous time limits for tests. One of them you had 30 seconds per question. I felt if I had a little more time, I would've done well on them.
The material was hard but the class was great. As long as you study and use the quizzes for practice, you'll be golden.

The class was very easy but insightful. Theres a quiz and a discussion every week but very easy. Make sure to go over whats in the module. He creates note sheets for the articles. If you do not submit on time he gives full credit. The midterm and final are harder than the coursework. There is also a final paper that is fairly simple. Def reccomend.

Good professor and easy to contact outside of class. If you need help or an extension he is available. Took this course over the summer and found that the really outdated software used was very inconvenient. I struggled to understand the topics and found them difficult, even after studying. Make sure you READ and do the practice problems provided.

Probably the most painless class I have ever done at UNCC. There are quizzes with answers online and video forums that are due along with a 5-page paper. He lets you turn it in all at the end of the semester with no late penalty. I basically did all of the class in one day at the end of the semester and got an A. The midterm & final is curved.

Very flexible professor! The content of the class can get a bit confusing since its about software and digital ethics. Online class but you do have video forums that are due about every week. Readings and notes to go along but they are complicated readings so beware! A little more effort is definitely needed even though it is an online course.

Professor Riley is always available, even at odd times of the night, for help and feedback and accepts late work starting in the second half of the semester. He's very accommodating, probably because he uses literally decades-old applets for majority of assignments. If you don't have access to Chrome or a Chrome extension, do NOT take this class.

Professor Riley is such a nice guy. He is so understanding and will work with you on due dates if needed. He really cares about his students and even gives out his phone number. I didn't love the short amount of time given on tests, just because it made me feel way more stressed. Make sure to reach out to him if you're struggling.

I had PHIL2105 online and it was great. There are a few participation assignments and then we spent the whole semester constructing one paper. THATS IT! At times the paper could be stressful like any but he is available through email with any questions. You need to buy the books but you don't have to read everything only when needing specifics

I took this as a MATH credit . I had no idea what I was getting into. But his textbook breaks everything down perfectly you just have to TAKE YOUR TIME &READ!!! The weekly assignments are good once you understand concepts. I would take again for sure. He was very patient and was easy to reach and responsive throughout the semester.

He's very friendly and definitely has an engaging teaching style, but doesn't give much constructive feedback and is a bit soft/lenient. Good if you want a very chill professor, but not if you want to learn a lot and have your ideas challenged.

Dr Sanders has nice lectures and can be funny. But.. there was never a syllabus for the final papers and the group project guidelines kept changing very close to the deadline. The lack of organization was stressful. However, the class was easy, Dr Sanders is chill if you respect him and participate.

Dr. Sanders is a great professor of philosophy. His classes are fun and encourages participation. There were a couple of papers and group projects that required a lot of readings. His lectures were sloppy. He seemed like he was teaching on a whim and that's how the class felt. Very go with the flow.

People rating him low are soft, if you dont do the readings and dont put in effort it will reflect. The only assignments were 2 papers and some smaller things in between. The papers are graded pretty tough but if you actually try you will be fine.

Dr. Sanders was one of the best professors I've had in a while. His classes are fun and he cares a lot about his students' success. Only two big papers and a few short paragraph assignments. There was also one big project towards the end of the class but it was also very easy. Take his class!!

He's the reason I added Philosophy as a major! It's clear he actively applies the philosophies he agrees with by emphasizing discussion rather than tests, making it fun to comb out abstract concepts. If you know how to write, even just decently, and are open-minded, you're good. (& the cough drops are barely noticeable idk y people r being mean)

He is a very clear speaker except when he lectures with cough drops in his mouth which sounds disgusting. He changes his deadlines and syllabus a lot which is annoying. His instructions are always super vague, he gives meaningless feedback. His work isn't too hard, but how poor the instruction is makes it almost not worth it.
Interesting class. two short papers, two other relatively easy assignments, and one 6-8 page final paper.  Tough grader but gives explanatory feedback.  Would take a class with him again.

Lectures are class discussions on somewhat interesting topics. Very few assignments you have to do. He likes to give lectures with candy in his mouth; it gets annoying. Takes FOREVER to grade assignments. No rubric on what he's grading for, just grades on the whim. Impossible to get in contact with through email. No real guidance on group projects.
He gives little to no guidance, never provides rubrics, and gets defensive if you challenge his ideals.
This guy loves his job and is very passionate about what he does and it's obvious. Show up to class and do the QPP's and you'll definitely end up with an A.

Professor Pearce is very easy-going and laid back. He is very nice, teaches his lectures well, and is eager to teach his lectures. His grading system is perfect because the exams are 20% worth your grade, but so is the homework and the rest. If you turn in all your homework with a passing grade, you get an easy A within the class.

This class was honestly a great class to take as an elective, the workload was not heavy and that matters to a stem major who already gets a lot of homework. He is also understanding and will work with you.
he is a fine professor the class is just kind of boring. not really his fault i guess but if you are really intrested in the subject he would be great.

I only took this class as I needed a global theme. His lectures are very interesting if you enjoy Asian philosophy. Even if you don't enjoy philosophy like me, his class is very easy to pass and the Friday breakouts you just have to participate in quick talking to pass.

Nothing bad to say about this professor. You can tell that he is passionate about what he teaches and the lectures are actually somewhat interesting. He is understanding and helpful. I would reccommend.

I took AMST 4050 in Spring 2023 w/ Dr. Pearce and I loved it! Every day, we had deep discussions about Alain Locke's (Father of the New Negro & Harlem Renaissance) readings & other related readings. Assignments: Two papers, 1-page summaries for each class, and attendance. Can be picky about grading on papers but if you work with him you'll be fine.

Incredibly passionate professor who clearly understands what he is talking about. Lots of reading and summaries are randomly taken up. The only thing I didn't like about this professor was that his lectures were a bit confusing, although this kind of comes with the territory in Philosophy. Papers are tough to write but there are only two.

The effort you put into this class is what you get back. However, he is a VERY flowery speaker and gets caught up in his own thoughts sometimes while trying to talk in class. The works you'll read use heavy academic language so be prepared to take 1hr+ to do the readings. Class is also discussion-based, so be ready to talk every class session!!
Is available and supportive outside of class. But grading and comments are very vauge. He looks for a lot in weekly summaries. Either hit or miss
Weekly reading with summaries, 1 narrative/presentation, and final paper. Is available outside of class. method of grading/feedback can be vague

Only had 2 classes with him. I followed my instincts to GTFO! He lacks the ability to use technology. Couldn't even TURN ON the projector the first day, assignments on Canvas were always messed up, talked THE WHOLE LECTURE TIME. He's nice but BORING and the final straw was when 11 people dropped the class in one day. I felt my GPA was in danger.
Dr. Souffrant was not a very good teacher. I highly recommend avoiding him. He does not have a clear grading criteria. He is difficult to have discussions with and interrupts constantly.

Unclear grading system and tends to be lost in his own opinions. Expects you to read and then teach the class for your group project. Weekly assignments are based on lengthy reading and his grading comments can be condescending. Cannot respectfully debate.

One assignment per week but asks you to cover 30 pages in 250 words and may mark down if you go over. The zoom is just making pointless illustrations. Bad grading criteria (no numeric grades). AVOID, he talks respectfully but is not accomodating and thinks only he is right and wont regrade. Not a good look for the department.
He grades too harshly on essays and discussion boards. There are so many long essays and textbooks to read with lots of pop quizzes. It is a tough class and a hard concept to grasp.

Easy A. Just be present. Class was 2 hrs 15 mins but she always ended class early. No final, just a paper/PowerPoint/podcast. You have options. I did the 5-page paper. Super understanding. Class bored me a ton but it only bored me a lot because the people in the class were dry. HW is just 10-page readings.

Hands down one of the best professors I've had in a while. She makes learning contagious. If u show up, youll get an A. She says from the very beginning, "I'm not here to trick u or fail u. I want you to get an A", and I'll say shes a woman of her word. Of all the students who don't walk away with an A, its due to their own lack of accountability.

I highly recommend Professor Ritterskamp as a teacher. She is extremely accommodating and approachable, making the class easy to pass. The workload primarily consists of light reading and group discussions to review the weekly chapter. Overall, it's an interesting and simple course that I would recommend to anyone.
Just show up. Easy A+

As a senior, she is one of my fav professors at UNCC. Class is super easy and straightforward. Skim through the reading, take the 2 question quizzes every class & then a 1 page, hand-written journal at the end of class. Really easy-going and open-minded. Do a PP with a voiceover instead of the paper at the end of the semester, way easier.

Very accommodating professor. Every class begins with a reading quiz, so textbook matters, and ends with a journal entry that has to be roughly a page long. She's also principled in avoiding the use of "us vs them" rhetoric in her class as she pulled someone out of the class because of it. Good professor

The only thing you have to worry about is showing up to class on time for the quizzes. She's very nice and understanding and is always willing to make accommodations for students. GREAT PROFESSOR, easy A.

If I could recommend anyone at UNCC take one professor, it would be Prof. Ritterskamp. It is incredible how you learn in this class without having to put in strenuous amounts of work. Not only is class easy, but it is enjoyable, and I looked forward to it every week.

Only graded on 3-4 tests (I don't remember), so study! Tests are based on what she says in class and the notes. There is two extra credit assignments for 3 points each, but one is like 2 paragraphs and the other is like 6 pages. Also 2 extra credit questions were test. She really knows what she was talking about and it was an interesting class.

Avoid this class if you want an easy elective. The prof is passionate and knows her stuff, but tests are based on what she says in lectures and not what's on the slides, so attendance is a must. Grades come from 4 tests and 2 all-or-nothing extra credit assignments. Guest speakers and the documentaries were a highlight.

The teacher is nice and respectful, but I didn't like the class much, it was SK. There was 4 test and each has 2 points extra credit paragraph you can do. The presentation ar really disorganized and so hard to study.
Only has four grades. TESTS, I hate it but I like the professor. Shes respectful and knows what shes talking about. if you are a good test taker, you should take her!
Entire class based off of four tests. Only extra credit assignment seems to intentionally have a weird due date. Professor claims that class cannot be passed unless you attend every lecture.

This class is extremely challenging for what it's worth. This was supposed to be a free A elective, but instead, due to the 4 tests being the only grades, it wasn't. This professor seems to enjoy the failure of her students, and it's truly disheartening.

She is a sweet woman and is passionate about the class. You're graded on 4 tests alone. She provides 2 extra credit assignments but is a tough grader on them. No late work is accepted, and no partial credit is received either. Overall, the class is fairly easy, you just have to show up to class and take notes. Lots of memorization!!

Dr. Coston is a great professor! All her lectures were really interesting and she is passionate about what she teaches. My only complaint about this class is that it's graded based on the four tests you take throughout the semester with little to no extra credit and other assignments to back you up if you bomb one, hence why my grade dropped.

Dr. Coston is a great professor! Her lectures were very informative and she is very passionate about the subjects she teaches. My only complaint about this class is how your grade is based on only the 4 tests you have throughout the semester, with no other assignments to back you up if you bomb one of them like I did. Great class overall though!

Dr. Coston is a great professor. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but the tests are dependent on what she says in class. You will want to take a LOT of notes on essentially everything she says. However, as long as you study your notes, you will get an A in her class. She also brings some guest lecturers and puts on interesting documentaries.

If you attend class, it is very easy. While she does provide a copy of her slideshow, attending the lecture and taking notes is important to succeed, as she often "fills in" areas of the notes in class. You get a PDF copy of the textbook, but the questions are solely from the lectures.

Professor Coston is very knowledgeable and makes the lectures engaging. With only 4 exams as the grades, the class is manageable if you attend and take good notes. unstuck ai was super helpful for test prep.

Honestly, if your not good at tests, steer clear of this professor. I got a 74 on the first test and I was trying to get my grade up the entire semester. ONLY 4 TESTS, NOTHING ELSE. There was one extra credit assignment at 11:59 am instead of pm, and I missed it because I read the time wrong. Take a weekend to study for the test, u need the grade.

Good prof! I like that she doesn't use a txtbook & brings in guest speakers & shows films in class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you should go to class bc your only grades are 4 exams. As long as you go to class and study the material you will do great. Dr. C is very knowledgeable. She will go over what you should study.

Only grades were the 4 unit tests. Every test had an extra credit question and she gave multiple other extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Many guest speakers spoke with the class that were very interesting. Professor heavily knows the information she is teaching and is very willing to answer all questions.

This class wasn't too difficult overall, but your grade is determined by just 4 tests. The test questions can be very specific, so make sure to pay attention closley during the lectures. She does review classes that tell you what will be on the test and goes over the entire unit in depth. The first few weeks, she will let you go early most classes.
She was a great teacher but the only grades for this class is tests. They are 100% off the slides which she goes over in class (they are also posted in canvas).

A very caring and nice prof, class is a lot of memorization but as long as you have notes the tests are pretty easy. She is a great teacher with lots of experience. Thought it would be a boring elec. class but was actually interested in what we learned. P good communication, and made mistakes with the tests a lot but she would fix it quick

Dr. Coston is an amazing professor that knows what she's talking about. She works in the criminal justice field and her lectures are interesting and keep you engaged. The class itself is not too hard but it's a lot of information to remember so pay attention during review. She also tends to make some mistakes on tests but gives points back for it.

Professor Coston was pretty good, she was thoughtful into all of her work and truly knew what she was talking about. The only down-side to this class is that we only have tests, there are no other assignments to boost your grade so you need to study, but as long as you review the presentations you should be good.

Online course that consist of four exams and one final presentation. The first exam will be due about a week and a half after the first day of class. You have to read two books for the first three exams and test four is an essay question. I managed to pass the class with a B and didn't do much of the reading but that might not work for you so......

Professor Coston is a phenomenal professor and an expert in the Criminal Justice field, her lectures are engaging and entertaining (also easy to understand). However, her notes are purely based on the lectures, and (given this was an online course), the test questions would be out of order (they were shuffled on each persons test). Overall, 8/10.

Very friendly and knowledgeable woman. Lectures could be boring sometimes, but overall they were entertaining, and the information was fascinating. The only graded things were tests, but an extra credit assignment was offered. Multiple guest speakers that had a lot to share and gave a lot of insight into CJUS.

Professor is engaging with some opportunists to go experience things haven't done before. I was nervous about assignment, but see why she made us do it. She does some cool easy class opportunities so u have to go to class. Prof Harmtna makes class easy to talk about hard topics. She does a good job of listening to all sides and knows her stuff.

The best professor in the CJUS Major. Incredibly helpful to all students. Class was organizes really easy to understand but still was challenging. I liked I could discuss things in more depth than other classes. I can recommend to go to the lectures there is participation grade and make note cards for exams. You will learn life long stuff.

I'm sure Hartman is great, but she should NOT be holding online classes. All semester, it seemed she had no idea how to operate Canvas without constant typos, miscommunications, and unclear instructions. It is VERY reading-heavy, and there are several written assignments; I've been told she doesn't require this of in-person sections, though

Prof Hartman is engaging and knowledgeable. While the class has a lot of work, she provides helpful feedback. I found Unstuck AI and the free textbook to be great study aids alongside the lectures. Overall, a challenging but rewarding course.

It took a bit for me to engage with Professor Hartman, but once I did I like her style. She is a good teacher who is VERY passionate about equal justice for all, especially marginalized communities. Goes over American histroy of how we got to today in the US. Also learned about masculinity and patriarchy. Online course w lots of content but was ok.

Its lots of material to cover. Online so recorded lectures and lots of powerpoints. Four exams, lots of quizzes and writing stuff.  Grading was fine. Best part is prof hartman made herself available to answer questions. Not an easy grade but i did learn some stuff.
Accessible outside of class and has been supportive

Took as summer class because I need class for my major. Don't like onine classes, but she made it ok. I guess. Prob would have given more stars if we were in person. Online did let me keep my job, so I did like this option. A few tests, but you drop worse one. Some writings but have had worse graders. I do like she gives written feedback.

Prof Hartmanis engaging and knowledgeable on the topic, Gender, Race & Justie. Great teacher, class should be required for all CJ majors. All of the books where pretty amazing. Best part was being encouraged to ask questions about race, gender issues that I would never bring up in another class. Class changed by mind on a lot of things. Take it!

He is genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had. I loved going to his class. He was knowledgeable and funny, and made lectures entertaining. Take good notes and make sure to read the book as tests come from the book but they are fairly easy. I would definitely recommend Dr. Mckee to anyone who wants to take Criminal Justice.

Genuinely one of, if not my favorite professor. He is funny in class, you get opportunities for extra credit, he is great at teaching the material, he fosters an open learning environment, and he tries to connect with his students. His office hours are also very productive.  DO NOT TAKE IF:  you hate fun,  you hate this review,  you are a bum
Great professor, always made the class very fun and interesting even at 9am! Attendance is not mandatory but he gives extra credit for attendance randomly so go to class.

Amazing professor. Lectures were very entertaining. Talked slowly enough to take notes on everything. Everything on the exams is from the lecture slideshows. He gives you a study guide that is exactly like the test. Gives random extra credit quizzes, and you get one extra credit point just for being there. 100% take this class.
Super funny and a great lecturer.
Not a bad teacher at all, just didn't have assignments, so if you do badly on your exams, you won't do well in the class.

Professor McKee is good. He keeps his lectures fun and engaging, and teaches well. However, the class only has 3 tests, the first being the worst. He doesn't post slides on canvas so attendance is needed but not mandatory. Pop quizzes are also very common, but only for extra credit
Great professor! Just make sure you show up to lectures as most of the information from notes are on exams. Probably one of my favorite professors. Course was super interesting too!

Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but you pretty much need to show up if you want a good grade. He keeps the class fun, interesting, and engaging. There are readings, but I never did them, prolly could've gotten an A if I had. Sometimes class is canceled so we can watch a short film or documentary, which is nice. PowerPoints are NOT posted.

Great professor. Attendance is not mandatory, but he doesn't post the slides on canvas so it is highly recommended to show up. He is really funny and I find the lectures interesting. In my opinion the tests were not hard, as long as you read the textbook and take notes during class.

A discussion every 3 weeks in person, three total tests, and a couple other grades. He gives a lot of extra credit. He also makes lectures very entertaining to the point that I don't even understand why people skip! This a need to take a professor especially for a gen ed.
He's absolutely hilarious! Great and interesting class! The only real grades are the tests and there aren't many of them. DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE THE FIRST TEST!

I truly enjoyed his class so much. He's very funny and it's easy to get a good grade in this class as long as you keep up with the lectures and textbook. While attendance wasn't mandatory there would be discussions that you had to be present for but he would let us know when those would be beforehand. I loved being his student!

He gives no assignments so if you do bad on the exams you're pretty screwed and have nothing to fall back on. He tries to be funny in class and keep it interesting but there is nothing on his canvas and doesn't allow you to have access to anything he shows in class. If you are a good test taker you would be good but if not I don't recommend him.
really funny and cool professor ! 4 tests and 4 discussions, no assignments so you have to do really good on them. attendence isnt mandatory but his lectures are very very important to be there for.

Dr.Mckee is a good professor. His lectures are kind of boring but he does his best to make them funny and interesting. You do have pop quizzes - there not terrible if you pay attention and read the book, and they count as extra credit and attendance. He does talk alot but also likes to make discussions engaging.

Professor McKee is a good professor. He gives great lectures and is pretty funny. However, even though attendance is not mandatory if you don't show up to class and if you don't read the textbook you will have a hard time. This class is built up of 6 discussions, 3 tests, & 1 paper so each assignment is crucial.

Professor Mckee is a very cool teacher. Has a lot of stories about his life that relate back to Criminal Justice and is so laid back that he doesn't really care much if you study or not. Very simple rules in his classroom no disruption, don't ask for extra credit, and if you know that you can't show up don't. Very simple rules and cool to talk to.
Best professor in the department by far. His lectures are actually interesting and he's super chill. You'll learn a lot and have fun while in his class.

Very straightforward professor. Hard class, and you need to find your way of studying the material, or you will struggle. He is available to help, but you have to reach out. Lectures are long, so finding what is important is essential. Not an easy class at all, but it could be worse. I would recommend him to anyone who needs this class

He is an amazing professor. The class is very interesting and he gives great lectures. Make sure to be in class because he doesn't post lectures anywhere, but if you come to class and read the textbook and pay attention you will be fine in his class. The course is test heavy but you should be fine if your paying attention and doing the work!

Class consists of weekly 2-question quizzes and 1 major paper, along with exams throughout. The exams are an EXACT COPY of the lectures and the textbook. Whatever you do, make sure to read the textbook as it sneaks up on you on the exams. Professor McKee is hilarious and very engaging, so the lectures are entertaining at the very least.

Doesn't have many assignments to grade so if you mess up on a test your grade in this class will not be the best and if you have to miss an exam for whatever reason he will not care, Ego is thru the roof with this guy

The professor is super chill. Everything he talked about in the lecture was interesting. Had exams every quarter but he made a study guide. If you pay attention in class and take you will be fine. One final paper at the end and a few videos we watched throughout the semester. It was my first CJUS class, and I would recommend it to others!
Great professor, made class fun. Does not have a lot of grades, end grade mainly reflects test grades.
This guy is awesome. He is super knowledgable, funny, and respectful. Your grade is primarily based on exams, but everything on the exams is clearly in your notes/readings. Highly recommend!

Professor McKee is like no other. He makes the lectures engaging and has great comedic timing. Attendance is not for a grade, but in order to succeed in the class you need to take notes each lecture because they are not posted on Canvas. There are 4 total Exams and 6 Group Discussions that make up the majority of your grade. 10/10 would recommend.
Really funny, pop quizzes and about 3 test during the whole semester, WHAT YOU LEARN IN CLASS WILL BE ON THE TEST, great and simple notes on power points, would take his class again.

He was a great and engaging professor. The discussion are easy points and are actually enjoyable, he gives extra credit opportunities for doing the reading but it doesn't affect your grade if you don't get it, and basically all you have to do is do the reading and show up to class. Attendance isn't required but if you don't go, you won't get notes.

I liked this teacher until the end of the semester. I had been struggling with health issues that resulted in me missing one of his discussions and not doing well on an exam due to being at the doctor and in the hospital. When I emailed him explaining he didn't care in the slightest, implying that I had only emailed him to get a boost in my grade.

He never lets anyone take pictures of his presentations, saying that is his personal property.
