Overall Mr. Petersen is an awesome professor, very laid back, helpful, and up to discussion during class, I highly recommend!

You will need to actually read the textbook and take notes/study to get an A. Exams can be confusing but she will go over them with you after if you ask. You have to show up to class because she does 6 pop quizzes. Overall pretty nice and engaging lectures

She is a nice person but I don't recommend this class. CJUS majors NEED this credit and she makes it very difficult to pass. She does not take attendance, but you have to show up to every class. There is 6 pop quizzes and 2 tests + final exam, and those are the only grades that go in the gradebook! You have to teach yourself from a powerpoint!

Professor Hodge may seem intimidating because of the 8 pop quizzes she gives, but if you pay attention and are actively aware of what's going on in class, then the pop quizzes should be light work. If you're taking her in person, make sure to go. Her lectures are fast but very easy to understand! Trust, she's a nice person and knows how to teach.
Really nice and accommodating. Her class is pretty straightforward. Exams are worth 20% of your grade each but the study guide covers all the material. Final was easy as well.

Professor Hodge makes this class very interesting and adds personal anecdotes to relate theories into real-world scenarios. We had a total of 8 pop quizzes and they were given at the end of class. The tests aren't too difficult if you pay attention in class and study the material. I would take this class again.

I have taken two classes with Professor Hodge and I absolutely love her. Even though the test are on paper, in person, and kind of hard, she does a review class before the test going oven almost everything on the test. If you try you will do okay. Participate in her lectures even though they are not mandatory. The best CJUS teacher I have had.

She is such an amazing professor and an inspiration for women wanting to join the CJ field. This class was really hard, tests are worth almost all of your grade. However I would take her she is such a passionate professor, and she is always there to help you. The material is very memorization-heavy, but it is really interesting.
She is a very good teacher, respectful and fun. Test are really really eassyyyy. As long as you read it and see the PowerPoints you will get 100. She is recommended.

It took me a bit to warm up to Professor Hodge, but once you get used to her she is a good teacher. This class contains a LOT of content, so be ready to STUDY. You're graded on 3 tests (the final is worth 30% of your grade), 13 short response papers, and 2 in class activities. Attendance is not mandatory, but go to class to do better!!!

I found this course challenging primarily because most of your grade is depended on 3 test grades, although you have a 250 word essay each week that doesn't raise your grade but if you don't do it, it tanks it. There is no extra credit, so if you do bad on the first test don't expect to raise your grade!!

Good professor, lectures were interesting. She's very helpful if you have questions about the major. Tests are 50 questions and final is 100 questions. Make sure to study. Textbook provides some extra information, but we really only used it a couple of times in the beginning. It helps with weekly discussion assignments though.

She's a great professor, and you'd love her class. She's very passionate and you can tell she likes what she does. It's interesting but it 's graded by few things and it can be hard to get a good grade if you mess up on 1/3 exams. Final exam is worth 35% of your final grade and it can be stressing. Be ready to read and answer to weekly prompts.

I loved learning about theories and why people commit crime to begin with. The only thing I would recommend is to make sure you really study for the tests, because there are only a few they make up a big portion of your grade. Her lectures are engaging and she connects crim theory to her personal experiences and it keeps the course interesting.

My favorite professor so far. She really knows what she is talking about and makes sure that the class is absorbing the material. You have a 200 word submission every week, 2 tests, and then the final exam. Even though you turn in many short answer submissions, the three tests overall make up about 85% of your grade so really study for them.

Changed majors after taking her class. Little to no real experience in the criminal justice field and spews nonsense in lectures. Most of the class is graded on 3 exams and weekly writing assignments, both of which have no feedback. Take another professor.

Mr. Foushee was an excellent professor who kept me engaged across the entire semester. He talks in a way that's very easy to follow and is very knowledgeable on what he teaches. I always look forward to attending his class, and the tests are open note so it's not too difficult either. Not sure I'd enjoy this class as much without him.

Interesting and engaging lectures. His stories and life experiences are super interesting. Quizzes are an even combination of chapter and slide material. Not a difficult class if you pay attention. Tests and quizzes are on Canvas, no in-person tests.

I would take Professor Foushee again and again. His lectures have a good balance of student engagement and lecture. He does call on students quite a bit, which keeps everyone engaged. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I strongly recommend coming to class because he gives you what he will ask on the exams. He's down to earth and funny as well!

He is hilarious, and his career experience seems to make him great at being comfortable/funny while also knowledgeable. Tests open note/textbook & online. Few assignments overall. Other review/s claim that his bias is noticeable, but I found him to say things that vary all over the place.

Professor Foushee comes off as a genuine and interesting person who does deeply care about the engagement and quality of his class. That said, I found both his lectures and his choice in textbook to be politically biased. Of course, no professor is neutral but more effort should be placed in concealing one's beliefs while teaching criminal justice.

This teacher is amazing! He is actually the funniest professor I have ever had and I would take his class again and again. Class got out early most days and he was engaging! Beware he will call on you randomly with no warning but he is super fun and keeps the class entertaining! He knows what he is talking about with personal experiences too!

The funniest teacher I have ever had. I would take his class again. He interacts with students so if you do not like getting called on do not take the class. But very interactive and entertaining during class. Always an enjoyable class and looked forward to his lectures.

Hes an amazing professor. I had him first semester freshman year and it was a great and interesting class. Its really important to go to lectures because he gives away a lot of answer for the test there so please go!! But hes funny, down to earth, always willing to help, and the tests are sooo easy. U should def have an A at the end of the class.

Very funny.  Has lots of real-world experience in the field.  Does a great job of engaging students, even in a 3 hr lecture.  While attendance is "optional" certain test questions come from the lecture, but not the notes.

Loved Professor F. He was understanding, willing to help us with additional understanding of the class material, and hilarious. Grading was fair. We only had quizzes, exams, and a paper. We could use our notes and class resources, making it hard to fail the class. He also rewarded us for being in class because he didn't have an attendance policy

Horrible, the weighting for exams makes everything else irrelevant, as 3 exams make up 85% of the total grade. The lectures are long with boring slides, and he'll scream so much you'll have a headache at the end of them. Lectures are mandatory for test questions that are only understood if you attend lectures. Stay clear of this professor, please.

Attendance is not mandatory but many test questions are said during class so if you miss class you won't do well on tests. Tests also make up most of the total grade at 30% for exam 1 and 25% for exam 2. The tests are not difficult but just missing 1 class impact your grade so severely due to the missed test questions.

He's amazing, the exams are all open note but you have very limited time. The final will not be open note, just pay attention in the class and you will be great. He also does test questions from going to class, so it helps to be there.

Great guy gives very funny lectures and gives interesting, relevant anecdotes. As long as you show up to his classes (which is optional) you get the answer to test questions as a reward. Very easy and engaging class, I recommend studying before tests a bit, as they are reasonably fair difficulty but completely open notes

He's a funny and caring professor. Not much extra credit, but if you try, he'll help. Grading is fair and clear. Attendance isn't required, but he gives test questions and answers in class—get those notes. The essay project is easy. Tests are worth 30% of your grade, so study hard and make sure you do well on them to keep your grade up.

I LOVED this class purely because of the professor. He made the lectures interesting by acting out situations in classes, showing videos, and asking the class things. It's a lot of in-class discussion. Attendance is optional but some questions on the tests are given in person during class. Tests/quizzes are open note, powerpoint, and textbook.

I've taken Professor Foushee twice. He  is a great teacher who cares about his students succeeding. GO TO CLASS, he will literally say what is going to be on the exam you just have to listen for it and it pays off. He will ask you to put away your phone if he sees it, but its because he cares about you passing. He had a great dynamic with students.

Really entertaining guy. Tests are online, there are 3 tests where test 3 is the final and they are open note. Attendance isn't mandatory, but examples that he gives in lectures are like 30-40% of the test, so it's important you go to class. HW every week, but they are easy A's. I learned quite a bit and it's overall a great class for an elective.
He's one of the best teachers I've had so far! He's an interactive teacher and the work itself is not hard as long as you read the textbook.
This class is very easy, as long as you attend class. His lectures are really interesting, there is not a lot of homework, and the tests are open note. I would take his class again.

Grading in this class is very strict, and assignments can take a long time to be returned. Feedback is minimal, so it's not always clear how to improve. Late work is not accepted, so missing even one assignment can significantly impact your grade. Deadlines are often set at 10 PM on Saturdays, which can feel inconvenient.

Every negative review on this site is accurate. I usually try to give professors the benefit of the doubt bc they're people too but she is not a good professor. Our very first paper she accused me of AI, after I proved her wrong I never got another good grade. Will not grade for weeks and you'll never get a chance to improve.

She will not grade your papers for weeks on end but you absolutely can't turn anything in late (it should go both ways) She also has no clear grading criteria, one paper would be up to her standards, then the next wouldn't be. I would avoid her at all costs! She ruined this class for me, I really wanted to enjoy it. I suggest taking ANYONE ELSE

Her grading essay criteria is vague, and has it set up to where a "regular" score is a C; if you are an average A student expect a C or D. She never gives a good scale of expectation and takes off points for little things she never mentions before. She is condescending in her email replies. Six weeks behind on grading is unacceptable!

Your only assignments are essays due each week based on websites she links. It's really not hard, but don't expect to ever actually get a perfect score on anything or actual feedback on what's wrong. Always a couple points off for unnecessary things. Unreachable for grade updates. Refuses late work and is currently 6 weeks behind on grading.

Only take this class if you are an expert paper writer. Otherwise you will not pass with the grade you want. This was an easy class but she grades so harshly and will not accept anything late even though she herself was late to upload assignments and grade them..I probably won't see my final grade till next year I'm sure. She's kind of the worst.

She uses vague instructions and expects you to be an expert in this INTRO class. She also doesn't grade until the very last week of the course, so you don't know if you're doing well or not. I was stressed because I realized I was doing an assignment wrong in the last week, and it was too late because she doesn't grade anything!! Gives NO feedback.

Do NOT take this professor under any circumstances. She requires her assignments to be turned in on Saturdays at 10 pm every Saturday. She grades weeks behind and deducts major points regarding criteria that she didn't ask for. She is one of those professors who looks for anything wrong with your assignments, simply so she can take off points.

The coursework was easy, just a discussion board + one quiz per chapter. She's very slow at grading. During the final week, there were still a majority of my assignments that hadn't been graded. Despite what many say, she is nice if you turn in your work. I submitted my signature assignment in the wrong format and she still gave me partial credit.

This class wasn't difficult but it isn't something to put off. Professor Guido is clear with assignment instructions and has the same assignment layout each week. 1 quiz that corresponds with the chapter reading and a chapter writing assignment. All work is based off the textbook so it is required. Work isn't hard but they are due Saturday at 10pm.

Never in my life have I received below a B in a Criminal Justice class. This professor is so clearly desperate to prove that her life means something. Miserable people such as Jeri Guido should not be eligible to teach a course at this school.

Very unhelpful throughout the semester, did not grade assignments in a timely manner. Assignments are due at inopportune times, usually Saturday at 10PM. Final paper is open ended and simple but was posted with a vague rubric, and was graded harshly without any specific feedback provided. Not a good teacher or considerate person.

Horrible teacher. I pulled off a good grade in the class by the grace of god, but this teacher is absolutely someone who peaked in high school and takes it out on her students. Extremely harsh grading for a class people take for a GPA boost. Jeri Guido should no longer be a teacher at UNC Charlotte if her sole purpose is ruining GPAs.

What an atrocious woman. Quite obviously wants her students to fail and makes it very obvious. I needed an 85 on my final paper to make a B in the class and she gave me an 84 despite directions being followed and points being met. She also refused to round up my 79.9 to a B. Left a comment saying she owes no explanation for how she graded it.

(CJC212) I've been at CPCC for 2+ yrs; I have 60+ credits; I'm a straight  A  student; this is my fifth CJ class. Professor Guido did not grade homework till the end of the semester. It was impossible to know how you were doing/what she wanted with the homework. She gave little to no feedback on assignments. Overall, poorly structured, poorly ran.

This professor has no respect for students, their time, or their situation. Attempting to turn in late work is like pulling teeth even if it's within an hour of the due time. This professor purposely sets her due date to be Saturday at 10 PM which tells you everything you need to know about her thoughts on students and their lives outside of class.

Great Class! I wish she gave online lectures so that you can understand the material better. The assignments consisted of weekly papers on a question related to the court system, if your interested in the legal system it will be super easy. The only issue with this class was the textbook was expensive even to rent, I paid $135 for it on amazon.

I LOVE PROFESSOR GUIDO. I was nervous to take this class after reading reviews, but Guido was an extremely good professor. She gave me timely feedback and I believe her grading to be very fair. The course material was awesome and will help me for the future. As long as you follow the directions and work hard a good grade is easy. TAKE THIS CLASS!
Did not grade anything until the last 2 weeks, easy exams but too harsh on grading papers. The final paper is worth half the points in the class and provided no feedback on the final paper grade.

As I am typing this she is still grading papers a day before they are due last week I had a 97 in her class now I am at a C because she did not grade anything until last minute. Class is easy material is easy quizzes and tests are easy, but the grading for written assignments is the strictest you will ever be.

He's okay... pretty passive aggressive if you email him with genuine questions about the course and the way he has canvas set up. Other then that you probably never interact with him. Take notes on the textbook chapters and you'll get A's on exams. 4 exams, quizzes and some guest speaker quizzes.

Only graded by quizzes, tests, and one extra credit assignment. Does not interact with students at all, and basically relies on the textbook to teach for him. The only time we actually got to hear him say anything was on guest speaker videos, and those were prerecorded in 2020, so even then there is no interaction with students at all.

This class was really easy. Weekly quizzes and guest speaker quizzes which were engaging. No online lectures or videos, so you learn everything from the textbook. There are extra credit opportunities, but this class was an easy A. Final exam is with lockdown browser.

Make sure you have the textbook on hand for all quizzes and tests as these are your only grades. There are lots of guest speaker videos and quizzes which are interesting but not engaging as they are pre-recorded from 2020. Pretty easy A. He gives one extra credit documentary quiz to aid your grade.

He is a very nice and laid back guy. No recorded lectures. The only assignments were exams, weekly quizzes, and quizzes on guest speakers. The guest speaker videos were incredibly interesting and insightful. Exams and quizzes were straight from the book. There are extra credit opportunities at the beginning of the semester and at the very end.

This is a high level class. 3 exams and 1 paper, thats it. Exams are anywhere from 70-150 questions. Professor knows what she's talking about. The class is worth it if you are up for a challenge, and you do learn a lot of interesting things.

This class was interesting but the lectures are very long. She also doesn't post the lectures on Canvas so you have to take good notes. If you don't study you won't do well. The way she words the test questions can be confusing. You have one paper to write on your drug of choice which isn't super difficult, and it can definitely be a grade boost.

Attendance was graded. A great teacher, really funny, and you can tell she knows what she's talking about. There's 1 paper and a few exams. As long as you take good notes, you will be just fine. She does not post her powerpoints so I highly recommend going to class. She will tell you what things on the slides are important to remember for tests.

I am currently in Professor Kocsis' class and it is sadly almost over. She is by far the most articulate, intelligent, and funny professor I have ever had. I highly recommend this class. It is very interesting. As long as you show up and take good notes, you will do great. Her feedback on the paper is extremely helpful.
She's great, if you pay attention you will do well, four exams and one paper. Test questions can be confusing but you should be able to get enough right that it won't hurt you.

She is a great professor, attendance is mandatory but she will keep you engaged. Information is interesting and you will want to go to class to learn more. I have never actually wanted to take notes until this class. Definitely would recommend. She had three tests, one short paper, and no textbook requirement.

One of the best classes offered in the CJUS department at UNCC. Professor Kocsis is extremely engaging and knowledgable, the material isn't difficult to understand and is both entertaining to learn about and extremely informative. Just attend class and study before exams and you'll be perfectly fine; excellent course and excellent professor.

This class was amazing, she is very engaging and you can tell she really cares. There are 3 exams, and one group paper that involves an interview and a presentation but nothing crazy. The class was amazing!!

If you don't actually care about law. and are just looking for an easy class, this class isn't for you. There's a lot of reading but I found most of it interesting and the classes were engaging. Study for your tests way ahead of time and read and you'll be fine

Prof Nicolaides' class was great. I learned a lot, and my passion for, and interest in law intensified. This class is intense, though, and it really feels like "undergrad law school." Come to class, and study for her tests and you will be fine, but you have to be willing to put in effort. She also does a good job of creating a classroom community.

It was a good class. Do not take this if you want an easy A. You have to study hard for every test. You should also go to class every day because she does pop quizzes throughout the semester. There are only a handful of assignments, 3-4 quizzes and 3 tests.

Professor Nicolaides' LEGL1100 class is challenging but engaging. The lectures are informative, and she clearly cares about her students. While the grading is heavily test-based, using Unstuck ai and the course textbook can help you succeed. Overall, a worthwhile class for those interested in law.

I would recommend this class if you are interested in Law. However, I will say that this class was INTRO, and the exams and tests did not seem to be that way. This class only had exams, pop quizzes, and two extra credit opportunities (a total of 10 points worth). The exams, in many peoples opinions, were difficult and graded harshly.

Professor Nicolaides is one of the best professors I've had. Her lectures are engaging and informative. She's very prepared for class. Be prepared though, your grade is based off of 3 or 4 quizzes and 3 exams. If you enjoy the legal system and reading, this will be completely worth your time. 10/10 recommend.

If you don't go to class and take notes you won't pass, power points are posted but coming to class is way more beneficial, only graded by a few things so if your bomb something its hard to recover. Go to her office hours she's really nice and so so knowledgeable. Definitely best law professor ever.

I believe that professor Nicolaides does truly care about her students, but her class was very difficult. She was my first C in college, and her grades consist of 3 tests- if you do bad on the first one it is almost impossible to raise your grade. She also provides quizzes for attendance but they do nothing. This is not treated as an intro course.

This entire class is taught by revel. There are no lectures to listen or read. Your grade is composed of revel modules, flipgrid posts, and 2 exams. The modules and the exams are easy, but the grading of the flipgrid videos can be meticulous. She takes off points if your video sounds too "prepared."

I remember taking her class(es) several years ago as a CJ major It took a little to get used to being called out and elaborating on answers, but it sure motivated me to be ready for each lecture! Highly recommend if you excel in critical thinking skills and class participation.
Class was easy but informational. Assignments can be a little confusing at times. Just make sure to really take notes and read the textbook

Usually one assignment a week, 3 exams and a good amount of extra credit opportunities so make sure you do those. Very accessible outside of class and sends emails daily to remind us of assignments coming up. Her assignments require a lot of critical thinking so be mindful that these aren't "easy" assignments. Definitely would take her again

For a completely online class, I absolutely loved it. Professor Bersot makes this class very interesting and the assignments feel very practical. It is a lot of applied knowledge and field practice assignments, actual work you would do in the field of juvenile corrections. If you're not good at online classes I promise this one is worth it!

Im not sure how those kids are getting a's in her class. im an a student but her class is crazy. I think she grades the hardest she can on purpose and does not really try to help you understand. Her instructions are so vague ,seems like a 4000 level course. The kids on here bragging probably dont work and are privileged to only focus on school.

Professor Bersot cares so much about her students.  The content of the course heavily involves critical thinking and the ability to put yourself in professionals shoes.  It was hard work but extremely worth it.  She is a fair professor and I felt I knew her even though it was an online course.

Great professor. She is very reasonable with grading, provides through feedback, and has extra credit opportunities. There are 3 exams that are open book/ open note. The other assignments require citations from the assigned textbooks, so I would suggest buying them.

I have taken two of Professor Bersot's classes and she is definitely one of my favorite professors. She is kind and really cares about her students. She wants you to do well and will work with you. She does recorded lectures and relies on the textbook but assignments are fun! 10/10 recommend to everyone!

You will definitely need to buy the textbook because every assignment requires citations, but you can find it for cheap in many places. The class is actually interesting and her video lectures are great. If you take good and thorough notes on the lectures, you will do just fine in this class. She is very easy to reach by email.

This professor cares about her students and works hard to make sure every student succeeds. If you watch the lecture videos, read the textbook, do the assignments, and try at the tests, you should pass with flying colours. If you ever have a problem or need advice, she will help you the best she can.

After taking her class, I won the lottery and my wife came back to me (Sharon thank you so much for giving me another chance)! In all seriousness, she is an amazing professor. She expects her students to engage with the material and is a strict grader, but she deeply cares about her students and facilitates their success in any way possible.

For your sanity, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Im not sure if bad reviews are not being published or if she suddenly became extremely difficult this semester, but this class is WAY too difficult for a 3000 level course (I am taking 5000 level courses that are easier). Instructions are longer than the actual assignments and she makes the course miserable.

Prof. Bersot is passionate about her field and student learning. Apply the research to do well on the critical thinking responses, discussions, and field application assignments. Do your work with integrity. Follow instructions and feedback to the letter. Brilliant and good conversationalist. One of the best instructors of my academic career.
very kind professor. cares about students mental health. the work is not overwhelming, and grades are fair and justified.

I was dreading taking an asynchronous class, but Prof. Bersot made it a favorite! She does her own lectures, which help break down concepts and research findings. Expectations can be high, but not unreasonable. Feedback is always encouraging. Field assignments and guest speakers (two went to prison as teenagers for murder!) were so inspiring.
great professor. caring. the class is not "easy" per se, but is not much strain for an average student. would take her again 100%.

She was awesome and I enjoyed her lectures a lot especially since it was an online class! The material was super interesting to read and she had a couple of guest speakers come to talk to the class for extra credit opportunities, loved her!

Theres like 10 assignments and some of them really affect your grade. Theres 3 big test, that you have one day to do, and 2 writing assignments. The other small grades barely effect the overall grade after the big ones are due. Prof Duncan is very strict on due dates, but there are opportunities for extra credit on your lowest grade.

You need to read all chapters listed on syllabus & there are weekly 5 question quizzes (are timed for 15 mins; 1 attempt) that are difficult if you don't read. The notes provided in the modules were confusing & missing parts, so you have to take your own to understand the material. There are also two big research assignments, fairly easy.
this professor is headache. she doenst help at all and exams are super hard. does not do any lectures and says to read the book but none of the answers for the exam are in the book. annoying.
SO AWFUL. THE TEXTBOOK PROVIDES NO HELP TO THE TESTS.

Professor Duncan was great at giving clear feedback and grading criteria in order for students to do well on assignments. Her online class was incredibly heavy on tests and quizzes with a few writing assignments. If you do the work, read the textbook, and look at the slide shows, you should get an A or a B. Overall, she did well teaching online.
Great teacher
Assignment were time consuming and codes he provided did not always work.

This was the last course for my degree & when I realized I had to code/use statistics, I freaked. I saw how many assignments he had & the long lectures & I wanted to drop it. But, Dr. DeWitt is hands down an amazing professor. He will help you with any & everything. He is attentive & understanding. It's hard, but manageable since he will guide you.
I would never take another class taught by this professor. He was absolutely terrible. If you can take a different course I WOULD. Your GPA will think you ever. He does not care about your grade.

Hard class, made easier by an awesome professor. The math is not hard, the concept of using it is the toughest part. As someone who has always been bad at math, Dr Turner made it understandable. Work hard and its an easy c+/b, you'll get an A if you really really try.

Dr. Turner is a great professor and wants you to do well in his class, but you have to be willing to put in the effort for this course. As a 4000 level course, and a statistics class at that, the content is naturally going to be difficult. That said, I found that he made the material fairly easy to grasp as long as you take notes and follow along.
One of my favorite professors. If you just listen and follow his instructions you will pass. It is not that hard.
Solid professor super relatable and fun class environment just show up and you will get a easy a
The definition of an easy A.
Absolutely loved taking his class.

Dont take a class with this professor if you want to have a coding assignment on top of a reflection paper with an exam every other week. Data analytics and crime is a 8 week course and no one can learn R studio let alone coding in 8 weeks on top of having a 5 page paper due. He doesnt offer extra credit or any supplemental work to help students.

Professor Jakeway was an absolutely incredible professor! She is very personable and kind, and she clearly cares deeply about her students and the courses she teaches. I highly recommend her to anyone interested in German culture or the German language!
If you guys just attend every class you will definitely get an A+

Prof. Jakeway is AMAZING! She's very understanding. Canceled class multiple weeks: did work from home. Can leave class when done with work. 1 weekly group assignment done in class. no homework or readings. no test or final. Final is group presentation that you work on throughout the semester. flexible with attendance but fun to show up. Easy 100!!

Professor Jakeway is my favorite professor. I've taken many courses with her and she allows you to decide to take a class online or in person depending on your schedule needs. She requires attendance in person but most of your grade is from showing up. Online is a bit more difficult but the assignments are clear.

Professor Jakeway makes this class engaging and fun. The personal insights and cultural comparisons are fascinating. With the help of unstuck study, I aced the course. Highly recommend for anyone interested in German and American cultures.

The BEST professor/teacher I've ever had! Not just in college but my whole life. This class was optional to take in person or online so I chose online. The subject matter was interesting for me because the class was about German culture, laws, and history and I like learning about that. It's literally the easiest class I've ever done. Take her!!

Professor Jakeway is absolutely the best Professor I have ever had. Her class is engaging, the work is simple,  and you can either work by yourself or in a group on assignments.There is no textbook required and you can tell she really cares for her students. If you see a class that she is teaching, register for it immediately! You won't regret it!

This was for AMST:3050. The professor is very understanding of your personal schedule outside of school and is willing to help. Truly cares about her students and seems to care about the topics she teaches. We had to read about 6 books, they weren't too long, and the assignments were easy after reading the material.
Very neutral class since I had it online, but be prepared for LOTS of work and reading each week.

Super easy online class! 2 assignments a week that are either a long reading or documentary. The class is very interesting and graded by multiple choice canvas quizzes or discussions. Midterm is cumulative from class assignments, would definitely take her again!

Took this class as a 6 week summer course and it ended up being a great fit even with a busy schedule.  She posted all the homework for a few weeks at a time so that you could work ahead.  Hardest part was the quizzes due to the small details she would test you on.  Overall I loved this professor and would be happy to have her again.

Dr. Watts was great! Hybrid course so most of it was online and we met IRL once a week. Most of the time IRL was canceled. 2 weekly quizzes (vocab + general chapter) per week based on textbook, and up to 2 discussions a week. Final exam was optional and final project was an infographic. She's very sweet and has good energy. Pretty easy course.

It's easy for an online class. You have to read about five books throughout the semester, with discussion posts every week. The hardest part about this class is reading the pages, but I never exerted a lot of energy on it. I did email her a couple times and she never responded so I'm not sure how accessible she is over email.

Classes are not structured. Hard grader when it comes to exams. Does not grade exams or homework in a timely manner nor gives clear feedback. Did not retain or learn much in the class. Is a super nice professor but needs to have classes structured better with some type of lesson plan. She comes into class and just writes on the whiteboard.

This professor has too much energy at 8 am in the morning. She is a mess every class and nothing you talk about in class relates to the work. All work is done through canvas but her instructions are very vague. Do not expect an email back because she wont answer. Along with grading she takes forever! Would not take her again.
Professor Watts is a great professor, especially with this new course 1512. Prepare to read a lot and to do around 2-3 assignments a week.

Don't relate any in-class work to anything you will do outside of class. You will read 4 books in 1 semester and are forced to read over 100 pages in a short amount of time. A lot of the text is in Spanish but she will not tell you that until after you already receive the texts.

her lectures are pretty different from her modules, her class is very easy, assignments are not difficult, she is super nice, outgoing, and does not make her classroom awkward at all. If you're truly looking to learn Spanish/Spanish culture, choose a different professor, but if you're looking for an easy grade and an easy class, this is for you.

I know 4 other languages so it's kinda easy to learn Italian, some rules/words being familiar. But if languages are hard for you, you might find her too fast and going to need time to study a lot outside of class, especially vocab. There is plenty of practice though and she is engaging, funny and caring. She's understandable and not a harsh grader

Mrs.Rains is an engaging and supportive teacher! This was my most joyful class of the semester and my most smooth experience learning a new language. I am inspired to minor in the Italian language because of her and I highly recommend to her to anyone who wants to learn a foreign language or Italian!! She also has lots of office hours if needed. -M

I was extremely nervous about taking ITLN 1 and 2, but with her it was one of my absolute favorite classes I have ever taken here at UNCC in my 2.5 years here. She was always engaging, and she does not grade harshly. Just show up and show that you care. What matters most to her is showing that you care!!

Be ready to teach yourself a new language. I took her for Elementary Italian 1 and I had to teach myself. We go over things, but very fast, she will barely go back if you ask questions. She speaks very fast and will speak in italian because she expects you to be fluent already. If you ask her to slow down or explain it in english, she won't.

One of my favorite professors ever! She is easy to get along with, willing to talk and extend deadlines. There's a lot of homework, expected for a language course. She's very understanding and loves teaching, making her class memorable for me. 10/10, would recommend.
Very clear professor, gets straight to the point. Follows the textbook, has strict attendance policy. Very kind and keeps class engaged. Just go to class and do the homework and you will pass.

Loved Professor Rains! On test days when I couldn't focus, she let me work in her office. She is very accommodating! Her lectures are to the point, and she also gives several opportunities for extra credit in class and outside of class. If you participate in activities with the Italian club you could get some bonus points on exams!
Doesn't linger on 'useless' topics and gets to the point when teaching. Nice to talk to and keeps lecture interesting enough!!

You'll think you did an assignment right and then he'll take points off, no feedback or anything. It's hard to understand his criteria even though he lists it honestly. 

Do the assignments early and you'll pass with an easy A, just don't expect to gain much from this course in the long run.
Easy class. Do all the assignments and you will do fine. He stopped replying to the last couple of emails I sent though, so if you have pressing questions, I would go to his office hours.
Loved her class getting to go to Paris was amazing! We will miss her!

Mrs. Houston is a fantastic, sweet professor who cares greatly for her students. Class participation is very important, along with online assignments that do not show due dates on canvas (my only issue). She isn't very tech savvy canvas wise but I learned so much and was always happy to go to her class. Easy class, tests are very straight forward

Jane Houston is one of the kindest, most caring professors I have had at UNCC. All of the French professors are amazing, but she really cares about the success of her students and goes above and beyond to make sure you understand the material. Her teaching is straightforward. She is passionate and loves all of her students. Def take her class.

Very sweet professor. I faced some hard time this semester and she helped me a lot and extended some assignments and allow some time for me to return them back. She is so caring and nice. She always smiles and she is not tough grader. If something wrong with your paper she gives you time to work on it !

Professor Houston is so sweet her teaching just isnt up to date. the papers she shows can barely be read by students, even those on the front row. If you listen to what she says, its easy to pass as long as you participate and do well on the papers. the tests will be the most important part of your grade. they are tough and she is a tough grader

if there isnt a different professor for this course, dont take this course. its very unorganized and there is no clear description of what needs to be studied. tourist videos take up most of our class time and its just confusing overall. the papers that are assigned are also not at all relating to the material she is covering at the time.

She is really nice and caring but her class is hard to pay attention to. You are graded on the facts you remember from videos and the textbook. I feel like a lot of her criteria are not clear because she does not post reading assignments online other than the first readings. Her tests are pretty much all open-ended about very particular topics.

Isabelle is amazing. She really cares about her students, and is like a proud mom who just can't get enough of you. She is not a tough grader and gives you credit if she sees you genuinely tried your best. Just a ray of sunshine who wants the best for her class. She's very open to meetings as well, and not hard to get in touch with. She's the best.

This professor is absolutely amazing. Every class she was able to make fun and interesting. I really feel like I learned a good foundation for French. She was also always available outside of class whenever we had a question. Tests also were very easy because she would give us points for trying and translating sentences.

I loved this class; the teacher is very sweet and caring. If you need to take a language course, I would take her class. She is a ray of sunshine, although the lectures are really fast-paced, the professor makes it worth it. One of my favorite professors ever.
She's really nice and easy to talk to. Her class is interesting and you get a lot of practice in class. She's very helpful and not a harsh grader.

If you need to take French, take it with this teacher, I promise you. 10/10 AMAZING!! Her class is engaging and genuinely fun, and her sense of humor makes learning even better. She cares about your success and makes sure you understand the material before you leave. Tests and quizzes are easy IF YOU STUDY. She's one of the nicest teachers at UNCC.
She is so amazing and so caring! I took 1202 and 2201 and they were so easy!
She is an amazing teacher and makes learning French super fun. She is always willing to help you, too!
If you ever need to take a french class, this is the professor you want. She is one of the nicest people I have ever met, and makes class very easy if you do the work.

Love her! She was super amazing and helpful. I'd highly recommend her. Even though our class was an 8:30, she still made it fun! If you have any questions she's always quick to help and will stick with you to make sure you understand. The homework was pretty easy and the reviews for the exams were 10/10. Take her class if she's available. Best ever
The nicest teacher I've had at UNCC so far. She is very fun and sweet. Makes it very easy to learn. I would always recommend her for any French class.
One of the most caring professors I've ever had! She made class engaging and worked difficult things out, it was clear she truly cared about her students success.
Hands down the nicest professor I've ever had. She clearly cares about her students and their success!
One of the best professors i've ever had. She is so encouraging and helpful! Attendance is graded but class is enjoyable.

Loved her so much! She truly cares about her students and is always willing to help! I was doing poorly at the beginning of the semester and she really took time to explain things with me! She's an easy grader and helps you to actually learn! She's also hilarious and her bubbly personality is contagious! Would take her over and over again!

She is AMAZING! She is full of so much life and cares about her students. Never be shy to ask for help with anything, she cares more about if you try than your pronunciation or correctness. Come to class, do your hw, and engage with her.

Isabelle has got to be one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. She is so caring and if you tell her you're struggling with anything she will support you in any way she can so you don't fall behind. She's hilarious and energetic and made learning a foreign language so much easier.
she's perfect

Madame Isabelle is hands down my favorite prof at UNCC. She's the sweetest lady ever. She's very understanding and forgiving with mistakes, and acknowledges that learning a language is difficult. Before every quiz/test, she tells us exactly what'll be on it and does practice problems beforehand that are almost identical. She's the absolute best!

Profe Cisneros is wonderful! It's been a while since I've taken a Spanish class, and I can say that she really helped me build my confidence. She cares deeply about her students and tries to encourage you to ask questions and try your best, even if you make mistakes. The VHL assignments were a bit much,  but they were good practice!

I passed the class and as long as I did all that was assigned I managed, but she does give sooo much homework the first half of the semester. I'll also say her approach and demeanor can give off passive aggression and rudeness, to the point where I felt hesitant even reaching out or asking a question. Not the worst but not the best :/

This professor goes above and beyond! I am very happy I took this class, I definitely learn a lot and I am able to apply these skills into my future career. This professor really cares for the students and wants them to be successful in their career.

Profesora Cisneros truly cares about her students and their wellbeing. She is tough on you but it is for your own benefit in the end. She is a wonderful profesor, she adds her own personal experiences in her lectures which makes you feel more connected with her and her topics she teaches, for a better understanding.

I loved this class with Profe Cisneros! She cares deeply about inspiring students and applies real world concepts to the class. The assignments not only practiced Spanish, but also genuinely had me reflecting on my identity. There are a couple of small presentation assignments and in class writing compositions that are graded fairly. I recommend!

She will assume everyone is on the same page and you should know everything from the previous classes (I took the placement test and did not take any previous classes). She teaches very fast. It's hard to keep up. There is heavy homework load and a lot of testing with exams and compositions. She doesn't teach the material well to keep up with it.

Prof. Cisneros gives you the attention you give her. if you don't care neither does she BUT if you care about the class and your grade she will stop at nothing to support you in whatever way necessary. I'm so bummed shes not teaching 2202, I will take whatever i can with her in the future!

Profesora Cisneros es fantastica! She upped my confidence in language learning. Her lectures were very engaging and easy to follow along and try the in-class activities. Her passion and enthusiasm encouraged me to work and it and learn and treat it like an activity and not a chore. I even excelled in the difficult presentation and Boomalang.

Profesora Cisneros made language learning easy and engaging. At first, I was worried about taking this class since I had not taken Spanish since high school. She built my confidence up and I ended up keeping an A for the duration of the class. She always responded to emails quickly and was eager to help.

Prof. Cisneros is so funny and truly cares about her students. There are many homework assignments but they do have a purpose and do help with upcoming tests. She has little patience for late assignments but due dates are fair. Put in effort and you should succeed.

Profesora Cisneros is awesome! She will definitely challenge you in this class but recognizes that people are coming in at different fluency levels and considers that when grading. She is such a caring person and is always willing to help you, whether in class or outside of class, and is very accommodating and considerate of her students' needs.

Overall a very sweet and caring teacher. She mentions every class that there is help provided and resources that are available to you if you are not doing well. I feel like when she writes stuff it could be more organized but that's it. Overall a really good teacher, the class is not bad, just study up.

I want to love her bc she is so lenient on due dates and cares about helping but her class is so beyond difficult especially for non native speakers. A seven minute presentation without notes or words on the slides is crazy. She is so intimidating, but so nice at the same time. I just wish I was actually learning and not scared of the class.

As a student speaking Spanish throughout all my years of school, I was worried that this environment wouldn't be reciprocated in college. Taking Profesora Cisneros my first semester of college was a great decision. She is so nice and positive. You can truly tell that she cares and her class topics are very deep/useful. I love her class
Definitely a very understanding professor as long as she knows you try in class and you actually attend! Sometimes she doesn't explain material or the exams enough, but it's still doable

Professor Cisneros is a kind soul. She is very sweet when it comes to extensions and helping with concepts you don't understand. I haven't had any issues with her at all. It was a little hard for me to adjust to her Argentinian dialect as opposed to past professors. Other than that, very good professor.

Honestly the best Professor at UNC Charlotte. I studied abroad with her in Sicily, and it was such an amazing time. Professor Daniela genuinely cares about her students. She also really cares about what she is teaching. I would take her again and again if I could. BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!!

Had Professor Dal Pra for a study abroad and she was the best professor that Iv ever had. The assignments for the course went with everything that you would see in person. 10/10 would do it again. I highly recommend a study abroad experience with her.
All online responses that were graded on the grammer more than the content. Use a grammer check if you take her class.

I love Professor. Dal Pra so much. She is one of the best professors I've ever had, and she is super flexible. She likes to change the courses depending on what interests her students. She is an easy grader for the most part, but when people start taking advantage of her, she starts grading slightly more harshly.

Daniela is an amazing and caring professor. She is very fair and knowledgeable. I have taken multiple classes with her and her classes never disappoint; they are hidden gems. UNCC is very lucky to have this professor. Just show up, participate, ask questions, do the work and you will be fine.

Proff. is very passionate and talks about the topics in cinema with proper information but she is VERY repetitive. She will pause the films to talk about exactly what (and will) happen/ed. Participation is HUGE and even grades harshly if you don't praise the topic enough. You take class notes for everyone and even with that, you'll be graded harsh.

He is an awesome professor at his core, his classes are not hard nor are his assignments. I would however advise anyone considering taking him for an elective in addition to major requirements to look elsewhere. The amount of assignments is absurd and you will not keep up if you have other demanding courses that also have a ton of assignments.

Bledsoe's class was very easy, featuring online quizzes, discussion posts, journal entries, and papers tied to approximately 11 documentaries. The grading was lenient, allowing for three missed classes without penalty, and students often received extra points for quality assignments. While Bledsoe attempts humor, it can be cringeworthy at times.

Great professor! I took his anime class, JAPN-3140. Not sure if the code changed, but it wasn't listed. There are a lot of online assignments, but they really don't take long to complete. There are a couple of long lecture videos, but they were interesting. Mainly watched anime/documentaries in class.

Prof. Bledsoe is an okay professor. I took JAPN1502 (previously 1201 I think) a gen ed class. Its easy as long as you keep up with the 6+ weekly online assignments including 4 discussion videos and multiple quizzes based on lecture videos. He doesnt teach in class we just watch documentaries, all the actual learning comes from the online lectures.

I had him for JAPN 1502. There is a lot of homework in this class, however, if you do it while the class is going and do not wait until the last second, it does not seem like a lot. He is a great professor and cares about his classes that he teaches. I would 100% take him again. I do not have a problem with him at all.

Professor Bledsoe is an awesome professor who really cares about sharing japanese culture with students. The class I took was new so the curriculum may very well change but if i doesnt, expect a ton of easy assignments. He is also very lenient if you miss any as long as you communicate with him. Take his class if you want to relax and learn.

Professor Bledsoe is very chill and his lectures are fun. There are a lot of assignments, but they are super simple and do not take very long to complete. No tests, only a final project at the end of the semester. Attendance is required so show up. There a quite a bit of asynchronous days for the class, which was nice.

Amazing professor! Keeps class engaged and entertaining and is very lenient with homework. There is LOTS of homework, but at the end of the semester, he drops a lot of our lowest ones. Also no tests or quizzes, just assignments that are easy 100s.

Professor Bledsoe is great at explaining japanese and makes easy to learn! He does a "flipped" classroom where you watch videos first and practice in class. Attendance is required and you practice with classmates throughout the semester. He also gave us the opportunity to turn in certain assignments with no late penalty.  Definitely take him!

Lots of group work, but as long as you have good teammates, the class is super easy. This class would only be difficult if you don't try at all and think presenting in front of a class is the most difficult thing in the world. Very little investment outside of class is needed and overall it was a fun class, I learned a lot more than I expected.
Mori Sensei's stricter schedule makes it easier to stay on tract to learn Japanese but it's nothing impossible. It is a class that can be done at any reasonable pace you want to do.

I absolutely loved her class and teaching style. I felt challenged and extremely motivated throughout the semester. It's pretty fast-paced but you get used to it because it's very structured, and it didn't feel like we rushed over any lessons. Overall, one of my favorite classes I've ever taken!

This class was so much fun, it felt more like a group of people practicing Japanese together than a traditional class.  There is a lot of work to do but it genuinely does help you learn the material, I didn't have to study at all outside of the assigned work.

I loved Mori Sensei's Japanese course! She is very kind and genuinely cares about her students and their success. Japanese is hard (that's a given) and the course is fast-paced but grading isn't too harsh. Tons of homework but I found Genki work to be fun. The TA Yuki-san was great too! :)

I heard that Mori-sensei is intimidating but I didn't get that feeling with her. I would take her again if I could. She's caring and brought snacks closer to finals. If you have any questions, don't hesitate to ask her for clarification. My favorite class of the semester.
Sensei Mori made this class not only fun but challenging (in a good way). If you are wanting to get your Japanese skill up quick, I would recommend her.

Mori-sensei made me want to keep learning Japanese, since I nearly debated dropping the major. She's very joyful to be around and helps you understand the content one on one if needed in a clear manner. So easy to reach out to and teaches in a way that is helpful to everyone in the class. Still calls on you though lol so be prepared to study!

I was scared to take a class with her at first because she was known to be strict and fast paced. In a nutshell, Mori sensei ended up being one of my favorite profs. I once spent over half a class crying in the bathroom and she walked in on me by accident. She didn't say anything but she counted me present despite the fact I was absent for most-

Mori-sensei is an amazing lab professor to have, very engaging and reviews content efficiently. She does call on students a lot and participation is something that makes or break this class, but her feedback is extremely helpful and she is always ready for questions. Sometimes, she might misunderstand them though.

Lectures are super boring however he is a nice guy, lots of group discussion which is fine. I didnt really try in the class however if you put in a even a little bit of effort and show up to class youll be fine. He could be better but he isnt bad either, just meh

Professor Stone is as average as they come. I thought he did an okay job but didn't do much to prepare students for quizzes or exams. He would give pages of the textbook instead of taking the time to make a simple study guide. He's not a bad professor but I think there are better professors to take that will make the class way easier.
Professor Stone is an excellent professor. You have to really pay attention if you want to learn, but it's a super nice grader. Extremely understanding and cares about his students.

Prof. Stone is an amazing person and good teacher. I would definitely recommend taking him. The only reason I didn't do well was bc of personal circumstances and couldn't catch myself up. He did try to help me and work with me, but I just think Spanish wasn't my thing anymore. Anyway, DEFINITELY TAKE HIM!!!

He gives alot of homework, kind unorganized sometimes. One oral presentation but not infront of the class. He helps when it comes to compositions but test review "study" is just pages in the textbook. Slow grader. Final was cumulative.
Really kind professor, but be prepared to do lots of homework

SPAN 2202: He explains concepts well. I'd recommend taking him! Hw can be a lot since it's due every Mon/Wed, but as long as you stay on top of it, you'll be fine. Tests are fine just study and do the VHL hw!, and he goes over material beforehand, especially if he knows students don't understand something. He's really sweet/chill, you'll like him!

I have taken Professor Stone 3 times (1 3000 level class and 2 4000 level class), and I transferred here in my junior year. He is a fantastic teacher who really does help you. I really can't recommend him highly enough.
Is very kind and good at teaching. Only downside is that there is a lot of homework so be prepared for that.

Professor Stone is the nicest guy, his lectures are great, and he manages to make basic Spanish a lot of fun to learn. He prepared us for the test well, the homework wasn't too long and reinforced topics from class. He was always available if you need help.
Such a great professor

He's a respectable man but this class has been so difficult for no reason. He uses the textbook and there is no room for synonymous words as he will take points off if you don't use the direct translation for words from the textbook, direct wording for concepts and accent marks. On average 1-2 quizzes per week, can't miss class, final is cumulative

He takes a long time to grade assignments and doesn't give much feedback when he does. Study guides were just a list of all of the units we had been taught. Taught us lectures after being tested on the content already. Its finals now and still hasn't graded several assignments. He is nice, lectures well, and is helpful when you ask in class.
Easy class as long as you read and do the online homework, there are a few tests throughout the course and an oral exam professor stone is great

He genuinely cares about students and wants you to succeed. I am a spanish minor, and struggle to keep up with native spanish speakers, but this class was fun and I didn't find myself staring at the clock like usual. He's very understanding, and his lectures are actually helpful and taught me a lot.

An okay professor. He's super nice and understanding but he doesn't do too well at explaining. I can tell he tries his best tho. He's very soft spoken so sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. Long hw but that's every Spanish class. Lectures can get boring & interactions w/ classmates are required. Exams are okay bc half-point is allowed.

Really kind teacher and very easy to work with! I took this class online, but probably be better in person. There is a discussion board almost every week where you watch movies or read the textbook. One midterm, a mini project on an Arab country, and a final interview. Not difficult just follow the rubric. You must show your face for the project.
She is very nice and her class is relatively easy just a class where she talks and you listen.overall kind teacher.

If you are learning Arabic for the first time, Dr. Noha is the best professor. She perfectly explains everything and makes learning the language enjoyable. She annunciates letters very well and emphasizes where there might be any confusion. There is a lot of homework, but they are for your benefit. Plus, she drops 3 lowest HW and attendance grades.
she was terrible, NEVER take her class PLEASE.

You are expected to read textbook chapters before coming into class, gets disappointed if you do not. She is very cooperative- makes the deadlines favorable to the students. She is a tough grader with no clear rubric for discussion boards. Very heavy DB class.

Mrs ghali is truly kind and cares for the students this review is for her Arabic cultural studies class she's a very good explainer with easy assignments that just require effort make sure to attend and read the material provided and you will be fine she's a great teacher.
If you want an easy and enjoyable class, this one is a great choice! The material was straightforward, and the tests weren't difficult. I definitely recommend taking it.
Great Professor, very genuine and wants everyone to succeed in the course.

Dr Noha is a very good professor. If you are looking to learn Arabic, she is the right professor. Walking into the class, I had no knowledge of the Arabic alphabet or language. Now, I know the whole alphabet and can read decently with just one class. Overall, I learned a lot from her class and would highly recommend if wanting to learn Arabic.

This review is actually for her 1502 class. Professor Ghali is nice and caring. You will have a discussion board question every week and in class discussions. Attendance matters, not much but it can drop your grade if you miss say 6 classes. She sometimes makes you align with what she believes so when you post discussions, write notes in class.

One of the best teachers ive ever had. tries to make the work load as simple as possible for the students while still making sure we learn the information to do well. her teaching style is amazing, shes funny, pretty, and nice. only thing that people may not like is that attendance is mandatory.
A very good professor, she makes a point to really hear her students and gather their opinions. However If you don't like participating don't take her. She is an amazing professor though.
n

Dr. Ghali is really nice, and answers emails promptly. I liked this class, and it taught me a lot about Arab culture. However, towards the end just about every assignment had a movie that you had to pay for in order to do your homework. Not that it was expensive, we just already pay so much for college in general and we paid for a textbook.

Took ARBC-3211 over the summer. For a 3 credit hour class the work involved should have warranted at least 4. Three discussions per week, each requiring no less than 500 words. Lengthy lecture videos, excessive amount of resources required. Watched several films, read books, wrote way too many papers for a non-major class. Not worth the headache.

the TA's teach the class, I had Miriam, she was a sweet girl but she made the class soo boring that it felt really long. easy work but it was textbook heavy. the TA would also be so mad at us if she spoke and no one answered, understandable tho. You do have to meet with David one time for a grade (zoom call) hes sweet tho just boring class.

Attendance is mandatory, but I missed a few classes, and it only hurt me a little. He answers emails quickly and is always willing to help. You literally just watch movies about Latin American history and do some quizzes and canvas/discussion posts. Very easy general education course.
This class almost made me start a therapy that I've been denying for years. Do not recommend.
class was overall pretty easy, mostly graded on movie and textbook quizzes. midterm and final were both online but had lockdown browsers and had essay prompts.

Amazing professor, only saw him once or twice tho. The TA Diana was beyond amazing as well. The class does have a weekly discussion board which you have to answer to two classmates, two quizzes, and watching a film + reading textbook. There's two exams, pretty easy but both include short and long essays. Overall great experience!

Dr. Dalton appeared in class for the first two weeks of the semester. I was excited for this class; I wanted to learn more.
