Class is overall easier to get past, make sure to stay on top of your assignments and pay attention. The only thing that bothered me was how much attendance is worth of your whole grade. Even if you have an A in the class and have more than 4 absences it can drop to a C. Make sure to go to class and if you can't provide good documentation.

Although the class was boring, it was an easy A. You just have to actually put effort in what you are writing. Presentation was really easy and Portfolio at the end, 50% of your grade was not difficult to do if you have been doing the work throughout the semester. I would take again

Lovely teacher with great feedback. I was late on a lot of my papers, but she was always willing to help me understand anything I was stuck on and provide helpful and encouraging feedback. Understood when you were absent, late, or left early. Very interesting papers and the semester project was really in-depth and enjoyable.

+ online savvy, inspirational & many papers. Writing class so papers make sense. You can tell she cares, and her grading focused on improvements rather than perfection. Emails back quickly and doesn't hesitate to set up a zoom mtng. I feel welcome in her office and I can't wait to take her again. Highly recommend WRDS 1103 or 1104 w/ her.

Mrs. Halaburda immediately stood out to me as a genuine person who cares about her students and doing a good job in her work. She always provides useful feedback in a timely manner, and sets up a great environment in class for everyone to feel comfortable and actually enjoy being there. 

Highly recommend anyone to take her class(es)!

professor halaburda will forever be my favorite professor. i took her class over the summer and she accommodated to me based on my level of writing and was such a caring and helpful professor. i highly recommend
She is super nice, if you communicate with her and don't miss more than 5 classes (unexcused) you're gonna pass. Gives great and helpful feedback, and I actually liked going to class.
she gets off topic pretty easily. really nice and is a good teacher. not much work, but it takes a while. sometimes i dont understand the point of these assignments.

Professor Halaburda is extremely helpful and grades fairly. She gives clear and concise feedback on major writing assignments. You have to put in a lot of effort for this class. It's not a class where you can procrastinate it. She's flexible and understanding if you need extensions on assignments.

She is a great professor & wants her students to succeed! There is A LOT of homework, so be ready for that. We read 2 books, had a HUGE group presentation, and a final paper. She is very knowledgeable about the class & always has a positive attitude. I would 100% take her again. Just don't slack on the work, go to class, & you'll be fine!
I took her class for CTCM, she is a great professor and makes the classes fun. Attendance is mandatory and if you skip more than 5 you drop a letter grade. Go to class for an A!

nice teacher, helpful and very lenient. also helped me out when I was struggling with juggling my time and allowed me to make up certain assignments. if you want a simple class that challenges your mind a bit, take this professor for this course

Participate in class, she allows up to 5 absences. Responds quickly to emails. Homework assignments are simple and less are assigned later in the semester. Put effort into your homework in order to get 100. One final essay, gives a lot of time to complete and gives feedback so it is easy to get a high grade even if you are not a skilled writer.

I loved Mrs Thomas' class! She always includes feedback when grading assignments and is always open to giving feedback on assignments before you turn them in. She doesn't grade harshly at all and makes it very clear what she wants in assignments. She also grades more on the content of your essays rather than spelling and grammar. Take her class!!

Ms Thomas is super nice and respectful to all of her students. She's very understanding. I took her during the summer term and I felt like she did assign a significant amount of work, although it was an accelerated class (being the summer term) so it's understandable. She gave very clear expectations for work and was not a harsh grader at all.
Professor Thomas is a good instructor. Although lectures could be boring sometimes they are easy to understand. Heavy textbook reading, and she takes off points after 5 days of unexcused attendance.
Very nice and grades easy. A lot of work but I actually feel like I learned something for once. She cares for her students and wants the best for you. There's no way you don't pass with an A.

She's such a great professor. I took her fall semester as soon as Covid had began. She is really generous to extensions if you ask for it- but you have to work for it and definitely keep up with the work in her class. She's super sweet and encourages your success in her class.

Class and materials are interesting and the work isn't hard, do it and you'll be fine. Assignments and tests are weighted oddly, and are often not graded until weeks or months later. Can be difficult to reach outside of class and due dates are different on assignments versus what's posted in Canvas. Very independent work style.

Dr. Leak did not grade things critically, but he did grade them unfairly. A girl in my class basically relayed what she learned in the class to her boyfriend and he got better grades than her. He made questionable comments about women and I felt there was an underlying bias that effected his grading. Also he wrote questions on the exam w/out nouns.
Class is easy, but I don't like this dude at all. The English teachers that teach 3000/2000 classes are not it. How they treat their students is ridiculous. Just get that degree though I guess.

For one I was robbed of seeing my progress this whole semester because he only submitted two grades the entire time, classes are over and I still haven't received a final grade. Assignments are due on awkward days at awkward times, discussion post were majority of the assignments. He's very intelligent and his lectures are fruitful when you listen.

Prepares you very well for the tests as long as you participate in class and do the readings (lots of reading). There was one group project. The content of this course was decently easy and she was very helpful whenever I had questions about assignments or essays. Explained things clearly. I recommend her if you need a lowkey elective.
She could be a more effective professor. She doesn't give good feedback either.
Very liberal class, but still learned a decent bit.

Dr. Miller was likely my favorite professor of the semester. The textbook is dry, but the concept of the class is naturally hard to make entertaining to read, but she makes the information entertaining in lecture. She allowed up to 5 absences before grade penalization. Friday discussion groups on concepts covered during the week
My favorite professor in the English department. She has the most accessible lectures and gives very good feedback. I really wished I could have taken another of her courses before graduating
Dr. Flores is wonderful! Depending on what class you take with him, you may have some complicated readings, but overall, he is great. He is very helpful and responsive to emails.

Dr. Flores is one of my favorite professors at UNCC. He is always engaging in class and is willing to work with you if you need extensions or miss class. Assignments are relevant to coursework and he often gives time in class to work on them.

His lectures can be confusing at times, especially for 3220, but he grades on completion. As long as you participate, you will get an A. Skipping class is better than showing up late because he will call you out. You learn more because you don't have to stress about grades. 3215 is all group work, and 3220 is discussion and essay-based. Take him!

I just didn't feel like I received any real feedback from this professor. One of those nice professors who says all the right things but doesn't actually want to be inconvenienced enough to give you the kind of feedback you actually need to improve.

He's one of the youngest professors in the department, so he understands student's struggles. He cares about our mental health and always wants us to succeed. His assignments are simple and are available when it is confusing. There is so much creative freedom in his class.

If you want an easy class, this is about as easy as it gets. You have an assignment once a week that takes an hour or two at most. Occasionally you'll have a paper that takes a little longer. If you want to learn anything about creative writing, then don't bother. Gives contradictory instructions, bad feedback, and releases grades absurdly late

Professor Cook is a person who does not give clear instructions on what he would like. He is incoherent and does not provide examples for you to abide by what he wants. He gave me a 65 for a well written paper, I emailed him and he did not reply. His class was easy but he was just not a good instructor on what he wanted to see on a paper.

I love Professor Basu. She is one of my favorite professors. I have now taken three of her classes and will probably take another next semester since it is my last. She is so passionate about the things she teaches, and it shows. She cares for her students and encourages them when she sees potential in the things they are doing.

very very easy class, you do not know what assignments or readings you have to do because she does not give much of a heads up. This is a professor who lets you know from the beginning that every student starts with a B. So you must do more than she asks to get an A. She is a very odd teacher, but an easy A. Pretty much a one-credit-hour course.

The class itself isn't difficult, but she only publishes assignments week by week. Every other professor I've had has them all published or, at the least, has a course schedule available so you can see what is coming up. She does not. Other than that, the class is fine. Pretty easy as long as you try and don't rely on AI.

Class consisted of listening to albums, watching movies/documentaries and reading 3-4 books. The assignments are always discussion boards and are very easy. Make sure to put thought into the discussion boards and don't use AI as the discussion boards are not supposed to be grammatically correct. There are some weeks with nothing to do fyi

Professor Basu genuinely cares for her students and loves what she teaches. Lectures are a large discussion, but she does not force anyone to speak and openly listens to everyone's opinions. The books in class are incredibly diverse and showcase many different genres. I would 100% retake this class!

i watched beyonce, collin kaepernick, and taylor swift documentaries and read hunger games, and 3 other interesting books. she is discussion board heavy. i actually forgot i was in the class tbh bc she went without giving us assignments for a few weeks. easy A to me. you can be a lazy student. i didnt have an exam? not complaining though!

She's an amazing professor who's really passionate about her work. I took her over the summer & it was quite an easy class. The class didn't have any specific timings & each week you had to answer a discussion board. The discussion board assignments were really open ended & she gives great feedback. I highly recommend taking her class.

Balaka was not a horrible professor but was not good. the class itself was strange. Didn't learn anything we were supposed to. She made lots of strange comments that made me uncomfortable. She called herself a benign dictator and referred to loners in life being school shooters. You also have to read like 7 books and the class was uncomfortable
Professor Basu was a great teacher she was truly interested in having a discussion and wanted to hear everyone's opinions even if they disagreed with her own.

Dr. Basu is a great professor. It was extremely interesting to look deeper into the implications of pop culture with her. Witty and thought-provoking. Lots of required readings but they aren't difficult to comprehend. Essays every couple of weeks. The TA, Briahna Henry, was fantastic as well.

Dr. Basu is my favorite professor I had this semester, and I am already waiting to take more classes with her. She was incredibly engaging and empathetic, and I loved the books we read this semester. I high recommend taking any of her classes!

Professor Basu has been my favorite instructor throughout my whole academic career. Very understanding and I still managed to get an A in the class even though I didn't read half the books. If you communicate with her and show her you care youve got a good grade.

Basu is the best professor I have ever had. She offers an incredible perspective on the assigned reading. It is a YA lit course, so we read a novel a week but I am encouraged to read them if only to be able to participate fully in her lectures. She encourages great conversation and brings humor and empathy into the classroom.

I personally really enjoyed this course. If you like discussions, this class is for you but you do have to read the material she gives out and constantly make connections to the reading when doing any of her writing assignments.
Great professor, she really cares about her students and you can tell she's an expert in her subject. Do the work and you'll be fine.

I have thoroughly enjoyed AMST with Professor Bruner. She provides detailed readings to succeed in an online course. The work load is light with discussion posts & a few papers. The content is actually interesting. She provides a clear rubric & feedback for every assignment. I love the personal touch of a weekly email. Extra credit opportunities

This professor is passionate about the material, but is not well-organized. There are weekly posts and responses, as well as two research papers and a final group project. It is not easy to do a group project with people you have never met. She does not use traditional modules in Canvas. She needs to modernize to the rest of the University.
such a sweet lady, the lectures were literally just about her life and the fifties in america. i played solitaire on my computer the whole time and i got a 100 in the class.

Don't let that person below lie to you, she literally has no idea what she is teaching. She gives you a a discussion board with questions and then ask you to write about it, when there is nothing on canvas for you to go and search for or read!!!
10 Discussion boards and one paper and a research project. Simple as that. 300-500 words and 150 words to reply to two or one person for the discussion board, but you can do everything ahead of time.

In several of my AMST classes, Professor Bruner was the best and most kind instructor I ever had. She gives good feedback, has a clear grading criteria, the lectures are not a heavy worlkload, and she offers to look over your rough drafts when it comes to writing a 3 to 4 essay. I recommend having Professor Bruner as my teacher again.
Completely online, all discussions were graded on completion. Easy A

She teaches only off of memory and stolen articles from magazine websites. She just rambles incessantly about her childhood and how music is so much different now and not the same. When the political aspect enters the discussion, she silences those with differing opinions. Overall an insignificant and boring class, but very easy.

This professor unfortunately does not know the topic she is teaching.  She is extremely difficult to reach outside of class and often shuts down any opinions different from her own in class.  Overall, the course is very easy and mostly just discussion posts but do not go into this class expecting to actually learn.

She was terrible, I am lucky I can write papers fast and well because my god, she gave so many papers with such ridiculous lengths. This was supposed to be an intro gen ed writing class, but I would believe you if you told me, it was an honor or ap class. The grading she just makes up criteria on the spot sometimes, and the workload was ridiculous.
INSTRUCTIONS ARE NEVER EVER EVER EVER CLEAR, SHE MAKES UP ASSIGNMENTS ON THE SPOT, HER GRADING MAKES ZERO SENSE, THE LIST GOES ON!!!!!!!!!! UGHHHHHHHHHH

She is a very nice individual but not good at teaching. She doesn't give clear instructions and is often spending too much time explaining unimportant things. Her grading scale is unfair, but it's easy to pass her class with minimal effort and a good grade.
Worst grading structure I've ever encountered. You will gain nothing from her class. Avoid her.

SHE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER! I signed up for every course that she teaches because she is so amazing. The books she challenged us to read were engaging. She prioritizes multiethnicity education in all her courses (I've taken 2). She's understanding, kind, challenging, and engaging. Any student would be lucky to have her.

ENGL 3125-Latino Literature. The class itself wasn't really difficult. She just requires you to read a lot. Some weeks, we'd have to read 200 pgs between our Tuesday and Thursday classes. She's not a super  harsh grader, but she does want you to dig deeper and go into detail. You can't get away with a broad thesis statement and/or paper.

She's not a good professor and she's very rude. Most discussion was just surface-level meaning so the class was not very helpful or stimulating. I was very disappointed because the subject matter was so interesting. She's disorganized and all over the place and I will NEVER take her again. She also does pop quizzes like we're in elementary school.

Dr. Socolovsky was a professor that grew on me. She knows what she is talking about, yet will listen to what you have to say every time. She truly cares about helping students and will get your feedback on the books she chooses for the class. Beware, she IS a tough grader on her papers. But in a way that is actually helpful for you as a student!

Disrespectful, petty, sarcastic. Quizzed us every class. I tried to ask questions about and was met with very defensive responses. She teaches classes she has no connections to... Very much the pretensions "don't question me" type professor... Its not hard, but I dropped the class because I was sick of childish English professors. Get in & get out.

This professor was adamant about providing good readings over the course. Though the expectations were high, there were none that were unreasonable. Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed the material in class and how the teacher got us to connect their intersecting themes together. It is clear this teacher is knowledgeable in her field.

She is a very condescending teacher, responds to questions with an attitude and as if she's always right. Doesn't give feedback! Assignments are graded without comments to explain what was done incorrectly and/or how to improve. The grading system is also pretty harsh and usually has little instructions.

Get ready to read in her class. She can be very insensitive to students' situations. She also tried to completely disregard my disability accommodations, saying it was "up to the teacher's discretion", which is so not true. She is a very tough grader, and gives very vague feedback so not helpful on how to fix the problems. Would not recommend.

Overall fun class even if you're not going into education. Very discussion based. Watched movies and episodes of shows every month or so. Broke out into breakout rooms every week/class to discuss questions. Grades are in-class writing, weekly homework based on text and final exam is an essay. Attendance got mandatory when #s got low.

Started out promising, but she got more strict as the course went on. She does not give feedback on grades even when you receive a zero so it's hard to improve when you don't know what you did wrong. She has the TA grading and teaching the class so I'm not even sure what she does. I wouldn't recommend this course to anyone.
Doesnt give good feedback, harsh grader,
Sometimes makes you feel bad for asking questions. Other than that she's a cool teacher.

Every class's main idea was how great teachers are and how important they are in everybody's lives. The entire class was an ego stroke for this woman. Not to mention she doesn't even grade most of our work nor teach most of the classes herself. Almost completely taught and graded by the TA.

Grades are out of 10 points, doesn't seem to give more than a 9/10 (causing the average grade to be at most a 90). Tries to give feedback, not often and not well detailed. Uses Instagram as a form of assignment, very interesting and modern. I enjoyed the content. 8 books in 5 weeks (Summer course).

Dr. Avila is one of the best professors at UNCC! Her class can be tough she expects a certain level of work but I learned more in her classes than anywhere else. I have received multiple teaching awards in my first two years of teaching and her class certainly helped me get there. Work hard (you won't be sorry).

A wonderful professor and an overall respected man. His class can be challenging at times, and the essays are strictly graded, but he crafts a wonderful course, allowing his students to improve their writing over time. I learned a lot from Dr. Blair; his feedback is always detailed and very kind. Loved him!

Professor Blair is engaging and understanding, though the workload can be heavy. Staying engaged, using the free textbook, and trying Unstuck study for study prep can help you succeed. Overall, an enjoyable class worth taking.

Amazing professor, his lectures are super dynamic, and he really helps you when you have questions. Very flexible and very attentive, there is a lot of homework but most of them take 20 minutes to do. Just be ready to participate in class and you'll be fine. He's a very fair grader overall. One of my favorite teachers ever.
Kind and patient teacher. If you stay on top of coursework and pay attention when he calls on you then you will have no problem in his class!

Honestly the best professor at UNCC. Loved his class, he's a great lecturer and really gets you to engage with what we're doing in class. Really caring and understanding, fun to talk to,would take late work with no penalty, and gave great feedback both in class and on assignments. Also was great at explaining what he was looking for on assignments!

Dr. Blair was one of the most caring professors. His course was super easy but it did require some reading and a lot of writing. Since it was an online course, attendance was mandatory. Just show up to class and do your homework and you should pass the class.
Be communicative of your situation with this professor and he will help you out.  He has a lot of respect for his students and is willing to help you out.

The lectures weren't so bad b/c the prof. would try to make it engaging by cold calling on the students. 3 major essays made up most of the grade but were graded very strictly. There was a lot of homework attached to reading and they made up concerningly an insignificant portion of the final grade compared to how time-consuming they were.

Professor Blair was honestly an amazing teacher, his lectures were entertaining, he is very understanding and would take late assignments if needed. While there is a lot of writing in this class, if you do your work and participate in class discussion you should be fine. I actually enjoyed this class and would take it again.

He has so many assignments it is extremely overwhelming. I see a lot of good reviews but I think that's because he is a very nice guy. He is understanding and everything but he is also a really hard grader. I would take him again in an in-person environment.

Very surprised by the overwhelmingly positive reviews for him.

Even after I made changes to the rough draft after given feedback, he would still take points away for some random reason. Also if you don't answer when he randomly calls on you, he'll take away participation points, but won't tell you that's even a thing until the end of the semester.

Dr. Blair was Good! Very nice guy, but he will not hesitate calling on you even if your hand is not raised. As long as you read the agenda for each class, and do the readings/ stay involved in class, you will probably do well. Also, BE PREPARED TO WRITE!!!!.
He is really understanding and offers help when you need it. Be prepared to read and write a lot. Easy A class definitely worth it.

Dr. Blitvich is one of the few professors I've had who makes it a point to give insightful and detailed feedback on each assignment. The reading content can be very difficult, so show up to class with questions & be ready to participate! I have never felt stupid to ask clarifying questions, even if they may have been repetitive. Amazing professor.

Dr. Blitvich is an outstanding professor! Her well-structured lectures, clear explanations, and practical examples make complex topics easy to understand. Her enthusiasm and genuine care for her students' learning create a supportive and inspiring environment. I highly recommend her class!

Dr. Blitvich is an incredible professor. I've taken most of my linguistics courses with her, and I would again if given the chance. She has high expectations for students but takes the time to make sure the concepts and readings are understood. Very knowledgeable and passionate about linguistics. I HIGHLY recommend taking a course with her.

Anyone interested in the field of linguistics MUST take a class with Dr. Blitvich! So knowledgable and practiced in her field yet also kind and accessible. Has high expectations for her students but equips them with every resource necessary to succeed. I cannot sing her praises enough! (I've had her for 3+ classes across 2 degrees)

Professor Blitvich is so smart and a wonderful person. She doesn't have too many assignments peppered throughout the semester, but there are two big papers and three big tests. She is always ready to answer questions and be as helpful as she can. Would definitely take her again.

Lectured in class for the entire time but never really taught the actual material. Assigned a lot of reading assignments in a short amount of time, on top of other classes. Also your entire grade banks on top of three analysis papers and the attendance.participation grade. You can only miss two days of class before she fails you.

I'm not sure if this year was just particularly difficult for Dr. Blitvich, but she was very condescending throughout the entirety of the semester. Chastised class for going to the bathroom too much, called on random people and then responded rudely if they were incorrect, and was generally very harsh and not helpful. Did not look forward to class.

Took her for ENGL 4073. Was excited to take a girls lit course. Dr. Hogan was the worst English professor I've ever had, possibly at UNC Charlotte as a whole. One 300-400 page book a week. No recorded lecture or main takeaways from each week. Rude feedback. Got an 84 on a minor paper for a few grammatical errors. Vague directions yet so strict.

There's no leniency on any of the papers or discussion boards when it comes to mistakes. It could be tiny mistakes that we didn't mean to make but she won't budge on taking point off. Discussion board doesn't have clear criteria in terms of word count but if she feel you didn't do enough she takes points off. Interesting reading material though.

Kind lady who gives great feedback. Discussion boards each week, two papers, and four quizzes. Really interesting materials and the work was not too bad. Definitely looking for lengthy responses for discussions, so keep that in mind. Good asynchronous class, overall.

She was amazing and really helped me with my critical responses. I learned so much in her course. She takes time to edit and help with every writing assignment. She it also flexible if things come up in your schedule. 10/10

This class was a waste of time due to the materials she chose to cover. It was clear that she was looking for the students to regurgitate specific ideals in assignments. There were discussion board postings every week and it was pointless. I wanted to become a better writer and reader of literature, this class didn't help me at all.

You have a textbook that you will only use for the first few assignments. After that, you are expected to teach yourself completely. He quite literally grades writing assignments as if you are Quentin Tarantino himself, instead of a college student who is taking an ENTRY LEVEL film class with absolutely no knowledge of film. Never again. DON'T TAKE

Worst class ever. You must purchase a movie and write two papers weekly, with no clear rubric. The assignments are due at 11am so beware if you work or struggle with time management. He is an incredibly harsh grader, and the comments he leaves are snarky and unproductive. This is not an enjoyable or easy film class, though he states that himself.

This professor was good about answering questions and comments in a timely manner, especially for an online class. I truly learned a lot from this course and would 100% take this professor again. You just need to be prepared for a lot of writing and have good time management because all the assignments are due at 11am.

This professor was always available through email with it being an online course. If you just take this class and don't ask for help when you don't do well, you won't learn. You have to want to do better or you won't grow in this course. For an online course, this professor gives a lot of help and does it well.

This class not only drained me to the point where I skipped several assignments, but it also killed my GPA. He makes you watch 2 hour movies then do assignments where you have to explain every single appearance of a certain thing in a movie. If you didn't get the movie, or "didn't stay true to the facts" you're failing. He is also rude in comments.

For my review, go read the other one stars. 

I will say, he was nice to me over email, but the class was horrid. He was also very snarky in the comments with me and I hated that. He also didn't tell us what to look for, but he did say "everything is shot the way it is for a reason" and that's it. If you have to take this class w/ him, DON'T...

This class is the absolute worst. Don't take it just for the credits! 

To sum this up:  
- Grading is HARSH, No rubric, confusing instructions, 
- lack of good feedback at all, all on his opinion
- 11 AM submission, Intense writing.

This class is meant to give you stress than teach, if you're pass the withdrawal date, Good luck.

All assignments lacked clear feedback and did not have a grading rubric accessible, assignments were not clear and often confusing. He expects you to write like you are a film major when the class is an entry level fun studies class.

UNC should be ashamed for continuing to let HORRIBLE professors like him teach. He grades based on his opinion vs if you did the assignment right. Told me I "wasn't doing enough for prompt" when I asked for feedback he had none to give. Had issues opening a document and when I wrote him his response was, "I'm not sure, you'll have to ask IT" Be fr

The lectures and his clear knowledge of filmmaking were great, but the expectations were unrealistic. Each week, you would watch a film and essentially write a multiple-page essay on a specific characteristic or scene and apply terms learned to describe them. It was work overload, only take if you are a film major and do not mind writing a lot.

Tony Jackson clearly cares a lot about film and I am sure he is a knowledgeable person but he does not run his classes well. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS ONLINE! As far as I understand his in person class involves discussions but his online class is two multi page papers every week with unclear instructions and he does not teach you at all.

He gives no modules, PowerPoints, readings, or anything. All he says is to buy the textbook. The assignments are rigorous for an intro class and grades harshly. Doesnt not give any tips or examples before the assignment due date which is also at 11 am. He only provides examples after assignments have been graded.

For the online asynch class, the topics studied were interesting but he grades as if it is an advanced film class. He expects you to use every film term correctly every time. Class is writing heavy which was fun for me, but his expectations are a little high for an intro film class. If you are not super interested in film I wouldnt take this class

This professor is actually horrible, UNC Charlotte should be ashamed. I've reached out for help and get snarky, short replies. Please, don't take this class. This man enjoys seeing people struggle. I can't wait to get out of it.

One of the worst professors Ive ever had! Theres two papers you need to submit at 11 IN THE MORNING on Tuesday's and Thursday's. Hes a very harsh grader and does not give effective feedback. Although I learned a lot from this course, I would not take this class with this professor.

Professor Metzl is an incredible teacher. Her class is interactive and she is extremely knowledgeable. She is understanding of students circumstances. There is a good amount of assignments but everything is explained clearly. She provides feedback & offers to review assignments prior to submission. I have learned so much in an intro level course.
Ms. Metzl is the most caring professor I have had. She truly cares about her students and their success. She does care about attendance and loves to provide feedback.

It took me a bit to warm up to Mrs Metzl, but she is very knowledgable about journalism, so she has a lot to offer. The class met once a week, and then we had asynchronous homework each week. There are 5 big writing assignments, and she is always willing to help you on them. No tests. 2 textbooks (one online, one physical).

Literally the most sweetest professor I have yet to have. Very much respected in her work and gives back great feedback. She has a very strong background in journalism and does everything possible to make sure you understand AP style and how to write great journalistic articles. Love her so much, please take her class if possible, you will learn!!!
Interesting content and good lecturer. You read an entire textbook front to back. Four quizzes online quizzes, midterm and final and two papers and attendance are entire grade.

Thiede is the goat. The subject matter gets real in-depth so it might not be your cup of tea, but the actual grading is generous, and there aren't many assignments. If you aren't interested, space out and you'll be fine. If you enjoy the material, you'll have a blast. Very funny, very kind. Charming.

Thiede is the GOAT. Very funny, extremely knowledgeable. Great lectures. Quizzes and Midterm were pretty tough but the final was super easy and he gave us the answers the class before lol. Only other assignments are 2 papers. I really enjoyed them and thought they were fun, but other people found them very challenging. Thiede is a great man. Take!!
Super helpful with assignments for his own class and other projects. Lectures are super engaging, and he's really passionate about what he does. Would highly recommend this class and professor.

Dr. Thiede has a nearly encyclopedic knowledge of linguistics, yet is still approachable and engaging in lectures. The material is dense, but he takes steps to ensure students understand difficult concepts. The quizzes and tests are open-book, and he is an easy grader for the two required papers.

This course delved deep into the psychology of linguistics. Although I am not a linguist by any means, a fair bit of what was taught intrigued me. However, if this is not your major, no matter how nice or respectable this professor is, the way this class is taught will leave the material flying over your head or leaving it as soon as you pass.
If you do poorly in a Rowney class, it's your fault, and you should consider whether English is really for you.

This professor is an extremely tough grader. As a non English major I found it difficult to understand what he meant. Office hours didn't help me much either. Further investigation my classmates also struggled. There are no rubrics for this class not even for the 10 page final paper for the class.

Does not give clear instructions and gets sassy when you ask him to clarify. Talks about nothing the whole class. I participated frequently and he basically told me I was wrong, even though it's an English class where you can interpret things differently. He wants you to interpret things his way. Worst professor I've had at Charlotte.

never again. loved literature at one point never taking another literature class again.
love the professor though, he was sweet.
but never taking another class like this again. save urself some stress and tears and dont take this class, please.

I personally really enjoyed the professor, not so much the subject material. He is a relatively strict grader, however always leaves great comments on how you can improve, and makes sure everyone is on the same page in class. He is such a great guy, and if you're interested in the in-class readings, I recommend taking him!

Is not clear with directions. Gives the floor to people who think they are smarter than everyone. Lecture skills so awful. In person class is beyond boring. Talked about one of my papers in front of the whole class. Unfair grader. Penalizes you for not following directions that he doesn't even mention.

While he engages with students and loves an open discussion about the texts that are read in class, he is a tough grader and in my opinion an unfair grader. He does not make instructions clear and then penalizes you for not knowing instructions that he failed to mention. And when I say penalize, I mean penalize. Like C's and D's.

had him for approaches to literature. class discussions were boring unless you are someone insightful and wants to add something and i spent most of the class doing other homework. he is very helpful though if you seek his guidance and goes into a lot of detail if you're confused. he himself is a gentle person. canvas page was hard to navigate.

I took this class online. The workload was not clear and there was no syllabus. I would go do assignments based on what was due on Canvas. She never mentioned that we had daily writings to do, until the last day when I had to write out a semester's worth of daily writing within a day so my grade didn't drop my 20 points

Majority of the class is about your family history. requires you to do 5 generations when most students only knew 2 cuz immigration. Rude comments, vry disorganized, will take off points if your family history isn't sad enough, or if your artifact isn't exotic enough. Whole class had to redo entire assignments due to unclear instructions.

Prof. Raymonds workload was intimidating at first, but once you get into the groove of her assignments it becomes very easy. You are given two semester long projects. A family project which is 50% of your grade & an e-portfolio which is 20%. She has a lot of energy & gives awesome feedback on assignments. Do the work & attend her classes.
Grades are tough but is a great teacher. Don't skip classes and assignments and you're good to go.

Prof. Raymond is a spunky old lady! Engage in her class questions and form a relationship. She gives great feedback and easy going. Her class revolves around lots of small parts of a big family history writing. I was intimidated at first, but it was the best class that I wanted to go to at 8 am !

NOT FOR WRDS 1104 (was the only thing I could select). Dr. Hall has been one of the best professors that I have had at UNCC. His lectures are very entertaining and he is always willing to work one on one with students an answer questions. If you participate and do the work, it should not be too difficult.

You HAVE to meet with him outside of class (the sooner the better). This class is really challenging. You will be forced to change the way you write and view writing completely. You must participate in class to pass!! Only 4 major writing assignments, but do not underestimate the weekly readings. Continue to go back to weekly readings to revise.

Let me start off by saying this class really hard. It takes a lot of time and hard work if you want to succeed. Office hours are a must if you want to do well. There are 4 major assignments and weekly readings which can take a while to complete, DO not underestimate the weekly readings. If you communicate with him, you are bound to do well.

There will be 4 major assignment over the semester with random response readings in between then. He will be grading them really hard making it extremely difficult to get a good grade. No rubric to follow and he will give the same feedback to every student even if you have written a decently good paper. Made this class horrible. Worst professor

Terrible professor! Wrote 4 major papers that needed to be continuously revised throughout the semester. Weekly reading assignments that can take anywhere from 30 minutes to 3 hours apiece. Really tough grader. Feedback is copied and pasted onto every student's assignment. The grading criteria is super unclear. Participation is graded.

Practically impossible to get an A in his class even after writing several pages of work for his assignments. The highest someone got in my class was a B. Would not recommend taking him for this class as the workload is just enormous and the grading is awful. Not a great teacher at all and don't take his class if you want an A and less coursework.

Monica was knowledgeable and kind, but if you're seeking an "easy A class" AMST-Food in America, is not the one. The course requires outside volunteering hours and a project throughout the semester. Homework mainly comes from the textbook and takes time. It's good for credit, but not for those looking for an easy route.

She is a great professor. In a online course it is one discussion board and one quiz a week. You do have to read the given material to understand and pass the quizzes and discussion boards but nothing that has been given to read/ watch is hard. You have to read/watch the material to understand the quizzes and she uses lockdown browser.

She is a great professor (I have only had her online) she cares about students and explains grades that are given. In a online course it is one discussion board and one quiz a week. You do have to read the given material to understand and pass the quizzes and discussion boards but nothing that has been given to read/ watch is hard.

I took a half term summer course, which consisted of reading ~200 pages per week, a discussion, and a reading quiz. Overall it took about 10 hours per week. The quizzes aren't hard, she gives some of the questions beforehand. There are no lecture videos, just readings. 

As long as you have the time commitment, the class is an easy A.

Very kind professor who gives good feedback. Read a book a week and had one to two discussion boards and a reading quiz. Quizzes could be a bit tedious, so do them right after reading while info. is fresh. She is a very easy grader with discussion boards and a simple annotated bibliography as the final.

Absurd work load. You are expected to read a novel that is up to 149 thousand words long each week, and then remember pedantic and meaningless details from the book when you take the test each week. unless you are anything but a practiced speed-reader with photographic memory, don't take this course.
Dr. Belus' class was an interesting overview of the 1930s as a decade. I enjoyed the content, and the reading was easy to manage. Final exam was optional. I definitely would take her class again!

You typically have two assignments a week: a reading quiz and a discussion. Make sure you read the books because you WILL fail the quiz if you don't. The questions are not something you can Google and pass. However she chooses good books that are very engaging to read. If you don't skip the assignments, you'll get an A. Final is an annotated bib.
Pretty easy class for writing intensive
YOOO do not take this professor! 40 LONG questions + assignments + discussion due every week. 100-question exams and you only get 60 minutes. 15 PAGE final paper.

Very inspiring class, learned a lot. It was very meaningful and I would definitely take this course again. A lot of written assignments and discussions but on good topics so it wasn't bad. Easy A as long as you do your work on time because she doesn't take late work!!
A lot of writing, reading, and homework, with not a whole lot of teaching.

A liberal studies class that was a Gen Ed requirement. 2nd year level class with homework equivalent to a masters program. You will read more than you have time for and will have more homework than all your other classes combined. The readings, ironically, rarely have anything to do with the reading guides. Not a fan.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS Online class but in syllabus she expects you to put around 60 hours a week, meaning 8 hours a day just for this class. Every week there are study guides that consist of 20-40 short answer LONG questions, which takes days to complete. TAKE ANOTHER LBST

This was an interesting course, but you definitely need to read all of the materials and watch all of the films; the quizzes and exams were heavily dependent on those. It can be time consuming, so plan accordingly. Overall, not bad. If you enjoy watching Disney films, this can be a good course for you.

The information in the class was great. Theres a lot of quizzes and discussion boards. Only had the midterm, and final for 'tests'. If you don't go through all the material (which is a lot) you're screwed. Theres a lot of readings that go with the quizzes. But she is very clear as to what she wants you to look at and do for an assignment.
Very straight forward with the content, as long as you put in the effort you should be fine. Felt like the class had a lot of busy work, but easy nonetheless

Not an easy A because of amount of work given. Assignments are very easy but there are so many and so much content she expects you to consume in a short amount of time. She does too much for this class to be what it is. It says texts are required, but I did not buy any of the books or movies and was still got an A. Interesting class nonetheless.

Prof Rand is super caring, she's like a mom that loves you, maybe a little too much, she kind of needs to back off a little. Super caring, she really wants every student to succeed in her course. The entire second half of the course is just one big group project though, if that's your thing then go for it.

Dr.Rand is one of the best professors. She gives lots of feedback and wants everyone to do well in her class. Make sure to participate, a big part of this class is about MEETING other people as you will have a group project for half the semester. However, I recommend her 1000% out of any other professor!

Dr. Rand is an AMAZING professor. I took her in my first semester of college for WRDS1103 and am currently taking her course for CTCM 2530. She is so understanding if you ever have a conflict, she will always accommodate. Her assignments and projects are relevant to careers and understandable directions. 10000/10 recommend. Best professor ever!

I enjoyed Dr.Rand's class. She's kind and wants you to do well. During the second half of the semester, you have to do a major group project so keep that in mind. Besides that, you can ask her for critiques on assignments and she'll give you details about it and will explain things to you.

Dr. Rand is a very passionate and caring professor who made the course material for an LBST interesting to follow.  The course had a bit more work than I was expecting, but she reviewed all work and gave feedback on every assignment that was submitted as well as checked up on every student on a biweekly basis.  Overall a great professor
I loved her lectures and instructional time. She gives great feedback and is very approachable. Dr. Rand is one of the best professors I've had so far.

Dr. Rand was very kind and I really enjoyed her class. Although we had many papers and it was tough to finish them at times, she gave us a lot of time to work on them during class and gave great feedback.
She was a very caring and understanding professor. This is definitely a 4 credit course (the workload was sizeable) but she thoroughly taught the material, and was always available after hours.

I'll be honest, I am not biggest fan of Dr. Rand. I am not entertained or felt like I have been taught by her assignments. Sometimes I can't tell if the course material or her lectures are boring and tedious. However, I cannot deny that she is great editor and comment maker. She is kind and loving person. And wants everyone to get an A.
Throughout this course, I looked forward to coming to the class. Her grading criteria are proficient, and as long as you participate in the conversation and listen, you'll do just fine!

Professor Rand was very thoughtful and it truly felt like she cared about me, taking time outside of class to check up on things that were going on in my life. The last month is probably the hardest part and is where I slipped down to a B. If you attempt to do your work you will be fine.

I took Dr. Rands LBST2301 class in the fall of 2021. She always wanted students to give their own thoughts on things so she wouldn't be talking the entire time which I thought was great. She is very approachable, caring, and will be more than happy to talk to you if you don't understand something or are struggling in the class.

Kailan requires a lot of work for this course. During the semester is would take for forever to grade assignment. She was also not good at responding to emails for this course. Her lectures are long and not helpful at all. Most of the time other students would email students because everyone was confused.

Took online asynchronous. Turn your papers in early for peer reviews, or else you won't get any feedback before turning it in for a grade. A super cool teacher, you could go to office hours just to chat if you wanted.

I love Dr. Mitchell. We had an unusual class where the professor left and she had to step in. She let us chose the assignments and was very flexible with deadlines and getting help. She wants every student to succeed and will help you with whatever you need.

Dr. Mitchell is a wonderful professor that will make you a better writer GUARANTEED (as long as you put in the effort).

Full transparency: I maybe opened the textbook twice throughout her course and still got a 94

She was extremely caring and down to earth, showed up with a smile and energy each day. She cared about our well being and constantly asked if everyone was okay and up-to-date with the work. Slowed down to comfort us, and wasn't a harsh grader at all. Gave great feedback and understood certain situations. TAKE HER if you can, 10/10!!!

Dr. Mitchell was AMAZING, I had her my first semester & thought I was going to be run through the wringer with a Writing class. She made the assignments so easy, broke them down specifically, accepted them late, and also gave great feedback. She not only cared about her students, but also knew that we had life & other classes outside of hers.THANKU
Dr.Mitchell is a fantastic teacher! While the course is essay-heavy, that's just the class. She is a fair grader and accepts late work. If you can take WRDS with her, 100% take her class.
She is kind and will give good feedback whenever you ask.
She gives very clear instructions, has a good attitude, and will provide help if you need it.

(Messed up on other rating, class is a 2 in difficulty not a 5) If you're looking for a WRDS teacher choose Dr Mitchell. I have nothing but good things to say about her she is phenomenal and makes the effort to connect and be personal with everyone in class.

Yo I absolutely love Dr Mitchell. She is very energetic and you can tell she loves what she does. Due dates are assigned but she takes late work for full credit. She gives great feedback and allows you to make up bad grades. There is quite a bit of work, but it's reasonable. Talk in class it will make her day. 10/10 would definitely recommend.

Dr. Mitchell was a great professor. There is a lot of homework and readings that you must complete outside of class, but they are very helpful towards your large projects. She was an easy grader and gives you lots of good feedback on your writing. You also have the opportunity to revise your work at the end of the semester.

So so kind! Truly cares about students. Homework questions once per week, a few exams, a creative essay and final paper. Not a harsh grader and loves to hear what students have to say. So passionate about literature :) Highly recommend Dr. G

I would not recommend this class to anyone. She was sick for most of the semester and expected us to accommodate her and stay late for an already 3 hour class. Her feedback was so nitpicky yet most times, unjustified. She always sends out emails about class late the night before and didn't grade most of the assignments until the semester was over.

Dr. Gargano is by far one of my favorite professors. She's caring, and respectful, and shows that she truly cares about you and your work, especially if you're a grad student. Though she does get off topic at times. She's a fair grader and as long as you actually put effort and show that you care about the class, you should receive a decent grade.

Nadine was super kind and caring when you got to know her. If you stay on track, get assignments done on time, and stay focused during class, she will have no problem with you. If you don't do one of those things, she is extremely willing to help you. She is extremely respectful and caring. Not a super hard class, but assignments can be tedious.

If you attend class, are active in discussions, and do the work on time, you'll have no issues. She jumps around a lot and can be confusing. Grading is sometimes immediate, other times it's 2 months. Grading isn't that harsh, if you perform quality work you'll get an A. Prepare to have issues in Canvas + ensure you read the weekly module b4 class.

She's a strict teacher who gives out a lot of work with short deadlines. But she's an easy grader, as long as you do your work and pay attention you'll be fine. If you communicate any concerns you have, she's very understanding but she may question you.

Professor Gordon is great and focuses on many creative and inspirational writing topics that make you rethink many aspects of the subject. Assignments are quite easy if you are a semi decent writer. The class mainly asks you to challenge your previous notions of literature and compose papers or projects.

She picked favorites and also chose to pick on specific students. I do not think she understands that different students learn in different ways and not everyone is like her. She changes due dates without telling anyone and flips out when you do not have it done. She also makes faces and scoffs at you like you are in elementary school.

- does not grade things unless you ask IN PERSON and sit with her while she grades them
- Yells/Screams at you for things she did
- Calls you out in class a lot
- Easy workload; she is insane in the head
- I had an F for 90% of the semester because she wont grade or loses assignments
- Due dates change as she pleases...

She's very good with students that regularly show up for class and participate, but if you aren't willing to share opinions and be challenged on what you think, definitely don't take the class. She's very unapologetically herself and provides her number outside of class. When I've texted her she responds within an hour. Can be insensitive sometimes

So unclear. No one in class had a clue what was going on ever. Never gave straight answers. Subtly racist and transphobic. Called students annoying in front of the whole class. Reads text messages that pop up on students laptops. Slammed her hand on my shoulder whenever she talked to me. NOSY! DOES NOT RESPECT PERSONAL SPACE! DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!

Shes not a bad professor but can test your patience . Takes forever to grade things but is an easy grader . Also provides the textbook . If you dont come to class she will call you when you show up again .

She's very strict about attendance. If you go over her six-day policy then you get an email saying you're at risk of failing her class. She also gives vague feedback and then when you do that feedback on the drafts it's still not enough because it's not exactly what she wants. The class is fun and you'll meet great people in there but she's tough.
Dry. Real dry. Nice woman, but gee did I fall asleep.

This professor was critical but provided many good works for students to digest. Critical does not mean bad, although if your style of fiction writing does not align somewhat closely to that which she teaches in class, it is clear she will be harsher on your works. Luckily, I aligned with what she taught and enjoyed it, but not everyone will.

I took this class not knowing much about Russian History but I learned a lot from her. This class wasn't hard and the professor was very easy to work with, it was a few assignments weekly and multiple choice quizzes. I would recommend her if you want an easy class.

We only used the textbook at the beginning of the semester (find free pdf if able). Professor Rhodes is very considerate as long as you pay attention and participate in class. Be sure to go and talk to her after class - She is very accommodating as long as you put in the effort! Lots of extra credit so no reason to get below an A. Low stress class.

She ensures that all students participate, and makes EVERYTHING easy to understand. She's fun, caring, and understanding, and is extremely passionate about English. Most assignments are in class, and any homework assignments are simple, with ample time for completion. Failing this class would be a result of poor attendance and lack of effort!

Professor Rhodes is a bit unorganized and often puts together assignments the day of class, so we're waiting for her to post it in class. Instructions are often vague, so double check you're doing the right thing. There's a lot of time wasted in her class and she often posts assignments a day before they're due without sending an announcement.

This teacher said I was not paying attention in the class and that she would complain about me. She took two of my assignments and turned them into zeros, stating that I could redo them for credit (for not following directions). This teacher is extremally vague on purpose (I have complained) and she will not answer simple questions (Nightmare).

She is a very nice person and the class should be an A if you just do the assignments. She did seem unprepared at times and assignments usually didn't have clear instructions. I would take her class if you're looking for an easy A, just expect there to be some frustration.

She is a super nice lady. Yes, the class sometimes had a few bumps in the road, but she did her best by being flexible with us. Everything she wanted from us was so straightforward and it was never a hassle getting the assignments done. I would take her again solely for her personality, she was very positive and caring for all the students.

Professor Rhodes was okay. The class wasn't difficult, so it's an easy A. However half the time we sat there and did nothing because it appeared that she didn't have much prepared for class. Most of the instructions are hard to follow but if you ask her to fix them, most of the time she'll explain more. Overall she was mediocre.

He is a great professor. He gets off track a lot but he really cares about his students. You don't do much in his classes and they are easy As. I would recommend going to his office hours and getting to know him because he is helpful and cares a lot. He has helped me with a lot of professional things outside of the classroom.

Truly cares about students as people, graded on VERY few assignments but an easy grader -- and I mean easy. Don't take him if you dislike class-length lectures, writing, or reading, otherwise you're golden. Knowledgeable and experienced, has an expansive background in biology and literature. Will take a while to respond to emails.

He's fine. Just... perfectly average, actually. He's decently funny, but he gets off topic a lot to the point where it can get annoying. Don't take him if you want to focus on the material, or want solid grades for everything.
I learned a lot from this class. Definitely not bad for an LBST class I had to take.

This was a really cool class on science fiction! The professor had an interesting teaching style and most of the readings were enjoyable. The class was discussion heavy with some lectures, so participation is a must. The grades were spread out between smaller assignments so your grade didn't count on one final paper. Would recommend!

This professor was a great guy! He taught in a way that was extremely unique but kept students engaged. He does pop quizzes but they're easy if you keep up to date on reading! Some of the books are also really interesting. Put in some work and make sure you participate to get points, and you'll get a good grade!
Great class! Enjoyed the material and found that Prof Ward was willing to meet to discuss the final papers and projects as I needed. Very helpful.

There were four textbooks, but two were just short stories and one was a comic book. The professor also assigned some movies like Blade Runner and Ghost in the Shell, which was cool. There were three papers, and the professor wasn't the easiest grader, but he let you edit the paper to get points back. All in all a fun class!

Took her ENGL 4161 Modern English Grammar class in-person. Really nice & knowledgeable professor but class is super tough. Pay attention to the lectures, follow her outline notes, and study, study, study. She is super caring and always answered everyone's questions & was available outside of class, too. The content is just a lot to understand.
She explains things so well!

Dr. Roeder is awesome! I took ENGL 4262 with her and she was not only well-versed in and passionate about her field but also incredibly kind and encouraging. I won't lie, the work and theory can be challenging and the readings are consistent, but if you're interested in English at all she is is a must-have professor!

Dr. Roeder was an exceptional teacher. Although I am not a linguist in any sense of the word and do not understand its many intricacies, her class primarily focused on the societal ills surrounding linguistic distinction. This, along with her genuine nature and clear care for these issues, was what intrigued me and kept me eager to learn more.

Dr. Steele is a true activist through and through. Very lenient w/ deadlines as long as you communicate ahead of time. Lots of seminars, but they were simple enough. Pen pal project was the highlight of this class.  Topics were controversial yet eye-opening. I would recommend if you actually want to challenge your beliefs. Very caring too. 10/10

Dr. Steele is the closest I've ever gotten to having a good relationship with a professor here like I would in high school. So far, this class was the best one I've taken even though it was difficult. If you want a professor who is passionate about what they do, take a class with Dr. Steele, please!

I really enjoyed ENGL 1105 with her. She made lectures entertaining and stayed on topic with the course outcomes. The papers that were do were well spread out throughout the semester and she provided time for feedback.
I hate writing so this was a hard class for me, but Amy was super helpful and understanding. Hard class but good professor.

Great choice for a writing professor. Was very caring about the class and wanted everyone to excel. If you're confused about something she's always glad to clear any doubts. You'll have about 4 writing projects to do with one final portfolio at the end, so get ready to do some writing. There will also be weekly questions based on textbook passages.

I love Professor Colombo. She's very kind and caring to all of her students. She's always going to be there for you 24/7. Coming into the class I was not really a fan of writing but she made writing really fun and interesting to learn about. She a top 10 professor at UNCC fasho

Very passionate about her subject and clearly an expert. She made learning very enjoyable and her energy was high each and every day of class. She was very good about engaging with all students and making sure that everybody understood what was being taught and what was expected on each assignment. Extremely caring and understanding professor. (((:

I really enjoyed this class even for a writing course. She gave amazing feedback and made class pretty interesting for what it is. There was lots of homework and a lot of reading which was not fun at times. I gained so much from this course and could not recommend her enough even for such a boring topic imo. Just do the work and you'll succeed.

You will read a fair amount of diverse children's literature. While this isn't terrible in concept, the stories themselves are mostly subpar at best, even for simple works. Although there is worthwhile messaging to pick from the entries, most are trite and poor examples of what children's storytelling can be. The teacher was nice, at least.

This was a great creative writing class and worked well to introduce the different types of writing forms that fall under the given umbrella. The teacher was also great and she worked hard to keep us invested in our work and the works of our classmates. Taking this class helped to prepare me for my advanced classes further down the line.

Genuinely such a great teacher. She's funny, her lectures are very easy to understand and therefore makes the course way more engaging. I honestly hope I have the chance to have her again in the future!
Awesome professor! If you go to class she explains things very well. She uploads notes and attendance isn't a huge grade. Minimal assignment.
literally so nice and fun. if u miss a class, her PowerPoints and easy hw make it easy to catch up. highly recommend
Amazing Prof!!!

I loveeeee Dr. B. She is so amazing. She did stress us out by saying that people usually bomb the first test and that it's not the end of the world, but I honestly made a quizziz flashcard set and went over it for three days and got 95, 95, 100. Just pay attention in class and in lab, and take good notes. Also do Dr. B's challenge! Free extra cred
Dr B was a fantastic professor for a difficult course. Notes are the most important part of the class and be prepared to memorize!

She is so nice! Comm theory is a hard class and she makes it easy! definitely use her study guide, attend class, and study hard for the tests and you will
do just fine! just make sure to keep up with your assignments, because there are not many assignments so it can heavily affect your grade

You either read the book or pay attention to the lectures. I passed this class with a high B and studied right before the exam. She is very sweet and the lectures are enjoyable. Don't take this class with anyone else. All the other teachers have interesting reviews....

Dr. B is suchhhh a good teacher. She explains things very thoroughly and is open for questions if you don't understand something. Lots of easy assignments, but the tests are pretty hard. Definitely make sure to go to class tho bc there aren't many outside resources other than the textbook.

Dr. B was awesome! Attendance is not mandatory, but she makes class fun, and everything she lectures on WILL be on the exams! The material is difficult, she posts each presentation in Canvas, but you need to go to class as she goes more in depth when she teaches. All assignments are very simple and def help when it comes to studying for exams :)

Known to be a hard class. The homework assignment is super easy, and is used for studying material. Discussions are also good, you go over your test grade. You just have to study a week prior to the exam. I failed the first test I did not study in advance, 2nd test I got an A. She also does games for extra credit. Good lectures and slides.
n/anananananana

Dr.B is hands down one of the best professors ever! She makes her lectures very understanding and relates everything to the real world. She gives out multiple opportunities for extra credit, especially with Dr.B's challenges. Her TA, Alexa was amazing as well. Overall, HIGHLY recommend taking her to any COMM classes.

Best teacher I've had since high school. She took one of the hardest classes in COMM and made it simple. Does not give out any homework but has a TON of extra credit opportunities. Her lectures are engaging and funny and keeps them relatable. 3 exams total but she makes sure your well prepared for them. Just show up. Job well done, Dr. B!

Dr.B is fantastic! She is honest about the course from the start and you need to put in the work. You pay for the course, so attend the lecture... She's and is not boring at all, super friendly and so is her TA (shoutout Alexa Adams)! They were a wonderful tag team, and help teach you the material and find ways to improve their course!

She isn't very strict, but if you want to succeed in this class you need to show up to class. The good thing about Dr. Basinger is that she keeps lectures interesting and with activities. She is the best professor I have ever had, don't miss out on Dr.B's challenge!!! Best professor I have ever had at UNCC.

I loved this class, Dr. B was an amazing and hilarious lecturer, you can tell that she cares for her students success! The class is extremely easy in my perspective, just attend class, take notes because her examples will be on the exam and STUDY!!! There are only 5 grades for the entire semester, 3 exams and 2 essays.
Extremely easy class if you are studying ahead (1 week before). If you want to pass, come to class cause everything on the exam usually relates to her examples given in class.

It is a tough class, however Dr. B makes it fun, and she is a very personable prof. She responds to emails and id very understanding, and open to ways to improve the course. If you're taking COMM2100 you should def take it with Dr. B

Dr. Basinger is an amazing professor, witty and fun, she cares about students' feedback. Course isn't hard if you study 4-7 days before. 3 tests, 2 papers, easy if you follow directions. Lots of extra credit. Attend lectures, study ahead, follow instructions, guaranteed A!

I could not get a hold of him as he does not leave his email for his students to find him. I tried to connect the TA that he listed but he gave the wrong email so I could not contact them either. I had to search him up in the faculty/staff directory. This was a pass/no credit class and I could mot even reach him for help on the test.

To be honest, this class is a very easy A. He's a decent professor, just a bit unengaging at times. This class is very dependent on breakout sessions with your TAs. If you just want an easy class to pass, this is what you're looking for.

Prof Paddock is awesome. His class has been my favorite college course so far. He's super friendly and willing to work with you on just about anything. My whole class loved taking this course with him, and I highly recommend him. We had lots of fun and he's just great.

Have had Mr. Paddock at least once every year since starting college. Really nice professor, cares about students, wants to help them succeed. For JOUR classes, he grades harshly, but the feedback is detailed and helpful. Most grades were a B, even if I thought I did my best work. Not a negative, just be aware.

Paddock is a tough grader. He will nitpick your entire news story and often not correct what you did wrong. He will instead write what he would have written as a story and then make you email him for details on what you missed. If you're wondering about the averages that his classes are making. For assignments, the mean grade was a 38/50...

Mr. Paddock is very funny! His lectures and classes are engaging since it is a smaller class you become very personable. Very helpful - always willing to give feedback through email, and even offers class time to review assignments or big point assignments like news stories. Does not have a clear grading system (no rubric for assignments)

Professor Paddock was amazing. I was scared after he said most people don't pass the final exam their first time. He gives you 4 times to take it and I passed SIGNIFICANTLY my first time taking it just from him being such a good professor and I genuinely learned stuff.

Professor Paddock is extremely friendly but in my 5 years of college I have never seen a professor grade harder. Our whole class seems to believe he grades our reports on a whim and no one got any 100s.

If you have to take him it's not the end of the world but it will not be easy and very few of the grades you receive will make any logical sense

Paddock had a great relationship with the whole class. Public speaking is tough for everyone, but I think he does a pretty good job on feedback and specifics to improve on. Lectures were super engaging but sometimes material was vague so you hope that your speech was good enough for what he covered in class. Overall great but hard to make a high A.

I took this business comm course online. Videos and assignments due every week- it is a lot of work but if you take the time to do it, you will do well in this class. He is a very personable professor and truly cares about his students, but is kind of a harsh grader on writing. Overall I recommend and he's definintely one of the better professors.

Professor Paddock is a very caring and kind Professor, just please make sure you come to his class. The only thing hard about his class is the exams. Although the class was very boring, the professor was very understanding and you could ask questions. Professor will know your name and you will be in Professor's good graces by coming to class!

Professor Paddock is an extremely cool professor. I really enjoyed his lectures in Ethics in Journalism simply because of how funny he was. The course is made up of 12 quizzes, a midterm, a final, and five short-answer questions, so it's very doable. I learned a lot about how to remain ethical as a journalist and I would definitely take him again!

This is a pass/fail class, so as long as you receive above a 70 on the final exam, which you have four chances to take, you will pass the class. In order to take the exam you have to complete four modules, so make sure you complete those pretty early in the semester so you can take the test a few times.

I had Mr. Paddock for UCOL, and took this class because he was teaching it! The grading is based off of only a few speeches over the semester, so it is important to take his feedback into account after your first couple speeches, but he is a very lenient grader. Great guy, definitely hope to take a class taught by him again!
Paddock is an all-around great professor. Teaches editing very directly and has background in the field as well which is very nice. One of my favorite professors at the university.

Professor Paddock took the time to get to know each student individually, and the class itself was super easy as long as you showed up. So happy that I get him again for Public Speaking, he is a great professor!

She's a very, VERY tough grader. You cannot make any mistakes, or she will call you out on them. The writing assignments cannot be done at the last minute. Be ready to go to actual school events to write your papers about them. Not an easy A. Gives very good feedback. Read the rubrics thoroughly, do the assignments on time, and you'll be okay.

Firstly, you have to know that she's a really tough grader. No slip-ups and no makeups. She makes you write a lot and read a lot too. There will be assignments where you have to go out of your way just to create accounts to finish the assignment. I got banned from "X" for making tweets that were needed for her assignment.

This class was difficult for no reason. You have to follow Professor Hubler's instructions on the assignments but the instructions don't seem clear.  This class is not an EASY A-Class. Only 1 extra credit assignment. You also have to do weekly questions that don't seem relevant. Take this course with someone else if you can.

I took JOUR2160 with Professor Hubler online. She's definitely a tough grader, but I found the class and assignments to be pretty straightforward and simple. There's 5 major writing assignments, 5 completion assignments, and a few quizzes. If you enjoy writing, I definitely recommend this class

Dr. Hubler was incredibly knowledgeable on the topic of Journalism and made it really easy to understand for beginners. She is definitely a tough grader, but as long as you read and make changes based on her feedback, you will do fine! Very interesting class and I would definitely recommend her to anyone new to Journalism.

Hubler made sure we always knew what to expect and gave us a clear schedule. You do have to write a lot but it is to be expected in a journalism class. She made sure she was available for any questions or feedback via email. My skills have grown in her class! Make sure you are grammatically correct and follow the rubric and you'll be set!

Dr. Scott is knowledgeable and a great lecturer. You are going to think you don't need to read, but when it comes to tests and pop quizzes, they ALL come from the book. You can go off the lecture, but I noticed a big difference between when I read and when I didn't. I suggest his class, I learnt a lot from this course.

The material from this class was harder than I expected, but he's a good teacher and makes class enjoyable. DON'T SKIP CLASS. If you miss a pop quiz for any reason, you get an automatic zero, even if you're sick or have an emergency. The tests are very hard. One good thing is that the assignments are really easy and not time-consuming at all.

I enjoyed this class and this prof! He's very striaghtfoward and down to earth. He does random pop quizes with not much warning, so this is where attendance matters. I reccommend going to as many classes as possible, because the tests are based on lectures more than the textbook. The online resource he gives called A First Look is SO helpful!

If you do not show up to lecture you will fall behind. Dr. Scott has very thorough lectures with information that is not on the posted slides. I finished with an A by taking good notes and doing the Packback throughout the semester. There are pop quizzes on textbook readings. Absolutely would take him again.

Dr Scott doesn't require mandatory attendance, but it really will benefit you to go and take notes. He and his TAs were very helpful, and I thought his lectures were interesting. He is a really funny guy. He doesn't assign much, so make sure to do the work he does give and attend lectures; you will do just fine. Great professor, and I recommend!
Great class, great professor.

The class was okay, but it was tough. A lot of reading, lectures, and notes. MUST do those things to succeed even barely. Questions are written by him, Quizlet will not help. Exams incredibly tough (best: 76 worst: 55). TA did most of the work, found her to be very frustrating and difficult. Communication with Dr. Scott was obviously poor.
