I studied an insane amount and still felt confused by 95% of the final exam as well.

Professor Armour made this class quite difficult for a 1000-level class. He could also be rude sometimes in his emails. He was ok in the lecture. His tests were quite difficult, but he did allow a cheat sheet for every one of them.

I honestly have mixed feelings. He's clearly a very passionate guy, but by god his class is awful. The things he teaches in the lectures never show up on the test. I missed the infamous projector question test and my grade is still ok luckily, but on the last test I filled out a massive cheatsheet of everything we learned and I used 2% of it. Avoid
Took this professor twice for two different classes. Amazing dont listen to other reviews

The professor was nice but I would NOT recommend this class to ANYONE. This was an introductory course and yet it seemed you had to be an expert to pass the tests. You have to do the extra credit to get by or you are cooked.

Hands down the worst professor I have ever had. He doesn't explain his assignments and often rambles on about his "adventures". He loves to go over class times even though he says he won't. He never explains why you received the grade you did; he expects you to know and move on. He does do a lot of extra credit, but the assignments are very long.

Wouldn't recommend taking this class. Like many people have said, he used a projector for a test but the most recent test he gave that up. His lectures are useless because the tests are on stuff that's never covered. He surprised us with a decent sized project that we have to work on over Thanksgiving and a final exam seven days after that.

Puts 1-2 test questions on a projector screen at a time, gives students a bubble sheet, and slowly scrolls through questions making students take long tests all at the same pace. There is no purpose coming to class as nothing he teaches is relevant towards the test. However, there are plenty of extra credit opportunities and cheat sheet is allowed

the tests are awful for my class he used a projector it was barely readable from the back of the lecture hall some students had to sit on the floor just to see. We were all give a bubble sheet and he would manually swipe and display 1-2 question at a time. 0/10 took the whole class for 50 questions

put a test on the projector infront of the class and gave us all bubble sheets. students were not allowed to go at their own pace and he displayed each question one (or up to three) at a time. that test would have been easier if he actually taught the class, instead of going on large useless tangents.

This teacher is very nice but does NOT stay on topics for his lectures. The tests will be on 3 heavy chapters and he'll yap about a couple concepts for the whole chapter. in reality, you are teaching yourself.

The class itself is very boring and the tests can be very hard. However, he provides up to a whole letter grade worth of extra credit, so as long as you're participating to the fullest, you should be fine.

Took this class to satisfy a science w/o lab, and I honestly regretted it, as the tests felt impossible, the lectures were very boring, and the content was confusing (for me). However, there were ample extra credit opportunities, but be prepared to pay attention during lectures, read the book, and utilize the 'cheat sheet' you can use during exams

Overall, Professor Armour is very kind and friendly. He's always willing to help students with anything class-related, and he clearly knows what he's talking about. BEWARE OF HIS TESTS. The grade you receive will be largely dependent on your test scores, and the tests are extremely difficult. He gives a lot of extra credit throughout the semester.

I heavily suggest avoiding taking one of his classes. There is a lot of group work that requires you to be in labs outside of class time, but he will not give you access to these rooms, so you just have to figure it out. The material was very difficult and I don't think I've learned much from his lectures.

He's a brand new professor. I took his Stable Isotopes class and greatly regret it. Grading was inaccessible because he refused to learn how to use canvas. The homework was assinine and made no sense. He ripped through lectures like we were at a PhD level when the class was full of undergrads. Then complained that he didn't have enough time. AVOID!
He's a really good teacher who cares about the topic and he's very passionate about geology, would recommed him for this class but he does a accent but once you pick up on it you'll do good.
His accent is a little hard to understand and he tends to ramble sometimes. Had to do A LOT of self studying. He had like 3, 50 multiple choice exams before the final exam and unit homework.

Do not take him. Most horrible class I have ever taken. He takes forever to grade and claims attendance is not mandatory but it is because that counts towards your grade…. He literally does not help you if you ask him questions. I took this as a gen ed and literally it was the worst decision I could've made.

He's very knowledgeable and passionate about his work but has the worlds heaviest accent. Few assignments, lots of lectures, but it's pretty easy if you take notes and study for the exams. We barely used the textbook, I'd honestly try to find it online somewhere. He can be hard to understand but his slides cover most of the words he can't pronounce
For a gen ed there was an unnecessary amount of work. Final project was graded harshly and the rubrics were unclear. Other CTCM courses have a smaller workload.

Valerie was an awful professor. I did every assignment fully and she gave me 100s on all of my assignments, until the last few weeks. Out of nowhere she became a super harsh grader. One assignment you had to do research, and I did like 4 hours of research, and I still got a 42 on it despite following all criteria I needed to for the assignment.

The structure of this class makes it very difficult to apply feedback. Grading criteria isn't always clear, and I didn't enjoy this class overall. Improvements can be made for the class content and structure. Overall not difficult, but can be workload-heavy.

Easygoing professor who provides lectures that are helpful for the test and is accessible outside of class. She is active in the geography and earth science department while also being apart of the geo club. The test she gives are relevant to what was taught in class. I rarely studied for them but attending the lectures allowed me to pass them.

Overall this was a great professor.  Took this as a 6 week online class and she posted everything for the week so that we could work ahead.  Lots of reading and lectures however I would pick one or the other to do because it's too much to try and do both.

Professor Reynolds is amazing. She makes the class so interesting and is really knowledgable and passionate on the subject. She responds fast to emails and wants to help you understand the material. You cover a lot of material throughout the semester and she gives in class assignments so attendance is mandatory. She is great!

Do not take the asynchronous online version of this class! It is a lot of work that doesn't make much sense as well as doesn't really relate to the course. If you enjoy learning about fracking and environmental law then this will probably be up your alley. The course also is set up really odd and is unorganized.
A great professor who genuinely seems interested in her class and tries to keep the class engaged. Class is easy to understand as long as you go to class and do your work.

100% recommend any class that Lauren Burns teaches!  Easy to understand and work with, always happy, and tries to engage the class.  Homework is due Friday nights, and you have a week to work on it.  No surprise quizzes, and midterm & final review in class.
Changed my life if you have opportunity to take her class sell your soul to do it I'm not joking it's worth it!

Professor Lauren is one of a kind! Even though she is young she knows so much about meteorology and is super passionate. The homework assignments are super easy and as long as you come to class and study the slides for the quizzes you will easily pass. Lil tip the Midterm and Final exam are all the quizzes put together into a test. Plz, take her!

Professor (now Burns) is the best professor I have had so far. She told us at the last lecture that this was only her second year teaching, but you couldn't tell at all, as she is a pro. She dumbs down lecture material into easily understandable concepts and always makes sure we are well prepared for quizzes. She was simply a joy to be around.

She is caring and provides a good amount of extra credit. This was an elective and it was a walk in the park. The most time consuming part is reading a whole chapter of the book every week. Multiple choice quizzes and exams. Her lectures are good overall, no attendance required but she gives out in class assignments that count towards the grade.

This course requires a lot of vocabulary and terms. She is so sweet, and she will answer all your questions. The lecture can be a little boring, but I recommend attending exam review sessions, which are helpful and similar to the actual exam. So many extra credit opportunities are provided. I would take her again if given the opportunity.

Professor Decker is amazing. She is so kind, caring and compassionate. On our final exam, she put a page on it with three thoughts... 1: Perfection is not attainable 2: Your grades do not define you 3: Failure is a GOOD thing.

She is younger, so it's easier to relate to her in classes and I did not feel intimidated to talk to her.

This professor was amazing; she taught for the first time after receiving her degree, & even though she's young, she understands what it's like to be struggling. The tests are definition heavy and the study guides are a lot, but if you study & go to class you'll be fine. Lots of extra credit as well. She even gave some for the final as well.
Great teacher! All the homework is very easy and she does a great job teaching so the 2 tests are easy if you go to class.

Professor Decker cares about her students and the class is very easy if you do the work. The one thing I didn't like is she tests very heavily on definitions and doesn't go in-depth on the actual science and its physical impact. If you are good with definitions take her, otherwise, consider taking a different professor.

Took this course because I needed a science, and Professor Decker actually made me really enjoy meteorology. She is very caring and the lectures are fun. There is some in class work that you will have to do but other than that there wasn't much work for the course.
Tons of content. Review outside of class. Seems like a little too much content for a Gen-ed.
she's super sweet and loves what she does. assignments are very clear and easy to do when you pay attention
if you are looking for an easy and quick class to take dont take her ESCI 1101 class. she assigns way too much homework during the week.

I loved this prof, it was her first year teaching after graduating and she did a great job, she is young so she definitely gets it if your struggling.  She always made our class laugh and offered extra credit on every test we had, the tests are heavy but most multiple choice.  Its really easy to learn concepts and there was not a lot of hw. 10/10.
Too much work for an introductory class. 5 assignments on Cengage + discussion board (250-500 words) every week.

She definitely wants her students to succeed! If you put effort in to learn the material (which is straight forward) you will get an A. Only two tests and the final which were all based on the online textbook (ESCI 1101). Very good at responding to emails as well :) I would take it again for sure

Great professor, the only thing is you have to do a lot of learning/readings outside of class. She did teach but a lot is needed to be done outside of class. She is a very considerate professor and allows you take a test if something comes up!

Her meteorology class is one of the easiest gen ed sciences you'll ever take. Be warned there's a lot of vocab to memorize, but she gives out tons of participation note packets and has oodles of opportunities for extra credit. Lots of assignments from the reading but she drops a ton of them, she really wants everyone to get a good grade
Good teacher

Professor Chapman was a very polite professor who was definitely prepared for her class.  However, I felt like this was a super difficult class for just a gen ed.  Luckily, she is very graceful and rounded my grade to an A, which I am super grateful for.  But just know that for a gen ed, this was really hard and I had to put a lot of effort in it.

This class was so stressful. Test were ridiculous and when we voiced our concern, she basically said try harder. The tests are worded weird and the images she draws for test are jokes. The test are made for you to fail. She was no help so do what you can to avoid her!

You have to put in a lot of actual hours and work to pass this class with high marks. Attendance is taken by material poll everywhere questions but not once a class, 4-5, sometimes 6x during the class period and also counts against your grade if answered wrong for every poll. Only good thing is that she had zoom options everyday

This class was iffy, I got a good grade but as a gen-ed class it wasn't worth it with this professor. VERY lecture heavy its all you do in class and it gets boring. You can have a cheat sheet for exams, the study guide we use for the cheat sheet never really goes along with it. YOU HAVE TO COME TO CLASS and try hard or I promise you will not pass.

The people who complain about her just don't put enough effort in. Overall if you actually keep up with the textbook your good. Anything you don't understand from the book you definitely will after the lecture because she explains things so well. You can make a cheat sheet for every test and you get very comprehensive study guides too.

If you show up and write half the things she says down you'll be fine. PollEv is used for attendance but if you get over 75% of them over the semester its goes to 100% which helps your grade A LOT. If you care enough to listen and review its hard to fail.

I would literally voice my concern everyday because I was on the verge of failing because of the poll everywhere questions. she doesn't actually care about you as a student, so this is your sign to run!
Literally she is the worst professor I've ever had.

She is a terrible teacher. all you do is listen to lectures and read a ridiculous amount of text book pages. Yes her tests are open note but all the questions are conceptual so they're not always the most helpful. The class is way to much work and way to hard for a gen-ed. Do yourself the favor and take it with a different teacher. Horrible.
Attendance taken by poll everywhere; pollev is used for everything including participation but its really easy. As long as you show up and take notes, youll be fine.

Attendance is taken through Poll Everywhere, and homework is through Cengage. Lectures can be boring. A lot of information is covered but Chapman makes it easy to understand. Take notes on the study guide as you go to class and youll do fine on the tests.
I took Dr. Bredy both online and in person and I would not recommend taking her online. She is not the best with technology which can make it difficult and frustrating to complete class assignments.

I took this as an online section after reading her reviews. Overall the course itself is quite easy and nott too much work, however with it being an online class, she felt that she could keep assigning assignments past the last day of class. In addition to that, she locks our assignments every week until thursday which was incredibly frustrating.

For my section she did not require attendance, since class was used to do extra credit group projects or for her to read PPT presentations. She might change how she ran the class this semester since it was her first time teaching the class. And she said she has some things she wants to change for next semester.
She was a super sweet and kind person. Not much work at all and easy to get an A in. She often made classes asynchronous or on Zoom which was nice.

The section I had her was pretty chill and never got more difficult than a 2 page paper. Mostly a class to get introduced to the campus and it's notable class gets turned asynchronous often and on short notice. Ms. Bredy herself is very kind and doesn't really have the 'teacher' barrier during her class, she's casual in a good way.

Avoid this professor if you can. The course is disorganized, instructions are unclear, and she responds dismissively to questions. She doesn't accept late work despite what the syllabus says. Listen to the reviews; they're not lies. I still earned an A only through constant self-advocacy and frustration. Anyone but her!

CTCM 2530 — Dr. Bredy is an amazing and inspirational professor. While she grades rigorously, she provides valuable feedback and allows you to improve your assignments without penalty. She is very helpful and answers any questions you may have. I would rate her a perfect 10/10. Although there is a lot of reading, the class is manageable.

If you email her for help, don't even bother; she won't offer help or fix any grade issues, but instead complain how the email isn't "professional" enough. Grades harshly on formatting with no rubric and takes an excessive amount of points off for small tedious things. Half the time class is cancelled on important dates.

The absolute worst professor I've had throughout my time in college. 0 communication regarding her grading standard. She grades harsh at seemingly random and hands out 50's for trivial errors. She is extremely rude and combative through emails. Succeeding in this class was very difficult, not because of the material but because of her.
terrible terrible teacher just avoid her !!! whatever you do
Dr. Bredy is truly an amazing profesor. I learned so much in her class and if I had to take it again I definitely would!

She was super disorganized and her assignments were not clear on grading or directions. All emails to her have to be super professional or she will ignore the original email and say you have to redo it because you approached it "disrespectfully".

Have to email her twice within 78 hours to even get a response if she feels like it. She has zero rubrics and when asked for feedback on why you got a low grade on an assignment and what you can do to improve she doesnt answer. She set up meetings with her students to discuss her teaching and how she could improve. She did not even show up.
Course was okay, everything was disorganized and assignments were given to us at the last minute.

Professor Bredy's class is extremely disorganized, and grading and rubrics are super unclear. Don't even use the rubrics because if you follow the rubrics you will receive a 0, if you ask for feedback or more clear instructions she will ignore you. Worst class and professor I have taken at UNCC.

She provides little to no instruction on her assignments and when students ask her for a rubric or help she ignores them. so vague and disorganized. She gave us a 1:35 min video. Over 1 minute of it was her figuring out how to share her screen. and the rest was her reading the vague instructions to us. This is ridiculous.
Poor communication, unprepared
This professor ruined my career, i am now suffering because of her. MY dreams are over. Everything about her is bad!

Professor Brady is disorganized and unprepared! Lectures consisted of watching TED Talks, listening to podcast, and doing group work. Through the semester, instructions were unclear and feedback did not match assigned grades. If you desire to learn and grow professionally, I would suggest taking this course with a different professor!

The class could be a little bit disorganized at time but Dr Bredy was one of the best professors I have ever had! She truly cares about both her students & making sure she is aiding us in understanding the material. Participation does matter but she tries to make the lecture interesting & fun! I would take definitely take her again in a heart beat!

Love professor Halfmann, such a hard working, caring woman. She is so ready to help and prepare you for real life. This class is tough and the project and tests hold majority of your grade but I genuinely learned a ton of useful skills.

Great communication, very supportive. She's such a nice person, u can tell she wants her students to succeed, albeit with tough love. Do not to procrastinate your final project. Exams were very hard but I got an excellent grade on the project and ended with a low A. Don't be scared by low ratings, just work with her if u need help.

She genuinely wants you to succeed, but the tests are hard. Since they are most of your grade if you do bad it's hard to get an A. She offers office hours and is really helpful and the QI project is not that bad, it's easy to get an A on even though she says you should be proud of C.

AVOID. She makes simple material feel impossible and you end up teaching yourself. Her tests look nothing like the study guide, and one bad exam ruins your grade. No extra credit, no flexibility, and zero empathy for students. The QI project barely helps. The workload is miserable, the grading is brutal, and the class is pure stress. 0 empathy!

Test heavy and they are nothing like the study guide, final project was graded harshly was told if you receive a C on this project then you did what the project asked and had all the requirements and should be proud of yourself, personally I dont think I should be proud of a C. Feels like she got joy out of us not getting high grades.
Great online course. Dont be scared!

Professor Halfmann is by far one of the best professors I have had at UNC Charlotte! She is kind, encouraging, and desires for students to succeed. However, this is a challenging class that requires understanding of a lot of information each week. If you read the book, come to class, ask questions, and work hard on assignments, you will succeed!

If you go to class, you will pass. Gives you info relevant to every quiz, exam, project. Willing to help you and makes class interesting even though info in lecture may be slow. Very personable and cares about your wellbeing. You need the textbook, some info on quizzes may not be in lecture slides.

From day 1, she tells you "this is a tough course, but it's a 4000 level course so it should be" but hands-down one of the best I've taken in this program. Go to class because she helps and gives hints about quizzes, tests, and projects every lecture! There's 1 major project that does take a while, but it's very applicable in the real world.

Although the exams for this class were very hard, Professor Halfmann gave us options to increase our grades that many strict professors don't. She's a very nice lady and you can tell she wants her students to succeed. The only thing hard about this class is just the exams but other than that, the quizzes and assignments are really easy.
Needs another professor for this class, nothing on exams is in the study guide. Also, way too much information to even study. So hard to learn anything with not great explanations.

Professor Halfmann is a friendly and enthusiastic teacher. While she doesn't require attendance, I highly recommend it since most of her slide's info come from her lectures. Her tests can be a bit heavy but she goes through the entire study guide with her class the week before and gives you hints on what to really look for. Overall a great class.

Dr. Zuber is very knowledgeable about public health and as a professor, she's alright, but the grading is absolutely ridiculous. She hands out zeroes like it's nothing just for not numbering your submission. If you ever have her, make sure to check the instructions and your assignment twice before submitting!

Dr. Zuber may seem strict at first, but her goal is student success. During her lectures, all you do is just write down your answers to her fun questions for attendance. With no tests and only midterm and final group projects, clear assignment guidelines make earning full points (which is likely an A) very achievable. The class is her/TAs teaching.

The actual class had huge potential, but the professor just felt short. The assignment was easy, but at the beginning of the course they gave you this syllabus quiz, which I did and got 100%. Because I didn't screenshot it and turn it in again on Canvas, I got 0s on all 3 quizzes. I emailed the professor to get half credit, but she said no.

Dr. Z puts exactly what she expects in assignment instructions. Yes a zero may be harsh but everything she wants is right in front of you so just double check your work and you'll do fine. One of my fav professors.

I think Dr. Zuber is incredibly smart and loves what she does, but many of her students dread going to her class. She's very tough with grading and I took this class as an elective like many other people do and I felt that the grading was very harsh. A lot of the in-class work isn't helpful and we're given A LOT of homework.

DR. Z was extremely unfair when it came to grading. She would hand out zeros for simple human mistakes that most professors would just take off points for. Can't access the document zero, forgot to number your responses, zero. Two big group projects and three major tests; if you score low on any of them, it's impossible to recover your grade.

Takes forever to grade and answer emails. Sometimes she is funny and sometimes she just seems aggravated. There is a lot of mindless busy work and her grading is not always clear or overly complex when it does not need to be. She just makes things harder than they should be overall.

She is a tough grader, and takes a while to grade assignments which means you wont know if you need to withdrawal until it's too late. The group projects are demanding and are for the midterm and final. If your group members have work, or multiple classes, and it's hard to meet, you're going to struggle. There is no in class time to work on these.

she is an awesome person and kinda funny. not a great teacher. i will say, we just do group work every class based on what we had to READ outside of class and if your name isnt on the paper, zero for you! she waits until every end of the month to grade EVERYTHING FOR THE MONTH so you never know what to fix until its too late.

Dr. Z is one of the best professors I've had. She is extremely kind and understanding and genuinely wants to see her students succeed. The content itself of HAHS 1511 isn't difficult, but there is a lot of homework. You'll also be put into small groups taught by a TA who you'll work on group projects with. Make sure you participate and take notes!

The class was ok, just felt like was very time-consuming class. Easy material, but grades hard. She does tend to be a little rude. The first day of class, she said she wanted to be referred to as Dr.Zuber and not to be called Pilar because we are not her friends, which is like ??? It's just the way she says things that can be off-putting.

The class isn't bad at all; Dr. Zuber is a very kind and caring instructor, and not nearly as bad as some of these ratings suggest. She's understanding about late work if you explain your situation. Attendance matters, and she expects participation. Although for a one-credit class, it's more work than expected.

She most definitely is knowledgeable in her field, but she is not good as a professor. I was in an accident an hour before class, which led to me not being able to go to class, the next class meeting I went up to her and asked if I can come to office hours to do a debrief and she said to me, No I will post the slides on canvas review them.
Course is pretty easy but can get annoying because of how interactive we have to be.

Dr.Z is a great professor who is very knowledgeable in her field. Her lectures are very good but she assigns a lot of work, I had more work in her 3 credit hour class than I did in my 4 credit class. Her test are a bit challenging as they are based on application instead of memorization but an A in her class is still doable.

At first I was very iffy about taking her HLTH 2102 class due to the other ratings, I will say they did scare me but I still took my chances. Long story short, her class is amazing!!!! I absolutely loved and enjoyed it, she made my friend and I felt comfortable learning and applying the material to our coursework and tests. Please take her class :)

Really easy class but she wants it to seem difficult. She should be teaching elementary schoolers with the way the interacts with her students. Excessive instructions on everything that make things look overwhelming, but every assignment was very very easy. Also passive aggressive and will call you out if you're not paying attention during lecture.

I don't know why she has so many 1 stars and I am usually one to avoid one stars but I took her class and literally it is so simple. You'll have assignments maybe every two weeks and they're basic writing assignments with word counts and you have to use correct citation. If you follow the instructions literally you'll pass.

Honestly this teacher was so much better than expected, the set up of the class requires you to do very minimum homework and they're easy assignments with straightforward instructions. We broke into groups so we rarely seen her. when we did she was a good teacher, she's nice and funny. Attendance is mandatory so if you don't come you will fail

The class overall is ok, I had to take this class for credit, but honestly, the topics we talk about in class, I feel as though are common knowledge and probably do not need to be a class tbh. But prepare to be in group projects for half of the semester. A lot of papers. Easy to pass just do the assignments and theres no tests.

This class was frustrating. Constantly went off topic and made comments that felt unprofessional or unnecessary. When students asked questions or offered different perspectives, she shut them down. It created a space where many of us didn't feel comfortable speaking up. Unfortunate that this professor is required to work with.

major attitude, passive aggressive. my first MPH class and making me rethink charlotte.. she is supposed to be our support but it feels like a burden when you ask for help. i think she has too much on her plate and she takes it out on us, not cool. as far as assignments, i wouldnt know takes forever to grade!
Bias and passive aggressive. Take out her stress on students.
Takes too long to grade assignments!
Very late in assignment  feedback!

first MPH class has made me rethink this program. kind but can be passive-aggressive, bias and inconsistent. presents assignments as easy, but grading feels misleading. rubrics are unclear, and expects us to know her shifting expectations. quizzes don't align with lectures or readings. feedback is late. seems overworked, which affects her students.

HLTH 6200-Case Studies. Miss. Beete, while seemingly knowledgeable, is overworked making her grading process impossibly long. She assigned multiple projects/papers that were not graded and ended up giving the entire class an incomplete to compensate for her lack of time management. The class was chaotic at best, and a waste of time at worst.

Didn't learn much, just assigns busy work. Doesn't teach, will assign pdfs to read. Not even a Writing intensive class and expect to have a minimum of 2 essays, 5 quizzes, and discussion posts weekly. 
Have a final project AND a final test. 
Would recommend someone else.

Honestly, I am not someone who Rates professors, but I felt the need to express my experience in this class. I am an all-A student who turns in work ahead of time and is constantly studying, but professor Beetes assignments/quizzes don't match up to the materials provided in class, resulting in students not being prepared for upcoming assignments.
Prof. Beete is awesome! She has a great canvas layout and is great at responding to questions. She grades by the rubric and word count. Take her!

Terrible professor. She grades assignments at the last minute and expects you to just accept your grade the way it is. Grading is also very harsh and she takes major points off for the smallest things. Overall I would not recommend taking her class.

So much busy work that included articles, ted talks, videos, chapters, and research. But loved how organized the canvas page was, incredibly caring and thoughtful. Typical week had a discussion post (250 words), response (75), writing assignment (300 words), short MC quiz and matching (multiple attempts). Final is optional, final project was not.

There were weekly assignments that consisted of 2 quizzes-each 2 attempts, a discussion post, writing assignment. There were also critical thinking assignments which were papers. Midterm/Final but final was optional. There are extra credit opportunities as well as some of your lowest grades get dropped. Highly recommend her she will succeed you.

I loved Professor Beete for this course! Although this course was fully asynchronous, Professor Beete made the Canvas page very organized and was also super sweet. I would definitely take another one of her courses! The assignments are very easy and theres not many of them each week.

My previous rating has been deleted so it is clear that they are being deleted to maintain a relatively well rating overall. There is a lot of busy work, there is no account for what is useful and what is not. It will take up more time than any other class you have.

If you are an HSMT then I could understand how some of her assignments are applicable, however, most of the work is busy work. Like a minimum of 6 activities each week. Don't take this as an elective because it will waste most of your time.

I've had professor Beete in two other classes now and she's overall a pretty nice lady and her assignments are pretty straightforward. However, there's just so many assignments, especially discussion boards. I've gotten an A in each class of hers, but it always requires a lot of work. Not an easy A.

Overall an okay class. Professor Beete is a nice lady but theres too many assignments every week. This class will take up most of your time. Plus there are a couple projects, including a final voiceover presentation .

Shes one of the best professors Ive had. Shes super sweet. All of the assignments given have clear directions. She and the TAs are very responsive as well. She will take a little time to grade assignments, but shes definitely worth it.

She is a very good professor but she has her moments. She grades slowly and has times where her feedback is not clear. I learned a lot in her class but do not love to not know what is going on due to her not being clear on instruction.
vague instructions, no feedback, does not respond to any emails at all. do not take her.

She has her TA's do all the work. Grading and rubrics are loose and up for interpretation I guess. Pretty unresponsive, missed a meeting with me this semester and followed up the next day in a rude manner, lol. This class can be an easy A if you just do your work and carefully go over your assignments to ensure your grade isn't butchered.

This professor was not only hard to access but was passive aggressive in her responses. She did not give you time over breaks and would continue to assign work over holidays. Additionally she accused almost her entire class's worth of plagiarism and sent a threatening email when students tried to take action against it.

Dr. Piper-Smith is tough but very clear in the syllabus and instructions what she wants. Most people who have rated her low didn't follow her instructions. Can sometimes take a while with emails and is sometimes super quick. If you read the instructions and do the work it's not hard

Very difficult and condescending in emails. accused most of the class of plagiarism and then made us redo plagiarism checks to fix our grades. The syllabus was not helpful at all and had the final essay due at 8 am when all other assignments were due at 11:59 without any reminders or telling us beforehand the turn-in time changed.

She is extremely rude in her emails. She was reported several times to the HSMT director for her grading and behavior. 0/10 recommend. Had several issues with her during this semester about assignments. Worry about whether the class will be canceled. Yeah, she gonna cancel every chance she gets because she prioritizes her family over everything!

Overall class was mainly discussion posts were required you to write ten sentences and a citation and respond to a peer. There were three final papers/project. Her syllabus was very confusing and none of the papers had a rubric. Horrible at responding to emails too.Very condescending professor. Do not recommend.

Great professor, easy class. Midterm and final projects that you pick the topics of. I enjoyed this class a lot, I'm not sure why someone gave her such a bad review tbh.

15/10 
Literally one of the best professors I've ever had!

If you don't come to class you will be very behind. She really does care about the success of her student and wants to see them succeed. She reminds me of one of my favorite high school teachers. Overall pretty tough grader but gives good feedback.

While some students took advantage of her caring attitude and relaxed teaching style, she was a great teacher and I learned a lot. If you actually listen to her advice, you will grow as an artist, but she knows when not to push her students too hard to keep them from burning out.

Dr. Pizzato is one of my favorite professors I've had. He is considerate of absences, but he takes participation points, so I'd avoid missing many classes. In all classes I've taken with him I have received an A, and I learned a lot in his courses. Make sure to read the textbook before the lecture so you can participate. Extra credit opportunities!

Dr. Pizzato is pretty lecture heavy, and most days in my classes with him were just discussions, which can get a little boring. Overall, he is a nice guy and is extremely accessible outside of class. (Quick at responding to emails.) He does have a weird grading scale, but his class is not hard if you do the work. Attendance was required.

Genuinely one of the worst professors I have ever had. His lectures are endless and extremely boring, and the "group" assignments are absolutely ridiculous. He seems to always find a reason to take points off. Dr. Pizzato is clearly passionate about what he does, but just CANNOT teach it at all.
Good professor. Made a very boring class as interesting as he could, you can tell he genuinely cares what he is talking about. Make sure to show up to lectures, especially before tests.

One of the easiest classes I've taken so far. All we did was talk about shapes, colors, and lines and how they felt. He takes attendance with poll everywhere but doesn't notice when you are absent. He is a great professor and was super understanding with absences.

He is very nice with entertaining lectures. If you miss a class he makes it easy to catch up. He is always willing to talk and is a very laid back guy. his assignments do not ask much out of you, as long as you can show you tried. I would always look forward to his class because I would actually learn something interesting while also laughing.
The class itself was pretty easy but sometimes it was difficult to stay engaged unless the topic we were learning about was interesting. Textbooks were needed for quizzes every week

Overall, I think Professor Lathe was a great professor for LBST 1105. The only reason why I'm not giving him a 5/5 is that he's sometimes inconsistent when giving out assignments. For example, some of the quizzes require the lockdown browser while others don't. Other than that, I don't really have much to complain about him. I enjoyed the class.

Ashley Lathe is a great overall professor. He is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about the topic. The class is not too difficult with chapter quizzes and two exams, including the final, and there isn't a lot of homework. There are a couple assignments that are a little tedious but help prepare you for the final.

Lathe's a very genuine guy who clearly enjoys his career. The assignments he gives are easy and super fun. There are weekly quizzes on textbook material and not much homework. He does require you to attend a few out-of-class activities which is a little questionable. Other than that, he's a cool guy and genuinely cares about his students.

He is supposed to know that this class is just a general education class and it is supposed to be easy. Not everyone chooses to take the class. It is embarrassing when you are literally failing this class. I just want to get through this and never take it again.

Visual arts as a freshman, the class starts out very easy. Makes you do assignments that require watching 1:30+h videos and are extremely boring. Lectures and assignments are boring, expects you to have supplies such as paint/colored pencils unless you're good at photoshopping. He doesn't give feedback on essays. Gives bad grades w/o elaborating.

Lathe is a solid person and a great guy, I will say he does seem to lack teaching principles and isn't exactly a teacher as much as he is just a guy that loves art. His class was very easy, show up sit back and enjoy whatever he says, very few assignments and online quizzes are easy too. Tests are rough but it is what it is.

As a person professor Lathe is a great guy who tries to keep you engaged in the class but the lectures are very boring especially if you are not interested in Art. Online quizzes for each chapter are very easy and assignments outside of class are simple. Exams are difficult and he grades tough on essays.
My grades really dropped here in this class, It does not feel like actual art cause it is too stiff. I usually do art as a hobby because I like it.
Lathe is laid back and lecture based class. Minimal assignments and tests. Online quizzes every week, to review the upcoming topic.
Cool dude but difficult to get ahold of. The exams where the only hard part, only because you weren't sure what to study.

Prof. Lathe was a horrid professor. For such an easy class, he made it so difficult for no reason. All his exams have written portions which he grades but doesnt give feedback on. Towards the second half of the semester he went MIA. He barely responds to emails and he posts assignments the day before they're due. Avoid this professor if you can!

Be prepared to do actual art activities for this class. Had to go to art exhibits and attend artists' talks for a few assignments which is honestly too much for a gen ed class. Doesn't give feedback on exams. Doesn't answer his emails. He seems like a cool person tho just not a fan of his class.

Ash was a good professor for the Drawing course. He presented himself as very knowledgable as an artist and provided good constructive feedback on drawings in class. The class itself is tedious because it is basically just working on a single drawing for the whole 3 hours. Try to give it your all on every assignment but just make sure you improve.

This was one the of the worst and most unorganized class I have ever taken. He never updates canvas due dates until the day before, never responds to emails, and grades without giving feedback. I have no idea how anyone can give him a rating any higher than an OK. Definite do not recommend taking his class at all.

Dr. Domle is definitely a professor you'll want to continue with for French courses if you have the chance. I naturally pick up the language through her teaching, and the films she selects offer excellent and insightful depictions of French culture.

Dr. Domle is an incredible French professor who does an excellent job introducing students to French culture. I traveled to France over spring break this semester, and her course prepared me to navigate and appreciate the culture. This will help ensure your success, regardless of what your interest in French may be.

Dr. Domle created a comforting classroom environment that was judgment-free. She made us all understand that learning a new language is hard and it can be fun to laugh together. Her class is not very difficult; you get what you give. Show up, take notes, and ask questions, and you will be just fine.
Take her class she will make you better at French

This semester was a real eye-opener! Dr. D's class, held on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, was the perfect way to get through my days. She is thoughtful, encouraging and straightforward. I learned so much about academics and French in her class! I am so excited to tell you that I will definitely be taking the class again!

Mme Domle has been my favorite professor at UNCC! She's super fun and caring and wants the best for her students. She has a lot of interactive ways to practice what you learn in class like kahoots and blookets! She was a great professor and I would take her class again if I could!
Great knowledgeable Professor
Best Professor ever. Really knowledgeable. Would take any classes she teaches

She is the best professor I've ever had. She genuinely cares about each of her students and is very understanding when it comes to late work, missing assignments, and tests. Ask her for help with anything! I wish she taught more levels of French so I could take her again.

Loved this professor! One homework assignment per week, 4 exams, 3 quizzes, 1 oral exam, 1 final. Very easy assignments as long as you pay attention and learn. She will get to know you, push you and care for you.

There's lots of work, but for foreign languages you kind of need it. In terms of learning the language, she excels at explaining the same thing multiple ways to make sure you completely understand what's going on, and she'll take the time to go over anything as long as it takes until you are comfortable with the content and are ready to move on!

AMAZING! I took her for Elementary French 1&2. She was hilarious. Classes were easy, just keep up on VHL. She's amazing with feedback, and will let you redo assignments if you have a good reason you missed it, or if you did poorly. Often would let us use notes on tests/quizzes. If you have the opportunity, TAKE HER!
There was not enough time for the midterm. You have to go above and beyond on the discussion post. Too much for a LBST class.
Overall not a hard class, discussion posts every week, MAKE SURE YOU DO THEM THEY ARE YOUR ENTIRE GRADE. Bi-weekly quizzes, not too hard, just make sure you are ready to type long essays.

For a LBST this class was insane. Be prepared to write 100 words above the word requirement to get an A. The grading on the quizzes was also pretty random. I would compare results with peers who had the same answers as me, but our grades would be letters apart. The final and midterm had a lot of writing but not enough time to finish each adequately

Prof. Domle is overall not bad, she's very good at clearing up any confusion you have. Her grading is extremely hard though, especially for an LBST. I think her grading criteria is not fair based on what she is asking you to do.

Before going into this class I never thought I would enjoy learning a language, but Dr. Gomoluch made it genuinely fun. As long as you make a decent effort to participate in her lectures, you will get an A.
Amazing professor who encourages her students to speak German. Highly recommend and would definitely take another course with her

As long as you are coming to class and participating, you cannot fail this class. Dr Gomoluch creates a great environment for learning a language in class. Lectures are quite casual and students are encouraged to be social.

I love this professor. Probably the best class I have taken at UNCC. Make sure you come to class and participate. Otherwise, you will not learn anything. She makes you feel extremely safe and comfortable trying to speak the language. She can be pretty funny at times and always does her best to explain things to you in a way that makes sense.

Strict, but fair. Homework is sparse in her class, usually only one assignment each week, so there's virtually no excuse for falling behind. Lectures are fun, she brings a good energy to class and makes sure that everyone is given a chance to participate. Planning on taking her class next semester.
Prof. Gomoluch was a great professor. She is clear with class expectations and it's really hard to fail this class.

This is the professor to take a foreign language with!

She encourages her students to speak German, but won't hold it against you as long as you make an honest effort to try and speak the language. 

Vocab quizzes last 10 minutes, always at the start of the class period, be sure to study. 

Can leave as soon as you are done with chapter tests.

If you get a chance to take Ms. Gomoluch, for sure do!! I took her global connections online class and she was amazing. Left great feedback and cared about her students. 5 assignments a week and 1 final project. As long as you do the work thoroughly, you will get the credit.
Professor Gomoluch is truly so sweet. You can tell she cares about her students, and leaves comments on a lot of things you submit. She is the best, take her!
Literally love Frau Gomoluch. Super sweet but knows how to keep her class under control. Easily a very respectable woman who clearly cares about her student's success.

Best professor I've ever had. She was understanding and caring along with funny. She has a strong passion for teaching and would encourage you to ask questions. Class was easy as long as you did the work.

Professor Gomoluch has been an amazing professor, always ready to answer questions and help you if you need. She often talks in German during her lectures so you need to be paying attention, but if you are having difficulties understanding especially in the first intro class, she will still help you understand.

Professor Gomoluch is one of the most genuine, kind, and understanding professors I've ever had. She is extremely gracious with slow learners, and it's clear that she is passionate about her job. She wants her students to be the best that they can be in German and will do whatever she can to get them there.

Professor Gomoluch is the best teacher I have ever had. She truly knows how to teach her students in a way that is fun and interactive. She wants you to be able to speak the language, not just read it, so she will regularly ask questions directly to students. Truly incredible at what she does and I am excited to take her again.

Professor Gomoluch felt like more of a mentor than a professor. She is super approachable, yet can be serious when necessary. She gets to know her student's names and interests, and is generally very enthusiastic. She is open to questions and makes sure to integrate culture into lessons to support linguistic understanding.

I had Professor Gomoluch for the online version of Global Connections and it is so far the best class I've taken. She responds to emails quickly and gives great feedback. You can definitely tell that she has a passion for teaching. There isn't a huge amount of weekly work. I would highly recommend taking her!!

They really brought this class to life. You can tell they are passionate about what they teach, which makes a big difference. They give a lot of feedback and add comments to your papers to provide more information. I thoroughly enjoyed this class and would definitely recommend this professor!

Attendance accounts for a decent sized portion of your grade, if you tend to miss classes here and there, this is not your professor. Bad at responding to emails, although sometimes will. Can be overly stern in grading policies.
She is literally the best professor ever! She is so nice and makes class very fun. I would definitely recommend having her as your german professor! I had her for both elementary german 1 and 2
Virtually impossible to contact outside of class. Does not bend any sort of rules for anybody, I would say she is very strict. Picks favorites. Attendance policy is strict.

I had professor Werbeck for GERM 1502 he is really nice, he's very easy going and is okay if you turn something in a day late. He's very funny in class and overall a good professor. I would 100% take his class again. He's also really good at responding to emails.
EASIEST CLASS ever. Literally all you do is watch movies, and then fill out a 3 questions worksheet about the movie. There is a final paper, but you can choose any German movie you want to.

He responds quickly to emails and makes class interesting. The structure is really conducive to people who like repetitive structure. If you really hate writing though, I wouldn't take this class. All of the assignments are papers pretty much. But they're all short other than the final. It's an easy A.

Dr. Werbeck is a very good professor. I find his lectures to be very engaging and I find myself listening to every lecture attentively. We watch about 10 movies, you have to fill out a worksheet after but as long as you pay attention you will get an A. You have to participate in class discussions to get points. There is one final essay at the end
You HAVE to pay attention to the movies he shows in class or else you will fail the exam

You literally watch movies and discuss about them in class! There's a worksheet to do after every movie (about 8), but as long as you fill them out he will give you full credit. One midterm and final, both simple as long as you pay attention in class. You also work on an 8 page paper that's due at the end of the semester. An easy A! TAKE HIM!!

Dr. Du is incredibly knowledgeable. Her classes were not just lectures (though they did include lectures), but also involved group work, discussions, and analyses, which made learning the course content easier, more fun, and more interactive. She assigns a lot of reading, but it's always interesting (and sometimes surprising). Highly recommend!

Dr. Du will push you to be a better student. She is a super kind and caring professor but she is also no nonsense. If you come to class on time, pay attention, and do the assignments on time you should have no issues with her. She gives a lot of homework but also provides excellent feedback. She really helped me learn and I would take her again.
Do not become complacent in this class, grades one day are 15 points higher or lower than the next with minimal explanation

Dr. Du is highly unforgiving and unfair. 90% of the assignments are group related, but she grades you individually. She docks full credit if you are missing one part of a citation, such as a specific page number. I absolutely do NOT recommend taking any of her classes. There are also participation quizzes based on readings and they are very long.

Despite a syllabus note requiring students to show up at least 10 minutes early he is never even on time. Does not respect your time holds you after class ends and keeps talking nonstop. will start a new ppt if there's even four minutes left of lecture.

He is the sweetest professor ever. The lectures are a little boring at times, but he wants you to do well in the class. He accepts late work, most assignments are completion grade, and gives back points on tests if most people got a question wrong. He really cares about his students and wants them to be interested in the class.

Super easy going, took him for anthropology and everything was pretty clear he didn't care to much about late assignments and still gave credit. Very easy going and a wonderful professor who seems to care. His lecture are a little boring and he is not to interesting to listen to but beyond that pretty good

Prof. Lai is a very kind, good person. He really does care about his students. But... his lectures are long, generally nonsensical, and his quizzes are oddly worded. I had a very hard time understanding the material in this class. The way he lectures is almost at a graduate level. He does not do a good job of explaining, and that makes class boring

Expect "Mini-Research Project" to be the reverse of "mini."  Expect to read dense portions of the text book a long with multiple articles and book scans before every class.  The final research project is way too much to ask for and you basically have to bs your way through it.  His lectures are also extremely boring, and hard to understand.

Dr. Lai is a really caring professor, it is obvious he cares a lot about his work and his students both. While he can be a bit hard to understand and, at times, quite difficult, the content he teaches is really interesting. Make sure to reach out to him outside of class, he is extremely helpful.
Incredible professor that wants her students to succeed. Organized course with clear expectations. Study guides provided for exams.

Ms. Wyble is a very nice teacher she is very knowledgeable, helpful, and does an amazing job helping her students learn and understand the course. The assignments are very easy in regards to how amazing she is able to prepare us in the sparing two classes we have throughout the week. I strive to be as great of a teacher as her. 11/10.
great professor, easy to understand and kind. explains material very well

Very helpful to all her students and accommodating to everyone's different levels of Spanish knowledge. There's quite a bit of homework, but it's a 4 credit hour class so it makes sense. The homework assignments on Connect are very helpful for the quizzes and exams.

Had her for SPAN1201 as well, and it's pretty much set up the exact way. Attending class is important, especially if it's once a week. Don't be afraid to ask questions, she will definitely help you. Lots of homework but nothing too difficult. Very good professor.

She is a very nice professor. Attendance is mandatory or you'll get points taken off. The class is really easy; the exams are easy and connect is really annoying but it's easy enough. She helps if you need help just make sure you ask for it. Very understanding professor!

Attendance is mandatory, points docked for missing class. Half of grade is online connect assignments which are helpful for learning, only good part about class. Other half is 3 exams and oral exam. Exam is relatively easy if connect assignments are done. Unless you have prior spanish knowledge, should probably attend class.

Amazing professor for a beginner Spanish class! She is always making jokes and makes you feel very comfortable even when making mistakes. Aside from attendance, homework is due every Monday and Wednesday which is very easy to complete all in one day.

I honestly enjoyed taking her class and attending her class. I have a background in Spanish and I feel like I have learned a lot more in her class. She was very clear on what the test would look like and for our final exam as well. She was very strict on attendance but was very considerate if you had to miss a class. 10/10 would take it again.

Mrs. Wong's class was one of the easiest I took this semester. There are assignments due every day before your class, a couple of quizzes, and three total exams. Most questions on quizzes and exams are multiple-choice, with a few writing portions toward the end of the semester. As long as you do the VHL assignments and show up, you should get an A

Professor Wong is very nice and funny, so I really did like her class. Sometimes she can come off as upset/intimidating, but I don't think she means to. If you have a problem with some of your grades or homework, if you bring it to her; she'll most likely help you. She just wants to see her students succeed. Overall, I would recommend her!

Profe Wong was great. If you show you are dedicated she will help you out. Studying is a major part but even if you don't do well on the test but partipate, do your homework, and make good grades on it you will be fine. You will pass with a C or better even if you do terrible on the tests. Had her for span 2202.

Profesora Wong came off as a little bit intimidating when I first met her but that changed quickly! She is overall helpful and very sweet. You just have to do the work on Connect. She doesn't give extra credit. Also, she has a thick accent just in case that's a factor that might turn you away but I promise she speaks legible enough to understand.

She's sweet but so difficult. Had two deaths in my family and she tanked my participation grade and I worked for two months to bring it back up. Hard to communicate with and be prepared to feel stupid when you don't know the answer and you're called on. Sprung a 5 min all in Spanish presentation on us with no rubric. I dreaded this class everyday.

Professor Wong really cared about her students understanding the material. The textbook and homework site is very confusing and does a horrible job of explaining things. Class time was used to work on pronunciation/ go over some of the harder topics. She was good but the class set up was not ideal, but that was due to the department not her.
She was an okay professor. You mainly just learn from the homework, you don't really learn anything from class. but it's pretty easy to earn an A as long as you do your homework on time.

She is a nice teacher, but didn't feel as though I was learning anything in class. I had a little bit of knowledge on the language which helped me get through but can't see this being a good option for folks new to the language completely.

Attendance was mandatory I missed a couple of classes and it did not affect my grade. A moderate amount of homework but that was all assigned through the McGraw Hill homework and wasn't that difficult. The test was not that hard. I enjoyed this professor she was super nice and funny. Answer questions in class. Recommend taking this class

This class is heavily based on teaching yourself from the textbook since it's hybrid. The day in class is spent going over how to pronounce things not really explaining concepts. The tests are hard and you really have to know what you're doing in order to pass them.

Ms Wong is very nice, but I would not take her class again. Attendance is mandatory and a grade, and she only really practices Spanish with us and doesn't really teach. The whole class is just her calling on people to answer. The online assignments is what teaches us, so its nearly impossible to learn a language that way.

Attendance is taken everyday. I highly encourage going to class. Professor Wong is very nice and tries to make every comfortable speaking Spanish and not be afraid to be wrong. The assignments are easy, there are no projects or papers. There is an oral exam, but it is just you recording yourself completely speaking in Spanish for 5 minutes.

Almost the entirety of this class was taught by a preset module course. As in, there were no meetings with the teacher and the only communication made was through our rare interactions. This course teaches itself: online, there is almost no need for a teacher to fill this position. I'm sure this is better in person, but this teacher taught nothing.

Okada is an excellent professor, and she is hilarious. Easily one of the most engaging and enjoyable classes I have taken in college. She can be a tough grader for certain things, but if you a mild amount of effort and get your work done, this class should be an easy A.
I took Okada-sensei for my JAPN 1201 lab, and she was a fantastic professor. She is always so positive and makes the Zoom courses fun, and is always willing to answer questions and help you out.

I had Okada-sensei for both 1201 and 1202 and loved her. Although the class was fast-paced and we sometimes ran out of time for the lesson, as long as you kept up with the textbook work and show up to class you could easily get an A. She is very helpful with any questions or struggles you may have.

Awesome professor! She was very excited to teach us and obviously put a lot of care into her lectures. She challenged me a lot but in a good way, and you will be called on! She is very lively and expressive so it is really hard to fall asleep in her class. Just study hiragana and katakana before taking the class and you should be able to get a b!

Professor Okada is funny and she does try to make class fun. Although my class was only 55 minutes, I wish we had a little more time in class. She is a little bit of a strict grader only because she has to follow the guidelines of the department. Although the work was not hard. Just make sure you ask questions and study and you should be good.

This was Professor Okada's first semester, so I do give her the benefit of the doubt. Nonetheless, she had trouble balancing students and tended to gravitate towards the less introverted students as limited time in class didn't allow her time to touch on everyone. She is hilarious to be around though. You will get called on.

professor okada shows clear bias toward certain students and could not care less about others. not particularly helpful with feedback but likes to grade very strictly, and not very understanding toward students. probably one of the worst professors that i have ever had.

She is one of the best professors I have had at my time at UNC Charlotte, she is a very caring professor and actually cares about her students.  The material is somewhat difficult but if you watch the videos she gives you and show up to the class, a B is easily attainable.

While there is definitely a work load, you also have to remember you're learning a new language, so it's not going to be easy. She did the best she could and I truly had an enjoyable time in her class. She's always willing to help and isn't too strict or controlling. She lets you have fun and play games and I really can't complain. Would recommend.

It's so terrible I want to give you 0 but that's not possible, so I will give you a 1. She was very bad and did not improve from the last time I had to take her. Only passed because of my previous knowledge of taking her class.

This was only her 2nd semester teaching and I felt like she did better than professors that have been teaching for years. She gives ample extra credit, is a fair grader and tries her best to help us grasp the material. If you do not show up or do not engage in class, you will not succeed. Sounds like previous reviews are influenced by bad grades.

Ms. Poore was honestly a rollercoaster ride for me. I will admit, I absolutely hated her at the beginning of the semester. But then as the semester went on, I began to get over my hatred as she began to come out of her shell. Her grading can be confusing, but we do communicate differently. She may not be the best, but she's really not that bad.

She is a good professor. She gives good extra credit opportunities and is super nice. I do think she could do better teaching. But overall she doesn't push you to participate or to do your work. But she does want you to try.

It's sad to see so many bad reviews of professor Poore because I really enjoyed her as a professor.  She is NOT an easy A professor but I value that. The tests are tough as everyone said but not unmanageable. Just do extra activities in the textbook and send her them. I found quite a few activities in the textbook were actually on the test.

I really enjoyed professor Poore. I think what people struggle with is that she drills grammar hard. Whereas some teachers just appreciate you trying, she wants to make sure you really understand the rules. I think a lot of people wrote negative reviews because they wanted an easy A. If you truly want to learn French I recommend taking her classes.

Please take another professor if you have the chance. She is the worst professor I've had in my 4 years at UNCC, condescending, ill-mannered, and not appreciating REAL effort. I tried multiple times to ask questions/seek her help but she always told me this was something I should already know, even though we didn't spend enough time going over it
I had Ms. Poore this semester and I learned a lot but the tests were difficult. I tried hard but I should've asked more questions

Hardest professor I have ever had. I had to WORK for a B in what is supposed to be an Elementary level class. Rachel is rude and does not care if you pass or fail, only there to give you a meaningless lecture for 50mins. Don't take this professor if you have the opportunity to, trust me you'll regret it. Had half my class drop after the first exam

If you're able to get any other professor, do so, She's condescending and her quizzes/tests are absolutely ridiculous for a 1202 course. On the first quiz, she had us write 3 paragraphs along with having to make up about 5 sentences for each page. She is reluctant to offering extra credit. She teaches in French using vocab you wont understand.

This is her first year of teaching so I'll give her the befit of the doubt, but, her class is hard. She talks in french most of the time and will look at you like you're insane if you don't understand her. She's nice and funny, but homework is heavy and long and tests make or break your grade. She offers NO extra credit so beware of that.

Wouldn't recommend. She is very quiz and test heavy with very little elaboration on material assessed in examinations. Very condescending. Doesn't provide classes with a clear avenue for practicing the language and only bases her course around grammar with no vocal practice or retention which is the most important part of learning a language.

Terrible TERRIBLE professor, quite possibly the worst professor I've ever had here. She is extremely condescending toward her students and is very rude when you don't know how to answer her question. The tests are extremely difficult and you are expected to write pages of fluent sentences, which is a lot for someone whose only in French 2.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She does not teach well at all and is extremely condescending if you do not know the answer. It’s ELEMENTARY French and she teaches entirely in French. There are so many exams and they are all extremely difficult.

This professor is very kind, but she does not understand that learning a language takes time. The tests and quizzes are all three pages long front to back and you only have fifty minutes to complete it. On the first quiz, you are expected to know how to write a paragraph. I attended tutoring since the beginning of the semester. I am still failing.

Quite possibly the worst professor on the entire campus. Even if you go to every class, and study for hours for the exams, I bet you won't get an A on exams. Exams are sentences and paragraphs. She is EXTREMELY condescending to students, and if you don't know the answer she will not help you at all. if you have a will to live, don't take her class

WORST PROFESSOR AT UNCC. As a senior taking her course, I have never had trouble with other professors, but I absolutely can not stand her. She's frankly a jerk and treats her students like we are dumba***es. SHE SHOULD BE FIRED OR AT LEAST LEARN HOW TO TEACH SOMETIME.

It was so bad I wanna give you a zero but thats not possible so I give you a 1!! Dont take her unless youre literally fluent in French. The quizzes are 6 pages long and for every answer you are expected to either write a sentence or a paragraph. This seems pretty advanced for elementary level French. She offers no extra credit, I barely passed.
Shes a very nice person, but the class is extremely hard to follow. The class is taught entirely French which may be difficult for some people to follow. Youre pretty much on your own in this course.

She was an amazing professor. This course was fully online and her assignments were super easy. As long as you read an watched her resources provided (which weren't boring or long) you would get an easy 100 on the assignments. It's literally all busy work.

**Review for LBST 2101 Course**

The class was really good for being an online class. The content was interesting. The professor's grading is fair. Not hard at all, just go through what is posted and you should be fine with the assignments! Final exam was a 2 question paper (not hard at all).

Took GERM3201 with her. She's been one of my favorite professors at UNCC, if not my favorite. She's very understanding and will help you out if you just communicate with her. She's very supportive and makes presentations auf Deutsch way more comfortable. She's not a tough grader and wants to see you put effort into the class if anything.

She is so sweet and very caring about her students. Class is chill and engaging with many group activities. Weekly online homework takes ~ 30 min and an oral exam at the end of the semester.
