I took this course Summer 2022. And it was pretty easy! Dr. Lapietra was straightforward with assignments and reading. There was a quiz and a writing assignment every week. With the topics that were at hand, Dr. Lapietra handled lectures wonderfully. It was a nice summer class, and I think I learned a lot.
As a summer course, this professor made it extremely straightforward and was very respectable!

This class has been my ultimate favorite. Professor Agah is also a student so she understands perfectly. Her grading scale is amazing. Only one assignment due every week or so but its an assignment that youll enjoy doing while watching cool films and researching cool media topics. Stress Free Class. Easy A as long as you do the work.

She is genuinely the most grounded and understanding professor I've ever had. She's personable, very, VERY accepting of late work as long as you bother to participate every once in a while, and she could not be clearer on what is going on a quiz/test. No pop quizzes, no last-minute assignments.  Literally all you have to do is do all the hw.

She's overall a good professor but there is a good amount of work. You'll get assigned 3-5 assignments biweekly and there is a lot of reading you need to do for the class. She responds well to emails but I wouldn't take her class again.

Took her for SPAN 1512. It feels like busy work but it was an interesting course. Mostly discussion posts, quizzes and tests. Class feels kind of disorganized, she took till the end of the semester to grade every single assignment.

I felt like the pace was too fast for a beginner's language course. I also felt like the instructor was kind of unprofessional at times and was too focused on being "buddies" with the students. I understand wanting to connect with your students, but it gets to a certain point, especially when some people just want to learn.

She is really nice and understanding with late work, however, she is also very disorganized. Lectures didn't seem to have any structure to them and I don't feel like I learned anything from her class.
She was amazing! I took her for SPAN 2202, not 1102, online over the summer. She is so down to earth and understanding, and explains topics in a very accessible way. Take her if you can!

(Took POLS 3169) The lecture slides were extremely unorganized and weren't coordinated with the weekly memo rubric. He also isn't truthful because the rubric says we have two week but we actually only have one. He was quite unhelpful and didn't respond after I asked for support and asked to meet with him during the meeting times HE offered.

I joined this class on the last day of add/drop because I needed one more elective. I missed the first week, emailed the professor to reopen the assignment, and he refused. Now we have to read 88 pages and film 10-minute videos every two weeks to prove we understand the content we read. For an elective, the workload is ridiculous. DO NOT TAKE!!

Took African International Relations (3169). The professor is extreamly disorganized and the layout of the canvas page makes no sense. When I asked a question about why there were no instructions or distriptions under the assignments he was unhelpful and rude. He might be better in person, but this online class is a disaster.

Hands down one of the most caring professor that I've had. Weekly memos, 500 word minimum, and he writes 2-4 pages worth of feedback on them. He grades harsh but provides great feedback for you to improve. It's an essay heavy course so be ready to write. If you read the readings, comprehend it, and can write about it, you will pass. Great professor

I had him for African Politics. While you will learn a lot in this course, it's easy to be overwhelmed because he assigns a 500-word minimum memo, which usually ends up being 800+ words, and a discussion post. Overall, he is a harsh grader but will provide plenty of detailed feedback (sometimes condescending) so take only if you like writing.

Professor Yao-Kuoame is an amazing professor. I'm surprised to see how low of a rating he has. He is a professor that you want—very caring and engaged in your work. He grades harshly because he wants you to improve on every assignment. Every essay he provides detailed feedback about what you did well on, and how you can improve. Easy to reach too!
He is incredibly condescending and whenever you ask for help he's rude about it.

No exams, the papers you write are your midterm and final. Weekly memos have a ~500 word minimum along with discussion boards. There are at least three papers: a 2000 minimum word midterm paper, 5 page paper on the novel paper SINGLE-SPACED, and the group project paper. His grading is erratic. Would not recommend.

He's a harshly grading professor who assigns 50-100 pages of reading per week and 500 word (ideally 800+ if you want a decent grade) memos every week along with a long paper on a novel and a 25 minute group presentation. It's hard, and it sucks, but you will learn the material, and he does give good, thorough feedback. Take at your own risk.

Grading made no sense and the memos are a ridiculous amount for reading to build up to a project at the end, but nothing made sense. He gives feedback on your opinions and is not available to meet other than a couple of times. do not take it unless you want to be stressed over an elective.. smh.

He wasnt the worst professor out there. I got a better grade in this class than African politics. Theres a 500 word memo due every week, which you can get 100s on as long as you connect the readings with one other. In the middle of the semester - be ready to cram. There are 2 ten page essays due around the same time, on top of the memos.

Worst professor I have ever had, and I have only had him for about 3 weeks. Super disrespectful, degrading, and confusing. No rubric, instructions, or information given on most assignments. Gives the WORST feedback in video format so you can watch in real time as he puts your work down and vaguely talks about assignment expectations. DO NOT TAKE!
He's an incredibly unreasonable grader and gives almost no effort into his class.  Everything was on quizlet and you practically have to teach yourself.

The worst class I've taken ever. Essays with little time to prepare. Terrible feedback. Takes points off for disagreeing with him. He takes forever to grade assignments with little feedback. He doesn't want students to be lazy, but he's often lazy with his own grading (the only job he does because he doesn't do anything else).

Koffi is one of the worst teachers I have ever seen. His attitude toward his students is condescending and his grading system is baffling. His communication outside of class is nonexistent, his grading policies are inconsistent, and his expectations on individual assignments are a mystery to his students and sometimes even to himself. DO NOT TAKE.

Very glad I dropped out. I don't even care that I have to make up the class, but avoid the stress and anxiety and DO NOT take this course. No good feedback and the expectations for the essays are ridiculous. Doesn't provide clear instructions, so I had to email him several times for him to explain them well.

Wow....I'm a senior taking this class in the summer to student teach in the fall of '22. Easily the worse professor ever. No rubric, no guidelines, unclear expectations. I'll have to acquire a waiver and take a this course AGAIN while I student teach. 

DO NOT TAKE even if it puts you back a semester.

Professor Koffi is quite honestly the absolute worst professor Ive ever had. His grading criteria has no rubric and if he wants to give you a 5 on an assignment, he will do so just because and then give you 0 feedback in the process. Takes forever to grade assignments for personal reasons but has no regard if anything comes up for a student.

There's an absurd amount of writing in this class. I got an A because I just have a knack for making critical thinking concepts into well written paragraphs. Many people don't have that skill. The homework questions are released 24 hours before they are due (which is insane) and it took a full MONTH to receive grades/feedback sometimes. Not a fan.

This is by far, the most ridiculous professor that I have had. He is tough on grading and the annotations he provides to the papers are usually just "???". He grades based on personal opinion even if you make a good take on a question. He takes a couple months to grade the essay questions. Goodluck getting an email back on time. Easy weekly quizzes

Daniel Cozart is a phenomenal professor that opened up my worldview significantly. Some other reviews have said his lectures are boring but I strongly disagree. The subject matter was not something I would normally have been interested in, but Cozart's strong understanding of the material and respectable approach made it one of my favorite classes.

Took him last spring (2022), I loved his lectures! Took both a hist. + film class, both had lots of essays. He gives good feedback, even though he grades hard. He showed good, interesting films and his lectures were great too. He mentioned leaving UNCC last semester tho.

Dr Cozart has a heart for Latin America and it showed. The class was not too difficult, but I definitely learned a lot. Although Dr C leaned toward the progressive side of the political spectrum, he worked to remain neutral and just present the evidence. I would take him again.

Dr. Cozart was a great professor: Very knowledgeable about Latin American History, small group assignments were easy 10 pt grades. Cons: Dr. Cozart graded too meticulously on essays & PowerPoints didn't follow his guide, making it hard to take accurate notes. With that being said, I'm glad I took this class because this was his last semester here.

Great guy, and seems to enjoy the subject, but his lectures are just BORING. He seems to know his stuff, but he just reads off of a script for some reason and it is awful. Having said that, not too harsh of a grader.

This class was a worthwhile one due to the material, but it is hard to say I remember much about it otherwise. The overall grade is focused upon a few key assignments: if you are not keen on your ability to handle this pressure, prefer to take classes with more busywork, and the material does not interest you, this may not be your class.

Dr. Cozart is passionate and knowledgeable about Latin American studies so it's easy to be engaged. The quizzes and papers aren't difficult if you at least skim the readings and pay attention in class. Dr. Cozart is kind and fair. He isn't super tech savvy but is open to receiving feedback and tips from students, so it works out.
Just never take her class! Very tough grader.....
Acts like her class matters. A LOT of points off for small errors. So much work for what should be some gen ed.

would not recommend it. Makes the work harder than what it has to be. lots of reading and grades tough. all you do is read and do an assignment (there are not examples provided with the assignments). this class was way too stressful and took up so much time.

Honestly her class isn't hard at all just have to put in the minimum effort and you can pass her class. She doesn't give out a lot of assignment it's 1 per week, a discussion or 2 page essay, not difficult. However, because of this her assignment tends to be worth 20 to 40 points so you can definitely fail if you miss more than 1 assignment.

Professor Valvo is a really tough grader and her assignments are tedious. She takes points off for the smallest things and takes a significant amount of credit for these small mistakes. Assigns things and doesn't put them on the calendar. Would not recommend her. Not willing to work with you.
A lot of APA format papers and five textbooks are required for readings. Also, get ready to do film and literature reviews that are 4-5 pages long too

Every week is either a discussion board or two page paper. Textbooks are easy to skim and the papers aren't difficult if you dedicate time to them. She responds to emails quickly and gives specific feedback.

Professor Valvo is amazing!! Her weekly assignments are the same every week: open Monday and close on Sunday. There's usually a short reading and a written response to go along with it. I think she is a great grader and provides feedback. There was not a single exam, and were given our expectations each week very formatted. I LOVED THIS PROFESSOR

He is an amazing professor, the class is super easy, and you get out early every day. No tests, course load is one 30-minute presentation with a partner, where the presentation can consist of videos for most of the time allotted. The only homework is a mini-essay for each presentation, which is only half a page each. 10/10

By far one of the easiest classes I've ever took. Professor is chill and understanding. All you have to do is mini-papers on each issue, which doesn't have to be super long. You present once with a partner or solo, and as long as you cover all the criteria an A is almost guaranteed.

One of the best/easiest professors at this University. Class consists of multiple mini-papers (2 pages) where you just summarize two different sides of an argument and then give your own opinion. No final or midterm. There is one presentation, either solo or w a partner, but even if you read off slides, you get an A. Easy class, great professor.

Really easy class, just lots of one page mini-papers to write which all follow the same structure. Two papers and a discussion post due weekly. No exams or final. Just one project you work on with a partner and present. Even if you stutter and read off the slides, you'll still get an A on the project. Professor is very lenient and understanding.

LBST-2301 is so easy. 17 mini papers throughout and one presentation which you do with a partner. You can take notes on the presentations in class and write the papers from those. Very easy grader. Everyonegot a 100 on their presentations based on what I saw. The Online textbook sucks, and the actual useful info is in the physical textbook.

(Fall 2023 semester) This professor is so nice and would talk to his students about personal life and offer leniency. Assignments included creating a 30-minute presentation that we could work on with a partner, two three-paragraph papers per week, and one or two discussion posts per week. Discussing controversial topics in class was optional.

Best professor and the best section for LBST 2301. You just read a couple of articles from the textbook and write up a summary about them. One presentation project that is not hard at all. Easy class, great professor. Refusing to take him would probably be the dumbest decision you've ever made.

Lets out class 45 minutes early every day. Two essays a week but they're covered in class so you can take notes and write them off that instead of textbook. One partner project that's not very hard. He's very nice and easy grader. Attendance mandatory.
Take this professor by any means. Very easy and you will have an easy A. There is homework but it's easy. No test at all. Do all homework and project online.
She's so fun and super nice! She cares so much about her students. Little to no homework and tests. 100% recommend for everyone!
Super easy. Take her!! No tests.

Dr. Harden likes to have people interact with her for the whole class. She likes for people to have conversations with each other during class. She gives out weekly quizzes that she made up on her own, so you actually have to read the book, but it is interesting. She talks about current things that are going on, which I really liked.

Class is extremely easy. I think she has good intentions, but lets her bias get in the way while she is teaching. Makes her political views very clear which was just kind of uncomfortable how open she was talking about it. Wasn't really appropriate. Not the best teacher when it comes to actually teaching and lecturing. "Who wants to say something?"

Professor Harden is caring for all of her students. Lectures are about real things happening today and it's always an open discussion which is cool. You have a chapter book that your quizzes are in and the answers are in the book but you have to read. Sometimes attendance didn't work and if you're marked absent, just let her know and she fixes it.

Dr. Harden cares for all her students and tries to present resources in the education field. Her lectures are a little boring and seem pointless sometimes, but she grades easy and will give u a extension if you ask for one.

As a person, Dr. Harden is very kind and caring. As a professor, she is not ideal. She doesn't put due dates on anything but then gets mad at people for not having assignments turned in when she wants them to be...make it make sense. Her co-teacher is also unhelpful, and the actual class periods feel mostly pointless.

dr. harden is the sweetest ever! she cares a lot about us and made sure we were doing well in all of our classes. she always checks on us and wanted us to be friends with each other, which i respect. she cheers you on and motivates you to do well, even if you're changing majors or going through a lot during the semester.

The class is fun and easy and Dr. Harden does a great job of making sure everyone feels welcome and loved. Her projects and assignments may seem tedious or silly but they help you learn the fundamentals of teachings. I would take her again in a heartbeat!

Don't get me wrong, she is great, just some of the assignments we were given didn't feel very effective. I feel like we spent more time in the class trying to be friends with everyone then actually learning. Unfortunately I don't feel like I have taken away much from this class. It is however an easy A.

I loved Dr. Harden. She actually cares about her students. The assignments were all pretty easy and she always offers to help with them if needed. She checks in on everyone a lot. She's easy going and you can tell she is passionate about what she does! A lot of the assignments due dates were often flexible. She's all about her students succeeding!

She is so sweet. She takes time to make sure you're doing well and that you get any help on the assignments you need. The assignments are really simple and we have good class discussions, even if they sometimes feel long or unnecessary. Due dates are not fixed and she will often extend deadlines so everyone can finish.
Not a good lecturer
Not a good professor and worst at responding to emails. Do not take her! Dr. Brown is often late to class

Dr. Brown is a very engaging professor but her lectures won't help you be successful. You WILL NOT pass the class without the textbook. The test questions are often direct quotes from one obscure sentence in one paragraph of one chapter. Passing is based on memorizing every sentence from the textbook chapters instead of understanding the concepts.

worst professor ive had for undergrad. she talks way too much about her personal life. attendance is mandatory, but you dont learn anything by going, and all the assignments can be done from home. ive spoken to several other students who all agree that we have learned nothing this entire semester. if you have to take ctcm, avoid her.
Do not take this professor if you want to get an A. This professor rarely knew what were on her own exams and often made rude comments to students.

Attendance is mandatory and she doesn't budge...ever. Her lectures are very important as most of the information you need to know comes from what she talks about. She assigns a lot of reading and depending on the class, very quiz heavy and they're weighted pretty unfairly.

She makes offensive comments. She is very passive aggressive and rude to students when she is in the wrong. She doesn't know how to use/navigate canvas and blames the student when an assignment is posted incorrectly. One time a quiz was posted with the wrong amount of time and her response was she didn't want to "deal with it".

Interesting class but she's a tough grader, great personality and engages students but I found her passive aggressive at times. Also, multiple instances where she has had to apologize for unprofessionalism and WILL embarrass you in front of the class. Material is do-able but expect 0s and to do her work in other lectures with the crazy due dates.

Took GRNT 4366 for my major, bc I had to. She forgot that Gerontology is offered as a major, as a Gerontology professor how do you forget...? Class is not for shy ppl as you will have to give a presentation. Her reasons for presentations is because it's so she knows where we are... very dumb reason. I will never take her again if it's possible.

By far the worst professor I have ever taken so far in my undergrad. She didn't care about the students. The final paper was just some bs. She said that you have to earn your A but she makes the class so difficult for no reason. It is titled communications and yet she never communicated on what she wanted!!!!

Took LBST2301. Don't be fooled by Dr. Browns personality. She is a very harsh grader and can be passive aggressive. Most of the lectures have nothing to do with the assignments and the assignments have confusing rubrics. Not much communication for a communications class. How well you write doesn't matter, its following the harsh rubrics that does.

Dr. Brown seems like a good person but just not a great teacher. There arn't many assignments so the grade in each matters. VERY HARSH GRADER. Group projects are very heavy in this class. Most of the assignments don't make sense with the course work done. 

Rubrics are very draconian. This is a course about how to follow instructions, not growth.

His class is easy while you dont have many grades (only 4 tests and a presentation) he did offer extra credit. If you read your textbook and take notes from it you will excel in the class. Attendance wasn't necessary but going could help clear up things from the reading. He also would tell you what would be on the tests.

Would I take this professor again? NO. There were 15 extra credit points given out this semester, for which I got 10/15 points, and he has only put in TWO points. This class is only graded on FOUR exams, ONE presentation, and attendance. So show up for class and don't do the extra credit because you will not be awarded the full amount of points.
Easy class, didn't have to communicate much but when I did he responded pretty quick. You get one hour for the 40 question final which is open book, but the time limit is pretty annoying.
Really enjoyed this class. Not an overload of work to do and he grades fairly.
He is very understand if you need something or extra credit. He made clear what was going to be on exams the week before. Overall he tries to make the class fun while being productive.
Teacher was very nice and everyone felt comfortable participating throughout the semester.

DO! NOT! TAKE! HIS! CLASSES! He was incredibly unclear is all of his teachings, he did not know what he was talking about half the time and always seemed lost. he is a tough grader, and the worst part is the reason he's tough is because you get handed questions he made, that don't make sense, then he fails you.

The professor was clearly passionate about what he was teaching, which I can always appreciate. However, that was quickly masked by how unclear and confusing the coursework was. Upon receiving clarification for assignments, I'd be more confused than I was beforehand. Overall, the content of the course is enjoyable, and he was a pretty easy grader.

Easy grader, a couple of tests and everything was straight out of the questions from the book it seemed. Group project but that seemed easy to do if people work. Is pretty vague in what he expects but you can still easily get an A.

The weekly quizzes never make sense, the grading guidelines are never clear, and he takes off points for the smallest things. Doesn't help that we use his own textbook, which is so stale and difficult to get through. Oh and good luck talking, he interrupts everyone.

You have to participate in class no matter what. Even so, he interrupts everyone! If he disagrees with you, you will be disregarded. Having a bad day? Doesn't matter. Miss class? Be ready to receive an email from him asking for an excuse! He rambles on about everything. No rubric for any assignment. Grading criteria are unclear always. 0/10.

The textbook was extremely hard to read, I would have to dissect basically every couple lines to attempt to grasp what it was trying to say. Also his feedback for discussion posts wasn't very helpful and didn't always seem relevant. His grading scale was strange as well.

Readings in class and then assignments after, attendance definitely needed and if you missed a day you wouldn't get to make it up, however, he was very fair with this and gave lots of opportunities for extra points. Very receptive and a lot of fun activites in class as well.

Class was pretty simple, 90% of the work was open at the begenning of the semester. Takes a while to grade due to his postion on the bench. Grades pretty strictly, very nnoying, does give feedback. 

He grades like a judge lol so expect nothing less, I've had worse professors so can't complain. Just do the work and put in effort and you'll be fine
Great guy and great professor, he gives great feedback and actually wants you to improve, if you try in his class, you will get an A and actually learn something.

Dr. Perry was a great professor! He gave really clear feedback which was really helpful since its the same assignments repeated with different cases. He also offered lots of extra credit which was helpful since he was a relatively strict grader and it was hard to make a 100% most assignments.
Wonderful professor. Highly recommend.

I have taken judge Perry for two classes and am planning to take more. He provides a genuine insight where you feel like you're actually learning, not just learning for a test to then discard the information later. If you can take him for anything that helps your degree, he is an absolute must take.

Great professor, given it was a long night lecture he is able to make it interesting and enjoyable. He gives lots of resources including videos and texts for the assignments. A lot of it is done in class and he gives some fun group projects for everyone to do.

Judge Perry is very knowledgeable and fun! There is usually one writing assignment a week and you are graded on how many points you accumulate. Not difficult to get an A if you follow the grading outlines and accurately examine the cases. If you complete all assignments and still don't have 90pts there are also several extra credit assignments.

Judge Perry was an amazing professor, would give lots of resources for assignments, that meant a lot of reading but it was all there. Grading was more than fair. He made the long night lecture less boring with engaging group activities and would put a video up for us to watch on the current subject, some of which I found interesting.

Great professor. He is a judge so all of his classes are held at night, but don't let that stop you. He knows a lot about con law and i've learned so much from being in his class. There is one assignment weekly due on Sunday nights and no exams. Quite a bit of reading is required but that's to be expected in a class like this.

Judge Perry is by the far most amazing professor at UNC Charlotte. Amazing professor! Take this course. You will not regret it. Very knowledge of the law, (of course, right, he's a superior court judge)

Very well respected. You will not regret taking this course unless you're not into the topic of the course.

JP is hands down the best professor I have had at UNCC. I know the fact that it is a night class is daunting, but it is 1000% worth taking it. He is a very fair grader, and typically there are only 1-2 assignments weekly. And if you ever need help career wise he is always there, 10/10 take his courses!

I really appreciate the personal experience that JP brings to this class. His stories and examples really helped me understand the concepts we talk about in class in a real-life situation. The assignments were interesting, and he is a very fair grader. Overall, it was a really fun and interesting class.
Very good professor. Makes the class as entertaining and interactive as possible. Not hard but make sure to take your time on mid term and final exam.
Somehow made a 3 hour class on a Thursday engaging and fun. You need to go to class but he know what he's talking about.

This was an almost 3 hour night lecture but he made it so fun and engaging. Easy grader, gives amazing feedback on all assignments, weekly case briefs and LOTS of extra credit available. He is so lovable and kind. 10/10 recommend him!

He's a cool guy, pretty much you show up and you pass. We only had a couple of assignments but they're pretty easy and you can tell he wants you to get an A. It was a 3 hour night lecture but he made it bearable. When you're picking the topic to put you into a group pick the one that sounds the smartest so you get in a smart group, worked for me.

While she is a fairly understanding, she can be a bit of a stickler for solutions that are not her own. She takes forever to answer simple questions. Thankfully, going above and beyond on assignments is not necessary. As long as you follow her instructions (which can be a little confusing) you'll be fine.
The class isn't hard at all. It focuses on city text and campus text. The small groups are fun, but she isn't the best at organizing things.  There were three canvas pages, which confused me.

Mrs Lynch is not a good professor. She thinks that this is a writing class and she tells you that you will most likely get a C or lower on your first paper. She grades unfairly and takes lots of points off for the smallest things. She also waits until the last day to grade everything so you only have an estimate of what your grade

An overall interactive, fun class, but extremely disorganized! You won't know your grade till the last day. But she did ask us at the end of the semester how she could work on that, so I'm sure she will be great. I would recommend her.

Very unorganized overall and she waited until the night before grades were due to grade the bulk of the assignments. There are walkabout assignments, reflections (completion grades), and a group final project. Not bad workload, Ms. Lynch is sweet, it just feels a bit like a semester of disorganized busywork.

I needed to take the class to fulfill my honors college requirement. I didn't think that this was a bad class, but I don't think that I got much out of it. The biggest assignment for this class was City as Text meaning you spend 7ish hours in uptown Charlotte, so prepare for a long day. However, we also did book clubs which I really enjoyed.

I specifically waited to Spring semester to take this class with Ms. Lynch. She always welcomed/appreciated my opinions. My favorite part was going to the concerts, then debriefing each. My only issue was that Ms. Lynch graded too harshly on the persuasive papers; I couldn't really argue my points, as they were deemed too direct (need evidence).

I liked the small groups because my group created a group project solutions to the homeless crisis and affordable housing crisis. Ms. Lynch set up plenty of large group exercises, so you never felt alone. I loved City As Text because we were able to roam the city and explore places that were important to us. Ms. Lynch always welcomed my opinions.

The LBST honors music class was pretty easy-going, but you HAVE to participate in every class discussion to get a good grade. If you're shy, this will have to be the class where you break out of your shell. Some projects and papers definitely require you to think out of the box. Other than that, I really liked the class.

Very caring and understanding. This is for the Honors Capstone, which is very difficult, but she isn't difficult herself. Gives lots of grace and gives good feedback. Good at informing us of how the capstone will work, and is good at preparing us for the capstone slowly. Could give more time to write the capstone itself, though.

I took HONR 3790 with Dr. Adnot and she's the best. She is very understanding and made criteria very clear. We did mini assignments to help us shape our Capstone Project. The assignments made choosing and narrowing a topic so much easier. As long as you put effort into every assignment, you'll pass.

Mr. Hooker is hilarious. He makes class fun and engaging. He prides himself on being able to confidently call every student by name and getting to know them. He is very accessible outside of class and he provides numerous resources for class usage. He gives us activities to do in class that includes socialization and movement so we are not bored.

Honestly the class was extremely unnecessary to say the least. Professor Hooker was cool the two or three times we saw him but the guest speakers were unnecessary and annoying. Easy A, the only real effort-requiring assignment was the 1200 word essay at the end but its nothing overly difficult, just annoying.

Easiest class ever. Prof. Hooker is young and relatable, but he doesn't really teach. You have guest speakers, then a 6 week seminar, then 2 more guest speakers. Class is the easiest 100 if you just do the work. Final is a 1200 word paper but if you just try you get a 100.
Professor Hooker was funny, relatable, and approachable, despite the utter uselessness of HONR1700 as a class. There were only a few actual assignments, all of which were busywork 100s.

I recall him "teaching" one time. Every other class for HNRS 1700 was either in small seminar groups with student teachers, or he had guest speakers come in. No problem with it, this class is just all busy work(pretty easy just time consuming) and a massive waste of time imo, just a check in the box for UHP first year requirements.

MANDATORY FOR UHP! Easy course, but annoying guest speakers! Loved Faculty Interview & 6-week Senior Seminars w/ articles to read/analyze. Hated Honors Colloquium. Terible prof rarely speaks & runs HCEs, so stuck w/ him for 3 more years. You journal/write 300-500+ words for assignments. If you write too much or too little, you lose 1/2 the points.
Does a great job of engaging students and making lectures fun. Assignments were very easy, and you can absolutely get a 100% if you put a reasonable amount of effort into them. Would take again.
I took this online and it was overall pretty easy. Each week you typically read a chapter of a book then write a 350 work reflection on it but that's it. I enjoyed thinking deeply in this class.

This class was easy, it was the first class in the honors program and Dr. Boyd was a great professor. The only downside is there were often times where emails went unanswered or took a long time to be answered. If you needed to ask him anything your best bet was finding him on campus.
Please take his class, you learn and he is a great person and actually talks about interesting stuff. It is impossible not to get an A.

I took this course in Spring '23 as part of the UHP Honors program. I loved this class because Mr. Boyd was a great professor & very open to talking about his familial anecdotes. Course content: Race, class, and education, and was right up my alley! Mainly discussion-based, which I liked as well. If you're in the honors college, TAKE HIM! CTCM 2530

Professor Boyd is extremely sweet and understanding. Classes were discussion-style and on important subjects. It can be a little boring/slow at times, but for the most part, just be ready to share your ideas. Great guy and great class!

Mr. Boyd's LBST-2301 course is required as apart of the honors program curriculum. I am very grateful I was able to have him as my teacher. His in-class discussions are thought provoking and he is extremely kind and considerate towards every student. The work given was never too overwhelming and the class layout is well-organized.
first rating deleted for being too mean. all i have to say.

I don't understand why her rating is so high. She gives more work than my calculus class. She gives extra credit but most of the time you have to travel really far to go to the event, she disregards people who don't have reliable transportation. Overall, I'd say her class isn't worth it if you just want the credits.

Jill sure is something. She is super sweet, very eccentric, and engaging. She shows up to class, tells a story or complains about something, makes an assignment up on the spot, and you leave after 15-20 minutes. It''s very strange. Total waste of time (still a waste even if there's no classtime) and money. But so incredibly easy.
This class is about nothing. She does not have a curriculum, and we pretty much supply the learning material for the class. WASTE OF MONEY.

Fall 2024: This genuinely might be the easiest college class ever. Jill is an amazing professor and hilarious! The class requires you to do very little and all the work is very fun! Class usually lasts no more than 20-25 minutes and you usually have Fridays off. This is a must take course, even if you don't like theater. It's an automatic A.

I love Jills tough love and fun lectures. If you take this class and expect an easy A, it will be fine, but I encourage participating in this class and having fun. The variety of assignments can be annoying if you don't get into them, but putting in effort makes it so much fun. This class is great for creatives and extroverts.

Jill's class is fun and easy, with simple assignments like script reading, acting, and videoing. No midterms or finals, just quizzes based on stories and videos u read/see. Have to attend 3 productions and write essays w the format she gives u. The final project involves creating a personal story with a protagonist (u) an antagonist. TAKE HER

Had Jill for my 1502 course and had so much fun. She'll end class early most days but will get on you if you show up late, so just don't. Has plenty of opportunities for extra credit, final grade is project-based. Participate in class and she'll love you.

decided to take thea 1502 to fill my arts/humanties credit for general education and I am so glad I did. literally such an easy and fun class, make sure to make friends as there are some group projects (which you do in class most of the time) and there's no final exam just a little movie project. She lets us out early like almost always too!

She cares about the students and she will make sure everything is going well for you. She will call you out if you are late but if your on time she is great. all of her lectures are really interesting.

Jill is great! Assignments are mainly projects, then there's a final project. Put in effort and you'll get an A. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she's not very tech savvy, so if you don't show up to class, you often won't know what the assignment is. All assignments made public someday. If you show up late, she will stop class and call you out.

Jill is honestly a very odd person but this class is super easy. Most class meeting days are cancelled and class meets for 30 min max on most days. Easy to get an A and probably more interesting if you are actually into theatre.

Ok, I'm honestly surprised she has so many positive reviews because I found her extremely mean-spirited and cruel. She is constantly degrading students, making comments on their appearance, mocking how some talk, and yelling at anyone who shows up even a second late (she will stop class every time someone is late). Really not a pleasant human being

Professor Bloede is very nice and funny. The class content mainly consists of small personal or group projects. Attendance is somewhat mandatory as some assignments are only in person. Easy as long as you put effort into your work.

I LOVE professor Jill! She is a very easy going professor and the class is fun! While there are a lot of assignments (which you need to be in class for most of), it's all based on your creativity. I actually wanted to go to this class. Take this class for an easy A but also for fun.

TAKE HER! I didn't know how much I needed Theater in my life until I met this woman. She's interactive with her students. She gives many projects throughout the semester, but they're easy imagination based things, so you can't give a "wrong answer". She brought out my untapped creativity.

This professor is truly caring and hilarious. Its a great intro class. She gives clear grading instructions for assignments. Although attendance isn't mandatory its definitely recommended to go. Overall really easy, fun class. In her words, "you have to really try to fail this class."
You will need to do some things on your end but it's overall great class. She is a great teacher and helps you become more creative.

Jill is so incredible at creating a safe and comfortable environment in her classes and I'm actually devastated that our class is over this semester. She's so incredibly caring and is so beneficial about your growth and actually cares about improvement and patience. She gives you so many opportunities to be yourself and find who you are.

Although her class was not what I was expecting, it was super fun and a great intro to college. She is super funny and charismatic. She helped me gain confidence in group projects which will help me in the future.

Robin is an absolute gem on Charlotte's campus and everyone could benefit from taking a class of hers. She has such exquisite expertise on the industry and isn't afraid to get real. She is the best professor to talk to and truly cares about everyone she teaches. I've learned an insurmountable amount from her and I'm glad to have her in my corner.

Professor Witt wants you to do well. She is very flexible and understanding and just wants you to do the assignments and engage with the material. Attendance isn't mandatory but she does take attendance and give participation points. There's about 8 plays you have to read throughout the semester. There's quite a bit of homework but it's not hard.

While the course work and curriculum doesn't entirely feel like what you may have expected, Robin is such an excellent professor and at the end of the term I feel like I have a heightened appreciation for directing styles and visual aesthetic choices. She's truly the best professor this campus has to offer and I'd recommend everyone take her.

This class is definitely reliant on reading the plays, so don't be mad when you don't do well because you didn't read. Robin is incredibly understand and creates a very comfortable environment where you aren't judged for your interpretations of the plays you read. She provides you with opportunities to talk with those in the industry and is great!

My goodness she's absolutely amazing. There is a decent amount of work, but if you do the readings you'll be good. She is so passionate that it makes the class so much more enjoyable. She cares about everyone, and is always clear with directions and due dates for assignments. She is always willing to work with you and is just the absolute best.
By far one of my favorite teachers at UNCC. She is so kind and considerate and you can really tell she cares about both her material and her students. 10 out of 10 would recommend.

I liked how the class is set up. The class is taught through an equation, which makes it very straight forward in my eyes. The material was engaging and interesting. The quizzes, while confusing at first, end up benefitting you. You can get everything wrong and still get a 40/100. Make sure to bring something for the scratch off grading sheets.

He grades quizzes based on his own subjective judgment, which feels inconsistent and illogical. He tends to talk excessively and often goes off-topic from the PowerPoint, making his lectures confusing. Some of his scientific explanations are inaccurate, and he isn't very understanding or tolerant.  I don't agree with the overly positive reviews

Dr. Scheff is a good person who cares deeply about what he is teaching. He does have a weird way of grading quizzes, but class work and tests are very straightforward. There are a lot of reading responses throughout the semester, but it isn't every class, and they aren't difficult. I would recommend going to class, but it isn't required.

Dr. Scheff is super down to earth and sweet, very passionate about what he does, has a lot of opportunity for extra credit, and makes the content easy to understand. My only critique is that he can be rather blunt at times, so just be prepared for that.

I absolutely love Dr Scheff! He's a super awkward guy but he's nice and cares about your learning. There are quizzes every 4 classes that are a big part of the grade so make sure to come to class and you'll do well on the quizzes. He offers a ton of extra credit assignments around the midterm and final.
He's a very nervous person but a great teacher. You can tell he cares about everyone learning.

I personally was not very interested in the material. Overall the class was easy, you only have to show up every 4th class for a quiz. Overall he was not my type of professor and often had a very nervous and chatty personality.

Dr. Scheff is genuinely one of my favorite professors I've had. You're able get some points back for missed questions on quizzes. Lecture slides are clear and have all the information you need, so it's really easy to catch up if you miss class. If you do show up, the lectures are interesting. Study the lecture slides and you'll do great.

This professor is supportive and very helpful. Clear with what you need to do there is a reading & quiz due each week. The reading is graded on completeness and can be done late for half credit. Gives so much extra credit through doing more reading. Overall very easy to learn and pass the class. One of the best teachers iv'e had.

His class was fine. You had to give him the answer he specifically said or wanted else it was wrong. Some things are confusing bc they are half his opinion but it's whatever. Lots of quizzes and lots of reading, does give extra credit though. He's a nice guy although just a little awkward.
Lectures can be dry but attendance isn't mandatory and his slides are very well written so you can learn almost everything from the slides alone without attending class

My absolute favorite teacher! Great attitude towards teaching and makes lectures fun. I also love how he does quizzes. Two parts, the first part is solo 10 questions, the second part is with a group and you get a chance to redo the questions! Uses a cool scratch-off quiz sheet. NEVER has pop quizzes. Going to miss this class. 100% RECOMMEND!

Most work is quizzes and group assignments with unclear instructions and late rubrics. My group often didn't understand expectations, expect harsh grading. She calls on students a lot but is genuine. Group assignments need clearer guidance!

hate this class so much, pop quizzes after every chapter lecture, I legit don't even know what shes talking about half the time or even if it is relevant to the major seems like a waste of time. She hates phones, will call on you so you need to be paying attention at all times, her assignments confusing, attendance mandatory, nothing good to say

class is monotomous and frankly not needed considering we have to read for homework anyway, its just talking about 1/2 relevant points of the textbook word for word instead of instruction. unclear quizzes and very strict policy, considering we are master's students. teaches as if we are sophomores, considering its been done this way for 10+ years.
Please just take this online. Teaches nothing in class and has weekly quizzes, at least she gives you notice. Clear, right? Clear! Clear.

Passed this class with a 92 ONLY because I tried to do really good on the quizzes. Couldn't really understand the professor, she was very rude when students had questions about assignments, and shes strict on grading. Final exam is optional.. don't plan on taking this professor in the future.
She is an amazing professor who will grade you as per your performance.

The class is graded off 3 exams, a group project and an analysis on the group project. Attendance is mandatory and is strictly used for lectures and presentations. Sometimes things can be a little unclear but she has no problem with asking questions or adapting to what will work for the class. If you pay attention and take notes you'll do fine.

I won't lie, this class has given me several mental breakdowns in just the 16 week period. Why is attendance mandatory for a course where the professor just reads off of slides? There's only 3 exams, 1 group project, a synopsis, and NO homework to help your grade. She's inconsistent with replies. If you have to take her, I give you my condolences.

I personally did not like Dr. Platonova since she treats her students like middle schoolers. She drops your grade a whole letter point if you miss more than 6 classes and gets upset when people have to leave during class to use the restroom. Very few grades, just 3 exams, a group project, and a paper. I would avoid taking another class with her.
Great professor and accessible as a resource

Dr. Clark is a very relatable professor who genuinely wants his students to succeed. He encourages understanding and real-life application of the material. While the content can be challenging at first, staying engaged makes it very enjoyable and applicable. Exercise Testing Lab was unique, hands-on, and highly engaging with lots of group work.

A complete waste of time and money. The material was a vague recap from ExPhys, Applied Kin, and Nutrition. Quiz grades are not posted until right before the exam (if at all). 
READ THE BOOK. There are NO lecture videos, NO detailed PPs. Just a short 12min podcast and a 5 slide max PP with vague info.

I took EXER 4285 and served as a TA for Dr Clark and have had a positive experience with both. He pushes you with the coursework; however, I have gotten the most out of this course and have used the material in a practical setting, such as my Strength & Conditioning internship. He is not only a great professor but is also a great mentor!

Dr Clark is very passionate about getting every student prepared for the real world. Taking both of his classes I learned to read what he says to read and pay attention in lecture. IF YOU DO NOT READ YOU WILL FAIL THE QUIZZES. He makes sure you know what you are learning and how to apply it, it is not mindless memorization but long term knowledge.

He used to be a coach and you can tell. Quizzes every week on a mix of what he claims to be lecture, notes , and textbook based but I only used notes and showed up to every class and barely passed them (averaged Cs on almost every quiz.) makes you workout and acts like a coach and not a professor. cool man but bad professor

Dr. Clark is extremely passionate about what he is teaching. He goes to great lengths to make sure his students understand the material he teaches. He expects you to critically think when going through quizzes which is great for real world application. My favorite part about the class was getting to go outside and move our bodies!

I wanted to like Dr. Clark's class, but he made this course harder than it needed to be. I am aware that his background is in coaching, which is very apparent, but having his TAs do weekly Kahoots was not enough to get the information needed for the weekly quizzes that comprised most of our grades. I'd recommend the other S&C prof.

The class was taken in the summer and was fast paced but Dr. Clark made sure we got everything we needed and even gave us an extra day if needed to finish labs. The quizzes can be hard but you just need to look at the lectures given and the lab packet and you'll do good.

Dr.Clark is a gentle professor and by far one of my favorites. He's big on proper writing, but that's in your best interest. He's not a tough grader, just GIVE YOUR BEST EFFORT. He is very passionate about the S&C field so you have a front-row seat to networking with him. Come to class prepared and you'll be fine.Easy A course IF YOU apply yourself

Dr. Clark genuinely shows an interest in his students and their understanding of the material. He takes the time to explain things in a manner that shows his depth of knowledge while also ensuring a depth of understanding with students. He gives constructive criticism that is meant to make an individual better in the field of Exercise Science.

Dr. Clark is a coach first and foremost, and was relatively new to teaching in a classroom setting when I attended his course. He decided to implement practical days into this semester and I believe it helped immensely. It broke up the lectures and gave us an opportunity to put what was in those lectures to practice. Great guy, give him a chance.

This class is very easy! Majority of what's on the quizzes and tests are on the lecture slides and some info from the book. The way he explains things helps as well you just have to pay attention! Overall he's an amazing teacher and if you love the gym this is for you Final is not whole semester cumulative only half semester same as the midterm.

I've had Dr. Clark for 2 classes now (EXER 3787 and EXER 3285) and I cannot speak highly enough of him! Dr. Clark truly cares about his students and their learning experience! He's very passionate about the material and it shows in the way he teaches this class. He's very understanding and willing to meet you where you're at/help in anyway he can!

Had 3285 and 4285 with him. 3285 was very textbook and quiz heavy and 4285 was more discussions and participation heavy. He's new as a professor but his experience in the strength and conditioning world shows when he lectures. In my opinion, 4285 was the better class. He is easy to get in contact with and responsive to emails.

There are multiple labs that require you run, jump, skip, and so much more. To survive this class, look over the small quizzes at the end of each chapter!

Dr. Clark lectures with no enthusiasm for what he is teaching, making the class a bore to sit through. Professor Clark is by no means a good professor. The class has multiple lockdown quizzes, one midterm, and one final. really not that great at teaching. somewhat knowledgeable. quiz heavy. only has midterm and final exam. takes forever to release quiz grades. half the material on the exam isn't presented in the lectures. most students in class are going for OT, PT, PA, but assumes/expected everyone to have the same level of understanding he does about sports.
Extremely fast pace. Unable to answer students questions. Quiz every class

My favorite professor I have ever had. Gives so many extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Lectures and information provided is very good and educational and presented in an easy to learn way. If you go to class you will pass the class. Professor Whitaker is the nicest lady ever and always available to help. she wants you to succeed

By far the best Anatomy professor I have ever taken! She is literally amazing, If you don't choose her what are you doing? She gives great lectures, but you will need to read the chapters before you get to class for the in class assignments and because the goes fast.

Professor Whitaker is very knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches, I really enjoyed class with her. Study hard because there are only a few grades throughout the semester, she did offer extra credit though. Go to office hours to review your exams! She is super down to earth and caring, she will call you out if youre acting up in class though!
I really enjoyed her teaching and her lectures. Her exams were a bit lengthy but she was a really great professor.

There are only a few opportunities for grades in this class so be prepared for the homework and exams. If you're a good student and study hard you'll be fine! Whitaker is super down to earth and kind, i really recommend going to her office hours to see what you missed on exams and ask questions. There are extra credit opportunities!!

You only have a few opportunities for grades in this course so be prepared for the homework and exams. Study the powerpoints and attend class and take in depth notes and you'll be totally fine. Whitaker is incredibly down to earth and nice if you're a good student who shows respect and effort in the course. Go to office hours!

Mrs. Whitaker is very nice. The class is made up of 4 exams (the last being a cumulative final). The class takes a lot of memorization. The modules increase in number each week which can feel a bit overwhelming at times, especially over a summer course. Meeting w her after each exam is very beneficial!

Whitaker was really nice and direct on rules and information that was important. There are not many grades except for quizzes and exams so make sure you study up (everything is in her power points). It was really fun being a part of her first class!

She was really straightforward in lectures (letting you know what was important to know). She offered potential extra credit for every exam but it's pretty difficult to get. The class is hard but she did everything she could for you. Just get ready to study her power points and know lots of diagrams. It wasn't fun but that's just the class.

I think professor Whitaker was an amazing professor. There are only 4 exams and 12 5 question quizzes going for your grade, but if you study her powerpoints and study the notes you will be fine. Anatomy alone isn't easy and is a lot of memorization, but if you study all the notes and diagrams the tests are very straightforward and simple!

no lectures in this class, expects you to learn material outside of class by reading the textbook. In class is only activities with different groups each week. VERY strict on deadlines but will also move deadlines to an earlier time without a heads up. Instructions in class werent clear, had to ask if you wanted reasonable explanation.

I can honestly say, I was very shocked to see that Dr. Cacace had any nice reviews on here.I am a Senior in college and I have never had a more frustrating class. Do not take this professor!!! Professor Cacace is impossible to understand and talk to. Professor Cacace made the course interesting and helped with understanding the material well. Her inspiration for teaching her class was clear and made learning the material fun. I would highly recommend taking her for an exciting learning experience.

The instructor was very helpful and able to respond in a timely manner for me to be able to make adjustments in assignments. Fairly easy in-class assignments. Just show up, do the work and weekly knowledge checks, and you'll do just fine.

If you want an easy credit, there are better options than this professor. All you do in that class is watch movies and take notes. if you show up to class the notes will help on the exams. If you don't show up to class, the class is still passable. Each class is comprised of taking notes for a short amount of time then watching a movie for the rest of class. Class is easy besides the speed of his lectures which are not posted online which makes notetaking challenging.

The class is exactly what you think it is. You watch movies in class and then possibly have a short quiz at the end. Attendance is optional but with that said, IF YOU DON'T GO TO CLASS, YOU WILL FAIL.
Left halfway through the year but was a good teacher for the time I had him. Class is basically watching movies and taking quizzes on them so I highly suggest anyone take this.

Prof Davis was fantastic! The Canvas was perfectly organised, and each assignment had clear rubrics. The weekly work was simple: just a few notes, a short quiz, and a discussion board. Interesting class. Great professor! Great sense of humor. Easy grader and the exams are super easy as long as you pay attention in class. He never tries to trick on exam questions they are very straightforward. He is an easy A.

I personally really enjoyed the movies he played (I liked exploring the different types of film). This class was overall pretty easy. Most of it is listening to Professor Davis talk about certain areas of film. The midterm and final exams are easy, as long as you show up to class and pay attention.

For the love of God fire him! His classes are 3 hours of us just hearing him talk about his life. You learn absolute nothing for his classes and unfortunately he teaches so many of the film classes. Honestly, this class is super easy. Watch the videos he posts every week/view the notes he has in each module and you will end with an A. Honestly, I hardly even watched the films. I purposefully registered for Professor Stringfellow's Introduction to Film and Media Art class because I had heard how much previous students loved taking his class. They are absolutely right. Best professor I've ever had! He's incredibly passionate about teaching and genuinely cares about helping students. I look forward to taking more of his classes.
Incredible!!!! Incredible professor! If you're a film student, his classes are a must-take. Very inspirational and very passionate about teaching. Love Stringfellow!

Rodney is the easiest person to listen to when he teaches. Even in classes that go late into the night he is unwavering in his enthusiasm and passion. There's no question he loves what he does. Great professor that made attending class enjoyable, gave me a better understanding of cinema.

Best professor I have had during my time here! He is extremely kind and encouraging and really cares about the success of his students. His lectures are very informative and engaging and he goes out of his way to help students achieve what they want.

Normally don't write reviews but this professor was so amazing I thought I needed too. She is absolutely amazing.
