I started the class thinking it was going to be easy, which was quickly disproved. However, the professor did adjust to the class's needs, made the assignments more manageable, and offered extra credit. He made the class one where you could learn about the subject and not worry about the grade. He cares about his students and wants to set them up.

Prof. G has repeatedly shown he truly cares about his students and their successes. He is a great professor to interact with and is always willing to hear his students' feedback. This class has the complexity and value I want from a DS degree. Yes, it's hard and a lot of work, but manage your time well and put in the effort, and you'll be fine.

This class is challenging but the time management, reading, and writing skills I learned but really useful. T PSET 1felt hard at the time but once I completed it, I felt accomplished. I felt prepared for my other courses. I could be passionate about data science. The professor is caring from what I learned from my conversations with him.

DATA 120 seems like a tough class at first, but it gets much better. Neil often stayed behind after lectures to give  instruction on that week's reading so that the readings were much quicker and easier to get through. Neil clearly cares about his students, and putting your best effort in gets you very far in this class. I learned a lot.

Professor Gaikwad is one of the best professors at UNC! He is so passionate about the course, starts every class by asking if we have any questions, and has office hours every day! While there were initially some challenging readings and question-heavy problem sets, Professor Gaikwad was open to feedback and even extended the assignment due dates.

Professor Gaikwad is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches. The workload at first was a bit overwhelming, but as you progress through the semester it becomes more manageable. As long as you do the work, you will succeed in this class.

At first, the workload felt heavy, but Professor Gaikward quickly adjusted to the student's needs as the semester progressed. I've never met a professor more passionate about his subject. He genuinely cares about our success and consistently goes above and beyond to support us, making sure we have the tools and guidance to thrive in the course.

The beginning of the class sucks, but it does get easier over time. Professor Gaikwad is slowly becoming more understanding and giving more time for assignments. His lectures are confusing, and the workload is at least 4 hours outside of class per week, but that number is starting to go down, thank goodness. The final is a project which is nice.
If you do the work, you'll be fine
He has improved with the workload and it is a lot better now. He has passion for the subject and strives for everyone to learn!

The professor is very passionate about this class and you can tell how much he cares for the students. At the beginning of the semester, the class expected a 100-level class to be easy. The class is challenging, but you are guaranteed a good grade if you do the work decently. Professor Gaikwad is learning and throughout the semester he has improved

This class will be challenging, difficult, and at times extremely frustrating. However, it is important to realize Professor Gaikwad assigns us these things because he truly believes they will help our understanding of the topics. He has been extremely understanding, flexible, and easy to reach outside of class. Take this class with an open mind

This class does have a lot of work, but Prof Gaikwad is incredibly passionate about this subject and is even more passionate about teaching. He only wants the best for his students and even ensures everyone will come out with a good grade. Neil is always there to help even beyond just classwork offering to support even our career after this class.

Neil is an assignment heavy prof. I feel as though many students, especially younger ones, took this class expecting an easy A, which is not the case. This class is not overly difficult, but takes time. Lectures are engaging if you participate. He is truly very understanding. Reach out to him, go to office hours, make a connection and you'll be OK!

Senior in Stats and DS, so I've taken most of the hard classes. The workload is WAY too much. I can't imagine how the freshmen/sophomores feel. My stochastic modeling class is far easier than this class. All three of my other classes combined are easier than this class. This should not be an introductory course. He's certainly passionate though.

This place is a mess, I must confess, The ambiance? Well, it's a no-go. The staff's in a daze, as if in a trance, Their customer care? Doesn't stand a chance. So if you're indoubt, take my advice, Avoid this disaster—it's truly precise. Worse than a purse, it's a rip-off at best,
This place is a nightmare; it's failed the test.
Pointless busy work that doesn't actually teach you anything of substance.

If he says "space out the workload" one more time. Great professor but doesn't understand that this is not the only class students have.  The amount just on those should be enough each week, but then there's the Problem Sets that never end. Gotta work on this final project now  I wish the professor would understand the workload is too much.

This class is a lot of work, but I think it is manageable if you space it out correctly. He is super passionate and is very understanding if you need help or have something come up. If you do the work, you will get a good grade.

I just wanted to take a moment to highlight how incredible Professor Gaikwad is! His passion for DATA 120 is inspiring, and his teaching style brings even the most complex topics to life. Whether he breaks down challenging concepts or goes above and beyond to support students, he makes learning an engaging and enriching experience. Thank you, Neil!

Amazing professor, Neil truly cares about this topic and students. However he cares too much and expects the students to have the same passion. Which makes him assign vast amounts of work to try to make us "experts". Which would be great if this was a 400+ lvl course, but this is a 100 lvl course. Only take if you are taking no other courses.

Everyone complaining about the reading reflections is wrong. It takes maybe 3 hours max to get a 10/10 and that's if you used NO readings strategies. There's no midterm instead a problem set which is admittedly mind numbing and way too long. Everyone in this class doesn't listen during lecture anyways, so do your problem set...passionate professor!

Professor Neil Gaikwad is truly a dream! If pointless busywork is your thing, look no further. Expect endless readings, problem sets that make you think sleep is optional, and the occasional “catch ChatGPT” trap for extra fun. And who wouldn't love writing essays for problem sets? Truly, an unforgettable experience!

I am a junior pursuing Applied math and Comp sci, and I am done with my math major, and I will stand on it that I have never taken a class harder with more workload than this class. My semester is dying because of this exact class, and I have taken much harder much more stressful classes.

Do yourself a favor and avoid this class. I'm doing COMP283 and COMP210 this semester and this class requires more time than the time I put into both combined. The workload is so unnecessarily overwhelming. He is trying too hard to give the class a reputation for being hard, thinking that will result in more learning, but it really doesn't.

Incredibly difficult and frustrating with an insanely huge workload. Instructions are unclear and material is WAY beyond 120. All Professor Gaikwad talks about is how easy the class is and how we need better time management. Meanwhile, the assignments and material are impossible to keep up with or understand. PLEASE someone fix this class.

he is passionate but the workload is too much. we read 30+ pages/week, write 4+ pages reflections, & some assignments end up being 20+ pages. there is no clear grading & it feels like random grades are assigned. this is an introductory class, yet there's more work than my upper level classes. he says to manage time well, but it's just so much work.

Professor Neil Gaikwad is an absolute legend! He is not only incredibly knowledgeable but also caring and supportive. His sense of humor makes every class enjoyable, and his inspirational teaching style motivates students to push themselves. He is highly respected by his students and peers, making him one of the best professors I've had.

Wont even make a funny review, this class is genuinely incredibly difficult in terms of course work. He assigns 2 assignments per week that are 30+ required readings and reflections that are 3-4 pages long. The final project is so confusing and there are 3 assignments that are 23+ single spaced pages long. Professor is nice but way too passionate.

The class has an extremely big workload for being a 100 level introduction class. Lots of readings and writing during week. There is no clear grading and lectures tend to go off topic a lot. Overall, it is hard, a lot of work, and lectures are confusing. Final project is also not clear and confusing.

I must give this class a 1/5 simply because he has killed my enthusiasm for data science. This class has singlehandedly caused me more stress than any other class I have ever taken. The problem sets and readings seem endless, and he even has the gall to criticize our time management skills. I have a life to live outside this class.

I really really really want to like the professor -- he's really passionate about ethics in data science, but there's so much work. If this was a later-year class, sure, but I'm not even in an actual major yet and I'm expected to write thousands of words on advanced content that I'm not even passionate about

Neil's a good guy but the workload for an INTRODUCTORY level course is absolutely insane. Went into the class thinking it'd be philosophy-heavy but he's trying to teach us the intricate interworking of machine learning which is not what I signed up for. Hardest class of my life and single-handedly ruining my semester.
Get ready to do 7+ pages of writing and 40+ pages of reading per week.

I'm in his DATA120 class, and it has interesting concepts but SO MUCH WORK and SO MUCH content thrown at you. He is treating this introductory level course as an MIT graduate one. I have not been able to comprehend anything. I really hope this class gets improved in the future. PSA: I'm in DATA 140 also, and it is less than half the work of 120.

Professor Gaikwad is very knowledgeable on the subject but assigns a ridiculous amount of homework. Had a 42-question problem set, 60 page reading, plus 3 pages of writing all due in the same week. Questions are vague, barely addressed in the readings, and have multiple long parts. Interesting class but far too much work for a 100 level.

Prof Gaikwad seems like a perfectly nice guy but the amount of homework he gives is truly insane. I'm talking 30+ pages of articles per week with several specific multiple part essay questions. I get that he wants to reinforce the concepts and all, but I am not working my two brain cells overtime writing essays for him just bc he's from MIT smh.

Dr. Ghani does not require too much from his students, and you can put in very minimal effort and still receive a solid result. His class was very test-focused with some coding assignments. The class is very relaxed and all the info that you need is easily accessible online.
Easy class but lectures are pretty boring
Professor Ghani was excellent at teaching data structures but I felt that the material covering algorithms was lacking. Overall it was a good class and the lectures were available online.

It could be a hard course if you really want to understand everything in this course (for people with no much foundation for data structure in general). However, Dr.Ghani made it easier through lecture videos and very detailed powerpoints (which cover EVERTHING on exams). 
It's a bless that tests are not hard! Just make sure to read materials.

There is no attendance grade and all lectures are recorded, which is nice. But content of the class is just  kinda boring. Dr. Ghani speaks monotone throughout the lecture, but honestly who can blame him? At least the exams are not bad. You just have to watch the lectures closely, and he gives generous deadlines for the homework assignments.

I loved 210 with Dr. Ghani. His lectures may seem boring but I urge evryone to actually go to class because it makes it so much better and interesting! My grade in the course is not the best but that was due to other personal reasons, otherwise I think Dr. Ghani really sets you up to succeed! Really chill, wholesome guy!

Professor Ghani is very knowledgeable. It is honestly better to just not go to lecture and watch his videos on 2x speed because he is very monotone and boring. I found myself sleeping in his class a couple times and I went back to watch the vids anyway. Midterms (one dropped) and Finals are weighted heavy so make sure you prepare for those.

Dr. Ghani is awesome. Lectures got significantly more interesting as the semester continued. Midterms and the final are largely based on the lectures, so attending them will help you do well. Extremely lenient with due dates, and practice exams are very similar to the actual tests. Ghani even drops 1 midterm.

This is a relatively easy class. The lectures are pretty boring, but very necessary to watch for the midterms and final. The assignments are pretty easy, but sometimes take a little longer to complete.
He was a pretty good professor and obviously knew a lot about the topics. Lectures weren't the most interesting but they were all recorded. Midterm and finals were chill.

Lectures are recorded so you don't have to go to class, but it was kind of weird because the material on midterms was nothing like our assignments, so you have to read the slides and listen carefully to lecture to do well on the tests. 1 homework and 1 midterm are dropped. Class is super boring at first but gets more interesting towards the end.

Ghani has lenient deadlines on hw and is very helpful when you ask him questions, but going to class is a waste of time. Lectures are posted, so I learned by watching in 2x speed before midterms and I did fine. Just beware that they don't teach you java so coding hw can be difficult if you have no experience. TA office hours were helpful though.

drops one of two midterms so that *can* be nice - try harder on the first as it is way easier than the second. don't cheat on the homework, and you'll do great! he doesn't do a great job explaining many concepts - went to office hours and he just walked through it with no real explanations. try not to fall asleep in class

Lectures are super boring but not his fault it's data structures and attendance isn't mandatory. All lectures are recorded so you can go back, drops one out of two midterms. Overall wasn't a bad class and he's good at explaining concepts.

Pretty enjoyable/interesting class at times, but it was definitely some of the most BORING lectures I've been to. The lectures are recorded though and the assignments have extensions. He also dropped one  midterm and coding assignment.

Wish all my classes were taught by ghani. recorded lectures made learning easy. he drops a midterm, extends hws, and does so much more to allow you to succeed than any other profs. coding hws can be tough but office hours are THE best. sure lecture is boring, but watch the recordings at your own pace and you'll see how well he explains concepts.

Ghani is a nice guy, but his lectures are incredibly boring. He records all lectures and puts slides on Canvas. Like 110, coding assignments are autograded but are decently harder. He does not explain Java well as the class is focused on learning Data Structures with Java as opposed to the other way around. He drops the lowest of 2 midterms.

Good. Very passionate but he's just got an ASMR voice so it's hard to stay awake (I have never fallen asleep in a class, I came close in COMP 210). Kind of a very theoretically heavy class, so for projects you don't really know *how* to do anything. But there's like 700000 TAs so just go to one of the many office hours and they're super helpful.
Lectures are extremely boring, all he does is read his slides. Homework assignments are not very hard and don't take long. Exams are fairly easy as long as you study the content in the slides.

While lectures can be a little boring at times, he makes up for this in his caring personality and plethora of resources (videos, practice questions, etc). Ghani and his TAs were always available for questions, and it is undeniable that Professor Ghani is a king in the comp sci department.
He is not good at explaining things and assumes too much knowledge from students

Ghani teaches 210 fantastically. The first half of the class is definitely a snoozer, and the second half rather difficult, but he provides you with so many resources, makes exams extremely fair, and is very good when it comes to grading. Absolutely great, every lecturer should record their lectures like Ghani, they were so useful. Great prof.
Just lock in honestly. Typical professor but chill and nice man.
absolute snoozer class, but easy tests and homework if you understand the concepts/research them independently

Ghani is the chillest prof at UNC. I can see why people say his lectures are boring, but you learn a lot if you attend because he's always posing questions to the audience. The exams are easy and similar to the practice ones. Every homework was extended, but they get a lot harder throughout the semester, so don't slack off on the early ones.

if we azzume that you need to take COMP 210, dr ghani is a good option. the lectures are kind of dry but it's data structures and algorithms; i don't know what people were expecting. he does a pretty good job explaining concepts, and lectures are recorded (with varying audio quality). lowest midterm and assignment are dropped so overall pretty easy

Ghani's lectures were definitely on the boring side, but I would not worry about not passing the class. For both midterms, if you listen to lectures and study for at least a day, you can get a 100. If you put enough time into assignments, you will get a 100. Grading on midterms is lenient. The only negative is that office hours are poorly run.

class is graded on labs, one midterm, and a final. labs are free 100s, if you don't get it OH will get you to the 100. midterms you have to study for, but one is dropped so you get a freebie. the final was slightly hard b/c lots to memorize, but put in a few days of studying and you'll get an A. all exams are very fair. watch lec on 2x speed!!

The lectures for this class can feel long and difficult but they are very useful for learning content. The grading for the course was nice since 1 of 2 midterms was dropped and assignments were auto-graded with infinite submissions. A lot of the grade does rely on the final so it is really important to be very well prepared for the test.

He is personally a great prof but you dont know your exam results until end of semester. his classes are boring but acceptable as the attendance is not mandotary and he shares the recordings on youtube, so you can watch them on 2x.

He is a nice and caring professor, his lectures sometimes are a little on the boring side but I enjoyed the class nonetheless. I wouldn't worry about COMP 210 with him. The slides are helpful enough and you can always go back to them later when he posts them online. The midterms were both fair, if you do the assignments, you'll be all set.

Ghani is the goat. His lectures are boring, yes, but if you watch the recordings on x2 speed its not too bad. My man constantly extended due dates, and curved the class after a rough final. He was approachable, yet on top of business.

One of the goat cs profs. Loved that he recorded his lectures, teaches very well with thorough explanations and engaging questions. Dropped lowest midterm, cared for his students, extended coding assignments due dates. Everything about this guy is great. Class in general is not too hard, assignments can get challenging but office hours are great

GOATED. Gives assignment extensions. Teaches data structures very thoroughly. Didn't go to a single office hour. His lectures are lowkey boring, but if you participate / review content before class / watch recordings at 2x speed, it becomes pretty fun.

I felt that Professor Ghani was a great teacher, but struggled to keep to the assignment schedule. He made the content fairly easy to digest. However, he does not go over the basics of Java which I know was a struggle for several students. If you are familiar with Java and thinking about data structures, the class will be easy.
very boring lectures but a nice guy and always willing to help outside of class. grading is lenient, lowest assigbments dropped as well as the lower midterm
Flexible class. Study well before the tests and you will be fine. Assignments are chill. Low stress and fair tests. Ghani is great!
W prof bro is chill

Lectures are recorded, lowest of two midterms dropped, and fair final. I only looked at the slides to complete assignments or a few days before exams and still did fine (as a non-CS major, too). A very hands-off, flexible class where you have everything you need to succeed.

Dr. Ghani is a great professor. His lectures could be boring at times but it is because he makes sure everyone understands. He is very lenient with grading and makes sure all questions are answered clearly. He stays after class to answer all of the students' questions and provided an unneeded curve at the end after all the grade drops. Nice guy.

Professor Ghani was amazing. His lectures were thought-provoking and engaging and his course was structured in a way that everything logically flowed together. I can't recommend Professor Ghani enough. My only complaint is that some of the tests are graded in a very nit-picky way but he drops the lowest midterm so that makes up for it.

Professor Sayeed Ghani, the beacon of light in the dark abyss of computer science despair that is Professor Snoeyink's class. While his lectures may not be the most fun thing to listen too, listening to him is like being wrapped in a warm, fuzzy blanket of compassion and understanding compared to snoeyink.

Professor Ghani was a very understanding and caring professor. He posts lectures on youtube the day after they take place and allows students to watch them async. The content is easy and he takes his time to explain (almost to a fault I would watch lectures on 2x speed).

Dr. Ghani is one of the best teachers I've had in terms of grading. Very lenient grading distribution (takes best of two midterms and best 6 of 7 assignments) and exams have very generous partial credit. Allowed me to actually care and learn the content without having to worry about my grade. Lectures can be boring but they are recorded!

Prof. Ghani is great! Very caring guy, basically every assignment got extensions if someone asked. Midterms/ final are fairly straightforward if you are up to date with lectures, which are all posted to his YT and take practice exams. The assignments were pretty difficult but if you go to office hours or work with others you'll be fine. Nice curve.

Professor Ghani cares about his students. Any material mentioned in his exam is not there to trick you. The exams are very straightforward, and if you attend class/watch his lectures, it is very easy to do good on them! Definitely utilize the practice exams that he provides, because it gives you a fair idea of what the test is going to look like.

The most boring lectures I've ever been to after the first week of class I just watched them on youtube on 2x speed. Homework is pretty easy but your midterm and final count for 70% of your grade combined so its pretty easy to do bad in the class even if you get 100 on all the HW.

Boring lectures. He monetizes YouTube recordings so there are ads, which is annoying. My biggest issue is that I found him to be very inaccessible. Several times I needed to contact him urgently and never received any response, even about accessibility and accommodations issues which created a lot of anxiety and stress around this course.
Ghani's class is good. You don't ever have to go to lecture, just watch the recordings. Midterms and assignments are simple enough. Solid class.
Some of the most boring lectures I've ever witnessed, but he had relatively easy exams and homework that made self studying not too difficult.

His lectures are boring, and i skipped a lot of them, which ended up making me study for the final 2 weeks before it so i could watch his lectures online. doing all that made me realize his midterms were slight, so if you just watch his lectures and know what your doing there was no code writing on the final, only one question on the second midterm

Professor Ghani is caring to his students. His lectures can get very boring, but he ensures his students understand the concepts being taught. He has a VERY lenient syllabus, dropping 1 out of 2 mid-term grades and 1 out of 6 HW grades. Go to office hours and they will help you receive 100 on HW. Exams are also very similar to practice exams.

Good professor, lectures not compulsory and recorded so easy to watch when free, grading criteria is super clear. More practice questions would have been helpful but he's pretty lenient when grading so that's a plus. Drops your lowest midterm (1 out of 2) so thats also great. Overall he made 210 understandable and less intimidating.

Lectures are incredibly dry, majority of class skipped because of recordings. Lowest exam drop and generous grading are a blessing that takes away stress. I enjoyed the assignments and found them reasonable coming from an intermediate background in Java. There is a large chunk of content, but Ghani's section should be conducive to your success.

Great professor, I highly recommend taking his section of COMP 210. He is very flexible in that he streams all of his lectures on Zoom and later uploads videos of them to YouTube. The tests are a very large portion of your grade, but they are fair. He is very willing to answer any questions about the material.

Prof Ghani's class was very organized. He had recorded lectures on Youtube and he always had practice exams for the midterms and final, which were a great way to prep. His coding assignments can be tricky, so do review some Java and make sure you go to Office hours and get help from the ULAs (Shoutout Bek!) He is a fair grader, so put in the work!

Profressor Ghani is an understanding profressor when it comes to homework and extensions. All of his lectures are recorded and the tests are pretty straight forward and don't try to trick you. Overall he is a good profressor.

Very accommodating; recorded lectures, extensions, zoom option. He definitely cares about his students. Conceptually easy class, but assignments can be difficult if you don't know java as they're pretty intricate. Lectures can be boring, but Ghani is very good at explaining and makes the class very attainable. I enjoyed taking this w Ghani!

Ghani is a good teacher but his lectures can be very boring. As long as you pay attention to the material & understand the concepts, you will be fine on the midterm and final. This was portrayed as a java beginners friendly class, but i can assure you that it is not. you do need to be somewhat proficient in java to do the assignments, tho OH helps
Very nice, records all lectures which are informative and helpful, extends hw all the time

The grind never stops for this man, as another review said. Class on zoom, class in person in two different lecture halls, extensions with no warning (good?), etc. Man will lecture at 3AM if he needs to. Clearly he cares about the class, although his TAs don't, they're lazy. Data structures is naturally pretty boring imho, dont expect the world.

nice professor, always pushed back hw, lectures are boring but if you pay attention to the lecture you will do good on the exam, and office hours are very helpful if you are ever stuck on the hw, not a hard class practice exams are very similar to the exam and he takes the best score of two midterms
professor was still trying to have a zoom class while people are getting shot at
There is currently an active shooter at UNC and he still demanded that we hold a lecture on zoom having no sympathy towards any of the students in his course and how they might have been affected.
There is currently an active shooter at UNC and he is literally still having lectures today on Zoom. Grind never stops for this man.

He is a very clear lecturer that curves the class(via grade drops) and provides practice midterms that are basically identical to the actual test. The material is presented well and his expectations aren't high. Every class is streamed on Zoom and recorded. The only downside is that some homework was tough, often b/c of poor instruction on the hw.

The HWs rarely seemed related to the lectures & were pretty difficult. The lectures were also not great for my learning because Ghani had the attitude that we all should be following along easily & CONSTANTLY asked questions of the audience. However, dropping 1 of 7 HWs and 1 of 2 midterms definitely helped my grade. Overall, so-so class.

PROS
- Very nice with extensions.
- Practice is really similar to exams.
- Drops a midterm grade for final grade.
- Zoom Access

CONS
- Dry lecture


TIPS
- Read Piazza before the exam because he sometimes tells you what's on the test 1 hour before the exam.
- Submit them assignments early G.

Easy class as long as you show up in person.

Unless you are already proficient in Java or have baseline knowledge about data structures, I do not recommend this class. It is extremely inaccessible for students new to the subject matter. Assignments will put you through hell, fair warning.

Prof. Ghani is a very average professor for compsci. His entire class is lectures, with no interactive coding work during. He goes over the concepts, but leaves figuring out the java coding language completely up to you. Somewhat an organized professor but lecture is the most boring I've had to sit through at Carolina.

There were 7 assignments total and 2 midterms. As long as you watched all the lectures, the midterms were a breeze. Ghani is very lenient and extends most assignments, and he drops our lowest midterm grade. The only thing that I don't like about the class is that lectures can be a bit dry.
I thought Ghani explained everything very well and was very lenient when it came to the homework and extensions.

Lectures are sometimes a bit dry, but you have the option of watching them on Zoom. You have to learn Java yourself since he doesn't teach it in class. He gives us practice tests before the midterms, and as long as you study what he teaches in the lectures you should be fine.

If you're not Jeff Bezos, don't expect to know a lot from this class. Ghani talks as if you already know everything. People said he was interesting/funny but I don't really see it. His assignments are hard, he only gives a week to do them, TAs are rarely available, etc. Wish I had taken Stotts. He's apparently more boring but his class is easier.

I genuinely think bad reviews are just because people got bad grades in the class. He wasn't the best as it was his first semester, and he wasn't a great lecturer, but he did everything in his power to help us succeed, like giving us tests exactly like the practice tests. Assignments were hard at times but it did follow the content taught in class.

He constantly asks the class the answer to in-class questions even though he hasn't taught the concept. Does not actually teach java you have to go to office hours or figure it out on your own. He'll just go on and on about the concept and then have you hand-write code on the tests.

Dr. Ghani is a very unorganized professor, but is very "fair" with his extensions on assignments. I say this with quotes because, he was almost required to give extensions because he would give students a long assignment due shortly after assigned, and no one would be done on time. He also brushes past almost all important information in lecture.

It was Prof. Ghani's first semester at UNC and he was informed almost last minute for teaching this course because of one professor left, and he did a fantastic job! I come in with no prior knowledge in Java and find this class very helpful. I recommend go through all codes on his slides for understanding. Assignments are hard but really fun.

I enjoyed this professor's way of teaching, he tries to get students to think as much a possible during lectures. He is pretty forgiving when it comes to grading. He started students off with a programming language they didn't know, but overall good professor!

Midterms are similar to practice ones, but answer keys had mistakes, so it was hard to understand topics and grading criteria. His teaching was difficult to understand and midterm grading was arbitrary. Got a much lower grade on the final than I thought, and said we couldn't see our exam "per policy". Assignments are 40%, which helps your grade.

Doctor Ghani is a great guy. He is friendly to students and passionate about teaching. However, he was bad at teaching, and he made some mistakes when teaching. First impression is important for new learners! We were behind, and then he went super fast at the last several lectures. The good thing is his exams are really similar to practice exams!

Very obviously new to teaching. Had nothing due for months and then 7 assignments crammed into the space of like 4 weeks - and these assignments were hard. So be prepared to spend hours in office hours - I averaged 8hr/assignment. Some tests were similar to practice tests, others wildly different. Nice guy, and funny too - not for me.

He is chill and just wants to teach us algorithms. Class is a good start if you've never done leetcode, but you'd probably do better if you did do leetcode before taking the class. Exams are like half copy and paste from the problem sets and half impossible problems. Definitely one of the hardest classes in the major content wise.

Class is doable bc he's a lenient grader. Problems and posted materials are enough that you can teach yourself algorithms outside of class. Pacing is fast but Kevin does a solid job teaching hard material. Tests are 50% from problem sets and 50% completely unsolvable, but he curves.

Over half of the exam questions are from problem sets with new questions being very difficult to get right. Algorithms is typically a difficult class but the pacing of this course is very fast since each lecture covers ~2 problem types. Lectures are pretty good but are definitely not enough to good on tests. Class avg curved to B+.

- Grading criteria is generous (65 is a C)
- Content is difficult but useful
- HW is 40% of grade and easy A
- No attendance
- Tons of high quality resources

The course encompassed difficult material and difficult exams. Requires a deep understanding of each algorithm and they get more complex throughout the semester. Expect to spend a good chunk of time studying. Midterm averages were always low 70s. Final was even harder. Still, Kevin was supportive and did a good job teaching.

Really chill guy who is obviously passionate about this class and teaching as a whole. I thought he explained concepts pretty clearly for a difficult class. The material is interesting and a good bit of it is useful for interviews. Midterms are 5 Qs and always have one tricky question that most people don't solve but he curved so median was B+.

Actually a really cool dude, the class was pretty forgiving and concepts were interesting. Ramps up around the 2nd midterm, I'd recommend really understanding the fundamental building blocks of each algorithm - it helps a lot for the conceptual algo questions where you need to come up with stuff off the dome.

550 is a hard class already, and Kevin's insistence on memorizing 20+ algorithms, their runtimes, and proofs didn't help. Prior LeetCode experience will be very helpful, but not totally necessary. That being said, Kevin is a cool guy, and the grading is pretty generous: the median grade was a B+, and the cutoff was at least under an 81 to get it.

Don't take unless you have to. Kevin is chill, but we see ~4 new algorithms every class, yet only understand ~25% of each. You basically brute-force memorize the problem sets and hope for partial credit on exams. We never learn how to optimize algorithms, but just solve particular problems. At least the TAs were cool and VERY helpful.
THE GOATTTTTT easy homework, great lectures. 10/10

I'm writing this rating for COMP 283, although listed as COMP550. 

He's honestly just a chill dude. Final could replace all midterms. Although this class was semi-proof-heavy it was not compared to that of Jacks. Homework was a breeze. The proofs were easy to follow and understand. Just do the practice problems he provides and you'll be good.

It's disgusting how much cheating happened during the final. People standing up at the end to quickly check their answers and others that used pre-written notes are absolutely shameless and don't deserve to pass this class. Others that actually sat through every single lecture and struggled deserved the amount of leniency our professor provided.

Took in SP25; FA24 ppl, your median was curved to an A bcs of how bad y'all did n y'all fell under the halo effect. Tests 2 hard (~70% of grade) r freeresponse with rubrics defined as "minor error"+"major error" making it hard to judge valid regrade requests. Good lectures+HWs. TAs r👎, (prob bcs SP25 was harder) sry babes💔. B+ median no curv givn

Great professor who explains things well and really cares about students learning the material.
Unfortunately, there was a lot of cheating in the back rows despite assigned seating. I was in the front and took the final fairly, and struggled, while many behind row 6 used phones or talked.
Unfair that honest students get hurt while cheaters get As.

Took this class in Fall 2024. Kevin is a great guy, but I should admit that the class is not easy. If you're trying to learn how to write algorithms to be prepared for interviews, this class is great. Otherwise, I see why ppl might complain given that the class implicitly requires some leetcode experience unless you're an ultrafast learner.

I took this class in Fall 2024 but this class was super doable. As someone who knew essentially nothing about the algorithms we would learn in this course I found that the exam structure and grading scales were specifically designed to give students grace and help them succeed. Kevin is a super nice guy and I really enjoyed taking his classes.

Exams are extremely difficult and graded harshly. It is nearly impossible to get through all of the problems (write out algorithm, explain why correct, and determine runtime) in the allotted time. Doesn't even know how to explain what he teaches (just waves his hands & says it's too easy to explain). If you can take with another professor, do that.
This is one of the worst CS classes I've ever taken. I wish we had more time on the exams and the test problems weren't so difficult.

Weekly assignments are very doable in groups, which is encouraged. They are also very lightly graded, showing a decent level of understanding is full credit. Kevin is a good lecturer and very chill. I attended every class and almost always felt like I learned something, and the class overall definitely made me better a general coding.
Not hard, but most of homework and exam questions are from leetcode
Good professor, easy to get A
The median final grade in this class was an A. It's not hard.

you have to be an actual bum to fail this class. grading is extremely lenient, out of 105%, free 100% on hw, quizzes, punctuality, and he reuses prev questions on half the midterms and final. for context, i got about median scores on both midterms, and to just PASS the class i wouldve needed a -20% on the final. you have to actively try to do bad
Great lecturer. He breaks down hard concepts and makes them feel intuitive. Generous grading scale. If you spend some time after class to review the material, you will succeed.

Solid lecturer, extremely generous grading scale (out of 105 total points), tons of drops/late days on homeworks, follows his own concise/efficient online notes, uploads recording of all lectures, takes half of exam questions from posted examples with solutions
Kevins the goat

Kevin Sun is dope. Very straightforward teacher. Has super generous grading (The class is out of 105%). This idea that you need a bunch of "leet code experience" is wild. I had none and did well by just attending lectures and completing homework. I think he is teaching 283 next semester, so if looking at this for that I think he will teach it well

This class is as forgiving as it could be. Kevin Sun makes the class out of 105%, gives partial credit for extremely wrong algs, tells you 60% of the midterm qs verbatim beforehand. He also records lectures, no mandatory attendance, 5 late drops, etc. This class could be much much harder. Overall great guy and really interesting lectures.

Don't listen to the other reviews, he makes this class as easy as possible. There are 105 possible points to get out of 100, he's very generous with the partial credit, and every exam has 2 problem set problems on it, so you only need to actually solve 3 questions. With just a little bit of studying before exams, it's almost guaranteed to get an A.
imo, not a decent class

He covers too much material in a short period. Not to mention, he requires a lot of writing on exams within 65 minutes. He doesn't know how to measure the difficulty of his exams. His exams are hard, despite the fact that 2 out of 4 problems are from problem sets. Basically, you should be a LeetCode wizard to do well in the class.

Exams and exam grading were weird. Imagine having several algorithms to write, plus proving why they work and explaining their running times. It's nearly impossible to get all the points on an exam. He will always give you partial credit, even if your algorithm is correct. He doesn't even know how to properly explain the correctness part himself.

Someone said, 'Not doing LeetCode prior to this is on you.' Really? Where in the prerequisites do you see that LeetCode experience is required? Just because you got a good grade due to prior experience doesn't make your review valid. Not everyone in Computer Science applies for jobs that explicitly require knowledge of algorithms.
decent class imo

Class is difficult (as would any algorithms class be) but it is very doable if you put in effort. lot of people complaining that the material is too hard but as a CS major if you havent done any leetcode prior to this junior/senior class, that's entirely on you. basically dont be a bum and this class is great. i found material to be very interestin

His notes are completely illegible, resembling a doctor's hastily written prescription. When you take this class, you should have already been leetcoding for quite a while. If you were not, good luck because the guy is making the class ridiculously hard.
This class basically prepares you for an IQ test that you can't change. Memorization? Yes! Giving hard problems on exams? Yes! Good luck!

I wish this class wasn't so test focused and that the midterm wasn't right after break, but the professor was nice, easy to talk to. With that being said, I do wish he was a bit more formal at times though I could see some students enjoying the more intuitive explanations so this may depend on who you ask.

It is true the homeworks are hard, but the grading scheme and tests were very easy. Don't buy most of the reviews, he is very chill and this class is not nearly as hard as it arguably should be. If you just memorize the algorithms decently and do some practice problems (lots of algo problems from other unis online) you should get an A no problem.

This class could've been much worse! He is a very boring lecturer (partly due to the boring material), so most people just skipped lectures (he also records them). He did offer a bit of EC on the final, but the material is pretty hard to understand if you don't leetcode in general. HWs were very hard imo, but quizzes were easy. Tests were fair too!

I hate a proof based class but Professor Sun makes this class super accessible and all the assignments/exams were super fair. He's also super understanding and takes student feedback into consideration. It was really nice to felt like he cared about student opinions and wanted us to succeed!

Professor Sun was excellent at lecturing and offered helpful homework assignments. Even though the midterm was challenging, with a median score of 60%, he provided 20% extra credit on the final. He ensured the final was manageable enough for the median score to reach 103% with the extra credit!

Professor Sun is a great choice for 550! The midterm was extremely difficult (and had Leetcode style FRQ questions), but his drop policies and EC on the final exam made up for it. He also records all lectures and post notes online, which makes it easy to review. He focuses on graph algorithms and DP. I feel like I learned a lot in the class.

Honestly the Algorithms professor the department needs compared to its prior teachings. Great lecturer and emphasizes important topics for interview prep like graph theory, dynamic programming, and shortest paths. If he makes the midterm too hard, he'll likely make the final really easy like he did for us (median was 103% w extra credit).
Can you imagine the median of the final exam is out of 100%?

lectures were informative but a drag, did not do enough to explain how to approach more advanced problems, review sessions focused on early/easy content and not on the more advanced concepts, grade is mostly on exams (30% midterm, 30% final), quizzes were decently easy, hw were very hard and took several hours at office hours to complete

Kevin Sun is a great teacher for 455 and 550 and a very chill dude. The homeworks or exams can be difficult and thought-provoking, but ultimately his grading is extremely generous. Attend class and put in some effort and you will be fine.

A great professor teaching interesting material. The midterm was a little hard but extra credit opportunities more than made up for that. Homework and quizzes allowed collaboration and it seems like if you try in this class and attend lectures you'll get a good grade.
If you are not good at leetcode, could be a hard course for you.

Professor Sun is a great lecturer who excels at making complex algorithms feel intuitive. The material is hard, so you'll have to keep up, but his explanations make attending the lectures worthwhile. Side note: if you do a lot of LeetCode, you'll definitely do well in the class.

Like the last rating said, way too much emphasis on tests and a bit informal but funny and nice person. However, I am giving this rating purely based off teaching and not likeability which is why it is so low. He should engage more with the class in lectures as well so that people are given the opportunity to ask questions others may have too.

Syllabus puts heavy weight on tests but overall Kevin's lectures are enjoyable. I do wish he was a bit less informal at times and didn't go off on tangents quite so much but other than that have enjoyed his class on the Models of Language and Computation.

Great guy who genuinely loves the stuff he teaches, but he forgets that the rest of us haven't been doing this stuff as long as he has. Midterms were hard, but I think he'll improve once he teaches a few more semesters. Besides, it's an algorithms class, it's going to be hard. Seemed like he genuinely cared about our learning and our grades.

Great lecturer, all lectures recorded. However, the midterms were extremely difficult in the time given - the 2nd midterm's avg was in the 50s. Offered generous extra credit on the final that helped boost people's grade. We had a more normal distribution after. Kevin's class and his exams are helpful for technical interview prep - I learned a lot.

Kevins a good guy; this class was very hard and I think the midterms were a bit harder than necessary, causing a large portion of the class to fail them, however, this was rectified by the final exam having and extra 50% of extra credit points which allowed the majority of the class to improve their grades. Stressful class but hes a good instructor
very hard

The course material is confusing, I had to read through the textbook and his own website to understand the course content. What he teaches in class is hard to understand and not really applicable to tests and homework. He teaches foundational algorithms, and test us leetcode questions that does not 100% come from the algorithms.

Worst experience of my semester. It has caused me countless panic attacks and made me lose sleep and weekends all for Kevin to test unrelated material to his lectures on his exams. While Kevin seems to be very knowledgeable about algorithms, I think he fails to understand that this is our first time learning this subject.

The exams are not as hard as other comments, the overall material is challenging; however, the question in the midterm is at most the easiest question in Leetcode and it could be solved within a minute or two. Strongly recommended.

I really enjoyed learning new algorithms and their application. However, this class is not based on the content you study over weeks but rather the intuition that comes with years of practice. I think Kevin forgot how new the material was in his love for it. Half of your advanced CS students FAILING vital exams does not reflect well on you :( .

We have quizzes, 2 every other week, and we also have hw with 2-4 multipart questions. Nothing on the quizzes, in the lectures, or really even much of the hw was on the exam. Instead, bro literally just gave us leet code on the exam. The average on the midterm was a 50. I learned tracing well, but doesn't matter cause we all still failed the exam.
The lecturer is great, but it seems like he really enjoys making exams tough. No matter how much you prepare day and night, the questions in the exams are on a whole other level that's hard to reach.
Caring professor and amazing lectures, sufficient OH and extra practices, with patient and passionate TAs

goated prof. 6 quizzes, but up to 2 can be replaced by the final. Quizzes were short, and weren't too difficult. Final was also not surprising. Labs were a bit tedious, but weren't difficult (would take about 2 hours per lab, 6 labs total). TAs were good.
Lovely time.
My favorite class I've taken in the CS dept so far! frequent quizzes but generous drop policy and they aren't too hard if you are staying on top of the material. very fair imo

Too many quizzes and lab which was a sure fire way to make everyone feel burnt out. I did not enjoy this class. Fair warning. Avoid professor if possible. Lectures were disorganized and it was hard to study.
She's pretty cool and relatable. She also listens to her students and changed her methods based on student feedback.
KAKI IS THE GOAT!!!!!

She makes COMP 311 a breeze. Actually cares about her students and wants the best for them. Lectures are easy to follow, quiz heavy which makes it easy to stay consistent with studying, very accessible outside class. Genuinely loved her and the class. ENROLL WITH PROF RYAN SHE'S AWESOME TRUST ME.

Amazing prof. I thought I'd hate this class but her teaching style made it so engaging and interesting. Frequent quizzes make sure you stay up to date on material, and slides are clear and easy to study outside of class. Can't wait to take 435 with her, kaki is my goat
A bit timid but wonderful teaching. Makes some mistakes in lecture but catches them. Would 100% take again, you can tell she cares about her students and content. Highly recommend!
Really cares about her students and cares a lot to the subject. One of the best teachers I have had in the UNC CS department. She da Goat
Truly cares about her students and really wants them to succeed. I wish we as a class were a bit more quieter but she really is one of the best in the department. TAKE HER
Very nice person, class is not difficult at all, a lot of partial credit given on exams

Professor Ryan made COMP435 a wonderful and interesting experience. Topics ranged to give overviews of various security topics. Not difficult, quizzes were easy with light studying, labs were enjoyable!

Kaki was amazing. 311 is a tough class, but she made the class very easy imo. 6 quizzes worth 8% each (all very similar to the worksheets you're given for HW), 6 Worksheets worth 20%, 5 labs worth 20% (designing circuits), and 1 final exam worth 12%. She dropped lowest 2 quiz grades for your final too, and always gave extra points on her quizzes.
I love kaki
this course was great and kaki handled the incredibly disrespectful class w positivity and humor. idk how she did it i wouldve crashed out

i honestly was so scared of 311 before taking it but it was my favorite class this semester. i took 435 w/ her too, she structured them both similarly -- lots of quizzes, labs, practice problems (in class, worksheets for credit). 435 just had a project too, which was fun. and the TAs were amazing!!

Kaki is my angel. Her lectures are kind of boring, but the slides are clear and descriptive enough that I was able to get >90 on every quiz except quiz 6 without too much studying. Quiz 6 was the assembly quiz and we were a little rushed content-wise, but she had a generous curve. Final was the easiest final I've ever taken in a CS class
Shes very nice, but uploads stuff way too slow
Kaki was a great professor for a historically more challenging class. Assessments are frequent but fair and Kaki cares a great deal about her student success. Highly recommend for 311!

the course is like a sampler of different areas of security, so she covers a lot of ground but doesn't go super deep. smaller quizzes, a final project & final exam too. lots of labs + written assignments too but it felt reasonable. loved her as a professor

Her lectures can be a little boring which led to low class attendance, but overall she is a really great person. She responds quickly to emails and is understanding of extenuating circumstances. Had short quizzes throughout the semester instead of midterms which is super helpful. Lowest quiz gets dropped. Really tries to help you succeed.
Amazing professor that truly cares about the success of her students. I wish she taught my other classes fr.
she's such a sweetheart. expectations straightforward, grading super fair. she does frequent quizzes vs. big exams which really helped me stay on top of everything. highly recommend
what they said ↓
Kaki is the best thing to happen to this department.
I appreciate how this class is set up so much. Kaki really cares about students.

Kaki is very kind, but her lectures can be more confusing than self-studying. As a newer professor, her lectures are still developing. The quizzes are harder than her practice questions, though she offers a small curve. no midterm, 48% on 6 quizzes, 12% final, 20% hw,  20% coding hw, 2 quizzes can be replaced by the final grade
I am in kakis 311 and 435 classes this semester and loving both. The grading is fair and the lectures/practice clearly set us up for the quizzes. she is a real one

I am beyond excited that Kaki is faculty now. I had her when she was still a TA for COMP 110 and she's genuinely the best. Coding has always been difficult for me but she truly put in the time 1 on 1 to help me whenever I asked. Would definitely recommend her classes!!

I tried getting help during office hours, but all I got was a “go watch the lecture” response. The lectures are long, and the way they explain things doesn't match the exercises. There's zero follow-up from the professor if you're stuck.

Honestly, office hours feel like a waste. You wait in line, ask a coding question, and they tell you to watch the lecture again. The examples in that lecture don't even resemble the homework, and the professor doesn't seem interested in helping students who fall behind.
learned so much, but I wish I took this during a regular semester -- material moved FAST. Class was hard, but Kaki is great. She made the 8am semi-bearable

Kaki and Ajay both are superb instructors in their own ways. Quizzes are challenging but fair (2 each week so study consistently). Make sure to start programming exercises early. The Final exam replaces up to 4 of your lowest quiz grades. And the written report and presentation are straightforward.
Kaki is super sweet and caring! It was a decent amount of work but office hours saved me. Ajay (the TA) was awesome too!
A lot of work for a summer class but she makes it doable and is very reasonable + sweet.. Shoutout to the amazing TA Ajay!!

Overall, it's a very generous class. There was ample extra credit on assignments, which allowed most of the class to earn an A. The course was pretty straightforward until the final month, when LISP was introduced. I'd strongly recommend starting assignments early, especially to take advantage of the extra credit offered for early submissions!
I forbid you from taking this class.

This class is hard for all of the wrong reasons. Prof. Dewan's assignments are nightmarish to decode (some reaching 35 pages in length), and his slides/lectures are verbose with many typos. Way too many hoops have to be jumped through to setup assignments, request help, or participate in class. Everything just feels artificially difficult.

The professor's assignments are unclear and overly wordy, making instructions hard to follow. Many students struggle, not due to the material but because the writing is poor. English fluency is an issue, and it hurts the learning experience. Lectures are fine, but written work needs serious revision. Using Grammarly, AI, or a fluent TA would help.
i wish i could go back and never have taken this class
Prasun the goat

If I could give zero stars, I absolutely would. It's as if the professor went out of their way to create the most frustrating and pointless assignments imaginable. It's not just a pain in the ass – it's an outright assault on your sanity. Do yourself a favor and avoid this class at all costs.

Dewan's slides were an absolute nightmare to follow. They were so confusing, I felt like I was trying to decipher hieroglyphics while blindfolded. If I had to sit through another one of his presentations, I'd rather roll naked through a pit of boiling tar while being pelted with jagged rocks.

DO NOT TAKE THE CLASS IF YOU CAN AVOID IT!

The grading is lenient as you can get tons of extra credit. Professor Dewan's lecture is also pretty good. However, the assignment is a mess. A pain in the ass.

Professor Dewan wants nothing more than for you to learn as much as possible and learn the course material at a very deep level. He offers an abundance of extra credit on the programming assignments that can boost your grade. The midterm is straightforward is you attend class. Put forward an earnest effort, and you will almost certainly do well.

COMP550: Sridhar is a really great person who definitely cares about his students. However his lectures are pretty unorganized. Instead of slides, he projects his handwritten notes that are almost illegible. His exams are worded ambiguously and can be difficult, but his homeworks are perfect. Curve was generous and ensured no one got less than a C+

I'm not sure why the ratings are low. I found that he was a pretty good professor and was really kind. I think a lot of people rating low just didn't show up to classes regularly or office hours. Attendance isn't mandatory, but basically is if you want to do well, since it is a harder class. His handwriting can be difficult to understand at times.

Really cool dude, he's one of my favorite comp sci professors. I also thought he was a good teacher. It is tough material, probable should have went to office hours and would have probably done better.

Very knowledgeable, not mean, gives extensions, gives extra credit, but teaching was just not great. Difficult to follow handwriting and lectures. I don't think I really absorbed anything. Maybe the material is just extremely difficult, but the homework and exams felt impossible. You don't know your grade until the end, and it's too late by then.

If you wanna take any class with this guy, think thrice. That's the worst professor I've ever had—unclear grading, low-quality teaching, and tough exams. OMG what an awful journey it was. I lost 10 pounds and some hair on my head bc of the stress in this class. His lectures were useless; hw are extremely difficult; horrible exams. I can go on with the negatives bc i don't have any positives to say about him. He's funny? Yeah, creepy funny.

His grading is very unclear and unfair. I don't know where he was educated but his style of teaching doesn't fit into the standards of American College Education. ok yeah he sucks at teaching and the hw is hard but if u put in the time (as u should for a class at this level), u will do well and pass. the curves are HUGE, and he has dumb extra credit like making memes. he also really does try to be funny/engaging, just kinda fails at it. but srsly if ur complaining, just take some time to like...practice?try?

Homeworks were insanely difficult. Midterms were also very difficult (not as difficult as HW's but still absurdly more difficult than needed). Practice Exam answers were incomplete or hard to understand!

Sridhar is an amazing professor with clear grading who gives us more curve than we deserve. So curved that you could probably get a 70 and still finish with an A. Homeworks are very difficult, but relevant and helpful. His handwriting is truly scary, but otherwise lectures are fun and abstract. Taking 550 with him next semester, would recommend!

I've finally finished the course yesterday. This was a tough and awful journey. Hopefully no other CS professor would be that horrible in terms of exams, hw, grading, and relaying information during lectures. Didn't attend the class bc I thought his lectures were just useless. Class is not well-organized. We missed a few lectures bc of the weather and bc prof decided to cancel one of the lectures. He covers the material very quickly with his bad handwriting. just very bad. have no clue how

OK prof but his exams and hw are extremely tough so don't take 455 with him if u can. Midterms were very difficult and long. The assignments were challenging, requiring several hours to finish. Rather than focusing on basic understanding with simpler problems, all the homework questions were difficult. Very knowledgeable guy who's not the best at teaching. Bad handwriting and lectures are difficult to follow, but maybe because the material is just difficult. Homework and exams are very challenging and time consuming. He's not mean or anything and I'm sure he's trying his best. Overall, lots of room for improvement and would recommend another prof

Homework was graded strictly, likely due to TAs, while exams were more lenient. Prof. Duggirala was very helpful during office hours. Many complaints stem from students avoiding responsibility. Go to an Ivy and you'll see teaching isn't perfect there either—welcome to academia.
Didn't show to class bc duggi was p useless, but the class content is not hard and midterms/hw were generally chill. idk why we take this class

The worst CS professor out there. Thanks God I'm taking COMP 550 with Kevin Sun next semester, not with Duggirala. This guy might be a good researcher, but he's a horrible prof. Hope he will stop teaching bc I don't want other students to go through this hell.
Avoid at all cost. His slides, homework, and exam grading are horrible. The whole semester was just full of stress.

While he is clearly very knowledgeable about the topics, he is not a good professor. HW's take forever to complete and don't really help with understanding.

He's a nice person, but his teaching isn't effective, so think carefully before enrolling in COMP455 with him. Just a bad professor. Not tough, not strict, just bad. He's clearly a genius in his field, but teaching is not his strong suit. This class is so tough -- I can't imagine how it's possible to succeed in his class. Not many people show up to his lectures because his slides are useless, so you should do a lot of self-studying. It doesn't make sense how this guy was hired as an instructor, he's terrible at relaying information and teaching. Not only that but his handwriting sucks and he's hard to understand. Don't take 455 with him. He makes the class unnecessarily difficult. Other sections with different profs had easier time with this course. Duggirala's 455 is illegally hard. One of friends even attempted s…. while taking this class.

The other reviews are accurate: this is probably one of the harder CS professors out there.  But he gives so many opportunities and resources to learn the material, and OH are invaluable.  If you put your nose to the grindstone he you will certainly do good

Professor Duggirala's class is extremely proof-heavy and harder than other sections, but he makes up for it with curves and plenty of extra credit. Great professor and gave us so many materials to learn the class. 126 had so much content and so many things to memorize, but it was doable.
