My guess is that the TAs, not Professor Nijorn himself, create the midterm and quiz questions. This might explain why many students perform poorly on these assessments.

Exams and quizzes are made by Tarik and other TAs, but Tarik can't create effective midterm questions. Many students did poorly on the midterm, and having a quiz for each assignment feels excessive, especially given the poorly crafted questions. Avoid this class if possible; it's frustrating to pay tuition for a class that isn't properly taught.

Not an easier elective as it used to be. He made the class more difficult, and I don't think he really knows the stuff he's teaching well. Midterm was very difficult, and I can't imagine how difficult the final is going to be.

Nirjon was good, no complaints. His lectures could be boring but they basically give you a walkthrough for the assignments which build off the last.  Class is easy if you attend lecture and complete the "Class Works".  As stated below grading was a little frustrating as it took all of class period for the TA to get to you. Overall great class

programming assignments were fair and not very difficult, they are pretty much cumulative and so is the final project. Dry lectures, but nice fella. the grading system for the assignments was pretty frustrating b/c they need to be manually checked off but the prof or TA and you end up sitting around waiting. exam questions try to trip you up though

This is an easy class if you put in the work. And you will be learning more on your own than from the professor. But don't be mistaken, you will get a lot out of this. 

By the end I had a functional mobile application that I am very proud of.

Despite the deteriorating CS faculty at UNC, this class is one of the few that is truly amazing. It's the hardest class I've taken, but it genuinely teaches you. Saba is generous with grading, and there's a TA for every schedule. It gets much harder after the first midterm, so reconsider if you're very busy. Otherwise, this class is a masterpiece.
Amazing class and genuinely learned so much. Nicest professor ever. I love that guy!

This will probably be the hardest class you ever take (content-wise; passing isn't as hard). You may understand very little because the content is super theoretical and might not even exist. Saba lectures fast, so LOCK IN and go to every one! Homework's hard and graded harshly but exams are easier and curved by free points. Take 455,550,M381 first!

While the content was difficult, Saba and TAs are more than willing to explain throughly during office hours. The problem sets always require a bit of ingenuity, but the programming assignments are almost always very straightforward. The exams were challenging but the final grade cutoffs are rather generous. I really enjoyed his class.

Agreed with other reviews there was a great opportunity to learn through this course; however, grading was at times punitive or ambiguous. Rubrics were never posted before assignments or projects. Verbal explanations of grading often felt vague, and quizzes were quite difficult, with some questions ambiguous or asking for material not covered.

Amazing prof. Very difficult class, but tried his best to respond to any confusion you may have (during or after class). Good homework and clear grading scheme. Not a tough grader. Accessible after class, and many oh offered by him and TAs. Strongly recommend to anyone who's interested.

Probably the best professor I've had from the COMP department. Yes the content is difficult, but him and the TAs are always willing to help and the structure of the psets really do make you think and maybe even learn something. Taking COMP455 (or any abstract math classes) before this will make the class easier to digest for sure

Cryptography is a challenging and interesting class that Saba teaches well. The class is structured  predictably, the TAs are helpful (thanks David), and the programming assignments are very cool applications. The midterm was hard but his letter grade ranges were forgiving in return. Overall a great class and a very cool niche in CS.
Amazing lecturer! Hard concepts but he makes them interesting

Dr. Saba is very passionate about cryptography. He brings the same enthusiasm to teaching students. I took COMP537-Cryptography. A difficult course for sure, with lots of assignments, and very little to start from. He makes up for this through his and TA's office hours. He's very kind and understanding when it comes to both assignments and exams.

Saba is a great lecturer, and I found all the material accessible for someone with few privacy knowledge. He clearly shows that he is interested in providing a good class curriculum by asking for feedback and hearing back from students on implemented feedback. He encourages students to be more involved in the department as well. Great guy

One of the best additions to the UNC CS department, Saba is kind, caring, chill, and funny while being able to teach advanced cryptography and privacy-related courses with incredible effectiveness. He motivates students very well in pursuing the material and is super receptive to feedback. One of the best professors I've ever had!

Saba is a great professor with a true passion for the subject he teaches. I learned more in his cryptography class than I've ever learned in another class, but it was simultaneously the most difficult class I've ever taken.

Saba's classes have been my favorite ones at UNC but also probably the hardest. He is very accessible and wants people to do well! Has tons of office hours if you don't understand. The class policies are very collaborative and designed for people to learn the material well.
I had 0 formal coding experience and this class was tough.

Has an incredible industry background, and is always happy to talk about what he's done and how he got there. A great lecturer in all the material we covered, from applied linear algebra to concepts on virtual reality hardware. Homeworks are long, but feel really useful towards your own skills and what you'll need for the final project. Awesome guy

I took the honors class and it was a nightmare. His lectures were poorly executed, as he would often rush past important details; i had to teach myself everything. He also had a propensity to only call on the male students in the classroom. I often felt like he was talking down to many of the other female students and didn't take us as seriously.
Great person and professor. If you do assignments and go to class, you'll do well

This course is pretty easy if you have previous coding experience and it is structured very clearly. There are a few homework assignments and required labs, but the attendance is not mandatory and he posts all of the lecture slides on canvas. He also allows cheat sheets for exams, so you don't really have to study at all. Overall good prof!

Attendance matters for Lab but not for lecture! Professor Marks is a really cool professor. He has extensive experience with the tech field like Sony, Google, and others he might say. Easy class if you have coding experience, but even without it just make sure to ask a lot of questions to your TA's or on Piazza.

Rick as a professor is fine, he incorporates his experience into lectures and gives extra credit, but flies through concepts. The class itself is tough without coding experience- I had to rely on experienced classmates to help me, and comp110 helped some. The homeworks and tests can be long and challenging, but the final project is pretty enjoyable

Marks' lectures are AWESOME! Super engaging lectures. The course work was perfect for an intro course. As someone who has 0 coding experience it was a little more difficult, but if you have taken a coding class before it will be easy.
Overall, he's super mellow and chill. The difficulty level is very reasonable for an intro level class, and you grade is dependent on a lot of factors.

He was very nice and approachable inside and outside of class. There is a group project at the end of the semester that felt very rushed, but he seemed to grade pretty leniently because it is a first-year class. The midterm was straightforward if you study the slides

Rick's lectures were interesting and pretty easy to follow. I enjoyed the concepts in this class and learned a lot from it. Final project was good experience and he grades very leniently. The midterm also was very easy with basic straight forward questions. Overall, he is a really cool guy and makes the class fun and simple. Definitely recommend.
Overall kind of boring lecturer, but the class wasn't too difficult. I did find hard to get help from him outside of class though and ended up having to get help from other professors.
He was an ok professor, I just didn't enjoy the class very much and found him to be kinda boring.
he's a really nice guy who is clearly passionate about the subject and cares for his students
Insanely knowledgable and respected professor in the AR/VR space. Taking COMP 590 (VR & 3D Graphics) – although extremely challenging – was my favorite class at UNC.

The lectures were informative, and he was readily available for office hours. The 1st half of the class (3D Graphics) was more mathematical, requiring linear algebra. The 2nd half (VR) was more conceptual. The lectures fairly prepared me for the midterm, and the exam itself was fair. The final project's grading could have been more detailed.

Pretty good for a first-time professor! We had multiple quizzes, HWs, midterm, & a final project made in VR. The workload was manageable & fair overall. There was a lot of math involved in the 1st part of the class about graphics, but the topics got more conceptual after that. If you're interested in VR/graphics, he can provide a lot of expertise!

Interesting class and the prof was pretty funny sometimes. Very knowledgeable. Barely anyone ever showed up to class which is probably why the other reviews didn't get a good grade. If you go to class, you learn a lot. If you get a good group for HW and final project you can easily get an A. Generous grading and a good guy.

Waste of a semester. unengaging lectures. 4 grades TOTAL. hw required to be done in groups-easier to grade ig, yet grades werent returned until end of semester & was limited to single letter grades rather than question-by-question score breakdown (including midterm). too little feedback far too late. didnt learn much. better off reading a textbook

I have no clue what to say, I don't even know what is going on in this class. Avoid at ALL COSTS. He's too busy working his job at SAS to teach us. 

But... that's just my opinion.

This was probably the worst class i have taken at UNC. Throughout the semester, we had 2 hw assignments, one midterm, and one final project. The midterm was hard, worth 30%, fully written by chatgpt, and we didn't get our grade back until finals season. his grading criteria sucks and his lectures are disorganized and he uses someone else's slides.
Hes the GOAT. DA GOAT

He's clearly passionate about the content and does a great job answering questions after class. Great overview of various topics in AI and fair/lenient grading. Definitely go to lectures and make sure you get a good group for your HW and final project. Slides are usually the same as previous years.

The course is very insightful and you have the opportunity to learn a lot. Jorge doesnt do well in teaching the content, most of them are tangents on a slideshow, which is not engaging whatsoever. Theres also no practical experience, as the course believes in learning the theory behind ML. Grading and assignments were easy, online exams.

The 5pm lectures are kind of rough. He is actually a pretty good lecturer and clearly very knowledge. The course is adapted from the graduate version so if you just look at the slides you will be very confused, as he cuts out some of the out of scope math. THERE IS NO MORE EC, so likely harder than the older reviews suggest, but u learn a lot.

If you do the homework and understand the lectures, you're good. The exams are difficult (worth 90% of your grade) but he is an understanding person, and curves generously at the end. He drops your lowest midterm.

Lectures were unpassionate, filled with technical jargon, with little explanation. All homework was graded for participation, making it very hard to correct wrong strategies. Zero study resources were ever provided, and class averages on midterms were squarely in the 50-60 range. He obviously cares very little about teaching or any of his students.

Lectures are extremely boring. He is literally an automatic text-to-speech reader and does nothing except for reading his slides word for word. You are better off not going to class. Exams are not the most difficult, and there is a curve at the end.
Good lecturer, fair tests, I didn't have any real complaints.

Not very much homework, lecture attendance is not mandatory nor needed. His policy on makeups is extreme, without my UAA I would have been forced to drop due to missing the first midterm. Otherwise very nice and humorous guy.

Overall a pretty solid professor. The class was quite difficult and after the first midterm, the teaching felt slow and sometimes not as engaging as it used to be. However, the homework was insightful, the exams were perfectly fair and the curve was generous. Thiagu is very intelligent and there is a lot of valuable theory being taught.

He was a superb professor! Very intelligent it was an honor to learn from him. 

People complaining because you have to learn difficult material are Lazy Bums LOL!

Not much to say about him. Fairly dull lecturer but nonetheless taught the content well. Has detailed slides so you can just rely on those if you need to. Homeworks and midterms are doable as long as you study.

Worst professor I have ever had. Gave my group a failing grade on our paper because we asked for a one day extension (religious holiday). He holds grudges if you ask for an extension because he has to give them under certain circumstances (other groups who got an extension also failed in prev semesters). He makes up his own rules so you cant argue.

Good sense of humor, but lecture material was pretty dry. He did explain the concepts well though. Homework was fair and had questions that were relatively similar to exam questions. Exams were tough (especially the length), but our overall grades were curved. Lots of material to learn, practice, and remember, but very doable.

The Slides were ok. The lectures were boring and I felt like sleeping. The homeworks were ok, you would need to go through the slides and go to office hours early. The HW were doable. The midterm and final exams were very hard. One thing I wish I did: Reading the book and practicing from the book for being competent for exams.

Absolute favorite! Personality reminds me of Carl from Up; Class is hard, but he really makes you fall in love with learning (I am not a math fan or coding whiz). As long as you make a sincere effort, your grade will be fine. UNC CS needs more talented individuals who excel at CS and teaching instead of department politics.
You can just rely on the lecture slides for the material. Tests were more difficult than the homework but they weren't that bad. Solid lecturer and welcomes questions.

He's not bad, but nothing really stands out about him -- all he really does is read slides in his lectures, which can be pretty boring, but they do help you understand the material enough to do well on the homework assignments and exams. Grades do take a long time to get back, though, and I'm not really sure what my final grade is going to be.

He is very accessible outside of class and makes things digestible in class (so make sure to go). Directions for term paper were a little unclear. Fair grader on homeworks and tests (which were not difficult). Sometimes he would omit problems and leave them as extra credit (leaving most of the class with a 150% for one of the homework assignments).
don't take if you haven't taken a coding class before, you will be confused.

No required attendance and slideshows posted so you can teach content to yourself if you like. Cheatsheet allowed on the three quizzes and final is a group project that isn't too bad. Overall recommend, pretty easy especially if you have previous cs or stat knowledge.

I took data 110 with professor lee and the class overall was very easy, we were allowed a cheat sheet during exams and the final was a pretty fun project that could be added to your resume. Overall, was a great insightful class that was not too challenging.

She doesn't care about her students and is extremely rude. Ive seen other students come to her with personal matters and instead of being understanding she refuses to give extensions or any type of understanding for a 100 level class.  Her grading is also all over the place, lectures are boring, and her TA's are accusatory.

Harlin is a great person and very caring of her students. The class is not hard to do well in at all, but her lectures tend to be really boring and I found myself not able to pay attention. Her lecture slides are also not very clear and can be really confusing. I had to teach myself most of the course content, but it wasn't hard.

Harlin was a great professor to have in Data 110! She is easy to reach and very accommodating. Attendance is optional, but you have the opportunity for extra credit if you attend a certain number of lectures, and her slides are posted on Canvas. The material is easy to learn if you put in the effort for the quizzes.
Very kind, down-to-earth, and caring professor. The class was easy if you paid attention in lecture or had stats/coding experience. TAs and the professor were accessible outside of class.
Chiller. The difficulty doesn't represent the class though, it's not that easy if you aren't computer science or data science.

Extremely kind person, and was a blast to have as a professor. Would highly recommend this as an intro to anyone even dabbling in the idea of Data Science, she makes things very easy to understand. She's down to earth, and is actively working towards our sucess. We were allowed cheatsheets on both of our midterms. Highly recommend!

Professor Lee is an incredibly kind and caring professor. She knows the material well and clearly gets excited by it. The homework can be time-consuming sometimes but there's not many and they really help you understand the different concepts. The class is very statistics heavy, but the exams are pretty easy. Professor Lee is also very accessible.
Very kind professor! She is easy to reach outside of class, incredibly helpful, organized, and gives lots of extra credit opportunities.

Easy class if you have experience with stats and coding. Only challenging thing can be the coding HW, but they aren't bad if you pay attention to lectures - TAs and Lee are accessible for help. Really comfortable class and a great intro if you're considering Data Science.

extremely easy if you have any background in stats/data science. The 4 HWs, 11 recitation labs, midterm, and final project were all free 100s. this class taught less than one semester of AP stats I'm ngl. recitation is mandatory, lecture is not (and slides are on canvas). gave tons of extra credit. lee is very kind and a good lecturer.

Harlin is absolutely amazing. She is genuinely so caring, and for the first time this class is being offered, she did an absolutely amazing job. Graded by 4 HWs, Labs, Final Project, and One Midterm. Veryyyy easy if you pay attention and have experience in Data Science (ex. STOR 120, STOR 320, etc.)
goat. super chill, derives ideas bottom up. dense but well organized lectures
The exams for this course are difficult if you don't have a very strong math foundation. However, the assignments and teamwork are very helpful. You can learn a lot from them.
Do not take this class.

Prof. Oliva is fantastic. Amazingly intelligent, articulate, and he stands out as one of my favorite professors at Carolina. That being said, he teaches a difficult course—be prepared to work. There will not be much hand holding and lectures will focus on key theoretical concepts instead of implementation.

Junier Oliva is by far one the best professors I have ever had. The class itself (Machine Learning) was extremely difficult, requiring somewhere about 5-10 hours per lecture to supplement, understand, and digest the material, especially for some later lectures. However Oliva makes sure to teach the nuance and it makes for a very eye-opening course.

He covered a good number of introductory ML topics but I don't think I took away much from the course in terms of understanding. Inconsistent grading criteria and a large gap in knowledge expected between class and the final project and exam. Other than bits of theory and derivations, I almost feel like self-study would be more productive.

The professor is passionate about the subject but he doesn't realize it is under the CS department. The only coding component is Google Colab assignments you'll figure out on your own. Lectures and the midterm are entirely math-based with no programming instruction. Avoid if you want to learn practical Python skills for building and training models

Definitely not an undergrad level course. You need a good foundation in stats, cal, and linear algebra to take this course. Otherwise, I don't think you would understand much of what he is saying. So I rec you don't take this class if you don't have enough prerequisites. Otherwise, he is nice and passionate about ML.

What's the probability of this professor understanding that the students taking the class have other things to do? Probably another annoyingly long mathematical equation involving various interpretations that would be infinitely easier to understand if the professor actually taught the class instead of dumping random equations every lecture.

He's nice and enjoys his specialization but he's teaching this course to undergrads at a grad level. Lectures filled with formulas that nobody understands how to work with. Idk how to actually train a model, what a tensor is, or how to use tensorflow. Only take this if you wanna research. Don't take if you wanna be an ML engineer, Udemy is better.

One of those classes where you go to lecture and watch as 1 person understands everything, and the professor takes this to mean that everybody gets it. 

This is a MATH/STOR course, not a COMP course. Heavy on the symbols, low on connections to real life. Little programming. 

Strong assumption that you memorized all of LA, Probability, and Calc 3.

Homework and tests could be stressful for this course but the teacher is very approachable and responsive to students' questions and concerns. He seems to be very passionate about his field and is an excellent resource for anyone who really wants to learn

This is a GRAD level class not undergrad. He taught the exact same material as his COMP 755. Possibly the worst comp class I have had at UNC. In order to do well on exams/HW you have to already know ML/LinAlg well. He has no problem assigning an exam, project, presentation, and homework all the same week. He curves but not worth the stress at all
goat. don't listen to 560 reviews. knows and teaches material extremely well

Shashank is the most brilliant professor in the university. He is also one of the best instructors in the CS department. The course is very math-heavy, but he cares deeply about the students' learning, and has an extraordinary knack to explain complex math concepts and equations in English.

There are homework and quizzes almost every week, and the classes are pure math calculations, and the homework after class is all code. 
But I understand some of the knowledge of deep learning by learning to derive these formulas. These are somewhat useful for my job search because I will be asked these questions in written tests and interviews.

At the beginning of class he said that lectures wouldnt be recorded, and there would be no practice midterm. But students kept on asking him for it, and he finally started recording classes and gave a practice midterm which was not useful at all in preparation for the exam. Overall, a pretty difficult course.

There was only 1 TA with 1 hour office hours a week. The professor had an appointment based 1 hour weekly office hour. There was Piazza for unlimited questions. If you are taking more than 12 credit hours and taking this course, I would advise not to. Make sure that you have a good foundation in Probability before taking this course.

I think because this is a 500 level and artificial intelligence course, and hence the professor made the course challenging. I think its not the professors fault, but I think that the department makes these rules. I think the course should have been made easier since it was the professors first time teaching this course.

This is a hard course, labeled as "Higher Level Course". 30% got A/A-, 55% got B+/B/B-, 15% got remaining. He teaches theory in class and did not type/write even one line of programming in class. In the assignments you had to do programming. The midterm was hard, he used chatGPT to make the midterm question.
AI is a buzzword. If for some reason you are not able to get in this course, because too many students want to take it. Do UC Berkeley's CS188, which is freely available online.

Very heavy curve which is a bit stressful since you don't really know what you'll get until the end.

Course content wise, I thought it was good overall. There were 3 units (search, probability/bayesian stuff, and ML). I thought search and ML were nice, but the bayesian/probability unit wasn't the best.

pretty good class for first offering, lectures could get difficult to follow at times. professor is clearly smart and knowledgeable. hard assignments and exam but grade was curved and nobody failed. learned a lot

A very nice guy who wants you to learn but grading was much more difficult than it needed to be. Only one midterm that accounted for 40% of the grade and that was unreasonably difficult and lengthy. Class was meant to be curved but it barely helped the grade in the end. The final project/homework were not given enough weightage to make any impact.

Shashank was clearly new to teaching, and there were times when he wasn't the greatest teacher, but he cared about students and learning and was pretty funny and generous with grading. He improved as the semester passed and would probably be a good choice for this class in the future. Overall a solid person and teacher.

Shashank is the smartest man in the computer science department. His lectures were amazing and you will learn a ton. One of the best classes I took. There is only one midterm, so study hard. The homework can get tricky. There was a curve at the end, however you still need to do well.

This is a review for COMP 581 - Intro to Robotics
Great class with hands-on group projects where you build your lego robot and program it to complete tasks. The material covered in the lectures and exams is relevant to help you build your robot.

My only complaint is that sometimes the lectures move slowly covering basic introductions for too long.

Why are there negative reviews? Because there were no quizes or exams, and no one studied regularly. When professor asked students questions, no one answered because they did not study. Because of this, Professor would never offer a course again where there is no quiz or exams. And its the students fault.
Definitely one of the few professors who really care about students.
A hidden gem in the CS department!

One major project over the course of an entire semester was a bit underwhelming.  We wasted a lot of time doing nothing really besides talking and spinning our wheels. The class was easy, so it gets some points from me on that side, but the course wasn't good.  I had harder classes as a freshmen.  Dan is a nice guy though. All around average.
Awesome professor. Learned a lot about research from this course. Doing the research project was fun.

Human Robot Interaction course. A research based course. Awesome Professor, good as a Kris Jordan. No midterms, quizes or exams. Projects, discussions, papers and presentations. If you are interested in an intro to research course and research related to Robotics, this course is for you.

This review is actually for COMP 581 which was not listed. Professor Szafir was an excellent intro to robotics professor. The most challenging part about the course was the robotics assignments in which you have to design your own controller for a robot. However, pay attention in class and you will be fine as he gives EC and allows retakes.

Mike Reed is an amazing professor. Lectures were so good and genuinely taught me so much about graphics, different ways in mathematics to do the same thing, and how to write very performative code. Take this class if you wanna learn from one of the best in this field and have it lectured to you in a very clear and intuitive way. I love that guy!

I dont think people realize that Reed is a graphics legend. We are talking about the same dude that made skia (and sold it to Google). You won't learn cool 3D techniques (hence the course name) but for people interested in graphics it builds a solid grasp of techniques used in the field. Taking this class is not even negotiable if you like graphics
This guy would teach you how to do your finals.

Reed is a great lecturer and professor. His passion for graphics and teaching couldn't be more clear. His lectures are easy to follow and informative. Assignments are difficult, so start early and follow along. Very clear grading scheme, most of final grade is from 6 projects. You will learn a ton about programming skills, graphics, and c++.
Mike clocks in as the greatest graphics professor I've ever had.

I quite enjoyed this class. Honestly, I don't care about graphics that much; I mostly enjoyed the performance/software engineering aspects. Mike was very good at explaining things, though it was a hard class. All labs. Final (10% of grade) was basically a lab you had to do quick.

Mike is a great instructor; he goes over the implementations for the 6 labs in lecture. Grade is composed of 6 labs, each worth 15% and they build off eachother so its important you keep up with them. Final is basically like another lab where you implement 2/4 methods. Class is tough but fun, felt like I learned alot.

Best and clearest lecture slides in the COMP department. Labs were only hard because the sensors were not reliable but tests were pretty easy. Content is very interesting and I learned a lot. Would definitely recommend taking this class. But remember, there is a lot of unpredictability and a lot of uncertainty in robotics...

There wasn't too much homework, but there is a group project where you build a robot and design it for the given lab days. The labs get progressively harder and make up the bulk of the class grade, and took my group anywhere from 5 - 10 hours a week outside of class to prepare. The assignments/exams were fairly challenging (mostly trigonometry).

I took COMP 89 with professor Alterovitz. SUPER easy class. 3 assignments and 2 projects for the entire semester, no homework. Class can be boring sometimes but Professor Alterovitz is super passionate about what he researches and studies. He does not take attendance. I highly recommend taking this class for a FC and easy freshman launch.

He's very passionate about tech., only talked about robots, AI, & internet instead of many topics. Grade based on a few assignments and 2 presentations (7 & 15 minutes). Attendance policy is unclear but as far as I know, he did not record attendance (syllabus said he would take it 3 random days). Lectures are somewhat boring but the class is easy

Dr. Arguello is patient and cares about his students! The material could be confusing, but he explained assignments clearly in class. You can even replace a bad take-home midterm with a take-home final. He's passionate and lets you choose your own project topics and groups, making it more enjoyable.

Nice guy and interesting content but does not seem qualified to teach this course. Seemed like he was relearning the material as he looked at the slides. Still remember when a student asked to demonstrate smoothing and he acted like it was tall task when all he had to do was some basic addition (that was literally already in his slides). Easy A

Best professor in INLS. Professor Arguello is very kind and really wants his students to understand the material. Class isn't necessarily mandatory, but would be helpful for exams. 3 Assignments, and Take Home Exams. As long as you put in the effort to understand the material you should be good!

Best professor ever. So kind, humorous, really wants his students to understand the material. I would suggest going to class because the slides are great, but sometimes the homework is hard to do solely based off of the slides. Only grades are 3 homework assignments, a takehome midterm and final, and a group research paper. Grades very easily.

This Professor was amazing at teaching and really cares about his students, but the class should be marketed as a math class than comp because of how demanding it is for linear algebra and some differential equations. Also, his TAs were amazing and was helpful even outside of their office hours.

Although the professor is a fantastic teacher, if you are not a math major or at least highly interested in matrix algebra and controller design the class is challenging. You are expected to memorize the formulas for exams which isn't undoable but notable. The toughest part is there is no partial credit on exams so you essentially get it or don't.

She's an amazing lecturer. Yes, she might come off as rude but she is genuinely not trying to be based on my long conversations with her. She helped me a lot with understanding NLP concepts. She's definitely a gem of the CS department given her experience and the fact that she takes her job seriously.
Made the course a lot difficult. No lecture recordings, no practice for exams, homeworks are difficult. I would avoid taking a course with her.
The content of the course is good. The Professor was rude.
A good lecturer, but not a good person. Half of the class could not get their projects right, and fundamental mistakes were caught. It proves how much less support she gave the class. Dont take.

She can clearly explain concepts fairly well. She is incredibly unresponsive, though. She mostly uses Piazza for group discussions, however we don't get an answer for days or sometimes even weeks. There are some challenging concepts in the subject, therefore having a supporting lecturer would be more beneficial.
Dont take unless you are ready to go through some brutal crazy hard stuff.

Dr. Gotz is nice, accessible, but I wouldn't recommend this course. As a statistics major, I found the content too basic. While JavaScript is used for projects, his teaching is extremely minimal, and you're expected to learn it mostly on your own. If you're seeking a more in-depth or challenging experience, this course may not be the best choice.
Amazing! Lectures were asynchronous and easy to follow. Seven coding assignments, an ungraded midterm (participation grade as long as you do it), and a final. Very accessible outside of class.

Tough course and rewarding. Roni explains things well if you have sufficient background in computer vision. If you keep reading and follow the course you will learn a lot. Overall the project is not too much. The grading is rather generous.

Really challenging but rewarding class. The lectures are pretty math heavy, but Roni makes them interesting and is willing to review concepts. Her grading scale is also very generous. Would recommend if you're even slightly interested in computer vision.
Speaking style can be a bit hard to follow at times. Difficult midterms. Not an easy 590 but if you put in the work you have the opportunity to learn a lot.

This was a rough class, but I can't see it being taught any other way, since computer vision is a complicated field. Might have preferred another lab doing something with OpenCV over the mathy hw. This is an extremely mathy class btw, don't take it if you aren't a linear algebra god.

If you are looking at the RMP that means you are thinking about taking a class with her. Do not delay register for it ASAP; super fun. Its clear that she knows a TON about the subject while at the same time not trying to kill you with content.

I'm taking COMP 590 for both times, 1 information visualization and 1 design. Both classes are really good and relatively easy. 80+ students enrolled in the 24'fall class so you can imagine how popular Prof. Szafir is. Great professor and great class!

Her 590 was interesting & had a very manageable workload! The TA, Matt, graded our projects very kindly :), & outside of 3 projects & a final project, the only other grade was participation. Explored different methods of visualizations, including using D3 & making physical representations. Sometimes the topics felt a little too abstract though.

Szafir is an excellent professor and amazing lecturer! The content of the course is very interesting, assignments are light and engaging, and there are many opportunities for extra credit. We got introduced to D3 as well, which is super useful. I would definitely want to take another class with her again.

Professor Wu was fantastic, engaging, & informative. I learned a lot, and would absolutely take another course with him. There were only about 3 assignments total, and the semester focused on building final projects, making the end manageable. He cares deeply about his students and creates a collaborative environment. Highly recommend INLS 382!

I learned a lot and really want to take time the amount of effort Professor Wu took to make sure his students learned the topics in the most meaningful way. Always went above and beyond and really a gem of the INLS department!

Danny is such a caring professor. The course is graded based on three short homework assignments and a multiple-choice final, for which he provides the correct answers beforehand so students can study.

Chill class. How much you learn highly correlates with how much you put in. Class projects can be hard for people without computer security background. But the most important pre-requisites are OS and Comp architecture. Prepare to learn before enrolling. The professor is knowledgeable and approachable.

This was his side channels class. Was reading papers with 2 labs that weren't too hard; better to start labs in advance though, so you don't get stuck. Really enjoyed this class and felt like I got a lot out of it. This is Andrew's hyperspecific research area and so he can talk in great depth about the papers and also what the paper don't tell you.

The material is difficult, but Dr. Anderson does an amazing job of explaining it in a digestible manner. He may not say it, but he truly cares about  each student and structures the course in a way that is intended to foster passion, challenge you, and enhance learning. Work hard, ask questions, and study with others and you'll learn a lot! :)

He's a researcher not a teacher. Whole class was confusing but he's some kind of genius. He doesn't lecture, he assigns someone new to lecture every class day. Great class for feeling out how much you like AI /multimodal. Everyone from undergrad to PHD students are in this class. His feedback ranges from dissertation to “ok”

Professor Byrnes was awesome! I had never coded before, but she made it so accessible and clear. Her lectures left little room for confusion, and the quizzes were never too difficult. There was extra credit on all exercises if submitted early, and the grade distribution makes it easy to get an A if the effort is put in.

Dr. Byrnes is a respectful professor with a fair grading structure: 50% assignments and 50% exams. The final replaces your lowest quiz grade, so attend all exams. Grades are not updated on Canvas and slides lack annotations. The content is computer science focused. Recommended for those interested in the subject, but avoid the 8am section.

Very chill professor and made an otherwise very hard class doable. The quizzes are heavily influenced by the homework, so study those. The TA Randal also carried my grade with his great review sessions.

Absolutely wonderful professor but everything going on is kinda mass up. I personally find difficulty to follow every homework instructions. And the use of vs code is kinda no clear some time. It is impossible to proficiently use the software through simple textual explanations.  And this class require much more time to study than I imagine.
Overall, a good professor, sometimes the exercises were a little extensive, especially the last one, other than that, the course is fine
Everyone knows she's the best! COMP 455 is known to be hard, but she explained the concepts in a way that they stick with you forever.
Comp 455 can be conceptually tough, but the way Alyssa taught it made it really easy to understand. The slides and lesson were perfectly clear. Tests were very fair too.

Pass/failed. Didn't post recordings, which for material that has meticulous steps and reasons for them makes it incredibly hard to review a concept more than just seeing the end result. Tests made up 90% of the grade, and were taken entirely from homework questions. Rewarded cramming over really understanding the material imo. Still a nice person.

Dr. Lytle is super nice and a great professor! I've never taken a comp sci class before, but she made it really easy to understand and is gracious with quiz grading. Office hours are super helpful if you're ever stuck, and the class is mostly smaller assignments that you can redo until you get 100%.

As someone who had no background of computer science, I was scared to take this class but it ended up being one of my favorites this semester! Go to lectures, submit homework early (you get extra credit), and take advantage of office hours! The quizzes are super similar to the practice questions provided on the class site. Would recommend!

No required attendance and slideshows posted so you can get by without going to class. Quizzes and final fairly straight forward and many question were taken from the practice questions she posted, which were often actually harder than the exam itself. Overall, she is very nice and would recommend taking the calls with her.

Maybe she's only really good at teaching 110, because the 455 lectures were overall the most confusing lectures I've ever attended. She didn't know what she was talking about and neither did we. At least the quiz questions were all off the homeworks, but like just know in advance that 90% of your grade will be exams.

Not sure how the high ratings happened. Lectures were often confused, turnout dropped fast, and many who stayed left frustrated. I left the course disappointed in the quality of instruction. Would recommend another professor if you want solid understanding.

Easy class and she's super generous with grading, you get bonus points for submitting things early and your lowest quiz gets replaced with your grade on the final if it's higher. Quizzes are also super simple and similar, if not easir, than hw/practice.

i was terrified of comp bc i've never coded in my life, but comp110 with dr. byrnes was super helpful with the basics of python. we do a lot of in-class practice/walkthroughs and the TAs are also really helpful. the quizzes are straight from the homework and the memory diagrams get easier with practice! 110 is nothing to be worried about.

This was my first time coding, and Dr. Byrnes was amazing! She explained things clearly and was very nice. It was fairly easy to pick up the material. EC is given if you turn in exercises early. Quiz practice questions are harder than the quiz questions. Practice memory diagrams, go to office hours, go to quiz review sessions, and you will be set!

Definitely the best professor to take COMP 110 with. As someone who had never touched a line of code before in my life, lectures were extremely interesting and the content never felt like too much. Assignments were dispersed throughout the semester and never felt like too much. Just practice memory diagrams before each exam and you'll do great.

Alyssa is great, and so are the COMP110 TAs. Coming from someone with ZERO prior coding experience, I won't lie, this class is NOT easy. Seek help from the TAs early and often!!! Content isn't super hard, it's just a plain grind. Lock in, DON'T USE AI, ask for help, and you'll succeed. Good class to meet bio major supplemental math credit.

I am really bad at COMP110 and would not recommend taking it if you can avoid it, but it is required for many majors so if you're gonna take it, Byrnes is a great professor. She knows her stuff and is very kind. Class is hard but that's lowkey just me, if you lock in from the beginning (AVOID RELYING ON AI) it will be fine.
Professor Byrnes is the best! She is a great professor, especially for a class like COMP 455. Extra credit is given for solving homework and quizzes are very manageable with study.

Dr. Balan is an incredible professor who's clearly very passionate about data science. I loved listening to her lectures even though I was taking the class as a pre-req for a totally different major. Very low pressure, simple exams/assignments, and a really fun group project at the end of the semester! Overall a great professor and a great class.

She's a lovely professor and the most caring person I have ever seen. The grading is really clear, with 2 quizzes (40%) and a group final project (25%), with almost 10 extra credits at the end of the semester. Definitely taking more classes with her!!

Prof. Balan is an extremely kind woman and teaches a great data110 class. She formats it so you can learn a ton about coding if you want to, but doesn't make your grade dependent on being really good at data science. She lets you use notecards for the 2 exams. Final group project. Definitely take this class if you need a stats credit.

Balan is very fair and she makes class super welcoming for beginners to Python and Stats. Attendance is mandatory but counted only on days where there's classwork, so many skip if they know the material. Two exams which are super easy and similar to study guides. Lab session about once every 2 weeks where you work on a very simple group project.

Professor Balan was awesome. There are 2 quizzes and a final group video project. A couple things do get a little technical with some code and using the correct formulas, but if you study, you will be fine. Attendance is optional but she brought several guest speakers who were interesting to hear, so I'd suggest going. Very good experience.
Very nice and wants everyone to succeed.

Super chill and knowledgable professor. Final project was fun and just enough of a challenge. Gemini makes all labs and homework a cakewalk. Quizzes are clearly laid out beforehand with ample review material. Incredibly easy class and material is taught if you actually want to learn it. Take if you need a stats credit but don't want to learn stats.
Prof. Balan is very nice and sweet, definitely take her course!!!

Dr. Balan is good at making things make sense, especially if you have no expereince in computer/data science. Her class is very easy but it is just her lecturing, labs on friday are when you  get to actually interact with class material and the people in your class. Final is a group project, but watch out for quiz 2 it is harder than quiz 1.

Dr. Balan is very kind and a great professor. She makes all assignments very easy and clear. Had some guest lectures in the course which was very interesting too! As I already took other data/comp courses, it was a bit boring at times, but otherwise good content! I would definitely love to take more courses with her in the future! 5/5!

This class is definitely super helpful for topics that translate to the real world and Kris is a great lecturer. There are a LOT of readings though, and the projects take a long time to complete, so expect a lot of work outside of class.

Although not mandatory, attending lecture is definitely better than watching the recordings. Kris utilizes lecture time to do lots of practice. Tests are similar to practice exams. Lots of office hours. Overall great intro course, though exercises can be a little difficult (as expected).

Kris has set up a good network of TAs to help you succeed in this class. Lectures are useful, and you'll definitely learn a lot more from going than learning it yourself. Assignments are fairly straightforward, but can get frustrating as things get more complicated. No midterms, only quizzes and a final, with the lowest quiz grade being replaced.

Kris is seriously the best professor at UNC. He cares so much about his students and is very passionate about teaching. He has plenty of experience, so he knows what topics translate to post-grad. This class helped me land a summer internship and has been so useful for it. Take this class if you can!

I took COMP 110 in Fall 2024 with Prof. Byrnes. Prof. Jordan subbed in for her halfway through and did such a good job of it. He was super understanding and was an excellent teacher. His lectures just made sense even though I had never coded before COMP 110 (I credit Byrnes too though - take it with her if you can). I highly recommend!

Not a difficult class by any means, but Kris teaches you a lot about industry standards and tools that you will actually use in your future careers. Quite a bit of readings for homework, a couple of quizzes, some small coding tasks and a sizable final group project. Very enjoyable class overall, but do make sure to find a good group!

Kris is honestly one of if not the best professors at the UNC CS department. He teaches concepts that genuinely apply in the industry and it is very clear that there is an astounding amount of effort that goes into making this class practical and efficient for students to succeed. His lectures are incredibly insightful and you learn a ton.

Great class learned a lot. Grading was kinda annoying. Where told we would have bi-weekly quizzes ended up only having 3 that a lot of people did bad on. Sprints where fun and engaging. Your group for this class matters A LOT, it will make or break ur grade/sanity. I ended up getting screwed over by a lazy group. Also Kris doesnt respond to emails.

Kris Jordan is the greatest professor that ever existed of all time. There is no professor ever greater than Kris. Anyone who disagrees that Kris is not the greatest professor of all time gets a 100% tariff. Big league

Kris Jordan is a heavily invested professor in the UNC's computer science community and it shows in how in-depth his lectures are. The amount of content that we go through in one 3.0 credit class is a lot, but it's definitely doable. Keep up with the readings and content and you'll be fine

Loved this class! Class is fast paced but I learned so much in just one semester. One most useful practical classes in the department. Group work makes up a large part of the grade, so get good group members. Final project was involved but fun. Attendance is mandatory but a lot of days are reserved for work time. Great TAs as well. Must take!

Had Jordan after filling in for Alyssa when she went on maternity leave. His course content was notably harder than hers. Didn't even return last quiz until day BEFORE THE FINAL. which is crazy. didn't even know what to study for next quiz because wouldn't return it in a timely fashion. Exercises not graded til right before the final.

Kris is great, and 590/423 is chugging along fine. Attendance is key, particularly in the last 1/3 of the semester (a big group project). Not hard to make an A as long as you show up to class, do the readings & exercises, and study a little for the quizzes. You'll learn a lot, too! This is by far the most practical COMP class I've taken.

Had Kris in the section where he took over for Alyssa. The end of semester email explained some of the disconnect between the two, and grade adjustments were made to address it. The only issue I had was grading time. 2 days before the final, we had 5 assignments and a quiz yet to be graded. I thought he was a good lecturer, but I preferred Alyssa.

Kris took over from Alyssa and class changed for the worse. Lectures became confusing, disorganized, rushed, and we didn't finish content. He also got rid of so many opportunities for practice problems, which are needed. Quizzes also went from 2-3 pages to 6 pages and were way harder. He didn't respond to my many emails about ARS accommodations.

Quizzes got significantly harder after he took over, and it was hard adjusting. We wouldn't get past quiz grades back before the next quiz. He would occasionally assume we knew a comp sci concept when we didn't, and his lecturing could be unclear (though he was always open to answering questions). He dressed like Bob Ross for LDOC which was funny.

I think Kris did a good job at covering the last few weeks of COMP110 and although his lectures were a little more difficult than Alyssa's, he clearly cares about his students and seems like a nice guy. He dressed up as Bob Ross for LDOC which was really funny, he definitely seems like he has fun with what he does.

The class was disorganized (see: negative reviews), but I believe this was due to the abrupt switch between professors rather than Prof Jordan himself. He's an engaging lecturer, and he altered the grading policy to account for issues with the course. I wouldn't be dissuaded by the negative reviews.
Kris was a great teacher; he came in at a tough time halfway through the semester and did a great job. Overall 110 was a good class.

We had a prof change in the middle of the sem from Alyssa to Kris, so the class was a bit disorganized as the style of teaching changed. The adjustment for the switch was kind of hard. The turnaround for the quizzes was way too long, making it harder to prep, but Kris was a pretty good prof, explaining content in a broader context.

Professor Hinks is amazing. I came into Comp110 with 0 coding experience and ended the class with a 98. I went to class about 60% of the time, but honestly didn't really pay attention. She gives practice a couple days before that's basically exactly what's on the quizzes. I only studied the night before and always got 90+. EX credit on all big HW.

Pretty good choice for comp 110. Some questions on the quizzes seemed to be tricky and intentionally made to be more difficult than necessary but the material is just basic python so how hard can it be. Learned all the material in like 3 days for a different class. Class average grade was a A-.

A lot of people were not on top of the class this past semester. The end of year was bad with a huge final exercise and a late release of quiz grades but she was overall a very nice and caring teacher. I hardly went to class and still managed to get an A-. If you're on top of your stuff and pay attention, there is no reason you won't get an A.

Dr. Hinks is a really nice person, and honestly a very good lecturer. I didn't do super well in the class, but it was really my own fault for not paying more attention in class. Quizzes should be called exams, they are worth 10% of your grade each (40% total). Homework can be time-consuming but generally easy to get a 100 on.

Quizzes are often considered easy, but I struggled with no prior CS experience. The instructor is kind, but I did not feel prepared for exams. Help from TAs can be slow and feedback takes a long time. I liked the teaching, but the exams were hard and I'm worried about my grade. I would not recommend if you care about your grade.
She explains things well but quiz grades took so long to get back

The final is in 2 days, and we haven't gotten our grades back to review our most recent Quiz, Quiz 03. We also had a final Exercise assignment that my partner and I spent 7 hours on, only to find out AFTER finishing it that she decided to send a nice email saying one Exercise would be dropped, giving benefit only to people who procrastinated on it.
the quizzes were extremely difficult for me and her lectures were not helpful and too fast paced. if you have no experience in coding avoid her and this class at all costs

Took for my last math requirement, doable but annoying.  Lectures were extremely boring and not helpful but attendance wasn't taken so I suppose you don't have to go.  ~4 quizzes (10% each), final (~15%) and lowest quiz dropped if final exam grade is higher then final is 25% of grade.  EC given if you turn in homework early.
Extremely good professor! A must-take for comp110

The lectures are very informative and she explains things very well especially if you are new to the topic. At first I did very poorly on the quizzes but after I went to tutoring with the TAs I did way better on the quizzes. I recommend going to tutoring right when you see yourself struggling and recommend it a bit more the office hours.

She is a wonderful professor and explains things very clearly. This class is hard so once you start to see yourself struggling on quizzes take advantage of the tutoring (this is what I did and it truly helped me). At first, I got 60s on the quizzes and after going to the tutoring with the TAs my scores went up to 80s/90s!
Nice and caring professor. I got a 40s in one of the quizzes and still managed to get a B+. However, slides and homework weren't really helpful.
really great person and a pretty great lecturer. highly recommend.

Dr. Hinks is so nice and breaks information down really nicely so that students can actually understand the reasoning behind the code. She doesn't rush through lectures and is generous with grading. All quizzes and the final have roughly the same difficulty level.
Very great professor. Class can feel repetitive at times but she tries to keep everyone engaged.

Very clear lecturer; the content takes into account that not everyone has prior programming experience. Values student feedback. The course is already pretty generously structured, and she still gave additional grace with quiz and participation grades at the end.

Great teacher for Comp 110. If you don't have any coding experience I can see how this class could be a little challenging, but she teaches really well and is extremely sweet and kind during lectures. She records and posts lectures as well as review sessions, and there are ample opportunities to get your grade up. If u try, u can get an A.

Dr. Hinks is very nice and the class is super easy! Lectures are honestly pretty boring and you can skip them if you already have coding experience. Quizzes are easy, just make sure you know memory diagrams and do the study guide. Exercises can be tedious but are helpful in making sure you know how to code.

Big lecture hall class, but very manageable. She goes through all the slides with explanations. Study guides are very accurate for quizzes and the final. Lecture notes are online to relearn topics. Grading also has generous partial credit. Knowing how to code beforehand helps a lot(less studying), but not required. Memory diagrams are hard.

cece is great! the class isn't easy (make sure you lock in for the quizzes) but her lectures were great and she obviously cares about teaching. super helpful and the TAs are too if you need to go to office hours. take her for 211!!

Professor McMahon was the most effective instructor I've ever had. Her teaching style emphasizes hands-on practice rather than simply reading from slides. While some topics took longer than others, this reflected her commitment to making sure everyone understood the material before moving on. The exams and homework were also very manageable!

A great professor, just beware checkoffs and be sure to ask for help if you don't understand the lectures - if you can't understand the lectures you'll be lost when it comes to quizzes and the final. Checkoffs were the most nerve-wracking thing in the world - but easy once they were over with. Latter half of the class was just memory diagrams.
One of the best profs in the CS department! If u go to class and understand the lectures, you'll be fine.

One of the best professors I've had in CS. The majority of the material was new for me since it was hardware oriented, but she did a great job explaining it. I learned a lot and would love to take more classes with her! I will say her labs were unnecessary tedious and way more difficult than class material though and quizzes were poorly spaced.

Only caveat is that lectures are very boring an convoluted. Having to code in person was stressful especially if you had a rude / snarky TA (took it couple semesters ago). Class itself was easy but every exam had grading errors, sometimes up to 10 points.

Super fair class. Honestly pretty good IF you go to class, do the assignments by yourself, and go to office hours if you need it. Not a terrible class at all, put a bit of effort in and you'll end up okay. Only thing is she's a super fast speaker but since we have the slides to look at after it's not a big deal in the end. Very hands on class

5 stars because all the honest reviews that are either mid or low stars conveniently get deleted. Take it with someone else at NCSU and transfer the credit in if possible. You'll thank me later. Really a kind and inspiring person though.
Cece is awesome! Very dedicated to her students and does everything she can to help you learn!
Super sweet professor who seems to genuinely care about her students. The class isn't overly easy, but she is very reasonable. I enjoyed her class.

Cece is one of the sweetest professors at UNC. She truly cares about her students. 211 with her is a breeze as long as you go to lectures and put some effort into the out-of-class assignments and studying. Exams are straightforward and very similar to practice exams and slides. Just don't zone out during the lectures and you'll do fine.

Cece was AMAZING! I very much enjoyed going to class, she was genuinely so sweet. Her lectures were engaging, she provided helpful practice for the exams, and the exams were very fair. 40% of the grade is basically an automatic 100 (made up of labs, participation, etc.). Best prof for 211!!

Hot take: overrated. When she does pollevs, she turns off the projector, so you need to go dig up lecture slides on the (often disorganized) canvas page. This and the constant "canigetathumbsupthumbsdown"s annoyed me significantly. Much of the content on midterms is not covered in the review materials. However, she is friendly and fine at teaching.

Cece was an amazing lecturer making the massive classroom feel almost like a small office hours. While this was her first time teaching the course it was only apparent when she asked for feedback on things she was trying out. The tests where difficult and covered a lot of different content however I never felt like I could not catch up to the class

Good professor who cares about her students. Class was easy, beyond systems, she also covered git and command line, which are useful in general. Go to lectures and do some review, and exams should be pretty easy. Not all assignments are coding based. Good TAs too but they take some time to grade.

This was an great course that taught a lot about tools for computer science and basics of systems programming. Tests are similar to practice material and the course is paced quite well. There are plenty of resources to succeed like check-offs, extra-credit, and helpful TAs.
Loved taking 311 with her. Very engaging for any class let alone CS which is notoriously boring at times. She was a great hire by the COMP department.

Great professor. Taught 311 last semester and is now teaching 211 and I'm sure she'll do a great job. Informative and interactive lectures with participation mandatory (with a few skips). Highly reccomend.
as someone who took this in spring of 2024 and thought the general consensus of this class and cc was that she and the class is dope what happened last semester lol

This class was designed for students with iPads. Steps for examples were not shown on the slides because she draws it by hand on a tablet. Solution slides also do not have the steps for examples, just the answers. If anyone tried to ask her to wait to write down all the steps she would keep going. Hw and labs were difficult without steps on slides.

The lectures were sometimes disorganized and prone to tangents, but his assigned readings helped compensate for these gaps. His exams penalized incorrect answers, and the assignments were challenging for those lacking exposure to systems programming. Despite these challenges, I am glad I took his course, as it strengthened my skills considerably.

What makes Professor Joshua truly exceptional is the genuine passion he puts into teaching. explanations are exceptional, his support is personal, and he continuously follows up with students individually. Many of us witnessed significant improvement in our understanding, participation, and overall academic progress because of his guidance.
I took it in Spring 2023. I wish if professor took time before the semester began to organize this class, the course would have been much better.
Learned more in a single review session than I did inside his classroom

Prof. Bakita showed potential as a new professor but took on too much as a first-timer. Lectures were sometimes unfocused, and the slides were unhelpful for review. Assigned excessive readings with irrelevant info. Challenging but good assignments, though often needed office hours for clarity. Lenient grader too, and encouraged participation.

Prof. Bakita is definitely a gem of a person but he took upon too much work to ensure a thoroughly enjoyable semester for us. His TAs were the best, and he was accessible outside of class. I wish more people tried to appreciate his effort, and I would definitely take a class with him again considering how much I learned! Stop worrying about grades!

Everything about this class was absolutely ridiculous. To top it all off, our final was almost 3 weeks ago and no grades are in. The entire class has "not reported" for the grade on their transcript, and it now says that students never took this class, leaving ppl unable to alter their schedules until a manual grade change is done for each student.

Explains the material clearly in lectures and office hours. Releasing assignments was disorganized but he gave generous extensions to make up for that. The assignments were interesting and I learned quite a bit. Test material comes from the lectures and assignments. He's very helpful and quick to respond on Piazza.

Bakita put a lot of effort into this class, and clearly tried to put his own spin on things. However, it was probably too much work for too little time which resulted in some disorganization. However grading policies were overall quite lenient and there was a generous curve on the second midterm. The assignments were difficult but pretty rewarding.

The class was a bit disorganized at times but he was always transparent when he was late and he gives a VERY generous late policy. The fact that he subtracts points for wrong answers is stupid but not too bad because the tests aren't insanely difficult. He assigns a lot of readings but I didn't do a single one and got by fine.

5 assignments (would have been 6 if he had done any preparation before taking on the course...), mostly with late instruction writeups, short timelines, and expecting far more incoming knowledge than standard for an introductory course. Lots of tangents. Only teaching the class because he likes the material - not because he wants students to learn.

fairly uncoordinated, expects you to already be an expert from the readings. lectures are obscure applications of concepts, while the entire class is still struggling with the basics. former TA, makes sense his lectures are more like directed office hours. assignments are fairly difficult with full directions not being released for a long time.

He started out the class giving high hopes by saying he "understands our struggle as students". Bro was the cause of ALL MY STRUGGLES this semester. This mans has me wishing I never was a CS major. I've never had a more disorganized class in my life. DO NOT TAKE unless you're ready to spend hours questioning your sanity as you complete assignments.

Worst 211 professor the university has ever had.  He treats us as though we should be experts at C instead of newbies with his needlessly punitive "style guide" grading for labs.  Additionally, he is extremely late with putting out assignments, his slides are garbage, and he has negative points on tests for choosing the wrong answer.  AVOID!

Prof Bakita is a mediocre at best lecturer (would be better if he was more focused) & his slides are useless. His grading is extremely unclear & on tests is awful. Negative pts for wrong ans. Style grading on assignments in an intro class in a language 90% have never used & never giving feedback until 2 wks before the semester is over is absurd.

Prof Bakita assigned a lot of readings, wrote fair tests, challenged you with difficult programming assignments, and was extremely accessible outside of class. I enjoyed his class and respect his professional work, humor, and patience. Would recommend taking 211 with bakita - he is passionate and merits a lot of respect

Prof Bakita knows his stuff, but lectures are beyond comprehension for an intro systems class. Assignments are overly complex and I don't know how anyone learning C could reasonably complete them. Exams are graded harshly with points taken off for every incorrect answer. Highly disorganized class at a very advanced level for intro level CS students
Tough, but super interesting. Great lecturer but be prepared to read.

Professor Bakita is so nice and so passionate. The class, however, is unfortunately very disorganized. The material itself is already hard and the lectures don't help clear things up sadly. I can tell he wants us all to do our best and learn. Help is available is you need it. If you really invest in this class and go extra miles, you can do okay.

By far one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Extremely disorganized and doesn't finish writing assignments until a few days before they are released. He expects you to know a lot of info ahead of time and goes on unnecessary tangents. The assignments are extremely hard and doesn't give enough time to complete them. Would not take prof again.
Very good and passionate about the subject. Learned a lot!

A unicorn in the CS dept, Ajay is a professor that understands what it means to teach to an audience topics that are difficult in concept. Each lecture is really interesting, and the assignments are so much fun to do. Super understanding, passionate, and caring, two midterms (really easy and worth less than attendance), otherwise all projects!
Me when a grad student teaches better than the actual professors

Ajay is the goat. It's very apparent how much he cares about teaching and how much effort he puts into this class. One of the most useful classes here if you want to go into SWE and I learned lots of useful things from his class. Each assignment is a fun project, and there is a final group project. 2 midterms both pretty easy.

Take this class. Ajay was an amazing professor and 426 was the best class I have taken at UNC. His lectures are super useful, the assignment are fun and practical. Very easy A if you need an elective.
Great amazing guy. I turned in an assignment late due to procrastination and a mishap from a past course interfering with the setup required. He let it through with no penalty. Goat status imo frfr.
Him and Kris Jordan are the best professors. Really fun class and very easy to get a good grade

Lectures are usually straight out of the textbook.
Grades super hard and the grading guidelines make no sense at all. Even if you put the answer key word for word, you'd probably get an 80 on an assignment.

Lectures were unhelpful and the flipped classroom didn't work well. Homework was confusing, and even ULAs struggled with some questions. The professor helps if you ask but can be belittling. No curve when the class average was ~50, we were only allowed to retake 2 questions for half credit.

Worst prof I've ever had. Other Calc II classes were SO much easier: They had curves, extra credit, easier tests, and their professors were nicer and more accessible. burkhead doesnt care if the test avg is a 40, she will never curve or give extra credit. calc is inherently hard but she makes it so much harder than it needs to be. AVOID AT ALL COST

She uses a flipped classroom style, so you kinda have to teach yourself the content. Mandatory reading responses before lectures count towards your grade. She uses no notes and sometimes has a hard time making concepts easy to understand. Relies too much on you understanding the textbook before class. Take someone else if you can. Hard midterms.

Worst prof for calc 3. Take literally any other prof. Class averages for exams in her section were 20 points lower compared to other sections, yet there was no curve. For some reason she likes having 40-minute exams and then 35-minute lectures right after. The common final exam was much easier compared to her midterms.

this class had me questioning if i was cut out for math in general. don't take, no chance for improvement. i worked super hard too, never have i studied this much... did all the practice problems, read the textbook, maybe i really am not cut out for it lol :(

Save your grade and don't take 381 with Burkhead. Inaccessible and hard to approach with questions related to grading or asking her to explain concepts. Asked her many times to explain the material, and was often met with snarky remarks. Office hours are even worse, as she is not much help if you're lost.

This is a really hard class and Burkhead does not make it easier. She spend the entire lecture doing proofs instead of teaching us how to apply the content to questions we will be seeing on the exam. The exams she writes are significantly harder than that of other professors. Nice person, unhelpful professor. Take literally anyone else.

Incredibly caring towards students and easy to access. Really emphasized the reasoning behind concepts! Tests matched the material decently well but homework felt a little off. Hosted a final review session which I really appreciated :) Hard class but I loved having her as a prof!

Please don't. Your life will be actually horrible with her - she is so hard compared to other calc 3 profs for no reason. 4 tests + recitation quizzes + she writes a horrendous final. Take with literally any one else it will be better.
Don't take pls. So hard for no reason compared to other calc 2 profs

Very solid Calc 3 professor; very willing to answer questions during lecture. Tests are generally in line with review packets and probably easier than them. Dr. Burkhead is fairly good at explaining the "why" behind things, so you'll be fine if you have a good mind for math and did decently in Calc 1 and 2.

Don't take this professor IF YOU CANNOT HANDLE THE FLIPPED CLASSROOM MODEL because she barely teaches anything in class. Your grade is completely dependent of the practice and the reading you do outside of class. There are no lectures, no slides, no notes, so if you are someone who needs those resources, don't take it with her. She doesn't teach.

Prof. Burkhead is very smart and a good teacher. However, the lectures are very fast-paced. You have to read the textbook before the classes to get the most out of them. The tests are not easy, but they are fair. Expectations for the class are very clear, and she drops a generous amount of assignments from your grade. I would recommend!

Her lectures are barely helpful and I had to teach myself this entire course because I learned nothing in the lecture. She is very kind and offers plenty of resources. The lectures, homework, and tests do not match each other making it hard to study.

My choice for calc 2 was either between Compton or Burkhead and I'm thrilled I chose Burkhead. Compton is an amazing professor but I believe Burkhead really tried to make connections with her students whether in class or outside.  She sometimes curves but tries not to if possible. Her homework consists of like 10-20 questions depending on the unit.

Words can not express how unnecessarily difficult she makes everything. My roomate was taking calc 2 but with a different prof and her tests were a million times easier. She's also just kind of patronizing. Don't take her.

A hard class for sure. Objectively she is a tough grader, and you should expect to put in a lot of time for this class, but she is organized, fair, and provides a lot of resources to help you learn. 

Also, knew all students by name after the couple of weeks.

I feel bad saying this because Dr. Burkhead is genuinely really nice lady but this class just wasn't it. I'm bad at math so I won't talk about how well things were explained but: 
-Recitations were graded by quizzes that, in my opinion, were harder than the exams. 
-Our exams were not curved, where other calc professors gave curves

In honor of everyone just bombing their finals I can say with absolute confidence: worst teacher at UNC.  I studied more than I ever have in the entirety of my life and have nothing to show for it. No one I know did well. She's not a bad person, just a bad teacher.

Why this professor is so against students succeeding, I'll never know. I'm a junior and have never had a teacher so woefully underprepared to assist students during lectures or office hours. Going genuinely was a waste of time, and no one would show up by the end of the semester. The tests are insanely difficult, and the majority of people fail.

DO NOT TAKE HER PLEASE!!!! Genuinely take any other professor. Lectures, homework, and recitations never align with the textbook material AND tests. She makes the tests far more difficult than necessary. The averages were always shockingly horrid and she straight up refuses to curve (first midterm had mean of 61) She wants her students to fail!

Very hard tests and content compared to other profs. Test questions are overly complicated and not enough time is given. She is nothing special as an educator and can be intimidating. I have not had a great experience with UNC math profs, I thought she would be good teacher thats hard. I was wrong. Just take it with another prof she kinda blows.

Very bad professor, a very fast-paced class does not care if you know the material or not. She does not curve tests and she expects you to know everything before class. I would not take this professor again since she grades harshly and does not give you opportunities to show improvement and improve your grade.

Easily the worst teacher I've had at UNC. Acts like she has something to prove and in doing so constantly uses the hardest examples during lectures, for homework, etc. Considering that Calc 2 is arguably the toughest class at UNC by itself, this really doesn't help. Take anyone else.

Flipped class which makes an already difficult subject that much harder. Test heavy, and she doesn't shy away from making questions more difficult than needed--Be ready to master the material, not just know it well. It is evident that she cares and will try to help you if you're struggling, but just take it with a better prof
