She also offers grade boosters like lab attendance and worksheets, though labs aren't very helpful, and grading varies by TA.

This class feels hard if only listening to lecture, but if you keep track of the homework and try to really understand the material getting at least a B+ is def doable. Professor Newhall might not be the best lecturer but she's a really nice person, and she gave out curve at the end which makes 92.9 an A and 89 and A-.

Prof Newhall listened and attempted to make exam 2 (mean 50) + final simpler in order to match the concerns of the class (which was appreciated) it's frustrating because the structure is confusing & she teaches so abstractly there's no connect to the material. Wish there was more depth & clarity, without so much difficulty in getting a good grade.

DO NOT TAKE, never have I struggled in math as hard as in MATH-235. Never taught the class before so she could not do half of the problems in lectures. The tests are hard. They usually do not include the material given in the review sheets. The final had no review material, topic lists, etc. The labs aren't helpful.

Honestly maybe not her fault since this is her first time teaching this course but awful. Did not teach half of exam 2 and has not curved it. Very disorganized, not responsive, overall just a difficult class. Self taught most of the material bc lectures were insufficient leading to poor grades. Avoid!!

Nice person, horrible professor. Can't lecture/teach for the life of her, tests have material that were never covered during lectures. Doesn't know what she's doing (didn't create class material, didn't create homework, lectures like she went over the slides the night before) and is only available two days of the week.

Course content was challenging but grading was generous. It was her first time teaching the course so things may change. Worst parts were the weekly homeworks (took me around 8 hours), the VERY hard exams, and the lectures (felt like she was just reading the textbook). Best part was the amount I learned (a lot of very interesting stuff).

Professor Newhall is a overall a great teacher and lectures well. She is clear and open to questions, making sure students understand and follow the content, if not in lectures, in OH. She is also open to feedback when it comes to exams and workload. However, the subject matter itself was challenging, and we often felt overwhelmed by the material.

Exams are 80% of your grade and graded harshly, while homework is essentially completion. With a TA who couldn't answer basic questions in office hours, this was tough. It was also odd that the professor couldn't work through an exam problem in a full lecture, while holding the answer key, right after we were expected to solve several on the exam.

Lectures come across as esoteric and move at a pace that is much too fast to follow. She does follow the textbook closely, but I find that the textbook explanations are MUCH easier to follow than those given in class, even after already having read the same explanations from the textbook.

The lectures are informative and engaging, but they sometimes move too quickly to follow. Also, I enjoyed the textbook by Strogatz which was used. My main issue is that the homework is MUCH too long. Given the time required for assignments each week, it's tough to also balance studying for exams (four in total) alongside other courses.

Dr. Newhall is a great prof. Splits her class into half lecture half worksheet, so even though there's no recitation she can answer questions and gives lots of practice. Super helpful in office hours. Tests are totally reasonable compared to homework. Take her for diff eq!!
Fair Tests, good worksheets, proper homework. I self learned but thats more due to my inability to focus in class rather than any problems with her lecture.

Lectures are easy to follow and recorded for future reference. Worksheets help you learn and give you free participation points. Tests are reasonable. Material may be difficult but office hours are a great resource!

Super caring about his students and very accessible outside of class. He would cover questions regarding the homeworks in depth during office hours. Supposed to be one of the harder undergrad maths at UNC but he made the class super interesting and showed how the techniques we learned in class are used in areas of applied math in an engaging way.👍

The grading is very harsh, with assignments often losing 10%-20% of marks and exams graded strictly. Even for answers you're confident in, expect around 80%, while uncertain responses might score only 20%-40%. Test preparation materials provided are minimal. 521 is a difficult course, Marzuola didn't make it easier, or harder.
Really good lecturer teaching a tough class; Goes above and beyond to help students understand course content. Super nice dude overall.

Dr. Marzuola is really excited and passionate about math and for me that made the lectures engaging and fun. The midterm tests were too long for the testing period and I had trouble finishing them, but you get cheat sheets for the midterms and the final and he curves final grades. Overall I loved the class and I loved Dr. Marzuola!

I found his lectures hard to understand sometimes. He definitely gets into some abstract stuff which I couldn't always follow but I understand that the reason was usually to explain where something comes from or why it's useful. His midterms were ok, though kind of hard overall. The final went really well somehow. Going to office hours helped.

Initially Professor Marzuola was a little difficult to understand, especially when he sometimes did his somewhat abstract proofs, but his main idea was to give us an intuition for the topics at hand. I appreciate Professor Marzuola because he would always clarify and do things multiple times to help us understand, be it in office hours or lecture.
Ignores students on Piazza, didn't give any info about what the final exam's gonna look like. just blindly studying atp
just dont. im stressing out rn studying for the final exam because its worth 40% ?!?!?!?! and he does not give any practice or tell us anything
don't take
gave homework of spring break and lectures are impossible to understand

I started the semester liking him but the lectures just got more and more confusing. He only teaches in theory and basically does no practice problems so you have to self study outside class. There is no study material so if you are confused it's your problem. The only good thing is how easy the first midterm was.

I reccomend taking 548 with Smirnov. Tests and Final were very easy, homework is all from the textbook. I skipped the majority of lectures and did well. Unfortunately he doesn't post lecture notes but as long as you do the homework you'll be fine.

Despite his confusing lectures and insanely tedious homework, I had a solid B+ going into the final exam. Midterms were graded leniently by the TA, turned out final was graded incredibly harshly by Smirnov with seemingly no curve. The average was a 61% and my final brought me down to a C-. Absolutely ridiculous way to conduct a class in my opinion.

Chill professor. Class covered less content than expected, just a handful of different solving methods. No proofs or numerical methods were covered at all. Weekly homework assigned on Pearson. There were 2 midterms, each had 4 questions. Pretty straightforward if you came to lectures and took notes. Final was longer and harder than both midterms.

Chill professor teaches well but doesnt give feedback other than test grades. Class is pretty easy because you only learn around 10 methods total. Midterms were pretty easy and graded on the lighter side but the final is hard and graded harshly. Come to class to learn but you gotta do a ton of practice problems outside of class to do well.
The class is very straightforward and pretty easy as long as you just show up to class. There were two midterm exams with only 4 questions each, all very fair to what we went over in class.

Terrible course if you're a math major and want to learn theory. All you learn is ODE solving trick after ODE solving trick and the cycle never ends. No proofs, no understanding, just rote memorization and robotic pattern recognition. Teaching is obviously a mandatory obligation for the professor. You will learn nothing in this course of use.

funny guy, but expects you to know calculus before he teaches it. writes exams with questions that he does not really teach you. Kinda have to fend for yourself. His accent is a plus, though! But do not take him if you are not good at grasping difficult calc concepts quickly, as you WILL fall behind and become lost.

People give him a hard time, but I don't think he was too bad. He was very honest the first day of class- read the textbook, watch videos online if you're confused, and this class is hard. I did both and did pretty good. You only have two tests (that are five questions). He does not write the final, so something to keep in mind.

Don't take Smirnov without having a solid understanding of Calc beforehand. Lectures are mostly theoretical and don't prepare you for problems. There are few resources provided for exam prep. He's a very kind, funny Russian guy, but my understanding is that he thrives in teaching much more complicated subject matter. Calc 1 is not his strong suit.
He's a nice guy but the examples covered in class are not reflective of the exams at all. Take 231 with literally anyone else.

Expects a large pre knowledge of calc. He can also be quite sassy during class and will make you feel like you asked a stupid question. Also randomly asked the class if he could move class times an hour early for a week. Debuts heinous outfits too (not rating based on this but girl...) Literally Gru reincarnated.

Only take this class if you already have a perfect understanding about calc and you did well in the class in high school. He doesn't explain anything and the tests have have more challenging   content than we learned in class. The other professors actually explain concepts so I started going to their lectures instead.

Smirnov is funny. I pass/failed this class because I was focusing on other things but the material wasn't too difficult. Hardest stuff came at the end of the semester but he was always willing to talk in office hours about the material. Lenient on homework due dates and was always willing to give extensions. The final was lowk the easiest exam.

He is very kind. For a 500 level math course, it was one of the easier ones I have taken. Very accessible in office hours. He listened to students on due dates and would give extensions on homework often. He followed the textbook very well making it easy to stay on top of the class. He grades the tests by hand and gives them back to you with notes.
He is so silly. Very funny guy. Midterms/finals were not that difficult, just practice the homework. Good lectures.

Jason is always on Piazza and has office hours often and genuinely seems to be nice, but exams are horribly, unnecessarily, unforgivingly hard (class medians on midterms/final were 65, 43, 51, 48). Homework is due twice a week at 3pm (of all times) and take hours just to be graded harshly. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS EVEN IF YOUR LIFE DEPENDS ON IT!

521 is a brutal class but Jason makes it digestible and enjoyable. He wants each and everyone to succeed. He provides plenty of practice materials and holds review sessions before each exam. Exams are pretty difficult and are graded fairly. If you put in the work, you will do well. And take 521 with Jason.

Dr. Metcalf was an excellent professor to have for this class. However, this is an AWFUL class. Def a humbling moment for a lot of math students, everything has to be intuitive on tests which means a lot of independent work outside class I didn't have time for. He provides a lot of the guidance you need in class, but you have to implement it.

He is a great instructor. Lectures are well-designed and the homeworks are generally pretty good, though they had high variance in difficulty. I felt that expectations regarding grades were not well-communicated. I expected B based on my grades and ended up with an A, which was good, but also concerning in that I had no idea if I was doing well.
Super chill guy, tests are more challenging than other calc teachers, but he teaches well and you'll be really well prepared for the final.

Professor Metcalfe is an extremely kind professor who will answer any and all questions. The midterms are tough but they make you very prepared for the final. Would definitely take a class with him again.

Class is very well organized, lectures are clear and build on each other and there are many helpful resources on Canvas. Not a ton of homework, and the homework is relatively easy, but additional practice is definitely needed to do well on exams. Jason is very supportive, will answer any question asked and is a great professor. Def recommend!!

Jason is amazing, I can't imagine passing without him. He is available what feels like 24/7 with office hours and answering questions online. BUT this is a VERY VERY hard class. BE PREPARED to spend an ungodly amount of time studying to get a 50 on the midterm. If you can avoid this class you should but if not be ready and take Jason if you can.

I took this class last spring, but I wanted to say this guy is the GOAT! 521 is hard but you can do well if you put the work in. Make sure to do practice problems, go to office hours, and read the textbook
Excellent math professor who explains quite difficult concepts in a digestible way.

Tough Tough class.But I also can't say enough good things about Jason. He truly wants his student to succeed in this class and will challenge you to be a better mathematician. 521 is the gateway to many higher level proof based class so take it with him will set you up for success.

Metcalfe is hands down the best lecturer I've had in the math department. 521 is supposed to be the hardest class, but with him teaching it, I would rank it among the easier math classes I've had here. He is exceptionally good at explanations & ensuring understanding.

100% worth doing whatever you need to do to get into his class.
Prof Rose doesnt really understand what his student want in his class. most of the time he seems taking to himself. The homework is graded through quizzes which is very unfair.

brilliant dude. Knows what he's talking about when it comes to discrete math. However, for people who have no exposure to the subject, he moves a bit too fast. If I could redo this course, I would read the textbooks prior to each lecture so that i can follow what he's saying and ask good questions. This can be a challenging class
Not a great person, hard to communicate with. He makes mistakes and students are the people who have to pay for his mistakes.
No homework solutions or test solutions but extremely helpful in office hours. He very clearly wants everyone to succeed and was super nice. Really wish I could take another class with him.

A good seminar on knot theory. Material was a little difficult to understand in the last half of the class, but Professor Rose is passionate about this topic and willing to help. No homework, and projects and tests were graded very lightly. There's a clear grading scale, and tests weren't a large part of the grade.

at first i was scared that it was gonna be a hard fys bc it is math based but he made sure to treat it as a first year class. there was no hw, participation, easy tasks and an easy project made up 75% of grade. he also heavily curved final grades. really nice guy and super passionate about the topic and teaching.

This class was a first-year seminar and he treated/graded it like such. Prof Rose was passionate about the topic and took the time to break down the complicated concept of knot theory into easily digestible chunks.

Professor Cherednik was a nice and funny professor. He has an extremely thick Russian accent that can take a while to understand. He is too smart to teach a class such as MATH231. Had a weird grading scale that ended up making a lot of people have their final exam as 80% of the final grade. Overall, I would recommend with someone else if possible!

He has a very heavy accent but you will get used to it. He is a funny guy and he kind of goes all over the place while teaching. In my opinion he is too smart to be teaching 231 to the point where he glosses over the importance of certain subjects.

Dr. Cherednik is a kind and caring professor. Unfortunately, he has a super thick Russian accent, so learning discrete mathematics from him is a challenge. He is very clear about what to prepare for the exams and is very understanding. The class, especially the homework, is complex, but he makes himself accessible and his notes are helpful.
It was a very difficult class but Professor Cherednik provided comprehensive preparation for each exam, which helped tremendously.

Do not take this course unless it is required. The professor has a very strong Russian accent, which makes lectures difficult to understand. On the first day, I was completely lost and could not follow what he said. However, he reviews material for the midterms except the first take-home exam. Later midterms usually have about four questions total.

Friendly personality, but is hard to learn from. Our first to in-class tests were very fair, but the final was very intense. If this professor is your only choice don't completely despair, but get ready to put in a little work.
Professor Cherednik is a very nice guy and definitely wants his students to succeed, but his lectures are very hard to follow, so be ready to teach yourself a lot of content.

If I wasn't paying really close attention to lectures, it was very hard for me to understand what he was saying ( thick russian accent). He does seem like a nice and caring person. The final was so much harder than any prep material we were given, and everyone seemed to agree.

Guy has a heavy Russian accent, so if you're bad with accents, I wouldn't recommend. Took about half the semester, but I understand him now. He's alright at explaining things, but I spent all class looking at his slideshow and following the explanations on there, not him actually doing it.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO!!!  Extremely smart, but thinks you should be on the same level as him. He WILL test you on things not covered in class. He 's extremely inequitable, never listening to my remarks about how I was one of few people in class that never cheated. No duh the students that use chatgpt are doing better than me.

Lectures are often confusing, but he breaks down the problems that will be on each exam the class before. One of the easier 500 electives for math. Lots of extra credit on the exams, so as long as you come to class it is very straightforward to get an A. The homeworks (worth 10%) are much harder than anything you see on an exam and can be daunting.

He's not a great instructor, and he's bad at answering questions, but he's nice and wants you to succeed. He has extra credit built into all of his assignments (e.g., there are 28 points available on a test, but it's only graded out of 20). The material is also interesting when it makes sense, but there are weird difficulty spikes here and there.

Super smart and nice professor. Ridiculously hard content. I'm a calc tutor and still struggled with the concepts. If you're going to take this course, you're going to need a good grasp of math - it's not for the lighthearted, but it's not that hard to get an A. Gives hints on HW, fast email response time, take home final. GO TO THE FINAL REVIEW.

Ivan is a genius but impossible to understand in lectures. Every time I went to class or asked a question, I came out feeling more confused. Thankfully, the final grade only counted the last exam (take-home) and final group project, and the final had bonus credit which was very helpful. Homework takes forever, don't take if you don't know math.

TERRIBLE PROFESSOR! Incoherent lectures with random thoughts. Course prerequisites were high school algebra but the class was harder than Calc 3 and Differential Equations, which I took at UNC. Despite a grade of a 90, I received B+. Homework was impossible with little support. Only those who devoted their lives to this class got As. Please avoid!

TERRIBLE PROFESSOR! Incoherent lectures with random thoughts. Course prerequisites were high but the class was harder than Calc 3 and Differential Equations. Despite a 90 score, received B+. Homework was impossible with little support. Only those who devoted their lives got As. Avoid this class!

Great mathematician, ok lecturer. For a class that only requires high school algebra, it is significantly harder than one would initially expect. His lectures are fast paced if no one tells him to slow down, and he talks with a heavy accent. Lots of extra credit on a final that's worth half your grade makes it pretty easy to get an A.

Professor Cherednik is sweet and caring, but this class was nearly impossible. This class should not be a first-year seminar, much less one without prerequisites. The class required calculus, statistics, and physics knowledge. It's doable with hours of research spent on homework, but it will not be an easy A. Prof. Cherednik has a thick accent.

Ivan is very nice, but the content was not explained well. Spent hours trying to comprehend what was in the textbook so I could get the homework problems correct. He responds to emails very quick and there is extra credit on the final, but this math was far too advanced for a first-year seminar. Not as easy A.

He was a very tough grader. There was extra credit options on tests, but that was for a reason. Tests were so difficult that he had to give us the built in curve or else everyone in the class would have failed. The positive reviews are from the .1% of students who spend hours upon hours just studying for this one class. DO NOT TAKE!

Ivan is an amazing and great person, however, as someone who went into this course thinking they could skate by with the prerequisite, which was high school algebra, I STRUGGLED with this course. If you are a fan of computer science and discreet math, you will probably love this course, but beware that Ivan does have a THICK accent. Love him tho :)

Many opportunities to get extra points (quiz 14/10, midterm 28/20, final 70/60). It is very hard to understand him not just the accent but also his logic. Content is self teachable but WILL take time, his notes is more like a guide use textbook. He provides study guides for each test that includes ALL type of question that will be on the test.

Easiest MATH elective, many opportunities to get extra points (grades 28/20 for midterms, 70/60 on final). I never went to class because it was so hard to understand him, but the content isn't that difficult and most of the questions he asked you can teach to yourself. If you need an A, take his class.

If you need a math elective, take this course. Exams are 80% of your grade. He will tell you the exact problem type for each exam and solve examples. Grading wise, he put 28 points on a midterm, scored it out of 20, and put the remaining 8 points towards your final grade. Same with the final (70pts scored out of 60, i.e 10pts extra credit).

Prof Cherednik is a wonderful human being who is a math wizard! But I'm ngl it was really hard to follow him in lecture. He is really approachable though so do not hesitate to reach out to him for help. Promise it will be worth it, this man has his grading criteria set so that everyone who tries can pass with an A. Hw due every other week.

Professor Cherednik is the sweetest man ever. He's very passionate about math, and cares about his students. That said, taking his class was scary. There were few homework assignments, a project, and an exam. He gives as much credit as possible, but the material is very difficult to comprehend.
Absolute banger of a class. Lectures and homework were tough, but the midterm and final were easy. Highly recommend if you like math

He was a super nice and funny guy, and taught well. I felt like I understood most things after he explained them. Make sure to follow along with his examples, it's easy to get lost if you zone out. The midterms were super easy, but the final was way more difficult.

I was looking over all the reviews, and there is one thing people forgot to mention. He does not post the notes on canvas from the lecture. He uses a blackboard to write notes, so try to sit in the front. We have 2-3 homework assignments every week online with four tries per question, 2 very easy midterms with 5 questions each, and a common final.

Dr. Varchenko is approachable and willing to help students. His accent may take a short time to get used to but does not interfere with learning. Lectures cover most material, but some concepts on the final may not be discussed in detail, so reviewing the textbook can be helpful.

Lectures are indeed dry, though they are enlightening imo until the last few units. He does make mistakes on the board so it can be hard to follow. The midterms are easy as long as you understand larger concepts, I learned more during my recitation sessions. You have to self study for the final using other classes resources if you want to do well.

Lectures are not necessarily engaging but he gives you all of the information you need to do well on his mid terms that aren't too difficult. You may need to read the textbook to gain a deeper understanding of information for the final. He's nice and willing to explain concepts. The final is harder than his mid terms. Overall a good experience.
Funny Russian guy. Lots of homework and hardly covers all the topics needed to do the homework in class. Final was a little harder than the midterms, but his grading curves are very generous.
Midterms were easy and similar to examples from lectures. Would recommend him over other professors. Lowkey funny and sassy. BEWARE the common final, it's so much harder than his midterms.

Varchenko is kinda just a cute old Russian man. He's got thick accent, he's sassy and occasionally really funny.
Lectures were boring, but manageable. Homework can be a lot if you're struggling with the content, but it's nothing crazy.
Midterms were generally pretty easy; study a little and you'll do fine. Final can catch you off guard.

Varchenko's lectures are him writing on the chalkboard for the entire class, but he gives plenty of examples to supplement the notes. His midterms are infinitely easier than any of the other 233 sections, but that does mean you have to put in extra work studying for the final. By the end of the class you will appreciate his Russian humor and smile.

Midterms were super easy, lectures were very boring, and he does not prepare you well for the common final exam. You can skip all lectures and read the textbook instead. Go to the recitation and make sure you're staying on track with the textbook or YouTube videos.

Overall bad lecturer, heavy accent but you can get past that, only writes talking to the chalk board, goes incredibly fast and does not stop for questions, writes small so you can't read it. Homework is difficult but its similar for all the classes, midterms actually pretty easy, but he only has two midterms while other sections had 3.

Secretly funny. You get used to Russian accent after a week. May need to take pics to read handwriting. His lectures match his midterms—pretty easy. Final written by other teachers so much harder. Moderately difficult hw. Recitation with TA helps since he's not super available.

HW and textbook plus lectures made midterms quite easy. Final exam was much harder than I was expecting. Answers emails quickly, and rounds up final grades nicely. Textbook proof problems are necessary if you want to do well on the final. (Did I forget to mention the final was hard?)

If you can learn from the textbook, take this class. I loved the textbook. HW assignments were perfectly reasonable and the perfect amount to learn. The content was so easy - if you didn't hate discrete. Attendance was annoying but can easily do other work or read a book during. Super fair exams.
the goat. he's chill and lowkey sassy but i love it cuz he's right. easiest class in my life.

383:best prof i ever had. like other comments say, if you dont like him...ur just not paying attention. literally is so clear and gives examples to everything. sure his lectures are "dry" but its a math class. i dont expect for him to come in hootin and hollerin to put on a show for us. he means business (math) and thats what he delivers.

Review for MATH 383. Worst professor I have ever had. Extremely dry lectures with mandatory attendance, exams questions were easy but few questions with zero partial credit. Homework is busywork and due on a random day that changes each week. Curves the class downward at the end. I am a junior and this class broke the 4.0 I had up until this point.

This is a review for Math 383: Not too bad in all honesty for this course. Everything was on pearson. He gave two attempts per exam, so achieving a good grade was not too difficult. Lecture was a bit dry, but he had an attendance sheet. If you review HWs heavy and some textbook for exams, you'll be good. Some basics of linear algebra as well.

This class is extremely boring. It's just him talking to the chalkboard for 90 minutes. I don't see any reason why you should attend class, the textbook makes way more sense and explains the topics better. He also grades pretty harshly i made very minor mistakes on some exams and lost 1/2 points on questions. He is also not accommodating at all.
He is obviously very intelligent but that does not translate to being a good teacher. Doesn't seem to care to much about the student but other then that nice guy.

Dr. Varchenko is the honestly the best professor I have ever had. The people that complain about him are the ones simultaneously on their phone while "taking notes". I was able to get a 100 on everything just by paying attention to his lectures and going over them before I did the homework. Exams are clear.

Varchenko is a great prof. Had him for 383. Those who rate him low just don't know how to do math properly. He is very clear. Students would scoff when he would ask to be more specific with their questions but they would ask things like "should we include that C is a real number on midterms". Like no duh. if you don't specify, C could be anything.
This guy's lectures are dryer than a camel's butt in the Sahara Desert. Just read an abstract algebra textbook and you'll learn a lot more.
Don not take his class, half of the classmates can not see his writing on the blackboard, also not curve

If you are willing to teach yourself or good at picking up patterns, take this class. The tests have multiple attempts and although the homework assignments are long and time consuming, they are pretty simple to complete. He just reads to the board, so if you don't require interactive lessons, you should be good.

Lecture is often confusing: Varchenko includes some unnecessary proofs and can make concepts more complicated than they need to be. I also think he could have chosen a better textbook for the class. A lot of the time, I felt like lecture and the textbook did not prepare me to do well on the tests and homework. However, he does curve

An OK professor. He showed great intellect and his math was organized. However, he sometimes got stumped on questions you asked him and would often get a huge piece of his math wrong on the board. The homework can get tedious (especially 15.7, what a monstrosity) and getting one question wrong on a test can bring your test grade from 100 to 83.

The tests are worth 80% of your grade and there is no curve. Only take this class if you are very good at math and willing to spend A LOT of time learning the content independently. Lectures are confusing and his handwriting is hard to read.

He's not a bad professor, but he's not spectacular either. Lectures feel more like presentations, especially since he brings pre-written lessons and just writes them on the board. The lectures will get you started with homework, but you will need to read the textbook to completely understand. 2 midterms and final make up 80% of grade.
For example, it's EAZY.

TAKE Professor Hong for Math 233 if you can!! His exams were so straightforward, absolutely no surprises at all. However, there is weekly homework that can be quite time consuming. His accent makes him difficult to understand, but he's really sweet and will answer your questions as best as he can.

Homework seemed very sporadically graded, as students may have the same answers but different grades on certain questions. Lectures were average but sometimes it seemed like even he didn't know what he was talking about, and sometimes seemed annoyed at answering questions. Exams were tough but very fair if you know the content.

Lectures were fine if you have a strong background in calc. He sometimes makes mistakes on the board but he's open to questions during lecture so just ask. The homework was a huge pain but standardized across all profs. Tests were so easy you reasonably don't have to study more than an hour for them if you're confident on the material.

If you're decent at calc take him. Bad at explaining but his tests are by far the easiest. If you just start preparing a few days before and watch some YouTube vids you can get 100s on them. Edfinity homework is annoying, if you can do the first 5 problems in each, you will be fine. For the final just do the past tests, it was almost a replica.

The lectures were confusing, but midterms were easy (96 and 99). The final exam was significantly harder, but similar to past exams which you can find online. Attendance was not mandatory for either lecture or recitation

Take a different professor if you want to learn during class. He is very kind but the only way to learn calc 3 was from YouTube videos. The midterms are super easy but the final is common across all professors and significantly harder, did not feel prepared for it.

For starters, this class is pretty tough and is gonna be hard no matter what. However, professor Hong gave pretty poor lectures making it very difficult to learn the material. Many people stopped going to class altogether and opted for youtube videos to teach them. By the end of the semester, this was my solution as well. He was at least kind.

Nice guy but lectures weren't very helpful and I stopped attending in general before the second midterm (no attendance policy). If you can teach yourself via YouTube (Prof. Leonard) or other textbooks you'll be good, as his midterms are extremely easy compared to other sections. Final is harder so make sure you prepare for it accordingly.

Lectures are useless tbh. His class works very well as a flipped classroom. Go watch Professor Leonard, use the UNC practice midterms and finals, and the practice tests he gives you, and you'll be more than fine. He also lets you drop a midterm and replace it with your final grade, so it's lenient to that regard. Tests are very easy too.

Nice guy but very confusing lectures and not great at answering clarifying questions. Very thick accent which caused confusion on important topics. Class is extremely test-heavy but lowest score replaced by final exam score if that's higher. Office hours were inaccessible. My advice: invest in a private tutor.
Lectures are slighly disorganized but not hard to follow if you pay attention. Tests are very straighforward and homework does a great job of preparing you for relevant problem types.

Dr. Hong is just not a very organized professor and is not easy to follow along with during lectures. I ended up learning more from YouTube videos than class. He didn't explain concepts well and I didn't know what we were doing most of the time.

Easy class and easy exams. Homework once a week (around 12 problems), nice and caring.

Lectures wrerent comprehensive. Extra study is required. Tests were easy. The main problem is that a lot of content is covered in a short time. Watch Professor Leonard's youtube lectures to suplement. My-lab-math had very difficult homework sometimes.

don't take this review lightly. i mean it, when i say please please please do not take this professor. he teaches material to you in a way where he believes that you know the material beforehand. he does not care about you. he does not care about your grade. he certainly does not care your safety (regarding what happened earlier this semester).

a unique combination of vast subject knowledge and incompetence in teaching. lectures are v hard to follow so I would recommend going to class fairly infrequently. use textbook and internet to learn on your own. griffith has easy exams and this is generally a pretty common sense course so self-learning and just taking the exams isn't too difficult.

Moosmueller is my favorite professor I've had at UNC, forreal. I loved that her lectures are recorded. Her sense of humor was refreshing and she was through in her explanations. wonderful amazing human being please never be mean to her she is such a pure soul i love caroline moosmueller

sawon is so kind and this class was not too difficult, but the lectures were painstakingly boring and hard to follow. he was kind of all over the place and the most monotone lecturer. however, the two midterms were easy and the final was doable. just do the edfinity and read the textbook and you'll be fine. Easy course, 4 solutions and attendance are all you need to get an A. Suggested for students in majoring in Mathematics.

takes points off for the smallest mistakes, confusing

he's a really nice guy, albeit a bit awkward, and you can tell he's really dedicated to his field! office hours weren't super accessible timing wise (few hours, during class times for me) and he does sort of just read off his notes but he's not bad. i didn't read the textbook but i def would recommend it. hw and practice problems are helpful

Lectures are boring as a non-math major, but Tosteson explains concepts fairly well (although he makes a lot of small errors). Attendance isn't mandatory but is important to doing well on the exams. There are weekly hws, but they only take 1-2 hrs.

His lectures can be a slog, and there were even a few times I walked out of class early due to sheer boredom. However, most of the information is not posted on Canvas so attendance is vital. The class is boring but the test questions are basically straight from the homework or in-class examples so they felt VERY fair. Not fun, but relatively easy.

My GOAT! Truly an incredible professor. He makes learning discrete math weirdly fun. His tests are fair and his explanations for topics in class are clear. Discrete is by no means an easy class, you need to train yourself to think in certain ways which just takes practice. His test questions are often similar to stuff discussed in class and in hw.

I've seen a lot of reviews about his stutter, and it DOES NOT affect his ability to convey the material. I thought his lectures are good and the homework sets you up to do well on the tests. He is very nice and willing to help outside of the classroom.

He's a good guy, and clearly understands the material very well and is very helpful and responsive outside of class, even if his lectures aren't engaging and can be pretty hard to follow. You may have to teach yourself for a fair portion of the class, but this is aided by the fact he applies heavy curves on the midterms (not so much on the final).

There were two midterms which were curved, I'm not sure about the final. Tosteson was a great professor overall and the lectures were recorded. There is a lot of homework and it can be a pain but I think the online homework was good for practice. He made a lot of mistakes during his lectures which students had to catch and seemed scatterbrained.

Be prepared to teach yourself calculus. Homework sucked and took a long time. He did drop 10% of homework at the end of the semester. Each test was curved heavily because our class average was so low. I made a 54 on one and ended with an 80. The final was not curved a lot which sucked. You can not fall behind in this class.

A very sweet guy but pretty hard to follow: stutters heavily, overcomplicates concepts, makes little mistakes when working through problems (students would have to correct him often). Homework would often take hours to complete and rarely ever lined up with class notes/examples. The two tests we had were HEAVILY curved; the final exam was not.

He was a really nice guy, and this was his first semester teaching, but the lectures were to follow. To understand the material you would need 8+ hours a week to teach yourself. The two tests were hugely curved (because class averages were so low), but the final was not. A good amount of homework. Do yourself a favor and avoid!

Chill & sweet but VERY scatterbrained & not a good teacher. Lectures were a pain to sit through & he sometimes had no idea what he was doing. hella hw that took HOURS & is nothing like class examples/tests. There's only two tests & they were heavily curved but the final was BRUTAL & not curved. Attendance is not mandatory and you can join on zoom.

Professor Tosteson really did try to set all students up for success. Although sometimes he made mistakes in lecture, he used guided notes and all his lectures were recorded. The homework was challenging but if you used it as practice, you would do well on the tests. There was leniency in grading including good curves and dropping lowest grades.

Tosteson is super sweet but I think he still has a lot to learn with teaching, hopefully, it comes with time. He struggles during lectures and often makes math mistakes that go unnoticed. moves very quickly, no time to process anything. If you have the time to spend another 10+ hrs/wk teaching yourself, you'll be okay...otherwise you will STRUGGLE

Tosteson is a chill person but not a good teacher. His lectures were hard to follow, and I had to teach myself everything on my own. Exams were very hard, but he curved them nicely (this was prob the only reason why I passed this class). He also extended due dates on homework often. I would still def take this class with another professor though.

This was Professor Tosteson's first semester. However, he is a very genuine and nice guy and wants to help you especially if you go to office hours. I have also heard no good reviews from any calc 1 students about their professors so I would argue Tosteson was the best because of his HUGE curve on the exams. Use The Orgo chem tutor to review!!

Where should I start? He makes mistakes in every lecture that the students have to catch, creates very hard exams, class examples don't help with homework/exams, rushes through lecture, hard to follow in class. If I taking this class with a different professor, I would have done significantly better. AVOID!!!
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS THE LECTURES ARE AWFUL AND ONLY TWO TESTS.

This was Prof Tosteson's first semester, so granted at times the class seemed a bit unorganized. He's a super nice guy and is very responsive to questions/emails, but I think at times he's a bit scatter-brained and overestimates our abilities in a calc 1 class. His lectures were him solving problems and his tests were hard but did have a nice curve

She explains everything as complicated as possible and goes so fast. I went to every class and still had to teach myself everything. The edfinity homeworks took forever and were much more difficult than anything we saw in class or on exams. On the plus side, she's nice and the tests were all very easy.

She's lovely but her lectures tend to be a little boring. The grading was kind of fair, with 3 midterms (30%), 3 homeworks (30%), attendance (10%) and a final group project worth 30%. Be careful with the second midterm cause it was so hard for some reason.

Don't know why so many people give her bad comments. I enjoyed her lecture and easily got an A. If you go to the class everyday, it's easy to do well in this class. The practice exam is almost exactly same as the real exam. And there's no homework other than edifinity. I love her.
Lectures could be a bit boring but this class is SUPER easy. Def take this is you want an easy A

Lectures were disorganized, difficult to follow, and somehow felt rushed even though she was going slowly through the content. Exams were easy. If she continues to use Gilbert Strang's textbook, then I highly recommend watching his lectures on MIT OpenCourseWare (18.06SC)—he explains everything much more clearly and makes the class a breeze.

Editing this review bc it was too harsh when I first wrote it. Lectures are confusing, but you can still get an A if you work hard outside of class. Yifei wants us to do well, and I'm sure the course will improve more from when I took it (Yifei's first sem at UNC). I didn't have the best experience, but I still learned a lot abt linear algebra.

She wasn't a tough grader and was very lenient with the syllabus, dropping a midterm that she originally had counting for credit. She wants to help your grade. Lectures aren't the best but material isn't bad and it's not set up for you to fail.

Lou is really nice and explains things very clearly. The workload is manageable, and the exams are about the same level as the sample exams. However, she sometimes talks a bit too fast, so you need to stay fully focused throughout the whole class to keep up.

Show up to class and work hard, and you'll get an A. Her other reviews are so low prob bc only 20% of students actually went to class. There are 3 midterms (avg = mid 80s) and a final which are v fair and based off the HW + practice tests. Her lectures sometimes were fast-paced and confusing, but I expect she will improve as this was her 1st sem.

I actually really liked her. I'll note I believe this was her first semester at UNC, which it was also mine so I understand the adjustment and I think she did well for it.
She definitely talked a bit fast, but I was engaged in her lectures and liked them. She did take constructive criticism of what to focus on in lectures like less proofs.

Dr. Lou is extremely nice and caring, but it was a bit difficult to understand her lectures, especially later on in the semester. The exams got progressively more difficult, and I had to supplement lectures with a lot of YouTube and online resources to explain things more clearly. Would highly recommend Gilbert Strang's videos.
had an A until the final and i got absolutely finished

I hope that she never teaches Linear Algebra again! Lectures were all over the place, and if you miss one, good luck understanding her lecture slides. Her practice exams are laughable compared to the real ones. Final was extremely hard. My advice: don't go to class but watch the Strang lectures instead. And don't forget to do the worksheets!

The content being taught is not incredibly complex, but her lectures are often disorganized and she makes a lot of mistakes. Make sure you are able to self teach if you take a class with her, especially because the online homework covers content that was never mentioned in class. If you take Lin Alg with her just watch the Strang lectures.

I have so much to say about Yifei Lou. First, I want to start off with how such a nice person she is. She is such a sweet lady and she has a great fashion taste. On the other hand she sucks at teaching. Like holy hell. She is not clear at what she's teaching. She goes crazy fast during lectures too. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. NOT WORTH IT.

She is really sweet and while the midterms ARE difficult, she gives example problems and stuff that are similar in difficulty so I was never surprised by anything. Doing examples with us in class was very helpful if you're that kind of learner. At the end, she offered to drop more things if ppl filled out the course evals.

She's so sweet and genuinely wants to help. She is willing to compromise with hours and will answer questions without complaint. She does work fast but she will stop for questions. Office hours were very helpful because you could just work in there and ask questions when needed so it felt like a a safe space.

Quizzes were in every recitation. The lectures were chaotic. The main difficulty of this class was the exams. 3 exams worth 15% each and a final worth 35% which would also replace your lowest exam score. She did let us get half credit back on one exam by doing test corrections on any exam of our choosing which helped my grade a lot in the end.

Yifei Lou feels like she's holding your hand through calculus. She is very lecture-heavy so if you're not paying attention in class you will have to watch videos instead on your own time. Her practice problems before each test are very similar but she tends to get creative so you have to know everything beforehand to get a good grade on the tests.

Let me start by saying Dr. Lou is a VERY nice and understanding person. HOWEVER, teaching is just not her thing The class was extremely difficult. I failed every exam and I'm praying for a miracle on the final to pass the class. She talks extremely fast, is hard to understand, and does not explain things in lecture. Hardest class I have taken here.

In the halls of equations, where numbers dance,
There lurks a professor, devoid of any chance.

She lectures on, in a monotone drone.

Her graphs are crooked, her proofs a mess,
A mathematician's nightmare, I confess.
she shatters dreams with her cold disdain,
