Yifei got me feeling like a English major! I switched to english major thanks to her!

Absolutely terrible lectures. Nobody in class understands a single thing she teaches. She goes extremely fast and skips a bunch of steps. She is also very disorganized and not at all neat when solving problems on the board. Everybody walks out of class confused and annoyed. Uses a bunch of terms without explaining what they mean. DO NOT TAKE HER.
Amazing lecturer, she explained difficult topics super well. 521 was definitely a learning curve as it was different from other math classes I'd taken before but she made it easier to adapt.
Professor Bhattacharya is fantastic! Math 521 is a very difficult class but she made it very fun and easy to learn and understand. I can't recommend her enough!

Dr. Bhattacharya was an amazing lecturer despite the abstractness of a lot of the concepts in real analysis. The subject was hard, but she was very fair and generous with grading, along with guidance outside of class during office hours or by email. Incredibly hard class, but she made it more tolerable.

I actually love her. She's genuinely so smart, and this is a hard class, so I'm aware of the challenging content. But still, her lectures were great, and she stopped for questions a lot. The first midterm was definitely not easy, but she was generous with grading and made the second one easier. She's a very responsible teacher.

The first exam average was 51%, which isn't unusual for MATH 521, but grading has been pretty unclear. We were only told a "nonuniform curve" will reduce the number of students who fail, leaving many students completely unsure how they will be affected by a curve. Lectures are generally good but often feel a bit rushed.

This was a very tough class. Prof Bhattacharya is nice and understanding, but often did not explain class concepts fully, and homeworks were unreasonably hard. I learned more from my recitation TA. The final was near impossible, with the class average being an F. the class was curved a full letter grade at the end. I don't recommend this class.

Dr. Bhattacharya is a wonderful teacher! I found it particularly helpful that she always uploaded her lecture notes and homework solutions on time. She is also very kind and respectful towards students, which made me feel comfortable to ask questions during class and office hours.

I learned a lot from Professor Bhattacharya's class. I knew that if I followed the material taught in class everyday, then I would have no problem solving homework problems and getting prepared for the exams. She is a very professional and fair professor. Her office hours were very helpful and she was always ready to help.

Dr. Bhattacharya is a very fair professor. Her lectures are very dry and she is not very personable, but the course overall was not difficult and was very fair. She is open to any questions both in class and outside of class, and is happy to help if you just ask for it.

I really enjoyed this class. Her first midterm was very easy, the second one was really hard and the final exam was very fair. She was very open to feedback throughout the course and to curving final grades. Her homework is challenging but if you put in enough time and effort on it, you will really start enjoying the beauty of the subject.

I learned a lot in this class. Her lectures are very clear and I really enjoyed her style of teaching. She delved deep into the material and it was very enjoyable to understand the proofs behind a lot of theorems that we use to solve problems. She is also very nice and office hours were always super helpful. I highly recommend this class.

This is the best math class I have ever taken! Professor Bhattacharya is amazing! Her homework really made me think and challenge myself. She is super helpful and I learned a great deal of good mathematics from her. If you love math, then this class is for you.

Lectures boring and does not explain things very well (I second the 15 minute silence that one person said, this happened). She is more helpful in office hours, but they are at 4 on Fridays and 5 on Tuesdays, and sometimes she isn't there. She's nice, but it's clear she doesn't care about teaching and want to put in much effort to see you learn.

Avoid at all costs. Extremely dry and boring lecturer and creates zero participation or engagement in class. Once spent 15 minutes in complete silence in the middle of a lecture. Exams are much harder than homeworks and in class material. Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had.

Professor Bhattacharya clearly cares about her students and her grading system gives buffer room. She was available for office hours and was very nice when I asked questions concerning the grading of the course and was very receptive to feedback. This was her first year teaching at UNC so I feel like she'll improve a lot with time.

I have taken a lot of calculus classes in my life and I can tell you that Bhattacharya's class is the only one from which I learned anything. She explained things in great depth during lectures and that is when I finally understood the point of calculus. She is also super helpful and would always stop and ask for questions through out class.

I loved Professor Bhattacharya's class! She is the reason I learned to at least like math. Her lectures were great and I loved the fact that she used chalkboard instead of powerpoint. The only thing is that I wish she posted videos of the lectures for this class after because it helps with reviewing.

She explained things in great depth and gave a ton of good examples. She always made sure to stop and ask for questions and was willing to go back and rephrase anything that wasn't clear. It was clear that she really cared that we understand the concepts.

Cut some slack guys. It was her first time teaching calc, she was very open to suggestions and encouraged questions if anyone was confused. The curve was very generous too. I am convinced that she will improve and change the class structure. I would still recommend taking the class with Linda Green but please don't be discouraged by these reviews.

If you are ok with boring, heartless lectures then she's the professor for you. I understand calculus is not the most interesting subject, but she seemed like a robot when she taught, which made the content harder to understand. The homework and rec problems were also miles harder than any of the tests, so if you can do those you'll do fine.

So she wasn't horrible, but she wasn't amazing either. It felt as though she didn't explain the concepts well enough and found myself teaching the information to myself most of the time. Also, the final exam was impossible (avg was around a 59%).

Although her lectures got boring sometimes, that is the nature of Calculus, overall she did a good job explaining the material. I understood exactly what I needed too and whatever I didn't understand my TA did an amazing job of explaining. Idk if he is still going to TA in her calc next year but get Isaac Weiss if you have the chance.

I took the honors version of this class, and it was extremely difficult. I cannot find a single student in class who didn't use AI on our homework, but the tests were incredibly easy... until the final, which had Fibonacci and Catalan numbers. I think Professor Weng is definitely one of the best professors for this course, but brace yourself.
Go to class and study a lot for tests and you'll be fine, his class is hard because of the tests and their weightage.

Discrete was a hard class for me, but Daping is a good teacher and very fair. Gives you a lot of homework, which might not be the most applicable. However, practice midterms echo the real midterms. The final was a bit difficult, but he did give us a curve! Just make sure you put in the time, cause it is a time-consuming class.
Loved this class. The work is hard and you really have to put the time in but Weng makes it easy to understand in class. Funny guy.
Lots of fun

He is truly passionate about teaching. His lectures are always engaging and well-organized, which makes even complex topics easier to understand. Whenever I had questions after class, he was always very patient and willing to help. Highly recommend taking his class!

He makes mistakes in lectures and then blanks when asked about it. Also makes mistakes in HW and sends announcements out at night like 2 days before due. Still due on original date tho. Harsh grader gives very little partial credit. However, there was a 10% curve to the overall grade though and he is always willing to help in office hours.

Professor Weng is pretty organized in terms of lectures and lecture notes. He posts his lecture notes after every class so attendance isn't really required. Tests were relatively easy (compared to other professors) and overall grades were curved a lot at the end. There is a lot of homework and it is pretty hard.

Great professor. Didn't feel like I needed to read the textbook at all because his lectures were pretty good. Very accessable outside of class and very helpful on everything. Homework is super hard but it makes the tests way easier (if you don't look up all the answers). Tests were very reasonable since he didn't ask any crazy questions.

His midterms match his practice ones but are MUCH easier than the common final. No curve/drops on midterms, but the class has an overall curve. Learned mostly from YouTube + skipped lectures. Weekly friday quizzes(very easy). To prep for common final, I went way more in depth than his midterms and challenged myself outside of what he taught.

LOVED Daping Weng and he had the best attitude. He would always work with students who had questions. Loved his weekly quizzes and only 2 exams for my course, took off weight of exams. he was super flexibe and light on homework

I thought he was a great lecturer at first, but he did not teach some of the hardest topics in the most intuitive ways. We were all entirely unprepared for the final. It was often unclear how in depth we needed to understand each topic, and it showed in the homework, final and recitation worksheets, which felt disconnected from our lectures

Dr. Weng is a nice guy, however, he is a very bad lecturer. He often gets too deep in the weeds and is bad at delivering the high-yield content. Only 2 midterms (instead of 3), and they are very similar to the practice midterms. The common final was MUCH harder and had content we did not cover, and went further in depth than we did in class.

He's not a bad professor, but I just feel like his lectures were rushed and not in-depth enough to even come close to preparing us for the final or Edfinity. Quizzes weekly. He was however nice and funny. It was hard to choose a rating for him. I attended and engaged in every lecture, yet still feel like I did 99% of my learning through youtube.

Dr. Weng is a middle-of-the-road professor. His midterms are very similar to the practice midterms. He does two (as opposed to three) and relatively easy weekly quizzes. But, he rushes through content and his explanations aren't always clear or complete. The level of depth at which he teaches won't adequately prepare you for the common-made final.

Calc 2 at UNC isn't fun no matter which professor you choose to take. However, if you can choose than I would for sure choose Dr. Weng to take calc 2 with. He moves pretty fast in lecture, often goes over multiple topics in a 50 minute class. Be aware though, he has quizzes every Friday except test weeks and the first Friday of the semester.

Daping Weng means very well. He is very sweet and will be there to help if you need it. His lectures are, however, not the most reflective of the required course material. I did a lot of self study and learning just to complete the assignments. I recommend you really put work in on recitation and homework because it helps in the end.
Good professor and made the concepts easy to understand. Pretty lenient grading if you put the work in. Definitely recommend for any math class.

He is a good professor, really good at explaining concepts and answers questions well, he really lets students practice a lot and doesn't just lecture for an hour, it is an extremely hard class so be prepared to dedicate hours to it, especially the edfinities that take forever to finish lol

Dr. Weng is great! He's very clear, posts notes, and holds office hours three times a week. Calc is hard, but Dr. Weng is a really good choice for this class. He doesn't post a homework schedule, because he reviews each homework assignment to make sure it's reasonable.

I mean it's a calc class, its going to be difficult, but the best prof ive had in the math department so far. New teacher, if you go to all the lectures and just actually try, you're fine. Lots of Edfinitys, sometimes its a but much, one due every mwf, but help outside class is available. I'd recommend.

Professor Weng makes the topics pretty simple to understand, even in a hard class like Calc 2. He moves very fast, but his midterms are fair and easy compared to the homework. Practice midterm is exactly like the midterms. Very funny and a nice guy. He does copy directly from the textbook, but gives many examples!

(Fall 25). Gregory is a really solid professor who is too smart to teach 231. He has an incredible fundamental understanding of math, but it can be confusing to learn at times. His tests were solid, but the final was very difficult. I'd take him compared to other bad Math profs at UNC or if your a math major, he's definitely qualified.
Sweet guy, genuinely wants you to do as well as possible. Also we had 2 home exams! Would recommend, especially for a second semester senior

Greg is a hilarious professor and his jokes made lectures entertaining. His teaching style wasn't for me (he tried to cover as many examples as possible rather than explaining what he was doing). This class is extremely test heavy, but he gives decent review sheets. At the end he changed the syllabus so everyone got the highest grade possible!

Dr. Forest is very funny and an open book. I think he truly wants his students to do well. His style was often rather chaotic, and this was sometimes frustrating. He releases a practice exam before any exam that he promises looks exactly like the test, and this is true sometimes even to the question.

One of my best classes ever. Although I had taken calc in hs this was a  much harder and required studying. He made sure to explain each concept and for our final exam he went through each students grades to adjust scores to make sure we got the highest grade we could also also rounded many people. Would 100% recommend taking calc 1 with him.
Really kind proferssor and I can tell how much he wants the students to get an A in this course, would love to take again!!!

Very nice person but very bad teacher. He uses no technology in class, and writes everything in chalk with not so great handwriting. He is better for those who are comfortable with their calculus skills, but if you are learning calculus for the very first time I DO NOT RECOMMEND. He does not curve his hard tests which sets us up for failure.

Very sweet man.. very hard class. I could definitely tell he was not used to teaching 231 because a lot of things did not make sense and he did a poor job explaining. Course moves very fast and it is quite easy to fall behind due to old school teaching style. Don't purchase textbook, it's free online. He does not have office hours-relies on TAs.
Bro let me take my final in his office for an extra 3 hours after I missed the first 2 purely because of my mistake. Absolute goat of a person. lectures are somewhat difficult to understand.
Very great professor for calc, would tell what's on exam, didn't try to stump and a great guy.

He seems like he knows what he's talking about, but I don't think he should be teaching introductory classes. I wish he would use technology more instead of scribbling on a chalkboard (with not the best handwriting i fear). It feels hard to keep up with him in his lectures. The only reason I've done well in this class is because I took calc in hs.

*This was for MATH 231*
Greg is the most caring professor I've had. He genuinely cares about the success of his students, and will work with you to make sure you succeed! You will probably have to put in effort outside of lectures to be successful, but he doesn't try to stump you. Take Calc with Greg!!!

TOOK MATH 231
Super sweet guy, lectures were pretty confusing, most people lacked understanding when tests came around. confusing test review materials.

Great professor and interesting classes, though sometimes hard to follow. Leaving this review because he changed the syllabus with three weeks left, requiring everyone to take the final—even though it previously stated the lowest exam out of all the midterms and the final exam would be dropped. Disappointing to see such a major change so late.

Great lecturer and a kind, funny person who genuinely cares about his students' success. His exams closely match the practice materials, so putting in the effort to complete them and check answers pays off.
This review is for 528. Just had one class with this guy. Giving 20/10 without hesitation. Best prof I've ever seen in UNC.

This review is actually for Math 528. Greg was wonderful, he genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. Exams are just like the practice but with different numbers. Our second midterm and 4/5 of the final was take-home. Do the work and you'll be fine. He's super approachable and accommodating! Overall great person and prof.

I've taken two classes with Greg. He is the most caring prof ive had, super accessible outside of class, and easy to talk to (about math or just to chat!). he wants his students to succeed. whatever he says is on the exam, will be on it, nothing more nothing less. his study guides very similar to the exam. very smart, great mentor. hes the best.

Good professor for an easy A but I felt like I was lacking more concrete knowledge of diff eq. Often learned shortcuts instead of how to actually do things which is good for those who don't need diff eq for other courses. Wish I was taught a bit more formally but I appreciate his approach to the course. Nice guy.

Greg Forest is the GOAT! His lectures were very straightforward, and his study guides were essentially the midterms. He would also walk you through the study guide before the test, so his test average was around an A. Also funny and was very approachable. If you need to take a class and he is teaching it, definitely take it with him!

I absolutely love Professor Canzani. She teaches in such intricate detail and genuinely cares about all her students. One time I did not do as well as I wanted on a midterm and she sat me in her office and went through the test with me and gave me a cookie. She is so sweet and caring and wants success for everyone. She pauses for questions as well.
Yaiza was one of my favorite professors last semester for calc 3. She was so nice and graded super fairly! Overall a great professor and person!

She truly cared about her students and wanted them to do well. She was very accessible outside of class. The material could be difficult, but with her lectures, the homework, and some outside videos you can do well in this class. The tests are all structured the same which is nice. Attendance isn't mandatory but definitely worth going.

Professor Yaiza is probably the best professor to take MATH 233 with. I took the launch version of the class, so it was a smaller class size. She was able to spend more time on certain concepts and made sure everyone fully understood what was going on. Definitely start studying for tests early!

i love yaiza!! i took the FC launch (smaller class ~30) and had such a close knit of classmates. initially it was a bit hard for me to understand her but that was only because of the fast pace of the class. we would finish a section or two of a unit a day so it was really important to put the work in outside of class. would def reccomend her.

Her lectures were informative although a little fast paced (I took pics of the board and rewrote my notes later). Her colorful chalk is actually a lifesaver while taking notes. I  recommend priming yourself with the content before you attend her lectures because it can get slightly confusing if that is the first time you're seeing the content.

Yaiza is genuinely the best professor at UNC. She cares so much for all of her students. She makes a hard subject easy and accessible with color-coded notes on the board and discussion based learning. She made sure everyone understood all the concepts and aren't just memorizing formulas. 10000% recommend taking a class with her if you can.

Yaiza is by far the best professor I've ever had at UNC. Not only are her lectures extremely clear and thorough, but she is always willing to answer questions- during class, at office hours, and even after class ends. She seems to genuinely care about her students' success in the course. 521 is extremely hard, but Yaiza made it so worthwhile!

Love Canzani! Had a bad prof for 381 so I didn't understand a lot of what I needed to know, and was expecting to have to retake, but her partial credit and lenient curve saved me. I really wanted to learn in this class, and her lectures are great and she cares abt every students understanding (even has meetings with struggling students to check in)

Yaiza is the most caring professor I've ever had- she really wants you to succeed in this class and is very accessible outside class (office hours/piazza). Her lectures are very clear and her board work is color coded, which makes lectures easy to follow. Though this the hardest course I've taken at UNC, I've enjoyed it with Yaiza.
Amazing prof. I hope I get to take another class with her. 521 is very difficult but she accommodated and was very caring.

A hard class, but Yaiza (and Jason) were great teachers for it. I've never seen such nice board work, she makes sure to color code really well. You can get away without practicing, but if you want to be sure for an A, definitely practice problems outside of homework. They're both active on Piazza so it's a great resource.

I don't think I've ever had(nor will I ever have)a professor care about their students the way Yaiza does. MATH 521 is probably the most difficult math class you will take at UNC but Yaiza made it so worthwhile. She always made sure that everyone in her class is doing what they need to do to succeed. I truly can't say enough good things about her.

MATH231-Sped through content and you can't understand w/o learning by urself.I stopped going bc its unhelpful.He'll push due dates if asked.The practice tests are similar to the tests/final,do them.He'll say if an answer is incorrect on tests and tell you how to fix it!would take him if youre going to learn by urself and use him to do good on tests

In my opinion, he's too smart to be teaching math 231, but I highly suggest taking calc with him. The class was very difficult as he teachers very quickly, and I had to do a lot of learning on my own. But he is SUPER helpful during exams (even the final), and will straight up tell you if your answers are incorrect. A really chill guy.
Dr. McLaughlin will make sure you understand the material. Though he'll push you to your limits, he really cares about his students and is super sweet. You can tell he really loves math.

Nice guy, but awful for lower-level math. Teaches way above Calc 2 level and teaches things we don't need to know. I stopped going to class—just used Khan Academy (Calc BC) and office hours, which saved me. He records lectures. He's flexible with homework and gives hints for exams, but they can still be tricky. Effort = extra points.

Lectures were very confusing and often unhelpful, especially when it came to the homework and common final. Midterms tracked pretty close to study problems but did not adequately prepare me for the problems on the final. Good with partial credit, extra credit, deadlines.

Really nice guy, willing to move homework deadlines back. Gives practice problems before midterms that are very similar to the actual test - but no answer key. His lectures aren't very helpful, he doesn't explain things very well and goes into a lot of complicated topics that you don't really need to know for the class.

Prof McLaughlin is a really nice person and wants everyone to succeed. He knows his students personally and is very lenient on midterm grading. His lectures were confusing as he tends to do more physics based problems and proofs of what we actually need to know. I learned more in my 50 minute recitation than I did in the 3 hours of his class.

I'm really grateful I took this class w Rich. His lectures weren't always the most helpful (and imo were easy to not be paying attention to) but his exams were very similar to the practice problem set that he provides prior to the midterms. Very caring, he adds bonus to each midterm and really wants everyone to succeed.

Pros: easy grader, nice guy, the exam is literally the practice exam and his lectures (just tweaked slightly), he doesn't try to trick you
Cons: lectures are hard to understand and disorganized, goes through the material very fast, not many resources available to help understand the material and doesn't give an answer key for his practice exams
Lectures can be a bit confusing but exams are very straightforward and exactly like the practice. He's very lenient with the partial credit. Super nice guy that wants you to do well.
Not a good lecturer. At all. Switched my major because I knew I wouldn't be prepared for 233. Nice guy, just did not like him as a professor. Everything was rushed and poorly explained.

He's a great guy, but not a very good/clear lecturer. This is a hard class in general, but he doesn't explain the concepts well and rushes through everything. He does record every lecture and is very good about pushing homework back if asked, but his exams are tough. He makes them harder than the final and teaches unnecessary topics "for fun."

Incredibly smart guy, and he's really lenient with homework extensions which is great. The biggest downsides are that his lectures are kind of unorganized, and he doesn't post notes or videos. Tests are really straightforward if you do the homework and practice exams though

Honestly my goat, he's awesome. Calc 2 is just a hard subject in general but he's a great lecturer with great energy. He records lectures, gives plenty of resources for exams, was flexible with homework due dates, and offers plenty of other ways to get your grade up. Overall great guy that genuinely wants to see you succeed.

In my opinion he is the guy you should take math with at UNC. Calc 2 is a difficult course but he makes his expectations very clear and exams are extremely fair. He genuinely wants every student to succeed and pass, so he allows for two different grading schemes to help with your score. Do yourself a favor and take his class.

Great person who understands the struggles of an undergrad, but if you actually want to learn in class, take it with another professor. He's not tech savvy and would spend a lot of lecture fixing mistakes in the notes, which were otherwise pretty comprehensive. Midterms were extremely easy, common final was evil. Must do outside revision!

Easy midterms, and amazing human, but not the most organized nor did he do an adequate job preparing us for the common final exam which is a lot harder than his midterms. Overall, I highly recommend him for kids repeating calc from high school, otherwise, you might want to find a more organized professor. But not to scare away all, he is very kind.

Awesome professor. Take advantage of office hours as he will take lots of time to help you understand concepts that may be hard to understand during lectures. You can tell he cares about all his students and genuinely makes an effort to help them succeed.

I struggled a lot with calculus in high school and I noticed a clear difference in my work with McCombs. He is a funny guy and really cares for his students. He will fight tooth and nail to make sure you get the most points possible on a test. Great professor and even better man.

Mark Mccombs has been one of my favorite professors, he is super funny and kind, but I did end up learning all of the class material on khan academy because I found it easier that way. There is no attendance required and the grading is 10% homework, and the other 90% on 2 midterms and 1 final. The exams have so much partial credit and he is great.
Good if you want things to be easy, but the course is super disorganized and confusing. Would not recommend if you want to actually learn anything. Easy to get a high grade, but nothing else is good

I took his section because of the great reviews on here, but I would never take him again. He is a nice person and means well, but we are extremely behind other sections and are so close to the final. Notes are inadequate, lectures are unhelpful and insufferable to sit through, and there aren't enough external resources/ practice supplied.

Not sure what most of these reviews are on about. Although he is a great person, his lectures are incredibly confusing. You can barely hear him, he goes on long tangents on unimportant topics, and he generally makes no sense. Although his midterms can be easier than other sections, this just means the common final will be atrocious for you.

Math diva with a dog! Makes calc so approachable. Please go to his office hours because he is super helpful and passionate and caring. He's not the best at explaining things, but he'll try very hard. We love the effort! And his stories!!

While the class wasn't hard besides the final, which tanked my grade, do not take him as your 381 professor if you need to take 521 after. I am coming back to write this review because it has made 521 nearly impossible to understand, because he did not prepare us at all to build off the material.

Mccombs is a very kind person. I found his lectures to be pretty unhelpful, so I skipped a lot. The best part of the class are the MyLab assignments; they allow multiple attempts, so I ended up teaching most of the course content to myself. PREPARE TO TEACH YOURSELF EVERYTHING.

He's very entertaining, but not good at teaching large lectures. He's amazing one-on-one. He takes ages to grade things. I didn't know my midterm grade until the week before the final. He cancels class at the last minute constantly.

McCombs is a genuinely great, warmhearted guy who wants his students to succeed! He often shares stories of his family, childhood, and dogs during lectures. There is a lot of work outside of class you need to do, though, since lectures alone aren't really enough to fully understand the material.

2 tests + final = 90% of your grade

McCombs is THE GOAT and famous. take him you won't regret it; He's known for his high heels that he wears one time in class... He cancelled class 3 times and that was really good. However, you will have to learn some stuff by yourself because all he does is go through a slide show and just explain what is done.
TAKE THIS CLASS, TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

McCombs is a nice person, but an inadequate teacher. He repeatedly canceled class hours or minutes before the beginning of the class and did not finish teaching us all of the units necessary for the final. If you have the option to take this class with a different professor, DO IT.

So nice. Lectures are pretty boring but they are straightforward. He cancels class from time to time and attendance is not mandatory.There are mylab homeworks for each unit, but they can be done in about 2 hours and they are due the night before the exam. There are only 2 tests which are simple/fair and then the final. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!!!

As a person, Professor McCombs is the best! As a professor, I found it hard at times to understand his teaching as he solves his work via talking it out, which isn't a good way for me to learn personally. Really nice guy, I think it depends on if you are able to meet halfway and learn portions from him, and self learn the rest yourself!

This man did not know this subject. He's probably great at other math concepts that he teaches, but he even said in lecture that he does not know this subject, and he has no idea what its purpose serves. I could go on, but I feel bad, he's a nice guy but for the love of GOD he should not teach this course.

if you don't have a religion, get one and pray. If you love listening to people yap about anything other than what you're supposed to be learning, he is fantastic for that! I had to teach myself everything, going to his class and attempting to follow his erratic lectures was a waste of time and money. Save yourself and take it with someone else.

Professor McCombs cares a lot about his students and their feedback. In fact, for this course, he even handed out a feedback form based on RMP feedback he recieved asking what kind of class format we preferred. Very clear and helpful and is always willing to work with students to help them understand and improve. Awesome professor!

Very engaging lecturer. There is a lot of content to get through so at times it feels a bit rushed, but Isaac is great at explaining the subject matter and provides review days before exams where students can ask questions and go over practice problems. Definitely recommend!

Isaac is the goat. Extremely passionate and engaging lectures that are easy to follow and he encourages asking questions. The material itself is pretty hard, but I understood almost everything because of the great lectures. Very accessible outside of class and has extremely easy "pop-quizzes."

As someone who already had precalc with Isaac i knew taking calc 1 with isaac was a must. He is a hidden gem at UNC and is great at explaining math even as someone who wasnt confident in their math skills going into college. You can feel the passion he has for teaching math despite not beind an actual professor yet.
Best Calc Professor EVER.

Isaac is great! I was doubtful on this being a flipped classroom at first but then I quickly loved it because it allowed students to ask as much questions as possible in class. Isaac 100% knows his stuff so never hesitate to go to one of his office hours. Lastly, he gives you a lot of partial credit on the midterms.

Isaac is a great option for 130. Genuinely cares about students' success and is super available through email and office hours. I got a B+ in 110 and an A in 130 and it's because of how good Isaac is. His style of teaching is pretty casual, but fast. However, I never felt like I couldn't ask a question or felt dumb for not knowing something.

Great guy. Moves a little fast during lectures but he wants everyone to succeed. His office hours are great. His tests are very fair, and he gives lots of partial credit. The Pearson homework can be pretty tricky but it doesn't weigh very much for your grade.

Isaac is by far the best professor I've ever had at UNC. He makes the course easy to learn, is super helpful when you have any questions, and genuinely cares about his students. Math doesn't come easily to me, but in this class it did. I couldn't recommend a class with him more!

This guy is AWESOME!!! Funny, caring, and is a great guy in general. I took his MATH 100 last semester and 130 this semester. He wants you to be good at math and fully understand the subject. I used to hate math, even having AP Calc under my belt, but he helped me enjoy math again! Call him Isaac and not Mr. Weiss :)

Issac was a great professor. While I struggled in the class, he always had office hours and was willing to meet with you whenever he was available. He genuinely cares about each student and wants them to succeed. You will do well if you go to class, take notes, go to office hours, and ask for help.

He does not explain the content very well. He moves very fast, and if you get a question wrong in class, he is insolent about it. His office hours are not helpful. We spend a day learning the material and move on to the next thing. For an introductory class, it was a bit much. The content is much harder on the exams than what was learned in class.

Isaac is amazing for Pre Calc, he makes the topics easy to understand and is super helpful especially during Learning Catalytics. He's eager to help and very knowledgeable, clearing up any concerns. If you do poorly on a midterm, the final can replace your lowest score. There are random pop quizzes, they're not graded harshly and can help guide you

Isaac is an amazing professor, definitely one of the best I've had at UNC. He's enthusiastic and knowledgeable and his lectures are informative and fun. I am not a math person at all but I really enjoyed taking calculus with him and I would 100% recommend him.

Might be my favorite instructor at UNC. Certainly my favorite graduate teacher. Lectures were extremely engaging and he never failed to make the class laugh. Issac obviously has a strong passion for math and he does a very good job demonstrating that and passing it onto his students.

Loved the class. He was funny and it was obvious he wanted to see you do well in the class. He found partial credit where he could and was amazing with providing grades fast. Would take any math class with him.

Isaac was a great instructor. For Math 130 being a flipped classroom he really made an effort to instruct the material and ensure that students understood. Exams are worth 75% of your grade so my best advice is to come to class, do the work, and turn in your work on time. If you do that 100% is achievable in the other 25% of the class.

Professor Weiss is incredibly knowledgeable about math in general and he is more than willing to help you if you need. He is very funny and relates well to his students. The math department is kinda bad overall but Professor Weiss looks out for his students and will let you know weeks in advance if there is something you need to know.
Isaac was a great teacher, was overqualified to teach math130 but still did a great job of explaining concepts. Take him
He's the goat. All there is to say.

I really enjoyed recitation with him, even though some of them were very difficult. He is funny, willing to help, and easy to talk to. Fun fact, I believe he has like 10 pets. Definitely recommend him.

Greg is so nice, accessible, and passionate but seemed to overestimate our math abilities, esp on MT 2. MTs avgd 64, 51 -> curved to Cs. It was just demotivating to take such tough exams lol. Overall on par for unc math: a rewarding class without any coddling/hand-holding. But the final was easier and he offered a project for +5 EC on course grade!

hardest class ive ever taken at unc and hardest class i will ever take. lectures make no sense, he doesnt post any notes or anything at all, all the other classes had multiple choice exams but ours were 6 proofs, graded SUPER harshly, exams worth 85% of your grade. im very sorry if you have late registration like me and have to take him-- good luck
Don't let bro cook ever again, for the sake of humanity and future generations of students to come.

Genuinely the worst class I've taken at UNC. I'm a math major and have taken math 521 which is considered to be the hardest math here and this class is still by far the hardest one I've taken so far. Lectures don't make sense and are all over the place and exams are just so unreasonable. Very upset because this is going to bring my GPA down

Midterms are hard but reasonable. Ended up teaching myself everything, but still had to come to lecture to see what stuff is relevant and not from the textbook. Terlov is a really smart dude, but aint nobody keeping up with what he's saying in class. +5pts Extra credit offered...wish he just made the tests easier.

Honestly hurts to see so many bad ratings because I genuinely thought he was a great professor that cared about seeing people do well. Fairly easy course up until you get into multivariate but if you have a bit of time to study and go to office hours you'll do fine. I thought his lectures were also very helpful though not many people came.
Read and practice with the textbook if you want to understand anything. His lectures are extremely disorganized and his homework assignments are not helpful at all for the exams.
Don't expect a decent grade
Very disorganized lectures. We had a sub teach two classes and I genuinely understood more from his two days than every lecture from Greg combined.
so disorganized. just rambles on about complex proofs during lecture. i genuinely don't think i learned anything from this class.

Greg is passionate, but he's not the best teacher. My favorite lectures were with guest lecturers because I could understand what was going on and why I should care. His grading is an exercise in banging your head against the wall since you have to assume the grader is braindead and write significant prose to get points rather than just solving.

Better read the textbook than attend his lectures, which somehow makes more sense. Even then, you're not surviving the exams because he "Hates multiple choice questions" and loves to throw curveballs on the free responses.
He had a substitute teach us for the second to last week of classes. The substitute taught me more in one day than Dr. Terlov taught me all semester.

His teaching style involves reciting the textbook very poorly and very quickly.  Sets unrealistic expectations for exams and pays no attention to where his students actually are. You are better off reading the textbook directly than attending his lectures.

Incredibly difficult midterm 2. One of the hardest I have ever taken. He allows a cheat sheet but these exams certainly favor the math majors in terms of required intuition and problem solving experience. Be very smart about how you prepare.
Lectures are disorganized. Very hard to follow. Tests are designed to trick you. Focuses more on a complex problem set up than actual probability concepts.

Lectures are hard to follow due to the fast pace. The professor pauses for questions, but most students seem too unsure to ask, so it doesn't help much. Concepts move on before they fully sink in. Slowing down and spending more time reinforcing key ideas would make the class more effective.
accuses everyone of using chatgpt on homework and not studying because of bad exam grades. very disorganized lectures. take with someone else

On our second midterm, he gave a question that he briefly talked about in class before our very first midterm. It was an interview question for one of his past students. His explanation after the exam was confusing. Don't take this class, take another section.
His lectures are very confusing and hard to follow. The homeworks are manageable but the second midterm was very difficult, questions written in ways we had never seen before.

90% of the class grade is calculated from midterms and the final exam. All multiple choice exams so no partial credit. Homework is required but does not grade the assignment so you cannot tell how you are doing outside of exams.
90% of the grade is exams. Lectures do not prepare you for the exams.

90% of grade is tests, no notecard and a lot to memorize. The beginning was easy but it got a lot more difficult. The tests are easier than the HWs and practice. She put a lot of emphasis on proof in her lectures instead of application (not helpful for MC tests). up to +4% extra credit and a small curve at the end

Dr. Huang teaches and links concepts well, but she overestimates students' computation skills, so the lecture can be hard to follow. Lectures can be better paced to increase attendance. Contents are pretty hard, but her tests are fair and much easier than hw in terms of high-level thinking. Providing more basic prob and calc practices should help.

Hard class, have some exposure to probability/stats or this is going to suck. Gives really hard tests (all MCQ) but makes up for it by offering 4% of EC to your overall grade. Must do more problems beyond homework/classwork for practice, since there are so many topics covered we do not go over all relevant examples in assigned work.

Generous weighting and extra credit are blessings. She honestly provided good explanations and solidly attempted to engage our uninterested class. Your experience will likely be determined by previous exposure to the material. I'd imagine Zoe is the best option for 435 and would be excited if she was the average teacher in the STOR department.

Exams are worth 75% of your grade, so do not mess up. She gives 4% extra credit at the end, which was a little bit helpful. Lectures are pretty difficult to follow, so I recommend reading the textbook. Do not leave studying to the last minute and do a bunch of practice problems. Exams are all MC.

very difficult. practice every day. tons of stats majors and they bring up the average bc they have done stats before. i have no stats experience. this class was so difficult for me bc i did not have the time to sit down and practice. take this class with max 2 chill classes bc this one will be your priority. exams are all mcq (cries)

Very sweet.class is really hard. She explains stuff well but if you have never had any stats experience, it is really hard to keep up in class and it will probably take you hours longer to understand a problem than someone who has done stats before. its a completely new way of thinking that requires a TON of practice. read the textbook b4 lecture

1st midterm, 18 questions MCQ. Not difficult but if you have never taken a stats class, you NEED TO PRACTICE A TON. I am a math person and got a 56. It wasn't hard but it was just too much for the time. Practice, practice, and practice every waking moment you have. The hw is not enough, open the textbook and do everything. Find more probs online.

Clear schedule, clear lecture notes. U don't need to go to the lecture if u understand all the homework and lecture notes. There's also extra credit added to the final grade on midterms like 0.5%. I didn't get any grade yet but bro rescheduled the midterm to next week, which is huge for me bc otherwise I will have 3 midterms this week on 2 days lol

HWs were manageable, and tests were not too bad. The final is worth 45% of your grade, so make sure you don't mess up. Don't know if she even curved it towards the end, but the 3% EC she offered definitely helped. If you practice from the textbook you'll be absolutely fine, and the MCQ format for the tests help as well.

She tends to give about one homework assignment a week, which is very manageable. Her exams are multiple choice and are in many ways easier than the homeworks, so as long as you pay attention in class and go over the content in the homeworks and lecture slides you'll be fine. Be aware that difficulty ramps up significantly after the first exam.

this class isn't that bad... i would recommend not going to class and just doing reading from the textbook and doing the practice problems. i got a B+ but couldve pulled off an A if I didnt sell on the final

I went to a few classes before realizing she lectured pretty much directly from the textbook. However, this is not a bad thing -- it gives you the full freedom of whether you would rather read the textbook or go to lecture (I never went to lecture). She is very nice and the exams were quite easy (you can't really make a super hard MCQ stor exam).
She's super nice, but RUN. Midterms and final are hell.

Really nice professor. Homework is easy (takes like an hour to do each week). Exam are tough but fair. Study hard and you will at least get a B. If you put in the work, A range is definitely attainable.

Taking class 24F. If you are good/talented in math, take it. If not, consider others. Her class is full of proof with had nothing to do with exam. Exam based on textbook, so BUY IT and go over textbook before exam. Her practice exam is JOKE, no connection with exam. If you are not good with math, RUN. Did give 3% free EC. not sure with curve yet

Lectures were focused on proofs/theorems, but tests (which made up 75% of the grade) were entirely based on applications. To succeed, you have to do textbook practice problems on your own. She provided several extra-credit opportunities and was very accessible during office hours to explain HW (which was the main workload on a weekly basis).

Kind and approachable person who is accessible, definitely take advantage of that; class was WAY harder than it should have been. Lectures: extremely hard to follow, and it often felt like she didn't know how to teach the material. The content taught barely matched the midterms, if it weren't for the practice exams I would have failed the class.

Ms. East was very sweet. She genuinely cares for the success of her students. However, I feel like her teaching style was not the best, as lessons were not always taught in a clear manner. I feel concepts could have been explained better in a simpler way; it sometimes would feel overly complicated. Her practice exams were very helpful!

She's very quirky and a fun professor, gives a lot of extra credit and is very understanding about test dates, and when to make things due. However, not the best teacher she writes how to do things, not why she's doing it. Overall, the lenience she had balances out the teaching

Felt significantly underprepared. She was accessible outside of class, but was always behind on lectures with rushed complex content! A nice person, but this class was extremely difficult. Still inexperienced. Appreciated how she supported the class. Caution taking this class though. Take the good and bad ratings with a grain of salt.

She's genuinely one of the most loving people I've ever met. I would absolutely take the class again, but I just think she could benefit her lecture with a bit more structure, with clearer resources and more practice exercises.

Prof East is one of the most caring professors I've ever had, she teaches really well, she is mostly organised and super adaptable. If you're gonna take 110, take it with her, she actually understands what it's like to be a student and she's flexible, considerate and has the best dad jokes. She's such a sweetie

Extremely inexperienced when it comes to teaching. She grades very harsh and unfair, will take off multiple points for small mistakes. She does not allow you to discuss any exam grades with her. She has terrible handwriting, making lectures difficult to understand. Does not take anything serious, she found it funny that her class average was 70%.
I don't know guys. I wouldn't take a class with her again. I lowkey regret my decision taking this class.

Professor East is a very open minded and caring teacher who tries her best to make a fast paced summer course feel manageable.Very understanding of students' varying math backgrounds and acknowledges that even an "easy" class like Math 110 can be challenging due to outside circumstances.  The Dad jokes be hitting too sometimes lol.

Angela is clearly caring and wants us to do well, but is still a bit inexperienced with teaching. While she will help you outside of class hours, sometimes her lectures aren't super clear. She tells jokes and wants us to enjoy math but just needs to figure out some stuff. Also, for some reason math 110 seemed unnecessarily hard.

I took this class before and hated it, but Angela genuinely made math class fun! She tells awful dad jokes and is charming. She really cares about your success and has so many office hours sessions available. She explains things in a way beginning math students can comprehend, so she's perfect to teach this course! 10/10 would take again.

Lectures were not very helpful as he would just copy examples from the textbook onto the board and expects us to know everything. Even though he was a pretty nice guy, I would NOT recommend taking him for discrete. Classes are very disorganized, and you are honestly better off self-learning. The homework's were also graded pretty harshly.
Bro it was so haed to underrstand the writing bro

I took in Spring 2025, and I believe it was his first time teaching. He was not very confident at the front of the room, and he could be somewhat condescending at times. He was late to his own office hours and at times wouldn't show up. He grades the homework strict but drops the lowest 2, and the class was curved. I would avoid taking it with him.

Nice guy but harsh grader. He took off points easily by a few things, and homework were harshly graded. Final was not easy as agreed. It's hard to get decent grade in his class although he curved the boundary.

Nice guy, horrible teacher. Unorganized lectures, unclear expectations of students, no resources for success. HARSH grader - doesn't accept certain proofs even if they're correct in the textbook. Was late multiple times to his own office hours. DO NOT TAKE DISCRETE WITH HIM. but he is willing to work with students.

He was an okay professor for discrete, but sometimes seemed confused on what he was teaching or by simple questions students asked. A very tough grader and doesn't accept methods other than what was taught in class (even if its in the textbook/still correct). Office hours are slightly helpful for explanations.

Lectures can be a little dry sometimes, and the time would be better spent going over textbook yourself at certain points in the class. The class can be pretty hard but eventually becomes pretty easy. It was also pretty hard to do well on the homework assignments. He's a genuine guy despite that, and made sure we know how to write good proofs.

He was not super great at communicating what we NEEDED to learn during lectures and seemed to focus more on what he felt like teaching versus what would be on the overall (professor determined) final exam

This professor and his class was difficult and I've taken calculus before. Tests are 45% of your grade and I'm struggling to get an A No offense but his accent is very strong and I cant understand him sometimes. He also makes many mistakes in his examples and TA's have to help or even students.

The professor was extremely hard to understand. Often rushed through notes and never went through them to allow students to fully understand the concepts. The professor was only worried about getting through the entire syllabus for the exams (which are heavily weighted). Extremely kind and understanding guy, but not the best teacher :(

Truthfully, I did not enjoy a single class period of his. We either had boring lectures where I regretted showing up or times he didn't even show up... I spent most of the time teaching myself the material. He doesn't respond quickly to emails, provides little feedback, and overall, is just disorderly. Fair tests were the only good thing.

Lectures are a little fast and he assumes you know stuff that he hasn't taught often. Seems like he would be a great prof for higher level math but not the best for the basics. Exams are very fair and cover the same kinds of problems that we did in class. Lowest midterm gets replaced by the final.
Good class and good professor.

MATH 383 is difficult regardless of the professor, but I think Tamim made the content as understandable as possible. I felt like my midterms were graded harshly, and some homework was difficult, but I was always able to get help.

Wonderful professor, gives clear explanation for all concepts. Cares about his students, very accommodating. Class is not difficult if you engage with the material, do the homework, and practice problems. There is nothing on exams that is not covered in class; very straightforward, I got a 100% on every exam. Lowest exam grade replaced w/final.

Great for a math prof. Got an A. Let us replace our lowest test score with our final if it was higher. TONS of resources available for outside of class (i.e. practice problems, so if you do all of the practice you'll do well on exams). Never puts anything on the exams that we haven't covered in class with practice problems or in previous exams.
I was crying after leaving this class.  His political based problems and Naruto problems cracked me up!
amazing class loved his naruto problems!
meh class i guess.

Saiful moves kind of quickly through the material, but he explains things well. Tests weren't easy but they weren't too difficult either (not actually a big step up from homework), especially since we were given a one-page cheat sheet for each exam. Definitely recommend taking advantage of the textbook practice problems he gives for exam prep.

Tamim is a very genuine professor and his class is pretty manageable even with a hard course load. His exams are doable but do require some studying if you want to do well. Highly recommend him for 383.

Saiful is a great lecturer and teaches 383 very well. It can be fast if you aren't well-rooted in previous math classes, but it is still doable. He is nice, pretty funny, and considerate. It is best to go over lecture notes and provided worksheets to study for his midterms and finals. The tests are hard and worth a lot of your grade, study.

Tests make up almost all of your grade, and he doesn't do a very good job of presenting what will be on the test in class. Lots of people say he is a good lecturer, but he mumbles a lot. Doesn't give many resources to study, and the homework and textbook problems don't adequately prepare you for the tests, which are typically 4-5 questions.

If you are at all good at math then there is no need to attend. He provides about a worksheet per class, combine reading his posted class notes for 5 minutes a day and solving the worksheet, you will do very well and save several hours per week.

Tamim is a good professor and gives great lectures and is also very engaging in class. He wants the students to understand the material. But if you care for your grade, I do not recommend him. His exams are harder than the worksheets and review material he gives but he is a great lecturer so you will learn the concepts if you attend class

Explains the content well but the exams and homework problems are much more difficult than what we go over in class. Many worksheets and MyLab's to complete. If you care about your grade, you may want to consider another teacher.

Saiful was excellent at explaining the concepts clearly, and the class moves at a great pace. There are two exams which are difficult to finish within the 50 minutes. However, the final exam was rather easy and you have plenty of time for it, and it can replace your lowest midterm. Definitely recommend for diff eq!

If u are the type of student who depends on good explanations, take this professor. He explains things super well. However, his exams in 50 minutes were brutal and rushed. Final was super easy. Really great lecturer, goes at a good pace and explains everything really clearly. Only downside is that his final grading scale was not very clear, nor were our final grades released, only saw our grade in Connect Carolina at the end.
I had a good experience in MATH 523 and MATH 524 with him last year. He sincerely cares about his students and offers lectures clearly with extra credits in all exams. Highly recommended!

Great professor! He explained complex topics in understandable ways, which reflected in high class averages for all exams. For reference, my midterm scores were 102 and 96, with final exam 100. Govanni is really understanding. If the class doesn't understand a certain topic, he is willing to walk us through step by step. (Summer) Soft-spoken prof. Great penmanship. Aware students are busy and gives HW accordingly. Teaches at a steady pace (and goes over many examples). Straightforward exams (avgs typical for the course and dependant on you doing practice problems to reinforce concepts). Slight curve.

Dr. Granados is a great professor. Super clear, patient, and fair. He explains things well and actually wants you to learn. Exams match the lectures, and he's easy to talk to. Definitely take him if you can.

Chill and demure. Nice grader, very lenient. I got a perfect score on one of the midterms while shitting my pants right before the exam. Professor Granados is great. He's super good at explaining concepts and logic, especially when linking materials from different parts of the semester together. He's very accessible outside of the classroom and is absolutely willing to help.

Dr. Granados delivers clear, well-structured lectures and designs fair exams (with extra credit) that aren't meant to trick you. Made my last semester at UNC learning complex analysis truly enjoyable.

Govanni is the GOAT! Taking Complex Analysis with him is enjoyable and interesting. Besides, he truly cares about his students and all exams are fair and lecture related. Homework is very helpful for the test. I would love to take more math classes with him in the future.

He's a great guy and teaches very well, with great tests. Easy to get an A in the class if you do all your homework and study well. Lectures were worthwhile to go to, and online resources also taught in similar ways to this professor. Everyone should try to get him for MATH 381.

He was my favorite professor last semester. He is a great option if you want to actually learn the material AND want to get a good grade. He is willing to help answer questions for anything and clearly wants his students to succeed. His tests were very fair and went over material we had learned.

Literally my favorite person ever! definitely do discrete w him because he is so kind and goes super slow in lecture so you have time to actually process what he is doing. Fav math prof at UNC for sure.

Dr. Granados is extremely knowledgeable about discrete and is super helpful in office hours. I would definitely recommend a class with him. He's the goat. Didn't go to most of the class but when I did he was great.

He is very a caring man but he is very knowledgeable of stats (which is a good thing), but he tends to go off topic and explains too much that is not necessary to know which can make things very confusing at times. Professor Smith is very kind and I can tell he loves what he does and his students. However, this was one of the hardest classes I have taken. Prof Smith is a very genuine guy, but class was quite difficult. Lectures were confusing at times and hard to follow along. One homework a week. 3 Labs for extra credit. Exams make up 85% of grade. Content was theory heavy, and more difficult than some other Diffeq classes, but Pedro lectured well, and cares a lot about his students. Rounded up grades, and final was heavily curved. final paper was graded too harshly with a presentation we were forced to do but didn't count towards our grade.

Calc 2 at UNC is difficult but professor Saenz did everything in his power to help his students succeed. the class is quite hard but otherwise HIGHLY HIGHLY RECCOMEND PEDRO FOR CALC II IF POSSIBLE
Pedro's a great professor. He clearly cares about his students learning and made a difficult class enjoyable. Take a class with him if you get the chance

Pedro was so kind, funny, and understandable during lectures! He explained most of the concepts pretty well and I thought his grading policy was very fair. Attendance is not required for lectures but it is for the weekly recitations, since there is a quiz at the beginning of each one.
Calc 2 is gonna be a hard class no matter how you frame it, but Pedro is a very kind teacher and has good lectures. I would chose him for my math classes again.

I love Pedro! I have friends in all other sections of 232 & Pedro is by far the best prof. He was a great professor, very kind and gives lots of partial credit

This class is extremely hard, no way around it. But if I had to take it with anyone it would be him, he's very nice and seems to understand that not everybody is going to be passionate about calc. Dr. Saenz is a good professor but the class is extremely hard!

Professor Saenz is very laid-back and passionate about math. His lecture notes were clear and understandable. From the very first lecture, he made it obvious that he cares about his students and wants them to do as well as possible! He is very enthusiastic about math and I would definitely recommend him for MATH 232 as he is very generous with grading exams.

Prof. Davis is has really educational lectures and goes at a good pace. He also is very understanding and posts all his lecture in case you miss anything. Took for MATH 233 during summer school. He gave very precise, cogent lectures. I now feel that I could teach anything that he taught me.

Discrete math was not easy, but he made this class very manageable. He was a wonderful professor that cared for his students. Class is extremely boring. Not hard to get a good grade because there is a heavy curve and bonus for in-class quizzes. Homework takes a lot of time

Nice guy who is obviously very smart. Tests weren't bad and were curved. Homeworks could be tricky but he helps a ton in office hours. A lot of homework, the exam is difficult, the class is not clear, not recommended

Dr. Liu is a GREAT prof. He rescheduled two exams to fit classes needs, includes extra credit, and has great lectures. He is hilarious, and very good at explaining concepts. Highly recommend taking. If you pay attention, you will get an A.

Professor Liu is very caring and understanding. I struggled a bit for the exams but if you show up to class, pay attention, and start studying early you'll be fine.

Dr. Liu is a very great lecturer who explains thing pretty well. His midterms and individual part for the final exam are easy. amazing professor and lecturer, plus hes pretty cute and has a nice accent

holy what a mess...............

If you are willing to teach yourself the whole entire lesson again this professor is for you, he writes on the board and does not provide explanations, his grading wasnt the best, if you don't follow his exact way of solving the problem but still find the correct answer...immediate points off.

I'm not passing the class at this point, but learned a great deal on approaching heavy courses and fast-paced instructors, definitely! Difficult class but the teacher is willing to help.

He's a great prof.He is very clear and very helpful during office hours, also willing to answer questions during class. I believe the other ratings are because it was he's first time teaching but I had him this semester and he is the opposite of what people are describing.He's one of the better ones.He's exam were clear,just make sure you practice.
Classes are a waste of time. Terrible teacher with no skill or passion for teaching. I had to hire a tutor. Don't take this class.

He is a nice guy, but the class disorganized. The lectures were hard to follow and there was a lot of homework. The tests were somewhat difficult. He is nice and does pretty good, the class is just fast paced and can be hard. I have a lot trouble with math like many people in the class.

He is a nice guy, but isn't a good teacher. His lessons are sometimes disorganized and he breezes over a lot of topics because we "should've learned it in HS". He does give extra credit on tests. He isn't the worst, but I wouldn't take him again.

Nice guy but overall he seems like he hasn't taught a day in his life. When you ask him to re explain he just says, "we learned this last time." The tests are much harder than what we do in class. He is a nice guy, but his teaching honestly makes me more confused about topics I already know. I would be better off staying home and reading the textbook than going to his lecture.

Can't read his hand writing on the board. He over teaches concepts and makes it harder to understand what he is teaching. He also doesn't teach what is on the homework or tests. Overall, I would never take him again!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Dr Foster is great! Super funny and charismatic, makes lectures entertaining. Goes really fast and is sometimes hard to follow. The class content is difficult but Dr Foster does a great job of preparing you for exams. Homework was unreasonably hard and couldn't do any of it without outside help. Still a good experience and great professor.

I love this man. He explains concepts thoroughly and goes through several examples every class. Don't miss class, pay attention, and go to the review sessions! The EdFinity HW was much harder than the exams, so I usually ChatGPTed it. His practice midterms and final are more accurate to the difficulty of the exams.

Dr. Foster is the kindest teacher! He gives out candy at review sessions and helps students as much as he can. He gives very helpful study guides for everything. The tests are very difficult, but if you study with the study guides, you will be ok. The lectures are hard to keep up with, but he is very funny. If you take this class, take it with him!

To preface, I'm not the strongest math student and Prof. Foster's lectures were quite stale but you you tell he's an enthusiastic individual and passionate about math. He didn't use guided notes and would often introduce a new topic and then run through examples on the chalkboard until the end of class so don't make it a habit to miss class.
Genuinely my goat. He's so funny and I loved going to class. Hadn't taken a math class in over a year and I had a great time. Very fair exams and engaging lectures, normal amount of homework.

I LOVE ALEX FOSTER! He is such an amazing professor and all around guy. He teaches very well and while attendance isn't mandatory, you'll definitely miss a lot if you don't go. Does every lecture on the chalkboards which makes it a lot easier to learn, though sometimes methods other than his are simpler.

Amazing professor. He is very enthusiastic and excited about math. Overall, his lectures are informative and engaging. Things do move a little fast so you need to study on your own a bit. Attendance is not required but highly recommended as you will miss a lot of material and class isn't recorded. You do need to attend recitations though.

One of the best professors I've ever had in terms of teaching the material. Provides definitions, gives quick and easy to understand conceptual background, works through an example, lets the class do an example, then goes over it. It's crazy how you don't often come across professors like him who actually understand how people are meant to learn.
His enthusiasm for math rubs off on you and makes it easy to learn! Classes move fast (as with all other 231 professors), so be ready to learn

Prof Foster is a hilarious guy. Clearly he had a passion for math, even though not many students in the classroom matched his energy. If you study enough and go to his study sessions you can get an A on the exams. He's sometimes underprepared though like not having the midterm the night before the exam.
Great fella

Really nice dude, and you can tell that he loves math. No recorded videos or slides so be ready to attend class and take notes. Lectures consist of brief introduction to new material, followed by lots of practice problems. Exams aren't bad as long as you pay attention in lectures and do the homework. He's a funny guy, which makes class enjoyable.

Professor Foster taught efficiently, preparing students for success on midterms and the final. His lectures were all on chalkboards, resulting in a perfect pace for taking notes. Instead of bogging the lectures down with proofs, he provides many examples. Students with an aptitude for math will easily succeed in this class.

Fun teacher and seems excited to teach which is refreshing. Very helpful during office hours. As someone else mentioned, he does not record lectures. My only complaint is that the most difficult material was crammed into the last couple weeks. Generally good and well organized instructor with reasonable midterms.

Alex was super engaging in lecture and helpful in office hours. I also thought the exams were very fair. Homeworks were also pretty challenging, but super nice guy and so passionate!

Actually had him for 233, but it wasn't listed. His lectures were great! He was funny and engaging, and really good at explaining difficult concepts in an understandable way. The HWs were sometimes hard, but the midterms were very fair and based on the review materials. He even brought candy to the review sessions :)

233 not listed BUT anyway great teacher. Very passionate about the subject and is able to teach super complex topics very well, incredibly well-liked. Sometimes got a bit sidetracked but it was interesting. I had conflicts with all office hours, he was easy to communicate with and set up other times with so I could get my questions answered!

Calc 1 is tough, no matter how you slice it. Dr. Foster went the extra mile to help us succeed; he even made review papers for each exam. His lectures are humorous, with tangents that provide brain breaks necessary to digest everything. Midterms were fair, and homework was challenging but excellent study material. His class is study hard, play hard

I loved Alex! He made the material super easy to learn and in a quirky way. He was super sweet and held review sessions for all the midterms and final. The homework was time-consuming and extremely difficult buttttt the midterms and final were significantly easier. He also replaced our lowest midterm grade with our final if we did better!!

Her way of teaching makes it extremely harder for me to understand. My tutor does a better job. Questions on exams are COMPLETELY DIFFERENT to the material we learn in class. I was acing all of the quizzes (one every week) and getting 10/10 but then on the exam only a 30/100. Do not take a class with her!!!

She is a very good person and offers lots of resources like offices hours. If you have trouble her office hours are very helpful. Tests are graded harshly but so is every math class here. Logan means well but the test are incredibly difficult and are far harder than the given study guides and practice problems. Harsh grading and there were questions on the final that we had never even covered in class. Do not take her if you care about your GPA.

I came here to make JUSTICE to the name of this woman!!! LOGAN'S CLASSES ARE THE BEST ONES IN MY WEEK, with her, math just comes naturally, there's no way!!!!!!!

Don't take this class if you don't want a terrible grade. Gray cares about her students & is a good person, however she's a terrible teacher. Be prepared to teach yourself & take tests on the concepts that weren't even taught.
Would never take again. Screwed my GPA for business school.
Avoid like the plague. Allegedly obsessed with teaching, but is just so bad at it it's embarrasing.  Also on a weird power trip all the time.

I found Logan's lectures extremely hard to follow and had to teach myself most of the material for the final exam. Tests were awfully graded. Logan read off of her notes instead of focusing on genuine teaching leading her to explain things in an awful manner. Logan is a good teacher professor but quite harsh compared to other math130 professors. Logan Gray test were harder than what she prepped for you. You must set aside a lot of time in order to do well in this class. Logan is so nice and broke down the material really well. Also her tests were pretty easy in my opinion. Def take pre-calc with her if you can!
Logan is very nice and always helped when I reached out for assistance.

Their lectures are quite dry and they don't explain the topics too well. I will say that they try their best and are accessible outside of class by email and in person. The tests are not too difficult but it ultimately depends on how you utilize the homeworks to study (do it!) and don't bother with the TAs (they're no help).

WORST TEACHER!  80% of your grade is the tests/final, and considering his inability to teach, the class average on almost every test was a D. Worst teacher ive ever had - spare yourself.

The semester started off really rough, but he progressed in his teaching a little over time. I did not learn anything from his lectures; basically taught myself everything. The notes he would write on the board were pretty useful tho.

He sucks... all of his midterms have a D average, these exams are worth 50% of your final grade; he offers no extra credit or corrections. no one ever knows what he is talking about and he does not teach material that is aligned with the course requirements.

It was clear that he had not taught for long, as he struggled a lot early on. His teaching got better over time, and he has office hours sections where he will sit and explain material to you. The first midterm was incredibly easy. The second midterm was a lot harder, but still chill if you study hard. Final is demonic, but he curves accordingly.

Tiger is a really funny and patient professor! He is very approachable and wants all students to do well in his class, but sometimes his explanations were hard to follow. I left this class most days understanding the material! He starts with easier content and then builds on it so we have the foundation to understand harder concepts. Office hours and in-class questions were available and very helpful. The second midterm and final were more challenging than the first test, but he curved generously at the end. The textbook aligns well with the course material and is a useful reference

At the begining of this class he did not really know how to teach well, but as the class went on he got better. There are 3 exams, homework due usually every Wednesday and a final. Terrible teacher don't take if u want to learn
