Literally the longest hw assignments I have ever done. Took 5-7 hours to complete a problem set. Exams were take-home and also took about 5-6 hours to complete. That being said, things were graded very easily, and the class taught a lot of useful techniques in R.

Terrible lectures, but self-studyable. Prepare to spend 5-7 hours on each homework, of which there are 6. Attendance gave +2 pts of extra credit, an A is 93/105, and final was curved by 20 pts, so it wasn't hard to get an A.

This is a time-consuming class, the homework (total of 6) will each spend more than 6-8 hours to do. However, the midterms are take-home and the final is opem-internet. So it is easy to get a good grade, I never showed up in class but still got a 99 out of 105.

Didn't go to class (only on first day and maybe once) and got an A. Midterms are take home and open note. Homeworks are long but not hard if you spend some time on it. Not really sure his teaching style but the one or two times I did go his lecturing didn't seem to make much of a difference in understanding homeworks and exams. Overall chill class

Extremely easy grader. Never went to class and got a 97. long homeworks that took me about 7-8 hours but they are only biweekly so its honestly pretty fair. expect to self learn but midterms were online and the final was open internet.

Be ready to teach yourself everything about R and regressions. However, he is a good guy and it's not hard to get an A (93/105) if you put some effort finishing heavy homework on time. The exams are open book and much easier than homework, and often have some extra points.
he is a nice guy .heavy accent though so cannot understand what he is talking about .but midterms and final are good because they are open -book

Lectures are irrelevant and deeply confusing, they truly make little to no sense.  Be prepared to teach yourself how to code in R. The homework takes hours to do in coding that he does not teach in class. Rejected the request to give examples in class that better fit the homework. I would not take again and I regret taking it this semester.
Needs to curve the exams or idk what's gonna happen.
what can i say....
a good guy but a hard course

If you want endless homework, lectures that make zero sense, and your midterm 1 grade still missing after midterm 2… this class is for you! Grading speed? Snail pace. Clarity? Nonexistent. Save yourself the pain and take literally anyone else.

Writing this the mid-completing one of the ridiculous homework assignments for this class. The lectures are extremely boring and rarely relevant to the homeworks. Prepare to learn R on your own. Very condescending when asked if we could start doing examples in class that actually relate to the homeworks. Avoid.

I barely pay attention in class and still have an A. I'll admit the homework was complicated as hell, but the midterms aren't too bad especially since they're take home. Plus he grades everything super leniently.

The lectures at 9am is mandatory but really hard to catch up with. Professor Ray is a nice guy after class, but he is such a genius that all the material is more difficult than the other professors'. The homework is super beyond average students' ability too, usually taking more than 5-10 hours to complete.
Disorganized lectures and super hard homework. Rather drop and take it with someone else next semester.9

Super generous curve on everything. That being said he teaches so abstract and theoretical so be wary of that. He is the type of guy who can design the tiktok algorithm from scratch but have trouble explaining to you a linear equation. Easy A though.

Prof Ray is definitely an extremely intelligent guy but he's honestly just not meant for teaching. His lectures are extremely boring/stale and only 10 people show up. That being said, the course content itself is extremely self study-able. Also gave us around a 20 point curve on every homework and exam and the entire class is out of 107 percent.

The professor had issues throughout the semester to be interactive and involved in the class. Easy overall, can study on your own and obtain a good grade, but be weary of his method of teaching, it isn't very engaging.

I had Dr. Wells for Spring 25 and he was a fair professor. Even though I did not get an A I think it is doable for math oriented people. His exams were similar to practice exams. I wish I had went to his office hours more because he was pretty helpful! Attendance isn't mandatory but I recommend going to class anyway.

Easiest 381 professor. If you want an A just take this guy. Biggest cornball ever though. The way he erases the chalkboard makes me crack up every time. Tests are super easy because he gives you practice tests that are just like the actual test. Final was the only thing that was hard. Tips for success: read the textbook and watch Kimberly Brehm!

he wasn't the best lecturer so i spent a lot of time studying the material on my own. his tests are very straightforward and he offers practice exams. however the common final is made by all the profs and was a lot more challenging than his exams...
Good professor and nice guy! Straightforward course and pretty generous grader. Exams weren't too bad and he gives a lot of helpful review materials. Certainly worth taking.

I find Dr. Wells awesome. Discrete is naturally a difficult class but Professor Wells makes it easier than it could be. His exams are extremely fair, and he gives past exams for practice. His lectures are not fantastic, and he doesn't always have the answers to questions, but hes slightly awkward which makes them hilarious. I would take it with him

This course was clearly just another task for him. Lectures were unproductive and a lot of the class ended up teaching themselves the material. He went off on tangents often. He had very flexible office hours, but would sometimes struggle to solve problems he assigned us for homework. If you can take other options, take them. He is nice though.

Dr. Wells was one of the easier professors when it came to grading, but offered no resources to learn outside of the textbook. It was clear he had other priorities and didn't care much about teaching (as are all the postdocs teaching 381); many days he came to class unprepared and frequently he didn't know how to solve the HW problems he assigned.

Professor Wells is not the best lecturer but is very nice and wants you to succeed. His 381 class was extremely fair and was very similar to homework. There were no surprises on any exams and he was willing to have extra office hours sessions if you couldn't make his designated times. Challenging class but very fair.

I had him as my Math-231 recitation teacher. While he is really nice, he does not do a good job of explaining concepting and he always made mistakes when working out problems on the board. The students had to tell him his answers were incorrect and then he would rework them using the answer key. Attendance was mandatory.

Frane taught my MATH-232 recitation. Attendance is not mandatory so most people stopped coming, but I always thought it was nice to show up since he would empathize with us when we complained about the long waits to receive grades from our professor and he would even talk to us about the problems he had graded and showed us our grades early!

Frane is a nice guy, but he was not good at explaining the concepts we were being taught. If you don't study in your own time, you're not going to make a good grade in that class. High school level math should not be made as complicated as it was in this class, so if you don't have good studying habits, take another professor.

If you put in the effort, this class shouldn't be hard. I got a C due to my own lack of effort. He was a decent professor and the content is not difficult. Only downsides are that his accent was sometimes hard to understand and he overcomplicated some things. Very friendly though.

Professor Frane is an awesome professor, and I would 100% recommend taking his class. Do not be fooled by the other ratings for Frane as our professor was very clear on his grading criteria and even went above and beyond to clear confusion up both after class and even in office hours even though not many would stay for help. He's really sweet!

Frane is a nice person, but as a TA, his lectures were not effective at all. As Math 110 is a review of high school algebra, it should not be that complicated to teach. He would stand at the front of the classroom and do problems without explaining steps. I had to teach myself everything outside of class and got a tutor. Would not recommend.

His lectures were confusing but he posted detailed notes after class. I didn't have to pay attention because the notes were so good. The tests were graded with partial credit so even if the answer wasn't right you could still get at least half credit. The final exam replaced the lowest test grade which was also helpful. Overall not bad!

He is not effective in getting content across. He stands at every lecture and simply completes the work without explaining any concepts, and is much less rude when you ask for anything. I did not enjoy my experience in this class and would not recommend for anyone that is anything below efficient in the material he is supposed to be teaching.

Exam heavy 45% not including the 20% final. On previous reviews they said it was 5% each and it has changed Exam 1 is easy so try to do good on that Exam 2 was rigged against the students very difficult Exam 3 was more lenient but I assume that was because half the students who went to Exam 2 were not there exam 3 leading me to think a lot gave up.

Mclean seems nice but the course was not. Very boring I learned the same amount in lecture as I would have if I didnt attend. Openly said the exam scores were bad and proceeded to not add a curve. For future reference if the class average and median are low that is not a student error it is a prof error. Take with caution

Exam 2 was made to hurt with no curve Took COMP and STOR so it should have been easy and I can safely say this class was hard. Lecture he just writes code and doesn't explain it You will learn more plugging in past exams and using ai to explain it to you No practice exam or previous one so you can only use your old one after the hit

Dr. McLean is a great lecturer! Super clear with what he expects, and he breaks down topics very well. I never felt lost in his class and his exams are fair and not meant to trick you. He is kind and his expectations for attendance are very lenient (you can miss 7 lectures + records everything). Would definitely recommend taking him if you can!

Very low stress class. One homework and lab a week, they were usually pretty easy. You must do these to have an understanding of the class. Exams were hard but very manageable if you did all the assignments and watched lectures. All lectures are recorded and his own notes are posted. Mandatory attendance from a sign in app.
Exams aren't hard unless you do hw and labs on your own. I think it's really important to understand readings before the class. He's very willing to help!

This is one of those courses where, if you don't actively seek practice, you will not do well on the tests. Barely a stats class, if you've taken Comp 110, you'll be fine with the coding. Test 2 difficulty really comes out of nowhere. Lectures are just follow-along, which doesn't help with active learning in class. Really only a 3-credit course.

McClean is a good professor, but the course is ridiculously hard. The course description did not mention the endless amounts of coding. I went to tutoring for 2 hours a week, spent upwards of 12 hours a week on homework and studying, just to get a B-. Attendance is mandatory, but it only makes up 2% of your final grade. He is super nice tho.

Professor McLean seems like a pretty nice guy, but his lectures can be pretty boring. His midterms are also super difficult and he had said the class averages were very low, but doesn't curve the grades. It's doable if you actually put in the work.

Lectures are good and the readings are very helpful if you get confused. The hw and labs are a lot of work, but they're also the only way to prepare for the exams. I wish that there were practice questions to study, but he is good at answering questions in office hours. He is a little awkward, but very nice if you make the effort to be friendly.

Very code-heavy class. Lectures focus on syntax and go through stats quickly. About 2 HW assignments a week that are graded strictly, but aren't too hard. Attendance is lenient, but the final was difficult. He makes lectures interesting, but isn't very accessible outside of class. I'd recommend it, but prior stats knowledge is really helpful.

Decent prof. Awkward to talk to but nice & willing to explain things. Barely a stats class, basically only coding outputs that most of our tests were based on. No practice beforehand but tests only weighted 30% total and 20% final, so HW/labs brought up my grade. Not sure why this class needs a lab, but decent class overall.

his lectures are organized well, but he moves too slowly through the python snytax and too fast through the stats equation. I alr knew most of both, so it was fine for me, but he didn't fully explain how each stats equation worked, but did explain every word in the python syntax

I don't think this is Mclean's fault, but the class is structured to be an "intro" for people without stats or CS experience, but boils down to a very stats-heavy class (conceptually) and mostly simple code. If you've taken stats, the class is easy despite in-class midterms being somewhat tricky. Mclean does a good job of explaining and being fair.

Even as a pre-med, I think learning how to code statistical concepts in Python is useful, and Dr. McLean is a good teacher. The textbook is free, and the day-to-day assignments and even midterms are easy. The final was a bit difficult. Lectures are him coding stuff and you following along.

McLean is a very cold unapproachable guy who rarely answers his email. Even if everyone fails a test, he will proudly put the grades in- no curve/ rounding. I got a fine grade in this class, but it was such a nightmare as he genuinely tried his best to make everyone fail. Not sure why he's so intent on everyone doing poorly? but here we are

McLean is extremely knowledgeable about the subject but is also super kind and caring. He did his best to make the class as easy as possible for those of us who are new to coding and/or stats, and is very understanding and generous. 3 midterms and a Final (cumulative because concepts build on each other throughout the semester). Best prof for 120!

I'm not good at coding and but I think that Prof. McLean explained all the concepts in class pretty well and explains how to do the code by going through it all in class. I think the midterms were a little hard, but not impossible, and the homework/lab assignments will pick your grade up.

Also, the textbook is free, so don't worry about that.

Professor McLean's organized style and teaching style were very good. Watching him go through code, and then using the code in a weekly lab helps drill the concepts in. Tests were not very difficult if you go to class and pay attention and study the textbook/previous assignments. Made me want to take another data science class.

McLean overall is a great professor! Ignore all the reviews about the insane workload, there's a lab and hw due every week and it really does not take that long. Exams are difficult, there's no curve and they're on paper which can be a little frustrating. Overall I learned a lot in this class, I would recommend if you're willing to put the work in!

McLean is the best professor I have had here at UNC so far. His lectures are so well structured and he is very caring and passionate about the subject he teaches. STOR 120 is NOT the easiest introduction course but if you pay attention and do the work you will be fine. I would ONLY recommend McLean if you need to take STOR 120.

This class was a nightmare. I P/F the class, because there was no way I was going to get out unscathed. I put in 10 hours a week and ended with a B- (i.e., a pass). Ultimately, don't take the class unless necessary. If you take it, go to the TAs and ULAs every week; they will give you the answers. In my experience, boosting HW and Lab grade helps.

The class content is relatively chill, but the exams can be unfairly difficult. Lectures focus too much on coding with little exam prep. Definitely use unstuck study and the textbook to study - they were super helpful.

this class is labeled as an introduction to datascience, but even the tutors i went to said it is absolutely not an introductory course. i think this shouldnt be labeled as a stat class, it should be labeled as comsci, there is little to no actual math happening-all coding. as a freshman just trying to fill focus capacities, do not take this class.

I don't think Dr. McLean is intentionally difficult, but our past semester was rough. New paper coding exam format, no practice materials, incredibly late homework grading, rarely answered forum questions, poor slide decks, robotic lecture coding sessions. Course content is relatively chill and will hopefully be ironed out. Disappointing.

Professor McLean lectured well overall. He always answered my questions with detailed explanations of concepts. The first exam felt unfairly difficult with no past exams posted, but the rest were good, including the final. However, exams are more conceptual compared to lectures. Midterms were closed note and written, involving some written code.

This was his first semester with exams for this class and it is evident that he himself wasn't prepared for them by not grading homeworks in time, by not covering the statistics content that would be on the test (emphasized too much coding during class), and by not providing correct answers after the exams so that students know what they got wrong.

If you are a good test taker you will have success. I deeply understood this material, but dont work well under time constraint, and my grade suffered because of it. 68% is test, which is normal, but the tests covered irrelevant material that is not useful in real life. Got nearly a 100% in homework, but did bad on tests even tho I study well.

Professor McLean is engaging during lectures. Homework and labs take a few hours to complete, 3 exams were really hard for me, but the take-home portions were better + weighed more for grade, weekly quizzes and lab, final exam is the easiest exam in the course, overall a great course and I learned a great deal!
4 midterms 12% each, they were not super hard but READ THE QUESTIONS CAREFULLY. The final was not bad at all and in all it was a cool class and McLean does a good job explaining the material.
Explains concepts well and this course is not terrible for conceptual difficulty. But my word the amount of homework was so unnecessary.

Only take if you are a statistics major. Material is fast, but useful. Takes a lot of studying and effort, even with previous coding experience. However, if you are hardworking, study, and take good notes, you can do well in this class. But it definitely is not an easy grade, you have to work for it. He doesn't release exam or homework solutions.

This class was super difficult. Exams were all written and about equations yet we only played in R during class. He goes super fast and his approach to teaching the material is not the best. He'll spend the whole class in R just for the exams to have 10% coding questions. Would not recommend especially for a data science elective.

The class content is not too bad, but there are four midterms, one of which was during the second to last week of class. There is plenty of study material, but homeworks are not graded in time for the exams, so you don't know if you made any mistakes. He doesn't also release answers for homeworks or solutions for the midterms.

I wouldn't take this class if you don't already have a strong background statistics/coding. The whole lecture consists of coding practice problems from templates he creates. The whole class seems very robotic. The midterms and and final were pretty difficult and the majority of the class didn't score great. For a 120 level class this class was hard
Great professor, solid tests. Only issue is the homework, it would be a lifesaver if we got 4 drops instead of 3.

Dr. Mclean is a pretty good lecturer. The homework is using methods of data analysis in R, while the 4 tests are mostly conceptual data analysis questions. The final is then similar to the homeworks. The one complaint I have is that that he really does not give guidance on what to expect on the exams beyond "what we covered on the slides."
This professor would be amazing if he dropped the lowest HW assignment.

As a statistics major, this class is honestly not that difficult, but it does take some getting used to. Don't worry about memorizing large chunks of code for exams (you will learn what to prioritize after the first exam). Lots of homework and annoying group projects though.

Not sure why all the hate-He is a good lecturer, and the material is useful. Do not recommend without R experience. The tests are hard, but if you study they are doable. Homework is doable by going to lecture and taking good notes. Overall, it is a 400-level class and the material reflects that, but if you are a hardworking student, you'll be fine.

Class would be doable with previous R experience. Material is good and Professor McLean is accessible outside of class. I wish he was responsive on Piazza though. Have not gotten HWs back before the midterm. It's not the code, it's the analyses. Knowing if our thought processes are correct is vital to learning, or post an example of HW problems.

Jeff is a very nice guy, but this class was all over the place. The exams were very conceptual despite focusing on mostly application in lecture. The homework was fair and I thought that they reflected what was taught in lecture. Lectures were also all over the place and sometimes it was hard to follow what he was trying to get at.
Dr. Mclean is a very strict professor for no absolute reason and he has unnecessarily tough standards. He needs to drop the students lowest homework assignment from their grade.
Awful group projects, awful grading system and awful teaching. The materials are not difficult but lectures are difficult to understand and too complicated.

This class is all python coding and you use it for data analysis, which I wasn't expecting and makes the class more difficult than it should be. The labs and textbook are helpful to learn the actual coding aspect of the class. The in-class midterms are a lost cause, the class average is normally a 50/60 percent. Difficult for being an intro.

Jeff is a good guy but the midterms were horrendous you should definitely take STOR 155 and COMP 110 before this class. I dont hate the class but i literally dread the midterms and Im a cs student who took comp 283 with jack. I borderline consider the in class midterms a lost cause. Big man also assigns 2 assignments to be due the day of midterms

This class is 4 midterms; however it is a class clearly for statistics major. If you're not interested in statistics in any way avoid this class. The exams were purely conceptual which I think is a very good way of preparing for the data science world. The professor tries his best to accommodate everyone.

This class by far is one of the most difficult classes I have had. The material being taught is not bad, but the assignments that he expects you to complete and the closed-note exams make the class difficult. Does not respond in the Piazza, so not point in joining it, and takes relatively long to give back the HW grade and leaves no comments.

He wants the students to fail. The clas average for the first midterm was a D and he's not curving it. The homework is very hard and time consuming. He doesn't teach he just codes on his laptop during class.
never ever ever EVER in your life take 455 or any class with McLean. TERRIBLE

Terrible professor. Tests have absolutely nothing to do with homework. Assigns a group project that is impossible to coordinate within the due date. Test averages in the 60s and claims he won't be curving.

Not sure why he's being review bombed. It's true that the tests switched to closed-book (unfortunately), but he's genuinely a good lecturer. Apart from one bad question, the first test was fair if you actually did the readings and completed the HWs thoughtfully. I do wish he would utilize all of class instead of finishing 5 minutes early though!

This professor is unorganized and lazy because before the first exam which was a couple of days away, he had not made the exam yet so it was a poorly written exam. Moreover, he doesn't provide any study resources and the homeworks before the exam were not graded until after the first exam so there was no way to know if we did the homeworks right.

He just plays in R studio during class with no explanation at all. Only our first homework has been graded and there is no explanation for any grades. The average for the first midterm was a D and he didn't care. My discrete math class is easier than this class. Do not take this class with him.

The class format was changed this semester. Exams are no longer open-note, which makes them extremely difficult. The average for the first exam was a 60, and all that he said was that the exam grades are not going to be curved. The homeworks are graded very slowly and there are no study guides, so studying is nearly impossible for the exams.

He changed everything about the way this class works. No more open note tests. He doesn't teach and expects us to understand new material automatically. I have all A's, and now I'm afraid I won't even pass. Grades way too harshly.

Exams are no longer open note. He is a very harsh grader overall, and grades very slowly. For grade feedback, all you see is what you got wrong with no explanation as to why it's wrong. There are also no study guides for his exams. Attendance is required, but all he does is code in R with no explanation as to what he's actually doing.

Took this class because the tests were supposed to be open note. He changed his policies this semester. Lectures are hard to follow, all he does is open an r notebook and code whatever he is feeling that day. Provides no materials for exams and grades homework slowly and harshly. Also had nothing to say about the first exam average being a 60.

His lectures are not helpful as he just codes and uses random R functions with little to no explanation or context. As a CS major I'm used to reading documentation, but you aren't given enough time in class to read about the function. Attendance is mandatory, but useless. Expect to learn the entire class on your own with a poorly written textbook.

The midterms are no longer open note like people said below. This class kept me up at night stressing because he didn't teach us how to do anything well at all. Thank you for inspiring to switch out of the statistics major lol.

His powerpoints are not helpful and the work does not feel like the only preq needed is stor 155. The homework is so hard and so was the first midterm. The midterm average was literally a 67. He doesn't teach he just writes code and expects you to learn everything on your own.

Out of all the comsci courses I've taken hes got to be the most usless. He doesn't answer the piazza questions students have, his lectures are pointless (he just does the code and doesn't explain it), has weird trust issues during exams (and then tries to one-up you by saying hes recording you). Just overall, not very good.

McLean has insane trust issues. He wants to report students for breaking the honor code. He records the room while you take exams. Obviously, you'll be fine, just do your work yourself, but his obsession with finding cheaters makes the course stressful. The entire semester I was worried about accidentally breaking honor code, even though I wasn't.

Mclean is a very kind professor and really cares about his students, but is still very serious about his work. He does give a lab every week for the lab portion, but there is time to work on it during the lab time. The class was project heavy since there are no tests/midterms but there were quizzes and analyses which worked as assessments.

Absolutely don't take STOR 120 with McLean. He makes all labs and homeworks due before each midterm. His in class midterms are difficult but his take home midterms are all right. The final was the only reason why my grade boosted, but he never curves each midterm or final, so beware. Even on the last midterm, the average was low but he didn't care.

Nice and smart professor, very organized, a lot of homework that was sometimes difficult, occasionally dull lectures that were more because of the material than him, a group final project that maybe could have been structured a little better. Quizzes had a bit confusing layout but they're all common sense so they were often pretty easy.

he's a nice guy but work load went insane. it was extremely fast paced. quiz, lab, homework due every week. midterms were hard but thank GOD for the take home tests and that cushioning. oh lord study for that final, prepare for it as much as you can, I AM WARNING YOU! girl next to me started crying during it (not even being dramatic).

He is an amazing guy. The third midterm was brutal but if you read and understood the concepts you will do very well. The workload is massive, but it is a 4-credit course for a reason. I will take him a zillion times. Nice guy.

Jeff McLean is a nice person outside of class. In class, however, the lectures are organized but difficult to follow. He does NOT record lectures anymore and unless you are typing notes for every aspect, it will be tough to go back and follow. Homework and weekly labs are graded on correctness. Take this class with friends and a peer tutor.

Amazing! He was very understanding and genuine in wanting each student to succeed. He took the time to answer all questions clearly and was very approachable. If you try your best, come prepared, and get clarification on anything you are confused about, you will do well.

McLean is great. The complaints about too much work aren't quite fair; the class is 4 credit hours after all. And it is definitely NOT more work than the average stem class. Good lectures and fair exams. Cheating is rampant so I understand why McLean is vigilant about it.

Edit: Lowered to 4 because of no curve. The tests absolutely need a curve.

Dr. Mclean is serious about the Honor Code Violations and WILL give them out easily. he recorded class during an exam to check later if we were cheating or not on in person exams. there are 6 midterms and get ready to dedicate most of your study time to this class. this class is more work than your average stem class.

There is an unreasonable amount of work for this class. Mclean has 6 midterms + a final. Labs+HW take up at least 10+ hours a week. I have no time to do other work or study. I was up til 4am working on a take-home exam due the next morning instead of studying for my other midterms and I ended up failing everything due of it. DO NOT ever miss class.

An outrageous amount of work. Im a junior, so I understand a workload, but Prof McLean thinks this is our only class. Next week, we have a take home exam on Mon., due Wed. Also on Wed. We have an in class midterm. We just got assigned a homework and lab due the day of the midterm (takes hours) that is graded for accuracy. Im drowning in work :(

I took this class over the summer, and it was manageable. You do have to pay attention during lecture and keep up with the constant homework and labs (which were all graded for accuracy). Do not fall behind. Dr. McLean and the TAs were helpful in answering questions on assignments. The class structure is straightforward and organized.

Prof McLean assigned a TON of assignments. Do not take this class alongside other difficult classes, it will be difficult to manage. Very difficult class if you do not attend every.single.lecture. and pay 100% attention the whole, also very easy to fall behind quickly.

Overall a nice guy and decent professor. A ton of homework and assignments, but drop grades make it very doable. Only complaint is that the final was pretty substantially harder than the in-class and hw content. Definitely better at explaining the code than the underlying statistics, but recorded lectures are always nice.
He was a super hard and slow grader. The final felt designed for ppl to fail. Decent class but very mid from the final

Very organized, the class was nothing special but was very straightforward. McLean gives clear lectures and is happy to help students outside of class. If you can, take this class with a friend or make friends. Coding is easier with more people's input!
Good professor, lots of homework/lab assignments. Midterms were open note but still kinda hard. If you work hard, you can easily get an A!

Dr. McLean is definitely the most organized professor I've had during my time at UNC. You can always find what you should know and what you should be doing. Some of the exams were a bit tricky, in terms of asking for niche concepts that were either briefly covered or require an amount of intuition that might seem random. Great content to learn tho!

Ji's lectures are confusing and his homework is difficult and irrelevant to the test material (prepare to use AI). The tests are easy-ish but no one knows their grade because Ji's TA doesn't grade any homework. Literally only 10 people come to class but it's funny because probably over 50 people show up for the exams.

This professors' lectures are very sporadic and unstructured. His notes give little to no detail as to what we are learning, and he constantly go on tangents during lecture. The homeworks, while easy so far, is not representative of what we covered in class.

Cons: Lectures pointless. He goes on tangents every class and does not stay on topic. Does not respond to emails. Does not even upload grades to Canvas. Changed the entire format of the final on the last lecture of the semester, from open note/open internet to closed note written response. 
Pros: crazy grade curve at the end of the semester

Lied about the content of every exam. Said they would be multiple choice only to find out when the test is passed out that its free response. Said the final would be open note, ldoc says lol nevermind. We basically had to bully him into allowing our lowest midterm to be dropped. Not a fair professor, not a good experience.

Granted this was his second time teaching this course, it was very unorganized, grading was unclear, the midterms did not reflect what we learned, slides were repetitive, and he kept interrupting students to get his point across when they asked any question
I didn't go to a single lecture and just self studied. Really didn't learn much. His tests weren't straightforward and I got an A by some divine providence.

Professor Ji's class (in terms of graded work) is easy. You don't need to attend lecture or put effort in. He allows cheat sheets on all exams and posts previous exams in canvas. These exams tend to have reused questions. For a cheat sheet, I printed the previous final, answered the questions, and the final we had was over 50% the exact same.

Hate to say this, but you might as well not attend lectures. Professor Ji tends to go off-topic and is difficult to understand. I taught myself mostly from the textbook, since the homeworks he gave us weren't reflective of exam materials. He doesn't seem to care about the class in general, as he was late to the final exam and never answers emails.
JUST NO! NEVER!!!

The most frustrating class I've taken! Professor Ji rambles endlessly, rarely writing anything down, and somehow makes simple topics confusing. Emails? Always ignored. Exams? Brutal MCQs with no feedback. He even added random quizzes after the spring break because no one showed up. If you take this class, be ready to self-study everything.

He is so useless. Spends so much time talking on one slide (one time he spent like 40 minutes on ONE slide) and goes off on crazy tangents. I was fine just teaching myself because his lectures were useless but then he implemented a random pop quiz rule because almost no one was showing up. Also his exams are MCQ and pretty hard.
Tests were sooooo hard, and it was not a situation where you can study until it works. It really just doesn't. So frustrating but very nice man.
Does not speak easily understandable English. Lectures are pointless.

dropped halfway through the first class because I genuinely cannot understand him and have never been so confused trying to understand what a person was saying. seems like a nice guy but I can't believe he still teaches at UNC.

DO NOT TAKE WITH CHUANSHU. I have no idea how I made it through this class alive. I did not learn anything from prof, I taught myself EVERYTHING. If you are down to teach yourself and be clueless 24/7, go for it!
Ji's lectures can be unfocused, but using the textbook and unstuck AI for extra practice really helped me grasp the material. His exams are challenging but fair if you stay on top of the work.

He was unable to answer questions in lectures, gave exams with content entirely different than that in lectures, and won't respond to your emails. The TA's listed weren't even for this course and he's inaccessible outside of class. Awful
Take this class if you are good at self study, his lectures are useless. The tests are super hard. No attendance, and makes no sense to go since his lectures are super boring
Terrible professor and terrible course :(
JUST NO!!!

Do NOT take this class with professor Ji. Lectures are boring, and slides are vague/unhelpful. Get ready to teach yourself. Exams are nothing like homework, and he doesn't go over practice problems. He is also extremely hard to reach via email/canvas. Do yourself a favor and take the class with someone else
DO NOT TAKE STOR 155 WITH PROF. JI !!!

THIS CLASS IS SO BAD. I have never made a class pass or fail quicker than I did. The textbook is so unclear with the lectures being even more unclear. I attended so many peer tutoring sessions, just to be told that the material covered was never taught to the peer mentors. The teacher is even less helpful, just take with another professor, trust.

Professor Ji seems like a very nice professor on the outside, but in the lecture hall, he is one of the most boring professors I've ever seen. He takes a million years to prepare for every lecture. The slides are older than some of the buildings at UNC, and the way he talks makes It super hard to understand. Thank god attendance was optional at 8am

Horrible lecturer. Difficult to understand the material from his unorganized lectures and he doesn't bother to work out examples. You get very few practice problems before exams and homework does not align much with what's on the exams.
Just don't
He is a good guy, but his teaching is just horrible. His tests are tricky. I don't know how it's possible to get a good grade in this class.

Worst communicator I've ever encountered. Never answered email like literally ever there was no way of getting to him!!! Only positive is you never have to go to class. I did better teaching myself the material. But you are screwed if you have questions. My final grade for the class was just posted yet I have ZERO clue what I got on the final.

Ji is pretty incoherent in his lectures, and the course feels, as someone else put it, like a graduate refresher more than a first course in probability. Ji offers intermittent office hours where he will reexplain things to you, but he doesn't do a great job making it very understandable there either. Exams are very similar to practice and lecture.

His lectures are 75 minute yap fests and his slides are only a few pages long - get ready to teach yourself. Unreachable by email/Canvas. Homework problems are only loosely related to exam questions. Worst professor/teacher I have ever had in my life; he should not be allowed to "teach" this class the way he does.

Any of his courses are ok if you're the type that doesn't go to lectures would rather self study all of the material. Homework is significantly more difficult than exams, which are pretty predictable. Speaking to him directly after class or going to office hours are probably the only ways to get in touch with him: NOT reachable via email/Canvas.

Professor Ji is a super kind man and he seems to care about his students, but the course material and lecture style was largely inaccessible. It was very difficult to reach him since he didn't respond to emails, and lectures were often just 5 or 6 slides without much written down on the whiteboards. Super kind person, but not great lecturer.

The course is not great, he doesn't teach so much as he summarizes concepts as if you already knew the information. There are 2 tests and a final along with maybe 14 HWs on Cengage. H said he would reopen some dates on the HWs but never did. I take my tests at ARS and it became routine for me to have to wait 30+ minutes for it to be sent. not fun

Really bad professor. Bad lectures, bad communication, and confusing exams. Literally just reads off of powerpoints that are older than we are. We had a maximum of 15 people show up to lectures in a class of 150+. Exams are nothing like homework and we literally zero practice problems were assigned for exam. DO NOT TAKE. 8 AMs would be better.

Worst teacher I've ever had. Makes an intro level class near impossible for those without a background in stats and is completely unreachable outside of class. You will have to teach yourself EVERYTHING, so be prepared. Would highly recommend another professor, none of my friends are having the problems I am.

Prof. Ji has some of the most outdated and confusing lectures I've ever seen. Very unorganized professor who gives VERY little supplemental problems (4-5 per EXAM), and overall makes an intro class more difficult than it should be. 2 midterms and the final are worth 70% of your grade and they look NOTHING like the homework/problems you've done.

One of the most unclear lecturers I've ever had, but he is also such a nice soul and a treasure of a person. I would've loved to have met him outside of the classroom for a conversation but in the class he commonly speaks without writing on the chalk board or will show a slideshow of 4 to 5 slides... including the title slide.
DO NOT TAKE HIM. Doesn't reply to emails. Use one class to cover three lectures rather than postponing the midterm. Horrible lecturer. Forgot to post study materials before exams.

Doesn't respond to emails. Has no idea what he's teaching. Lectures are useless, most skipped them after the first few weeks because they were a waste of time. The practice tests he gives out don't help. You know what you got wrong on the exams but he doesn't tell you how to do it right. Final is 40% of grade. Textbook is unclear. Do not take!!!

Nice guy, but it was hard to follow his lectures. The examples in the slides are very hit-or-miss, and the textbook was often unhelpful. Also, the material in this class gets MUCH harder after the first few weeks. The exams were pretty fair, though.
I'm not sure how he's allowed to teach at this school, thought this was a top 10 public University.

Professor Ji teaches this course as if you have already learned all the material, and he is simply there to provide a supplemental higher level abstraction of the topics being covered. It's almost more like a graduate refresher course on probability than an introductory undergraduate course. The Pitman text is difficult. Good luck.

The class is straightforward, especially if you have a background in high school statistics. The instructor is personable and kind, though there might be some communication challenges. Nonetheless, it's manageable.

Doesn't answer emails. Gives no feedback on hw or exams (you know WHAT you got wrong but no explanation ab how to do it right) Lectures are a joke and will leave you with more questions than answers. You WILL need to teach yourself the content. Went to the Learning Center to review midterms, told me they'd never seen questions worded so weirdly...

Professor Ji was very disorganized and went off on a lot of tangents. It was very difficult to follow the lectures as he never gave straightforward lectures. The homework was much more difficult than what was taught int he lectures and was sometimes completely unrelated.

DO NOT TAKE!! Never responded to emails & most skipped his lectures because he mumbled and stayed on the same slide for 30+ mins. He doesn't demonstrate any concepts, gets distracted, and often couldn't answer student's questions. BE PREPARED TO SPEND HRS TEACHING YOURSELF. I even considered talking to someone above him because of this negligence.

Professor Ji was unreachable outside of class hours. Our first exam was rescheduled 20 minutes before the start time due to his negligence. While tests were online and open note, his unintelligible lectures made it impossible to understand any of the content. Be prepared to find a tutor to meet with once or twice per week. Avoid this class.
He's a good professor: he's nice and will answer your questions. His exams have been okay so far. Also, he doesn't assign too much homework. I expect to get an A in this class.

A good teacher but does not care about his students at all! Very strict when it comes to grading and even if you make a simple error which can be fixed, he is not lenient at all. Lectures are really long and boring with required attendance. Class is pretty easy but he makes it harder. Would take with another professor if you can. HARSH GRADER!!!!!!

Randomly assigned group members for a final project worth a quarter of your grade... Grading rubrics are extremely unclear and the class itself is extremely boring, so if you have to take this class for a major requirement please do yourself a favor and find another professor.

Extremely strict grading with unclear rubrics for the final project. Got a ridiculous amount of points off for not being original enough in an intro to DS class. He's funny but lectures are sometimes boring or difficult to follow. Does not reply to emails at all and is unaccommodating.
Dr. Remi is honestly a great guy and lecturer, made the material so easy to understand and accessible!

Extremely unclear grading policies. For 25% worth group project, he was extremely vague with instructions. Cannot read handwriting. Rude in office hours. I stopped going to class after the midterm because, unless you have a passion for R programming, it's boring and hard to understand the ramble. Needed class for an elective, wish I didn't take.

Solid class for learning R and films lectures. Overall, he teaches well and is easy to learn content if you follow along. He is very blunt and doesnt rly care to be accommodating. DONT send him emails; he WONT respond. 25p of your grade is an assigned group project, so if u get a bad group, you're cooked.

He is very passionate about what he teaches and he teaches slowly and checks in with students during lectures to ensure they're following along. He made an 8am lecture worth going to. He is a little tough at grading but also he gives you all the proper resources to do well in the class as all his assignments come straight from his notes. Take him!!
lowk the goat. if you put in the work and effort youll be fine, he really does want his students to learn and is always willing to help.

This class and Professor Abayomi's teaching was not very intuitive for someone who doesn't have any coding/limited stats experience. It isn't necessarily extremely challenging, but I would recommend taking this class when you have a lot of time to rewatch Abayomi's lectures and dedicate to the labs. He is funny and friendly, but pretty strict

I loved this class. Dr. Abayomi makes sure no one is left behind when teaching new content. He is very nice and didn't make it feel like an 8 AM. SQL is a straightforward language and has some cool nuances. Not that much work outside of class so can't complain. Exams aren't too bad and you have a cheat sheet too.

Very fun, approchable professor. Passionate about teaching and patient at explaning stuff to you. I feel he is too lax in this course. There are only 4 homeworks over the semester (each takes 0.5-1h to do) and there are not enough exercises provided to master the class.
Does not respond to emails.

Dr. Remi is a very funny and good teacher. He has a no nonsense mindset though, so don't be suprised when he doesn't give any leeway around late work. The course content is not that hard, but you need to actually put in work learning it yourself if you want to crush this class. Got by doing sort of the bare minimum and got an A-

Dr. Remi's personality made it worth it to take an 8am statistics class. He is a charming guy, and likes joking with his students. He taught pretty slowly- but only because he wanted to give everyone a chance to understand the material in this course. The workload for this class is very managable, and we had cheat sheets on the midterms/final.

Dr. Remi is an amazing lecturer; he explains concepts very well & repeats important ones we should know. However, he is a ghost outside of lectures. Never responds to emails & is not accommodating. I was one correct question away from getting an A- but he didn't even respond to my email about bumping me up. Make sure you have friends in this class.
Very mid lecture. Easy content, but the harsh grading makes the class harder than it needs to be.

The worst professor i meet in unc. The lectures were unclear, yet we were overloaded with assignments . The professor made no effort to support students, making the course feel unfair and needlessly difficult.
He is a good teacher and explains things clearly. However, he assigns a lot of work, sometimes not in a timely manner. You might have homework and midterms due in the same week.

The class itself is useful, but the grading was unnecessarily nit-picky. The professor was egotistical and unwilling to answer any questions or provide any sort of help. They spoke with an air of superiority and disrespect that I've never received from any other human being. I've never cried so much over a class. Do not take this class.

Overall, Dr. Remi was a good professor. Although this class has a lot of homework, it was relatively manageable. If you didn't take AP Stats in high school then this may be a difficult class. It is taught in python but you are expected to understand basic statistical concepts. I would recommend taking the class with him.

Old review got removed because I did not speak graciously enough about our lord and savior Dr. Remi. This class was not fun and he barely taught stats yet all the exams are about statistics. Take 155 instead. Also, if you ask a question in class he responds very condescendingly.

Extremely unaccommodating professor. Offers no extensions or drops on homework assignments, regardless of the circumstances, which makes the course unnecessarily stressful. Communication is a major issue—they rarely respond to emails, and when they do, the tone often comes off as rude or dismissive.

If you put in the work and time to really learn the course material, you'll do fine (think a few hours each week). However, the grading criteria isn't very specific, so there are many loopholes he can (and will) use to deduct points. Also, when going to office hours, he doesn't try to answer questions but makes you find out the problem on your own.

Take STOR 155 instead if you can, it is much easier. Got the worst grade of my entire UNC career, and I've taken chem and calc ll. In-class MC never reflects what we're learning and awards no drops for HWs, even though there are over 25 assignments. Also, emailed him more than two weeks ago and still haven't gotten a response. This guy is bad news.
The class isn't too hard, but the grading can be ridiculously meticulous at times. However, this is a great course for learning python and statistics.

We took our final exam on Friday but we still haven't received our grades. He was extremely rude to people who asked questions and he frames his final coding section with things we aren't familiar with and expects you to be able to complete it in 3 hours along with the multiple-choice section

Be prepared to hear, ‘Are you following the story?' and ‘This is very, very crucial,' along with gems like, ‘I'm already making my money; I don't care if you learn or not,' and, ‘In my side of the world, we did it this way...' all shouted at 8 a.m. on a Monday. If you don't need it, don't take it.

He says he's accessible, but he'll shame you for asking for help and make you think you're asking dumb questions. He argues that ‘it's 4 credits, so it's hard,' as if we signed up for boot camp. In his mind, students are the enemy, I guess we declared war by enrolling. Good luck surviving his battlefield of homework and take-home exams!

Beware of this class! It is insanely challenging for an intro-level course. There are no HW/lab drops or curves. You could be on your deathbed and Dr Remi still would not give you an extension. Never answers emails and talks down to you during office hours and when asking questions in class. Goes indepth on easy concepts, but breezes by hard ones.

Hardest 4-credit class I've taken at UNC (even compared w/ chemistry + physics). Workload and expectations are disproportionate for an intro level. He spends significant time overexplaining/ complicating straightforward concepts, while breezing through the difficult coding. No grades are dropped and no curves.

This class is just a cheap knockoff of UC Berkeley's Data8—he's stealing their work word by word and claims it as his own. At times he would switch the states from CA to NC to not make it as obvious. If you want to get a feel of how the class would be I encourage you to look it up, and practice. You'll pass the class with flying colors!

He presents himself as accessible but isn't. He shames students for asking questions, making them feel inadequate, and seems to view students as haters. The workload is excessive, because is 4 credit course you'll be finishing a take-home exam and multiple homework assignments at once. It feels like he prioritizes his ego over student success.

Dr. Remi is very smart, but he is not good at teaching the things he knows to others. As a student with no coding background, this class is very hard and Dr. Remi does not provide sufficient support to help you succeed. He does not respond to emails and is not approachable to ask questions, saying we would know had we paid attention in class.

Overall I  think Dr. Remi is a good professor and I  believe the exams are fairly easy. However, when it comes to asking questions about the content or meeting with him during office hours he is very discouraging and almost looks down at you for asking a simple question. On top of that some weeks we would be piled with so much work and assignments.

His teaching style is very engaging so time flies by in class. The content he teaches is interesting and he often draws illustrations on the board to help you visualize and better understand the material. He is clear with what he expects from you, reviewing outside of class, submitting labs/homework on time, etc. Definitely recommend!
Prof. Remi is really nice and makes this class easy to understand. The material gets more difficult once the statistics part starts, but it is not bad.

Hard to understand. Accent is so thick that I was left wondering what he was trying to say. It was online which made it that much harder to understand. He's extremely cocky. Felt like he was mansplaining everything with an attitude that he was better than the class. Math is not easy and he didn't help this. I suggest finding a different teacher.

He doesn't care if you fail or pass. He won't take extra time with you outside the classroom because “he's busy”. Not a very good professor if you have to get any extra help. I did this all on my own because he wouldn't help me in any way.

not a good teacher for STOR320; didn't grade final project EDA part as stated on the requirements/rubric(ie. rubric said to use table or graph for each question; deducted points on putting only a table or only a graph and said in class that it is because only one table or graph is not enough; argued but didn't work); TA too strict for hw/analysis

Professor Remi is a great professor who really seems like he enjoys what he teaches. Took his class in the summer but the work didn't seem like too much. Very reasonable and the tests were manageable. Very respectful of student's times. He made statistics understandable and provided many examples with opportunities to ask questions!

Dr. Remi is the sweetest. He made lectures engaging and easier to understand. The homework didn't seem like a lot, but towards the second half of the semester, it piled up. It was also very time consuming. There is no extra credit!

Dr. Remi is always respectful and fair to all his students. I was originally scared as someone who had never taken a stats class before, but his lectures made it so easy and he is willing to meet with you outside of class to answer questions. Although his homework deadlines are strict, he is very understanding and wants to help you succeed!
His written portion of the exams are easy, but the multiple choice make it to where its so easy to miss a few but they count for a lot. He makes class fun which is important!

The class is demanding and time-consuming, but Dr. Remi makes expectations clear at the beginning and provides helpful resources (lectures/notes posted online, accessible outside of class). There are 12 homework assignments, 11 labs, 2 in-class and 2 take-home midterms, and a 3-hour final. Pay attention and it will work out.

STOR120 is an easy class, especially if you have prior statistics/python experience. Most lectures consisted of him re-explaining the same things over and over, which got pretty boring after a while. He seems nice enough, but I will say he does come off as a bit condescending when answering questions from students. Just an okay professor IMO.

Love remi! he is great and is very clear about grading and what he expects of you. not a difficult course if you stay on top of your work. only 8 hw assignments for whole year, 2 midterms, final exam. gives a lot of study resources that will prepare you VERY well for the exams if you do them(DO THEM).
Take this with him!!! He is so nice and cares for his students. Tests are just like the study guides and quizzes

I learned so much in this class and it definitely challenged me. Professor Remi is a wonderful professor and cares about all of his students. He challenges his students, but his class is do-able with a lot of practice. I would not recommend taking this class with a lot of other demanding classes.

Easiest class I have ever taken. The homework is pretty much the exact same as the exams. I always struggled with paying attention during lectures but still managed to get a 100% on one of the midterms. The attendance grade is incredibly generous.

Dr. Remi uses lots of examples, which helps bring some life into the material and make lecture interesting. He's careful to clearly explain difficult concepts to avoid confusion. His guided notes and study guides are great when you have to study for exams. Dr. Remi is also a friendly guy and seems to always be in a good mood for class.

Dr. Remi was a great professor and lecturer! His exams were 60% multiple choice, 40% written. He gives a study guide before each exam that is helpful. He also allows a 1 sided cheat sheet for each exam, and both sides for the final. Definitely recommend.

Remi is the goat. He is an amazing teacher and an even better human. Despite having big classes, he cares about every student and is easy to reach outside of class. I'm not a stats major, but I hope to take another class with him one day. He definitely knows how to teach the content in an easy-to-learn way. Take any class with him.

I think the class has helped me learn a lot. However, the class meets four times a week, with only 2 unexcused absences, which is kind of insane. It is also A TON OF WORK. Like kind of a crazy amount. He assigns take home midterms and in class misters, so if you have any other homework or exams, balancing them will be difficult.
Remi was a good professor. Be prepared to study and review lectures! He was very accessible outside of class.
If you make a mistake he will not allow you to correct it and has no grade space.

I took Remi for STOR 155 and STOR 120 and he was great in both! He really cares about his students and is knowledgable about data science. Remi makes sure you understand basic concepts rather than focusing on the small details. He is strict about deadlines, but if you stick to them there shouldn't be any issues.

Dr. Remi is quite caring for his students, though he could be stubborn sometimes. Most learning are through his lectures which is quite fast paced, so pay close attention during class. The exams have 2 parts, in-class multiple choice and after-class coding. I would say the coding parts are easier than the statistic-focused in-class parts.

Good teacher and super easy class. Very easy and low effort homework, midterms, and final. Got an A+ on everything with minimal effort. This class gives me breathing room for more demanding classes. Good lectures too if you're genuinely interested in statistics.

Had great lecture notes that made homework fairly easy. Offers plenty of office hours if you are confused. Posts completed notes so missing a lecture isn't the end of the world. Would definitely recommend for STOR120.
He does not remove two of the lowest grades in our grade books.

Dr. Remi is a hilarious guy and makes this class fun. Strongly recommend his STOR-113 class to those applying to the b-school over MATH152, especially those who are not the best at math/calc. He reviews algebra at the beginning and takes all material very slowly. His main priority is that the students understand. I suck at math and got an A-.

Dr. Remi has been the best professor Ive taken a class with at UNC. His lectures are clear, interesting and fun. He wants the best for his students, is easy to contact and is by the book when it comes to grading and exams. He makes the work easy to understand and links it to real world examples. I will most definitely take another class with him.

Dr. Remi was amazing! Dr. Remi gave amazing lectures and provided plenty of examples that made the concepts so much easier. He also had very clear grading criteria and exams were straightforward. He was obviously passionate about what he was teaching and wanted his students to succeed. Highly recommend him for STOR-155!

Remi is easily one of the best professors at UNC! He is routinely disciplined, intelligent, and very caring. Strict with deadlines, but with good intentions. I had Remi as a professor during his first semester at UNC (he was great)--he has grown significantly! He is organized & communicative while retaining his kind heart and sense of humor.
Dr. Remi made me care about statistics and I am not a math person, nor am I a statistics lover. It is clear he cares about his students and his work.

prob one of the best teachers I've had as a freshman. He explains EVERYTHING so students are able to follow his classes and makes sure students really know what they're doing by going back to old material while teaching new material. Tests were very fair. Many laughs in this class, a non stressful course, gonna miss this class next semester!

Dr. Remi is an excellent professor and was very thorough in ensuring that we understood the lesson materials. He would make sure that we understood a concept before moving on and encouraged questions and concerns. I could tell that he cared about students' wellbeing and took his role as an educator seriously.

He makes jokes in class, and actually cares and answers questions in multiple ways to make sure you understand the material. 8 homework assignments total, throughout the entire course, about 20 questions each- very doable and understandable to what we are learning. Tests are worth abt 75%, but he preps you well (do study guides!). Def take him!!!

Dr. Remi is an amazing professor who truly wants you to get your money's worth out of the course. Even though this class is a lot of material, he tries his best to condense the information for anyone to understand. Can be a bit hard to follow sometimes, but overall is the best option for stor 120.
Probably only has such a high rating because his homework and tests are so easy. But the lectures are hard to follow and have no clear learning path

Professor Abayomi is one of the best Professors I have had. He is a great lecturer and the problems provided prepare you well for his exams. Some say he is repetitive, but he repeats topics that are important to your foundation in statistics. In STEM classes this is a luxury, most professors would cover a topic once (or not at all).

I appreciate how he takes his lectures slowly as that is unlike many other math or statistics classes. This makes it easy to understand the material and I don't have to spend much time outside of class teaching myself. His tests are also fair if you study and pay attention in class. He is also engaging in lectures and makes class more enjoyable.

While his lectures are slow-paced and often slightly repetitive, his class overall is very easy to follow and does a good job at teaching the basics of statistics. Homework assignments are clearly communicated and not overbearing. I would absolutely recommend Dr. Remi for this class, I feel as though he has taught very well.

Remi doesn't explain things well. He always makes mistakes unconsciously in lectures; you will be extremely frustrated if you don't figure it out yourself. Assignments are also confusing, which is even worse if he is not a good lecturer. Be prepared to self-teach if you choose a class with him. NOT going to take any class with him.
Not too much outside work and he is a super energetic and thorough lecturer. Would highly recommend.
Dr. Remi was a great professor really new how to make STOR 155 really fun. Made the class really interesting and made me more interested in statistics.

Dr. Remi is a great professor that was extremely clear on what he expects fro, his students. He always tries to make his lectures entertaining and push students to participate and to ask questions. He is very understanding and eager to improve. His well-rounded knowledge of soccer is a huge plus (he supports Chelsea). Definitely recommend!

Tests and quizzes are not an unfair percentage of the final grade. Participation and homework still mean a lot which helps cushion your grade. Remi is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter and he explains every topic in depth. Tests and quizzes are easier than the homework so you feel extra prepared.

I see negative reviews for stor 120 so it must be a lot different than stor 155 because the class was so manageable and easy. His exams were completely fair and he taught everything well. Definitely recommend for stor 155

I loved Dr. Remi's class! He is super passionate about what he teaches. His classes were very straight forward and his study guides are extremely helpful for the exams. If you know how to do the study guide questions, you will be prepared for his exams. The homework can be time consuming so I would recommend doing a portion each day.
Remi is a really good professor he explains so clearly the concepts and will help you out of class if you still have some doubts.

Excellent professor, and makes introductory statistics fun and comprehensible. We got behind in lecture but this was always accommodated for, rather than leaving us to self-study foreign material. Exams are very fair and have study guides; however, don't ever become complacent or it will reflect in your grade.

I'm not the best at statistics so I was very cautious to find a good professor before a stats class on. Dr. Remi is the best professor for this, he's straight up, extremely intelligent, has guided notes, and more. He made this class a (somehow) enjoyable 8am class. If you are questioning if you should take his class this is your sign you should!

Professor Remi is great! He makes sure to stop if anyone has questions during the lecture or if he senses the class is not understanding. He uses great real-world examples to help the class remember concepts. My grade could have been better if I studied differently for the first midterm. USE THE STUDY GUIDE/PRACTICE PROBLEMS!

Dr. Remi was an amazing professor! He teaches passionately, and has a sense of humor. He explained topics with clear and concise real-life examples that made it easier to understand opposed to other stat professors who just throw you the complicated looking formula straight from the text book. He makes stat easy you will not regret taking his class

Dr.Remi is a great professor who takes pride in his ability to help his students be successful in their coursework. He makes difficult concepts easier to understand and is very considerate of students circumstances outside of the classroom.

Dr. Remi was a very thorough teacher but was very condescending as a professor. He had very little patience and was rude to students on occasion. While his lectures were thorough, he spent a lot of time explaining simple concepts that everyone already knew.

He is the best choice for Stor 155. He reuses so many in class/study guide questions on tests that really reward you if you show up and pay attention. You also get a cheat sheet. I never had to worry about my grade in this class because I showed up and did the study guide before tests

Dr. Remi was a great choice for STOR 120. The midterm exams DO reflect what he lectures about in class for the most part. He explains most things more than once and will almost always ensure the class follows before moving on to the next topic. He is a really caring and passionate guy, and I would 100% take another class with him.

Professor Abayomi is awesome. He is very organized and provides many resources to prepare for exams. 2 midterms and 1 final. Midterms are fair and very similar to the study guide. You will do well if you pay attention in class, watch the recordings (if necessary), review guided module notes, and complete the study guide he provides.

Professor Remi is such an amazing professor and his class is so well organized. The exams are exactly like the study guides so it was not difficult to study. We were also allowed a one-sided 'cheat sheet' for every exam. His notes are so helpful! I definitely recommend taking STOR 155 with him!!!

Dr. Remi was not clear with lectures or material. Half of the time we would not finish the lectures in class and our homework and labs were graded incorrectly. Midterms were graded very harshly and were not very correlated with material learned. He seems like a nice and very knowledgeable guy but I would not recommend taking STOR 120 with him.

Dr. Remi seemed to randomly grade the homework and lab assignments which made it difficult to get feedback on how you are actually doing in the class. He doesn't convey the material well and puts concepts on the exams that were not clearly talked about. You'll have to teach yourself if you take 120 with him.

This was my first time using Python, and I think Dr. Remi did a good job teaching first time users how to code and then apply that to stats. He takes his time in lectures to repeat key things, which some people feel is repetitive but I thought it was helpful as someone that struggled in the class at first.

Professor Remi is great!! The material is not easy, but he explains concepts well. The study guides are very similar to the exams and you get a cheat sheet. He is lenient on HW due dates and not a tough grader. Gives fill-in-the blank notes. The exams are hard to complete in 50 mins, but he does give some credit even if you haven't completed it.

Dr. Remi is awesome! His lectures are great, engaging, and fun. The material isn't super easy to understand but Dr. Remi makes it enjoyable to learn. Great professor and would 100% take his classes again.

Remi is the best for stor 155. Tests are fair and just like the study guides and homework, he doesn't try to trick you. You also get a cheat sheet. Requires barely any time out of class just 1 homework every ~2-3 weeks and then complete study guide/review notes a day or two before exam.

Dr. Remi is a nice guy but doesn't get through the information we need in lectures. The in-class exams test on something entirely different too. I would not recommend taking 120 with him unless you're prepared to teach yourself a lot of the material.

Professor Remi is a nice man, but is unfortunately disorganized at times. However, it was his first semester teaching at UNC so it's understandable. Exams were difficult to complete within 50 minutes while other classes had open note take-home exams. Sometimes, he was slightly condescending during class when questions were asked and through email.

I can't recommend Dr. Remi enough, he makes concepts so simple and the exams are literally exactly like the study guide he doesn't try to trick you and you get a full page for a cheat sheet. 4 free unexcused absences, the hw give you 5 tries per question and he drops the lowest 2 hw. Couldn't have picked a better prof for this class

The course content is not that hard, but it's not easy either. If you do the homework and practice problems on your own, you'll be totally fine. There are three midterms, each worth 17%, and one final exam. All the exams are very similar to the homework, some are a bit harder, but nothing outside the expected range.
Take this class with Pataki. He does an amazing job of preparing you for the exams. One of the smartest professors at UNC.

This course is not too hard but not too easy. If you put in the work and STUDY THE HOMEWORKS you will be fine. Pataki gets hated on because he can be very direct. Personally, I think he is a great instructor that means no harm. Can be very funny too. Take this class for the BUSI math requirement.

Gabor Pataki massages your brain to think outside the box, iykyk. He cares lots about his students, and it shows during his lectures. If your bad at math this class is pretty easy, just put in some work and you will be fine. He does have an accent, but worry about his handwriting more. He's also pretty funny too, in a mathematical way.

I would definitely recommend taking this class with him. He is good at his job, and the class is not very hard. Just make sure you take notes and put in effort to study, and you will be fine. Not really sure why he has bad reviews. He can be a little blunt sometimes, but I don't think that's an actual issue or reason to not take the course.

He assigns too much homework for how little it impacts your grades. If you do not do well on one exam, you are going to have to get around 94-100% on every other midterm exam and final to end with an A in the class, and if you do bad on more than one you are basically screwed.

He's a great professor for STOR 113. He's very respectful, teaches with intent, and constantly checks in with the class to make sure everyone understands the content. He's always happy to answer questions, explain a concept more, and is very helpful outside of class.
not too easy not too hard. if u don't like him it's just an iq filter

Don't understand where negative reviews come from. Dr. Pataki is caring and patient, willing to put tons of time into teaching, whether in lecture or in office hour. His lectures, though can be clearer for some concepts, is well prepared and align well w hw and exams. Exams are graded harshly, but you will do well if you read questions carefully.

Cannot imagine what this person had against professor Gabor.  His passion was infectious, he held engaging lectures, and gave very fair exams. Course material was super interesting and made me understand what linear algebra is actually good for. People say that anyone getting a letter from him to grad school gets in!

He's very condescending when you ask questions and will make you feel stupid for not understanding. I would recommend going to TA office hours instead. However, exams are similar to homework, but are graded very harshly. I lost all motivation for statistics because of the professor and this course.

Go to class...don't assume you will pass this because you've taken calculus before. Just like study and find someone to do the homework with because running it through ChatGPT it'll be wrong...pretty boring lectures and I was always just waiting for the class to end but I guess it was pretty solid.
Great professor, fair exams, hardass grading.

Boring lectures. Some of the methods he teaches are outdated/have simpler alternatives. 

The content is easy, especially if you've taken 305. The homework doesn't take that long, not sure why people are complaining. The exams are VERY straightforward. You can skip class and still get a good grade, just read his notes.

Course content isn't super difficult but Gabor isn't great at explaining concepts and teaches outdated methods. He grades leniently compared to other courses/professors in the STOR department and will ask students for feedback during lecture, which is helpful. Weekly homeworks are time consuming but prepare students well for exams.

Very interactive lectures, very willing to answer questions and help. In some lectures students talked more than he did. Lots of hw, but not too difficult, and they will prepare you well for the exams and quizzes.

Somewhat scary guy. Gives pretty straightforward and easy tests but is a harsh grader. He will ding you a couple percent for the smallest mistakes but pretty easy to do well. Tests are very similar to homeworks

Professor Gabor takes  some getting used to, as he can come across as grumpy some of the time. But he explained the course material very well, and was super helpful in OH. He really wants you to learn. Exams were just like the hw, so if you study, you will do well.

The course teaches you very useful skills. Rather than teaching flashy stuff, prof. Pataki goes into the math of optimization, and uses a language to solve big problems. Simplex was kinda boring, but the many problem sessions were super interesting.

I strongly recommend avoiding this professor if possible. While the course content itself is manageable, his teaching style makes it unnecessarily difficult. He consistently comes off as condescending and dismissive toward students. Even when students ask genuine questions, his tone often feels rude or belittling.

Very straightforward professor. His notes are pretty helpful if you don't attend class. HWs are extremely long but not hard at all. The class itself is not hard, you just got to do the HWs that's it. The midterms seem hard but it's all questions that he has asked before either in HW or quizzes. Nice that he drops solutions though.
Go to office hours and ask questions in class. Professor Pataki likes to answer them and will take as much time as needed to make sure you understand even if he seems intimidating.
