Professor is mind numbingly boring. Homeworks take longer than your lifetime and somehow get progressively longer each week. Class is a real grind and pretty miserable.

I've been in this guy's class for about a month now, and I have probably spent more time doing his HW than all my other classes combined, and no, I am not exaggerating. The HWs get progressively more difficult as you work through them and are insolvable with the techniques he actually teaches in class.
One of the worst professors I've ever had.
Gabor is demeaning to students who ask questions. He uses the chalkboard exclusively and grades homework harshly. Hard to follow his accent.

A genius instructor who comes across as slightly abrasive some of the time. He explained things very clearly and was always available before, during, and after OH. He really cares that students learn, though his passion is also reflected in the amount of hw he gives :)

It's obvious that Pataki is a super smart person, but I feel like he teaches the course in only a way that he understands. He does care about his students but his grading is strict and its sometimes hard to understand what he is saying in class. He also changed our grading scale with a couple weeks left in the semester and barely uses Canvas.

Gabor is a terrible professor. He is hard to understand because of his accent and his handwriting is also hard to understand. He doesn't give leeway for mistakes on exams and homework is extremely long and grades every aspect of it. Do not take him.

The class is difficult, but if you truly put in a lot of effort, you can get an A. Weekly HW can take a while so don't wait till last minute to do it. It is also graded very heavily. If you mess up on one exam, you are kinda screwed so be sure to prepare a lot in advance. The exams are very similar to the HW, so just practice the HW. Good luck

Very rude towards students and only cares about his top students. He has a heavy accent and can be difficult to understand his accent and handwriting. There is lots of homework and takes off lots of points for mistakes, even if not clarified what to do he just expects you to know. I would not recommend him and would suggest you take Calc before him

Pataki is an OK teacher at best. He sometimes complicates things more than they should but if you put in the work you'll be fine. Go to OH to check over HW's (which take a while). I found that the TA's help way more than him. The quizzes and tests are easy but the final was harder. Go to class, go to OH, do the hw, and study and you'll be fine.

I think the people who gave him a poor score  are fresh out of high school. I am a sophomore, so better used to university courses and was never good at math, but still got an A. What you need to do well in this class is not AP calc, but algebra. He does give a lot of hw, but this course will prepare you well for the B school.

Professor Pataki gives way too much homework and it's all graded on accuracy. Homework will take you minimum 3 hours each assignment but there's only one a week. Both midterms were relatively easy and exactly like the homework. Final was a good amount harder. Lectures are difficult to follow as he's bad at explaining and often makes you feel stupid

professor Gabor goes veeeeeryyy slowly, he has to, so that everyone cam follow. So it may be boring for some. He is very open to meeting students on zoom and really cares that students learn. Exams are just like the hw, so redo all hw, and you will do well. From what I hear, this is the best option for B school calc prereq.

Gabor was a good math teacher. He simplifies things down to the max and does lots of practice problems. While he sometimes make things confusing, all quiz and test are just homework questions so not hard. One homework assignment per week so not bad. If you understand the homework you'll do good. Very strict grader. Not time consuming.
Wow, this class was a bore. He is by far the worst professor I've had at UNC yet. It's easy, but he does not understand students or how to teach them. Goodluck.

Goes at an extremely slow pace in class and simpifies things so much that it actually overcomplicates simple concepts. The HW is way harder than the stuff taught in class but the quizzes and exams only consist of the main easier concepts. TAs knit pick the crap out of HW. Honestly worth self studying bc Pataki moves at a snails pace.

Pataki explained all material very well, and he regularly asked for student feedback in each lecture. He really cares that students learn, but has a habit of answering a question with another question. He pestered us a lot abt catching up on algebra, which sometimes got annoying.

This professor is not a good teacher. This being said, I have never taken calc before and did fine in the class. There is tons of homework that is graded very harshly. As long as you understand how to do the homework you will be fine. I would definitely recommend this class over the other options for business pre reqs.

He is not a good teacher. He expects you to follow along scribbled notes that are uncomprehensible because he deosn't providew context or even explain what hes doing. Good luck learning everything he assigns throiugh the TA or online.

I think prof. Pataki means well, but when asking questions he almost makes you seem dumb for asking. Exams & quizzes are fairly easy. 1 HW assignment a week that's graded very harshly, takes 2hrs MINIMUM and could be on the previous week's lectures. Just walks in and starts writing on chalk board. Overall not a fan of his lectures/teaching style.

He is not a good teacher, he scribbles on the board and when you have questions he is super demeaning. Many students just went to the TA to learn everything. the homeworks were super hard and took multiple hours but the midterms and quizes were easy.
Dr. Pataki gives a lot of hw, but then makes the exams exactly like the hw. Midterms were basically 3 hw questions, and midterm  scores were in the 80-90 % range. So if you study, you will do well.

Please never take him! He is insulting when I genuinely want help and essentially calls me stupid whenever I have a question. Study guides are not like exams; exams are like 3-4 questions, so you can fail if you miss one part. He has a heavy accent and gives lots of homework that are graded harshly. Does not give any extra credit. Just do not take.

In his class, you may have to teach yourself how to do some things if you space out in lecture, and it can be challenging to figure out. I found tests and midterms to be easy if you study. You do have to be very precise on homework and exams. My one qualm is that I don't know what my grade is. I estimate I'll get roughly a B.

Pataki does genuinely care about his students and always asks for feedback on tests, quizzes, and lectures. That being said, even with having calc experience, the homeworks are graded very harshly for no reason and the tests/quizzes having so few questions makes it hard to get an A

Don't take Pataki; HWs are so tedious and long, and I still get BIG deductions on them despite my clear understanding. Lectures are so boring, and I failed the first midterm, partially due to me understudying, having taken calc, but MOSTLY his grading and lack of care for his students. Class is so much harder than it should be. Quizzes are easy.

One of the better professors in the STOR department, did tons of examples which made studying for exams easy. There is always homework, but usually not that difficult if you went to class and doing so much homework builds in studying. He has a particular style of teaching and applies the socratic method for hw help, but he wants students to learn.

Some of Gabor's jokes made me groan and some of his hw turned my brain into mush. But I learned an awful lot. He is  nice and helpful  in OH but he surely makes you work for your grade. I cannot imagine what the person below me had against him, other than the  grade they got.

Gave a lot of homework, along with 2 midterms and 4 quizzes. All of them are fairly easy. Boring lectures, possible to learn from notes instead of attendance. Used AMPL software for solving LP. Class could have been way harder, so I appreciate him going easy on us.

Easy A class but the semester was miserable. Professor Gabor's lectures are extremely boring, and the homework assignments are unnecessarily long (4-5 hours each with very repetitive problems.) He does not have a grading rubric for the exams and you can get a 10%+ total grade off for copying down the wrong number. Mandatory in-person office hour

Gabor is a true gem. He is definitely one of the best professors in the STOR department. His exams are fair and makes sure you understand the material but does not try to trick you. He is very kind and will learn you name rather quickly if you come to office hour/participate in class. Wish he taught more upper level undergrad classes!

Bro, idk what happened but I thought Lassiter was a chill guy and gave a lot of A's but I am pretty sure they nerfed it this year and now his exams are like battling Satan himself. I have to redo the class, but I know good and well as a Bio major thats taken gen chem and a ton of intermediate bios, that STOR-155 shouldn't be this hard. Dont take.

85% of this class was exams, which were all free response unlike any other professor teaching this class. Do not take STOR 155 with him if you are not naturally gifted at math. Your spirits will be crushed.

Very genuine guy who you can tell cares about his students. Attendance not mandatory, but he sprinkles in comprehension checks that you need to be in class for. Homework was very light and doable, and his exams are VERY similar to the practice exams he gives you beforehand. Overall, great professor and would totally recommend for entry level stats.

Professor Lassiter's class is definitely challenging in the sense that exams make up the majority of your grade BUT he is very caring and WANTS YOU TO SUCCEED. If you attend class, pay attention, and answer/ask questions in class, you will do very well. He also offers decent amount of office hours and extra resources outside of class time.

I would be happy to have any STOR class with professor Lassiter. He takes time to make sure students understand, provides adequate time for questions, and gives mini lectures before class for bonus points. The only negative is that homework problems aren't very reflective of test difficulty.

Exams are worth 85% of your grade in this class, so be ready to study outside of class. However, Dr. Lassiter was very straight-forward in his lectures and got straight to the point. Honestly such a chill guy and is very open to giving feedback during office hours. Definitely recommend.

In his class currently and really enjoy it. Attendance is not mandatory. The tests are lengthy but doable if you study. You also get a two sided cheat sheet for each exam that you can use your ipad to make. He is very accessible and always willing to help you go through a few practice problems in office hours which has helped me a lot.

Dr. Lassiter was an engaging professor. Homework was weekly (sometimes he extended deadlines) and manageable. The exams were a bit long so it will be hard to finish in time if you get stuck, but most if not all of it is addressed in lectures or practice exams, so I would say they are fair! Although I didn't go to office hours he encourages us to.
It was a chill class, you get cheat sheets, extra credit, and some easy bonus points from watching his Mini Lectures. Some homeworks do take some time. Overall good class for stats major!

Very fair class with opportunities for extra credit. You get a cheat sheet for exams however they are somewhat difficult, particularly the final. Lassiter really knows what he is doing and takes time to ensure everyone understands.

It was shocking to see bad reviews. He cares for the material, being a teacher, and seeing his students succeed. He has very dry humor but it works for a stats class. The lectures and homework build effectively for midterms and final, and he allows cheat sheets. Attend and do the work on time, the material will stay fresh. I can't recommend enough.

AMAZING. He holds 3-hour office hours twice a week and is always accessible to answer questions. Attendance isn't mandatory, but to know what you're doing, you have to go since he doesn't post his lectures. The exams are close to the practice given, but can get tricky. Overall, he truly cares and is easily the best professor I've had at UNC.

He's truly an excellent professor. He's kind, consistently responsive, and always willing to help when the material gets tough. One of the top instructors in the STOR department. If you get the chance to take a class with him, don't hesitate.

It's his first time to teach STOR 415 but he did a great job on it. The lecture notes are clear and the homework questions are similar to the exam questions. Have 2% extra credit if you go to class every time and finish the bonus quizzes. He is also really caring as he holds 6-hour office hours per week and is always ready to offer help.

Take STOR 155 with Lassiter, you won't regret it! HW was 25% of grade, you got 5 attempts. Every exam you're allowed a FULL sheet of paper of notes. They were fair, material and grading-wise. Attendance is 2%, but you get 5 freebies. Only graded by: attendance, HW, 2 midterms, final. He is nice and organized and easy to reach outside of class.

Lassiter was a very engaging lecturer, and I enjoyed coming to class. Gave 4 extra credit "pop" quizzes which each added .5% to total grade. OH were helpful especially for homework. Exams were fair and similar to HW, make sure to study the examples he gives in class.

Lassiter is tough but fair. His tests are very challenging, but they are material he covered in the lecture. You get one cheat sheet on midterms (2) and two for the final. For lecture, he goes over various problems in detail. You should be fine if you listen to the lecture and understand the hw. He is a tough grader, though.

I took his STOR 415 class—he's the best professor I've had. He's kind, patient, and truly cares about students. His slides are clear and well-organized, making hard topics easy to follow. I highly recommend him if you're starting STOR 415. A great teacher for this course!

Prof Lassiter is a great choice for stats. Tests were extremely fair and only covered what was discussed in class. He's very helpful in office hours, I went every week to stay caught up. Homework is straightforward and cheat sheets are allowed on both the midterms and the final. Highly recommend, I was terrified of stats and he made it great.

take this class with lassiter!!! he was so nice and his lectures were super engaging as he posts fill in the blank notes which i enjoyed. he allows cheat sheets for all midterms and the final, as well as access to calculators. would take again!

He's a fine professor. The lectures and in-class examples are fairly straightforward. Homework and exams pretty much make up the entirety of the course grade, but both are pretty easy. We didn't get through all of the material, so he ended up cutting stuff from the exams.
Good professor for STOR 155, very helpful office hours if you go, exams weighted a lot, use cheat sheets
He genuinely cares about his students and is always willing to help clarify the material. The exams are challenging, but he curves the final grades to be fair. Highly recommend!

He is so great! The midterms and final weren't that hard, he will curve the grades if necessary. There are also some chances for extra credit, he is super organized and approachable. I would recommend taking his class!

Professor Lassiter is a pretty good teacher, this class moves fast but is manageable to keep up with. It's very test heavcy but you get cheat sheets so make sure to use them. His lectures move pretty quickly, so pay attention to everything he says. Overall, he is pretty good and also helpful during office hours.

I've never taken a statistics class before, but Lassiter's lectures were clear and exams were fair - you also get cheat sheets. Pay a fair amount of attention in lectures - the content jumps from easy to difficult quickly. Sometimes he was standoffish or annoyed during office hours, which was tough since new material lectures were dense/confusing.

If you have to take stats here take it with prof Lassiter! His exams were very fair and he wanted you to succeed. Traditional lecture style and homework was weighted as much as an exam. Best stor 155 teacher by far.

If math/stats doesn't come easy to you, prepare to study a lot for this class. If you do all the homework and study a good amount before exams, you can deff get an A. Info goes from easy to hard pretty quickly. You get a cheat sheet for all the finals, PACK them with info from the lectures. Lassiter does a great job going through the material.
Very hard class for me, as someone who hasn't taken statistics before. Very test heavy around 70% of your grade. Final was curved.

Professor Lassiter is such a great teacher! His lectures are clear and organized, and the mini lectures definitely aid the understanding of the course materials. HW every week, but they prepare you for the exams. You def need to put in effort to earn a A, but it is a very fun course to take!

Just go to class for 2 points to your final grade thru random bonus quizzes(completion). The hardest problem of the HW was usually gone over in class so those were pretty chill too. Exams are super fair, and there were points back for a hard problem. Office hours were really good as well. Overall, nice professor and an interesting class.

Amazing clear lectures. Opportunities for extra credit for showing up to class (bonus "quizzes"). Homework is manageable and we usually go over a problem the class votes on. Exams are fair and the practice tests prepare you well. Show up to every class and pay attention and you should do well. Prof Lassiter is good at answering questions too.
You will do well if you do homework, go to class, and watch mini-lectures. He gives time for questions and goes over one homework question per assignment that the class votes on.

- Clear lectures
- Weekly Homework (about 3h per)
- Bonus quizzes which improve your grade by up to 2% if you simply go to class
- Super helpful and gives lots of time to ask questions 
- Fair grader
- Responsive on Piazza if you have questions outside of class hours
Professor Lassiter makes this class very manageable. Just watch the mini lecture videos and go to class and you will be fine.

He has very solid lectures and his homework was exactly what we practiced in class. He was always super positive in class and happy to answer questions. Friday class wasn't a lecture, he would work out a homework problem that was voted on by the class before the homework was due which was great.
So long as you show up for lecture and do/review the homework, you should be able to get an easy A.
Lassiter is dope—he got Brandwein's for us during final project presentations

Worst class I have taken at UNC. Lectures are difficult to understand. I studied the most for this class than I did for any of my other classes that semester and still barely passed. At office hours he was extremely rude and unhelpful. Test heavy course with barely any feedback. Class is essentially self-taught.

He was really nice and always willing to answer questions if needed. Some of the exams were a little long for the amount of time given, but overall the amount of content was manageable and we were allowed a cheat sheet. I am not a math person but I felt that he taught in a way that was clear and didn't assume prior knowledge.

Lectures were fairly dry and I think the content could've benefited from more IRL examples and applications. The class isn't too difficult as long as you pay attention to lectures and do the homework seriously; both exams and homework are fairly written (make a cheatsheet with formulas for sure though). It was an okay intro to simulation.
he is so great and lectures are organized.

Workload not bad - 6 HWs, 1midterm + Final
Material is pretty intuitive and straightforward but it is a technical class (uses Arena + Excel for tests / simulations) - pay attention because it becomes easy to get lost post-lectures on how to do things if you don't
Fair teacher - explains things well and is willing to take time, pretty accommodating
Lectures were boring, class was graded by a few things that were harshly graded, and I did not feel that he could explain things in an approachable way when asked a question.

Take Lassiter for any STAT/STOR class you need! Grade consisted of 20 HW assignments (he gives points back at the end of the semester), 2 midterms, and 1 cumulative final. He gives partial credit on tests! He is the best explainer and really wants you to succeed. He's happy to answer any questions you have. His response time is respectively fast!

Very hard final, does not give a lot of material to prepare for exams, every other professor was MUCH easier with a substantially better class average. He also grades extremely slow. Nice guy, but take with easier teacher if you can.

extremely hard final exam. does not give answer key for midterm to help us improve. also teaches material to the last day not allowing much review. also does not put in any grades fully until the class is all the way over. nice guy but not a good class.
Slow grader, useless lectures, exams are hard

He was honestly really bad. And the thing that gets me is he takes down all the bad reviews, so it looks like he is a good professor. Please don't take him. By far the worst professor I have taken, and that is being nice. Goes through lectures very quick, is rude, and just overall not a great teacher. His exams also are hard

Good lecturer. One cheat sheet allowed for the two midterms. Extra credit: 0.5 points to final grade for each pop quiz you're present for but doesn't hurt grade if you're not. Class test avgs: 80s. Doesn't curve but had a points back opportunity when he realized a test question was particularly hard. Not doing too well in the class personally tho.

By far the best STOR class I have taken. Prof Lassiter keeps class interesting and is always willing to explain concepts further. He gives extra credit (2 points added to your final grade) for attending class and is generous with HW credit.

Overall a great professor. Worked with me in a time of crisis, allows cheat sheets on tests, and only a couple homework assignments a week. Attendance mandatory and graded but he builds in extra points to accommodate non-emergency absences. I definitely recommend him for stats. Lots of office hour opportunities and genuinely cares about ur success.
Professor Lassiter is so nice. His lectures are clear and easy to understand. And he gives us extra points through bonus quiz. If you put in some effort, you will get a good grade. Take his class!

Prof. Lassiter made the material easy to understand and was very accessible outside of class. Our class was at 5:45 MWF, which is a horrible time slot, but he made Fridays homework days (so it wasn't necessary to come to class), which was very nice considering the class was so late in the day. Would recommend!

He's a nice person, but the class sucks. Would not recommend 515 with any professor. Lassiter did alright, but I think his lectures can be a bit bland at times. He is very very helpful outside of class, and was a lenient grader. He wants you to succeed, but the class does not.

Professor Lassiter's 305 class was a great class. He thoroughly explained the material and taught the basics of excel. He was great at answering questions and mindful of explaining topics in ways to make sure everyone understood. Lots of opportunity to ask questions. Grading is based on weekly hw, 2 midterms and a final. Would highly recommend!

The homework is online tablesets you can take until you get 100. The rest of your grade is midterms and the final. He is a good lecturer and wants you to understand. Go to his office hours if you are unsure of a topic. I failed to ask questions when I needed help, so do that. He is nice and caring, and sometimes funny. The content is not too hard.

Professor Banerjee is clearly very kind and passionate about the topics but this class was just difficult to follow. I attended every lecture and did well on the homework, but found the practice exams and midterms to be significantly harder. Beware midterms are multiple choice and very short - I got 3 wrong on the 1st midterm and got an 86.

The exams were just like the practice exams he gave out, and we were allowed a cheat sheet on the 2nd midterm and the final. the first final was pretty easy, but the next 2 were a little more difficult. overall, manageable and he curved slightly at the end.

Very nice and passionate professor, but lectures were unnecessarily confusing. After the 1st midterm, I stopped showing up to class and just self-taught myself everything, and this worked better than the lectures. Practice exams similar to the real exam and cheat sheets allowed. Midterm 1, 2, and Final averages are as follows: 79.5%, 77.7%, 78%.

Professor Banerjee is a really nice guy and is really smart, however, I feel like his teaching was really confusing. I found the class very easy because I took AP stats in high school, but if I didn't, I would've been completely lost. Basically your entire grade depends on the two midterms and the final so if you don't do well on those, it's over.

Good professor who cares about his students and does his best to help everyone understand. This class is very hard, one of the hardest I've had at Carolina! Exams were fair (if you're able to do the more difficult hw without help you'll do fine) but still hard. All exams multiple choice so no partial credit. He curved the class slightly at the end

A very nice guy who is obviously very smart. However, he's probably one of the worst lecturers I have ever had. Boring and confusing lectures that failed to teach the material. His grading structure is also set up for you to fail not succeed. Exams are 20-30 difficult MC questions so if you get a few wrong you're guaranteed not to get a good grade.

Sayan is nice and reachable outside of class. He goes through things in detail in office hours to make sure you understand. All exams were MCQ and fair. Workloads very manageable, but lectures are boring and proof heavy. He said no curve but curved anyway. Would be nice if he posted worked lecture solutions rather than have us copy from chalkboard.

Professor Sayan is a clearly knowledgeable and incredibly kind man who loves his field, but he is single-handedly the most confusing professor I have ever taken. This introductory Statistics course is supposed to cover a basic understanding of stats, but dived into some overly complex topics that aren't taught in other sections. Maybe 400+ courses?

Banerjee is very nice and passionate about statistics but overcomplicates a lot of the material. He uses a lot of higher level formulas and lectures tend to become confusing and boring. Allowed cheat sheets on the second midterm and final. Wouldn't recommend him if you're just taking this class for a credit. Also hard to reach outside of class.

He is nice and clearly loves statistics, but I struggled with following him in class and found his lectures boring. Homeworks weren't similar to test but he gave review problems where some were similar to the exam. Tough exams but allowed cheat sheets after 1st midterm. Prob would've done better if I tried harder but idc abt stats
Sayan....GOAT take him!!! even though this is a hard class
Banerjee really likes to make jokes. He's available during office hours. He likes teaching and listens to our feedback. The class is just hard but he takes a lot of time to answer questions.

He is definetly the best professor for this horrible course. He tries his best to explain everything and make it intitutive. Homeworks are not bad at all. Just follow the textbook and do examples you will be fine in his class. His exams are also not meant to trick you they are pretty straightforward. I really liked him

Honestly, underrated profesor. His lectures are slightly boring, and slightly confusing, but if you spend a bit of effort outside of class you will be fine. His pre-exam practice exams are very nice, sometimes extremely similar to the real thing. Don't expect him to give extra credit, but he will curve slightly at the end, and is very accesible.

If you need to take 435 at UNC take it with Sayan!! He honestly gives great lectures if you pay attention and he's extremely nice and funny. The only critique about his class is decently long weekly hws and the fact that he doesn't post annotated lecture notes. Exams are exremely fair but be sure to study for them since they're heavily weighted.

Sayan is an alright professor for probability. He's punctual with grading and explains what you should expect in exams. Exams are also weighted heavily. Expect this to be a tougher course to go lighter hours with. Only nitpick for Sayan is that he doesn't post lecture slides with his notes, so either you attend lecture or look at the textbook.

If you're a statistics major, take this course and prepare for a challenge. It will be your valuable asset. Some lectures feel like grad-level, but the exams are easier. All midterms are multiple choice and graded quickly. Medians - First 14/15, Second 12/15, Final 25/30. Since exams have almost equal weight, don't underestimate the midterms.

Highly recommend taking 435 with him. Pretty tough topics, but he genuinely cares about everyone understanding. Only issue is he just posts the unannotated lecture slides, but if you show up to class you'll be fine. Only multiple choice exams for better or for worse. I tuned out after midterm 2 and still got a 90 on the final (80 on both midterms).

Sayan is one of the best professors to take this class with. His lectures are engaging, and he explains concepts really well.  MTs were 15 MCQ and the final was 30 but tests are similar to questions on slides, homework, and practice problems and are generally straightforward as long as you study. I had a great experience and enjoyed the class w him

Best teacher for STOR 435. Class is difficult with hard concepts, and the grading scale is very heavy towards tests (Final was 40%, and cumulative). Funny teacher, engages with class, worth going to class to listen to. Lectures posted and review sessions given before tests.

Sayan has gotta be the best professor available for Stor 435. His lectures are incredibly intuitive and well thought out, the homework isn't very heavy yet is still helpful and the exams are exactly what you expect. Definitely recommend, and you will definitely have the easiest time understanding the content with Sayan.

Middle of the road prof and I was generally indifferent to his teaching. It may have been more boring for me because I wasn't interested in the topic but he is passionate about stats and you can tell. Lectures were boring for me but as long as you pay attention now and then and understand HW you should be good for exams. Pretty easy A.
I couldn't stay awake so I stopped going and just read the slides before exams and it kinda worked ig. Cheat sheet for exams and a nice curve at the end.

Lectures were confusing and explained poorly. Although his exams were pretty similar to the review, they could trick you easily which was brutal when having just multiple choice. Slides weren't organized and didn't contain answers. That being said, Banerjee did curve and was a nice guy!! Just a way harder class than it needed to be.

TAKE DR. BANERJEE IF YOU CAN! If you are actually interested in stats then Dr. Banerjee does an excellent job teaching and developing concepts in lectures and makes it easier to understand if you just pay attention. If you're just doing this class for basic credit then you might find it difficult or boring, especially with the only MC exams.

He was not an amazing professor but definitely not the worst. He is nice with deadlines and it is very clear he loves what he is teaching. However, the class is very difficult if you have never taken any stats. I recommend finding another professor.

Do NOT Take STOR155 with this professor. He confuses everything to the point you do not know what is right and wrong. Test Heavy and HWs are nothing like the test. Does not give good test prep or keys in advance either. You had to learn everything in your own time. The tests are MC but I wouldn't say that's fair either.

Does a great job explaining concepts thoroughly making it easier to study for exams. He spends the first 15 min of class going over previous class content but it's not his fault that some people cannot remember content despite him going over it multiple times. Class consists of weekly homeworks (answers can be found online) and fair MCQ exams.

Didn't realize this until like halfway through, because I thought stats was maybe just a topic I'm not good at, since this is my first stats class. However, after speaking to people in other STOR155 classes, it turns out he's just very bad at explaining, as well as badly organized. Slideshows don't have answers; homework is not reflective of exams.

Worst class ever. Do not take. Nothing he says makes sense and most of the people that show up to class are asleep during class (including first row). Worse than Organic Chemistry 2, or any UNC Chem/Maths/Stem course. The whole class is always confused.
overcomplicates material, and couldn't understand half of what he was saying. Had to teach myself. Test heavy.

He was okay. The most significant issue was that there needed to be more grades. He was also not very accessible out of class. Exams were all multiple choice and very short, so every question was worth many points with no partial credit. There was minimal homework and going to class was not bad. Never felt stressed but never felt prepared.

Dayan is a great 435 professor. His class was definitely the most difficult of the the three teaching during the semester. However your understanding of material while taking his class will prepare you for further study in stats I would recommend his class for anyone who is serious about a future in stats

He's a professor I would certainly recommend to STOR majors. His lectures focused on providing depth on covered topics, but his exams were multiple choice and generally very easy in comparison to many of the problems covered in lecture. The homework assignments were generally not hard until the last few, and the two lowest are dropped.

Class is very easy to understand. All lecture slides posted earlier than class. Homeworks are easy. Exams are multiple choice so it can be easy for some and not others. Class is exam heavy so prep well.

Overall the course material is not very hard. However, I only learned the material through the Organic Chem Tutor. Dr. Banerjee would over complicate EVERYTHING. He would compare concepts to integrals/calc even though Math 110 was the only prereq. He provided us practice exams and refused to provide solutions. The only good thing is that he curves.

Do not take a class with Sayan Banerjee. He is rude and has made me feel dumb in class. He overcomplicates everything when this class really should not be that difficult. He literally used calculus to explain a stats topic when calc is not even a prereq for this course. His tests are straightforward but tbh I had to teach myself everything I know.

Not a good lecturer. Complicates things way too much, teaches untested material before exams to overcomplicate. Funny guy, but the opposite of straightforward. Uses a bunch of complex symbols and equations when I know it could be taught in a much easier and more understandable way. Good guy, but wouldn't recommend.

Going to lectures often seemed pointless and taught STOR 155 in a more difficult way than necessary. Used lots of high level formulas and over complicated basic concepts using symbols and figures that meant nothing to many people in my class.

Dr. Banerjee is one of my favorite professors at UNC. Very laid back and an expert in stats. His intro class is very straight forward. If you can get him, take his class. You don't want a graduate student.. trust me

AVOID HIM AT ALL COST! He is not caring his students. I went to the office hour with my friend. He totally ignored us and stopped explaining unless we continued asking. During his lecture, the classroom is as a hell since no one can understand. His TA use chatgpt to generate the solution to hw, even though the solution is wrong.

Could've gotten a better grade if I invested some time in the course. Guanting is nice, but his second exam and final were really really difficult. After the first exam, I didn't know why people were stressing over this class but learnt why after the second exam. Study hard 445 is a difficult course.

Very very hard class. The hardest class I took at UNC. Guanting is a great guy, and I can see myself grabbing a beer with him. That being said, he was not a very helpful teacher for such a difficult class. Though, that does not by all means he is mean or rude. Ignore other comments about him being rude because he isn't. A nice guy who can't teach

Good guy but not a good teacher. If there is another option, I would go for that instead of taking it with him. STOR 445 is a very difficult class, and he just doesn't explain things enough while speeding through everything. There was only a 7 point curve despite low exam averages and him telling us that there will be a big curve.

Good guy but may not be a good lecturer. Teach yourself everything through textbook and ChatGPT, and go to office hour for questions instead of emailing him. Homework is hard but you can also use GPT and counts for 40pts. 2 midterms and a final  only count for 10+10+40 pts but still provide a 7-pts curve and A is >92.9. Therefore easy to get an A.

Guanting is horrible. He responds to the email for weeks! The curve is +7 for everyone and +10 for those who get better on the final. However, the final exam is ridiculously hard, making it impossible for us to improve. Homework is not helpful; the practice test is way easier than the actual test. Class is boring and avoid it at all costs.

Guanting is not that bad. He is just alright. His lecture slides are useful but goes fast in lecture. He has responded to the emails I sent. He will say grades for midterm/final will be released "tonight" but not do not fall for that. He did add a 7 point curve, so very appreciated. Exams were fair, but long given the amount of time we had.

I can see why people say he's rude and condescending, but he doesn't mean it. He's a much nicer guy during office hours, and he is a sweet and nice person. However, I don't recommend him. We were much faster than the other section and rushed through everything without enough explanation. Also, his practice exams don't reflect the actual exams.

Class was interesting, tests were fast paced but cheat sheets were allowed. Final was not difficult and grades were generously curved at the end. Just follow the lecture slides he posts and you'll be fine.
Hey Professor. Chen, reply to my emails, please

He's a decent lecturer, however he, along with the TA, did not care in the slightest about instructing the class. He gets annoyed when asking questions in class, ignores you in his office hours and rarely responded to emails. I believe they even used ChatGPT to grade some of the homeworks. Just overall a condescending, apathetic dude.

This dude is genuinely so useless to try reaching outside of class. He doesn't respond to emails and doesn't try to be helpful in the slightest. The class isn't ridiculously hard or anything, but it's pretty difficult. First midterm was chill, second midterm was way too much for a 50-minute class(whole class was still taking the test). Bad teacher.

If the entire class is not doing well, that is a reflection of the professor. He is inaccessible and rude during OH and class and makes condescending comments about students not doing well. The midterms were hard and there was not enough time and when asked about a curve for passing he was not helping out clearly anxious students.
Avoid at all cost.

I stopped going to lecture after a few weeks and still scored at least the median on the midterms and the final, just by doing homework, looking at posted slides before exams, and some youtube videos. I feel like the excel knowledge and combinatorics were useful. Overall though, I feel like we just didn't do much. It was an easy grade overall.

I almost didn't take this class because of the terrible reviews. On the contrary, Dr. Chen is a good lecturer. Practice midterms and final are nearly identical to the real thing. Dr. Chen is very helpful. When I asked to meet, he went out of his way to schedule a zoom call even though he was in the airport. Don't let the reviews scare you :)
The final is 40% of your grade. I think I self-studied majority of the time, but I appreciate the breaks he gives in class. He is smart-- just maybe not my preferable teaching style...
The final exam is as hard as it could be. Too much course work, should be STOR505 in terms of difficulty.

The class shouldn't be that hard, but it feels like Chen goes out of his way to ensure students fail. Chen is pretty passive-aggressive when presented with questions. Lectures are awkward and ultimately unhelpful. Graded on: 4 homeworks (one due after LDOC), 2 midterms, and the final.

Lectures weren't helpful. Homeworks and midterms each took a month to be graded, and we have homework assigned after LDOC and before the final. Midterms were way harder than practice questions he gave us (only gave us three practice questions for midterms). Don't take this class with Chen unless you're willing to teach yourself everything.

The lectures were incredibly unhelpful and I ended up teaching myself most of the material from online or other resources. The midterms were much harder than any practice we got. The homework grades were never given back in a timely manner and one of them was made due 3 days before the final exam.

Just to add to what I wrote yesterday, I wasn't just unable to understand, I mostly didn't listen. The professor handwrites everything on a blackboard, which isn't ideal given how disaster the classroom is, an iPad would be better. Plus, Dr. Chen is actually pretty cute, and the curve was definitely generous.

I attended almost every class, but I honestly couldn't understand a word he was saying at all. I realized that the only way to pass this class was to just read the textbook, which he was literally just copying straight from it. I did end up getting an A, but only because his curve was generous.

The final grade curve is generous, so getting an A isn't too hard, but the material is really difficult to understand. There are only six assignments, and the lectures are tough to follow, so the best way to succeed is by reading the textbook over and over again
The professor is awesome, but the classroom is a disaster. The lighting is poor, the seating is super uncomfortable, and the desk surfaces are way too tiny to be usable.

I really enjoyed Dr. Chen's lecture! He's super smart and has a great way of explaining advanced concepts. His teaching style focuses a lot on mathematical thinking, which I found really natural and engaging as a math major. Plus, there isn't an overwhelming amount of homework, and he's pretty generous with grades.
Dr.Chen gives lots of partial credit on exams. The material is tough.

Dr. Chen was by far the worst professor I've had at UNC. His lectures always had mistakes and the notation he uses is not consistent and hard to follow. When you ask questions, he is very condescending and assumes "it's obvious." His actual exams were nothing like the practice exams or homework problems. He slept through class and office hours...

Puts little effort into the class/lectures, but almost directly follows the textbook and uploads all notes. Very few homeworks and still drops one. Also get tons of cheatsheet for exams (4 pages double sided final). Skipped most lectures and did fine, the content is interesting enough if you like probability. Half convinced the 5 reviews are fake
"He who is not courageous enough to take risks (his 445) will accomplish nothing in life" - Muhammad Ali

He clearly does NOT care about this class or students, and it's absolutely TERRIBLE. I had friends who took his STOR305 and told me he was AWFUL, but I didn't believe them, so I took his STOR445 - and he really is that BAD. STOR445 is hard, and his indifference literally makes this class even harder, and he seems to push everything onto his TAs.
Homework has to be typed(In latex for 10+ hours). The actual exam was completely different from the practice. Cancel the class for no reason.

Test heavily, the average of the exam is around 60/100. He comes to class late very frequently and made bunch mistake during the lecture. Office hour and homework is not helpful at all. Just read the textbook NEVER go to the lectures!

He sometimes arrives late to class, and he's definitely very, very chill. However, it gives me the impression that while he has an excellent grasp of the material, but most of us can barely understand what he's actually saying. He might be a genius, but as a professor, I honestly can't say he's OK—he's truly AWFUL.
worst professor
Easy A. Best professor at STOR department.
The coolest professor at UNC! He's super chill, smart, and truly cares about his students. Highly recommend taking his class!
Amazing professor with decent lectures! Guanting really understands what we need and what matters to us, and he's always ready to help us sort it out.
An incredibly helpful, skilled, and intelligent professor. Although the class was tough, he made it much easier to handle.

Guanting is very helpful and ensures everything is convenient for his students. He gives great lectures and releases notes before class, which allows us to focus more on understanding the material rather than just taking notes. He is also very understanding about deadlines, often extending them when many of us need extra time.

Guanting does a great job explaining concepts, and is super approachable if you need help. The exams are tough but they are curved, which helps a lot. STOR 445 is a challenging class but he makes it much more manageable.
Guanting gives good lectures. I used to struggle a lot with probability, but after his class, I've gained a real understanding of the subject. The exams are fair, and there isn't too much homework.

Before taking Professor Chen's STOR 445 class, I noticed it had some sketchy reviews, but he turned out to be a pretty good teacher. Homework assignments were hard but we only had 4 of them. Tests were generally straightforward and Professor Chen was transparent about what would be on them. Also grades were curved.

He is not a good a lecturer at all. very confusing and hard to follow. questions on exams are always poorly worded, misleading, and confusing. homework and exams are insanely hard compared to in class problems. he laughs at students before answering questions they ask. exam averages were consistently in the 60s. was not a very helpful teacher.

Awful. Lectures are unclear, assumes the content is intuitive, is condescending and not helpful when asked questions. Homework is excessively long, and much harder than any examples done in class, and the exams are even worse.

The extra credit is almost useless, and if you didn't do it, you might even be curved downward. The wordings on final were ambiguous and hard to understand, and the test was long and counted for 40% of the total grade. The lectures were also not good; it seems not easy for him to explain things clearly.

Exams are extremely difficult and long, the median of his midterm are around mid 60. The final grade is determined by how well you perform compared to your classmates, with only around 15% of students can get an A. The grading structure is unreasonable, especially this course is one of the easier electives in the STOR major. Don't take his class.

He explained the content poorly. The exams are extremely difficult and long, and the wording of the exam questions was often problematic, making it even more challenging to understand. It seems like he doesn't care about students' grades and their overall learning experience. Avoid him if you can.

Exams were twice as hard as any homework. Exam averages were around failing but will curve the final grade.  Will need to find practice problems through the online textbook for more practice. I recommend going to the lectures even if it is not mandatory.
Exams are super hard with an average C.
Exams are super hard with average around C.
Nice professor, very caring. Good office hour.

This class has a steep learning curve for python.There is not explanation, only a lecture or 2 on each topic, and one example/ concept. Basically 0 practice material that resembles what will be on the tests. I went to office hours, he was not helpful w/ explaining where mistakes on tests/quizzes.TA knew nothing, didn't help w/ labs or assignments.

This class is decently difficult but Professor Fraiman is absolutely amazing. He is very kind and passionate about the subject and is always willing to dive into more detail. His lectures are helpful and his exams are very fair and quite lenient on the grading. He also scales down grades based off how the class does to make it easier for an A.

Professor Fraiman is an amazing lecturer and very kind, respectful, and understanding. His exams are very fair and based on homework. There is a good bit of homework for this class, but it is worth it as it helps solidify the content gone over in lecture.

Awesome professor. This class is not easy, however Professor Fraiman is an absolute gem and wants the students to succeed. Highly recommend anyone to take a class with Professor Fraiman especially this one.

Really hard class but really great professor. Dr. Fraiman is knowledgeable, kind, and passionate about the subject. If you go to his OH you will learn a lot more. The examples in class can be really hard and might be quite challenging to people without a strong foundation in math

Had him for STOR 120 in the FY launch section. It was easy for people with coding experience, but if you don't have any coding experience, this class has a steep learning curve. took a bit for grading to get fully developed for grading to be fair, but eventually became enjoyable to work with the coding environment. Also, made a 90 an A.

I loved Dr. Fraiman for STOR120. He was super passionate, and really cared about his students' success. I absolutely bombed one of the tests, and he was more than happy to go over it with me to explain things. He made the class really captivating, and was a very generous grader. I am adding a stats minor because of him. Take Dr. Fraiman's classes!

Writing code in class was a nice way to learn Python and I enjoyed the datasets and examples in the lectures. The autograder was nice to have but sometimes was a hit or miss. Professor Fraiman was very helpful during office hours and he lowered the cutoffs for grades making it easier to get an A.

I took this FY Launch with Professor Fraiman. Overall, I found this course very challenging, which isn't the professor's fault, but the structure of the course. We had three exams and the final, which covered a lot of Data Science. I do not advise you to take this course if you've never taken Comp Sci or Stats as you will struggle.

Love professor fraiman. His lecture is so intriguing and interesting that you feel 50 minutes is short. Very fair exams, he drops one of them making this course a lot easier. Really wants to teach us things. Great class.

Prof. Fraiman, while incredibly knowledgeable, isn't the type of professor that explains concepts clearly. He often explained to us the proofs instead of explaining how the concepts might be used in a problem. He made it easy for us to ask questions, however, and his tests were incredibly fair. Use the back of the textbook, slides, and WebAssign.
Learned a lot in this class. I really enjoyed the labs and coding to solve some problems. His lectures are well organized and you can just study with the slides.

Great person, good lecturer, difficult final. The labs were a nice touch. HW consistently took 3-4 hours per week. The 3 midterms were ok, but read the Q's carefully, as there are only three questions (with one or two parts). The final was hard as it was weighted for the end of the course, which relied heavily on knowing how to set up the solution.

Prof Fraiman made it clear from day 1 of this class that he wanted as many of the students to get As as possible. There was nightly homework (that was sometimes difficult), but the tests (and the final) were generally much easier than the HW.

Nico is honestly a really sweet & caring guy. However, his lectures can be boring & get nothing out of them. Very understanding that his tests are hard that he curves at the end. Went from a D+ to a B-. HWs x3 a week and can be challenging, 3 tests, 1 final and lowest exam gets replaced by final if higher. Again, sweet but hardest class I've taken.
I really liked the labs and code he showed in class. The last month was much harder than the rest and the third test was rough. However, the final can replace your lowest test and it was much easier.

Material on tests is simple but some of the homeworks are a little challenging. If you just do the homework you are more than prepared for every test. He curved the class heavily and dropped the lowest test for the final which wasnt hard. Fraiman's lectures are hard to follow and not very interactive so I would not take again for harder material.

Very reasonable and nice professor who lectures fine but at the end of the day the material is just going to be objectively hard no matter what. 2-3 Types of Homework per week which can be pretty difficult, important to have friends and resources in the class. Tests pretty reasonable though. Class a little more difficult in the later portions.
He's funny and I like the art and anecdotes he shared at the beginning of class. The final and the tests are quite easy. Homework is more difficult but that comes from the book.

The homeworks were very time consuming and extremely hard to complete without OH or a study group. The lectures were fast, but Fraiman taught well. The midterms were pretty easy and fair if you study well. The final was insanely difficult. I have an A as of right now, but I'm expecting a 50% or worse on the final exam.

Fraiman is a relatively laid-back professor who's humorous and clear. However, the workload is pretty intense. The homework was challenging, and the tests didn't align in difficulty. I wish I could rate higher, and as positive as Fraiman is, the lectures and communication are maybe a little above average.

Have cons but all the pros make up for it imo. HW is hard, but exams are easier and HW is still doable. Lectures can be confusing sometimes but do not hesitate to ask questions because he will take the time to address your questions. Appreciated him dedicating multiple classes to review for the final and the curve. Hard but he is very considerate.

Super kind guy. I could understand why this class would be difficult if you haven't taken a statistics course before but honestly if you just actually read the text book along with coming to class you will be fine. The tests are really straight forward and way easier versions of the homework (which can b hard).

Here's the deal, Dr. Fraiman just is not the greatest professor. The homework is insanely hard and doesn't align with his easy exams. If you are going to take Fraiman be prepared to be bored out of your mind during class. Seems like a good family man though. The 3rd Exam is hard because he didn't explain the content in an interactive manner.

Stor 390 has been my favorite class I have taken with the department. Nico wanted the class to succeed and applied large curve at the end. The content is really interesting and Nico is more than will to help if you are lost.

This class was interesting but could have been structured better. The exams were extremely easy as long as you know what the formulas mean and the homework was often graded generously. Professor Fraiman didn't always give examples and there are not many online resources, but if he will give examples after class and office hours if you ask.

i can tell that he really likes what he teaches, and he tries his best to teach us the content. he's really receptive to feedback from all of his students. i feel like he had fair exams, fair homework. would take again
He always helps students to learn and improve. He gives students a lot of support and cares about students.
The GOAT in UNC STOR department. no doubt.

Love Dr. Zhang! Gives out a bunch of extra credit, open note exams, and is overall a nice guy. I really didn't have a hard time understanding him, and even if you did, his slides explain the content well. I was almost never confused in this class. If you need a 500 level STOR elective, take 556 (or anything) with him.

He is definitely very knowledgeable but his knowledge is blocked by the way he speaks. I don't think it's the accent issue but just the way he speaks. So in lectures, it's hard for students to receive knowledge from him. But overall he is a very caring and knowledgeable professor. Please take his class if you could learn from slides.

I simply really like Dr. Zhang. He's very caring, approachable and has an excellent grasp of his material. I took his STOR455 and STOR556 courses and got an A in both. If you're worried about your grades, he always offers extra credit opportunities. The only downside is his accent, which might take long, but finally still fail to get used to.

Professor Zhang provides detailed lecture slides and tries to ensure students' questions are answered during class. He provides ample extra credit opportunities so try to attend all classes. His midterm and final exams (open note) are fair but can be tricky so make sure to study all of the homework and lecture slide concepts and problems in detail.

Professor Zhang is great for 455! Students write codes in R along with him during lecture. Homework isn't too difficult if you pay attention to the codes in class. The textbook is incredibly useful for interpretation/conceptual questions on HW/Tests. Open book exams which is nice. Provided many opportunities for extra credit. Definitely recommend!

Theory of time series can be hard but the exams and homeworks were quite computation / surface-level theory focused and so getting good grades is really manageable in the class. Professor is really nice and gives lot of extra credit opportunity, love him and overall a very useful, fair, and manageable course.

great leader and an accomplished researcher but fails as an instructor. very hard to understand him cuz of his accent, so you have to self learn. lecture slides arent informative so you have to learn through only the html files. everything was posted timely and accessibly, but, he is not able to teach a class of students effectively. so much ec tho
HW and Exams were difficult but he gave so much extra credit.

Overall he's nice but pretty disorganized. Sometimes he assigned "weekly" hw 2 days before the due date. About 30% of each midterm/final was composed of concept questions which aren't always explicitly covered, so you have to understand all the content. The plus side is that there were multiple extra credit opportunities that helped my grade.

Provides a lot of extra credit opportunities which significantly helped my overall grade. He's very accessible outside of class. Midterms are pretty tricky, but they require a deep level of understanding to be successful. Overall a really good class and applicable to all sorts of majors/careers.

Prof. Zhang is a great professor! The class is fine if you take time to study R codes and slides outside of class. The homeworks are also pretty helpful for reviewing the material, and exams cover what gets taught in class, so there are no tricks.

Professor Zhang tried to teach the course well, but he is unable to explain concepts clearly. The easier topics were explained decently enough, but he struggled to teach the more difficult topics. Class was spent watching him show stuff in R without any explanations, so be prepared to spend a lot of time outside class teaching yourself.

Love him. Class is super manageable and hw is 40% of your grade. Exams are pretty hard but he is super accommodating and wants you to succeed. My favorite professor in the statistics department for sure

This was the first time Professor Zhang was teaching this class and honestly he did pretty well! He offered a lot of extra credit after the average score for the first midterm was lower than he expected. Tests are open note but not open internet, and as long as you take really good notes after reviewing lectures, the tests are easy.

Zhang did a good job of fostering baseline understanding of the material, but he struggled to explain more advanced concepts, and this was shown sometimes in unclear homework and exam problems. However, he is very open to questions and feedback. I think he's learned a lot from his first semester of teaching STOR455 and will do better in the future.

Very hard course and very heavy workload. It is also his first time teaching it. But he takes feedbacks from students to improve teaching. He is also accessible and patient and helpful with questions. Definitely a great teacher.

Lectures the whole time in every class and you just watch him play in R, which I would say is not the most helpful learning technique. There is no coding pre-req for this class, but there should be. I had absolutely no coding experience and even on LDOC, he just jumped right into R. It took a lot of work to catch up on my own.

Look, 445 is an evil class. But Ziya teaches it in a way that makes it doable. His lecture notes are exactly what is done in class, and self-studying for the last half of the semester really helped my understanding (complex explanations in class had me frazzled). I ended feeling comfortable with stochastic modeling and a B+ out of a 70% final grade

Prof Ziya has done a great job of making a difficult class understandable and enjoyable. He is really good at lecturing and gives a TON of review material for the tests that is super helpful. If you go to class and do the review material you will be fine. I would 100% take this course with him!

**FOR STOR 113 - only a few homeworks, tests make up majority of your grade 3 midterms and one final. I had taken Calculus in highschool so this class was easier for me, but if you haven't before I think it would make this class a lot more challenging (exam averages were normally around a 65). Very generous curve, kind person.

STOR 113 -- Prof. Ziya gets a lot of criticism on here, which is understandable due to his sometimes confusing lectures. That being said, he's very helpful if you reach out and this class really isn't that hard material wise, although exams are often harder than class problems. Very generous final curve. DO NOT take STOR 120 with him though.

STOR 113 The exams are challenging and make up almost 75% of your grade. Averages were quite low but most people did not go to class. If you go to class and his office hours you will be fine, Ziya is very accommodating if you can't make it to his office hours. The exams aren't curved but final grades are curved significantly.
Grades are very hard, and do not provide good advice. Very hard tests.
Hard tests, great curve.
For STOR 133 - not engaging, confusing lectures, and terrible exam averages. exams are majority multiple choice and conceptual. try and take with someone else if possible.

FOR STOR113
Not sure why ratings for this class are low. Professor Ziya walks through every step during his lectures and allows for discussion and makes sure to answer all questions you have during class. His exams are short and if you do the homework and practice exams you will do good. So much better than any other math professors I have had.

This review is for STOR 113. This is a very difficult course. The professor is lecture-heavy, but his lectures are not very clear, and he does not stop to explain what he is doing. The tests are much harder than the practice he provides, and the class averages are consistently low. If you have to take this class, try to find a different professor.
*THIS CLASS IS STOR 113*** One of the worst classes I have ever had at UNC. This class was so hard, averages were very low and tests were nothing what we learned in class. Do not take this class.
Loved Dr. Ziya, he was a great teacher for an interesting class. Everything is exam and no need to do homework really. Just do the old midterms and finals to prep. Great Prof would take again.
Not as good. He did explain things clearly, but the course pace is too slow in my opinion. He didn't even get to queuing theory because the slow pace. The course is boring for me overall.

Your entire grade is based off of tests for 445 but this is standard across department. Compared to other options for professors, Ziya is the person you want to take this difficult course with. I found that, although the material is tough, I enjoyed coming to class each day because the professor made each lecture seem like a set of puzzles to solve

Prof Ziya is a great lecturer and explains concepts well. I haven't read the textbook any and have done fine just from paying attention in class. The entire class is based on 3 midterms and a final. The first midterm average was a 55, but he curves the final so the average student gets a B+. Just study previous exams and hw and you'll be fine.

Prof. Ziya put this class on Auto-pilot mode. No HW and midterms were graded by the TA. He recommended some homework in the book, which is easier than the actual exams. His lectures are from the book, they were not very helpful.  60% for 4 midterms, and 40% final. The midterms are very long and complicated for the 50-minute time frame.

STOR 445 by Prof Ziya is one of the greatest STOR classes I've taken. He explains every concept clearly and he fosters thinking and discussion in the classroom. No homework so the workload is pretty light. There are 4 tests and a final and they are not easy. However, he does curve a lot, so It's not so difficult to get A/A-.

Useful class for industry. Attendance and hw is optional, but textbook is sufficient for learning. Reviewing hw and past exams is enough for exams, which were relatively easy. He drops the lowest of 4 exams which is helpful. Nice guy who is helpful with questions.

This class was hard. 4 tests worth 15% and a final worth 40%. The average on our fourth exam was a 52.33. However, he does curve the class and I do like him as a teacher. I just wish HWs were apart of our grade bc I studied so hard and still received a lackluster grade

Fantastic stats professor, explained things clearly and did not rush to fit in more content. Exams were similar to practice exams made available and open note, and he was helpful in office hours to explain answer keys further. There is no graded homework, so you have to motivate yourself to study and do well.

This class said it was beginner friendly, it was not. I could not drop or pass / fail a launch. Now my GPA is going to go down -1.0. I would not suggest taking this course if you have other STEM classes and you are a beginner coder.

As a course requiring no previous knowledge of stats or python, I expected the professor to do more than copy another professors lessons and provide no explanation of concepts. He admitted to never using python and had no problem with more than half the class failing the midterm. He is a very stubborn grader. The TA was the only helpful resource.

This class was advertised as a first year launch with no need prior knowledge of coding or stats. That was a lie. He never used python and just copied off his notes. Spoke in circles without answering questions in every aspect and found no problem that over 5/6th of the class failed the midterm. Overall, very stubborn grader but nice guy.

Only "teaching" that occurred was copying code off the board supplied by the other professor as he told the TA he had no idea how python works or how to use it-he did not explain any stats terms and expected us to know the significance/how to use the formulas. Class description says "no prior knowledge of stats or python needed" it lied. Enjoy!

Professor Ziya was fine, although fairly boring and can be very detailed with grading. He was fair in grading, he gave all the students one question right on a midterm exam because of poor wording. If you can code, this class will be somewhat easy.
Definitely in the top 2 STEM professors I've had at UNC. STOR 435 is very hard material but he is hilarious and great at explaining the material, and there are many office hours every week.
Great class. Teaches very well. Only issue was loads of homework.

Shankar is incredible! STOR 435 is a very hard class, but he explains things so well and makes the course as straightforward and clear as possible, and the exams are very fair. Lots of homework, but they are very helpful. He is also hilarious.

Highly recommend taking him for 435! Very fair exams and grading, and he allowed us to use a cheat sheet on the final. The hws take a while, but the exams were all variations of hw or practice exam problems. He's also very accessible outside of class and explains difficult concepts in 435 well. Definitely would have done much worse if not for him.
Amazing guy. Super funny and knowledgeable. If you have to take 435 with anyone make sure it's him.

Professor Bhamidi is an excellent professor and cares deeply about the success of his students. On multiple occasions I was able to meet with him outside of his scheduled office hours because I had class during his office hours. He curved the grades at end of semester. Also a funny lecturing that makes a hard class more enjoyable.
I had Dr. Bhamidi for 435H. He's a super nice guy, and class is very manageable if you put in some work. Take Probability with him if you can!!

Shankar was great. He explains the course material very clearly, grades very fairly, and the tests are written very clearly despite the difficult course material. His self-deprecating sense of humor was amazing and kept the class alive. Somehow got an A, thanks in large part to Shankar's clear teaching. My only wish is that he recorded lectures.

Prof. Bhamidi was great this semester! He made calc 3 seem super easy, and although there were a lot of HWs, quizzes, and labs each week (apart from worksheets in class to track attendance), the workload didn't seem unbearable. Be prepared to go to class since he uses the blackboard a lot, and uploads empty slide decks. Stay on track and it's easy!

Shankar made calc 3 very easy to understand by showing us how it is used in the real world. There are weekly homework's, quizzes, and labs. You need to go to class because he works out the problems on the board, and he tends to show super long proofs that may cause you to zone out, but a great professor overall.

Great professor, there are a bunch of assignments for this class that help to balance out your grade and it helps you understand the material well. Explains the material really well during the lectures and is very accessible outside of class. All around great professor.

One of my favorite professors! Coming into the class, I was really intimidated by the topics on the syllabus due to previously struggling a lot with calc. Luckily, Shankar is an excellent lecturer and explains complicated concepts in a digestible way. No surprises on exams; they reflected the difficulty of HW/quizzes. Super nice guy. Def recommend!

Shankar is one of my favorite professors at UNC. The exams were fair and always questions we had seen before in homework or class. You have lots of grade buffers to boost your grade. The final was harder than our other exams, but not unmanageable. If you don't go to class, you will do poorly. His lectures are very important to do well.

Probability is a hard subject, but Shankar's explanations are thorough and his exams are very fair. The class is accessible to people without much statistics background. The exam questions are easier, multiple choice versions of the homework questions. If you stay on top of the homework, it is not too difficult to do well in Shankar's class.

The content is very hard, but Bhamidi is a good professor. It is really easy to get behind. Please pay attention in class and stay up to date because it is so easy to get off track and never get back on.

GOAT. He was a very clear lecturer and explainer and was very nice to the class. He wants you to learn the material but understands the content is hard. His tests aren't too hard (most of my misses were bc reading errors). There is a lot of stuff to do and learn, but he makes it as easy as possible while still teaching you everything. Seek him out!

An absolutely amazing professor. It is very important that you go to lectures as I didn't halfway through and my grade suffered because of it. Regardless though, it was an amazing class and he makes a really difficult subject super accessible. Best STOR 435 professor out there.

Professor Bhamidi is a great lecturer, the reality is just that this is a really hard class and it is very easy to get behind. There is a homework and a quiz each week, and he allows a note sheet for the final (but not the midterms). Go to lecture and pay attention because he doesn't post notes, just slides.

Shankar gives you everything you need to succeed in this class. Homeworks are lengthy and can get difficult, but he is super accessible during office hours and explains problems very well. The lectures were good, and in case you miss lectures there are scribed notes for every class. Awesome teacher and awesome person with a great sense of humour.

I feel bad writing this rating but...the last rating is just not true. I got an A in the class so this isn't a "bitter student rating." He's a very smart man and nice but that's where it ends. He does not know how to teach students, he doesn't give good feedback, and disorganized. And the worst part was the exams and the format...
I love his teaching style. He always helps students to learn and think.

Ridiculously hard and lengthy exams and lectures are not at all helpful as he goes too fast, is very condescending, and is unaccommodating. Has homework due during university holidays. Plus, his textbook is extremely unintuitive to use. Avoid at all costs if you want any chance at saving your grade.
Nice guy, but posts no lectures and then has homework questions that he does no examples of in class. Seems counterintuitive.

Prof. Kulkarni is clearly very smart and knows a lot about the subject, however he does not teach the info. in an effective manner at all. His lectures were very difficult to follow, you really have to teach yourself most of the information. All tests are open note, but exams also make up the vast majority of your final grade. Attendance is graded.

This course was challenging but manageable. The lectures aligned closely with the instructor's textbook, which I liked. Solving the textbook's practice problems and focusing on key concepts are essential. The unknown grading scale made it difficult to guess the grade. My weighted grade was around 92, for your reference.

Very difficult class, maybe more suitable for grad students. Extremely proof heavy lectures with (almost) no proofs on final, so you don't get exposure to what you'll need for the tests except for in homework, which is ambiguously graded
Homework due the day after our wellness days due to the school shooting?? And office hours today, when we're supposed to get the day off for mental health

Kulkarni is a good lecturer. The class material is difficult so you definitely have to put in the work, and the tests are hard, but he gives a very generous curve. Tests are also open book/note. Also he wrote and provided the textbook for free and there are hundreds of practice problems. Grading scale a little unclear. But he does curve.
Difficult class but lecture is fair and the textbook is really good - grading on tests can be hard but the class is curved

Cares for his students sets you up to succeed. Before each class, there was an easy poll everywhere pertaining to material from the last class. Then he goes over it at the start of that class which gives you a chance to see the thought process and ask questions. Professor Pipiras is a very impressive man with plenty of knowledge and accompanying wit. The class is difficult, but doable. You get out what you put in.

Very Easy class. Never went to lecture. Only big grade is group project that is also very easy. Very Easy A!

Super easy class, graded off out of class homework and a final project. No one really goes to lecture as she just posts them anyways.

Super easy. But as other review says, the class proceeds very slowly and only covers very little knowledge that is actually useful and interesting. Clear grading rubrics. lenient and easy grading criteria, 40% homework, 20% pop quizzes with points that could be earned back through extra credit, 40% final project. lectures were dull at times but followable with motivation

Difficult course, but Budhiraja was a great lecturer and was extremely helpful in office hours.

To all future students, if you're planning to take STOR555, get out while you still can. Find another way to get credit for this class, because this is not the way you want to do it.
Nobel's lectures are clear and very concise. I compare to other lectures from the same classes of different schools, they are basically similar. He is very nice and approachable outside class.

cant find a 555 option, so im putting this under 565. its laughable how bad bro is at lecturing. tests are needlessly long. only thing that saved me from failing was decent hw grades. hard agree with the other person who said this dude says you tell me to every question.

a lot of homework but no final and shes a really generous grader. will give you full credit on the final project if you put a good faith effort in.

horrible midterm

genuinely hell experience. awaiting final grade and likely to finish anywhere from B to A- but just an absolutely horrible class that was 100x harder than previous iterations of it for no apparent reasons.
