This was by far the hardest class I have ever taken. The exams were very hard and you needed to study for two weeks to just pass the exams. Mariana however is accessible outside of class and wants to help. Just know if you plan on taking this course, buckle up. Originally, I had a D but my final grade was "curved" to a B so that slayed.

Class started off strong with a decent first midterm. However, the second exam had an average of 40 with most of the blame being put on us, with content we really had not seen before. 80% of your final grade is exams, it requires a lot of work and studying with no results, seeing as how the final was also extremely difficult.

One of our midterms class average was a 40. She just reads exactly what the textbook says and makes the tests harder than the homework. She spent 2 classes asking us why we did so bad on the exam that she wrote. Do not take a class with her.

Weekly homeworks which get very difficult and I spent a lot of time on them every week. Attend lecture but if you really can't, she follows the textbook closely. Tests are hard. Our second midterm everyone failed so she released the same exam as a take-home to count as 40% of it, so she tries to help when she can.

This is by far one of the hardest class I've taken, but Prof Olvera is a great professor. She gave good examples, but she did go pretty fast so you definitely have to pay attention closely to pretty much everything she says. The tests are super difficult and require A LOT of studying and practice.

Prof. Olvera has a clear passion for math and teaching, she's so understanding and holds your hand through otherwise impossible problems. Homeworks and long and incredibly difficult, midterm exams are just as hard even though open note. Open note final is 40% of your grade but almost copies examples from lecture notes.

Super sweet lady. I like her as a person. Hardest class I've ever taken x1000. Tests were nearly impossible. Other stor professors would look at exams and be shocked she asked us those questions. Said she was giving same tests as she did to engineering students at Columbia University. I have never worked so hard in a class just to get a C.

Overall a good lecturer, but she missed a week in the middle of the semester and then tested the class on concepts that we had not learned yet. She also moves through examples a bit too fast, essentially copying from the textbook with little extra explanation unless questions are asked.

Good professor. Lectures were straight out of the book, but she answers questions well and attempts to help people understand. Regardless of the professor, the class is extremely difficult. Two midterms: 1st easy and 2nd very hard, final tough, and homeworks are weekly. If you have to take 435, try to take it with her, but be ready to struggle.

Professor Olvera is a genius and she is extremely well spoken when it comes to statistics; however, that does not take away from how difficult this material is. If you fall behind, it is almost impossible to catch up. I respect her so much as a professor and it is clear that she wants her students to learn, but be prepared to fight for your grade.
very hard! the tests are way easier than hw (so much hw) but still hard. the first test was easy and the second was hard. avoid taking her for 435!

Didn't enjoy 305 (stor minor). Really wanted more active learning opportunities in class. She gave us a 2-part HW due 2 days before the final. The HWs require excel and on average took me 10+ hours each but exams don't even use excel. Stingy exam partial credit; 1st exam median was 77. 2nd midterm and final pretty easy though.

Mr. McCance is a nice guy- but if you want to learn stats, I would suggest taking a different professor. He uses the chalkboard- often with illegible writing. His lectures are not well planned, often reads slides off his phone. I basically taught myself the entire course. Exams curved 20-30% because so many people fail. UNC stop making TA's teach.
McCance is really nice, but at the end of the day his lectures are very difficult to follow.

This guy did not show up for the last two weeks of classes. Took forever to grade midterms. KhanAcademy might be your best friend if you end up taking a course with him since you have to teach yourself a lot.

Easy class if you have previous experience with stats, but lectures were extremely boring and hard to pay attention to. Exams were medium difficulty but get insanely curved, so its hard to get a bad grade in this class. Also takes forever to grade exams. Only allowed to miss 2 classes before attendance deduction. Prof is funny sometimes though.

Kind and caring professor outside of class. Accessible for office hours, but the lectures were very boring and hard to follow. Basically taught all of stats to myself using the textbook. Very disorganized professor and takes forever to grade. However, the curve is generous, and he is accommodating.

Canceled classes the last weeks of the semester, gave us our midterm back days before the exam. Notes were all over the place and he would sometimes get his own problems wrong when writing them down. The homework was inconsistent and I had to teach myself most of the material in the class. He does heavily curve the exams though.

McCance is probably one of the easiest professors to take STOR 155 with. He starts with the basics. We only had 7 homework assignments which take about an hour. He does take a while to return the midterms but curves them a lot. The exams are fair and he allows cheat sheets, so you can write all the equations and steps down.

McCance was very nice and tried his best to be helpful. Overall, the class was challenging and I had a hard time following lectures. I had to learn a lot on my own and the midterms were kind of unreasonable and took a long time to grade (but he didn't have TAs), but they were curved a lot, which made this class worth it.

Very nice guy and cares about his students, but his lectures were pretty disorganized and confusing. Also took ages to grade our midterms. However, you do get cheat sheets and curves for the exams, which made it fine, but I didn't really learn statistics.

Not the best teacher but i only attended like 4 lectures. Exams are difficult but curve is INSANE taught myself the whole course because hes lowk a bad teacher but super kind and cares a lot about his students. Gives great accommodations lectures put me to sleep though lol
Very little homework, easy exams with heavy curves, allows cheat sheets for exams. You don't learn a ton but can achieve an A with very minimal effort.

He is very nice, but very disorganized and unresponsive to emails. He hardly posts materials/hw for review and lectures were very confusing. He curved the tests a lot, which made the class worth it tbh. Don't take this class if you actually need/want to learn stats. Not having taken AP STATS made me struggle more than others lol

took forever on grading midterms. made office hours at 7pm to find out our midterm grades and didn't show. he barely posts study material for the midterms. lectures are terrible and he says intuitively a lot lol. he never answers emails even though he says to email him. he cancels class a lot (says he's sick tbf). this class made me WANT to do hw

barely homework, and tests aren't impossible, but he doesn't show up (idk how else to say it) for the last two weeks of school he cancelled basically every class because he was sick to be fair but he didn't even hold zoom or offer alternative ways to learn the material. He doesn't answer emails and is inconsistent w being present at office hours
Very unorganized and hard to follow. Lectures are super boring, he just reads off the text book the entire time. He lost my exam I took in October and still hasn't graded it almost 2 months later.

Very unorganized. As of May 12th at 9:48 p.m. (graduation was two days ago), our grades still haven't been posted. Be prepared to deal with this during the whole semester. He quite literally took 1 month to give us our first midterm grade, which was about a week after the last day to withdraw.

He's super unorganized and hard to get a hold of because he doesn't answer emails. Simply a bad teacher but luckily he curved the tests a lot because we all did badly. The lectures were boring and he explained every topic poorly.

Nice guy, horrible lectures, curves a lot. Terrible attendance policy, which is why I have a B+ and not an A. Also takes FOREVER to grade. Took him 1 month to grade midterm 1 and 3 weeks for midterm 2. Took even longer for him to give us our curved grades back. I wish UNC would stop making grad students teach because they're just not good at it

Lectures were awfully boring and I hated how he used the chalkboard instead of slides because it was super unorganized & confusing. Attendance was required but I never paid attention and just read the textbook sections. Midterm 2 was crazy difficult but he curved it a lot. My score went from a 52 to 92. Cheat sheets allowed and each midterm was 20%

lectures the entire time, everyone falls asleep. teaches on a chalk board with his own page of notes. taught myself the entire course from youtube. second midterm was extremely hard for no reason. Nice guy tho, cares for his students. But course was harder than it needed to be.

Eva is very passionate about statistics, and you can tell she is very knowledgable but she tends to get ahead of herself during class and makes errors throughout the lecture. She also explains concepts poorly. If you have the option to take this class with someone else then do that.

Unorganized and gets stuff confused all the time. If students don't correct her she will be teaching incorrect things She is also making the final hard. She makes everything more complicated than it has to be. If you have the option to take it with someone else you should, but you can still get a good grade with her it is just a miserable process.

Dr Loeser is enthusiastic about stats, but made a lot of math errors when doing calculations on the board for us to follow along. She is very nice and always willing to explain something, even if it seems obvious. 2 exams, she is a pretty fair grader. I didn't study too much besides making my cheat sheet the night before exams.

She cares about her work & is compassionate for her students. Grading is fair & clear & she always answered any Qs. She's slightly disorganized & made errors in lecture. Explanations were difficult to follow: imo it's best to go to lecture then read the textbook. Show up, do the work, stay up to date & you'll be fine. I barely studied and got an A

Loved having Dr. Loeser, she is a kind, genuinely happy person. She is excited to lecture everyday and gives time for the material to sink in while she's talking, as she wants everyone to understand what concepts we are learning. Let's you have cheat sheet on both midterms and the final, isn't terribly difficult.

Do not take this course. The professor constantly makes mistakes during lectures, especially with formulas. Students have to correct her mistakes in almost every class. We get emails after class correcting what she taught. Exams are inconsistent with how we learn in class, and she won't release correct answers. One of the worst classes I've taken.

She's super excited to be teaching and will explain things in different ways for understanding. Super accessible and helpful outside of class. She tends to make mistakes when writing and talking at the same time, but it's easy to keep up as long as you pay attention. As long as you understand the homework, the exams will be an easy A!

She is a very kind and generous teacher. I know professors are allowed to make mistakes, but Ms. Loeser makes many, although the mistakes result in more flexible grading. I had a background in statistics already so it was probably easier for me than others who don't.

Prof. Loeser is very patient and understanding. STOR 151 may not be the most exciting class but she truly cares for her students. I would highly recommend attending lectures and office hours!! Especially if you have any questions on the homework, prof. Loeser is excellent one-on-one!
Took 415. Cannot teach but is a lenient grader
took stor 415 with him, this professor CANNOT teach

Took stor 415 with him, he made hardest exams and homework take forever to do. In class, he will give you the most basic examples, but then have the exceptional cases on the quiz and homework, where you have no idea how to even approach them. Lectures are super uninteresting.

Currently taking for STOR415 (not listed on ratemyprofessor). Held class on Tuesday despite class being cancelled due to the winter storm (we were in condition 2 until 12pm, and he held class from 9:30-10:45AM). Holds quizzes throughout the semester, and makes you to stay in class 10 minutes late if you want a chance at completing the quizzes.

I liked him overall. A bit difficult but that's discrete, not him. Overall, he graded pretty leniently and I only got a B because I sold on the final (maybe not a good first semester class while taking 17 credits!) BUT that's more on me and I think if I had less credits and more college experience it wouldn't have been such a crunch at the end. W!

I had Prof. Nezhad a few semesters ago, and I'm not sure why there are so many negative reviews. He went above and beyond to be accommodating when I was having a tough semester. Lectures were detailed and clear, discrete is just a challenging subject. It's possible something's changed since I've taken a class w/ him, but I had a good experience.

He should not be teaching Discrete Mathematics. He implied a curve that he did not deliver on, was difficult to understand, and did not take our critiques for the length of exams. The second midterm saw the entire class scrambling to finish. He rambled on in class but to be fair was a kind professor. Take MATH 381. This is not worth it.

Took him a while ago. He was not an understanding professor and could not teach the material well. Would get hung up on seating assignments during quizzes, so much so that he would single kids out to move around the classroom as if we were playing musical chairs until it was to his liking.

got 100 for both 2midterms but for final only 86…Really hard!!
Quiz is based on homework but with slight change, homework is long and weekly, lecture is good but his handwriting is hard to distinguish
Hard class Hard professor...RUN

Very difficult professor that didn't understand the needs of the class. I found it difficult to study for the course due to the lack of guidance on what would be tested. There are slight bonus points on the midterms and no curve or bonus points on the final. I would not recommend.

Worst professor I've had so far at UNC. When the class expressed concerns over a lack of time for the midterm, he dismissed us and made the next midterm longer. He's one of the most unapproachable professors at UNC. He tends to mansplain and answer questions in a way that makes them seem insignificant. The homework was a nightmare and midterms and the final were much harder. We didn't even get a heavily implied curve at the end. Overall I would recommend switching majors over taking this class with him.

He pretty much summarizes the information from the textbook without going into much detail. Tests have a slight curve, but the material is more difficult than that of the homework. There was no study material for the final exam either.

Professor was not understanding of my circumstances. Worst experience at UNC (coming from a straight A student)

One of the best professors I've had in the STOR department. However, the final in this course on probability was much more difficult than the midterms and what we did in lectures/homeworks. He is also a very generous grader if you show your work.

Agreed with the last comment on Piazza over office hours. He did seem distracted in person but I prefer Piazza so that's alright with me. I have not had many professors lecture like him before as he is very interactive with the class. I enjoyed him stopping to ask us questions to be sure we understood but did feel he was a bit patriarchal at times.

Lots of homework but he gives great feedback on Piazza if you ask questions. I'd recommend this over office hours because you can definitely tell his mind is elsewhere. It's not the most interesting subject. Pretty easy class, as the grading is just very generous. Whether that's on homeworks, quizzes, or tests, they always give heavy partial credit. The first 3/4 of the class is very easy, the last unit on probability is a bit hard. You learn a good amount, some real world application especially with excel.

Professor Ali is a great lecturer and teaches concepts really clearly and well. His homeworks are straightforward and relates well to the lecture content and exams. Lenient grader on quizzes and exams. Gives extra credit questions on exams as well.

STAY FAR AWAY!!! This was the worst class I have ever taken at UNC. The exams were not fair at all. He included trick questions on all the exams that were already out of line with his lectures. His handouts weren't even his, and I don't think I learned a single thing from his teaching. Run as far away from this class as possible.

This class is extremely evil, but so is every STOR155 section. Mario is the only professor who teaches 155 that is NOT a grad student, so he has much more experience teaching the coursework. Mario's a great guy with great sense of humor, but Disclaimer: THIS CLASS IS HARD. If you do not want to challenge yourself, do not take this class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS... Mario is undoubtedly the worst. He will tell you to read the textbook, but not have the same material on exams, ridicule you, and waste your time. If Mario only curves to "fix the mistakes in his teaching," but there is a 20% curve, how can he claim that he's a decent professor? Nightmare professor for an introductory course.

If you do not have a foundation in statistics please find another Stor 155 professor. Midterm averages in the 50s because he designs the most absurd, convoluted questions to trip you up. It's obvious he despises his students' success: he just rambles about his own code and the "slides" are just ss of his own code. He offers a 7% curve, since only two people had an A before it. Mario is not a good teacher, he talks very fast and goes off on tangents. For an intro level stats course, this class is way too hard. The tests are designed to trick you. Don't take Mario, the first week he said we would hate him and that it was his job to weed us out. Studying was stressful, he was rude, lectures made no sense, didn't grade ANYTHING until 2 days before the final, did curve heavy though.
He's really funny and makes the material memorable. The class can be challenging, but the curve helps. Overall, he's a great professor if you pay attention and put in the effort.

Good teacher if your willing to learn, ask questions, and go to office hours if you need help. Goes in depth about every topic if you ask. Super rememberable and funny. Practice the homework, don't use AI, create one pagers, & study. I wish the curve was lower, seriously, some people deserved to fail.
Do not take this class. truly the worst professor I have had at unc. even though he curves at the end, the amount of pressure during the semester when you saw your grade was a 40% was insane.

My rating probably would have been lower but the professor gave a 20% final curve, effectively bumping my C+ all the way to an A. Listen, this is a HARD class. If it was supposed to be easy, everyone would just get an A. It's HARD. Dr. Mario is a nice guy who laughs at himself and cracks jokes. Doesn't explain concepts well and over complicates things, also goes on lots of tangents during lectures. 2 midterms (25% each) and the final (35%) are all MCQ but he intentionally makes the questions very tricky. Mario was a pretty mediocre teacher. He was a nice guy overall, but his lectured were pretty confusing. He makes very difficult exams and you will have no idea what your final grade is until the end. Do not take this professor. The class isn't hard, but the exams are poorly written and don't match the lectures. A midterm had to be curved by 20% because of how badly it was designed.

Hilarious but extremely egotistical and conceited. Don't take this class if you've never taken stats before, but if you have, you'll be fine. Gives zero insight on exams, so studying feels like a gamble.

Condescending, egotistical, bad lecturer, and exams don't reflect the homework at all. He wants his students to fail and has a weird complex about proving that we "don't belong at UNC Chapel Hill". Pope Francis once said that he hopes no one goes to hell, but I promise you he wouldn't have said that had he met Mario. Horrible. Save yourself.

Confusing lectures and tests that look nothing like any materials given. Said he hopes we get weeded out and have to work at McDonald's. Super unhelpful and rude. Some may say he's “funny” but it's just a waste of time. I was a straight A student before this class.

He's intelligent and personable but I have some gripes with his teaching style. This is the first time I've felt compelled to write a rmp review. The content itself should not be that difficult, but she barely explains anything in an effective way. Really great professor, must have just been a bad 320 curriculum.

I have never rated before but I had to for her because how harsh the prior ratings are. I think she's an incredible teacher who clearly is passionate and is good at explaining the content. For 455 at least I would highly recommend. She gave extra credit/test correction possibilities for everyone.

Terrible Professor. Reads off slides like a robot and doesn't know how to teach. Honestly Kendall is a very nice person who's willing to help us learn something, but there are so many assignments for this class and the grading is super harsh, making this class is more workload heavy than some 500-level STOR classes.

Horrible grading, she's a nice person, but her TA grades exceptionally harsh. Also an absurd amount of assignments, 4+ a week. Just save yourself the trouble and take the class with someone else.

The lectures aren't as bad as people say, but I think there are way too many assignments in a given week. do not take this class with her. also, grading is harsh and also take forever.
although she is difficult she is a nice lady def does not deserve this much hate

Kendall is mid. She gives a lot of assignments which take hours to complete. It is insane and the grading is very harsh as well. She is nice if you go to office hours, but the class gives too much work.

I agree that for an intro class, the amount of work we do is a bit much, but seriously it's not that bad. 30% of your grade is based on midterms, but there is still a huge cushion for it with homework assignments and the final project. He is very friendly and the class can be dry but is straightforward. Gives very helpful practice materials for midterms. Very accommodating on deadlines and changed the class based on our math backgrounds. Daily quiz for attendance. 1 HW each week that takes < 2hours

Probably one of the best options for the required 500 level class in the statistics major. Exams are all open book/open note and align very well with practice exams. Difficult but reasonable given the course level. Homework takes about 2-3 hours per week.

Dr. Smith tries to enable students to understand the intrinsically difficult material for the Advanced Methods of Data Analysis class. Grade comes mostly from tests. Prof Smith is obviously very knowledgable about the subject. Lectures can be pretty boring though. Professor smith has been one of the best professors I've had at Carolina. He cares about his students and helps his students succeed. dont bother going to lectures. dude talks about swamp water

CHEM at UNC is very difficult; however, Bliem knows her stuff and is very kind. Her lectures are very helpful for exams. I've had a year of gen chem with her, and my experience has been fine. Definitely a lot of work, but the professor for gen chem has little bearing on your grade. Just go to Chem Possible and use other outside learning materials.

the unc chem department is notoriously difficult, and there's no other way she could teach this class because of the curriculum, but her lectures were extremely helpful in outlining exactly what to look for in the exams. go to gpss, use peer tutoring, do chempossible, do the exam type questions and you'll be okay.

Just not a good lecturer. For the chems your professor doesnt matter that much, but I have heard that every other professor is better than her. It is easy to tell that she doesn't want to be teaching Gen Chem, just take it with Fostvedt.

Bliem is fine, i never rly spoke w her personally but she seems funny and kind. Good handwriting. Gives eccentric aunt vibes. I loved taking 102 with my table (shoutout carroll 111 active learning lab!) You MUST study above and beyond to be prepared for niche details on exams. I found 101 (test avg 98) much easier than the 102 exams (test avg 89).

The Chem department in itself is very difficult, and it was already highly suggested to attend GPSS and ULA sessions outside of class. However, Professor Bliem was very charismatic in the 6-minute meetings, and she does a good job attending to questions in GPSS.

Transferred in and took 102 my first semester. Do not use AI to help you with your smart work or you are so screwed on exams. you need at least two days to review the smart works and slides. I've heard people say Chad's Prep helps. You need to do all the problems on the slides before class. Pretend you're a ULA.

Bliem is a decent professor for CHEM 101/102, but she can be condescending. She gets annoyed when you ask about testing accommodations or midterm questions, even when you're just trying to prepare. She knows the material, but her attitude can make asking for help uncomfortable.

The Textbooks do not suffice for being a flipped classroom. I never was able to learn from Bliem's descriptions- find a good ULA and cling to them. You MUST attend the worksheet sessions and ChemPossible and do the practice problems. I never figured out how to crack the exams.

Bliem does an amazing job at explaining difficult concepts. Her lectures are interesting if you actually pay attention. Although chem is hard, I feel Bliem does a great job of making it easier and doable. The Chem department in general is hard, so even though you will have to put in a lot to succeed, it is very doable with her.

Professor Bliem is amazing and extremely good at her job.  The class is difficult and requires a lot of work but she is clear and doesn't confuse you in lectures.  Her lectures are a little mono tone but its chemistry.
Dr. Bliem is an amazing professor who wants each and every one of her students to succeed.  The content is not easy to learn and requires an absolute ton of outside studying.

She seems like a nice person, but the way she delivered her lectures were so boring. Fell asleep multiple times in class because of how boring the lectures were. If you have to take Chem with Professor Bliem, sit in the first 3 rows so you don't fall asleep during the lectures.

chem101 at unc is HARD, regardless of who's teaching it. Dr. Bliem is super nice though and knows what she is talking about, and I'm very glad I had her. Go to lecture, sit in the front row, actively participate, ask questions, do all of your homework, study hard, and you'll be alright! It's a hard class, but she wants to see you succeed.

Chem 101 is going to be a tough class no matter what. Bliem is one of the better chem profs imo and actually cares about you succeeding and understanding. Lectures can be boring and monotone, but I actually enjoyed them and thought she was really funny. Exams will be harder than you expect, be sure to study everything before and after class.

She was a very nice and caring professor and made us laugh at times. But sometimes her lectures were pretty boring, and I had to learn it after the lecture. The midterms were hard and the final was harder

Prof Bliem is a great person but chem at UNC just sucks. They expect you to know the content before lecture so the lecture isn't much help if you've never taken AP chem. Prof fostvedt's slides were the most useful in studying so I would try to take her. I also just stopped listening in lecture and began to teach myself and seemed to do better.

Chem is hard, and I don't blame my grade on Dr. B but on the organization of the dept as a whole. Bliem is as kind as it gets and made me feel very seen in class. I ended getting close with one of her TAs which significantly improved my experience. I made sure to enroll in her 102. she's a gem and deserves the world.

Professor Bliem is very kind. Especially with a hard class like chem, she is really approachable and I felt comfortable asking questions in and outside of class. She is also pretty funny. You do have to work hard in the class but I think that's because of the subject and I think Professor Bliem does a good job of explaining the concepts.

Dr. Bliem was very enthusiastic and kind all semester. A lot of the bad reviews are here because the tests are hard. It is a weed out class... that's just how its gonna be. I think she does a good job of explaining the content and makes lectures interesting. Chemistry tests get a 2/5 Dr. Bliem prepares you well and gets 5/5.
Professor Bliem did a good job explaining difficult concepts. This class was difficult but doable if you have the time to work hard for it.

Bliem is the best. She's straightforward and her lectures are very understandable. CHEM 101 is difficult no matter who you take it with but the best way to succeed is by leaning into the flipped classroom. Also be sure to ask the ULA's whenever you have questions. I would absolutely take 101 with Bliem again if i had the opportunity.

Dr. Bliem is a good instructor who has engaging lectures. CHEM 101 at UNC is just very difficult. If I had to take it again, I would take it with her. CHEM 101 is essentially only graded on tests, which are very tricky. My best advice is to keep up with the readings and do the homeworks without Googling the answers.
Really funny and engaging during lectures, explains chemistry in a way that makes sense. Coming from someone who does not like chemistry, she made this class enjoyable and understandable.
Gen Chem at UNC is horrific but Bliem is probably your best bet as a professor.

Ive taken chem101-adjacent coursework three times and I can honestly say bliem does an okay job teaching it. The main struggle comes with exams which are purposely made INSANELY hard for no reason. As a chem major who enjoys chem, exams are not an accurate reflection of your knowledge. Take fostvedt if possible, but bliem is still solid.
She is an effective teacher for a challenging class. Exams are quite difficult, but she doesn't make them.

Prof Bliem obviously cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. However, I found the class to be incredibly difficult and I will be retaking it. Sometimes I felt that she glossed over important topics or did a poor job in explaining them. Get ready to teach yourself most of the material.
She is the best CHEM professor you can get. Utilize her office hours because she cares and wants you to learn, chemistry is just a hard class.

Honestly, at least for CHEM101, I don't understand Prof. Mclaughlin's low rating. She gives great lectures and, despite being in a classroom full of 200 students, makes an effort to ensure everyone understands the topics. Chem midterms are difficult, but this is not Bliem's fault.

Bliem is a very sweet professor. Her lower rating isn't deserved quite honestly. The chem department at UNC is hardcore and she does not reflect that. She does a decent job at lecturing. She is funny and genuinely a kind person.

This class sucks, no matter who you take it with. The tests are brutal, the homework is long, and there's a ridiculous number of things you have to buy. Bliem's fine. She adds a bit of humor and some fairly clear lectures. Most of class is spent on practice problems, so use the opportunities you have to make friends to study with.
I love carribeth

Chem 102 as a standardized course is difficult, considering the majority of your grade is based on 4 exams, Bliem herself is a great, funny lecturer and really makes sure you understand the content. I took the launch section with a class of about 20 which made the experience more personalized, def reccomend for any freshmen with 101 credit already.

Chem 102 is hard and its easy to lose a lot of points on the tests. Bliem was always very kind and cheerful in class. She does kinda expect you to understand everything from the textbook, class is mostly just practice problems. The test questions are usually harder than in class questions. I wouldn't have gotten an A if I didn't take AP chem in HS

Professor Bliem is, overall, a good professor for CHEM 102, but you have to teach yourself how to use a lot of concepts outside of class. As long as you study the practice exams and LA review sessions you will do fine and she is clear about explaining concepts in the lecture.

Dr. Bliem is probably your best choice out of the 101/102 pool. I had her for both lectures and have done well in both because she explains things well. Chem is chem but hedge your bets with Bliem instead of someone else.

Bliem is a great professor who truly cares about her students. CHEM101 is challenging, but she provides the resources to succeed, like annotated notes. Attend lectures and use unstuckstudy AI for helpful study prep.

Professor Bliem while covering all of the topics provided vague and often confusing lectures. Most of the learning was done outside the classroom or by reading the textbooks and I often referred to other professors notes when looking back at the lecture notes. Although exams are the same get a professor who teaches in a more in depth way.

I loved Bliem. Chem at UNC is no joke, but Bliem definintely made it easier. She clearly wanted us to succeed and was always willing to help if I had a question after class. The important thing to know is that you will have to study to do good in this class, but the content itself really isn't that bad.

If you are looking for a Gen Chem professor, look no further. Dr. Bliem is a great lecturer and loves to interact with students. She takes her time explaining concepts in class and has no issue with explaining them again. Gen Chem is hard, but it doesn't have to be painful. My grade truly doesn't do her teaching style justice (or maybe it does).

Professor Bliem is very sweet. You can tell she truly enjoys what she is teaching. She also starts off class with her 'pet of the day' trend she does and it's absolutely adorable. Would recommend if you need CHEM-102.
I absolutely loved this professor and she always had a positive attitude and was very helpful. However, the course in general was just too much and I do not recommend. TAKE AT A COMMUNITY COLLEGE!
I took this class a year ago but she was the goat as of May 2023.

Chem sucks, but it wasn't that bad if you put the work in. Mrs. bliem was an okay professor very monotone. Get fosvetdt or however you spell it. Use her annoted notes they help a lot.  Also don't get behind or you're cooked.

Professor Bliem is a fantastic professor who truly cares about the students in her class. CHEM101 will be a difficult class, so you should prepare accordingly, but she gives you all the necessary resources to succeed. Make sure you attend lectures, and an iPad may help too.

Professor Bliem is a great teacher, Chem 101 is by nature, a very difficult class. She cares about you but there is only so much she can help you with. A lot of the learning is on your own. I say make good study groups with the people in your class and take advantage of the 6-minute meetings offered (no matter which professor you get).

Bliem is hilarious and a good teacher, but you have to work even more outside of class to go above and beyond to understand the concepts because she does not teach that in-depth. Smartwork assignments and participation points help boost your grade just like 101. If you don't spend time every week going through the material, you will fail the class.

Bliem was a great prof, and probably the best option for 101. I haven't heard any complaints about her, but I can't say the same for the other 101 profs. Definitely the hardest class I've taken here so far, and requires a lot of outside work to succeed. I think Bliem would be close to a 5.0 if the course wasn't so difficult.

Professor Bliem and the Chem Department get a lot of hate that is really unwarranted. I ended up pass/failing this class, but I would have gotten an A-. The UNC chem department is hard no doubt, but as long as you actually do the work, attend class and recitation, and go to an occasional GPSS if you have questions, you will be fine.

Dr. Bliem was a great 102 professor. She spent time breaking down the content into more manageable problems and Bliem does a great job of pointing out common errors. The content is difficult and does take time to wrap your head around but GPSS is available outside of lecture. She also cracks some good jokes during lecture :)

Dr. Bliem is a hilarious lecturer and a wonderful professor! She tries really hard to make chemistry accessible, but if you are struggling you need to go to GPSS while you're doing the material in lecture. Overall, I loved her class and thought she made the painful experience of learning chemistry fun!

She does not thoroughly go over any topic. She spends 1 minute on each problem and goes so fast I can't keep up. The textbook did not give enough step-by-step instructions. Info was scattered across lectures, study sessions, and extra help sessions. I spent 10+ hours a week and still did horribly on the tests.

Prof. Bliem is a great person but not very good at explaining. You either understand the content or you do not and then it is up to you to learn it on your own. It is clear she expects you to understand what was read in the textbook prior to class and will not spend time explaining in detail. She does detail problems on sides which is nice.

Prof. Bliem is a solid teacher. Chem 101 has a common curriculum, so she teaches the same slides and content as the other professors. Sometimes lectures can get dry, but she is very clear and there are a lot of resources to succeed in the class. Chemistry at UNC is tough, but she did a good job explaining concepts and supporting students.
tough exams and lots of hw

Prof Bliem is great and does what she can with the terrible UNC chem department. I had her for both 101 and 102. She is aware of how difficult this course is and makes lectures bearable. Overall if you have to take chem here, Bliem is a solid option.

Bliem is funny, kind, and a great prof. This class is super hard. If you plan to take it, take Bliem or Fostvedt. The other profs do not know how to explain content (at least when I went to their group problem solving sessions) I bombed the 1st midterm but if you lock in from the start you could make an A for sure bc there are a lot of resources.

Dr. Bliem was a great professor. The class sucked. Chem 101 was difficult for me and a lot of other students. Ratings for Dr. Bliem are not fair (she's a great professor, but the class is just hard). Three "midterms," where the lowest is 12%, and the two others are 18% of the grade. The final is worth 27% of the final grade. So VERY test heavy.
Honestly everyone warned me that she wasn't a great teacher, but she really is not that bad. It is a "flipped" learning style so if you don't do the reading before class the lecture makes zero sense

She is an ok lecturer and the class itself is relatively difficult. Her lectures are organized and give you sufficient time to practice she just doesn't offer anything unique. She has a dry sense of humor and can be a little rude at times but otherwise, she's a fine option for chem for anyone with a decent stem background and aptitude.
The worst professor I had in my 4 years at Chapel Hill

Bleim explains concepts poorly, and contradicts the textbook daily. When she asks questions to the class, she does not pass a microphone to students who are answering questions, and doesn't really explain why they are right or wrong.
Worst class I have ever taken in my entire life. Bliem is not helpful and contradicts the textbook daily.

Took in the fall. Please do yourself a favor and take a different professor for CHEM 101. She doesn't explain things that well. Will be retaking with Fosvedt. Regardless of the teacher I definitely recommend CHEMpossible, SI sessions, Peer Mentors, and Peer Tutors for this class. Very hard. Exams are a nightmare. It IS a weed out class.

I loved this course so much and Dr. Bliem is extremely helpful, intelligent, and can explain things on a great level! I think that this was the perfect introduction to CHEM.

YOU MUST PRATICE TO DO WELL.

EVERYONE WHO RATED HER LESS THAN 4 --- it is because they did not do enough work or use the resources on campus.

Overall chem is a very hard course. With any teacher it is required to read the textbook and teach yourself most of the material. Bliem did a decent job at teaching and connecting pre-reading to lessons. The prework and homework wasn't too bad but the tests were the most difficult.

She is an ok teacher although I feel as if she went too slow some times and it was hard to pay attention to her. My bigger issue was that she was absent for the redox reaction lesson and then a few questions of the redox reaction lesson were on the final and I along with multiple people I know were unable to answer those questions due to that.

Dr. Bliem is a severely underrated professor. She is very skilled at explaining new concepts and answering q's during lecture. 101 will never be an easy class, but she provides many resources for studying and asking q's to the point that any issues I had were more about the time and energy I spent using them. Also she's very funny.
As long as you read the textbook you will be fine. Just make sure to do the work and the notes and then the class won't be too hard.

Do not take this class with Bliem. Literally contradicts the textbook everyday in lecture and instead of explaining her reasoning she simply says "got it" and goes on. I have learned nothing from this class, thank God I was able to pass fail it. In the end I would have likely gotten a B+ but this class is hell and not enjoyable at all.
Good at explaining things and can always point out common mistakes and misconceptions. This class is hard but Bliem is a good bet to get through it.

She's respectful and funny and her lectures were always easy to follow (as long as i did all the homework and warmups, which requires some time). Make sure to not fall behind with the content and be ready to study a lot. That, together with following the lectures, prepared me for the exams better than just studying by my self the days before.

dr. bliem is a really sweet professor, but her voice made me fall asleep in her lectures. honestly, chem 101 isn't hard at all as long as you actually do the pre-class readings and learn how to apply the concepts properly by putting effort into your assignments. also since shes the boss lady she gives valuable info on what to expect on a test

Two midterms, equally weighted, one short presentation with a discussion post, one long presentation which spans over several months. On top of this, there is a cumulative final exam. Must meet with him in office hours for the presentation. Rates "engagement" but doesn't even remember who speaks and still takes points off because he can.

Really enjoyed this class. Content was very manageable and exams were straightforward if you studied beforehand. Large part of the class focuses on a chemistry presentation on your own topic, which was fun to make. Beaver was accessible outside class and was very helpful with presentation prep. Can't recommend enough.

Dr. Beaver is a great teacher during lecture and really breaks down the material in an enthusiastic way. That being said, his exams are very difficult and contain a lot of niche material. I gave him a 3 because he is quite rude and condescending to students who asked him questions on 1 to 1.

I loved Beaver for orgo 2, genuinely wants his students to succeed and get the most out of his class. Orgo 2 is a hard subject theres no workaround, but if you put in the effort it is very doable. Listen to his suggestions on how to study. Attend GPSS and do the ULA worksheets. Sit in the front, ask and answer questions in class.

man he's a good prof but unless you're confident you know the material he's not worth it. his exams are the hardest out of the entire department and the stress is unreal. i got out with an A but then my physical health genuinely declined due to the stress solely from that class. unless you want your entire life to be chem, dont take him.

Beaver is a great guy and probably knows the course content he's teaching better than anyone. Yes the midterms are very challenging but the final is much more fair in my opinion. If you got through orgo 1 with a decent grade, you know what to expect with Beaver. Study hard for the midterms and practice practice practice and you will succeed.

Dr. Beaver is one of my favorite chemistry professors at UNC. He genuinely cares, will listen to student feedback, and is amazing at breaking down difficult concepts. His GPSS is super helpful and his class is very engaging. I highly recommend taking 262 with him.

Dr. Beaver is really nice and truly wants you to succeed. Explains content well during lecture and provides a lot of resources to succeed, but the exams are HARD. You need to do all of the practice material he offers and understand everything fully, but that's probably true regardless of the professor for organic chemistry.

His lectures are great and he's incredibly knowledgeable about the material. He expects lot from students, but also cares about learning if you want to learn. I'd recommend if you truly want an understanding of organic chemistry, take it with him, but if you want the best letter grade you can get, take it with someone else.

I enjoyed 262 with Dr. Beaver. His lectures make sure you will know the content. There's just a lot. Exams always have a few trippy questions, but fair overall. Did amazing on the first 3 and poorly on the final due to other stuff. An A is certainly possible if you spend 1-2 hours a day practicing. He gave some extra credit too so can't complain.

Orgo is just a hard class, and it takes a lot of time to understand and memorize it. Beaver was a good lecturer and 100% cared, but he made his exams SO HARD. You aren't screwed when you take him, you just need to know 110% of the content to do at least OKAY on the exams. It isn't like you can know 80% and make an 70 on the exam, you need 100%.

Dr. Beaver definitely knows his chemistry and is good at teaching it. He just creates next level difficult exams that are hard to do well on unless you 100% understand everything in the class. My highest score on any exam was a 66% and I would study about a week in advance.... I did much better in Zurcher's 261 and found her exams to be more fair.

Organic chemistry is just such a hard and content filled class. Dr. Beaver was a nice guy and lectures seemed to be helpful but his exams were next level hard. He is not the worst professor but if there Is an easier option, go with that one. Office hours were only held in 8 minute increments and sometimes answered questions a little backhanded.

Man, first stem class I took at unc as a transfer student and it makes me want to switch my major. Required iClicker in class, weekly quizzes online, no required practice but you're screwed if you don't do the recommended. Hard exams, I thought I could study but it just got worse as the semester went forward. Probably will retake w/ someone else.

I took CHEM262 with Dr. Beaver over the summer, and I can confidently say it was one of the best classes I have taken. Orgo is a dense subject, but with how lectures are given, the support outside of the classroom, and with enough practice problems, an A is possible. I plan to take intermediate organic chemistry with him! Do recommend.

Literally the least accessible person on the planet. Ignores every email ever and didnt respond to any office hour requests. Went to one problem sesh and he made me feel stupid. Mid teaching style. Lectures weren't horrible, but him ignoring me made them horrible. Overall, came in with high expectations, left with a low GPA and anger in my veins.

Like other reviews are saying, Beaver is a good guy but his exams are awful. I did much better in orgo 1 with Zurcher and also prefer her teaching style. Beaver does want you to succeed and is nice in lecture. Can be oddly passive in office hours/1 on 1 interactions. Again though, his exams are SO hard so be warned

I took Orgo 1 with Zurcher and much preferred it to Beaver's Orgo 2. He has a tad bit of weirdness to him; gets very easily offended (became very passive aggressive the lecture after our second exam because students were less engaged and pissed at the exam difficulty). He wants you to learn, but its beaver method or death. Exams are hard .

Great lecturer, but was VERY standoffish 1-on-1 sometimes. Make sure he knows your name. Exams were EVIL & if you didn't know 100% of content exams will get you. I never got > a 90 on any exam but ended with an A thanks to Rogue Chem and solving every textbook problem. He was fair with points back and cared for his students-you WILL learn orgo 2.
Beaver wanted to see us succeed as shown by the 4 final EC points he provided. Be warned that he always tests the hardest parts of each concept and the "exceptions to the rule"

Orgo is difficult, but Beaver's engaging lectures and clear expectations make the class manageable and even enjoyable at times. He is tough, but honest and tries to connect with students and help them succeed. He knows it's hard and pushes you to get help EARLY. Keep up with your rxn cards, practice DAILY, and consider rogue chem for the final!!!

Please take any Orgo class you can with Zurcher. Beaver is not a horrible teacher; he is just condescending at times and creates the most diabolical exams you can imagine. 3 midterms (70 or below was the median on all) and just took the 70-question final. Class is hard but doable.
Dr. Beaver is an exceptional lecturer who really cares about his students.

Dr. Beaver does an amazing job working with the lecture hall, making the large lecture hall feel like a small classroom. You could tell he cares about what he's teaching and who he's teaching it to. His tests are supposed to be the hardest out of all the orgo professors, though. Also, his voice is very easy to listen to lol.
Dr. Beaver is great but the class itself is challenging. The material is difficult, but he makes an effort to give students the resources they need to succeed.

Dr. Beaver is truly a beacon of light in the UNC Chem department. While the class is difficult, Dr. Beaver made the material very accessible and was always down to help us out with material. He is a very effective and engaging lecturer. Sometimes he is a little sassy, but never condescending or mean. He also tries to be reassuring, which is nice.

Professor Beaver is a really great orgo instructor. The content is just really difficult. He is very accessible outside of class and makes an effort to learn your name and truly wants to see you succeed. I am satisfied with the grades I got in this course and feel that they were fair given I crammed before every exam.

Chem261 is a tough class, but Dr. Beaver was an incredible teacher. If you're considering taking orgo with him, do it. He's incredibly understanding and caring. He learned the names of everybody who participated in class and would say hi while walking around campus. Attend ULA sessions, don't be distracted during class, and STUDY! You'll do great!
It's a no from me dawg.

Liked beaver in 261/262, not as much in 460. 460 was v difficult & structured poorly imo. You must be VERY confident with orgo 1/2 content, esp orgo 2, even if you took it years ago. Majority of class did poorly esp on exam 1. Added 15 pt curve to exam 1, 10 pt curve to exam 2, & a curve at the end, which was v nice and unheard of in UNC chem dept

The class is definitely a lot of work, but Dr. Beaver's a good professor. He's very caring and explains the material well. Exams were also fair. Just make sure to keep up with the workbook problems and rxn flashcards.

Beaver's got good lectures and very accessible via OH so don't be intimidated. His LAs were just awesome! They single-handedly saved me in the class with super clear explanations. Study hard for the thermo exam, that by far is the hardest exam in the course. You've got this!

This class was so informative and engaging. Exams were hard but extra credit opportunities were given, and the final also had a take-home portion. Group presentations were a good grade boost and also enlightened us on modern orgo research. Dr. Beaver was also very helpful during 1-on-1 office hours.

CHEM 101 was horrible for me, so going into CHEM 102 I was terrified, but Dr. Beaver was a great lecturer and made the class interactive and easier to understand. The lecture was a launch so the class was only about 35 people. Dr. Beaver was respectful and his LAs were great too. The tests were difficult. Go to the LA review sessions!
this class was unnecessarily difficult with him. beaver is rude and condescending at times, and sometimes appears to have an ego issue. take with literally anyone else.

Chem 460 review. Lots of prerequisite knowledge required, make sure to brush up on orgo 2 before taking. Lots of pre-class reading, and exams were extremely difficult (be he did give a generous curve). The class has a large presentation component, which is fine, but just be aware.

This review is for 102. Dr. Beaver is a great professor. He made learning chem easier and made sure students understood as much as he could. Chem 102 at UNC is hard, and the exams are ridiculous. But Beaver is definitely the best professor I've had in the chem department and is passionate about what he does. I would definitely recommend him.

Verily, this course is no mere pursuit, but an odyssey of torment where only the steadfast glimpse enlightenment. The lecturer bestows knowledge in fire and fury, yet we, mere mortals, are left scorched, grasping at fleeting truths. My soul writhes beneath this incantation of madness! And yet, is not true wisdom born from suffering?

Dr. Beaver was awesome. Set the best foundation for Organic Chemistry and his lectures were very informative. He is very smart and forces you to think through the course material. His lectures are also engaging and I would definitely take him again. The only slight is his exams are difficult, but I learned so much in this course.

I was pleasantly surprised by this course. Joshua Beaver was extremely professional and knowledgeable. He always came prepared and stuck to schedule, never falling behind on the course material. He was genuinely compassionate with his students as well, encouraging participation and making a point to remember people's names.

Great course overall. Orgo here is hard but getting a good grade is definitely doable. Beaver is a very caring and engaging professor. I can see how he may come off as condescending sometimes but he's very empathetic and receptive in office hours. Don't take Orgo with too many other hard classes. That was my mistake and I didn't lock in enough.

It's UNC orgo, it's going to be a lot of content. I bombed the first test before learning how to prepare for this class. Skim the readings before class, don't spend too long on them, there's a lot of unnecessary info. Keep up with the workbook, it's the key to the midterms. Go to the ULA session and at least one problem solving session a week.

I love Beaver. He was amazing, and the class is very manageable if you stay on top of it. He has q&A sessions and office hours to help and genueinly wants to see you succeed. Many people said he seemed condescending, which at first he kinda did, but as soon as I talked to him a couple times he is the best prof ever.

It's definitely possible to succeed by doing workbook +textbook problems, ULA worksheets, going to q&a sessions -- uncommon most students with other hard classes. Midterms are pretty fair, but Beaver is not super accessible; condescending and judgy -- gatekeeps info at his q&as, so go to those if possible (or todd). Has a buffer for graded work.

Prof. Beaver was a nice guy and could be pretty engaging during class. However, lecture slides were often vague. Midterms were significantly harder than the final exam, and final grades experienced a slight curve. When in doubt about whether you should have received credit for an answer on a midterm, submit a regrade.

Dr. Beaver is a wonderful lecturer and instructor.  Organic Chemistry is hard, and requires lots of practice and attention to detail; Dr. Beaver emphasizes these things daily in class, and puts a ton of effort into helping people correct their misconceptions.  Easily approachable, spent a lot of time making the class digestible. Curved final grade.

Dr. Beaver cares about his students but I do not think he is a good lecturer. The slides are a bit confusing and his explanations were vague so we could "teach ourself". The review sessions only helped if you knew what you were doing and had a few questions. Orgo is one of those subjects that requires consistent studying so don't fall behind.

Orgo is fairly challenging and requires a lot of practice. Attention to detail is key in the course. As for Dr. Beaver, I don't have much positive to say. You ask him a question, he will not only not answer your question, but he will make u feel like a fool for even asking. I got more clear answers on EdStem, the TAs do better than he does.

I quickly came to the realization that some people are good at orgo and others just aren't. I did the preclass, ULA sessions, the GPSS, workbook, and slides every week and still did bad in the class. Some people that didn't even do half of what I did would do better. Make sure you don't take any other hard classes bc this class is time consuming!
Doctor Beaver's lectures were interesting and easy to follow, but you have to be prepared before the class. Make sure you take his advice in the syllabus and you will do good in this class

Doctor Beaver's lectures were interesting and easy to follow, but you have to be prepared before the class. He cares about his students; however, he expects a lot from you. I would say do absolutely everything he offers, and you will do great. 
Overall, Doctor Beaver is one of my favorite professors at UNC, even though Orgo1 is hard!

Very intersting lectures and very nicely planned out lecture slides. Dr. Beaver wants students to do a lot of practice questions outside of class and I do not like the pre-class reading quizzes (Easy to get points but heavy reading and does not really help me to understand the content). Easy to get daily participation and graded work points,.

Organic chemistry is very difficult to navigate, but Beaver truly explains these concepts and ensures his students have a deeper understanding of the WHY behind everything. I am very glad I took this class with him!!

Organic chemistry is going to be hard no matter who you take it with. Beaver was a good lecturer and provided lots of problem-solving in class so lectures were never boring. The textbook for the course was actually very good and Beaver's slides were very helpful when studying for exams.

Extremely difficult course and main source of learning, his own written workbook has no solutions...so outside of the scaffolded answers he provides on canvas, ALL the other practice, good luck getting and if your schedule doesn't allow for you to go to office hours, sorry for you. Smart guy, fair but hard tests, and cares.

Lectures were engaging and easy to follow along, however the difficulty of the course was extreme at times, especially in the tests, tehy were nothing like the previous exam questions given for practice.

He does not know how to teach.  He is the most condescending man that I have EVER met and that's saying a lot.  He is also so misogynistic.  He is so self-centered, everything is about him and nothing is about the ACTUAL content of the class.  This class literally bombed my mental health.

Became an alcoholic, it was that bad. Honestly, the main issue is the problems done in class are infinitely easier than the ones on the test. That being said, he's a really good guy and cares about you if you put in the effort.

Dr. Beaver's approach is high structure active learning - it rewards students who practice every day using all resources (workbook, blank slides, worksheets, office hours). Was 261/262 hard? Yes! Does Beaver have high expectations? Also yes. This can be intimidating for some, but it motivated me to try my best. Orgo @UNC is high risk + high reward.

In 262, there's SO many rxns to know; prioritize this class. Keep an errors notebook. You need to understand WHY things happen. Beaver was more personable in 262 than 261, but still had high expectations of depth of understanding. Have him and the ULAs answer all of your questions, all the time. He is more willing to help if he knows you by name!
Do not take a class with him

The best chemistry teacher I've had.  You definitely have to put in the work, and go to his Q&As and LA sessions as much as possible.  Content is difficult but he genuinely wants you to succeed and will take student feedback to heart.  Test questions are pretty straightfoward and fair.

This is a very difficult class and Dr. Beaver is known for making hard tests, however, he genuinely does want his students to learn and succeed in the class. You will need to devote a lot of time to studying and practicing the material but you definitely can do well in the class.

Def a tough class and still harder than 261 (esp the second unit). Having a good foundation in 261 is KEY. Insider info: every test had a huge predict the products section, and acid-base shows up every time. Encouragement: first midterm=worst grade in orgo ever, last midterm=best grade in orgo ever. Midterm med were 77, 74, 77; final med was 79.

Dr. Beaver is a great guy! I had him for 261 and 262, and you can tell he really cares a lot about his students. Orgo definitely was not my favorite subject but he was always engaging and it was nice to come to class where the professor knows your name in a big lecture room. The course is hard but if you take his advice, you will do just fine!

Seems to be a genuinely good guy and a solid teacher. However, he expects all of his students to have a near-perfect understanding of all of the material. It comes across as if he thinks this is our only course.

Orgo 2 with Dr. Beaver is way better than orgo 1 (had him for both)! You NEED to do the legwork for this class - do the workbook/textbook problems concurrently with the lectures, study well in advance, and you will do fine. I got a B- in orgo 1 and I'm maintaining an A- in orgo 2! He cares a lot about his students - work hard & you'll be fine!

Beaver is a difficult professor no doubt but I accredit much of my ability to study and learn effectively to his guidance and mentorship. He genuinely cares about your well-being and if you show effort, he'll reciprocate. Exams are pretty difficult but not impossible by any means. Go to class, participate, do the readings, don't fall behind.
poo. avoid.

His exams were definitely the most difficult to take and understand by far. If you do not have a thorough understanding of the material, and fall short of 100% understanding, the exam will be challenging. They are not impossible; rather, they test your overall comprehension through every possible question that could be asked.

Organic chemistry very difficult in general, especially when you're taking it here! Dr. Beaver, however, is a very good professor and I really do think he cares a lot for his students. You have to do the reading, practice, study and work very hard!

Dr. Beaver is very knowledgeable and truly cares about his students succeeding. However, he has a very condescending demeanor when explaining concepts in office hours or review sessions. He expects students to learn at the rate he would which comes across very heavily. He is very organized and lectures really clarify the textbook readings.

Dr. Beaver was nice and clearly knowledgeable about organic chemistry. However, I felt that he did little to explain any difficult concepts during lectures. All midterm medians were in the 60s and there was about a 1% point curve at the end of the class. Exam questions are harder than lecture and practice questions.

I'll try to cover what the other reviews haven't covered already. I honestly thought Beaver was a great teacher and I always found his problem sessions helpful. I know it's hard, but try not to stress too much about your grade; there is a slight curve at the end. Here are my grades for reference: mid-80s on every midterm, low 90 on the final.

Beaver explains concepts well & learns names but orgo itself is a menace. CHEM 101/102 at UNC were pretty easy A's for me, but I spent several hours a day on orgo just to get a B+. Tho its possible to get an A- or A if you get in the 80s on exams bc they curve slightly at the end. Redo the slides, go to ULA sessions, do as much practice as you can.

Beaver is a respectable guy who deeply understands Orgo, making for a good professor, but he also has extremely high standards for students, so merely keeping up during lecture will not get you a good exam score. Tests medians were around 68, so you must deeply understand the material. This course is what you can expect of a Orgo course at UNC.

I don't know why everyone talks badly about Professor Beaver but he is a very caring man. He is straightforward and will say that a problem was "easy". However, don't take that to heart.  Attending his office hours is also great because he gives you tips on how to succeed in the course and he wants everyone to succeed.

Nice professor who learns your name if you participate. He can be pretty fun to learn from when he's in a joking mood, and is clearly passionate about chemistry. Chem classes here are what they are, but he does his best to help you succeed. You have to be the one to put in the hard work to succeed. Medians on tests were 66-68 so study hard.

I know orgo is notoriously the most difficult class at UNC, so I'm trying not to let that get in the way of my rating, but Beaver didn't help my understanding of the material. The workbook was helpful, but to get the answers you need to go to ULA sessions, and they only solve a few problems. I worked my butt off, and I'll still probably get a C+.

Dr. Beaver is a decent lecturer. Not the best by any means, but he was also not the worst I've had. Nonetheless, tests are very tricky and grading can be pretty cut-throat, so make sure you study and understand the material very well.

BEST CHEM PROF!! Made an effort to learn everyone's name. Commended individual students for improvement on exams. Explained the material so well. I did so much better in ORGO2 than ORGO1 w/austell. I absolutely adore Beaver. Extremely kind. iClicker for attendance. The exams were what I expected. I did devote a lot of studying time, but u should.

Dr. Beaver is the best chemistry professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and tries to get to know everyone's names. He wants the best for everyone and always had great advice on how to succeed in the class. I would definitely recommend taking a chemistry class with him.

I feel like a lot of Chemistry professors get a bad rap because they teach a difficult class. CHEM 262 was definitely not easy, but Dr. Beaver explained content well and clearly wanted us to succeed. I wish he had written all of our exams rather than alternating with the other professor, but that is not his fault. I'd take another class with him.

Dr. Beaver was extremely kind and respectful. His lectures are interesting and engaging, and he's a very smart, fair person. The exams are stressful, but Dr. Beaver does his best to make sure you're not too scared for his exams. I recommend him wholeheartedly.

Pretty solid professor and a good guy. He seemed to truly care about his students and their success. He understands that the material is hard and does everything in his power to allow students to be comfortable with it. I enjoyed taking his class.

Beaver is a good teacher. The test were hard but fair and they are always good about giving us the partial credits. I believe Beaver wanted us to succeed and provided tips outside of class material on how to study.

Dr. Beaver seems to be universally despised for no reason. Organic chemistry is never going to be a cakewalk. However, Dr. Beaver was a funny guy who often told us many anecdotes. He did a great job with conveying difficult orgo 2 concepts to students. Exams were graded generously and Dr. Beaver actually (wait for it) wants you to succeed.

Orgo 2 is naturally hard, but I think Dr. Beaver gave us everything we would need to succeed. He is available for questions, has regular office hours and problem solving sessions, and responds to emails promptly. He overall hasn't done anything wrong in my book, even if he may not be the most exciting or charismatic guy.

Don't listen to anyone who says that Dr. Beaver is uncaring, manipulative, etc. They are just people who have become frustrated with organic chemistry - its a subject that takes a lot of work. Dr. Beaver truly cares about his students, is willing to help them in any way, and also is quite generous with his exams.

Orgo is obviously a hard class but Beaver is a good professor. His lectures are always clear and have lots of class participation, and there are tons of resources to get help and practice after class. He's also very generous with partial credit on exams

Dr. Beaver does a great job of making lectures engaging. He also makes a conscious effort to learn student names, and is really invested in helping students be successful. He is also a big help with study strategies.

Chem 262 is a hard class regardless of the professor. Dr. Beaver does a really great job of making the content on the tests reflect what was taught in class. He is very accessible outside of class and makes a conscious effort to learn everyone in the classes name.

The only positive thing I have to say is that she was generous with curves & EC. However, she is very petty, extremely hard to follow during lectures, creates ridiculously long exams, and gives very few practice problems that I did not think looked anything like the exam. I only did well because I am comfortable with stats and put in a ton of time.
Erin Baker graded almost solely based on midterm exam scores, and didn't assign much homework to practice lecture material.

She did change the grading scheme because of issues with AI which was unfortunate, but although the exams became weighted higher, I have never seen a professor give such generous curves on exams as her (even if average = 70s). She does problems slowly and in detail, and super open to questions. Exams are long but every 241 professor has long exams

very poor lecturer. was extremely difficult to follow along - expect to spend tons of time outside of class teaching yourself the content. 

tests weren't difficult but very long, so there was never enough time to check over work. 

but, if you are math-minded, you will find this class easier than other 241 sections because of its focus on stats.

Makes ARS absence accommodated students do a problem you didn't learn how to do (only blank slides provided) and submit it by 5pm the same day for credit. Admitted to people outside of the class that she made exams extra difficult on purpose after the AI issue. Punished class for some people's wrongs to be "fair." Taught unnecessary extra stats.

Different content from other 241s. Tests are based on lecture content (not textbook). Teaches extra math that won't be tested on, but she lets you know what will/won't appear on a test. Tests are long and seem hard, but curves are generous +EC. Didn't post slides afterwards & only wrote on chalkboard.

Overhated for AI imo - we were not faultless.

Dr. Baker seems sweet but the AI incident definitely left a bad taste in her mouth (She changed the syllabus to be 85% exams right after). Exams were long but she curved them all. The final was fair. I would take the other 241 sections over her's because she mostly teaches statistics, only the last 1/3 of class was actual chemistry.

I ended up getting an A after a near perfect score on exam 3 and replacing the lowest midterm grade with the final grade, however, her class was hard and not really reflective of what other 241 classes teach. Her lectures were confusing to follow, and my success at the end of the course came from reading the textbook, not from her. Kind of petty.

Covered half of what other CHEM241 sections did, which is unhelpful for the lab/MCAT. Said that the final would be a certain format, then changed it without informing students. Overcomplicates the simplest concepts and doesn't upload her slides/work half the time. The rare extra credit doesn't compensate for the stress you'll feel from this class.

Dr. Baker is rly nice and clearly cares about her students. That being said, this class was really math/stats heavy (big content difference from other classes or the lab) and the explanations weren't always the easiest to follow. Tests were really long but not terrible for UNC chem imo. Unnecessary hate.

I had only positive interactions with Dr. Baker. However, I found the most challenging part of this class to be that she wrote on the blackboard only and I struggled to read it a lot. I did appreciate the practice questions she provided and they were always very similar to exam questions. Once I understood her expectations, the course got better.

Go ahead and take her if you want extra premature balding. I genuinely did not comprehend a single thing this woman taught all semester, and trust me, I normally enjoy chem. I appreciate the extra credit but never have I seen such terrible grades as I had to dig thru everyone's exams to find mine. and don't even get me started on the AI situation

Acted like a child the entire semester. Held a grudge and retaliated against the ENTIRE class for ONE assignment that had nothing to do with the core curriculum. Was condescending and sent nasty email replies, if she ever responded at all. Told us she purposely releases exams after class, because she doesn't want to have to answer our emails…

Dr. Baker handled this semester's 241 class with complete immaturity and lack of professionalism. She doesn't know how to teach to save her life, her lectures are all over the place, she made her own crazy curriculum, and changed the syllabus and grading system in the middle of the semester. Her midterms were 40 questions long, longer than finals.

Her exams are extremely long, and the class is disorganized, but I feel she deserves some credit for how she tried to make up for the first half of the semester. Generous curves, extra 3 points on exam grades just for coming to the next class, and a very fair final exam. It is frustrating to have such a different experience from other classes.

Other reviews are unnecessarily harsh. She was an okay lecturer and her exams were very hard, but she was pretty clear about what was going to be on them. She posted review sheets beforehand and graded generously. Honestly if you can do the practice exams you'll be fine. Most stats heavy than the other professors, so avoid if not your thing.

While Dr. Baker is a brilliant researcher and kind person, she is not a very effective instructor. She struggled to convey even the simplest of topics, resulting in students needing to learn the majority of the material on their own.

While Dr. Baker isn't the best lecturer and doesn't cover some of the content that the other 241 sections do (which makes 241L more difficult), the other reviews are a bit harsh. She makes it very clear what will be on exams and she curves them + additional bonus points. She definitely has her faults, but the generous grading makes up for it.

Dr. Baker writes all her notes on a blackboard and doesn't post notes that you can go back to. Half the time she has to look at her paper to see the work she did before continuing on the board. The way she does problems is more complicated than it has to be. She is so strict about sig figs but messes them up on answer keys and lacks consistency.

Dr. Baker made CHEM 241 a terrible experience. She is incredibly immature and lacks professionalism. While some students used AI on an assignment, instead of punishing those who did, she punished the whole class. She did the same thing on participation grades. She is condescending and acts like she got her feelings hurt and needed to retaliate.

Nice lady, terrible prof. Do you want to succeed at UNC Chem 241 - don't take Baker. That's a fact.  Why would a professor have to curve and give extra credit for each exam?? Because most students did bad!!! It's a sad story; people fought to get into this class, just to be played in the end. This is the Carolina STEM experience.

Syllabus change, lack of partial credit, long exams, and limited practice. BUT she curved, gave extra credit for attendance so you could get >100 on exams, and is so kind and personable when you go to OH. Final exam almost all directly came from past exams or in-class slides. She's also famous but you'd never know just from class. Would recommend!!

Though this class was incredibly frustrating, I think Baker also had many saving graces in the class. Extra credit during certain class periods, curved every exam, and the very straighforward final after you make it through the class. Did I enjoy the class? No. Absolutely not. Very disorganized. But she makes it possible to get a good grade.

Extremely exam-heavy(85%)and unforgiving grading. Changed the grading scale weeks into the course. Penalized the entire class for "AI use" with no evidence. Rarely responds to emails. If you want a fair, transparent, or supportive instructor, avoid this class. Change your schedule around if you must, do not settle for Dr. Baker, you deserve better.

Yes, she teaches a different course than other analytical profs, and yes, she's not AMAZING at teaching. Keep in mind that half our class DID use AI to shortcut an easy paper, so take all you see here w/ a grain of salt. The content doesn't always feel like chem, but it's really not hard. Go to class, do the work, and go to office hrs. She cares.

Her exams aren't conceptually difficult but are very heavy on memorization. The course often felt more like stats than chemistry, but she didn't clearly explain either aspect. She seems friendly but her communication can come across as passive-aggressive at times, which made the class environment less comfortable.
