Honestly, this was one of the worst classes I've taken. Partway through the semester she changed the grading scheme so that exams suddenly became 85% of the grade. On top of that, she barely taught actual chemistry and spent most of the time on statistics, which other 241 sections didn't even do.
just dont take her class or you will be played like a dog

Trash, absolutely trash. worst i have ever had. she changed the grading scheme in half of the term and made tests 85 percent of the whole grade. she canceled all attendance grade and a project grade which were easy for students to get grade on. she didnt even teach chem. instead she just teach you bunch of stats which the other 241 class does not.

Very passive aggressive. She goes on 30 minute tangents explaining the math behind something just to tell you right after that you don't need to know it. She accused the class of cheating and instead of reaching out to those students, she penalized everyone in class and made exams weigh more. She also took away in class participation a month in.

Very spiteful and immature. Obviously the AI thing (several students cheated on a participation grade using AI) was bad but instead of punishing the students who used AI, she made exams much heavier. Not only that, but there is very limited practice for her exams which are designed to be lengthy and tricky. No dedicated final exam review. Avoid her

Dr. Baker is one of the most condescending professors I've had at UNC, and I tend to like professors even with a bad rep. Her exams are insanely long (she had to extend time 30 minutes on all three midterms) and her lectures are super confusing. She messes up simple concepts while teaching them and makes them way more complicated than needed.

A few students cheated on an assignment and instead of giving those people 0's she took 12% of the whole class grade coming from attendance/easy assignment and added it to exams. Literally bad at teaching during lectures, unnecessarily long exams/not enough time, entire grade is exams. Not much HW. Stubborn + mean, not willing to help students out.

Take everything you read with a grain of salt, the AI thing was bad, but the ratings she gets are not deserved. If you show up to class and pay attention it is very manageable. She is clear about what we will be on exams, and they are fair(plus a curve to around a C+ average for each exam.

Wouldn't take at all. Her lectures are disorganized and often seems like she doesn't know what she's doing or how to solve problems. Very different curriculum from other CHEM 241 classes and seems to do things the ULAs don't even know. Does apply a curve but that's because the tests are difficult and lengthy (almost 40 questions long). Avoid.

I 100% agree with her response to students using AI to cheat but I want to focus on something else: her class is incredibly disorganized, but everything from the test comes from lectures that make little sense. Slides/textbook don't correspond with her lesson. She is generous with curves but it does not make up for her inability to convey content.

Her exams are extremely unfair. Both times she has made them 36 questions, with some being multipart and has had to let everyone stay at least 10 min more + barely anyone finishes. She also basically creates almost an entirely new course. Compared to the other analytical classes we learn things they've never heard of.

No annotated slides posted and lectures fall flat relating to math examples. This class relies more on self teaching than other UNC chem courses. While I understand her response to the AI situation to some degree, it also served to punish students that actually did put in the work. Removing attendance buffer was just further retaliation IMO.

DO NOT TAKE, like actually one of the worst profs at UNC, said half the class cheated on an assignment so replaced 10% of the grade into the exam category, making the class 85% exam weight? Then doesn't record lectures, doesn't drop any assignments or exams, no flexibility at all. Doesn't even fill in slides to post online. Lectures are scattered.

The material we are supposed to know isn't really explained to fullest extent that it can be. Often explains problems in the most complex way possible. Exams material isn't the hardest, but the sheer amount of questions given is too much. Lecture was mostly full even after extra time was provided. Keeps brining up the ai situation.

Don't take analytical with Dr. Baker - if you work hard enough you can get through it but it will be miles easier with any other professor. Her slides are disorganized and she is not the best lecturer either. She does not explain concepts clearly and will often go on material tangents and then say that we don't actually need to know any of it.

It's actually true that more than half our class DID cheat using A.I. That in itself is problematic. But the cringe reviews complaining about the fact that Dr. Baker actually did something to address the cheating? They really devalue the UNC brand. The school seems to admit a lot of cheaters, who retaliate when caught because they resent working.

please just dont. its october and we've barely even touched actually chemistry. shes obsessed with math so we've literally been learning statistics since the start of the semester. so unfair to give such a different experience than the other classes. her slides make no sense and her test questions are obscure (and first test was legit 36 questions)

Much easier than any other chemistry professor at UNC. While accusing students of using AI and changing the grading scale to weight exams higher was unfortunate, it shouldn't really change anyone's grade in the long run if they're coming to class and putting in the work. You can tell she truly loves the subject she teaches and curves exams to help!

Avoid Erin Baker at all costs. Right before the first exam, she accused half the class of using AI, despite having no proof, and proceeded to change the entire grading scale to make exams weigh more. She has been nothing but spiteful since then, using obscure test questions from unrelated topics in class and being condescending in emails.

Take take take! She is miles easier than any CHEM241 prof with extra credit and curves to meet 85% test averages. Super caring and sweet. Although beware she has her own syllabus that will not match with lab - you will have to learn most of that content on your own.

I highly recommend Dr. Baker! She keeps exam averages around 85% and gives extra credit if they're lower. Her exams are very fair and she only tests on what she gets through in lecture. Her grading isn't very exam based for a chem class (only 70% of grade comes from exams). Also very accessible outside of class, friendly, and a very lenient grader!

Extremely caring and passionate professor! Tests are long and quite challenging but review questions are very similar. Didn't cover all topics that regular 241 sections got to but she writes her own exams so it's whatever. Recommend!

I took the honors section of chem430 and loved it. We did a capstone project and got to present our work at the Undergraduate Research Symposium. I was able to learn new how to work with data and even apply some of what I did to my own research! It was hard at first but I learned a lot about myself and team science. This was my fav class at UNC.

Dr. Brunk is kind and clearly cares about her students. She is very busy, as most research faculty are but she answers questions when you bring them to lecture. The flipped classroom can be an adjustment, but it reflects med school style learning. Biochem is challenging (DUH). Homework load is heavy-it helps and can be a grade saver for exams

This class was really hard but really good. It changed my view of medicine and it changed what I want to do with my life. I love the real world applications and learning how to work with data. I loved the lectures on precision medicine and things that are really happening in science.

Took Brunk because Hogan's section was full - worst mistake ever. My friends in Hogan's section had a walk in the park compared to what Brunk put our class through. Prone to mistakes in videos/lecture, very confusing explanations when asked for clarification (which I had to ask at office hours bc she never responded to my emails!), tricky exams.

She is rarely available and actively makes it harder for you to find help. She doesn't let you email her so you can only get help from the TAs. I had to have my final exam rescheduled and she refused to help me out. Keep in mind it was an EXTREMELY easy fix. Don't expect any notes or videos to be posted, and her modules don't match with the exams.

Dr Brunk is very nice, but not a great lecturer. There were mistakes on nearly every assignment including concept check quizzes and exams. The lectures were quite confusing at times. I couldn't get answers for the exam problems I got wrong because she doesn't release keys to us OR the TAs, and I could never make her office hours.

Dr. Brunk has a unique style of teaching for her class that some like and others do not. In order to do well in this course I would suggest preparing to understand the concepts on your own outside of class.  Dr. Brunk is good at teaching but it just seemed like her style of teaching was out of date. Also took long times to return tests.

Genuinely don't know why she provides us with an email to send questions to. Also, you'd think having only video lectures would result in clarity and infrequent speech errors, but that's why you're the student and not the professor.

Professor is hard to reach, takes a few follow ups for a response, even with the designated email. Final exam date was told after having “TBD” in the syllabus up until almost two weeks before the final. Flipped classroom, 0/10. Tests included small details from DEs, practice exams unhelpful. Grading scale somewhat curved to help though.

This is why research faculty shouldn't teach classes. It seemed like Brunk didn't have time to teach the class and didn't care about the students in it. Very disorganized: never released answer keys for exams, incorrect answers on CCQs, lecture content often contradicted videos but barely able to get ahold of her through email to ask questions.

Terrible class. The content itself shouldn't be bad, but Brunk is incredibly inefficient in lecture while also not teaching anything. She was extremely difficult to get in contact with and to communicate with. The coding for this class had almost no guidance and Brunk was very unhelpful. 0/10.

Brunk teaches biochem fine... the class had its own issues. Quizzes had wrong answers that wouldnt get fixed. Exam content wasn't weighed well: class emphasized big on topics just for there to be 1-3 exam questions on it. Wouldnt drop a quiz during the snow storm. Coding projects (DEs) were annoying. I didnt learn any Python I could practically use

Data exploration assignments are accompanied by a quiz, where the questions are incoherent. They refer to the wrong section of the DE, they have demonstrably multiple correct answers for questions that are choose 1, and multiple answer choice is on for questions that specifically ask for 1. Canvas quizzes are frustrating beyond content difficulty.

Interesting method with adding coding into the material. Biochem is a bit tough but the layout is manageable. If you come to class and ask questions about the material from the lectures you will be fine. Lots of opportunities outside the exams to get your grade up.
Flipped classroom is confusing and no one likes it. Weird assignments, like python coding but its more like reading about how the code is made than learning coding.

Flipped classroom, meaning watch an 60+ min of lecture video before class and lectures are practice questions, they go incredibly slow because, well, she didn't actually teach the material. Writes small on whiteboard?? for some reason in a GSB classroom. No attendance. Believes in the flipped class too much, unorganized/a little incoherent in class

Dr. B, is incredibly sweet, caring, and fair. They create a supportive learning environment, encourage participation, and provide clear, engaging lectures. Their grading is fair with helpful feedback, and they're always available to assist students. An exceptional professor overall!

Dr. Brunk uses innovative technology in her teaching, which can feel challenging at first, but she provides all the resources needed to succeed. Her lectures are well-organized, and she explains complex concepts clearly. She also dedicates class time to discussions, giving students the chance to ask questions and deepen their understanding.

Dr. Brunk is not a great lecturer, but she cares about the class and tries to engage the students as much as possible. The course content is interesting, but the flipped classroom model really did not work for me and it was hard to motivate myself when we would just do a few practice problems after a 30-60 minute lecture video the night before
take the class with any one else. would take weeks to get exams back when she had less than a 50 person class. so so so boring. hated the flipped classroom and felt like I learned nothing

Exams were straightforward as long as you studied the lectures and did the homeworks. Textbook reading is not required at all. Pre-lecture quizzes are a hassle, but manageable. Also, class isn't as test heavy as usual due to a decent portion of the grade dedicated to protein modeling in Python, which was a grade boost and gave breaks btw content.

The class isn't based off readings which is nice, but the research assignments are difficult even though they were interesting. Overall, if you put in the work you should be fine. Just prepare to be frustrated if you need her help. Hard to reach, lots of question mistakes that she would end up docking you points for, gets worse as semester goes on

Dr. Alexanian is a sarcastic funny guy, teaching style (talking at us) was ok but the pace is fast and lots of review for nuances in reaction mechanisms is required to understand what was going on. He's doing his best but he is def a research prof.

So far Dr Alexanian is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He was slow during his lectures, but it did not hurt me. However, during QA sessions and office hours he was extremely nice. His exams are so much harder than Dr Eskew's; however, questions he asked were fair.

Would ramble in class about his lab -- unclear on what we had to know as fact vs fluff? The midterm he made was ?? (average was a 63), and our class's grades were lower than Eskew's, but no curve. Final was also not easy. Condescending to questions in class. Interesting guy though, with a dry sense of humor. Allegedly gatekept things at his Q&As.

Erik is maybe the most mid CHEM professor at UNC. He's pretty nice and funny during class, but if you like a fast paced class, he moves EXTREMELY slow. His midterms were not too bad, the second one was rough but the other two and the final were really easy. He was very dismissive of people that asked stupid questions, but I liked him overall

This class has pretty fair midterms. It goes pretty well for me until the final, which was insanely hard. Erik is nice and understanding, but just be ware of the orgo final, which was the hardest chem exam I have ever taken at UNC.

Taught content well and clearly knew his stuff. Would move a little slowly through lectures; we were always 1/2-1 lecture behind the other section, which would sometimes hurt us on the end-of-week assignments if we didn't get to cover everything. Was late to lecture by a few minutes consistently. Nice guy.

Alexanian is a pretty good teacher. His lectures were pretty slow paced and understandable but we did always get through all the content. At times his answers to questions during lecture came off as condescending. The midterm he wrote (other sections professor wrote other midterms) was significantly harder than the rest. Final was pretty easy.

Erik is pretty nice but blunt, which may come off as condescending. He's a decent lecturer but goes at a very slow pace. For the honors section he only had 1 online OH session, but he did reply to emails fairly quickly. He also assumed we were the "smart kids" and ended up not explaining some things that he thought we'd already know.

The classroom is purely flipped. Class sessions serve as problem solving sessions rather than instructional time. Office hours are useful for difficult course content. Exams are difficult but fair. Sizable (~5%) curve added to final grades.

P Chem 1 is going to be hard, but Professor Cahoon has designed this class to be as effective as possible. It's a flipped classroom, which is kind of annoying, but it's much better than the alternative, since you can pause and rewind the lecture videos. He offers plenty of office hours if you need extra help, and his explanations are always good.

Same content as chem 430, but instead of cumulative final, there is a final group project with a poster and presentation which count as the final grade. Still 3 midterms, but lowest is dropped. Dr. Hogan is the nicest guy, passionate about chemistry and so chill.
Dr. Hogan is a great professor, he is open to questions and is enthusiastic. We had a final group project where we did coding and two exams.

Dr. Hogan was an amazing prof for Chem 430. His lectures follow active learning protocol and his course is in flipped classroom format. Dr. Hogan even gives students skeleton notes for pre-class reading/videos. Low commitment if student has good study habits.

Dr Hogan was great for 431. Exams were all take home and the last midterm and the final were projects (individual or group). Class mostly consisted of reviewing different Biochem papers and their methods/data. No memorization at all which was a relief after 430. 91.5% and above is an A as well! Can't complain.

Great prof like everyone said. The best tip for this class would be to watch the prelectures!! if you know the slides well, you would do great on the midterms. Attendance is not mandatory but I would HIGHLY suggest watching the prelectures before the class and actually go to class- amazing for long term retention of the info especially if ur premed

If you have to take this class, take it with Hogan.  Exams are like 70% of your grade but they're mostly multiple choice and fair (the final was significantly harder imo) and you get to drop your lowest.  The rest of your grade is HW assignments and asynchronous quizzes which are pretty easy.  He also offers 1% ec to your overall grade.
Just awesome

Dr. Hogan is hands down the best professor I have ever had at UNC. He is so knowledgable, makes difficult concepts easy to understand, and is funny and engaging during lectures. Most importantly he is kind and understanding, and gives the best life advice while telling stories about his experiences. He is amazing. Take every class you can with him.

Biochem can be tough, but Dr. Hogan makes it manageable. His online lectures are comprehensive, and the practice problems are super helpful. For study prep, try using unstuck AI alongside other resources like Quizlet. Just stay engaged and you'll do well!

All the content is taught from 1.5 hour videos before every class. Actual lecture feels pointless. There's EC and 1 midterm drop, which is nice. Insane amount of memorization on miniscule details. Not a good preparation for the MCAT even though it is advertised as such. It's much easier than other UNC chem classes, but don't sleep on the exams.
lots of memorization. But he gives a lot of oppertunites to do well in this course. super easy compared to all the chem/bio classes taken before this.

Hogan is an engaging lecturer but expect 1-2 hour videos for homework before every class. There are three midterms, one is dropped, and a cumulative final. Memorization HEAVY! Also if you try to email him with questions expect a single word or short sentence response - not formal at ALL and kind of comes off rude.

Dr. Hogan is an extremely fair professor. His tests were very reasonable to content and did not try to trick you or use extremely nit-picky details.  The final grade is determined by a lot of different things (not attendance!) and he drops a midterm.  You also don't have to buy/read a textbook since he provides pre-lecture videos. Highly recommend!

Super nice and chill professor. I liked the flipped classroom, but much of the in-person class is repeated information but nevertheless helpful to do practice. This class is a ton of memorization, so as long as you take the time to learn it you'll be fine. The amino acid app helps too.

This class has a completely useless amount of memorization involved. It has been a week and a half since I took this exam, and I've already forgotten everything I learned in this class. That being said, Dr. Hogan makes this course bearable with his quick wits and sense of humor. I wouldn't have wanted to suffer through this class with anyone else.

Although the content for biochem is challenging, Hogan makes it doable and is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Be prepared for a flipped classroom format but do not let that scare you as his online lectures are long but extremely thorough. He gives a lot of practice problems and if you put in the work for this course you will succeed!

The pre-lecture recordings and class discussions were essentially the same, so after the second midterm I stopped going to class. His jokes were mid and were always along the lines of "everyone doesn't like something but no one doesn't like_____" I recommend making lots of friends to help you learn the material with and learn how cyverse works.

Dr.Hogan is a nice guy. The honors section was combined with the regular section and it just had an extra assignment. The honors section didn't even meet once and we got 0 feedback on the project we worked on. I was really disappointed since my honors science courses are usually quite good. 430 Lecture is skipable and the assignments are clear.

Dr. Hogan is proof that many of the STEM classes at UNC are so hard solely because professors choose to make them this way. I have never felt less stressed in an upper-level science course as I have in biochemistry with Dr. Hogan. If you watch the pre-class lectures and make a Quizlet from the slides, you will be fine. Love Dr. Hogan!

Dr. Hogan is the epitome of what a professor should be like. We had so many resources for this course, it truly made me happy to be able to come to lecture because I knew what was going on beforehand and after If I needed more help. Explanations are always clear, and this guy is very engaging. I highly recommend him!

Only the best professor ever at UNC!! She is so kind and caring, explains concepts so thoroughly and clearly, and answers questions with clarity and patience. Exams are all fair and she gives so many resources to help.

Dr. Fostvedt is genuinely one of the sweetest and most caring professors ever! She is a great lecturer and makes it easy to understand the topics. She actually makes an effort to get to know the students as well, even in a huge lecture room, which means a lot! Definitely take her for this class.

Dr. Fostvedt was a great professor and she did a good job of clarifying chem 101 topics and making sure we didn't stress the concepts that were less important for the exam. Her GPSS sessions were helpful so I recommend going to those during the challenging units. She is a super sweet person and I personally enjoyed her class. Take 101 with her!

I would retake Chem 101 just to have her as my teacher again. Though 101 is hard, and exams are standardized, having her as a teacher was amazing. Go to her GPSS, her teaching is easy to understand! Favorite professor at UNC.

She was not my professor, but I attended her GPSS sessions whenever possible. She is so kind and caring. She explains concepts and reviews questions that professors are likely to ask on exams. Coming from someone who made a D the first time taking Chem 101 to finishing with an A- the second time, she's amazing (ESPECIALLY IF YOU STRUGGLE WITH MATH)

Fostvedt is a blessing in UNCs chem department. She stood on her feet the entire lecture despite being over 8 months pregnant by the end. She clarifies things so perfectly, and takes time to explain if anyone is confused. You will not regret fighting for a spot in her class, I think I would of failed without her.

Awesome professor! She is very patient and willing to help you understand Chem 101. I highly recommend going to her office hours with her. Chem 101 itself is difficult, but she makes it easy to understand.

I LOVE HER. Genuinely one of the most caring and engaging professors at UNC. She breaks down topics very well, so if you're someone that needs to be taught this class is for you. Plus, her annotated slides are super clear + have written out steps incase you missed a class/ need to review topics!
Chem 101 is very hard, but she does her best to make the content seem less daunting and lectures as interesting as possible!

Hands down my favorite chem professor so far (junior chem major). I love Dr Fostvedt so much. She cares about your learning, is kind, and is very accessible. She also wants you to succeed and do your best. Dr. Fostvedt will meet you where you are and try to help you every step of the way. Truly a wonderful human being--her kindness is contagious.
Take her. Favorite class ever

Dr. Fostvedt is awesome! Super sweet and takes all the time needed to answer questions. Since CHEM101 is 90% freshman, she validates us by acknowledging that chemistry is hard. Most of the TAs are great too

Fostvedt is literally amazing, she always has fun ways to teach you content (dances, yoga, models, etc.) and is sooo caring. She will slow down to answer questions and makes jokes inbetween. I only need to take chem101 for my major, but she also teaches 251 and her personality is tempting me to take 251

Her office hours are extremely helpful. ULAs are very helpful too. She has extra credit opportunities. I would take her again. I have never had a more understanding and kind professor, which is rare in UNC's CHEM department. She had helpful practice sheets. On the downside, multiple-choice questions on tests were difficult, in my opinion.

Would give 6/5 if it was an option. Fostvedt is incredible at explaining difficult concepts in ways that are understandable to students. She is also extremely caring and wants all of her students to succeed. She has options for 10 minute meeting every week — strongly recommend. Side note: If you're taking 251, don't read the textbook, it's useless
Dr. Fostvedt is a great profesor and makes sure her students succeed in class

Dr. Fostvedt is by far one of if not the kindest and most down to Earth professor I've ever had. She makes chem 251 and absolute joy, and is one of the most accommodating professors ever. Her exams are always fair, and her lectures are really interesting and taught extremely well. Additionally, she gives a lot of practice.
Leaving love

One of, if not the best professor I've had in college. I learned a ton in this class and had fun doing so. This course was also not overly-demanding at all and I enjoyed it even though synthetic chemistry is not my field of interest within chemistry. Definitely take a class with Dr. Fostvedt if you can.

Dr Fostvedt is the best professor i have had at UNC! The textbook for this class is DENSE but in class her explanations make it so clear. So many opportunities for practice (TONS of practice exams) and her exams are so fair! Hard material but if you go to class it makes so much more sense.

Offered virtually no resources outside of her lectures besides office hours, where she was blunt and condescending. Lectures were given too fast, often skipping steps, and not very informative. Exams were fair if you reviewed and used the practice exams. Grade was determined entirely by exams. Would take with someone else if possible.

While attendance is not mandatory, only what she says in the lecture is examinable. Goes fast in lectures and tends to skip steps to save time. Zero resources or notes outside of lectures!! Exams are somewhat nitpicky, but overall very fair in partial credit. The textbook is okay, but understanding and then memorizing the lecture notes was the vibe

Dr. Pieri is way too smart to be teaching this class and it's clear she also thinks that. Lectures are dull but pretty relevant to her exams which focus heavily on derivations and conceptual understanding over problem solving (except for the final) which made them substantially harder to practice and prepare for. Take with someone else if possible.

There are no resources besides the textbook. If you miss lecture you are completely out of luck unless you get notes from someone and even in that case you don't know what anything means because lecture is completely derivations.

Clearly does not want to teach and takes it out on her students. Class is 90% test and is completely based on lectures which are very boring. There is a textbook but she goes out of order and will not tell you what chapters to read even if you ask. Harsh grader and was very rude when I asked her to explain a question I got wrong on the test.

Class is 100% exam, and exams are difficult. No practice problems given, no learning objectives, and she won't tell us what chapters of the textbook to read, even if you ask. The only thing you have is 1 short practice exam. In my opinion, the Silbey textbook explains things better, but she won't tell what chapters to read. Try to avoid.

Dr. Pieri clearly has no interest in teaching and her class reflects that. Your grade is 100% exams. She doesn't provide resources. No learning objectives, no class schedule, no practice problems, she doesn't post her notes, her lectures are objectively boring, she has difficulty explaining topics, and she often makes mistakes in her lectures.

Do not take her, grade is 100% exams. Gives no practice problems except 1 practice midterm which is different than the content on the exam. Just derives equations from the textbook. Doesn't explain anything well.

Dr. Pieri was very nice and will make you tea/coffee in 1-on-1 office hours. She tried relating the material to real world implications which was cool due to how abstract thermo usually is. Her classes are 100% lectures and derivations from the textbook, so we didn't really get to do much problem-solving which I would've preferred. Exams are fair.
Learned PChem and how to make pasta. 5 stars, would recommend

Pieri lectured verbatim from the Atkins textbook, so if you read before class, you'll be fine. Problem was she didn't give us reading assignments or have a schedule for what she'd be lecturing on, so I had to guess. Lectures were not engaging at all. No class curve, but no homework & she dropped the lowest midterm. Office hours were very helpful.

She's a really good teacher and will emphasize the concepts you need to understand.  The chem department is notorious for giving difficult exams, but in my opinion they werent that bad. As long as you go to class, review the slides, and understand the content, you will do fine.

The UNC chem department is tough, but Dr. Curtis does a great job teaching students the content needed to pass exams, and she does so in a way that is easier to understand than the textbook. Dr. Curtis is also a friendly person, and it is clear that she wants her students to succeed. Definitely take with Curtis if you can!

If you are a pre-med and thought this course was difficult, you should take a step back and reconsider your long-term goals. This class is by far one of the easiest STEM classes you will take. If you got anything below a B+ and are not 100% sure if becoming a doctor is what you want to do, drop medicine now. It is easier to pivot early on.

Dr. Curtis is wonderful and very accessible.  However, exams are 85% of your grade (20% per midterm, 25% final) and they were tough.  The rest of your grade is homework which is graded very leniently.

I had her class in Spring 2025. She was a fine chemistry teacher, and she is definitely passionate about her job. I didn't really find her inspiring, and some days she could go from being the sweetest lady to quite snarky. The chemistry department is also just tough. Self study and practice is super necessary, but take with her if you can!

101/102 get a bad wrap, but they're some of UNC's best-designed courses regarding evidence-based learning and avid practice problem exposure. PAY ATTENTION AND BUY INTO THE SYSTEM. I learned so much + Curtis was clear + qualified. Take accountability for your learning, and trust that 102 provides everything you need to succeed. TLDR: loved Curtis!!

The UNC Chemistry department is extremely difficult; however, I found her teaching to be extremely helpful. She really emphasized understanding the underlying principles of chemistry - the “why” - which, once you actually learn, is crucial and helps with your chemistry intuition. If you take 102, definitely take it with her!!

Chem is hard no matter which professor you have for 102, as it is the same slides and the same exams for everyone. I think Curtis was a great professor, especially outside of the lecture. In GPSS she was very sweet and helpful, and she was great help for study habits in office hours. She's a little corny and had a few laughs in class too.

UNC gen chem is definitely not perfect but Curtis is super caring and approachable and explains examples/topics well in class. Class is designed for you to learn from the textbook and lectures just reinforce the topics from readings. If you read the textbook carefully her lectures are helpful and you will be fine.

The way gen chem is structured at UNC tend to be more dependent on how well you prepare yourself and less about the actual professor you have in my opinion. Curtis was clearly passionate about chem and was kinda entertaining and quirky, but because of the nature chem here I simply can not give her above a 3. chem here sucks but it is what it is.

Anna Curtis is a great professor, chemistry here is just difficult. She is a little quirky but is genuinely excited about chemistry and helping students learn. She really emphasizes knowing the reason why behind concepts and equations, which does make exams harder, but she does a good job explaining things.
If you're not religious, pick a religion and pray. I have never been in such a difficult and unnecessarily confusing course like this. Truly good luck to everyone who has to take this. Godspeed.

She's very passionate for sure but only teaches surface level, and on the midterm, they expect you to be Antoine Lavoisier (the father of chemistry). The class is 84% midterms and finals together. The lectures felt pointless but you have to go because attendance is graded. Go to GPSS if you want to pass. GPA killer for sure.
If you have to take chem 102, I would take it with her. It's a super hard class and the tests are awful, but she as a teacher is very nice and enthusiastic about her subject.

Professor Curtis is not a good professor by any means. She is very bad at explaining basic chemistry concepts and prepares her students in a poor manner for every midterm. The averages in her classes are incredibly low because it requires students to self study to the fullest to perform well. Do not take chemistry with her by any means.

She is incompetent. I would rather watch paint dry than sit in her class. She does an awful job of keeping students engaged. She goes over what 2+2 is like we are in first grade and doesn't prepare us for the exams.
Doesn't do a good job of explaining anything. Very incompetent
She is a very sweet lady but tends to repeat herself. Also, her pacing varies: one day she moves through the slides very slowly, then the next class time she rushes. Wouldn't recommend her :p

I am not joking when I say she is likely the worst professor in the chemistry department. During her lectures, she repeats the same idea numerous times and takes forever to finish simple problems that anyone in the class would understand. If you are taking Chem102, take it with any other professor who doesn't waste their students' time.
She was a good teacher, but chem 101 will be hard no matter who you take it with. Ask questions and go to GPSS if you are having trouble.

Chem 102 is standardized so in that sense you aren't learning anything different in other sections however you will have to deal with how they teach. Dr. Nevins while being very nice is very unprepared. She constantly has tech issues and at the end of lectures ends up rushing and doesn't annotate till after class. She is very nice however not worth

Look, Chem at UNC is super difficult. There are a bunch of major tests, homework all the time, and the concepts are hard. Dr. Nevins was a fantastic lecturer. She was easily able to make hard concepts clear, and was available after class for follow-up questions. She was also understanding of personal difficulty. Definitely recommend.

I never interacted with Dr. Nevins until the day of the final. Overall, Chem 101L is just a lot of work that seems tedious and unnecessary. The classwork is a lot but doable. Just be prepared to take a lot of time for this class and be bored out of your mind during the in-lab activates. So happy that this class is over!

Honestly, for Chem 101L, she plays a minimal role. I saw her once during the entire semester, and it was on the first day. Overall, this class isn't great. Grading is very dependent on your TA, and post-labs take a very long time to be graded. A one-credit-hour class required a lot of time. Just do your work diligently and you'll be okay.
Would give zero stars if I could. Emailed her 7 times over the semester, and she never answered. Avoid at all costs.

Chem101L is by far the worst run class I've taken at UNC. A 1 credit class shouldn't need 3+ hours of homework. Grades were slow to release; half of the labs were ungraded by LDOC. When they were graded, points were removed without explanation, and most labs had grading errors. 1 TA even told me they WEREN'T ALLOWED to give 100s on participation.

She had many students with Chem 101/102, Bio 103, and Chem 101/102 lab finals within 19 hours. She was not willing to let anyone take the test a day later, even though there was a section of students taking the chemistry lab exam a day later. We had to take 3 STEM exams in 19 hours, and she was unwilling to help.
Super disorganized; tells guidelines for assignments AFTER they are due. This is the only chem class/lab I have ever disliked. The points taken off for things are ridiculously high. avoid

Professor Nevins' lectures were easy to follow and really helped me understand the material! She is an engaging professor who focuses on conceptual mastery through lots of in-class practice and review. I also found her to be very caring and respectful to her students. Dr. Nevins is great, so if you're planning to take Chem 102, take it with her!

Dr, Nevins is an amazing professor, she is really kind and really cares that you understand the content. She is really fun and keeps the class engaged, while also keeping it pretty relaxed. all her ratings are low, but that's mainly for the lab, but if you can take 102 with her, do it! I'm assuming all her other lecture classes are great too!
one of the worst experiences of my undergrad now that I am at the end. avoid if you can.
Unreliable person, disorganized, and horrible treatment of students. One of the worst experiences I had. Run.
extremely rude person and barely responsive
Experience so awful at a personal level of communication as well as the educational aspect in CHEM, I do not advise, go away if you can
Goes on a power trip and I feel ashamed of the entire CHEM department at UNC and the people they hire
Horrible treatment and method of communication to students. Disappointing.
Extremely rude and does not communicate
She threatened me for academic reasons and I said that a detail was not communicated and I think she is just awful for an authority position. I have no trust in the entire department.
Incredibly insensitive, uncommunicative, and unresponsive. No wonder students are left in the dark. Horrible department.
Nevins is one of the main reasons I quit chemistry because of her condescending attitude and lack of respect towards students. The department is awful in general.
CHEM101 is a difficult course but Dr. Shepard is so kind and personable, if you can take the class with him then I would!!
Dr. Shepard is so sweet and clearly is passionate for chemistry. Any chem class you take here will be difficult but Dr. Shepard makes it a little more enjoyable with his personality and dog acedotes.

DR SHEPARD IS THE SWEETEST HUMAN ALIVE! I love him so much. He does cute dog analogies (meet them is office hours) and is so kind and caring. We were behind in lecture, but so were the other sections. Like genuinely he is the only thing that got me through the class. Chem101 is hard, but Dr. Shepard stands up for us against the evil chem dept.

chem 101 is genuinely not easy and you're lucky if your professor is as decent as dr. shepard. he is a very kind person and checks in on us throughout class to see if we understand material. he is the only good thing about the chem department.

Chem 101 is HARD, and it will be with whoever you take it with. Makes content easy to understand and emphasises tested materials. Great analogies to make hard concepts easier to understand. Lectures are also entertaining because he has lots of energy and wants to help students understand.

Chemistry at UNC is extremely challenging, but Shepard finds a way to make it better. He is very kind and helpful in explaining difficult topics. I will say that we often get behind in lectures, but I didn't have too much of a problem with it since you'll have everything in time for exam day. Loved him and his dogs!

Dr. Shepard is passionate about chemistry, and he is very kind. However, his lecture style does NOT help you better understand the material. He will start class by talking about his dogs, and we are always behind in lecture. We typically talk about material from a day or two before. You'd be better off taking 101 with another professor.

Chem 101 is notoriously difficult but standardized, so it has nothing to do with the professor. Dr. Shepard is super kind and always encourages class participation. He's a great teacher and seems like he genuinely cares about students and ULs. Love hearing his dog stories and analogies!
Only went to his GPSS sessions and he's great. Doesn't make you feel bad for not understanding the content
I really struggled with Orgo, but Danielle is def the lesser of two evils when compared to Todd. TBH, don't study how they tell you to. Find your own way and seriously practice every day.

Orgo was my first chemistry class at UNC and I was dreading it. However Zurcher made the content much more manageable. She does scare you sometimes like when she says that stereochem took her 8 years to understand, but overall she's an amazing professor and the curve saved my life.

Orgo 1 was very difficult for me, especially bc its my first chem class at UNC. However looking back all the exams were very fairly written, it's just the content that is difficult. Got a B, C, then D on the midterms then an A on the final. It IS possible to do well and Zurcher makes orgo 1 more manageble.

Dr. Zurcher is an amazing lecturer and explains everything in such a clear and engaging way. Genuinely makes orgo super accessible. The CLASS is hard, but SHE is not a difficult professor by any means. Exams are challenging but fair, final is much easier. Best option in the entire chem department IMO. Reccomend.
Really hard class, but great professor. Midterms were pretty hard, but the final wasn't that bad. Make sure you study hard, and it should be fine.
Love her down. Expectations require you to practice a lot on your own. However, tests are difficult. I'd recommend not missing a class.
she reached her full potential quite early in life
Karma will come for her

Dr. Zurcher is nice but all the chem 101 professors use the same slides and have the same tests. No matter who you have you'll have to self teach for the most part. You also don't know your grade unless you calculate it yourself. Would recommend her but be aware its mostly going over practice problems, she doesn't truly teach most of the material.

Dr. Zurcher is great. Explains topics well BUT UNC Chem department sucks. This class will humble you. You'd think you understood the topic well until you get your exam back. The slides cover everything, but even if a topic was only mentioned once with no practice questions, it's fair game. There is so much content. Practice problems are a must!
Wish I had her for the entire semester, super engaging and clear lecturer and the one exam she wrote was extremely fair.

Professor Zurcher's lectures are engaging and easy to understand, reading textbook helps a little but paying attention in class and going over the slides are more important. The course is designed to be very test heavy, but the chem department provides a lot of practice materials. The chem department requires an iClicker.
The class content is very clear, but there is too much of it. The exam covers a wide range of topics.

Chem 101 without taking AP Chem is difficult. READ the textbook assigned readings before class. Use active recall, take practice tests for midterms and finals. Do all homework until you get a 100. If you do not understand a concept, PLEASE UNDERSTAND IT before you move on to the next lesson. ALWAYS review your midterms, bc graders make mistakes.

Professor Zurcher was awesome and made the material clear and easy to understand. Unfortunately, Chem 101 at Carolina is a weed out class so there was a LOT of material thrown at you over the course of the semester. The class was difficult, and the tests were 75% of our grade, but that's the fault of the chemsitry department, not professor Zurcher.
I thought Professor Zurcher was awesome for 101. She was great at explaining concepts and you can tell she is passionate about the subject and her students.
Good professor with many opportunities to meet outside of class, explains content clearly and wants students to succeed but teaches a very hard topic so deserves a little slack for that.

UNC chemistry is difficult as a whole, but I always really enjoyed Dr. Zurcher's lectures. She is a very caring a sweet woman with a clear passion for chemistry, and she tries her best to make the subject approachable. While you do have to buy the textbook to access the homework, most test questions are pulled from the daily slides.
although unc chem is hard by default as its all standardized, zurcher is definitely one of the best profs. her lectures are very helpful, and she's frequently present at after-school review things.

I love Dr. Zurcher! She is genuinely so sweet, caring, and just wants to see her students succeed. She does have high expectations, but she makes her expectations clear and holds every student to the same standard. Chem 101 is a difficult class, but she was great at explaining concepts and providing resources! She is my favorite professor so far :)
The overall course material wasn't bad, but he is a tough grader. Despite that, Dr. Miller is a great teacher and flexible! He is easy to reach out to, and the course was pretty interesting.

Dr. Miller was a fairly straightforward grader and the exams were fair with the exception of a few questions that made you think about the content. Lectures got kind of boring at times but the slides is all you need to know. Textbook is pointless and is a time waster so don't bother. Overall not too bad for a chem course here at UNC.

Really sweet and funny guy with great lectures and explanations. Textbook sucks, attending lecture is the way to do well in the class. Gave generous extra points on exams to bump up averages (ex: 10 extra points out of 75 on the 2nd exam). Only complaint is handwriting could be messy when looking at answer keys.

Content-wise, it's a fun course that's not too difficult, no real chem knowledge necessary. He's a nice teacher and knows what he's talking about. Grading isn't harsh, but it's not just completion, so you need to do well on the projects.

Ok so basically the whole semester I thought this class was a piece of cake but then our final project was terrible. He was not very helpful with the project and didn't even explain how to use the program and told us to look up YouTube videos. He does busy work readings due each class and random small projects. Class was boring but not impossible.

Very kind guy whose last intention in the world is to stress you out with work for this class. If you need a very easy FYS where you basically have to do no work and not really learn anything, this is it.
whatever you do, DO NOT have similar answers to your lab partner. recieved zeros on multiple things for simply having similar answers which is so frustrating because its a LAB?

I don't know much about Mac McNamee himself, but my TA was amazing, and it really depends on that because they are the ones grading your assignments. The lab manual is trash and needs to be redone. It makes no sense. Also, TA hours are useless because a lot of the TAs don't really know what they are talking about. The lab final is stupid.

Lab depends on ur partner and TA and it can be annoying when the lab content doesn't match up with 102 course content. Overall not too hard & my ta was rly nice. The final was harder than expected but not weighted too heavily so your lab reports decide your grade. I think the reports have gotten easier in the past few years. Also he only curves up!
This class was such a time suck. It was overly structured with so much information it became overwhelming at times. Grading is super TA dependent and the final wasn't terrible.
Chem 241L is a time consuming class. But, if you go to office hours, YOU WILL BE FINE. The TA's want you to succeed. Office hours genuinely helped me so much and made the class not that bad.

241L is an unnecessarily tedious class. Besides the equipment being janky, the in-lab portion is actually pretty cool. However, the grading of the lab reports incentivizes copying the 10-page manual to a tea instead of understanding the material. Having graph gridlines or a graph title, and you're getting docked. Reports were very time-consuming.
Overrall ok prof. Can be very rude at times.
No rubric for post lab which sucks. Overall pretty easy class though. Just a lot of busy work. Final isn't that hard.

Super tedious for just 1 credit hour. The lab equipment was faulty or of low quality. In addition to our in-lab assignments, we had to do pre-lab quizzes and post-lab papers (some were unnecessarily long). The final was easy but the grading for the rest of the assignments seemed nit-picky. The experience depends on who your TA is as well.

102L is a joke. Post labs are lengthy and somehow always the week of chem midterms. In labs have MINIMAL instructions and lab manual is very unclear. TAs are harsh graders and not very nice. They really cracked down on attire this year to the point that it was silly. Being assigned partners in our second year + of college is crazy.

The chem102L is kind of disorganized as a whole and the assignments are lengthy and confusing but the lab also only meets around six times. Your TA really determines the actual in-lab environment and my spectacular TA that explained things clearer than the lab manual, helped with procedures, and answered questions about the lab assignments.

Pros: Mac is handsome. Cons: Everything else... the grading is insanely harsh, the final was hard, the labs took forever along with the post lab assignments being very unclear and longer than a book.
How to Study: Pre lab quiz questions... know the math

Absolutely terrible compared to Chem 101L. Took the night lab and we were constantly kicked out of the lab 30 minutes to an hour early so they could start cleaning up for the night. Mac was consistently rude and the TAs were not much better. It is clear that everyone who works there hates the class as much as those taking it.
Buns lab. Truly a disappointment and a real damper on my semester.

Shocked at these reviews. Yes, CHEM 102L has some lengthy assignments and some pre-lab quizzes were confusing, but all in all, there's only like 6 actual labs. Mac sent out lots of communication, offered an extra credit opportunity, and curved the overall grades slightly. Focus on getting correct data, communicate with your TA, and you'll be fine.

I second what everyone else is saying here. On top of it all, after an entire semester of my lab partner and me (and I imagine other people) calculating our final grades based on 1110 points on the syllabus. This man goes and changes it to 1135 after the final exam. I should've have a B+ and my lab partner should've had an A-. Not okay.

Where do I even begin? Literally, the first post-lab report was 16 WHOLE pages. The lab assignments were extremely confusing and I feel like I didn't learn anything in lab. He isn't flexible with students at all and I'm so glad this class is over. The entire chem dept needs some serious work FAST!!

Absolutely terrible class but unavoidable if you need lab credit. Unorganized and each TA grades differently. I attended office hours multiple times and had one TA tell me my graphs were perfect and 10 minutes later a different one says I need to redo the whole thing. This department seriously needs to get itself together and standardize grading

Chem at UNC is notoriously bad, but this lab was just impossible. No one is ever on the same page, quizzes are difficult and post-lab grading is strict. All of the TAs were lost and office hours were always packed with 20+ people, so it can be difficult to get questions answered. All assignments had very unclear instructions and took forever to do.

I absolutely hate chem102L. the grading is ridiculously unfair and the rubric is posted AFTER your assignment is graded. I agree with the other rating that she is always acts out of breath and that she hates her job

Dr. Lockett is a great lecturer and makes the concepts very easy to understand! The exams are incredibly fair, and you are able to score above 100 on them if you try. Overall, he made analytical chemistry fun, especially with his stories.

Friendly and approachable with clear-cut expectations and tons of extra credit. I had to be very self-directed and mature but as long as you do the basics like understand + rework the hw/quizzes/worksheets, come to class, follow expectations, and ask questions early, you will be more than fine. Easier than gen chem and other 241 profs for sure.

The content and lectures can get pretty boring but he is pretty entertaining and funny. Can go on unrelated tangents. You have grade and extra credit quizzes after every class but are graded on participation. He gives a lot of partial credit on exams and the grade can be replaced by the grade on your final pertaining to that unit.

Dr. Lockett was a very good teacher and was very precise and understandable during lectures. He focuses more on the content than grading, so if you get the final math answer incorrect, but the process correct, he will give you credit. I loved taking his class so much, and he was a great friend overall.

Horribly disorganized lectures, would go on strange tangents and convolute simple topics with vaguely related metaphors. It was difficult to follow with notes as he didn't really use the empty slides he posted. Didn't post notes or recordings and answer keys were often inaccurate. I did not learn a single thing about chemistry from this class.
Basically whatever you get on the final is your grade in the class based on the exam replacement strategy. Kinda hate that but its fine. At least I passed

Don't get me wrong Lockett seems like a great guy and his humor made lectures enjoyable but I cannot recall a single thing I learned this semester. Tests seemed impossible because of the sheer amount of questions/ work needed. Everything was curved and extra credit was generous but I regret not taking Tiani and actually learning instead.

I generally liked Lockett except for his exams. He is a hilarious guy and his lectures I didn't think were too boring for an analytical chem class. However, his exams were difficult especially the final exam(brutal!). I finished in on the last second thinking I failed it for sure. There was a nice curve though at the end so I guess it worked out.

He was nice and funny. His tests were very difficult though. Open note exams, but they were much harder than the practice provided. Final was open note but extremely hard and most of the class took the whole 3 hours. Probably still the better 241 option but it was very hard.

Pretty funny professor and cool topics. Go to class, he literally tells you the exam questions! The final is very lengthy and has harder questions than the midterms. However, there was an excessive amount of extra credit and a final grade curve too! Probably the easiest chem/prof combo at UNC. Don't look at any other option if you see this!

Hilarious guy, very to-the-point lectures in terms of what you needed to know for the exams, very generous grading policy. The Canvas materials were pretty unorganized. Skipped over a bunch of content during lecture, making it hard to use previous exams for practice. Ultimately don't feel like I really learned anything despite making an A.
Best Teacher!

I struggled in this class until I followed Dr. Lockett's advice to use flashcards. At first, I ignored it, but before the final, I made flashcards from quizzes and past exams. It changed everything—I scored high on the final and got an A+. Trust the process and start using flashcards early—they truly work!

Was so excited that I got into his class because of his 5.0 ratings but wish I took a different professor. Did not like this class, tests were hard and much different from the in class practice. He would say the test was going to be easier than practice exams and then it would be much harder.

Worst class ever!!! Everyone told me that he was a good professor, however he did not live up to my expectations. I genuinely don't understand how so many students like Lockett. Lectures were disorganized and didn't help with understanding the content. Half of his answer keys are incorrect. Tests are extremely difficult!!

I waited a semester to take this course with Lockett because of his amazing reviews but I was incredibly disappointed. Expect to go over the easiest question in class 4 times only to open the HW to the most impossible unrelated questions. All the tests, including the final, are open note but he makes them very difficult.

Dr. Lockett is an amazing professor. He cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. He offers extra credit and a curve on the final exam. Definitely make sure to practice outside of class so you can have a better understanding of what was covered in lecture. He can be mean sometimes but just be respectful and you will be fine.

Lockett was an absolutely amazing professor, he taught the class in a traditional format. The class also has 20 points extra credit if you just complete the EC quizzes. He also curves the final which is one of the hardest finals I've ever taken but still ended the class with an A cuz of the curve. The final is open note and open internet.

I genuinely don't understand how so many students like Lockett. He would teach something completely different in class and test us on something else entirely. This made the class incredibly difficult. Maybe it is because of the pacing of summer session but I have never done worse in a class despite my consistent study habits. Disappointed.
Lockett was a truly amazing professor! "Big 'D'" was the highlight of the class by far.

Kevin Weeks is the best gen chem professor at UNC in my opinion. Very kind, smart, and emphasizes the most important topics that will be on the exam. I think any bad experiences with him are related to the nature of the course and not him as a lecturer.
AVOID at all cost. He always talk to students in condenseningly and having no respect for students. Made lots of mistakes during lectures which confused our studies.
Super hard class, be prepared to study a lot.
Super nice guy - Chem 102 is tough but team-taught so individual professors don't matter as much. Would definitely take it with him again.

Come to class everyday. Practice as much as possible. Very good prof tho but he doesn't control exam difficulty. Best CHEM 102 professor the issue with this class lies in the difficulty, not really the professor.

The best chem professor for CHEM102. Do the homework and show up to the LA sessions. He's very kind and caring, he will answer questions patiently after class. There have been more than one instance where he stayed late after class on exam days to answer questions from groups of students. Tests make up the majority of the grade.

Weeks is a great professor. He was super nice and gave so many fun in-class demonstrations. Weeks knows what he is doing and gave clear information in the lectures. I highly recommend Weeks to anyone hoping to get to know their professor too since he is always trying to meet all of his students despite how big the class is.

Weeks never seemed to know what was going on. He made numerous fundamental mistakes that would confuse our understanding of concepts and overall, wasn't a good lecturer. I felt like I learned the content for this class by myself. I went to a couple Fostvedt lectures and she is actually AMAZING!
102 is hard but Kevin Weeks is the goat. He's super nice and caring, and explains concepts fairly well. Definitely take him.

I love Weeks. 102 is a hard course and the exams weigh heavily, but this is true for any professor. Weeks made little jokes and would try to help you to read the questions for what they're asking. I had issues with something exam related and he made a special case to help fix the error and is very responsive to any questions in/out of class
love weeks!

grade is almost entirely exams, but your lowest test is weighted less (i got a c on one exam and still got an a in the class).  he's not perfect and would make mistakes in lectures but he is very knowledgeable and will go back and explain if you ask.  better than the other 102 profs imo

While prof Weeks wasn't perfect, I'd definitely recommend him over the other chem 102 professors.  He was prone to making mistakes in class but his explanations were overall relatively good and he prepared us well for the exams (84% of your grade btw).

Dr. Weeks is a gem. Even though I've only had a few personal interactions with him, I can definitely vouch for his character and kindness. CHEM102 is humbling even for those who excelled in AP Chem. It's definitely possible to end well even if you tank one of the midterms (speaking from personal experience). Don't get discouraged and try your best!

I had Curtis for 101, and Weeks was so much better in my opinion. He is so encouraging and makes the material much easier to understand. He is really trying to teach and not trick anyone, which I appreciated. His demonstrations were awesome, and it was obvious he cared. Take his class if you can.

A Very good professor, very genuine, and a nice guy, he does demonstrations and plays music before class. He is very easy to talk to and is knowledgeable on the subject. There are occasional problems with the iClicker participation, and he sometimes gets tripped up on random questions.

Sometimes Professor Weeks gets a bad rep, but I don't think it's deserved. He's a really nice guy who cares a lot about his students. Sometimes his jokes are corny but honestly I think they made class fun. His demonstrations were the best, and made people actually want to show up to class. I really liked this professor!

Professor Weeks is amazing! He teaches with simple terms, so he's easy to understand in lectures, and even cracks jokes at least a few times in a class. He makes an effort to get to know his students even in a giant lecture.
Dr.Weeks is super passionate about chemistry and it shows in his lectures. He did an amazing job of explaining difficult concepts and always made jokes!

Dr. Weeks is one of the most genuine profs I've had in college. You can tell he truly cares about his students and how they are doing as people. He has funny examples to show chemistry concepts and makes the overall class a very enjoyable experience. Personally, Chem 102 has so many resources -- choose a lecturer that cares.

Passionate professor but difficult course. He spends more time on iClicker questions that most students get wrong and did a couple fun demonstrations related to the class topic. Chemistry itself is hard and you'll need to put in the time, regardless of professor. I would recommend him though because he's funny and decent at explaining material

He's so passionate about chem and has a molecule of the day, that said the chem department is evil so you probably won't do too well on exams. Lecture can get boring but I think that's honestly any chem lecture. Use your resources.
Professor Warren is decent at explaining concepts, textbook is easy enough to understand to fill in the necessary gaps. Exams are reasonable, no trick questions.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. He is out of tough and doesn't relate the reading, lectures and homework. He will test you on material that was never discussed. Test are impossible and he gives almost no credit for work. Doesn't respond to emails and out right rude.

Course grade is 100% from exams but don't be deterred, he is very clear with his expectations for the exams and the specific content you will be tested on. Lectures were always shorter than class time, and it was easy to follow his slide deck if you didn't attend class. 10/10!

Hands down the best chemistry prof at UNC. Lectures are informative and engaging (he's also funny). Course grade is 100% exams; he outlines exactly what will be tested, but the grading is pretty harsh. I'd definitely recommend taking him if you get the chance.

Dr. Redinbo is super cool, makes class interesting, and is a funny guy. He is one of the most respected chem professors at UNC but he's down to earth and makes class easy. Exams are straight from the slides (it is a lot of content though), no homework, and no unnecessary assignments (like in other CHEM courses).

Dr. Redinbo made learning biochem very engaging and easy to understand. Although the class is mainly 3 exams, he is SUPER clear with test material - all you need is a few days to learn the material before an exam. No homework either.

Professor Eskew gives good, clear lectures. This class is pretty difficult, but she writes fair exams. Grading (which I don't think she's responsible for) on said exams can be pretty harsh, however. She's a good choice for lectures nonetheless.

Dr. Eskew is kind, patient, and caring. This class is like 90% outside practice and 10% lecture, which is expected. She made Organic Chem II feel far less intimidating than I thought it would be. Definitely nail down NMR, as it appears on every exam. Her exams (unlike Beavers) are actually fair. Would definitely recommend! Such a sweetheart!

Dr. Eskew is absolutely the best chem professor at UNC. Her caringness and willingness to work with students were a much-needed breath of fresh air, and while the content of CHEM 262 is objectively difficult, if you put the effort in, it is without a doubt manageable!

Dr. Eskew cares about teaching the content and walks around the class from time to time to answer questions. Exams are difficult but fair, with very few curve balls (Looking at those energy diagram questions). Overall, a great teacher, and I highly recommend her for orgo. Watch Chad's Prep 2x speed before the lecture for an A.

Dr. Eskew is sweet and fair. She tries her best to explain concepts to students and help out anyone having questions on Orgo. Her exams are straight forward application and very fair. This is a hard class indeed and she did a great job getting the most important information into the lectures. Definitely attend class, GPSS, and ULA sessions.

She does not explain concepts or mechanisms well, I found Beaver to be way better of a prof. I went to GPSS, ULA sessions, and all the workbook problems and still barely passed the class. Exams were unnecessarily difficult and written sloppily. I did better on Beaver exams than hers. I don't learn much in lecture, she goes over things too simply.

Eskew is super nice, but was a pretty average lecturer. My main complaint is that professors constantly failed to address student questions. Exams were written sloppily, not super difficult, but would make mistakes and go to unnecessary lengths to cover their tracks. Ed Discussion is encouraged until it becomes an inconvenience to the professors.

I found Dr. Eskew's lectures to be a bit dry at times. However, she's a very calm lecturer, and I appreciated this as the class stressed me out at first. I did much better on her exams than I did on Dr. Zurcher's and Dr. Beaver's at the beginning of the semester.

Orgo is going to be hard. I think Eskew does a pretty good job of teaching, covers the material and gets through what needs to be done. Not much to be said, regardless of what professor you take you really just have to do a lot of practice and lock in on exams to do good.

Exams were difficult, and were graded harshly. The first exam (taught be Beaver due to Eskew's absence) went much better compared to the exams done with Eskew. The final exam she wrote was abysmal. I would not recommend this experience. The class is graded off exams, which are much more difficult than they need to be for a college level class.

Eskew's a pretty good professor. She started out a little shaky, but I'll give her grace because she came in halfway through the semester, which is tough. Overall a solid professor and exams are straightforward with her.

I mean orgo is orgo, but she didn't make it any easier. I had Dr. Beaver for a little bit and my first exam was my best score, as soon as eskew switched in, the concepts started getting fuzzy and the exams were kinda all over the place. She is extremely dry and i am not excited to take 262 with her to say the least

Her lectures are dry but she doesn't overcomplicate topics. Sometimes she doesn't go in-depth into a topic and then it shows up on the test but it's not too bad. I also only had her for like 1.5 months so I don't know what she's like for teaching all of unit 1 and half of unit 2. The one test she wrote for us was pretty easy.

Dr. Eskew is very caring and always willing to give extra help. Her lectures aren't the best, but orgo is orgo and requires a lot of self-teaching no matter who you take it with. Her exams are super straightforward and it's not hard to do well if you practice consistently.

I do not know what happened to Dr. Eskew. She used to be great (hence the old and incredibly positive reviews), but this semester she was just awful. Boring lectures, didn't answer questions in class, slides where illegible at times, exams were graded incorrectly-- I could go on. Please take either Dr. Zurcher, or  Dr. Beaver.

Prof Eskew was supposed to teach my class all semester, but randomly took off for the first month. I had Prof Zurcher, and she was amazing. Then Eskew came back and my grade tanked. She's just such a boring lecturer, and she doesn't explain anything. When people ask questions, she doesn;t actually answer them and just moves on.

I liked Dr. Eskew's lecturing style and her very fair exams. Class content isn't bad if you try to learn instead of pure memorization. Since the content builds off the last it's vital to keep up with whatever is going on in class. Do practice and understand the why behind the madness. Also, don't bother wasting money on the model kit; it's useless.

Dr. Eskew is a caring professor and really good at teaching orgo. She explains things clearly and answers questions in class well. Orgo is hard, but she approaches it with low drama and seems to really care about her students. She was patient and responsive about a tech issue I had. Has a good sense of humor too!
Great professor. Very clear and understanding in lecture. Exams were fair for the most part and I enjoyed the course overall.

Easily the best choice for orgo. Eskew actually tests on what she teaches in a fair way and genuinely seems to care about her students. Office hours/problem sessions are helpful and her lectures are clear. She is very caring and helpful despite the class being inherently very difficult. Definitely choose her over the other professors.
The grading rubrics is very unclear and TAs expectations vastly different across sections. Labs are very complicated and the workload seems endless.

Grading depends on your TA obviously, Motley only posted announcements for all 241L kids, but he is very precise and thorough when explaining grading and such. These lab reports take FOREVER! Start early, go to TA office hours (super helpful), even if it isn't your TA. Experiments were pretty interesting in general.

Hardly saw him in lab by the course is very well structured and expectations are generally clear. Last lab report is extremely long. Even though it's a group/partner effort, it took a lot of time and is worth a lot. No final tho. Rounded my 92.4 to an A so I am forever indebted to him :)

They gotta change this up. Writing in a certain font or using gridlines in graphs doesn't mean I dont understand the lab. Really annoying and nitpicky when it comes to these things. If you have a bad TA or a bad group, you're screwed! Just do lab manuals and follow every single guideline and you will be fine

Dr. Motley is pretty chill. This class completely depends on your TA though. The lab reports are a pain, so make sure you start early and follow the addendums exactly. The final exam is somewhat rough, but just read through the lab manuals for each experiment and you should be fine. Probably the most work for a 1-credit class at UNC.

Of course, your TA interacts with you more than Dr. Motley. Nonetheless, Dr. Motley ran the course in an organized and flexible manner. He operated smoothly during mid-semester setbacks in our research project. Lab reports and research papers are the biggest portion of your grade, but the class is absolutely doable, and there's no final.

No one talks about how much orgo lab sucks. It's hard- experimentally, conceptually, etc. There's no workaround, you just have to rely on the curve. Motley could have given clearer guidelines for grading and done a better job at ensuring that all TAs graded similarly. I was told my multiple people that my TA was simply a "harsh grader."

I always dreaded days when I had 241L. The TAs do Dr. Motley's dirty work for him, and to do well, pray you get a TA that grades somewhat leniently. Additionally, lock in on notebook assignments and lab reports, because the final was one of the worst I have ever taken at UNC. Grading criteria is always super unclear.
Grade is *entirely* dependent on TA to be honest. Lots of work, arguably more than the lecture but enjoyable.

Labs are completely dependent on the TA so take this with a grain of salt, but Dr. Motley did a pretty great job of making sure the students were comfortable and able to do their best work in the class.

Dr. Motley is very caring, and he is extremely clear about everything. The lab reports do take forever, but you can definitely do well on them if you follow the rubric to a tee. TA office hours are super helpful as well. The labs themselves weren't too bad, just tedious at times. Overall, a much better class than most people say!

Very dependent on TA, but as far as chem labs go, Motley is the best I've had so far! Clear communication about grading exams/end-of-semester timeline. Does take off a lot of points for minor things, such as going one sentence over a page limit, so be careful

Dr. Motley is the best lab instructor I've had so far, and I feel like he really cares for the students and making sure each lab section is fair! The lab reports do take FOREVER and some TAs (or rubrics) can be very nitpicky, so I def recommend starting early and attending TA office hours with any questions.
Although you primarily interact with your TA, Dr. Motley was still a cool professor who made it clear he just wanted everyone to have a nice time. The class is manageable, but not easy.

While your grade in this class is primarily dependent on your TA, you can tell that Dr. Motley puts a lot of time and effort into making the lab experience the best it can be for the students. Reports do take some time, but grading criteria is clear. Start early and the workload should be manageable.

Motley was fine? I didn't have a whole lot of interaction with him, but I found the lab overall very doable. It was by no means easy, but I think it's a reasonable amount of work if you start early and are prepared to ask questions when you need it.

There is a word for Dr. Motley but I can't use it on this page... really insensitive and his ego is bigger than this entire school. The grading in this course is kind of ridiculous and no, Dr. Motley does not care. Overall, the course is a ton of busy work and graded tediously but its for sure possible to get a good grade.

Take this class with Moran. It is lecture heavy, but he doesnt surprise you when it comes to quizzes and exams. What he teaches in class is exactly what he wants you to now. Very helpful with matlab troubleshooting. Most of the grade is six open note quizzes and an open note final

Dr Moran is a very nice and reasonable professor. However, he does skip through a lot of introductory material and only covers derivations very briefly, which made it difficult to understand the reasoning behind a lot of the concepts. The quizzes and final were very straightforward and simple though.
One of the easiest labs in the department, and you actually learn a lot about how computational chemistry is done. The TAs are also extremely helpful.
This is good. Just take this class with Dr. Moran--Trust me.

ABSOLUTELY take P chem 2 with Moran!! Hard material of course but open note quizzes and final. Used poll everywhere data so you have to go to class but offers zoom if you have a legitimate reason. He is also very nice.

Super knowledgeable on the material and welcomes questions. Prof. Moran values polling data from students, so you must complete the polls to succeed in the class. That said, they're a great template for the quizzes & final exam so students benefit from them too.

Lab sessions are not required to attend, but the class is very manageable if you attend them. The lab assignments are tricky due to the complicated nature of the material, but the TAs are very helpful. Just one weekly assignment and no exams. Recitation/lecture session is once a week and very chill.

He has a deep appreciation for genuine polling data. Everything you need to know he goes over thoroughly in class. Lectures were recorded and posted on sakai, this was a helpful tool to revisit topics, but his slides are very detailed and will also serve as great explanations. This is good.
Curves grades down. Went into the final with an 88, now I'm retaking the class
Looking forward to the day he is out of a job
