No. Just no. I cannot believe I took orgo I and II only to get downgraded to a worse grade than I received in either class because of Pielak's curve.

Just don't do it ;) Save yourself from having to retake it elsewhere. Unless you are a consistent 95%+ type of student, you will not get an A. Dr. Pielak did nothing to resolve the intense downgrading and neither did the UNC Chemistry Department. His lectures were also very confusing and I learned more from Dr. Hogan's videos than I did in class.
By far the most stressful class I've taken at UNC.

I got a B-  I got a 93 or so. It was easy class. But curved. It's in the syllabus. But just know that it is that way. I do not believe this is the best way to grade. Never had a class that took my best work and smudged it.
Curves down grades

The worst experience in college. Lectures were bad, everything is said better in recorded Hogan videos - except you'll miss things in lecture he puts in tests like his wife's name or a riddle's answer. Was disrespectful in office hours. Curved everyone down by up to 5 letter grades based on normal distrubution. 87% in class overall, ended with a C.
Got an A. Course material was easy but graded on a curve. Was not a nice person.
This was the worst professor I could ever have a nightmare about let alone actually have. He grades on a bell curve scale so he can make himself feel better. It's as if he wants his students to fail.
I received a 91.6 in the class. Got curved down to a B. DO NOT recommend taking this class. Please take with Hogan!
Curving a 95 down to a B+ is insanity.

I have never heard of a professor who says an 80 is a C- in the class!! His entire grading system was based on how other students perform. If everyone does well, he will curve the class down. Please don't take.
Don't do it.
Did great on my midterms and assignments. Professor decided to curve down the final and I ended with a C… around 41% of students got a C as well which isn't normal for a class.
What everyone else said

Inconsistent grading. Lack of effort placed on creating exam questions. Lack of effort preparing for lecture. Most effort placed on pointing out mistakes in Dr Hogans slides. Your grade in this class literally depended on two midterms (no effort in furnishing an actual final exam). Fantastic researcher but does not care about students. avoid.

Do not take him! He rambles in lecture, claims oh you already know this when going over the learning objectives. Often skipped part of the lecture and never came back the next class. It was a very uncoordinated semester, canvas never showed the correct grade and many answer keys weren't available til 1-2 days before an exam such as concept checks.
avoid at all costs

Uses all of Hogan's materials but makes his own exams without disclosing any differences in content that will be on the exams. Misleads students heavily without being communicative. Unfair grading scale and just overall a poor professor who lacks any consideration and genuine care to see his students succeed.

He's not the greatest at explaining challenging concepts but he's really not all that bad. He made lots of mistakes and sometimes did problems wrong, but he's receptive to corrections. He also doesn't write the exams so it wasn't a problem.

The key to success in orgo, unfortunately, is often not the teacher you get. You teach yourself most of the material from the textbook, and if you are confused, go to GPSS or SI Sessions. That being said, Dr. You made some mistakes at the beginning of the year, but really hit his stride towards the end. He was very funny and approachable.

Success in orgo isn't dependent on the prof, but he made (and corrected) mistakes in lecture that were kind of confusing.

Orgo is basically taught flipped-classroom. There are lots of resources that you can use to study (practice ?'s, slides, graded asgmts, textbook, CHEMpossible, EdDiscussion). Exams can be tricky, so pay attention to details.

dude, if you can't teach to save your life please don't write such criminal exams. I was questioning my life choices reading the instructions on exam 3. TAs are super stringent on grading. Final exam is the same level as midterms, not easier by any means

Professor You is, as other reviews mentioned, a genuinely nice guy. However, he has not taught orgo in a very long time, and he was getting his bearings this semester. The lectures got better as the semester went on, but you should still be wary and choose a more experienced professor for orgo if given the option.

Orgo is a difficult class no matter who you have, but it's not like Dr. You helped.  He's a perfectly nice person, but his lectures are all over the place and he often has to correct himself mid-sentence or mid-explanation, making everything even more confusing.  There were also lots of exam grading debacles this semester, but that's not all on him

You is a ball of sunshine but isn't an experienced teacher. He is funny but bad at explaining and is prone to making mistakes. He also is responsible for a test that had many mistakes. Orgo has PLENTY of resources. So TBH it doesn't matter what prof you have. Do the readings thoroughly, do plenty of practice, and go to ULA sessions. You'll be fine.

Dr. You is a sweet guy, but teaching is certainly not his strong suit. Frequently made mistakes during class and our section was continuously behind the others. Lots of self-teaching. Went to his office hours once and he didn't even know the answer to my question...had to email me at a later time clarifying the answer. Workbook problems are a must!

Dr. You is a rly nice professor and was accessible outside of class but (respectfully) he cannot teach orgo. He frequently got questions wrong and recorrected himself in class and was rly bad at explaining content (never anything more that reading from the slides). I ended up going to a different professor's lecture to actually learn the content.

Prof wouldn't be my first choice for orgo, but imo orgo is more abt doing as much practice as possible, do all the workbook + textbook problems, and go to ULA sessions. Most annoying thing is the workbook problems do not have answer keys to over half the problems so find a study group to compare with. Dont fall behind bc orgo builds on itself

Orgo 1 is challenging no matter who you take it with and I think Dr. You did an okay job especially because it's his first year teaching the class. He does make mistakes occasionally which can be confusing but always corrects them later. He tries to encourage people to participate in a 200 person class which I will also give him credit for.

You is a nice enough professor, but just isn't as familiar with the content as other instructors. He is funny and pretty accessible outside of class, but his lectures are a little disorganized and he was prone to making mistakes on some problems. Not the best choice for 261 but not too bad.

He's nice. Orgo is really hard, wouldn't say professor made it better. Hasn't taught in a long time, so material is fresh to him as well. His teaching wasn't very effective. Overall just not a fan of how the class is done in general. Make sure to stay ahead even before the semester starts, that's where I went wrong.
i love dr. you sorry not sorry, obvi orgo is hard but the entire dept makes the exams and for his first time teaching orgo in 20 years i cant complain.

Dr. You changed the quiz dates and grading distributions on the syllabus 2 or 3 times in the semester. He often scheduled other meetings during office hours. Book was dense and outdated. He curved overall grade, but still, I had to constantly ask for points back to get a decent grade. Nice person & interesting class, but very disorganized.

I didn't have a problem with the class, but I could be biased because I wasn't worried for my grade. Textbook was meh but he uploaded 3 others. Didn't curve exams but did curve the class. Hes a nice prof. Lectures towards the end were confusing. Slides were easy to review. Would sometimes upload late but there were always other resources.

I had no idea my class was split about Wei. The grading rubrics were a bit harsh, but I never had a problem getting points back. He always treated questions kindly and was very caring. Slides were mostly pictures, so he def wasn't "reading off" them. He also frequently used the chalk board to explain. It wasn't too hard overall but it's still 400.
TERRIBLE class. the lectures were just him reading the slides. would not take again.

CHEM 101 is standardized but Werley does a good job of getting through the topics.  She is very concise, gets the point across, and consistent every lecture. She was very engaging for an 8 am class and would start the morning with a cat picture or a meme. Sit in the front where you can ask questions during practice problems.

Even though I am having to retake CHEM 101, that is not a reflection of Professor Werley. She is incredibly encouraging and kind. I constantly find myself remembering things she said during lecture that are finally clicking now. Professor Werley truly cares about her students, and I am very grateful to have had her as a professor.
Enthusiastic about teaching, GPSS is a great resource for chem students

Very chill and engaging professor, sometimes would go too in depth and would miss the rest of the lecture leading us to get behind a little bit. Stay on top of studying they are not joking with the 3 hours a day to study.
Werley is a very engaging professor, especially for an 8am class. as long as you put extra effort you'll probably do better than i did

Surprisingly somewhat engaging as an 8 AM lecture professor. This is Chem 101, so expect lots of studying outside of class and treat the lectures more like a review session of concepts you might've not understand from the readings and smartwork.

no matter what Chem101 class you take they are all the same. Werley was more on track with lesson plans, but she often rushed through it. If this is your first time taking chem ever (i never took chem in hs ) UNC chem is really hard.... I got weeded out! Read, go to tutoring, dont cheat on smartworks. The actual exam is 2x harder than the practice.

chemistry is a difficult class in general, especially if u didn't take AP Chem in HS (like I did). she's an okay professor, the 6 min meetings r lowk stupid imo since you can't discuss much during that tine, but she is very sweet and knows her stuff. I barely passed the class but put the time and effort in and it'll pay off

Managed to enjoy 8am chem after being convinced chemistry wasn't real in HS. Loved the consistency of the lectures. Super standardized course, but after Zurcher subbed I was grateful for Werley's lecture style! Would def take with them again and I learned a lot :)

Werley is clear and her lectures provide really useful content to know what to study for tests. She has the perfect balance of asking students questions and talking, creating an engaging environment. The readings can be tiring, but if you stick with them and the homework, you should be successful!

Chem 101 is a weed out at UNC, so no matter the professor, the class is hard and takes a lot of work and studying outside of class time for you to do well. However, I found Prof. Werley to be a lot more engaging than the others. The one time Zurcher had subbed for Werley, I found the lecture extremely boring and just unengaging.

It isn't the professor that is hard, but rather the content and class itself. A fast paced class, and heavy on content. Tests are extremely challenging, and weigh heavy into your grade. It is nice to have a recitation to talk things through. Professor was easily accessible and willing to meet outside of class time to go over study habits, etc.

Like someone else said, Chem101 is a mandatory prereq so every lecture is probs the same, but I think Prof. Werley is pretty chill and detailed for a MWF 8am lecture. I like the memes they choose for Monday because the corniness wakes me up lowkey. They also actually care to answer questions in deatil

Chem 101 is a standardized course, so it doesn't matter which professor you take, but Werley is pretty good. In her lectures, she often goes into detail and asks for questions from people. Chem 101 is a hard course - I recommend finding another student who has already taken the course and asking for advice on studying, you're going to need it.

she was a really good prof. this is a hard class but she made the lectures useful and worth going to. if there's logistic issues with the class, she's not incharge of it since its a common course. she's really as good as a chem 101 prof can be

not the most friendly professor but they are very good at explaining and i actually learned a lot in lecture despite it being a very fast-paced class. chem 101 is difficult and standardized so it really does not matter who you take it with.

Since all chem 101 tests and content are standardized, it doesn't really matter who your professor is as long as they're not absolutely horrible. I would say Professor Werley is decent, not the most engaging lecturer but not super boring or anything either.
I mean chem 101 is a hard class, especially since it's a weed out. Werley wasn't exceptional, but there are definitely worse professors for this class.

Werley is extremely sweet and makes the most out of this team taught class.CHEM 101 is a flipped classroom, so the clarity, consistency, and reliability that Werley brings to lecture is amazing. Sit in the front rows. CHEM 101 is cutthroat b/c there is no exam drops, but exams are genuinely straightforward. Great class, contrary to popular belief!

Bryn Werley is a new teacher, but she was good nonetheless. She is extremely thorough with the lectures and oftentimes did not get through all of the material intended for the given day. The tests were extremely fair and overall it was a good class.

She's alright ngl. Hand writing kinda mid but she explains things pretty well. Professor doesn't matter too much for CHEM 101 but I'd def choose a different one. Overall, chem 101 light asf yall just gotta lock in and learn how to reason and to problem solve

Dr. Dempsey consistently had engaging lectures to help clarify information that we learned the night before, since this course uses a flipped-classroom model. This is a challenging course but she held group problem solving sessions weekly to further explain certain topics. She is very enthusiastic and knowledgable about the course material.

The class difficulties are from the chem department standards, but as a professor is very helpful and not derogatory like a lot of other chem professors. Slides were detailed and was willing to admit mistakes on slides.

She is a good professor and explains the concepts in a way that is easier to understand than other chemistry professors I have had. She answers emails promptly and is really kind! However, UNC general chemistry exams are extremely difficult. I used Crambetter tutoring to supplement my studying in class and it was extremely helpful.

Professor Kosovsky was very kind, but it was clear that she was a little nervous to be teaching a big lecture. Also, chem is just hard so I think it's unfair to blame her. If you put in the work outside of class you will be fine. I used crambetter for the final review and it helped to have extra videos and practice problems to use.

Class was hard, but any chemistry class is at UNC. Leah wasn't great, but it was her first class, so you have to give her the benefit of the doubt. The only way I passed was by using Crambetter outside of class to review material that was missed during class.

Leah was not only kind but helpful and knowledgeable. I know the other students are writing that she answered questions incorrectly, and stumbled a bit, but I can't imagine how challenging it would be to step into your first year teaching and expect it to be exactly smooth sailing. I entirely trust that she will learn from any teaching stumbles.

Although she might have misspoken during lecture sometimes or not elaborated on a subject, she retroactively corrected her mistakes and answered questions well. If you actually did the warmups and actively paid attention in class, these little slip-ups shouldn't have affected you for more than a minute. Just ask the ULAs if you're confused.

She seemed sweet, and I feel bad that her RMP is being bombed her first year of teaching. She pretty much just read the slides in class, but she often got the wrong answers to the practice problems, so time in the next class often had to be spent clarifying errors from the previous one. Learn from our mistakes and just take this class with Bliem.

prof kosovsky was really sweet but consistently got questions wrong in class, which was very confusing. she explained more than bliem which was helpful, but often led us astray. her annotated slides are good but her in class was honestly more hurtful than helpful.

I feel bad because she's super nice, but she's not the best at answering questions, because she doesn't know the answer half the time. Also, on the exam-type-questions, she gets different answers to Bliem which is frustrating. I think she just needs more practice teaching, but I'd take one of the Professors if you can
Take bliem and save yourself. She doesn't have the skills to teach.

Chem 102 is very test-heavy. The only reason I found this class so difficult is that Kosovsky would often mispeak while lecturing and confuse everyone. I would say she seems a little unsure of the content and not confident enough to be teaching this big a class. I would be sitting in her lecture, thinking I'm going to have to look this up later.

could learn all the same info by not going to class and searching up a youtube video tbh, not very engaging lectures and there have often been mistakes in slides and answer keys, the content is simple but the tests are hard because you get points of for really small things, tests do not demonstrate understanding of content AT ALL
Good and knowledgable lecturer. Chem is hard but she does a good job at simplyfiying complicated topics.
I thought she was a good lecturer, new to teaching but she definitely explained concepts well. Tests are pretty hard but common between sections.

Kosovsky is very bad at answering questions during class and often doesn't give a direct answer. She often dances around the question instead of answering it. I think she is trying her best, but she is not ready to teach this big a lecture.

I thought she explained concepts well and her annotations on the slides are very helpful. She always makes sure to reiterate important points, and I appreciated how she always reminded us to get our iClicker points. She's not always the best at answering specific questions in class though. Also, chem at UNC is just hard and tests are standardized.
I cannot learn from her because she describes concepts that don't make any sense, even the ULAs are like what is she talking about.
She messes up on her slides and explains things in the most complex way possible.
She is so confusing

She is the worst chem teacher I have had at unc. She is so bad at explaining concepts and just jumps around everywhere. She doesn't finish her slides during class and then just rushes through everything at the end. She seems very new because she doesn't know how to answer questions during class and seems unsure about a lot. Overcomplicates things!!
This course is one of the more doable chem courses at UNC. I would recommend taking it with Tiani.

His exams were fair. Lectures and practice sheets were helpful. However, he can be a little derogatory and overall unhelpful when you ask him a 1-on-1 question about a concept or question. ULAs were very helpful. He gives lots of resources to help you succeed. Easiest chem prof/class at UNC so far.

I took CHEM 241 as a first semester freshmen so my difficulty rating may be a bit high. Dr. Tiani gave clear lectures and the LAs would answer questions promptly. The only downside is that when drawing on the slides, his handwriting can be very hard to read at times.

Tiani really cares about students and is a very fair professor. Exams are challenging but expected based on what was covered in class and the practice problems. ULA sessions are VERY helpful. His practice sessions are also super helpful as well.

Good professor, good lectures, grades pretty fast. Actually teaches the material. CHEM241 is a lot of math and conceptual questions. Was nervous for the class but heard Tiani was the best, and he delivered! Make sure to read the textbook, stay on top of homework and pre class assignments. Review for at least a week before exams.

The material is super dry but I really liked Tiani. Most of the exam questions were pretty straightforward, but some questions are very niche. Go to review sessions, especially Tiani's. If you skip class, make sure you have someone you can ask for notes. His handwriting is so bad.

Analytical chemistry is not the most exciting of classes, but I did really like Dr. Tiani. He is quite helpful during office hours and his exams were challenging, but fair. Unlike other professors in the chem department, I believe Dr. Tiani truly cares about student well-being and success. Would overall recommend him!

Tiani is very understanding of academic pressure and wants his students to succeed. If you want to do well in his class make sure to do all of the ULA practice problems before tests and go to or do the worksheet from his twice weekly review session. Sometimes he uses problems from these sessions on the exam.

this chem lab is not taught by him but he did write the final which was impossible and caused my grade to go from an A to a B+. however, this is just standard of all UNC chem lab finals, where they are impossible to do well on and unrelated to the actual course materials.

tiani is the best chem professor i have had at UNC. his lectures are extremely helpful and to the point. he goes over exactly what you need for the exam and his exams are extremely fair. they were all problems i had seen before, whether it was on homework or from his problem sessions. however, his handwriting is impossible to read on the slides.

I can't say too much because this lab isn't exactly taught by him, but I will say I was shocked as he was extremely gracious and understanding when I got violently sick mid chem exam week; he let me take the lab final the next week. Overall seems very understanding in terms of student well-being (although I can't speak on his teaching capabilities)
His handwriting is quite literally indecipherable. If you miss one class be prepared to be lost for the remainder of the entire unit.

very lecture heavy, yet the exams almost always have content that was barely touched on. I never once skipped his class, took notes, and studied with plenty of time, and i found it super difficult. he is very knowledgable about analytical chemistry but also kind of rude when students don't understand a concept. discouraging a little.

Dr. Tiani clearly knows analytical pretty well but his class is very lecture/textbook heavy. He seems caring in class but 1-on-1 he can be super rude and unwilling to explain difficult concepts. The material is extremely boring but he doesn't ask any trick questions on exams.

Dr. Tiani sounds like a professor who knows the information that he is teaching, but this is another case where his exams don't match what he teaches sometimes. Theory questions on exams are easy, but math can be ok to very niche and crazy sometimes, rarely in stuff he gives. He is very helpful in his office hours, would recommend him overall.

not a bad teacher at all, but very tough. my main issue with prof. tiani is that about halfway through the semester he would get mad at students asking questions in the lecture/just answering a question he asked wrong. it kinda discouraged engagement a bit. also for exams, study the content that doesn't get reviewed often. it WILL be on the exam.
Dr. Tiani is really good at teaching. I enjoyed his class and it came out well. He is really a nice person, and it's helpful to go to his office hour.

Dr. Tiani was one of the best professors I've had under UNC's chemistry department. I was personally a big fan of his lecture style, as he'd often go over the exact content that you needed to know to do well on his exams. The lectures are somewhat rapid paced, but if you set aside some time a day to work/review practice problems, you'll do great!

Dr Tiani is an amazing professor. He is always eager to help you and answer the questions and hold multiple help session for students to grasp the content. He's a very caring toward the success of his students. The only challenge was the final, which was a lot harder than the midterms imo. Would 100% take again.

I took Dr. Tiani for Summer 241 class. Overall he's a very nice teacher and always happy to help you whether it is discussing study strategies or helping clear up concepts. His exam questions are similar to problem session and poll ev in class questions so make sure to attend his sessions whenever you can.

Schoenfisch is funny and happily replaced bad midterm grades with higher final grades, which was very helpful. However, his powerpoints weren't good if you couldn't grasp part of the lecture, but he could be discouraging when people asked questions. Not a bad professor compared to other 241 profs, but he could improve his accessibility
Best chemistry class I've taken. Professor is caring and provides you with opportunity to learn the material and overcome mistakes. Outside of class prep is not excessive either.
I enjoyed the class and he made the material easier to understand. Focus on the lectures and suggested homework, and come to class. You'll get an A or B without too much more.

Too many babies take this class apparently! He is by far the best and most fair chemistry professor I have had. Sure he is tough and has high expectations, but if you are wiling to put in the work you will be rewarded with experience and knowledge beyond what's stated in his syllabus.

I've never rated a prof below 4/5 or difficulty above a 3/5. This has been the most hopeless class I have ever taken, which sucks b/c you can tell Schoenfisch is extremely intelligent and really cool. Just bad slides, unclear hw/expectations, unsure how to succeed. He said the whole class gets replaced by the final tho if its better pray for me!...

I've never taken another chem class at UNC and never left a rate my prof review before but take this with a grain of salt. 
Tests aren't hard but he doesn't make clear what's going to be required in exams. He's cool. A lot of people on here complain just because it's hard work and he could be a better teacher but at the end of the day that's life.

He's mean, he makes people feel stupid for not understanding concepts, he doesn't give LOs or practice exam/midterm keys, and half of his lecture slides are unhelpful. He has terrible partial credit on exams, but the exams are fairly accessible, and he'll replace every midterm with the final, which is nice. He's funny at times, but DO NOT take him.
The exams were very tough and the slides don't help review content. Please don't let this class tank your GPA.
Chemistry two forty one

Yeah if you're taking this class because the final replaces all the midterms just quit while you're ahead. The final is the most hopeless thing I have ever taken. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you skip you will genuinely do awful. This guy takes 3 points off every tiny mistake so kiss your grade goodbye.

He does not care to include answer keys to anything. None of his exams have answer keys and the answer keys that are provided give very little. He is snarky and will be "disappointed" that the class didn't do as well as HE would on exams. For midterm 2, he held office hours to discuss dropping out. Run. Do not take this class with him.

Does not have good slides or notes, and just rambles in class making it hard to study for this class. He tends to pull exam questions from material he did not assign or recommend we do in the textbook. Holds Q&A sessions which are helpful, but refuses to give a proper answer for anything. Does't provide the answer key to ANYTHING :(

I feel like my standards for teachers are decently low. I'd love learning objectives, keys to practice exams, slides with words on them. Lucky from me he offers none of these!!! His exams are fine if you figure out the style of questions he asks and happen to remember questions he does in class- if you can't keep up with his rambling, too bad!

This class is the best Chem class I've taken at UNC. He has a sense of humor that's sarcastic which could be why people think he's condescending. Hard class, but has GREAT opportunities to fix bad grades (replace ANY/ALL exams if score higher on final). Exams are heavy, but he prepares you decently. Last thing, you MUST show up to class to do well.

TERRIBLE. the worst professor I've ever had. very snarky/rude. went to office hours to ask a question but was too scared of him to even ask bc of how he was talking to other students. i had to P/F this class because of how harsh he grades the exams. will say that he replaces any of your midterm grades with how you do on that section of the final.

His lectures can be a little all over the place but as long as you go to class you should be fine. His exams were fair to what we went over in class and he offers to replace all 3 midterms with the final.

Genuinely the most insufferable professor I have ever had. So rude and condescending, does nothing to help the success of his students. No learning objectives, no answer key to practice exams or the midterms; grades exams harshly, if you dont use the exact word he's looking for you get points off. Tries to come off as a nice guy, def not

Get ready to learn literally nothing. Analytical is already hard enough as it is, then add a teacher who can't teach to save his life on top of it and you will be crying. His slides make absolutely no sense and he scribbles like a maniac on the chalk board pretending like you understand what he's saying. He makes this class miserable

Professor does not care for students. Exams are graded EXTREMELY HARSH. Attendance not mandatory but if you skip, it is next to impossible to learn the content outside of class. I have an A in orgo and a C in this class. Not worth the time. He's a funny guy but don't let that fool you.

He is tough but wants the class to learn. Gives clear direction on what is important and how to study for exam. You need to work hard and want it. Otherwise he will get you on exams. But it is doable. I preferred his style over Tiani who I dropped earlier in the summer.
Professor Tanner was a great teacher. He was funny and explained the topics pretty well. Chem 101 is hard no matter who you have but he made it manageable.

Professor Wolf was a decent professor. It was his first year teaching so he struggled with pacing and his lectures weren't great but if you know CHEM 101 content already you can still do good in the class. He doesn't do good with broad topics but he is good at explaining detail in chemistry.
Although I received a c- for this class, Prof. Wolf truly is a great professor. He's also hilarious.

Super nice/funny guy, but struggles with the pacing of the course. Doesn't get through the slide decks/wastes time overexplaining simple concepts, leaving him with little time to get to harder problems. Your grade heavily depends on your work outside of class, though, and you can still do well with him as a professor.

I like Professor Wolf, he explained things very good and set the expectations for the class. One thing about the exams is that you really have to think critically for them, not just knowing surface level concepts, but thinking in depth. This course also builds on itself a lot. Overall good teacher, especially for a content heavy class.

Chem 101 is a hard course but Prof. Wolf explained the concepts very well. He was very clear on what will and will not be on the exam. I also really enjoyed going to his office hours, he does care about his students. Overall a very funny and good lecturer. Only class I would enjoy going to at 9am.

Wolf is a young grad student who very much has a passion for what he teaches and does a pretty good job articulating the concepts you need to understand for the punishing exams. Chemistry at UNC is standardized for each professor so the difficulty isn't his fault, and he's been great at providing resources and keeping us engaged in lecture.

can't rlly blame the guy for the wack tests or amount of work, but dr. wolf breaks down the problems pretty well and make sure you understand the topic in gpss. i had him the first year he taught and he had some trouble with pacing and tech so we fell a bit behind, making the test material unfamiliar. still, he's nice and approachable. i recommend!
Nice guy, good lecturer who made class interesting. Exams are awful but that's all chem courses, not just him.

101 success depends more on independent work, but he tries his best to help you succeed. Explains problems in depth, even if it causes him to fall a little behind. His GPSS sessions are more helpful, and he really is a nice guy and funny. Put in the effort outside of class and use lectures as a review and you can do well, regardless of professor.

Prof. Wolf is very chill, but it's very clear he's new to teaching the subject. He can often go off track and many classes we had to sit there while he tried to get the techonology to work (which isn't enitrely his fault, but still.) Chem 101 overall is a hard class, and you'll need to study hard regardless of what instructor you get.

I took his class for his first year of teaching, and I found it overall to be beneficial knowing how hard chemistry is within the departments. Best teacher in my opinion for 101, pacing is slow at times and rambles about certain topics more than others, but I didn't really mind. Really chill and nice guy! 

(Chem is hard regardless of professor.)

He is a pretty good lecturer. I think he does a good job with what the chemistry department provides him. Out of all the chem professors, he's good. Hard to reach via email, but he's good at explaining. Chill guy, very understanding too.
Chem 101 is hard but he takes his time to go over stuff that is hard. Chill professor but he doesn't control the hard exams.

Professor Wolf clearly cares about his students, but struggles with the pacing of Chem101 and very often explains something wrong or gives us incorrect explanations which makes the concepts so confusing. I'm sure he'd be better if we had more time, but the other professors are much more experienced and helpful in teaching content in class time.

Professor Wolf is great at explaining difficult concepts and very kind! He obviously wants us all to succeed and understands very well what it is like to be a student. Your grade and understanding is very much dependent on your work outside of class, but Prof Wolf is extremely helpful and caring. Take chem with him if you can!
He is a great professor! This class is definitely challenging, but his lectures are interesting and he is very passionate about chemistry. He is easy to reach out to with questions and very kind

Your grade in chem 101 is def more reflective of individual effort outside of class, but I always go to his GPSS and he does an amazing job of making the difficult concept accessible. I'd only taken honors chemistry sophomore year, and didn't remember anything going in, but the way he broke everything was very helpful.
He is a great professor and really and explains the content nicely. Very chill guy, just make sure to study

I had recitation with him last semester, and he's the best. CHEM 101 is a tough class, but Tanner really wants every student to succeed, even if chem isn't your forte. Don't be afraid to ask him questions, he excels at finding different ways to describe a concept until everyone understands. If you have the option to take CHEM 101 with him, do it!

Marcey is one of the nicest and most caring professors I've had at UNC. The course content is up to date and very relevant to actual research being done in chemical biology. Exams are tough but graded fairly, and the proposal assignment is an excellent learning experience for aspiring scientists. 10/10 would recommend.
TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Dr. Waters was one of the best and most caring professors I've ever had. We were expected to do the readings, but if we had questions she would very patiently go through them with us. She was also super accessible, offering 2 office hour sessions and an additional problem-solving session weekly.

She holds problem-solving sessions every week and exam reviews right before every exam. If I want to learn a lot, I can definitely do this. Also, she responds to the email about the learning content very fast.
she is helpful for both class content or other things like career planning or even finding the lab
She is enthusiastic, I feel very engaged.

Dr. Waters is a very busy person (google her and you'll see why), but she did her best to set us up for success in this class. The midterms and final were all free response, but totally doable if you studied the class slides. There is a 15 minute presentation at the end of the semester on a modern organic chemistry topic of your choice.

Incredibly kind professor. If you go to her OH she is so helpful. Even if u didn't do wonderful in Orgo 1/2 you can do well in this class like me. Lenient grader on the presentations. Offers one opp for EC. Missed a couple classes for trips but if you pay attention to her slides you can ace the exams!! Don't listen to the bad review!!!

Best way to put it is disorganized. Lecture style was more conceptual than hands-on. Very hard to reach via email, which made the research project unnecessarily difficult. Putting in grades was a big issue. It sucks to graduate without knowing if you ACTUALLY graduated. This has been one of the most frustrating experiences of my college career.

She is a great professor! Her lectures are very helpful despite the content's difficulty. I would highly suggest reading the textbook before coming to class when doing the prework. The tests are difficult but I would suggest redoing the slides and doing the textbook problems along the way.She gives very useful practice exams(similar format w exams)
Loved this class! Don't be scared of it if you didn't ace Orgo 1 and 2, Prof. Waters has tons of resources and her office hours are very helpful.
Dr. Waters is awesome!! Take advantage of her office hours and try to participate. Shes a great lecturer and is also super nice/approachable.

Professor Kanai is a very passionate lecturer. His main goal is for us to develop a strong grasp on the course material (which is quite elegant) without worrying too much about grades. While his lectures are math heavy, the math always has a very satisfying payoff.
Great professor and very understanding of the difficulty of the content. He assigned a couple of problem sets as well as a take-home final exam, which were all graded fairly easily.

He's not a bad professor but he definitely could have been better. Beware that the practice tests are way easier than actual test. Try to keep up from the start. Try to be involved in lecture as it's easy to just glaze over the lectures. He's new so it's okay but yea could have been better.

Truly a decent professor considering it's chemistry but the practice tests were nothinggggg like the actual exams and the workshops were useless. I am required to get a B for my major in this course, ended with a 79, and he decided to not only not round up but literally ghost my emails. hope he's more communicative towards his incoming students

Had him for CHEM 1251, & he is one of the best professors I've had here at UNCC. He is a passionate & funny individual who makes learning something enjoyable. He is dedicated to helping students as he helped us individually with any questions that we had. This class requires a ton of practice but having it with Chase Slowey makes it less stressful.
im in chem 102 now and i miss slowey like a lung. one of the funniest and most engaging instructors in the chem department. you couldn't have a better 101 teacher.

Worst department known to man, yet a gift of a teacher. The department needs an entire faculty reset, but with the sole exception of Chase Slowey. So very energetic and fun, I will never forget the pneumonics and stunts pulled. Genuinely chem is miserable but if you don't get Slowey just wait for the next semester would be my advice.

Chem 101 is a relatively difficult class no matter your professor, but Professor Slowey made going to class so much more enjoyable. If you turned a theater kid into a professor, you'd have Slowey. He often simplified complex topics and related them to real-world scenarios, which still helps me in 102. Do practice problems and you'll be fine.
Chemistry is always extremely difficult, but Slowey made the lectures entertaining! Make sure to do all the exam type problems on the lecture slides to prepare for exams.

I had Professor Slowey for CHEM 101 and I'm so lucky I was in his class. The chemistry department at UNC is really difficult, but his lectures were always entertaining and memorable. If you're taking CHEM 101 here, definitely try to get him!

Chem101 is a tough course. TAKE IT WITH SLOWEY! The man is maybe the most passionate lecturer at UNC. He is ridiculously energetic, a great explainer, and loves to use himself as a model to demonstrate chemistry principles, like running around the hall pretending to be an electron. In such a poorly run department, Chase Slowey is a beacon of hope.

Professor Slowey was awesome! He is really enthusiastic (even for an 8am class) and I never found myself zoning out or bored in his class. The actual test grades were pretty similar to practice test grades so I would just say to read the textbook and do the practice tests. I hope he would teach higher leveled chem courses in the future.

Absolutely AWESOME! Chase explained everything crystal clear with a few sentences and is very accessible outside of class in GPSS and 6-minute meetings. He is such a delight for lectures every morning and hilarious with body demonstrations! UNC needs to HIRE HIM!
Chemistry really sucks but Slowey makes it a bit more enjoyable and funny.
Chase is super fun and very energetic! He's probably one of the best Chem professors at UNC right now. Still, his class can be difficult. Definitely make sure to study a lot on your own time.

This guy has a lot of energy for the class being so early in the morning. He's a good lecturer and makes a lot of silly analogies to help you understand the content. I will say, despite being engaging, he is not the best explainer, but perhaps that is just me

Professor Slowey loves chemistry and is super passionate and energetic about it that it makes you excited about it too, he makes it fun to learn chem. He explains topics and concepts well and he gives a bunch of analogies to help you understand the concept better

I had Chase for when he was a professor as well as when he was TA'ing BOTH my summer classes. (My first time around was not his fault) HIS EXCITEMENT IS INFECTIOUS. You can very easily tell his love for chemistry and his earnestness to share his knowledge with his students. If he teaches another class, he will not disappoint. Favorite TA ever.
Professor Slowey is a good teacher and very good at explaining things. He was a good TA, too. I would definitely take it again.

CHEM 101 is one of the hardest classes at UNC Chapel Hill, and the grading is harsh for every professor. But in terms of lectures, Professor Slowey is the best. His excitement is infectious, and he makes all of these high level concepts much more accessible. Also he is just such a cool guy, his 6 minute meetings are always great.

Prof Slowey made me excited to go to class every day. He explains all the concepts SO well, while adding personal anecdotes to help you remember certain topics. Definitely one of the best (if not THE best) 101 professor. I'm not sure if he will teach again since he is a graduate student, but definitely try and take Chem with him if he does.
Awesome man. Hard class.

I really liked Dr. Garland! Her lectures move veryyy fast and she seems a bit stressed sometimes, but she's passionate about teaching and is very good at explaining concepts. I think BIOL 103 is just a hard course so you have to put a good amount of time into it to do well, but she is a great professor for the course.

She is a good teacher, but her tests are more of a reading comprehension test than actually understanding the material. If there is another professor, I would take it with them, but she's not the worst option. If you take this class with her, know that your effort most likely won't correlate with your results.

Dr. Garland is clearly knowledgeable about biology, but is the most unorganized professor I've taken a class with. Her exams are majority select all that apply with no partial credit and she is difficult to reach outside of class.

Dr. Garland is very approachable and makes it easy to ask questions. She genuinely cares about her students as people, not just grades, and takes time to explain concepts clearly. Her exams are challenging, but they push you to really learn the material. Overall, a great professor who wants her students to succeed.

Dr. Garland is very kind and accommodating, especially when I had to be out of town. Lectures move quickly and cover a lot of material, so I rewatched lectures at home. Exams have many multiple select with no partial credit. Class is interesting, but be ready to look over bio 103 if you took it over a semester ago. Reviewing everyday helps.

I took this class first semester freshman year and didn't do as well as I wanted to. However, Dr. Garland is a very intelligent professor and I thoroughly enjoyed her class. Her midterms are designed to trip you up, but if you memorize the learning objectives (aka the study guides) you WILL do well in this class. Be prepared for busy work though.

I took this course as a freshman. I was a bit nervous bc the last bio class I had taken was 10th grade (AP Bio). Honestly a chill class and a good transition to unc! She's caring and always willing to explain a concept in office hours. Last 2 units are a bit rushed, but lock in (esp on first 2 units), and an A is very manageable.

No basic knowledge will be covered in class. Preparation before class is extremely important. The professor's lecture sequence is different from that of the textbook. There is too much content, and the exam content is very diverse and detailed. Lesson quiz, unit quiz, three midterms, and final are worth a lot.

Her lectures can be a bit boring at times, but there are definitely days with a lot of peer interaction that are more engaging. The homework can be relatively long at times, but her quizzes aren't too bad. Her midterms can be a bit more difficult as well due to being very heavy with "select all that apply" questions that offer no partial credit.

Definitely spent a LOT of time studying for this class, but she does try her best to make it fair. Go to SI sessions and study the lesson quizzes/practice exams. Often gives points back on exams for multiple questions if questions were vague. Had a 92.85 but she was kind enough to round everyone with a >.5 up:). Consistent review>cramming is a must

Despite her bad reputation I thought she was a good lecturer, but exams were definitely hard due to them being majority select all that apply and no partial credit. The material itself isn't super difficult if you study hard, but the exam structure made it difficult to score high (tests were worth 72% of your grade). Be prepared to put in effort!

A true sweetheart, seriously SO compassionate & roots for everyone. Tests are hard, with half select all that apply and tricky wording but not impossible when you learn her patterns. Rework quiz questions and ignore GRQs. DEF go to office hours - she shares really cool info that deepened my appreciation for bio. Garland is a QUEEN!
Great teacher, great class. Lectures are a small percentage of your grade but you can without a doubt still get an A without going to lecture.

Homework is boring and the tests are an exercise in reading comprehension rather than subject mastery and occasionally include trivia questions. Lectures are designed to not really provide much content, but slides are helpful for exams. I didn't make an A on any test the whole semester. Definitely harder than Ott.

BEST BIOLOGY PROFESSOR. Anyone complaining about her just didn't put in the work. Honestly, such a sweet human, such a great class. Garland did everything in this class to help us succeed. Nearly every midterm was curved, she let students debate her on questions on exams and that occasionally raised our grades, and she drops your lowest midterm.
She does not teach at all! She expects you to learn everything before class and barely goes over power points. Please do not take care. She is not a good professor. Wish I took Ott.

I had Garland as the main instructor for Bio117. The class format was great and very engaging as we had a variety of healthcare professionals as speakers. I learned a lot from this course and was glad I took it. Attendance and participation are mandatory, but you are allowed to miss up to 2 assignments and 1 class.

I hated the class in the beginning of the semester and it's definitely killing my gpa but the material is interesting and I feel like I've learned a lot this semester. I wouldn't expect an A unless you're a god at bio but I wouldn't avoid it
always screaming at kids for having their laptops open in class, which I KIND of understood because this class is a pass/fail and only attendance based, but she was kind of strict it was weird.

Dr. Garland is nice, a good teacher, and knows her stuff. The course content is not objectively difficult but the way the tests are written (select all that apply, trick questions, subtle nuances) makes the class quite hard and time-consuming. BUT, all in all, if you put the work in, you WILL come out a much stronger bio student. Worth it IMO.
Really fun class with interesting material, but a lot of work and reading. Lots of group work and the lectures are engaging, but the tests are tricky so be prepared to study!

Dr. Garland overall was a solid professor for BIOL 103. The class itself is a lot of memorization and not as much application. Her lectures are somewhat engaging, but sometimes she didn't explain concepts too clearly. Her exams are definitely a little tricky, with many select all that apply questions and little partial credit.

Midterms are so incredibly difficult because of wording and she always try to trick you. On every question. Also does a lot of "select all that apply" with no partial credit. Lowest midterm exam is dropped though! She is a very nice person, super easy to access, and always willing to work with students to help them succeed in the class.

Participation and Homework matter a lot, make sure you re read your answers after you submit. But overall good if you are going into healthcare and want to explore different fields. All you need to do is pay attention in the once a week lecture.

This class is definitely challenging but it is very worth it. Her questions are worded weirdly sometimes but after a while you learn the style of her teaching. Succeeding in her class does require dedication so definitely make sure you have time to really look over material. She is very nice and funny if you go to her office hours!

Would not recommend for freshman. I took this course in my freshman year and went through a massive learning curve. I feel the way she words her tests are tricky, otherwise this is a straightforward class, 100% doable.
Just no. If you want to pass this class, do not take it with her. She is text heavy with many select all that apply questions with no partial credit.
Don't take it with her if you want to protect your sanity.

Avoid for any biology classes if possible. Lectures are 90% talking to neighbors and the rest is spent desperately trying to keep up with her as she flies through slides. Exam questions are meant to trick you and majority are select all (no partial credit). Content wasn't difficult but it felt like we were teaching ourselves. Wouldn't take again.

Dr. Garland's canvas page was so unorganized, and it was hard to find class materials. Her exams were so difficult, and all the questions were select all with no partial credit. She doesn't seem to care about her students, breezes over content, often cancels office hours, and doesn't explain problems in class. It was impossible to take notes. Avoid

She's not a bad professor/person. She knows her stuff. BUT you gotta work your butt off. I procrastinated and always studied until the last minute, and it turned out ok, but if I could redo it, I would study much harder. Content itself isn't hard, but she tries to trick you on the tests. Hate the select all. Grade not revealed until very end.
I didn't like the format of her exams; select all that apply with no partial credit for most of the questions.

Tests are written to trick you and many questions are select all that apply with no partial credit. Her lectures are terrible; she does not explain things clearly or even at all and pads lecture time by making us talk to our neighbors an excessive amount. She grades slowly and has a poorly organized canvas page. She seems very lazy and doesn't care

BIOL 103 is hard because the tests try to trick you but if you really focus during the exams, I do think you can figure out what she is asking you. The content isn't terribly difficult. Definitely learned something, just always felt super unsettled before exams lol.

thought i would get a C in the class don't know how I managed to scrape by. the exams are HELL, so many choose all that apply with ZERO partial credit. She's nice but purposefully tries to trick you up. Not to mention all the prework we have to do and she asks questions BEFORE teaching us

I had Dr. Garland and Dr. Ott. Garland is much more respectful than Ott and goes over more of the content from GRQs in lecture, but her teaching style isn't great for an introductory course. She does a lot of hand-waving and only reads from the slides. Exams can be crazy difficult and Garland doesn't give enough application-based practice.

This class gave me anxiety simply because I did not know what she wanted. At all. Lectures were so quick, she barely taught, exams were all trick questions with no partial credit, and she does not drop or replace. Just avoid if you can.

Avoid if possible -- if you go into the exam having reviewed the HWs (not related to lecture) and lectures and with the mindset she's trying to trick you, you might do ok. Quizzes open for an absurdly short time with no late policy -- tanked my grade. Lectures are pretty disorganized and unrelated. She is a very sweet woman though

what the actual **** was that class, shes not a bad person dont get me wrong but she is the worst professor you can ever take. she talks too fast, she's too smart, and not in a good way, she doesn't know how to teach an introductory course, the way she words her exams is more like a comprehension test than a bio test and overall it was very unfair

Bio 240 is pretty rough with either professor and as any general bio class here the exams are tricky even if you know the content. Study smartworks more than you think, exam questions related more to those than they did to lecture I felt. Pretty decent lectures and class is pretty interesting.
Was in the Co-Taught section. The amount of select all that apply no partial credit questions on the final was ridiculous. She's not very enthusiastic during lecture.

I was in the co-taught section with Dr. Garland and Dr. Ott. They are both great professors, but definitely have different styles, especially for tests. Dr. Ott's are more application while Dr. Garland's are more memorization. Dr. Garland was very kind and helpful in office hours. The tests are difficult, so be prepared to study.

I ended with an A, but I quite literally had to kill myself for it. This class is HARD, and it feels unfair. Admittedly, I have learned more in this class than I have in any other biology course. You truly have to work yourself to death to get a good grade though.

I took the co-taught section of 103. While Ott was teaching (the first two units) I made high Bs on both exams. While Garland was teaching (the last two units) I made low Cs. The majority of her test questions were "select all that apply" with no partial credit. Seems like a fine person but her exams are WAY too hard for an introductory bio class.

Not a great lecturer. I took this class with Ott & Garland, so the structure got super messy. Dr. Garland was always behind in lectures, and didn't explain topics well. The tests are more of reading comprehension than actual biology content. They dropped the lowest midterm and gave EC on the final, which I appreciate, but the tests aren't fair.

never studied more for a class and gotten this little payoff. lectures useless but rewatching was a must bc she blew through content. never ever knew what to study bc the learning objectives were only tip of the iceberg compared to what's on the exams. INSANE amount of "select all that apply" type questions. process of elimination won't help you gl
This was by far the worst professor I've had at UNC. Please avoid I say it for your own good.
Every day I go to class and every day I left confused and feeling defeated. Take Ott. Do yourself the favor.

Genuinely made this class so much harder than need be. The most unenthusiastic lecturer ever, you would think she despises her job. Doesn't reply to emails requesting personal meetings, exams are all made to trick you and ridiculously hard. It gets to a point where there is no point in studying. Drop it if you can, P/F if you must. Worst bio prof

She seems like a good enough person, and was pretty caring to her students, which is why the difficulty of her exams confuses me. The majority of the exam questions were multiple-select with misleading phrasing and no partial credit, almost like she wanted you to get it wrong. Overall decent professor, but I'm not a bio major anymore.

alaina obliterated my gpa. studied for the class, did all the work, went to reviews/ta sessions, but the exams made a fool of me. knowing the content cannot save u from the hate she channels into each exam question. they're literally designed to trick you. hahahaha, u really got me with the tricky wording alaina! thanks for making me feel dumb!

dr. garland seems like a nice person but she sucks at lecturing. she moves way too fast. I literally gave up at coming to lecture halfway through the semester because I knew I would have to rewatch the lecture recordings anyways. I had to teach myself and I would recommend taking this class with dr ott because you will actually learn something.

Get ready to study all the materials by yourself because the lecture are useless. The majority of class she makes us talk to our neighbors and waste time instead of explaining it herself. Tests are ridiculous and half the questions are multi-select and no partial credit. She doesn't replace or drop any exams either. Would recommend with a diff prof

Doesn't provide practice exams or hardly any study materials for exams, reads directly off slides in lecture, uses niche Smartworks questions on exams but changes one word to "trick you", stops answering questions on Piazza the day before the exam, etc. Constantly asks you to turn and talk to your neighbors just to rush through an "explanation"
Genuinely ruined STEM for me. Should have been a better experience with the way the class is designed.

All of the bio classes here are super tough, but she does an okay job. The format of tests is really weird though, it's a lot of multi-select with no partial credit given and you have to read a full paragraph for the question. Super hard tests, and lots of lecturing.

Dr. Garland was personally very kind and I enjoyed talking to her and going to her office hours. I disliked how incredibly difficult and tricky the exams were. Every question was a trick question, and multi-select with no partial credit. The content was also so ambiguous and the class outlines were SO disorganized it stressed me out.

dr garland has misery in her heart. this class was miserable. tests were unnecessarily hard and had no may multiselect with no partial credit. she was always behind on lectures and the slides were very lackluster.

I studied for WEEKS and WEEKS on end and still didn't do well on her exams. She will deliberately add "multiple choices may be correct" and then have only one answer be correct - just to trick you. She does not lecture properly, is inconsistent, and does not have the best interest of the students at heart when making exams. AVOID PLEASE!!!

Please avoid her. Exams are heavily applicational, but no cheatsheet is given. You are expected to know EVERYTHING inside out. If you are not 100% sharp on any content, you will not be able to answer them correctly. It also doesn't help that questions are often multi-select (without partial credit) and worded vaguely. Please avoid her, please do.

She didn't even taught in class---No passion, bad explaining concepts, etc, so self-learning required as always. But her EXAMS are RIDICULOUS. Keen advocate for multiple select while most of her answers are questionable / arguable & worded weirdly. It's a pure battle in finding who is best at reading her mysterious mind. AVOID!!! Take Kevin Slep's.

changed exams from Gradescope w/ cheat sheet to closed-book,pencil-and-paper tests & doesn't drop the lowest midterms; since she didn't have a question bank, many exam questions were taken directly from Smartwork homework; also doesn't post quizzes on Canvas because of technical issues which doesn't make sense because it works for another class

If I could give her zero stars I would. I honestly think that is class would not have been bad at all if anyone else was the instructor. She has no passion and her exams are always messed up somehow. Also, she grades LC based on CORRECTNESS, so keep that in mind. If you can take this class with literally anyone else, DO IT!!!

The content was manageable but Dr. Garland takes the "flipped classroom" too seriously. She asks questions in class before even teaching the material as if we're supposed to master everything before class. She also loves to trick you on exams by changing one word from the practice she gives.

Does not post slides unless asked, does not make practice for exams, no study guides, exams have select all questions with no partial credit, does not drop an exam, sometimes stops responding on Piazza, goes insanely fast and expects us to take notes in milliseconds, makes us "talk to our neighbor" for majority of class. AVOID.

Good person, but not a good professor. Does not update grades on Canvas so no sense of where you stand in the class. The exams are like SAT style, meant to trick you rather than test knowledge. Also, the midterms have select all that apply MCQs, which do not have partial credit. No cheat sheets allowed, and Garland no longer drops an exam. AVOID!!!

Dr. Garland is one of the most straightforward and direct professors. She speaks very succinctly, makes her expectations clear, and provides ample resources to succeed. Her tests are challenging and she loves to ask trick questions, but she never asked anything outside of lecture content. Spend the effort and you'll do well.
Be prepared to commit a tremendous amount of time if you need to take this class

Just took first midterm, was not particularly hard but many questions (40%) were select all no partial credit, which may end up wrecking a lot of grades. Oops tokens in the class, homework (GRQ + questions) can take a very long time especially if you actually read. Lectures are important, have a lot of exam level questions or straight up exam qs.

Dr. Garland is so sweet and caring for her students! The course however was very difficult in my opinion since the majority of your grade is based on exams that are extremely tricky and typically select all that apply with no partial credit. I studied for hours on end and knew the concepts but would often be thrown off by the wording of questions.

Dr. Garland was a caring professor, but not the best lecturer. We learned material for the purpose of answering test questions, not understanding biology. Content was scattered and the GRQs were not  helpful. However, Dr. Garland is very accessible outside of class, so make sure to ask questions! To study for the final, rework practice/past exams!

Garland glosses over concepts at times, but she explains things very clearly and is willing to help when you ask her questions. I went through course outlines at least 2 times for each lecture to truly retain the information. She only tests on lecture slides. Take your time and read every word on exams! Ask questions in class to peer instructors.

Because of my background in bio, I did not find the content of the class to be overly difficult. However, her tests are unnecessarily confusing. She writes them with the intent to trick you and when asking for clarification during the test she gives none. She's very condescending and it genuinely felt like she didn't want students to do well.

Solid teacher but devious tests. The content itself is light work but every question was 3 paragraphs and purpose-built to trip you up. I felt like I knew the material well but only just pulled out an A by the skin of my teeth. Mandatory attendance at 8 AM was not fun either. Group seating was good though.

I retook this class as a transfer and despite already having credit for the material I found this class incredibly difficult. If you rewatch her lectures and understand her slides before you attempt quizzes you're usually fine. Her tests can be tricky but if you actively review her practice tests you can do well.

Good lecturer. Tests are very similar to practice + unit quizzes -- variations of same questions. Big grade buffer (drops 1 exam). Accessible in office hours + piazza. PM's + SI's pretty good. GRQs pretty useless -- don't waste your time on those or reading textbook. Lectures a bit unorganized at times. Preps you well for later stem classes at unc.

Exams were tricky and often composed of questions meant to confuse you rather than test your knowledge or application of knowledge. Spent the whole semester discussing how cheat sheets were not useful, but then let us have a cheat sheet on the final??

The quality of the lectures was not good, much of the time is spent waiting for learning catalytics questions, lecture material is intended to be used for a "comprehension" of the material, but tests are based on application for case studies. Most egregious thing is the GRQs that have nothing of use, and the exams frequently had errors.

If you can avoid Dr. Garland PLEASE DO. I have never felt so discouraged, belittled, and not prepared no matter how much i understood or studied. Her lectures aren't good, theyre very unorganized and all over the place. She doesnt explain and expects you to know, then proceeds to give the most diabolical tricky awful exams. Just dont take her.

I hated this class lowkey. Not very hard content but it is presented in hard ways. Lots of homework but most of it feels really mindless which does not help in the long run. The slides are incoherent and usually out of order so its hard to go back and look at them later to study. A vast majority of the diagrams shown are burry and unreadable.
She was super cool. Took the class at 8am so my attendance was awful but she was a very good professor. Class is hard I'd say

Homework matters for this class, it's pretty much just a sampler through guest lectures. She's very strict about not having phones and laptops out during class. I'd recommend this class to pre health people even though it is at a weird hour.

Healthcare professionals came into speak with us and prof. Garland had participation grades, writing reflections, and pre class assignments. This was an easy-A that allowed us to learn from different healthcare professionals.

3 guest speakers from varying healthcare fields + pre-hw + post-hw every week = great exposure to diverse minds. Can be tiring at the end of the day (5:45-7:15 pm) when your mind is on other things, but attendance determines if you pass. Can't use devices/do hw (out of respect for speakers!). Def recommend for those w/ genuine healthcare interest.

I took AP Bio (BIOL 101+L) recently as a HS senior, which helped. No more cheat sheet, but exams are reasonable--based on lectures/slides, quizzes, and practice exams. Lots of grades dropped, including lowest midterm of 3; seek help from tutors, TAs, and office hours. Group seating makes the class fun. Dr. Garland knows what she's doing!

***BIOL 117 IS IN PERSON NOW***

It's really what you want to get out of this class. Great for people who don't know what they want in healthcare, but dangerously easy to fall asleep in this class. Attendance is HEAVILY monitored in this class.

On one of the first days of class, she said 'this is a weed out class'. Pretty much sums up Dr. Garland's point of view - she only cares about making the class hard enough that people don't pursue upper level biology. One of the least caring biology professors I have had here. I don't know how she keeps winning teaching awards.

Dr. Garland is one of the nicest and most knowledgeable bio profs I've had at UNC. Exams are difficult, but quizzes and HW are representative of test questions. Attention-to-detail and close reading are vital. However, an A or B is very doable given the buffer points and the lowest exam being dropped. Stay on top of deadlines and rewatch lectures!
Pretty easy, just utilize the TA's

Tough course with exams that test more on reading comprehension than content knowledge. Lectures move quickly, so rewatching them is a must. Cheat sheets didn't help much. unstuckstudy ai was a lifesaver for practice questions to prep. Overall, a challenging class that requires consistent effort.

Her content was pretty simple, especially if you took 103 at UNC, but the tests weren't really based on the content, more like application.  You get to drop your lowest midterm grade and have cheat sheets for tests.  Don't be afraid of her - a lot of her test questions are ripped directly from quizzes and homework problems.

Wasn't a super hard class. Annoying for sure. Long GRQs and mastering. Dr. Garland is really really nice. Her exams are pretty hard but DO the practice exams. Learned my lesson after the first one. Also, she rounds. Overall, not as bad as people say. Just stay on top of things.

Heard bad reviews but took anyways. Test are not knowledge based and weren't knowledge based. Cheat sheets did not help at all. Nothing was thoroughly explained. A lot of critical thinking blooms questions that she never explained or taught how to approach. Avoid at all cost.

Dr. Garland is nice and good at explaining things, but her exams are extremely difficult. I was putting previous exam question variations on my cheat sheet instead of the actual content. The whole class is based on lectures, not GRQS. I knew the reviews were bad, but I still took her out of necessity. It's NOT worth it.

The content of this course was all over the place. The exams and quizzes are reading tests and do not test your knowledge. She flies through the lectures so you have to rewatch them after class because she likes to test on what she says rather than what is on the slides. We were constantly a lecture behind and rushing to catchup. AVOID her please!!

AVOID! I had only heard bad things about her before I took this class but had to sign up as it was the only section offered. She is a nice enough person but a HORRIBLE professor. This was definitely the most challenging class I have taken at UNC so far and I took a 400 level CHEM course with 240 this semester that was exponentially easier.

She's not as bad as some might say. Many of the questions on tests are reused from previous tests and practice exams. She posts the lectures but attendance is part of your grade. Overall, she's a great professor.

Professor Garland's exams are difficult, but she'll often reuse or rework questions we have already done on the tests, so practicing these is really helpful. You definitely have to put in the work, but she gives a lot of resources to help you
Exams felt like the SAT reading section. Very poorly written questions that are unnecessarily wordy. Avoid at all costs.

I have taken her for the past 3 years out of necessity and every time I think it'll get better, it doesn't. The content itself is learnable, but her exams are not. They're tested on reading comprehension rather than your actual knowledge of the content. The amount of review I had to do for this course was appalling. Please avoid at all costs.

I was excited for this class and Dr. Ott made it a nightmare. It feels like she expects you to do poorly which really grated on me all semester. GRQs are beyond arduous, and she did a poor job explaining the content. Take someone else.

Dr. Otto lectures in a very organized and it's possible to follow her train of thought. However, she can sometimes come across as a bit condescending. Her exams are very wordy and difficult. Reviewing the lecture slides is probably the best study method. Make sure you actually memorize and understand the material.
While initially confusing, class set up was helpful and she dropped an extremely generous amount of assignments while also giving extra credit. Best 103 option.

If the devil and Dr. Ott fought, she would mop the floor with him. I took the class with her a few years ago when she had personal issues going on. In most cases, I can sympathize, but she took her stress out on us with hard exams and a worse attitude. I would recommend taking this class with absolutely anyone else.

Dr. Ott is super smart and great at her job but can be a bit condescending. Going through the lecture slides is by far the best way to study. GRQs were long and not always helpful, but it was nice to be told exactly what sections of the text to focus on. Lots of drops for lowest quizzes etc. and lowest midterm is dropped too.

Attendance is weird as the points are partially based on accuracy, but overall it's not bad. You might not love going to class, but if you do, you should do pretty well.

dr. ott's class was challenging, but her lectures were engaging and the workload was manageable. GRQs were long and sometimes unrelated to what we were learning. she drops quite a few grades at the end, including the lowest midterm, but exams are still weighted very heavily. even if content on the exam was easy, her wording made it a bit confusing.

Didn't love her at first, but as the semester went on she really grew on me. May seem a bit intense but you can tell she really cares about her students and I felt like exams were about as fair as they could be. She will try to trick you pretty frequently, but I felt like the lecture style did a great job of preparing me for the exams.

This class is hard, but doable if you pay attention and use the resources.  Exams came from lecture and there were no surprises.  Drops your lowest midterm and allows a cheat sheet on the final exam.  Ott is direct with students, but I found her to be kind.
I found her pretty passive aggressive and sassy. 103 is quite challenging for an introductory-level bio class. Her office hours were very helpful, though.

Dr. Ott is not a bad professor, and this class is NOT easy. She is very caring and easy to reach outside of class, but can be very passive-aggressive. Exams sometimes feel like they're completely unrelated to class content, and GRQs are often unnecessarily lengthy with little connection to class content. Review lecture slides to do best on exams.

Her class was somewhat overwhelming, but Ott does a good job of making it manageable. I think she was really nice and was engaging throughout the class. Her exams are quite challenging, but everything has been covered in class, so review the class slides and quizzes, and you should be fine.

Dr. Ott is very kind and approachable. Lectures were engaging, but exams were full of trick questions that did not always feel like she was testing your knowledge of a concept. Heavy emphasis on molecular techniques. GRQs took forever and were honestly useless.

Would recommend taking with Dr. Ott! Her lectures are pretty engaging and straightforward. Everything that is on the test is covered in her slides. She is also pretty accessible outside of class for extra help. Tests are pretty heavily weighted but they aren't too bad in terms of difficulty and she also drops a midterm. GRQ's are time consuming.

Dr. Ott has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. In my opinion, she is a clear lecturer (mostly) and has a lenient grading policy, as she drops the lowest midterm and several other homework assignments. Dr. Ott is also very accesible outside of class, offering both group and individual office hours. I would take another class with her!

Ott, in my opinion, isn't the best lecturer. It could be my learning style, but all the material appears very vague and disorganized. The homework and assignments are completely unrelated to class content, and I've had to teach myself the entire course. That being said, the course is fairly easy, except for the reading comprehension exams.

Biol 103 is a deceptively hard class. It's interesting, however there's a lot of busy work (useless/unhelp GRQs imo, more useful Pearson assignments. I learned everything needed in lecture. That + quizzes & practice tests helped me do well. Tests are difficult though: questions are hard to understand and correct answers feel ambiguous.

Her exams are weighted very, and i mean VERY heavily. However, your lowest midterm is dropped. I would watch out for how she phrases the questions on the exam. I also would strongly advise to drop everything (like don't even take notes when you're doing the GRQs) and to just pay the most attention to the slides.

Don't skip 101, especially if you are a freshman. She's amazing at teaching, but exams are super tricky and there is a TON of work to do outside of class. The exams are weighted very heavily (48% midterm, 24% final). There are many resources outside of class, so it isn't impossible to do well. If you have to take this class, take it with Dr. Ott.

I thought this course was very doable. I did the homework and made Anki decks from the slides she provided in class. Overall, very great and entertaining lectures, would highly recommend! Just study and definitely do the practice exams, she bases a lot of her questions similar to them, especially the final.

She is direct and doesn't take crap from students, but I think she's effective and generally understanding if you seriously have things going on.  Exams are hard, but all her questions come from class.  She also drops the lowest exam and is allowing us a cheat sheet on the final exam.

This class is unnecessarily difficult. I swear to god the amount of times I have been screwed over by the wording of her questions is unreal. I am sorry, but this class is absolutely not it. Avoid if you can.
