Dr. Lopez is a very caring professor. However, he will NOT curve very much. Your final can replace it all, but the average final grade was around a D. If you pay attention in lectures, show up to office hours, you will do fine. If you just coast through the lectures and look up homework solutions you will struggle; the tests are very unforgiving.
The best physics teacher I've ever had.

Dr. Erickcek is knowledgeable and does a good job covering the material. The material is difficult though, and your grade comes down to how well you do on the midterms so study accordingly! Still, they are fairly graded and often were curved slightly (including the final) if she saw the majority of the class struggled on certain sections.
She is really nice, gave good feedback on all assignments, but the material is vast and she doesn't give exam practice problems. So it is difficult to study for those exams.

Dr. Erickcek is amazing, this class made me switch my major to astrophysics! Fantastic class, lectures, and professor. The homework can be difficult but is totally manageable if you start on time. Having python experience can be helpful.

She is an exceptional teacher, her lectures are so thorough and well-planned. She is so helpful if you make it obvious that you're trying to understand. The content of the classes are super challenging. she doesn't downplay the difficulty. She delivers excellence in her teaching and expects excellence from her students. It's intense, but worth it

Dr. Khveshenko is one of the worst professors ever. His lectures were useless and completely unrelated to exams. Anything he wrote on the board was impossible to decipher, and his accent is difficult to understand. He cannot answer any questions, and talked to us as if we are PhD students in physics. Please avoid for your sanity.
DON'T take physics with Dmitri he's hard to understand and doesn't show his work. He just clicks through the slides. Bad lecturer.
just a bad lecturer, will just read off of slides and click through how problems are worked out. 50% of the time when students ask a question he answers a completely different question

I wish I could give him zero stars. I have never encountered such an AWFUL professor. It is obvious he does not read the slides before class, nor does he care about teaching the material. No work is ever shown and explanations are always unclear. Take this course with a different professor, or at a different institution. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!

I wish I could rate him zero stars. I have never encountered such an AWFUL professor. It is very clear that he does not read the slides before he comes to class, nor does he care about teaching it. He shows no work when solving examples and provides unclear explanations. Take this class with another professor or take it at a different institution.

I have never disliked a teacher enough that I have been compelled to leave a review until now. Do not take a class with this man AT ALL COSTS. He does not read the slides before the lectures, so he encounters them for the first time along with the students. Genuinely the most confusing and hard to listen to lecturer I have ever encountered.
i wish i could rate him a 0 but it is not an option. Avoid at all costs

Lectures were easy to follow and went by the textbook layout identically. Hints at certain problems that might be on exams. The course was fair, and homework + lecture + reading was enough to prepare you for exams.

He's a little bit of a dry lecturer, but course is pretty clear cut. Especially after being traumatized by E&M I, this class felt very fair. Exams were hard, but nothing unexpected. He graded very generously, and homework assignments weren't too bad either.
Doctor Wu is super enthusiastic about physics. He is really caring and understanding. The only thing is his expression sometimes is not clear enough. Overall, he is good.

The TA teaches, grades and creates homework for the lab section. Professor simply gives the recitation lecture. In those lectures he is a slow speaker, does not get through all the material in a timely manner. He is also a poor communicator outside of the classroom. He once forgot to tell us about an assignment and then tried to blame us.

Lecture plus supplemeting with textbook make the material clear and manageable. Fun lecturer and engages with students. Grades exams rather strictly, (i.e., you want textbook work) but is very lenient when it comes to getting points back. Akaa wants you to succeed, and he was very forgiving with final rounding. Put in the work and you will do well!

Great professor. The midterm exams were both a bit disorganized, but he was honest and fair when grading them. Doesn't take attendance traditionally, but gives pop quizzes throughout the semester as a substitute. Overall very understanding and a funny guy in lecture.

Professor Akaa is a caring instructor and wants us to do well. He goes through lectures very diligently and they are easy to follow. Pop quizzes are nice to help provide extra practice problems outside of hw and midterm reviews.

He's a very decent professor. He's a funny guy and clearly knows what he is talking about, and he expects that from you as well. If you put in the work, you'll do just fine. Only reason I didn't get an A is because I was lazy.
Made mistakes on each of the exams. Strict grading scale. Provided a lack of practice for final due to poor lecture/hw planning.

Changes exam grading criteria during the exam, grades were always over a month late, consistent mistakes in derivations, didn't appear to truly understand material. Slides copy and paste from textbook. Homework supposed to be consistent over semester, ended at spring break. Disorganized, better off skipping to study and do practice problems.

I took 281L with Dr. Ayangeakaa, and again I found that he was a caring professor that only wanted the class to learn and succeed. Homework sets are a little disorganized and can be long, but the lectures are well-structured and clear, and include examples to work as a class or in small groups. Tests are fair and he prepares you well with examples.

Akaa is amazing. Great lecturer and you can tell he really cares about you and will do anything he can for everyone to succeed. He does not want anyone to fail his class and he really shows it. He's able to take difficult material and break it down for students to understand.

Lectures were good and enjoyable but hard to follow for me because he almost seemed too smart for his own good. Make sure to learn python before you take the class. Beginning of the class was difficult because this was my first time programming.

10/10 class, and 10/10 professor. It was certainly not an easy A, but most definitely not unachievable either. Quizzes, final exam, and final project were all very fair and was the perfect amount of challenging. Highly recommend.
Best class - the TAs and prof really cared. So much fun

I loved professor law and his TAs they are all very kind and helpful, but if you are not good at astrophysics do NOT take this class. The description is very misleading as we didn't start actually talking about aliens until halfway through the semester and there was a lot of math to do with this class.
Overall, he's a great professor and a great guy but the class was pretty rough and hard to understand. Confusing concepts and lots of math. This was a rough semester for him in general though.

dr. law & his TAs are fantastic. i'm a humanities major & really struggled with the class content, but they truly care & are more than willing to work with you. the class & especially the tests are tough but law is great. i'll also add that he was fantastic during the shooting incident this year. i wouldn't have wanted to be in any other classroom.

law is such a sweetheart. as a person who came to unc with no love for physics, I'm starting to get interested in it and will be minoring in astronomy because of him. he's very supportive and his TAs are amazing too (s/o to lawrence, doctor procter, will). they all go out of their way to make sure you understand the content. 100% would recommend.

Great professor and lecturer, but this class is very misleading. The class is labeled Alien Life; however, the class is 3/4 Astrophysics. I did not expect this when signing up for the class. The last lectures are very interesting because they are about aliens, but the rest of the class is about material that is difficult to understand.

Prof Law is passionate +nice! He really cared for our mental health after the 2incidences this semester as pollev+ lecture tutorials weren't mandatory +he removed 1 exam! But the exams are difficult. They're mainly math word problems +the lectures are mainly concept based. We did some math in class but not enough or in the same depth as the exams

This was a great class and the lectures were very interesting; however, the exams killed me! The material is not difficult but the questions on the exams are worded unclearly and most of the grade is based on the exams.

Prof Laws lectures were always so interesting. You can tell he has a great love for the subject. The exams in this class are crazy hard. Didn't enjoy the homework or lecture tutorials but he was great. I'd give the class itself a 3/10. Not my major i just took it for the credit hours so that's probably why I didn't like it. Not really about aliens.
Professor Law is caring and kind. However, I don't know why, I just feel kind of sleepy when listening to him.
Professor Law is a great lecturer!!! You can tell that he is passionate about what he's teaching. You learn a lot of cool stuff in this class.

You can't really hear him during lectures to the point where people dozed off, talking to themselves because it felt pointless. I do think he would be better with a public speaking class for sure. Overall, the class itself wasn't bad, just practice and get old exams.
African Blackneck Spitting Cobra, Electric Eel, Y. Qiu. What do all of these things have in common?
DO not TAKE HIM

This is for PHYS115 but I agree this guy needs to take a public speaking class before he can lecture.  I can't imagine him teaching his own class don't take him if you don't want to raise your cortisol levels.

This is actually for Phys 115. I cannot hear Qiu, he just reads off the slides and WHISPERS. He doesnt explain anything or write anything to solve it he just talks. Please avoid him, you will not learn.

Prof. Qiu does not explain concepts in class: he reads straight from the PowerPoints. He doesn't even try, even if students ask him to write out explanations in class. Stay away, if possible. I do not know why he is teaching intro physics as he does not seem to care whatsoever.

Professor Qiu struggled to read the slideshows, which made understanding difficult physics topics even harder. In fact, I got a better grade in 118 than 114 just because of how bad professor Qiu was. He also never answers questions, always seems nervous to lecture, and seems so out of touch with his students. if you have a class with him, DROP IT.
He's an awful lecturer, and reads off the PowerPoint word by word. He also just doesn't explain things even if someone asks him to.
He is awful

He needs to take a public speaking seminar before teaching again. Also he needs better awareness instead of staring down, as I saw a girl with her hand up for over 3 minutes without him so much as looking at her.

Just don't. It's clear he's very nervous up there and I feel bad for the guy, but you literally can't hear a word of what he says. And I sit near the front of the lecture hall. He's someone who may be too smart for his own good. It's much more productive to watch the YouTube lectures from 2020 during class and follow along with poll everywhere.
Writing this review as I'm sitting in class. Awful lecturer, reads off the PowerPoint word by word,  sounds sleepy a bored doing it.
Jesus christ, this guy is an absolutely HORRIBLE lecturer. Thank god that he's not the only professor for this course

So so nice! It is clear that he is passionate about what he does. Basically gives you what is going to be on the exams. I would say to make sure you know what time assignments are due so you don't miss one, he doesn't make them due at 11:59 and there are very few of them. Also can be a little condescending if you answer a question wrong in class.

Professor Zhou is a great instructor. He's passionate about what he teaches and his tests are verbatim the concepts taught. There was little homework but that meant that the class was test-heavy. The content was interesting and we were able to go to the labs! You needed to be present in class to understand concepts as his slides were confusing.

Dr. Zhou is such a king! You'll probably feel intimidated at first but he tries so hard to make the topics interesting and make jokes during class. Very few grades and he doesn't really use canvas so you won't really know how you're doing in the class. Slides are not detailed so go to class and pay attention and the exams won't be too bad.

Dr. Zhou is a great professor and taught some really cool things about nanotechnology and science! Class is pretty chill with few homework assignments, a midterm and a final for the year. I just wish lecture slides could be more detailed, but if you pay attention in class, you should be fine!

Dr. Zhou is a character. The class feels a little just thrown together, but the material is not difficult at all. Very little homework while is nice, and as long as you payed attention in lecture you will be fine. Incredibly laid back class that I would recommended for your first year seminar if this sounds interesting to you.
midterm + final are on pieces of printer paper! it is mostly a lecture-heavy class and you can make friends within the class. unclear on grading, however, pretty lenient on the final grade

Professor Zhou is passionate about what he's teaching, and he makes the material rather interesting. Most grades are participation/completion-based, plus a midterm and a final. The review he gives you is basically what's on the exam. He also takes you on little field trips to the labs!

Dr. Zhou always seemed interested in the course and always promoted participation. He made the course suprisingly interesting and was very knowledgable on what was taught. The course is graded on attendence, homeworks, midterm, and final. Detailed grading but as long as you pay attention in class you should be fine (lecture slides lack a lot).
THIS GUY IS AWESOME. JUST PAY ATTENTION AND YOU WILL LEARN. TOOK HIM FALL 2023 AND THE THIS GUY KNOWS HIS STUFF!
There are no grades except one midterm (was given on three pages of blank printer paper, and he just said write this information if you know it), a final, and a final project

I loved this class. Dr. Zhou made it the least stressful physics class I've ever taken while ensuring we still learned a lot (which I did). Not worrying about the class made it easier to learn and enjoy the material. Highly recommend this course to anyone going into the medical field or a physics field.
Clear lecturer, minimal studying required

Dr. Gruszko was extremely accessible and answered questions thoroughly. The class was difficult, but don't let the midterm scores discourage you as the studio grade will bring you up. If you find the time for it, go to the review session before the midterms and the final, they are a great way to remind yourself of the many concepts covered.

Lectures are a MUST. You will not glean enough information by simply going through slides. Work the problems out in class, do the homework, and pay attention in lab. This class was sneakily difficult for me, but if you practice, pay attention, and work to do well on the final, she will take that into account. She is also super nice and accomodating
AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! Always listens to students, if you have any questions ask and she'll always be there to help you. Office hours are incredibly helpful and she knows what she's talking about.
has an accent, but it isn't bad and she explains things very well in the lectures

Dr. Branca is the best. She was very caring and accessible through Piazza and O.H. and really cared about helping as many people as she could. For someone that has never taught PHYS 119 before she did a really amazing job. You will definitely have to put in a lot of effort on your own, but she really does want to help along the way. Great professor

dr. branca taught phys 119 pretty well for her first time. there were times where we didn't cover the last little bit of the lecture but that was remediated by the studio work. tests were reasonable except for that second one D: lots of help available and the hw is great practice.

Did not provide complete slides and some of her solutions were blatantly incorrect.

She chill tho

This course is very very hard, It is for physics students only. These are concepts that are super hard to wrap your head around.There isn't enough visual learning to justify taking this course in person, all you do is read of the board, the homeworks are very difficult. My understanding of the topic increased minimally.

Very funny guy. The class is hard regardless, and he did a pretty good job of making things go as smoothly as possible. Always asked for feedback and for questions, and worked with students' requests quite a bit. Definitely recommend him.
The best professor at UNC.

All around wonderful guy. Class is made up of weekly homework and quizzes with a large semester project at the end. Attendance isn't required but you're better off going to most lectures (or attending on zoom). Grades leniently and cares for his students.
He is a great guy!
Very passionate and easygoing professor!
Chill teacher, really is passionate about what he teaches and makes class accessible to all!

Professor Hill is a great guy; he is passionate about his subject and it showed in every lecture, along with a lot of humor. If you keep up with the homework and quizzes, you'll do well. I found some of the content hard but asking clarifying questions during lectures helped. Both midterm and final were take-home, open book, and open note.

Brad is the goat. Exams and homeworks are a near carbon copy straight off the slides. If you are at all interested in Astr, take this class as he is def the best professor. Very engaging and loves what he does. All exams are multiple choice and they are all very fair questions, not suppose to trick you like other professors.

Awesome professor. He gave amazing lectures that were genuinely interesting and enjoyable. Possibly the best lecturer I have ever had. Class was relatively easy with exam material clearly outlined beforehand and minimal work day to day. Highly recommend
The literal greatest professor/teacher I have ever had. I actually looked forward to ASTR101 on Tuesday and Thursday.

I looked forward to this class every time I had it, Professor Barlow gave me a newfound love for astronomy. He is hilarious, and keeps his students engaged at all times. The 3 exams + final are based off of the homework and in-class quizzes, and require studying. He cares about his students immensely, and is fun to chat with after class.

Dr. Barlow is truly one of the best professors you can have. He cares deeply about his subject and you can tell. If you have a chance to take a class with him, DO IT! His office hours are extremely helpful and he will explain things down to whatever detail you need and make sure you understand it. He is extremely kind and willing to help.

Class itself is easy. Learned content from outside resources and then reviewed the slides to understand the class. Topics aren't hard and plenty of opportunities to ask questions in ~3 hours a week of office hours.

I did good in this class because of Youtube learning. His lecture slides made no sense, and they had errors on them. I learned absolutely nothing from Rodriguez. Shows up late and unprepared, and he doesn't care about teaching. Grading/tests were not as bad as I was expecting, but If I didn't have Youtube or ChatGPT, I would have been cooked.

Literally awful. The content of the class is presented on slides that he just repeats it. Nothing makes sense. I was taking 383 during this class and I literally didn't learn or comprehend a single thing unless it was something that we had gone over during 383. If u haven't taken linear algebra and a proof based class (like math 381), do not take.

Professor Rodriguez is a great professor. He will take time to explain things that you do not understand and enjoys teaching. PHYS331 is a tough class if you have not taken linear algebra and a proof based class. There are tons of proofs in the homework. It seems they need to update the prerequisites for the class. Otherwise, it is a great class!

He's a great professor. Low stress high learning environment. Unfortunately, class was at 8 am, so made it hard to pay attention, but that was no fault of the professor. Highly recommend taking a class by him: he's clearly a very smart, very experienced individual. Lucky to have him as a professor.

Super cool professor, makes sarcastic jokes and jokes around with students. Content was a bit difficult as I hadn't taken physics before, but if you pay attention in class and do the hw, the exams are not difficult at all. Also a super generous grader, effort matters!! would recommend this seminar.

The GOAT. Explains things very well and has us do example problems in class so we actually know how to solve problems. I've never seen a physics class collectively understand the material so well. Dr. Iliadis is also kind and funny; class was always enjoyable. Take a class with him if you have the opportunity.

This class was teaching HS Core Physics using movies for examples. If you have never taken physics, this is probably not for you. However, if you have taken physics, it will be a solid recap. Professor Iliadis is very personable and funny while teaching so it was enjoyable to go to class.
Professor Iliadis is a great professor and makes physics incredibly easy to digest and understand. 100% recommend you to take any physics courses with him!

Best physics professor at unc. Loved the physics of movies class. The final is only 20 percent! and rest is all group projects! The syllabus is like Physics I and barely Physics II from AP high school. He is hilarious and loves to interact and make the class a better place. You ll love it

Very straightforward and down to earth. Very fun class. Class is fast-paced so make sure not to miss class and take good notes. The material could be a lot to digest for students without a physics background, so don't fall behind and prioritize fully understanding the concepts. Not much homework.

Class lowkey ragebait work but it can guarantee you an A. If ur a senior trying to do this it's a snooze fest and the prof lowkey too into his subject matter to the point ur like fella calm down it's only some pics of the sky

This guy knows SO MUCH ABOUT OUR UNIVERSE, it's awesome! He answered even my most off-topic questions and kindly entertained my curiosity. His video recordings walk you through the homework in a very helpful way.
Dude is hilarious I love him.

Your grade WILL get curved down. If you don't go to every extra credit opportunity (which are @10pm on going out nights LOL), you will not get the grade you DESERVE! Take another lab, even if you are in ASTR100! I'd say I understood and absorbed 100% of the material here, yet didn't get rewarded... what a joke.

Loved taking ASTR 101/100L over the summer w/ Reichart! 101: You basically just watch his recorded Covid lectures, but I really enjoyed them. Tests on minor details but you get to use a cheat sheet. Math is all plug & chug. Weird grading system though; see other reviews. 100L: easy & fun. Reichart is great and super responsive. I love astro now! :)

ASTRO 110 with Dr. Reichart is a must-take for anyone interested in space, He's incredibly passionate and makes complex ideas clear and exciting. The TAs were friendly and hilarious, and winning cat stickers for Kahoots made class fun. If you don't do well, it's genuinely your own fault, they do everything in their power to help you succeed

Honestly a blast. Am not an astro/physics major and I loved it -- he knows a lot of students are just here to get their FC Create and he throws in some physics and astro knowledge. We got to use fancy equipment to take cool pictures and edit them, we made a radio map of the universe. Easy A, and is super interesting! Would highly recommend.

Great class, 10/10 no notes. Super fun, easy to take with no physics background and low stress. Show up, do the work, get an A and make very cool images of space. Everything is done in groups made at the beginning of the semester so pick good partners early.
Pretty good experience so far. Although there was a blog to complete every week, the grading was quite lenient. Overall, it was still a very enjoyable experience.

Dan is a nice guy, but I hated ASTR 110. The class is poorly designed and has too many people for you to get help you need. All assignments are blogs you make with a team. This wouldn't be so hard if lectures aligned with the pacing of due dates—I rarely understood what lesson we were even covering that day. Material was a jumbled mess.

(For ASTR110) My favorite professor so far at UNC. The work/research Dan is leading in the astronomy field is so inspirational, and his passion for teaching truly shows. Class is an easy A as long as you participate in your group and complete assignments on time. The projects are SO cool and I've learned so much about our universe! Highly recommend

I really liked Dr. Reichart, but I didn't like how this class was set up. The grades are based on your rank relative to others in the class, so only a few people will get A's. Made the course more stressful than a 100 level class should be.

Professor Reichart's ASTR101 class was a mixed bag. While the lectures were engaging, the grading structure was frustrating. To succeed, you'll need to stay on top of the material and use resources like textbooks and Unstuck AI alongside class attendance.

I took 110 with Dr. Reichart and it was super interesting. The biggest issue was the class was really big and fairly disrespectful to him as a result, so it was hard to focus/hear at times (not his fault!). Reichart and his TAs are always available and respond quickly, eager to help. If space fascinates you, jump on this class.

A great and interesting class; however, the professor was never present. TA graded everything. I was very lucky to have a caring TA who helped me tremendously. Your grade will primarily reflect who your TA is. Lot's of work for a 1 credit class but very interesting.

This class is entirely group based so make sure to form a good group. Professor Reichart's lectures explain the topic in depth but most of the class is graded by making blogs that are performed as a group. The TA's are very helpful and accessible. Overall, a great class.
His lecturers were either super boring or super interesting but never in between. The exams felt extremely hard for an introductory course.

I took both the 101 course and lab online and they were both ok. There was a lot of work every week and the grading system was very frustrating. Reichart is a really cool guy though. He was patient, responded quickly, and was very understanding.

This review is for ASTR 111, Dr. Reichart's program called ERIRA, but he in general is just such a fantastic guy and lecturer I'd recommend him for any class at UNC. He is smart, funny, caring, and understanding, pushing his students while recognizing when they need help.
This rating is for ASTR 111, ERIRA. This was my favorite experience at UNC thus far. I learned so much from Dr. Reichart. Also, basically, everyone who takes this course receives an A. Great guy.
The best class at UNC, hands down. Borderline life-changing.

This was my favorite class all of freshman year. The readings are interesting and she truly cares about teaching the content of the class. Most of the work/grade is doing weekly team presentations and participating in class.

Don't be turned away from taking her seminar just because it's physics. You hardly have any work besides weekly group presentations and all the prof cares about is sharing her passion with her students.Genuinely an amazing and caring woman.
Showcases a clear love and enthusiasm for her work.

Took a physics course back in '06 at UNC.  She was easily one of the worse teachers I've ever had in my entire life.  Assigned the hardest assignments with an exceptionally poor ability to explain concepts.  Test average somewhere around a D.  There were many complaints regarding her at the time.

MSA is the GOAT!!! She leads amazing lectures and ensures that no student is left behind. The HWs prepare you well for the midterms. Attendance is crucial b/c she covers all content in class. Legit just using calculus to prove common sense (ex: prices rise --> quantity decreases no way lol). Understand derivatives thoroughly and you'll be chilling!

Very caring. Sometimes felt like she could have gone faster and finding "tricks to memorize" the concept instead of understanding it deeply. Midterms and final are majority of the grade and you need to be doing well on all 3 to get an A. Very manageable. Need to be very comfortable with derivatives.

So nice and really funny, BUT her flipped classroom model taught me NOTHING. I went to office hours, all lectures, and watched all the videos and still didn't learn anything. The tests make up a majority of your grade so you can't do bad, and you are expected to intuitively know econ or you're cooked. The TAs and ULAs were also bad at explaining.

Amazing, best econ professor, literally study the exact way she tells you by grouping practice problems and you will be fine, flipped classroom is annoying but it works, no other econ professor compares, if you did well in calc you will do amazing in this class

I had the pleasure of taking Professor MSA for both ECON 410 and 415. ECON 415 builds on the concepts from 410, but she does a great job of reviewing the fundamentals needed to succeed in the course. While 410 was a bit trickier, both classes were very manageable as long as you stayed on top of the material and completed her practice exams.

Without question the best professor I have ever encountered. She is welcoming & considerate & leads lectures extremely well and efficiently, giving students plenty of chances to ask questions and absorb info. She is accessible via email and office hours (DEF RECOMMEND GOING), knows how to teach in a way that students will understand...0 complaints.
MSA is a great teacher. This class is not very hard if you are good at calculus and have prior exposure to a lot of the math beforehand. Very fair grader and wants students to suceed.

I like everything about how MSA does ECON 410. She is warm and caring but commands the room and lectures with confidence. She provides a wealth of helpful resources and gives fair exams. If you can get the math down (hardest concepts are exponent rules and partial derivatives), then nothing is more difficult conceptually than the stuff from 101.

MSA is hands-down one of the best professors I've had at UNC. I love her! Somehow, she is able to explain every single micro concept clearly and do it with patience and care. She is very generous with weighting your best exam heavier, dropping homework grades, etc. If you are going to take 410, take it with her!

MSA is amazing! ECON410 is a heavy course, but she has an insane amount of resources. This class is also a flipped classroom (but I never watched the video and did fine, just gotta grind a lot later). Looking over 101 materials/taking it the previous semester can definitely be helpful. Grading is fair, though she doesn't curve or give extra credit.

MSA is an awesome instructor, as she was able to explain abstract concepts very clearly. As long as you strongly lock in September, you'll be fine the rest of the semester. Many resources are provided throughout the semester.

Econ 410 is not a breeze. Content picks up pretty quickly, math intensive (calc 1), etc. However, MSA made this class extremely feasible. She was always there to help before/after class and in office hours. 2 midterms, a final, and HW are pretty much your entire grade. A is def possible if you keep up w the course videos and ask questions!

She has the magic of explaining complex stuff in the easiest way to understand. Very kind, interesting, approachable, and generous about grades. Exams are extremely similar to the homework. I personally feel the pace of the course is slowed by the class size (~200 people) and many polls during class (each could take up to 10-15 min of class time)
She's lowkey hilarious.

Mother. I wish she taught 101 I definitely would've actually absorbed the information more. Just do the work and don't take this class in general if you can't do calculus because that's on you. Everything else she helps you so much with

I love MSA. Recommended to literally everyone that needs to take ECON 410. Honestly I didn't have McDonough for 101 so I felt like I barely learned anything about Econ but still just fine because of all the materials -- you just have to know calculus so review that if you don't. MSA is going to make an amazing grandmother one day

Incredibly respected and organized professor. Clearly a ton of experience in instructing 410, and her online resources reflected that. Review the homeworks and do practice problems pre-exam. Review sessions were also very helpful. Exams are tough but fair.

MSA seemed to be a good teacher but the way she taught did not work for me and I really struggled in this class. Go to office hours, study hard, but she wasn't as great for my experience as people told me to expect.
Great professor worth waiting for the long waitlist. Really knows so well how to explain stuff clearly and concisely. Love the flipped class mode

In all honesty, she's a great professor, and it was a great class. She's a great lecturer who knows her stuff and is always organized. Calc-1-based econ, which I didn't have too strong of a base in. She made the class manageable and offered a ton of resources. The class itself is challenging, so be ready to put in the work.
Very good professor and tests are very similar to homework and recitation. Lots of resources to get help outside of class. Just have the fundamentals from calc 1 down and your set.

MSA is awesome! The math itself isn't even that hard as long as you're familiar with basic calculus/derivatives. She provides so many resources to help you succeed and you learn mainly from practice especially the homeworks. There is a lot of content but as long as you stay on track and start studying for the tests early you'll be fine!

MSA is awesome! So many resources to take advantage of if you are confused about a topic. Class is mainly practice, so watch videos to have a clear understanding of the topic. Exams can be tricky but if you can do the homework, you can do the exams. 410 is difficult, both conceptually and math but MSA is easily the best professor available for it.
MSA is great, easily one of the best professors at UNC. ECON 410 is on the difficult side. A is possible if you lock in and grind. Need to put in a decent amount of work outside of class.

Best Econ professor! If you watch the pre-recorded class videos, pay attention during lecture, and study the lectures and practice problems before tests, you are guaranteed success. There are also a lot of resources outside class if needed.
BEST PROFESSOR FOR ECON!!!

dare i say the best professor ever at UNC. extremely organized, very helpful in OH, basically gives you the answers to homeworks if you go. homeworks are super similar to exams, just practice those. so much practice probelms and there are review sessions every week if you need it. the best professor fr, so easy to interact with as well.

Nice professor and fair gradings. Materials are not hard if you are good at algebra and calculus. You only need to understand the concepts and apply mathematical way to solve problems. All 3 exams have an average of ~78% (she even curved the final exam by 3 points to make that). This semester 28% got an A and another 8% got an A-. MSA is the GOAT!

GET READY TO MAKE THIS CLASS YOUR LIFE OTHERWISE YOU WILL HAVE TO RETAKE IT…this class will LITERALLY BECOME YOUR LIFE. IF YOU THOUGHT ECON101 WAS HARD GET READY FOR DOUBLE THE STUDYING AND DOUBLE THE STRESS. Make sure to STAY ON TOP OF HW/go to EconAid, if you check out for even a week you're SCREWED because new things build off previous concepts.

One of the most organized professors I've had, and she seems passionate about what she's teaching! She provides a lot of resources to help out. This class required a lot of work, though, so be ready to put in the time. I just don't like how the midterms/final determine almost your entire grade.

ECON 410 is difficult, but MSA does a great job making the material make sense. Plenty of resources/practice problems to study for exams as well, which is nice. While attendance in lecture/recitation is technically mandatory, she offers an alternate grade scale that gives extra weight to tests to replace attendance grade. Overall great experience

MSA is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. She's an incredibly good lecturer that makes difficult content easy to understand. She had pre-recorded videos and a lot of resources to help students. She's always available for questions and her tests are very fair. The exams are not easy, but if you pay attention and study, you will be fine.

MSA provides a lot of resources however the amount of resources she provides is overwhelming. In addition, I've found the pre-recorded lecture videos to be unhelpful as later on in the semester what she teaches in class doesn't align with the lecture video and it can be confusing. 75% of your grade is two midterms and final with no curve.

You need to be good at calculus and algebra, I struggled at first and I'm pretty good at math. MSA is super nice and very passionate. She gives tons of resources/ practice problems, but the class structure is annoying. She expects a lot of time outside of class, which is fair but if you don't watch pre-class videos you will be lost during lectures.

Class is not that bad you should be fine as long as you are decent at basic calc. Tests are actually way easier than she makes them seem. Like she will hype up how hard they are and say you will need to apply concepts in new ways we have not seen. This is not true, practice problems were for sure harder than exam.
MSA is the goat. Not only does she make 410 understandable, but it provides a great foundation for a lot of the stuff you use throughout the econ major. She's hilarious and charismatic too.

Do not take this class with her. Just had our first exam and she purposely tries to trick you. She is an awful teacher, I've had to teach myself everything on my own. Studied more than I ever have and still did bad on the exam.

I don't understand how her reviews are so high. Everyone I know in upper level econ courses says her class is taught very poorly for learning the basics that are needed later on. Do not take this class with her.

I took this course with MSA because of her reviews on here, but I strongly advise to not take this class with her. While there are a lot of resources available, they are not beneficial and are overwhelming. Her lectures are all over the place and have no structure. Everyone I know in this course with her is extremely confused.

MSC is good at explaining concepts and providing resources. My complaint is that 78-83% of the grade comes from timed exercises and exams. Only 17-22% of grades will be determined by things that students can take their time on. This class feels like taking the ACT and is a neurotypical-focused class where testing alone judges your capability.

GOAT status in the economics department. Networking with other students and engaging with genuinely enticing class content. No exams. Procrastinating the portfolio is not advisable, but you'll survive...probably. Best of luck to any future ULAs.

She really knows her stuff. Try to go to class as most of my notes are from class. I didn't really use the textbook at all. Everything builds off of each other so make sure to know the beginning units very well. I took this 2nd semester freshmen year and thought it was doable- used all the resources she gave. Def go to her help sessions with TAs.

MSA gave us many resources to succeed in this class including lecture videos, help sheets, etc. Exams and homeworks were somewhat difficult but the amount of practice and guidelines she gave make it possible to do well if you put effort. In general she and the TAs were very helpful as far as answering questions if there was confusion.

MSA is easily the best prof I've ever had at UNC. If you do the pre-class videos and pay attention during lecture you will be fine. The midterms were not too bad, and I thought the final was a little easier. Your grade in this class will reflect how much work you put in. If you are willing to work, I would definitely recommend taking 410 with MSA.

MSA is a fantastic professor and if you have to take this class at all, take it with her. She provides so so so many resources, and those are the key to doing good in the class. Truly understand the content to a deep level, and know how to apply concepts in conjunction with when to use them! Exams are SO fair & class felt easier than ECON 101 tbh.

MSA made ECON410 so much easier than I thought it would be. She's a great lecturer and truly cares about her students. The exams aren't too hard as long as you pay attention in class, watch the lecture videos, and study practice materials.

She is the best professor at UNC. This class wasn't the hardest but definitely not easy, however she is super accessible and gives tons of resources. Study hard, do the practice problems and an A is definitely attainable
She is an amazing professor, but the course might be one of the hardest at UNC. Take 410 with her if you need it, but prepare to lock in like never before.

I wish that there was a way to rate her as more than a 5. MSA is the sole reason that I am interested in economics now. She's worth the wait to take her if she isn't teaching 410 at the moment. The only reason that I rate her as a 3 in difficulty is just because the material is more difficult than average.

MSA is the absolute best. She is super sweet and cares so much about each student. She's amazing at explaining concepts in a way that makes sense. She also told so many funny stories in class that related to the material which made it memorable. I never struggled to pay attention during her lectures because they were so interesting.

MSA once again is unmatched in her ability to teach complex concepts in a clear, concise way. Her teaching style and quizzes were set up well for us to succeed in the class. Overall, relatively easy class but very enjoyable and interesting.

This is my second class with MSA and she's an amazing professor (probably one of the best in the department). The content is an extension of 410 so a lot of the lectures are familiar which is nice. She was really accessible outside of class and a 10/10 class!

MSA is a true gift to the ECON department. After having her for both 410 & 415, she is my favorite professor by a mile. She is kind and takes time to get to know her students individually. For a professor to teach such difficult classes and consistently be rated amongst the highest, you know she is worth it! When I think UNC, I also think MSA!

MSA is one of the best econ lecturer I ever had. She is funny and obviously passionate about what she teaches. She has very clear grading criteria and wants you to succeed. If you just keep up with her class, attend lectures, do the homework, and use the resources she gives you, you will get an A. I was sick for three weeks so I fell behind.

MSA is the best teacher you will ever have. Pre-class assignments and problem sets are short, but useful. She creates study guides for every quiz that are super helpful for studying. Very responsive to students ideas and questions, via campuswire, email, and office hours.
Dropping the lowest quiz grade???? Praise the goddess that is MSA.

MSA was my favorite professor at Carolina. She was fair, encouraging, and willing to spend time out of class helping students understand the material. I got a C+ in her class (totally fair), so be ready to study. Her 410 class was tough, but I enjoyed learning from her so much I took another class with her - would do it again.
Humble and kind energy in the classroom. Expectations are clear and concise. Resources are organized and bountiful. She did her part, the course is on you.
Hands down the best professor at UNC. Passionate, caring and extremely knowledgable. I fought tooth and nail to get into her summer class and did not regret it.

If you find yourself in the unfortunate situation of having to take ECON410, you must choose MSA. She is the best at getting you through this weed-out class. She is highly organized and provides you with every resource you could possibly need. Make sure to attend ALL lectures and you'll be fine.

ECON410 is a difficult course but MSA offers a lot of resources, is very organized, and is genuinely good at teaching. As long as you stay on top of your stuff in this class and put in effort to understand the material as you go, you'll be fine.

Great professor that provides numerous resources, practice problems, and help sessions to help students succeed. Content is challenging, but exams are fair and not designed to trick you. Her lectures are very engaging and help you master the material. I definitely recommend taking ECON 410 with MSA!

MSA is my absolute favorite professor at UNC. She has so many resources available to help you succeed and explains things very clearly. Her lesson videos are great and while she is not willing to bend deadlines, she has enough built in drops in the syllabus that you will be fine.

MSA is the professor to take for 410. Do not try to take someone else because it is a challenging class and MSA is the best one at making the information clear and understandable. Wants each student to succeed but will not give any particular student extra advantages over others.

I really liked my 101 experience. It probably was harder for other people because I had already taken 2 years of econ in highschool, but I do think he was a pretty fair test maker/grader. He's very passionate about econ and was very accessible in office hours.

It's a hard class but he is an incredible teacher. Very funny and engaging lecturer who doesn't make the content too difficult compared to other ECON101 profs. 70% of your grade is from exams. Do the problem sets and practice exams and you'll be fine. Highly recommend over Staub.

I took this class for the love of the game, and it was alright, nothing to heavy but nothing light. He does use a textbook but its optional, midterms and final exam are the same thing. Overall I liked him, and the cases were very fun to read.
Good professor for Econ 101 when you other option is Staub.

Dr McDonough is a passionate, engaging lecturer, who does not try to make Econ harder than it needs to be. The tests aren't too bad as he gives you previous years' exams to practice with, and if you go to the lectures and recitations, you should be able to do alright.
McDonough is a very energetic lecturer and is passionate about what he does. ECON 101 is challenging but I think he is a great professor.

Take him, that's all I can say. Econ is hard regardless, I felt prepared for all the exams so far, and he's already posted so much stuff for the final. He tries to relate to the students, take a hard class, and make it something understandable. HW is complete, and there are tons of ways to boost your grade as long as you just do your work.

McDonough is truly an amazing person. Treats every student with the utmost respect and is so intentional with how he teaches and responds to students. You can tell he puts SO much time and care into his course and students' progress. Exams are hard, but it's UNC. If you have to take ECON, take it with McDonough!!!!
great lecturer and there's a bunch of attendance & requirements dropped so you could get a higher score.

Great class and great professor. ECON 101 gets a bad reputation, but it really isn't too bad if you pay attention and do the homework. Robert really cares about people understanding the content and ensuring people have ample opportunities to do so. Tests can be tricky, but they are very fair and with enough preperation you'll do fine.

He was a good economics professor and did a good job explaining topics. If you have taken 101, this will be the most boring class. If you need this OR 101 - definitely take this! Hes really nice and the class is relaxed with a few problem sets and kinda difficult but fair exams. 2 midterms, 1 final exam, 7 problem sets. Easy workload, not easy A.

Apparently his target GPA is 2.7 and his confusing lectures really prove it. The exams were also super difficult even with a lot of studying. This was also my first econ class ever for reference. However, Professor McDonough is an amazing person
Professor Mcdonough is an entertaining lecturer, his tests are fair, and the class material is manageable as long as you put in a decent effort. Great survey course of basic Econ topics.

I think McDonough gets a bad rep. The tests are multiple choice and they are hard, but u go to UNC, all the tests are hard. It's totally doable and there's lots of other opportunity to do well. He also is very generous and final replaces lowest midterm. Plenty of easy A homework, just put in effort and ur fine

I personally loved Professor McDonough! He is a very engaging lecturer who clearly loves econ and really wants his student to succeed. Honestly, I didn't find his tests to be too hard and the work load was pretty manageable. Overall, would definitely take another class with him if I could and highly recommend!

Prof McDonough's class is very hard. Heavy focus on midterms + final exam, which are very hard to get a high grade on and count for 70% total. His lectures were engaging but be careful if you care about gpa.
People who complain about McDonough often do because it is just a hard class. He is very organized, knowledgeable and accessible and cares about his students.

If you work hard to get an A, it is possible. Two midterms and final were difficult (three tests = 70% of grade) drops lowest midterm if helps your grade. Lectures were engaging. Lots of textbook readings and achieve weekly (completion) with problem sets every few weeks (mix of completion/accuracy). Two recitation skips and graded for completion.

I loved Professor McDonough's lectures, this class was very interesting and relevant overall. Some of the quantitative stuff could be difficult at times but he gave opportunities for extra credit throughout the course and was always willing to answer questions.
Tricky exams even though he said the at he wasn't trying to trick you. Exams are worth 70 percent of grade.

McDonough is a good professor and his lectures are good. He is inspirational, genuinely cares about his students, and is overall a really nice guy. Beware though his tests and final exam are absolutely horrendous and there is no way to practice them bc that level of difficulty is not taught. Not an easy A at all

Do not choose this for Econ elective. Doesn't explain the math in class and makes exams harder than practice. I genuinely think he doesn't know how to do the math himself. Gave us impossible numbers to work with on exams. Lectures are pretty engaging tho and McDonough is a very passionate lecturer. He puts T/F trick questions also. Don't recommend

Professor McDonough is very passionate about economics. However, I do feel like sometimes his lectures get boring and it's hard to stay focus in class. His exams are also harder than the practice exam and honestly the Achieve homework does not help me prepare at all. I feel like I learn a lot in class when it comes to the test I still feel lost.

Not an easy A, but this was my favorite Econ class at UNC! Robert is a great guy and made the material relatable and engaging. Exam was harder than expected, but he took our feedback about not having enough concrete practice and actually followed through with it. It's clear he actually is interested by the material and wants us to be too

This class was one of the only classes I didn't struggle to pay attention in. Classes were engaging, and he was clear about what would be on the test, so it was easy to prepare. By far the best elective ECON class I have taken. Anyone who complains about this class just didn't prepare enough.

Very enthusiastic about economics which is great. Somehow lectures are still incredibly boring. No point in going to class cause tests are exactly like practice tests. Super forgettable class and teacher like most in the UNC econ department.

His lectures were engaging, but didn't really prepare us for the difficulty of the tests. We were expected to know the material at a higher level and we just didn't have enough QUALITY practice material to get to that point.

People only dislike him because they didn't put in the work. This man is a goat. So accesable outside of class and gives so many resources and practice. If you put in the work and truly understand things and go to econ aid you can do well and he is such a smart and nice guy who explains concepts wonderfully.

As long as you're willing to put in the work, you'll be fine. Reading the textbook is pretty important. McDonough cares about us doing well and is a respectable guy - he gets so much hate because his class isn't an easy A

McDonough is very overhated, don't be scared because of his reviews. If you put in the work, read the textbook before class, and give yourself enough time to do the problem sets and achieves you will be fine. Your midterms and final make up a lot of your grade so really lock in for those, you'll get out whatever you put into this class.

I took in Spring 2025. Prof. McDonough is tough and speaks very bluntly, but I cannot speak highly enough of him. He deeply cares about his students and is passionate about all things economics (great guy to have for 101). He curves exams, drops the lowest grades on assignments, and most of his lectures are entertaining and have real world meaning!

His tests are not fair. He is kind, lectures are good, HW is retakable, problem sets are fair. BUT his exams come out of nowhere. He asks questions that he never taught. The math is the easy part, true/false is basically impossible unless you're a fantastic guesser. It's like jeopardy, but your grade depends on you being a good guesser. Frustrating

His lectures are informative, and the textbook is a very helpful resource. The class is test-heavy heavy but he offers some extra credit, and depending on overall performance, dropping of a midterm or curving of grades at the end of the term.

This class is notoriously hard and although I took both micro and macro in HS this class was tough. He is a great lecturer and makes the content pretty engaging and has a genuine passion for the subject. When it comes to tests on the first mid term I would probably compare him to a drill instructor with how stressful he made the test on the day.

Robert is an amazing teacher. Some people give him a bad review because it is a hard class, but the reality is ECON101 is a weed-out class and has hard content. If you are diligent about studying, practice problems, and actually understanding the concepts of econ, not just memorizing things, you will be fin in this class. Great lectures, too

Professor McDonough is a great lecturer and I learned a lot, but the exams were extremely difficult, tricky, and focused on the hardest topics. They made up 70% of our grade. He curved our final grades and gave extra credit on midterms, which helped. Only take this class if required—it's very hard to get an amazing grade even with lots of studying.

He is clearly a passionate lecturer. The reason for the low rating is due to how unreasonably difficult his exams are relative to how he prepares us. Averages for each exam were often below 70. I felt I did everything I could to study but some of his exams questions are worded to trick you. FYI, this is the only class I did not receive an A in.

Class and material itself weren't too difficult but exams were very tough compared to other classes I've taken. I liked McDonough except for on exam days where he created an environment that was extremely uncomfortable to be in. Would take again for 101 though.

The lectures and homework do not align with the difficulty of the tests. You think you know what you're doing and then are completely blindsided by his exams. He's a good guy, you can tell he cares but he makes this class WAY harder than it needs to be. Go to Econaid and interact with the peer tutors; it's the only reason I got a B.

Every lecture and recitation is extremely dumbed down and then every exam question is a extremely harder level with no access to practice of that level except a measly 2 previous practice exams that feel nothing like what you end up taking day of. Relies completely on TAs and textbook to teach anything that isn't the most basic definition/question

The classes are good but unnecessary, just do the mandatory poll everywhere from your dorm for the atttendance credit. Study the powerpoints as thats where the questions come from. Midterm 1 is the easiest and the final is super duper hard. It's a weedout class for a reason.

Dr. McDonough is awesome. He teaches incredibly well - so much so that he makes you forget the class can be hard. He gives out a ton of extra credit so it's not that bad. Go to the lectures, listen, and do the homework and you should be fine. You do not have to read any of the textbook unless you feel super unconfident. Study maybe 4 hours per test

All the bad reviews are most likely first years not taking responsibility for truly understanding the stuff. Not the easiest stuff but very doable if you are consistent in reading the book and doing practice problems. Exams are very fair, people do not understand how to prepare.

One of the best lecturers I've ever had. Very passionate about economics. Only issue I had with him was that his exams had very tricky questions. He makes the questions himself which can lead to a lot of unclear questions. This results in very low test averages (60s and 70s) but he does curve the final grade if needed so I wouldn't worry too much.

McDonough is my favorite professor to date. He is very passionate about economics & gives clear lectures. ECON 101 requires a substantial amount of work - I read the textbook chapters before class, took detailed class notes, & spent hours studying concepts. If you genuinely put in effort, you'll do fine even on his often quite challenging exams.

You need to work hard for a good grade!! I strongly recommend skimming the textbook and taking notes. I found it really important to go to lecture,  recitations were pretty helpful too. His tests are fairly difficult and have a few trick questions, but he offers some partial and extra credit! He was really passionate and cared about us learning
You need to work hard for a good grade!! I strongly recommend skimming the textbook and taking notes.
The class was pretty chill, he was a great lecturer. All the assignments were not too hard and didn't take too long. Tests did feel unnecessarily hard though. Not a terrible option for 101.

ECON101 is a weed-out for a reason but you can get an A if you put in the hours. Find a study partner, always read textbook before lecture, always go to recitation, and study hard before midterms and finals because they are weighted heavily. Dr. McDonough is very dedicated and engaged. He was also very generous with curves, extra credit, and drops.

Excellent lectures but exams were extremely difficult. Offered extra credit and a midterm drop. I really struggled at the beginning and did horribly but put in a LOT of work and ended up doing well in the class. I think Robert cares about his students but has a weird way of showing it. He is very accessible and helpful. Use EconAid/peer tutors!!

You get out what you put into this class. Can be overwhelming if you take textbook notes but it's more helpful to stick to class slideshows. He is very passionate and has interesting lectures. Yes his lectures are not as hard as the test but you would get the same from any other Econ 101 teacher- you have to apply yourself outside of class

He sets you up to fail. I found this class interesting and really enjoyed the content. I felt that I understood all of it. I read every single page of our textbook, start to finish, and cannot even tell you how many hours each week I put into this class. He screws you over on tests. His final exam average was a 67% and that tells you everything.
hard midterms hard final makes you read a billion pages of econ textbook.

Although McDonough is very passionate about econ and is a great lecturer, it seems like he doesn't care much for his students. I had a medical emergency and had to miss the second midterm. Makeups weren't allowed and the weightage was shifted to the final instead. This made it difficult to be successful in the course. If you can avoid econ, do it.

Robert is a fine professor and a pretty funny guy. It's just that ECON 101 is a hard class since it covers both micro and macro in a single semester. The tests are hard because every question seems like a trick question. To that, make sure you actually understand the content and not just memorize the information. Also gave lots of extra credit.

Econ 101 is a for sure a weed out class as the B school is pretty competitive and this is one of the key pre reqs for it. Mcdonough's lectures are usually pretty interesting just know the class is pretty test heavy. Overall, solid class just make sure to really work as the exams can be difficult.

McDonough is a great lecturer, he is able to simplify complex topics and and put key ideas into real life scenerios. Tests are difficult because theres a lot of content but I wouldnt blame him for that. He covers everything you need to know you just have to know how to apply it.

Not sure why the rating isn't higher. There was clearly a lot of effort put into the assignments and lectures to make sure we had plenty of time reviewing the concepts, and he is an animated and engaging lecturer. A bit test-heavy (70% of the grade), but you could easily get extra-credit if you did short reflections on the midterms.

Robert is great and you shouldn't be deterred by the poor reviews (most are from a previous year where he hadn't yet calibrated his tests properly). If you keep up with lectures, take notes, and go to office hours, you will be fine. Robert is a really great lecturer, makes the class interesting, and is really good at explaining tough concepts.
Great professor, best class I've taken at Carolina. Just do the work and read the textbook, and you're good.

great professor, sometimes lectures were behind curriculum. explained things well and super engaging. class tends to be challenging and exams are tougher than the homework and course material. best way to do well is take practice tests and do the problems that he/TAs/ULAs design.  make sure you understand the material super well and study for exams

He is very enthusiastic. For economics, an old man course of study, he's definitely a unique young guy to be teaching it. He was very generous answering questions in a big lecture hall. He held us late every class. "We have 1 minute left..." and would proceed to talk for 4 minutes. Tests are convoluted with sports references. Tests count a lot!

While this class was certainly not easy, Robert is easily one of my favorite professors I have had at UNC. He brings a constant, genuine enthusiasm and passion to lecture that is deeply infectious. He maintains objectivity when speaking about potentially divisive topics, and is always open to questions and discussion.

McDonough is a good professor but the content is extremely difficult. He does a good job teaching and is always willing to help but the midterms/exam are pretty difficult. Gives extra credit opportunities and lots of homework/pollev drops but is never quite enough to counteract poor exam grades.
I don't understand the bad reviews. He was so helpful during lecture. Also just a cool dude. However, it is econ and that is hard and you will have to study to get a good grade.

Robert is a super funny and kind guy. He is extremely smart and really knows what he is talking about. His class is lecture heavy but he makes it enjoyable. This class is definitely difficult and you have to work hard outside of class and homework to get a good grade, but Robert really tries to help you succeed to the best of your ability.

Prof. McDonough is a very smart individual who really cares about the material he is teaching. However, this course is definitely a weed-out course. The homework, achieves, and practice exams are good, but the exams are way too difficult in comparison. In order to actually succeed, you should definitely read the textbook as it's very digestible.

While ECON101 can be a challenging class but I was glad to have Professor McDonough as my teacher! He provides a ton of resources and is open to answering questions to help you succeed but you will have to put in the work to use the resources to the max. Do the homework, actually read the textbook, and pay attention in class and you will do great!

Professor McDonough's lectures are much easier than his exams. I think I understand everything during class, but when I get to the exam, I have no idea what is going on. He is also too strict on his anti-cheating measures to the point where he will not accommodate if you need a make-up exam.

He explained how the class worked in the first lecture- if you put in the work, you can get a good grade. You have to study for the tests, do the homework, go to lectures and participate in recitation if you want to be successful, but he gives a lot of easy points and is always available to help if you need. 
10/10 recommend him for Econ 101.

Last midterm was extremely unfair. Some of the questions were unsolvable (he had to omit them after because of his own mistake), his answer key was wrong, and he talked the entire test yelling in his microphone. You cannot think during the test.

the issue is how he writes his exams. you could be doing all of the other assignments w 100% accuracy but still get a D on the test. his goal is to trick you and although all multiple choice sounds better than free response, they are extremely difficult and convoluted. this class made me go on anti depressants, if that means anything to you.

RM is definitely the best of the ECON 101 professors. He is VERY passionate about economics and truly does want to see his students succeed. He has a lower rating on RMP simply because ECON 101 definitely is a weed-out course and is challenging. That said, he does provide you with all the resources to succeed. He is very accessible outside of class

I'm not done with ECON101 yet, but I currently have an A in the class. It is a lot of work, and definitely requires you to put in the hours, but Dr. McDonough is really good at explaining topics that the textbook couldn't quite convey. He's also helpful in office hours and offers quite a few chances for extra credit/small assignment drops.

Econ 101 has a bad reputation at UNC, but McDonough is fantastic. The exams are very difficult, but I would recommend going to extra tutoring for anything you don't understand. His lectures are very clear, and he is very engaging.

Overall McDonough was a great lecturer. He is obviously very passionate about economics and if you lock in during his lectures you should have no problems on the problem sets or homework. The problem is the exams are 70%. The exams are meant to trick you (this is a weeder class after all) so be careful
This class is manageable. Not too much work! Just be ready to study quite a bit for the midterms.

Way to many people complaining on here. This class is genuinely not hard at all, to be clear had 0 experience with econ before. I am also not a genius, just study the concepts he goes over and if you understand them tests are easy. Just because they are not the same as homework does not make them hard, it is clear which concepts to apply.

His lectures are amazing, and it is really easy to understand the topics covered. He gives a lot of chances for extra credit and the assignments outside of class aren't too bad. However, the exams he gives are near impossible. Studied for days/weeks and still barley passed them. They resemble nothing you've done throughout the semester.
Great person, good professor, still learning the best way to go about a large lecture. Knows the content well, yes its a hard class and a weed-out but he will help you a lot at office hours
not a good prof to take for 101 especially if you want to apply to the business school. take someone else.
The most charismatic lecturer I have ever had. Tests are the heavy work so you need to prepare the most for them.

I love Robert and the way that he taught this class so much. Not too much work, lots of assignment drops, and extra credit for both midterms which helped a lot of people. His exam questions were also easier than the other econ teacher that semester.

Robert is great and makes class interesting to college students. Class is a weeder and is rushed - take only for major requirements. Grading is fair: 1 midterm is replaced by final exam, easy assignments weighted at 30%, course curved slightly. It is difficult to get an A because the practice is not too similar to exams. The final determines a lot.
Not a fun class to take

he was fine. i took him fall 2024 and i think based on what ive heard he got better over time so maybe he'll be better for future courses too. the content isn't easy and its a heavier workload but as long as you get your achieve homeworks and problem sets done you'll be fine i think

Great lecturer. concepts were easy to pick up. two midterms worth 20% each, final worth 30%, participation/homework worth 30%. I took AP macroeconomics in high school, so I think that helped too. definitely would take econ 101 with McDonough.

If you show up and genuinely pay attention, you should get at least a B. Robert is definitely the best lecturer I have ever had. The exams are hard but he gave free points back on both midterms if you did a reflection form. The lectures are the same as the textbook, so if you understand the lecture, there is no need to read the textbook.

Professor Robert is passionate about the material and tries to teach in a fun way, but he wants to make the exams tricky (he literally said that was his goal). He mostly had conceptual questions that were somewhat/barely mentioned in lectures. And exams made up ~ 70% of the overall grade, even though we had problem sets, hw and recitation stuff

This is a weed out class, but it's not impossible to do well. Robert is a great lecturer but obviously exam questions are going to be harder than examples covered in class so the textbook and the practice midterms/final are the most helpful study materials. Also, he gives extra credit after midterms that act as curves.
Robert is an alright teacher, his exams are rushed and make up most of your grade. Most definitely a weed-out class. unless you are an econ major, I would recommend taking this course at a CC.

While Econ 101 is a tough class in general, Professor McDonough makes lectures super engaging. I think he's hilarious and he explains things / uses examples in college student terminology. The tests are tough and feel super rushed, but I really liked this class and having him as a professor! Hands down best option for Econ 101.

Do NOT take Econ 101 with McDonough. His exams are very hard and make up 70% of your final grade. The final is 50% and it is the hardest exam of the semester. Robert's lectures are relativity pretty simple however his exams are astronomically harder. Take econ 101 with another professor. Robert is a condescending new grad PhD professor.

Do not listen to other reviewers about "putting in the work and getting a good grade." McDonough DOES NOT prepare his students for his exams that are worth 70% of the overall grade. No practice offered is to the caliber of his exam questions, and there are complexities to concepts that are not discussed in class. Do not take Econ with McDonough.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS AS A GEN-ED! This class was unnecessarily hard. Dr. McDonough is and amazing person and awesome lecturer but the tests were unfair. Not only did he talk loudly into his microphone for the majority of the time during exams, our class stayed averaging in the low 70s/ high 60s. It's also hard to find help outside of class.

As much as I enjoyed Robert as a person and felt he really loved the material, the exams in this class determine your grade and are far more difficult than the material we learn during lecture. The amount of studying needed to do well in this class was unreal. Reading the textbook closely is the best resource for learning the material!

I knew this class was going to be hard. Honestly the work load was very fair. The issue was I would go to peer tutoring, do extra problems, go to the econ help center, go to office hours and still could not do well on the exams. Honestly, the first and second exams were fair I just did not fully understand the material yet. The final was not fair.

While Robert is engaging, and LOVES Econ, the difficulty of exams (70% of grade) makes it very hard to get an A in the class. Exam averages were 72, 67, 69 for MT1, MT2, and Final respectively. The class ended up being curved 2%. I learned a lot, but the issue is class and recitation were like doing 2 + 2, and the exams were like discrete math.

Class is a lot of work but manageable if you put the time in and are willing to teach yourself. Succeeding depends on time spent outside of class trying to understand the concepts as the lectures will not prepare you for the exams. He barely mentions the textbook but it's the best resource outside of class. No curves except final grade scale.

As much as people say this class is impossible it's not. His midterms and the final were designed to trick you and lectures were not at all helpful for them, but keeping up with the textbook chapters definitely helps. Midterm averages were 73 and 67 before extra credit and final course grade average was an 80, although he curved the course 2 points

This was the hardest class I've taken at UNC so I would only recommend to students who are math/stats savvy or you will be lost like me. Prof Handy is very smart and a great lecturer and can answer any question you have in terms you can understand (for the most part). His curves are VERY generous to account for the difficulty of the class.

Great professor, but an incredibly challenging class I would not recommend to anyone but the smartest of students. Handy does a good job breaking the topics down, but for simpleton like me it doesn't matter. I am in so much pain because of this class and I feel like an actual bozo. Great professor but only if you have a brain, would not take again

A tough class, but once you get the hang of how everything flows it's manageable. He is a great professor - very organized, has clear guidelines, and offers a lot of resources for help. One of my favorite econ professors I've had even though stats isn't my strong suit.
bro got the magic of explaining things so clearly and organized

By far the most organized professor I've had at UNC. Gives incredibly clear guidelines, grades everything in a timely manner with plenty of opportunities for feedback. Provides plenty of resources for each exam and is always in his office happy to help his students. I love Christopher Handy.
Hard class but great professor.
Very fair class structure. Lots of materials available for studying. Tests were very similar to the practice he gave and he makes the material very easy to follow throughout the semester.
Clear and to-the-point teaching style which is needed for this course content, have flexibility regarding the grading of homework and exams

Econ 400 is a hard class, but Professor Handy is not a bad teacher. He does his best to make the information digestible, and honestly, you just have to push through how hard it is and be willing to work and use his resources as much as you can and you'll be fine.

Handy is an awesome guy with a great personality. My grade was definitely a lack of understanding on my part, and not his fault. Was a very difficult class, never scored above a 60 on any of the tests. Curve saved me.

Lectures were not interesting in the slightest. Homework was difficult, but he held office hours in the econ aid center and would answer any questions. Mostly a boring class and requires prior statistics knowledge to keep up with how quickly he goes through topics. 200 person lecture with no connection to the professor. Curve is lifesaving.

Handy provides every resource needed to succeed in a moderately challenging class. Tests are tricky but fair, and homework load is reasonable (1 assignment/week takes ~2/3 hours). Watch the couple of 5/10 min pre-class vids he gives before class and don't chatgpt every single hw like half the people and it's really straightforward.

Assignment workload was high. His organisation is great, records his lectures, posts worked solutions, good attention to detail. Not sure why there are 1 star reviews. If you've done stats before it's not a difficult course but hard to score high as small mistakes are costly. He's quite flexible and lenient, gives partial credit for wrong MCQ's.

Handy is one of the most organized Econ professors out there. He makes studying so easy and has so many different resources that people can take advantage of to learn, and even takes the time to answer every single online question a person will post. He breaks down hard concepts and actually makes them understandable.

This course is basically an intro stats course (like AP stats). Dr. Handy is very good at explaining things clearly in a way easy to understand. He is very knowledgeable, approable, kind, and generous about grades. All of the class materials are extremely well-organized.

I'm not sure if it was because i've never taken any type of statistics class before, but I did not follow a single thing he said. The lectures felt really long and the exams were hard. He seems very nice tho. I would NOT recommend taking this class if you have never taken a statistics class before. There should be a stats pre-req for this course.

Do yourself a favor and do not take this class with him. TAs are 100% writing the good ratings. I will say he is smart, like every other professor here, but he is an awful lecturer and purposely makes the exams hard by trying to trick you. Least favorite class I have ever taken here.

I'm honestly confused how he has good reviews on here. His lectures are absolutely terrible and he makes the exams ridiculously hard. He may curve the class, but it doesn't feel like you are actually achieving anything when you are just relying on the curve. Terrible.
