Prof. Handy is a great teacher who made difficult material in ECON 400 easy to understand. His tests are fair and reflect homework and in class activities. Be sure to take advantage of his videos explaining concepts and come to class prepared or you may feel overwhelmed. The lecture moves quickly into polls as he expects you have watched the videos

Most organized professor I've ever had. Provides so many resources to help you succeed. The content can be conceptually tough but he wants to see you suceed and is very accessible for questions. Tests are fair and grading criteria is fair/straightforward. Definitely would recommend. Students that have taken any stats class before have advantage.

Very straightforward lectures - tells you what you need to know! Very reasonable grading policy, and give extra credit. Love his class and genuinely cares about each student (answers all your online questions if you are confused)

Professor Handy is approachable and kind but also highly organized and skilled as a professor. He provides numerous resources to help students succeed in this course and is happy to answer questions outside of class.
Handy was a good professor, 400 is just really difficult material. He does typically curve pretty significantly at the end of the semester.
Really terrible. The lecture is too terrible

Brutal class. Lectures are confusing and hard to follow—I stopped paying attention and just taught myself after class. Office hours helped, but I waited too long. Pre-class videos and the textbook are useless. Exams are awful and nothing like the practice, which has 150+ separate questions and is super tough. Only the curve saved me.

I have taken other classes that had content which overlapped with 400, and Professor Handy was able to explain concepts I struggled with before in a clear and concise way. He is clearly familiar with learning methods (unlike some professors who are an expert in the subject but don't know how to teach it). Very willing to help if you are confused.

If you're not particularly strong in math the course is exceptionally difficult. Handy is an amazing speaker who is always available through various resources, I enjoyed lectures even if it made no sense. Final grade curve is very generous, I think a C+ was a 55 most recently. If you're looking for more application based info, take handys course.

Handy is a very good econ professor; his class and Canvas page are organized well, making studying for exams easy and structured. Lectures are nothing special, and the homework can be a bit long, but most of the grade comes from exams. His study guide is very helpful and he CURVES so dont be scared by the low averages my grade went from a C to a B.

He makes information very accessible but you really have to stay caught up and engaged in all materials to do slightly well on exams. Certain exams can be different from practice problems just study way ahead of time!!
One of the GOAT in the ECON department. He is always patient with students. He curved a lot for your final grade. I got an 82 for it, and it is an A-.

Took 470 after also taking 400 with Handy. 470 is much harder but he does a good job of explaining content as clearly as possible - one of the most articulate econ professors. He records lectures so it's helpful to go back and watch them to review. He communicates well with his students and is very accessible on CampusWire. His curve is generous.

Any class that Handy is teaching is going to be hard, but he is the most organized and helpful professor in the econ department. His lectures can get boring, but he doesn't waste time outside of stuff you genuinely need to know or review.
Great professor, very hard class

I wouldn't say his lectures are engaging, but he is very good at making the content digestible. He answers questions regardless of how stupid it was, and is accessible outside of class. Pay attention, do practice problems, and go to recitation. Easier if you took AP Stat. Class gets harder as it goes though so you have to stay locked.
Honestly about as difficult as I expected a more upper level econ class to be, not unfair at all, but you have to do the homework and study for the exams to do decent overall
straight to the point, solid professor
Goated prof

Prof. Handy is an awesome professor. Homeworks and in-class examples were consistent with test material, and he did a fantastic job explaining the material. He also curves your final grade in the class, not to mention has generous grading thresholds. If you put the work in and go to class you will not only learn a lot, but do well in the class.

Not sure if it's just the material, but nothing Handy said made sense. He seems like a really nice guy but I was lost when it came to the content - and so were my friends in the class. We still managed to get pretty good grades, but going into 470 I am concerned about my level of understanding.

Memorizing how to use the equation sheet can get you an A but it will be a lot more work than if you just sit and think about what's really going on with the math. Handy is very good at decyphering students' questions.
This guy is a chiller. He loves econometrics and I felt engaged in the content, somehow. Hard class, just put some effort in.

Handy is super accessible on campuswire which is really helpful. Once the homework assignments start they never end. Watch the pre class videos so you don't get lost in lecture, but he pauses lecture to ask for questions, and he's available during office hours. Exams are fair and practice problems are on par with exam difficulty. Lovely curve!
Professor Handy's class can be challenging, but his thoughtful approach and helpful resources like Campuswire make it manageable. unstuck ai was a great study aid alongside the practice problems.
Unless you've completely dropped the ball, you will pass. I did the absolute bare minimum, pass failed the class, and scraped by with a PS on the transcript. HEAVY curve. Nice guy. You will be okay.
Good professor

Econ 400 is a hard class, but Professor Handy makes it doable. His lectures are nothing crazy or exciting, but he covers the material that will be on exams. He also gives sooo many practice problems which is super helpful. Do those and you'll be fine!

Two midterms, 20% each, final 30%, extra 10% for highest exam, 5% participation, 15% homework. HWs included R-studio which made them difficult. Watch pre-class videos to understand content or else you'll be lost in class. Posts 40-question exam reviews before each exam but almost too long to be helpful. Huge curve at end bc of low averages.
Handy is the peak

Dr. Handy is my favorite professor I've had since being at UNC. He's very clear with expectations and lets us know plainly how we can succeed. His pre-class videos are helpful so you can work on just practice problems in class. The formula sheet is very helpful and he is easy to reach on CampusWire. I'm excited to take another class with Dr. Handy!

He's a good professor but lectures can be a bit boring. I kind of just suck generally with numbers so look at pre-class videos they're very helpful. Textbook is good but take it with a grain of salt when reading it. Would take again but be prepared for a hard class if you haven't taken AP Stats or STOR-155
Handy is a very reasonable person, he curves everyone's grades at the end of the semester, very clear lectures, highly recommended ECON professor!

Dr. Handy explains content clearly and thoroughly in lectures, and even provides pre-class videos that cover the material in brief. The pace of the class is quick, but if you've taken AP Stats or STOR 155 there isn't much new content. Test averages were mid-70s despite the tests covering similar content to class and the review materials.

Somehow manages to make the material harder than it is. Homework can be a bit difficult and definitely requires studying outside of class. Tests are basically the same as homework in terms of difficulty, so if you struggle on homework you will struggle on the tests.

Class makes me feel like I'm being put to sleep. The professor talks for 90 minutes, yet I leave more confused. I've turned to Khan Academy and The Organic Chemistry Tour for help. When I'm lost, I can't even ask questions because I have no idea what he's talking about. He rambles on without engaging. He's not cut out to teach, more like a tutor.

Dr. Handy is my favorite. I do not have a strong background in math, but my grades are decent because I spend over 6 hours on class each week, not including the lecture. Both 400 and 470 are quite challenging, but if you want an A, the time you invest in studying will pay off. Besides, he is very caring, encouraging, responds quickly on campuswire.
Great professor, the class itself isnt that hard either but Professor Handy is by far the best professor I've had here at UNC, and his grading is clear and he curves the class as well.

Great professor. His arms can be slightly distracting but that is okay. He curves at the end because I definitely did notttt get an actual B, I'll tell you that. All of the resources to get an A are there, he gives videos to watch before lectures, practice exams, practice homework, all of the grading keys. I just fell off mid semester lol

Dr. Handy objectively lays everything out properly, but misses the "engaging" mark. Between spoonfeeding us coding content and dropping two of six assignments, I found myself ignoring the class until exams. Handy comes across as a robot presenting his same research papers with a few trick questions on repeat. Mildly more difficult 400 downgrade.

I have had Dr. Handy twice, and I wish I could take more. He is kind and fair, and while his class is hard, he acknowledges that we are all upper-level econ students and curves final grades heavily to reflect that. His lectures are well-designed so students can best grasp the material. He is also so intelligent and can answer every question well.

I enjoyed learning under Professor Handy for both ECON 400 and 470. He teaches remarkably well, frequently pausing during lectures to see if any student has questions. He is also very responsive on CampusWire, always answering students' questions. The practice problems he offered before every exam were very helpful in succeeding in his courses!

Chris Handy is a moral and altruistic person. He shows that a man can be absolutely shredded and embrace a nerdy fascination with economics. What distinguishes Dr. Handy from his contemporaries is his infectious sense of humor; He's undeniably witty. His ability to spread laughter effortlessly is a rare and invaluable gift. Do the practice tests!
Chris is a great professor, yet the classes he teaches have hard material. He cares about students' success and will curve the grades to adjust to the class distribution.

Genuinely god bless this man, his class is ROUGH you will have to pay attention and take notes to learn the concepts. BUT there's only 6 homework and 3 tests throughout the whole class. AND he curves the final grades so that the average course grade is in the middle of the 'B' range and adjusts grades accordingly #stats. He is EXTREMELY helpful.
G.O.D.
So nice professor, well-structured class materials and willing to take his class again!

One of the best professors I've had. Despite challenging material, he makes topics digestible. He is accessible (Campuswire) and answers questions in a way that students (not just economic experts) can understand. Exams are challenging but representative of class material (lots of practice problems). Attend office hours for help on assignments.

Dr. Handy is great with explaining the topics in this difficult course and being available through office hours, after class, and on Campuswire to answer any questions you might have. While it can seem to be boring, he does a good job of using real-life studies and examples to make econometrics more meaningful.

Professor Handy is a great professor who puts a lot of effort into teaching this course and gives us a lot of practice material as well. However, the content is hard and the exams were not easy. But he is very accessible outside of class and always does his best to answer questions when asked. Would definitely take a class with him again.

He was a great professor. Super accomodating and no questions were stupid to him which was great. I personally did not use all the resources available like his office hours, but I'm sure they would've been great. He was really quick to reply on campuswire which was a life saver. You can tell he really wants us to succeeed. Would 100% take again.

Professor Handy is by far my favorite econ professor. His willingness to work with his students and adjust exam difficulty/curve is greatly appreciated. Lectures are thorough and he provides plenty of resources. 470 is definitely a hard class, but as long as you put in the effort, there's no reason you can't learn a bunch and get a good grade.
Really hard content. Solid teacher. Sligthly overrated but I liked him.
Couldn't pay that much attention to stats bc I was distracted by his shoulders

Everyone LOVES and is OBSESSED WITH Chris Handy. The way he structured 400 made a difficult class much more digestible. He offered plenty of resources to help students learn, was very organized, and was generous with the curve at the end. I'm walking away from 400 with a strong foundation in statistics and I highly recommend taking a class w/ him!

Awesome professor and one of my favorite classes this semester. The smaller class size gives a lot more ops to ask questions imo!

The class is weighed heavily on exams. But don't be scared because they reflect the class material and are fair. He's knowledgeable and super willing to answer any questions to help you out. Take this class if you can!

Great professor who cares about his students but the course itself is kind of dry. Exams were a lot tougher/more conceptual than in-class problems and homework assignments, so make use of office hours if you can!

This class was super tough but Professor Handy is a great teacher. He does videos that you must watch before class that are about 15 minutes or so before each class then goes back over it in class alongside practice problems. He does a curve at the end of the class as the tests are very hard. Overall just a great teacher teaching a tough course.

ECON400 is a hard class but Prof Handy gives you tons of practice problems and materials to succeed. He's very accessible outside class with Campuswire. Performance on exams is pretty low, with class averages being around 70/71, but he curves the course at the end of the semester to compensate. Overall I  would recommend him for this course!

Prof Handy clearly cares about teaching his students.  This class was very difficult for me and my performance was poor, although I can really only blame myself.  If you want to learn this subject I would recommend taking this class but you will probably need to put in a decent amount of effort.

Great professor, and loves statistics. it's just a hard class. He wants you to do well, and all the resources are there, you just have to put in the work. But don't miss an exam, even for a legitimate reason, you can't make it up and that puts a lot of pressure on the final. but I found this class very interesting and would take it again.
Great professor. Well structure course. Lots of help and practice problems. Cares about students' success.

ECON 400 is neither an easy course nor really an economics course as it is more Statistics Part 2 but Handy is a great professor who explains things well and is incredibly accessible outside of class and on campus wire. Make sure you put the work in and use your resources as the class is difficult but manageable.

ECON 400 is a tough subject but he makes it so digestable and is excellent at explaining every topic.
Cares so much about students and outstandingly organized and helpful teacher. Great guy.

I was dreading taking 400 because I'vge heard awful things about 400 and 470 but this was easily one of my favorite classes this semester because of handy. I LOVE HIM. He is incredibly kind and intelligent and does his best to teach each concept in several ways ti appeal to diff students' learning styles. I hope he has the best life ever
He is incredibly organized, and he gives you all the resources you need to succeed. All you need to do is put in the effort. Just take his class.

Definitely one of the hardest classes I've taken at UNC. Show up to the lectures, stay on top of the material, and you will be fine. Watch the pre-recorded videos before class. I'd highly recommend doing all of the practice problems before exams as well as redoing the homework; they prepare you best for what you might see on the exam.

Prof Handy is a knowledgable and caring professor, and his grading is very fair, with a generous curve for final grades. His lectures are extremely easy to follow, and are very clear and straightforward. The homework and exam practice problems are very representative of the exams, so if you do those, you'll likely do well in the class.

This class wasn't bad, but I found it more challenging because there was less intuitive content and more data science heavy. Econ concepts that I normally find interesting weren't a big part of the course. The exams were pretty challenging, definitely study a lot and do practice problems and redo homework. Caring guy though and very accessible.
470 is a very difficult class, but Handy is a great professor. Was very generous with curves and final grade cutoffs. Also was very accessible outside of class.

Best lecturer I've ever had. He is so clear, concise and offers lots of practice. You can tell he's an expert in the subject and is really passionate too. He is very easy to reach outside of class and on Campuswire. The topics on midterm 2 can be a little confusing but asking questions in recitation and doing practice in EconAid Center really help.

Handy is a nice guy and a decent lecturer; however, his exams were extremely hard to the extent that he will add up to 10 adjustment points to each Midterm and then add something like a 10% curve for your final grade, and still it would not be enough for you to get an A-. Be prepared to dedicate a LOT of your time to this class as it will be tough.
Nice professor, but a tough class. He is super inspirational, caring, and accessible, definitely take ECON470 with him too.

The class is built for you to succeed you just have to try. I made the mistake of not trying for the first part and it almost cost me a D. He puts so much effort and shows that he really cares. Tests are worth a lot and make sure to do the homework, it's a lot like the test.

470 can be confusing content but Handy does the best possible job explaining it and is always available to answer questions, the campus wire platform he uses is especially helpful. It's not the easiest class but if you have a math background it will be much easier. Tests could be challenging but there was a generous curve applied at the end.

Chris Handy is a kind, gentle, and extremely knowledgeable professor. I have taken both Econ 400 and 470 with this gem of a human being. While 470 remains the hardest class I have ever taken in my life, he has done absolutely everything to help me, and I truly appreciate him. Take his class if you can, you will not be disappointed.

I LOVED this professor! I honestly don't know how he doesn't have a higher rating. His lectures were great and easy to follow, and he always allowed you to ask questions in class. Yes, tests and assignments were hard, but ECON-400 is a hard class. Nothing insane, especially with how accessible he is outside of class.

Great professor, had very clear lectures, and a much better choice than Guilkey. If you did the pre class notes you came into class with everything you needed to do that class' problems. Never went to office hours but any question that I asked on campuswire was answered fairly quickly by him or a ULA

The professor is nice. I slept in his class, but he still treated me well. And the class material is not hard as long as you watch the pre-class videos and do the homework carefully. Though the attendance is counted, the class has recordings. I really cannot understand why there are students who dislike the class...

Hard class-be sure to always do the pre-class vids and take good notes. He's a good professor (despite overestimating our background knowledge on topics at times) and really strives to give everyone all the tools to succeed. Great guy. Keep up w the classes and go to TAs for help on hw.

Difficult material but not due to Professor Handy. The class is built for you to succeed but you need to stay engaged. Lots of examples and problems during class. Only weird thing is you have to use R code for homework assignments and he doesn't really teach you how to use it.

Dr. Handy is one of the best professors in UNC. He cares about his students and uses interesting examples in class. Stat class is unsurprisingly hard but it is worthy at the end. I would definitely take his other advanced econ class. Highly recommend!

I have taken 420, 425, 525, and 490 with Dr. Roark. He's the best professor I've had in my time at UNC. The QFE is the most valuable experience I've had in the department. I would recommend taking any class with Dr. Roark.
Roark's QFE is the most valuable program in the econ department

Professor Roark is great! I've had him for both 420 & 425. He is generous with curves, accessible, and provides PLENTY of test prep. There are weekly assignments, but he will sometimes extend deadlines. Had an injury I was out for a month for, so he met with me via zoom to keep up. Hard content, but if you do hw will do fine. Take with Roark!

I like this better than 420, and he's genuinely a really nice guy which makes it a lot better. It isn't super easy content, but my complaint is really just that he makes the homework sometimes unnecessarily hard. One question will be completely fine, easy even, and then the next has math so convoluted that a TI-84 can't process it. Just annoying.

I generally liked Roark. The structure of the class was logical, and content built so by the end I still remembered early stuff for the final. It's not a super easy class, but I preferred it to 410 and thought it was a little more intuitive. Lots of graphs, and some math like derivatives and iffy algebra. I did feel like it got harder throughout.

I did not enjoy 420 with Dr. Roark. Lectures are quite boring and there are plenty of mistakes on his slides. We also did't solve a lot of practice questions and mostly focused on theories. Midterms 1 and 2 were fine, but the final exam was extremely difficult and tanked my grade. Homework grading is quite harsh as well.

Roark is a caring professor and the goat grading-wise, but I'm not sure I love his teaching style. He's clearly a macro expert. However, during lectures he often skipped math steps or implicit assumptions about the concepts he was teaching, which made it difficult to follow. I had to become an EconAid warrior and teach myself some concepts.

Dr. Roark is a great person; he cares about his students, and it shows throughout his class. However, his lectures are heavily based on the theory of Macro, and he does not explain much of the math behind the theory. The exams are difficult, but his grading scale makes the class easy to pass. Be prepared to teach yourself some of the concepts.

Roark is an expert in this field and I enjoyed this more than 420! I'm in QFE so I'll be taking 525 with him next semester too. Exams are hard and there is only one midterm. He drops one problem set and the last one is graded for completion. Group investment project which is a grade booster but also annoying to deal with if you have bad groupmates.
Slides, problem wording, and grading criteria were super confusing.

Roark is a super nice guy and very helpful. Only gripe is that he spent a lot of time on topics which weren't tested at times which meant some important concepts (like fed policy) were rushed. 

Overall the exams are difficult but doable. You have to be proactive and address uncertainties early or you will fall behind.

This guy is a total beast. Very generous with curves and willing to answer any question. Very available to students and honestly just an expert at macro. Don't know why I got on the final but very easy to do well if you put in some effort

Prof. Roark can be a little bit disorganized and confusing at times, but he is a super nice guy whose humor is often misunderstood. If you are engaged in this class and ask questions when things become unclear you will succeed. Definitely not an easy class, but there is no reason to avoid Roark when signing up. Making friends in class will help.
The only people who liked this class are the ones who do not care about their grades. I actually had a stroke trying to understand all the contradictory points in the materials.
he does a good job of making a bad class ok. he wants everyone to succeed and came to our office hours despite being sick.

IM WRITING THIS AS IM STUDYING FOR MY FINAL EXAM. PLS DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WITH HIM. Chris is a chill person and hes funny but his lectures are SO UNORGANIZED. I actually studied so hard for the midterm but the materials he gave were super confusing and I got a B. Compared to Chris Handy and MSA, this class was x100000 more unorganized.

Very disorganized class, no clear grading expectations, and very passive aggresive with students. Thinks he's funny (he's not). The class itself is an amalgamation of idiosyncratic economic teaching that is not found anywhere but his lecture hall, so good luck studying outside of class. However, curve is forgiving. Overall just a "meh" class.
Many self-contradictory points on the slides...
Was a sleeper class. Not that much work, just study problem sets before exams.

Dr. Roark is a fun professor and an overall good guy. Highly recommend going to office hours regularly (Roark or TA/ULA) to discuss homework questions and exam review material, as 420 can be unintuitive sometimes. Class is curved generously so that the median is a B+. Biweekly assignments + textbook readings not required ⇒ relatively light workload

Professor Roark is the best! He really cares about his students' learning and success– don't be afraid of this class if you take it with him. It's also curved so much and he posts a lot of practice tests and past exams. Super funny.

Dr. Roark's lectures are a little messy and hard to follow and his multiple choice grading is frustrating. But macro is just not intuitive, and I think that's why 420 is so challenging. His curve is generous though, and he is accessible outside of class in office hours and on CampusWire. He answers questions well in class.

Would give 0/5 if I could. Bad lectures, confusing MC questions with the worst grading system for them ever, passive-aggressive, unhelpful TAs and office hours, need I say more? If you have any reason to take this class, take it with another prof if possible. You will save both your GPA and your life.

He is a super personable professor. Really cares about student learning and wants us to succeed. The curve (already in the syllabus) is really generous. Its a hard class but the practice exams he gave were super similar to the actual exams, a lot of it is a matter of reasoning through a problem which was fun

I think some of these reviews, while containing valid criticisms, are a bit harsh. Yeah, he does make a decent amount of mistakes, but he's pretty flexible with deadlines and shifts them around to account for errors on his end. The curve is pretty generous as well, and I personally didn't find this course as taxing as 410. Also a personable dude.
Ngl I think people give him 1 just because they screwed up their exams. Overall a nice and approachable guy with some humor. Helps are available on campuswire and Econ aid center.
It is a difficult class, but Roark and the ULAs and TAs want to help you pass and do well. Just use the practice material, and you will do fine.

grading scale isn't terrible like some other Econ courses, decent guy just comes across as odd sometimes. never went to office hours but am currently passing with an ok grade so not the worst class just do the practice exams he gives they're almost identical to the actual ones. also relearn algebra tricks because its heavy on the exams sometimes.

Funny how as soon as a 1/5 rating appears, it's followed by at least two 5/5s to inflate the overall rating. If it's not obvious enough, those 5/5s are from trolls, or the few people who actually liked this class. 

Pros: Responds to CampusWire questions quickly
Cons: Arrogant, terrible grading system, near useless lectures, mistakes EVERYWHERE

Really hard class, but not impossible. Roark cares about his students, he can get frustrated when people are not understanding concepts, but this is fair since his office hours are usually pretty empty...if you are struggling go get help!!! The econ aid center almost always has someone to help with 420.
This class is not as difficult as people make it seem. It is a lot of work, but it is manageable, and tests are curved if people struggle.
Really kind, cares about his job and his students. It is a hard class, as all econ classes at UNC are, but Roark does a great job being available for students and is always patient and respectful.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS! If you need to take this class, take it over the summer with literally anyone else.

Didn't curve any tests when I had him. Awful wording on HW and test questions. MC system is the worst I have ever seen. Very passive aggressive and will not hesistate to humiliate you in front of the whole class for things you didn't even do.

didnt like his teaching methods, his "multiple choice" grading is the worst I've ever seen and the lectures and slideshows don't help that much without added notes and teachings on top of it. didn't enjoy the class at all but I managed to pass it, will not retake with roark ever again.

I loved this class and I love Chris, had him for 420 as well and that was much harder for me since it was a lot less intuitive. Graded by 6 homeworks (1dropped, 1 for completion), a midterm, final, and an easy prospectus project.

Roark is a chill guy, he's pretty understanding and fair when it comes to grading, this course is just hard to perform well in for a lot of students. Make sure to do practice problem sets/exams before tests and you should be fine. Go to office hours and go to class!

I think he gets way too much hate tbh. Had him for 420, and I think the content in that class is just not intuitive hence the ratings... but he was awesome for 425! Super active on CampusWire and made a 3:30 class bearable. While he does make a lot of /mistakes, he's pretty chill about correcting them and willing to help clarify anything confusing.

Difficult exams with a final worth 35% of your grade. The slides are incomprehensible sometimes and Roark would often make mistakes whether it be the answer keys, slide information, or hw question wording. He seems to know what he's talking about but has difficulty relaying the info. He can be extremely passive aggressive when answering questions.

Roark really cares about students engaging with and learning the material. He is very accessible and wants to help. The investment project is super fun and a grade booster. The tests are as to be expected, but if you can do the problem sets then you will be fine, utilize the practice sets. Don't get the textbook it wasn't necessary.
I loved this class! Learned a lot and he really cares about students. Lenient with deadlines and just wanted us to participate. Not easy exams, but to be expected in upper level Econ.

Roark got upset with our lecture for not being enthusiastic enough (mind you - it was during a semester when many students' families were suffering in W. North Carolina). Tests were pretty hard and it took months for homework grades to be returned so you couldn't really use those to study. He lets you drop a couple hw grades though

Don't really get the other reviews. I sat on my phone pretty much every day and learned through the slides and homework. Wound up with mid 90s on just about everything.

I thought he was entertaining and was able to communicate well. His slides and other resources (i.e. previous hws) were everything I needed. Generally don't do well in econ either.

Overall lectures are confusing, problem sets only minimally help solidify concepts taught in lectures, and his responses to questions on campuswire are often vague. Chill guy but not great at helping to understand material which is already difficult. Takes up time trying to be funny at least once every lecture but speeds through difficult concepts.

Very nice and funny guy but something about his teaching style just didn't click with me. I often left class feeling even more confused. Answers questions but, again, answers just didn't usually click, which is dangerous in a class like 420 where the material is hard to wrap your head around. EconAid Center was also unhelpful, unfortunately.
Get ready for Mr. Grumpy.-and by that the most entertaining and quirky professor you'll ever have. Can't believe this guy is so polarizing, his lectures are straight comedy.
I kid you not I've had to copy-paste his slides into ChatGPT with the prompt "Reword to be more clear and easier to understand" at least a hundred times.

Good guy and it's obvious he tries, but his lecture slides are genuinely the worst slides I have ever seen in my entire life. They are border-line indecipherable and are rarely helpful for studying. If you're unlucky enough to miss a lecture, you might as well just not try to understand the material you missed because the slides won't help at all.
Genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. And not a good person either

He has to curve the class by 10-20 points at the end of the semester because everyone performs so poorly. Homeworks are insanely hard and lectures are comprised of bullet point slides that are extremely hard to follow. I recommend just ignoring anything in lecture and teaching yourself. The overall quality of this class is horrendous.

I'm a micro person, so class was kinda hard but not too bad. Lectures weren't helpful, too fast, not recorded, didn't really explain things well. STILL don't know half of my HW grades. Roark was kinda condescending and tried to be relatable but it was just a bit weird. Seems like a fine guy, but teaching style didn't work for me

Roark is an awesome guy, hard to get close to him in a 200 person class, but he's super easy to talk to and is funny/down to earth. Tests aren't too difficult compared to content, averages were in the B range. ECON aid center is super helpful.

His lectures are really bad. The slides aren't easy to follow on your own, he moves way too fast, and then will randomly ramble about nothing for 5 minutes. It's honestly easier to just not pay attention in class and try to figure out the homework on your own, vs trying to use what you learned from his lectures to do the homework.

Chris is a great guy, really cares about all his students and their success. Macro was very tough for me, not as easy to conceptualize as micro. I made a 42 on the first exam and finished with a B-. If you put in the work, you can easily make an A.

Dr. Roark is my favorite professor in the econ department. He is super accessible outside of class, curves generously, and his exams reflect the in-class practice problems and homework sets. It is also clear he really cares about his students, and I found him to be generally pretty funny. He made class engaging and worthwhile.

Professor Roark is great. I was really struggling in this course and was failing for first 12 weeks, ended up finishing with a C+. Roark assured me that as long as I did my best, I would pass the class. Very nice professor who wants the best for his students!

Prof Roark does a decent job of explaining things but could be a lot more concise and clear in his explanations. Problem sets were easy enough and tests were very fair and closely resembled problem sets and practice exams.

Roark genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them succeed, he gives helpful and quick responses on Campuswire, all of his exam questions pull from concepts you will have seen on a real/practice problem set, which have useful answers and grading criteria. TA's also give helpful feedback for psets, go to office hours and ask questions!

Super smart guy, not the best professor. Can be rude sometimes when you ask questions but he still likes when people engage in lecture. If you are afraid of taking this class like I was, don't be. Dr. Roark curves GENEROUSLY on exams. My best advice would be to complete entire problem sets in TA/ULA office hours!!!

I found this class to be comparable to 410, its a lot of material that econ majors need to know to succeed. Roark does his best to give lectures and problem sets designed to teach more than we will be tested on so we have the best chance of success. Roark is funny, engaging, and intelligent, I enjoyed his lectures, and found office hours useful.

I've taken 3 courses with Roark (420, 425, 525/493) and he's a good professor. He gives engaging lectures, though sometimes confusing, and he's very personable. He designed a good curriculum for this class that reinforced concepts from 425 and built new skills, such as research and programming. Overall, this is an interesting and useful course.

I don't know if he personally understand what he was talking about. Going to office hour will just make you more confused. He was inconsistent with what he said, which is the key why so many people though this class was hard.

Overall he is a great professor, but sometimes the way he explained was really confusing. I have 17 credits this semester but i spent nearly all my free time with this course. it's hard to get an A, but A- is easy because you got it when overall grade was 86

Professor Roark is a solid professor who I think has gotten a lot better considering the reviews for him the past few semesters. He is a bit all over the place at times and his problem sets can be very tricky and graded a bit harshly. However he makes up for it with the midterms being a lot easier and straightforward (which he himself admits).

He's a definitely qualified professor as in he knows what he's talking about conceptually, but the way he formats and words his slides can give you a massive headache. You'll also have to read through some grammatical errors that can sometimes make learning the material more frustrating.
So far best pf in econ department

Dr. Roark is a little scatterbrained and his lectures move quickly. Yet, he's a great person who cares about his teaching. Homeworks are difficult, yet the tests are relatively easy (he even admits that). He's accessible at office hours which helps. Just work in groups on assignments and he gives a lot of practice problems that help for exams.

Roark is a great guy and a great professor. 420 is hard, but it's clear that he really wants all of his students to succeed. He's super funny and accessible. Just make sure you study a lot for exams and do as many practice problems as you can. You don't really need the textbook because his powerpoints are pretty comprehensive.

Roark cares a lot about his students and has been restructuring his class to make it as fair and manageable as possible. His exams are hard and you will have to study a LOT, but if you have this expectation going into it, you will be okay. Definitely utilize campuswire and your ULA's. Don't fall behind and ask him questions, he wants to help.

Prof. Roark genuinely wants you to do good. He assigns weekly problem sets + there are 2 midterms and a final. You need a very holistic understanding of the material to do good on his exams. If you utilize practice questions, past papers and attend class, you'll do fine. He also answers every Campuswire question he gets, and curves generously.

The second half of this semester is more difficult than the first half, but still doable. I unfortunately was sick for three weeks and fell behind in all my classes. There are plenty of practice resources. He tries his best to help you but the class is just too big for only one professor. The ULAs are your best resources.

I second the wholesome sentiment and enjoyed generous curves, but too many mistakes on in-class examples and problem sets for me to feel Roark is an authority. Just teach yourself the content from more thorough sources and hope the content transfers. Encouraging "game theory" on multiple choice is also goofy.

Roark is nice, but class is Hard with a capital H. Go to office hours to compare PS and USE CAMPUSWIRE! He answers so fast basically texting him. Multiple choice grading system SUCKSSSS. Never got above a 33% on an MC section. 54 on first midterm, and ~70% on the others, still ended with a B. Big overall curve. Good luck econ majors stay strong.

For Econ 420 you should review the slides and all relevant practice problems (he gives past problem sets and exams for review prior to each test). Additionally the textbook is helpful if you are confused on a topic and need a more in depth explanation, however he does not completely follow the textbook and to excel in the course it is not required.

He's a caring prof and explains things pretty clearly. The material can be challenging and confusing, but he's always willing to help. The exams can be difficult, and sometimes there are problems that feel unfairly difficult (i.e. we never did such difficult problems in homework), but if everyone does poorly, he curves, so don't stress.

He's a great professor who clearly knows his stuff. He's very funny, very accessible, and kind to everyone. The class is by no means easy, but he offers a generous curve. The workload is relatively light, but it is in your best interest to study throughout the semester.

Roark is the saving grace of UNCs econ department and one of few professor I look forward to taking again. He is good at explaining concepts although he can sometimes make things more complex than they need to be. He is extremely helpful and responsive via email/office hours/campus wire and genuinely wants students to do well. Also pretty funny.

Roark is a genuinely nice guy and cares a lot. I'll be honest though, his natural teaching abilities are pretty horrid. He has extreme difficulties explaining simple concepts, and most of the time comes off as condescending/sarcastic when he isn't even trying to. He makes this class more difficult than it needs to be but that's the whole department

Nice Guy. That being said, on test reviews and during tests there is stuff that wasn't really in the lecture. He tests for a complete understanding of the material. But, homework is not like this. He doesn't teach the understanding of the concepts well. Tests are harder than the reviews and problem sets by a good margin which is hard to study for.

Good guy. Course Material is tough and he was a fairly new professor when I took the class. You can tell he continues to grow and learn the more he teaches the material. ULAs were helpful. Was accommodating and held office hours for assignments. Generous curve at the end of the semester, so don't panic.

Roark is a good professor, and he really does care about his students. Very reasonable grading policies and problem sets, but the class is really hard (especially if you have no experience with the stock market/finance industry). Great guy, difficult class.

This classes' topics build on each other throughout the semester. If you get lost in the first units then the remainder will be more difficult to grasp. Roark cares about seeing you succeed, the class is just difficult for most people. Make sure that if you don't understand something that you take the time to get help or figure it out.

Excellent professor, knowledgeable and caring. The class is simply the hardest I have ever taken. Roark does his best to bring the material to the students. He is funny and wants to cut everyone a break, but at the end of the day it is still Intermediate Macro.

Makes the class way harder than it needs to be. Homeworks are overly complicated and take hours to complete. Constantly makes mistakes in lectures and on answer keys. Can be hard to follow at times during lectures. Also will round some students grades up and not others. Nice guy besides all that though.

The course itself has difficult concepts but as a professor, he is really great and understanding. He always wants to make sure we understand the material which is nice. His HW was harder than the exams.

Honestly, the material itself isn't that hard, but they he teaches it makes it much harder. There were moments where the same info was presented differently during the semester, which seriously confused me on the final. Prof Roark is a decent lecturer, however, I would recommend looking for alternatives for this credit if you want a good grade.

Great guy, one of my favorite professors in the econ department. The content in 425 is interesting although sometimes lectures can get boring and seem overcomplicated. Really straight forward grader though, and the work load is super manageable. Only downside is how long it takes for things to be graded. Overall loved Roark though, nicest guy.

Genuinely the best econ prof. I've ever had, I cannot write a review that does him justice. He's insanely nice, funny, and accessible, and is the first prof. I've had that has actually made sense regarding the material. 8 problem sets (2 lowest are dropped), 2 midterms, and a final. I would literally take every class with him if I could!

You can tell that Chris genuinely cares about the success of his students and I haven't felt this seen by a professor before but I really WISH he would change his multiple choice rule. Some MC questions have multiple answers but you can't get half credit if you get one right and one wrong and it is so absurd

Professor Roark is a very nice and funny guy who has the bad fortune of teaching a very difficult class. Though I feel that he occasionally struggled to explain concepts in class, he is accessible outside of class and easy to ask for help. Above all, I feel that he wants his students to succeed.

Chill dude but moves a bit fast and skips steps in examples, though outside of class he's super accessible and gives great explanations. Main concern was that most of his MC questions have 2 right answers and you have to get both for full credit, and one answer is usually far more convoluted than the other. He's the only prof I've seen do this.

Roark is a good professor and a very reasonable person. He uses Campuswire extensively and will answer messages and questions very quickly online, which is helpful when completing the (very difficult) homeworks or studying for the exams. The lectures can move fast, but you can always ask clarifying questions later.
just took the final and oh my god. Last semester reviews were right that the final will kill you. His personality is the only reason I'm giving him a nice review because that final was not very nice.

Chris genuinely cares about us and he's the most accessible prof I've had so far at UNC. His personality makes even macro bearable to learn
He's a really good prof but the material is still pretty hard you have to spend a fair amount of time out of class to get a good understanding 
My one complaint is the exams are DAMN hard. Very painful. Very.

Chris is the man. The content is hard and sometimes I blame him for making it overcomplicated, but overall hes such a genuinely good guy with a great sense of humor. I'll miss his presence in the classroom. 
Also he makes up for the difficulty of the class with a great curve so I have no complaints.

This class by no means easy. Our first exam was given a 15-point curve this semester, but the second exam was given a 4-point curve because of how the C. Breezy likes to curve the mean of the exams (or sometimes the median) to a 75. The grading scale makes the class passable, but the exams are tough, and the homeworks collaboration.

Roark is a very nice guy and has been one of the most accessible professors outside of class I've ever had. The material is tough, but if you attend every lecture and take notes on what he says instead of copying the slides it's not that bad. Homeworks are tough but you can collaborate and he answers questions on campuswire. Gives curves on exams.

His explanation of concepts and the lecture slides are difficult to follow and on occasion do not fully elaborate topics being covered. His tests occasionally, without warning, involve more complex math than he teaches.

Granted, he makes an effort to answer questions and presents in a friendly and engaging way.

Gotta self study to pass 420.

This class is just really tough. As someone who got As in Econ 410 and 400 without working that hard, this class really pushed my limits. Roark is overall doing his best with a massive class and hard material. He does really care about wanting all of his students to do well. Go to office hours, get ready to study, and you will be okay. Curves a lot

I've never had a professor so accessible while at UNC so points for that!! I wont bs this is a really hard class lol but it could be a lot harder...dr Roark does a great job at simplifying concepts during lectures and is always ready to answer questions/listen to feedback to adapt how he's teaching the concept. Don't be scared to take the class

Ignore past years' reviews. He's an incredibly caring and kind professor and the material is not easy but he's always accessible outside of class and willing to help. He's also a funny guy and makes boring microeconomic theory better!

Complaint #1 – Sergio is a bad teacher
Yes, but he clarifies if you ask.


#2 – You need to learn a new coding language

Yes, but it's not too difficult. All coding is at-home work.


#3 – The midterms and problem sets are different formats
Yes, but the midterms are MUCH easier than PS.

Mostly open-note. Only non-open note for conceptual stuff.
The class was ok ish because I already took a course like it, however it was a lot of self studying to do well in the course.

Sergio's lectures weren't very clear but but the class is interesting enough to make up for it. The homework and pop quizzes were often unnecessarily difficult and over-weighted in the grading. Heavily study the readings for his midterms, and you'll be fine. Would recommend taking this class over some of the other 400-level econ courses.

He's a super nice guy, but an awful college professor.

His lectures are unorganized, unengaging, and bland. He tests on content that often is never present in problem sets or lecture discussions, I'd even go as far as to say that he misdirects you by assigning you practice on concepts that he never even tests on!

This class outsources all math to a coding website, which is then not used for exams, leaving students to do math by hand after having only done examples in class and homework with the coding program. The code can be tricky and a tough learning curve, and if you aren't comfortable with some syntax of coding languages, beware. Insane effort required

Overall, nice guy, horrible professor. If you want to put in a ton of effort only to be tested on niche concepts from the thirty-page readings that have nothing to do with the practice questions in class or problem sets, then this is your guy! Take a different 400 level elective- you will put in less work and get a better grade.

Professor Parreiras is a good guy just trying his best. However, he's disorganized, and though he knows the material well, his teaching doesn't always reflect that. Quizzes and exams can be heavily based on a mere sentence of a covered topic. He is getting better as time goes on, just be warned, one bad grade makes an A nearly unattainable.
As long as you read the textbook chapter before class most of it made sense. The wording on the tests was confusing but if you know the topics you will be fine.

Just awful. I would happily get a beer with Sergio (seems a great, funny guy), but trying to learn economics under his professorship is like being taught by Borat. Just impossible. Somehow, it was quite a forgiving class, and he clutched some extra curves at the end, but I've come away pretty clueless about economics. Don't take.

Really nice guy but unless you have to take do not take any class with him. He is very smart but as a professor is extremely disorganized frequently 5-10 minutes late to class and grades problem sets very inconsistently. Do not take this care again for your GPA or for any reason unless you want to learn the whole curriculum on your own.
Tf was that? Barely communicates. Extremely disorganized. Randomly uses out of pocket examples like watching prn or something.

TAKE THE REGULAR ECON101. Sergio seems like a nice guy, but his class is terrible. His lectures are disorganized, he never responds to emails, won't give us study guides for practice exams/finals, and is not a proactive professor. The free response exam format is nice, but it's not worth it. Be prepared to teach yourself everything.
Walks into lecture and seems to prepare lessons as soon as he walks in. Nothing is taught that is on the midterms. If you take this, PREPARE TO TEACH YOURSELF EVERYTHING.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS. He can't lecture, the only saving grace was our TA who should have been the one who taught the class. He takes points off on assignments for things he did not ask for in the questions. Posts practice exams for studying, but doesn't give you the answers so you don't know if you are grasping the concepts.

Seems like a nice guy when I interact with him but is completely unqualified to teach anything, much less an econ class at UNC. Entirely inapt at technology which made his lectures very disorganized. Did much of his math on Mathematica but never actually taught us how to use it so was impossible to follow. HIGHLY recommend taking a different class.

This class has brought me to a level of rage that no other UNC class has. I have my final tomorrow and have no clue what I learned this semester. There's no textbook, only extremely vague powerpoint with complicated formulas. Avg exam grades are around a 60 or less. Find another 500+ if you can or I'd recommend pass/failing.

This class is nearly impossible to prepare for. He tends to ramble, so lectures are hard to follow and often looking back at your notes to study isn't helpful. His question style varies so much that using practice material is wishful thinking at best. Plus, you don't even really learn anything bc most of your energy is spent learning code.

Sergio is a sweet guy, but not the best at teaching. Be prepared to self-study to get an A. He goes on many side tangents, but does eventually teach the core concepts. There is a LOT of required textbook exercises. Some extra credit. Doesn't get to know you personally for a 30 person class.
Have my final tomorrow and am terrified because we actually do not learn in this class. Please avoid this class.

Sergio is the worst professor imaginable. Each lecture is a tangent of random non course-related topics and doesn't even remember more than two peoples names when it's a section of 25. Homework isn't bad, but the exams are like five questions, no multiple choice, and no review sessions at all. Please don't take this if you have mental health.

It's incredibly frustrating that Parreiras is so disorganized and unresponsive to students. His delays in grading and failure to provide meaningful guidance for exams make this class a nightmare. While he may be kind, it doesn't compensate for his poor structure, lack of communication, and inability to teach.

Made the mistake of taking another class with Sergio. AVOID THIS CLASS. Literally nothing to do with economics. It is entirely based on your ability to navigate the clunky coding style of Mathematica...which he himself has not mastered since we spend a good 5-10 minutes each lecture in complete silence as he figures out his errors.

Parreiras has one of the most frustrating teaching styles i've ever seen. The entire class has NOTHING to do with microeconomics it's essentially a coding class only using the software mathematica. Seriously, there is no textbook and he just projects himself doing random coding questions. Avg test grades were always below 50%. AVOID AVOID AVOID

Look, he's a nice guy and obviously very intelligent. However, he is horrible at teaching. He shares practice midterms if you ask, but doesn't give answers, so it's hard to know if you're doing anything right. His slides are difficult to interpret if you use them to review. Even if you get the concepts, you have to do it in Wolfram, which is hard.
Don't listen to the slackers in these comments. It's not that hard to get a good grade. Doing the bare minimum will get you a B minimum.

While the content of this class is pretty easy, Sergio did a terrible job of explaining it and making himself accessible outside of class. He is not very aware of what people are struggling with and jumps around a lot in lectures. That being said, tests were fair and closely resembled practice problems/homeworks and "papers" were graded leniently.

Very disorganized, did not care enough to learn most of the student's names in a less than 30 person class. Did not explain things at all. Many people failed the first midterm as a result of his poor teaching and communication. Be prepared to watch videos and read the textbook to teach yourself nearly everything!

Without a doubt the worst professor I've had in my 4 years in the department. He runs the entire class through coding which you have to learn on your own. Incredibly disorganized and average test grades are D-F. Has an inability to teach and is disrespectful when asking for help. Appears disconnected from reality. Stay away to keep your GPA.

Sergio is a nice man who has nothing but good intentions for his students. That being said, as a college senior, he is hands down the most disorganized and unclear professor I have ever had. If you spend a lot of time studying on your own, you'll do okay in the class. But there are almost no resources, and he is an incredibly inconsistent grader.

Sergio is THE NICEST GUY but a disorganized lecturer. You have to go through the textbook to learn the content. Tests are manageable and he provides a good curve if needed. If you have to take econ with him, you'll be fine, just review the textbook after every lecture. Attendance is mandatory and graded. Extra credit opportunities available.

Worst professor I've had at UNC by far. The man cannot teach to save his life and is incredibly disorganized. His sign-ups for office hours are often very difficult to find, and there is little transparency regarding grading. His classes are heavily curved, but not so much that there is any comfort in that grading-wise.

Decent guy, very disorganized. Lectures were all over the place so most of the learning came from the textbook readings. Tests weren't particularly difficult and the curves were pretty generous. Overall seems like less work than 101 with Staub, but I recommend taking her class instead (especially if you didn't take econ in high school)

Sergio is a nice guy, but taking a low level economics class with him is difficult. I'd say he's too smart to explain simple topics, so me and my classmates were entirely reliant on the textbook. He was lenient with giving curves and grade boosts, so make sure to stay on his good side. Don't forget to check in for his attendance.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! Sergio is not a bad person, but is completely inadequate teaching at UNC. Horrible teaching style, frequently late to class, completely unreachable (office hours and emails). As a junior econ student, he is the worst professor I have ever had. Finished with a B- but was failing class for first 10 weeks. Not worth it!

Nice, chill prof. Funny guy, makes jokes and keeps class lighthearted. Slow pace in class so he can explain concepts very clearly and extensively. Only issues are: (1) Requires attendance and there's a portion of your grade attached to it. (2) Too disorganized, stopped posting anything (including notes/slides) on Canvas halfway through the course.

The only reason this is not a 1 is because Sergio is a likeable guy. No lecture notes, no practice problems, no communication between the recitation leader, and no clear lecture plan. This course was essentially self-taught by looking at answer keys from problem sets given 3-4 days before a test by our recitation leader. Definitely not an easy A.

If you did not take AP Macro and/or AP Micro do NOT take this class. You will learn how to teach yourself, because Parreiras struggles to create a coherent lesson plan and communicate ANYTHING with his TA. Coursework does not correspond with the work or pace of any other ECON101 class at UNC. We might as well have not had a professor at all.

Professor Sergio is, as correctly identified, really disorganized. He showed up late to a lot of lectures, often would get stuck trying to get stuff up and running, and would sometime just lose track in the middle of lectures.

All that said, he was very generous with study resources, extra credit chances, and gave very straight forward tests.

Parreiras is passionate about economics but teaches material at a pace that is incongruent with an introductory class. He gives few assignments, fails to provide sufficient practice problems, and relies heavily on Mathematica to attempt to lecture in class. You will spend many nights trying to self-teach all the material before the midterms/final.

Sergio was a great professor in my opinion. Sergio is a disorganized professor but cares about his students and when I was confused regarding the grading, he was very helpful. I think if you want to take Econ at UNC and do well, take Sergio because he makes Econ fun and gives extra credit! He doesn't assign a lot of homework either.

He is not very organized and does not really know how to teach so the class is kind of a major joke. Sergio does not like to grade things and will randomly give you a horrible grade on a quiz/hw and give no explanation. He is a horrible professor but the class is definitely manageable minus Mathematica.

Dr. Parreiras is a completely incompetent professor. Although he holds his students to a rigorous grading standard where only students who achieve a 95%+ receive an A, his teaching ability would be graded at a D at best. His english speaking ability is sub-moderate, consistently shows up to class late, and has no organizational ability at all.

Completely disorganized, can't understand him half the time. The slides are extremely difficult to follow and as are his lectures. Assigns groupwork for problem sets every week in which communication/working together is inconsistent on a week to week basis and difficult for planning/execution. Super nice guy but geez.

Homework is very difficult and I didn't find his lectures easy to follow, BUT, his tests care extremely similar to his problem sets, he pulls one problem from hw directly, others r changed slightly, one new one. Do the HW, memorize it, you'll do well. Gives partial credit generously. Funny, seems nice.

Difficult to get an A but not hard to get above a B. Lectures were not helpful in doing the homeworks, which ended up being 80% of the coursework (there is a homework question on both exams). Overall, just not a great course to learn in and had to teach myself how to work out most of the homeworks/exams. Very passable class.

Very lecture-heavy with no posted slides or notes, so attendance is important. Grading is based only on homework and exams. six homework assignments and two exams. The exams closely reflected the study guide, and one homework-style problem appeared on the exam. Grading is done in blocks, so small point differences can affect final letter grades.

Yates is a funny and straightforward guy, and lectures were enjoyable. Tests were similar to hw and practice ?s, and although grading scale made it very difficult to get an A, the tests were graded leniently enough for a B as long as you practiced. If you would like to learn, make sure to attend and pay attention in lecture.

Professor Yates is fantastic! Super funny and down to earth guy. Econ 410 is a hard class, and you WILL need to study for at least 20 hours before exams, but Yates has great lectures that really clarify the material. Although attendance isn't mandatory, if you want an A, you need to go to class. Overall, great class with a great prof.

Yates is passionate, but the class felt unfair at some points and did not feel like he wanted us to do well. His grading scale is super difficult because there's no room for mistakes. You need to do significantly well on both exams and perfect on homework if you want an A but a B is doable if you utilize econ aid.

Very caring and funny guy, but wow this class is hard. Not a lot of materials besides lectures, textbook is not really used outside of recitations. If you prefer a more structured class, take MSA. Hard to get A-/A, but also hard to fail with how tests are graded. Definitely use the ULAs/econaid, but expect to teach yourself a lot outside of class.

Loved his class. He knows what he's talking about and was very interesting lecturer. Made you pay attention which is great. Puts up with lots of ridiculous questions well. Only thing is I think the grading scheme based on basically 2 tests of 5 questions each is a little weird and I feel like I knew the content way better than my grade reflected.

Dr. Yates is a very different type of professor but it worked for me. I can see why people don't like it, but I enjoyed this class. His handwriting is hard to read for taking notes. Office hours with the ULA's will save your grade. Do the practice problems before exams and they won't be so bad.

Difficult to get above a B in my opinion. Only grades homework and exams. Drops one homework grade. One midterm exam on topics from the first half of the class. Final is content from the second. Used only one homework problem on the exams this semester. 5 questions on each exam with practice problems given about 2 weeks prior. Extra credit.

The test structure is fair, but exams are weighted too heavily. The class relies on upper-level math I never learned, so most problems felt overly math-heavy. I barely learned microeconomics, and the final tested random topics we hardly covered, so it didn't feel fair or representative.

Nice guy. Lectures consists of him completing practice problems on his iPad and attempting to explain along the way. May work for some but was extremely hard to follow or stay engaged for me. Not to mention his handwriting is hieroglyphic bordering on indecipherable. HW relates to class but you're on your own for most of your studying and learning

Agree with a lot of the previous reviews, Professor doesn't teach he just writes solutions with little to explanation. Very hard to follow if you are not confident in the skill before class. Easy to pass if you are willing to spend 20 hours outside of class to teach yourself. Exams are homework with numbers switched.

He's a great guy but absolutely hate his grading scale which is non-negotiable. You need a 97 to get an A and a low 90 is considered a B+. He gives review problems for the midterm/final and 3 out of the 5 test questions will be from those but with different numbers. If you grind those and know all the hw questions too, you'll prob end with a B.

Weird grading system but not hard to get good grades. 7 HW (lowest grade dropped), he randomly chooses one question to grade from each homework. 1 midterm and one cumulative final, both five questions (one past homework question, three questions similar to HW but with different numbers, and one new question). Attendance not taken at my recitation
He is not that bad as the reviews claim him to be
Be prepared to study hard for this class. It took me around 20 hours in total to study for the final.

While Yates was chill, energy economics wasn't a fulfilling class. He wrote a bunch of concepts & equations on the iPad, & we had no hw to reinforce what he was teaching us. He's funny & answers questions well, but it could be a bit more structured. I will say I did learn new things conceptually, but again, can't back it up with the econ side.

easiest class i've taken at UNC. Concepts can be a little hard if you're actually trying to learn, but he does a good job teaching it (other than his handwriting). You're given a bank of questions for all the exams, so you just have to memorize it.

Gives you a 20-question bank w/ answers for the test, and expects you to get 116/120 between midterm and final for an A. This makes the tests a complete joke (tip: don't just memorize the answers), but also forces you to study for the specific questions instead of reviewing actual class content, leaving you poorly prepared for future ECON courses.
great professor. He is a bit more casual than other professors which is refreshing and has good sense of humor.

I really liked 410 with Yates. It was hard but I loved his applications to real life. His handwriting is horrible so you need to focus during lecture to know what he's writing. He does make it possible to succeed in this class and even become passionate about it. My TA, August, was incredible and reinforced a lot of what Yates taught in class.

Obviously a smart guy, but an absolutely horrible professor. Operates under the assumption that we can mentally do complicated algebra in seconds, which he may be able to do but I was not. This made his lectures useless. That being said, office hours saved my grade. They will help on the homework. The exams were wack but doable.

ECON 410 is going to be challenging, no matter who you take it with, but Prof. Yates made it manageable. The only complaint I have is that his handwriting is illegible, so you have to take notes based on what you hear. HWs are tough so I had to hire a TA. For the final exam, I studied roughly 15 hours a day for three days to feel prepared. 4/5
Don't even want to talk about it. GTHY
love the new grading i dont know a single thing and i got a hundred on every single assignment

Truly a fun professor. ECON-410 is notoriously a hard class so he's probably one of the best to take it with anyways. His lectures are really funny and aren't too bad to understand if you have any quantitative background because then it's just definitions and learning how to solve problems. He also goes over homeworks and a lot of examples in class
GOAT!!!!!!

A year later and he continues to be the laziest man in the department. This class is easy if you cheat since he doesn't care, his handwriting is terrible so be ready to record every lecture back and review things by yourself. PICKING THE RIGHT TA IS CRUCIAL. He's better at teaching than MSA and less confusing doesn't over work students.

Prof. Yates is a good man but his quality of teaching is not. He moves quickly and his notes follow no sort of rigid structure which makes transcribing them onto your own paper extremely difficult. Handwriting is atrocious. By the time you figure out that he was writing a 'q' for quantity instead of the number '9' he has moved on to the next topic.

Andy's teaching style is woeful. Lectures are him saying a problem verbally, then solving it with no explanation on concepts while skipping math steps. His handwriting is the worst I've ever seen, and you have to decipher his notes. The class is graded easier now than before, but seriously, you're going to have to teach yourself everything.

I hope he sees this. I am a transfer student and was excited to take his class, he does everything but help you. He goes so fast you can't keep up, no pre-class videos, doesn't tell you what chapter you're on. He is delusional and in his own world. Very nice man but not fit to help students as he makes no effort to explain, elaborate etc.

Amazing Professor. Very caring and patient. Answer all questions that students have in review sessions. Do the practice questions before the exam, and you will pass easily. The only problem is his writing in lecture notes(a little bit unclear), so go to classes and listen carefully. Overall, great Econ professor. I will definitely take it again.

Andy was a cool dude, really enjoyed his personality. His lectures could be a bit fast and disorganized. He does a lot of examples but doesn't always fully explain the concept before he does so, so it can be confusing. Lowest midterm and lowest homework dropped. Overall though it is what you would expect from a 400 level econ class.

The lectures were disorganized as Yates would go pretty fast and go through examples before explaining the concepts fully. All of the homework and midterms were very math and calculus based, all FRQ. The lowest midterm is dropped. Yates is a caring professor and will listen to feedback from students. Responds to emails.

Andy is a bit disorganized prof, but very knowledgeable and ultimately got info across pretty well. Not an easy class, but about what you'd expect from 400s econ class. Grading criteria is super clear, you'll know what you need to get a grade. Very exams/final heavy, but a good grade is doable. 8(?) hws, 3 midterms (one of each dropped) and final.
If you fall behind in lectures even a little bit it can be hard to catch up. Overall, he's a very nice guy and you can get a decent grade even if you don't do that well on exams.

He lectures for the full class and it can be very information heavy so be prepared to attend class especially since his notes can have some bad handwriting. This is a hard class to get an A/A- in but his grading system will help you pass with a pretty good grade.

I really enjoyed Professor Yates and his class. He is funny and helps students see how to apply the concepts learned in class to real-world problems through realistic test and practice problems. However, it's pretty easy to sometimes get lost in all the calculus notation. I came from doing calc and econ AP in high school and did well in this class.

Yates lectures from the start to the end of every class period, and you need to be writing notes. 70% of the grade is midterms+final but the lowest midterm is dropped. You need to study hard to do well in this class. Teaches different stuff from other 410 Professors. Doesn't give a lot of review material but is a nice and funny guy.

I loved Professor Yates as a person but his teaching style is definitely difficult. I enjoyed his lectures although he goes too fast at times and needs someone to ask him to slow down. The tests are quite difficult it came to the point that I felt like studying was a waste of time since it was dependent on just what he asked on the test.

His brand of Econ is a 180 from the way MSA teaches. She is math-heavy, here, the math is simple, but he uses a lot more variables so the algebra can get very chaotic. Tests are 3 questions only and a large part of the grade, so do well on them. Hard to hear him through the mask that he is still wearing so be locked in during lectures.

Funny guy and def knows what he's talking about, took a decision making class with totally new concepts and think I can apply them in the real world no problem. Beware handwriting--you have to go to class bc you will NOT understand his notes. Also beware math, not always explained super clearly even when simple. Amazing professor, will take again!

Professor Yates is a great guy. He tries to make the class fun and more entertaining. Graded on 6 homework assignments (drops the lowest one), two midterms (total is three but lowest is dropped), and the final. Almost no extra practice problems, but if you can do the homework well then you will be fine on the exams. Worked kinda hard and got a B+.

People will hate on Yates for his terrible handwriting and difficult testing style. However, once you understand how he tests his material, you can start to approach the exams in the right way and ace them. The handwriting argument is so weak, just go to class and write down what he says. Super caring guy, very willing to help students in need.

The class is impossible to follow along with. Barely any practice problems are utilized so studying for exams and completing homework is incredibly difficult. The exams are obscure and the only way kids do somewhat well is because the exams are graded incredibly lightly. Yates is a good guy but the class is just rough.

He talks so fast and never stops and will get mad if you ask him to slow down or tell him you can't read his handwriting (it is atrocious and worse than a five-year-old's). The exams are not based on anything you do in class. He refuses to record his lectures so you have to rely on the poorly written notes (Mandarin would be easier to understand).

He is the kind of professor you don't know how to rate. Very funny sometimes, and a good lecturer, but gives out tough homework. Really need to figure out lots on one's own. If you study hard and go to him with questions, even re-grade requests, he is very nice about that and you'd do well. TBH after all those ECON classes, he is my favorite.

I really liked Prof Hill. If you show up to class youll understand material. He made midterms alot easier and took questions from assignments frequently. Yes the final was a little harder, but definitely because we ran out of time and not on purpose.
Do not skip class only notes are written on the chalk board, do not get tricked by the midterm final is way more difficult.
He was openly racist
Go to class and put in the time and he's great. If you don't you will fall behind quickly - Fair and results reflect effort

The material is very difficult and lectures do get dense, but he make it easy to pass, and even have a good grade without having to go crazy. He makes very clear what he wants in the exam, and if you follow the class it can be very interesting and useful. The final project was also interesting to make.

Took 410 with him before and felt terrible. This time he is pretty decent. Knowledgeable and the lectures give you insights. Exams are materials from the lecture. Simply putting everything he writes on board on your cheat sheet will be fine. Only note--the lectures are not based on textbook and he does not publish lectures, so attendance matters.
Was not a big fan of his lectures, but he did seem to be a much kinder person than reviews suggested.

Ignore other reviews about this class. The most annoying part of this class were poll questions in class graded for accuracy, but if you work with others on those then its alright. If you just go and pay attention to every class then its not too difficult and manageable. Over half my class didn't attend lectures on a daily basis.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! if you can avoid prof hill i would!! he is a very bad lecturer and he literally told me to drop out in office hours even tho i ended with an A but only because i dedicated the time to teach myself the material by myself

Some of the bad reviews are a little unfair, but I see where they're coming from. If you're in this class, TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OFFICE HOURS. Lectures were not the best (though he stopped using the chalkboard which was good), but he was decent at explaining 1-1. Also curves a LOT. Homework carries a lot of weight, so lock in for those the most.
