I do not have much to complain except he has awful handwriting. Professor Hill is not bad but there are a lot of topics to memorize. 470 is basically a statistics course so I guess that is fair. However, the course structure is bad. The notes most of the time are very vague and the exams focused on STATA a lot, which we barely practiced.

If you want to take ECON 410 at UNC, take MSA, you will get a good grade. If you take Jonathan Hill, you will be teaching yourself the course and actually learning. He is very passionate and knowledgeable, however his lectures are AWFUL. His handwriting is impossible to read, and he moves quickly. He gets too much hate, but don't take his class.
I would only say. I should have listened to previous suggestions and stay away from him awwwwwwwwwww!

He's honestly not as bad as people make him seem. His handwriting is not great but he always clarifies if asked about what he wrote. He's provided resources on top of the lectures and has been accessible. I don't see the critiques other people have of him but maybe he's improved himself from the ratings. He's nice too! Don't be quick to judge :)

Prof. Hill is not a good lecturer or teacher. He runs through hundreds of slides in his lectures, only reading them and not explaining the concepts well. The material mostly has to be self taught. Moreover, his tests and the class overall is graded quite harshly from what I have seen. Take this class with Handy if you can.

DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR HILL'S CLASS!! P.S. - I created a rate my professor after 3 yrs at unc just to leave this review, and I'm not one to do this. He is the worst econ professor, doesn't care about students/teaching, and you're going to be bored to death with every lecture - & good luck making anything above a B. DROP IT IF YOU'RE SIGNED UP!!
I would say every class have genius who always get an A. But if you're not, Please don't study with him!!!!!!!! The worst professor in the world

I didn't really expect such rating for Professor Hill. I will consider taking another class with him and l find him friendly. He even agreed to write me several recommendation letters and l am grateful for that. I got 100 in the first midterm, 95 in second, 98 in the final. and 100 points for all homeworks. So there's no need to fear him so much.

I left a bad rating after first exam but he isn't bad. The tests are a copy-paste of the textbook problems and he just rewrites the problems/numbers. No one read the textbook so a lot failed and left bad reviews. Also he lets us have a cheat sheet so if you use it wisely, you will do well. I got a 40 on my first exam and finished with a A- (curved)

Dr. Chao is the sweetest! She really cares about her students and made economics interesting. If you can, take ECON 101 with her she is AMAZING.

Take Econ with her! She is the BEST Econ 101 professor. She is so caring and even provides snacks in class! Dr. Chao offers to meet with students individually because she genuinely wants you to succeed.

This class is legit though so you will have to put effort into it to do well, but she is definitely the best choice

She's such an amazing teacher and is very passionate about what she does. I highly recommend her class. Although ECON 101 can be pretty tough because of the material itself, she does an amazing job of providing time outside of class to study it and explains things very clearly.

she is so amazing and makes me econ fun. Her tests are not super easy, but also not hard if you study. She cares so much about her students and I don't know anyone who doesn't like her

Absolutely phenomenal professor! Very caring and genuinely wants everyone to do well. She gives so many resources to prepare for tests and assignments and she is always willing to meet at any time to help you understand. 10/10 recommend if you want to take an Econ elective, take it with her.

The class was difficult for me, but the resources she provides are amazing. The homework and exercise problems are great preparation for exams. She is very sweet, caring, and accommodating, always ready to help if you have questions about a topic.

The class is somewhat difficult but as long as you study and go to class you will be okay. Vaidyanathan is clear on what can be covered on the test and the practice exams prepare you well for the exams. Enjoyable class, learned a lot. Great teaching style. Only complaint is can cold call and if you don't know the content she's asking about thats a hard situation to be in.

Professor Vaidyanathan is by far my favorite professor in the entire Econ department. Her lectures are easy to follow and the homework sets you up well for the exams. Dr. V is an amazing professor. The material is interesting and not too difficult to understand. Great professor, my favorite in the ECON department. Very caring and understanding, the lectures get a little harder to follow as the year goes on but there are a ton of resources to practice. Geetha is a great professor and explains pretty complex topics in a way that makes them easy to understand. Only complaint is that the actual exams can be significantly harder than the practice ones.

got honor courted by the ULA and the class was very hard and test heavy. Did not do well on exam 1 and then ended up doing worse on the harder exams (2 and 3). too much material to cover and there are many resources. hard to pass the class and one of the hardest econ classes ive ever took!

Took in Fall 2022. [Good] She is unbelievably extremely caring! [Bad] If she mentioned something outside PPT once, you will one multiple choice about it in exam. Very good teacher. Lectures are engaging and useful. Tests are honestly pretty easy if you study all of the materials; generally, the test averages were ~92%.
I guarantee you guys that all your effort will pay off. Not a challenging class, if you study hard, u will get an A.
Goat of Econometrics. Take class with him and enjoy an A
Approachable and explain the lecture in detail. It's easy to follow up if you forgot what u learned in the past.

Great class and professor. If your looking to take 470, do yourself a favor and take it with Verdier.

take him .he is the best professor I have taken in UNC.he will give you the exact structure of the midterms and final.and he will also give you the practice exam of the exact same structure of the actual exam .the things you are tested in the exam is exact the same as which in the practice exam ,he gives extra credit for all homeworks and exams

Prof. Verdier is a really nice, caring professor who wants you to do well. He is also a good lecturer, and as long as you attend lectures and keep up with your work you will most likely succeed in the class. Highly recommend.

The content of the class was pretty easy but he's such a bad teacher it made it more difficult. Genuinely learned more from the TAs.

Very tough class. Tests make up 90% of the overall grade.

Worst class I've taken at UNC. I'm a math and econ major and found Calc 3, Linear Algebra, and Discrete Math all easier than this class. Horrible at explaining concepts, does practically no practice problems in class. do yourself a favor and AVOID.

Dr. Gong is one of the best econ professors I've had. You can clearly tell that she is passionate about the subject, and mentions real life applications. If you're confused on anything, Dr. Gong will clarify everything during office hours. The class isn't as easy as some claim, and you do have to put in effort.
Easiest Econ elective, very few homeworks. Fair exams.

Dr. Gong is a really great professor and lenient grader. She really wants you to do well which is uncommon in UNC Econ. Best professor I have had in UNC Econ not because I did well but she is so passionate about teaching. This is good to see and something that UNC Econ needs more of.

Excellent econ professor, wants you to learn and that's it. This was the easiest 500-level econ class ever; great choice for an easy semester but still worth taking seriously because the material/skills are important and Dr. Gong really cares a lot.

I LOVED her. She doesn't try to trick you at all and gives you everything you need to succeed. Exams are extremely similar to problem sets and hw. She is always there to help if anything is needed and such a nice person. Can't speak highly enough about her!! 100% take this as an Econ elective.

Professor Gong was one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She is very accessible outside of class and she genuinely wants to help you succeed. The class consists of short homework assignments and one group project that you work on throughout the semester. I cannot recommend this class and Professor Gong enough. Take this class if you can!!

Only thing that I found slightly annoying is she does not take any questions during exams at all, not even clarifying ones. However, overall this class was one of the best econ ones I have taken. She is not trying to trick you at all where it feels like a lot of econ professors try.
Makes it very easy for you to succeed, if you go to class do the 3 problem sets and do the practice exams this class is barbecue chicken

The nicest econ professor I've ever had. She told us on the first day she wants us all to get As and she makes it very manageable to do so. The problem sets are for completion except one randomly selected question for correctness. The tests are never cumulative and exactly like practice and old tests. So funny and nice!

Super nice lady, she really takes the time to explain everything clearly in case you ever forget the basics from Econ 101 or Econ 410. You have the option to take the class form zoom instead of showing up in person.

Agree with others - best ECON prof at UNC. 552 is a readings/policy-based class, doesn't really involve typical econ math, just understand and apply data analysis. Unprofessional

Prof. Francis is a nice professor and explains topics well. 
He is lecture heavy, and doesn't provide a lot of material besides the lecture. I would recommend attending the lecture and keeping track of what he is saying, because he might announce something, or highlight a topic and if you miss it, it's gone.

For a 500-level econ class, this one wasn't that bad. Neville's lectures are pretty confusing at times, but if you study and do the practice problems you'll be okay. He curves the grades, and if you come to class and show that you're trying, he won't let you fail. He's not very accessible outside of class and often won't respond to emails.
unclear expectations for class projects. not considerate of students.

Professor Babii is clearly very well-versed in the topics of this class. However, he is an extremely boring lecturer. His slides are long and extremely detailed, but his monotone way of presenting them doesn't emphasize the importance of actually important details. His homeworks actually take forever. Extreme bias towards R over python.

I loved this class. He does a great job keeping the class interesting. Homeworks are long, but helped a lot to prepare for the research project and final exam. They are doable as long as you do the labs. Professor Babbi is well-organized and his class has good structure with detailed references to textbook chapters.

Prof. Babii's lectures rely on textbook slides. Homework takes forever, though beneficial, but occasionally covers untaught material. He's often very disorganized, and not very communicative. Also, our research project lacked clear expectations. Previous exams for reviews are good, and this is an interesting class, it just needs better structure.
One of the most useful Econ classes. The material is hard but he makes it doable. Professor Babii was very helpful with the research project throughout the semester.

Really boring class, especially if you have any background in machine learning already, but extremely easy. Not many assignments and everything is graded really leniently. Final exam was crazy long and unrealistic to finish in three hours but appears to have been graded very easy.
Heavy on the homework. Lectures are a bit boring. Seems inflexible at times.

Professor Peter is the best Economics professor I've had at UNC. Her class was very well structured to account for the stressful times that senior year can cause (recruiting season, etc.). Very Stata heavy but if you did well with coding in 470 it shouldn't be too difficult. Highly recommend.
Dr. Peter is very knowledgable in labor economics. She really wants everyone in her class to succeed. Very approachable outside of class, and offers generous help with Stata coding.
Best professor in the econ department!! She really cares about her students.

I rarely leave RMP reviews but for Prof. Hendricks, I will, simply because he is one of the best Economics professors at UNC. Prof. Hendricks is someone who really wants you to understand the intuition behind the macro models. He's extremely patient, helpful and accessible outside class hours. Econ520 was so smooth and easy with Prof. Hendricks.

While his lectures were a little bit dull, if you attend class and pay attention you should be ok overall for the class. He was really accessible and willing to help you with the two assignments, and has a really relaxed grading scale which makes it easier to do well in his class. Overall, not the worst Econ 500 level course you can take.

Although the lectures can sometimes be a bit dull, Prof. Hendricks is very clear in what he wants you to know. He is a fair grader, the class and the curve the class is graded on is very lenient. He also gives help if asked for it. Genuinely not a bad 500 level at all.
Great guy, makes macro easily understandable. The lectures can be boring but theres only a few grades and he really wants you to do well, so he helps a bunch. Really interesting class
He is an amazing professor, he tries his best to make the material easier. He is a very easy grader, if you put a little bit of effort, he will give you the points. Very easy.

Hendricks has been my favorite Economics professor by far. His goal is to teach you, not make you suffer for a good grade. Only 2 assignments, which were graded on an heavy curve and very similar to class examples. Lutz is a gem in the econ department. I cannot stress enough how great this class was. Take it as your 500 level!

He's the best econ professor I've ever had. His lectures are sooo clear. He grades so so leniently, and thats even after a curve (85 is A). This was a 500 level class with the difficulty of a 100 level class but I still learned a ton. Exams are tough but with the curve and easy grading it's not bad. Also no calculus in this, just conceptual!!!!

It's the middle of the semester but I'm here to help you guys in deciding which 500 lvl Econ to take. take this one! I've never really understood Econ until his lectures and im a senior. He grades extremely leniently, and his exams are well prepared for you. Also the curve is crazy. 10/10
Covers a lot of basic economic concepts using relevant examples. He was very organized and thorough in his lectures but required a lot of readings before class, even though only a few were covered.

He is great in teaching those concepts. But I would say his part was the hardest in the entire IDST 111 class. You have to answer the question from all perspective to get a good score. But if you pay attention to class and do your homework, it will be an easy A

Professor McManus did a great job covering the Economics portion of IDST 111. Although I already had ECON 101 credit from getting a 5 on AP Micro and Macroeconomics, I learned a lot of new things and fields within economics from his lectures. The only downside is he does take off points if your answers are not exactly what he is looking for.

I loved how concise he always was during his lectures and he does engage the class. He is very willing to help but won't just give you an answer straight off the bat because he's trying to make sure you learn. Note that the grading criteria can be more specific for short answer questions than question prompt asks.

Do not take the PPE triple I with Brian. His multiple choice questions are confusing and he grades open responses harshly. Lectures can be confusing. Take a different triple I. Taking PPE with Brian will wreck your GPA. Do not recommend

Dr. Williams cares a lot about teaching and is a great lecturer. I wish there was more time to hear him talk about IO, but 70% of the course grade is based on a group project, so he knows that we know that that's the focus of the class. He is a compassionate teacher and grades fairly (if a little on the forgiving side).

The class does involve a lot of independent learning as not much is taught in lectures. It is also almost all group work. However, Prof. Williams is an incredibly nice guy and he is always willing to help if you come to office hours and lend a hand. He wants you to do well even if you might not understand a lot at first. Overall, good experience.
Can he please update his slides for Econ410. You can tell he would take it as a compliment if half of his students failed his class. Not a girls girl

He was not helpful. During meetings regarding my project topics, when i asked him what would be his advice be, he pretty much throw the question back at me. He was pretty condescending and tried to act as if he was being as helpful as he could. His lectures regarding coding were not clear either.
Will is an awesome professor. He makes the topics really engaging, and his slides are very useful. The exams were really manageable, and the content is genuinely fascinating
Will is an awesome professor. He makes the topics really engaging, and his lecture slides are extremely useful for studying. Certain

Professor Jungerman is clearly a very smart person and knows so much about macroeconomics. However, this doesn't translate to good teaching. He cannot explain any math derivations and that's what most of the 150 slides in each of the lectures are. He's very slow to post practice problems and answer keys were missing solutions.

Will is a very solid instructor. His command of macroeconomic theory and its application in current and past research makes for genuinely engaging lectures. The content itself is high level, but the exams were easier compared to all the content discussed. I really think it would be hard to teach this class with a better way than Will's approach

Worst class I ever took at UNC. Graded almost completely on exams with no homework or relevant practice material given. William didn't proctor the exams so we couldn't ask him questions. Giant slide decks full of impossible derivations and no clear expectations about what we are supposed to know for tests. Unresponsive to questions and emails.
Good professor, caring and very sweet.
She is nice and carings

No attendance but you should show up bc she explains topics in depth you won't understand as thoroughly by reading the slides. Truly cares about you understanding the material. The workload is very manageable, haven't needed the textbook. Her shoe game is subtly strong and her resume is impressive (she was on Biden's Council of Economic Advisers).

Chari is the best econ professor I've had, by a longshot. She has yet to be corrupted by the denizens running the econ dept. She gives ample extra credit, actually cares about us learning, and has the professional experience to back her up. I didn't take 460, and I did well despite putting in minimal effort. Highly recommend taking 560 with her.
Having him for math camp is like a match made in heaven :)

Professor Suvorov was great Ivan was very understanding and always willing to help. He slowed down when students were struggling and made sure we followed along.
You still need to work hard and study, but his lectures were extremely helpful. We reviewed key concepts and practiced problems in class.
I would rate him 100 out of 100 highly recommended
He is still understanding how to teach - sometimes it's easier to teach yourself.

Professor Suvorov was a very well put professor, taught lectures well and examples were put in order to understand material. Attendance is required and recommended, as much of the work  comes back in homework's and midterms. Very understanding professor which is very useful! Would take again and recommend for others!

Mr. Suvorov is so patient & helpful. His explanations are clear, the materials are helpful, and the tests are fair and manageable.

As a full-time student balancing the recovery and growth of my business remotely after the tough years, I wish I could have devoted more time to this class. It reveals the real-world insights.

Thank you, Mr. Suvorov.

The professor always made sure that we all had understood the lesson, always clarifying every concept and reoeating it as much as it was necessary. It is true that there were many homework, but they were very useful for both midterms and final exam, so it was a good way of keeping up with the subejct

Professor Suvorov was great! Going to class is very beneficial because he works out problems in class that will prepare us for the exams. He is always willing to help if there is a question outside of class and sets up office hours if multiple students have questions. Homework and exams are graded quickly as well. He wants his students to succeed.

Man's an epic. Although he has some accent, he explained most stuff clearly and he designed the course in a way that if you followed his instructions and did the works you will find this class pretty easy. I heard a lot of bad things about ECON 410 and felt non of them with professor Suvorov. Definitely recommend taking this class with him.

Ivan is so caring and makes himself accessible outside of class. It being a condensed summer class, he held office hours 4 times a week and always encouraged us to reach out via email if we ever had any questions. Despite it being so quick, the class setup and plethora of in-class practice never made me felt overwhelmed. Had me excited about econ.

Ivan is a very kind and understanding professor. Although he doesn't project his voice well, he does a great job at explaining concepts and giving students many resources. He always sent emails that consisted of exactly what was going to be on each exam, along with study guides and practice questions. Lowest midterm and homework are dropped!

You can tell that Ivan is knowledgable about the subject, but he lacks any ability to communicate that knowledge to the class. He reads the slides, verbatim, in a soft mumble for the entire class period. I stopped attending class for the last half of the semester and my grade improved, as I would just teach myself based on the textbook.

Suvorov knows a lot about labor economics and is a good teacher, however, he talks extremely quietly and mumbles while he teaches. Many students have asked him to speak louder during class but he still hasn't. Very difficult to stay focused during lectures and ended up teaching myself all the material a few days before our midterms

Prof Suvorov is really caring and an awesome instructor. He gives so many exam reviews, and is always very willing to help students with understanding class material. All exams are open notes, and he basically tells you what each problem on the exam will be like. The class is very straightforward, and it's easy to do well as long as you try!

Ivan is kind, caring, understanding, and very patient. He holds his office hours directly after class so you can immediately catch up if you missed anything. Very willing to help students and genuinely want them to succeed. He has a slight accent but you can perfectly understand him. Very responsive to emails and gives lots of exam review sessions.

Ivan was very understanding and was willing to slow down when students were struggling. His office hours were held directly after class, which was helpful for clarification about concepts that we had dicussed during the previous class or recitation. I would reccomend Ivan for a summer course, as he was very prepared and able to condense the course.

Don't be dissuaded by Mr. Suvorov's heavy accent, and quiet nature, he's actually an amazing instructor. Plenty of resources, always accessible, and always receptive to student feedback. I thought the workload was very manageable for an Economics class.

He cares about how well you do, so don't be scared to ask questions about anything. If you try in this class, you'll be straight. Problem sets are where I missed the most, but these mistakes are the reasons I did well on the tests. If you have an opportunity, take Professor Suvorov.

Took his class this summer and learned so much from him. The content was very difficult and time consuming but he provided a plethora of assistance through the learning the process which made completing his course more feasible. If you desire to achieve high performance in his class you definitely will need to put in the effort!

He was a good teacher. The class is hard so you have to apply yourself. He cares about his students. When I missed class he would email me to make sure I have watched the recorded lecture, not many professors will do that. For me it was hard and I got off to a bad start but was able to finish with the grade I wanted. He offers lots of office hours.

Professor Suvorov was a great teacher. I took ECON 410 as an online summer class and was initially worried about keeping up because the course is so condensed, but Professor Suvorov put a lot of time and effort into ensuring that his students had the chance to succeed in his class.

Dude's a G, don't worry about the other ratings those people are just lazy af; he will adjust your scores with curves and give ample opportunities to make back attendance and other places where your score may have dropped

She genuinely cares about her students. Your grade is primarily based on tests (~70%), but she does offer extra credit questions and a curve. Her lectures are easy to follow and posted after each class. Additionally, she gives past exams as practice. Overall, she has been a great professor.

Say goodbye to this "easy econ elective" you thought you had... your grade is unclear until the final day so prepare to be BLINDSIDED with a C+ like I was. The material isn't that bad but I do not advise skipping this class since it all builds off of itself and there's a million little things to remember. Tugba is a very amazing person though.

A very straight-forward Econ elective. She is super kind and even though sometimes it can be tough to follow her lectures, if you put it any effort to come to office hours she is very willing to help out. Content was pretty easy and course was curved generously.

Well, the class is challenging, and it takes a lot of effort to understand all the materials. Her homework doesn't really help with the test, so it's better to redo the practice exam again and again. But she did curve 5 points at the end, which makes an A to be 88 percent. A takable class, but not recommended.
Horrible, the practice makes u feel like u never went to class. Tests are really hard

Not a bad econ elective. Attendance is unweighted, so I never went to class. But she posts amazing lecture notes that allow you to learn everything for an exam without ever stepping foot in the class. Tests are difficult, but fair. Easier than other econ courses I have taken and spent

Bro thinks median score of 50 was fair. Large discrepancy between homeworks and exams. Meaningless presentation: she wanted student to self-study graduate level stuff to present. Save your grade and don't take this class.

Very caring and kind person, but a bad professor. Gave us 600-700 level material and exams included stuff never taught or in the study materials. Made mistakes during lectures/answer keys that made studying hard - never knew what was the right answer. No communication between TA/ULAs. I've seriously reconsidered being an Econ major after her. RUN!

Exams are worth 70% of your total grade and they were all horrible. The first exam average was a 56 where she blamed us in an announcement afterwards for our poor performance. She does not update grades in canvas so you will never know your grade during the semester, her accent is hard to understand early in the morning--just not a good professor.

Tugba is very passionate about Econ, but she isn't a great instructor. She cold calls students because nobody raises their hand to answer questions. The lack of engagement was usually due to communication issues, as Tugba often rushes through material and has a very thick accent. Take with a different professor if you don't have Econ experience.

The exams were pretty difficult and the hw and practice exams weren't much help. The group project in my opinion was unnecessary but not too much of a hassle. Dr. Somuncu is nice and clearly cares about the topic but she expects us to also be as knowledgeable about the topic. The grading scale curve at the end was generous.

The midterms were definitely tough, the class average was around an F or D but if you go to her office she really takes the time to help you. I improved by over 20 points on the final compared to my midterm. She's kind and caring and wants her students to succeed. There's also a generous curve at the end, which helps a lot.

Topics were interesting and informative. Lecture was at times hard to follow. Homework was significantly easier then exams and didn't really prepare me for the exams. If you need an Econ elective, I would steer clear, this was easily one of the hardest classes to get a decent grade in even though the material wasn't too challenging.

In lecture the content seems manageable, but the exams are much harder. Dr. Somuncu has a thick accent which makes lecture difficult to understand. Go to her office hours. I found the topics discussed in class interesting, though. She gave us extra credit question on final because we reached the 85% threshold for course evals. Her curve was nice.

Her grading is beyond unfair. She told us she was curving based on the median instead of the avg, and the median was higher on all exams than the avg so that just puts every student at a disadvantage. McDonough also curves the avg and allows people to replace their final with a midterm score. So we are just at a disadvantage for the same class.

Tugba was a great professor. She provided us with many study materials for the exams, like problem sets, past midterms from last semester, and the exams were representative of the hw. People are saying they struggled in this class but the reality is 101 is hard and you have to work to get a good grade. If you study, you'll pass. Take it w/ tugba.

I think these reviews are a bit unfair. I took ECON 101 as a required class and I LOVED it. I am not even an econ major, yet she made me love it. She was not difficult to understand despite everyone talking about her accent. All her slides were extremely detailed and very easy to study from.

Very difficult course because her english is very poor which made the lecture slides and test questions difficult to understand. Going to class is required as she takes attendance, however you will have to teach yourself most of the material on your own. Review questions do not reflect the test questions.

The exams are insanely hard and relate nothing to the content you study. She doesn't curve any of them either. She seemed like she wanted students to learn, but then yelled at us for coming to office hours. The TAs are very unhelpful, and the review sessions were always unorganized. They seemed like they didn't know what they were talking about.

The test questions felt like they would make sense if you could read into her way of thinking, but not if you purely studied the class's concepts. In other words, they were far too difficult. I knew all the material before the tests, and I still did not get an A. Would not recommend.
Dont take Norman. Simply so bad.

He's a chill guy, but a bad teacher. First exam was easy and then downhill from there. When he gives answers to practice problems, they are extremely hard to understand. Often writes "look at the slides" instead of giving the actual answers. Sometimes refuses to give the answers at all. Subject is very interesting, wish he taught it better.

Avoid him if possible. After the first day of class I knew I was in for a long semester. Im not sure how he is employed as a professor, nonetheless at UNC. Economics department should take a long hard look at how this guy teaches. Get ready to teach yourself.

One of the nicest teachers i have ever had. I agree with most of the reviews below but I think giving him a 1 is harsh. Thing about his class is that he is smarter than everyone else and does not really explain the work he does because he assumes we all understand already. YT will be your best friend for sure. Light grader on hw, hard on tests.

Guy has indeed a great personality. But when it comes to teaching and being tested on, things become a not enjoyable. Concepts are vaguely explained, and there are few examples and practices given, and you are expected to to have masterful application of things you haven't seen nor practiced. Do yourself a favor and stay clear of his classes.

One of the worst professors I've had at UNC. It's the last week of class and I don't know a single grade that I've gotten (on homework and/or midterms) and the overall material/design of the class is terrible. Disorganized, typos in slides and HW answers, and I've learned more from youtube videos about game theory.

Class is most definitely not a free A, a lot of work. Annoying part is you can have a horrible idea and do very well, and vise versa. Professor Greene is very smart and knows what she is doing, she is also a very good person, but not an easy class and would only recommend taking if very interested.

10/10 professor, pushes you out of your comfort zone and creates a very fun but professional environment. Pushes for participation in a large class which seems scary at first but you get used to it. Interesting lectures and often brings in guest speakers who are entrepreneurs from UNC. Always willing to help and easy to reach outside of class.

Not impossible to get an A but def a lot of work for a FC. Random group assignments that you work with on a project the entire semester, a good group could make or break the class. She likes to cold call and spin a wheel in a lecture of 300+ people. I normally don't mind group projects but this class was atrocious

Do not take this class if you do not enjoy assigned seats in lectures, group projects with 4 randoms, and being cold called in front of 400 people using a wheel spin. Class itself is not that hard to get an A in but mostly just annoying and full of entrepreneurship buzzwords and random "models" to remember for midterm and final

Susie is the BEST professor at UNC. Seriously. My UNC career took a 180 once I look this class with Susie. You MUST go to office hours to yap even if you don't have a question about the material just make one up she's so kind and caring and you'll be so grateful you did. Def need to put in work for the class but thats what makes it rewarding.
Great professor and has great experience. Put in the work with the group projects and you'll thrive.

Prof. Greene is amazing. This class ignited my passion for entrepreneurship and completely transformed how I see business and my future. It is energetic, hands on, and very collaborative. If you show up, participate, and prepare for the midterm and final, you will truly thrive.

Susie Greene has such a brilliant mind and I believe no matter what major you are, you will get great skills out of this class. She takes student ideas and builds on them in the moment and gets students thinking of great ideas-- her lectures are very clear and you will get a lot out of the class!

Susie is awesome and one of the most accessible professors outside of the classroom. The class is not an easy A but an easier A-/B+. Take it just to get to know her and MSA and I promise it will be worth it

One of my favorite classes I've ever taken. The Shuford Program is truly such a special place and this is the gateway to it. Susie is an incredible mentor and professor to have, so highly recommend meeting with her outside of class. Get ready for group project work (semester long project coming up with a company is the crux of the course).

just go to class and be a good team member=easy A. everyone who rates susie and this class low clearly did not research the class-thats on them. its a unique structure (Semester long group project) BUT SO HANDS ON! whether or not you want to do shuford i 100% recommend. my easiest class that semester but i learned the most.
annoying class

Dr. Greene knows her stuff. I really recommend the class- you have guest speakers, coaches, and hands-on sessions like no other class. Group project heavy, but projects and tests are pretty straightforward. Got a lot out of this class. This does have more work than other 3 credit classes, but def worth it. Highly recommend!

All the bad reviews are just people who expected an easy A. 125 isn't even hard and it's not a ton of work, I would say it's pretty average on both ends. I hate group work and was nervous since the whole semester is a group project, but i LOVED my group and it taught me so much. Susie is an AMAZING professor+this class is like no other. take it!!!

Overall this class isn't bad. If you are taking for a focus capacity pretty easy. This class feels like it shouldn't have a midterm/final but it does and they provide basically no guidelines on how to prepare. Not too much work, just some readings and videos with a quiz before each class. You grade is pretty reliant on having a good group.

Professor Greene knows her stuff. It is obvious that she tries to really engage the class and get them into the world of entrepreneurship. The class is really project heavy so be prepared for that but it is really rewarding in the end. Most students who take this course are too obsessed with their grades to enjoy learning the cool content

The professor is not at all flexible with grades after the semester is completed. Attendance is mandatory and missing 3 classes will result in a 50 on attendance grade (5% overall off grade), and missing 4 or more will result in a 0 (10% overall off grade). Under no circumstance would I recommend taking this class unless absolutely necessary.

Susie does a great job and illustrates lots of entrepreneurial qualities. Most guests are genuinely interesting presenters. However, 125 is such a goofy class. Group project is obviously a mixed bag of freeriding. Shuford feels too corporate; there are WAY too many frat bros on Snapchat during class to feel like I'm learning anything meaningful.

group project all semester long, I will say I wish there were no exams bc the project takes a lot of outside time already & that's all we focus on. Exams weigh a lot of your grade so even if you get 100s on all the assignments, the exams can do you dirty, however they aren't too bad. Study lec slides & take notes on Virtual sessions. final>midterm

It's fun and different from any other class I've taken- making me want to do the Shuford program! They bring in speakers (can be boring but still super interesting). Class consists of 1 midterm, final, group project, and virtual sessions and quizzes every week. Yes this class is time-consuming & depends on your group, but it's still pretty easy.

The class is structured like a seminar. Homework&project are fun and manageable. Has very open attitude toward AI. Lectures give you insights. Midterm is a little hard but the final is easy af, and he gives grades with flexibility. The only complaint is that he jumps between slides so fast, making it difficult to follow.

Omg this class was HARD. Material is extremely useful but also super challenging, ton of math/stats stuff you may not have seen before. However he really wants you to succeed, so the tests were graded very nicely even though they were tough. High expectations but willing to meet you where you're at.
He is a great professor that has taught me so much that I will be able to use in my life :)

A very insightful teacher with lectures and notes that are very clearly given and easily understood. Prof. Hansen is one of the best professors I a have had in economics, and I believe his teachings will guide me through the rest of my life.
best teacher of all time. If you do not take his class you are making a mistake
Hanson is a terrible teacher and an awful human being. Take anyone else.

Beware of this class! It looks similar to econ 470 but requires a crazy amount of background in stats and coding. Lectures are very boring and hard to stay followed with his monotone voice. Homework set due every week. And prepare not to see any of your grades or feedbacks until your final letter grade is posted.

The hardest class I've ever taken and the worst professor I've ever had at UNC. One time, when a student asked for an answer key, he said "If you understand the material, you'd be doing it right, so you don't need an answer key." On LDOC, he listed off a number of things to know for the final that we never went over during the semester.
He is Cool
Professor Kedagni is the BEST professor. He is easy to follow and always available if we need help.

Desire is a great professor and also a joy to talk to. He made econometrics enjoyable to learn and his problem sets, although somewhat challenging, are great review material. I would highly recommend you study and understand the problem sets and attend each class since he goes through important math proofs.
The exams felt very long and math/proof and he does not curve

ECON 470 is very difficult, no matter who you take it with. Kedagni was a really nice guy, but resources were super limited outside of class. Thankfully, I passed/failed this course because the average on the final was a 70 with no curving whatsoever.

I didn't like Econ 400, but Kedagni made me love econometrics! You have to go to class, since he takes attendance for a grade and includes concepts from lectures on exams. He's a chalkboard lecturer, which isn't everyone's cup of tea. My one gripe is that the midterms are way too long. However, their content isn't difficult. You just have to study.

Desire is a good lecturer and kind to students. Easy to follow along with, and he doesn't expect you to do any complicated proofs. His exams can be (very) long, but are almost exactly like practice problems, and all exams are graded out of 100 points but have at least 10 bonus points on them. Good option for a class as notorious as 470.

The average on the final was a 72. He refuses to curve anything in the class. His actual teaching style was not terrible, and a lot of the exams reused questions from the problem sets, but the fact that he did not curve a single test with the justification of "if 4-5 people get an A, the grades work" was terrible. The average class grade was a C+.
I took ECON 470 in fall 2023 and this course covers everything you need to know about linear regression. The pace of the class is very reasonable and Professor Kedagni's notes are easy to understand.
Probably the easiest 470 professor. The concepts in the class are not that complicated, he just grades the exams really strictly. Really nice guy to talk to in office hours.

Kedagni never made you feel bad if you asked to go over a topic again. Exams were p long but many problems were repeated from problem sets. So just study those solutions you'll be perfectly fine. He also works through problem sets in office hours. Attendance is taken but also there's not many resources outside of class anyway so don't skip!

I really enjoyed Professor Kédagni's lectures -- he's very enthusiastic about the material, making lectures very engaging. The problem sets are good practice for the exams, as the questions on the exams tend to resemble the homework questions. He also sometimes pulls questions from the textbook, so looking at some textbook problems is helpful too.

ECON 470 is hard no matter the professor, Kedagni has some issues with pacing/understanding our prior exposure but has the right idea. Attendance is mandatory and the lectures are helpful for actually applying what you learn, but working through textbook problems will help on the exams. Sometimes gives bonus points for answering questions in class.

Highly recommend taking 470 with a different professor. The class was disorganized and we didn't get through much of the material, which was super frustrating. The exams were really similar to the homework which was nice, but the lectures were really dull and overall left me with little new knowledge about the topic.

Must unorganized professor I have had. Was supposed to cover 6 chapters of material but only got through 4. Required to learn the other 1/3 of class material for the final independently during the last week of the course. Would not recommend this course for anyone, just wait and take 470 with different professor.
Really great professor who was helpful in office hours.
Best 500-level Econ elective. The course is very manageable if you keep up with homework and understand the lecture slides.

Stan is such a great professor. Lectures were very clear, and he is very funny. All the topics are grounded in real-world applications, and the models are pretty similar to those in classes like 410 or 420. Exam heavy, but exams are very similar to practice problems so study those and you will be good. Might be the best 500-level elective.

I really recommend taking a class with Mr. Rabinovich. His class is engaging and the material is interesting. He is helpful during office hours and checked in with me to make sure I was preparing well for the second midterm as I couldnt take the first one!!! 522 is based on three exams and a final theory paper.

Professor Stan is one of the best econ professors I have taken a class with. If you pay attention in lectures and work on the problem sets you won't have much trouble with the exams. Very funny guy and highly recommend for an econ 500 class. Minimal math, and ties a lot of previous econ concepts together.
Boring lectures and weird curving of the class. Your whole grade is based on exams. Not my favorite teacher.
Honestly, this class is not easy but Stan makes it so much better! His lectures are never boring and he always gives real world examples to help the material stick better! I LOVED this class!!
Stan is really nice, and the class is exciting, but the grading scale is based on distribution, need to prepare well for the exam.

So intelligent and funny. He makes macro easy to understand and his lectures are awesome. Tests can be tough but if you do the practice problems you will be fine. 522 is a good option for a 500-level econ course.
The best macro prof I ever met. So humorous, smart and crystal clear.
not good if you want to learn

Hincapie is a great professor, and every single class was actually interesting. He offers different grading schemes but if you always show up and are able to answer a question when he calls on you then its a free 8%. I will say that his exams are very difficult, though. Make sure to pay attention in class and understand the PS's and you'll do fine.

Pretty interesting topics covered in this course, difficult exams and some tough hws as well but he allows for cheat sheets which was nice. Also an option to be graded for participation to take some weight off of midterms grades. I opted not to do that but if you're good which being cold called it's chill. Overall fun class and would recommend!

Andres is a chilllllerrrrrrrr. Don't acknowledge the old reviews. Not sure what he used to be like, he's definitely not a 2.0. 48% of this class is FREE (easy HWs, attendance, participation). Exams are tough though. Content was extremely interesting, especially rational addiction. -1 star for an A being a 95. Decent 400-level elective overall.

Really chill dude. He tried to get most people to participate in class and make sure everyone understood the stuff. The class material was pretty slight as well, especially for a 400-level ECON elective. 2 MT + Final + Final Project(free 100). Overall, really cool teacher, idk why the ratings are so bad. Also, he kinda swole.

Is he the best teacher of all time? No. But his rating makes him seem a lot worse than he actually is. Cheat sheets for both midterms and the final. Attendance, homework, and an easily graded project account for 48% of your grade. Don't take him if you don't need to, but don't be worried about taking him if you have to. Pretty average course.

Professor Hincapie is a great person, but maybe not the best teacher. The grading scheme gives you a little bit of flexibility with attendance but I really recommend coming to class and asking questions. The lectures were pretty confusing and the homework, while easy, didn't really prepare me for the exams. Very accessible outside of class though!

Don't take this class if you don't have to. The lectures are difficult to follow, so completing the homework becomes pretty challenging. Definitely would be a pretty easy ECON course if someone else taught it, but Hincapie is unfortunately hard to follow.

Compared to the other Econ electives, this one wasn't that bad. But I still wouldn't take this class unless you have to. Extremely lecture and test heavy. Grading feedback isn't always clear. Only graded by a few things and he takes a while to put in those things. If you're willing to go to every class, do it. If not, say goodbye to a good grade.

+1 star for relevant coursework. Moral hazard and the rational addiction model were very interesting.

+1 star for practicing what he preaches. Buddy is jacked, appropriate for a health econ class.

Exams were difficult, but the curve was nice. He also released final grades during the main commencement ceremony, not a cool move.
stay away from this class

Old reviews are lame, dude is a G. Grading scheme has enough easy components that its overall pretty fair. Cheat sheets for exams. This class is pretty average for a 400-level elective, always posts annotated slides and practice exams. Lecture notes are clear and exam questions are pretty fair save a couple T/F questions that might be nitpicking.

Hincapié has clearly improved based on feedback. Unlike past reviews, I found him approachable, fair, and an excellent lecturer who encourages critical thinking. This class is challenging, yet manageable, and promotes interest in health ECON. You'll do well if you complete the homework and study the slides. Highly recommend taking a class with him!

I really enjoyed this class, I cannot believe this review is so low. Super straightforward, not condescending at all when you ask for help. I found this content really interesting and relevant to our current political landscape too - probably one of my more favorite electives I have taken at UNC.
The class is definitely tough, but everything, literally everything is in the textbook. Lectures aren't difficult to follow, homeworks are easy and so are the exams.
This guy gets way too much hate. I had a wonderful experience taking this class.

Andres is not as bad as his reviews suggest. While exams aren't easy, there are plenty of opportunities to boost your grade through homework, attendance, and an easily graded project. The reality is that easy 400 level Econ courses don't exist and if you are on this RMP you clearly aren't in a position to be picky. Take the course, you'll survive.
I feel like he just does not understand student learning in the slightest.
Horrible. Stay away from this guy
grading is ambiguous. Takes off points without saying why.
Professor Balaban is an excellent econ teacher and led engaging lectures throughout the semester.

I know she retired but she is a inspirational professor who deserves her jersey to be hung up in the rafters. Her ball knowledge was unmatched and knew econ well too. I'll never forget when she dropped this bar I'll leave you with: "If your partner doesn't treat you like their valentine every day, leave them!". The class went wild - my goat.
Econ 101 with Professor Balaban is no easy feat, but with dedication and the right resources like unstuckstudy ai, it's doable. Attend lectures, review practice problems, and you'll nail the exams.

Professor Balaban is super knowledgeable about economics, and I actually enjoyed her 101 class. It is a hard class and lots of studying is the only way to get a good grade. Lectures were mostly good but could sometime get boring.

This class is so incredibly hard. Professor Balaban is a very kind happy person but her class is impossible. I would definitely recommend attending and paying attention in class as well as taking advantage of her out of class help!

Professor Balaban was fantastic for ECON101. She well-prepared all of her lectures, clearly cares about her students and wants us to do well. If you do what you are told, it is easy to do well in this class.

Always do the 60-question multiple choice on every chapter to succeed in the midterms. 
Rita Balaban explains everything in great detail, but it is also quite boring since most of the problems can be solved in 15 seconds and her explanations can go as long as 5 minutes. However, she can crack a funny joke sometimes. Totally recommend her.

Balaban truly is a great econ101 prof. She provides many resources to do good on tests. Econ101 takes MUCH effort but put in time & energy you'll get good grades. Take econ a sem w/ easier or fewer classes bc it requires a lot of time. Test study tips: read ch. notes, LOTS of practice problems, review recitations, and def review her lecture slides.

I swear to yall that Balaban is by far the best Econ101 Prof at UNC. You should easily pass this class as attendance and completion is worth around 1/4 of your grade. The exams are difficult but should easily be able to pass the class. I never studied and finished with a B, so with minimal effort should pass.
Subject material is quite difficult but Balaban teaches it as well as anyone. If you apply yourself you should do alright.

Prof. Balaban does a fantastic job teaching a course that has way too much material packed into one semester. Study hard for the tests, they are hard but if you go through the additional resources she provides, you will be fine.

I cannot say enough good things about Professor Balaban. She is a legend and an amazing lecturer, this course is set up for students to optimize their economics knowledge. While this was a tough class and you have to put a lot of time into it, I enjoyed it and Dr. Balaban taught it very well. She also has a very funny personality, highly recommend!

It's so clear that the people who left bad reviews did not study nor care about this class. The amount of outside resources that Prof. Balaban should have set everyone up for success. Her midterm Q.s are similar in concept/difficultly most of the pollev Q.s and recitations. It is more than attainable to do well in this class.

The reviews saying she is awful are so dramatic. You do have to put a lot of time into this class but if you manage your time you will do well. Do all of the practice problems after her class lecture. She gives all of the resources you need, you just have to actually do it. Exams aren't easy but they follow her content. It is flipped so do the work

Dr. Balaban sets up the class in a way that maximizes your potential to succeed. The course is objectively difficult, but she provides extensive office hours, practice questions, and class examples that help you succeed if you take advantage of them.

Econ was a difficult class, but Professor Balaban was fantastic and was extremely transparent and honest about her grading expectations. She offered so many helpful resources throughout the semester, and her TA team put a lot of effort into trying to help everyone succeed. She truly cares and tries to make each student ensure that they can succeed
This class was torture. She is super nice, but not too helpful outside the classroom. The tests play a huge part in the grade for this class. Just be ready to study and cry :)

Prof Balaban was an amazing lecturer and so good at explaining concepts clearly. The exams were nearly the exact same as the MC practice problems she gave in Sakai. The grading was really fair too, esp with higher grade midterm weighted more than lower grade midterm. As long as you study and pay attention, the class is not difficult!

Econ in itself is a challenging class but she makes it harder for no reason, her ULAs even said that the questions she gives make no sense at times or are way more complicated than it needs to be. I literally broke my back to try and get a good grade in this class.
Do NOT take ECON 101 with Rita. It is a flipped classroom which sucks. Her exams are 10x harder than the practice problems she gives in class.

Professor Duarte was an extremely caring and passionate professor. I found him funny and tried to make a boring class more interesting through real world examples. With that said, the class is very difficult. I could not follow along in lectures easily and it took me time outside of class to grasp the topics. Tests are very hard, but have big curve

Duarte is great. 445 is a math-heavy continuation of Micro with a lot of game theory involved. He keeps lectures interesting with real-life legal examples. Exams are hard but the curve is very generous. If you're decent at math, you'll be fine for an A-.

Class is insanely hard. That being said Marco works with you to ensure you don't fail. He has numerous extra credit opportunities, hw is graded for completion, and exams are curved extensively (30=C, 40=B, etc.). While this class is not by any means a guarranteed A I found it easy to obtain a B with pretty average effort. Just go to class.

Arbitrary grader. The topics are interesting, but he speedruns through them, and lectures have little to do with his horribly difficult math-heavy exams. Gets easily frustrated and mad when the class doesn't understand his teaching methods. I threw up one question into midterm 2, and he wouldn't let me retake it. Don't take this course, trust me!!

This class will have super challenging midterms where you just speedrun solve everything you know, but the curve will SAVE YOU from getting below a B unless you skip class/put in 0 effort. Legit got a 14 on a midterm curved to C- LOL. Content is super interesting, pricing strategy/game theory, you actually learn something meaningful in this class.

I would avoid this at all costs unless you have to have it for credit. As far as a general 400 level econ elective this is a horrible choice. Class is ridiculously difficult, averages on exams are in the 40s. 80% of the class is graded on exams. There is curve on exams where a 30 is a C and 60 is an A. Overall just a miserable experience.

Do not take this class unless you need the credit. Exams are nearly impossible to finish, and lecture notes lack depth or relevance to the math-heavy tests. Lectures are dull and hard to follow. The professor is brilliant but assumes everyone can keep up, making this one of the toughest and least rewarding econ classes offered.

Material is challenging enough that going to lectures is important even if not required. Problem sets graded on completion, which offsets extremely difficult tests with averages below 50%. All exams are curved extensively. Marco knows his stuff and applies class topics to real world issues. A must-have class for those interested in consulting

His lectures are fun, tho sometimes a bit hard to follow. However, his lecture notes explain everything. He is very accessible for help, and responds to emails quickly. If you keep up with class, you should get an A- at least. I unfortunately missed the deadline of a problem set and fell behind in class after being sick for 3 weeks.

Overall Marco is a great guy and can be very personable. His information that he teaches you in class isn't too hard and pretty interesting but the test were quite intuitive and takes further knowledge from outside of what he teaches you. Everyone would fail the test but would curve a lot to match older section grading scales, a 30 would be a C.

Marco is a nice guy, but this class is just not worth it. The material presented should not have been that difficult to learn, but there was an utter lack of resources, and each homework and test question had layers of intuition stacked on it. Midterm averages were right around 50%. With 20's curving to C's. Homeworks are graded for completion.

Absolutely love her, her lectures are very interesting and she is super sweet. She makes sure to answer any questions or even just chat when you need. Very heavy on group work with a debate, a final presentation, and in class assignments. Large thesis at the end but you work on it progressively throughout class so no worries. Tough grader though
I loved this class and Dr. Griffin was always so knowledgable and helpful. The guest lectures she brought in were amazing too. Would love to take more classes with Dr. Griffin in the future!

Dr. Griffin is super kind and very knowledgeable in her field. Enjoyed her lectures, midterm and final are oral exams, projects were long but interesting. She brought in a lot of guest speakers, so it was great hearing different perspectives in clinical psych. Would take another class with her again
She is really good.

Dr. Griffin was an amazing professor. The grading for the case studies are a little strict, but as long as you are extremely detailed in your responses you will do well. Dr. Griffin is super understanding and goes above and beyond to support her students inside and outside of the classroom.

Go to class! Lots of points from the exit tickets and group activities. The semester-long project was cool. I like how she focused on applying the content rather than testing. I learn a lot from her classes! Only downside was the final was oral, and was graded kinda harshly imo.

All of this class is is group work, which is horrible because a lot of the group members don't do the work and you get penalized for it through your grades. Get a good group for the final project because I  had to end up doing primarily by myself. She's nice but I swear half the time she doesn't actually know the facts she just speaks like she does
This class was great until the final. It was an oral exam, and Dr. Griffin asked very hard questions compared to what the TAs asked.

The class was great until the final. She introduced a new oral exam that was poorly structured. We had 4 minutes for 3 questions, but my interviewer, Professor Griffin, asked harder, extra, and off-guide questions that were completely unrelated to my client. Other students with TAs had simpler ones. It felt unfair and biased.

She wants really specific and strong evidence for each case study. While that is not unreasonable, she sort of gives off the impression that there is only one right answer and grades harshly based on that. She expects extremely clear and detailed work while her questions in themselves are vague and feel like they're up to interpretation.
No tests, lots of group work. The homework and in-class assignments are pretty chill. She's a very knowledgeable and great professor.

Dr. Griffin is great and very knowledgable in the psychology field. I mainly interacted with the TAs, but she is very organized with her assignments and grading. There is a good amount of reading but it was helpful on the assignments and tests. The material is straight forward but can get repetitive/boring at times. Overall great class/professor.
For the group days, your grade depends on the TA you get that week, but otherwise the class was awesome. I was able to learn a lot with a reasonable amount of time going to the class.

Super great profession who wants you to learn and succeed, not just pass a test. Class very lecture based and homework includes lots of textbook readings and GRQs. Work with a group throughout the semester and on one big presentation for the "final."

Griffin is a good teacher, knowledgeable but understanding. 245 was a pretty easy class, considering there were no exams and only case studies. Plenty of leeway with missing classes (I think you can miss up to 20 almost) - most important consideration is to choose a good group at the start of the year, since you will be with them throughout.

Dr. Griffin is very likable, so much so I feel bad for not enjoying her class. Even more so because the content was interesting. The workload isn't too difficult, but it's poorly implemented. Restructuring the assignments could instantly lower to difficulty of this class to a 4 to a 1 or 2 without losing any content.

Dr. Griffin is the best! There are no tests, instead, you are graded by your analysis of a case study in class each week. The case studies are done with a group and include answering 4 - 6 questions with 1-2 paragraphs. Grading is super kind, and professor/Tas are very willing to help. Very little work outside of class. HIGHLY recommend.

This class has been my favorite so far! Every week is set up the same. Readings, short online reading quizzes, lectures on read material then group case studies. She is incredibly sweet and offers wiggle room. Allows drops due to potentially sensitive material (ex: suicide). No final exam but a large group project.

Dr. Griffin was a fantastic professor! I highly recommend taking any class with her. There was a very intensive clinical project, but it was interesting and we had a lot of time to complete each part over the course of the semester. Her TAs graded fairly. Overall, I loved this course!

Engaging lectures by Professor Griffin, with insightful guest speakers. Tests require prep, but Unstuck AI was a big help for studying. Assignments can be harshly graded by TAs, but overall a great class.

d InQuizitive assign. due before every class. Lectures are copied & pasted from the textbook readings, & you learn no new info during lecture. All the test questions came from outside readings, NOT from the textbook. I failed every test due to this, even though they were all multiple choice & I made 100s on InQuizitive assign. & paper.

Dr. H seems like a good person but not the best lecturer. I really tried to pay attention in class but he speaks very slowly and quietly so my attention would drift away so fast. Despite not having great notes, I honestly didn't think the exams were that bad and all I did was go through slides (and speaker notes!!) before the exams.

70% of your grade comes from exams which are impossible to prepare for as no study guide or practice questions are given. For the final, we were told to review everything. The material isn't difficult, but lectures are not engaging. Homework isn't representative of the difficulty of exams, and counts for a very small portion of your final grade.

Just not it at all!! I wish I was more prepared for his class, test are extremely hard and it's so much content that it's really hard to figure out what you need to study for. He's nice but class is just really challenging

Prof H is sweet but RUN! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! or really any class with him. Lectures are boring+confusing, I learned nothing from this class,and grade entirely depends on 3 exams that areso HARD. When I asked him how to prep for exams he said basically "idk, just review every single thing we've read or talked about". Sweet guy, horrible teacher

Professor Hallquist was okay. Test are very challenging and you are only graded by a couple of assignments. My only advice is make sure you really prepare for the exams bc they are tricky fr. This is for PSYC 501 btw.

While she is a funny lecturer, she makes this class way harder than it needs to be. Her exams are designed to trick you and contain little details mentioned once in class. She isn't accessible outside of class either, only TAs

Loeb is an amazing lecturer (and imo the funniest prof at unc), but be prepared to study a LOT outside of class to do well on the exams. This class is really brute memorization, so be ready to spam flashcards. I personally never read the textbook as it felt like a waste of time, but memorize EVERYTHING on the docs she provides for each unit.

Don't take this professor. Psych101 isn't a standardized class, professor actually matters. Doesn't record lecture, textbook and what she says contradict, her exams are extremely difficult consisting of “what is false” questions rather than application questions. Attendance is lowkey mandatory, small details she says in lecture matter on tests.

Funny lecturer but goes on many tangents. Don't study solely from the textbook. Lowk just study the Guided In-lecture class notes and add a bit more and spam practice problems. She asks for very specific things in her exams and they're kinda hard so don't procrastinate! Made it more difficult than it had to be… Fond a diff prof if possible

She makes psych 101 way harder than it should be. Tests are pretty difficult and consist of pretty much all pick which is false questions. She also picks and chooses what she thinks is right and wrong from the textbook. If you don't study for the exams and read the textbook you will fail. The mandatory studies are also a pain.

she is so funny, her lectures are always engaging and interesting I highly recommend taking at least 1 class from her. I had this first semester freshman year and she has been my favorite professor so far. tests are relatively challenging but study all material and you'll do good!
Despite it being a large lecture, she tried her best to be engaging. Attendance was taken and checked daily, but there was also extra credit given for participation so it's worth it to show up.

Great professor and engaging lectures, but exams are very difficult for a 101 class. Average tends to be low 70, and the wording on questions seems to be intentionally confusing. I enjoyed the content matter but was not the free A i expected.
Really interesting lectures!

Dr. Loeb is genuinely so engaging and hilarious. Her lectures were enjoyable and easy to listen to. The exams were a bit more difficult than anything in class, but she provides outlines for each unit leading up to the exams. Definitely take 101 with Dr. Loeb!

Dr. Loeb is hilarious and every class was engaging! The class is very textbook and lecture heavy. Spread the textbook readings out and write down the examples she gives in class as they are helpful when memorizing for tests later on. Great class!!

Absolutely loved Professor Loeb. Even for a class with 350 students, lecture was extremely engaging and hilarious. Midterms were very easy and logical. While there was no curve on midterms like previous sections, we did receive a generous curve for the final (not cumulative and very easy).

The class was fine in terms of difficulty. You have to study for the tests alot but u do have a lot of opportunities for extra credit. It is not hard to get an A in the class what so ever. The lectures however are so boring but decent class to take

Actually enjoyed going to class! Really flexible grading - allows drops for every grading category, including exam. Attendance assignments give you lots of credit just for showing up! Tons of extra credit chances. Do the work and you'll get a decent grade.

Prof. Loeb is by far my favorite teacher I've had! This class is solely lecture-based, but she is incredibly engaging and hilarious. I genuinely enjoyed every class and felt like the time flew by. Easy A if you show up and pay attention since she covers everything you need in class. Honestly never even opened the textbook but did very well.
honestly easy to get an A if you put effort in.
Loeb's exams are fair.  However, not an understanding professor with regard to class policies and attendance.

Great professor! Recommend showing up to the lectures as you'll learn most everything you need to know just by listening. Spend a few hours studying before each exam, and you'll be fine. Great class for anyone studying or interested in psychology.

3 exams, she drops the lowest one. 1 non-cumulative final. Not a great lecturer, but not bad. Quizzes at home over each chapter (best 8/11). Participation assignment each class, but you have 3/4 absences. Particpation Pool required, which was annoying but is for all psyc classes.

lectures are engaging and build off of the textbook. Read the textbook and take quiz at home before class. Participation is taken every day, but three are dropped. Also, extra credit oppurtunities just for talking in class and she gave us a 10% curve on the final. Would highly recommend for a freshman.

LOVED the content of the class and Dr. Abramowitz was very laid back and cool. He really doesn't try to trick you on the exams. He doesn't grade your attendance, but you won't get notes without going to class. I loved not having any assignments, but the entirety of your grade is based on 3 exams (2 midterms, 1 final), and 2 case conferences.

Dr. Abramowtiz is MY GOAT! He is such an amazing lecturer and makes class super engaging and entertaining.  He truly wants his students to do well. All of the exams are easy if you just go to class and pay attention! This is of my favorite classes Ive taken yet at UNC! It is very test heavy, but if you study and go to class you will do great.

Dr. Abramowitz was always funny during lectures. Always willing to help. You're graded on 2 midterms, a final, and a few case studies (group assignment). No grade cushioning, but exams are pretty straightforward, mostly factual and not application based. Attendance is not graded but you have to come to class since he puts very little on his slides.

TAKE THIS CLASS as a freshman. It's an easy and interesting class with no tests, only short weekly writing assignments, and a group project. You get to learn from a really caring and intelligent professor who makes the class fun. He is very helpful and understanding with deadlines or missing class. He's the best professor I've had so far.

If you are a freshman, TAKE THIS CLASS. It is not overwhelming at all. No final exam or final paper, so you have more time to study for finals for other classes. You have very short (around 200 words) writing assignments each week, and one presentation you do in a group in class. It was so easy, and let me get close to a great professor.

As someone who likes biopsychology and understands it, I didn't like this class at all. Professor Christoffel just read off his slides and his lectures were long and not engaging. Tests were cumulative and unnecessarily difficult which dragged my overall grade down. There is a group project which is easy to get full points on.

Tbh Dr. C isn't bad.  Sure, the first paper was a little rough, but just the rubric for the others, and you're fine.  Exams were not too awful if you study.  Take- home quizzes/scientist spotlights were grade buffers.  Also, you can always email him to talk about grade issues.  And he always let class out early. Overall, not a TERRIBLE class.

Just don't. Lectures were so painfully boring and sometimes vague and exams were insanely precise. No feedback was given on assignments, you just got a grade for no reason. His exams were SO unorganized, even though they were online and automatically graded they were graded wrong. Do yourself a favor and take it with someone else.

He has been one of the worst professors I have had at UNC so far. You basically have to teach yourself the material and the exams are very detailed. He seems to not care about teaching at all and lectures right off of the slides. He doesn't give feedback on papers and the lectures are not engaging at all. Take PSYC 220 with anyone else!

I really did not like Dr. Christoffel because he wasn't good at lecturing, tests were wildly hard, we always left class early (meaning it feels like we missed a lot of content that was still on tests). Group project is easy. There is no feedback on the 4 papers due throughout the semester (got a 76 on one with no explanation). I do not recommend

Do not recommend. Extremely boring lectures, difficult tests, and he clearly was just not prepared to teach this class. One time the highest exam score was an 89 and he did not curve at all. The group projects and pre-class quizzes did boost your grade, though.

Content is pretty cool; class could have been a lot better if Dr. C was more enthusiastic & accessible. Quite obvious he didn't care much about us, he would answer questions in class but wasn't helpful beyond that. Beginning of class was a wreck as he didn't provide any insight on grading or studying criteria. Tests and lectures are overly detailed

Not a great professor. Nothing has clear grading standards, you can get a failing grade on a paper with literally no feedback. Exams are hard as hell (all of the test averages are in the 70s) and lectures are short without enough info. Do not recommend.

Dr. Christoffel's lectures were monotone and didn't really provide anything that you couldn't gain from the book. He tried to take attendance but his pollev's never worked, and while the quizzes were really easy the exams were very hard. We had to beg him to give us a rubric for papers, but at least he lets class out early. Take with someone else!

He can come off as condescending/rude. He lectures monotone the whole time, and he doesn't even try to keep students engaged. He grades papers harshly and doesn't give feedback. The questions on exams can seem random but aren't too bad if you study. You can get a good grade if you put in the effort, but I'd take this class with anyone else.

Second time taking it with Dr. Harrison for 210 after psyc 270! Truly such an amazing professor and an overall really kind guy. He's passionate and caring for his students and even makes it a point to remember your name in such a large auditorium. Best professor ever I've had!!

dr harrison is the best!!! he is so caring and will go out of his way to help his students. take home midterm and open note final. grade can depend on your TA and how harsh they grade though. otherwise, definitely take 210 with him! hoping to take 270 with him in the future!

Dr. Harrison is one of the best professors at UNC. He's an amazing guy who makes a genuine effort to form a relationship with his students. Class itself was very simple, although some TA's graded a lot harsher than others. Take-home midterm and open-note final made the class a breeze.

TA grading could be variable on the assignments but I learned so much. Lots of extra credit opportunities, one take-home midterm and in-person final, both open note. Lectures were funny and worth the walk to B school. don't hesitate to take!

Professor Harrison was very encouraging and gave great feedback when I needed help. He is always there if you have questions and answers emails quickly. Take assignments seriously and always ask questions in class! Definitely recommend this class for freshmen and hope to take him for 270.
Super chill and all the assignments are easy!! Open-note and open-internet midterm and final exam. Take this professor during your time at UNC!! You will not regret it!
He was a great professor, I learned a lot. I felt like he really cared about the students and wanted them to succeed. I cannot recommend taking his classes enough!
One of the nicest professors at UNC. He is understanding, responds to emails, and makes a kind of boring subject much more engaging. Highly recommend taking at least one class at UNC with him
