Dr. Harrison is so kind and a great lecturer! He genuinely cares about his students and does all he can to see them succeed. Would definitely recommend taking any of his classes.
Such an amazing professor and overall nice guy. You should definitely take a class with him if you have the chance to.
Amazing professor and genuinely kind man. Take class with him!

Awesome guy who takes you through how to do a study and write a research paper. He made it all very doable and was always there to help. Quizzes are online and open notes. Final is also open notes, but in person. The major part of the grade is the paper.

Professor Harrison is kind and accomodating, and this course is super helpful for writing. The course involves a semester-long research paper which is broken up into sections, and there are clear rubrics to follow for each. Take notes during class to make studying for the final easier, as the final is open note!  Attendance is through PollEv.

Believe these reviews, Professor Harrison is amazing. I am not a psych major, but I was still able to gain a lot from this course. It strongly helped that Professor Harrison always cared about his students and their comprehension of the material. If you're like me and simply in need of a research and discovery class, I highly recommend this course.

🐐

There is groupwork but it's manageable and he is always happy to help you out
I took him for PSYC 210 online, and he's very nice and helpful! He's also pretty chill and understanding.

Very kind and accessible professor who responds fast to emails about any questions. He is there for you so utilize those office hours. Grade is mainly made up of project papers which is just sections of one big paper you compile at the end for the final project.

This is my second semester with Dr. Harrison after 210. He remembered me and is still so kind and understanding. Amazing lectures, funny, helpful, and fun to talk to. It's clear he cares a lot about his students and loves what he teaches. Highly recommend taking any classes with him if you can.

Dr. Harrison is a great guy and wants everyone to succeed. No question is stupid to him. The course involves a semester-long research paper, but it's broken up into manageable sections. You are given everything you need to do well (examples, outlines, rubric, data, etc). Attendance was only counted for the first week or so.

Phenomenal professor! Very passionate about the topics in class! The class itself is very draining in the sense of the semester is spent writing a research paper. Don't procrastinate and you'll do great! If you do, you'll be fine! To me, the content of the class was kind of dull, but it's centered on research, so it's expected. Definitely take it!
Super sweet, passionate about teaching, and available outside of class!

This class was amazing! Dr. Estle was always accessible outside of class and her lectures were always engaging with an activity at the end of each one. Creating quizlets definitely helped, and I did not have to rely on the textbook as much for the exams. As a double major, content is very manageable with STEM classes.

She really cared about her students. Interesting lectures and in class activities. 3 exams with multiple choice worth 80% of grade and take home essay questions worth 20%. Final exam is optional and replaces lowest midterm grade+ half a page cheat sheet. Textbook quizzes take home for each chapter, 3 tries and 4 homework assignments.

One of my fav PSYC classes here! She is very knowledgeable and slides are clear and highly applicable to the exams. Need textbook for quizzes, but are open resource. In class activities were for attendance, but also very fun. I would say I've learned much information in this course compared to any other at UNC.

Exceptionally engaging lecturer. Exams were very fair, plenty of resources available to prepare for them and they aligned perfectly with lectures and learning checks. Understanding of students and fair penalties for late assignments. Approachable and helpful. Lectures very applicable to real life, which made them even more interesting.

Dr. Estle was a great professor. You literally don't have to read the textbook because her lectures cover everything. For the homework quizzes you might have to glance at the textbook but its not necessary. The tests are verbatim from the lecture slides (which she gives to you) so just make some flash cards on that and you'll be good.

Loved this class and the lectures were pretty engaging and easy to follow along. Not much homework and grade mostly relied on tests, but the tests are simple multiple choice questions with a take home essay question.

She is so kind. Exams were fair and all from the learning checks. She is very helpful with stuff you dont understand. No need to read the textbook, just search during the quiz. Homework isnt hard if you follow the grading rubric, and FINAL EXAM IS OPTIONAL!!

Dr. Estle was an amazing professor. She truly wants you to succeed in her class, and if you need help understanding a concept, she takes the time to help. She is so kind and is always high-energy, but not in a corny way. She is sunlight personified, and truly understands her craft. If I could, I would take every single class with her!

Genuinely the sweetest prof, she truly cares about her students and the content she teaches. For 220, she always tries to incorporate an interactive learning activity that helps most students learn the content better. She is very considerate, and her class quickly became my fav over this semester.

Easiest NSCI prof & class ever. Her lectures drag quite a bit and she is not super engaging, but she is extremely kind and cares about student success. The exams can be a bit tricky, but her learning checks are gold for exam prep. The final is optional if you are happy with your grade and the homeworks/quizzes are super easy. Very easy A.

Oh how I love this woman. She truly is such a caring and passionate professor who wants you to succeed. Tests are a little tricky with the wording but if you read the textbook you can make it out. Homework and class assignments are incredibly easy.
She's very sweet and caring. The tests are easy as long as you attend the class and prepare for them.
Such a sweetheart. Her tests are super, super easy. Very lenient attendance and other assignments. Easy A
Overall, Sara was one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Super caring and nice and would make an effort to see you succeed.
Really sweet professor and engaging lecturer! The content of the class is pretty interesting and straightforward.

Dr. Estle is incredible. You can tell she really wants you to learn, and cares about the subject she teaches. The content is difficult, but she makes it very approachable. Final is optional (replaces lowest exam grade) and there are plenty of assignments other than exams to help your grade. Please take this class with Dr. Estle, she's the best!

Dr. Estle is one of the best and kindest professors I have had at UNC. She makes otherwise tough content really approachable and her teaching style and sense of humor make class a really welcoming environment. However, you do have to attend lecture because she adds a lot of things that are key for exams but aren't on the slides.
True Queen, nothing to say. If you take her class, you will have the best experience forever. I can't say how much I enjoy about the lecture, and the grading is mild. BEST PROFESSOR FOREVER!!!
Nicest Psych professor at UNC. Entertaining too

I thought Dr. Sevetson was an excellent professor. Towards the end of the semester, they become very flexible with grades, as there are numerous exams you take throughout the semester. As long as you pay attention in class and try hard on your exams and projects, Dr. Sevetson will push you to ensure you get an A. Definitely take a class with them!
They are a fantastic and kind professor and they do not deserve the negative reviews. Learning definitely is dependent on attending lectures and asking good questions!

Not sure why she has anything other than 5s on here. Most reasonable professor I've ever had, not necessarily a free A but doesn't make it harder than it has to be and it's clear her main goal is for you to learn. Very approachable, accessible outside of class, engaging in lecture, and makes it clear that she cares about you.
One of the best professors ever!  Love Dr. Sevetson, highly recommend!

Dr. Sevetson is really passionate about what she teaches, and it is very clear from her lectures. Assignments and lectures are incredibly clear and always have very straightforward instructions. Group projects are fun and make learning a lot more enjoyable. Attendance is important to actually understand the material for quizzes!

Dr. S is a great professor. Attending class is crucial for understanding, as it is lecture heavy, HOWEVER she makes learning very accessible. While she does have some formal assessments, she makes learning more fun and approachable by allowing for many collaborative opportunities and fun projects in place of tests as well! Highly recommend!

She oversimplifies the material, and the exams expect much deeper understanding. Most of the learning comes from the TA, not her. The group work only helps if you choose a good group. She will interrupt herself 100 times before she completes a sentence, so it is impossible to follow her train of thought.

Takes class WAY too seriously. Can never "game" attendance because she makes sure to count people in classroom and compare it with PollEv numbers. Slides posted but unhelpful because 80% content is based on what she says and assumes she taught (but didn't!!). Very stressful for a 200 level class so expect a project/exam due every other week + HW.

Great person but NOT professor. If you want to take 222 because you heard it was easy, take it with another professor. Very knowledgeable but expects PhD level analysis from students. 4 exams, 4 projects, a final project due on LDOC. Grading very subjective and assumption-based. TAs not helpful whatsoever. Same group whole semester.

Dr. S is a great lecturer, very knowledgeable and excited by the material which imo makes it easier to pay attention. Funny too which helps! Dr. S takes feedback from students to improve the course; very willing to hear critiques if necessary. Also answers questions almost conversationally and doesn't mind back and forth to help us understand.

Material wasn't hard, but lectures were extremely rushed and test questions were way beyond what we learned. NEVER enough time for tests because there was an individual & group part in 45 mins. No time for group projects, and grading was slow & subjective, lots of points off for no reason. They are condescending & disorganized. I don't recommend.

Dr.S is very flexible and accomodating, and she is great at explaining complex topics. She relies a lot on student feedback, which is great. She was also very open to helping you understand concepts beyond the class and fostered curiosity. The only bad thing was the collaborative quizzes. It is hard to do well in the class if you had a bad group

There was lots of work in this class and quizzes were tough, but it's not hard to do well because she balances them out with group projects. Projects were often very tedious, so definitely pick groups wisely. Dr. S is pretty accommodating though. Overall, really liked her as a professor and as a person. The class is doable, just takes some work.

This class was interesting and Jess is a good prof. This class was pretty easy to do well in, but it comes with a lot of work. There is either an exam or a project for each unit (8 units) so your pretty much either studying or working on a project every week. The exams for each unit have an individual and collaborative section, but are difficult.

Very kind and understanding professor. Alternates between assigning a project or quiz for each unit. Projects do take a bit of time, but they help you learn material well. Quizzes were pretty easy if you just review lecture slides and learning objectives. By just attending / paying attention in lecture, you can guarantee an A for sure.

This is one of my favorite classes to take at Carolina! The professor is incredible and really tries to get to know you as a person. She breaks down material in an easy-to-understand way. The collaborative assessments can be hard, but they test your knowledge of the material. You have your group to work with, and if you study, you'll do great!

Dr. Sevetson is the best professor I have ever had! Her lectures are hilarious, and she knows how to "dumb down" hard topics for you to understand. She gives out a lot of group projects and group assessments, so choose your group wisely. I would 100% take this class again.

Sevetson seems great and all, and even tries to make jokes and come across as very nice. However, she always gave us huge projects on our breaks (fall break, wellness day, etc.) and does these things called collaborative quizzes... her quiz questions are worded so obscurely that I literally felt like I couldn't understand the English language.

Professor Sevetson has a very flexible way of administering exams, giving projects and exams for every unit. As long as you don't procrastinate and truly engage with the topic, this course will be an easy A. She curves exams based on how the class did. She makes an effort to get to know you and wants to see you succeed.

Super nice but she reads off her slides and class is very boring. Attendence is mandatory so you can't just teach yourself in your own time. Only 2 exams that are weighted pretty heavily and weekly assignments. Also there's too much content shes trying to cover and we rush through every class. Easy A but still wouldn't reccommend.
talks super fast and goes through material quickly. but, shes a great lecturer and assignments are super easy if you try. this course is just a lot of material to memorize.

The material and case studies were always very interesting! The tests were fair and many questions came directly from the pollev reviews. The other assignments were pretty light. Attendance was counted, but 5 absences were allotted. There is a textbook but I didn't even need to use it.
she's so great and a really great lecturer! totally recommend this class - only one midterm and one final and very litter work outside of class. Plus very interesting!

You can tell she knows the way to teach effectively after studying human memory. While studying, I felt like I remembered everything because of the helpful examples she showed and elaborated on. Assignments are easy and poll everywhere reviews are also very helpful.

I LOVED her class! She shows real-time examples of complex topics, and it makes learning so much better. She's also really understanding. I had some things come up and couldn't make it to class, and she didn't count it. She took the top 4/5 quizzes and 8/9 assignments. You also got 5 attendances free without punishment. Overall, HIGHLY recommend.

She's a really good lecturer for being a grad student and makes the information very accessible. Lots of interactive examples and videos. Assignment and quiz pretty much every week and due on Friday night which is annoying.

She is very nice and very down to answer questions. She also is very easy grader when it came to the hw assignments I got 10/10 on all of them and I think the longest I ever spent on one was like 30 min. The tests are also pretty easy, I got A's on both. Plus she curved both which was nice. There is one midterm and a final.

Prof Powers was so resourceful!  Detailed lecture slides posted, 9 assignments (lenient grading), 6 textbook/lecture quizzes, and only 1 midterm. Participation is taken for each class using pollev, but the questions are SUPER HELPFUL for exam studying. Final is 100 MC questions, but if you study and pay attention in class you'll do really well!

Although Professor Powers is a graduate student, her lectures are super clear and engaging! All exams are multiple choice, and almost all materials are covered in the lectures. She also has weekly assignments which is fun and also easy points. She is also accessible outside of class which She responds to emails in a detailed and timely manner.

Great professor, I really enjoyed this class. There is extra credit offered and the workload isn't super heavy. The exams are also not too hard and you can choose between different grading options for the class.
Lowkey boring lectures, but not a hard class

While her tests were difficult, she had a clear, organized structure for her class. However, I did feel like "just a number" in this class, which made it difficult sometimes to ask for help. Otherwise, clear instructor, grading isn't too difficult, and very interesting content.
She is not that nice but it's not a bad class pretty straight forward go to class and do work and you will be fine.
Dr. Li is an amazing and thought provoking lecturer.  I truly enjoyed her Psyc 180 class last spring. If I had another Psyc course to take that she taught, I would sign up!
Very interesting and easy psych elective. Professor Li is great and very knowledgeable.
A great class for some of your first semesters, interesting and super easy

Dr. Li is superb! She assigns very creative and fun assignments, is very good with communication, organization, and you can tell she loves what she does. She is very accessible outside of class, and incentives you to do so. She is very well-versed in her craft and I hope to take another class with her soon!

Dr. Li was super helpful and very accommodating to all students.  Class has 2 midterms and a final (non-cumulative), 2 papers (short like 1-2 pages) and a group project (easy), lots of extra credit opportunities so you would genuinely have to try to do poorly in the class.

There are weekly mini quizzes that are open note and pretty easy, and the group activities, almost every week, are also easy. Other regular lecture days are lowk boring, but not bad. They are a nice break from the other days imo. You need to know textbook terms for the exams, but you get a clear study guide and cheat sheet!
tests are worded very weirdly and you have to kind of guess on what she wants. also be aware NO ROUNDING UP. if you have an 89.9 tough luck but that's not an a- to her.

Rosa Li is generally a nice person, but her exams are unnecessarily confusing. Many of the questions are worded in an unclear and overly complicated way, and it often feels intentional. The difficulty of the class comes more from how questions are phrased than from the actual material. I'd avoid unless required.

Dr. Li genuinely cares about her students and makes the course content easy to digest. I appreciate the frequent use of studies, examples, videos, and real-life scenarios in her lectures. Made it very fun and engaging. Tests/LCs aren't bad.

I might be in the minority but I enjoyed every lecture and though Dr. Li did a great job teaching content during lecture in a very professional but still entreating way. I also took 180 with her and I feel like exams can be weird but once you figure out the general form and use the ability to bring a cheat sheet, you will do fine.
her exam questions are worded very weirdly and you can tell she wants to make the class harder than it should be.

She does a lot of things right, but a lot I would change. Review sessions are not very thorough. ULAs didn't seem to know any material. Her formatting for the class is nice but lectures are not easy to pay attention to and tests are not easy because of how she words questions. Pretty interesting content either way

I've gotten the impression that she wants to make the class unnecessarily more difficult than it needs to be. Will take grades off for things that are never explicitly mentioned in the rubric. She can also be quite hostile if you miss class. I personally would avoid taking a class with her if you can.

This class is super easy, and the 2 essays are also graded easily. You just have to memorize some terms for tests. There are grqs before most classes but shoulnt take more than 15 min to do. No other HW. Very low stress class.
Didn't really learn anything from the class. I would agree with some of the other comments made too about her grading.
weird grader which makes it difficult to do well even if the work is put in

Worst class I have taken at UNC (aside from anything in the chemistry department). Dr. Gordon seems kind but he doesn't care at all. Very difficult to get an A because the participation grade skews you down (cannot get past a 98). He reads off of his slides for the lectures and doesn't know how to use technology. Take 225 with Dr.Chanon (trust me).

His lectures were very heavy in content but he had lots of participation assignments that made class a bit more interesting. The only really hard thing was that his class was graded on just 3 exams, 1 final, and participation assignments. The participation assignments weren't hard but you could only get up to a 98% even if you did all of them.

1. absolute king (we bow peter gordon)
2. has dementia
3. hasn't seen a computer before…?
4. could very easily be the kooky grandfather in one of those early 2000's family sitcoms

Dr. Gordon is a nice guy but his lectures dragged on. Some of his content was very interesting, and he incorporated current events. Most of the test questions were right off the slides, if you pay attention you will be fine. Admittedly, some of his lectures were quite boring.

Not a fan of this triple-I course; Peter was the best professor out of the 3 because he provided good slides and study guides. The class was hard to follow and unorganized, I am glad I ended with an A , though.
Best out of the three professors. Hard to hear and very lecture heavy. Not engaging at all.

The best out of the three professors hands down. His lectures might be a little slow, but he posts study guides and his questions on quizzes/final were clear and easy, unlike the ones from the other two professors.
Gave a quiz right before break which was annoying, but was a better prof compared to Ariel and Taj.

Peter Gordon does not project to the class properly, therefore it is difficult to understand him. His slides are incoherent, unorganized, lack proper punctuation, and overall is something you would expect from a 6th grader in terms of format and cohesiveness. He continually uses "uh's" and "um's" to the point that it gets quite enervating. BAD.
Pretty easy Triple I, Peter is very nice. His portion is lecture-heavy and his slides are very wordy though.

I could never understand anything he was saying because the microphone didn't work and it was a 400-person lecture hall. I taught myself all the material and somehow managed an A. Don't take this class if you want to learn something.

For PSYC 433- The prof seems nice however lectures didn't benefit me at all, I found myself confused the whole semester. Had to teach myself the concepts. Don't take this class unless there's no other option. The final was a nightmare and the prof doesn't know how to use canvas/technology well

He is clearly a sweet guy with good intentions. However, it was very difficult to understand him while he lectured, and I found I had to teach myself the material. I am sure he is a better teacher in smaller courses, but do not recommend him for a large lecture class.

He's fairly older and tries to relate to students, but it comes off odd. He seems to care about students, but is mainly stoic. Participation is out of 13 assignments (the 13th is 2.5 ec points --> 102.5% for participation - 30% of grade). Three tests, including a final (20% for midterms, 30% for final). He doesn't know how to use Canvas... bad lol.

While I think Professor Gordon means well, this course wasn't taught well. He couldn't get the microphone in our lecture hall to work, so it was hard to hear him. He lectures with slides, but it is often unclear what exactly he's talking about/expects from his students. He is probably fine in a smaller class but I do not at all recommend IDST 129.

idek what to say, I couldn't hear him at all. I can tell he means well and he's pretty funny but not a good IDST teacher at least. I think the class was screwed from the beginning, he did what he could, but a 400-person lecture is the wrong place to take this professor.
literally hated him. he taught my triple i and i almost fell asleep in every class. if you have him, drop the class you won't learn anything. quizlet taught me everything I needed for the test.
Don't even take his class
RUN

he looks like a nice guy but actually shady in his grades. if you want anything psychology take tons of the other good teachers out there who would nicely put a good word on your rec letter and transcript. don't force urself onto this mess please.

Don't take this course for an easy A! This class is heavily research-based, not learning-based. You will be doing a lot of experiments, writing, and research projects. Dr. Arnold is accessible for office hours, however she takes forever to respond to emails. She is slightly passive aggressive and a tough grader.

As Kim K once said, "It's like no one wants to work these days". Truthfully, this is a "tougher class" but its also a RESEARCH BASED class, you're gonna do research in a research class, you're gonna write research in a research class. If you think the class is an "easy A" or "fun" class its not but if you're open to work you will do fine.

DO NOT TAKE FYS. The class was originally about mindreading but Dr. Arnold focused way too much on her own research and didn't care for our opinions much even though It was a seminar class. The grading is extremally tuff and devastating as the low grades set you back much time and effort for no grade replacement. Does not offer support, blames you.

Long, boring lectures. There was never clear grading criteria on assignments which was confusing, and an overall grade for the class was never given to us at any point in the semester. This class focused on psychology research, so Dr. Arnold would be a good resource if you're interested in that field; Otherwise, don't take the class.

Not an easy A. This class is incredibly intensive and although she has high expectations for honors students, she's really accessible during office hours. She's passive-aggressive, and getting feedback from her outside of assignments is hard. Get ready to write a lot; many small and group assignments with a 10+ page research paper at the end.

This class was VERY boring. Dr. Arnold is fine, but she is definitely more of a research professor than a teaching professor. The last bit of this class was a research project, and she was very helpful with that. This class is not an easy A, but it isn't terribly hard. If you don't want to be bored and hate your FYS, don't take this class.

I had extenuating circumstances this semester and would not have passed this class without Dr. Arnold's help. She cared about my success in her class and reached out often to make sure I stayed on top of the class. She grades intensely, but I do think her feedback is super helpful. She really showed tough love, which I deeply respect.

Do not take a class with her. Her grading standards are incredibly harsh and she gives very vague instructions for all assignments. She is very disorganized and has no idea how to use technology, she was not even able to post quizzes on Sakai without there being serious glitches. She is a researcher, not a teacher.

Class does not teach about language, it teaches about research. If I wanted to learn about research, I would have taken that class again. Lectures are super dry and she's completely unorganized, does class work out of order, and does not know how to communicate. -10/10 Do not recommend.

Horrible lecturer. Doesn't teach or answer questions well. Course content is painfully dry. She's disorganized, constantly contradicting herself, and has no idea how to use technology. Assignment instructions are vague and confusing. She's an overall atrocious communicator and is so out of touch with her students. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!!!!!!

By far one of the worst professors I've had at UNC. She copies all of the information on her slides from the textbook and is horrible at explaining concepts. Class is not hard just expect to learn almost all of the material outside of class.

Dr. Parekh is a great professor! There's a lot of material to cover, so completing the guided readings is important, but her slides are really helpful for filling in any information that you may not have gotten from the textbook. Her grading is very fair, and she offers extra credit. The tests cover a lot of material, but are not too bad.

I loved this class! Dr. Parekh is a super caring person, and I enjoyed office hrs. 3 midterms with a cheatsheet and open note final. You need to have a strong understanding of the material to do well though. Since it's an intro to neuro class, it covered A LOT of material in a short amount of time which makes every lecture seem very disconnected.

Dr. Parekh is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. She genuinely cares about her students and gives extra credit opportunities (and a fair grade distribution) to make sure her students aren't overly stressed. There is a lot of information in this class so I highly recommend doing all of the textbook readings.

Dr. Parekh is understanding and cares about student success. That said, her lectures were boring, unengaging, and apathetic. Midterms are not intuitive and are mostly a test of how well you can search for information on a notes document. I think I learned more from one engaging and enthusiastic guest lecture than the entire rest of the course.

DO NOT take this class unless you want to drown in work. She does not understand that we have other classes as well. You'll be writing/editing a paper along with doing many busywork assignments every week. Midterms take forever to complete. Not worth it especially if you have a bad group. Take this class with anyone else; you'll have a better time.

She did an amazing job with this class! She is understanding and provides feedback while still being nice. Work is mostly project-based, and the groups are random, but it seemed like most people in the class cared and did the project. Small class (~20 people), so it was a good vibe to get to talk to people/ask questions.

Parekh is genuinely one of the best professors I've had. I took this class online, and it was HARD, especially with 60+ pages of notes crammed into a summer session. But her lectures are so clear to listen to and interesting, and her assignments are easy if you put in a bit of effort. I highly recommend taking her (and go to office hours!) :)
NSCI 279 was such a doable lab, unlike any of the chem labs taught at UNC. 10/10 recommend taking with Dr. Parekh
Dr. Parekh is the best professor ever, she totally understands tough circumstances and even though her tests are a bit difficult, they are fair and you can totally get through them!

Dr. Parekh is incredibly thoughtful and kind. She genuinely cares about her students' well-beings and adjusts deadlines to accommodate. Although the material is dense and the exams can be tricky, there are many opportunities to boost your grade. The tests are also online and take-home.

Loved this class, she is so sweet and really loves her students, she offers a ton of help outside of class and is very understanding when it comes to outside situations, Exams were a bit hard but If you study in advance it is manageable

THE SWEETEST PROFESSOR ON UNC'S CAMPUS!!!  Dr. Parekh loves what she does, and you can tell!  She is very patient and will go out of her way to make sure you understand a concept.  Don't get me wrong, this class is tough and there is a lot of material, but the way she teaches makes you feel very prepared for exams!

Dr. Parekh is a professor who cares about her students. This class is not an easy class since there is a lot to learn and memorize but she tries her best to help her students. She is accessible outside of class for any questions or just chatting. Don't buy the textbook it is available online! She gives optional guided readings which are nice.

Amazing teacher Who truly cares about her students, I think she was one of the best professors I have ever had and truly inspired me to pursue the field of neuroscience. I think that she is a wonderful person and teaches very well and is always very very willing to help.

I took 418 this semester. Dr. Reissner is very kind and loves to know her students! Her lectures are entertaining and very fascinating, and she loves answering questions. Tests were fair and were exactly what was mentioned in class, and her slides are very helpful. I would love to take another class with her.
I took 418. She's super funny, lectures are engaging, exams are fair and not many other assignments. Her grading is good, nothing to complain, I would definitely take her again

Reissner is the sweetest person and amazing teacher. However, her tests are tricky because there is so much information and little guidance. Same goes with her papers-you never get a score back and have no idea how you did.

She really enjoys what she's teaching! Very approachable. 
She was quite accommodating and seemed like she cared about how we were doing. 
However, she takes forever to give back grades. 
Tests were not bad. Doesn't give a rubric for papers, kinda vague.
Dr. Lysle really cares about what he does and he made this class super easy! Midterms were very fair and lectures were active.

Amazing class, amazing professor. Discussion based class, but is very easy if you pay any sort of attention at all. Even though it is so easy, you still come out of it learning a lot. If you have to take this class, take it with him. He is very accessible during office hours and wants everyone to succeed.

Professor Lysle was my favorite professor last semester! He was a very flexible grader and the class was very easy and engaging overall. I took the Honors section and it was by far, the easiest Honors course I've taken at Carolina.

I literally cannot say enough good things! This class is one of the simplest I've take at UNC and it wasn't overcomplicated like many classes can be. Dr. Lysle is AMAZING and understands situations come up and most importantly understands that his class isn't the only one in the world (BIG AT UNC). He's fantastic and you should take the class.

If you need to take this course please take it with him!! He is so nice. The course consists of 15 "assignments" but really they are done in class and super easy. You also have a journal that you work on throughout the semester, but again super easy. There are three midterms and a final, which are all easy. He is really great.
Dr. Lysle is a really great guy and makes his lectures engaging and informative. As long as you came to class and did the readings, exams were very doable. He was accessible outside of class often.

Hands down one of the most informative but also one of the easiest classes I've taken at UNC. For pre-meds, this class and Dr. Lysle's explanations do great for covering material on the P/S section of the MCAT. Grade in the class was never in concern – easy A if you put in any sort of effort, and the tests were very light. Great guy!

Dr. Lysle is my GOAT - the exams are really straightforward and fair. Your grade is determined by participation assignments, one semester-long journal (light), and exams. Beautiful beautiful beautiful class.
Dr. Parikh is an absolute sweetheart and is very caring. The class is incredibly easy and straightforward. I highly recommend taking this course!

Professor Parikh is a great professor. Her class is structured well and her grading criteria is very clear. She is considerate of her students and wants them to do well. Her teaching style was giving lecture 2 days of the week and then allowing us to work on our group project the final day of the week.
Dr. Parikh is amazing. If you are able to take a class she offers, do it.

Dr. Parikh is an amazing professor and she truly cares about her students! The learning quizzes, even the final, are all asynchronous and open-note. Make sure you have a good group because there is a semester-long research project that requires lots of communication/collaboration. The grading can be harsh on the project, but Parikh is very helpful.
She's perfect I love her take any class she ever offers
Second time I've had her as my professor!! One of my favorite teachers here at unc
I'm not convinced IDST is much different between professors but she was nice enough and an easy grader
She was a good Data Literacy Lab instructor. If you turn in your work, you will do very well. There are only a few in person meetings of the class but she made those as engaging as possible.
Natashas amazing, no work, everything so slight, and shes so sweet
AMAZING! A wonderful class with a wonderful professor, who gave great, informative, and USEFUL lectures that all of the quizzes/exams were based off of. Take this class if you have the opportunity!

Amazing Professor! She made retaking stats an enjoyable experience. The one downside I had with her is that she often would respond to emails very late, and many times she wouldn't even respond. But, it was not an issue as she was very welcoming and always had time before or after class to speak. I would recommend taking a class with her!
The best professor ever. She is so understanding and welcoming to everyone. Work is not difficult because she posts in-depth explanations of content.
Genuinely easiest class if you just submit the assignments and do the pollev. She is super sweet and understanding so no worries taking this course with her.

She was wonderful. The course was structured where you watch lectures before class and do some compression questions (but that should take about an hour at most). In class we do review, poll everywhere, and work on assignments, which is really nice because you can get a lot of help from both Dr Parikh and the ULAs/IAs. Overall a great course!!!

Prof Parikh is a wonderful teacher! All assignments are online and take a short amount of time to complete, can finish in class with time to spare. Quizzes and exams are online, open note. She is very good at answering questions and will go out of her way to help your grade.

Prof. Parikh is a great professor! 210 content was a bit dull just because it's statistics focused, but she made it as interesting as it can be. Easy A! Labs are automatic 100s as long as you try, and assignments are pretty easy. I liked how detailed instructions were provided. Overall, take it with Prof. Parikh.

Professor Parikh is really caring and sweet. In the class, there is weekly assignments and labs which are not hard at all to complete. And all the exams will be taken online. Easy class and the lecture could be a little be hard to concentrate.

take this class! pollev in class, so attendence is required but u get 2 missed days. tests and quizzes are online at home. labs and assignments are once a week for accuracy. prof. parikh is a great instructor! i am taking another class with her next semester :)

Fantastic professor that truly cares, the work she assigns is very simple and can usually get done during class time. She provides so many sources to help, if you even need it because she is a fantastic teacher in the first place.
She is so great! You have an online midterm, and some assignments but they are very easy and straightforward. I would 100% recommend taking this class with her.

We had several quizzes and a writing assignment to apply what we learned, but aside from that your grade is based on exams, which were fair and pretty much entirely based on the slides. He was also super nice!

Dr. Thiele was a caring professor who made the intricacies of a neuroscience-based learning course doable. I enjoyed our semester-long journal project that allowed for a lot of creativity in applying class concepts to real life. I feel like I am leaving with some useful knowledge beyond my Neuroscience major! Definitely recommend.
His classes can be kind of boring, but the tests aren't that bad. Just memorize the powerpoints, and you'll get in the A range. He is very nice though!!

Dr. Thiele values straightforward exam/quiz questions, so do not worry about him trying to trick you. Grading criteria is extremely clear, and the slides contain everything you need to know. Go to class so you can ask questions - he checks in frequently to see if students have any confusion.
So so so much busy unnecessary work. She will act like she does this busy work to boost your grade but will then take points off for things not outlined.

She is a super tough grader but then won't provide clear guidlines on what she expects so it doesn't really matter how good your projects are she will find some mystery criteria to take points off on. She is also one of those professors who likes to pretend she cares about you but don't be fooled she doesn't gaf.

Professor Gaudier-Diaz is very cryptic with her grading criteria. Getting a good grade in this class is like pulling teeth. Her quizzes are weird and confusing and she gets caught up on technicalities that don't make much sense. She is willing to work with students sometimes, but she is unnecessarily harsh when it comes to grading assignments.

This class is very frustrating. She expects a lot out of you, but does not hold herself to the same criteria. Typos in nearly slide, announcement, test, etc. Her tests are full of misleading and purposefully confusing questions, where you'll be trying to interpret what the question is even asking. She's very kind, seems knowledgeable, but I'd avoid

I loved having Dr. Gaudier-Diaz; she was very caring and wanted to create a safe space for learning. I enjoyed this class; I found a few topics connected to some other courses I have taken, such as biology and anatomy. There is not a lot of homework, but it is essential to complete the readings and review notes.

Professor Gaudier-Diaz made me love neuroscience. This class was so interesting and I learned a lot. She is very caring and makes an effort to get to know every single one of her students. She seems strict at first, softens up a ton and offers lots of EC. I am not a STEM person at all, and made an A-! It's not hard if you follow along with the LOs.

Professor Gaudier-Diaz was really nice, but the course itself is very dense. She provides grade boost opportunities (extra credit, bonus points, cheat sheets for exams). I never read the textbook and did fine. My only complaint was that she didn't release slide decks after class which made it very hard to study since it's a lecture heavy class.

Overall she was an ok professor. You have to put in work to get a good grade. Take notes on what she says in class (download and annotate the ppts), make good cheat sheets, active learning, quizlets etc. Because the class is so difficult I wished she had implemented more active learning things/questions in class. Had to push her for practice Qs

I took this class for my neuro minor. Like most intro classes at UNC it's way harder than it needs to be. I felt like she could have made this class so much better. First she never gives your exams back and you have to go to office hours to see what you got wrong (final is cumulative). But I did ok so maybe I'm overreacting but I didn't enjoy this.

Wonderful professor with lots of extra credit to improve your course grade. Midterms can be hard sometimes but she gave us bonus points on Midterm 2. Final was pretty easy and fair. This course also expanded my view on neuroscience. Would 100% take again.

Open note quizzes. Tests are HARD with many "select all that apply". You get a cheat sheet for each test. Put all your notes/diagrams on the cheat sheet in small font. Watch and rewatch all pre-class videos. She is a really interesting lecturer. The class pushed me, but work hard to do well. I went from a C- after the 1st test to an A- by the end.

Interesting but difficult class, considering this is supposed to be an introductory level. Diaz is an effective but dry lecturer, really just reads off the slides. Exams are difficult and very specific to things said in class or in the textbook. Lots of extra credit and participation grades, which act as a nice buffer. Good experience overall.

Dr. Diaz is a great teacher that care about her students and will go above and beyond for them. However, the course is very challenging so if you think that just because this is label as an "Intro" class and that you would get an easy A. THINK TWICE before you enroll. In short, amazing professor but you have to be willing to put in the work!

Professor Diaz has genuinely been one of my least favorite professors at UNC. She does not stick to her word and constantly changes what she says she'll do or offer. She gave us a midterm on the last day of classes this semester. While also having a cumulative final. She has repeatedly given me inaccurate participation grades.

3 midterms, 3 essays, a semester-long group project, a reading quiz before every lecture, a cumulative final, PollEv attendance, and an exit ticket after every lecture. Our midterm 3 is on the last TTH class of the semester; make that make sense! Dr. Diaz is nice enough, but her lectures are not engaging at all. Senioritis + this class = bad combo!

I love Prof GD!! She is so friendly, excited about neuro, and receptive to feedback. Ppl complain about the workload, but the course content itself is so dense there's no way around it. 20-40 pg. of reading 2x a week. Attendance via PollEv. Cheat sheet on exams. Showing up & taking good notes = success. Challenging but fascinating class!

This class is too difficult to get an A in. You need to read so much + do all the quizzes (2 per week with 80+ pages of reading). The tests are half “select all that apply”. I could not do well in this class it was too overwhelming, but Dr. Gaudier Diaz was kind.

so much info and expects you to write it all down during dense lectures. her slides are incomplete "to encourage people to come to class to get all the info." must know everything she says for the exams. the exams are extremely specific and have many "select all that apply" questions. if you aren't good at soaking info in like a sponge, rethink.

Prof. Gaudier-Diaz is a tough but fair professor. NSCI175 is a difficult class, but if you have to take it for the major this professor is a good option. Her lectures were solid and she was accessible outside of class. I felt that the extra credit and test curves she offered were fairly generous when added up at the end. Get ready to study though.

Prof. Diaz is a sweetheart. She cares so much about you and wants to get to know her students. She will go above and beyond to help you. Take advantage of her office hours and extra credit. There is one group assignment that is a good chunk of your grade but is SUPER easy to do. The slideshows are all you need to memorize word-for-word for tests.

Super sweet and very accessible if you have any questions or concerns. She is very engaging and fun in lectures, tests are relatively ok with a couple tricky concepts and wording but she holds office hours to review missed questions. Quizzes are online and homework is really easy.

I LOVED HER! she is so clear and gives you so many chances to make a good grade and genuinely wants you to learn. 3 exams and a final, the lowest of the 3 is dropped. She is so understanding, and the work is not difficult. The exams are slight if you put in the effort. She gives you everything you need to do well, you just need to do it.

Recommend everyone to take PSYC230 with Professor Chanon. Her lectures are clear and amazing and her grading is very generous, the grade is mostly determined by HW, participation and cumulative quiz and learning check( which can drop the lowest)

Love love love Dr. Chanon, she is the best!! I enjoyed her class so much, and it's genuinely been one of my favorite classes I've taken. She puts in a lot of effort into making it such a great experience.

I would love to say this is an awful class to get off her waitlists lol, but Dr. Chanon is an amazing professor. She's incredibly kind and personable and learns everyone's name, and her lectures are fun to attend. This class was mainly group project focused with that taking the place of the final, which I really enjoyed. 20/10 reccomend Dr. Chanon.
Dr. Chanon's lectures were really engaging, and she had a lot of demos that made class more fun. She also made the content easy to understand.

I love Vicki down! Super kind and cracked me up all semester. She learns everyone's names and her in-class participation is engaging and solidifies concepts. Exams are pretty straightforward, 2 homework drops, and quizzes that you can take until you get a 100. You can also miss 6 classes which is nice. Very easy class and an excellent prof.

Dr. Chanon is just a great professor. Super kind and enjoyable to be in class with. She has a weird attendance policy with the use of flashcards to answer in class questions and then you turn in the flashcard the same day so you will have to be ok with that. She'll learn everyone's names so that's nice.

One of my favorite professors I've had at UNC! Her lectures are very engaging including fun activities to understand the content. Her exams are very straightforward and she also offers a few extra credit opportunities. Also, one exam is dropped, and you can take the quizzes as many times as you want. I genuinely enjoyed going to her class :)

Dr. Chanon genuinely cares about her students, making an effort to know everyone's name, and she also makes class enjoyable to attend. There are a ton of interesting demonstrations that make lectures fun, and her grading scale is super chill. 3 exams, 1 dropped, weekly homework that will get full credit if completed, and the final.

I absolutely adore Dr. Chanon! She's hilarious and gets to know every student in her class (and our lecture was definitely more than 50 people)! She's really great about posting slideshows and recordings! Number one tip is to fill out the outlines for learning checks! The lowest learning check is dropped! Homeworks are pretty easy too!
Nice professor but the learning checks were hard for me and there was a lot of content on each one

LOVE HER super nice she learned everyone's name in a 100+ lecture, exams were super easy, attendance is mandatory via notecards you write on during class but for completion, lets you review exams in office hours, lectures recorded, hw one a week but rly easy, take her!!

AVOID AT ALL COST! Her teaching style was so confusing and inconsistent and never align with the textbook content order.  I spent most of my time just figuring out where the content she taught on the textbook. Her learning checks were one of the hardest STEM exam I have at UNC without any practice problem sets. DO NOT TAKE. SAVE YOUR GPA.

I loved going to this class because of Dr. Chanon. She is absolutely hilarious and so much fun to listen to. I really enjoyed the activities we did in class, they made the lectures engaging even when the content could be dull. Dr. Chanon, on the other hand, is never, ever dull. Also you get four absences, two homeworks, and one midterm dropped!

The class is super chill—graded based on weekly homework, a few quizzes, and a group project (you get to pick your group). Chanon is awesome. This is my third class with her and I honestly have nothing bad to say. She even says everyone should get an A.

Dr. Chanon was an amazing professor, probably one of the best I've had at UNC. She makes an effort to learn every students name (even in a class of over 100 students), is very understanding, and makes lectures fun. Homework and quizzes are guaranteed 100s, and the midterms and finals are easy. As long as you pay attention and try, you'll be fine.

dr chanon is so sweet, yes this class is kinda difficult, but as long as you put the work into it, you'll def do good, if you study hard for the final, you'll get an A, weekly hws, take home quizzes, 21/25 lectures need to be attended, 1 quiz and learning check is dropped, 2 hws are also dropped, def take it w her.

Dr. Chanon is so funny and upbeat! Attendance matters a lot and is mostly done by using notecards and answering questions. She is super knowledgable and honestly this class is very easy and straight forward especially if you prior knowledge of the nervous system and actually come to class.

Dr. Chanon is the Gold-Standard. Her lectures are engaging, grading criteria is clear & fair, & she gives you every opportunity to succeed. She cares about her students & will learn your name in a class of 200 students. I plan to take every class I can with her, and I recommend you do, too! She's the type of professor that changes students' lives.

There is a reading and test for every single class, and there was a lot of out of class work/meetings. Had to meet out of class 15+ times for hours and classes were lecture heavy. She's very passionate and a good teacher, the work wasn't super difficult, but it was a lot.

Professor Bardone-Cone was super sweet and passionate about the class. Her section of the Gender Triple I was the easiest and had the most engaging lectures. If you complete the readings before class and take decent notes you will be totally fine! The reading checks were super easy and the project exams were straightforward. Highly suggest taking.

Bardone-Cone did a good job for what gender class was, but it was still pretty boring and overly difficult for a first-year required triple I. Gender is a bad triple I; it's just too much for a class if you're not interested, and it's not very intuitive, so it isn't easy to guess through it.

Professor Bardone-Cone's material  was the one part of the gender class that I actually liked. She seemed to be caring and gave interesting psychology lectures. Her part of the exams and quizzes were a little easier of the three. I think she would be a good professor in a psychology course; however, she was placed in a tough course being gender.

By far the most reasonable and tolerable professor in this remarkably unlikeable class. I was miserable almost every lecture except hers; boring, readings with quizzes every class, three separate group projects, and pretty tough exams. She is the only good part of this class. Her psych content is straightforward and most of it is inferable.

Dr. Bardone-Cone made psychology exciting and easy to grasp. She was incredibly respectful, and if a student ever asked a question, she'd come back the next lecture having researched it. To study for the exams, just reread the slides and note key vocabulary. On the final exam day, she baked cookies for each student, which was greatly appreciated.

Super kind prof, I loved her the most of the three. Her lectures were clear and easy to understand, but I definitely needed to review them before exams. Super genuine person and wanted to get to know everyone, despite it being a huge class. I would never recommend anyone take Gender, but I would love to take a different class of hers.

One of my favorite classes I've taken at UNC so far! Dr. Bardone-Cone is a great lecturer and really tries to make the class engaging. She is also very accessible outside of class and always willing to help if you need assistance with the content. I can't recommend her enough!

she is super caring and the best lecturer out of the 3 professors. her section was the most organized and she made cookies at the end of the semester. the material is very straightforward. tbh you don't need to do a single reading for the class. i highly recommend gender.
Didn't love gender, but psychology section and in class activities was very interesting. Some triggering things of eating disorders was hard to read. Kind professor.

Her lectures were engaging, and the content was interesting and relevant. I really liked the clips from pop culture that she presented. I would take a psych class from her. She is honestly the most organized of the three instructors. Her TAs take FOREVER to grade.

definitely my favorite professor from gender! a lot of people hate this triple-i but I thoroughly enjoyed it. if you're passionate about gender then I highly recommend it. her lectures are easy to understand and she makes the concepts relatable. i definitely want to try and take a class with just prof. bardone-cone in the future.

Professor Bardone-Cone was definitely my favorite professor that taught IDST 116. Her lectures were interesting and understandable. You can tell that she truly cares about what she teaches. She seems approachable and understanding. I would definitely take a psychology course of hers.

Prof. Bardone-Cone presents interesting information, but does seem a little disorganized/flustered when teaching. However, although I've never talked to her directly, she seems caring and approachable. Her psychology lectures are interesting and generally more engaging than the art and law sections of this class.

This woman is the only reason that Gender was even remotely bearable for me. She actually makes her slides comprehendible and her lectures are pretty interesting. I think that it's a shame she got stuck teaching such a ridiculous course.
She is by far the best professor in Gender, explains things very clearly but many of her topics feel like common sense if you have any knowledge about gender. Super easy to do well in her sections.

Dr. Bardone-Cone is an amazingly kind professor who really cares about what she's teaching. She has real life experience and cares more about student's general understanding than perfection on assignments. I really loved this class and found that Dr. Bardone-Cone is one of the best professors at UNC.
i love bardone-cone and she is so nice and caring about students. some textbook reading but lecture heavy. take good notes. 3 exams with about 50 questions.

Bardone-Cone is clearly a very nice professor -- outside of class. She seems so kind, and she obviously likes the material. In the class, you will find straight lectures, for hours on end. Unfortunately, the class is lecture-heavy with uninspired slides, slides filled with dense information, and very few breaks. Not difficult, though.

Professor Bardone-Cone is a gem. Her lectures were my favorite in Gender because they were funny, interesting, and engaging. I liked the interview assignment and her reading check-in questions were the most straightforward.

She is very clear in what she is looking for on exams or assignments but it can be hard to meet those if you miss any days because she does not include them in her slides or announcements. Super kind and great at getting everyone to participate in class. Loved having her, just be prepared to contribute in discussions.

This class was amazing. Tests and the project require you to be very specific and to the T but Dr. Gil provides thorough explanations of rubric and study tips. Dr. Gil is an incredible professor who cares about students and wants to see them succeed. Lectures are very thorough. Do the readings!

She did a great job getting us to understand exactly what we needed to for the course. She even gives "study tips" for the test to make sure you can pass. Attendance is not required, though you do have to complete like 10 in class assignments.
Very nice! Highly recommend!

I loved her class. Seriously ignore the negative reviews. I learned so much from her and she fostered a great environment for participation and personal growth. She was invested in all of us as individuals, always mentioned us by name, and thanked us for sharing when we participated in class. Genuinely so kind! Take the class!
Amazing professor, not too much reading (but they're all very interesting!), kind woman, and great lectures. If you participate, you will do well! Pay attention and enjoy. It's a great class.

Professor Gil is amazing I have no idea how she has any reviews saying otherwise. She literally tells you exactly what is going to be on exams. She's so nice and knowledgable. My favorite PSYC class I have taken at UNC by far; so interesting and pretty easy. One project that is 25% of grade but you turn it in in October so you get it out of the way

She's so passive aggressive in her tone. She heavily relies on her TA to do most of the presenting and then answers questions with "I'm sure Google could answer". She's a tough grader with wording on exams, the material is really common sense but because of the importance on specific wording, it's not so easy. Her canvas is also all over the place.

will not accept dr gil slander! the class will be hard if you don't come to class and don't take notes, but just be present and participate once in a while and you will do well. i will say she is very particular about wording on exams, but she will tell you what she wants to see. gives out lots of "study tips" which is basically answers on the exam

By far the worst professor l've had; I should've trusted the negative reviews and avoided taking her class.
Condescending and unwilling to work with you even if you reach out for help.
The only pro is that there isn't much homework but she's also a tough grader on exams and doesn't give feedback.

One of my favorite professors I've had at UNC. She is super knowledgeable and funny which makes lectures interesting and engaging. There's 3 exams, a final (just another exam), and a project. The project is pretty easy, and you barely have any homework. Just show up to class and its pretty easy to get a good grade. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Gil is a legend in the UNC psych community. She is funny, a little bad at tech (lol), and loves participation. She gets to know her students and gives hints about what will be on the tests. The HEP is not that hard and as long as you follow her rubrics, you'll be fine.

Dr. Gil is great! Very friendly and wants to engage students in the material. Gives lots of "study tips" if you show up to class. Lots of mini group assignments you have to be in class for. One project that is over by midterms so you can live your life in peace. Great choice for that final upper-level psyc credit for majors.

Dr. Gil is one of the best professors I have ever had.  Not only is she brilliant, but she is kind and truly cares about her students. The course material is so interesting, and she is able to speak on it so well from years of experience. Tests are straight forward and if you go to class, you will succeed. The negative reviews are simply false.

Dr. Gil has been one of my favorite professors here at UNC. Her lectures are super interesting as she will relate them to her previous experiences as a Health Psychologist. There is no homework for this class, other than a project that is due in the middle of the semester. Assignments completed in class. She will give hints for the tests as well.

She's so nice and caring. Assignments are easy and you only have to do ten throughout the semester, and there's one big project that will start near the beginning of the semester and is due in the middle of the semester which reduces the stress greatly during finals and big project seasons. Frequent group work and quick presentations during class.

Dr. Gil was a joy to have!! Like someone else said, she assigns the big project at the beginning of the semester to make midterm and final season more manageable. She is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, which shows in her lectures! She also is very accessible outside of class and is happy to help you if you need it.

Y'all hating on Dr. Gil for no reason. The assignments are super easy. Some of them require coming to class and doing small group discussions, but they're graded for completion. The project is simple, just put effort into it. Literally just study the powerpoint and read the required chapters for the tests! Plus Dr. Gil is so nice and personable.

The harsh reviews are mind-blowing. She was the most understanding professor I've had at UNC. Complete 10 assignments for 20% of your grade, she front-loads the semester so stress decreases with time. Attendance isn't mandatory but some assignments require you to be in class to complete them. Assignments are graded by a checkmark. I recommend it.

Dr. Buzinski is hilarious and gives amazing lectures. Final exam wasn't cumulative; research project was extremely easy since we did it in bits over the semester. Very kind and clearly knowledgeable in his field. Absolutely would take another class with him
This class is amazing. Best teacher over. So interesting. So fair. I recommend to anyone and everyone.

Dr. Buzinski? Oh you mean the GOAT. Second time taking one of his classes and honestly they should let him teach everything. He is an incredible lecturer who makes class fun and clearly cares about his students. Upon first glance it can look like a lot of assignments but I promise they are not bad at all. Exams are super fair as well.

Professor Buzinski is an amazing teacher, and his lectures were super interesting. Grades are 3 exams, online learning quizzes, and a semester long project. The exams are straightforward; if you attend every class, you should do well. The course-long project is clear and approachable, broken up accross the semester. Overall, an enjoyable class!
great professor super cool! i think if i went to class more often i would definitely have an A. not a hard class if you show up!
He is absolutely amazing. Just take his course.

Half of the course lectures were for lectures, other half were for project work. Super slow at getting grades back but all assignments were easy. Four exams, drop lowest score. Structure of class forces spaced studying, which makes exam prep easier later on. Can be flaky/slow over email, so get questions/requests in as early as you can. Nice guy.

Professor Buzinski is an engaging and accommodating instructor. His lectures are fun and informative, and he provides helpful resources like extra credit and note cards for exams. Though the workload can be demanding, unstuck AI proved to be a valuable study tool alongside the course materials.
Very funny, engaging, and kind.

Dr. B is one of the best professors this university has to offer. He is the most understanding person I've ever met. He truly cares about his students and wants them to do well in the class. Provides extra credit. Exams are very fair and comparable to worksheets/practice exams. All assignments come with thorough instructions.

This was my favorite class this semester and really solidified my choice to be a psych major! As a freshman I was nervous about taking a 200 level class, but I absolutely loved it and found it very reasonable! Dr. B is amazing and made me laugh in every lecture. He was also willing to speak with me about research and grad school! TAKE THIS CLASS!
Dr. B is such an amazing professor who cares a lot about his students. He is such a funny guy and tries his best to get to know his students. He is my favorite professor ever.

Semester long research project broken into reasonable amounts with very clear guidelines. Grading was fair with the exams not worth too much and you can have a note card for the exams. Mostly lectures and you answer poll questions but it's a pretty interesting and easy class. He is also very connected to research on campus and always open to help.

Dr. Buzinski was fantastic. Had chapter readings every week or so (along with an easy open-book quiz). Readings were a little boring at first but got more fun as the semester went on. Tests were fair + we were given a study guide. Lectures are important to attend. He's very friendly / approachable and I appreciate how interactive his classes were.

If you have the chance to take him, please do! He is extremely kind and his lectures are always entertaining. Class assignments and exams weren't too hard either. He is one of the best profs I've had at UNC
BEST professor I have ever had.

I always looked forward to class with professor Buzinski. His lectures are extremely entertaining and he is hilarious. His content was genuinely interesting and he used a lot of polls throughout class to gauge your understanding. He is very helpful during office hours and his slides made it easy to prepare for tests. I really enjoyed IDST133.

I took a triple-i that professor Buzinski taught, and he was amazing. Any day that I walked in and he was teaching, I was genuinely excited. He is kind and so funny, and the topics he covered were always interesting. I will definitely look into taking some of his other classes he offers!
what a dude. such a pal. love 'em. Very nice guy and his lectures were very interesting.
Attend class and you'll make an A

I can't say enough good things about Professor Sanon. He is a great lecturer and makes sure the class is understanding the content, even if it takes a little extra time. More importantly, it's clear that he cares about being a great teacher, and was always asking the class for feedback on himself. Highly recommend, will make a great professor.

Super cool and chill teacher. He gives really good examples when the content gets confusing. Easy to reach out. Hw and quizzes are chill. Reviewing learning objectives prepares you for the exams really well. Exams are straightforward, he doesn't do trick questions. Super funny too.

Attendance does matter, but you can miss a few classes and still get full credits. He was very kind and tried to make lectures fun. Him being a grad student made him more relatable and he was able to have examples that even undergrads could relate to. Given the option, I'd take another one of this classes. The final is "optional" if you do good.

One of my most interesting classes this semester, and it definitely helped that the professor explained everything really clearly. Very lecture-heavy, but the lectures cleared up a lot of the confusing topics in the textbook. Great class overall!

Dr. Sanon was a fantastic professor and was very knowledgeable about the subject material. He really wants students to succeed and understand the content. I would absolutely take more courses with him!
So nice and understanding, my fav prof this far. Covers topics thoroughly, so as long as you pay attention, you should know everything on the midterms.
TOOK HER FOR PSY 3361 STAY AWAY OMG THIS CLASS HURTS MY GPA SO MUCH, PLEASE STAY AWAY AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!!!!!!!! EVEN THE RUBRIC IS HARD TO UNDERSTAND

The title of this class was very misleading. Rather than doing archival research, we used pre-existing small datasets to learn the basics of the programming language R. Most of the lecture was given over to personal stories, and the rest was on basic coding.

Incredible professor. Had the absolute pleasure of having him as my Developmental Psychopathology prof at KU and he was honestly out of this world. Super kind to students, fair exams, engaging lectures, and gives lots of insight into the research world of psychology. Would leap at the opportunity to work with him again if i ever got the chance.

My favorite professor ever. She is a great lecturer and very fun in class. Her exams are very fair and she understands you have other hard classes. Attendance isn't mandatory but going to class with her is always fun.

There's nothing negative to say about Dr. Silver; she's caring and supports her students. Even if the class is at 8:00 a.m., her engaging style makes it worthwhile, and you won't regret it. She fosters a positive, motivating environment.
Lovely professor, lectures can move pretty fast, but if you pay attention and come to class its no problem. Also the assignments were very reasonable and same with the exams.

She is a wonderful professor. Only good things to say about her. She truly cares about her students. Her lectures are engaging and she makes them so light hearted. Drops the lowest exam grade. The only grades are 3 exams and 3 papers. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she made it so fun that I went to my 8 am often. Loved her !

WOW!! Please take Professor Silver. She is hilarious, welcoming, and has easily become my favorite professor at UNC so far. Her curriculum is straightforward and extremely interesting. Attendance is not required, but I still went often even though it was an 8am because of how much I loved it. She drops one exam (including the final). TAKE HER!
Her lectures tend to be dull, and her exams are difficult and often unclear. While the class material itself is not especially challenging, the exams do not seem to reflect it well.
Boring lectures and exams are really difficult.
Prof. Stephens is a very nice professor and the lectures were very entertaining. Would definitely recommend for an intro class

She is actually the kindest professor ever. Has such amazing lectures that are super engaging and just seems like a lovely person overall. There were plenty of opportunities to raise your grade and the tests were not too difficult. Overall my favorite class taken at UNC so far!
So kind! Will answer questions during exams. Weekly reading checks and short papers every two weeks. Highly recommend taking her class!

I loved Prof Stephens! She made class super interesting with group activities, videos, question of the day, and gave time in-class to comprehend material on our own too. Exams were fair and essays (response papers) were simple. She also showed us pictures of her adorable kids in relation to what we were learning (ex:development) which was so fun.
She is the best professor I have had so far. She is very kind and her class overall is very good too. Classes are more enjoyable when you like the content and the professor.

She was always super nice, even in the 9:30 am classes. She is good at teaching the material and not just telling it, which is a rarity. The exams are all multiple choice, and she provided study materials for all of them, so if you didn't know where to start, you had a study guide. She also did not test on anything not taught in class.

This class was really fun and interesting, Dr. Stephens is very caring and engaging. There is a lot of reading in the textbook, but most of it is only on the before class quizzes and not on tests. The exams are pretty information heavy but not super difficult, the questions are pretty straight forward.
Great class. Stephens is passionate about psych and makes the class very engaging. Cares about student success. Tests are fair and the amount of homework is definitely manageable.

She is incredibly caring and loves to answer questions during class. She is also very forgiving with grading. She drops your three lowest reading checks and written responses, and her final is noncumulative. Her tests are multiple choice and can be tricky- so studying is important. She also records all of her lectures; overall great professor.

Great professor and class. Dr. Stephens has two small children, so it was really interesting to not only learn about the milestones in early childhood, but to also be able to see them happening as she shared updates about her daughters. Her class was a comfortable place to ask ask questions and join discussions. Highly recommend.

Amazing class and professor. Professor Stephens is super caring and understanding. Class is a little difficult but professor Stephens is amazing. Extremely clear and engaging lectures. One of my favorite professors and classes here.

Dr. Stephens was incredibly engaging in her lectures, provided opportunities for extra credit, and was accessible! I got by just fine without reading the textbook but still paying attention to the lectures, which are very interesting!  The exams are a little tricky sometimes but overall, very manageable. She's great!

Dr. Stephens is passionate about her work, which shows through her lectures. Lots of cute baby pictures. There are quite a few assignments and quizzes, but there's extra credit opportunities. The tests have so much content and are very lecture and textbook heavy. Overall a caring professor, but get ready to memorize a lot.

The test are pretty hard, but if you actually study and take the time to read the textbook it should be ok. There was also a lot of curves and extra credit given because they are so difficult. The homework and quizzes are super easy though. Overall she is an extremely sweet teacher and cares about her students

Dr. Stephens as a person is extremely sweet however she does not prepare you for the difficulty of the exams. There is a lot of information in each Learning Objective that you have to know. Tests are all multiple choice but very in depth. Would not take her again purely because of the tests!

so accommodating (it's built into the class :D) as far as dropping assignments/missing class (still go it's acc so fun), AMAZING lecturer, always answers questions and doesn't care if the class gets behind bc of it (in a good way). hw is easy, exams are ok (they're still exams /: ) and she's just genuinely so cool and funny like take this class omg

Dr. Stephens is really nice! The content is kind of difficult but I would still say that it is worth it. Lecture is engaging but even if you miss something, they are recorded and posted on Sakai. Strongly recommend taking a class with her. A lot assignments get dropped, making your grade higher.

Great professor for child development, lots of pictures of her kid :) Only complaint is that we constantly seemed to be behind, but this is because she took the time to answer student questions thoughtfully. Go to class, do extra credit if you need, and follow study guides and you should be good.

She is nice as a person, but as a professor, she is hard to swallow. She would go to lengths to ensure her students do not get an easy A; it is unbelievable. Her exams are difficult, she is a heavy grader on writing assignments, and although she offers bonus credits, they are worth nearly nothing. If you can avoid her classes, do it.

This class was fairly difficult, but really interesting! There's a paper or a quiz after nearly every class, so it feels a bit homework-heavy, but the papers are graded pretty leniently and the quizzes are open book. Professor Stephens was very well-versed in everything about the course, and it was clear she wanted us to succeed.

Dr. Payne is a great professor!His lectures are pretty straight forward and clear,which makes up for the fact that most of your grade comes from your 3 unit tests and final.The homework was also fairly easy and worth 20% of your grade.I honestly could've gotten and even better grade if I didn't miss a couple HWs.Overall, take this class if you can!

If you actually go to class and/or study the slides he makes the exams pretty straightforward. readings and homeworks outside of class aren't difficult and if you do all of them you get an extra credit point. he's a fun lecturer and does some in class activities that actually help with content.

Dr. Payne is awesome and this class is incredibly interesting. He is a fantastic lecturer, there is little work and the tests are easy. I recommend taking this class, purely because the content is interesting and Dr. Payne is an amazing storyteller.

This is a great class and Dr. Payne is amazing. However, exams are about 20 questions so if you miss 3-4 you will be stuck in the B range and it's hard to get out. If you're a good test taker this won't be a problem. The only other assignments are comprehension questions for class readings. I learned a lot and went to every lecture.
