Loved this class and prof! Found lectures very interesting and easy to follow. Attendance is optional, but I still hardly miss any classes. No graded groupwork (yay)! Kind and funny professor. He is very likable. If the topic sounds intriguing to you, take the class. 'Textbook' is a $20 book. Strong recommend!!
THIS CLASS IS AWESOME!!! I recommended taking this class with him! He's an amazing professor.
Class is lecture-based with short reading questions, 3 exams, and the final making up your grade. Super straightforward, easy, and interesting class. Would recommend to any psyc major.

Payne's lectures could feel long, but he's a genius in his field and I use his lessons in my daily life with my view of the world. Class was easy, just tests and some daily assignments, you don't have to go to class, but I'd suggest it! Plus suggest doing the readings

Dr. Payne is very respected in his field and also down-to-earth. Good lecturer and really cares about helping students understand the content. Each exam is 20% of your grade and about 20-25 MCQs so if you miss more than a few questions your grade will take a hit, but they are pretty straightforward. Difficult to finish with anything less than a B+.

Professor Payne is an excellent lecturer, and the class material is engaging. Exams are straightforward and based on lecture content. While there's no formal attendance policy, attending class is recommended since much of the exam material comes from lectures. I highly recommend this class and it is easy to get anything above a B+.
He's really good, lectures pretty much go hand in with what's going to happen on the exams! Overall he's great and class is interesting!

Dr Payne is great, one of my fav UNC classes! Class content is fascinating and relevant, lectures are pretty engaging. Graded on 3 MC tests, the final (1/2 repeat of prev. ?s) & weekly comprehension ?s graded on completion. All very reasonable expectations- attendance is not mandatory, but you need to understand the lectures to do well in the class

This class was super easy, definitely would recommend. The material wasn't hard and he explains it very well. There are discussion questions due every week, but they are easy. There are 3 exams and a final, and they were all easy as long as you paid attention in class. Plus you get to use notecards on the exams.

Great class and even better teacher. Tons of extra credit and grade boosting assignments, also super interesting classes and readings.

Dr. Robertson was very kind and tried her best to keep students engaged during lectures. Very heavy textbook readings, learned quickly to just scan the chapters. Take notes on the powerpoint slides and speaker notes in them instead. Very memorization heavy. Often did not get to important information until the very end of class so it felt rushed.

Sabrina is nice, but time management was often an issue. We would cover the most important material in the last 2 minutes as everyone was packing up. Tests are very difficult and hard to prepare for. All other previous sections got a cheat sheet, not us. Don't really bother with the textbook, only use the footnotes in her PowerPoints and the LOs.
Dr. Robertson was great! The course has a lot of material - but her lectures and activities helped me understand. Definitely a great choice for 175!

There is a LOT of content in this class, but Dr. Robertson does a good job of making it seem more manageable. Pre-class reading is very overwhelming, but don't worry about it and focus more on reading through lectures post-class. She is very caring and wants everyone to succeed, so don't be afraid to ask her questions or go to office hours.

Dr. Robertson was a great professor. While at times I didn't appreciate the amount of group work and activities, it forced you to pay attention in class and somewhat know the material. Her expectations for exams were very clear, and she often gave opportunities for extra credit. Highly recommend taking a course with her if you are able.

as a first sem first year, i do not recommend taking this class until you have gone through other NSCI courses. everyone in that class was either a junior or senior in an "introductory" class. the content was SO heavy, so many L.Os, etc. i would def say to make this one out of two stem classes you have for a semester which was my mistake (took 4)

Dr. Robertson is a great lecturer and very approachable and available outside of class. Studying for exams can be difficult (there's a TON of content), but there are learning objectives that are helpful. Also don't be scared when she says there's group work, the in-class assignments are chill and the group project doesn't take very long either.

I loved her. She's one of the best professors at UNC. Gives you LOs that are clearly correlated with tests. Tests are demanding but as long as you go over her slides and especially the notes she includes under the slides you'll do just fine. Lots of extra credit. Caring and will work with you.

There's a lot of content but everything you need to know is clearly outlined, so if you prepare well there's nothing unexpected + Dr. Robertson teaches really thoroughly. The exams are more memory based than application and there is lots of opportunity for extra credit.

Dr. Robertson is the best professor to have for a content-heavy class like this. She genuinely cares about her students as individuals and learned my name by the first week after I met with her once for 10 minutes. The test questions are directly from the slides so just study those and you'll do great. Very fair exams and lots of extra credit.

This class is not the easiest. It is a lot of knowledge and it is really hard to do well on exams unless you prep properly. Dr. Robertson is really nice and really cares for her students and is very understanding with having off days and built in make up work. I found that you never learned content in lecture however. In groups all semester

Holy, I'm coming here the day before the final to talk about how much content is actually in this course... I'm genuinely tweaking out cause it's almost like 1000 different things to know and I have no clue how she's expecting the class to do with this much info. It's mostly memorization however, there are so many random terms and I genuinely can't

Dr Robertson is amazing, she is so sweet and teaches really well. She is super accessible, she wants her students to succeed and provides resources for it. The course for sure requires the student to study, but the content is enjoyable.
The only problem is the group project, if you have a bad group like I did you might not enjoy it as much.

This class has a lot of assignments and is heavily group project based. You have one group all semester that she makes and you are stuck with them. How much you enjoy the class is dependent on your group. Overall it's not super difficult but just an annoying amount of work. Also requires a decent amount of background knowledge in NSCI.

Amazing class. You learn how to best tailor your application to any opportunity and how to network. Lots of professionals come in for weekly panels. Assignments are very low-stakes, and you get extremely good feedback. Professor Robertson is great and it is apparent that she cares deeply about your success at UNC and beyond.

This class is a lot of material too cover but the professor was always adamant about getting help if you need it! Offered lots of extra credit opportunities and one group project with assigned groups. Overall decent professor just a lot of material in the class which makes it hard to keep up.
Probably the most organized and most interesting class I've taken at UNC. Prof is nice and respectful which is seemingly uncommon these days. Tests are hard and I always do worse than I think I do.

You definitely need to put lots of efforts into this class. The workload of this class (homework, pre class quiz and reading) is INSANE and exams are kinda hard. However, you can learn a lot from neuroscience. All the TAs and professors are supportive and caring

Dr. Robertson was a decent professor. The class itself was demanding and required you memorize lots of material! Her lectures were dense and long at times. The exams were open note, but don't let that fool you, as you still need to know the content to do well (take it from me). Take advantage of the extra credit!
interesting class
He's a very nice professor and seems passionate about psychology. Very easy class, super easy assignments, I did the bare minimum and passed with an A.

He tends to be a monotone lecturer, but very passionate about psychology! He has lots of interesting stories about his experience with disturbed juveniles, which he works into the curriculum. Very easy grader on assignments, and the majority midterm/final exam questions are submitted by students so you can study the correct answers.

Dr. Wiss is a super nice guy and you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. Lectures mostly consist of PowerPoint presentations and rambling from Dr. Wiss, but it is definitely an easy A and MUCH less work compared to other PSYC101 profs. There were two exams and you basically created them yourself.

Overall really nice guy who cares about his students. However, there is absolutley no structure to this class and no assignments are graded until the last day of class which is inredibly frustrating. He also does not respond to emails. Again, really nice guy and the class is really easy but if you want structure, clear grading criteria just dont
This class is legit so funny we talked abt if it is moral to have intercourse with a dead chicken but easy and entertaining, def a good senior year class

Lots of discussion posts and readings outside of class (very easy though). He is a really nice guy and loves to ramble on about topics. This was a pretty interesting class and for the final project you can pick your topic which makes it enjoyable. Overall this was a very manageable class that did not take up a lot of time.

Class was RIDICULOUSLY easy. Exams are he has everyone make 4 of their own mcq (which everyone can see) then picks from them; rote memorization for a 100 on both exams. Lectures are usually on a tangent rather than content. But if ur premed and need psych for the mcat, you're not gonna learn ANYTHING. Take for the easy A tho, why not?

The class is just talking through different topics, and discussion board posts every week. He uses UNC Check in every day. The midterm and final is around 60% of the grade, but you get the questions beforehand (the students create them). There is a small individual presentation and we read 6 articles, do a task and discuss it. Def recommend!

such a nice guy. psych 101 is very easy but may not cover psychology in an in-depth manner compared to other sections. my friends in other sections covered a lot more material. if you are taking the class to get a deep understanding of psych, choose another section. if you want a fun, interesting and really easy A, this class is PERFECT for you.
Easiest class I've ever taken. Go to class, do all assignments, participate in class and you'll make an A. Exams are student made and questions are posted to discussion board. He's a King.

Prof Wiss is very funny and passionate about psyc. Lectures are pretty boring because he goes on tangents. If you want to learn the content thoroughly, he is not for you, if you want a good grade, he is. Assignments are one mini project, a few reading discussions, a presentation, a paper, and 2 exams. All are easy if you do more than bare minimum.

Professor Wiss is a very nice guy and lenient grader. He made the midterm and final very easy. He doesn't put strict due dates to assignments but don't submit it too late or you will still receive a deduction. His lectures are engaging and the pace is easy to follow even for international students. Overall a great professor, take his class!

Professor Wiss is a kind but disorganized teacher. While the class is an easy A, the content is not very substantial. Using unstuck ai alongside the free textbook can make up for the lack of in-class learning.

This was a strange class that deviated from evolutionary psychology and into biology. We often discussed sexual acts and I felt uncomfortable numerous times in the class especially when Professor Wiss said that humans were designed to be polyamorous. The coursework was easy to understand and the exams were easy as the class is discussion-based.

easy class, and tests/projects are designed to be simple and graded easily. occasional assignments but a pretty stress free class and the teacher is very insightful and will talk for a while in depth when asked a question by students/on discussion forum about psychology.

I'm currently taking this class online over summer, so attendance is not exactly mandatory and I'm not sure what final grade I'll receive, but Dr. Wiss is amazing! His lectures are extremely interesting and filled with many fascinating clips and real life examples. He cares a lot about his students and the work is all very reasonable!

Professor Wiss is SO SWEET. Didn't learn any textbook psych, but many of my questions about general psychology were answered. If you are majoring in psych, I would not take this class because it's not textbook at all. Projects are graded by classmates, and test questions are made by classmates. EASY A, just need to show up to class.

Dr. Wiss is a great guy but this class was useless to me since I didn't learn a lot of psych (my goal behind taking this class was for a general understanding). Class was disorganized, often went on random tangents, & despite full participation, grading seemed arbitrary. Take this class for an easy A but don't expect to take anything away from it.
Dr. Wiss is so kind and a great teacher. He is a little disorganized but completely owns up to it. I would 100% take this class with him again

I really liked this class! Not a poet by any means, but I had a nice time. Each week, we wrote a new poem. We read two poetry books, attended 2 poetry readings in the area, and wrote short papers for each of those things. Joe was really personable and supportive, and gave great feedback.

Very caring prof, if you send your papers for him to comment on before its due- cheat code! I aways got better grades when I did this. He's funny, and we had only 9 assignments/papers. You are able to deep dive into a topic you are passionate about, and he's always ready to give feedback if you ask for it. Very nice and considerate Prof.

Dr. Fletcher is an amazing professor. He truly cares about his students and always checks in with us regarding our experience as freshmen. Always has funny anecdotes to share and creates an extremely welcoming environment. I'm a STEM major, but Dr. Fletcher has been my favorite professor yet.

Amazing guy. Workshop structure class where you'll really care, even if you don't plan to. Do the work, give feedback to others, grow as a poet by revising your work and trying out what he teaches and you'll do well. Best CREATE class there is! I looked forward to going to every class.

Prof. Fletch is THE man! He is by far my favorite professor. He challenged me and inspired me. He is very compassionate and cares about his students. If you have a chance to take a course with him, do it! He will always be the prof. who set me on the math to minoring in English!

Incredibly funny and a super chill guy. The workload was incredibly light, we had 9 assignments the entire semester with plenty of time between due dates. Very generous grading. My only complaint is that class could be boring and unrelated to the work, but that's to be expected from a required English course. Highly recommend for ENGL105I.
Great guy, easy grader, enjoyable class! Hard to complain.

Fletch was an amazing poetry professor! He gives great feedback and is super encouraging on assignments and during group workshops. He's an easy grader but still helps you learn and grow. He's funny and personable and does a great job gently pushing people out of their comfort zones to participate in class. Definitely take him if you get a chance!

Only went over a little bit of the textbook during class, no need to buy the textbook. Grade is largely based on writings: 1 literature review, 1 presentation, 1 popular science article. Each is preceded by 2 feeders for peer review and feedback from him. He is a nice person and gives detailed feedback. Lots of small discussions.

Dr. Fletcher was a great professor to introduce me to college writing. He understands that people in his 105 class are first years who are still adjusting to a new writing style, and he helps his students figure out where they may have messed up.
a true renaissance man. kind and caring + reasonable grading.

Take Fletcher for 105 especially if you don't have a strong background in writing from high school. He genuinely cares for his students and takes the class seriously. Cutoff for an A was 95 which was achievable but annoying because it took much more time and effort to achieve the same grade as the majority of 105 sections.

Dr. Fletcher is my favorite english teacher I have ever had! I took engl105i with him (natural sciences) and LOVED the class. You get to pick your topics for all projects and he gives great feedback on all papers/projects.  The workload is extremely manageable and he is a funny guy who cares a lot about his students. Take classes with him!!

Professor Fletcher is the best! He genuinely cares about his students and wants you to be engaged with the course material. I took writing in the natural sciences and the course was split into 3 units. Papers are very manageable and the longest was only 6 pages. I am definitely going to try to take another one of his classes.

Dr. Fletcher is arguably the best teacher you can get for any ENGL class. His teaching style is very laid back and though attendance is mandatory, if you miss a day you can watch the class recording and submit a 1-2 paragraph summary response to earn back the participation. He is incredibly caring, hilarious, and very easy with grading.

Dr. Fletcher was the best!!! Very funny guy and gets work back to you quickly with pretty good comments. I took ENGL 105i: Writing in the Natural Sciences with him; it was one of my favorite classes for the semester. Attendance was mandatory, but there were "peer-review days" where attendance was optional.
Great professor with manageable work. Expect lots of writing. Amazing personality.

I loved taking Joe's class. He does assign a lot of reading whether it be novels or short stories from a collection. Mine was online, so it was hard to keep engagement going from other students. Great novels, great insight, and the final project is so fun because you can get creative. He also loves talking about horror outside of the works we read.
Really nice guy! Class had a good amount of reading but quizzes were open note and not too difficult. Some of the feedback I received was iffy (not super clear) but overall a solid gen ed course.

Professor Fletcher was extremely nice, understanding, and chill. You will have to do about an hour of reading for every class but they're just books/stories. You have a quiz every Friday on the readings which is open note, so the class is pretty light whenever you're not assigned a paper. Just a chill class with a good professor!

Absolutely loved this course and Dr. Taylor. The class is very interesting, but be ready to read a lot and read very in depth. Two long papers, but he provides excellent feedback when asked so definitely check out office hours! Easy 100s on the quizzes. This class definitely helped me become a better writer!

I took this with Prof. Taylor in Fall 2024. This was my hardest class in my first semester. It is lots of reading, lectures get really in-depth, and the 2 papers are hard. That being said, Prof. Taylor is a super nice guy and maybe the most well-spoken teacher I've ever had. Lectures are discussion-based. Take your essay drafts to office hours.

loved this course and the professor. He always brought the best energy with the best readings ive had for a course. He did do pop quizzes but super simple. 2 big papers, super simple but he loves a good deep read. Great seminar structure!

I absolutely LOVED Dr. Taylor! He is extremely kind and more than accommodating if you need extensions. The content is engaging, the final "exam" is take-home, and he offers a good amount of extra credit. Dr. Taylor is the sweetest, he even brought cookies for us on the last day of class - highly recommend his class!

He does want you to become a better writer but expect to dedicate time to this class. This is definitely not a 'free' FYS. If you are passionate about his class, he will give great feedback, and all assignments other than essays should be easy to do well on. There are two essays that can be very time-consuming, and their total weight is 55%.

This is an amazing first year seminar class! The course heavily focuses around close-reading and we analyze a variety of sources throughout the class. As it is a seminar class, a lot of the class is focused on in-class discussion. There are some important essay assignments but there are many resources to be prepared for writing the essays.

An amazingly caring professor, great for a FYS! Participation graded. Papers are daunting at first, but he's very approachable and available. Gives good feedback. Pop quizzes are straightforward if you read the texts. Two low-stress presentations make up rest of grade. Content is interesting and relevant. Take if you want to become a better writer.

Prof Taylor is an excellent professor and ENGL 146 is a very interesting class. Be ready to read between the lines in text and write a lot - but reading quizzes (easy 100's) and participation pads your grade. Overall would take again.

Professor Taylor is a supportive, engaging professor. You can tell that he wants every student to succeed. There are a few pop quizzes, but they're easy as long as you've read. I found the coursework to be sometimes challenging, but manageable. I definitely learned a lot in this class. Highly recommend!
One of the nicest professors iv'e had at UNC

I had a really good time in 057 with Professor Taylor this semester, and I would definitely recommend taking his class if you have the opportunity! He is extremely forgiving and has extended due dates for big assignments multiple times to help us all out. He's really accessible outside of class and always gave good feedback on drafts of my papers.

Matthew Taylor is the man! He is THE KINDEST teacher at UNC and he creates a fun and welcoming class environment. The coursework is manageable with only a few articles to read each night. There is one group project, one low-stakes individual presentation, and 2 papers for the class. I definitely recommend Future Perfect for your FYS!

ENGL 57 was one of my favorite classes this semester. The topics and discussions are so interesting! There are pop quizzes on some of the readings, but they're easy as long as you do them. The essays seem daunting, but Professor Taylor helps a lot with in-class workshops. My whole class had a great time and grew so much as writers in this class.

Prof Taylor is incredibly kind and helpful! He gives extensive feedback on essays and is always willing to help you improve your writing. I loved his novel selection, and the class discussions are always interesting!

Really nice and a great professor, gives a lot of feedback on essays and grades relatively well. The class does challenge you to look deeper into what your reading, and Professor Taylor really makes class entertaining with daily class discussions and interesting topics related to the curriculum.

Professor Taylor was a fantastic professor, especially for a first-year seminar. He led super interesting and insightful discussions and created a supportive environment that made it easy to participate. Professor Taylor was more than willing to meet outside of class, answer any questions about assignments, and give any help you needed.
Professor Taylor is awesome- I learned so much in ENGL 57 and he made me a better writer and thinker.
Amazing professor, showed care for students and was always willing to lend a hand!

Dr. Taylor is such a kind professor. His lectures are extremely engaging, and he seems to genuinely care about his students' opinions and impressions of the course material. He's a bit of a tough grader, but as long as you follow the instructions on his essay prompts and employ close reading skills, you'll be fine. Take this class if you can!

This class singlehandedly made me not hate English classes. I learned SO much about how to read deeply into texts and how to write well informative papers. However, there are a lot of readings to do each week and quizzes on them. There are also many papers to complete, but these are pretty normal guidelines for any English class. So amazing!

He is very opinionated and you have the be an amazing writer for a first year class. If you are not a good writer and don't enjoy talking, do not take this class and if you do like discussions I also advise against it. There are a lot easier 105 classes that will allow you to enjoy the class while still earning a good grade. Do not take!

Dr.Ross allows multiple drafts to be submitted and he gives detailed feedback before they're due. He primarily lectures, but the workload was manageable throughout the semester and he was easy to meet with to discuss feedback.

Dr. Ross is clearly a very knowledgable man, but we spent most of our discussion-based seminar listening to him talk about *his* opinions. I did not know my grade all semester... But, there are no essays only short-form discussions posts. It's a super easy class as long as you can stay on top of the readings (YOU 100% NEED TO DO ALL OF THEM!!!!!).

We had zero assignments the entire semester (other than online discussion boards), and not a single grade was entered into Canvas, so I didn't have any idea of my grade until I received my final grade. There's so much daily reading, and even in an opinion-based seminar class, if your view goes against Dr. Ross's, you are "wrong" (he will say so!)

It's clear that Dr. Ross is very knowledgeable and passionate about English. My main issue with him was how opinionated he was. English should be about interpretation, but with Ross, there is a right (his personal opinion) and a wrong (any other perspective, no matter how well-supported it may be).

If think if I could go back in time and have the choice between taking 105 with David again or pulling out all my hair one by one, I would choose the second option. If I had to pick one word to describe his class it would be frustrating. He grades HARSH, lectures are insufferable, and he treats his opinion as right and anything else is wrong.

Intense of a grader for English 105. I showed up to every lecture (except for 1), actively participated in class, and showed improvement in my writing. He would constantly leave degrading comments on my work and give extremely confusing advice. Makes weird comments about women too! DO NOT TAKE! Please just take an easy English for your own good

I took this class because it seemed interesting, but realized Professor Ross was teaching a class on something he didn't have any knowledge on. First thing he told us in this class on the use of AI was "I have never used AI in my life." He would cut us off mid-sentence when we would talk in class to express his own views. Do not take his class.

I have few qualms with Dr. Ross as a person, but I would advise against taking his courses if you have a history with sexual trauma. He would often make derogatory and uncomfortable remarks about fictional women and almost every piece of media assigned included and poorly addressed the topic of sexual violence. Please be wary when registering!

UNC-Chapel Hill is one of the top schools in the country. It should not be admitting students who complain about having to show up to class or who moan when a professor has actual standards for written work. Ross's standards are high. But he's very thorough in his advice about how to meet them. He's a great teacher, if a little idiosyncratic.

If you talk in class and offer your opinions during his unnecessary and endless tangents, he'll love you. Expect to write and expect LOTS of feedback in a pretty condescending tone. I wouldn't NOT take him, he'll definitely improve your writing, just be very wary of your grade.

Professor Ross is a very smart professor, but is way too far hard of a grader for an English 105 class. He provided good feedback for essays, but didn't take into consideration most people taking this course that it's their first college-level english course. He also had very strong opinions and could come off as pretentious lecture.

Dr. Ross is a brilliant guy but should NOT be teaching a English 105 class. He's a tough grader and it's unfair how broad the spectrum of difficulty is for Engl105. Do not take him unless you are passionate about english. His classes are attendance mandatory and he sits in a chair and talks about irrelevant things the entire class period.

Ross is a lovely guy, but his grading criteria for English 105 is too harsh. Your grade is dependent on your natural skills as a writer. I spent hours revising my papers and could not get over a B+. For 105, this should not be the case. If you are Shakespeare, go ahead; he will improve you. If not, your grades will suffer.

Professor Ross is extremely wise and well-spoken but continuously goes on tangents every class, and the lectures are almost useless. This class goes way beyond what a first-year requirement should ask of you, and you won't get an A unless you're Stephen King or Shakespeare himself.

Look, I understand why some dislike him. He can be a little insensitive, out of touch, and he is not tech savvy. However, he is absolutely passionate. He cares tremendously about students genuinely improving and will give you all the help you want if you ask. Also, he is forgiving. He has an abrasive personality but meets students where they are.

Dr. Ross is a very particular man; his essay prompts were very odd and didn't allow much room for your own interpretation. His feedback was very subjective, and my grades on the essays never improved throughout the semester. He tries to be helpful if you stay for office hours, but he kind of drones on (he does in lectures, too).

Very reading heavy class. Took the class online so did not get to know much about him, but seemed to be very passionate about the books and films at hand. I am not sure what my grades for any of the assignments were after the class ended as he had ended the course on canvas and directly put in the final grade. Not bad but prolly wouldn't take agin.

If you want an easy-A gen-ed professor (fair enough), then choose someone else. However, learning from Dr. Ross legitimately improved my writing skills. The essay topics were generally engaging and his draft feedback is gold. His actual lectures are hit-or-miss; one day it is an insightful lesson on concision, and the next is a huge tangent.

I have complicated feelings. On the bright side, I felt my writing improved under his instruction. For every essay draft, he wrote paragraphs of feedback. Incredible attention to detail. However, as for the actual class, it felt unnecessary... lots of tangents + condescending. He's extremely knowledgable, and believe me, he will remind you...

I really enjoyed taking Dr. Barbours class. The class itself is very lecture-heavy, and paying attention to the lectures/taking notes is essential for the midterm/final. He is very available and open to giving feedback on essays, which is super helpful. He is super passionate about this class, and it was by far one of my favorite English classes.

Barbour is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about the course content. However, his lectures are purely him speaking without slides, so if you miss a day, you're screwed. Nice guy, fair grading (though only 5 grades), and flexible with deadlines. His teaching style just wasn't for me.
It is an honor to be taught by this man. He is beyond brilliant.

This is a bit odd but I'm reviewing Professor Barbour based on the three classes I took with him as an undergraduate at UNC 20 years ago (I picked the Milton class designation). Needless to say, Reid is one of the two kindest and most brilliant professors I had at UNC (Gregory Flaxman, also in the English Dept, is other).

Reid is an incredible lecturer, accessible, and understanding. Loved his quips and, for such complicated material, he really does a great job breaking it down while still challenging you. This course requires serious grit, but if you put in the time, success is absolutely possible. Note: No Canvas page & no slides; just the book and lecture.
I really enjoyed Dr. Barbours class and I felt like I really learned a lot about literature and history in this course!

Barbour is extremely passionate about the material and genuinely wants each student to succeed. Graded by a midterm, final, and 3 large papers. He gives great feedback and will help you revise your writing heavily if you email or go to office hours. Pay attention in lecture and take good notes; exams are straight from them.

Dr. Barbour is an amazing professor! His lectures are entertaining and he teaches complex material very well. His papers are challenging (start them early!) and he has high expectations for his students, but he readily offers himself as a resource and gives constructive feedback/guidance.

His lectures are very well-informed and passionate, and he entertainingly sounds just like Martin Short (in my opinion). You have to attend the lectures to know the material for the exams, and he is very specific and exacting about how he wants his papers, but he is a very clear professor, and you will learn a lot from his class.

He is an amazing professor, easily the smartest professor I have had. He is super accessible outside of class and if you like the material this class is for you. However, if you are looking for an easy gen ed class this is not for you. Lots of work and reading, though I thought he graded fairly.

I enjoyed Dr. Barbour's extensive knowledge and passion for the topic, however this class was tedious due to the lectures. Additionally, Dr. Barbour often expressed that he expected us to devote lots of time to our papers, which was a bit frustrating since this is an entry-level course and I worked part-time in addition to a full course load.

The course was very fast-paced, but the readings and lectures were interesting. Attend class as often as you can--your grade will heavily reflect how much you know on the subject and lectures were critical in explaining the material. The papers were not too bad, just attend office hours for feedback (his feedback is very helpful).
Very nice and super knowledgable. Accessible outside of class and will give great feedback. you are graded off three papers (2 5 pages and 1 10 page paper) and then a midterm and final.

I was so stressed about the midterm and why? Such a generous grader, with papers and tests. Extremely intelligent and inspirational but you have to be on your game to follow along with his lectures as they go in circles. Take good notes. Start papers early. Go to his office-hours. Don't be late; it throws him off when he's lecturing.
He seems intimidating but really so generous with time. Go to office hours! So helpful and caring.

Dr. Barbour is the stuff of legend. Somedays he starts lecturing as he walks into the classroom. Wild stuff, but his knowledge of the subject matter and passion for literature is unmatched at UNC. And even non-majors will get stuff out of this class on Milton. Take notes, do the reading, and you'll do alright!

His lectures are just him talking, without much structure. While this seems like a bad thing, I actually enjoyed him talking about the topics and thought his passion made the subject more interesting. Grading is based on attendance, 3 papers, a midterm, and a final. Everything was graded fairly imo. Be sure to go to class and take good notes.

Barbour doesn't use any supplements to his lectures--just him talking. This isn't bad, but I think his lectures lacked structure. The TAs provided lots of opportunities to meet outside of class. Barbour graded the midterm and was an easier grader than the TAs. Paper topics were not relevant to the pieces we read in class, which was frustrating.

Barbour is awesome! VERY intelligent and accessible. Lectures are fast but very interesting. Be prepared to do the readings, write papers, and attend class; otherwise, you will not do well. Definitely recommend his courses to English majors/minors, others may find it too dense. Not an easy A! Final advice: CHOOSE YOUR TA CAREFULLY.

Barbour is passionate about this subject and gave great lectures, but this course is intense (even for an English major). Communication was extremely lacking between Barbour, the TAs, and the class, and this caused a lot of confusion/stress. I would not recommend unless you have specific interest in 16th and 17th century British lit.

Dr. Bolling is organized, hilarious, friendly, and an easy grader. All materials including rubrics and samples are provided in the files. Assignments cover resumes, cover letters, and legal writing such as case briefs and legal handouts. You get 3 free unexcused absences, but each additional one drops your grade by one third of a letter grade.

Super nice and funny guy. Very down to earth. So approachable and an overall great resource to have on campus in terms of interview prep and overall life advice. Definitely a lot more work than other ENGL 105 classes, but it was interesting to me and I think I became a better writer.

Ben is the GOAT. I wasn't even sure I was interested in law, but he makes 105 fun and made me reconsider pre-law. There's a lot of work, but none of it is too hard. This guy is super funny and makes class interesting even at 9 in the morning.
I took his comics class for an area requirement and really enjoyed it. He is serious about the reading, but as long as you do the work and come to class, you'll be fine.

I didn't know this was a 105 focused on legal writing before signing up and I almost dropped. I'm so glad I didn't. Professor Bolling's class is one of the best classes I've taken at UNC. It's harder than most 105 classes, but I feel like I really learned something. The work is constant, but you will learn a ton even if you're not interested inlaw.

Great teacher, A LOT of work for a freshman english class. With that being said, you do improve a lot with your writing skills. He grades pretty easily, so you will finish with an A as long as you do your work. If you put in the effort you will see improvements in your own work.

I really enjoyed this professor's class. He created an engaging and enjoyable learning environment, with a strong balance between lectures and independent work. The workload was reasonable, and his teaching style made the material easy to understand, which made it much easier to succeed in the course.

Great class, great lectures, and there's a great selection of books to read. You have quizzes, 2 major projects, and a final that is open notes. Be prepared to read comics and don't skip out on the readings, he'll know....
I initially took this class to fill a focus capacity, but it ended up being my favorite course of the semester. I loved learning and writing about comics at a university level!

ben is such a chill dude. he literally says he tries to get everyone an A. there were maybe two assignments the whole semester that i thought were hard, but the rest were so calm cuz he gives rly detailed instructions and expectations. also i learned a lot! highly recommend if you have any interest at all in law.

Take the comics class when it's offered with Professor Bolling! I didn't know anything about comics before this semester. He clearly loves the material and it's infectious. Do the reading and you'll be fine.

Dr. Bolling was the best professor I had during my first semester and helped me transition to UNC. There's a lot of work in this class but he gives really detailed feedback and is always able for office hours.

I had Dr. Ben for 105 and learned a lot about writing from him so decided to take his comics class. Highly recommend. Made the material interest even though I didn't know much about comics going in. Always willing to make time to talk about projects during office hours.
I thought visual and graphic narrative was a film class but decided to stick with it because this guy was so funny. Knows the material like nobody else. Chill and kind.

Just straight up mean and condescending, easily offended. Took a student outside mid-class and I could hear him yelling. unclear assignments & class is a lot of work. assignments build on ones before which wouldn't be so bad if he could actually grade anything so u knew what was going on. when he does grade comments come back clearly ai generated.

Ben was so supportive and offered wonderful feedback. It was a go go go class, starting a project right after another, but it was manageable. I love Ben. I learned so much in this class and recommend him so much!! Very very funny.

Truly the best professor here at UNC!! He's so funny, caring, and easy to talk to. All his assignments were difficult, but they were also time-consuming. However, he provides samples for every assignment and is extremely helpful. He was such an amazing professor, I've decided to take another one of his classes next semester.

Ben is an amazing professor and an amazing person. I thoroughly enjoyed taking Writing in Law and I learned so much from him. A couple group projects and every unit was structured. Definitely more difficult than a regular 105, but so worth it if you are considering law (also worth it if you aren't). Prepare for a busy schedule but a great class!

Professor Bolling is someone who genuinely cares about their students and their success. He provides really good feedback on assignments that typically involve analyzing constitutional cases and writing/presenting about them. The class was super interesting and I really enjoyed it.

Great professor. Grades come in somewhat slowly, but he's a very easy grader. Assuming you try and put effort in, you'll do well. Great class if you are interested in law. It is a very consistent workload and can be tough at times, but grading is easy.

Probably the worst teacher I had the last semester. Assignments were overly large and instructions were often unclear related as to where the assignment is or where to submit. During finals time the class becomes extremely hectic as you're asked to incorporate all your feedback received to even be in a good standing to be average and receive a B

Jillian is very kind, she respects you as long as you respect her and follow guidelines. Grading is different than standard classes where you are given a grade at the end based on all of your work. Stay on top of deadlines and try hard and you'll be fine. And don't use AI lol.
As long as you do what you are supposed to, you are guaranteed a B. She is almost always late though.

Very nice woman but the amount of unnecessary assignments, peer grading, discussions, revisions, etc... in this class was hard to keep with. Tough grader with little specific feedback on what was done wrong. The final project was revising ALL of the unit projects within 2 days during finals week and tons of revisions expected/required.

By far the worst teacher I've had at UNC. Assignments are overcomplicated and confusing. After I completed the laundry list of revisions I was given 2 days before the class was over, she gave me an A- for the whole semester without any further explanation. When I reached out for feedback, she didn't bother responding. Completely unprofessional.

We still have undegraded assignments two days before the final exam. The course feels disorganized overall, and I wouldn't recommend it if you prefer structure. There have been last-minute changes, like adjustments to the word count for the final paper just hours before it was due, and sometimes reading assignments weren't posted on time.

The class did not receive an actual syllabus until three weeks into the course. By the end of the semester, half of the assignments, including the final paper, were not graded. Five hours before the deadline for the final paper, she changed the word count, made quizzes with no expectations, and readings at the last minute.

Jillian is the sweetest person especially when seeing her in office hours. She is a very good lecturer and I enjoy our class discussions. She takes quite a while to grade and often posts the homework at the last minute. I enjoyed what we read in the second half of the semester. If you like analyzing literature you will enjoy this class.

The semester is almost over, and she has only graded 2 assignments. Also, she is incredibly prone to instilling massive changes in a class format, so if you are like me and like consistency and routine, then don't take her class. The reading quizzes are awful, too. She blamed students for her late posting of readings. Would never take again.

Nice teacher, but the problem is that we don't have any grades yet. None of our assignments have been graded, so we have no idea how we're doing in the class. It's hard to know what to fix or improve, and we probably won't know our final grade until the semester's over.
Jillian's great. Very understanding with students and accessible outside of class. Makes English classes bearable if they aren't really your thing.

I have never been more confused in my life. The instructions are the most unclear thing I have ever read in my entire life. This is not an English class. IDK what it is but it is not English. We also have no idea what our grade will be until the very end as she doesn't give real number "grades" whatever that means.

Jillian is a very good instructor. Her grading criteria are very reasonable and forgiving. She is more than qualified to teach this class. Some of her lectures were hard to pay attention to, but I attribute that to the material, not her abilities. Overall, Jillian's class was worthwhile; I would take another class with her in the future if I could.

Ms. Kern was always really caring and understanding for students. A bit disorganized but never penalizes students (grade wise, deadline wise, etc.) for her own mistakes. She's open to discussing and revising grades, but is slow to put grades in. Everyone gets an 85% if they do the work.
Jillian is a 10/10 educator. She's always superbly prepared for class, never wastes your time, and demonstrates genuine care for her students. Take a class with her if at all possible!

I went into this class expecting it to be very easy, but it turned out to be difficult due to the effort that the projects demanded. I got very frustrated along the way but at the end of the class, I found that my writing had improved drastically. Take this class with Jillian if you are interested in actually improving yourself.

Adele was great! Really chill class and when you talk she always listens and you can tell she cares and never judges. She does give a lot of work/reading for 105 though compared to my friends in other ones, so keep that in mind but as long as you participate some and do your work you'll get an A

I took Writing in the Natural Sciences and found that I had more essays to write compared to my friends who took other ENGL 105 classes, but I don't regret it. She lets you write about practically anything that you want. I highly recommend attending her office hours at least once and she is understanding of absences and late work.

Dr. Williams is an AMAZING professor. I highly recommend taking writing in natural sciences with her. She gives a lot of work but also extremely clear directions so the work is mostly easy. She actually gives instructions and thorough feedback. 10/10

Dr. Williams is an amazing professor for English 105i! Attendance is mandatory but you get 3 unexcused absences before you start losing points. Assignments and readings can be long but you can write about anything you like. Participation is 20% of your grade, but if you turn in work and participate in discussions you'll get an A.

It is very clear that she cares about her students! Dr. Williams will be able to tell that you're trying hard and participating in class, and will reward you in kind. Actually made me really enjoy a composition class, which I haven't done since middle school. 11/10

She is seriously the best teacher ever, I couldn't recommend a better English professor. She is so leniant and will work with you. Not a very strict grader and gives great feedback. There are a lot of papers, but that's literally all you do, and she gives you a lot of creative freedom. English has never been my favorite subject but she made it fun.

Great class if you enjoying writing, no exams but three papers that get longer each time. There is weekly discussion posts and weekly writing assignments that can feel tedious. She is very sweet and is considerate in adjusting due dates and late work. Highly recommend this class, but do be prepared for lots of time devoted to writing.

Goated prof. I honestly don't like taking English classes and only took this one because I had to, but Prof Williams was great and made it fun. Course work was pretty easy, there's some reading to do but not a lot. Attendance is technically mandatory but she's understanding about it. You can basically write/present about whatever you want.
I took her for writing in the natural sciences. Very kind professor and open to helping you with anything writing related.

Professor Current clearly cares about her students but the way this class was run confused me. I think it's supposed to be discussion based, but not much discussion ever happened. Also, she would often ask questions that were either way to specific or way to vague and it always seemed that she had a specific answer in mind.

Very relaxing class if you are comfortable participating. Readings can be overwhelming (~50 pages per class), but they are very worthwhile. Essays were not given any criteria or rubrics, but were graded fairly as long as you put in a good effort. Also, she sometimes gave pop quizzes/reading responses, so come to class prepared every time.

Dr. Current is super nice and the class is not too hard if you're doing the readings. Class participation is super important, but if you have anxiety about public speaking you can talk to them because they're very understanding.

Dr. Current always gave me good feedback on my writing, and I believe I improved as a writer by taking this course. I never had any problems with her but some of my classmates, from what I've heard, would disagree. A lot of class time is spent listening to her explain assignments, but sometimes we would get off topic. Overall, pretty good class.

I appreciated their personal care for each student- immediately remembered our names and passions, will even go out of her way to email articles she feels will benefit you in their class or future profession. Make sure to call her Dr. Current, not Mrs!
I took the class online during the summer, and she was delightful. She gives you a 100 as long as you follow the rubric and apply previous criticisms.

Worst professor I have had in all my time at UNC. Beyond unorganized, fails to lay out clear and succinct expectations for assignments and grades like you are supposed to know exactly what she wants when she doesn't tell you. Doesn't bother updating assignment information from previous semesters. Avoid! Find a professor who has their act together.
Very unorganized and confusing system of giving assignments and describing student tasks/responsibilities. Never specified exactly what she wanted and then left negative comments on all assignments.

She is very lecture heavy, and a pretty tough grader. She kinda purposively makes sure your papers are below 88% so you have to do revisions, but I was able to bring my grade up to an A after them. I thought the books very interesting to read. However, as much as I enjoyed her, this is not a class to take as a GPA booster.

Dr. Current is a great professor. If you take this class you will definitely improve as a writer. They are really caring and guide you through the assignments. Also if you get a bad grade on something she lets you resubmit for a total new grade. Everyone rating them a 3 or lower probably just didn't put in the effort.

I was personally not a fan of the very lecture heavy classes. Professor Current frequently spent a lot of class giving her personal analysis. While this was valuable, I would have preferred more open discussion with other students and developing our own analyses.

Dr. Current is very passionate about what she teaches. If you are looking to improve your scientific writing, take her class. If you want an easy A in engl 105I, take one of the classes taught by grad students. Dr. Current is very kind and cares about her students, she just sometimes goes on tangents for entire class periods.

I thought Dr. Current was very passionate on what she taught and how the course material was intertwined. I wish the final exam was not as big a part of our grade considering we also had a final paper. I particularly enjoyed the discussions that were had each day about what we read as they challenged me to think more critically.

Dr Current cares abt the material, but the classroom discussions tend to be rly repetitive (asking what we thought of a book/chapter, and writing down bullet points). It's a lot of reading and there isn't much instruction given on papers (each of which were 8-10 pages) and the final. You can do revisions on the midterm paper which is nice

Dr. Current is at best an arbitrary grader. Her syllabus has a specification stating if a student gets under an 88 on the midterm they can do revisions for a regrade, but it seems she will go out of her way to nitpick so a student is below that point. Be ready to read and basically go to a book club as a class. Can't tell you one thing I learned.
She was an amazing teacher.

Taking ENGL105 over the summer before college was the best thing ever. Dr. Current gives examples of what work should look like and posts rubrics for assignments so expectations for earning A's are clear. She is always willing to read over your work before you submit it, too, so you know what she thinks before she ever grades it. Just do the work!

Dr. Current's class was incredible. I strongly recommend ENGL105i to anyone planning on a medicine/research career. I learned how to read research and understand it well even if the words were big. Plus, we got an in depth lesson on how to make an academic research poster which is super great. Office hours are super helpful so be sure to attend.

I loved Dr. Current! She's fun and kind and great to talk to outside of class. She will give feedback that may sound harsh, but it's all to help you get better. She also allows resubmissions if you get a bad grade. You get out what you put into her class, and if you plan on going into medicine, she gives a great introduction to medical writing.
Super sweet and caring, and gave me an extra opportunity to revise one of my papers, but also a bit tough if you don't REALLY try.

I loved Dr. Anderson. We got to record podcasts, make wellness videos, use AI in an intellectually ethical way, and look at different styles of wellness writings. Our portfolio, which 100% of grade, hasn't been graded yet so not sure how tough of a grader he is but clearly cares and I think he'll see the effort I've put in and be fair and kind.

Prof. Anderson was awesome. He really helped me see wellness from a different perspective and most importantly allowed us to be creative. I can't say enough good things about this class and work is quite minimal. But some effort in and you will do well, great professor to build a good relationship with!

Only teacher I've ever had that actually acted on the belief that learning/creativity > grades. All our assignments were turned in as "drafts" and the final portfolio was what was graded for accuracy. Kind, caring prof who was awesome to talk to. Minimal restrictions on assignments as he wants you to find your creative voice. Take him, he's great!

I had Professor Anderson for English 105, so I was excited to take him for the first year seminar requirement. However, the class was a nightmare, as  there was so much homework, reading, and papers, with all being graded difficult. He took the seminar to a whole different level of seriousness. This was the first class I struggled with at UNC.

Dan was great! The class wasn't exactly what I thought but I learned a ton about how to use computer programs to make video and audio projects. The project deadlines seemed like a lot but those were all rough draft deadlines so (I didn't realize) I didn't need to take it so seriously (made the final draft part at the end easier tho).

ENGL 148. Good lecturer and engagement, can tell she has a passion for the literature. There is in class canvas discussions at the beginning that is used for participation and assume she used this in place of a student not actively speaking in class. Did this class more for fun and to retouch on reading outside main major.

Instructor Fowler was a very nice person, just not a great instructor. They would be late to many meetings and these meetings felt unprepared. However, they were very accommodating when it came to due dates and attendance. I felt my tuition was wasted, but if you want an easy class, this is the way go.

Professor Fowler was very inconsistent with grading assignments (providing feedback), and often cancelled class last minute (or was very late). In their defense they had a lot of personal issues going on this semester, so I can't speak for their teaching under normal circumstances, but overall I learned little to nothing from this class.

Professor Fowler is the most compassionate and caring professor you will ever have. Prioritizes student well-being over everything and will work with students no matter their situation. It's hard to lose your A in this class as long as you complete your feeder assignments and give good effort on your unit projects. Couldn't recommend them more.

I actually had her for ENGL120**
Mandy was excellent and caring. She was clear and concise in her feedback when grading and was incredibly accessible outside of class. She was always great at giving advice when I needed it and was very accommodating with deadlines if an extension was needed. She also helped students create networking in the class.

I really enjoyed Professor Fowler and her class, she's one of the most caring professors I've had and is always willing to extend deadlines or work with you if you're struggling for any reason. Assignments can be pretty long, but the feeders truly help you for the unit projects, so I wasn't even mad they were long. Definitely recommend!
Super chill. No tests, quizzes. You get an A if you have a 3/3 on 2+ assignments with the opportunity to revise if you have a 1 or a 2. Never went to class and still got an A.
Good prof but lectures could be boring at times.

Professor Lee is incredibly supportive and makes expectations very clear. His feedback is detailed and genuinely helps you improve your writing. He encourages collaboration, keeps the class low stress, and is very accessible when you need help. I took the business focused section of ENGL105 . I would absolutely recommend him.
Simply the best
Such a chill professor, honestly didn't gaf but if you went and talked to him then he was really knowledgable about his topics. Mostly talked abt AI (or LLMS) and honestly the easiest A.
Recitation instructor. He gave A's and wrote straightforward MCQs for quizzes. He's funny (always on the contrary with assigned films lol), but he had lots of technical problems.

Charlie was a great professor very lenient and helpful when it came to due dates. When it comes to grades he would give feedback so you could receive a higher score. Their is three units centered around LLMs and AI, two papers and one presentation. Overall great class and no complaints.

Charlie was an amazing and phenomenal teacher. He's very nice and overall it's a really easy class. 2 papers, 1 presentation. He's very lenient on grading and his class had a focus on LLMs. I absolutely recommend.

Was always super available outside of class and had super helpful feedback. Very lenient with grades and offered extensions a lot. I thought the focus on AI and LLMs was interesting, so if thats something you think you'd like to write about for a semester, definitely take it with Charles!

Charlie is such a nice professor! This class was such an easy A, and I have heard that English 105 can sometimes be tough, depending on the professor. We never used the textbook, and attendance was not really necessary. Three projects that he grades on a 1-3 scale, and you can correct your mistakes to get a 3.

Charlie is a very caring instructor, he is super kind and is patient and helpful during OHs. Easy grader. Just keep your work updated and consult on what to improve with your drafts then you will more than likely succeed. This class was not that easy for me but Charlie really cured my day. Easily the best professor ever.
Prof Lee made ENGL 105 very easy. I was a bit scared of all the writing but he is a lenient grader and is also very flexible with due dates! Take ENGL 105 with him for a good experience!
Charlie was such a kind and caring professor. There is barely any homework, and the class is very manageable -- only three projects.

Prof. Lee is such a genuine person, when I had some personal things going on he was very understanding and allowed me extra time on work. He is very flexible on due dates and always wants the best for his students. His assignments are not that hard, he really is the best.

Professor Lee (or Charles, as he insisted we call him) was by far the most caring professor I had this past semester. There are 3 "units" to the class - a scientific research paper, a social science paper, and a online portfolio. Each of these papers were very simple and clear, not difficult at all. Each unit was broken into manageable steps.

Prof. Lee is a kind-hearted man who really wants the best for his students. The assignments are not too difficult and are structured so that students can complete them in a timely manner without getting behind. Lee offers helpful feedback and makes students feel heard. His tone and mannerisms make it clear that he cares. Overall great professor!

Suuuuper chill guy. Very understanding of the fact that students are humans and not robots, and he is all around an understanding guy. As long as you do the work, you'll get an A. Take with him if you can!!! 10/10 recommend.

He is very passionate about course content which made lectures insightful. 1 group project, a few easy assignments, but lots of reading that you have to discuss. Had a pop quiz when people stopped reading. He never gave feedback on stuff or responded to emails unless you asked him in person. Caring in class & office hours.
Very chill dude. He is a very slow to grade but I'm sure that's normal. Super easy in class sessions and easy to get an A.

i did not appreciate a lot that he had to say on my work, acted like it was a 400 level writing class. but class time was easy, never put in grades, i dont know im not really a fan even though it was easy.

Super cool. Accommodating and lenient grader, but attendance is important. The class is very conversation-based, so the more you speak up, the smoother it goes. Pretty great, especially for a required class.

Bro is a D1 chiller. He doesn't take attendance. Very lenient on deadlines and was just nice. You can't ask for much more in a professor. For ENGL 105, having him as my professor was such a blessing. Love you Emilio

Emilio is a great teacher. There are about 3 relatively easy major assignments for the entire semester. Overall, the class was super easy and manageable. If you go to class and complete the work, you will get an A. If you can't make it to class, email him, he is super flexible about attendance.I HIGHLY recommend taking this class with Emilio.

Emilio is super nice and really chill. Attendance is not mandatory as long as you email him. The class is composed of three unit projects that each consist of a couple feeder assignments, annotated bibliography, and a paper. He always asks for feedback on assignments and how we are feeling about them. I definitely recommend ENGL 105 with him.

I loved Professor Weed; she was brilliant on the subject matter and always made class interesting and engaging. The class itself was not too hard, with in-class participation. One major paper and unit quizzes. Overall, would recommend her!

Dr Weed is really great. I am a stem major and I still found this class really interesting. More quiz based than I was expecting for an English class but I rarely did the readings and still did well though I did go to every single lecture. One longer paper on a topic of your choice. Grading was often slow but not harsh.

Class is based on readings she provides, some are long and others are short but overall, they are easy reads. This class wasn't hard but if you don't do the readings or study for the quizzes, it will become hard. I definitely loved her teaching style and the way class worked. Overall, it was an interesting class and had great points to take away.

Such an interesting class and not at all what I expected. Focus on people's lived experiences and how disability relates to society. Definitely makes you think and offers new perspectives. Lots of in-class discussions and readings, but nothing was difficult. Prof. Weed is accommodating and very likable, I loved her lectures!
if you show up you will be just fine! super super caring will never make you feel dumb about anything. a lot of discussion in class but she will never call on you so rest assured if you're shy.
prof weed is super nice, understanding, and super accommodating.

two attendence models: one is graded by being present in class (with 3 missed days), the other is submitting reading notes. there are 3 in person quizzes, but not too hard as long as you do the readings and study the slideshows. option for final exam or project. i loved this class; prof. weed is a great instructor!

She gives many options, even for attendance. You are able to go to normal lectures or you can write article summaries in a journal and in certain dates you have to come in to get them checked. Even for the final she gives an option to either do a project or take the final.

Professor Weed is respectful and available to students. Her disability studies class was really interesting, with well-selected materials and topics, and in-class discussions. Exams were really easy if you had done the reading/shown up to class. The essay was on whatever you wanted to focus on and the group projects also had a lot of leeway.

Very insightful professor that helps you understand complex topics. Provided more perspectives to view from and understand the importance of diversity within literature. The course was mostly discussion based, but you work in pairs or groups pretty often. Assignments were of reading notes, small paper participation, a midterm and a final/project.
Awesome professor, super respectful and understanding. Meets every student where they are. Definitely take a class with her if you can.
Prof. Weed was awesome. Class could get tough at some times, but never an insane amount of work and she gave great feedback. Put in the effort and it shouldn't be terrible to get the grade you want.

Readings are very long, but wasn't mandatory to read everything. Come ready to discuss in class as it is discussion-heavy. Essays and projects are graded harsher, but nothing crazy. Interesting and would reccomend!

Prof. Weed was super caring and understanding, and her lectures were always engaging and thought-provoking. While it did have a good amount of reading, none of it was boring or felt like busywork. As long as you do the readings, you should be fine. Nothing but love and respect for this professor.

I would highly recommend any class taught by Professor Weed. She cares a lot about the subject being taught and even more about her students. She is flexible and understanding when it comes to deadlines. Your grade in this class is based on reading notes, a final project, a midterm, and a paper (written about attending a Health Humanities event).

Very caring and organized. Recommend for those with interest in medical profession. She offers extra credit, and is lenient on extensions/attendance if you talk to her. Very engaging class environment, high respect for all insights/ideas raised in class. Outlines expectations in a clear way and sticks to them throughout the semester.
I took this async over the summer. There was 30-60 pages of reading everyday which was a lot and took a while. However the grading was pretty easy. There were two papers.
Wonderfully insightful Professor. Highly recommend you take any class she has to offer, as you will learn so much from any class Dr. Weed teaches.

Dr. Weed is intriguing and presents good lectures, but this class structure is awful. She is an incredibly slow grader which leaves you wondering your grade for most of class. There are multiple group projects in this class. The final was also set up to be pretty tricky compared to most Engl classes I've taken at UNC.

Dr. Weed is by far the BEST professor I've had at UNC. I took ENGL 163 with her, which for some reason isn't listed, but I would 100% recommend taking this class. The lectures were almost entirely discussion based, so as long as you do the readings you'll be good to go. The material was interesting, and I always looked forward to this class! 10/10
Cate is super nice and flexible about due dates. Assignments are helpful for creating final unit projects and workload is not too heavy.

Cate is a great teacher to have for ENGL105. Classes aren't very interesting, but props to her for trying since ENGL105 is just boring given it's nature. She's very understanding and lenient on grading & attendance as long as you are communicative. Very little work overall and lots of opportunity to get points back. Easy A. Highly recommend!

Cate has clear rubrics for everything and is flexible with deadlines. In class was sometimes a little boring because she gives a lot of presentations, but the projects are not that difficult. She's clearly passionate about English and very accommodating. Would recommend for freshmen English.

Cate was a great, easy professor to have for ENGL 105. Class was very laidback, though she does expect participation in discussions. Deadlines were sometimes pushed back and grade/feedback was slow, but wasn't awful. Would recommend for freshman English.

Cate is super kind and lenient with extensions—no late penalties if you ask. She's a bit disorganized and class can be boring, but if you participate when she asks questions, you'll be fine. Overall, an easy A for English 105 if you want a chill semester.

Very disorganized in class and is all over the place. Takes it a little too seriously for an ENGL 105 class and takes forever to return feedback, so deadlines end up being pushed to the last few weeks of the semester. That being said, she's very lenient with deadlines, but is a little nitpicky when grading after consistently pushing due dates back.
Super nice and very understanding. Will give extensions on almost all work if you simply ask. A little disorganized, but overall clear in grading criteria.
Just take this class if u need your ENGL105 credit. its very very easy if you try.

Overall she gives amazing feeback and really knows literature. She is understanding with personal issues or needing extensions. Class would be boring sometimes because no one would talk and she would sit and stare at us until we did lol. But in-class assignments and the last two projects were really easy. Grading rubrics are really clear.

Cate is very caring and understanding. Most classes are lectures and can sometimes get boring or difficult if there is no class participation. Not a lot of homework and reasonable due dates. She is lenient with extensions and late work. Grading on papers/assignments is not harsh if you listen on what to focus on in class.

Professor Rivers was a good professor. She was very understanding of personal issues when they would come up and made arrangements to get you the information you needed if you had to miss class. Her lectures can be a little dry and boring but overall a good person and an easy grader.

Cate consistently arrives late, handles class issues unprofessionally, lacks preparation, and surprises me with the number of positive reviews she has received. She is impolite and fails to make the class interactive. Additionally, she does not provide clear instructions for assignments, which leaves the entire class confused.

absolutely do not take her, she shows up late every day, is never prepared for class, doesn't explain assignments, if she hears you whispering she'll call you out and make you say what you were talking about, one of the most disorganized and poorly taught classes I've been in
She's cool. Don't take advantage of her kindness. Best ENG 105 to take.

Cate is super understanding and passionate about writing. Provides quality feedback on all assignments and will provide even more if you request it. She makes the class interactive and fun. I would definitely take another class taught by Cate.

Cate is super sweet, funny, and passionate about literature! She's extremely understanding and accommodating for illnesses etc. The in-class assignments were easy and engaging, and she gives good feedback on the portfolio pieces. There are three main projects for the semester, a literary analysis, a zine, and a scientific article. We love Cate

Expects you to have some type of draft for peer review every day. Not hard to get an A with grading contract. Did not provide any feedback until Apr 22 (ldoc on Apr 27, the feedback was for an assignment we turned in Feb 16). Kinda picky and pretentious, likes to hear himself talk, but wants you to improve. Wish there was more consistent feedback.

Professor Smith is lowkey a try hard but is smart. He gives detailed feedback but peer feedback is most common. He cares about you learning how to write better so his assignments will be slightly more difficult than the chill and laid back PhD students. If you take him though you will do well, just know you actually have to work and do many drafts.

Will not shut up about what every word means in Latin. I agree with others, he loves to hear himself talk. Instructions are incredibly vague and confusing, deadlines are not clear. Constant unnecessary group discussions and peer reviews that add nothing.

Professor Smith's ENGL105 class is structured using a grading contract. It is impossible not to get an A unless you decide you don't want an A. Nothing is graded subjectively, everything is completion. His lessons were easy to follow, and you'll be fine if you submit your major assignments on time. He's lenient with attendance and small assignments

Prof Smith clearly cares about getting his students to learn and grow, but he doesn't really grade anything, it's a completion thing. So-- you have to do some extra assignments and outside of class stuff in order to get an A. If you're looking for real, consistent feedback on your work just know that it will come from peers rather than him.

Nice guy for ENGL 105! He made a grade contract to guarantee an A if you put effort into this course, and gave super detailed feedbacks on unit projects (though always a little bit delayed). The lectures are intriguing and the group workshops are helpful. I really want to take other ENGL courses held by Professor Smith.

Professor Smith is such a kind human being! He is passionate about his work and teaching this class. Definitely take this class if you are interested in Law - if you are not you may find it boring. As long as you submit all papers/projects on time and attend class without the max number of misses you can obtain an A.
Never returns graded papers. Self-important. Rambles endlessly. DO NOT TAKE.

Professor Smith has a clear grading contract, so it is relatively easy to keep up with your grade. Nothing you submit really gets "graded", and their feedback took a very long time to get back so I never really knew if my writing was improving at all. Sometimes his tangents seemed a little far fetched, but interesting nonetheless. Nice professor

Smith is a very insightful and thoughtful professor. You can tell he cares about his students. This class is tailored towards freshmen, as it is a first year requirement. He has a grading contract which sort of guides your grade for the class, therefore as long as you put effort in and show up you will do fine.

So many more assignments compared to any other English 105 course and never grades anything. He does have a clear grading contract but you will not get any feedback all semester and he expects you to turn in everything yet doesn't look at any of it. His class is so boring and he doesn't teach you anything, he just likes to listen to himself talk.

Kind professor that truly cares about her students. Very passionate about business communication. Gives great, tailored feedback and guides you throughout the semester. Attendance is mandatory, but she's very understanding with circumstances and willing to work with you. Take with her if you can!

Take Holly Thompson. Very kind professor who gives great feedback and truly cares about her students. Class is a lot of work, but she guides you through it, and it's not too difficult as long as you don't fall behind. Few presentations and a little bit of reading. Attendance is mandatory.

She gave timely feedback and always uplifted you and your style of writing. Her syllabus and writing examples were ultra-specific, so you knew exactly what she expected of you. She provided 4 late passes for the semester, which were really helpful when I did not feel like doing my work. There was very low pressure to speak up in class.

Professor Thompson is who you want for English 105! Im an English major, so I found the class super doable. However, for non-English people I would say she is the best professor for this class. We had two essays to write, and an infographic and they both had a very minimum word count. I learned a lot in this class and she is so personable!

She was a very easy and understanding professor. If you have a problem, go talk to her. She is easy to talk to and is willing to work with you. Read the syllabus and understand exactly what she wants. She sticks to exactly what the syllabus says. Just follow her rules and you will be fine.
literally loved this class and I DO NOT LIKE ENGLISH!! Was really dreading having to take this and Professor Thompson made it so useful, I got a lot from it
just a seriously good professor. good person, cares a lot about the subject matter, and will put in work to help you

Prof. T is super kind and cares deeply about both the subject and her students. Her class has more work than some other 105 professors but I don't see the point of a class that has one essay a semester.
