She gives great feedback, and I promise that as long as you try, you do not need to worry about your grade. Shes very understanding.

I really enjoyed Prof. T, and she really cares about her students and their learning English, but she gives a lot of work, and some of it feels like a waste of time. Her assignments are thoughtful and help you reflect and produce good work, but you will probably have more work than some other 105 classes - but it is all effort-based!

I can truly say that Professor Thompson🔥 is one of the best instructors I've ever had. Her unconventional, relaxed approach to teaching has done WONDERS for my writing. She single-handedly changed my perspective on the writing process. She is a wonderful human who brings tremendous empathy and humanity to her class💕.

Prof T is very kind and effective. She is able to toe the line between meaningful coursework and care for her students. Her assignments are thoughtful and all have extremely clear and helpful instructions. She acts as a coach and model writer, helping you develop your voice within the disciplines. Prof T is very good, IMO.

Professor Thompson is truly a light in a world of seemingly hopeless professors (sometimes, lol). She not only cares about her student's lives, but she understands what it means to be a freshman in college. She is not only hilarious, but she is intelligent, kind, and motivated to making us better writers. All of the writing you do is well worth it!

Prof T is amazing!!! If you get the chance to take ENGL 105 with her you should 100% take it! She is soooo kind, intelligent, funny, and helpful. She truly embodies the writing *coach* role and made this seemingly boring or useless class very useful. The environment of the class is great, the homework is easy and enjoyable, and improvement is key!

Did the grading and gave solid feedback and writing suggestions. Short MCQ quizzes did ask for tiny details over plot (supporting character's job on three different occasions lol), so keep an eye out. Guest lectures were great.

She's super sweet and a really knowledgeable professor. In class we mainly did group discussion boards, which weren't that helpful but were interesting. She canceled class a few times which was nice, and dedicates full classes to asking questions about your papers, which were useful. She's not a hard  grader and is a great choice for ENGL 105!

Professor Maller is amazing. There are a lot of group assignments, but they aren't super long and only one person actually has to type/ submit the work. Gives amazing feedback and will stay after class to chat about anything and help with whatever. Definitely my favorite professor so far.
Very kind and perfect teacher for 105. Lots of in-class group work, but the articles she assigns are very interesting!
She does NOT grade harshly at all, just submit your work and you will do great. There are some papers but you basically have an extension for each assignment.

professor maller made english 105 so enjoyable! she is so knowledgable about the subject she teaches and has a true passion for helping her students succeed! she was very flexible when it came to choosing topics to write our papers on and providing extensions when needed! i would recommend her to anyone taking english 105!!

So chill. I got a 100 on every single assignment. She didn't give timely or extensive feedback but to be fair you can't improve from 100. Canceled class a few times here and there too which was nice. Solid prof choice for engl 105, she is def one of the best.
Dana is the coolest professor and made English 105 my favorite class. I got 100s on all of my papers, and the class could choose their topics for the unit projects. Overall, she is incredible!

Absolutely love her! As someone who isn't great in English classes, this was the complete opposite of stressful; she gave good feedback on rough drafts, was lenient about due dates, let us out of class early often, and is overall just super sweet. There's never much of a rubric but doesn't grade harshly at all. 100% take her!

1000% take Dana Maller. I would retake her for any other class, she's amazing. Super chill, we skipped like one class every other week. The class couldn't have been any easier and she's so so nice. She even helped me with a personal project and gave me amazing resources and feedback. 100/10 would take again.

I LOVE Professor Mailer. She is so understanding and truly cares about the livelihood of her students. She even structured class so our (very manageable) workload would decline as the semester went on to accommodate the pace of other courses. Not to mention, she is always excited to review papers during office hours too. 100000/10 would recommend.
anyways understanding when I needed an extension!!

I really enjoyed Professor Velez, she made classes interesting and tried her hardest to engage and connect with all students. Homework can be a lot, but for the course its understandable. Overall I feel like my writing improved and I would take another class with her if I could!

Creative writing classes are always going to be super reading heavy, but Professor Velez makes in-class discussions fun and always has brilliant advice to go for new writers. She has a lot of practical experience and gives a lot of feedback on your writing submissions. One of my favorite professors at UNC!
Loads of work, tech free classroom, murky guidelines, open class critique of your work

Professor Velez is a wonderful professor! She's accommodating, funny, knowledgeable, and always prepared for class. All of this being said, the class is a 300 for a reason. You have to write two 15 pg installments of a story (30 pgs total) while still doing other homework for the class. Lots of fun, but be sure you know what you're getting into!

I absolutely adored ENGL 130! She was incredibly caring and understanding about deadlines and did a great job of inspiring creativity within the class. She wasn't a hard grader but she still did a good job of critiquing. I was scared to take this class because of the workshop aspect but she made the classroom a space of a lot of respect.

I really enjoyed Professor Velez's class. She is extremely caring and created a positive atmosphere. She really lets students learn from each other, so this course felt like one big group project in the best way. She does assign more homework than usual but it's easy enough to not be too tedious.

Nice but assigns work like it's your only class. I know people in her 100 level course with the same amount of work. You have to write a 20-30 p. story, read & critique everyone else's, revise & resubmit your own, read 2 novels, complete assignments on the novels, & do a presentation. Also technology free classroom & expects you to print everything
this is for engl105. we literally had 3 in person meetings all semester. easy A. W prof

This class was fine. He did a short lecture and then we discussed readings (lots of it). He is very knowledgeable on everything and was funny when he let his personality out. Not many assignments, just some writing. You can get away pretty easily with not reading everything. Class was pretty boring if you're not interested in the content
No option for 105, but I took ENGL105 with Prof Gadaleto. Best 105 prof no questions, take his class. Super caring and very accessible outside of class
This dude is awesome!!!
I actually took 105. This class was wonderful, take him for English 105!

Professor Gadaleto was a great professor! This was one of my favorite English classes I've taken. There's unit reading quizzes and some short essays throughout the semester, as well as a midterm and final.Professor Gadaleto is super passionate about the topic (and about Milton!). I would absolutely recommend taking any class with him if you can!!
The class was very interrupted and moved to zoom due to uncontrollable circumstances, but, in the brief time before that interruption, he seemed very passionate, personable, and well-informed.
Love love love Prof. Gadaleto!! This is the best class I've taken at UNC so far. Go to office hours, get to know him, engage in recitation, and you will get so much out of this class.

225 was uniquely challenged this semester but Mike and his TAs did a really good job considering the circumstances. Personally Gadaleto is one of the kindest professors I've had and he is intensely knowledgeable and passionate about Shakespeare. His slides are dense…but he's very chill and accommodating.

An absolute gem of a professor in the English department. He had to move class to Zoom near the end of the semester and had recorded make-up lectures, but he was very understanding of changing the schedule. He didn't get to the plays he wanted to get to, but nonetheless, the class made me fall in love with Shakespeare more.

Gadaleto is a kind and fun professor who is obviously passionate about Shakespeare. He is super approachable and genuinely loves talking with students and appreciates their insights. He has a tendency to cancel classes or move them to zoom, however, he will make recorded lectures to compensate so the class remains on pace with the syllabus.
Great vibes.
Prof. Gadaleto makes Shakespeare come to life through his palpable passion for the subject. 100% recommend even if you aren't sure what to think about Shakespeare's tricky verbiage.

Gadaleto was a really good professor. He truly cared for everyone of his students. He is a bit of a tough grader, the feedback he gives is almost all positive so it was a little hard to understand what we did wrong. Overall would definitely take again.

He is caring and fun but his class was just okay, boring at lectures. There was a lot of reading, but I barely read anything and got away with it. He grades participation very harshly (you have to talk in class). There were 2 papers (no feedback) and a final discussion (small group, cumulative); it was not difficult but also graded harshly.

First Professor I've felt I should review. Class itself isn't too much work if you can interpret Shakespeare well. Professor Gadaleto is a cool dude and definitely knowledgeable and good at what he teaches.

Professor Mike is possibly the most understanding teacher I have ever had. I took ENGL 89 with him (seminar about Hamlet) and he was very accommodating as well as just plain interesting. I started the class not liking Shakespeare's work and ended it extremely emotionally invested; please take a class with him!

I took English 105-i, writing for business, with Mike. He is the kindest professor I have ever met and he cares about each of his students so much. This class was by far the easiest class I have ever taken; I don't think anyone received anything other than an A. Major projects included writing fake emails to coworkers and applying to a fake job.

I thoroughly enjoyed Dr. Gadaleto's class. He always adjusted to the needs of the students. I appreciate his dedication to his lecturing as well as his passion for the material and content matter. I'd definitely take a class of his again.
Literally the best professor of all time. I took engl 105i - writing in business and her could not have been a better teacher. I want to take all of his classes the next couple of years.

Dr. Tucker was a wonderful person and is so passionate about writing. She was an excellency professor who was very understanding and constructive on the work we did. The work in the class consists of a flash fiction piece, a short story and then discussion posts every week. Participation in class is part of the grade but with 15 people it's easy.

Dr. Tucker is so kind and truly cares so much about her students. She is really understanding and checks in w students every class. The assignments for the class include one flash fiction, one short story (6-10 pgs) and then just discussion posts on the work of the other students in your class. This class is super enjoyable. Would highly recommend!

The best prof I've had at UNC. She was so understanding regarding everything-if you were sick, going through something, etc. She's a phenomenal person and professor- very helpful with perfecting your writing regardless of what your writing level was. Being around her just made me so happy. Easy A too!

Professor Tucker is incredibly patient and caring. She grades based on improvement, not just achievement, which I appreciated immensely. The workshop set up of the class itself is a little tricky if you're not used to sharing your work with others, but Dr. Tucker does a great job facilitating positive feedback. Highly recommend for an FC-CREATE.
Rude and condescending. Would never take again.

Nice but super liberal. Got a 100 on everything. Be ready to have your short stories read and discussed. Participation is important. Super chill class. Doesn't like when you miss class. Very fun, creative class. Lots of reading. Discussions are easy and low effort. Daily readings with discussions and then talked about in class. 2 papers.

Dr. Tucker is the best! She truly cares about her students and wants them to become better writers. I have never felt so cared for by a teacher. It consists of 2 papers (8-12 pages), and as long as you put effort into them, you get a 100. Gives you the freedom to try different things even if you fail, would highly recommend taking a class from her.
Dr. Tucker is an encouraging professor who clearly wants to see her students succeed.

Prof Tucker was a good professor, but can make comments about your work that are a little unnecessary. Readings for every class and you MUST participate. One presentation about a story, one 8-12 story and one 1,000 word max story. Your final is revising those. Not hard at all and fulfills FC-CREATE. Class is mainly workshopping your peers stories.

ENGL 138, not 130. Dr. Tucker is the best. She's a kind soul who speaks her mind (in a good way) and loves to read, write, and TEACH. You'll get full marks on each paper (one 500-800 words, another 8-12pgs) as long as you meet the word counts and try your best; she wants passion and improvement, not perfection. Absolutely take this class!!!

English 138 - If I could take this class again I would. She is awesome and cares so much about her students. And honestly, an easy straightforward class if you do what is asked of you. She doesn't care about perfection, she just cares that you attempted. Everything  she teaches will be helpful throughout your years in college and also your career!

There is nothing negative about Dr. Tucker. She is kind & makes sure all students have what is needed to succeed (I had mental health and familial issues throughout this semester). The class is just participation and completion grades, & she makes sure goals are achievable. I've taken her twice now and will be taking her a third time.

Dr. Tucker's awesome! One of my very favorite professors I've had at unc. We wrote one 4-6 pg story and one 10-12 pg story. She gives lots of time to work on them in class and provides as much guidance as needed. For homework we read our peers writing and leave comments but everyone is really encouraging of each others work. Super easy A and fun!

I really enjoyed this course. Each student writes and revises two stories throughout the semester, and there's also an informal short story presentation that was super chill. As long as you turn things in and come to class, you'll do well. Dr. Tucker is encouraging and also gives great feedback on stories.

Dr. Tucker was an excellent professor and made the class a comfortable place to engage with peers. She's clearly super knowledgable and can give really great insight into your writing in a way that is direct but doesn't make you feel inferior. Excellent and would take again and the class was pretty straightforward and not difficult.

Dr. Tucker was SO unkind to me on MULTIPLE occasions. When I was having a really hard time during the semester (mental health issues, my grandmother DYING, etc) she made it seem like I was just being lazy/not putting in effort. She was condescending at best, savior complex-y at worst. Her class wasn't hard, but I didn't feel respected.

She is amazing. Her classes consist of 200-250 word responses to colleagues stories and two 10-12 page stories, including revisions for the end of the year. She is easy to reach if you need help or an extension, and makes the class feel like a small community. I plan on taking a new class with her next semester!! Great professor!

Dr. Tucker was amazing! Her feedback on our stories was both kind and complementary, while helpful and critical when it needed to be. She picked out the best short stories to read and was so respectful of each and every student.

Got that grade due to mental health issues, but she's a caring teacher, and it's easy to do well in her class. Please take her course if you can! couldn't ask for a smarter, more interesting, or considerate professor. She knows what she's talking about, and will work with you to make sure you succeed. TAKE HER COURSE!!!

I can't even begin to say how much I loved this class. Dr. Tucker has been one of the best profs I've had here at Carolina. She gave amazing feedback that was helpful. She understands when you need a mental health day. And most importantly, she cares about you and your work. If you get the opportunity to take a class with her, you won't regret it.
Take her course. Literally an angel. Always caring and patient. Always ready to help. I really learned a lot.

Could not a recommend a professor more for 105. Very easy A, especially compared to the other ENG 105 section. You pick any research topic for the whole semester, and all the assignments revolve around that 1 topic. She is fair, and offers great feedback in office hours, guaranteeing 100s on feeder assignments.

This class is a straight-forward, easy A as long as you do the work. There is not much homework. The classes were pretty boring for me (probably because I was familiar with most of the concepts from high school). I really enjoyed the research project and I think I learned a lot from it. Also, Professor Horton is SO SO nice and gives good feedback.
The absolute best ENGL 105 professor. If you can, you should take her.
Literal ANGEL. Take her if you can. You won't regret it!!

Ms. Horton is so chill, an easy grader, and gives great feedback. She teaches the class so that students can research what they are interested in, so you won't hate this class even if you don't have an interest in English. I couldn't recommend a better professor for 105!!

Amazing professor for ENGL 105. Assignment guidelines were clear and I never felt overwhelmed with work. She wants her students to succeed. Attendance is mandatory but she is very understanding and also canceled class during extreme weather (iykyk). Take her for ENGL 105!!!!
The best prof for ENGL 105! Her grading is super easy and she will give you extensions if you ask her.
One of the kindest professors I have ever had! Great class and easy work. Definitely take ENGL 105 with her.
Great professor! Super easy class and very caring. Wanted her students to do well. Lots of ways to succeed in this class.

I absolutely LOVED her. Her class was easy and she is possibly the nicest woman I have ever met. I improved a ton as a writer too. Her grading is also fair and easy, and if you have outside issues like family problems or something, she is super chill about extensions. Definitely recommend

You do not have to read much at all to get by. 2 students per week must participate, and the schedule for that is posted on Canvas. He says exactly what will be on exams. Lots of memorization. 1 page of reading notes due per week. Lectures often get off topic.

I am fearful for all of the young women who are subjected to this man. He feels he is invincible, and perhaps he may be. 

Ladies, please document anything that seems awry, especially if you are fresh out of high school. Parents, listen and support your children. Create an environment where they feel comfortable sharing with you. Dangerous man.
Personally my favorite professor, cares deeply about student success. I loved Dr. T's eclectic lecture style because it was interesting, but people who like straight forward classes may not like it.
Good guy and clearly knowledgeable, but tends to ramble and stray from syllabus.

He's highly knowledgeable and passionate about teaching, but he rambles on a lot and doesn't stick to the syllabus. We're still on the reading from the first few weeks when we should be moving on. I don't really understand the objective of this course unfortunately. He's still a nice and resourceful guy though!

Super fun, well-connected, knowledgeable professor. Beware, the class is more comparative literature than it is diplomacy. He rewards good faith effort, so stay engaged, take notes on everything he iterates, and go to office hours. 3 quizzes, 10 pages of writing, and a weekly reading notebook. Lots of extra credit for participating in CFED!

Clearly educated at a British institution. Talks extensively about how complex all of his lectures are but fails to provide any real depth. If you read all of the texts he tells you too independently I believe you would receive the same level of education as if you took this course. Nonetheless a kind man who cares about his students.

Dr. Leinbaugh is the most interesting professor I've had at UNC. He's very knowledgeable and passionate. At times, the class felt sporadic, but I loved Dr. Leinbaugh's chaotic energy and how I always asked myself "What wild thing will happen in class today?" The class was reading packed & written quizzes were lengthy, but it was worth it!

While Dr. T is sweet & funny, there was no clear grading criteria, the quizzes were basically memory tests of the readings, and I had no idea what I had the entire semester, including how I did on the final exam and papers. He did give hints on what would be on the quizzes and final though.

Disappointed that this class was barely focused on diplomacy. He did bring in some pretty cool guest speakers though. Very reading-heavy and you have to do a reading notebook for the readings. He did not put in any grades until after the final which was very frustrating. It's not a very hard class as long as you do everything assigned.

One of the best professors I have ever taken. Really good guy and he really cares about his students. A challenging course but if you do the homework and pay attention to lectures you should be fine. Really worth it taking one of his classes.

He is incredibly nice. That being said, I felt like the grades in this class were practically predetermined based on how you were perceived as a student. Free A if you're one of his favorites. If he doesn't think you're an A student, I don't think any amount of work will change his mind since grading is arbitrary and completely unexplained.

Super cool prof and class! I took it as a gen ed and I ended up learning a lot about history, literature and English culture. He loves teaching and it's cool to watch. The material is niche and you will have to do a good amount of reading.

Weird class and weird vibe. I don't think I would take a class with Ted again. Everyone says the same thing and I can see he hasn't changed from when I had him for ENGL 120. Disorganized, eccentric, and little too conceited for my taste. Goes on and on about his accomplishments for most of the class and expects us to kiss the ground he walks on.

This class was all over the place. There's no other way to put it. Dr. T is very disorganized and egocentric. Easy class, with interesting material, but if you actually want to walk away from the course with knowledge you have to do a lot of outside work. Lots of extra credit opportunities, and easy grading. One class with him is enough for me.

very interesting professor, lots of high-level connections. Values participation and "office hour" attendance. Course is very reading-heavy and difficult to navigate. Take this class if you are interested in diplomacy, making connections, reading ancient epics. If you are looking for a structured class that is easily navigated, I do not recommend.

Nice man but very disorganized, grades include 3 or 4 free response quizzes(which are actually tests), reading notebook, and 2 five page papers. For a 100 level course, WAY too strenuous. Grading is not based on a rubric/criteria, and there's no feedback/ comments as to how to actually improve grades. Idek how my grade was determined overall.

amazing, really want to take another class w him. teaching style is unconventional but not uneffective, takes some getting used to. class is more seminar w/discussion. no slides, so pay attention to what he's saying & take good notes. TA was v helpful in prep for quizzes(freehand).learned a lot, want to take more humanities classes bc of this class

Prof Leinbaugh is incredibly well-respected and highly knowledgeable about what he teaches. His assignments are usually papers but he's very easy to talk to and gives great feedback. He'll connect you with someone in a field you're interested in and will be a great resource. This class is great because he brings in experts and lecturers frequently

Dr. Leinbaugh is invested in students' academic and personal wellness. Connecting with individuals in the classroom and through CFED/TFED, he cultivates a robust learning community. With his infectious enthusiasm for his course content, Dr. Leinbaugh fosters an appreciation of literature and a more comprehensive understanding of the global stage.
Very fun class and good professor, I loved the discussions we would get into and the thought experiments! Very interesting topics and I loved the assignments!

The best. Would HIGHLY recommend to take him, hes not an anal grader like most english teachers, and also incites really interesting lines of thought. Overall learned way more from this class than most others because he wasn't trying to shove it down your throat, wish more teachers were intelligent enough to understand this is the best way to teach
Best English class at UNC! I highly recommend Andrew for English 105!

This was one of my favorite classes at UNC so far, and I usually hate English class. We had a lot of free rein with the topics for our 3 projects which made it more interesting and enjoyable, and the class discussions were super fun and engaging. Just a great class with a great instructor -- definitely take this course with Andrew!!!

If you ever get the chance to take him, do it!!!! I was dreading having to take an English class as it is, but it became my favorite class that I have had at UNC. He is so caring and he makes the atmosphere of the class so comfortable.

This was my favorite class that I have taken here at UNC even though I dreaded having to take ENG105. He made the class so fun and it was such a comfortable atmosphere within the class that we all felt comfortable chatting out loud and it was rarely ever just silent. Definitely take him if you have the chance.
Best professor ever. So kind and chill and VERY lenient grader. Lectures were very chill and encouraged participation. Highly recommend!!!!
Just an amazing guy, would highly recommend.

I really enjoyed how easy this class was as a gen ed class. The class was divided into three units which has feeders and a project (project and two essays). Andrew Tran was a great professor. The class wasn't mandatory but because it is a small class he will know if you aren't there.

Best teacher I've ever had. There are a few papers but he gives you almost full freedom and genuinely cares about what you want to write about. Easiest class ever but I've learned more during his lectures than I have in any other class ever. Genuinely excited to go to class

Very chill and fun class with a light workload. "Lectures" are really just low-key guided conversations. Andrew is very intelligent and overall an amazing guy. Cannot recommend his class enough and I can't wait for him to start teaching more courses.

Professor Tran was by far one of the best professors I have had. I took his 8am English class (which is something I said I would never do) and never regretted it once. If you have any way to take his class... do it. This was the first time I have ever thoroughly enjoyed an English class. Every assignment was interesting and didn't feel like a task.

Take this Engl-105. Prioritize it. Seek it out. Andrew is an incredible teacher. The lectures are incredibly engaging, and make you want to take an English class. Take this class, I can guarantee you'll get a good grade if you do the work.

My favorite professor at UNC, Andrew is so funny and genuine and quite honestly the smartest, most witty person I have ever met. Class was always pretty entertaining and you never knew what he would bring to talk about next class. Had 3 papers that have planning assignments before they're due and just a chill laid back class. TAKE HIM

This is such an interesting individual. You have no idea what he's going to say when he opens his mouth. Take this man for English 105. It is easy, fun (as much fun as engl 105 could be, i guess) and you get a lot of freedom to express your ideas and write about topics you ACTUALLY like. Luv andrew.

Easiest A ever, the only way to not get a straight 100 is just to simply not turn in anything. Class can be pretty boring but attendance is not taken and hes a really nice guy. Could not recommend him enough
He is soooooooooooo nice!!!! Take his class!!!!!!!

He's the BEST professor to take your ENGL 105 with! It's my first semester at UNC and ENGL105 with him is definitely made my semester. Not a harsh grader at all, very reasonable amount of readings and homework. Fun group discussions, watch film together, and the final project is presentation on the topic you choose. Recommend this 10000000/100!!!

Andrew is incredibly understanding and is always willing to push back the few assignments that he assigns. Fun in-class activities and he is a very approachable person. I would take this class again in a heartbeat even though I usually don't like English courses. He even offered to keep in touch if we wanted to grab a coffee in the future.

If I could take this class again I would JUST for Andrew Tran. Funny, charismatic, and interesting he made me excited to go to this class and participate. Do anything at all costs to get him on your schedule! 10000/10 class!

Cushman is a very engaging and intriguing lecturer. Which is why it was so disappointing his class became so disorganized the second half of the semester. Several assignments were crammed into the last few weeks of class (one being a group presentation) with little to no description, rubric, or due dates. Incredibly frustrating and stressful
This class was very interesting and the discussions and lectures were worthwhile. Nice TAs and engaging professor.
not the easy A it looks like, if you don't like to read probably don't take, discussions are interesting, rather unorganized class, in class essays for finals
Course fell apart later in the semester. Doesn't put assignments on canvas and you will have a final exam.

Only did pop quizzes the first month then didnt do any more, midterm is super easy you study off a jeopardy, class seems so intimidating at first but it gets so easy so quickly, final is not too difficult, final project is super easy you get a 100 as long as you put in minimal effort, be ready to ask classmates for missed notes
Prof is huzz

Professor Cushman if you're reading this I'm so sorry. I almost hit you with my car the other day on campus. I don't want you to know it was me because you're my favorite professor and I don't want you to hate me but I want to say I'm so sorry it was me who almost hit you. I'll be more careful I'm so sorry. I hope you have a great break!
I took this class a year ago and another class with him last semester. He is very kind and knows a lot about the subject matter. Not too much writing, which is nice for a freshman seminar.

I don't understand why all the comments are good. Dr. Cushman is a nice person and can be flexible, also knowledgeable about his field. But the syllabus is super disorganized and looking back, I learned zero stuff in the class and really thought it was a waste of time. To do the final project you really need background knowledge outside or prior.
This class is so special. It's unlike anything I've ever taken before. Just take it and you'll see.

Seriously one of the best Professors at UNC. This class was so amazing, and I would totally recommend taking it. Its easy to read when you know you get to go discuss and understand further! 10/10 class

i loved this class and really enjoyed the book. it felt like one large book club! if you are even considering this class, take it. in fact, even if you don't enjoy reading, take it. it was so fun getting to hear everyone's different perspectives and takeaways from the novel—that's what reading is all about, after all!
Great class, fair grader, interesting discussions. If you read the book and go to class you'll be fine.

I loved this class so much! He is such a great teacher, and he really helped us think about the text deeply. It wasn't very hard at all. I looked forward to the discussions because everyone in the class was so into it. He is a pretty relaxed grader and very nice person.

This is a life-changing class. I'm a STEM major and this was my favorite class I've taken at UNC (and it's not close). Take it if you're not an English major or anything like that. I learned to like reading again after falling off after graduation. Don't miss this one!

Really solid class and even better instructor. The book was good, but even better were the discussions. Perfect for a first year seminar. Met some awesome people, read something hard, and got to know a good prof.
The most amazing professor ever! Super accessible and helpful. Lots of reading but it was so worth it with the meaningful discussions he led. Truly loved this class, take it if you can!

Such an amazing professor and class! The best first-year seminar I probably could have taken & I wish I could take it every semester on a new book. The class was mainly discussion based and Professor Cushman created an open, accepting environment for all answers and opinions. We did two interesting presentations on topics we cared about.

Great class. Did not think I would enjoy reading this book but I absolutely loved it. Prof. Cushman did a great job helping us through slowly and encouraging us to stick with it. I feel like I climbed a mountain. Would take again for sure!

There are so many amazing things about Dr. Cushman! There's definitely a good amount of reading, but his lectures help simplify any questions. Class is discussion heavy but is well-guided. Papers were graded with really good feedback and he would always make time outside of class to talk. The best though was him sometimes bringing his dog to class!

. She will not grade your assignments until the end of the semester, so you won't have any idea what grades you are getting, she takes off credit for just about anything, even if you follow the instructions perfectly. Teachers like this make me hate learning. Her feedback is pretty opinions based and doesn't provide good insight into the assignment

Her lectures can be very boring, but she is a kind professor. Her grading can sometimes be confusing, but if you focus and do well on the smaller assignments, a lower grade on a unit final won't be damaging.

Don't choose her, please. Grades came in literally months later. Expectations were so unclear. The lectures were boring. I felt like her feedback was sassy and made me feel dumb, even with 4 AP-level English/writing/research classes under my belt. All other classes had much less work. This class felt like a fight, and I wanted to be anywhere else.

The class is easy, but her lectures are boring, and the content is common sense. She also takes forever to grade assignments (I didn't get some grades back for over 2 months). There were only 9 assignments the entire semester, so I have no idea why it was so hard for her to grade things. She is a nice person, but take ENGL 105 with anyone else.

We had 3 papers this semester, and only got each one back about a day before the next one was due, so any feedback on what could be better was useless. On all my papers I got about 10 points off, with my only feedback being to "use more quotes," even on the next paper where I had them every other sentence. No feedback regarding my writing quality.

Hannah was nice and inclusive, and she was lenient with absences and late work. But, she gave us really easy lectures and made it seem as though her grading guidelines were very easy to achieve. She would have conferences with us and make it seem like I was on the right track, but then would grade in a very specific, harsh, and nit picky way.

Hannah is a good first year teacher to have. She sometimes is confusing with her feedback and some of the lectures have difficult topics, but she still expects you to participate. She understands that you as a student are busy, so she is lenient with due dates.
Theres no clear grading criteria for all the projects, and they deviate from what other ENGL 105 professors give (she gives much more work). Don't take her.
Hannah was an okay teacher and tried to make the class enjoyable, but she was an overly harsh grader compared to the other English teachers at UNC.

Hannah is so sweet but the grades I got were lower than what I expected (and she put them in literally 2 days before finals week was over). She's super picky over everything whereas every other ENGL 105 class was so chill abt grades. I got 5s on all of my AP exams, including Lang and Lit, and still struggled to figure out what she wanted from me.

Her class wasnt as easy as some ENGL 105 teachers but definitely not as hard as some others. If you do the work, youll get an A no doubt. Also, I was sick a lot during the semester I took her class, and she was always really understanding about work and would give adequate extensions. She cares about how you are doing as a person.

Kelli is a really knowledgeable and caring professor, and this class had very little work. I would highly recommend if you are looking for an easy A, which I was not, but it was a fun surprise. That being said, some of the class sessions are a little boring, and it almost feels like she's holding class just to hold class.

I actually learned a lot in Professor Holt's 'Writing in Law' class. She was always caring, her classes were engaging, and her grading was clear and fair. If you have any interest in the legal field, I'd take this over the regular ENGL 105.

Prof. Holt was wonderful and so caring for all her students. The class is very chill and she makes it lively with class discussions and activities. Gave us extensions on over half of the assignments without us even asking. Gave insightful and encouraging feedback on all assignments. I always looked forward to this class, can't recommend her enough!

even if your interest in law is small, take this class!! prof. holt is so kind and an easy professor. we were only graded on a few assignments and she gave us extensions on half of them. for the assignments that she did grade, she gave very insightful comments on how to improve for the next assignment. loved the environment of class and the prof!

Professor Holt is AWESOME. She makes the class so fun and is super easy. We only had two major assignments, and the work was interesting and fun. You'll have the chance to either work in groups or alone, whatever you prefer. Seriously consider taking her to fill in any of your focus capacities - she's the best!

She is one of the funniest professors, she talks about funny personal situations. She does care about her students and wants you to succeed. There are three main assignments, and the class is not difficult. If you like to talk, then this class is for you. The warm-up discussions took most of the class, which was fun.
She is the nicest professor I've ever had. She isn't a harsh grader, and even though this class was late in the evening, she made it engaging and fun. It's easy to get a good grade.

Actually the most amazing teacher, so caring and such a fun class. If you don't like talking, then don't take the class, but everyone in the class got so comfortable with each other, and it was just such a fun class, and I learned a lot. If you are into law, take this class. You get to learn so much about argumentation & just a great class overall!

Love Professor Holt! She is super sweet, and you can tell she's passionate about law. She is super available when you need to ask her questions and creates an engaging, fun classroom environment. If I could, I would 100% take her again. Enjoy her class!

Kelli is super nice and understanding. My poor grade is no fault but my own bc I submitted one of the three big projects without one of the components. Assignments: 3 projects plus in class writing- that's it. Do your work, participate, and go to class and you'll probably get an A. Fun class and she lets you out early a lot if it's a 75 min period

Super easy, and useful class. Ms. Holt is a very caring, chill, and knowledgable professor. Just put in a good amount of work and you will thrive in this class. Also just a great small class in contrast to huge lecture halls.

Dr. Holt is extremely knowledgeable about writing for the legal field and overall becoming the strongest writer you can be. The class is literally 9 assignments and the last unit is barely any work just a simple presentation. 25% of your grade is participation and you technically only get 3 absences, but she is super understanding!!
She is so awesome! Tons of time to do all the work in class, not a difficult grader at all, and interesting in class discussions

I love Prof. Holt's class! She is so kind and enthusiastic about the material! Class was so chill.  Only consisted of easy free writes during class, discussions, and 3 big projects.  Prof. Holt is a very chill grader.  Great class if you want to learn about podcasting or need a chill class.
Super caring and understanding professor! She really made ENGL105i a pleasure to take.

I LOVE Prof. Holt makes class very fun, and as long as you show up and try, you will do well in this class. Many non-pre-law students were in my section, and everyone seemed to have a great time in this course.

Dr. Holt is probably the best professor you can get for English 105. She is super accommodating and understands that students have other classes and responsibilities. Additionally, her lectures are usually very interesting, and the projects are often not that hard. She is also super kind and offers really good feedback for feeders

Professor Holt is really kind and allows students to do lots of in-class work. Your grade is based on a couple small feeder assignments and 2 large projects, along with a presentation. Showing up and participating is mandatory, but she makes class interesting! Really good class, take it w her.

really good prof, super nice and understanding. really helpful and gives good feedback. coursework isn't too difficult and you get enough time to complete it. good amount of reading which is expected given it's an English class.

Great class to take if you are interested in law but don't have much experience. You will learn how to read legal cases and brief them. Professor Holt is super kind and doesn't give too much work. Low stress class overall. Just go to class, participate, try your best to follow instructions on assignments, and you'll get an A.

I love Prof. SEG! She is so supportive and intelligent. If you are interested in creative non-fiction I can't recommend her enough. The readings are all posted in Canvas and they are short. She gives excellent feedback on assignments. A good balance of lectures, conversations, and writing. She is also open minded and easy to talk to.
I wouldn't take

Ms. E-G is by far one of the best prof's at UNC. She is extremely intelligent and engaging. All of the required readings are posted on Canvas, and you will need to participate in class discussions. People who have backgrounds in creative writing can coast by in this class with a confident A.

Love Prof EG!! She is super caring and respects all students. Like someone else said she doesn't post grades on canvas so it can be kinda hard to know where you stand. Other than that she has been one of my fav profs here so far. She has helped me become a better writer and her feedback is great.

I have mixed feelings. Prof EG is very nice and intelligent but class can be boring. The feedback given feels too opinionated. Grades are not posted on Canvas so you don't know what you have. Still, she is cool and supportive of students.

Stephanie was so kind and helped improve my writing a lot. ENGL 208 was a decent amount of reading and work, but I was never too worried about my grade in this class. She's the best possible resource for anyone interested in travel writing, and her lectures helped me see the world in new ways.

She's always welcoming of students' ideas during discussions. Always willing to answer questions on everything, from readings to life as a writer (and she's very transparent when it comes to that, too). You can get away with skipping a reading here & there but they're largely good, so if you have the time I'd recommend.
You will hate this class.

Readings for every class that can get lengthy, and you spend a lot of time discussing them. Just 3 papers due and a final project/paper plus another presentation. Gives very in-depth feedback and very willing to help if you go to office hours. Probably not the best class to take if you have no experience with creative nonfiction.

SEG cares a lot about the material, but I didn't learn as much as I wanted. Reading-heavy class time left little time for technical tips. ALL workshopping is done after submitting the final version (the version that affects your grade). If you already like creative nonfic, go for it. If not, keeping your head above water/learning can be a task.
Best professor I've ever had and one of the best and smartest people I've ever met. Amazing, amazing, amazing.

Stephanie is honestly one of the most important people I've ever encountered in my professional or creative endeavors. She gave (and still gives) me the most substantial, thought out, constructive feedback I've received as a writer and is SO transparent about the craft and the lifestyle of being a writer. She's such a wonderful professor & person.

You don't have to try that hard to do well in this class, but it's better if you do. You can get away without the readings, but they're helpful. EG is super caring and flexible to students' needs. She gives great & timely feedback but there's no grading criteria and I didn't have any grades until the semester end. Still loved this course so much.

Jessica was awesome! English105 is kind of an annoying class, but she made it fun. She's a very lenient grader and willing to adjust deadlines. Nice to talk to as well. I would recommend not buying the textbook (Tarheel Writing Guide) – we only used it a couple times.

Super nice and genuinely cares about you and how you do in the class. Three major projects, but only one real literary paper; the others are very fun and different. She is a lenient grader and is always available if you need help. Best English 105 professor I could have had, made an annoying requirement bearable.

As long as you do the work, this class is an easy A. My only criticism was that rubrics were often released late in the writing process, but it didn't have much of an impact because she is not a harsh grader anyway.

Jessica was a great 105 professor! Definitely passionate about what she does and cares for her students' wellbeing. As long as you put in effort for your projects and attend class you will get an A in this course.
Honestly she was great and with only three real big assignments I feel like the grading was lenient and the class was hardly time consuming. Jessica was an awesome first experience at UNC

She was super nice and kind the whole time. Honestly, she's so lenient with work and I feel like she was almost too nice. I wrote some pretty bad essays in this class but somehow managed to get an A on all of them. Her class isn't too much work and it's spaced out perfectly. She's also so chill and fun to talk to.
There a 3 projects and all of them were super simple and gave a lot of freedom. She has a lot of office hours and is very lenient on grading. She is an excellent choice to teach English 105.
Jessica is such an amazing Russian prof. I've had her twice for Russian and she's so nice and breaks down the material really well!

Professor Ginocchio was a delight. There is a lot of homework, but she was somewhat flexible about when you turned it in. Her lectures were good, her grading criteria clear, and her tests straightforward. RUSS 102 is challenging by nature, but Ginocchio makes it approachable for sure. I recommend her!

Whew, Russian 102 is difficult. Professor Ginocchio made it so much better though. Although it was still quite difficult, she cares so much about each and every student understanding every part of Russian. It's rare to see a professor care so deeply about the success and engraining a passion of a subject with students. She is an amazing professor.

Jessica is so great! Definitely take Russian with her if you can. She is super nice and also explained everything we learned super well. You'll be good taking Russian with literally any of the profs in the Russian department, but Jessica is amazing!

Genuinely one of the best teachers Ive had so far. She really cares about you walking away having learned something, and she tries really hard to make it fun. We got to visit the library and art museum to learn about their resources which was fun. She makes all her grades completion based. So if you do the work and put in effort youll get a 100.
Emily was great, she went deep into the topics, and because it is contract grading, you realy just do the assignments solid, show up to class and you should be fine.

She had a very clear grading criteria and would never grade you based on your writing skills. Rather, she cared a lot more about the effort you put into the class. She cared about coming to class, participating (does not have to be every class), and turning assignments on time. She was very flexible and understanding. Overall, the class was easy.

Very nice and relaxed teacher. You won't get away with doing nothing in the class, but as long as you put in some effort you'll do fine. She didn't grade individual assignments, but rather gave you a grade for a unit after it was completed based on the effort you put into the assignments for that unit.
Class was great, I felt like I actually learned a lot and her grading style made it a lot easier for me to develop as a writer without worrying about my grades.

She is a great teacher. She is very laid back, considerate, reasonable, and kind. She made the class very easy with her “contract grading.” All you have to do is show up, participate to some level, and put effort into your work, and you will get an A guaranteed. She has unlimited revisions; you get what you put in and don't need to put in much.
She had really clear grading criteria and would give an A if you followed them

Dr. Veggian is a really cool guy. He makes sure to know every student's name and always told us fun stories about his life. The only issue is he assigns way more work than any other ENGL 105 class. Even so, it was mostly useful, and I do feel I'm a better writer now. Also be prepared for lots of moments of silence as he loves to ponder.

Most entertaining class ever. Henry listens to his students extremely carefully, and takes careful measures so everyone is satisfied with due dates. In addition to being a great professor, he is a hilarious person. Personality is often lost in gen-ed classes, but NOT in his. He is an amazing storyteller and keeps students engaged with the content.

Henry is awesome. You will find yourself captivated by a long-winded fantastic story that initially seems completely irrelevant, but somehow at the end, every single time, he pulls the story to relate perfectly to what we are learning about in class. You will write in this class, but primarily only on topics that you are interested in.

While the daily lectures were just him going off on a tangent about his life or something he thinks is interesting, the class was generally okay, just kind of boring. Daily homework assignments and quite a bit of writing, but his feedback is good and mostly helpful.
Professor Veggian is an interesting guy but he loves to take up large amounts of class time with his tangents. He's an easy grader but assigns way more pointless work than other ENGL 105 classes.

Took feedback and added plenty of space between readings and films from big-name auteurs. The few texts he assigned were long but worthwhile for those interested in film adaptation theory. Two 5-page papers and weekly blog posts. Went on tangents, but always had great insight in setting up cultural and historical context.

He cares a lot about his students and makes a point to listen to them - changed homeworks or syllabus to fit what we thought was better, I've never met a professor like that. Definitely a lot of reading and movies to watch but most of them are fun. Does go on tangents and seems to get a little lost in his own head but he's funny.

I found him to be a very laid-back and thoughtful professor. Others say he is full of himself, but I think he simply likes to offer his perspective on the topics in the class. He's an interesting guy, and his discussions always held my attention. He's clearly very knowledgeable in his field, and he makes an effort to get to know his students.

Don't take his class for ENGL 105 unless you want to spend the entire semester hearing about how every other freshman in every other ENGL 105 class has loads less work than you. He goes on random political rants every class and is completely full of himself. Did not learn anything about writing except how to cite sources properly. Do not recommend.
You will learn how to write. Stuck up.

gives good feedback, is very helpful during office hours (as long as you have a VERY specific question in mind), and I feel like I learned a great deal from this class. Only downside is he makes the class atmosphere feel very tense so not a lot of people participated in in-class discussions.

Class was easy to get through. Ridiculous amount of reading though. Professor gave weird vibes. Talked about himself, tangents, etc. etc. You'll make it through, but be mind-numbingly bored and left with a weird aura that follows you around for a semester.
Dudes self centered

While this was my most intensive class of the semester, I feel as though I substantially developed my writing capabilities through his clear and strong feedback. The classroom environment was a bit tense, but he still cracked a few jokes and had some interesting lectures. There was a lot of writing, but it was worth it.

An ungodly amount of homework. Completely useless assignments. Henry has the aura of a pseudo-intellectual who definitely thinks he is the preeminent expert on every topic. He also loves to talk about his personal life for the entirety of the lecture. You should probably try to get a better professor to fulfill the ENGL105 requirement.

Dr. Veggian is a nice, smart guy. He clearly cares about what he's teaching. That said, he can be intimidating- he always seems like he's going to be mean, even though he isn't. His ENGL 105 class has so much writing. 3 units, 3 papers each (in my experience). He gives good feedback when he returns your papers, though.

Henry is a very intellectual person and perhaps one of the smartest people I have ever met. I think the topic of the class is what made his lectures boring but he tried to put as much emphasis on the historical figures as possible and how to "find the nail" (deeper analysis). He seems intimidating, but once you meet him he's a really nice guy.

Don't take this class if you don't like writing. There are a lot of papers in this class compared to other Engl105, but I really liked the topics and the assignments were buildable so u weren't doing a ton of work. He does tend to go on personal rants but he is very good at explaining what ur paper should be and how to do it. He is also a bit rude.

I took this class over a year ago, so I have had time to reflect. Henry is personally my least favorite of all of the professors I have had. I feel like much of our class was spent talking about his personal life, and we got an insane amount of work for an ENGL 105 course compared to other classes. I did well, but it could have been better taught.

This class wasn't very structured and consisted of open-ended discussions, so he went on tangents often. Grades included discussion forums due before every class, a midterm paper (many options, any topic), a speech (any topic), and a final paper (again many options, any topic). He was mostly a chill guy.

Dr. Rivard is kind and very knowledgeable in what she teaches. I had her for 114 as well, and in both classes, lectures were interactive and collaborative. I enjoyed the in-class activities and the conversations with her and other students. I thought the final project gradually built on everything we learned throughout the semester.

Dr. Rivard was very nice and clearly passionate about her work. Personally, I didn't enjoy the content of the class -- data science x english. I found her to be a bit of a harsh grader. The homework was around what I would expect for a 400 level class. Second half of the semester, the class builds on itself so don't skip or you'll fall behind.
Amazing professor and class! Interesting topics, clear grading criteria, and very understanding. If you are a data science student this class covers text analysis and Tableau.

Dr. Rivard's lectures were very well structured. Each week, we are assigned readings of about 10-30 pages. Dr. Rivard goes through a presentation during lecture which highlights the important takeaways. There are also weekly quizzes that are easy and meant to check for understanding. The class is well organized and due dates are generous.

A really fun class for game studies, even if you've never played a video game. Rivard's lectures were well structured, kept our attention, and felt relevant to the course. It sometimes seemed like she didn't know much about games themselves, but it was clear she made herself prepared to teach and understand the course. Very friendly and respectful.

If you're interested in game studies, the readings and quizzes are a breeze. They're assigned every week with about 10-30 pages each week. She provides ample resources for the midterm, final paper, and her lectures are amazing in helping you prepare for the quizzes. Was always flexible as well. Definitely take if you're interest is in games.

The way she structures her curriculum is very straight forward and easy to follow. Not a lot of work at all and still a really enjoyable, engaging class! Definitely would take another class with her. Midterm and final were all easy and helpful in digesting the info we learned through the lectures.
dr Rivard is amazing do take her classes
SO MUCH WORK! a lot of grading, long papers, short deadlines/turn around times, mandatory attendance.

Despite her unusual and somewhat outdated teaching methods, Dr. Frost is a kind, caring, and impactful professor. She shows a genuine desire to form connections with her students, and puts forth effort to get to know each one personally. I'm grateful to have had a class with her and would gladly take another.

guys, do not take class with her. she stresses everybody out by not putting in our grades on time, or fully putting them in wrong. she takes off for being late but won't have grades in until months after an assignment is due. it is so unfair how she operates.

I would avoid taking engl105 with her. You'll do well regardless, because this is a first-year course, but she assigns more work than the other profs do. She can be passive aggressive and isn't fast to grade things. She's fine, and I didn't hate the class, but I still wish I went with a diff prof.

I do not understand the harsh reviews on Dr. Frost. She has clear expectations and is super considerate when needing accommodations. This class is pretty paper heavy but that comes with the territory of an English class. As long as you come to class prepared, do the reading, and write to expectations it is not hard to achieve an A.

Professor Frost is not clear at all when making instructions, students easily get confused and are blamed even though it is not entirely their fault. Also, this class includes WAY MUCH MORE HOMEWORK compared to the average ENGL105/105i course. Though it may be an easy A, it is sometimes time-consuming and annoying.

Prof. Frost was nice, but could be passive aggressive at times and you never knew what would and wouldn't disgruntle her. The structure of canvas was weirdly complicated and expectations were often unclear. The class itself wasn't bad - not my favorite but not awful. Homework was not that difficult but there was a decent amount of it.

I took Professor Frost's ENGL 105I class for the humanities and it was very unorganized. This was her first year using Canvas so I would give her some grace, but it was confusing to decipher our assignments among other irrelevant things on her site. Each project had expectations with poor explanations, and rubrics were used loosely.
She can come off as passive-aggressive and WILL drop your grade as a way to get you to office hours, but if you apologize profusely, you and your grade will survive.

I have never held such animosity towards a teacher/professor like I have for Dr. Frost. She is passive aggressive and rude, and her rubric and instructions are often unclear. She made the class a lot harder than it needed to be. If I could go back in time and change one thing, I would never had taken ENGL 105/105I with Dr. Frost.

Dr. Frost made a required first-year class A LOT harder than it needed to be. No clear instructions/expectations for assignments. The main issue I had with ENG 105i was Frost's passive-aggressive attitude toward students. I will never forget the email she sent hours after the shooting trying (but failing) to assign asynchronous work.
While her class is easy, Prof Frost is not a good professor to have. She is very passive aggressive and is inconsistent with her grading. She often goes off in tangents during class which make

Dr.Frost is very understanding of students circumstances and will try her best to accommodate them. The course required a lot of reading, writing, and class participation was expected. Be ready to for presentations and interacting with the class. Overall it was fun and Dr.Frost has a bright personality and begins every class by playing a song.

Dr. Frost is a fantastic teacher with interesting material. She is very engaging, but class participation matters a lot. The more she knows you, the better the class will be. This class is a very similar dynamic to an AP Lit class.

The Leslie Frost PHD was an absolutely amazing Professor who cares for her students and the work the produce. Dr. Frost worked hard to ensure that every student had an equal opportunity to participate and even gave students time to catch up on their reading if they had not had the ability to do it.

It's been 2+ years since I've taken this class and I still remember how Frost went out of her way to personally insult me when she knew I was going through some stuff. She's very passive aggressive and picks on certain students for no reason at all. Takes forever to grade stuff and has extremely vague descriptions for assignments.

Discussion post, responses, quizzes, and a book club pitch that you do with a group. She takes forever to grade things, often does not know what she has written in her syllabus for due dates. Very rushed content, I was rarely ever to get in contact with her outside of class. Final was to write a three story thesis, when she never taught us that.

All of the work in this class is peer review, the only feedback ever provided is after projects are already done. Requires complete undivided attention at all times so you likely can't even work in the class.

Dr. Frost will help when you ask questions, but there was a lack of communication within the class. She sometimes believes she tells the class something but no one remembers her saying it which leads to confusion and everyone getting frustrated

Frost gives good feedback and is well-experienced, but I wouldn't take her again. Frost constantly confused her students with what was due and due dates. There was lack of communication and this made ENGL 105 much harder than it should be. I had friends that took this required course with other teachers with much less workload.

Dr. Evans is tad disorganized, and her feedback is somewhat limited. She clearly loves teaching and cares about helping students improve. This class did not vastly improve my writing ability, but it had decently interesting projects and easy grading. Bewarned: Dr. Frost like to hide assignments and requirements in Sakai. Check Sakai rigorously.

Dr. T is a great professor who is clearly very knowledgable in her field. This class was discussion-based but she does not require participation. She was great at guiding discussion but encouraging the class to lead it, and was always extremely encouraging. She is not a harsh grader but gives good feedback. Would highly recommend this course/prof!

This is a great class to take if you're a pre-med student looking for a relevant humanities class! Lots of reading, but the course materials and lectures are really interesting. Prof Thrailkill is super passionate about what she teaches and brings in some great guest speakers throughout the year. Would recommend!

I loved this course, the professor, and the TA's. If you are interested in health humanities or even need a FC this is a really good course to take. As long as you do everything you are supposed to and participate you will succeed in this class.
Dr. Thrailkill is great! The lectures are quite interesting but there is a lot of reading involved. I think it's a relatively easy A overall, as long as you do the work that's expected of you!

Not an ounce of clarity in anything. Reading was never announced; you often had a single day to read a book. Syllabus was all over the place; not one date was right. Nothing was graded on time; she was still changing grades days before the semester's end, and the rubric seemed to be just how she was feeling then. Your best will not be enough.

Dr. Thrailkill was a decent professor, but at times it was clear she wasn't prepared. She got lost during lectures and used students points to make her own. At times, she was unnecessarily rude to students. The class itself wasn't very difficult, just lots of reading. If you like health humanities this class is for you. Anna as a TA was great.

I feel like these ratings are sort of harsh. Prof. T was kind, brought in guest speakers to talk about our topics in class, and although sometimes the readings were not directly talked about in class we discussed them in recitation. Get ready to write if anything, but definitely a great class for those interested in health humanities.

One of the worst professors I've taken at UNC. Lectures are long and boring. Calls students out randomly and gets really passive aggressive when they don't answer correctly. Has no flexibility in extensions and doesn't have any opportunity to round.

Prof. Thrailkill isn't a bad professor, but this class style wasn't great. She has interesting content, but it gets lost in the lecture-style classroom. Overall, she's a caring professor, but the class wasn't that great.

she was an awful teacher for my triple I. she made way too many weird passive aggressive comments during her lecture, and even when it wasnt her turn to lecture. lectures were always the same, thought her lectures were more weird than they were insightful. the triple I itself was easier than the others, just prepare to be rage baited.

Professor Thrailkill is so knowledgable and discussions were very interesting and informative. All assignments had about the same weight, so nothing felt too stressful. One really big paper assignment, but she provided a decent amount of time to work on it. I would definitely take another English class with her. Interesting readings learned a lot.

This triple I was hilarious, they always had something funny to say. Although it was very much busy work that's kinda what a triple I is anyways. I would take Pandemics over some of the other classes, one midterm, one paper, one group assignment, and one final. if you put in effort you should be fine

The biggest problem with her lectures is that you honestly couldn't tell what you were supposed to be learning. Also, an odd amount of sexual undertones (or overtones) in roughly ~20% of what she says. She will cold-call on people to talk and then be annoyed when they have nothing to say. Overall weird dynamic with co-profs; felt like they clashed.

I really loved Professor Thrailkill's course! Super interesting topics and discussions. She graded fairly and provided good feedback. Grade is made up of a lot of assignments which gives you a lot of chances to make up your grade. The class could be disorganized at times, but overall super enjoyable!

Lectures were extremely unorganized. Lots of readings. She thought she was hilarious, but was really just making inappropriate jokes (ex: "I would want him to carry me"). She was always talking over the other professors. Hated on the class for being young and living in a progressive world. Constantly got dates/facts wrong

Lots of readings just for them to be recapped all of lecture. Would make horny comments about "young fine authors" or even actors in videos we had to watch. Yap-fest could never tell what was important. Class caught strays because "were young" and have it easy. Not the worst IDST to take just beware of strange professor.

She was not a very nice person and was a bit snobby. In class she misspoke and then called people out in front of the entire class for not understanding her directions after she said the wrong thing. Her attitude towards students made it difficult to enjoy the class and to feel confident about participating or asking questions.

Consists of 2 reading responses, weekly recitation quizzes on the readings (usually around 5 questions), and the illness narrative project + honors supplement for those seeking honors credit. 
Very understanding towards the end of the semester when my peers had concerns about their grades and gave a lot of extra credit points to help out!

Thrailkill's lectures had nothing to do with the texts we read, making either the readings feel pointless or her lectures useless. Sensitive topics such as abortion and racial discrimination were common themes, and while important, she handled them without delicacy or sensitivity. Very condescending and learned nothing new.

I liked Professor Thrailkill and she was very helpful to me during office hours. He lectures were very interesting and she is extremely passionate about med anth. I enjoyed the actual books that we read in class, but the articles assigned before each class could get daunting, especially because there were pop quizzes based on niche reading topics.
She's the best! Very clear grading criteria for the two major assignments. Classes were seminar style but very low pressure. Would def recommend!

Prof GR is one of the most caring and helpful professors at UNC. Her class gives you real-world skills. You'll leave with a resume, cover letter, and interview prep. She's accessible outside class and caring. Not as easy as other ENGL105s, there's HW due every class, but it's worth it if you truly want to improve. Even non-BUSI students, take it!

Loved ENGL 278 with Professor GR! Classes were largely discussion based with small bits of lecture to introduce authors, Irish history, and context for whatever work we were discussing. Lots of readings but they're fun and engaging. Prof. GR is super kind and really passionate about the course and material.

I missed our scheduled appointment once and Professor GR invited me to her house for dinner. Hands down one of the best educators at UNC. She communicates her criteria so clearly, taught us skills useful beyond the classroom, cared that we learned something meaningful, and was ALWAYS available.

PRGR was great! The class itself is very interesting, and the readings are rarely boring or slow. Lectures are free flowing with occasional small group discussions, and PRGR was very good at giving us necessary background info or clearing up any confusion. 1 paper, 1 media project, 1 5 minute presentation. She gives good feedback on assignments

Loved Pr GR! Everything I learned in this class was extremely useful for future use in business. Strong effort is required to get a good grade, sometimes minor details like to-be verbs can hit your grade hard. I would definitely recommend taking this class but it will require effort to receive an A so don't take if you want an easy English course.

I loved Pr GR! She is always available to students and genuinely wants us to succeed. I thought all assignments were useful (and easy enough if you follow the rubrics). Group projects are the biggest challenge because you share 20% of your final grade with a random group and if assigned an unmotivated group this requires a lot of out of class work.

Professor GR for ENGL 105i is the toughest by far. She does not round up to an A when I have a 93.56, and I believe relies too heavily on peer-to-peer feedback, so if you get crappy classmates, you won't have good feedback and your grade will suffer. She is also obsessed with the to-be verb, but never fully explains what it is nor why its bad.

Professor GR (as she is known to her students) has to be one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Irish lit was an awesome class that she taught very well. As long as you listen to the lectures, read the readings, and go to class you will do just fine. She was very kind when I needed extensions here and there and cares about her students.

I loved Professor GR! I would recommend taking her Business English class. I genuinely learned so much and all of the work was actually useful (ex: we made our resume, had a mock interview, and made cover letters for ourselves). Professor GR is so kind and caring and if you get the chance to take her class, you should do it!

I can't recommend Professor GR enough. She gave feedback on my resume that I attribute to landing my internship. Her dedication to her students is evident and was uncommon among my other professors. She assigns some kind of hw every class but it typically takes 30 mins. If ur a busi major TAKE THIS so much interview prep & resume/cover letter help

Absolutely love Professor GR. She is so kind and understanding, and she makes an effort to foster genuine relationships with her students. I am not a history person, but she made Irish history very digestible and I thoroughly enjoyed ENGL 278 with her. If you're looking for an easy but interesting gen-ed, look no further.

Professor GR is a great professor. She's caring and understanding of issues you have outside of class. That being said more than half of her class is structured with group projects, and if you get a bad group you are completely screwed. If you take engl105i with her dont expect to coast through it and do nothing like the other eng105 classes

Dr. GR is a really nice person, and brought us donuts on the final exam! She's genuinely so sweet. It's not hard to get an A or A-, but it wasn't as easy as I expected. There's a lot of reading and you really need to analyze the stories because you don't know what will be asked during exams. The final exam was pretty specific. Recommend though!
super easy class, readings for homework and discussions in class. one project, one paper, a midterm, and a final. teacher is super nice

Prof GR has been my favorite prof so far at UNC. I was the only non English major in a class of 9 and I felt like I was completely on par with everyone else. The class just involved coming to class having read the works, posting your observations on the forum, and analyzing them in the following class. Large focus on main themes and analysis skills

Professor GR is the best ever! She cares so much about her students and is so empathetic. The coursework is so helpful and applicable to the real world. She is always willing to meet with you outside of class and her input is so helpful. I could not recommend this class enough, but it is a lot of work.

Had GR for 105i: Writing in Business, honestly the best professor I've had here. Super helpful on the assignments and available all the time outside of class. The class is broken up into 3 units with the last two being group projects. The class is not easy by any stretch but it teaches a lot of practical things like interviewing and presenting.

She is honestly the best professor I've had at UNC. She obviously cares about her class and students, and clearly loves the material and teaching. She is amazing, if you are struggling at all both in and outside of class she is incredibly open to helping. Would absolutely recommend taking her class if you can.

i took irish lit. possibly the sweetest prof ive ever had here. class goes by fast bc the discussions are so riveting. she is just a lovely human & creates a v comfortable atmosphere for discussion. participation is needed, but its so easy (esp having anxiety) bc she is so encouraging and open. i rly cant get over how great she & her class was.

Dr. Cohen is a lovely person and will help you succeed in life in any way that he can. That does not make him a good English teacher. I could not imagine an English class being more boring. He basically spoonfed us all of the ideas we had to write and then told us to put it nicely. I don't think that the way he taught us to write was good writing.

I could not recommend Professor Cohen enough! He is very passionate about his studies, and it shows through the excitement he brings to each class. In this course, we read Winnie-the-Pooh and wrote our own adaptations in screenwriting format. We also watched films. He is very caring and makes an effort to get to know his students. Take his course!
Wasn't very kind or understanding if he didn't like you. The class itself wasn't too hard but there were short quizzes and reading everyday. Not difficult, but wouldn't take him again.

Cohen was one of my favorite professors I've had! He is obviously passionate about what he does, and he showed a genuine interest in his students' success and career aspirations. He gave great feedback on all of my work and helped me to improve my writing ability. Take this class! It's appropriately challenging and creatively fulfilling.

Cohen was one of my favorite professors I've had at UNC! His passionate for the content he teaches is obvious, and he showed a genuine investment in his student's success and futures. ENGL381 was appropriately challenging, and I do believe I have become a better writer thanks to Cohen's feedback. Take a class with him if you can!
