Dr Cohen provides a lot more work compared to other ENGL 105 classes. It's nothing too difficult, but it is very time consuming compared to other 105 classes. He gives good feedback and pushes for your personal improvement, however I'm confused by all the talk of “compassion” from the other ratings. He is disingenuous at times and can be rude.

Professor Cohen is a very sweet and interesting person, but he is also a strict grader. He will push you to improve your writing and gives unique opportunities outside of class for enrichment as well as for extra credit.

Cohen will use kindness to lure you in, and then act abusive. He is nice from an arms length. It's a façade. He will use the personal things he learns about you to attack you and put you inappropriate situations. I have never written a review on rate my prof before, but people need to know not to get close to him. Do not trust him.

Though the workload felt high at times, this was one of the most unique English classes I've taken. I got to use software and experience things on campus that I wouldn't have otherwise. I'm not a fan of the Tar Heel Writing Guide being a mandatory purchase though. We only used it for a couple days at the start of the course, and then never again.

Marc thinks in terms of set grading criteria (mostly focused on attendance + participation) and follows those to the tee. 

This is good insofar as it is transparent, and it also helps students who may be weak at writing, but I got the sense the class isn't really about the quality of your WRITING at all, it's about doing what he likes.

Professor Cohen is amazing! Each day, he conversed with every student. In this course, we went to a rock concert, toured the North Carolina Botanical Garden, and met a family of influencers. There is quite a bit of work outside of class; however, it mainly consists of notes. He can be a harsh grader at times; however, his reasoning is always clear.

Dr. Cohen's class is very unusual compared to other 105 eng classes, and there is sm homework and unnecessary complicated projects. He is caring, however. Also gives feedback but is a tough grader and it can be hard to understand what he wants on assignments. Beware of the amount of references you will do.
Dr. Cohen is a lovely man and takes a real interest in his students and their abilities. He wants you to get better and gives clear feedback and a lot of it. Lots of writing but very manageable.

Took online during Summer II. Highly recommend listening to all the audiobooks ahead of time instead of trying to read daily. Lesson videos (2x speed) help spark ideas for writing. Discussions, quizzes, and videos are easier than they look. Papers are a lot of work, and he grades tough, but his feedback is detailed and helpful. Worth taking.

Prof. Cohen is genuinely my favorite prof! His class is perfect for anyone who loves films and storytelling, and who is passionate about learning! He's incredibly caring and always accommodating to everyone's needs. There are no exams, a fun presentation, 3 major papers, + watching and appreciating movie clips. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

Don't take this class if you're looking for a light load for an English 105 class. This class wasn't necessarily hard, but it took up lots of time because we did have homework each night. Overall professor was nice and willing to work and help you in the class, but had way more work than the other English 105 classes.

Professor Cohen is one the best teachers I've ever had at UNC. Very nice and approachable, and gives lots of constructive feedback on papers. I really learned a lot in this class. Take ENGL129 with him if you can!
One of my favorite professors at UNC! Truly cares about his students and goes out of his way to support us. Highly recommend taking his class

Excellent professor who lectures with enthusiasm and genuinely cares about his students. The group projects he assigned were interesting and creative. I found the course load to be very reasonable and his grading straightforward.

Prof. Cohen is probably one of the best professors I have had. He truly cares for the success of his students and is even interested in keeping up with you after the class. He also gives extremely detailed feedback. You can tell how much effort he puts into making this class more interactive and memorable with the wide range of interesting topics.

Professor GR is genuinely one of the kindest and most passionate professors I've had. She makes learning about Irish history incredibly interesting and engaging, even for students not in the humanities. Plus, she makes amazing soda bread. Definitely take this class!

LOVED this prof and class!! I had never read any Virginia Woolf before and I ended up having so much fun with this class. Prof GR is so kind, intelligent, and encouraging. She is exactly what a great teacher should be. I will defend her to the ends of the earth. Take her- coming from a non-english major/minor.

Professor GR was great, all the assignments were super helpful, and she is very accessible outside of class and willing to help in any way. I would take this over regular 105 because the assignments are so helpful and prepare you for the future. Great Professor, take her she cares about her students.
Really loved Prof GR's class - one of the best English teachers I have ever had.

This is the second class I've taken with Professor GR and both classes were so worth it! The organization of the class — you come to class having read the day's reading and then discuss it throughout the class period in a low-stakes discussion — made preparation and participation easy. If you have the opportunity, take a class with her!!

Great professor and great class. Taught a lot of good life skills that are very applicable, even if you're not in business. a variety of assignments: resume, cover letter, interview, business proposal, shark tank. if you pay attention in class and follow her very clear directions, you will get a good grade.

I love Prof. GR! She made this class super accessible yet still intellectually stimulating. It honestly felt like a book club -- we did the assigned reading, came in, and talked about what we read. I understood so much more of the readings because of this. Learned a lot and enjoyed it! Would take again!

She is very fair, caring, and teaches very well. You can tell she cares about the lessons you take from her class into your future. If you put in honest work, you are rewarded and helped through all of it. I HIGHLY recommend!

Professor GR is an excellent professor. I learned so much from this class and it strengthened my love of Ireland. There was a new reading every class period but the readings were enjoyable and the discussions were fulfilling. There were few assignments (an essay, a video project, and exams), but they were all so exciting to create/study for.

Prof GR is probably my favorite prof I've had so far. This class was never boring. Class time was discussion-based, mostly as a class, occasionally in small groups. Grades were 20% each for participation, midterm (just one), a paper, a media assignment, and the final. All were very doable and she encourages students to ask for help. Great class.

Professor Gualtieri-Reed is an inspiring teacher who brings out the best in her students. She clearly cares about helping her students and will help you if you ask. I learned a great deal and highly recommend this class.

Great professor and very caring. The class is tough and is very demanding however, for business majors it is one of the most helpful classes you can take your freshman year. She helps create resumes, cover letters, and more in Kenan-Flagler's format.

Prof GR is incredible. As someone who had previously participated in business pitch competitions, upon taking her class, I realized that I had so much I could improve. She also helped us create resumes and cover letters that are absolutely amazing. You will get 10x for whatever you put into the class. I'd take her class again! Read the rubrics!!!

I took this course over the summer online. Professor Gualtieri-Reed is a kind and caring professor. This is a (reading-heavy course) with 2 to 6 maximum discussion forums weekly. Within weekly lectures, attendance and participation is required. I would definitely take another course by this professor! This is a good choice for a summer course!

She is amazing. I took her Irish Literature course over the summer and loved it. Lots of reading, but she enjoys teaching this content and is great at making it interesting because of her passion. Do the readings and go to class and you should do well. Attendance is important, but if you don't want to talk you can pass. A somewhat easy course.
Awesome lecturer. Very clear with students and caring in class. Great course to get LA credit.

GR is awesome! She is incredibly responsive to emails and loves forming a good relationship with her students. She typically assigns a small assignment each day that you complete in groups-- very kind, such a fun and practical class!

Genuinely one of the best classes I have taken here at UNC. Professor Gualtieri-Reed is really knowledgeable. Participation does matter for your grade, but it makes the class better when everyone participates. Readings were really interesting - mixture of poems and short stories. Your grade is made of a few things, but the rubrics are clear.

Pr. GR is FANTASTIC. This is my second class with her and I can't recommend her enough. She is very clear about what she expects, and is fabulous at teaching how to write precisely. I learned so much & loved this class. She makes students her priority and is always willing to make time in her schedule to chat. She is also a great Resume editor

PLEASE TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. She's an amazing professor and wants everyone to succeed in the class. All assignments are weighted the same and she's a lenient grader. Exams are not hard and if you don't do  a reading it's okay to look up a summary.

Amazing professor. One of the most passionate, fun, and lovable teachers in the english department. If you want to learn and are interested you will do well. Brilliant lectures and super detailed feedback for essays and quizzes, will push you to become better writer and reader. 10/10 recommend any class with Dore

Extremely intelligent and makes interesting connections from our readings. Class discussions were engaging. Some people got by without reading the books, but I'd recommend doing them. I'm a slow reader, and some of audiobooks were 15 hours, so keeping up was hard with quick turnarounds. Need to take quality annotations, books are used in exams

I took this class because Professor Dore spoke to my class the previous semester, and I found her to be an inspiring and engaging lecturer. The class was difficult but so rewarding, and as everything came together towards the end of the semester, I became convinced she is a genius. I highly recommend taking one of her classes and hope to again.

Unless you're passionate about the South, useless class. Dore had us read "The Sound and the Fury." Don't read the book last minute, and make good annotations in the book. Buy it, don't rent. Essay grading was a bit harsh, but you'll be fine if you know the book. Other readings don't matter. She can appear condescending and cold calls.

Everyone had pretty low grades until Assignment 2/3, and then they dropped our exam grade. It's a dreadful class and I absolutely hated it BUT most people ended up with an A in the end so it wasn't that awful.
The Triple-I class has four assignments, and Dr. Dore's assignment is very specific and will most likely be the reason you struggle to get an A. Not the worst Triple-I, but definitely not the best.

This class was dreadful. I'd rather do anything than read an incomprehensible book, get cold-called, and deal with her harsh attitude. She assigns ridiculous readings and expects near Shakespeare essays for a freshman class. No idea how I got an A, but it felt like nails on a chalkboard all semester. Brundage a chiller tho

I didn't think the class was hard at all overall, as long as you studied before the tests you had a good chance at making an A regardless of whether you read the material. However, I really didn't appreciate her attitude towards students. While trying to be funny, she was sometimes passive aggressive and wasn't afraid to cold call.

Sorry, but Prof Dore and this class was awful. I didn't think she was always respectful to students, and the exam she gave was SO hard. I think the average was a low C. The book she taught was hard (coming from an ENGL major). Graded harshly with a very vague rubric. By the grace of God, I got an A but it was looking like a B- for a long time.

Maybe it's because I had the easy TA but I really liked Dore, her lectures were super interesting. If you aren't a fan I highly recommend going to her office hours because she has great one-on-one advice and she's open to criticism of her analysis as long as you have good evidence to back it up. Buy the books so you can highlight for the exam!

Her lectures were not as unfair as people on here are stating. If you read the reading, which was a more complicated reading, you are fine on the exam. Her rubric was vague but you can literally ask her about anything in office hours or class. Your given the layout of the exam before hand. Read the book assigned/try and you'll be fine!

She is an incredible professor and truly cares for all her students. She is willing to take the time to give criticism and help with any work throughout the semester. She makes the class enjoyable and fun and values each student's opinions. 10/10,  take a class with her.

This triple-I isn't even a class next year, but she was truly one of the least enjoyable professors in this class. She was condescending, did not appreciate answers different from what she viewed as right, and cold-called. Allowed no technology and her lecturing was boring for a 1 hr 15 min course. Vague study guides/rubrics.
She is a TOUGH grader and doesn't give very clear rubrics which is annoying af. She is funny, but be prepared for Cold calling.

While I loved Dr. Dore's lectures and found her super funny, her expectations of students often felt unreasonable. Her exam was unnecessarily challenging, and the directions were unclear. I felt like many of her lectures focused on specific interpretations of literature, and she was not very receptive to students who disagreed.
Terrible, worst professor I have ever experienced in my academic career. Unreasonable and class is simply based on luck of your TA and she will not give you any help. Do not take absolutely horrible.

Her assigned readings were hard, but I enjoyed them. However, her interpretations felt extreme and far-fetched. She's not very receptive to new ideas in class and will tear apart your logic. She cold-calls. She gives midterms with WAY too little time to complete it and I have yet to meet someone with a good midterm grade from her section.

This class was taken for one of my first-year requirements. The professor is great. She is passionate about English and the topics she discusses, so it is a lot if you're taking it just for a requirement, especially as a first year. She has a great attitude and amazing personality, but grades harshly.

Dr. Dore is awesome. This class is an awesome create to take if you're a musician and/or songwriter looking to get feedback on your work. She was a little unorganized at times, but it was all part of the fun. Dr. Dore is geninely enthusiastic about the songs her students write, and she gives good feedback as an experienced songwriter and musician.

Dore really is intelligent, but I often find myself leaving class dissatisfied. For every text, and every subsequent assignment, I feel Dore enters with an air about her own opinion. Her readings are always categorically "correct," and when students deviate they are met with a bad grade. I understand why some like her though, she's just not for me.

Dr. Telegen is a very funny and quirky guy who makes it easy to enjoy his class. The workload is pretty light and it is very easy to do well. The final project is pretty fun since it's based on our topic of choice. The class is sometimes a little scrambled, but it's fun regardless.

Really great professor! The class itself is pretty easy if you submit the work (he allows for infinite revisions on assignments). As a professor, he did well to make sure the class engaged in meaningful conversation. Take him if you like a discussion-based class. Definitely recommend for ENGL105 credit.

He is very passionate about teaching; however, his methods are not for everyone. He is very dramatic and at times a bit disorganized. He has a lot of tics that might annoy some people. While his train of thought is often heading to an insightful and interesting place, it sometimes gets lost on the way there.  Super easy grader.
Had so much fun this semester!
Loved his class!

Joe was an amazing professor and I would love to take his class again. You can tell he loves rhetorical analysis. He does bring up the TV show Succession quite a bit, as well as Kanye West, Taylor Swift, and Elon Musk. He is very accessible outside of class time, and he makes sure you know where and how to find him.
If you aren't a super confident writer but need ENG 105 credit, Joe is perfect. Genuinely cares about everybody in class and lets you revise any assignment unlimited times.

By far the easiest A I got all semester. He goes on a lot of tangents, but I tended to find them pretty interesting. If you're an English major or particularly care about learning about the field, maybe choose a different professor, since there were some days we straight up just watched TV shows in class that vaguely related to course content

Joe is really nice, and very accessible outside of class if you need help. This class is great if you want an easy A and enjoy talking about pop culture. He does go on a lot of tangents and I didn't really leave the class feeling like I'd learned much about writing though.

Joe is a nice guy, but rambles about unrelated stuff for most of class and frequently goes off track so I didn't get much out of his lectures. He is very friendly and tries to connect to students, but goes over the top sometimes. Almost all in-class work is group work, but rarely is it productive. He is a lenient grader and is very accessible.
Take him! I would 100% take him again. Hoping to have another class with him in the future.
Professor Telegen (Joe) was a great 105 instructor and made the course super easy!

Honestly loved Joe.  He is a very easier grader but lowk bipolar.  He rambles in class but you don't have to listen.  Ended with a 100 in the class.  You can submit assignments as many times as you want.
Really recommend to anyone. Great professor.
Good GPA booster. Very caring and is always there to help you. Do the work and you will have a good grade.
Easiest teacher ever. Very accessible outside of the classroom. Overall, an easy A

This professor is quite odd. If you want an easy 100 I would recommend but beware because he goes on random tangents and you will not learn anything about English. He is obsessed with Succession and he makes us watch it both in class and for homework. Have fun!

Joe is probably one of the EASIEST Engl105 teachers you'll find. If you want an easy A take this class cause there are unlimited revisions on everything. If you actually want to learn something, then that's debatable cause he tends to go on a tangent often. Extremely accessible outside of class and very accomodating however.
A huge waste of time. Joe doesn't give a lot of clear instructions on homework so you may need to revise a couple of times before getting an A. But overall an easy class.

Professor Curtain is incredibly kind and knowledgeable! We only read 4-5 books the entire semester with most days only requiring movies. Your grade is mostly participation, but I only raised my hand once per class and it all worked out. There is a midterm/final where you have to know quotes from the works, so don't skip them!

Dr. Curtain is awesome! I really enjoyed his Sci-Fi/Utopia class—the entire course was just watching movies or reading books and discussing them in class. Dr. Curtain does a great job facilitating those discussions and challenging us to think deeply in a respectful manner. Attendance is required, but you shouldn't skip even if it wasn't!
Professor Curtain is a good instructor and I really liked his class. Participation matters a lot for his class and he will sometimes cold call if no one volunteers to talk

You will not regret taking this course. He knows what he is talking about and makes class very engaging. Often makes you think outside of the box and dive deeper into hidden meanings of films. Make sure to participate, actually watch the films and memorize the facts he asks of the movies. Not being to check grades was no stress honestly.

Loved this class. Very discussion-based class, that's why participation and attendance matters. Usually a smaller class so he'll notice if you're not in class for a few days. Lots of reading but exams are easy and grading is lax. I enjoyed his class tho! Easy A if you're okay with reading and speaking up at least once a class.

I LOVED THIS CLASS. It was SO interesting, and I would recommend it to basically everyone. If classroom participation really stresses you out, you might find this class to be scary, but he is so interesting to listen to and the seminar is very good.

I audited this class, so grain of salt, but Dr. Curtain is kind and extremely knowledgeable about horror movies. He isn't afraid to call on people out of the blue and challenge their answers, but he's also funny and encourages discussion. Really enjoyed this class.
Very weird about missing assignments. Definitely insecure about teaching a horror class haha.
Really chill class. Just watch movies and talk about stuff. Curtain is a chill dude who knows everything anyone ever needs to do about horror in general. Great dude with a great personality.

Genuinely a great class. Professor Curtain really makes you think about the films you watch, I have a whole new perspective of sci-fi film now. All you do is talk about the films/books in class, make sure to watch/read everything because he will cold call. All films except 2 books during the whole semester but easy reads. 1 midterm and 1 final.

Professor Curtain is very good at what he teaches and is good at getting you to think more deeply about you ideas on the material. You are graded on participation in class, a midterm, and final but they are fairly straightforward if you keep up with the films needed for class.

This is a great class! I was worried throughout the semester as your final grade consists of participation, one midterm, and a final and you never know your grade for any of them. The material is interesting and attendance is never taken. Ended up with an A.

Overall, I enjoyed this course. It's pretty much entirely discussion based where you talk about films and books. Participation is really important, and you're expected to be active in discussions. My only issues is his viewpoint can be narrow at times and grading is very unclear (there's no canvas site). Easy filler course if you need one.

Hilarious guy and so nice. Our in class convos were thought provoking and deep. There's a midterm and final as our only graded assignments (they're straight up memorization). Homework is watching movies and reading 3 books that we discuss in class. Exams ask for titles, director, and release year of each work we cover. Awesome class and easy A.

We had two assignments and one final that was a breeze. Grades weren't posted until after finals though, which was frustrating. He also refused to acknowledge points of view that contradicted his own, which was rather disappointing, because I wanted to engage in the material. After I gave up trying, the class was fine.

Professor Curtain was very relaxed, so there weren't many assignments or feedback in general which was stressful at times. I ended with an A in the class but got no feedback whatsoever throughout the semester. This was a great class though, your grade is based mostly on participation in class discussion.

Professor Curtain is fun, if not a little unstructured. This class had a 1/2 page syllabus and about 10 books to read. Attendance was not mandatory, but he would assign items in class for the following week and not post on Canvas or notify students, so you had to keep your head on a swivel! His classes were fun, but he would cold call sometimes.

Midway the semester, as we were discussing a film by James Cameron, I pointed out the racial stereotypes. As I did this, I also voiced how I could not finish the movie due to the movies racist nature. Professor Curtain stated that my viewpoint, as a POC woman, was incorrect. He also said that I needed to learn how to be uncomfortable.

As long as you watched the movie before the class and were prepared to talk, this class was a breeze. The only assignments we had were a midterm and final, and a final project sequence, which were all very easy. If you do the work, you pretty much get an A. Good easy filler class.
She is a super sweet professor who is always willing to help! She is easy to reach outside of class and keeps class engaging and entertaining.

One of the easiest classes I've taken. She focuses on plants which is different from other ENGL 105 classes, but there's lots of room to participate and engage with the content. She isn't a tough grader at all as long as you put effort in, and you get to do revisions to get a 100. To top it off she's the coolest professor at this school.
Her Engl105 is focused around environmental studies, which usually bores me to death, but she kept things interesting. If you're a competent writer you'll be absolutely fine with her.

Krysten was awesome. Her class is environmentally focused, which is not usually something I would enjoy focusing on, but she ran it so well that I ended up liking it a lot. She encourages discussions/debate in class (especially materialism vs. idealism). If you are a reasonably strong writer, you will have zero issues and appreciate the discussions

She was great, very approachable, an excellent choice for ENGL105. The class will be environmentally focused, even if you're taking a specific concentration of the class like humanities. I found her grading to be very lenient, everything I turned in was an easy A.

Krysten is such a unique and interesting professor to have. She really just cares about you becoming a better writer, without making you jump through hoops. She is very clear on what she is looking for and will let you resubmit papers for a regrade if you are not happy. I think most people in this class will end with an A.

I loved Krysten and I'm not even an English person in general. She's funny, I will say her classes are pretty much lectures but they're very engaging and she's super understanding about missing class.

She is great. She's super down-to-earth, gives no tests, and pretty much grades all projections/essays on completion(I ended with a 100.0), as long as you put effort and follow her instructions. She focuses a lot on plants from various perspectives to teach class, so if you find that boring, she may not be for you, but definitely extremely easy A.
Krysten is great, really funny and passionate about plants. Super chill with grading, and I'm really grateful she was my ENGL 105 professor!!

Given that you put effort into assignments, it is very likely that you will end the class with a 100. This is one of the best professors you can take for ENGL105, and she is very caring to her students. There is an attendance/participation grade, but she is very lenient with grading it.

I loved this class, and the teacher was very passionate, making each class interesting! There was a lot of writing, but she graded easily and helped whenever needed. I love her, she is hilarious, definitely take her class!

She is literally amazing! She is super into plants and coloniality so be prepared to talk about that for the entire class. She is very kind with her grading and attendance policy as well. I was really glad to have her as my ENGL105 teacher!
Easy A, just go to class and write the papers and you'll get a 100, definitely sounds easier than what I've heard from friends about other professors.
Easiest A ever. She is also very kind and understanding. She gets that we're just there to fulfill the requirement. I didn't go to half the classes... She is really cool definitely take this class!
She's great, easy A for 105
She is a really nice professor, and grades the assignments very easily. I've only not gotten a 100 0nce.

Great teacher. Gives in depth feedback and cares about your success. There are a lot of readings but she doesn't expect you to comprehend all of them in depth. Moderately easy assignments and opportunities for regrade and revisions on papers.

Krysten is a great english teacher. You have 3 main units; the first two are essays and the final one was a group podcast. As long as you revise your work and keep improving, you will get an A in this class. Definitely try to take it

Krysten is such a chill professor that balances her class better than I've seen any other professor thus far. I came out of her class feeling like I learned a lot but also never felt overwhelmed. Do whatever you can to take this class, you will not regret it.

Prof Voelkner has been my favorite instructor thus far at UNC. Her course material is SO engaging and interesting. She is super chill and I always looked forward to attending her class. She is also super accessible outside of class and understanding of personal conflicts. Take her for 105 if you have the chance!

I really don't have anything against Prof Seifert, just the class in general. It seems like a waste when you've taken advanced English classes in high school. The class is overall pretty easy and definitely doable on top of more difficult classes. Most of the grading is just completion, and you get some feedback. A bunch of readings.

Easiest A ever gotten. Prof Seifert is accessible outside class, understanding of situations and gave extentions whenever. Downside is they read off slides which makes class long and boring. Be prepared to learn nothing but hey its a free A

The class wasn't always super interesting, but it genuinely helped me with writing and research skills. Professor Seifert is perfectly nice as long as you're doing what you're supposed to be. Easy grader, I got a 100 on every assignment. Lectures were sometimes a slog to get through but it was fine for an introductory course. No tests either.

I think the class is really easy, and it's not hard to get good grades if you actually try. Yes, sometimes we have to do unnecessary busywork, but Professor Seifert is pretty accommodating for most things and is pretty nice.

Super easy A for me. Just do what you're supposed to and you'll be fine. Class was mostly developing a research project over a semester, which wasn't too stressful, and the grading wasn't too tough either.

Celeste is a good teacher. She was very kind to me throughout the semester and tried to make lectures very interesting. Although if you look at the learning outcome from engl 105 then she is not the one. She is easy grader but you wont learn anything in this class.
Can come off as rude sometimes whether they intend to or not. Not much homework though. Not much they can do though its an english class

Easy class but professor is incredibly rude and condescending. Honestly treats students like they are in middle school. She is an easy grader but if you are looking for a respectful and mature professor I do not recommend. Also coming to class was the biggest waste of time, she would take 20-30 minutes on an activity that should take 5.

Don't take this class! They grade easy with a lot of papers, but if you want a teacher that will be at least a little bit respectful this is not for you. Celeste is rude and treats us like children. at points they were very rude when answering a simple question. I never wanted to participate in this class because of how discouraged I felt.

English 105 with Prof Seifert is exactly what it should be. She is really sweet and understanding. She grades based on specific criteria and is helpful if you need guidance. I would totally recommend her!!

Engl 105 is a boring class but Seifert seemed to care about making it somewhat engaging for her students. The assignments take very little time and the grading is extremely lenient. Class is incredibly boring but I think that has to do with Engl 105, not the professor. She did get frusturated at times when people asked questions.

Classes are extremely boring and unnecessarily drawn out. Powerpoints each time where every line is read verbatim. Prof. Seifert is fine-- she usually is willing to help but sometimes she goes off on students when they ask too many questions

Professor Seifert has by far been my least favorite professor at UNC. ENGL105 is meant to be any easy class for freshmen to take and get through but Seifert makes the class unnecessarily complicated. She is unbelievably condescending and rude to her students. For a grad student, she has a very high ego.
I took the writing in Business class online over the summer. We only met online once a week. She was really nice and the class was generally pretty easy

ENGL 303 with Dr. P is a very enriching class. She pulls in a lot of industry concepts and incorporates them into relevant and fun projects. Occasionally can grade a little harshly, but she gives good feedback and works with you to improve your drafts. Definitely take this class if you can.

She is really nice and gives tons of examples for every assignment. Instructions are clear which makes it okay that there is a fair amount of work. If you want to get an A, you have to do the work. She is a fair grader.

Dr. Pappoe was good but not my favorite professor I had ever taken. I felt like some of the assignments were not really relevant to a first-year writing class and her grading was quite easy. It was hard to get a perfect score on any major assignment but she also didn't really grade below a B.

I would definitely recommend for Freshmen to take ENGL 105 Writing in Business if they can. Dr. Pappoe is very compassionate and grades quickly and fairly. As long as you show up and turn in the projects on time you will do well in this class
if u have to take engl 105 take english in business with her.

Dr Pappoe provided relevant assignments to Business and helped prepare you for careers in business. However her grading requirements are super vague and not super descriptive, will randomly give you a grade and feedback on only one section of your work.

Dr. Pappoe creates a welcoming and supportive environment that encourages creativity. Her grading is fair and straightforward, making it easy to understand expectations. She provides detailed and constructive feedback on assignments. Overall, Dr. Pappoe's class is a fantastic experience for anyone interested in digital composition.

Prof. Pappoe was my favorite professor this semester. She cares about each of her students and learns everyone's names. She grades kindly but provides valuable feedback so you can improve. This class is an easy A if you do the work, which is very manageable. I feel much more prepared after taking this class and enjoyed my time with Prof. Pappoe.

Dr. Pappoe is a very caring and nice professor. She cares about her students and enjoys 105. I thought the course work was applicable and helpful for business majors. The class is not a blow-off, but if you do the work, which isn't much, you will get an A. Also get to know her, she is a great person too.

Dr. Pappoe is very nice and she is very clear as to what is expected for the assignments. There are lots of group projects which often consist of busy work, but you will have a good grade if you take the time to complete the assignments.
Great professor, she was incredibly nice and accommodating. The work for the class was kinda pointless but that's not really her fault as it's a required class for UNC.
Clear grading material, group projects and individual assignments every class, mandatory attendance

This class has a lot of group projects, but it is not hard and the grading is easy. The only thing that made this class difficult was finding time for 5 busy college students to meet to work on a project.

I took ENGL 149 Digital Composition online with her. The class was easy, but she kinda forced participation when the topics covered were really simple so it didn't require deep discussion. She is very sweet and kind but I didn't like being awkwardly forced into participation with random groups and a lot of things felt like busy work.

Class is easy and she is sweet - easy A. The final is a Shark Tank Pitch project. The work out of class is simple but gets repetitive. Lots of group work and what you learn is useful for real life. Be careful about skipping - 3 absences and you're dropped/lose points from the course (15 mins late is an absence). Recommend her, overall!

Dr. Pappoe was by far my best professor this semester. If you are at all interested in business I would highly recommend this class. It's an easy A and you learn a lot of skills that can be used in business. There is no final and you spend half the semester doing group projects. Dr. Pappoe always gave great feedback on every assignment.
Excellent professor. She did a great job of explaining assignments and was always fair with grading. Would definitely take a course with her again.

The class was easy, but all group projects. She was an easy grader but doesn't grade everything immediately. You have to show up to class because she will take points off your grade. She is not easy on late work, do your work on time and show up to class and you will do good

Dr. Pappoe is nice, but this class is no use to 80% of people who take it. It is mainly busy work, and the actual projects we do serve little to no value. She is a nice person, but in all honesty I question her qualifications to be a professor at UNC. I feel many of the students in this class are more knowledgable about business than she is.
Definitely take Professor Ward for English 105, I was given many opportunities to make up assignments later that weren't finished in class, and the class never took up too much time.
Reasonable expectations, always easy to reach/happy to help, and very kind. Take this class, do the readings and essays, and he will set you up for success.
Very caring of his students. Will work with you if you are dedicated and show effort. Readings are really interesting, and he works everything back into lectures. HIGHLY recommend.

Very kind and understanding professor, I loved his ENGL 105 class. Accessible outside of class hours and explains the course's concepts well without being redundant. Definitely recommend to take his class!
Take ENGL 105 with him! Assignments are fair and doable. Lots of extra credit just by visiting the writing center. He is very kind and understanding. But plan to have an assignment due every week.

Professor Ward is my favorite I've had so far at UNC. Takes you through so many papers with ease, it seems like a lot of work but he's so lenient and tells you exactly how he wants you to get things done. If you're confused, ask for clarification, he's happy to lay it out for you. If you have to take ENGL105, take it with Ward.
The best teacher I had this semester. So nice and understanding. I would 100% take this class again even though we had so many papers.

Professor Ward is a great choice for ENGL105. As long as it looks like you put some effort into the assignment, you'll get 95s-100s on everything, and he usually doesn't take off for late submissions. There are some "busy work" assignments, but overall, the class is very light and exposes you to various topics and writing. Super chill and nice.

To put it humorously, Prof. Ward knows that we must take ENGL-105 and does his best to make the class bearable. His lectures are relaxed and interactive. He is flexible and clicks well with his students. He eased us through making a lit review, podcast, and research proposal so smoothly that I didn't feel intimidated by these tasks.

Professor Ward is a very good teacher. His class isn't very hard and he gives lots of feedback on all your writing, he genuinely wants students to do well and grow. You should expect to write a weekly 300-400 word explanation on a piece from a past sociologist. Other than that, there is not a lot of homework, and easy to get an A.

Great professor. As a freshman, I was very anxious and he answered all my questions throughout the semester with patience and kindness. I never felt like a bother. Great at lecturing, accessible, clear, calm and fair grader. Lots of reading and papers, but not too difficult. I would totally recommend professor Ward.

Great Guy - probably the best ENGL105 prof you could get. Gives very clear criteria for essays and great feedback. 3 unit assignments were literature reviews (1 stem & 1 humanities) and group podcast (social sciences). Lots of small 300-500 word assignments but usually graded for completion and just honest thoughts about readings and songs.
I enjoyed Professor Ward's class and this is a good English 105 to take.
Professor Ward is a great English 105 professor. He is very lenient with deadlines and the work load is not significant. If you can choose any professor choose him.

Great introductory English professor. Not a ton of work, and most "homework" is graded for completion and effort (as long as it seems like you put in some effort and thought, you got a 100). 2 Lit reviews, a podcast, and a final project. Very nice guy, provides good feedback.

Was a very understanding and lenient guy. Loved what he spoke about and was well versed in many topics, he wants you to do well and will help you no matter what. If you can take any ENGL 105 take his.

Mr. Ward was an amazing english teacher. His class was very straightforward and I was never concerned about getting a good grade in it. I really enjoyed having him as a teacher and he is a very nice and understanding person.

Professor Ward was by far one of the nicest teachers I have had at UNC. While English is not my favorite subject and can sometimes be dull he is so caring and is constantly looking out for the well-being of his students, lots of extensions, and lots of discussion about global events. If you have the chance to have him for ENGL 105 try to get him.
He's so relaxed, gives endless extensions, and is always happy to talk with you about anything, even not-class related things.

Mr. Ward was really caring and made sure everyone could succeed (offering extensions, resubmission for papers, etc.). The class did have a lot of writing, but the group project gave us a breather. He was very personable and funny, which made the class more enjoyable even though it was a general education requirement!

Professor Rambo is very sweet, flexible, and understanding. She frequently goes on tangents that make it a bit hard to stay engaged, but she's passionate about what she does. Unfortunately, we did not learn to write in this class, which was disappointing.

She's interesting to listen to and makes the class pretty fun, but you can't take notes on a computer at all and you have to participate a lot. You don't need the textbooks and the readings are chill, there are 3 main projects and they're not super hard.

Prof. Rambo is one of the most intelligent professors I have ever had. She's prone to going on tangents, but I always found them engaging and somehow relevant to the topic. You have to engage in the class, but she is a suuuper easy grader and most projects will revolve around things you're already interested in.
Very clear grading criteria and helpful feedback. Each unit has multiple feeders with a first draft (ungraded) and a final draft, so it's easy to get a good grade. Film analysis unit was enjoyable.

Prof Rambo is very understanding with deadlines and sick days. She is timely with feedback and it's very thorough. Class is a bit boring but it's Engl105 so that's expected. Three major assignments (journalism article, 1 min podcast, and movie review) but each have multiple graded feeders. Way easier than other engl105 profs! Can't recommend enough

Professor Rambo was great! The projects she had us do were relevant and interesting, and she was always very clear with the grading expectations. She took time to give genuine feedback on assignments that made me a better writer, as she really cared about helping us learn more than anything. Would take her class again 100%
Everything you get graded on has a rough draft, so just turn in your assignments and make the changes, and you can get a 100. It's so easy.

THE BEST!!! Take Engl 105 with Prof. Rambo, she is so chill and nice. Never did the readings but ended with above a 100%, just make sure to raise your hand and contribute to classroom discussions periodically.
The best, super chill and extremely nice. If you put in the work and participate in class, you will do great in the class. Ended with above a 100%.

Insanely easy class, only a little boring but not because of prof rambo, just because it's English 105. Come to class, turn in the practically participation credit assignments, do or don't do the readings, speak up every once in a while and you'll be fine. Easy A
This class was so easy and she is so kind! Take english105 with her for sure. Also, do not buy the textbook, we never use it.

This course was divided into three main units, with two "feeders" and one final project for each. No final exam. Participation is graded. The work is not hard at all, and Professor Rambo gives good, extensive feedback on drafts before you turn them in to be actually graded. Stick to the deadlines and you'll be fine!
Eleanor is awesome!! she is super kind, flexible, and wants her students to succeed. class was so easy and the workload was extremely light. take her for ENGL105 if you have the chance!

Great professor, slightly boring class (not because of her but because it's English 105). She's super nice and gives great feedback. She's lenient with deadlines and participation points. The feeders and projects are tedious but never take longer than 30 minutes. Great choice for a mandatory class!

Grad student who takes her first teaching job way too seriously. Loosen up a little, Ellie. Reluctant to give  constructive and SPECIFIC feedback on assignments. Only ever tells you that your work is bad, but never why. For someone who is so keen on revision, she sure hates to do her job and explain why she thought your work was "so terrible."

Nice lady, pretty chill. Lectures get rambly and I sometimes had no idea what the assignment was about based on what she said in class. Make sure you read the Sakai assignment requirements! Email is always open, very helpful there. I asked so many dumb questions and she didn't judge. Gave us Fridays async usually.

Actually took him for an English health humanities class. Super engaging and fun to talk to, easy A as long as you put in genuine effort. He isn't super strict on grading rubrics, mostly cares about if you engaged with the material in a way that's meaningful to you and genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

He is very nice and basically everyone got an A. Class was about as helpful as you made it to be. I wrote about by current STEM research which helped me learn a lot about scientific writing. Take take take.

I don't think I learned anything in this class, but it was pretty enjoyable. He basically just set up one project that we worked on all semester, with random assignments added depending on what we talked about in class that day. He is very funny and cares a lot about his students. Most of the class is discussion and he encourages everyone to share

He is extremely chill and tries his best to be funny. He doesn't actually teach much, but it's a basic English writing class so it is to be expected. He is open to what people can write about as long as it somehow links to what we are talking about in that unit. His deadlines are loose and he is very understanding if you need an extension.

Hill Taylor is quite possibly the best English teacher I've had in my entire life. He teaches you how to write important things, such as a literature review, podcast or magazine article. Although this was ENGL 105i, he gave a lot of freedom in what we could write about. He is a very nice guy and would 10/10 reccomend

Dr. Taylor is so chill. He was always excited to have students that enjoyed the writing process, becuse he knows good work comes naturally when writers are confident in their abilities. The unit assignments were very managable. Dr. Taylor is always down to banter with the class if your classmates are too.

I loved Dr. Taylor's class. He is an amazing professor, and his aim really was for us to learn rather than to give us work for him to grade. I came in thinking I would hate the English classes I had to take, however Dr. Taylor proved me wrong. You cannot go wrong with him as a teacher.

Best professor I've had so far. I think this class helped my writing abilities in the breath of scientific literature we explored. The focus of this class is less on getting good grades and more on exploring your interests aand how literature can help you. This class is representative of how college should be. I loved it. I'm sure you will too.

Kind, supportive professor who gives helpful feedback on writing. Offers revisions on feeder assignments to improve grades. Class has 3 unit projects with 2 feeder assignments each plus a few extras. Workload is manageable, and earning an A is achievable if you stay on top of work.

Grading criteria wasn't clear, and then she would take points off for things she didn't explain clearly. She was a little condescending if you had to miss class and didn't take well to being asked about your grades. And she didn't tell you what your grades were until the very last day of class. She had good energy and still got an A, though.

The class was made up of 3 units, each having two "feeder assignments" and one project, no final. Attendance matters. Grading system is weird, there are only three options for grades- does not meet requirements, meets them, exceeds them. Meeting expectations does not get you an A, you have to do more. Overall a good class, good and fair professor.

I took ENGL144 with her this semester (popular genres) and I would definitely recommend her. She is a very easy grader and your grade depends on a sustained commonplace book, in-class quizzes (very easy if you do the reading) and in-class writing (also very easy) as well as a group presentation at the end of the semester. Super chill class.

Dr. Ficke is super sweet and loves to teach this class. She grades assignments regularly and gives helpful feedback, encouraging all her students to do their best work. The class involves a lot of low-stakes peer review, which I found was great for getting advice before submitting something. Super chill class overall!

She always grades things based off of a scale of "does not meet expectations, meets expectations, and exceeds expectations". Iit is not clear what each of these even means and she literally never gives exceeds expectations right off the bat meaning she makes you redo literally every single assignment. I do not recommend taking this class.

I took ENGL 144 for an FC-Aesthetic requirement. The class was very relaxed, like a book club. We read about five books and discussed them in class. Each book had a 5-question quiz that was easy. I used audiobooks and found the reading manageable.

Sarah Ficke is a nice person and typically grades pretty fairly. However, her lectures are extremely boring and difficult to pay attention in. She also doesn't grade assignments on a normal 1-100 scale, but rather "exceeds" or "meets" or "does not meet expectations" which makes it difficult to gauge how you're doing in the class.

Her lectures are not engaging and often redundant. She's really unclear on her criteria and strict about citations, but offers chances for you to improve your grade on projects. She uses a weird grade scale and doesn't tell you your actual grade until the very end of the semester.

Professor Ficke is really chill. Her lectures can get a bit boring sometimes but the work is pretty easy. The feeders can be quite tedious sometimes but she does allow you to resubmit your assignments if you don't get the grade you want. You can only see your grade once in the middle of the semester and once at the end.
She is extremely strict with sources and citations, be careful because you wont know your grade until its over.

Dr. Ficke is very kind and accessible outside of class. The way the class is graded is on a grading contract, which can be frustrating as you can't really be sure of your grade until the midterm check-up and final grade are released. Class can be sorta boring at times, but she is very nice, and there is a lot of time to get feedback in class.

She's quite an easy professor, giving a good amount of assignments, and giving you enough time to complete them. I will say that she doesn't have a clear form of grading or deciding the final grade, which can confuse some, but you can argue your case for a higher grade. Easy final project too.

She's a nice person, like a grandma but she's one of the worst teachers I've ever had. Absolutely no form of grading criteria and she has a "grading contract" instead of normal grades. She makes a bunch of convoluted rules surrounding each assignment. Never knew my grade, and she hated giving feedback. Class was really slight, just annoying.
Professor Ficke was lowk evil. She is not scared to fail people and is so unengaging. She's definitely a nice person, but as a teacher I would not want to have her again.

Dr. Ficke is very nice, but I found this class to be extremely boring and un-engaging. It was very easy to just tune out and do work for other classes. Which is a shame, because I was very excited for this class. Not a lot of work though, easy A. I thought that the projects were kind of fun, especially the meme project and the final project.

Professor Ficke's class is not as easy as the other 105 classes, but as long as you put in the effort for your assignments and participate a decent amount in class, you should be fine. She gives good feedback and is lenient on deadlines. The only downside is that she only lets you know your grade twice: mid-semester and at the end of the semester.

Dr. Ficke is one of the sweetest professors I have had! The assignments were pretty easy, and I love that she gave so many opportunities for us to receive feedback on drafts. She uses a grading contract and when we had big projects coming up, she would host individual conferences to give us feedback on our work so far.

prof helps you lots with english/writing, gives much feedback, wants u to succeed. compared to other eng105, class is harder. contract grading where grades based on ability to meet standards(each assignment given grade of meets, exceeds, doesn't meet expectations. final grade is numerical so this confuse u abt where you are/difficult to get A

Professor Ficke was a great professor! She was helpful with providing feedback and was often accessible if you needed any help. The grading is a little bit weird in the class, as you don't know what you have in the class till the very end of the course. There is a decent amount of work for a 105 class, but not bad at all.

Actually ENGL323- Impossible to reach outside of class, and several times did not bother to show up. Very harsh grader for someone who gave no criteria. Only got grades back after everything was over, which was very unhelpful considering there was "feedback" in them. Very knowledgeable about film, but comes across as mean and pretentious at times.

Flaxman is a straightfoward lecturer and professor and his passion for film is evident. Engl142 is an great class if you do your readings/viewings and follow essay instructions. Everything was graded by TAs. Beware his dog.

His soft, slow voice doesn't engage or excite the room about movies, so skip class and use his online slides. Started with film theory, but this class is really all about basic terminology. He grades papers "harshly" (unclear guidelines), but he also sent us last year's identical exams. Encouraged AI use for an art project :(

He's a funny and nice guy, but I personally didn't mesh with the lectures. I thought a class about movies would be fun but more often then not felt like a chore. A lot of the papers are a pain to write and I felt as if most times I was just jabbering on to met the word count because there wasn't enough content to write about in the scenes/shots.

I just finished his ENGL680 (wasn't an option here) class and still have yet to receive a single grade. We had a midterm, paper abstract, and final paper, and I have no idea what my grade could possibly be because I've gotten close to no feedback. The classes are long and 95% him talking with no slides. He's very knowledgeable, just super difficult

Flaxman is an extremely knowledgeable professor. The class was lecture heavy but he did ask questions and encouraged class discussions. My biggest qualm with the class was the hap-hazard organization. There were only 2 writing assignments for undergrads but he did not communicate prompts and guidelines well. Still a chill class and Flaxman is nice.

His lectures are amazing, he is an eloquent and engaging speaker; as a film lover I learned so many cool facts from him. The class isn't very demanding and if you are interested in film at all is definitely worth taking! The papers are graded harshly, but you have plenty of time. Professor Flaxman is who I want to be when I grow up.

Great guy who really knows his stuff, really interesting lectures that are mostly just watching clips. Expectations are quite reasonable if you spend any time at all studying and thinking about the content on your own. Decent workload, but it's mostly films and readings. The TA sections can be less useful, but in general a very interesting class.

Professor Flaxman is clearly passionate about the subject that he teaches, which helps make his lectures a bit more engaging. Your success in the class is pretty much solely determined by your performance on the essays in the first half of the semester, which can be graded pretty harshly.

Greg is so kind if you get to know him! Go up and talk to him after class and he will give you great feedback and help (yoi will need it, this class is HARD). Don't be fooled by the level 100 this class is a ton of work

(INTRO) to film analysis is not expected by Greg. He requires great effort in understanding the material he gives. You have to live and breathe film in order to succeed in this class. Beware that its not easy unless you know how to BS ur papers and write about nonsense in regard to film elements. You will not just watch and talk about films here.

While lectures were interesting, very few of them stayed on topic and then we were expected to write essays and questions related to the reading or movie that we barely discussed. It was possible to get by with a lot of work outside of class and good reading and writing skills.

While the title "Intro to Film Analysis" alludes to an easy class - it is not. Professor Flaxman grades very toughly, but you will certainly learn from his critiques. He is very knowledgeable about the content and provides very good lecture slides and notes. Attendance to lectures is not mandatory, and you do not have to participate much.

I loved Flaxman's class! His knowledge of both history and production of cinema is unmatched! Professor Flaxman is passionate about teaching film and his lectures are insightful. Definitely a good beginner film class to take. Grading is collaborative with the REC teachers and they are typically not too harsh, but will leave lots of comments.

Two less than 1500 word essays, take home mid-term, and final essay on three prompts with greater than 700 words each. Lectures were philosophical at times and on many topics surrounding art in different medias. Grading's tough but great feedback and took a while to get back.

Took this class as a gen ed and it ended up being way more work that I thought. Papers were graded harshly and they made up most of the final grade. Despite listing a clear grading on the syllabus, the final grade you get in the class is changed based on a curve that can bring final grades down.

This class is a lot more effort than just watching movies, but I really learned a lot. Though the content was interesting and the accompanying assignments helped me learn, Professor Flaxman is extremely lecture-heavy and didn't speak very loudly, so you have to really pay attention. However, you could tell he cared alot about what he was teaching.

Really knowledgeable prof, but I did think that he graded a bit harshly on the few assignments we did have. Takes a while for grades/feedback to come back but it is helpful for other writing intensive classes. I wish he gave more guidelines for what he wanted to see but if you talk to him during office hours he can give you a lot of insight!
Flaxman is a horrible lecturer but the exams are easy, the study guides are very helpful. I never went to the class and am looking at an A. If you're a good writer you'll get an A.
An incredible professor. His lectures are always engaging. Seriously recommend.
Professor Wolfe was amazing!! I hope her retirement in Spain treats her the best! Highly recommend taking ENGL112!

FOR 227H!!!! Prof. Wolfe is the best, she helped my writing so much and make the very complex material super accessible. If you ever have a question she is more than happy to answer it and her office hours make a huge difference if you need some gudienace or help! CANT RECOMMEND HER ENOUGH!!!!!

She was chill. Showing up to lecture isn't mandatory, but I would still suggest going because it makes the readings that much more digestible. She also had slides available that were super comprehensive. Would definitely recommend.

Best organized survey-style English class I have taken. The lectures are super well done and very engaging. TAs are very helpful if this is your first college-level English class. There are two essays, but they are pretty short, and you are given lots of direction and prompts. All in-class assessments are handwritten on blue books.
Professor Wolfe is incredibly knowledgeable and cares about her students. Her lectures are very helpful and interesting.

Her lectures help you understand the material so clearly. I had so much fun taking the class, and I always looked forward to going to class and having her discuss the material. She's extremely caring and her office hours are helpful as well. The in class assignments are quite simple, and although the final is a lot of writing, it was worth!

Taking Jessica Wolfe is an honor and profs like these are what make UNC so special. Her lectures are the best of any course I've taken, but I'd only recommend this one in particular if you need it and/ or are passionate about the subject matter. The reading and preparation needed is heavy, but the knowledge gained from the class is worth it.

LOVED Dr. Wolfe. Went to office hours a lot and had many interesting conversations. The class is interesting if you read the material before, but I didn't read much towards the end of the semester and it didn't matter because we went over most of the important stuff that will be tested on in lecture. But that's why attendance is so important!!

Lots and lots of readings in the semester, very fast paced. 3 essays that are all 1500+ words, plus a (really hard and strictly graded) midterm, with a final at the end. Tons of work for a class that's only a 100 level class, wouldn't take this at all if you're not a CMPL major or whatever.

I love Dr. Wolfe. She is so kind and understanding. Ended up canceling the final since the class was doing so well. She gives really great feedback on papers and is super clear with expectations. Class is mostly lectures/discussions, but they are interesting and she takes time to talk about every point brought up. Take any class with her you can

Professor Wolfe's lectures were always super engaging and she is so funny. She makes obscure topics more understandable. The writing assignments were simple with prompt ideas given and the homework was usually just reading. The midterm and final is a series of short answers questions. No textbooks needed because the stories are online.

Dr. Wolfe is a great professor! This course was lecture-heavy, but the lectures were engaging, and Dr. Wolfe was always open to class discussion. She offers a lot of flexibility on essay topics and deadlines, and holds students to a high (but achievable) standard.

Professor Wolfe is great! She mostly only lectures with openings for commentary, questions, and discussions. She is extremely knowledgeable about Shakespeare/history relating to Elizabethan literature and is a great resource when planning essays for the class. She is a toughish grader and her commentary can be confusing, but overall, she's great.

Shes very nice. However this class was made more difficult than it needed to be. Paper lengths seemed unnecessarily long, the recitation sections were pointless, and the final was annoying. The final had terms that were only mentioned once or twice on the lecture slides, and had little to do with the actual material. There are better 100s to take.
The class itself was great but beware of TAs, mine was a harsh grader. Professor Wolfe is incredibly kind and very accessible. Good course overall.

Format of assignments was very individualized (submitting a number of assignments by the end of the semester, no deadlines throughout), so your stress levels are based on your procrastination. Graded nicely. Very lecture heavy for dense and dry texts. Wolfe was knowledgeable but dry sometimes. Don't take unless required or you have an interest.
Her class is great, and I recommend taking BUSI 401 with her.

401 is already a pretty weirdly structured course. Professor Geil makes it pretty manageable and in most of the other courses the feedback kind of seems arbitrary; hers is more concrete and very easy to implement if you read through it, grades a bit harshly but I was never upset about my grades in the course. 10/10 would recommend for 401

This class is amazing- essentially just a three hour class comprised of two guest lecturers plus commentary from Geil and Zoller. Fun, engaging, practical, and intellectual. This course is amazing and Geil is an asset to this class. If you can take this class, I cannot recommend it enough!

Super nice and caring person. Grades were't put in until after finals which made for a roller coaster of emotions. Tough grader with very vague expectations and guidelines. If possible, consider taking with another professor.

Dr. Geil is a fantastic professor due to her passion for teaching the class and her understanding of what she wants each student to learn. She wants each student to grow, is easily accessible outside of the course, and is very open to answering any questions during office hours! I definitely would recommend it to any student!

Prof Taylor is really kind and is dedicated to the success of each student. Main project is a literature review, she breaks it up into smaller projects so it doesn't feel overwhelming. I would recommend this class to people whether or not they plan on working in the writing center, good base on how to research if you've never done it.

I felt that Gigi truly cared about me as a student and wanted me to succeed. 

I recommend this class to anyone interested in writing; however, if you are not, you may not enjoy the class. The structure is mainly discussions and then writing coaching practice toward the second half; therefore, the class requires you to be present and engaged.

This class is pretty meh. The assignments are not too hard, but I do not appreciate it when she can micromanage or seem too overbearing. I respect her as my professor but I don't vibe too well with her demeanor and personaility.

She's from the North so I think that's where she gets her blunt and brazen attitude from. The class wasn't 100% amazing, but she's fun to talk to and get feedback from. If you have a real interest in writing, editing, and coaching then you should take the class, but if you don't, you definitely won't like being there.
Gigi is a very pleasant, brilliant, and kind professor. She really knows her stuff, and I regret not interacting more with her outside of the course.

Prof. Taylor is big on engagement, which I really value. She was helpful with research topics and writing. But she came across as very rude and surly. Some things that she said to us while I had her were insensitive, belittling and completely inappropriate for an educational setting. She's a good teacher but I won't take any course of hers again.

Prof. Taylor is an awesome professor. The class does require a lot of work and research since you're working on a big paper basically the whole semester. But Gigi is super accommodating, available to talk over assignments whenever you're struggling, and gave us countless extra days to complete assignments. I'd recommend engl 402 w/ Taylor anyday

Harsh and unclear grader. The class is pretty much all group discussions. Actual coaching practice doesn't begin until after spring break. One literature review and synthesis matrix make up the bulk of the grade.

This was a grad seminar, and discussions were engaging. Dr. Talpaz led us through difficult material and allowed us to connect our own research interests to the course material. She tailored the syllabus to these interests. Despite other reviews re: feedback, she gave feedback on our discussion forums throughout the semester. I enjoyed the class.

I liked Professor Talpaz as a professor. Lots of interesting discussions and interesting material. The only problem wasn't super organized, she frequently went off the syllabus and took a long time to put grades in. Would have appreciated a little more feedback on essays. That being said she's very understanding if you submit something late.

She was a good professor/lecturer and facilitated interesting discussions. However, she never graded anything the entire semester and never gave feedback on any assignment, so we never knew how to improve. She didn't put in grades until after the next semester started, and we had no explanation for said grade since there was 0 feedback.
She's very kind, but doesn't give advice on major assignments or put in any grades so you never know how you're doing in the class.
She's smart and can be critical but is supportive - if you try she'll support you

The class was fine and she presents the material well but isn't great at the administrative requirements of being a professor. She never responds to emails. Says she'll post the assignments and never does until very late. I haven't received a single grade all semester including my final grade that should've been done days ago.

Dr. Talpaz is my favorite professor here! Assignments were clear & each discussion/reading question was thought-provoking & useful for the weekly posts. She fostered an open, inclusive learning environment & this was evident in the high level of participation from each student. She's a passionate professor & truly cares about her students' success.

Never held consistent class, never graded anything and reported grades 10 days late (with no feedback), went over class everyday, never responded to a single email, AND held class over zoom during condition 2. Also the class wasn't even about monsters or monstrosity it was basically the usual comp lit literary criticism that any other class has.

grading isn't consistent, she'll leave feedback for drafts and will take points off even if you fix the mistakes. is never really clear about the requirements and grades harshly when you're putting effort. gave everyone the same grade for the final group project and takes points off for no reason. not a mean professor but not a pleasure.

The class was pretty easy but there was a ton of busy work compared to other ENGL105 classes. Theres a lot of group activities and the last unit was all group work. She grades nicely and gives decent feedback. She's always available for office hours and is a kind person who's willing to answer questions.
this professor is evil. she gives grades like she is using a random number generator. gave all the groups the same grade for a group project which made no sense to any of us.

I thought that she was really nice and overall a good professor. Kinda a lot of assignments but not too hard of a grader and I got an A in the class. Didn't really try too hard. We did not have to do a lot of the normal English 105 stuff like a podcast or anything difficult so would def recommend taking with her!

She is very nice overall and tries to ensure her lectures are interesting. Most of the content is set by the department. The class is very group work-heavy, with lots of peer review. I got something out of it and learned how to improve my writing, even though I had previous academic writing experience. Don't buy the textbook, you won't use it.

Not super clear with rubric and requires lots of peer editing. Her feedback isn't always specific and points that were taken off didn't always match the feedback responses. While this class requires significant writing as an individual, it is extremely group work heavy. Bought the textbook under suggestion and did not use it once.
Great professor who was always available for office hours and help. Course was a little boring at times but it was mainly just when we were doing work that was required by the ENGL 105 curriculum
Barely anything has been graded and it's literally LDOC

Nice guy, the class is pretty easy and involves a lot of group work and class discussion. There's only three big projects and the rest is mostly discussions. The syllabus is a bit vague and he goes off topic a lot so if that bothers you should take this class with a different teacher

He's nice and understanding when you have conflicts, the class itself is not difficult but he takes a long time to respond to emails and repeatedly shows up to class late. He would make updates an hour before class would start. Half of the assignments have yet to be graded this far into the semester.

Dr. Taylor was an incredible teacher. He made english fun and enjoyable and understands that a lot of students already have a lot of work for their other classes. He is understanding if you have a conflict or issue come up during the semester. If you try your best, you will do great.
Genuinely the best professor ever. If you actually care about your projects and papers you'll get a 100. Very motivational and tells hilarious stories. I could not recommend this class enough.

LOVEDDD Eng105 with Professor Taylor, as long as you do the work before hand, you will likely get a 100+ in the class. He's super chill and loves it when people participate and talk with him. He requires a lot of writing, but it's not difficult at all.
ABSOLUTE KING. Take this class with him!! He cares about his students and class is always engaging and fun!! I learned a lot in the course and I recommend Dr. Taylor to everyone!!!
Really great professor! Not too much work and you basically get to write about whatever you want.
Had one real paper and 2 pretty easy projects after that. Hilarious guy.

Absolute best ENGL 105I professor. He has hilarious anecdotes, and clearly cares about our engagement with the material over any specific approach we took with our work. Absolute goated professor and I would recommend his class to any freshman for an easy A.
Dr. Taylor is the goat. His class is very manageable and he is very willing to work with his students

TAKE THIS 105, I don't know if another 105 class tops this one. He is super chill and I never felt stressed once. The class consists mainly of open discussion on varying topics and had three projects throughout the semester. This might seem like a lot, but don't be fooled, as long as you put in an ounce of effort, you are sure to make an A

The best choice I made at UNC was to take my ENGL 105 with Dr. Taylor. Class is always hilarious. He's super engaging, and as long as you go to class put in a little effort you'll get a great grade. I learned a lot without ever struggling, something I can really appreciate. I loved being in Dr. Taylor's class and would absolutely do it again.
Dr. Taylor is very very laid back.

Dr. Taylor makes lots of jokes and is a very understanding guy. He teaches by digression but it is all relevant to the lesson. There are 3 projects that make up your grade along with two other minor components; participation (as long as you occasionally participate you get 100) and your journals which take 5ish minutes during class.

Dr. Taylor was a very understanding and easy going professor. He is not a harsh grader at all and just wants to see students make an effort and show interest. This is a great class to take to ease your way into university level English classes.
Dr Taylor was great! Honestly a pretty chill class, with homework here and there. Would highly recommend!

Dr. Taylor was such a funny dude! You only had three major assignments and they were leniently graded. I took writing in health and medicine and the only book you had to read was actually very interesting. Recommend taking your required English class with him!

Great teacher! Class everyday is just discussions and he grades super easy. A great person and is very lenient. As long as you turn in your work and come to class you'll get a good grade. My favorite teacher of the semester.

Dr. Taylor is a great professor. He is very conversational and heavily encourages participation, as it makes up 15% of your grade. No big tests/exams, just papers he gives you plenty of leniency for. Great guy, great class!

ENGL 394: A lot of discussions and readings (5+ books, a few movies, short videos, and shorter stories). Tests are very easy, assignments prior build your notes for the open-note tests. Overall, good professor, easy class (you can get by if you don't read every single thing), easy tests, easy assignments, annoying final paper, extremely easy final.

Professor Irizarry is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. She is passionate about Latinx studies which makes the class very engaging. The readings that we are assigned are not a hassle to do because they are so interesting. I took ENGL 164 and ENGL 464 with this professor and it was the best decision!!
Dr. I is amazing!! She works well with her students and is always there to help you :) There is a lot of reading in this class so get ready for that!

Dr. Irizarry is a great professor! I enjoyed her course because I felt like I was able to be myself and can tell that she cares deeply about her students. While there is a bit of reading, all of the text are great reads and align well with Latinx studies. I highly recommend taking a class with her before graduating from Carolina!

Was a very difficult grader during the beginning of the semester, and took points off for little things such as tiny formatting issues.
