As the semester went by she became an easier grader as she realized we understood the material clearly. A LOT OF READING + quizzes, Final project was fun and easy. She is a good person but okay professor overall.

Dr. Irizarry, the epitome of intellectual brilliance! With an uncanny ability to infuse humor into complex concepts, their lectures were mesmerizing. Their dedication to student success was unparalleled, going above and beyond to ensure understanding. A true gem, transforming minds effortlessly!
do not take. does way too much for 105, harsh grader w/ unclear expectations. engl105 should never be this serious.
avoid avoid avoid. did wayyy too much for engl105, graded extremely harshly and is very strict about her ridiculous google doc policy.

Hate this class with a passion. I took this for my first semester, and she was nothing but difficult. Even my tutors and external sources think she's on her high horse. Doesn't give constructive feedback, very vague about what she wants. Grading attendance way too harshly & participation. Do not take this course, I beg find another professor.
Her way of speaking is very demeaning and she acts as though she sees us as a burden. Her Google. Doc policy is way too strict.
Weird vibe in the class. The class is probably a good deal more difficult than the average 105 class but realistically it is not that bad.
This professor is unbelievably snobby and can't admit when she made a mistake

Be so careful in this course. She is strict and particular about how things are done. Use the extension policy to your advantage because she almost never says no. She will talk for so long and not actually explain the assignments. I only did well in this because of AP in high school. It's not a difficult class, she's just a difficult person.
Definitely a tough ENGL 105 Professor. Don't ask for grade bumps cuz she won't give them out lmao. Very harsh grading based on “objective” standards

Given how difficult English 105 SHOULD be this class was easily a 5/5 difficulty. My friends tell me about their 105 classes they took with easy assignments and short essays, if you take this class you are spending weeks on each assignment and getting graded very harshly, like she took .005% off my grade for being 2 mins late harsh.

You'll definitely have to put in the effort, and there's a lot of revising, but it's one of those classes where you can actually see yourself improving. The assignments are engaging, and her feedback is solid, even if it feels like a lot at times.

Sample work from past classes made assignments easy. The assignments build on each other, so you have plenty of time to revise and improve. There was also a lot of work time in class. Homework wasn't too much, though it picks up towards the end. Plus, the lowest Feeder grade gets dropped, which was super helpful. Don't try to use AI though.

She took the time out of her day to take off .001% on one of my assignments because I turned it in two minutes late. This would immediately be rounded out by the grading system so the fact she took the time out of her day to do that should really say a lot. Also doesn't post rubrics and is overall super pretentious.

DO NOT take her. She is incredibly rude to her students, will yell at you directly for asking a clarification question, will give you a 0 if you forget to turn on editing permissions in the google doc. She is just overall demeaning and rude and doesn't care to help you do better. Also, I did well in the class so trust I am not biased in any way.

Very hit or miss on grading. You could put 100% effort and receive a low grade on the assignment because it doesn't match her standards- which by the way she doesn't make clear because she doesn't believe in posting rubrics for the assignment. In general the material she covers in class is taught well, however it is almost impossible to do well.

Do NOT take Pur. She is VERY unclear about what she expects out of an assignment, and is an EXTREMELY harsh grader. She expects students to write like they have taken many college level english courses and will NEVER provide students with a rubric as she believes this is "pre-grading". She also is not afraid to accuse students of cheating.

Between the harsh grading, and little to no directions for what she was looking for in our writing, I would highly recommend doing everything in your power to avoid having Lara Pur as your teacher. If you want to put in a lot of effort for low grades, no improvement, and decreased confidence in your writing, take Lara Pur.

While you can tell she's trying and it's her first time teaching, definitely take it with someone else. Lectures aren't helpful, and your grade is essentially three papers, all of which are graded ridiculously harshly (the average on most assignments were in the 70s or worse) with no rubric or useful feedback whatsoever.

Her grading was random with no rubric provided. Your grade was basically just 3 papers that she randomly assigned a grade to. She was passive agressive in class and graded participation harshly as well. I would not take her class ever again.

There is not much homework in this class, but the work is graded extremely harshly and no rubric is provided. The average on the assignments is generally a 70 or lower. She is good at explaining concepts but grades papers like its a 200 level english class taking many points off for little things that were not listed in the assignment description.

Dr. Crystall was a wonderful professor who was always open to feedback from students about the structure and materials of the class. It was a lot of work and she is the fastest grader, but I adored this class.

Dr. Crystall was fine. She struggled with technology, was passive aggressive to students in class, and assigned homework to be due on a saturday night... however, she does provide a lot of feedback on assignments, grades easy, and is helpful. she also replied to emails very promptly. overall, not bad but did a little too much for engl 105..

A very easy class if you listen and take notes when she reviews the criteria for assignments. Class was often boring, but assignments were very doable. She's very eccentric, and some people might not mesh well with her.

She was extremely difficult. She would give you a bad grade on a paper and tell you to fix certain parts. When you fix those parts, she still gives you the same grade. Almost impossible to improve your grade

Dr. Crystal is very nice, and she teaches very well. She does struggle using electronics and anything like that, but she is very passionate about books, and there is always a great discussion within the class. She gives really in-depth feedback, but as long as you follow the rubric for the papers, you should be good. I recommend her!

Dr. Crystall was ok, but the lectures were so boring and she would just ramble on about what the assignment is rather than actually teaching anything. She has a difficult time with technology and was pretty disorganized. There was a decent amount of homework, but it wasn't overwhelming or super hard. She was really rude and condescending at times.

While I liked her more toward the end of the semester, I would not take English 105 with Dr. Crystall again. The class and assignments are extremely boring, tedious, and often seem to be more like busywork. She can occasionally talk down to students and I found the class to be incredibly monotonous. This class is a lot easier with another professor

Truthfully, class isn't awful. You will be fine if you do the assignments when you hear about them. Sometimes, she would change due dates, which confused people. If you get on her good side you will be just fine. She's an older woman who will treat you like you're in high school. Prepare to read slideshows.

I LOVED this class and Dr.Crystall. The projects were all super easy and quick. The class had amazing conversations and a great lineup of books. She cared a lot about respecting her students and making a comfortable environment for discussions about serious topics. Our class has no idea why she has such bad ratings. Definitely recommend!!

Best Professor at UNC!!! Do not listen to the other people- super understanding and nice.
She has so much to offer. The classes were literally just conversations, and the assignments were fun, easy, and straightforward.
There are some readings—obviously, it's an English class—but it is always something interesting and nothing too heavy.

Professor Crystall was decent in ENGL155, which I took online in the summer. The coursework was manageable but sometimes heavy, with daily forum posts and several papers/projects. Learning history through comics was mildly interesting but could be boring. It's possible to get an A in her class, and she thoroughly reads everything when grading!

She is very rude. Does not know what is going on, constantly contradicts herself. She is a really harsh grader for no reason and does not explain the ruberic of any assignment. It's harder to get an A in this class than it should be.

She is very disorganized and inconsistent. She'll tell you to do one assignment and the Sakai site will tell you to do another. She can be very condescending and treats you like you're a high schooler. The class isn't difficult, but her disorganization adds unnecessary hurdles. Don't take this class if you can avoid it.

She treats you like you're in high school. Everything online is scattered and inconsistent. The directions will say to do one thing and she'll say to do another. She acts nice but can be a bully. Avoid if possible.

She was alright, just very unorganised and doesn't seem to know how to manage electronic systems well with a confusing Canvas page to navigate. 3 out of 4 papers are needed for the course, and rubric is pretty straightforward and broad as opposed to how she communicates. Very discussion-based but maybe an "easy A", confusing to figure out format

Dr. Crystall comes off at first as a nice lady. However, as time goes on she seems to single out students who she seemingly doesn't like for any particular reason at all. When grading she will put things like "great job" yet give you and 80, with no explanation. If she didn't grade like this I would have finished with an A.

this class gives major high school vibes but not in a good way. Dr. Crystall is rude and condescending and treats you as if you're in high school. This class is very boring and seems like the kind of stuff I did in my ninth-grade English class.

The class was quite disorganized, expectations weren't always clear on some assignments. There were only two required essays out of four options, also forum posts and going to two of some events around campus that relate to class material in some way and responding to them. The final exam was designing a mini continuation of the course, it was ok.

Professor Crystall is very understanding of your circumstances. She also accepted late work as long as she hadn't started grading the assignment. However, her instructions were often unclear. Also, her due dates would be at weird and varying times throughout the day, and would often take points off of your assignment with no explanation for why.
Although she seems very kind, she can be condescending at times. The assignments were very particular, but as long as you follow the instructions carefully you should do fine.

Lectures are mandatory for understanding the material they are exclusively his breakdown of the book. I did not always read before class because of the long readings, but I did well in the course regardless. There are a few assignments, but they are weighted heavily. I would recommend it to English majors, but not as a focus capacity fulfillment.

You just read older American novels and hand-write (sometimes take home) short essays in class. I personally love reading so I liked these books but I didn't always finish some of them, and I was fine. He's a sweet man who cares a lot about the literature, and is willing to work through the book with you outside of class.
I got an A on every assignment, but for some reason, he gave me an A- without any explanation.

Not much to say. Obviously, lots of reading, but I skipped reading a few books and got an A on each paper. Had a few interesting takes (said he should technically be able to say the n-word because of the removal of DEI, whatever that means). Pretty nice and passionate about the novels. Little to no feedback, and the grade is unknown until the end.

i've seen some other ratings and wanted to add the context of Prof. Gura's use of racial language. referring to the book "Huckleberry Finn," there is frequent usage of the n word. he stated that past students felt more comfortable replacing that word with other things when he reads aloud, so that it was he did this semester. take it as you'd like.

the first book in the course was published late 18th century. prof. gura was super helpful in explaining context and events that were important. however, the lectures following i found less helpful. class was a reiteration of the same stuff you did alone. it's important to attend class bc he makes all announcements in person and doesn't email them.

I am an engl major and can say without a doubt this was the most boring class I have ever taken. I love US lit, but this class made me hate it. He obviously cares about what he does, but I personally wouldn't recommend if you want an engaging lecture.

This class is a solid FC Aesthetic. The class is mostly him rambling about the book which he is certainly passionate about. The class has three in class essays each 25% and a final that is also 25%. He just gives a letter grade not feedback for improvement. I didn't read the books and was able to do well.

I really enjoyed Prof. Gura's class for the reason that he loves what he does, and it shines through in his teaching. In my experience, if you provide a thought-inspiring paper for the book you read, you are almost guaranteed an A. He loves reading your interpretations! If I could sum it up simply: it's like your grandpa with his favorite book.

He says he doesn't use the n-word "anymore" but continues to use other offensive terminology. You're graded on in-class written essays, which are easy, but he is a tough grader and doesn't offer much feedback. If you need a good GPA, don't take this class.

Fantastic professor. Class is very lecture heavy, but its mostly him just going over the assigned readings. The best way I could describe ENGL 220 is like if you spent time listening to your granddad talking about his favorite books. Absolutely love Prof. Gura, he's a legend.
Dr. Gura frequently brings up the fact that he has said the N word.

You could get an A in this class and never read a single book, BUT the books are so good that you will want to read them! The class feels like a therapeutic book club; he brought his dog to the final exam if that tells you anything. Only complaint is that its all "lectures" but the lecture is basically just reviewing what happened in the book.

Super chill guy, the class is way easier and less work than the syllabus suggests. Read the books, or even just the chapters he highlights as important, and you will do fine. The essays are not graded harshly.
Such a sweet guy who is really passionate about literature. As long as you actually read this class is easy and so enjoyable.
The only professor who revived my spirit for reading, and made me step outside of my comfort zone. Incredibly nice and just wants his students to understand the literature.

I LOVE HIM!!! i am already signed up for his classes next semester. Amazing teacher truly loves the material and just wants you to love it too. I never thought i'd enjoy some of the books he showed us but he read them so incredibly and made me realize how much i love to read again.
I almost felt a pang of nostalgia when I walked out of the classroom for the last time...
Super chill lectures where he describes the books in detail, so don't worry too much if the reading is challenging.

I loved Prof Gura's class. We only had 3 assignments but they were very manageable (1 ID assignment, 1 short paper, and take-home final). He grades fairly and says attendance is mandatory but only took roll like 4 times. He loves the material he teaches and lectures the whole time, which seems boring but was actually relaxing.

One of the most intelligent professors I have had. Honestly, the class is slightly disorganized. No clear grading criteria (check plus check check minus), no clear grades included in the syllabus. Had to read a play every 5 classes, so lots of reading, but the discussions were insanely intelligent and I learned so so much.

I loved this class! Shakespeare felt very daunting previously, but Professor Baker's discussion-led classes provide ample opportunities for questions. He is very passionate about the subject and although he teaches based on his theories for each play, he is very open to feedback and every single classmate's interpretations.
I liked this class a lot! It is lecture-heavy and based on the readings. If you participate in class and read the plays you will do fine!

230 was not on the list so I had to choose the other class ^^: 

Professor Baker is a really nice guy and tries to make the class interesting, he likes to hear students opinions on the books, but he will go to the attendance sheet and call on people if no one has an answer. Grades fairly, 2 essays, midterm, and a final are only grades for the class

Professor Baker is passionate and kind! The class is definitely boring if you don't like Shakespeare though. He graded essays easily and we never had homework. Tests are essays too and open-book. But seriously, prepare for some reading.

I loved this class. Baker is super entertaining and he finds new ways to connect the texts to the modern age, I was never bored during lectures. Three major papers with fun prompts, ~5 pgs each, graded easy. He will cold call but if you talk at least once every other class he's less likely to call on you. Take if you really love Shakespeare. 10/10.

He's a great professor! The class consists of ~2 lecture days per play, plus one day to address any questions everyone may have. This format means the class is 80% his lectures. To me, I enjoyed them and got a lot out of them, but if you prefer more participation, you may not. 3 papers, easy grading, and he cold calls in class but is very nice!!

Professor Baker clearly loves what he does. The class involves lots of reading, but that is expected of an english class. Textbooks are required but sometimes he just scans them and uploads them onto Sakai. His grading is weird bc you dont know your grade until the very end. Very little assignments and loves student feedback.

I love this man. So funny, really passionate about the subject matter. I would recommend reading the text because he does cold call in class, but he doesn't seem to care when someone doesn't know the answer so you can get away without reading. Attendance is mandatory but I did really enjoy this class. Very lenient grader. This class made me happy.

David is a very understanding and caring man. The class was interesting enough, especially if you've never read Shakespeare's plays. Majority of the class time was spent analyzing the plays from angles you wouldn't expect, by forming questions and hypotheses. Not a harsh grader at all, and three papers were the assignments.

She is very chill, caring and is lenient about deadlines if you communicate with her. Class is completely discussion based but she never cold calls so you can get away with not speaking. She only has a few essays spread throughout the semester but they are pretty long and time-consuming, however she is a easy grader. She is also very knowledgable!

Dr.Stern was amazing. In this class she didn't take attendance but our discussions were so much fun. We just discussed the books and had open, zero pressure, conversations, and she was willing to clear up any confusion that the class had with the assigned reading. She wasn't a hard grader, but some of her assignments require a lot of thought.
Dr. Stern is a very knowledgeable and caring professor. She communicates very well and takes participation into consideration. Easy class, but you read several books over its duration.

Graded by few things, including 2 papers. Seminar-style, lectures discussed the works without a ton of structure. I missed a couple classes and was fine bc no lecture content was actually tested or anything. I did more poorly than I expected on the first paper, so I was unsure of what my grade would be, but ended up with an A somehow

She's very enthusiastic and passionate about the material that she teaches. Her lectures are interesting but if you're not into English it will be boring. Not an easy A, but she wants students to succeed. Only graded by 2 exams and 2 papers plus participation. Gives very clear expectations and study guides for exams and offers plenty help on papers

I really enjoyed Dr. Stern's class. She was helpful, accessible, and kind. The only thing I didn't like about her was her sense of humor, very dad jokey. However, she is incredibly smart and well-read. I learned things about the readings that I never would have thought about otherwise. Take her only if you love and adore Brit Lit.

This was my second class with Dr. Stern, and I would highly recommend it if you have any interest in Oscar Wilde! Readings and discussions were wonderful, and Dr. Stern was always encouraging and helpful. Grades are only based on one shorter writing assignment, 2 papers, a presentation, and participation, but she truly wants everyone to succeed.

Class time is only large group discussion, never any small group or partner work which got boring quickly. Readings were never too long, as we primarily read poems. Sometimes lectures lack clear direction and it can be hard to jump in and join the conversation. She definitely grades tough but wants you to do well.

Dr. Jack was very personable and made a clear effort to know everyone's names, even if you weren't an avid participant. The course material was a bit boring at times, but Dr. Jack worked hard to make it interactive and hands-on as often as possible.

My queen. Dr. Jack is an incredible scholar and absolutely lovely to have as a professor. She's exceptionally smart, but she's not at all intimidating -- she's a very warm, flexible instructor, and you'll learn a lot in her classes. All hail. Highly recommend taking courses with her, even if you're not an English major.

Such a lovely individual. This class was very relaxing and reminded me of the close-knit and collaborative environment I miss so dearly in high school. The work is very easy and minimal. I made some of my close friends from this class, too, and picked up some new hobbies (we got to cross stitch, play with typewriters, and more!) Very fun :)

This is a straight forward class, but don't expect any knowledge to be spoon-fed to you. This class emphasizes  working at your own pace, so much of what you take away depends on you. It's useful in forcing you to create a finished, professional product. Dr. Jack was very accommodating and insightful- all qualities you could want from a professor.

Dr. Jack is the best professor I have had thus far. Her lectures are relevant, and I know I will use a lot of the skills she taught in class beyond my undergraduate career. She gives helpful feedback on every assignment, and her time management is impeccable. If you get the chance to take a class with her, 100% do it. She also teaches ENGL 300I!

This professor is super easy so if you want an easy A take her classes. She has no idea what shes talking about though and lectures are airy with no context. I havent learned a single thing. The class is extremely easy though so I guess I cant complain.

This class was fantastic. I had a ton of fun, and learned a LOT about both online culture and rhetoric. Dr. Steptoe was very understanding, and the grading agreement was flexible. The class is based on 3 major projects, and weekly discussion posts. I had genuine debate with some of my classmates. 100/10.

This was an enjoyable and laid-back class. There is not a lot of homework, and there are no quizzes or exams. She was very accessible outside of class and made sure that you were caught up and doing well in the class. Overall, I really enjoyed this class and encourage you all to take it with her!

She's very nice and understanding when it comes to assignments and projects. The curriculum is straightforward and grading is set up for your success. Your effort translates directly to your grade, so just being on top of your work will get you an A.

Engl 117 was awesome! The curriculum was silly at times but Professor Steptoe did an excellent job at taking the content and helping us apply it to things we see online and see patterns in it. I would absolutely recommend this class!

The feedback that I received on my essays was very constructive and you could tell that she put a lot of effort in them. This class was a super fun and laidback class that should be easy enough to get an A- or higher.

I can not believe this was her first time teaching the class. It was AMAZING and very relevant to all of us since we all were able to participate. This assignments were cool took because you get to talk about all the brainrot you want and some of the discussion posts were fun to think about too.

Probably one of the funnest classes I've taken at UNC. I enjoyed the meme topics covered in class, and I actually had a good time writing the two essays required for the class. Overall, I would highly recommend this class.

This class is genuinly easy to get an A in as long as you pay attention for 50 mintues. She plays the brainrot to keep your attention for you. As long as you actually respect her and not play NYT games all of class youll do fine.

This class is really fun and really let you talk about your own experiences. Just pull out your own phone and you have the content you need for class. The topic also allows for a lot of introspection.

The class only has 2 essays (easy and she lets you redo them) and the rest of the assignments are fun. You get to make a video essay at the end which is really fun. There is a discussion post every week which has interesting questions and gets you thinking (there isnt a work requirement to it so you can actually think so it isnt that stressful).

There were only 2 essays in this class, which were both graded relatively easily. It is extremely hard to do bad in this class, unless you genuinely have no respect for the teacher. Do the assignments and you'll get an A.

She's one of the best professors in the english department. We only get 2 pretty short essays assigned to us and she gives great feedback on them that genuinely helps us improve our essay-writing skills. She allows you to revise the essays and get full points back based on the comments you get. She's really nice and wants you to get an A.
Though this class is super easy to do well in, be prepared to put in the work. Please don't goof off on assignments, because the professor genuinely cares about her students doing well.
This was one of the few classes I actually enjoyed taking this semester. Classes were fun and engaging, and the professor was willing to work with us.

She's actually a really nice teacher that lets us interact with current brainrot media. The topic in and of itself is interesting but I think she makes it a lot more interesting by not making it a bunch of memes. There are a decent amount of student led presentations so the class is what you make of it.
I took this class thinking it would be a chill class, but the teacher got mad at me for doing other work in the class. She gave me a C+ because of this, for an otherwise easy class.
One of the best teachers I've ever had. I learned a lot, but this class didn't stress me out and even though the films were a little odd, I enjoyed this course.

Rose is a caring prof who wants the best for her students. She is very flexible + understanding. Her class isn't too tedious — about a film per week w/ a short analysis, a video essay project, and 2 papers. The films were interesting and got me out of my comfort zone. Her lectures are also very informative and help when you're wanting the film.

Awesome professor. Very understanding about extensions and wants you to succeed. Her ENGL105 section focused on film, so prepare to watch about a movie a week outside of class. Do your assignments according to the rubric and you'll be set. Hardest assignments are the unit projects (only three), but as long as you don't procrastinate you're fine.

very understanding and willing to accommodate to anything you have going on. she is willing to give extensions and any help you need. her assignments were easy and helpful at the same time. great professor

Dr. Owain was a great professor! My only issue was that he is sometimes hard to reach via email. You do also only get two absences before your grade is impacted, which is annoying, but overall very minimal work outside of class. Most of the time is spent workshopping short stories! Great option for an FC-create.
Love him. Recommend. Good person who wants you to succeed and is available to help!

He sent me this email without knowing I am mentally ill and have been struggling with school. "I noticed that you were absent on the first day. Please drop as soon as you can. As policy, I do not over-enroll and the waitlist is 18 people deep and I am sure others would love to join this class." I dropped because of this. I found this to be rude.

I took this online/asynch over the summer and it was just okay for if you want to actually improve your writing. Not much work, easy for a quick credit or A. His videos were short, simple, & a bit awkward. He gave basically no feedback (it all came from our group mates) and the canvas was a mess. Decent bit of reading followed by peer discussions

Prof Owain is amazing, super enthusiastic and cares a lot about students. He fosters a safe environment in class and makes students feel comfortable sharing their thoughts. The assignments are really enjoyable and you edit them as a small group with peers. Pro Owain gives incredibly thoughtful feedback and is all around great, cannot recommend more

Very chill professor, highly recommend taking a class with him. Participation matters a lot, but it is easy to talk in class. Three papers and one final group project. He cares a lot and wants to see you succeed!
Just a chill guy. Fun and easy class to take, attendance matters a lot.

Take Professor O'wain! In ENGL 138, there were 3 easy papers, 1 final group project, and participation (30% of grade but just talk once or twice a class you will be fine). I enjoyed coming to class everyday and highly recommend taking any class you can with Professor O'wain!

Take ENGL 138 with Matt if you can! He's amazing; hilarious, gives great feedback, and creates a fun atmosphere. The class consists of three creative essays throughout the semester and a group project, but they're all interesting topics. Lots of workshopping in small groups.
Very caring and knowledgeable professor. Will take the time and work with you to improve your writing and ideas. Class time could be repetitive, but we always had fun conversations.
Best professor I have had at UNC! She is so caring and willing to work with students. Tons of reading but all of it is very interesting

Professor Lithgow focuses on students' improvement. She will sit down and provide as much feedback and guidance as needed. Classes were very participation-driven and focused on students sharing and discussing their thoughts on readings. She gives extensions and is understanding of extenuating circumstances.

Dr. L is the BEST! Although her ENGL 105i class comes with a relatively heavy workload (assignments every two days), it really pushes me to work hard on my writing. As long as you put in the effort on your essays, you're guaranteed to get a great grade. Her feedback is incredibly detailed and helpful. HIGHLY RECOMMEND if you really wanna learn

Do NOT take this class if you want to get your papers back on time, she STARTED grading half of the assignments we were given a week after LDOC, so you will have no clue what your grades are going to be. Even though she seems to really care about you and your success, it is ridiculous and I will never be taking another class with her.

Dr L is an icon. I'm so glad I chose to take 105i because it forced me to work hard and think critically. Dr L was flexible with deadlines since she really just wants to make sure you are submitting your best work. I would recommend taking a course with her if you can.

This is my second Lithgow class, and honestly, I'd take one of her classes every semester if I could. She is so sweet and goes above and beyond to get you helpful feedback to help you improve. This class isn't an easy breezy ENGL 105, but you learn SO much and it prepares you to write like a college student. 110% recommend.

Dr. Lithgow is one of the best professors at UNC. You have to put a decent bit of time and effort into her class, but she makes it worth it with her amazing teaching and clear desire for her students' success.
she's my goat

I loved ENGL 121 with Dr. Lithgow! The class is entirely discussion-based (only one paper), so as long as you do the readings, participate, and take the class seriously, you'll do just fine. Dr. Lithgow is flexible and does her best to work with each student throughout the semester. I enjoyed class discussions and would 100% take Dr. Lithgow again.

Though this class was very difficult, Dr. Lithgow made it worth it! I couldn't recommend her enough. SHe really cares about her students giving extensions with no questions asked. She is a slower grader but she gives so much commentary on how you can improve. I learned a lot in this class and am already signed up for another Lithgow class!

Dr. Lithgow is genuinely so fantastic. The class is incredibly enriching and useful, even for someone like me, a transfer student who had already done college english. Dr. Lithgow is so kind and willing to work with you on deadlines and your grade as long as you ask for help. Totally recommend!

Dr. Lithgow is without a doubt one of the best teachers I've ever had! It is clear how much she cares about her students and she goes above and beyond to meet with us one on one about papers and give specific feedback. Classwork is worthwhile with a clear end goal - 2 feeders and a final paper per unit. Highly recommend this class and Dr. L!

I'm so glad my first English class of college was with Dr. Lithgow! She may be a tough grader, but she gives A LOT of helpful feedback on ALL papers. She's very lenient on deadlines and is very open to meeting outside of class time to discuss classwork or feedback. Highly recommend taking her for ENGL105i-writing in humanities.

Absolutely love Dr. Lithgow as a person. She creates a welcoming, inclusive classroom environment and provides pages of feedback per draft/outline. She is also accessible outside of class if you want to discuss an assignment or life. However, this is the toughest ENGL 105i and has significantly more homework (most is useful, but some busy work).

Dr. Lithgow is a gem!! Her class seemed impractical if you have written academically but she still provides lots of amazing feedback that helps to improve your writing for college. Attendance is really important and there were times that it could bring your grade down. Three unit projects with lots of small "feeders" and she grades fairly!

Though Dr. Lithgow can be passive-aggressive and assigns a lot of homework, she provides excellent feedback and is more than willing to help you in any way outside of class. She is an interesting teacher, and I enjoyed her class. For English 105i, you should take her class as I have heard other English 105i professors are very difficult or boring.

Although I struggled at time in Dr. Lithgow's class because I was unfamiliar with research writing, she invested heavily in my success and it was clear that she cared greatly about each of her students. The assignments were often long and time consuming but I do feel that the payoff was 100% worth it

Although it can take a while to get feedback, the comments that Dr. Lithgow provides are extremely valuable. She definitely helped me become a better writer, and it is clear that she cares about her students. Dr. Lithgow definitely holds your hand through the writing process, but it never felt like she was dumbing anything down.

Such an amazing and kind professor! She gives extremely detailed and specific rubrics, so you know exactly what to do for an assignment. Expect to spend time completing work for this class, but all of her assignments have genuinely helped me after the class. She really makes an effort to get to know you and immerse you with other students. The best

If I could give her more positive accolades I would, 3 is not enough to fairly encompass her character. She is so kind and great at working with you. She works hard to have you succeed and only asks for a comparable effort from you. lessons are insightful. She cares about her job and her students- this will be one of the best classes you ever take.
I took his eng146 and liked it a lot! A big part of your grade is participation in small groups.
This class isn't easy but Prof. Peterson is funny!

His grading doesn't go by points, so everything in Canvas was just shown as "completed" meaning you don't know what grade you have in the class until the semesters over. Still, he's really nice and makes games studies interesting. If you wanna play some games, try to take his class.

Professor Peterson is an amazing guy and really cares about what he is teaching. I took him for his game studies class and I really enjoyed it. I am NOT a gamer but the class was still very easy. It's mainly group projects and essays, but every assignment was done step-by-step. We also always had a long time to do each assignment. I would take him.

Peterson's humor is very nerdy but funny. Lots of pop culture references in his lectures, so despite them being pretty long-winded, they were managable. His writing assignments were fairly easy and his section of the class was by far the easiest.
Very boring and basic class but since it's required he's great to take it with. Super easy grader and very flexible with missing classes and working around it.

IDST118 is a very boring and semi-difficult triple-I, but unexpectedly, I enjoyed Peterson's lectures the most. His assignments are usually rhetoric and analysis-based, so if you know how to write those assignments will help your grade in the class. His content is easy for quiz questions too.

Peterson, himself, is fine. His lectures are nothing special but he clearly knows his information. His assignments are not enjoyable nor are they helpful. The class itself is difficult and a poor representation of UNC's classes. The class is extremely difficult to recover from if receiving even a 70 on anything so I do not suggest.

He's nice enough, but can be a bit annoying. It all depends on what type of person you are, but sometimes I found his humor to be a bit off and it made it hard to take him seriously. He is a passionate guy, and his lectures were fine but nothing special. I wouldn't say never take him, but if the millennial humor style annoys you maybe avoid it.

He was an absolutely amazing professor. He cared both about the students and the curriculum. Being that the class I took had a large focus on climate change, he emphasized on taking care of ourselves in this difficult time. The final was a website of revisions of the 3 essays we were given feedback throughout the course. Loved this class!!

Professor Peterson is easygoing and makes english 105 a stress free class. Everything is graded on participation, including the three major projects, and as long as you put in a little effort you will get an A.
Lectures were boring. Lots of busy work but it was easily graded. Information hardly related to the course. Overall the course was very hard and boring. Hard to get an A.

As one of my friends described him, Dr. Peterson is "aggressively millennial". However, I really enjoyed taking his class this past semester. His section of ENGL105 is game studies specific, but I think he makes the couse accessible and fun for the average UNC student, not just gamers. We played games during classtime so automatic 10/10 rating.

In general, the class is challenging. DO NOT TAKE IDST 118 IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR AN EASY TRIPLE-I. It is uninteresting but difficult, which makes the entire experience insufferable. DO NOT TAKE IT FOR AN EASY A. IT WILL TANK YOUR GPA. Peterson seems nice enough, just a little behind on today's humor I'd say. He seems very kind.
Terrible and long lectures, humor sucks, gives really mid assignments also.

Prof. Peterson is awesome. The class is super easy. Three major projects (article, podcast, and research paper) that are broken up into small increments so they're really easy if you don't procrastinate. The final is a website with all three projects. Prof. Peterson is quirky, funny, and cares about his students a lot. Best ENG105 option

Professor Peterson has been my favorite professor at UNC so far, really understanding and funny! All assignments are graded based on completion, even the 3 projects (one per unit) you do across the semester. These 3 projects also form the "final exam" which is really just a website with your 3 projects revised based on feedback and a short bio.

Dr. Peterson took the essential parts of ENGL 105 as a FY requirement and created a course that isn't unnecessarily difficult. Primarily consists of 3 unit projects that can be completed w/o stress as long as you're consistent with progress and participating in class. Lenient with grading and understanding of things like mental health. Cool guy.

he is a good lecturer, created an environment in his classroom that encouraged creativity, and gave students flexibility to pursue topics that interested them in the course. this course was more workshop based and most assignments differed from what youd find in a typical english class (podcasts, videos, etc). he was also accessible outside class.

Took Prof. Peterson for ENGL105 and he was great! I'd highly recommend him for this course. Assignments weren't too demanding, but still interesting, and they were very fairly graded. Very funny personality and he genuinely cared about his students.

Hands down, one of my favorite professors ever. To describe Professor Toufas is to call her incredible and intentional. Despite having her ENGL 105 at 8 a.m, her charm, attitude, and care for students made me excited to come to class. And on top of that, she's actually hilarious. 110% take a class with Professor Toufas, you will never regret it. :)

Legit the best professor ever!! She truly cares about students' well-being and will work with you if you have questions/concerns. She is an easy grader and gives clear instructions for what is expected. Her lectures were kinda boring but they were manageable.
Great experience in her class. Super understanding and willing to work with you. Take Eng105 with her if you can!
The BEST English 105 professor!! If you can take this class with her please do! She was always making sure we weren't stressed, and had lots of accommodations.
Lexi is such an amazing professor! Please take English 105 with her if you can, she is so sweet and just wants all her students to do well. Great class, never stressful, couldn't recommend enough.
words alone cannot do this lovely lady justice. she must be experienced. amazing class amazing work amazing professor. they call her toufas cuz you wanna take her class twice. #thankyoulexi
Lexi is the GOAT, the sweetest lady ever. She's super laid back and is so understanding about everything. Best 105 prof ever.
LEXI IS A QUEEN! Take English 105 with her if you can it is the best. I have never laughed so much in a class and we never had a project that was not enjoyable. WE LOVE LEXI!!!!!
Lexi is coolest, most understanding, and fun professor EVER. She made ENGL105 a class that I actively looked forward to going to. She definitely understands her students and cares deeply about them.

Lexi was amazing. If you want an easy 105 class while still learning something I 100 recommend her. She is very sweet and understanding and only wants the best for her students. There is no homework only the projects that you work on throughout the class, and you have a week to finish each section. Easy class, great professor.
Super chill, super awesome, best 105 prof.

Lexi is the best ENGL 105 teacher ever! She is super sweet and cares about all of her students. Our class wrote Carolina Scientific article, gave a conference presentation, and created a podcast episode. There is no homework, you just have to go to class. I 100% would take another class with Lexi because I loved her so much! I highly recommend!

She is a nice person, but takes the class too seriously. Lots of homework and lots of essays, she is a hard grader. She does help and point you in the right direction, but save yourself the time and take a different teacher for ENGL-105, a lot of easier teachers out there.

This class definitely had a lot more work than some of my other friends with English 105 teachers that grade easier, but Professor Watlington tells you exactly what you need to get a good grade for each assignment and it's not too hard to get an A. She's very kind and creates a good vibe in the classroom. Good teacher!

Professor Watlington is very caring and the units of the class are interesting and give students room to explore their fields/interests. Her grading can be a little tough, but I still definitely recommend her.
I was actually in ENG 205 but option wasn't there. Save yourself and do not take her. She is a tough grader. She seems excited about teaching but she also seems to be on a power trip

I enjoyed this freshman english class. She gives clear instruction/rubric and feedback that makes it easy to correct things and improve grades. There are also extra credit opportunities. I would recommend!!

Professor Watlington is a tough, but fair grader who sets clear expectations about what she wants her students to accomplish. She's very organized and if you put in the effort, an A or A- is certainly obtainable. Nice lady.

Watlington graded tough but fair. Her feedback was very constructive and her rubrics were extremely clear making it easy to get good grades. She is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter and challenges you to become a better writer in a caring way and is accessible outside of class. I would recommend her for ENGL 105.

I went into the class comparing how hard the grading scale was compared to other asynchronous ENG105 classes. Watlington is a harsh but generous grader. Definitely had to utilize my writing skills and work hard to get an A, but there are opportunities to meet with her and gain extra credit. Getting to know her also allowed me to do better in class.

This class was taken asynchronously during summer. Professor Watlington gives great feedback. There is extra credit and points for participation. Compared to other friends that were in a different section of English 105 my class was harder but, this class made me a better writer and researcher.

Professor Watlington was a good professor. I wish the topics we picked were different, and Art museum visits not required, but overall a good professor who gives good feedback and understands what ENGL 105 is supposed to be. I would recommend taking her class, she fosters a great environment.
She's not bad. The topics she chose for our units though were bad. They were to complicated and excessive and overall didn't really make me a better writer.
He likes to listen to himself talk, will ramble for the entire lecture. He will argue with you if you disagree, so often better to stay quiet. The class is easy just painful.

Talks a lot lol. Also likes the show Succession. He rambles, so lectures can be boring, but worth it for an easy A. He gives unlimited tries on every single assignment and offers feedback. Is almost always available. Super friendly, but don't be surprised if he cusses.

Joe is a nice guy, but rambles about unrelated stuff for most of class and frequently goes off track so I didn't get much out of his lectures. He is very friendly and tries to connect to students, but goes over the top sometimes. Almost all in-class work is group work, but rarely is it productive. He is a lenient grader and is very accessible.

Oh my god this man does not shut up. Overly obsessed with succession (literally made us watch in class for 2 weeks). He starts arguing with students and makes class so boring. With that being said, the class is really easy and he offers unlimited revisions on all work if u turn it in on time. He is a easy teacher but he is just tweaking out 24/7.
Really sweet, just wants you to participate. Allows for resubmission until desired grade. Is all over the place but has a kind heart and it comes from a good place.

Joe's a funny dude, but can be a little difficult at times. Very unorthodox teaching style, you'll learn more about people and communicating than writing. Just relax, and you'll get an A, guaranteed, although not work-free. Don't try and argue if you believe you're  right, you won't win even though you are right. The writing's a joke, but not hard.

Joe is a super laid back and energetic teacher. He's fun to talk to outside of class, and he literally makes it difficult to not get an A in the class. I will say, he will not hold back at calling out students in class for bad takes, so he may offend some students.

Joe gave us his number and was available 24/7. He truly cares about his students and was willing to put the work in for everyone to receive an A. Class was low-stress and his rule is that you can revise an assignment infinite times until you get your desired grade. He sometimes seemed frazzled or unorganized but overall amazing guy.

Joe is honestly a great guy who has a great and genuine personality. His class is conceptually interesting and you will learn how to make rhetorical connections. However, if you are a person who values organization, this class might stress you out. This class was different every day I went which made me enjoy it better but some did not.

This class is an easy A. I took the 105I in social sciences. Even though it was easy, I suggest you find another professor. Joe is all over the place with requirements and it was never really clear what we were supposed to be doing both in and out of class. I didn't learn a thing. Great guy though and seems to really care about his students.
Telegan is a pretty interesting and charming guy. Just make sure to do your work or he might snap at you, leaving the entire class petrified. True story. Great professor though.

Funny and animated, but somewhat volatile. Discussion is encouraged in class, but need to stand up for yourself and be assertive to get your points across. This is not the best class for learning how to write (and if that's a priority, don't take it), but it is a good class to learn how to make connections. He cares about students' well-being.

Joe was a great english professor especially for a first year class. He lets you revise as much as you want/need, and gives you a lot of flexibility when doing the unit projects. His lectures can be a little chaotic and the lesson plan changes but he does a good job communicating any changes made. Definitely take 105 with Joe if you can!

Joe truly cares about his students. Lecture can be a bit overwhelming at times with all the side tangents, but overall it's a good class & easy to get an A as long as you revise your work. We didn't write a single essay & instead recorded a podcast, wrote an annotated bibliography on a question of our choosing, & chose our own creative form.

Professor Joe was very interesting, most of the time you won't know what he's talking about but that's okay! He's really nice and makes class fun. Veryy easy A just submit things on time. Lets you redo assignments till you get the grade you want. Definitely take him for engl 105!

Mr. Telegan honestly made my first semester a lot more tolerable. I am normally very scared to talk to professors but he was extremely friendly and made the class super comfortable and safe. I would 100% recommend him for English 105! He is also generally an easy and reasonable grader and he made class participation fun.

Easily the best English teacher I've ever had, he's super passionate, cares a lot about his students, and talks often about the importance of mental health. His classes were engaging and super funny, I highly recommend taking English with Joe!!
sweet dude. lets you redo the assignments as many times as you want for a 100%. VERY passionate about his job.
Super easy. You get to redo any assignment as many times as you want as long as you turn it in on time. sweet dude. VERY passionate.

Joe is an AMAZING prof who makes the English requirement at UNC bearable. Classes were mostly lecture based but they were always interesting. He is very lenient with due dates and always willing to give feedback. Extremely accessible outside of class. If you have the opportunity to take ENGL105 with him, take it!!!

ENGL 259 is an improvisation class that fulfills my GE requirement and the screenwriting track. The class is fun and low-pressure. We practice improv in class and write weekly journals. There is no midterm or final. We have two formal theatre performances, and you can learn a lot from performing in public and developing comedy-writing skills.

He's so caring about us as people and our growth. Accessible outside class. He will push you HARD but it's worth it. Be ready for a lot of work, but know it's not pointless and all very thoughtfully designed. Great guy willing to go to bat for anyone, and well respected

Prof White takes your work very seriously and expects that you will too, but if you work with him your writing WILL improve a great deal. This class was a LOT of work but it hardly felt like work, it was all edifying and will stretch you in the best way. If you're willing to put in the effort to learn and grow, Prof White is a fabulous instructor.

Prof. White was a difficult professor, but if you are serious about poetry, he makes your writing GOOD, really makes you think more broadly than you might have coming out of an intro/intermediate classes. He is almost clairvoyant when he prescribes you individual readings, and he will make your poetry better with his challenges.

The workload is hefty, but it never feels like busywork. Prof White makes it clear that he cares about you as an individual and your personal artistic growth. His feedback is sooo helpful (def go to his office hours!) and he has definitely helped me to become a better poet! I would 1000% take a class with him again, and you should too!

The most fun course (because of the freedom in creativity and comradery amongst students) at UNC which students dont know about. Make sure your sketches conform to the prescribed grammar if you want their likelihood of being selected for the final script.  Just have fun and a blast! I promise you that you will never regret taking this course.

Had Ross for Gramorama. Really likeable guy and the class was probably the best class I've taken at UNC. Was sometimes frustrating when he would force a sketch to conform to a sketch's grammar rules in place of coherence or comedy, but overall he did a pretty good job leading us through the bizarre concept of a grammar sketch comedy class. 4.3/5.

He made every class as entertaining and open as possible, he is really funny and laid back. Although, the class is operated entirely out of Dropbox, and assignment instructions and turn in policies can get confusing. He is nit picky with feedback on weekly poems, but you get a 100 in the grade book just for trying.

It's very clear that Professor White deeply cares both for his craft and his students. He was always willing to communicate and work with me when I was facing some difficulties that semester, and he was very encouraging which was valuable as a beginner in poetry. Assigned readings were mostly engaging, though we didn't always get to them in class.

Don't take his class expecting a light workload-- you will write and read a LOT of poems. I enjoyed the assignments, however, and I can see a marked difference in my poem quality before and after this course. Professor White's lectures were very illuminating and had directly applicable advice for becoming a better writer.

ENGL 351 has a good concept and is so useful.Ross himself is not. He has unclear guidelines and rubrics, unclear feedback (if any), and a snarky and backhanded way of speaking to students in the discord. Ross acts like he wants his students to succeed and then boohoos when we don't but won't change a single dynamic of the course or his behavior.

Ross White is hilarious so lectures are never dull but he does expect everybody to be there on time to participate in in-class collaboration. It can be intimidating getting that much feedback on your original work but the environment he creates among the students is right for it and the structure of the course overall makes sense and is well done.

Ross has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. Attendance and participation are mandatory and I found his grading of our annotations to be strict but justified. His lectures were very engaging and you are given a lot of creative liberty.

IF YOU'RE SIMPLY A WRITER LOOKING FOR SOMETHING  DIFFERENT, TAKE 384! This class seems like a burden at first but is actually enjoyable once you make the podcasts. Make a few friends in class, workshop with the prof, do the assignments (the non-podcasts stuff weighs more than the episodes), and you'll get an A. He's meticulous but amazing!
Ross is a caring professor and genuinely wants his students to succeed. There are a lot of small graded assignments for this course.
Prof. White is so funny, so caring and his lectures are chock full of material that he teaches in a relatable way. He truly cares for his students and wants them to succeed.

Ross White is my least favorite professor. His grading was so unclear and he could never justify why I received such a low grade. I get that poetry is subjecting, but I don't think you should get a bad grade just because the professor "doesn't like it." 0/10 do not recommend this professor for anyone. He's also just rude.

I think it's strange to see Ross have negative reviews, but I realize they probably just come from people who took a class with him as a "gimme" which, although he teaches several niche classes, is not the attitude to approach with. Ross is easy going, flexible with due dates, but VERY good at his craft and expects students to care like we should.

This class was quite a burden yet I'd still take it again. It was a LOT of tedious work, but I learned a lot abt a niche topic w/ an amazing prof. He's strict about deadlines & details, but tried to cultivate a friendly atmosphere in class. He lectured me for not asking for help sooner (in a kind way). Genuinely wants students to succeed. Cool dude

Prof. Calvocoressi goes above and beyond for her students, is clear and communicative, and is very understanding. She is a sweet person and truly tries to ensure everyone grows in their poetry in whatever way she can.

God bless Gaby! I had the best time taking Intermediate with them, and I found myself walking away from the class feeling fulfilled and supported as a poet. They did have a tendency to ramble a little bit, but it was always interesting and engaging. They prioritized us as a class and community, and I would pay to take them again!

Gaby is amazing! I have only wonderful things to say about them. They are kind, understanding, and inspirational  not only a talented poet, but able to translate their skills into helping their students grow.

Gaby is such an amazing person and professor! I was nervous going into the class, but Gaby created an open and caring environment that allowed me to learn more than I thought possible and improve my writing exponentially! I was always excited to go to class, and it was easily the my favorite class I've taken at Carolina. Take a class with Gaby!

Gaby is one of the best and most talented professors I've ever had the honor of studying with. They are empathetic, enthusiastic, and go out of their way to be accessible and transparent out of class while maintaining healthy boundaries. I was terrified of poetry and left this class so creatively fulfilled and with a new, nuanced understanding.

One of the chillest profs ever. She is super understanding and as long as you try a little, you should get an A+. There were 3-ish units, each with around 2 smaller assignments leading to one big one, but it was all easy stuff. Maybe 1-2 hrs outside of class a week max.

Professor Weber was so nice and a really chill ENGL 105 professor! She was a really chill grader and I easily got a 99% in the class. If we had a break or long weekend, she insisted we didn't do ENGL 105 work. Overall it was about 2 essays and 2 presentations with little assignments throughout the semester. She never took attendance either.

BRO she had a vendetta against me because the only one who would get points taken off for stupid things. I met with her multiple times and she never changed how hard she graded. For example i said, "amount of people" and she said "you need to put number of people", and proceeded to take off 2/12 points... idk I was the only one with this problem

Doing the readings before class will make you do just fine. Most of them are short, but we also read 2 books during the semester. 1 open topic paper, 1 group project, 1 midterm, 1 exam. A few discussion posts and attendance checks. Very easy and to the point class. I would take her again if I could; she is very kind!

Dr. Weber was a great professor for ENGL 105. The class was three units, each with two small assignments and one slightly longer paper or presentation. Nothing required too much work, and she was reasonable with time to do work in class. She rarely took attendance, and didn't mind if you missed more than the allowed number of classes.

Joke of a class. Doesn't care if you miss as long as you say something in advance. Very easy to write papers, don't put a lot of effort into it. I got a 100 on everything and put minimal effort and used help. Presentations and such are super easy and low stress. This will be an easy busy-work class. Let us out of class early.

She was a very kind and supportive professor, who helped everyone perform well in her class. The kindest professor at unc, if you want to meet a very generous and kind person, definitely definitely definitely take her class!

Why difficulty 5.0? Cuz I hate discussions

Professor Weber was genuinely my favorite professor I've ever had at UNC. She truly cares for each and every one of her students and if I could have her teach every single one of my courses I would. Dr. Weber is one of the best professors!! She is so kind and caring, and is very understanding when circumstances happen. She is a lenient grader and encourages communicating with your peers. Professor Weber was by far my favorite teacher this entire semester! She is so kind, respectful, and she is an amazing educator. Great Professor, I truly recommend her!!!

Professor Weber is one of the kindest teachers to grace this planet. She cares about every one of her students and gives great feedback. She lets us go early most classes and is super lenient on grading. I recommend her 100%.

This class was very insightful about LGBTQ+ literature.  This was a nice class to take over the summer.  It was asynch and the workload was very doable. I would die for this woman. So sweet and has such a nice energy to her. Loved the content and we had 2 essays and a presentation but they were soooooo easy.

after reading the other ratemyprofessor reviews I thought: "oh it really can't be that bad."

she was fine just loud

These I classes aren't the most effective way to teach a subject - too many shifts between professors like whiplash but Prof Jones was very enthusiastic and passionate. Lectures were interesting at least.
Professor Jones is very disorganized but she is so passionate you kinda forgive her for it. I do wish assignments were graded in a more timely manner, though. Interesting subject matter.

This class was just boring and this professor was way too excited and emotional in the way she taught things. Hard to follow and called out students at times. Don't recommend.
The ideas courses are terrible, but I actually found Dr. Jones to be fun to listen to in lecture - she's passionate.
If you want a boring professor, then Dr. Jones isn't going to be for you. Her enthusiasm for this subject is second only to her knowledge about the material. Great class, great professor.

Professor Moskal is incredibly knowledgable in her field and is always willing to answer questions, inside or outside of class time. I've had Professor Moskal twice now and she's one of the sweetest professors I've encountered. Her impeccable memory and devotion to her area of study makes her lectures truly captivating. Very sweet and KNOWS her stuff. Her memory is insane! Assignments were unique and fun (expanded my horizons). No canvas page so it was sometimes hard to keep up with deadlines/assignments. I had Professor Moskal for my 400s level class a few years ago. She valued student input greatly. I have 0 idea how she has won awards because she is legitimately awful. She has no Canvas page and an unclear syllabus that has been changed many times. Professor Moskal is the most incoherent professor I've ever had. She often was late to class or cancelled class 30 minutes before it began. Her tests and quizzes are based on extremely specific information that she maybe mentioned once in class. Never take this professor.

Moskal is overall an okay professor, but the negatives definitely outweigh the positives. Her final required an insane amount of studying and we were not given study guides. The most disorganized, difficult, self-conflicting, unclear, professor I've ever had. so unorganized and missed class several times throughout the semester, final exam was just random facts about authors she expected us to memorize, 3 total grades throughout the semester weighted about the same (2 papers and a final exam). DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS OR PROFESSOR.

Professor Moskal initially seemed like a knowledgable, caring professor. However, this dynamic shifted as we progressed into the semester. Professor Moskal is a gem. She's not out to fail anyone, and has easy tests and very clear grading criteria. Highly recommended.

Dr. Hammer is the most dedicated teacher I have ever met. He is very willing to spend time on us. Outside the knowledge of writing, he provides really cool advice on pre-med career (we should still have our own opinion though). I love him and hope him good health.

Dr. Hammer is one of the best professors I've had at UNC! He truly cares about his students and creates opportunities to succeed both in and out of class. Honestly, I'd say the course wasn't super difficult as long as you put in the effort, but the work can be a little time consuming and hard to understand at first!

Dr. Hammer is one of the most intellectual professors you will meet at UNC. If you're taking his 105i Health and Medicine, he'll try to scare you out of it, but don't be fooled. Dr. Hammer is a VERY intense person who cares a lot about this class and his students. He gives long and difficult writing assignments and will not be afraid to rip you apart. Dr. Hammer clearly cares about his students. Additionally, as a premed student, he sets you up with useful resources that will help you for medical school. Really funny and nice guy. He has a tough-love style of teaching, but if you put the effort into his class, it will not go unnoticed in your grades. Would only recommend for a certain kind of student. The hardest 105 section for sure, but if you put in the work, you'll learn a lot. He's scary at first, but when you get to know him, it's clear he cares about his students' success (+ very funny). Provides tons of outside support (peer mentor, free tutors, office hours). Participate in class!!!!
A lot of work genuinely spent hours on this class every week, but you will learn so much. Most helpful class I have taken, and Hammer is actually really nice when you get to know him.

Oh Dr. Hammer, from the moment I stepped into your classroom I knew this was going to be either the best or the worst class I have taken. Absolutely hilarious. The funniest professor I have ever had in my time as a student, not just in college. Dr. Hammer is extremely intelligent and a fantastic public speaker and presenter. The most dedicated professor I've ever meet. He always want to help students, always welcome everyone to his office hour. Provide useful advice for pre-med students. Very humourous and insightful. I respect him.

Dr. Hammer is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. If you're taking 312, be prepared for a lot of speaking! He gives plenty of feedback, but you need tough skin for what he has to say about your presentations. He makes it easy to build a class community, also go to his office hours! He has high expectations, but not hard to keep up with.

Boy oh boy where do I even begin. Dr Hammer....I have looked up to him ever since I first met him. The way he lectures and strikes passion into our minds. I wish it were possible to freeze time so I would never have to watch him retire. And now he's getting older, but still the goat, my goat. Thank you Doc. You changed the game of English.

Get ready for public speaking in this class! The hardest part about this class is overcoming fears to speak, joke, and more in front of your peers. No matter what direction your career will go, being able to communicate clearly to others is always a helpful skill to have.

Dr. Hammer is not for sensitive or lazy people, but he cares about his job and his students, and I can't say I have ever had a professor/teacher like him before. Dr. Hammer sets you up for success, and every pre-med student should take him if they can. His class is hard, and is a lot of homework, however, it is entirely effort-based. This is the best class that I have taken at UNC,would recommend 100%. Do no take if you are not serious about pre med,it will require a lot of time but at the end it will be worth it. He is a great prof. Don't be afraid to go to his office hours.

Dr. Hammer is definitely one of the most influential professors I've had. He cares about the wellbeing of his students and is extremely educated about the medical field. His class can be difficult conceptually, but I feel like I've grown as a writer because of it. As long as you participate in class and GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS, you can end with an A

Dr. Hammer is an amazing professor and person in general. The smaller class sizes in 105i allow for a fun learning environment. The class is a decent amount of work but it is all beneficial, and the one-on-one TAs are great resources. Definitely take this class if you are interested in pre-med.

I really enjoyed Dr.Hammer. Highly recommend this class, its a lot of work but your writing will improve greatly. He is very accessible outside of class. You also get your own TA who can help you with all of your work. Again such a great class sad it's over.
She uses a grading contract, and the rubric for all assignments is extremely clear. There is little work over all and if you just go to class and do the assignments then you'll get an A.
Great ENGL 105 prof! We ended the semester early, which was great. The coursework was a little annoying but nothing terrible, as long as you do the work and show up to the oral exam, you'll get an A.
The easiest ENGL105 teacher that I have heard of. Very easy class. Take
Took her English 105 in Fall 2025, the easiest English 105 professor, class ended a month earlier, and as long as you do the work, you will get an A. Also very nice and helpful
She is by far the best English 105 professor.

Took freshman english with Shelby last spring and was hands down the chillest class I could have imagined. If you have any grasp on analytical writing and are willing to jump into a writing and verbal feedback heavy class, you will be fine. Made expectations very clear for each and every assignment to get an A and made all Friday classes async!
chill af she canceled every friday class and replaced it with easy discussion post

professor jackson is amazing!! she is super kind and understands that this is a first year class. she does contract based grading and is very easy as long as you meet the requirements. she always is super kind and meets with her students one on one. i would take her class again in a heartbeat. attendance is optional and i rarely had homework.

She understands this class is a first year requirement. She approaches every single student and gives feedback during class. EASY + KIND ENGL 105 professor! She is always available for feedback and structures her classes so that students can get the assignments done (you get over a week to write a couple paragraphs) and she will discuss with you where you can improve. She's younger so she gets the class really well, even brought us treats on the last day! Take her class!

This class was a Lawyer Processing Course for Law. She treats you like you are in a high school gives "busy work" that does not help with the overall class's purpose. Professor Viscomi definitely comes off as a bit gruff at first, but he really cares about his students. The course material is fascinating; Blake's works, along with the aspects of popular culture surrounding them, are quite inspiring.

Professor Viscomi scared me at first, but as I took his class, it is incredibly evident that he cares about helping you learn Blake. He's a truly special professor.

I cannot express how much I loved this class. Yes, Professor Viscomi will tell you when you is wrong and he does very much talk at you, but he actually knows everything about William Blake. Class can be a little boring... but it is interesting and you don't have a lot of work. There are discussion posts throughout the week and a few essays.

I loved Dr Viscomi's class and learned a lot! He's definitely intimidating & expects a lot out of his students. Classes are lecture-based; you read a survey of each of the romantic poets in succession. You are expected to know some basic biographical information & dates of the various authors and their works, which can feel excessive/hard at times.

Dr. Viscomi definitely wants to (and does) come off gruff but he's an understanding and reasonable person. Content is not too difficult, be ready for lots of lectures. Grading is fair, he mostly grades on effort and time investment with the content.

Prof Viscomi was slightly intimidating at first, but he's great! Responded to emails super quickly and was willing to give feedback when asked. The class is mostly him lecturing about Blake, but the workload was light throughout the sem, no final exam, just a long paper. Take his class! He can be gruff, but he's very passionate & funny.

I was scared when I first registered for this class, and I didn't see many reviews for it on RMP. but I really enjoyed this class. There are two or three papers, and the final is a 8-10 page paper. I honestly had a lot of fun in this class. He is gruff, but he's sweet.

He's an amazing professor. Take this class with him!

He has so much knowledge and loves to share it. Class is mostly lectures, but they are interesting. He definitely comes off rough and honestly scary, but he does it to make sure that the people taking the course are truly interested. Eventually he lets his guard down and is actually pretty funny. Cares about teaching the history alongside the lit.

I loved Mr. Viscomi. What I appreciated about this class was that if you are consistently thoughtful in your work, you will be fine. He doesn't expect scholars of William Blake. He just wants students who are intellectually engaged and curious. He will tell you when you are wrong. Be on time to class, try, and you are in good graces.

dr. viscomi is VERY intelligent & his lectures, while long, are fascinating. a lot can be learned from him if you can get past his gruff exterior, which is admittedly off-putting (i wish he was more approachable). he doesn't ask for much & all assignments are extremely easy, just make sure to do them on time. fair grader, just wants to see effort.

Lectures are long and go off on tangents, but they are very rewarding if you listen. I found myself putting more care into this course than I expected because of how interesting it gets. Prof. Visconti is attentive to detail and highly critical. As long as you can handle that, and submit things on time as well as show effort, you will do well.

Joe is one of the most knowledgeable scholars in the field of William Blake and it shows in his classes. It's a small class, so he got to know each of us well. He grades extremely fairly, but expects his students to actually care about the course. If you're interested in the subject, you'll love his class, if not, don't take it.

Lectures are a little boring, but he knows what he's talking about. Assignments are not difficult and are graded. Syllabus is a little confusing but he is very responsive to emails and is flexible with sickness/absenses.
Kind of a strange guy but super chill and canceled our class at least once a week. Pretty much if you do the assignments you will get a A in class. I legit finished with a 100

He's a really great professor. I'm still in his class, but he's very kind, understanding, and funny. He assigns a good bit of work, but he always pushes back deadlines and gives us plenty of time. He also releases class early a lot. He relates well with the students and isn't a harsh grader, and covers important topics! Definitely recommend!

Very nice and laidback. Assignments were straightforward and did not feel like busy work. Class was 3 papers with 2 feeders each. Did lots of group work and feedback. Overall great experience, especially for a mandatory class.
Leo is a great, super nice guy. He made sure the class wasn't overwhelming, a fair grader as well if you review essays with him. Do work, show up to class, and you will be fine.

Mr. Collins is great and knowledgable in his field. His class is straight to the point and there is rarely any busy work. Class rarely went full time. He sometimes does not respond to emails. Participation matters - worth 15 points of your final grade. Wrote 3 papers. Easy grader and is understanding of personal conflicts with due dates.

Leo is awesome! He teaches what needs to be taught, and doesn't give busy work. he is very easy to reach outside of class and loves it when students go to his office hours. No one really loves a first-year English class, but Leo makes it fun, or at least bearable. 100% recommended Leo for ENGL 105.
