He's okay, he doesn't really respond to emails so you don't know if he got your message or not. Nice guy. Intimidating to talk to but is very knowledgable in the content. Younger teacher so he relates to his students more but overall could be better. Solid 5/10 teacher for the class

Can't say enough great things about Leo. He is such an easygoing guy and is extremely funny. He cares enough to learn everyone's names and makes class engaging even though he often has to pull teeth when asking the class for an answer. Assignments are super straightforward. If you participate, it goes the extra mile; he really appreciates it.
If you actually care about improving your writing, don't take this class. If you don't care, this class is so chill with barely any assignments and Leo cancels typically at least one class a week.

Leo is great. He knows a lot about writing and makes the class engaging by having lots of group work. The class is split into three chapters: pop science, social science, and literature. He had two extra credit opportunities which allowed you to score above a 100 for your grade. However, he was sometimes unorganized and repeated the same content.

I really enjoyed him for what ENGL105 is. Everybody knows that it is a somewhat silly but necessary class. He never made the class a burden and did exactly what was expected, nothing less nothing more. I enjoyed this and enjoyed him. He was a funny guy and made the class feel very close and I became friends with a lot of people. Take his class!

If you're looking for an easy A, Leo is the professor for you. If you would like a class where you learn a lot and is stimulating, he is probably not. He is super nice and funny but disorganized and lectures are boring. Love Leo but this class felt like a waste of my time.

Easy A, but if you like structure this is not for you. He is funny but chaotic. There are very few assignments and it's so easy it feels like you are wasting time showing up to class where he repeats the same thing as the previous class. Very nice guy though!
One of my favorite professors I've ever had. Very easy and not a ton of work.
Really cares about her students. Put the work in and you'll go far.

Mrs. King was a great professor and genuinely a really nice person. She gave very helpful feedback and allowed for resubmissions, which made the class both useful and pretty easy. Overall, it was a solid class and Mrs. King was a good prof to take 105 with.
Mindy is such a good professor! She is encouraging and supportive. If you can take 105 with her, do it!

Mindy was an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. She is super lenient on attendance although participation does impact your grade. You get 3 unexcused absences. There are open note quizzes with extra credit for the readings that are super easy in addition to 2 papers in place of exams. Class is discussion based.

I took Mrs. King for English 123 and she was amazing. She was very understanding and is willing to work with you if you have outside issues. The class was comprised of  discussions, weekly open note quizzes (and a midterm and final paper ( no exam). It was a very engaging class, just be ready to read so you can engage in active discussion
Very friendly

I took Engl 105i: Writing in Health and Medicine with Professor Buchanan King and I was very happy with the choice. The projects were really interesting, and she always took the time to go through the grading criteria, and if you met all the qualifications it was an automatic 100. This class was pretty easy, but at the same time I learned a lot.

Mindy is an amazing professor. The class is very easy if you do your assignments, which there are not many. She is very open to giving extensions and sometimes will let students decide due dates. There is a VERY clear grading criteria so it is very difficult to not get an A in the class. Just do the assignments, go to class, and participate.

Mindy is a caring professor with a clear grading contract making an A in the class easy. she encourages open class discussion and wants her students to succeed. She is very nice and tries her best to interact with the class while sharing her passion with the class. Easy A, and would recommend taking this professor

Extremely easy course as it is supposed to be a pre-english 105 class. We had 3 units and had to do a paper for each, but they were all extremely easy and a lot of time was given for each. The one thing I will say is that I was not challenged enough. It seemed a little too easy, but then again that is just the class.

Funny, smart, charismatic guy. This was one of my favorite classes at UNC. You read a short story before every class, then discuss it in class. You have a 10-15 page short fiction story (basically about anything you want) due at a certain point in the semester, where it gets workshopped in class. Chill A, cool subject, if you're taking 130 take him

Adam was an amazing professor and his class was very straight forward. You have small readings with short writing assignments before each class and then one final long story that you get to create. Show up to class, participate every now and then, and listen to feedback from your draft and you will get an easy A.

Adam was a super nice teacher and made the class feel very open for constructive criticism. My only complaint with him was his "Do Not" list for writing, but with the way he structured the class it never became an issue. He was flexible as well.

Adam is a super awesome guy, and he is funny and very passionate about his craft. The class itself is easy, but there is a lot of busy work. I really enjoyed the first few weeks, but it started to feel a little bit repetitive. You have to read a short story, write a paragraph, and later write discussion posts. Sounds super light, but gets tedious.

I enjoyed having Adam as the instructor a lot. I thought he was very knowledgeable on the subjective of creative writing and was incredibly passionate. The class itself is easy, particularly weighted on your submission of your own 10 page short story. He's very sarcastic, but I find him to be hilarious. I recommend!

Loved this class! Adam is funny, chill, and gives great writing advice!! Prompt and short story to read before each class. Final project is a short story. Shy people, FYI you have to share your story with class for a workshop - but everyone is nice and it is fun! It is an easy A if you show up and complete the assignments.

I've had Adam for three different creative writing classes in my UNC career, and he's been fantastic for all of them. He has a very different perspective and taste in literature than I do, which is actually super helpful in critique. He's respectful of everyone and genuinely wants students to write the best work they can. Also his twitter is great.

Adam is a very chill professor who wants to make sure you learn but is lenient on grading. Charasmatic and excited to be in the classroom. Just make sure you show up to class and do your assignments and you should be fine.

Adam was awesome -- super sarcastic sense of humor, so if you don't like sarcasm, don't take him. I thought he was hilarious. Makes everyone feel comfortable participating and class discussions are fun. We read "The Big Sleep" a murder mystery, so a fun read. Learned a lot as well! Gave most people a 19.2/20 on all assignments w/o feedback tho...

Adam was absolutely phenomenal this semester, and his class was without a doubt my favorite. He is hilarious and I feel like my writing has improved tremendously with his guidance. I had a few attendance conflicts, but he was very understanding with my situation. I can't say enough good things! Take his class if you can.

I liked this class. He didn't grade on quality of writing, but on participation. The "main" project was 10-20 pgs. you posted for critique. Homework: reading, prompts, critiques. I didn't deserve an A because I didn't do work on time (outside stuff), but I guess he appreciated me getting stuff in no matter how late it was. Super cool guy.

I would highly recommend Prof. Price's intro to creative writing class. The class is not graded on how well you can write, just on how much you participate and try to improve. Weekly readings and writings pushed me to become a better writer and critic. The workshops are super helpful too, and Prof. Price is an all-around great and chill professor.

This class was more work than I thought it would be but it is all very easy. Weekly writing workshop for short stories and no tests! I enjoyed that the class gave me motivation to write but I will say that this creative writing class does not let you do genre writing and expects you to focus on literary fiction which I was disappointed by.

I loved Adam's class. He's smart about writing and he's smart about the way he teaches it--everything feels important. He manages workshops so that they're always as constructive as they should be. Plus he's just a funny, interesting guy who clearly wants to see students succeed. Highly recommend!!

Professor Price's class is super easy to get an A in. The daily readings, workshop submissions, and daily assignments are not graded based on accuracy but on participation. Participation matters and keeping up with assignments are important in this course. It is a super fun class and easy to take.

Our textbook was a New Yorker subscription, and it was very cool to read contemporary stories while writing. His twitter is really funny, and he doesn't take himself too seriously which is really admirable. He cares about good writing, and he helps you hone a few great skills to prepare for Advanced fiction. I loved the assignments!

She was really chill, the class consisted of watching films and two people coming in with discussions questions about the movie for us to discuss. Shewouldstart of withlecture and thenwe wouldgo into discussion, butshewouldn't force peopleto participate although she did encourage it. Youcouldbring an indexcardfor everyquizandcheatsheet forthefinal.

This class is fairly easy, as there are not many assignments. The majority of the class is group projects, which make it more fun and interesting. Although class drags on and we often go off topic, Toni gives us everything we need to succeed in the class. I would definitely take this class for the english requirement.

Toni is a great and accommodating person, and cares for the wellbeing of us as students.  English 105i in the social sciences wasn't the most interesting for me as a STEM major, but Toni's class is very easy to follow along with regardless of your major.  I highly recommend!!

Toni just speaks at you in class with language complexity that many students can't understand. She is chill but her class drags on and is just to get the requirement done. As a stem major, I couldn't recommend it less. Maybe if you're business you would enjoy it more. Or if you know about Lord of the Rings, as that's all she talks about.

We covered all of the ENGL-105 curricula in the first month and spent the rest of the semester putting together conference papers. Toni gave us a lot of freedom, so I ended up having a great time researching a subject I had been interested in, but never had time to research before! If you have to take ENGL-105, take it with Toni!

They were not a great teacher to have first thing in the morning. Their lectures seemed to drag on and did not feel relevant to the PIT paper at all. But overall the class was easy, you do the assignment you'll get full credit. There is one big paper and you have to present it with a slideshow.

I loved Toni's class! She provides great feedback and was always super lenient with extraneous circumstances affecting assignments. I really felt like she cared about my success in and out of the classroom. The most caring professor I've had thus far at UNC. Also, the opportunity for the PIT conference in ENGL105 is one I wouldn't pass up.
GOAT

Very clear with instructions and gave really good advice. 3 main projects for the whole semester and was very accommodating. Considered the mental health and well being of students which was appreciated.
Loved her class: grading was gentle, few large writing assignments, lecture heavy

The single worst instructor I met, and it wasn't close. I am 100% certain she isn't actually interested in teaching. It's obvious in everything she does. Doesn't meet students where they are, refuses to clarify anything in question. Snide, irritable, impatient. Uses the post for research trips on the University's dime, probably. "Sublimely" awful.
My least favorite class I've taken in English at UNC.

Professor was unprofessional and unduly cruel to students. Expected us to have a ton of knowledge about philosophy before the class even started and was awful at explaining things/teaching. She could be dismissive of student concerns and had very little empathy. Take any other professor in English. If you have to take her classes, switch majors.

Assigned reading is at least half gobbledygook. Her idea of explaining difficult parts of the readings is to read it again, but slower, tracing the sentences with her finger. Very into metaphors. Couldn't explain how to tie a shoe without referring to Hegel. Aloof. Very ivory-towerish. Pick literally any other professor. Don't say I didn't warn you

The grading made no sense and you had no idea where your grade was almost the entire time. She was intimidating and unapproachable. The final exam lasted 45 minutes beyond the 3 hour university limit; we were given only a 5 minute break to use the bathroom. I saw 3 people cry in her class. I did enjoy the subject but will never take from her again

Class was titled "Literature and Race." Thought we would be reading books about race, but instead focused solely on the Black Lives Matter movement. Not surprising at UNC, but was pretty obviously indoctrination. Differing viewpoints about complex political topics were not encouraged. Readings were mostly philosophy-based.

This class was listed as a literature and cultural diversity class, but once we got the syllabus it was titled Blackness and Sublimity: W.E.B. DuBois, Anti-Racism, and the poetic sublime II. Everything was focused on the sublime and DuBois,not diverse novels. and grading was tough.There was a 7 page paper and an oral presentation due for the final.

Nice person, but teaching style is inaccessible and hard to follow. Some assigned readings are difficult. She will never explain them in a way you will understand; just hope you eventually grasp it. Refers a lot to Hegelian philosophy, so it helps to know about that. She is very big on metaphor (wrote a book about metaphor in Du Bois). Not easy.

Prof Fisher is not a professor to take if there are other prof options for a class. She insists on using inane jargon during answers to questions, resulting in even more confusion. The topics discussed during class are irrelevant too. Do not take a class with her.
Brace yourself for a lot of reading. She is a slow but tough grader.

Fisher takes forever to grade assignments; it will be around a month and a half to two months to get a five page paper back. She does not take the time to explain concepts simply either. Instead, Fisher repeats the ornate language from the text. She is, however, very passionate about the material, but that does not make it any less difficult.

I supposed Professor Fisher is better in other courses, but to echo the other CMPL 251 reviews, she is the most despicable professor I've ever had. She uses ornate and complicated language for introductory topics which makes them much harder to pick up. She also takes months to release essay grades so there is no room for growth and improvement.
Great choice for 105!
She is a great professor! She is also a graduate student so she understands if you can't make an assignment by the deadline and she will work with you.

Her class lectures are very easy to understand, and each class provides educational insight. She is very lenient with grading and will make any changes to the rubric if necessary. She is also humorous and will add in on class discussions. Her class does include group projects, so if that is something you like, definitely take this class.

I thought Prof. Bassard was really caring and passionate about teaching. She is very genuine and wants  a lot of participation from students, which is understandable. Good ENGL105 to take for freshmen, and she will answer any questions you have.

She was so nice and supportive! You should go to office hours because she will help so much with your essays! She is also really funny and personable. The class is mostly participation and group work (other than 2 essays). I would definitely take this class with her again because she helped me grow as a writer!
Not only did she let us have fun in class and have tangential discussions, she actually joined in herself! Super understanding of any issues and made English fun. Would definitely recommend!

Prof Bassard is very knowledgeable and clearly cares about her students. She is incredibly understanding if you need an extension on an assignment every now and then and always has available office hours if you need help. The class heavily relies on the unit projects which can be lengthy but doable.

Prof. Bassard really tried to make class interactive and fun. You write a lot of papers but she is a very fair grader as long as you put citations pretty much after every sentence. Also, we had to buy the Tar Heel writing guide which we used exactly once, so I wouldn't recommend it. Very chill class overall and an easy A.
She really cares about her students and does a great job teaching this class. Pay attention to her instructions about citations and you'll be totally fine.

Very charismatic and understanding professor. She's not a bad lecturer and I had a great time doing the projects throughout the semester. I do wish we did less group assignments though, but that may just be me. I never felt like I had to worry about a bad grade. Although, she was a tad unclear about citations a times.

Professor Bassard was funny, understanding, and fun to have as a professor! The class often involved group work, always done in a relaxed way. She was flexible when it came to extenuating circumstances, and I always looked forward to class

Bassard really made an effort to be the best teacher she could be. She was open to feedback about her class and listened to students comments. She would even change assignment rubrics and timelines in response to student concerns. That said, she was a bit underprepared to teach the ENGL 105 course. I think she will get better with practice.

Prof. Bassard really wants to see her students flourish academically. She was very understanding when it came to extensions and was a fair grader. She always made sure we understood the class material and was always willing to help with any questions. Definitely one of my nicest professors!

Professor Bassard is amazing! She has really cool activities, and she gives us plenty of time in class to finish work so you really shouldn't have any homework. Her grading is also very fair, and if you bomb something, she lets you resubmit and averages those grades. GO TO THE WRITING CENTER! You get extra credit on your papers!

Prof. Sabelawski is a very kind and relatable teacher. She gives a bit of busy work but nothing a UNC student shouldn't be able to handle. She's very understanding and is very easy to get along with. I looked forward to this class every session! Take English 101 with her if you want an easy A and an enjoyable experience!

I LOVED erica. She was very ADHD for sure but she was just as caring and a super easy grader. Technically engl105 has an attendence policy but if somethings up she will let you skip. Her mantra is that its just ENGL105, no one shouldn't get an A. There is a lot of busy work though, not hard just takes some effort. But no essays!

TAKE HER CLASS. She is so nice, chill, and funny literally I do not care if you're taking 105i and it's not in your preferred discipline she is so amazing. The environment is social and encouraging and the class overall is amazing with her I very highly recommend.

Erica is quite possibly my favorite teacher at UNC so far. Not only is she the most relatable human being on the planet, she's also really kind and extremely lenient with extensions. The best advice I can give to those who will have her is to TALK TO HER, she loves when people participate and the nicer you are to her, the nicer she'll be to you.
Simple class, very understanding, interesting person, great personality. Heavily recommend.

She is the best professor I have ever had in my life. She is incredibly relatable, funny, caring, intelligent, and sarcastic. She is so real and I honestly wished she continued teaching. People like her genuinely inspire me, and she has no idea how much she positively impacted my life. Easy courseload, and I actually learned the most in this class.

Erica is fun and flexible around your schedule and needs while actually teaching something. If you eng for busi, you will walk away with a cover letter, two resumes, a business idea (pitch and plan), as well as a great relationship with your classmates. Lots of projects and discussions. THIS CLASS IS EASY AND ALSO WORTH YOUR TIME
Super relaxed class but she will also provide help if you need it and she is super flexible; assignments aren't too bad and she doesn't grade too harshly. Just try and you'll be fine!

Prof. Erica Sabelawski is one of the best instructors I've ever seen and is flexible with assignment deadlines. She focuses mainly on teaching students how to write professionally and is accessible outside the class. One of the most noticeable features of Prof. Erica is that she uses idioms a lot and all the time.

Erica Sabelawski is awesome!! If you have the opportunity to take English 105 with her, do it! She is so caring and gracious. If you need extra time or help she will give it to you. The last thing she wants to do is make your life harder. Also, she is hilarious and has very clear grading criteria which I found extremely helpful. You will love her!

I absolutely adored having Erica as my instructor this semester. Even though she doesn't take attendance, I always showed up just because I loved being in her class. She is super funny and personable, and she truly cares about her students. The assignments are not difficult and she is very flexible with deadlines. I cannot recommend her enough.
She was so lenient, you literally just have to show up submit your assignments and you will pass this class.
Professor Rowen is incredibly kind. This was an enjoyable course and I cannot recommend taking ENGL105 with her enough.

An excellent, easy teacher for ENGL 105. You don't have to write any essays, just do projects that allow you to learn more about the resources, and they are as fun as you make them. Super accessible, easy grader, just follow her feedback and you will excel.
She was a great teacher and I learned a good amount of stuff in the class. I never felt overworked in the class and it was a chill A as long as you do the work. Take English with her
Take her if you can. Truly a nice person who wants you to succeed. She gives extensions and is available if you need any help so class is very manageable for someone adjusting to college.

Leslie definitely made ENGL 105 as bearable as possible. She is super understanding with extensions and absences and gives great feedback on assignments. The assignments build up to each unit project and the way she lays out the course is super helpful. Every lecture made the assignments easier and I never felt like I was just doing busy work.
Professor Rowen was so kind and really wanted us all to do well. She was really good about providing constructive feedback, and making the grading criteria very easy to understand before hand.

Leslie is one of the nicest, funniest people I've ever met. She knows engl 105 is a gen ed and something which doesn't need to be her students' top priority. Her assignments aren't too hard and she is always available to help outside of class, give extensions, and respond to emails. She grades quickly and not harsh at all. 1000/10!

Rowen is easily one of the best professors I have had at UNC thus far. She was super helpful and organized, and also made the content and unit projects interesting. She gave great feedback on assignments and was flexible with due dates. Overall, she is a genuinely nice person who cares for her students. I looked forward to days I had her class!
super accessable and caring to student's needs
Prof, Rowen was excellent! She was very flexible with deadlines and did her best to make each project/unit interesting and unique.

Professor Leslie genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well.She gives extensions for most assignments as long as you email her.Her lectures are fun and she gives you a good grade as long as you show up to class and do a decent job on the assignments.She assigns a manageable amount of work and is very helpful. Highly recommend her!

Professor Rowen is the nicest teacher I've ever had. She is extremely personable and loves to joke around with her students. That being said, she is an incredibly difficult teacher to have for ENGL105 (relative to others). There is lots of homework comparatively. If you hate english, take an easier teacher; if you like english, take it with Leslie.

Take her! Absolutely amazing she really cares for her students and it is very easy to earn an A if you turn everything in on time. She uses grading contracts so if you meet all the requirements you can get the grade you desire. Super nice, projects are engaging and she provides clear and constructive feedback.

Professor Kubli is kind. She was always accessible and willing to help. It is clear that she cares about her students. The projects were not too hard and you got to choose what you wanted to write about for all of them. The class is contract grading, so if you do the work and go to class you will get an A.

She is the best. I hope she stays a teacher because she has enthusiasm and the smarts to back it up. Such an easy class and not too easy where it was boring. If you're checking rate my prof. to see if she's a good teacher, the million 5/5 reviews should tell you YES

She is amazing and super flexible whenever you need her to be. very very easy and straight forward class but also super interesting. The class is what you want it to be because every project is very personalized and targeted to your interests. HIGHLY recommend her!
Super easy and straightforward class. Assignments were interesting and I enjoyed how diverse each project was. Contract based grading, so you will get an A if you do your work.
Sold pick for english 105. Puts in a lot of effort which I appreciate. Not her fault the class is boring

I definitely recommend Ms. Kubli for ENGL 105. The assignments for the class are actually interesting and she is a super fair grader. She's also very forgiving if you need an extension or extra help for an assignment.
Very solid professor for Engl105. Assignments were clear and there was plenty of time to do them. Class time dragged on at times. I would recommend.

Interesting projects, and a unique contract grading system alleviates a lot of the pressure to do everything perfectly. Super nice and fun to talk about literature. Does a good job of making the class easy but still allowing the student to learn things, which is optimal for a gen ed.

I like Ms. Kubli very much. This professor is very empathetic and down to earth, and just wants to bring out the best writer in all of us. On most assignments, she leaves feedback on what you do well and includes what you could improve on. She also does contract grading, where you pick what grade you want and she gives you the requirements for it.
She's literally so amazing and her contract grading scale is amazing. She also really helps you improve as a writer as she leaves clear feedback on everything.

Prof Kubli is the sweetest person ever. She so obviously cares about her students and truly wants each person in her class to do the best they can. She's so fun to chat with and does her best to make the projects engaging, fun, and helpful. Loved her and I'm sure you would too! She also has an awesome contract grading system.
She's amazing!
Very kind and cares about students. Writing of course but no final exam, perfect professor for 105

Prof Kubi is one of the best professors I have! It is clear that she cares about the mental well-being of her students just as much as making sure that we are learning. She gives you a very clear grading contract, responds to emails promptly, and gives detailed and fast feedback on assignments. If ever given the chance TAKE A CLASS WITH PROF KUBLI!

She is honestly the sweetest instructor I've had since coming here. You get to set your expectations on what grade you receive with her and she checks up on her students, too. You have to write, but it's English, and assignments are fairly spaced out. Also, she lets you attend in-person or virtually. I would definitely recommend taking her course!

Dr. Berland is awesome! She's so caring, gives really great feedback, and structured the class so thoughtfully that I got a lot out of it. I learned a lot about writing, and the projects were (mostly) fun and manageable. Take 105 in the social sciences with her if you get the chance!

Dr Berland was very kind and friendly with students. She cared about all of us and made time to talk to all of us outside of class. You definitely have to be willing to participate and put yourself out there to do well in her class.

Dr. Berland is a great professor. The assignments are spread out evenly across the semester, and you have a lot of chances to get feedback before one gets graded. The required topics (lit reviews, research, bibliographies) are hard to make interesting, but the assignments were fun. There was a podcast, a group lit review, and an infographic.

Dr. Berland was such a great professor. Her classes were engaging and I always felt like the class time was spent in a way that was useful to my learning. She gives class time to work on assignments and is flexible about due dates. Grading criteria was clear and fair. She truly cares about her students and their success. Take ENGL 105 with her!
Nice professor but a little bit unprofessional at times, overall easy class just make sure to not do other things during class time

Dr. Berland is one of the sweetest professors you will ever meet. She truly cares about each and every student. She breaks down everything she teaches nicely and clearly like no other English teachers in your life probably will. If you are having trouble in class, definitely book a meeting with her and she will help you in all the ways she can!

Dr. Berland is awsome. She is very funny and creates a very engaging class. The course is a big time commitment with watching multiple movies a week but its enjoyable. It is not that hard, just time consuming. Berland is one of my favorite professors I've taken as she cares about the students and loves what she teaches.

Very obviously cares for students and makes class always enjoyable. If I ever skipped her class it was never willingly. She gives great feedback and allows revisions for papers (which are short). PS if you REALLy want to get on her good side, sour gummies go a long way :)

Dr. Berland is an insightful and caring professor that is passionate both about teaching and film. Class contains twice-weekly reflection discussion posts on the films we watched, two short papers, a midterm test, and a video essay group project. Lectures are always fun! She gives great feedback about how to think about films analytically!
Take this teacher!

Prof Berland was amazing. I enjoyed watching new sci-fi movies, and discussing them in class. A small complaint I have is that watching a 2 hour movie before each class as HW was sometimes challenging, but she is very flexible with due dates if you communicate. You write 2 papers, and there is a final project where you make a video essay. Solid 5/5

Dr. Berland was my favorite professor this year! Not only was the class super engaging and fun, but she was super responsive and always willing to help no matter your question. She was a joy to be around and made this my favorite class, even though I am not the biggest English fan. Definitely hoping to take more classes with her.

I absolutely loved Dr. Berland and her class. Not only was she so much fun to be around, but she was encouraging and helpful and made class so enjoyable that it almost felt like it went by very quickly. I enjoyed the structure of her class as lot too, as there were opportunities to work independently as well as in groups.

Nicole Berland was truly a fantastic professor. She's kind, funny, and helped our class environment feel comfortable. I learned a lot in that class and I believe she has a great way of teaching students without overwhelming them. My only issue with her is that she definitely preferred her male students. She seemed to be more lenient toward them.

If I could choose one professor to learn form for the rest of my life it would be Dr. Berland!! Never have I felt more seen and heard by a professor before, her level of caring and connection with her students goes above and beyond and really helps to inspire confidence and friendships within the class. TAKE HER CLASSES!
I'm glad took Prof. Berland for 105 last year. She cares a lot about her students, and that helped me learn more in her class than I expected. Honestly, I wish more of my classes were like hers.

Dr. Berland is the best! She cares a lot about her students and tries her hardest to get to know everyone and make the classroom a fun environment. Assignments are pretty easy and she makes everything that she wants from you very clear. A lot of drafting and peer reviewing but the assignments are more creative than just papers ! Love her!

Dr. B is the best! She is super fun and gives great feedback on your work. She genuinely wants to see you be a better writer and succeed. The class structure with small and big group activities was super helpful and I enjoyed this class a lot. Work load is light as well. Definitely would recommend for ENGL 105!

Dr. Berland is awesome! She is engaging and tries hard to get to know all her students (she calls us her ducklings, lol). She gives excellent feedback and her instructions are always specific which is nice. I highly recommend taking her class. She always made me laugh!

Dr. Berland was amazing! Her approach to English 105 was really creative and I learned a lot about digital media projects. She goes out of her way to get to know each of her students through individual meetings! Class was relatively easy and if you participate in class and act enthusiastic you'll be sure to get an A.
Pretty accommodating and the workload is pretty light. Takes very long to grade and you really have no idea how you're doing in the class until after the semester is over.

Ms. Merz is genuinely lovely and very passionate about writing! She is super understanding when setting and moving deadlines and will always find time to help you outside of class despite her own busy schedule.

Professor Merz is a great professor! The course was exploring AI in writing, but you weren't required to use AI. She is very understanding and discussion is encouraged in class, but she is a little slow in giving feedback & grades. There were 3 papers with smaller assignments/drafts, but it was pretty light. There's a textbook but I didn't use it.

ENGL 105i - Mrs. Merz is very caring and understanding of all of her students. The coursework was generally light and project based. The material is not very interesting but I would definitely consider this course for an easy A.

(105i) SUCH a sweet and considerate professor, she means the best for students and is very accommodating. She wasn't able to grade very fast due to other life circumstances, but provided very specific and helpful feedback. As long as you demonstrate effort in the class, you will do well.

Very sweet prof. She didn't really grade much until the very end of the semester but she did give a lot of feedback and left comments on where to improve/what was good. None of the assignments took long to complete and she was always willing to answer questions about them.
I had her for 105i digital humanities. Kindest professor I've had so far. She is extremely helpful.
TAKE HER!! Very open, very flexible and understands your life outside of class, and just amazing overall.
Ms.Merz is a very kind and caring teacher. She offers plenty of extra credit and the work she assigns is not difficult. Easy A

Super sweet prof, cares a lot about her students and is VERY fair and lenient when she needs to give extensions. Kind of boring material but that comes with any english 105 class I would think. Gives clear criteria, good feedback, easy A.
amazing professor, I'm currently taking eng 100 and would highly recommend

Professor Merz was the most helpful professor I have had at UNC! She made herself available outside of class, provided great feedback on all work, gave numerous opportunities for extra credit, and shared brilliant lectures in which she took the time to advance all students' knowledge of the material.

Prof. Duvall was amazing! My favorite teacher during my first semester, definitely take ENG105 with her. Class was 3 projects, each with drafting assignments that prepare you fully for the final submission. She gave incredible feedback as well! Did not stress at all with this class.

super chill and easy class. Basically everything is completion if u put in a bit of effort. Attendance is not rly required either, she's pretty lenient with missing class as long as u email her beforehand, and it won't even affect ur grade. TAKE THIS PROF FOR ENGLISH
Easy course, but I don't feel like I actually learned anything.
If you can take a class with her next term you MUST.

Genuinely such an amazing professor and person. Class was not hard at all, and she made it clear she didn't want this class to be a stressor. Class consisted of some small assignments and 3 projects. Plenty of time was given, and she was very understanding on attendance (probably missed 5/6 classes from sickness). Great professor!

Emma made a class I thought I would hate one of my most enjoyable. She genuinely cares about all of the people in her classes. There are no exams, just 2-3 feeder assignments and a culminating project in each of the 3 units. She gives clear rubrics and feedback to help each student thrive in the course. If she teaches another section, take it.
Easy A for 105. Amazing professor who really cares and is invested in you. No tests just three projects for three units. No final as well. 10/10

Emma is an amazing professor! She is extremely caring and kind, and absolutely wants the best for her students. The assignments are very straightforward, and she is an understanding grader. I loved this class. If you are able take ENGL 105 with Emma, do it!

Emma was my TA for CMPL 120. Recitations were fun and really helpful for understanding the course, Emma was super knowledgeable on the course material. Emma was kind and caring, always super accommodating and willing to answer questions. Can't recommend her enough, she's awesome!

Lots and lots of readings in the semester, very fast paced. 3 essays that are all 1500+ words, plus a (really hard and strictly graded) midterm, with a final at the end. Tons of work for a class that's only a 100 level class, wouldn't take this at all if you're not a CMPL major or whatever.

Emma is an absolute sweetie. Most of her classes are discussion based, so it is easy to participate if you can get 1 comment in each class. There are 4 papers and she will review them before you turn them in as many times as you want. You can tell she wants you to succeed always. There isn't much prep that goes in and even if you don't it's fine.

Emma gave me a completely new understanding of poetry in the best way. Lectures were interesting and engaging, and she really made an effort to get to know each student. She is one of the most genuinely caring professors I've had so far. She was also very flexible with deadlines. The class workload was very manageable.
Emma is fantastic. Really interesting lectures and readings. Super accommodating and flexible when it comes to assignment due dates.

Lectures and homework were directly geared towards assignments. She's very nice, meeting with her will help if you need it for papers. Not a lot of work though, just a few projects. Just do your work and you'll do well, it's an easy class.

Emma was a great TA for CMPL 120. She is genuinely one of the most caring instructors I have met at UNC. She is very accessible outside of class to answer questions about essays. Her recitations were a great addition to the main lecture, having us perform close readings of passages or art pieces.
Definitely should choose her as your 105 teacher if it's possible!

Quick chase for those of you who just want it: 100% awesome professor. Finished with a 99%. Super respected. Very nice. Kind.
I found this class to be one of the greatest introductory classes, especially online, though the units move quickly, the class goes by fast, despite being 90 minutes, 5 days a week. 
Grades "easy" but you have to try!

Take her for your 105!! I would've never expected to enjoy ENGL. I didn't even mind going at 8am. She is so kind and uplifting and gives you an A for just attempting to improve from your draft. The units are all different so it's not just paper writing. 1-2 assignments per week, most of which took me 10 minutes.

She is very kind and accomadating for circumstances! ENGL 105 coursework relatively easy and she gives great feedback for your rough drafts so that you can do well on final projects. No midterm or final. Very sweet and respected by all of the classmates. Love her!

Take eng105 with her if u can (even if its early its worth it)!! She is so nice and understanding. Very reachable outside of class. Give u extension if u ask. Easy grader as well. Some say lecture is boring but thats not on her all eng105 lecture r boring its an intro class what do u expect. She will make ur life easier trust me.

Professor Duncan is a great professor. Just do the work (which is minimal and not difficult at all), participate, and you'll easily get an A. He does take attendance, but communicate with him and he's super understanding, and class was often asynchronous. I will say he is a tad bit strict, but overall, great instructor.

Professor Duncan was great! He gives great feedback and wants you to do well in the class. He is willing to work with you and is incredibly helpful, just make sure you actually go to class. I took this class as a major requirement but I really enjoyed it.

Minimal work outside of class and easy to get an A. He's also very caring for his students and offers lots of flexibility. English isn't always the most fun class, but he finds ways to make it engaging. He is very thorough with instruction and gives feeders leading up to the projects, which makes it so projects don't burden us with work to do.

Prof. Duncan makes taking eng 105 more bearable. He gives you time in class to work on assignments so that you do not have homework. He also is very understanding if you cannot make it to class or have a question about one of the assignments. Each assignment can be resubmitted to get back points. I recommend!!

While Prof. Duncan can be a little serious and the class isn't super exciting, it is exactly what I needed as a first-year requirement. We had no homework and time in class to work on assignments. You will get an automatic A if you show up to class and turn in your assignments on time. You get to do a mock interview, which is super helpful.

Professor Duncan is simply too serious about ENGL 105 which should be an easy pass first-year english class, but the assignments have to be submitted on time, he gets passive aggressive about attendance, and honestly expects too much out of us when we are just trying to do class to get the credit and get it over with.
Best Prof ever! Great person, great lecture, great project!

Professor Duncan was my favorite professor this year. If you do the work on time you get an automatic A. He did his best to do the HW in class so you didn't have to do it out of class. He was super understanding about physical and mental health if you missed the class and was good about responding to emails! I would 100% recommend taking his class.

Matthew was an amazing professor. All the assignments he gave during class were super useful and he gave extremely valuable feedback every time. He wants every student to succeed and understands that we're all first year students so most if not all assignments are relevant to each student and is super open to helping both inside and outside class.

Matt is a very easygoing professor. He likes to work with students to find solutions to issues. If you communicate your needs for an extension or anything else he is usually more than happy to work with you. He gives good feedback to improve our writing and presentation skills.

One of the toughest class to do well in, and also the part about now allowing anyone to get higher than a 95 on attendance is insane. Like I tried so hard in this class to get an A in this class even though I just needed this course for my PH credit.

Good professor. However, the structure of this class isn't great and it is very hard to get an A or A-. He does not believe in any grade above 95. My TA was very inefficient and disorganized and could not teach or give constructive feedback. Not lying when I say one of my least favorite classes I've taken which is sad because topics are interesting

nice guy and all, but a terrible class. virtually impossible to get an A. graded on three assignments, a midterm, and a final, and the highest grade you can get is a 95. I took this class for the mejo requirement and I do not recommend. its a really interesting topic so a bummer the class is structured so poorly

Tom is very passionate and kind, and the topics of the course were interesting. My main issue is that they do not give out A's unless we essentially recreate the text/rubric word for word. Also, students cannot get higher than a 95% for attendance. This course could be great, but it needs to be tweaked.
there are only a few assignments graded very harshly. I felt like I tried very hard on the argument reconstructions but they were wayy too harsh in grading them

There are 3 argument reconstructions and 1 midterm which are graded harshly, and you're not given good feedback. The lectures were irrelevant and boring. If you're a MEJO major, I would recommend taking Media Ethics over this class.

Really cool class and the topics were really interesting. Attendance is not mandatory, and you really only have to attend recitation. Just do the readings and you're good! Very fun. Content is tricky, but I felt like the TA's are very helpful and provide great feedback. Love Tom, they really are a great professor and I'm glad I got to know them :)

Class is predicated on argument reconstruction assignments and recitation discussions. One midterm exam and Final. I read only for recitation where we discuss readings, lectures are on interesting topics but can go pretty slow, but there's no attendance, questions or anything. Tom is a nice teacher and TAs are flexible for recitation. Fun class

Tom is a phenomenal professor and I feel so lucky to have taken my capstone with them. I had some of my favorite debates and discussions of my entire college career within our classroom community, but come ready to participate because this is not a lecture based class. Readings are provided, interesting, and easy to follow along.

Professor Tom is a really caring person and instructor. One class is a lecture and the other is a discussion every week and this kept the class engaging. The readings can be heavy, but the topics are interesting. 2 completion homeworks every week, mid-term, and final. Incredibly rare to give anything higher than a B+.

Tom is the most accommodating and kind individual I've met in this department.They foster lovely conversations & make sure anyones voice can be heard. I've taken classes where there's been argument reconstructions before, but Tom will take off points if you fail to mention any little thing.Despite this, the class was lovely and I would do it again.

Tom was incredibly kind and caring during a tough semester, and really encouraged good discussion. I don't think I was a huge fan of the textbook, particularly since the whole semester was just reading through the one book and discussing it.

Dr. Dougherty is very nice but does not give clear expectations for assignments. The rubric consists of 1) is your argument good? 2) is use of course content good? 3) is writing good? They do not define what good means. We only had one grade in that counted for 15% of our grade until the final so no one had any idea how we were doing in the class.

Professor Tom was the nicest professor I had during my first semester at UNC! The readings before class were often challenging, and we were graded on three essays from course content (2 take home and 1 in class) which are not graded easily. This class will make you a better reader and writer, and you will learn a lot from in class discussions.

Prof. Tom is incredibly kind and does a wonderful job of dissecting course material. The readings can be difficult, but investing time in discussions makes all the difference. All major assignments are writing based. I did not find them to be a notably tough grader, but be prepared to spend time revising and reviewing your papers. Highly recommend!

Heavily discussion-based, discussion questions directly from readings. Do the readings and submit the paragraph "prep assignments" and you're set. They encourage all perspectives and create a very respectful environment. One final paper, but incorporates rough-draft feedback day into schedule. Grading was not too harsh, feedback was constructive.

Professor Dougherty is so kind! This class really relied on group discussion so be willing to participate. The conversations and topics were very interesting, which made it a lot more engaging. But this class is literally discussion based off the take-home readings and self-paced writing assignments, so it's really on students to participate.

Professor Dougherty was one of my favorite professors this semester!! It's reading intensive and participation heavy class but you can skim the materials and still pass the preparation assignments. Three papers and a few sentence assignments to check that you did the reading.

Tom was an amazing professor. He was very inclusive and respectful of everybody in the class. He made discussion the main point of this class which made for a very engaging class. He was very educated and showed much dedication to the class. We did have to read a ton in this class, but it was manageable. I would take a class with Tom again.

Tom's class is super fun and you end up being bffs with everyone in there. Really moderate workload but it is a little hard to get A's on everything. If you're happy with a pretty easy workload, super fun class time and an A-, this is the class for you.

Professor is brilliant, clearly knows what he is talking about. Tough grader though. Seemed to grade exams more fair than some of the group projects/reflections. Participation is required, and he will give you a bad grade if you do not participate. 8 pop quizzes based on readings, pretty easy. Interesting subject matter, makes you think.

Most of my philosophy background is in applied ethics, but Dr. Worsnip made epistemology very accessible and interesting! I enjoyed this class and it was well structured. Pop quizzes but you'll be fine if you do the readings. He can be a picky grader but he gives very good feedback and is one of the best of this field. Participation matters a lot.

Love him. He is BRILLIANT (might be the smartest person I've ever met) and very entertaining!! He explains things so clearly and creates an atmosphere where everyone feels comfortable participating. Uses a stoplight system for participation. Pop quizzes every once in a while; just do the readings. 1 group project and 3 fair exams (not cumulative)

Tough grader, but fair. The class is very well-structured introduction to both classical and contemporary epistemology. Recommended for any philosophy major/minor. And Prof. Worsnip is the right one to take. Participation matters a lot, and he is grading based on depth of thinking and overall clear structure. He wants you to actually think deeply.
Alex is great. Take a class with him.

Professor Worsnip has a very engaging discussion-based structure to his course. I enjoyed all the daily discussions and hearing my classmates perspectives. I will say there is daily reading and random pop quizzes, so be prepared for class.

I really enjoyed PHIL140 this semester - engaging lectures that really made me think, interesting course content, & fair grading standards. There are pop quizzes on readings, but they are not extremely difficult. I would take this class again! An at-times challenging but rewarding course

After having Dr. Worsnip for a lower level philosophy class, I had to take epistemology with him b/c he's an amazing professor. He is beyond intelligent and can respond to any question. He gives great advice in many areas and really engages with his students. I've grown a lot as a student and philosopher in his courses. Couldn't recommend enough!
Deaven is a great professor who makes you think!

Participation heavy. Readings are due each class, they tend to get a little long. Deadlines shift around often which may seem good at first glance, but it does get frustrating if you have a job and are calling out for important dates (presentations and such). Set up meetings in advance because office hours fill up!

This class has readings, an essay, and presentation projects. Katie clearly cares about making the class interesting and informative. Grading is quite fair but the class still requires work and office hours are helpful. A lot of the work for the class comes later in the semester, so be prepared for the workload at the end.

You can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches and only wants you to succeed. If you put in the work and listen in class then you'll be fine. I will say that it is homework heavy, so a good amount of readings that can be quite difficult to understand.
amazing, would take.

I really enjoyed her teaching honestly, very enjoyable and the way that she would make the content was engaging. I would say that there was a lot of reading at times even though she tried to get the readings as short as possible. She's very engaged and passionate about the material and wants us to do the best we can in the class.

This is for 102 but there wasn't an option. Katie is very kind, accessible, and fun in class. Heavy emphasis on classroom discussion and participation. Easy to get B+/A-, not an easy A due to lots of reading and high expectations for understanding. I really loved this class and feel like I learned a lot about philosophy and good communication!

Dr. Deavon is genuinely one of my favorite prof! She is so caring/accommodating to everyone's needs. She'll work w/ you if you talk to her. She has a clear outline of what she expects. There are 1-3 readings each week (some are dense some not), video diaries, no exams, a final presentation, 3 big papers, + student facilitations. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

Katie clearly cares about her students and classes. While sometimes a little disorganized, she does not hesitate to adjust class or grades around it. Very generous with deadlines and assignments. Clearly loves philosophy and wants her students to learn. She really just wants people to participate, discuss, and ask questions. Would highly recommend!

I really enjoyed bioethics, not just the content of the course but also the materials Katie used to teach.  I loved the class was hands on and discussion based. I felt like I got what I brought in. I worked hard and got a grade that reflected that work. She is a fair grader, but it is def not a class you can coast through.

Katie genuinely cares about your learning. She focuses a ton on small group discussions and truly values every idea brought forward in class. When discussions weren't flowing she always adapts and gets people involved, super engaging and genuinely cares about her classroom environment and student success.

Topics in this class were a bit confusing, and her explanations were super long but I felt like I never gained much insight. Our first paper went well, but it was confusing when it came to the final paper draft as we got the rubric 4 hours before the deadline. While unorganized, she was understanding and fun in lecture.

Katie offers an inspiring list of topics and approaches them in a contagiously enthusiastic manner. Sometimes her lectures are overly "improvised" as she attempts to respond to whatever question someone raises. She may appear a bit disorganized, but at the end of the day she's a very charitable grader and the course overall was pretty low-stake.

Great person, Awful professor. Katie is terribly disorganized, doesn't tell her students what is expected of them, then proceeds to grade harshly. She doesn't do a good job providing advice and feedback on the papers, which make up most of the grade, and rarely has time to meet before big assignments are due. Would not recommend this experience.

absolutely goated. class is very discussion and small group heavy, and she cares a lot about students' learning. no midterm and the final is just a presentation. class was pretty disorganized, but this was her first sem at unc, so i doubt it'd be an issue in the future.
idk why people are wining about her grading; it's pretty average in difficulty

Katie is a little disorganized and grades go in late. There are lots of readings in this class (PHIL 143). There is also a lot of writing and your grade is determined by this. The final exam was extremely easy (a really short presentation). As long as you stay on top of the work and put effort into your papers, you should succeed in this class.

There is no grading criteria so you will never know what she wants. So, so disorganized. It almost feels like she has never taught before, everything is so unclear in this class. Do NOT take it. I have no idea what my grade is in the class because she's graded like 1 assignment total. Avoid at all costs. Class consists of random tangents.

The best class, my favorite this whole semester! No tests, lots of readings but they are chill. Make sure you are not afraid to speak in class everyday because participation matters a lot. Also lots of group work for the simulations. Overall super fun, Dr. Ross is so kind and funny.

Dr. Ross was a good professor, but I found his lectures pretty boring and short. He encourages participation a lot (both in class and on online discussion boards), and it is a pretty big part of your overall grade in the course. Only homework is Perusall readings/annotations for each class, and 3 reflections throughout the course.

Dr. Ross is a great Professor, and a great guy. He gives short lectures that ensure you understand the philosopher's arguments, and then facilitates classroom discussion that ensures you understand what YOU think about the arguments. His assignments are fair and creative, which makes doing them fun rather than a chore.

Prof Ross cares a lot about his subject matter and his students! Definitely take if you're interested in the class--do NOT take if you're looking for an easy A. Clearly makes a point to get to know his students to help them succeed. Easy homework and excellent class discussions.

Took the course last fall, and loved the class and the professor. Ross has a near unparalleled ability to make a classroom into a community and get everyone engaged in the material together. Amazing guy, not a demanding grader, and clearly invested in the content and his students. Take his class if you can!
Amazing professor, taught one of my absolute favorite classes (Phil 175). Highly recommend!

This class is very discussion heavy where participation will affect your grade. Mostly has group work (a presentation and one debate) and is an easy class but discussions often went off topic, and I don't feel like I actually learned how to argue.

The entire class was discussion based, which he did a good job leading and allowing everyone to give input. If you're shy he also has an option to post on discussion boards on canvas. We did two group projects which were honestly quite interesting. The first was a conspiracy project and the second was a debate.

As much as he was funny, i don't think i have learned much in this class as its mainly up to solely class discussion based learning where we went off topic a lot. I've participated, but still got a much lower score than i had thought which i think is dumb. he says the projects are laid back and we shouldn't stress, yet gives harsh grading on them.

if you don't like talking a lot because you are shy, do NOT take this class. it's all discussion with so many people who are majoring in similar subjects who have a heavy grasp on the material that like to dominate conversations and leave you out to dry. grading is also harsh, and group projects are graded unjustly.

Prof. Ross is the absolute best! He is my favorite professor I've had in college & is incredibly engaging and supportive. The material could be boring but he makes it interesting and I would 1000% take one of his classes again. He encourages participation and rewards it, but has options for those who aren't big talkers. Mostly essays and not tests.
Professor Ross is very engaging, whether through group discussions or personal talk. Would 100% take him again.

Professor Ross is very nice and not at all a harsh grader, he really just want students to be involved and active so as long as you do the work and contribute in class you'll be absolutely fine! I took PHIL272 and PWAD 324 asynchronous online and both were similar structure and he was very nice and friendly in both!

Prof Ross is one of my favorite professors at UNC. I've taken 2 classes with him, and enjoyed both of them. Class consists of pre class readings and comments, discussions in class, and group projects/reflections. Highly recommend taking Ross, you will enjoy it.

Dr. Ross is incredible. I learned a lot and his lectures were engaging and accessible for someone that isn't a Philosophy Major. Class structure is weird however and online platform could be used better to intregrate what people say in lecture. All in all a great professor and would highly recommend taking 272 with him if you need it for PWAD.
Take his class if you can!

Dr. Ross is awesome. This is my second class I've taken with him, and he always brought a lot of enthusiasm/energy to class. There wasn't a single day in which it felt burdensome to attend his lectures. Your participation grade makes up a good portion of your grade, but there is also a discussion forum if you prefer to write your opinions. 5/5

This is my 2nd class with Dr. Ross, and he did not disappoint! Class material was interesting.  Make sure to actively participate.  Class consisted of group discussions, 3 reflection papers, Perusall notes, and final group presentation.  Prof. Ross is a chill grader.  Follow his rubrics! He's also very funny.  He made a slideshow of the class as AI

dr ross is so incredible!! he's one of the most chill professors i've had here, and this class is super easy and engaging - just participate some and you'll get an A. there isn't a lot of work in this class, mainly reading (it's philosophy so expected). dr ross is super funny and makes class really engaging. 100% take a class with him

Professor Ross was an amazing teacher who cared about each of his students and wanted them to succeed! Even through I was not a philosophy major, this class was super interesting to me and I found the material accessible. Participate in each class and put some effort into the final project and you'll do great.

Very easy but boring class. You only have to attend 10 lectures for full participation credit. All other work are online Canvas quizzes. Final is long and tedious but worth the rest of the class having a light workload. Would recommend for an easy A.
Easy A. Took this class for over the summer online for a gpa booster. There is a good amount of work to do, though they are all very easy. Highly recommend this class

Professor Neta is very passionate about his subject, but his teachings can be very unclear. He uses the same examples for everything and students would often leave him stumped with their questions. He was accessible for office hours and his test questions were mostly straightforward. He is a very nice man, just is a somewhat confusing lecturer.
I feel like he was a chill teacher, although some of his content was confusing and not as simple as the other two teachers' content. Great person- okay teaching style.

Had him along with three other professors for lectures, and he was the most difficult to understand by far. He went on long tangents that did not relate to the course material which made it nearly impossible to understand the content, as well as the questions he provided on the exams were difficult and poorly thought out. Nice guy though.
Love Ram Neta!! very funny guy and very knowledgeable. makes sure you understand EVERYTHING by profu

He's a very good professor who knows his stuff. His only real problem is that he has a tendency to ramble and overcomplicate things when trying to simplify them for others to understand, also, he is the victim of having the other two professors outshine him : (
Very very very boring and gets lost in trying to make his own points. Lots of talking but saying absolutely nothing of value. However, the class is worth taking because of the other two professors.
He tends to start rambling, but if you can pick up on the important parts of his lectures, you'll do fine.

Neta was the most boring out of the three professors. Not a bad teacher per se, but just would ramble. He knows his stuff though. Nice guy just a little wacky and off-topic at times. The class was great though because the other two professors carried.

I had him for the "How Not to be Fooled or Fool Yourself" Triple - i. Just so dull and boring... would make a slideshow of only 5 slides last over an hour, and overcomplicated easy concepts. So hard to stay awake. I would take the Triple - i though, it was interesting.

Not a hard class, just be warned all the material is on Sigmund Freud. I did not know this before the class started as it isn't in the course description or anywhere else online. You read three books by Freud and write five essays based on his writings and ideas. Ram is a lovely guy, just so. much. Freud.

This class is made for students to succeed in and Neta aids that. The only difficult part was making it to lecture at 9:05 MoWeFri. His expectations for every assignment were clearly established making it easy to do well on the 4 major papers and 4 major quizzes. The only tricky assignment was the final which was lengthy and laggy online.

Professor Neta is a great PHIL105 professor. He lectures in an old-fashioned way and there are lots of videos to watch for homework online, but overall I learned so much from this course and it is very applicable in other classes and the world. Make sure to participate because he gets excited when students ask questions and engage in discussion:)

The entire class was watching YouTube videos that he recorded almost 10 years ago. The papers were peer graded, the TA's held recitations (which were completely useless), and the final exam was 153 questions which I guess was his way of stressing us out for no reason. Joke of a class, joke of a professor. Easy A.

Easy A for a PH credit. Online class. Youtube videos to watch to help with In-class exercises. Peer anonymous grading for papers. Professor is nice, but the class is extremely tedious. The exam is genuinely hit or miss. Around 153 questions with 3 hours to take it. Extra credit was provided toward the end based on your TA. TURN IN WORK BEFORE 5PM..

Really easy class but a complete waste of time. If you've taken discrete math the content is just a repeat of the easy stuff but easier. There are asynchronous videos which teach you all you need to know, so his synchronous lectures and recitations are useless. The papers are also really easy, probably the best PH if you don't like philosophy.

He was a good professor up until it came to the finals.The class is online. 
-There are in-class assignments to do every lecture,
- 4 30-question quizzes, 
- ALOT of online practice exercises that I knocked out in a month I believe, 
-Hard 153-question final exam to complete in 3 hours
Extra credit opportunity was provided towards the end

Professor's nice, responsive, patient. The class though -- totally online, assignments to do every lecture (twice weekly), a tremendous number of small quizzes (due virtually every single day), tons of YouTube lecture videos (the main mode of instruction), four larger quizzes besides, and a 153-question final exam. It's a lot to stay on top of.

don't take this class if you're trying to learn anything, but if you just need the PH credit I def recommend. this is the easiest class I've ever taken fr. kind professor and TAs and work is easy. four short papers that are graded very leniently plus daily quizzes, but I finished all of them within the first month. Easy filler class
Best class ever. It is always a privilege to take a class with Michael. This class has helped me become a better student, citizen, and person.
big michael fan
One of the most passionate and caring professors I've had. Attendance v important.

Michael is my favorite professor at UNC, hands down. I took two of his classes--PHIL 285 and PHIL 294. PHIL 294 is community based with senior citizens. An amazing and unique class. PHIL 285 is a more traditional course (philosophy of education). Michael cares about his students and makes the content digestible and very much worth your while.

Seeing as Michael's class was a highlight of my senior year, I had to write to here. Took the class based on a friend's rec. I learned a ton without the needless stresses of some of my other classes. Extremely well designed course that is obviously due to Michael's passion for the subject and teaching.

Had him for philosophy across the lifespan - such a wonderful professor. Kind, caring, flexible, understanding, engaging. Class consisted of meeting with a group of older adults at the public library and discussing philosophical dilemmas. We carpooled and were reimbursed for any gas money / uber charges. Learned so much without stress.

The kindest, most caring, and most intellectually stimulating professor I've ever had. There's a reason why Michael Vazquez's PHIL 294 class always has a waitlist! We go to CH-Public Library every week and facilitate phil. convos w/ elderly people. If you can take a class with him, DO IT. It will be the most enriching experience of your time.
Michael has a way of getting everyone to care about philosophy. A generous and sharp facilitator. Take one of his classes, especially PHIL 294, and it will be a highlight of your time at UNC

Michael is a wonderful person and passionate teacher. I wanted to leave this review to say that and also to recommend specitic class. Getting to know older adults in the area (through philosophy) is just not something you will ever do in another class, I bet!
This is probably the first and last review I will make on this website. Vazquez is the best and nicest professor I have seen in my 2+ years at UNC. Please take him if you can

One of my favorite classes over the course of my UNC career! So interesting, inspiring, and relevant! He cares about what his students think and encourages discussion and reflection. Vazquez is also very communicative and accessible in office hours. I went a couple times just to talk to him, and I had such interesting discussions with him.

This was hands down my favorite class at UNC! Dr. Vazquez was incredible—his enthusiasm and deep knowledge about ethics made the material so engaging and relevant. He constantly gave realistic examples that made everything click. Even as a non-major, I loved it and found the content so important. I'm really going to miss this class and Dr. V!

TAKE HIM! I took Michael's class on a whim (needed the class for a minor), and he is the reason I am now considering a philosophy minor/major. Really down to earth guy who knows how to open ideas and conversation up. He's very humble and does not make a big deal out of the fact that he is really sharp and knowledgeable.
Best professor at UNC. Engaging presentations, genuinely invested in student learning, and kind/understanding. Do yourself a favor and take one of his classes. (I'm not a philosophy major.)

Dr. Vazquez is sincere, enthusiastic, and knowledgeable. He does a great job facilitating a balanced discussion among students. It's clear he wants you to think for yourself. He's also funny, in a nerdy kind of way. Participation matters. He values peoples' ideas a lot. And he is helpful to chat with 1 on 1 if you're confused.

Among my favorite classes at UNC. I did not have much of a background in philosophy, but Prof. Vazquez made the material engaging. He did not water down the ideas, he just taught and facilitated really well. IMO some professors happen to teach as part of their job, while other professors are teachers at their core. Vazquez is a teacher at his core.
Philosophy GOAT

Professor Vazquez is one of the most caring and enthusiastic professors I've had. His passion for philosophy is contagious, and his lectures are always engaging. He wants you to think critically about the challenges facing democracy and our university. He genuinely cares about students and generously offers advice on graduate school and life. Take!

Professor Vazquez is definitely the best professor I've had at UNC. He is so knowledgeable and made every class genuinely interesting. Attending PHIL 285 never felt like a chore. All his assignments challenge you to think deeply and you actually learn from them. I recommend anyone take 285 or any other class with him.

Good person, goofy. Great teacher, passionate about the topic. Prepare for lectures by doing the readings and write-up assignments before class. Class discussions were valuable, safe space. Fair grader, good feedback. Always available to help with classwork. Graded on the write-ups, two group projects, and the final.

This class was definitely interesting and I enjoyed the course topics. That being said, don't take it if you are wanting an easy A. I barely got an A, and this class was definitely too difficult to be considered an intro level class. She grades very harshly and expects you to participate every class.

Prof Geenen was very thorough and knowledgable. Every class is basically a discussion on the reading for that class. There are quizzes, argument reconstructions, and essays. If you enjoy philosophy and the ethics of healthcare this is for you. There are 2 in class essays where you can't have any notes or any outside help that are 50% of your grade.

Ava was caring and accommodated for everyone's needs in terms of feedback and giving extensions. Lots of tough reading but she explained it well in class. Lecture and participation heavy, you will be expected to speak at least 2x a class for a good participation grade.

This course was fairly difficult for an introductory class and contained a lot of reading and lectures. Professor Geenen was always willing to help outside of class and had some interesting lectures. The material was pretty comprehensive as well.

Ava is a great professor. She understands the material extremely well and, more importantly, can explain it well. Her readings were thoughtfully chosen and refreshingly contemporary compared to many introductory-level philosophy courses at UNC. Additionally, her unit quizzes required meaningful engagement with the texts, which helped learning.

PHIL 140: Very nice prof. but class can get dull. Worksheets give good overview of papers but the subject matter is really confusing, especially for your first philosophy class. Half of class stopped attending. Papers are hard but if you go to office hours and the writing center you can totally do well. If you love philosophy, you will 100% enjoy.

PHIL140 was an awful experience. The class material felt like a giant circle leading back to the same discussion and topic we had on the first day of class. Paper grading was harsh for the class, and the lectures were very discussion-based, yet dull. Half the class stopped showing up throughout the semester, if that says anything.

Overall okay professor. Wasn't the biggest fan of the way the class was graded/assessed. The grading was not at the level of an introductory philosophy class. 2 essays worth 65% of your grade. The class content was interesting.

Took this class for a gen-ed and was disappointed. She takes lateness into account and if you arrive a minute past class start time, poof! your participation goes down. She grades harshly- even after meeting with her several times about a paper she gave me a B+ on it and her critiques are absolute nonsense. Will not give you the grade you deserve.

This class was so enjoyable and fulfilling; I learned so much. The lectures were a bit rough at first but got better as the semester went on. We had anywhere from 10–40-page readings due every class period and classes were discussion based. Expectations for assignments were clear, and Ava is very accessible.  I would recommend this class!

She is very reachable and caring to give extensions when needed. Her grading for papers is fair, with a clear rubric, and she gives line notes feedback. She incorporates different views, and grades based on the quality of arguments rather than her personal likeness. Reply emails very quick.

I think I would have enjoyed this course if it wasn't at 8 am. Ava is a very caring professor & is clear about what's required. Graded on outside reading annotations before each class, attendance/participation in class, 2 papers, and a final group project. Missing a class will make your grade plummet, otherwise the course content is doable.

Took this class fall, 2025. While the essays are difficult, she is very accessible in office hours and willing to help with any questions. Additionally, the tests are grade boosters and it was an interesting class!
Interesting class and good selection of readings

This class was the worst phil class I've taken in my time at UNC (I am a phil major). She provided rubrics but graded subjectively, graded the essays harshly with little guidance. There was a new reading before each class which was usually 20-30pg philosophy readings. Overall, the content of the class was interesting but I taught myself.
