This class was very difficult and you definitely have to put in the work. However, I think it's harsh to say she doesn't care about effort or time spent. She's very helpful in office hours and can easily provide additional instructions or feedback if you reach out, which helps a ton.

This class was intriguing, but pretty rough. It definitely leans more towards philosophy than polisci. In fact, history was rarely discussed in class. I also felt that grading was somewhat inconsistent (specifically, papers were graded much less leniently than tests). However, I enjoyed how we could choose our own war to research over the semester.
just don't do it
Tests aren't bad but essays are bc she gives like no instructions or super vague expectations for them so ur pretty much set up to fail!

Only take the class if you are really interested in the topic. Otherwise don't take it or take it with another professor. She is a ridiculously picky grader who does not care about time or effort put into assignments and will certainly not reflect that into your grade. Not a particularly bad instructor just has horrible grading guidelines

No textbook for the class. She provides materials for all readings. Her grading is strict, but fair and she gives ample feedback on how to improve. The class was reading heavy, but some were less dense than others. Two papers, two discussion posts, midterm, final, and a semester-long diary about a war you pick (you'll present your war in a group).

Difficult grader that uses complicated rubrics to justify unnecessary intensity that is inconsistent with the provided rubric. Gives very little viable feedback and at times makes the class both boring and difficult to follow. Avoid if possible
awesome guy
nice guy and interesting class. lots of reading but he gives reading summary sheets every class. no tests just 2 papers and a group presentation

This guy is awful. He is nice but that's about it. No structure to class. No clear grading criteria. Unnecessarily hard grader. Do not take a class with this guy. He literally just talked with one student the whole class every time.
nice professor, really helpful during office hours. class participation matters a lot. grade is based on 2 papers, 1 project, and participation. good class. reading heavy

Professor Fullhart is passionate about analyzing philanthropy through a PPE lens and assigned lots of interesting readings. Class was pretty lecture heavy and a bit heavy on reviewing the material versus discussing opinions/broader implications. Speaking up was the best way to stay engaged. The paper/project were also quite vague and confusing.
sam is a sweet guy and he definitely knows his stuff. however it feels like he has trouble making the content digestable for his students. his lectures are boring and confusing. wouldn't recommend

He is a great person and cares about his students. However, the class is unstructured, and the lectures are hard to understand. The grade is based primarily on papers that are graded harshly. Again, a great person, not the best professor.

Luc was my favorite professor I've had at UNC. Lectures were funny and easy to understand but you can tell he's a brilliant mind. Gives you plenty of resources to do well on tests and there was a video presentation in place of a final exam. Great class and great professor

Prof Bovens is a great professor, the class is graded on papers, midterm/final, which you are given a question bank for ahead of the exams and you answer the questions in recitation, you only have 4 absences throughout the semester but overall great class and you learn a lot!

Liked Prof. Bovens, his lectures were pretty interesting but not overly complicated for a minor intro class. Clear about expectations and had good office hours.
Eric Choi was my TA, we mostly just did practice problems during recitation & he graded a little tough at first, but gave great feedback that helped me do better on second paper and final.

choose TA Myreaka, who explained concepts so well and outlined midterm and final preparation perfectly to great grades on both. Her paper grading wasn't harsh yet still very helpful. Luc's lectures are great, though it can be easy to zone out in such a large class. Papers topics are up to you and weightage is balanced well with the midterm + final.

Professor Bovens is great–definitely recommend everyone to take PHIL384 with him. But, I feel like the gradings for the essays were a little bit harsh? The final and midterm were easy though, so it compensate for the papers. As long as you come to class, do the readings, you will do fine on this course.

Lectures are engaging and easy to understand, and the midterm and final are questions chosen from a bank, making them pretty easy. The harshest grade is papers, but even those are not that bad. Overall super great/easy class and Professor Bovens is a funny guy! I'd definitely take another class with him.

Bovens is the sweetest professor at UNC. He is so kind and cares about all of his students. His class was very easy with minimal assignments and no midterm or final, just a final paper and presentation. If you don't love philosophy, his lectures can be boring at times, but each class had group work to break that up.

Professor Bovens is the Goat in the Philosophy. This course requires effort especially for the essay. I personally think TA is over-harsh on the paper. For compensation, Midterm and Finals are very simple. So it's not very hard to get an A as long as you put time in it.
Professor Bovens is great. His class is super interesting and he is very accessible. Essays depend on TA grades but aren't too difficult. Highly recommend.

I enjoyed the topics Professor Bovens covered, but often felt that he was lost when teaching or didn't realize what he was supposed to be covering. I still feel that he was a worthwhile professor to take, but it was a bit confusing at times.
My best teacher at UNC, definitely the goat of philosophy department. Take class with him and enjoy it!

I generally enjoyed Professor Boven's first-year seminar as it was relevant and not too heavy courseload-wise. He assigned interesting nightly 50-word discussion posts but in-class was dry sometimes. He grades pretty subjectively with no rubric and honestly based on his own opinions, with convoluted feedback - which made it hard to predict grades.

Professor Bovens is one of my favorite professors at UNC, and he did a phenomenal job covering the Philosophy portion of IDST 111. He brought a lot of enthusiasm and energy to the 8 am lectures and strived to draw every student's interest. Moreover, I enjoyed talking with him during office hours about the various topics covered in class.

I liked Dr. Bovens and I think that this first year seminar was pretty decent. The content was relevant and interesting and discussion could be dry at times, but I understood the points he was bringing up and why we were discussing them. He's a bit nitpicky with grading papers, and it's really hard to predict your grade.

Amazing guy with a lot of experience. Grading can be a little rough on the essays (TAs) but rather than that everything was very fair. He makes the class fun and is very passionate about what he teaches.  The class is extremely interesting and the tests are structured in a way that you can not study for 1 or 2 topics that you don't find important.

This class is fairly graded and the TAs are accessible. He's the type who could teach this class for 20+ years and still show the same passion about this subject every time. If you're someone who wants to really delve into economics/political science beware that he only covers things at surface level since there are so many topics in one class.
Very nice man, grading is done by TAs but his lectures are very funny, graded by 15 reading discussions, 2 800-1200 word papers, and a midterm and final.

Luc Bovens is a good professor and he seems to like what he teaches. The class is composed of a few HW assignments, two essays, and two exams (which is the perfect setup in my opinion). He also offers EC which is helpful. He has said some questionable things in class but overall, I definitely recommend this course and this professor.

Overall very sweet and understanding guy! Your grade consists of 15 short discussion posts graded for completion, 2 short papers graded a little harsher, an easy midterm, and a final. You can even get 0.5-2 extra credit points toward your final grade by attending 1-4 PPE events throughout the semester. You have to put some work in but very doable!

I enjoyed engaging with the assigned material throughout the class. Prof. Bovens is funny and made the discussions interesting. His grading is not harsh, but nitpicky in a helpful way. Its made me a better writer, or at least more thoughtful about my own writing. His class environment also helped me overcome my hatred for public speaking :)
One of the best professors I've ever had.

Professor Conner is amazing! He is great at explaining dense readings and really cares about his students. I found the topics discussed in class interesting and the class materials he provides to be really helpful with the essays and projects.

Dr. Connor was very kind and it is clear he want you to do well. Sometimes the content in confusing but he was always willing to answer questions. The papers are scary at first but he is open to helping and they are fairly graded. The class is doable if you pay attention.

I recommend this class. Lots of readings but spend the entire class reviewing them. Professor Conner is interesting, caring, and understanding of his students' needs. Grade consists of 3 papers 2 presentations (random groups), online reading quizzes, attendance, and a final. Everything is graded easily-fair and it's clear he wants you to succeed.
Too big a work load too many readings

The class is lecture-heavy but interesting. There are readings for each class, but most/all of the content is covered in lecture. You learn to think like a philosopher! Dr. Conner is very caring and isn't trying to mess up your grade or give you a ton of work. I definitely recommend taking this class with him for the FC or just because!

Dr. Conner is so kind-hearted, approachable, flexible, and friendly. Definitely go to OH to get to know him better because he is so fun to talk to and loves what he does. Readings can be up to 20 pg but class time is spent rehashing the reading. 3 papers and a final exam; generous grader. Super interesting and low-stress class def worth your time!

Really enjoyed this class! mandatory attendance. Awesome prof!! Imo, his lectures are very clear and slides posted afterwards so studying for the reading quizzes (done for hw) is very straightforward-- the readings are not super easy but he breaks down all the important parts in the slides. Essays also graded very clearly with rubric.

The professor is new and overall very nice. He is a very harsh grader on papers considering that its a beginner philosophy class. His exam was closed note and based on memory which was quite tough but I liked him as a person. His slides were really confusing to understand (lack of clarity) but it wasn't difficult to learn overall. Great prof.

Professor Conner has a class structure that is fairly simple. He highly emphasizes class participation, so get ready to read to assigned readings and be able to discuss them. There are 3 papers that are worth 55% of the grade and they can be difficult if you don't know how to write philosophy, but if you go to his office hours you'll be okay.

Dr. Conner is an amazing, understanding, and intriguing teacher. The course readings are engaging and challenge students to think beyond their current set of values. This class teaches students how to build an argument, so it has been foundational in bolstering my analytical writing skills.
He is amazing and kind and he would open up discussion question based on the topic we are on, and it is engaging.

Honestly, have no idea why people have issues with Dr.Garofalo. Yes, he is pretty awkward and makes some weird jokes, but I thought his grading system was fair, the quizzes were SO easy (he gives you a study guide with exactly what you need to know, which can be taken from the lecture slides) and I found the topics and class discussions fun

very lecture heavy! very accessible outside of class but never updated grades. you didn't have to do readings bc they were covered in lecture. overall nice guy and i learned a lot in class but it wasn't the most life changing class

Final paper 40% with 5 shorter papers worth 25%. Liked how we were given time to revise final. Required to teach class for 1 hour and 15 mins twice with group. Supposed to lead discussion while teaching, but awkward because many times when you asked questions, you got no response from class. Garofalo is nice but students did most of the teaching.
Grades feel subjective and are at the teacher's whim. There is no clear grading criteria, and what constitutes an A. Thought-provoking class, and the professor is nice, but the grading is bad.

He is a fine person; however, his grading is entirely arbitrary. It seems he has a preconceived grade in mind, docking points until you reach his sentiment. The class is not a great option if you are looking for gen-ed credit, but it is not very work-intensive.

Overall, I thought he was a nice guy and was passionate about his work. The class definitely made me think and challenged me. However, he did not post all of the grades until the end of the semester, so I never knew my grade in the class. I feel like he is a harsh grader and would really nitpick every detail.

He's a pretty lax grader, though I think grading was based more on effort and participation (any participation--not just answers that he was looking for). Lectures reiterated the readings (~20 pages/class) and explained them in more detail, which Prof. Garofalo did a good job of. He was also pretty funny!

Lectures were easy to follow and encouraged active participation. Knows the content extremely well and excels at asking the right questions to challenge students' perspectives. Grades based on participation, 3 open-note free-response quizzes, three 4-page essays, a group debate, and an open-note final with two essays. Grades rather generously

Professor G was a good professor and always challenged his students. The "take-home" exams are time-consuming essays that typically sum up to about 10-13 pages of writing. You don't have to do the readings to succeed, but focus on them for the final exam, it'll help. Final was also long, took me all three hours

An eccentric, intelligent, and clever man. High expectations (unspoken rule: you don't have to meet every one; ex. you can get by skipping readings.) Exams are LONG, & thoroughly graded.  An anecdote: once in class the NYT game sound went off and he finger gunned and said: "Let's see... that was the mini crossword, was it?" All laughed. He's cool

This class, in theory, was not a hard one as quizzes (3) were open note and papers were assigned with ample time (5 short + 1 long). However, I always felt like he graded my work harsher than necessary (didn't give full credit for a participation assignment that met all requirements). Never put grades in Canvas. Agree with the first post for him

Prof G is a quirky guy. 1 reading to do before every class (~10-30 pages).Can get by without reading; he doesn't check and goes over the material. Quizzes are open note, 5 short essays + a long final essay (hope you're a good writer!) Topics aren't very applicable to every day life but gets you thinking about the things around you to a deeper level

He's a great professor, class consisted in two  take home midterms, a weekly reflection, a quiz etc. I learned a lot from him. He's very accessible after classes. He makes you do all this work but you don't know your grade throughout the course

Nice enough guy. Really serious abt the class he teaches so maybe dont take a phil class if it isnt your major. Pretty flexible and reasonable. Easy assignments, very easy to get an a. Very heavy on reading, its not required but makes the lectures not a waste of time

Dr. Garofalo is a nice guy and I feel like the class made me think. However, I do think that some of the grades he gave were based on his own personal opinion and were somewhat unfair. It was reading heavy, with 5 short response papers and a final paper based off of the readings. The 3 non cumulative exams were easy and open note.

I recommend skimming the textbook reading before class since it follows almost identical to the lecture. He has a stack of flashcards with everyone's name on it and will call on you for a problem. Attendance is not mandatory but come on time every day since it could be a group pop quiz that day. Exams do not weigh heavily and aren't difficult.

He's pretty disorganized with his lectures, but they're helpful and he's always willing to clear up questions. Attendance isn't mandatory, but be careful because he does group pop quizzes. This class was really interesting and wasn't too much to keep up with, I just did practice problems and only ever read the textbook if I was confused.
Worst class ever literally discrete math and hard grader

Love Dr. Roberts. He is so smart and explains things clearly. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are pop group exercises sometimes where you're put with 1-2 other students and you work on some logic problems. Also uses name cards to call on students to help him solve problems. 2 fair exams. Basically just solving puzzles; I thought it was fun.
I found 155 so fascinating and it satisfied a science credit for me! Dr. Roberts was a really interesting lecturer and I felt he explained everything very well.

Pretty solid professor. John Roberts is very kind and caring about his students. His lectures can be a little disorganized sometimes but still a great teacher regardless. Hard to reach by email though which can be an issue if you have questions about the homework which is 50% of your grade.

This guy was so chill. Wrote his own textbook because he said the others were too expensive. and doesn't even assign readings. Lowkey disorganized sometimes, but if you attend class relatively frequently and do the homework you are good.

Prof. Roberts is a great instructor. As long as you show up to class, you will do well. He doesn't take attendance, but will randomly do group work extra credit where you can get percentage points added to your final grade. He is a little discombobulated sometimes, but overall, he is a wonderful professor!

He was 10-20 min late to class a lot. I took an incomplete b/c of a Crohn's flare. He nvr responded to my emails to schedule the Final. I went to the testing center and was told he never sent them my exam. When I took It, he submitted my course grade as "0". I emailed the head of the Phil Dep to get a hold of him, and it took him weeks to fix.

Professor Roberts was a clear and knowledgable professor and he is super passionate about teaching this topic. The homework assignments were reasonable and the hardest thing was the midterm since you were on a time crunch. I loved this class but I could see how if you don't like solving puzzles you would probably not enjoy this class

Professor Roberts deeply cares about the class material, so much so that it is easy to sit back relax, and listen to him lecture non-stop about philosophy for an hour. He is very kind and caring and doesn't ask much of his students other than to participate occasionally in class discussions and do the readings.
Professor Roberts was very passionate and cared about his students. The class was slightly unorganized, but the assignments were clear and manageable.

John Roberts is a great guy; he is clearly a knowledgeable philosopher and educator. PHIL 155 is a tough class, but he made it very accessible - he even wrote his own textbook for us! Also, he is not afraid to curve. However, he was so willing to answer questions that material was often rushed at the end of class. So definitely go to office hours!

HNRS30533—Take this class for Honors credit! Seminar style class I took with two of my friends. Quiz every class, except it's two questions you had about the assigned reading and I always got full credit. Two mini-essays that weren't very hard. Definitely my favorite honors class at TCU so far! He's also just a funny and goofy guy as an added plus
Professor Rothfus presents material in an interesting and engaging way and encourages participation and discussion.

PHIL 163. Super interesting class. Topics include abortion, capital punishment, animal ethics, and procreation. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about philosophy and he wants students to be too. Read one paper before every class from either side of a moral debate and then discussed. Midterm & final papers + final exam (w cheat sheet). Fair!
This rating is for Phil 163 but the option wasn't on here. Great professor and nice flowing class!

Gerard is really an amazing professor. He cares about his students' learning so much and will do anything to make sure we feel comfortable with topics for exams and homework. I would definitely pay attention in class and  briefly review topics in your free time, as the subject matter can get pretty hard.

I had Gerard for my first semester and I really loved his class, other than it being at 8 am. The readings could be pretty long and dull if you are not used to reading philosophy papers, but the readings really helped prepare me for the PHIL class I'm in now. He was very caring and gave good feedback. Definitely want to take another class with him

Gerard is a very difficult grader, consistently gives 7/10 on homework assignments that are due before every class. Readings for the homework assignments are around 20 pages, for every class. He is not available at his office hours and has his office door locked. Do not take for PH credit.
gave low final grades, we complained and he changed them, dont bother writing about your true beliefs, youll only get a good grade if you write about what he agrees with

Papers shouldn't be hard but turning them in and then receiving harsh rubric afterwards. Grading not based on the quality of arguments, but simply how close we got to his."here's a 100 if you say exactly what I want, 0 if you miss anything" Made fun of me for stuttering in class and rolled his eyes. Horrible experience.

Reeve is brilliant. His lectures are incredibly insightful. The papers are sometimes difficult but he gives you plenty of opportunities to correct them and improve your grade. One thing to watch for, if you show up with a lot of enthusiasm or confidence, he'll give you more of a hard time than the other students.

Easy as long as you are willing to rewrite papers, he lets you rewrite as many times as needed to get a better grade. Very easy A. However, he's a specific personality and interrupts students after begging for involvement. The class itself was fairly easy, but I was frustrated with his inability to accept other ideas & students to fully conversate.

This class was an amazing, in-depth dive into Plato's "Republic" by one of its foremost scholars. Reeve is very passionate, and while getting good grades on the papers is tough, he gives excellent feedback and allows corrections. It's clearly his goal for you to gain a deep understanding, and he'll help you work toward the grade that you want!

Dr. Hofweber is a spectacular lecturer. He does a great job of getting you to think about things in a really abstract way, yet maintains your attention. His class is very lecture heavy, but it is easy to follow along.
I originally thought the lectures would have been a lot more interesting than they actually were. The recitations were fun; basically just talking with a group about various topics.

This class was enjoyable to attend, but if you are looking for an easy A, this may not be the class for you. Your final grade depends on your TA, which may hurt you in the end. As someone who studies a lot and dedicated a lot of energy to the class, my grade wasn't reflective of my effort.
Incredible lectures if you are interested in the topic. Essays and tests are graded by TA's, so you just have to hope you get a lenient one. Great class and I learned a lot.

I took the class originally just for the FC credit but ended up really enjoying Dr. Hofweber's lectures. The difficulty of the class really depends on your TA but mine (Mattesich) did an excellent job in recitations and was also really kind to give us study guides for the midterm and final which is all you need to do a good job on them both.

Phil 143 was a pretty interesting class. The midterm and final were pretty easy if you just go to class and take some notes. I didn't do any of the readings and still did well on both since he brings up any important points from the readings in class. Go to your TA's office hours to ask about your main argument on your paper and you will do fine.

The class is easy if you have a good TA. Attendance wasn't mandatory in lectures but recitations was. I didn't go to class after midterm and was still able to do well afterwards (review powerpoints and readings). You're only graded on 4 things (two 5-page papers, midterm, and final). Make sure to follow what your TA wants and you'll be fine.

Lecture was boring, but you need to attend to understand the obscure slides he posted. Your grades are composed of two 5-page papers, a midterm, and a final, so your grades depend pretty much on your TAs. Just do your readings and participate in recitation discussion, and you should be fine.

Do not think the professor was very fair overall. I had a 100% all semester and received positive feedback on all 5 reading responses, but then got a 7/10 on our final paper which brought my grade down to a B+. It seems unfair to not have received constructive feedback throughout the class to help me with my final paper.

the professor was great overall but the structure of the class was not good, we were graded on very few things but the work load was easy. it has no final but there is a final paper that is very hard and is 40 % of ur grade

Great teacher who encourages lots of in class discussion. Doesn't take attendance but participation definitely aids in comprehension of the readings. 5 one page papers, one final paper, and one partner presentation all pretty evenly spread out. Overall just a great teacher and cool guy.
Interesting lectures. Hofweber is a stickler for attendance and only gives recorded lectures to those with an official excused absence. Do the readings and attend class and you'll get an A.

This class was a pretty easy A. The class was graded by only two papers and the final, but the papers were pretty easy if you followed the format the TAs asked for or got feedback, and the first one had a rewrite option. I didn't go to lectures for the second half and the final was still easy, I just reread the readings. Lectures were boring though

The class is so interesting and taught really well. Prof. Hofweber is such a great lecturer and the readings never felt like "too much". The papers were great and the TA's really helped structure them. The class isn't hard at all, but it does have readings, papers, and weekly recitation discussions. I would highly recommend this class.

He's a great lecturer and gave some good extra credit opportunities. Big lecture style with TAs grading, mine happened to be a super harsh grader with very little explanations for points off. Class still enjoyable he's very passionate, just don't expect a gpa boost. Cold called a bit so do the readings.

Great choice for the PPE capstone (or any other course he teaches). Professor Munoz clearly spent a lot of time putting together a flexible but informative curriculum designed for his students, and his lectures were never boring. There was a midterm test and a 10 page paper final, which was a nice structure for the course. Also, The Wire!
Dr. Munoz is an incredibly kind, caring, and passionate professor. He ensures that the class content is thought provoking and engaging. The majority of class assignments are graded by TAs.

Large lecture-style class, so it's mostly run and graded by TA's. Prof. Munoz is passionate and approachable. His lectures are great, but the powerpoint slides themselves aren't very coherent. Lots of reading (15-50 pdf pages per week), and there was hardly any content about econ at all. Overall a quality class, but too much work imo.

Professor Munoz is great! He makes lectures entertaining even for the denser readings. He is very passionate about what he teaches. The 3 exam grades and final project depend on your TA, but he gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit and is very responsive to feedback from students and TAs.

LOVE DANIEL! He cares about his students so much. Office hours were at Carolina Coffee Shop and he bought me lunch when I went. Super accessible outside class, engaging lectures, great at explaining tough concepts. Grading isn't always the clearest, but he's open-minded and passionate about what he teaches! Going bowling during our final exam time!

Very engaging, clearly passionate about both his work and his students. Incredibly approachable, and gave feedback on graded assignments that was clear and allowed for further improvement. I hadn't taken a phil/poli/econ class in years, but I am glad that this was the professor I had for my first course back. The reading wasn't light but manageable
Daniel is the goat. super entertaining lectures and very generous. 10/10 would recommend
Daniel is the goat. Best professor ever absolutely would recommend.

He's a solid professor—definitely better than most options for this class. He's super smart, and the class had some great discussions. The first half especially was strong, and we even got to watch The Wire, which made things more engaging. Not perfect, but I learned more here than I would've elsewhere.

I'm not a Philosophy major/minor but this was definitely my favorite class this past semester mostly because of the effort and enthusiasm he put into his lectures and assignment. He was super flexible in almost every avenue and made a somewhat intimidating class very intriguing and manageable.

One of the kindest professors at UNC, he was very considerate when it came to attendance. There were two books we had to read, both of which were interesting and sparked great conversations. There were a few quizzes, two essays, and a final presentation. I am not a philosophy major, or involved in it in any way, but this was a really great class.

A lovely human being and the discussions in this class were consistently electric. Dan may be the professor whose office I visit most, even when I don't have classes with him. A wonderful person to chat with and will definitely push you to consider issues more deeply.

Best professor I have had at UNC!! Incredibly caring, super accommodating, and invested in your success. No homework except short readings. No electronics allowed during lectures. He puts a lot of emphasis on participation and attendance. 1 midterm test, 2 midterm papers, 1 final group presentation. A must-take professor!

Dan is a really great person and professor; he really wants for everyone to understand and will work with you. go to office hours! it is SUPER easy to pass this class, but equally hard to get an A. Participation matters (20% of grade). Graded off participation, 1 exam, 2 essays, and a final presentation. Overall an interesting class.

SO caring, engaging, and genuinely cares about his students. Midterms/final is about showcasing what you know. No homework, just a short required reading before every class. Classes were lecture and discussion style, I always felt comfortable speaking in class. Super approachable inside and outside of class, a genuinely good person and professor.

Computers are not allowed in the classroom. Participation is also essential in this course, as all the lectures are interactive but enjoyable. Assignments are manageable and take-home but it can take a long time to receive grades and feedback. Professor Munoz is a fair grader, and you get out of this course whatever level of effort you put in.
Great lecturer! Everything we discussed was very interesting! Be aware, you HAVE to attend class to do well, he takes attendance very seriously. Also, no tech is allowed in class.

LOVE him. pretty interactive. usually, we play a game that relates to the economic theory we are learning about. Must participate, but its easy/fun to do so. Like 2 take-home short response/mini-essay assignments. He took a long while to grade but was pretty generous and flexible. He's passionate and knowledgeable. I would take this.

no technology allowed in classroom! will grade all the way down to the 0.1 level using a largely holistic grading scale/without a rubric, so grades can feel unjustified. took 2.5 months to grade 1 paper but funny and engaging lectures. exams were manageable and enjoyable to do. participation MATTERS! lecture heavy, will cold call.

Only got grades back for one essay. Blamed snow days for lack of structure all the way until May. Midterm was way too harshly graded considering the lack of detail and structure given in class. Do not waste your time.

Was expecting a food study class would be fun. It's not. The instructor appears to be an expert in sociology and gender study, and spends most of time on critical theory cliches. If you like this then take the class. Disappointed and regretted. The teaching style and the personality are OK

You don't have to attend class or read yet you can still get a good grade.Not only is she late for class but she often fails to respond to emails.This inefficiency made it difficult to communicate after class. Good choice for wasting your time.

Jessica is an amazing, caring, and knowledgeable professor who really cares about her students and is down to earth. Don't take FREN 186 if you're looking for a mindless easy gen ed - in order to succeed students must do the readings and make an effort to engage in class.

Don't use ChatGPT and getting an A easy. While it's possible to get by without it, I recommend doing the readings in order to participate in class discussion otherwise you will be bored. Three short essays, a midterm, a final project, and a final is all the graded work for the class. Professor Tanner provided delicious food for the final.

Easy class and a guaranteed A. No need to attend, participate, or do the readings. Assignments aren't read or graded. The professor is often late or cancels for personal reasons. Good if you want credits without effort, but not if you want to actually learn. Disappointed by the lack of professionalism, it's disrespectful for student's time.

She is an amazing professor! Super caring, kind, and knowledgeable. The class itself had weekly readings, a few short pop quizzes, short writing assignments, a midterm, final project, and final exam, but it was super manageable with her. Try to participate in discussions and DON'T use ChatGPT at all (makes your life and her life easier)!

She is such a great professor and truly cares about her students! This is a great class and you learn some really cool stuff. Class discussions are super interesting. Make sure you don't use AI for any of the assignments, that's the one thing she really hates. She's one of my favorite profs at UNC!

Professor Tanner is one of the sweetest french professors I have ever had. 330 has a ton of reading, but most of the texts were very interesting. Literally just put in effort and do like 70% of the reading and you will be fine. Participate too! She loves discussion. :)

Took this class for the philosophy credit (STEM major) and I did not regret it! You do have to read a good bit, but she is understanding if you don't finish on time. Deadlines are soft and tests are easy. She HATES ChatGPT and is scarily good at identifying it in assignments so if you can't complete an essay without it, don't take this class.

Really incredible professor!! One of, if not my favorite professor at UNC. She really cares, and takes so much time giving feedback which I love. She doesn't want you to fail. I have a lot of social anxiety and she makes it very accessible for me to still listen in class while not needing to speak. She goes out of her way to bake for her class!!

AMAZING! She's super relaxed on attendance but I actually want to come to class because of her. Some of the books we read are pretty dense but she makes them accessible in class. Brought in baked goods for us. So sweet and gives a lot of grace for errors and due dates. My fav French prof at UNC (and I've had pretty much all of them)

Super chill when it comes to turning in assignments, only downside was getting grades back. It was her first time teaching a bigger class of 70 students which is understandable so grading was slow- only got back 1 assignment out of 4 all semester, but she's a good grader so I wasn't too worried. Overall tip is to do the readings & watch the films

Tanner is extremely understanding and knows college students have a lot on their plate. Dropped to 4/6 assignments needed to be turned in, 1 midterm, final project, and final exam. Everything was open note (strict on chatgpt). Final project had the option to make a dish! Lots of readings but still do them or at least skim!!! Assign films to watch

Dr. Tanner is an extremely caring and empathetic professor. She is very accommodating and kind to her students even to a fault. DO NOT use chatgpt on her assignments because she will know since it will not give you answers that make sense in the context of the class. Overall, she was great and I enjoyed taking FREN186 with her.

Dr. Tanner is by far the kindest professor I've ever had at UNC. She is incredibly accommodating and very knowledgeable about French food and literature. Sometimes, I feel like she's almost too nice, as she's always dropping assignments and extending deadlines. If you're looking for an easy gened class with a fantastic instructor, take this class.

Prof Tanner is seriously so caring, flexible, and understanding. She moves around due dates whenever necessary, and she truly wants her students to enjoy her class and succeed. There are a ton of readings for this class though and you probably need to read them to do well on the exams (open note for our semester due to being a hybrid class).
unclear grading formula, such harsh grading for a language course, take other chinese professors

Fan Laoshi is so invested in seeing each one of her students succeed and learn. She is very accommodating and understanding and gives amazing feedback to help you improve. She also pushes her students to do better!

Prof. Fan is really nice and easy to talk to. She explains things well and actually gives useful feedback. The class takes some effort, but it's fair, and you learn a lot. Definitely recommend taking 102 with her.
Very understanding of late assignments and is a very easy grader but also her class is entertaining.

Fan Laoshi grades harshly, but she is fair, kind, and has a great sense of humor. You will get at least a B as long as you put in the effort. I had about 2-4 hrs of homework every week, and an hour of studying. Don't take this class if you aren't conversational in Chinese. Hit the anki flashcards for every vocab quiz, and you will be fine.

fan laoshi and this class can be intimidating at first (esp if you can't speak fluently/read/write at all like me) but my improvement has been insane. she is very funny and understanding. lots of hw and vocab words to learn in a short amount of time, but if you put the work in you'll be fine. 2 oral presentations (generous grading imo)

Fan laoshi is really kind and easy to talk to, and the class vibe is pretty relaxed. It feels okay to make mistakes, and she genuinely cares about students. The class can be challenging sometimes, but it's manageable and not super stressful. I'm glad I took this class.

Fan Laoshi is a great instructor for Chinese 111. She explains concepts clearly and is very patient when answering questions. She encourages group discussions, which makes the class more engaging and helps with speaking practice. Overall, I learned a lot and would definitely recommend her.

she is understanding but there is so. much. work. like we would learn 50+ words in one class and have the vocab quiz the next. her rubrics can be a little vague so don't be afraid to ask because she is pretty lenient on some project deadlines and explains things well. fan laoshi also encourages group discussions so be open to that!

super sweet and funny, genuinely had a lot of fun in this class. if you're going to take chinese def take it with her. lots of homework, but very manageable and gives lots of extra credit opportunities as well!! weekly quizzes but they're very easy!

Took 111 and 212 with her and loved it. She's super funny and you can tell she cares about her students. These classes really improved my Chinese, especially reading and writing. There's a large workload but it's not too difficult, mainly practicing vocab.

204 is structured pretty much the same as 203. I definitely recommend taking it! This class is way smaller, and you get a lot of speaking and writing practice. I took Professor Fan for both, and my improvement from 102 to 204 has been huge.

Professor Fan is a great professor. The class is definitely fast-paced and intense, but very similar in structure to 101 and 102, just with more heavy-hitting tests. She's a kind grader and highly available for meeting outside of class. Ask lots of questions and you'll be okay!

her syllabus is very clear and fairly accurate, however be ready for a vocab quiz every other day (the day after 'learning' them in class). you do make a lot of friends in this class! and there are two oral presentations that you do with a partner. overall, a very good course, don't drop it, she's pretty generous with the final grade!
Fan is a good and friendly professor, but expect lots of hw, quizzes, and exams.

Fan laoshi was a good professor. Assignments were not bad but could take a while if you don't know how to read Chinese. However, she is a very easy grader for homework and presentations. Some students did not like her, but I think it was just hard for them to accept that you have to study a bit for your ethnic language. Take about 30min-1hr a week.
Take her class if you want a professor that cares about you. She's a very good professor, especially for students who want to get better with chinese. Her office hours are also very helpful.
Fan laoshi does listen to her students and will change aspects of the course based on feedback.

SO MUCH WORK. literally took the class just for the language requirement and had more work in it than any other class. also fan laoshi is definitely biased and favors some students, which definitely showed in the grading. will grade based on experience so tell her if youre not exactly a fluent native speaker

Fan laoshi is so lovely. She genuinely cares about her students and puts a lot of thought into how to make her class relevant to her students. I had her for 111 and it helped me adapt to 212 faster. Her grading criteria is clear and fair and she gives great feedback. I was able to make great friends in this class as well!

You don't know your grade until the very end. Nothing goes in canvas. Not even the quiz grades. It would be fair to assume it's mostly participation in class but he doesn't even tell you what the exam is weighted. It's easy if you participate and try, he's a good teacher and he really really cares about his students. No excused absences though.
Love this class, very engaging, lots of time to practice Dutch, and very clear expectations for quizzes and tests. Provides good feedback and cares for his students.

Professor Thornton is amazing! Take this class if you can! As a first-year student, this class was amazing for meeting new people and getting to know a tight-nit group. Participation goes a long way and he often just calls on people. Highly recommend spending some time with the vocab and practicing the material, it made this class a breeze.
Dr. Thornton was amazing! I was so excited to go to his class everyday. He made learning a language so much fun!!! Please take his class if you can!
Super simple language class, grade is mostly participation, great instructor. You HAVE to participate in class and if you do, you'll be fine.

Professor Thornton is the goat. He is a great professor and I am so thankful I chose to take Dutch with him. Easily my favorite professor here at UNC. If you need to fulfill your language requirement, CHOOSE DUTCH WITH HIM!!! The class isn't really a gimme, but if you keep up with the work, you will absolutely be fine.

Awesome professor! He's super caring and helpful. He genuinely wants you to succeed! You have to go to class and participation matters, so talk in class. Overall, great class and would take again. Dan also knows a thing or two about the Netherlands, so don't be shy about asking him questions!

If you need to complete your foreign language requirement, take Dutch with Dr. Thornton. He's one of the kindest people I've met at UNC, and he makes learning a foreign language very accessible. You take both 402 and 403 with him to finish the requirement, and you get to have the same class for two semesters which really builds a nice community.

This is one of the best professors at UNC! The professor cares deeply for their students and makes learning a foreign language fun and stress-free. The class won't be an easy A, but you're given all the resources to succeed. Also, you learn a great deal about the Netherlands.

I loved Professor Thornton's class. To succeed you MUST go to class, he covers things that aren't in the textbook. If you must miss class as long as you email him he is very kind about it. go to class as much as possible. His quizzes are fair and the study guides are very helpful.
One of the nicest people on campus. If you can take this class, regardless of your major or anything else, please do.

Dan is one of my favorite professors that I've ever had. He's very caring and really makes this a fun class. Dutch is definitely one of the easier languages to learn especially with Dan teaching the class.
Dan Thornton is one of the best professors at UNC. He is incredibly caring and truly gets to know his students. If you're going to take a language at UNC take Dutch with Prof Thornton.

Dan is so sweet and made learning Dutch a pleasure! He's super passionate about teaching, and this is by far the easiest language I've taken and there's not a lot of homework. He's also a very forgiving grader and there are a bunch of tests so if you mess up on one you're fine! Loved taking Dutch with him and feel like I learned a lot!

My favorite professor at UNC. Absolutely loved my time in this class and wish I could take it every semester. He is so obviously passionate about his work and his teachings which make the class a great environment to learn. Class size is small enough to where I learned every students name and built some new friendships. I recommend Prof Thornton!

Amazing professor! He went out of his way to make sure everyone understood the material we were learning. There are about 8 units and a quiz for each one, as long as you knew your stuff they were easy.

Dan is a good teacher who cares about his student's success. He tests comprehension every unit with small quizzes, but they don't feel overwhelming or too hard. Good class. This review was also for the 2nd level of Dutch - DTCH 403, but RMP doesn't have that option.

THE GOAT. Carmen is so chill and genuinely cares about her students. There are a lot of homework assignments, but she is accommodating and most are a completion grade. Great if you need an extension as well. So kind.

Prof. Hsu is clear, passionate, and discussion-focused. Readings can be dense but are reviewed in class. 2 papers and 3 quizzes (all chill), open-note quiz final, grading is super easy, and she's responsive and kind. Lot of HW is video-based (completion grade), which isn't for everyone. She always asked about our weekends. Highly recommend!
This is my favorite class at UNC. Professor Hsu is so knowledgeable. I've learned a lot from this class. She is very kind and willing to work with the class on due dates.

Topic: Love and Conflict in Spanish Literature - - -
Knowledgeable about the topic, cares about her students. She gives lots of opportunities for increasing your grade, but if you read the texts, participate in class, and do a bit of studying, you will do fine. She also gives candy sometimes.
Professor Hsu is awesome: she really cares about her students and is so knowledgeable about her stuff. I love her!

Topic: Love and Conflict in Spanish Literature
Prof. Hsu is super chill, all of the grading criteria is laid out and well organized. Just do the readings and the required amount of homework and you will be fine. She gives opportunities for extra credit, and the class is very discussion based. Hardest part is the essays, but she grades fairly.

Dr. Hsu is one of the most supportive professors at UNC! She is very kind and really wants you to succeed in her class.  It is important to always put in much effort when participating in class.  You do have to present a reading analysis and a peer review. Plus you perform 2 skits with classmates.  Final was just a 10 page paper.
uper sweet lady who helped me with personal matters outside of class. grades pretty lightly but she can tell when you don't try on assignments. just do the work and you'll be golden

Great professor who cares about her students and offered lots of extra credit. She really wanted her students to succeed and was very accommodating for people's needs, offering extensions and new deadlines.

Carmen is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. The structure of this FYS is largely discussion based, so make sure you come into class having read the readings (or at least able to contribute something of substance to the discussion which is pretty low stakes). Carmen is SO kind and caring. Go to office hours if you need more help.

I loved Prof. Hsu, she gives great lectures and is such a great person--she is a very harsh grader though. For a first-year seminar, there is very little guidance on how to write the essays and complete the assignments. There is also never a rubric, or if there is one, it is very vague. I love her, but I would only take a higher-level class.

If you had a good time in PORT101, you'll have a good time her in PORT102. Speaking is heavily emphasized, and she is patient and flexible with it. If you had a bad time in PORT101, you will probably be a little sad. If you put in any amount of effort greater than 0, you'll be fine.

Kristine has unreasonable expectations for 102 students, considering this is only the second semester a majority of students are learning the language. She expects us to be focused on Portuguese 24/7 and master new content the day after a flipped classroom assignment is due. Do not take if there are other options.
Prof Taylor had easy tests/quizes but was a harsh grader with oral and written assigments. Often condescending.
Profa Taylor is so kind and really wants you to succeed and enjoy learning. 101 was pretty easy but I feel like I got a lot out of it! Eu amo Profa Taylor.
She is a harsh grader and a lousy teacher. Pretty brutal combo.

An A is definitely possible and her expectations are clear. She cares a lot about her students and it shows. What little homework you have is very helpful and the tests are not too hard. As long as you put in effort to learn, you will do well. I wish I could take another class with her!

Taylor cares so much about her students and is genuinely the sweetest lady. You get out what you put in, and an A is easily achievable b/c she clearly lays out rubrics and what will be on the tests. She does not give any more tests than the other professors. Very little homework. She teaches 50/50 Engl + Port which is so rare for a 203 level.

As someone bad at languages, her style was perfect for me, taking time to go over grammar and explaining in English, which is rare in 203. She was kind and attentive to everyone from fluent speakers to people who had no desire to learn port. Everyone in the class spoke highly of her and I enjoyed her teaching even while I didn't love the language.

Do not do not take Professor Taylor's class if you want to do well, be supported, and congratulated for your academic successes! She doesn't give clear directions and she grades very harshly. When one thing is due 3 more are due in the next few days. I don't think she cares if her students do well or not.

Professor Taylor is great if you are just trying to finish the class for your language credit. There are issues with teaching and I do not think she prepares you for upper level classes, however, for most people they are not looking for that. Unlike most Portuguese professors, she teaches in English, making the class much easier than most.

AWFUL. DONT take profa's class, unless you want to feel stupid & worthless. She doesn't teach, just expects you to magically know everything Portuguese. She takes FOREVER to grade. She starts class early & ends class late, finding it rude when people pack up early. Im warning you, if you want to do well and feel smart chose a different professor.

I took Profa for PORT 101 and again for PORT 102. Although she's the only PORT professor I've taken, and I can't really compare her to others in the department, I think she's an amazing professor who truly wants to help you learn! It's pretty easy to get an A as well, definitely recommend. Just make sure to participate when you can.

Taylor makes PORT harder than any other prof. She is very kind and truly wants you to learn the language, but compared to other port professors she just makes assignments too difficult. I found that compositions and oral exams had ridiculous content expectations, making it hard to keep word limit and include content. Still a fairly easy A.

I learned a ton in this class, improving both my grasp of history and the Spanish language. I found the workload reasonable, and the final group project was really creative and actually fun. De Fays was kind and a super interesting lecturer as well; she's very well versed in the subject matter. I would highly recommend this class!

De Fays is very nice but can seem a bit intimidating at first. Classes involve a lot of participation and group work, but is very helpful to improve Spanish. Midterms and final are difficult, but doable if you study. Challenging class, but would recommend De Fays.

Profe De Fays is so kind, funny, and caring. She explains concepts pretty well, and she also makes class sort of conversational, which makes it easier to learn (though my class did have 7 people). There is a decent amount of online homework, but it's not awful. The final research paper could had more instruction, but she wanted us to succeed.
best spanish prof ever.
Very good professor, funny, cool creative project across the entire semester, very tough grader, very difficult exams. If you are a history buff this class is for you.

She is nice but didn't really seem to care about us. After I went to her with a personal issue and asked for some leniency with missing a few classes due to a family medical issue, she seemed understanding and said that since I let her know it was an "excused absence" but then gave me a low participation grade.

She is such an amazing Spanish professor. 261 has a lot of content so if you are not a strong speaker, you should prep in advance, but it was very easy and manageable. Tests are straightforward if you study for them, research paper is not complicated. Great professor!

A lot of HW for the class for a 3 credit language class. Be on top of things and make friends to form a study group. Any test was very hard and writing-based. On paper she will take off points for many simple things. I put in 10+ hours of work every week for this class to get a B+. But De Fays is very nice and funny!

Overall, this class really helped me with my Spanish and grammar usage. Doctora de Fays was a very nice professor and explained concepts well. Don't take this class with her if you don't enjoy participating and speaking a lot in Spanish because you will get a C- or lower for participation (and I mean participating multiple times per class).

Meant for SPAN261: Overall, this class really helped me with my Spanish/grammar usage. Dra de Fays was a kind professor. However, don't take this class with her if you don't enjoy participating and speaking a lot in Spanish because you will get a C- or lower for participation (and I mean participating multiple times per class).

Profesor De Fays was honestly so fun and engaging. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. This class did involve a lot of writing which made the class a little more challenging but she organizes it in stages so it is not as overwhelming. She genuinely wants people to love spanish and it shows in the way she teaches!

I loved this class, but it required a lot of work. Get comfortable speaking Spanish with classmates and Prof. de Fays because that is a big part of your participation. Reading comprehension and grammar homework each night, 5-page research paper, round table talk, and 3 exams. It is doable, but you need a good Spanish foundation to get an A.

This course is far from easy, but Prof. de Fays makes it a good experience. She's incredibly knowledgable on the coursework, so she encourages participation & different perspectives. Her lectures are engaging, and I feel like she genuinely cares for her students. Outside of class, she gives great feedback on assignments.

She is super sweet, open, and honest with the class. The entire semester, she was understanding of the difficulties of being a student and was flexible as long as you explained yourself. She was not too hard of a grader for this class, but attendance and participation is needed to succeed in the class.

Absolutely loved class with De Fays! She is so funny and makes lectures so so interesting! Loves it when you ask questions and participate. Exams are challenging, but the way your grade is made up of so many different projects and papers, it isn't too hard to get an A! Would 100% take more classes with her

Prof. De Fays is very nice, but her grading is very tough. She is very nitpicky in homework assignments and on the final project. You will lose 10 points for grammar issues and you will lose points for word choice, even if the grammar is correct. Overall, there is not much work in the class but the grading can be very harsh at times.
Love her! Very kind and understanding, accessible outside of class, and very funny! My favorite Spanish professor I've had at UNC.

De Fays was a really good lecturer! She really knew her material and was willing to explain concepts and provide feedback and help. She could be condescending or brash at times, but she was overall very funny and caring towards students.

Profesora is one of the most considerate professors I have had at UNC. She is very respectful of her students and is very fair with the material. I had specifically chosen 3 classes in the past just to have her as a professor again. She cares for her students and provides the necessary materials and class environment for you to succeed. 10/10 :)

She's amazing. It was my first college course, but she was very unintimidating and cared a lot about her students. She takes great note of participation, so be ready to raise your hand when you come to class. You'll have a lot of homework assignments, but nothing that takes incredibly long.
Just pay attention in class and you'll be set. She cares about her students and classes are fun if you make it fun!

Difficult class => learning new grammar and sentence structures. Helpful in-class slides and willing to answer questions about topics. Read textbook before class (at least the structures and vocabulary) to prepare. Not an overwhelming amount of homework (~1 to 2 hours/week + studying). Very kind. Harsh-ish grader (using department-wide criteria).

Professor Ansaloni did not know how to teach English speakers the French language. She wasn't able to understand our errors, which made communication difficult. She was an insanely harsh grader, unreasonably so. This class tanked my GPA and I would never recommend taking her class.

Professor Ansaloni is sweet and tries to help you outside of class. This class is very fast-paced, so you have to go to class and participate. She is very nice, but the class is difficult, especially if you're a beginner. Since this is a language class, the grading is a bit subjective and harsh sometimes, but if you work hard, you can succeed.

She is really caring and personable, but the fren 105 curriculum moves really fast and the lectures were confusing at times as much of French grammar can be. Her grading could be tough and also lenient but that was more on the department at not her.

I really liked professor Ansaloni. She was a great professor, there's a lot of homework in her class, but it's not really her fault as it's the FREN105 content. She was always easy to access and very accommodating. The difficulty rating isn't really her fault, it's just the FREN105 curriculum.

Prof Sara was a tough grader and the entire class is a flipped classroom so you have to teach yourself everything. It is supposed to be a "beginner" class but you are expected to enter with a LOT of knowledge and she only speaks in french the entire class. If you cannot understand french very well do not take this class. VERY fast paced class.

Professor Ansaloni is a wonderful teacher! She is very caring and creates a fun class environment. There is a fair amount of work through daily homework on MindTap, occasional papers, and tests about every other week. She is a tough grader. The class moves quickly, but she works with her students and heavily encourages participation.
she is such an angel and is so caring for her students!

She is such an amazing instructor! She makes learning super engaging and fun and is always available to help. She made grading and assignments very clear and created a welcoming class environment that made asking questions and speaking up super easy. I wish I could take another class with her!

Professor Jo is a great teacher and I always had a great time in that class. There were only 20 of us and we sat in a circle style while she went through slides at the front. There's a ton of practice, which is really good because I believe that's the best way to learn spanish. She cold calls all the time, but does it to everyone so its not bad.
Actually so engaging and funny. The GOAT.

such an enthusiastic and high energy professor! class material can be a bit dense at times and she's not the easiest grader but if you actually read the material you'll be fine. comprehension quizzes ('pruebitas') throughout the semester and weekly homeworks will cushion your grade.

Dr. Lindquist is absolutely amazing and you should definitely take a class with her any chance you get. She is very nice, funny, and eager to teach you about Spanish. Not only does she do a good job teaching the material, but she also interacts with students in a fun and enjoyable way. She genuinely wants to see her students succeed.

Dr. Lindquist is a phenomenal teacher! She does a lot of pair work and always makes us laugh. She is accessible through office hours, email, and even holds a couple review sessions. She is very understanding and helpful without judgment, and made Spanish one of my favorite classes. I wish she was our teacher next year!

I loved Dr. Lindquist and she's not the issue herself, but the SPAN 105 curriculum, which she creates (she's the head of the department). This class took SO much studying and there was SO much homework to where I stopped learning because I had to look up answers to have time for other classes. Just take at a community college I beg of you!!!

LOTS of working in pairs! I had concerns about taking it with her being the 105 coordinator, but it meant she could be much more flexible. Very kind and willing to help. Unlimited tries on online hw, so if you want you can end with a 100 for hw grade. Besides that, 3 tests and a final, a cool project at the Ackland, participation points, etc.

IMMACULATE PROFESSOR! Get ready to be called on, but she's always willing to help you get a better understanding. Daily homework can pile up, but it's honestly super easy. Her class was very enjoyable! Very hilarious and personable! If you take this class, take it with Lindquist! She's also the dept. head, so she'll make sure you know everything!

She was an incredible professor and I wish I could have her as my professor again next year. She's very helpful and makes sure every student is included and is following along. She is very kind and was understanding when I got sick during a test, and let me take it later. She is hilarious and very engaging, I loved this class a lot.

TAKE THIS CLASS! There is daily HW, but it's doable and is less HW than some of my 3-credit courses. Jo is genuinely super funny and kind. Participation matters, but she never belittles anyone for their mistakes and tries to make everyone feel welcome. Her canvas modules align a lot with the midterm content, so be sure to study them most of all!

Lindquist is a great option if you need to take Spanish 105 at UNC. If you ask for help, she is more than willing to support you. She was funny, caring, and absolutely loves Spanish. I also don't think she will ever run out of energy.

She was very nice and funny. She assigns a lot of homework and the due dates are set at random days and times so it was easy to get them mixed up. The test were not very easy but doable if you understand what she teaches throughout her lectures.Sometimes she just teaches a little fast if you don't learn the material before class.

She was literally so sweet and funny and I was genuinely happy to see her every day. Class was pretty easy as long as you follow along and participate and she is so helpful even if you don't know any Spanish. I loved her so much!!

Lindquist was so nice and caring, the class itself was also very difficult as I did not have much Spanish background. If you come in a similar situation make sure to look over material from the day after each lecture, I got quite behind and had to work back. Overall Jo is by far the best option for 105 and actually made it enjoyable.

My favorite professor I've had so far! I would really recommend taking SPAN 105 with her. She is energetic, funny, and incredibly kind. She is always willing to answer questions and provide extra help if you need it (responds to emails really fast). If you show up to class and pay attention, you're guaranteed to make a good grade.

Awesome. Absolutely amazing professor. Do everything you can to take this class with her. She is so fun and attentive, seems to truly care about students, and creates a great environment that is not overwhelming. She hints at pop quizzes and the tests are very straightforward. Make sure to attend class, you wont want to miss it anyway.

Professor Lindquist is simply an amazing professor. She is funny and passionate, and she made class something I looked forward to. There is a lot of homework, but that is expected for a Spanish course. She was super accommodating and created a welcoming class environment. She is one of my favorite professors!

Jo made me love Spanish again. Her reviews are right, she's very good at her job. U will have a lot of HW, but it's for ur own benefit. Be ready to study outside of class if u want a good grade. Class was energetic & fun! Clear guidelines & expectations. I wish Jo taught 203, I would take her again. I learned so much & enjoyed it. 1 of my fav profs

Dr. Lindquist is such a spunky professor that actually made me enjoy taking Spanish. While sometimes the participation in class and her constant group work can sometimes be a little nerve-wracking, she never makes you feel bad for not understanding. In fact, she will always go out of her way to help you in any way she can. Love her so much.
Jo is the best Spanish professor. Take her class!!

The homework in this class was light, easy, and helpful for learning. The tests/essays weren't bad as he always gave us a clear idea of how they would be structured beforehand and how he would grade them. He's a lenient grader and always seemed eager to answer any questions. His dad jokes and frequent out of pocket statements are a big bonus too.

Take PORT101 with Vernon! Extremely fair grading, straightforward assignments, and the grading expectations are crystal clear. He's easily accessible via office hours and email, and he has dad joke humor which is a plus. I've learned way more than I thought without the effort of every other language at UNC.

The most fun I've ever had in a language class. Compared to general high school level classes, I learned maybe 3x more but with 2x less difficulty. Super funny, super clear, super supportive, and just amazing. If you actually try in this class, it will be easy and fun.

TAKE 101 WITH VERNON! He's SO funny, understanding, and he knows his stuff. It's tough at first if you're like me and had no Spanish or Portuguese knowledge, but it gets easy fast. Textbook is online and that's where you'll do homework, which is easy. 1 midterm, 2 short tests, a couple essays, a couple speaking tests, and final. PARTICIPATE!!!!

Good professor for Spanish 101. He made lectures entertaining. The whole 101 curriculum is standard across all sections, and homework is all online and not challenging. The content of each exam is pretty heavily explained beforehand. The only thing is that I've heard other professors were much more lenient on the oral interview grade.

very chill person and classes were always laid back although participation is mandatory. Quizzes aren't  too bad if you study and homework is fairly easy and light. Not the greatest at actually teaching the concepts so I lived in the library for a week before the final but it turned out okay.

Professor Vernon gives you absolutely everything you need to succeed in a foreign language. He is very understanding and helpful to anyone who asks. He gives you plenty of resources. Homework is only on an application called Lingro Language and is not very difficult. Overall, it was a fun class with lots of participation.

Dr. Vernon is an awesome guy. He's not the best at tech, which is a very large portion of the course, but still, he is so sweet and funny nonetheless. He definitely made the class easier than other 101 professors, and is always cracking funny jokes. Would highly recommend you take a language with him.
King. So nice. Taking him for 102 next semester

funniest guy ever sweet easy grade, you can ask him questions on exams and he'll hint at the answer, lots of assignments, none are that hard if you put in the effort, def study for exams, hw you can cheat through if you dont feel like doing it, you can get through class without fully understanding the concepts,sometimes his instructions arentclear
He was very chill, go with the flow. MyPORT LAb for homework and 3 short written paper which he gives back with the option to make corrections and make better grade.

Richard was a great professor. Super laid back and funny. Gave three free absences. He was flexible and accommodating. He teaches well and makes the material easy to digest. I walked away from this semester with a pretty good understanding of basic Portuguese after going in not knowing a word.

Very fun and nice professor, not too intense in workload/difficulty. You learn how much you want to learn in the class which is nice and overall a great pick for a prof- very knowledgable in the material and the classes are loose!
He was one of my favorites! He was very kind and wanted everyone to do well. He gave us many opportunities to succeed. His class was very easy and enjoyable. I fully recommend him.
Vernon is an easy professor for 101. He's very lenient in his grading. Sometimes I think we could be learning more but I will not complain because he's easy.

Class is super easy but a bit boring and feels like a waste of time, I barely needed to study and got good grades on tests and he grades super super easy with not a ton of work to do.  MPL is for completion and you get participation by showing up.  we do kinda pointless and non helpful activities in class but its so so easy.

Professor Vernon is very chill. However, he was very hard to access out of class sometimes, and often times the syllabus homework did not match up with the homework dates on Mastering, so double check. Overall, the class was super easy, just know the vocab, and put a little effort into the projects, and you'll do great.
If you have a good understanding of any romance language or already know Portuguese, take these two classes and enjoy how fun it is. This is by far the best class I have taken at UNC.

For as bad I am at Portuguese, prof. Vernon makes the course manageable and is very understanding and lenient. In a department with a mixed bag of professors, you are most likely to get a good grade in his class, and he's all around a nice and funny guy.
He is super easygoing! The tests are very straightforward and are on stuff covered in class. Definitely take his class if you have the option!

Took FREN105 with him - He was my favorite professor by far this semester! He is super kind and funny, going to his class was never a bore. FREN105 has a good bit of homework but he is super fair with grading and gives great feedback.

David was easily my favorite professor this semester. I took French 105 and this class is tough but that's just language at UNC, that's not his fault. David was extremely helpful, he clearly wanted all of his students to do well, and he's just an overall good person. If you're taking French at UNC I would highly recommend his class.

I loved David's French 101 Class, super helpful and a great teacher. Highly recommend taking a french class with him!

Couldn't rate under french 101.

He was very helpful and nice, when I went to office hours he gave me plenty of resources. Despite not being very good at French because I tested into this level, he graded leniently and I was able to make an A in his class with just the assigned textbook reading. Definitely worth taking!!
One of my favorites at UNC. Cares so so much, and is well versed in Italian. If I could take all of my classes with him, I would. Go to his office hours he will help you in ANY way you need.

Aubrey is a great professor. He cares a lot about his students and is very willing to work with you. Language isn't always easy but he made it interesting and I learned a lot from the course. Highly recommend Italian for completing the language requirement.

I had Aubrey for 102, he was an amazing professor. He was very passionate about the language, and his passion really helped my passion for Italian grow as well. He was very helpful during class and office hours, and he is extremely patient. He also speaks Italian at a moderate pace that is very easy to follow. One of my favorite professors at UNC.
I had Aubrey for 102 and he was great! he cares a lot about his students and makes sure you know it's ok to make mistakes and not be perfect. I would gladly take a class with Aubrey again!

Mr. Hart is a phenomenal person and teacher! I had him for both ITAL-101 and ITAL-102, and overall, the Italian department at UNC is AMAZING! Aubrey is a great teacher and is super encouraging and understanding. For sure, I would recommend taking any ITAL courses with him.

I was taught by Aubrey for ITAL 101 & 102. He is an amazing Italian professor! He is a current grad student, and he is really passionate about teaching. He makes learning accessible and fun, and he is very understanding of the fact that we are still learning and will likely make mistakes. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Dr. Pruvost is a good teacher but grades very strict on grammar. There are lots of readings in FREN204 so be prepared to read a lot. Classes are mandatory and she gets kind of passive aggressive if you have to miss one. Overall, a sweet woman.
this class was super interesting, but the assignments were definitely harder than i anticipated. dr. pruvost grades meticulously, but provides great feedback and is there to help you.

Prof Pruvost wants you to succeed! She is very accessible outside of class. She is kind and a clear grader. Be sure to ask for help if you start falling behind. I would love to take another class with her.

Dr. Pruvost was a wonderful professor for FREN 300. Although she assigned lots of homework and assignments, she was very understanding and always there to support you. Extremely flexible with deadlines, she greatly appreciates communication and attending her office hours.

Honestly, 105 is pretty fast paced and there are lots of assignments to go through but if you're ever struggling Prof. Pruvost is always available during office hours. She wants you to succeed and also ensures that you know it's okay to make mistakes. Participation is super super important! I recommend going over your notes a couple times a week
Just not a good professor. Dry and boring. Lots of work, essays, and tests. Tougher than STEM classes honestly.

Dr. Pruvost was one of my favorite professors at UNC, and she was by far the best professor that I had in the French department. She was incredibly understanding and kind. She was great at explaining concepts in class, and she actually understands that people have lives outside of her coursework. 5/5 love her!

She is one of the most kind and considerate professors I have had. However, she is a pretty tough grader compared to other professor who can teach the same class. You will definitely learn a lot in her class but grades do not come easy.

Way too much information to remember for each test. The homework takes forever to finish. Even if you participate a lot in class, that part of the grade will still be pretty bad compared to what other professors would give you based on a similar effort.

Dr. Pruvost is a great professor and is very understanding if any circumstances arise. She is definitely a little nitpicky in her grading, but overall she is available to talk with her students and cares greatly. The topic of 305 was also fascinating, and she was very open to suggestion on how to improve the class
Took FREN 305 with her, class was good and her expectations were clear. The class was more eurocentric that I would have liked but otherwise the lectures/reading were generally interesting

rating ITAL 51. She is so sweet and really cares about her job and the material. For a first year seminar, the workload is not a lot which is really helpful and she allows you to be creative and have some fun. Overall solid FYS.

Really nice professor and it's telling from her classroom environment. She has a passion for what she teaches, but I found it difficult to gain knowledge through her teaching. 75% of the concepts you have to know are from what she says during lectures, so take REALLY good notes. The books can only do so much for what she expects on assignments.

Professor Fritz-Morkin was amazing! She's so kind and caring towards her students and is clearly knowledgeable about the subject.
