Although she encourages participation, she understands that the class is lecture-heavy and that not everyone is comfortable speaking. We only had a couple of writing assignments, and she's awesome!

Dr. Fritz-Morken is amazing!! She cares so much about her students and it shows. Classes are lectures with big group discussions. Talking isn't mandatory, but the class environment is comfortable enough that it's not stressful. There are two writing assignments, one project, a midterm, and a final exam. Listen in class and you'll get an A!

Super caring professor. Grading feels very fair and there is a lot of flexibility with deadlines. If you attend lectures and read summaries of the readings, you'll be fine. Only three big assignments and two tests- very low effort class.

I took ITAL-372 (didn't have the option to choose) with Dr. Fritz-Morkin. The course material was not my cup of tea, but she's a great professor. She grades this class fairly lightly and is a helpful resource both in and out of lectures. She has a good sense of humor as well. If medieval Italian literature interests you, you should take this class.

Genuinely my favorite professor that I have had at UNC. Prof. Fritz-Morkin is incredibly kind and understanding on top of her passion for what she teaches. Dante on his own can be dense and hard to understand but this class was a joy and made the experience much more enjoyable.

Prof Fritz-Morkin is very caring, was accessible outside of class, and gave great feedback on papers. The only grades are 3 short papers, 1 midterm, and a final exam, so the workload is minimal throughout the semester. As long as you go to class and take notes you can still do well without reading, would recommend for a gen ed

I actually took ITAL 130 but it's not an option to select. I never got below a 98 on any assignment and attendance was not mandatory (but I would still try to go because she's very passionate and tells you exactly what the tests will be on in class). She was extremely helpful during office hours. There were only 3 essays and 2 tests in total.

*ITAL 372, not 379.* Professor Fritz-Morkin is the absolute best. I was a bit scared of this class coming in, but it was interesting, fun, and low stress. The poems for each class were difficult to read, but she did a great job at explaining them. Graded off of a few small assignments, two papers, and a presentation. Highly recommend!

She is one of the best instructors I have ever had. She is very kind and approachable with every student, and her lectures are truly interesting thanks to the passion she brings to her subject. I recommend this course to everyone.

An amazing teacher who genuinely cares about her students. She will always take the time to meet with you outside of class if you need help, and she is a very lenient grader. The exams are not very difficult and if you ask for extra credit she will always give you something to do.

Russian Department Legend. She is super sweet, caring, and funny. Participation is a must, and her lectures are engaging. She simply wants all of her students to learn the Russian language. All the resources are available, and she provides excellent feedback. As long as you show up, participate, and do your work, you'll succeed.

Truly my favorite professor I've had at UNC, will do anything and everything to help you succeed in her class. She's so funny and makes me really look forward to coming to her class and I literally structured my entire schedule next semester so I can take 204 with her
I had her as an undergraduate in 96 and 97.  Loved her and her classes.

She's great at making the class engaging and really cares about each person's success. She will call you if you're falling behind/haven't been in class. A lot less talking in class than McGarry's class and harder to get an A. Still lots of small group work in class. Very funny
Simply the GOAT of the Russian department at UNC. The best lecturer there is, with a nice sense of humor. She is joyful and passionate about what she teaches.

Professor Magomedova truly cares about all of her students and wants them to succeed. Russian is an extremely hard language, but her class makes it seem manageable and I found myself wanting to study. She is engaging and extremely knowledgeable. Take a class with her if you can!

Eleonora is one of the kindest people I have ever met. Had her for 101, 102, and 203. She really cares about her students and is willing to help them succeed.  You will have homework every day, but they are short and take between 10-20 minutes. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC.

I haven't had much contact with literature and was nervous to take this class, but I ended up loving it! Eleonora is extremely caring and accommodating, and I loved every piece we read over the semester. I'd take it again if I could.

Prof. Stenz is great and teaches the class very well. He is very helpful for learning French. There was quite a good amount of homework, but definitely manageable. As long as you spend a bit of time actually learning the material, the class is great.
Great professor. full stop
Lowk is a really easy prof to work with and makes lectures not unbearable, wants you to succeed

One of the best professors I have had a UNC. You can tell he cares a lot about the students and he is VERY understanding. He also makes lectures really fun and interactive. He is a very bubbly person and extremely fun to have as a professor.
Very great professor. Super understanding, entertaining lectures. Highly recommend. :)

Professor Stenz was a great professor and very helpful during office hours. I was worried about the workload since I had a heavy semester, but the class was manageable. There were four fair quizzes based on lecture material. Attend class, participate, and use office hours and you'll do well.

Connor is a great, welcoming teacher! He was always available to answer any questions inside and outside the classroom. He started and ended lectures with a song and honestly, that was such a highlight. I always looked forward to going to this class. He also is very knowledgeable about study abroad! His lectures were easy to follow and informative.

Professor Stenz is an incredibly caring and fair professor who will make your language course the best class of your semester. He goes out of his way to make class interesting with extra vocab or relatable jokes about the material. He keeps his had on the pulse of the class and makes sure that everyone is on the same page.

Mr. Stenz in an amazing teacher! He makes class engaging, and he is very encouraging/supportive. French is difficult to learn, but he is always willing to help you succeed. There is a lot of homework due before every class, but that is standard across the department. I highly recommend taking his class if you can!

Mr. Stenz is a great instructor! French is a very difficult language to learn, and he truly tries his hardest to explain difficult topics in an effective way. He is very caring about his students and wants to see them succeed. When asking some clarification questions, he can get a little off topic, but overall he was great instructor to learn from!

Professor Stenz is a very kind person who cares about his students very much. He is also very knowledgeable about linguistics. However, this can be difficult because when students ask him a question about content, he goes very in-depth, which can be hard to follow along with. Overall, he is very good at explaining French in a way that makes sense.
Very Charismatic and flexible teacher
Had Mr. Stenz for FREN 101 and 102. He makes class fun and is a very fair grader. He's also super helpful and is forgiving if you miss an assignment or need an extension. 100% recommend!
Teaches very well.

Professor Stenz was super sweet and funny. He cared about his students and wanted us to succeed. Homework was given after every class and wasn't horribly difficult. Tests and quizzes were ok! If I had studied more I probably would have had an A!

Mr. Stenz is an excellent teacher. His class follows the schedule, and homework is assigned before every session, as is standard for all 101 courses in the department. He is encouraging and supportive. Grading is easy as long as you do it. Yet, the listening of his tests is close to the natural speed of native speakers. It was a great semester.

Professor Stenz was an amazing teacher for this course! He truly cares for his students and their success. He responds to emails in a very timely manner and always offered to go over certain material more if the class needed. French can be a pretty difficult language to learn, but he is a great teacher to learn from.

Mr. Stenz always made his classes engaging and really fun! He always makes sure that you are understanding the content and gives good feedback quizzes and papers. Overall he teaches this class very well and makes it a fun class to go to in the morning!

I am so lucky I got Mr. Stenz as my professor this semester! I think if I had a different professor, I would be failing the class. He is super caring and accommodating, and his feedback is incredibly helpful.
He is a great teacher. While the content might be tough for some, he is by far the best Prof to teach it. He is very understanding and overall wants his students to succeed. 10/10 recommend.
Probably the best Spanish professor I've had at UNC. Encouraged class participation but very welcoming and easy to talk to. Exams were easy the study guide tells you what to know.

Professor Knorr is absolutely amazing! She made taking Spanish enjoyable and really cares a lot about her students. Show up to class, do the VHL online homework, and participate in class and you can easily make a good grade. Highly recommend!!

She was actually the sweetest and you could tell that she truly cared about everyone in the class.  As long as you complete the VHL homework and at least glance over things before the exams you'll pretty well off.
great teacher, so nice, not hard at all. bought dog to class

I had put off taking this class since freshman year, but luckily, I got to take it with Professor Knorr. She has a contagious positive energy that made this class so much fun! She is understanding and will offer an extension for homework or other assignments if you ask. If you can, I 100% recommend taking her for Spanish 203!

Best prof ive had at unc. She really cares about her students and gives multiple opportunities for quiz redemption. Class isn't too bad and doesn't require too much homework/studying. She is an amazing teacher and encourages in class discussion. Would def take another class with her.

Best Spanish prof I have ever had. She is so caring and loves teaching and it shows. The class was very manageable and she clearly outlined all material that would be on tests/quizzes. She also offered opportunities to replace a low quiz grade. Would definitely recommend
This class was pretty easy and Professor Knorr was great at teaching it. She is an amazing Spanish professor and I would definitely take a class taught by her again.

Best Spanish professor I have ever had. If you are shy/worried about speaking Spanish in class there is no better environment for you than Profesora Knorr's class. Incredibly helpful and understanding, is clear with expectations and gives you all the materials/instruction you need to succeed. Couldn't recommend more!

sweetest teacher, I watched many people ask her for an extension and she agreed. she brought her puppy to class several times. curves on quizzes. she tells you exactly what is on the test every time. no pop quizzes. Homework was very easy. Overall my favorite professor, such an angel and kind soul. very understanding and caring. happy w experience

So knowledgeable and caring! She made an effort to talk with each person individually and tried to make class fun. She was incredibly understanding with everything at the beginning of the semester. Random groups are annoying but she never makes people feel judged for saying an incorrect answer. Would definitely recommend!

I loved professor Knorr so much! When I was having technology issues, she was willing to go above and beyond to help me complete my assignments. She is the best spanish teacher I've had during my time at Carolina! She also grades really quickly which helped.

Prof. Knorr truly cared about us and was so kind, I'm not very good at speaking when it comes to Spanish but I never felt judged doing it in her class. She made us all really comfortable and would bring her dog to class sometimes! I loved her and highly recommend for 203, naturally there's a lot of work but it's really not too bad.
Such a sweet and caring teacher. She accepted late work from students and let people retake quizes. Very kind. Brought her puppy to class a few times.

The harshest grader I have ever had  (coming from an all-A student) Her feedback was inconsistent, and she was condescending with questions. It felt like she put each of us at a certain level at the beginning, and wouldn't acknowledge improvement.  Time-consuming, impossible standards. Sad, bc the material was interesting/ thought-provoking.

She is the best Spanish professor I have had- so energetic, truly cares about her students, and is very sympathetic. I took Spanish 105 the previous semester and thought it was much harder than 203. Attendance and participation are needed, but if there is anything you are struggling with she really cares to help students succeed and understand.

Profesora Knorr is one of the sweetest teachers ever. She truly wants you to succeed in her class. She's kind and understanding of the fact that college is hard and does everything in her power to be accommodating. Participation matters for sure but you are free to make mistakes and learn from them. I would 100% take a class with her again.

Professor Knorr is super energetic and kind, especially early in the morning, and class was always interesting! If you're looking for an easy A Spanish class, this definitely is not it, as she is the director of the 203 classes. Everything is in person, on paper, and while she grades pretty leniently, it is much more difficult than other profs.
Awesome professor! A lot of fun! Very upbeat, positive energy. I really enjoyed taking her class. She advocates for her students and understands the importance of mental health in college.

Professor Knorr was definitely one of my favorite professors so far. I hadn't taken Spanish in over a year and she made me fall in love with the language again. She truly cares about her student's mental and physical health and will go out of her way. She is also trendy and incorporates the real world into her class making it interesting and fun.

Professor Lee is an amazing teacher. She is extremely supportive and open to students. The class is very instructive and if you put in a respectable effort it should not be difficult. The class is fun and informative. Furthermore, tests are designed to help and reinforce your understanding. This is the type of class you would want to take.

I enjoyed this class. She is an amazing foreign language professor; she explained everything well and made the class interesting. She does give a lot of work: quizzes, exams, homework. Almost every other day, and there is always something due. Participation and attendance are also a big part of your grade. Final exams are 300 questions.

I LOVE PROFESSOR LEE! Not only is she the kindest, sweetest professor I've ever had so far, but she makes learning Korean so so easy and fun. There will be biweekly quizzes, but I do like that because it provides a grade boost instead of just relying on a few exams. There is minimal homework also... if you know how to space it out well enough.

I really liked this professor and this class. I felt that through the semester, the class was tough, but graded fairly. I will say, however, she has a policy of giving partial credit on every vocab quiz and lesson test, but does not give any partial credit on the final exam. This was not communicated clearly, and did negatively impact my grade.

INCREDIBLE AMAZING WONDERFUL I ASKED HER WHAT OTHER CLASSES IN THE KOREAN MINOR SHE TEACHS BECAUSE IT IS A BLESSING AND A JOY TO BE IN HER CLASS. A LEGEND, ICON, ANGEL, THE KINDEST SOUL I HAVE HAD THE PLEASURE OF BEING IN CLASS. don't let the lots of homework stop you, it's not bad and very clearly laid out. especially 102 is less homework than 101

Even though learning a language is hard, Professor Lee helps to make is as easy as possible. She's always read to provide help and she explains the grammar and vocab in an understandable manner. However, be aware that you have to stay ontop of your work for KOR101 because there are many quizzes and workbook assignments in this course.

Loved taking Korean 101 with her. The class was easy if you complete the assignments on time. She's patient with students and gives many chances for students to express their confusion or worries about the course. However, the workload of this class is a little heavy. There was an assignment or quiz due for almost every class. I'd still recommend!
Very kind and caring instructor, genuinely wants to make things easy for you and help you learn!

I loved having her as a professor. She went over vocabulary and taught grammar concepts in class so it's important to attend class as your grade is deducted for every absence. She was very lenient when grading quizzes and tests, giving half credit for spelling and minor errors. I would definitely recommend her!

She is not organized in her teaching. The class lacks structure and is very confusing. There are no textbooks for this class, and we have to rely on her PowerPoint slides for exams. We are learning a lot of idiomatic expressions that native Korean speakers rarely use. I hated this class so much but had to take it for my major requirement.

Professor Lee was the best professor I've ever had. Not only was she kind and easy to feel comfortable around, especially given how scary a new language can be, but she's definitely the most lenient and I would recommend her to anyone. I've taken both 101 and 102 with her and I'll miss her in 203

Professor Lee is a wonderful person and professor! I was already excited to take this class because I was interested in Korean and she made me excited to come to class every day. Just be aware that this class is 4 credits for a reason, so put in the work and pay attention in class!

The professor is very knowledgeable and caring. The class can be very hard if you do not put in a lot of outside work into learning the language. There are lots of quizzes and homework, but you will know ahead of time to prepare. This class is pure memorization so get ready. I am taking her again for 102!
Professor Gatto is the best. She is so nice and her lectures are very clear and easy to follow. Her grading expectations are also very clear. 10/10
Loved Professor Gatto! So kind and understanding. My French improved so much, the class was fun, and nothing was graded too harshly. 100/10 definitely recommend.
100% would take Angela for any French course. My spoken French improved so much! It was also a pretty easy course and she's very easy going and understand especially with late work.

Professor Gatto is very caring and makes FREN 204 super fun. She is an honest grader but provides many opportunities to improve your grade if you dedicate some time towards improving. Definitely helped my French, and the A was fairly easy to get by coming to class and putting in 2-3 hours of work in a week.

Professor Gatto is the best teacher I've had at UNC! I cannot recommend her enough, genuinely the kindest, most caring professor I've had the privilege to learn from. She was extremely understanding and friendly. I always felt comfortable to speak up and ask questions. If you can take a class with her, do it!

Angela is great. She is so lenient with students and really connects with them. It is clear that the FREN 204 course design is very flawed, but she does not control that, she instead just tries to make it work for students. I would take a class again with her for sure.

She was just awesome, if you have the chance to take a french (or any language) class with her, you should definitely do it. She's a very lenient grader and is super understanding about needing extra time on assignment.

French 204 was hard, but Angela is super sweet and approachable. Lots of assignments but things are weighted small (final was only 15% of the grade) so the work is more tedious than difficult. Talk to her during office hours if you're struggling, she is very friendly. Loved her and would take her again!

I could not recommend Angela enough. I adored FREN 203 with her. It was a lot of homework on Mindtap, but she was so kind. Always so willing to help, just the sweetest woman. She teaches well and in a way that makes sense. You have access to every powerpoint and she's hilarious. I wish I could take a million more classes with her.
Professor Gatto is the best! French is difficult at UNC but she makes it so much better. She is so kind and willing to take time to help her students. Take her class!!

Angela Gatto is the sweetest woman. That being said, French 203 was impossible. To be fair, I'm also horrible at French and definitely should've been placed at a lower level. There is lots of homework and the quizzes are really hard. However, Professor Gatto is extremely warm and helpful when you meet with her one on one.

Best French professor I have had!! I am not very good at French, but this class was great.  She encourages participation and will occasionally cold call in class if you don't participate, but is understanding if you mess up. If you have a good reason, she allows you to have more absences without hurting your grade.

Absolutely amazing, very caring and very interesting slides. She writes lots of feedback for your redactions and homeworks, but she does not take a lot of points off them. A decent amount of work, but that is the same across the board with FREN 203. I would definitely take her class again.

I have had 3 semesters of FREN with her and she is AMAZING. I rearranged my schedule multiple times to have my french classes with her. She cares about her students SO MUCH and is super accessible outside of class. She only wants what is best for you. Although french is not my favorite, she made the class super fun and enjoyable.

THE BEST!!!! I have never written one of these before and never intended to but I just love her so much. Take her if you can -- Angela genuinely cares about her students and will stand up for our needs and preferences whenever possible. She is so kind and knowledgable; she never fails to make class enjoyable but you will always learn a lot.
I'm not a fan of UNC French, but she makes it bearable

Angela is such an amazing professor, Fren 102 at UNC sucks but she advocated for us and they're even changing the course pack for future semesters. She always makes time outside class, makes participation easy, and makes the content as digestible as she can. She really cares about the students. Definitely my favorite instructor at UNC!

Very kind and understanding, super helpful, and goes to great lengths to teach students well and make sure they can understand the lesson material. Great at explaining, and a very fair grader. Would definitely recommend her for students taking French classes at UNC.
Angela is an amazing French professor and will absolutely help you in any way she can. Volunteering in class isn't scary at all and she doesn't judge anyone for messing up.

Angela is absolutely incredible. I had her for FREN-101 as well and she's always been a wonderful teacher. She genuinely wants you to understand the language and will always help you when you struggle or feel like you don't understand something. The tests are a struggle but she always does reviews and is open to questions. Absolutely take her!

Dr. Smith is kind and clearly knowledgeable, but her grading is sporadic and assignment criteria is vague. Major assignments took a month to be returned, and I often could not tell what she was looking for in the major assignments.

Incredibly condescending and rude to students. Provides confusing guidelines for assignments, tells you to ask her questions, yells at you when you ask a question. Takes forever to provide feedback and does not tell you your course grade throughout the semester.

This class is pretty easy as long as you go to lectures, because the majority of assignments are taken from lecture. She is sometimes nitpicky about grading, but if you follow the rubric as much as you can, you can get an A in the class easily.

The negative reviews puzzled me so much I had to check this was the right Jennifer Smith. Class covered interesting topics, readings were all manageable, and Professor Smith is a sweet old lady. Midterm had a low 90's average and the projects were nothing to sweat over. Don't be on whatever these Ling 101 students are smoking lol.

Jen is a great teacher and is very organized with her lecture slideshows, daily syllabus, and expectations on assignments. She did a great job with pacing the course. However, she often assumes that if you didn't understand something, it's because you didn't read the slides/textbook and she can be unnecessarily condescending.

Dr. Smith is nice-ish, however, she stops becoming approachable when questions are constantly met with: did you even look at the slides/reading?
She doesn't understand that people need to hear different ways of explaining concepts. In my opinion, her exams are not super fair and her expectations are not realistic. This class was a struggle.

I really enjoyed Professor Smith's class. The material is a little difficult if you are new to the topics, but if you stay on top of things, it is not bad. Everything just builds on itself, so you have to make sure you keep up with your understanding. She is a tougher grader, little picky about certain things, but it challenges you in a good way.
linguistics 225

The class and info. itself wasn't too bad, but grading was frustrating. She's VERY particular about how she wants assignments done & will usually find anything to dock points off for. She also waited until the very end of the semester to finalize grades. Helpful class for learning about research tho, but definitely a harder FYS option.

I loved this FYS and definitely recommend it if you're interested in linguistics and/or education. I thought the grading was very fair, but grades & feedback were usually returned a month or later after submission. The rubrics were at times unclear. The class was organized well and the pacing was not too fast. Super manageable workload.

Do not take Ling60 as a first year seminar. Class content is incredibly boring and she was very particular about how she wanted you to answer a question. Impossible to get a perfect grade on anything, and she graded everything at the end so you have no idea. Everyone else I know got a high A in their first year seminar so take another one.

Prof. Smith didn't grade anything within a reasonable amount of time (takes at least a month). Sometimes her feedback is helpful, but other times it's wildly confusing. Her responses to your questions can feel a bit pretentious which is off-putting, especially for a class where she is a tough grader. I wouldn't take her classes again.

She doesn't explain concepts well. She also responds to questions in a sarcastic manner sometimes which makes you feel dumb. She doesn't provide any answer keys/rubrics to any work so most of the time you have no idea what she is expecting on graded assignments. She also is an incredibly harsh grader. Honestly, wouldn't recommend this class.

She does not provide any kind of examples for write ups worth 20% of your grade each and her feedback makes no sense since she takes off a significant amount of points for small mistakes. She also is very sarcastic when responding to questions in class or when students look at their laptops for a little too long.

She's a very harsh grader. She needs to incorporate into her rubrics the possibility of subtracting only 1-2 points for *extremely* minor mistakes. She personally admitted that a significant proportion of the class did badly on a big homework assignment, and that nearly always shows that the professor is doing something wrong, not the students.

She gets to class literally the minute it starts and finishes preparing the material right before class. Sometimes unprepared with links unattached, etc. She takes 1-2 months to grade things that she says she will have back in a week. Can be harsh if you are wrong. She is very smart, but almost too smart and expects students to be able to keep up.

Professor Smith was very kind and cared about the subject. She graded everything super hard and not everything was included on the rubrics that she graded on. It took at least 1-2 months to get most grades back and at that point it was not helpful on other projects that had already been done before grades were given back. Lectures were long.

If you can take any other gen ed do it. This class was so boring and I would never take this class again. 65% of your grade is exams which is nothing like the homework. What saved my grade was participation in recitations and homework. Which you need the textbook to do. The professor is nice though but lectures get very boring.

Very caring and nice professor. Lectures can get a little boring if you're not super into linguistics, but she definitely does her best to keep the material interesting. Exams took up a lot of the grade, which personally killed me. Do well on those, and you'll do great in the class.

I loved every moment of Jen's class. She makes sure that you understand all of the material. Her office hours are very helpful. She is genuinely a lovely person to talk to and is always willing to help PLEASE take a class with her. I loved LING 101!
The class is hard and a lot of work, but you will learn so much. He is such a sweet guy and genuinely cares so much about his students

No professor cares about their students more than Prof Kim. He's kind and funny, and puts in a lot of effort to make sure students have a good grasp of the material. That being said, exams are far more difficult than they need to be. Even with a deep and broad understanding of the material, most people will find trouble getting a 90+ on an exam

I loved this class. I learned so much and my Spanish improved a lot. It was pretty challenging, though. A lot of work and tough grading, but it's manageable if you put the work in. Prof Kim is so kind and funny and always willing to help. Just pay attention, participate in lecture, and study.

Hosun Kim is an excellent professor that clearly displays his passion for teaching and his students. His lectures are engaging so be ready to participate. His grading on papers is pretty tough but fair and is pretty lenient on writing portions of exams. His rubrics sometimes lacked instruction so pay attention in class to what he asks for.

This class was hard but very interesting and definitely worth it if you're willing to put the work in. Dr. Kim is always available outside of class and is willing to help. Pay close attention to the details and study from the coursepack not the slides.
Unnecessarily hard grader even though we made a plethora of mistakes on our exams and class slides (that he does not bother to post). Worst Spanish class so far at UNC.

Very kind professor who clearly cares about his students and course content deeply. However, the only assigned reading material is a personal manuscript that has not been updated since the early 2000s, something I found frustrating considering the entire class was centered around memorization of likely outdated legal procedures.

Dr. Kim cares a lot about his students, and therefore expects a lot from them. The tests require much more studying compared to all of the other Spanish classes I've taken at UNC, and my grade suffered because of it. He is a very good professor and wants more than anything for his students to be happy and successful. Great guy and great prof

Professor Kim truly cares about his students, but the course topic was difficult to understand. I liked professor Kim, but the business terms and information was a lot to understand at once. Grammar is used in tandem with the vocab and capitulo topic. Not too heavy of a grader, but he is slow at grading.
This class was very hard and the material is dense. Dr. Kim is so nice and cares about his students and really wants to see them be successful. Lots of big assignments that impact the final grade.

He is so sweet and u can tell that he genuinely cares about each of his students and wants them to succeed. He is one of the more harsh graders, but he gives good feedback. I would have had an A in this class if I had studied more. It was my first language course at UNC, so I wasn't sure what to expect. Try to participate as much as u can!

Prof. Kim truly cares about his students and loves his job. He makes boring content interesting just in the way he engages students. He is very animated and excited. The class is pretty easy but you definitely have to study for midterms and finals as they are super specific and many questions are designed to trick you. Prepare to participate often.

Professor Kim is the sweetest and most caring professor. He fosters a comfortable atmosphere which makes it okay to participate even if you mess up. His lectures are practice of homework content (where you actually learn the concepts). He grades fairly easily and gives good feedback on written/spoken assignments.

Prof. Kim cares deeply about his students. He tries to make lectures engaging and encourages the entire class to participate. Do the textbook readings and stay on top of the material, and you will get a lot more out of this class. He provides great feedback and is always willing to help outside of class hours.

Prof Kim was a sweetheart, it was obvious that he wanted us to succeed. However, be prepared to get called on multiple times every class, and he won't move on to the next person until he is satisfied. The tests are fairly easy and he has clear expectations. The only reason I got a B was due to being unprepared for the oral interview.

Dr. Kim is very sweet and funny; he truly cares about his students! I breezed through this class until I bombed the final, but that was my own fault. There is a lot of content. My main complaint is that he never returned some of our earliest assignments. Our 1st essay wasn't graded until after our final exam, so we wrote our later essays blindly.

He wrote his own textbook for the legal professions class with 0 law experience. Did not listen to what people (who were experienced in legal services) had to say if he was not correct. Do not take this class if you do not have to! Maybe 12 grades all semester and takes months to get grades back (with no feedback).

Professor Kim is very sweet and really cares about his students, but I learned very little in this class. It was a waste of time and I wish I hadn't done the professions minor. The information is stuff you could google and it's basically memorizing a bunch of nit picky details. If you don't actually really like law then it's not worth taking.

Prof Kim is genuinely one of the best profs I've had while here at UNC. He is so accessible, caring, and really wants to see each student succeed. As someone who is not a native English or Spanish speaker, he knows what it's like to learn a language and will do everything he can to prevent embarrassment. If you're worried about 203, take Prof Kim!
This teacher is one of my favorites I have ever had at UNC. Very passionate about his job although lecture heavy, I am never bored in this class. This dude is awesome.

Pepe genuinely cares about all of his students. He does whatever he can to make speaking in class less stressful. He is picky about grammar in writing assignments, but if you are hoping to improve your Spanish this is helpful. SPAN 328 is extremely applicable to anyone hoping to pursue health.

By far best Spanish teacher I have had at UNC. Genuinely cares about the people in the class, lectures are interactive and fun, and quizzes/exams are very fair. Had him twice and would recommend any of his classes.

If you want a class where you can get away with not doing readings, choose a different one. Class discussions and quizzes draw on how well you reviewed the textbook. However, class format is consistent and Pepe gives great feedback, flexibility, and is very kind. Don't procrastinate on papers and studying for the million quizzes like I did!

Pepe is nice, but he gave us multiple quizzes every single week, along with papers and other homework assignments due. His syllabus was wrong all year, and the grading scale on it did not align with the grades he was actually using to put into Connectcarolina. Compared with the other 320 class, Pepe assigns much more work and there are more tests.

Pepe is such an angel. SPAN105 is one of those with a curriculum he doesn't control but he makes it as bearable as possible. Pepe makes language learning so fun and is incredibly encouraging and understanding. He's a flexible grader on exams and is accessible outside of class to help students practice their Spanish. Highly highly recommend Pepe!

Pepe is an amazing person. He is a great teacher and is so kind and patient when you don't know a topic. The Spanish department itself is very flawed, but he did the best he could with what he was given. Spanish is very difficult and fast paced, but Pepe is the best way to go when choosing a professor!!
He is super kind and is always so understanding. He really takes the time to connect with students and help them learn to the best of his ability.
PEPE WAS AMAZING! He is incredibly charismatic and down to earth. He has a genuine interest in his students' success. 100% take his class.

I loved Pepe! He was a great teacher and really cared about all of his students. He wanted to make sure all of us were doing well and was always willing to help. The course itself was difficult because it moved pretty fast, but that was outside of his control. He made Spanish enjoyable!

Pepe was a very caring and knowledgable professor! He loved to teach and come to class each day, which created a great environment for students. Class was focused mainly on speaking practice, so be sure to take notes outside of class.

Pepe is a great professor who cares a lot about his students. His lectures are a little scattered sometimes but I still learned everything I needed to. The class can be hard sometimes but he is always willing to answer questions and help you out!

Pepe was one of the sweetest TAs I've ever had. He always encouraged students to try their best in class and it felt like he genuinely cared about all of us. He sometimes went a little fast through his powerpoints, but I think that's just the nature of Spanish 105. This class can feel like a lot but you won't regret taking it with Pepe!!
Very compassionate, friendly, and easy to talk to. Did his best to teach us and he knew what he was talking about each day. He was great.

Was told I'd have hours of homework, but had a normal amount! There are issues with the curriculum up of the class, but Professor Pepe did what could with what he was given. He genuinely wants us to learn and shares a lot about himself with you. office hours are helpful and he loves answering questions. Very personable!

Serenella is one of the most incredible people I have ever met! She is also one of the most knowledgable, with a clear joy for educating others. The class is not difficult, with a couple of tests and a group podcast project. Take a class with Serenella-- she's spectacular!

Serenella is not only one of the best professors I have had, but also one of the most incredible people I have ever met. She is so passionate and knowledgeable about material, and you can really see her joy towards teaching. The class was not difficult, with a couple tests and a podcast project. Take a class with Serenella!!!
Class rocked. She was very kind and fun.

Pr. Iovino is so sweet and caring, and this class is an easy A. She is very passionate about the material and will sometimes dominate the class time but overall I didn't ever stress about this class. She is also very accessible if you are ill or have to miss class for any reason. Would def recommend if you need to fulfill the gen ed.

Prof Iovino is super nice and genuinely cares about her job and you. However, I feel like she doesn't read the room well sometimes and kinda just talks for hours. She's also not afraid to interrupt you while you're presenting/talking, but not in a rude way though. Overall, this class is a free A.

Iovino cares about each of her students. She is super passionate about the subject and it shows. Sometimes this passion causes her to overtake a conversation and not let students speak, but overall she's amazing. She is not afraid to question a student's information or presentation, so be prepared to defend the information you chose to add

Prof. Iovino is very knowledgable and passionate about her lectures. Her assignments are straightforward. Sometimes, she becomes a bit too passionate and takes over the discussion, giving students less time to speak. She's also not afraid to question students on their research on a topic, so be prepared to defend why your information is relevant.

She handed out A's like it was nothing. You can tell she was very enthusiastic about her research and work. She cares for her students very much and appreciates each and every single one of them. She loves interrupting presentations to ask questions but never in a bad way.

Dr. Iovino is the most amazing professor I've had at UNC. She is kind, thoughtful, insightful, and so very knowledgeable about her topics! Her lectures are philosophical and very deep, concerning the environment and society as it is nowadays. The class is taught in Italian, you should be advanced in the language before taking this class.

The course was a seminar-style course so discussion was a part of the class. There were 2 written-response exams with 2 questions and the final project was a group project. Professor Iovino is energetic & you can tell her love for animals. She is a very generous grader and you would have to not show up and try to fail the course to actually fail.

She was absolutely amazing. She truly cares about all of her students and wants the best for everyone. I had her for a first year seminar and it couldn't have gone any better. The work load was not much at all and completely tolerable. I would highly recommend taking her classes.

Do not take a class with this professor. She changes her syllabus multiple times and is very unclear about guidelines for assignments. Professor is unkind to students and makes you feel like your opinions don't matter. Class material is boring and she is a poor lecturer.

Serenella is amazing. If you're an Italian major/minor definitely take a class with her. She cares about her student so much and is one of the kindest people ever. Readings were never too bad and grade was based off a paper, one test, participation, and an end-of-semester group project.
Super sweet professor and really cares about teaching the polish language. Even though it's a quite difficult language, she made it much easier and so much fun!
She is super sweet and the class itself is not hard if you pay attention. No textbook or anything like that and the homework she assigns takes like 5 minutes. I love her she's the best
Prof Majewska is so kind and genuine. She prepares us well for exams and announces what topics will be on each quiz/test beforehand. It is not difficult to get an A in this class.

Professor Majewska is a very sweet and authentic Polish Professor. She gives a daily completion homework, the occasional graded homework, four quizzes, two tests and a final presentation. Everything is super easy and requires mild-to-moderate effort. Everything is easily outlined, and her lessons are easy to follow. I am\ taking 402 and 403.
Pani Majewska is such a nice lady and she will give you feedback on anything you may have questions with. The homework and quizzes are light. Excited for the next 2 semesters!

Majewska is an absolute gem. I went in with 0 Polish knowledge and ended up having her for 3 semesters. She is very understanding and is as helpful as she can be. The key to her class is quizlets and repetition. There are plenty of opportunities for grades and the final exam is a low percentage of the grade.

Dr. Majewska is an awesome teacher and human being. Even though I was TERRIBLE at Polish, I still enjoyed all three semesters I took with her. If you are looking for a new language to try out rather than go through Spanish or French for your language credit, Polish is definitely worth a try.

Dr. Majewska is awesome. She's really funny and caring, and the class itself is quite easy, especially compared to other language classes at UNC. I am a very poor language learner, but I was still able to be quite successful in polish. I would encourage anybody who does not already have their language requirement completed to take polish with her.

Polish is a niche language- classes are small & Dr. Majewska is an incredible professor. I've had her from 401-403 & couldn't recommend more. The class is very participation heavy but if you can't make a class she records them. Short daily homework, a few quizzes, 2 tests, a short final project, and a final. Easier than most other language classes!

Professor Majewska is awesome. She really encouraged us to participate and become better at speaking Polish. She was always super open to questions and had a really easy-to-follow curriculum. About 15-20 minutes of homework each but no big large outside-of-class time sinks. Highly recommend.

Professor Gomez is super enthusiastic and clearly cares about all of her students. There is a lot of required reading, and the final project takes a substantial time commitment, but you will learn a lot.

I loved her and the way she structured this class! Just be sure to do the readings before class and be engaged and you will be fine. She is super nice and a great lecturer. Do not take this class if you're a chronic skipper because attendance is the most important part---she does not post lecture material.

Professora Irene is a fantastic teacher. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches and makes an effort to connect with her students. She assigns an intense workload, but it is definitely manageable. My only note is that this class would be a lot of work if you don't have a strong Spanish background.

Very easy to do well if you TRY. Any bad ratings are people who don't try trust. Best elective to take in the Spanish department - genuinely caring and the best part of my day is going in there and laughing lol.

I absolutely loved Profe Irene! Her class required a lot of time commitment due to the lengthy readings, and you are expected to be very engaged in the discussions, but she made class very enjoyable. I am not a huge reader, and she made me not hate it. She is such a kind and sweet human, and she became one of my favorite professors at UNC!

Profesora Irene was fabulous, definitely my favorite Spanish professor at UNC so far. She is super enthusiastic and kind, she wants you to participate in class but never calls you out or pressures you to answer. She gives lots of extra credit and if you do the readings/go to class, you will be successful & learn a lot. Super fun class overall.
She was one of my favorite Spanish professors that I have had at UNC. She taught class with high energy and enthusiasm. Would definitely recommend taking her course if it is available.

One of the best Spanish professors in the department. Amazing personality, hilarious, and made every class exciting. Extremely lenient and takes into account students' lives when determining due dates and assignments. She invited many guest lecturers to change the class structure, which made the course more interesting.

French 105 is a VERY difficult class, especially if you have only taken HS French. Aubrey was very caring and gave great feedback. I learned a lot about French in this class, but again, French is hard. If you are interested in French, Aubrey is great, but if this is for credit, take it at community college.
This is a hard class, but Professor Lewis grades fairly. She's very sweet and doesn't cold call.

Aubrey was great! She really made an effort to teach us to speak the language, but didn't make us feel bad when we messed up. Was very accessible for office hours, and prepared us well for the tests. Would definitely take again!

The problem is really mainly just the structure of FREN105, Aubrey is really nice but the structure of the class means there isn't much opportunity for her to teach, its very self-taught and the textbook was kind of weird. There are a lot of different grades though so it's not only based on tests/quizzes.

tbh I think the problem with fren105 is the class itself, not the professor, but the model just felt a lot like she wasn't doing much teaching, and we had to just figure everything out on our own outside of class bc that's how fren105 is set up. the online textbook is not very helpful, either. duolingo was my best friend. she's very nice, though.

Aubrey is first and foremost a sweetheart. She does her best to make class engaging, but overall this course sucks. It's not her fault though, she's a TA who is stuck doing what UNC has decided Fren105 should do. The textbook sucks too. It's not unreasonable in terms of what you're expected to know, so while you have to self-teach, it's not awful

I have a hard time understanding her other reviews. She is kind and tries to make class fun, and while you do have to participate often you have chances to volunteer yourself before being called on. It may feel a little more difficult if you haven't taken Spanish in a few years, but otherwise she gives very helpful study guides to do well on exams.

Seems sweet in class but grades harshly on basic assignments and exams. Cold calls consistently in class so pay attention, participation matters and is not an easy grade. Exams are 45% of grade and are taken in class on zoom. If you are looking for an easy grade, this class is not it. If I could go back I'd take this at community college instead.

Maybe she's super passionate about the material she's teaching - I don't know. But she is very condescending and teaches like we're in middle school. When I got questions wrong in class (she randomly calls people every 2 minutes), she would make comments in front of the whole class that my audio must be broken on my laptop or mock the answer.

Michelle is not understanding or sympathetic at all. Calls on you randomly in class, a lot of assignments, if you miss more than 3 days of class you will lose 10% of your participation grade for every additional day.

Gravatt puts on an act in the first class that she likes to "surf" and says this is class is like surfing you're going to try and get up and fail over and over. Meanwhile if you don't sound like you have lived in Barcelona for the past six years, she'll laugh at you and make you think you're an idiot. Not encouraging, doesn't care for you to learn.
The exams and quizzes do not match the study guide given.   Different information is tested than in the power point presentation or what is said to be tested.
The worst professor that I have ever had!
Horrible professor
Beware of this professor. Unkind and uncaring.

I had her for 105 but it wouldn't let me put it. Dr. Gravatt was such an amazing professor. She was super caring and did her best to accommodate and tried to help if she saw you struggling. I did pretty badly on my first exam but let me stay after class to finish it, and she helped me be better prepared for my next one. Overall great teacher!

Dr. Gravatt was very passive-aggressive toward me and my study group. She is difficult to contact via email and the Sakai site is poorly laid out. Be prepared to do a lot of self-teaching because she does not explain concepts over lectures. She calls on everyone during lectures so make sure to look over/complete the activity sheets before class.

Gravatt wasn't terrible by any means, she was a little passive-aggressive in my opinion though. She was pretty difficult to contact and not very understanding. Her class was fairly easy, the only reason I got the grade that I did was due to exam 2, which everyone in my group did bad on. Be prepared to be called on in every class multiple times!

Dr. Gravatt was a decent professor and a fairly easy grader. Many other reviews have a problem with passive aggressiveness, but I thought she was mostly kind and understanding. The class can be intimidating sometimes, but she was normally pretty understanding if you had questions or made a mistake.

Overall the homework and assignments are easy. However, the tests are a bit harder and oftentimes contain paragraphs with words we have not learned. Prof. Gravatt can be a little rude if you get something wrong during lecture or if you email her. The class was easy if you read the textbook and studied, but I would not take it with Gravatt again.
A little passive-aggressive and hard to reach (especially for an online class). Overall easy grader but do not expect her to be very helpful outside of class with any questions.

I'm not taking Spanish at UNC again. Class only meets on Thursdays & you have groupstudy on Tuesdays. You teach yourself the material and quickly review it in class. She is not easy to reach via email, which isn't great as this class is online. There is an online textbook and all of the homework is through Pearson. Fairly easy verbal grader though.

Took Cervantes class with Dr. Collins - reading heavy, obviously, but we took Don Quixote piece by piece and she knows so much about the book, so lectures were interesting, even at 8AM. Did not provide super clear feedback about grading criteria, but wasn't harsh, either. Take notes in class and you'll be prepared for the minimal essays + exams
Such a great professor. Homework is just reading. Good books ngl and i dont even like reading. Participate and you will do fine. Everything is super chill too

Amazing professor. You read a lot of books but she covers them thoroughly, so as long as you take notes you're fine! Few tests (Midterm, 1 paper, 1 group project and final). Gives comprehensive feedback and she's the sweetest teacher. Take notes and you'll be grand. Take this class!

This is the second class I have taken with her and it was the same format. There is one group presentation, a research paper, and two exams. She is very kind, but class can get kind of boring. It is all discussion and presentations. She grades fairly easy and I would likely take another class with her.

She's very passionate, but she teaches in a confusing way. Classes were discussion based and exams were based on stuff mentioned by students in lectures. No rubrics were given for anything. You never know what she's looking for, and she mentions out of the box connections in your assignments and takes off points if you didn't make the connections.

The class is discussion based and she chimes in to make sure the conversation is continuing. There is a group oral presentation that is fairly easy with pretty open guidelines. There is also one 12-15 pg research paper, but there was little instruction on what to do. No rubric provided either so really no idea what she was looking for.

Professor Collins is hands-down my favorite professor at UNC. She is passionate about her work and truly values hearing the interpretations and thoughts of her students. She would guide the overall structure of the lectures but for the most part she let us provide our opinions, point to places in the text, and ask questions. TAKE HER CLASSES!

She is passionate about her lessons and tries to be as engaging as possible. It's nice that most of the material is discussion-based rather than lecture style. She isn't a tough grader but gives helpful feedback and communicates well via email. 10/10 recommend :)

Chillest guy on the planet. Need to skip class to go on vacation he will send you what we covered. Everything is in the textbook. Tells you exactly what is on the exams. He literally forgot to grade our two major projects (20% of our grade) so everyone got a 100 on those. Loves having the funniest conversations in class and gives the best feedback.

Professor Matt is so caring and will give you a lot of support if you need it in and outside of class. This class is a lot of work and there is a LOT of vocab to learn, but if you put in the work, you will be fine. It was overall such a fun class and very engaging!!

Matt is absolutely amazing. Going into Russian I had no idea what to expect and it was more challenging than I had thought. He gave me so many helping hands that I frankly did not deserve and now I'm majoring in Russian. Make sure you're studying topics and vocab for at least an hour a night and you'll do well.

Nicest guy ever, makes learning a hard language worth it. Grades fairly, expects  constant participation. If you want to do well, be prepared for a fair amount of out of class homework/studying vocabulary (but doesn't that normally come with learning Russian anyways?)

This class is very homework heavy, especially in the first half of the semester. Professor is great though, he's nice and keeps the class entertaining. Grades things decently fast, encourages participation (you're basically forced to participate no matter what though). It was a fun class, one of my favorites!
He's actually so sweet y'all, don't be intimidated by Russian - it'll be one of the best classes you'll ever take at UNC.

this is your sign to take this professor. he is highly in-tune with his students performance and reached out to assist me multi times. there are many buffers for his class. homeworks are participation and he was forgiving for grades other than tests/quizzes. STUDY THE VOCAB-not starting the night before, that was my mistake- don't be like me.

Very good class, make sure to do your homework and study vocab. Homework and attendance grades weren't entered until the end of the semester. Tests are fairly easy as long as you pay attention in class and understand the grammar. Professor McGarry gets sidetracked a lot, so be prepared to check the textbook for additional coverage of class content.

McGarry is a great teacher and very caring of his students, though a bit quirky. Had him for 101 and 102 and they are both very easy to do well in as long as you try. Class is mostly reversed where you learn concepts on your own and practice them together in class (lots of speaking). Tests and final are easy and heavily resemble the practice tests.
If you do nothing else, take a class with McGarry.

Honestly the best teacher you could have for a language as difficult as Russian. Classes are very practice heavy so you have to read the textbook and do the homework. But he's a pretty lenient grader because he knows how you perform in class so he goes mostly off that.
One of the best professors! Every lecture was great and participation was encouraged.

McGarry is a good at giving resources and helping the class understand the course content at hand. He also helps you understand how Russian culture works. Participating in class helps a lot with knowing what is going on and also to apply yourself accordingly. You will need to do homework as well to learn in the class if you want to learn Russian!

Professor McGarry is probably one of the best professors on UNCs campus. He has a visible  passion for the Russian language and is always teaching you the most out of the box interesting things. He is a very easy grader, if you don't do well on a quiz he will most likely allow you to retake it. He is just a great and understanding professor.
Excellent choice for Russ 101. Matt is a funny, entertaining professor who cares about his students. Accessible during office hours and is always ready to help. Highly recommend taking with him!

Matt is simply fantastic. You'll learn a lot about Russia and Russian in a single semester. You'd better skim the book beforehand, because if not the lectures become useless. But he's very understanding, and if you have a bad week, just go to office hours, he's so willing to help. So glad I started this incredible language with him.

Matt is awesome. He is very heavy on participation in class and will call on you for answers, but will not ridicule you for being wrong. He is hilarious, a cool guy to be around, and is accessible with office hours and often encourages students to come by if they're ever struggling. Cannot emphasize enough what a great choice he is for RUSS101.

Professor McGarry was an incredible choice for Russian 101. He gives helpful and specific feedback, and is engaging and animated both in the classroom and in office hours. Russian is a difficult language and he is very understanding of that and goes into detail on the topics that he knows classes in the past have struggled with. Highly recommended.

McGarry was the best choice possible for RUSS-101. He is extremely easy to get along with, invests in his students' interests and takes the time to get to know them, has a great sense of humor, teaches well, and is all around a great instructor. He is probably one of the best teachers that I have ever had and I plan to have him next semester also.

Def take 101 with him if you have the choice. Very funny guy, great professor, and very good about helping you if you don't understand. This man will totally transform you into a russian speaker, and is seriously such a great prof.

She's very participation heavy, which makes sense with an introductory language course. She's always happy to help and offer office hours, extra practice, and support when students ask for it. She's very patient and encouraging, the class is a very welcoming environment.
She was really nice and really made sure the students understood the material. I slacked off pretty bad and failed the first 2 test but she worked with me and I ended up doing ok. Don't fall behind.

I absolutely adore Professor Chambless. She is a fantastic professor. In-class time is typically spent practicing skills, so I would recommend taking time to read/take notes on the assigned textbook pages so the content doesn't sneak up on you for the test. Grades fairly and generously, and always gives clear feedback. Take ITAL 101 with her!

I highly recommend Dr.Chambless for Ital 101 and 102; she is an amazing lecturer and has a lot of empathy towards her students. She grades fairly and provides plenty of feedback, as well as resources, to help you improve your Italian. She is very knowledgeable about the textbook content and is always available to meet with students.

She is very friendly and encouraging! Classes have a lot of fun activities to encourage constant learning.  There are short quizzes (vocab or the grammar concept you are learning), but they are easy and only count for 5% of your overall grade. There are also assignments w/each unit to record a conversation about a certain topic with a partner.
Highly recommend Dr. Chambless for any italian course at unc! Great lecturer, very friendly, and very caring

She is very well-organized and supplies a lot of resources to help you practice and understand the material. She also is a very fair grader and truly cares about her students. Participation is a super important part of the class but you definitely don't have to be perfect at the grammar construction or the pronunciation.

This was ITAL 300 not 203, but Professor Chambless is simply an amazing professor. Super kind and accommodating. There were 4 tests, a group project, and a final along with homework and participation. Definitely take Italian at any level with her if you can

Professor Chambless is an outstanding Italian professor. She makes learning a language fun and engaging! You focus on speaking and listening in class, and reading and writing on the homework.Your expereince in the class is very dependent on your partner (who you sit beside in the class). If you pick a good partner, you'll have a blast in her class!
The sweetest woman ever.
Genuinely just the sweetest, cutest woman ever. Such a great teacher! Adore her.

Amy is a wonderful teacher! She is so kind and caring. Something I love about UNC language classes is that the teachers just really want you to love the language as much as they do. I can say that by the end of this semester, I learned a lot and have more motivation to learn more about Italian culture and language.

Professor Chambless is genuinely so kind and patient with students. She's super flexible and understanding when it comes to grading and due dates. She's very encouraging and uplifting. I would recommend her for everyone but especially people who feel like they struggle in language classes. Love her!

Professor Chambless is amazing! Super nice and accessible outside of class, grading criteria is clear, and provides tons of useful resources to study for tests. Classes are mostly spent practicing in groups, so attendance is mandatory. Read the textbook and study and you'll ace her class

Amy is such a good prof! She was super helpful and easily accessible for office hours or after class. She would quite literally tell us what would be on the exams, which was very helpful. The class itself is similar to 101 and 102, but she focuses more on culture than exam prep in class. Overall I would recommend and would take her again!

He's very encouraging with students in class. He teaches by the book, so as long as you do the readings, participate in class activities, and ask questions, he's a great professor. He encourages students to take advantage of office hours, the Italian conversation table, and the Italian film festival just to get involved in the language community.

***This is for Ital 333. Daniele is a great professor! He is kind, understanding, and wants you to succeed. Participation, a presentation, 2 film reviews, and final paper a exam make up your grade. It was a lot of writing, but you could choose what films to write about. Take this class if you're interested in film/Italian culture, I learned a lot!

He's so kind and wants you to succeed. ITAL401 is an accelerated class designed for students with experience in romance languages. He was accessible and understood that sometimes life happens. Daniele is there to help. Just ask. He's approachable and funny. He'd explain harder grammar concepts with their equivalents in French or Spanish to help.

I had so much fun in this class! The professor is always willing to help and you learn so fast. He can be a tough grader sometimes but if you put in the work you can easily get an A. As in every language class participation is key, and there is a lot of homework because you cover 101 and 102 in one semester–but he made it super enjoyable!

Hated this class so so much. He talks very quickly so half the time I had no clue what was going on and he grades incredibly harshly. He expects us to know words he's never taught. He's a reasonable person in terms of needed extensions though. He picks on people constantly which is horrid when you're clueless as to what he's talking about.
Very funny and chill professor. His lectures are very engaging and interesting. However, he grades harshly and specifically so if your grammar is not perfect he will take points off.
He is very enthusiastic, cares a lot about what you have to say. He likes to yap a lot, and is a very nice grader. Would recommend, class was very easy- he taught my first year seminar.

Dr. Matharoo is really passionate about what he teaches and grades easily. He gives you a ton of freedom on the midterm and final to do whatever you want. Most of the homework is just reading before class. Just show up and try and you will be good.

This class was fun! We read some sci-fi books and watched some strange, but interesting, films. We took a few trips around campus and had guest speakers some days. He cares a lot about his students and grades on very few things, so make sure you try on the papers. I highly encourage taking this seminar!

Truly one of the most interesting french classes I've taken at UNC. Some of the readings are a bit dense, but we always break them down in class. We also only have one reading per week, the other half of the week we play video games. Projects/papers were also very doable. Great feedback. Really kind guy! He bought cookies for the final :)

Genuinely one of my favorite professors I've had at UNC!! I was in his French Comic Book class, and he always made things super accessible for me. I have a lot of social anxiety and have trouble speaking in class, but I let him know and he was very considerate. All comics are uploaded on the Canvas, very sweet and wonderful professor!!

So approachable and flexible. Watched sci-fi movies in class, read sci-fi stories for homework, and he allowed me to write my own sci-fi stories for the writing assignments and finals. He always gives great and detailed feedback for my work, and he really cares about students' wellbeing and not just academically. PLEASE take his class he is so nice

Best class this semester. Learned so much new stuff about people and science fiction. Professor Matharoo is super understanding with work and gives great and engaging feedback. Also helped me really come out of my shell in class!

My favorite Spanish professor at unc so far!! Very caring and very entertaining. UNC Spanish courses are just hard in general so you do have to be prepared to work hard, but he made it fun by bringing in plenty of relevant topics to connect with the class, engaging activities, and lots of laughter! If you can, take a class with Juneau!
Very funny, caring, understanding, and chill professor. Grades straight off the rubric. Class was always interesting, and he made it enjoyable.

Very happy to be there, super energetic professor so that's fun! Solid at teaching material but does fall a little short on the grammar aspects, luckily not much new grammar is taught anyway. Maybe a little harsh participation-wise but honestly, I felt that he was a solid profess for this class and really cared and tried to make it a good time

Professor Thomas was probably one of the best Spanish teachers that I've ever had. He is super kind, funny, and gets his class excited for Spanish every time he lectures. His homework is fair. However, be sure to study quite a bit if you want to do good in the class. It is a language course after all.

Professor Juneau is probably the best SPAN203 professor you can get. While the course structure for SPAN203, including homework, quizzes, and tests, is consistent across all classes, professor Juneau makes the in class experience enjoyable with his outgoing, friendly persona which makes participating in class easy.

I took SPAN 203 with him, not SPAN 105. He's pretty good and always cheerful. He had clear expectations and made sure we were clear on what we were doing. There is a lot of homework but he tends to remind students of upcoming quizzes and deadlines.

Thomas was super chill and I highly recommend him for Spanish. He cares about you and wants you to succeed in his class. Class was not very difficult. I was also in his class when the shooting at UNC occurred, and he was very calm and protective of his students. He could not have handled the situation better.
Zoe is great. She is super understanding of people learning french for the first time, and she it a pretty easy grader. Super approachable, but do the nightly homework or your grade will be knocked.

Super sweet and understanding; always willing to let you take things at a later time if something happens, and is very lenient with grading. I shouldn't be doing as well as I am honestly lol and she makes French actually understandable. Open minded and cares a lot, and follows a set schedule so you always know what's up! Highly recommend!

Love herrr. She's so sweet and just wants to help in any way she can. She's very flexible too - I had a cold and she let me retake a quiz a few days later. Participation matters, but that's expected in a language class.
too informal and unprofessional but very approachable

Zoe was a very fair grader and gave good, helpful feedback on the daily homework, as well as quizzes. She lived in Paris for an extended period of time so she is very familiar with how native French is spoken. She is also very friendly and easily approachable. I highly recommend Zoe for French 101.

Dr. Vieira was a wonderful professor, I took ROML 89, a first-year seminar with her and she led it very well, taught well, and often found opportunities for us to meet in other places aside from our classroom to engage in course-related activities or experiences. Wonderful professor, I would definitely recommend any of her classes.

Honestly she is the best professor/teacher I have had ever. Truly cares about her subject and lectures amazingly. She grades eveything fairly however there is a susbtantial amount of work if you are looking to just breeze through a class and skip this is not for you but if you want to learn she is great
I took ROML 89 with her and it was great. Easy A, one test, one paper, one final creative project. She's very passionate and makes it very easy for her students to learn while having a good time.
The GOAT. Amazing language professor and really cares about her students.

I loved Professora Vieira! She is so kind and welcoming. Lectures are strictly in Portuguese so can be an adjustment at first (especially if you've never taken a language like me), but you catch on after a while. Two test, two compositions, two presentations, and a final, all graded fairly. Take her if you get the chance!
She is wonderful and so caring. There is quite a bit of work, but nothing difficult, and she's a lenient grader. I loved my experience in her class, and I wish all teachers were like her.

Dr. Vieira was a great professor and truly cares about her students. She focuses on actually learning the language rather than for tests so she is easy in class and fair on grading. There are a few oral exams but she knows you're learning so you don't have to be perfect. The class is fun and she encourages you to learn while being nice and funny.

She will help you as best as she can and frequently gives points back for mistakes. A VERY fair grader. Pretty much gives everybody a good grade as long as youre trying since she just wants you to practice using the language. She's also very nice and encouraging.
The GOAT! I've always hated taking languages but she made me love learning Portuguese. TAKE HER CLASS IF YOU CAN.
I had her for PORT 101 and she was amazing. She is very caring. If you can take her DO IT!!!!!
Cute too!
I LOVE her!!! She helped me truly learn the material, gave great feedback, and made me actually enjoy showing up everyday for class.
love love love her!! Take this class if you want to learn portuguese but actually have some fun!

I don't think I can truly express my love for Vieira. She is the most caring, understanding, and effective prof I've ever had. She truly just wants you to participate and show an effort, otherwise she is not a strict grader at all. She is such a sweet person and genuinely wants to get to know all her students. Best PORT prof ever, take her please.

One of my favorite professors at UNC. Professora Vieira is consistent, clear, caring, and kind. She truly cares about her students. You can always feel comfortable being yourself and try your best in her classroom. She gives amazing feedback and her grading is very gracious as long as she can tell that you're putting in an effort. 10/10.

Really sweet professor. She really cared about her students and really just wanted us to learn. She is a great professor and gives really good feedback constantly, even if you aren't 100% correct on everything you're saying. Her biggest thing is just making sure we learn the language and loves to have us speak constantly during class.

Professor Lorenzo is an amazing professor. He's very kind and clearly cares about the students. The course is very content-heavy, and you have to know most of it for each of the four exams. The instagram project was fine, but I did the worst on that "quiz." Still, he's very receptive to feedback and easily accessible, I love talking to him!

Dr. Lorenzo is an amazing prof and I HIGHLY recommend to take Italian with him if you need language credits. He genuinely cares about his students and what he teaches, is very funny, and very accessible outside of class

Professor D'Agostino is very good at instilling knowledge into students without making it feel forceful or like work. There is lots of homework but you can always consult I'm about exceptions. He also has very useful office hours.

It was his first time teaching 204 and it showed. We had 5 exams throughout the semester, which worked out to be about one test every 2 weeks. Not sustainable at all for the amount of content. He's a good person and was available outside of class, but not a great teacher. We covered Italian history and politics too - none of which are on the exams

I don't have enough characters to describe how amazing D'Agostino is. His lectures are super engaging/fun & its obvious he really cares about his students. I was scared to take a language @ UNC because my highschool experience was awful, but D'Agostino honestly makes me look forward to class. Tests/ assignments are very straightforward and easy As.

Lorenzo is the best! Italian 102 is harder than 101 by far but he makes it manageable! He has such a cool personality and loves to interact with the students. He grades fairly. The tests are hard since 102 is mainly grammar but his reviews are the same exact format at his tests. He never throws curveballs, you always know what to expect.
Easily the best professor I've had at UNC! He is fair and non-judgmental, and he turned around my entire perspective on Spanish. He's a talented professor, and a cool guy all around.
Absolute baller

Prof. Clemente is the best ever. Super caring and kind guy who recognizes the common pitfalls and works to help you avoid them. He is Spanish himself and likes to share fun phrases or stories about Spain. He cares about you as a person and you learning Spanish. He is just awesome!!

This professor was one of the nicest and most understanding professors I have ever had. He always helped with any homework, test, or general questions I had and did whatever he could to make sure students understood what he was teaching. He always made everyone laugh and wanted everyone to succeed.

very cool man that definitely is passionate about teaching. gives clear feedback with homework. participation in class is very important for your grade. his powerpoints are useful. it has a textbook but you honestly DONT need to buy it

Sr. Clemente Rodriguez is a professor who demonstrates ample passion for the Spanish language. He always ensures students feel comfortable to participate and get out of their shell to converse in Spanish without pressure. You will love Spanish more if you take 204 with him.

This class was so much fun! Profesor was kind, funny, and helpful.  He gives good feedback on homework, and he's a chill grader.  Make sure to study for exams as they make up a good portion of grade!
