As long as you study, the exams will be fine.  He provides practice exams that mimic the actual exam.  Also make sure to participate regularly!

If you can take any class with Prof Cristobal, take it! He has 100% been the kindest, most helpful, and most genuine professor at UNC. He cares about his students and is very accessible outside of class. If you show him you care, he will work with you above and beyond

Professor Clemente was incredibly kind and funny. He also understood that many students in 203 are still learning some of the basics of Spanish and teaches accordingly. I hadn't taken Spanish for 3 years when I took his class and still did well. Would highly recommend.

The best thing about Prof. Clemente is that he really understands that we aren't fluent in Spanish. He comes prepared to class every day and tells us about his own life and experiences, which is really interesting. He makes class fun by encouraging participation and discussion, which is a must for Spanish. He is also hilarious. Highly recommend!

Professor Clemente is great! He definitely challenges his students to participate, but I feel like we all improved our Spanish skills so much during the class. Fair grader and obviously cares a lot about his students. I would recommend taking a class with him to anyone!

Dr. Langston is an AMAZING professor. His lectures are awesome and he is so much fun; I cannot recommend him enough. If you engage and read the material, it's an eye-opening introduction to so many different fields of philosophy. Lenient grading and not too much work: Dr. Langston states repeatedly that the goal is to give out A's.

This is genuinely the most engaging and awesome professor I've had. He brings energy and passion to every lecture and clarifies the readings very well. GO TO CLASS. Lectures aren't mandatory, but they help tremendously. Recitation attendance is mandatory, but is also helpful in clarifying the readings. Material is very interesting. 100% recommend.

I took this class to fulfill a gen-ed, and it's probably my favorite course I've taken at UNC. The content of the course is very interesting, yet simple enough that a good grade's attainable for students that aren't the most savvy writers or readers. Professor Langston's hilarious while simultaneously challenging you to think in new ways.

Dr. Langston is an incredible professor and shows up to each class full of positive energy and is very passionate about the subject matter! He makes an effort to get to know all of his students and strongly encourages participation. There is a fair amount of reading for the class, but he offers extra credit opportunities and gives great feedback!

Dr. Langston made this class so great! The content was super interesting too! We watched 6 movies and wrote two film reviews based on philosophical concepts. Then we wrote a 6-8 page final paper and had an opportunity for extra credit! All of my friends wished they could have taken this class so I definitely recommend it!

A lot of complex reading, but honestly the lectures make them so much clearer. That is due to Dr. Langston's clear passion for the subject and humor he weaves in. He is one of the most hip profs at UNC. Took this class for no reason besides to watch movies and was pleasantly surprised

Dr. Langston is one of my favorite professors at UNC! It was his first time teaching this GERM 282 and it was super engaging and interesting. There was a lot of reading, but it was all super interesting, and there weren't too many assignments. Biggest was a 10-page paper, but he helps you, so it isn't too bad. Overall, would definitely recommend!
Dr. Langston is by far the best professor I've had at UNC. His class is super engaging and really interesting. I had no interest in film prior to the class, but he made it super interesting and fun.

Amazing professor who really cares about his students and wants them all to succeed! The readings can be a lot and sometimes difficult to understand but he makes them very accessible. Generous grader as long as you attend class

Dr. Langston is an easy grader, an understanding person, and is passionate. I found every lecture interesting and thought-provoking. Participation is required but it's easy to do so. Homework for this class is watching films and is easy. The final project was making a film (but as long as you do it, you get an A). Take this class and Dr. Langston!
Super great professor! He's really nice and accommodating for his students. He really cares about students and values your opinions!

I'm so happy to have taken another class with Chloe. She creates a welcoming classroom environment that is fun to participate in. My conversational skills definitely improved and sharpened across the semester. The topics she chooses for discussion are relevant and important! Seriously, she's a treasure.

Very engaging lectures and prepares students well for exams. Participation is a big part of the class but she is very understanding and helpful if you make mistakes. Very organised class and I enjoyed the classroom environment.

I have taken 5 languages at UNC, and all I can say is that Dr.Hill has been the best instructor I've ever had. I took the intensive course for fun, if you are worried about your language requirement take Portuguese with her! She talks mostly in Portuguese, which can seem intimidating, but this is SO IMPORTANT if you want to actually learn

Chloe is great! She makes Portuguese very accessible and genuinely wants you to do well in the class. If you are taking this for your language requirement, take Chloe! As long as you show up, do the homework, and participate, you will be fine!
I loved this class and she is one of the easiest/most encouraging professors I've had at UNC. She doesn't make learning a language hard and is very direct with grading.

Chloe is absolutely phenomenal. I strongly believe she is sole reason portugese at UNC is labeled as "portu-breeze"/"portu-ease". Every assignment has super clear rubrics and as long as you put effort in, you will always get an A. I truly believe no one can fail this class. If you do, its not Chloe, it's you.

Chloe is the best. I was terrified of learning a language, but she made it easy and fun. She deeply cares about you actually learning how to speak Portuguese. She answers even my stupid questions well and with kindness. Easy class if you go to lecture.

There is homework every night, but it's nothing insane. Great Professor, she can be a bit harsh on the speaking assignments in my opinion, but overall great Professor, and she is willing to really teach and help you learn. Definitly take her if this is a new language for you, she is a great professor to ease you into the language
Chloe is so kind and class was easy but do make sure you go to class. I recommend Portuguese to anyone especially if you are thinking about quitting french.
She is absolutely amazing. Definitely take her especially if you aren't great at foreign languages she is so helpful and understanding!!

Chloe is SO incredible. She is patient, understanding, and genuinely wants to make sure you throughly learn AND enjoy the Portuguese language. Take her for PORT 101 if you can! And it is true what they say, "portubreeze"! Don't be anxious about this language or course, the entire department is STACKED full of incredible professors (Chloe included)!

I was scared taking a foreign language at UNC because I had started with Spanish and it was so hard. Portuguese was not only easy but very enjoyable. The workload was super reasonable and the material was straight forward. Take Chloe if you can!!!

Truly a treasure at this school. Looked forward to this class weekly and her passion for the language is palpable. Weights for assignments are nicely distributed so there are plenty of opportunities to boost your grade. I would recommend any class with her and hope to take another!

I can't recommend Chloe enough! She was an incredible professor that gave great feedback and she really wants to see her students succeed. I was pretty nervous taking a foreign language that I was unfamiliar with, but she made the class very easy to learn the material. If you are taking Portuguese, you have to take it with her she is awesome!!

One of my fav profs ever. Was so scared to take this class but I enjoyed it so much and wanted to learn a language for the first time ever. Easy homework, oral and written assignments in class. She prepares you well for test and exams- just go to class and put in some effort and you will learn so much. Wish she taught 102 this year :(

Take Professor Hill!! She is very caring towards her students and works to help them succeed! She is always accessible outside of class!! The homework is short and easy and her tests are very straightforward, she never tries to trick you.

Coming from someone who is terrible at foreign languages, Profa. Hill is a fantastic Portuguese instructor. She is caring, lenient, and tries to teach to the skill level of every individual student. She values effort above all else, so it is not intimidating to speak in class or participate. As language professors go, she is one of the best at UNC.
I loved Chloe's class! It was very engaging and you can clearly feel your Portuguese improving throughout the semester. She is the best and so funny!

I loved this class! Chloe is very engaging and brought in more interesting topics into the class to make the learning process easier. Our class focused on music, which was super fun to learn from. Highly recommend taking one of her courses!

Professor Hill is so great. She sounds like a native speaker when speaking Portuguese which is a huge help in conversation practice. She speaks very clearly and is great at explaining grammar concepts that may be a little tricky. She's very kind and patient as well. Two thumbs up.

These reviews are wayyy too harsh yo. I can't defend her for not returning grades- we literally got nothing back. But she graded everything really easily, came to class with lessons prepared, and brought us candy and sweet treats all the time. She wasn't mean or rude and encouraged fun conversations. Don't let these other reviews scare you slime.
expect not to know your grade the entire semester

Dr. Serrato has been my least favorite French teacher at UNC. She hasn't graded any of our assignments and is always telling us that her research has to be more important. When we do get an assignment back, she grades super harshly and there's no opportunity to improve because it came back so late. She's friendly in class, but not a great teacher.

Homework is graded for accuracy, harshly, but never reviewed. Stopped receiving grades after mid-September. No one truly knows where they stand in the course. Has you "grade" your own participation but does not give participation feedback. Very nice professor but literally told us her higher level courses get priority over us and that's that.
Just finished up taking one of her courses. No one knew what they had in the class until AFTER graduation. Please read that again. You do not get to know your grade throughout the course.

355: I have taken multiple classes with Professor Serrato and she clearly cares about her work. She does expect you to come to class (you get two free skips) and participate in group discussion. The projects are fun and flexible (the final is an art project) but you won't get grades back for a while. If you put in the effort, you will do well.

Dr Serrato can be disorganized, but grading takes the whole semester so she isn't as harsh of a grader. She facilitates and encourages insightful conversation, even letting students switch to English if they need. In office hours, she is incredibly caring if you show that you are someone who also cares about the class. She truly loves the material!

Unorganized. No grades in the grade book at all going into the final exam. Extremely passive aggressive?? Take a different professor. She is one of 2 French professors in the entire department that I would never willingly take again. I reorganized my entire schedule next semester just to avoid her.
Please do not take this professor. If you can, take someone else. No grades were given back the entire semester. Going into the final exam without a single grade. Content is also subpar.

I am TELLING you do not take this professor. She is not accomodating. Very disorganized and not helpful. She does not want you to succeed. This is coming from a French major who loves the French department at UNC. Do not take this professor.

Easy assignments, but lots of talking! I have severe social anxiety, and I've never had an issue with professors with it until Dr. Serrato. She says she is understanding and accommodating, but this isn't further from the truth. She's treated me unfairly for my disability, and I don't recommend taking any of her classes if you struggle with anxiety.

Professor Serrato is very smart but also very cold. Maybe she was stressed this semester or just did not like me. It was very hard to work with her and the class, FREN 355 is unclear, random, boring and unnecessarily difficult. Pick a different professor if you have the option.

*FREN 372: You can tell that Dr.Serrato is very passionate and knowledgeable about the subjects that she teaches, and she requires students to properly engage in the material This means that students should be prepared to do medium to heavy reading and engage in group discussions. However, grading was often done very sporadically and late.

Professor Serrato clearly has a lot of knowledge on the topic but taught the entire class on surface level subjects straight out of the textbook. Cultural and linguistic diversity in the francophone world is very interesting and I wish she allowed herself to teach it out of her own syllabus, on a deeper level.

Fren 354: Classes were not planned well if at all; no clear direction of class and heavily relied on asking students random questions about readings. Disliked this course and felt that I didn't learn anything. Assignments have no clear instructions and Prof. Serrato does not seem like she knows what she wants from them either. Would not take again.
She was really funny and I enjoyed her class a lot. Cold calls but just pay attention to where you are in the book and you'll be fine. Sometimes gives extra credit. Don't fall behind.
She was really funny but expects a lot from a beginner language course. I liked her but she moves fast so don't fall behind.

Dr. Lee is a funny and good person but I fear as a professor she grades too harshly for a 101 class and moves way too quickly.. While in general languages at UNC moved quickly, this is in comparison with other Italian 101 classes. Also be prepared to be singled out to say something you've never learned or had time to prepare for!

Professor Lee will respond to your emails super quickly and if you come up to her with questions after class, she is very helpful. In class, she does go fast through the lectures and cold-calls people for participation (which you're graded on). She doesn't grade too harshly as long as you have relatively good grammar/pronunciation. Extra credit!

Prof Lee really knows the content she is teaching, but can sometimes rush through the different grammar structures or culture that we are learning about. She does cold call and attendance matters, but she wants to help you get better at speaking and takes the pressure off of being perfect when speaking/writing in a new language.

Professor Lee is very encouraging and caring. She has so many funny stories relating to the countries she's traveled to and she's a pretty lenient grader. She often calls on people instead of people raising their hands to be called on but she is always so encouraging and never judges anyone for not knowing the answer.
Martina is my favorite UNC professor. I changed my schedule to take ITAL 204 with her because she's that great. I learned so much from her and loved her class!! I can't recommend her enough!!

I have taken Martina for ITAL 101, 102, and 204 because she is THAT amazing. She is a caring instructor and makes class so much fun. She is so funny and really cares about you succeeding in the class. She is always making sure we are comfortable with the material and comfortable in her class. Can't recommend her more!

Martina is amazing and definitely one of the best professors you could get for any italian classes. The course is set up the same as 101 and 102 with homeworks due before each class, 4 tests, a small group project before each test, and two very easy quizzes in each unit. Would definitely recommend Martina to anyone taking italian!
She is so sweet! Never judgmental of your ability level & meets you where you are. If I could I would have taken her for all 3 levels.

Martina made learning a new language enjoyable and easy! I took 101 as a gen-ed but am seriously considering an Italian minor after taking her class. She goes out of her way to help comprehension and uses hilarious real world examples. Take Italian with Martina!!
Great Teacher and great personality. She really wants you to learn

Dr. Demsey is incredibly caring and teaches French wonderfully. I really enjoyed participating in her class. She gave great feedback and encouraged us to expand our French knowldge. Highly recommend her!
Take this professor for 105, 101, or 102.

The greatest to ever do it. It's a shame she doesn't teach higher levels of french, but maybe that's smart on the marketing side of the department. Create an illusion that all other french teachers will be as superb as Dr Demsey so you take more french courses. She's the hook for the program.
Professor Demsey was the absolute best. I would easily take her class again if I could and she made learning french pretty fun.

Great intro French class. You cover a lot, but Madame Demsey is so nice and incredible at her job. You get partial credit for everything, so if you try, you can make an A/A- easily. A couple of group projects, but not that bad. Definitely recommend going to office hours, they're super helpful. Already signed up for her section next semester!
Great teacher, one of my favorites at UNC so far. I learned so much from this class, would highly recommend. As long as you participate and do the homework you shouldn't have any issues.
amazing professor for french who cares about you outside the classroom. pretty average grader but feedback is always clear and very helpful for improvement

Dr. Demsey is a very good lecturer of French, and despite teaching the class entirely in French, it wasn't scary. At the end of the day, this is a language class, so much of how you do is based on whether or not you genuinely do the homework. She is very caring and clearly wants you to do well in her class. I loved FREN 101 with Dr. Demsey.
very good! explains concepts and makes classes interactive
She is GREAT! French at UNC is difficult, but she cares about her students. Take her if you can
She is a great professor and always there to support you if only you go and see her. Attendance is mandatory and a tough grader. So far as you do all the work on time you should be good.

She is the coordinator for 101 and 102. You have it as a reversed classroom where you have to teach the material to yourself and complete HW on it before they help you in class. HW is 15% of your grade and its very hard to do without any in class help. HW makes 0 sense half of the time and many people have a lower grade than quizzes. Very hard.

I took ANTH-212 with Dr. Smit. He made lectures entertaining and understood that we have 4 or 5 other classes. Exams were based off the lectures/readings and were not difficult and the projects/labs were not complicated and very straightforward. I would definitely recommend taking his class.

Course is now 212. One of the easiest classes ever. Outside of that aspect, Dr. Smit is SO funny and makes lecture really fun. Take this class if you want something easy and fun! Exams are super easy, always have a throwaway multiple choice answer and extra credit question.

Lectures were boring and difficult to understand the main point sometimes. However the professor is a good guy and the exams were free asl if you studied the study guide. also basically gave me a free point when i asked about a question during the exam

I probably wouldn't take this class if you're looking for a gen ed history fulfillment. The lectures are all over the place and even though he's super chill and very kind to the students, I feel like he doesn't really care about this class. Haven't taken the final yet but the midterm was kind of difficult
He basically never replied to student's emails. Important documents concerning students are not ignored by him at all. This is the most irresponsible professor I have ever met at UNC.

The midterm didn't seem to align with the study guide, which was also released only a few days before the exam, making it hard to prepare effectively. I noticed inconsistent grading between recitation sections. Additionally, communication could be improved, as emails often went unanswered and lectures sometimes felt difficult to stay engaged with.

Professor Smit was my favorite professor this semester. He is funny and enjoyable to listen to. He relates hard-to-comprehend topics to simpler concepts in a way that's engaging and fun. He knows what he is talking about.

Prof. Smit was such a lighthearted and kind guy; you can tell he cares about his students beyond just the content we learn in class. You do need to go to lectures to get the content for exams (not much posted on lecture slides) but his lectures are pretty good as it is. 100% recommend taking his class.
Great professor, he really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well in his class.

Smit is a great professor! Lectures were very interesting and fun! Important to attend because not a lot of info online. This is a super easy gen ed. 2 tests for the 1st and 2nd half of content and some reflections. Tests are easy if u take good notes and look at the study guide. I didnt do any readings and the tests were still easy.

Overall an entertaining professor who is passionate about the topic he teaches. You will need to actually attend lecture and do the reading to do well or you wont do well (the average on the midterm was around a 70). He does curve and provide study guides though.

1/3 of the study guild wasn't on the midterm. 

midterm was written in a way to inflict maximum pain and frustration for students.
Pretty easy class for first years, great professor and very entertaining. One group project and a final paper.

Love Dr. Smit! He genuinely cares & wants his students to succeed. Canceled class a few times & went outside around campus. There are discussion posts for every reading (kinda long), but you can miss up to 12. Short artifact presentation, Midterm/Final, 2 papers. Honestly, I did badly on my midterm but he curved! Just DO the readings & youre good!

Best first-year seminar, Archeology and Pop Culture. Watch movies and read articles each week on which you write an easy 200-word discussion post; some are optional. There's a group project you will present and a final paper; with effort, you will likely receive an A. Participation is encouraged but not required. Extra credit possibilities.

Great prof., good at choosing really interesting readings and giving engaging lectures. Exams are pretty lax, but you do need to come to class to get all the info you're tested on. Very understanding and forgiving, but slightly unresponsive grader.

I highly recommend Dr. Smit he is an amazing professor. Class is easy, but there are pop quizzes. They are really easy if you do the readings. He is funny and appreciates when the class engages. He does take forever to grade things though.

Amazing professor. he had that cool professor vibe going for him, in a respectful manner. aside from that he was an awesome teacher and made the lectures very interesting. he was also a VERY fair grader and made learning what it should be. highly suggest.

This is not a difficult class but it can be very frustrating at times because of how slowly Dr. Smit grades. The papers aren't too bad and pretty quick to write. Some of the readings are more dense/boring than others but overall the course materials are fairly interesting and a lot of class is just discussion.

Professor Smit is my favorite professor at UNC. His lectures were always fun and engaging, and he often had some sort of activity to accompany them. He cares about attendance and has "Pop quizzes" on the readings from every class. They are straightforward and not difficult if you at least skim the reading. I highly recommend taking this class.

Lectures are somewhat stream-of-consciousness, interesting to listen to but sometimes feels unguided. About 4-5 graded assignments make up your grade, but she's a relatively easy grader. Incredibly caring and willing to speak with you during office hours, but the course would've benefitted from slightly better structuring.

Wellesley - ANTH 101 Really kind prof! Very accessible and inspiring/global with her viewpoint. Wants everyone to succeed and provides the means to do so. If you get the chance, take a class with her!
She's teaching at Wellesley now and I took her class last semester. Learned so much in her class, best professor I couldve ever ask for in college. I'd be thankful in my life to have Dr. Sadruddin.

The class I had her for was a seminar class about disability but the drop down didn't have the class I took under her. I absolutely loved her class. I definitely recommend her. whatever was confusing she made it easy to understand. she answered emails fast. gave a lot of feedback on papers which helped when writing the next paper assigned

She is really an amazing teacher and wants all of her students to succeed- I came out of this class with not only a catalog of amazing content but also someone I know I can go to for further advisement in my studies. Sadruddin is really great at lecturing and integrating concepts in very unique ways. I highly recommend her course!
One of favorite profs ever! Dr. Sadruddin is such a kind person and really cares about her students. She wants you to do well in her course. Graded mainly on papers but they were not too hard.

Billman is a great professor, I could listen to him lecture all day. His slides do not have much information on them so you do need to show up and actually listen, but if you do you will get an A. His test questions are all from the objectives he gives you before class, so just study those. Great guy, really funny, and interesting stories.

I found his lectures to be pretty interesting since a lot were about personal work he did down in Peru. Quite an easy class if you put in work for the essays and keep engaged. Would definitely take him again I love his sense of humor.

Took this class as my friends as an 'easy A'. Easy A's do not exist here, you're gonna have to put work in to get the grade you want. You gotta go to class, pay attention, and study. If you do that, you'll get a good grade, but don't think it's gonna be a joke of a class you can take as a filler. Class is fun and interesting.
Lectures were always fun and exams were pulled from objective questions, you want to take note of things he says in class because they're not on the slides; Exam 2 was slightly harder for some reason
Good GenEd, although exams and papers are slightly hard.

i loved his humor and engaging lectures! i recommend this class however it can be hard to do well on exams if you do not attend every single class. there are few assignments so exams are weighted pretty heavily.

I loved this class; he is a great/fun lecturer! Your grade is 75% exams (3 midterms, the last midterm is the final, non-cumulative) but they're easy if you go to class and study at all - he gives a list of possible exam questions and pulls directly from it when writing the exams. Attendance is mandatory and recitation has a group project (easy A).

Honestly a sweetheart! You should go to class (attendance + need notes for exams). It was a pleasure to attend-- never a chore. Studying was even fun, because the content was like a fun game of composing the story of history.

Professor Billman was a great professor. He's in the center of all archaeological lessons he's teaching. He has a lot of connections with anthropologists and archaeologists out in the world. He's very lenient on the assignments as long as you do it. Don't be afraid to talk to him.

Knows not to be too serious. Notes are easy to complete if you go to class and mildly pay attention.  He will often have some goofy tale or joke to make class interesting. Exams are ripped straight from the provided objectives. TAs were also relaxed and graded easy. Chill gen-ed with a chill dude. Would recommend.

Billman was easily the best lecturer I have had at UNC. His lectures were funny and very helpful for the exams. Very exam-heavy, but with a little studying of exam objectives before the exam. As long as you attend lectures, take good notes, and study before the exams you cannot get a bad grade. Easy focus capacity credit.
Pretty easy A/A-. Billman is cool, and his lectures are probably as entertaining as they can be.

I took this class for a focus capacity and I am so glad I did. Although the exams/ 2 papers were no cake walk, he is such a funny professor and made class super enjoyable. Just go to lectures and take notes, and you'll be fine.

Funny guy. Lectures are chill, he just shows you some pictures and tells you some stories. Exams and assignment were very easy. You honestly have to try super hard to not get a good grade in this class.
Loved him, clearly very passionate about the subject

Professor Billman keeps the class engaging with his hilarious lectures. While attendance is mandatory, the easy exams and lax grading make this a great gen ed. Unstuckstudy was super helpful for preparing.

Dr. Billman is a phenomenal lecturer and incredibly well-traveled. He has personal ties with half the archaeologists in the curriculum, and he's got a great sense of humor. The class was super engaging; attend lectures and take notes, though, because slides are sparse. Loved him so much that I'm taking two of his classes next sem as a busi major.

Very TA based, 4 assignments plus a bunch of just show up to class and get easy points. Its essentially 4 papers are the only assignments however I would not suggest this class as a gen ed. very boring and very TA based. However I should've gotten an A had I done all of the participation questions
Take this instead of Anth145 Prehistory

Billman is a nice, funny guy, and a solid professor. He was fairly accommodating. I am not an Anth or hist major, but his class wan't crazy. Might have just been the TAs, but midterms were graded a bit harsh. Two papers with a take home midterm and final. I put low effort into learning material and still finished with an A-.

Dr. Chua's class was enjoyable. Make sure you show up (or watch) the lectures as well as do the readings. The midterm and final exam make up most of your grade, but as long as you go to/watch lecture, and even just skim/know what the readings are talking about, you should do well on these exams.

Good lecturer, had zoom class option because class was put all the way in kenan flaggler.  Around ~4 books for the course, some being ethnographies that were easy reads and interesting (did not ask super in depth questions on the book content).  6 Reading Responses throughout the semester that needed to be ~1 page long, 1 midterm, then the final.
she is amazing. the content is so interesting and she actually wants to get to know u. midterms and exams were one of the easiest ones I have taken in college as long as u pay attention in class.

Dr. Chua is a great professor! I found her lectures and the readings to be very interesting. There are a lot of discussion posts about the readings. (She does assign a lot of reading, so just be prepared).

As someone who has barely done any readings for any other class, I fear I suggest you do readings for this class because the tests are very much reading-based. Even if you skim the chapters/readings, you would be in a good spot. Chua's lectures are really engaging, though. The classes always went by so fast because the lectures were so interesting.

This course was very reading heavy and there are reading quizzes every week so just be prepared for that. Prof. Chua is really good at keeping class engaging, I think she mostly cares that you are showing up and at least trying to participate in conversations. She is very respectful towards students and is always open to questions.
Lowkey mid class but good prof ayeeee

I wasn't sure if it was the class or the professor but I loved this class overall! I've never had a class where I genuinely wanted to do the reading until this one. The readings are engaging, and even if you don't do them, you don't feel behind during the class because she will usually catch you up on them or provide a brief summary.
bruh if u have a bad ta ur grade is cooked also tell me why I got a .5 on some participation when I was literally in class and responded to the question for attendance?? bs ahh ta tanking my grade

Interesting topics and Dr. Chua knows how to lecture. Grades depend on your TA, but I found the assignments and exams fair. She provides study guides and does a review before the exams. Would def consider taking another class with her.

This class did have some interesting topics, and I did enjoy it, it took a turn after the midterm. I had a 102-103 in this class until the midterm, and then I got a 75 on it, and my class grade is now a 76. Professor Chua is nice, however, I don't think this class fits me well. If you missed any lecture, you had no luck with any notes or material.

I am not saying she is not a good lecturer or a nice human, she is and I can tell how she is deeply respected in her field. This being said- the course was NOT an easy A, which sadly did hurt my GPA and many others. The recitation was actually helpful but the midterm and final exams were HELL ON EARTH

She is an amazing lecturer who is very caring and empathetic towards her students. She knows a lot about the topic and is very passionate. She does not share her lecture slides, so go to class because info from the slides will be on the exams. There are a lot of readings, but they were really interesting if you enjoy the topic.

Dr. Chua is an amazing professor, she is willing to answer questions and is passionate about what she does. The course has many readings which can be a lot but will be on the exam. Not an easy A, if you mess up on 1 of the 6 reading responses it will hurt (worth 21% of your grade with 21 points max). Make sure u get a good TA. Does not post slides.

Amazing prof and class.  Actually looked forward to going to lecture.  She's accessible outside of class and provides study guides for the exams.  6 short essays and in-class assignments for attendance, plus a paper.  Would take another course with her even though it's not my major.

I took this course thinking it would be fun and good bc of RMP. Instead, the lectures were SO boring and what really annoyed me was the midterm. It was SO specific.. I actually studied hard for that crap and did awful and everyone I know did too. It was extremely specific and they took so many points off of my short answers for no reason- DONT TAKE

While there are only six small assignments and one paper, the tests were extremely hard with very specific and impossible multiple choice questions and short answers that were graded very harshly. Only take this class if required for your major as it is NOT an easy A like other anth classes.
Dr. Chua is the best! This is my second class with her now and it's made me join the med anth major. Her lectures are so interesting and she is very accessible outside of class.  Chua is a gem!

Does not post the slides/recordings, but as long as you attend class & take notes (even if copied straight from the PPT) then you'll be fine. Lots of long readings but you can skim most of them - BUT TRUST they WILL be on the exam so have the main idea and examples ready. + 6 reading responses & 1 essay graded by TAs - be sure you have a good one!

Dr. Chua is clear in her expectations and gives students the tools they need to succeed in the course.  Content was super interesting as were the readings.  If you show up to class and do the work, you'll do great.
She was great! Her quiz was more writing-heavy than the other two professors but I enjoyed her lectures.
Way too hard for a first year seminar. Did not clarify how attendance/participation worked until she gave me a bad grade on it.
I do not recommend.
She is a great professor for IDST128I. Very kind and knowledgeable about her field. Lectures were engaging and understandable. This is a great class to get the triple I credit.

If you want an easy first year seminar DO NOT TAKE CLASSES SHE TEACHES. I got the vibe that she expects the majority of your time to be devoted to her class. Journaling assignments. Gave me a C on a presentation that I worked really hard on. Just don't take her if you actually want a decent grade for a first year seminar.

Came to class with genuine interest to learn more about the topic. One or two of the books had some depth, but most of the reading was really dense and class discussions were based on her views. Grades on papers were wildly inconsistent and was not given any indication of my poor participation grade until the term ended even after meeting with her.
Way too hard
STEM major and this was by far my hardest class.

I joined this class because I wanted to learn more about the topic. She made class horrible to come to and graded very strictly. You are obligated to read 4 books and write an in-person written essay worth 40% of your grade (each). Nobody liked her so AVOID AT ALL COST.

Professor Stuesse is by far the worst teacher I've ever had. Her class is extremely hard, with unnecessary amount of work for a first year seminar. She's a tough grader, and this class requires lots of reading that don't pertain to the class. Not accepting of opinions that aren't aligned with the class's structure. Still go an A, but DONT TAKE HER!
Horrible teacher.

Dr. Stuesse is knowledgeable about the material she teaches, but her attitude made the class difficult. She often came off as rude and passive-aggressive, and at times, singled out students. The course requires reading four books, each followed by an essay. It felt like she graded more on personal judgment than on the actual quality of the work.
Very rude and condescending. Grading seems to depend on you as a person rather than your work. Do not take this class if you do not share the same views as her.

Dr. Stuesse seems very knowledgeable about her field. Unfortunately, this is overshadowed by her behavior. She often responds with condescending statements and singles out students. More than once, she got upset about students not making "perfect" circles in small group discussions and even picked up a kid's backpack to force him into the circle.

She is clearly well-read and loves what she does. She is so passive aggressive and singles out students. There is never a square minute of chill time. She uses up every second of the class possible. In general, this wouldn't be a hard class generally, but for for a FY seminar, no bueno. She should stick with grad school or teach middle school.

She is brilliant, and I could tell she is very passionate and knowledgeable. However, assigned a lot of reading, participation was mandatory, and she was a harsh grader. She did too much and made us read 4 books and 4 hand-written essays along with a group research project at the end. TOO MUCH
Overall easy class. He lectures were a bit dry and could get a bit off track. Good option for Triple I.

Dr. Stuessee is an amazing professor. I enrolled in the online course a day later and let me do the assignments I missed, so she is really accommodating. Lectures are mandatory, as well as participation. Quizzes are super easy (quizlet), so are the discussion boards. The hardest part are the thought pieces due to having little time to write them.

Honestly, Dr. Stuesse should not be teaching concepts surrounding race in IDST128. I think she is a brilliant anthropological mind, but watching try to piece lectures together was laughable. Easy class though!

She's fine, I wouldn't take her again. Her expectations were too high leading students to cheat on their work. Nobody I knew enjoyed the class but she was nice and you get good exposure to ethnography. I recommend ANTH 582 with Rivkin-Fish if you want to learn about ethnography instead of this class. Make sure to participate - she docks points!!

Professor Arbuckle is super nice and approachable. The class is very interesting and the homework is minimal. Attendance isn't required, but it'll be helpful to have someone to explain the slides to you. Fun and easy class!

Amazing class!! Professor Arbuckle is so nice and caring. He is accessible at all times of the day and often answers emails very quickly. He answers any and all questions. Professor Arbuckle's lectures are very interesting and sometimes showed images about his archaeology experience which was incredible to see first hand.

Minimal feedback given throughout the class, didn't grade any assignment until the day before grades were due. Very unclear final essay rubric and if you don't write in the exact style he is looking for, you will not do well. But you wouldn't know what that style is, because he doesn't grade anything or give feedback throughout the class.

Best class ever! There were no midterms or finals. One 5 page paper in the middle of the semester, but not difficult if you don't leave it to the last minute. Professor Arbuckle is understanding and kind. While his lectures were not required, they were very interesting and worth your time to attend. Would 100% take a class with Arbuckle again.

kind, very interesting, understanding prof. easy A. 1 paper due in the middle of the year making it possible to actually be interested in the content. you get downgraded if you use AI but are given the (optional) chance to revise the paper at the end of the sem. this was good incentive to be more ambitious with the work resulting in an A.
One of the best professors I have had here. He is so kind and knowledgeable about archeology. He is so passionate in his lectures that they are absorbing.

Joke of a class. Took online during maymester. Got the 2 weeks of work done very quickly and very ahead of time. Never knew what grade I got on the final paper, but I got a 100 in absolutely everything else, and finished with an A. Watch the lectures on 2x speed, if you even decide to watch them. Super easy quizzes and super low stress final paper.
By far one of the best professors I've ever had. He's extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter and a great lecturer. He also wants us to learn and engage rather than stress about grades.
One of the best teachers I've ever had, he's understanding, an interesting lecturer, and actually wanted us to learn and engage rather than stress over grades.

Professor Arbuckle's class was very interesting! There were two short, easy assignments each week and no readings. There was one fascinating paper that counted as both the midterm and final. I enjoyed the lectures and personal stories Professor Arbuckle shared from his archaeological finds. Great class, highly recommend!
love this man. great professor. very knowledgeable. wants all of his students to succeed and really values what students can/want to contribute to discussions. highly recommend.

Love this class/prof! Very aware that students generally hate abstract theory classes and makes the material as approachable as possible. Lectures like its standup - very easy to pay attention. Lots of assignments that feel like busy work, but I probably wouldn't do the readings otherwise so that might be a good thing. Highly recommend this class!

Prof Arbuckle is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He is incredibly flexible and genuinely loves the material he teaches. He is fantastic and you need to take him at least once during your time at Carolina. This was a study abroad course so we had assignments every day but they were engaging and not too bad.

Dr. Arbuckle is a gem in UNC's anthropology department. He is kind, caring, and so passionate about the material. We covered a lot in this class, but he effectively broke the material down into easily digestible pieces. Professor Arbuckle worked very hard to make our classroom a safe, positive space and he 100% achieved this. Highly recommend!!!

I am taking this class during the Maymester. The class is online but professor Arbuckle is very engaging. I was nervous of the intensity of a Maymester, but it has been great. He is the best lecturer ever and has very detailed powerpoints so you are never bored. He is the most hilarious and caring professor ever + he is a Swiftie. Highly recommend!
I absolutely loved this class!!! Benjamin Arbuckle is amazing. Very clear guidelines and assignments so it's very attainable to get an A in the class. I literally recommend this to every person ever!

His lectures were funny and interesting. Assignments were simple, weekly quizzes or activities you could easily complete as long as you came to class and did the readings. Slides available online. Final project was a research paper and lightning presentation on a discovery of your choosing, which was super fun. Highly recommend him.
Absolutely spectacular. He is very personable and kind, and his lectures and readings are very informative and interesting. Best professor of my undergradate at UNC.
One of the best professors I have ever had. Super caring and energetic, really passionate about the subject. Definitely recommend.

One of the kindest people I've ever met. Grades were largely based off of regular homework assignments (reading plus written response). You can tell he really loves the content and wants his students to succeed. No tests! He does get rambley and runs out of time in his lectures, but he's a really sympathetic guy and very nice grader. I'd recommend.

Professor Delgaty was amazing. He was the most understanding professor I had last semester and his lectures were super interesting. He is quite young, so he knows what students care and not care about.

Delgaty is the best teacher. Definitely take him if you can. He is super funny and the class had great content- he knew what he was talking about. 284 is really what you make of it, attendance is not mandatory, and graded on one group project at the end which, if you do the work is graded easily. Fantastic course with a fantastic professor.

Prof Delgaty is very knowledgeable on how to promote products. His experience in market analysis and product/company evaluation makes his lectures very interesting since he brings in real-world examples. Do yourself a favor and take his class.

I ABSOLUTELY loved Professor Delgaty!!!! I would 1000% recommend him because he is one of the few professors Ive met that is very accommodating and truly cares for their students. Our final was essentially a project on what we thought campus portrayed and essentially collect data and do a presentation on it.

Professor Delgaty is the goat. Truly. His lectures are fantastic and the work he assigns is always topical and useful for the course. He is known to reach out to students who are struggling personally and check in on them. If you take a class with him just know you are BLESSED!
Miss this guy and this class

Yk when prof. think everyone knows what they're saying bc they have a PhD in it? Yeah this is her. Did not understand any lecture or reading she gave. 2 presentations with vague directions so she made you change them at the last minute. Often interrupted people while presenting and called out students when said something not up to her caliber.

Dr. Salm structured the course around an anthropology research project, which was time-consuming but helped build useful skills. Homework was assigned frequently, often for the next class, and usually graded for completion. She creates a collaborative classroom environment and is open to student input.

Professor Salm is very passionate about her work, however her lecturing style is hard to follow, unclear, and very messy. Personally, I would not take any other courses as she is unclear with her assignment instructions as well, however she is an overall easy grader and wants students to have a passing grade.

I love Dr. Salm as a person and a Professor. This class wasn't for me, and that's ok; the content is very dense and hard to digest. Sometimes it does seem overintellectualizing and pretentious, but I think that's the nature of critical anthropology and being exposed to new ways of thinking, not her personally. Overall, an amazing professor :)

ANTH 390: Dr. Salm is hands down the most charismatic and personable prof I've had here. She always meets her students needs and works WITH us, instead of just throwing us work. Her intellect is inspiring, she has an extensive background in super interesting topics and encourages students to explore things that they otherwise would overlook.

a LOT of reading (as is the case with any anth class) but a wonderful lecturer and makes hard concepts easy to understand. i don't think ill ever forget this class, it honestly shifted how i view the world (in the most neutral way possible)

The last 2 comments seem unfair. Professor Salm clearly knows what she's talking about and expects us to engage at a high level. She doesn't dumb things down.. so yeah, that might make the lectures feel dense. it's also what makes the class interesting. It's definitely pushing me to think differently and at a higher standard than my other courses.

Professor Salm is certainly passionate about her work and I like how you can clearly see that during lectures. However, she is not the best lecturer regardless of her knowledge and everything feels like it is inflated with unnecessary flowery language. Concepts are not that hard in theory but they are made out to be by the way they are taught.

I took 390 skepticism in science, with her but I wasn't able rate that class. I enjoyed this class, if you are going into pre-med it is definitely worth taking as it gives you a whole new perspective. There are several readings per week, few small assignments every week,1 presentation and 1 final paper. She is very caring and wants you to succeed

Dr. Salm truly listens to her students (what they find interesting, what we didn't like, etc.). There is a lot of reading to complete for class, but the response requirements (perusal comments) allows students to comment on what they find interesting. I found the class to be slightly disorganized with instructions often being given last minute.

Dr Salm is AMAZING! She really got us interested in the realm of science and anti-science. Hard but SO WORTH IT. Most of the topics in this class were to me and a different perspective than any other course at UNC. I would highly recommend Dr. Salm if you have any interest in policy making, research, admin, global health, ethnography, and more!

Professor Salm usually has pretty short lectures creating a lot of room for group discussion - so to get the most out of her class do the readings and come to class ready to discuss. No quizzes, or tests, just two essays (10-page final), and annotations for readings. Super interesting class, and Salm is very approachable, smart, and relaxed.

Loved this class! I'm a med anth minor and this class was refreshingly different than others I've taken in the past. Grades were mostly dependent on participation, in class and through the Perusal readings, and our midterm and final paper/projects. readings were sometimes long but even then still interesting. 10/10 would recommend!

EXCEPTIONAL!! Dr. Salm is genuine of the most amazing professors I've ever had at UNC. She is inspirational and motivating in every aspect of the course. Lots of readings (~60 pages a week) with graded annotations but very manageable and interesting content. 2 papers that build off each other. Overall, 1000000% recommend if you want a great prof!!

Inspirational, enlightening course relevant to everyday life! 2 heavy, but interesting free readings per week(annotations=30% of grade), EC available. Grade reflects effort! Everything a professor should be & more! Attendance/participation=30%, flexibility if you communicate (caring). Papers (midterm 20%, final 25%) worked on progressively+feedback

Loved her and the class was cool. Definitely a lot of reading for hw but most of it was interesting. If you do the reading and give the essays your best effort you'll do well. Be prepared to spend a good amount of time each week on the class if you want to get something out it. She's also so interesting to talk to outside of class, would recommend

Great teacher new teacher here at UNC. - Lots of reading (around 30pgs per hw). The beginning assigned were boring but then the readings got very interesting.
gives extensions when u ask and is very understanding. - 2 major essays that gave alot of time to complete - very awesome, a girls girl, easy to talk too outside. Take her class wont regret.

participation and attendance matters, large part of grade. 
lectures can be boring but she just trying to get us to understand and discuss what we feel towards the reading.
lot of readings that she doesn't assign for hw is extra credit which can be used anywhere
Would take her again in a heart beat
hw is mostly reading n giving 4 comments.

I really enjoyed Melissa's class! While there was a lot of readings, they were really interesting, especially when we got into the anti-science aspects of the course. There was a nice balance of lectures and discussions, and there were plenty of opportunities to ask questions. Overall, I would absolutely take another class with Melissa!

I just finished 151 with her and it was great! She made the class very interesting and wanted everyone to get an A. She made it very easy to get one as well. Just show up, do the group projects and quizzes, and email her if you need any extension. She is very accommodating, could not recommend her enough!

Dr. Briggs was very nice and I enjoyed the class but felt like we were talking about the same topics all semester. Two group projects with an easy participation based final. Do the extra credit and participate every once in a while and you'll do fine.

I loved Dr. Briggs. She was extremely passionate and knowledgable about everything we talked about. She will make you question a lot of things too. Some of the readings are difficult to read and understand but she will go through it with the class. She brings food for tasting days and the final is everyone bringing a dish. Please take this class!!
She is very nice and understanding. Lots of extra credit. Fun projects. Definitely recommend.

Dr. Briggs is a brilliant mind and passionate about what she teaches. However, her lectures were at times, seriously boring. The reading is very academic and above most college student's minds- I would even argue above most ANTH majors. If you are not an anthropology major, I would stay away from this course. She also has a strong liberal agenda.

She da goat. Big group porject worth 30% of ur grade, but its really lax on the grading and she is extremely generous. Extra credit is everywhere, and the quizzes are kinda hard but come straight from the slides.

Prof Briggs is truly a great professor. Even if you don't necessarily like anth, this is a great class. Grade is mostly based on take home weekly quizzes that aren't bad and some Minecraft group projects that are super fun. Briggs is super understanding and kind and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. Definitely recommend!
I love her

I never even write reviews, but Dr Briggs is truly a great professor. She wants everyone to do well as long as you at least try, no matter what your anthropology background is. If you commit to the weekly take-home quizzes and stay on top of simple group projects, you will inevitably do great!

Great for gen eds! Attendance was optional, online quizzes, no exams. 1 bigger group project. She brings in food some days. Overall super chill and exactly what a gen ed should be like. Highly recommend!

Dr. Briggs is so sweet and is a very passionate lecturer. I learned a lot and she was super understanding if students ever needed anything from her. Half of your grade is made up of take-home quizzes, the other majority is a semester-long group project that was really fun. You get one point added to your final grade for attending every lecture!

She is so sweet and such a good professors. her lectures are engaging but there are a lot of readings and a the recitations are a little tedious but I had fun over all and it was a decently easy class!

Easiest class I have ever taken. I barely showed up to lectures but did not struggle getting an A. Do the group work well and go to recitation. She is a very fun lecturer and the class was interesting. She is a very good person.

easiest A ever at UNC. attendance isn't required, no friday lectures on weeks w/ recitation, and assignments were so easy. grades were a group project throughout the semester, weekly quizzes, and occasional 2 page papers (double spaced) that barely required research. only exam was the final, which she gave us like 5 extra credit points on.

Great lectures and interesting topics. Attendance not required but helps for the final (very small portion of the grade). Be careful of who you pick for the group project in recitation- it takes a lot of time and research and can easily be a pain if your group is not helpful.

This class just didn't make sense to me. The topic is interested but Dr. Briggs gets off track and by the end of the class it is a waste of time to be there. Overall, it is a very easy A but the recitation and group project make it slightly annoying.
Gives multiple opportunities to get an A through quiz corrections and extra credit. Definitely wants to see her students succeed

This class is very well organized, and I highly recommend taking it for a gen ed or for the anthropology minor. Attendance was optional and you receive extra credit if you attend all lectures. Instead of midterms there are weekly quizzes that are easy even if you don't do the readings. Dr. Briggs really cares about the wellbeing of her students!
ANTH151 is an easy A class with a passionate professor. Weekly quizzes and a group project, but plenty of extra credit opportunities. unstuck ai helped me crush the final.

Nice prof! Discussion heavy- one lecture and one group discussion day. Graded based on weekly quizzes, a group presentation, a final group project, and participation. She was super nice with my class and wanted us to do well.
Class is super cool but lots of work, professor is great and very knowledgable

A really nice guy and a great professor. He's a tough grader on exams and can sometimes go on tangents during lecture. Not the easiest professor but he knows his stuff and cares about his students. Would certainly take again.

GOAT of Anthropology, this man is such a great professor and person. As a professor he is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the topic. He knows how to teach! As a student just make sure to engage in the lectures and you will learn. Exams are about topics covered in class and are straightforward.

I genuinely enjoyed this class with Professor Rudi. He's down-to-earth and wants you to succeed. Reading responses can sometimes seem futile, but they aren't difficult if you do the readings. I'd highly recommend for anyone in the major or who's interested in taking on an interdisciplinary approach to development.

Professor Colloredo-Mansfeld was really guy and passionate about the course material. You have to do a reading assignment before every class and really short discussion post. There were two midterms with tricky MCQs and take home essay. If you go to his and the TAs office hours and show you know the material they are very lenient with final grades.

He's a great professor and very nice guy! The course material wasn't too hard to understand, but the exams were hard and he's a tough grader. He doesn't offer powerpoints, so attendance is helpful. There's a decent amount of reading. And participations's also useful to. get a decent grade.

Rudi is one of my favorite professors at UNC! Two exams, two papers, and one take-home final made this class manageable. Some of the readings were mediocre and some blew me out of the water. Either way he will make sure to bring out the key concepts for the exams during lecture. Highly recommend!

This class was not easy but it was so fun learning from Rudi. We had few assignments that can make or break your grade, but the focus was more on the content rather than your grades. We wrote two essays and took 3 exams, which were moderately difficult, but manageable if you do the readings. Attendance is not required, but you will want to attend.

He is an amazing professor who clearly cares about his students. There were textbooks required to read for the class, but they were all available through the library. I looked forward to each class I went to!

He's a very nice and great guy, but this class was tough Much more difficult than expected for a 200-level. Content was very interesting and useful... but there are a lot of required readings, and a lot of writing as well. There were two midterms with multiple choice and an essay, as well as a research project/essay involving interviewing 2 people.
great professor, would highly recommend sending him drafts to revise before submitting final assignments, super easy class

I would 100% recommend this professor!!! He is very knowledgeable and really cares about hs students. I find that sometimes his lectures are a bit random at times though. The grades all depended on the RAs. He also threw a "burning man" like party at his house and it was super fun.

Rudi is a cool guy and I learned a lot from him. Reading and assignments were a lot but he's work-shopping the class so maybe he'll tone it down. Friday labs were also not very fun but kept us from writing a whole paper so I'll take it. Also hosted a silent disco for us? So perhaps it was all worth it. You need good writing skills to do well!!

The grading is super strict. There was an incredible amount of reading and a lot of homework. You will need to take two midterm exams that involve multiple-choice questions and an essay.  
I think he overestimated the level of the students in this 200-level class, but overall, a very good and knowledgeable teacher. Painfully learned a lot.

Do NOT take a course with him. All assignments/exams are online. However, he is a super tough grader, and without the extra credit he gave, I would not have been able to receive an A in this class. His lectures are boring and were just used as a study hall when I did go. If this class is your last option, then take it, but stay away if you can.

The reviews of Dr. Hilton are not representative of him as a professor. He is very easy to work with, gives ample opportunity for extra credit, and allows extended time for testing at the testers discretion. He speaks slightly monotone, but other than that he is a very good and caring professor who is easy to work with.

Prof. Hilton was not as bad as his reviews described. He has an old school teaching style and expects students to be responsible. He knows his stuff and is passionate in his work. If you enjoy molecular anthropology or genetics, then this is an easy course. I would not recommend this course to students not interested in anthropological genetics.

Dr. Hilton may come off as a jerk (he said it himself), but he really is a nice professor who's willin to help! Ask questions and he'll answer w/ a few extra tangents in there—but ur questions will get answered. 

There's basically 10 lab quizzes in a sem, but it's all alr inside you, so study a bit and u'll b fine! 

Take home tests r awesome too!

Although the lectures can be a bit dry, I really enjoyed this class and Professor Hinton. Make sure to show up to class! He gives out extra credit for attendance. Exams are not that difficult, and the recitation lab is interesting. Midterms are a dense part of your grade, so make some flashcards and study, and you will do great!

I  really like Professor Hilton. I think the content of the class was sometimes dry, but if you care about anatomy or evolution at all, it's interesting for sure! The tests are difficult, but the slides will provide you with proper study material. He is overall a cool guy and kind person and also wears some really cool earrings lol

the class is so boring but if u listen, he tells u the right stuff. the slides r super disorganized but if u attend class he will sometimes give u extra credit. the class just has a tonnnnnn of hard vocab terms s be prepared to spend a long time memorizing.

Great class. Lectures are long and dry, but you can catch up from slides and textbooks. Essentially weekly quizzes on bones + structure ID, so review flashcards OFTEN. Has a tendency to ramble when you ask him a question, but it's interesting stuff. Tests are take home, so very forgiving. Take advantage of when he opens lab up on weekends.

Prof. Hilton isn't that bad. Yes, his lectures are quite dense and dry, but the exams are take home so it's not like you have to memorize everything he says. Honestly, he's a pretty nice guy, but a little bit old school and a very specific grader. I can't say that this course amazed me, but it wasn't as bad as others have made it out to be.

The exams in this class were unreasonably diffcult and worth 75%. I understand the EC was given instead of a curve, but the exam averages were very low. The wordings of the questions were tricky. There are very few recitations. He reads off the slides in class but the lectures were interesting if you could pay attention. I do not recommend.

I struggled with the exams, especially since they were 75% of my grade. But he is a nice person once you talk to him. He offers extra credit and he's very understanding when if comes to exams and material. He is genuinely so nice and funny; however, the lectures were kind of boring because he just reads off the slides so its easy to doze off..

IDK if he changed or something, but he's a great professor. 

If I'm being honest, I was scared by the reviews because they seemed overwhelmingly bad, but I took his class for Anthr 143, and it was an easy class IF you attended the lectures and did your work. Overall, I enjoyed this professor : )!

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! Dr Hilton is a monotone lecturer and just reads directly off the slides. Sometimes he gets off track and is confusing. Also, the class has three hard exams, and that's it, with a class average below 70%. I ignored the bad reviews, and this class is the hardest one I'm taking (STEM major). Don't make the same mistake I did!

Lecture heavy, but he is very knowledgeable about osteology and has lots of experience in the field. If you're not interested in bones, you won't like this class. Not an easy A, but very rewarding. Gave partial credit for quizzes and lenient on essays. Clear expectations. Gave class time and opened bone lab outside of class time for extra review.

He seemed like a nice guy but the class was not easy nor fun besides maybe the recitations. In total I believe we were graded on 6 assignments and the exams were 75% of our grade which really sucked. He was also keen on the standard bell curve. The lectures were long and boring for the most part, avoid his classes if possible.

Highly recommend Anth414. This is few unc classes that you ACTUALLY get knowledge. Hard quizzes. He does provide extra lab time so use them. Take home exams, love that. you basically got 24 hours to finish them. He made slides boring but he is really responsible and knows a lot about osteology.

Wouldn't recommended Professor Hilton. He does mainly read off slides. His rubric for assignments are not clearly posted. It'll say on the syllabus that papers are due at midnight but also to turn papers in class? Furthermore, he waited until the very last day where grades were due to post grades in a lump sum. As of now he has no course structure.

Hilton does not hold up to his word. If you can avoid this class, do it. His tests are impossible and completely unpredictable. Not lenient with grading. Nothing he says is valid. Expect the total opposite of what he says.

Absolutely terrible, avoid at all costs. Final grade is based on like 5 assignments, and grading is harsh and arbitrary. He'll give no credit on questions that were fully answered just because he doesn't like your response. He reads directly off slides, and lectures are legitimately the most boring I've ever had at UNC. Refuses to use Canvas.

This man is so boring that he puts himself to sleep in his lectures. The tests are comprised of things we talked about once or twice during lectures, he has no interest in you knowing the information or doing well in the class, and there are very few other assignments to bring up your grade (which you'll have no idea what it is until way too late).

I enjoyed this class. There is a lot of reading, but all you need are the general ideas of each one, and you'll be fine. Lectures are very interesting; you can tell she cares about what she teaches. I didn't do that well on the midterm/final, but still got an A.

Dr. O is a great professor! The class itself was honestly not too bad, you just have to keep up with some readings (and you can honestly get away with not doing a lot of them). The tests were mostly short response with some multiple choice, but Dr. O and the TAs grade pretty leniently. Overall, fun and straightforward class!

Dr. O is a genuinely good person who cares about the class, her students, and the content. This being said, the class is semi-disorganized and can be redundant. Lots of reading, but you only really need to do it if you're doing the reading responses. Pretty liberal and not very open to other perspectives, so prepare accordingly. Go to office hours!

Attendance not mandatory, so I didn't go to class once. Assigns a good amount of readings but you only really need to do them if you're doing a reading response on them. If you know how to study for the tests effectively, you'll do good in the class.

We meditated before each class, which was kind of cool in my opinion. The course material is interesting and progressive, if you're into that stuff. The papers and exams were graded very leniently. If you can showcase within them that you did the readings / kept up with class, you will do very well. Attendance is not mandatory, but I recommend it.
Readings are long and tedious, watch a lot of very long films/videos. Exams are extremely easy. Papers are very straightforward, just follow the instructions.
By far my favorite class; she was a great teacher and made the content fun!

Dr. Osterweil's class was definitely the most unique I've ever taken really - it is obvious she cares about the material very deeply and really gets you thinking. Even though the class could've been a bit more organized and straightforward, I really enjoyed the energy and knowledge she brought to the course. She's also very kind, open, and driven.

Dr. O is a good person, but not necessarily a good professor. The beginning five minutes of every lecture were spent doing a grounding exercise and she rarely got through all of her slides. Reading was very heavy and mostly one-sided. She's very spiritual and Type B, which is fine, but might be better suited for a yoga studio than a classroom.

Dr. O might be a good person, but as a professor, not very much. She is less like a professor/educator and more like an activist, constantly trying to impose her soft agenda on the students. Not very attentive, and her course is utterly disorganized. I highly DO NOT recommend her. Undergrads, please be aware!!

I was in her graduate seminar.
Dr. O is very polarizing. I like the readings, because I like to read things that challenge the mainstream. As a professor, I find Dr. O pedantic and critical, she is not good at active listening or constructive criticism. I am unsure what I am supposed to have learned in this class.

This class felt very skewed and assumed many things that felt extreme. I felt very unheard, and felt that Professor Osterwail would dismiss anything I had to say in class, and developed a distaste for me due to my views. I also strongly felt that this led to her and the TA grading my papers more harsh if they expressed differing views.
It is discussion based and you should be ready to hear out a lot of unconventional and different opinions.
Prof. Osterweil is very passionate, knowledgeable, and interesting. This class was a bit more work than I expected, but was really valuable to me.

Nice professor, but the lectures felt very all over the place. It was often hard to take clear notes because she tends to go on tangents. However, the subject matter was interesting and she is very knowledgable and passionate about it. If you do most of the readings and pay attention in class, you'll be prepared for the exams and essays.

Dr. O is a hard one to rate. The concepts she teaches are very skewed-- very one sided, incomplete, and unacademic. Simply put, she says a whole lot of nothing... Nice professor, but really pounds her perspective only. Very liberal. If you are good writer, you will do well. Several papers, TA's grade everything, and a lot of work for a gen-ed.

Cool professor, but lectures/slides are all over the place. Concepts are vague, no clear definitions provided. Tons of reading every week, but not necessary to do well. Graded on 2 papers, 2 exams, recitation attendance/participation, 5 reading responses, 2 small assignments.

She's a super cool and passionate professor with a lot of knowledge. But to be honest, I learned very little from this class. Don't take 220 unless you need it for your major, she just makes things overly confusing and talks in circles during her lectures. The things she teaches are difficult concepts and she doesn't make it any less complicated.
Unless you are doing this class for your major, dont take this, its not worth it.
talks too much, says too little. unorganized.

Code wasn't available to rate but I took 450. This was my favorite class this semester and up there out of all I've ever taken. Reading and getting ahead on the research project are very important but Dr. Price explains clearly and is always willing to help. He clearly is extremely knowledgeable and helps to develop career skills - would recommend.

Dr. Price was phenomenal, and the material was fascinating. There's a lot of reading, but discussing it in class makes it easier to understand. As a seminar, there's frequent group discussion, and Dr. Price creates a welcoming environment that makes participating easy. Take this class!

Professor Price is genuinely one of the kindest teachers I have ever had. There is a lot of reading for the class but he makes everything easy to understand. The main assignments are a few essays but he is not harsh with grading and you can talk to him about what you wrote before submitting. I definitely recommend taking his class.

Favorite professor I've had at UNC. Amazing professor and an even better man. Go to lectures, do the weekly readings and you will be fine. Class is graded off of 2 midterms, a final, and essay based off of class readings. Also have to read a 300 page book. Will say lecture slides were unorganized. Great class, highly recommend.

Prof. Price was amazing! Freshies, if u are wondering what first year seminar to take, this class is it. 4 VERY short essays, 2 online quizzes, presentation, & final. The presentation you can either do a video or speak in front of the class which was good bc of anxiety. The readings were interesting. Learned a lot about myself in this class!

Prof Wiener is very focused on readings and not so much lectures. She wants you to work with others as much as possible. Almost no homework or tests--you're "graded" on your final portfolio. This class could've been an email.

Very sweet/caring professor. You can skim readings. As a first year seminar, this is many students' first anthropology class so at first it seems she believes that she's "always right", but she really intends to challenge the way you think. Particular about grading, but learn her language, ask questions, participate, and you'll do really well.

Take this class if you're ready to read a lot and discuss readings with groups. Grades are extremely harsh and hypocritical. You try and do one thing and she says it isn't fine, then you do what she says to do, and she says that isn't fine either. Wouldn't take this class again.

Assigns multiple readings due at the start of each class. It was so much reading that after the first week, no students did it. We did group discussions on the reading and then she would lecture and it was so boring. The entire semester you work on steps to your final research paper and she grades each of them HARSHLY. Take a different FYS.

Miserable. Grading criteria unclear, when she doesn't like your stuff she will let you know in the most rude and condescending way ever. 
Avoid this class at all costs. also it's boring

She's very nice & understanding. I got sick and couldn't get a university-approved absence,  but she totally came through for me and sent me the work & didn't count the attendance against me. There are a lot of pre-class readings.
She's very knowledgeable in her field, but she is a little strange (isn't everyone in the anth department though?)

I hesitated to take this professor because of the reviews calling her arrogant and entitled. However, I found that these comments couldn't be any farther from the truth. She is one of the most insightful people I've met. She is educated and passionate about her field and it shows. I've never felt more inspired and excited for my future! So thankful

Be forewarned that she is very nit-picky with her grading-- even if you send it to the writing center or use Grammarly you can count on her to find an error. Her comments are passive aggressive, a bit demoralizing, and often left me feeling discouraged. Wouldn't recommend for a first-year seminar.

She is a nice and polite lady. However, she is a VERY strict grader, especially considering this is a first-year/entry-level course. This class is very heavy on reading; you will have at least 20 pages of reading to do before each class. The lecture material itself does provide a unique perspective on dogs around the world.
She feels she is always right. Loves to assign long text. Your work is ever good enough to her.

Dr. Wiener assigns tons of reading, and will grade your writing by challenging you to think deeper about topics. As long as you think deeply and express those thoughts, she will appreciate your work. She cares very, very deeply about her students and wants them to succeed. Her greatest aim is to see you grow as a student and anthropologist.

SOOO MUCH READING AND WRITING. The class is self-graded she says until the end because she doesn't think you deserve the grade you think you do. Is extremely rude in her portfolio edits and emails.
