Also very passive aggressive. Expects way to much from her students in a 200 level course, probably one of the hardest ANTH courses in the department

This professor is extremely discouraging and I lost some of the passion and interest I had in anthropology. If you don't agree with her on something, she won't really hear your side (she is always right). She came across as arrogant, and some of her comments were pretty degrading. AVOID, there are many other amazing anth profs!
If you do not like writing , PLEASE DO NOT take this class. Final project is 50% and the criteria of grading only depends on personal preference.
Only multiple choices question is not that fair
No recording or slides. No round up

Professor Townsend is passionate and does a great job of sharing information and also fostering discussion within the classroom. I would 100% recommend this professor and this class, I thoroughly enjoyed my experience and would take as many classes with Professor Townsend as I could!
Townsend is definitely my favorite professor this semester. Concise and relevant readings, wonderful lectures, and very accessible out side of class....... I highly recommend!
The best professor and class you can take !!!

Towns was the best professor I took this semester. His lectures are very engaging, and it's accessible to get an A if you attend all classes. He is caring and understanding with all students. Grades are based on a 20% midterm, two 15% tests, and a 50% semester-long ethnography. Totally recommend!

Really great prof and his lectures were amazing - not required but very engaging. The readings weren't really required. Graded by midterm (20%), 2 tests (15% each), and a project you work on all semester worth 50% of your grade. Very good class - easy fc-global, as long as you somewhat attend lectures the midterms/tests are really easy.

Townsend is clear about what is being graded from the start. There is 1 midterm, 2 tests, and a final paper. Lecture notes aren't posted so even though attendance isn't checked its important to learn the material. As long as you take notes/pay attention the tests are very easy. The final paper is a sem long process with lots of help from TAs.
Townsend is definitely my favorite professor this semester. Concise and relevant readings, amazing lectures, and very accessible out side of class. Highly recommend!

Very engaging class, worth the hour and 15. Towns is funny and good at explaining topics. Lecture notes aren't posted anywhere so taking notes in class is a must. Midterm study guide but no study guide for the two other multiple choice tests. Paper is hard so would probably recommend for someone who has already taken a college level writing course.
I loved taking Towns' class! The tests were easy if you attended lecture and skimmed the notes. Very accessible too, he just doesn't post the lecture slides anywhere so go to class!
graded by very few things so messing up one will screw you over.

Middleton was a good guy with a fun personality, but he made the class more complicated than it had to be. I took this class as a gen ed because of his reviews but now I wish I didn't. He didn't post slides or lecture material, so you only had your notes and the readings to rely on for tests. There are only 3 test grades along with a final paper.
Its an easy class for gen ed requirements, but personally just not something that interested me. He did do his best teaching it although.

He is one of the best professors I have ever had. Coming to class was not mandatory but I wanted to go because he cared so much about the content. I understand globalization much better now. 2 exams (study the review sheets he gives), one final paper (semester-long), and recitation worksheets. Would 100% take this class again. Towns is the best.

Absolutely loved him. Best professor this semester by far. Super cool, caring, and understanding. The big, semester-long ethnography project wasn't too difficult just attend office hours if you have questions (he's super accessible). I loved the videos he showed in class and the tests were totally ok because he provided great review sheets.

One of the few professors I've had who fosters a truly bidirectionally educational environment where students and professor learn with and from one another. I cannot recommend him or this class enough. You get out of this class what you put into it, and he makes you want to be actively present. I'll never forget this experience. Thank you, Towns :)

I really enjoyed Townsend and his lectures were pretty great. He really emphasizes participation but if you come to class prepared then you will do fine. Grading criteria for midterm and final papers were limited but showing you spent time on it will be reflected in the grade.

She's a really good professor, but half of the semester it felt like we were learning the same thing over and over again. Overall, lots of assignments and only 1 midterm and a final, which were really easy, so def recommend!!

Dr. King is passionate and wants to share her knowledge, if you are taking ANTH270 after the spring 2026 semester the exams are in person and the classroom is interactive, with groups of four. Attendance is not mandatory but random attendance checks are done during the semester. Overall I would recommend this class and professor.

Her lectures are long, and she tends to repeat the same idea multiple times. There are at least 2 readings per week. There are asynchronous quizzes based on the reading, and there are 6 essays you need to write, and 1 can be dropped. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she includes pop-up participation grades that cannot be dropped.

Dr. King is very lenient about attendance, but there are in person assignments for part of the grade so it's still important to show up. Very easy class and 1-2 assignments a week. Lectures aren't super content heavy or interesting. Attending recitations is super important for your grade.

Dr. King is great! She is very knowledgeable and a good lecturer. The readings for this class were super interesting, and the discussion elements made class engaging—certainly an achievable A, but maybe not super easy. The final was discussion-based and creative, albeit a little odd. I would definitely recommend if you're interested in med anth!

Dr. King is a miserable person. She is not friendly, kind, or approachable. Her classes are also completely tailored to her woke agenda. ANTH 448 is supposed to be Medicine in the American South. 99% of the class was talking about one race, Black, and racism, specifically in the 18-1900s. There is a lot more to the American South than one race.

lots of readings. every week there was either a reading quiz (online) or an essay due. midterm and final are online. class was only monday and wednesday with one recitation. there are random attendence checks. overall, very interesting topics and not too time consuming.

Interesting med anth class, only 6 reading responses every other week and some annotation assignments. Grading criteria is unclear and grading is harsh sometimes so make sure to check over work. Lots of surprise in-class assignments so you have to attend every class as they do not drop any assignments.

The class is nice, and the readings are time-consuming, but so interesting! I found the lectures less engaging with Dr. King, since she (although passionate) can be redundant, but the most important points are in the slideshows. The content is great for someone looking for an intro to medical anthropology. Weekly readings + async assessments

she is def passionate about the subject and the class Is usually interesting. reading the articles is really annoying though but its really easy and there are no tests except for the final. super easy class. I like her

Find another gen ed to take because she acts like this class is a priority and is extremely rude and condescending. Provides a rubric for assignments that she doesn't actually use. Also, takes forever to grade even though ppl have alr graduated. It's easy to skip class and do the attendance from home, but beware of her horrible attitude.
as long as you do the reading and speak in each class, you will get an A

Content was interesting but lectures were boring and assignments were a drag to complete. Not hard, do your work and you will pass. You can get away with skimming the readings as they're only really brought up in recitation. Wasn't my favorite class but could float your boat

Dr. King was very arrogant/pompous. She liked to make smug comments to the class about our participation and discussion posts/responses. She was pretty rude. Most lectures involved her going on tangents or spewing her opinions to the class. She liked to talk about herself as well. Did not get a whole lot out of the lectures. Very reading heavy.

Knowledgeable about the course material, but monotonous lectures made the class extremely boring. She is unwilling to accommodate students who have to miss class for any reason and is not compassionate. Additionally, she refused to round up grades, even by 0.1% to the next letter grade, which discouraged me from ever taking a class with her again.

This class is interesting intersection of health and social issues but the lectures got very boring at times along with the out of class readings.  Assignments every week are either a short 10-15 question online quiz or short reading response which are super easy to complete so long as you do the readings/listen to the lecture.

Loved Dr. King but her lectures were so boring. You will be doing two-page write-ups so be ready based on weekly readings. The content is really interesting and makes you question your views on biomedicine as a system. Your recitation TA matters as they grade your write-ups which make up majority of your grade. Really easy gen ed and med anth class

ANTH 270 was not a difficult class, just a lot of reading that could catch up with you if you were not careful. There is either a take home quiz that you can attempt twice or a writing assignment due every week on Thursday night, but you can skip two of the assignments. There are also random attendance activities during lecture, so don't skip class

Easiest A yet! Professor was not as approachable, however, she was a great lecturer and very passionate about med anth. Participation was important, she did polls and canvas assignments. Only 4 useless recitations but the TA's were nice and graded lightly. Its easy to get an A as long as you do the work and attend class. Would take again!

Dr. King is definitely passive aggressive, but is so straightforward and I really enjoyed her passion about what we learned in 270. If you do as she says, you'll get an A. The layout this past spring was mandatory lecture (because of in class polls) and 4 recitations the whole semester. Would take her again!
His lecturing was clear and easy to follow, and he explained the main ideas of the readings really well. The exams weren't very hard but you do need to know definitions and main ideas really well.

Dr. Fivecoate is a really chill professor - 3 paper/projects throughout the sem but they're all easy and there's only one midterm exam and the final exam. My TA graded pretty flexibly but I'm not entirely sure if the class grading depends in which TA you have. He posts lecture slides right before the exams but not beforehand (go to class).

Dr. Fivecoate was really nice and passionate, but the class is more determined on who you have as a TA. Last year the class was super easy with take home exams and no weekly assignments, but this year it got harder. The content is easy but some of the assignments are graded on a whim w/o real reasons and your TA impacts your grade the most.

Easy class. Lectures aren't boring; he keeps them engaging and interesting. This class is reading-heavy heavy there is a weekly reading every week, also there are 3 projects throughout the whole semester, and they aren't that difficult. Easy class to get an A in.

Whatever university makes Dr. Fivecoate a full tenure professor will be lucky to have him. Made class so enjoyable and it really felt like the conversations we had in class were relevant and engaging. Made sure everyone's view was accepted in class and made the material very interesting. If you can, take one of his courses!

Dr. Fivecoate was one of the kindest professors I've had at UNC. All of the assignments  were very doable coming from someone who hates writing. The material was interesting though I will say the readings were pretty lengthy but you can easily get away with just skimming them. I could not recommend this class enough if you need a gen-ed!.

Dr. Fivecoate is such a kind and down-to-earth professor that clearly has a passion for his field of study. I had never taken a folklore class but now I can explain the importance of folktales in the study of folklore. A very theory-heavy class but still fascinating. He does a great job conveying complex concepts in digestible ways!

Professor Fivecoate was one of the best professors i've had.He was so nice and welcoming to everyone and was so happy to help with questions at any point of the course.If you needed an extension due to an outside commitment he was always happy to work with you.The course was informative and well structured.I would definitely take this class again.

Finishing up FOLK424 now and really enjoyed this class. We covered a lot of content, but it was very interesting and the assignments were all papers which were straightforward and engaging. Dr. Fivecoate is great--kind, knowledgeable, and cares about your success!
Such a kind and considerate teacher. Could not recommend him more. He grades very reasonably and treats everyone with dignity. Learned a lot too!

Dr. Fivecoate is an incredible professor! I am currently wrapping up my semester in his FOLK 424 course, and it has become one of my favorite parts of my day. Highly recommend this class as the subject is very interesting and the class is easy and fun, with the final paper being a bit long but with ample time to work through over multiple classes

Jesse Fivecoate is by far the most kind and respectful professor I have had at UNC. There are a few papers with very clear grading criteria. I am currently taking FOLK 424 and have learned so much and will most likely receive an A. I am already looking at another class to take with Professor Fivecoate. PLEASE take a class with him.

Dr. Fivecoate and the TAs for this course were kind but FOLK 202 itself was a bit silly for a gen ed because of the required attendance for pop quizzes and the evolving grading criteria; however, they were super accommodating and its mostly just inconvenient/tedious not at all hard though

Dr. Fivecoate and his TAs were very nice, but there was poor communication with students (no rubric for the final paper until less than one week before it was due). The pop quizzes were poorly timed/annoyingly specific and many of the readings were often long/repetitive. The lectures were interesting, but this class was not worth the stress.

I wouldn't recommend taking his class for a gen ed, there are plenty easier options. The 10 pop quizzes made lecture mandatory, and recitations were waste of time. ta's grading is arbitrary – sometimes they're easy & sometimes they're very harsh. there is an online midterm and final that you need to have detailed notes for, but are open note.

Mandatory attendance because of 10 pop quizzes over the course of the semester. Exams were just mindless regurgitations of the in class slides, so hopefully you didn't miss any classes. Seemed like a nice guy but the course material is just stuff that academics made up (a self licking ice cream cone if you will).

Actual lectures were interesting and Fivecoate developed the class in a manner that made it so. However, do be prepared to read plenty for recitation sections. Not mandatory participation, but random pop quizzes were given to encourage attendance. Relatively easy, biggest problems w/ grading I ran into were with the TA.

Great lectures, really interesting topics. There are quizzes, but if you show up and take notes, they're doable. Recitations are led by TAs who I think may also do the grading, so not sure if Prof Fivecoate is a hard or easy grader himself... still, it's a good class, and he seems to be a nice and caring prof!

There were 10 pop quizzes (multiple choice + short answer)in the class, an online midterm and a large paper, a small essay, for me the professor was a very kind person, he also has a deep study of American folklore, there is quite a lot of reading material but you will get a good grade if you read all of it.

1) inconsistent pop quizzes with variable formats, you can never be sure if you are actually prepared. 2) recitation is a waste 3) class material without trigger warnings!! we had to watch videos about murders and listen to horror stories, but attendance is mandatory bc of pop quizzes! beware! 4. weird subject material, literally wtf is folklore
VERY tough grader and directions made no sense.

Very tough grader. I never got an 100% on any of my assignments. I was carried solely by the final exam, which I studied VERY hard for. Copy all of her notes and do the chapter questions, and you will be okay.

She is dedicated to what she does and is strict with her syllabus/rubrics. Her exams are hard, however she gives a study guide for both the midterm and the final. Just study and actually listen to her advice on how to pass her class if you want a good grade. Overall, she's a good teacher and you will pass as long as you work hard.

Classwork and homework aren't bad, but if you want to do good on exams, make sure to read the textbook and really have a good understanding of material. Projects can be a bit tough, but typically she follows the rubric so just follow that and you should be good.

Don't get me wrong, she is very nice and is willing to work with you. Most of the time she will talk about one or two topics the whole lecture and will talk about them in great detail. However, when it comes time to the test, most of the material is based off the textbook as a whole and not much of what she actually talks about.

Professor Rocker (or Doc Rock as she likes to be called) is a pretty good professor. She grades hard but in a way that holds people accountable to a high standard that she clearly outlines for each assignment. She lectures well from a book if you do the reading and keeps up with a class, you should have little to no problems with anything.
She's an amazing professor! Her lectures are so engaging and the content we learn is so interesting. I really enjoyed this class. Recitations aren't bad at all, just make sure you do the readings.

Go to lectures, she appreciates students attending, and overall such a more engaging experience. She is charismatic and really just a wonderful professor. Honest and very well-versed. Passionate above all. Highly recommend
Great professor, boring class, Didn't attend or watch a single lecture, just study lectures and reading and you will be fine. Grading is heavily dependent on TA's though, pray you get a good one

I wasn't a personal fan of her lecture style, it was hard to stay engaged when I did go. It didn't help that it  was an optional 5pm lecture.. if you won't force yourself to go it might not be the class for you. Tests were very specific in the short answers... read ALL the material. TA didn't grade ANY of our assignments until after the exam.

Pretty interesting class. TAs grade leniently for assignments (just follow directions). Even though its easy, exams can be a bit specific when asking about the material. Best way to study is to find a friend and talk through all the disc q's covered for the unit. Dr. Rivkin-Fish is very nice and accommodating!

This is the 2nd class I have taken with her and she is an amazing professor who cares about her students and provides engaging, passionate lectures. It is relatively easy, but you definitely need to be prepared to do all the readings and know the terms for each exam. If you can understand and remember the analysis of the readings you will do well.
Loved this class. Super interesting and the class was chill, exams are chill if u do all the readings and watch the films. Fw Fish fr
Lots of reading, but incredible lectures!!!

Very easy and manageable class. Tests are designed to be doable. Lots of reading assignments but a manageable amount of work. Reading responses and recitation are annoying but chill. Lectures are optional and recorded.

Super interesting class, a great lecturer, and the exams were very fair and reasonable. Lecture is optional and they are posted online, but you should go because they never run over 45 minutes in length, and they are super interesting.

Don't use her IDST class reviews to sum her up as a professor. ANTH 147 with Dr. Rivkin-Fish has been my favorite, most eye-opening class this semester. As long as you do the readings, the assignments and exams are completely manageable. Lectures are recorded and only recitations are mandatory. She's very caring and knowledgable. No regrets!

I am currently in this class and I have made above a 90 on both midterms. Rivkin-Fish is an excellent professor who truly cares about her students. Attendance is not mandatory, however, make sure to keep up with the recordings and readings. There is a lot of readings but the midterm focuses on the concepts. tip: KEEP UP WITH READINGS AND LECTURES

I am saddened that Professor Rivkin-Fish's association with the terrible gen-ed that is IDST has given her a lower reputation. She is a phenomenal lecturer and an incredibly insightful person. The way she formulates her words is so thoughtful and expresses a deep level of reflection. The course itself was very easy as long as you did your readings!

Rating for all 3 teachers here. Class itself is manageable in terms of readings and class structure. There are reading quizzes each week that are simple and a few lowest scores are dropped. Midterm and final were literally based off the guide provided. There were some issues with grading throughout the semester, but emailing the teachers fixed it.

Prof. Rivkin-Fish was a good professor in a badly formatted class- all three of the professors for this class were kind and caring with students, but the class style is just not good in general. Her lectures were interesting and she LOVED hearing students' perspectives.
she was the best out of the 3 tripleI teachers. lectures made sense, she was nice and not passive aggressive. however still boring. the class itself was a joke, but easier than others.

She was the best of the three professors for this Triple-I. Her lecture content was the most interesting, and she seemed like the kindest. My biggest problem with this class is that you couldn't tell what you were supposed to take away from lectures and readings. Not a hard T-I though, you won't have to give too much effort, just do the readings.
Worst Triple I ever!! do not ever take, it is the hardest one out there and the professors are super boring. Attendance is mandatory and the TA grades harsh.

Overall, the class was quite boring, but one of the better Triple-I's. She was my favorite of the three professors, but mostly bc the anthropology side of the course was the most interesting. She tries to connect with students and is available for office hours. The class was mostly participatory with a mid-term, final, and a large group project.
Lectures were extremely boring and unorganized. The entire teaching team was always talking over each other. Definitely not a fun class, but probably one of the easier triple i's.

Dr. Hoke was a super interesting lecturer and taught me a lot of perspectives that I had never considered before. Attendance is key even though it isn't mandatory because a lot of key concepts are not on the slides. So many extra credit opportunities, not an easy A but hard work is definitely rewarded. First recitation I've actually enjoyed.
Dr. Hoke is awesome! learned so much in this class, definitely do all the extra credit. She's funny and personable, no complaints.

Great prof and great class! Probably would be an easy A, but I was a tryhard since I enjoyed the content lol. Hoke is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, so even though attendance isn't required it was fun to attend. Lots of extra credit, toughish (got an 82) midterm and easy (got a 96) final. Highly recommend!

This is a RESEARCH class, The majority of the grade is writing your final research paper/unpaper. Lecture was SOO interesting however. I had not learned so many concepts in an ANTH class as I did with her. She is also so likable. Recitation IS mandatory, but I enjoyed it. Go to lecture and take good notes you will do fine.
Altogether intriguing class with a lot of projects.

If you're looking for a gen ed this one isn't so bad. There are class readings but you can easily get by without reading a single one. Professor Hoke is pretty outgoing and engages with the class which I thought was cool. None of the assignments are too difficult.
Amazing person and professor. Anth 204 was a genuinely interesting and thought-provoking class.

Really interesting lectures made coming to class a nice experience, and extra credit didn't hurt either. The midterm was hard, but I feel the ethnography project and presentation were graded easily, so it all works out.

Dr. Hoke is very passionate about what she is teaching, and a lot of information is shared during class. While attendance is not mandatory, if you go and pay attention, you'll be fine. She gives extra credit out ALL the time. This class was very interesting for me, just had a lot of unnecessary assignments and readings. The midterm was kinda crazy.
not the easiest gen ed of all time. if you are looking for an easy A look elsewhere

Professor Hoke is a solid, caring, and funny professor. There are two projects, and there is a recitation grade to buffer. She had one midterm, and one noncumulative final, that were decently challenging. She says a lot of information verbally that's not on the slides, so you definitely have to pay attention, but there were no surprises!
lectures were lowkey boring but easy to comprehend and definitely didn't need to do the readings

Dr. Hoke was amazing! The class was very interesting and her lectures were very on topic. Her exams were fairly easy, multiple choice and written response but easy grading on the written response. The topics in the class were so interesting and fun to learn about. Going to class is not mandatory but beneficial for pop up extra credit opportunities!

Dr. Hoke was not only an engaging and knowledgeable lecturer, but a kind person. She puts her students first and is more than willing to work with extenuating circumstances. Tests are multiple choice, true/false, and have 1-2 written response questions. Lecture was optional, but consistently full. Always looked to provide extra credit for students.

If you go to class you should get an A. You don't actually have to read any of the assigned readings as long as you are engaged in class. Dr. Hoke also has a pretty cool personality so it's easy to stay engaged.

I went through a lot health wise this semester with things just feeling like it was continuously piling on. In all honesty, she was wonderful and helped me feel like I had a fair chance to be successful in her class. Attendance is mandatory and about 15% of the grade but gives chances for extra credit. I would love to take her courses again!

I love Dr. Hoke! She is incredible at lecturing, is personable and teaches unique and interesting content. Her grading criteria can be whack, and feels unfair at times, but overall this class is in the middle of the road difficulty wise. Few assignments and the midterm was fair but challenging. Wish I could take her to grad school with me!

Dr. Hoke is an excellent professor who lectures passionately about the course material in a simple, accessible way. She is super funny and kind, and the class is entertaining and easy as long as you show up and do your part (reading and attending class)! She wants everyone to learn and succeed, but won't give you free points if you don't care.

I really enjoyed this class and Dr. Hoke was a great lecturer! The grading and rubrics were a bit unclear, but the grading was fair and the TAs were able to provide a good outline for assignments. This wasn't a difficult class, just a bit unorganized because it was new this semester. The class was really interesting and pretty relaxed.

Dr. Hoke is one of my favorite professors at UNC! I learned a LOT in ANTH 190. She doesn't grade lightly, but for most major projects she has you submit initial drafts/outlines that she provides very detailed feedback on. Dr. Hoke is direct about expectations, and treats every student with a high level of respect.

*ANTHRO 364*
I loved this class. Dr. Dorsey teaches us about professional development as an Anthropologist, and I still use the notes I took in her class to this day.

Love her! One of the best professors at UMass. Her classes and lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Provides slides before class. She does have a lot of readings but only a few of them are compulsory reads. Fairly easy midterm and final. One final project, 2 other projects and a few Course Reflections.
Dr. Dorsey is a great lecturer and a very kind professor. I would highly recommend her classes, especially Anthropology 313 (Nutritional Anthropology).

Professor Dorsey was one of the best professors I had at UMass. She makes learning content fun and super interesting. I have a lot of respect for her. Take a class with her! You'll learn so much without being overwhelmed, and she's always willing to help if you need it.
amazing 10/10 recommend her

Need to do every reading and a discussion post after - not bad. He's a pretty disorganized person; lecture slides repeat lots of info, he jumps around between content/slides, not much communication between him and TA's. Group project is a huge part of the course - it's not bad unless you have a bad group member or two.

He is very kind, however very disorganized. It surprises me that he has been teaching for a while as it seemed that he was figuring out how to do everything as it were the first time. He asked us how many questions should be on the test... There was also a lot of miscommunication between him, the TA's and us. Also, be prepared for a group project.

Your grade in this class is heavily dependent on your project group. Do not procrastinate on the research paper; it is a high percentage of your grade. Exams were MCQ and short answer, study guides were provided. Attendance is through check ins at random points of the lecture. Lots of readings throuhgout and reading response due before every class.
genuinely he is my arch nemesis and the worst professor at unc
I LOVE HIM! HE CAN DO NO WRONG.

You will probably pass this class if you don't go to class but definitely  go to recitation due to a large group project. Lectures are a bit boring but the info is cool. Sometimes we just watched videos/documentaries and had to submit notes. Attendance isn't mandatory but does do random check ins that go towards your participation grade.

Mark was ok -- very passionate about the subject and lectures were long and rambly. Graded by only a couple things and if your recitation group is bad, sucks to be you. TA's are extremely hit or miss -- mine would take points off for no reason (???) Grading criteria overall is pretty vague.

Pretty easy-going and an easy class overall. Recitation projects are graded weirdly but that's more on the TA than Prof. Sorensen. His tests were open-note in class and he basically gives you the questions beforehand on the study guide. Honestly a pretty easy A. I just went to lectures for the attendance points and did other homework.

PROFESSOR SORENSEN IS THE SWEETEST PERSON EVER!!!!! His lectures were engaging and interesting and attendance is optional! Very fair grader and accessible out of class. Added the Med Anth major because of him/this class :)

Professor Sorensen was amazing! He was very passionate about the course content and that showed in his lectures, which I found very interesting. Not a lot of work, just some weekly discussion posts, 2 required (short) essays, and a few group projects in recitation. I really recommend you take a class with prof Sorensen at some point!

Professor Sorensen is so kind and I really enjoyed his lectures and their content. The only frustrating parts were that grading on the tests was inconsistent, but they gave extra credit and it ended up being fine. The group project is long, but since it is done in sections it is less overwhelming. Beware, he does random attendance checks.

HATED this class. I got put with a BAD group for my final project and my grade suffered. Exams were open note and the TA's graded them very poorly and I received little to no feedback when I reached out for answers. Recitation was a major waste of time although they were not weekly and little to no learning was done & were always very off topic.

Dr. Sorensen is my favorite professor I have had at UNC.  He really cares about his class, the readings are interesting and are accompanied with easy short reading responses due before each class, and there is a group project (which is annoying if you get stuck with a bad group but is turned in in chunks so it wasn't too bad).  Highly recommend!

Even though it is a loooot of reading, Sorensen is a great lecturer and is good at answering questions. Like most of the anth professors, he's a little unorganized, but it can easily be overlooked because he seems to genuinely care about his students and takes passion in his work.

The tests were scary as a humanities person, but they really weren't very bio heavy, focused more on applying concepts. The readings were very interesting and he was great at leading engaging discussions despite the huge class size. The group project being a major part of the grade was a pain, but the assignment itself was well paced.

Prof Sorenson was super kind and knowledgeable about medical anthropology. I didn't enjoy all the group projects in this class, but I looked forward to attending the class lectures, which were super interesting and chill.

If you attend class and pay attention to lectures you should not have a problem with this course. Lectures tended to be long and occasionally boring and topics were far and wide but everything related to the common theme by the end of the semester. Exams are written responses and are not difficult if you understand the concepts discussed in class.
his lectures always had tangents but they related and added to the overall experience. very passionate and knowledgeable.

Prof. Sorenson is very knowledgeable on his subject matter. Lectures are informative, TAKE NOTES!!!! Final & midterms are open note, so good (digital) notes are crucial for quick info finding. Ask questions, sit in front and he'll remember you. Recitation groups make up big projects and are sometimes harsh graders. Not good office hours.
nice guy but very disorganized

Professor Snively cares about her students, is sweet, and remembers names. She catered food for final review and baked sweets for midterm review. The class is graded on 2 exams, a quiz, HW, and attendance. The quiz is easy while the exams are tough so don't let the quiz grade gas you up. One complaint is the lectures for the final weren't as good.

I don't know what to say about her. She is the GOAT. She gave so much extra credit to save our grade. Just do your study and you will be fine. Test was easy and straight forward. She also made the final exam very doable.
Tanja is very nice but nothing really makes sense when she teaches the course concepts. Before exams I tended to have to self-teach to prepare.

shes amazing and will help you with anything. Protip: instead of buying the textbook get the 2 week free trial and knock out the homework questions since she opens all of them at the start. You get a flashcard for the midterm and final. Before exams, just go through all the slides and make sure you know how to solve everything.

Tanja is super caring and made the class easy. Had a lot going on and she understood. Course itself isn't bad at all, I think there was a big curve on the final grade. Can't go wrong in 407 with Tanja, just go to class and listen!

Tanja is amazing. The content can be hard at times and can go pretty fast but she makes her slides available and has practice exams that completely lay out what her expectations are for the exams. Quiz 1 is straightforward but the midterm was sneakily hard so don't let the first grade get you too comfortable. Such a kind person. Highly recommend.

Professor Snively is a very nice, caring, and knowledgable professor for 407. She made the class engaging and interesting, and I enjoyed the course. I would recommend taking 407 with her strongly. There are hw assignments, 2 midterms, and a final. I felt prepared for all of them
Take 407 with Tanja! She is so supportive and hilarious. I found accounting particularly boring but she makes each class interesting!

Tanja is the best Professor I have had at the business school so far. BUSI 407 is known to be a difficult course, but she made it so much better. Not only is she a great Professor, but she is super caring and understanding. I can't imagine taking 407 with any other Professor. I could not recommend her more!
Tanja is amazing. She's so personable and takes her time explaining the material. Accounting is hard but she doesn't make it any harder than it already is. Couldn't recommend her more!

She is literally the best professor I've had. She is so caring, explains everything clear, and we had extra credit. The mean for our exams was a 86ish. Accounting is usually hard, but she is a gem that teaches it sooo well. She also baked for us & caters food for review sessions. I actually love her. If you finish with around a 90ish it's an A.

This class is ridiculously hard but it's just the material that sucks. Tanja is amazing and I wouldn't take it with anyone else. She gives homework but you have unlimited attempts and hints and I got a 100 on all of them. She makes the class as fun as possible. Super understanding abt extensions. Just DONT GET BEHIND. IT WILL BE MISERABLE IF YOU DO

Best prof I've had at UNC. Tanja is so kind and cares deeply for her students. She is super engaging (hard for accounting) and is great with answering questions. Very available outside of class. If you study for the quiz and exam, you'll be fine in the class. Just make sure you go to lecture. Take 407 with Tanja.

Tanja is so sweet and is a much better accounting teacher than the other 407 prof. I got a B+ because I bombed the final but it was completely my fault. If you do all the homework and study for the quiz & 2 exams you will get an A. She bakes for the class & cares about her students a ton. Tell her if you're an athlete because she'll love it.

One of my favorite professors! Always available to help, grades promptly, and is super caring. Her exams are easy enough if you pay attention and use the resources available. She baked for us multiple times throughout the semester which was very sweet of her and she made class fun (which is kind of hard for an accounting class). Highly recommend :)

Super great and easily accessible for help. Sweetheart of a professor and baked us food multiple times. Class isn't terribly hard. Did alright on the midterm, quiz, and final and managed to get an A. She's def looking to help you out as much as she can so a few days of studying for the final and you can get a good grade. Highly recommend taking her

Avoid at all costs! Has no clear grading criteria, and just basically assigns a B to any work you turn in. Doesn't provide any guidance - just expects you to know what she is expecting. Also is disrespectful to students, and spends all class talking about all the "experience" she has in the field.

This absolute queen. I am baffled at how negative the reviews are - I adored Professor Mahin and this class! The lessons shifted based on current events, and the activities were engaging. And to people dissing her for mentioning she won Emmys, I would say she didn't mention it enough because I think that's really awesome.
Dr. Mahin was an incredible professor with amazing connections, many of which she brought to class to speak. She's a tough grader, but you can tell it's because she wants you to be successful.

the class is pretty much fully discussion-based and there's so much reading. she's a tough grader and not flexible with deadlines. She's nice but the class felt like she was just watching the students discuss and figure everything out while she sat there.

Also, Professor Mahin will demand you call her "doctor" or "professor" at all times. There are so many more modest, respectful, actually intelligent folks in the building who don't demand the same. Egotripping all class. There's a reason she doesn't get paid close to the amount of a finance professor.

Professor Mahin is a terrible lecturer who does not know what she's talking about. She likes to crow about her previous experience, but she has very little real-world experience in a position that requires any semblance of intellect. A glorified shell of a PR professor who likes to pretend her Emmy is remotely hard to get (literally local Emmy lmao

No matter how hard you try or how little you try on each paper you will get a B. She told us on the first day of class that a B in her class is an A in any other class, which is wild because some people are taking Biomedical Engineering and getting A's and we are struggling to get an A in a class about writing different types of emails.
Tough and arbitrary grader, avoid at all costs.

She is definitely not a monster, I would say she is a genuine nice person. However, she's a very tough grader and not flexible time wise. Lots of readings and quizzes. No midterms, only papers and presentations but it is still a lot of work. I have learnt a lot from this class but could've done it only with the readings.

After reading these reviews, I thought Professor Mahin would be difficult. She does assign a lot of readings, but she is caring, extremely intelligent, and very well-spoken. I thoroughly enjoyed the class. The negative reviews are most likely due to the fact that 401 in general is an either liked or hated class.

Good enough teacher and a strong lecturer but you really can't overcome her arbitrary grading policies. If you need an A in this class don't take it with her, because she guarantees you won't get it on the first day.

takes forever to grade things in the latter half of the sem. Participation is key to getting an A versus A-. Midterm and final are straight from the slides in class, memorize them as you go. Group project is fun, get a good group though.

Dr. Long is very kind and caring for students. The lectures were kinda boring, but she would include activities to make content more fun. Midterm and final were easy enough. My only gripe is that she didn't grade anything until after finals, which sucked because it would've been nice to know what our grades were throughout the semester.

This class was extremely disappointing. Every single class, without fail, included long lectures and writing a laundry list of ideas on the white board. Everything seems very basic/simple yet the exam was simply rote memory of theory which I felt was not applicable or realistic to organizations/teams. I dreaded coming to this class. :(

Professor Long is a standout to me. She is one of the kindest and most caring professors you could ever have. She is understanding as long as you send an email or talk to her about a problem. Remembering to do her small assignments can be a struggle but she does remind you at the end of each class. Brought snacks on exam days and LDOC.

Long is incredibly caring. My only gripe is that she doesn't release due dates for assignments on her syllabus so you have to keep up with her Canvas to see if assignments pop up. She has a group project where you fundraise which is cool but tedious. She is not a fast grader or email responder, but she truly is lovely!
Lectured most days and overall just fine. Lots of busywork that he thought would help with the final project, but just graded super strictly and was redundant.
He was fine, just a touch boring. Class had a odd grading system.

Lectures are a bit boring, but you have to pay attention as he asks a lot of lecture-specific questions on exams. He's a little nit-picky when grading assignments so really try on those too, overall exams are not hard as long as you pay attention in class and DO THE READINGS (don't save for the end read them as you go)

Lect so boring bc of his voice- he admits it but it's so hard to be interested in this class. Exams are all MC but they had some cop-out questions that you needed to be SUPER engaged in class to remember the answer. Too easy to mess your grade up, which is stressful for students applying to the B school. DONT TAKE if you aren't applying to B school

I took the course with him in Spring 2025. I liked him, but I thought he seemed uncomfortable at the front of the room (odd for a business professor in my opinion). This made the lectures dull and sometimes a little hard to follow. That aside, he lays out the course very well and assignments are clear-cut. Grading can be strict, so take your time.

Great guy who wants his students to succeed. Super accessible despite large class. Do the work, pay attention, and study a bit before tests and you'll do great. Was very clear in terms of assignment expectations.
He is great, kind of a boring lecturer but genuinely cares about his students. An easy class if you come to class and take the assignments seriously (40% of your grade).

Not a very difficult class unless you make it one. Market games can be tricky depending on your groupmates. If you do the readings and review lectures before exams, you will be fine. Mittelstadt can be a bit "dull" in his lectures, but otherwise is a good prof for a fairly unstructured class. Feels more like a 3-4 credit class rather than 1.5

The class is so unstructured, and Mittelstadt doesn't help much. Can't blame him, but he doesn't bring any passion to the class, which makes it very hard to pay attention. They ask the most niche things in tsets, which makes tests really hard.

Easy class where you learn nothing. All he does is assign readings loosely related to business and tests on those. He has zero sense of urgency when it comes to grading. Tests are taken on a scantron where grading should take a couple days max, but he takes weeks.

Learned so much from this class, basically got a job from it. Good enough lecturer, great course content. Is a very picky grader for no reason, really had to try and get inside his head to get a good grade. Requires lots of participation.

Professor Mittelstadt isn't bad, this is more a reflection of BUSI100 at UNC. Very unstructured class, weekly readings and assignments, but lecture is confusing and doesn't make sense half the time. PAY ATTENTION IN LECTURE, the midterm and final bring up random things talked about during lecture. Overall, just a mid class and professor.

Busi 100 is a very structured class and the prof had no real control over the content. I found him a bit boring, and when re-watching Panopto videos, I found he explained things more clearly in the morning sections. Also, you have to know niche facts, he says during class. But he says a lot of random things, so u don't know what will be on the test
Lectures were a little boring. But the content was easy to understand, and lots of quizlets are available to help.

Outstanding guy, really cares about the course subject and his students. He does grade fairly strict on the weekly(ish) assignments, but still my lowest grade on an assignment was probably an 84. Midterm is 20% open note, open internet. Participation is 20% of your grade, just talk, and he will write your name down for credit. Final project is fun.

Professor Mittelstadt is super passionate about what he does - very connected in the triangle and will help you out if you put in the work. Class is difficult, and the grading criteria are vague. He loves to do in-class group assignments, and his lectures are monotonous. If you're interested in sustainability, just do the work and you'll do ok.

Jeff is a nice guy but is not a good lecturer. He is extremely boring and didn't give all of the formulas needed for the exams. The exams weren't hard but you have to know super random facts he mentioned one time during lecture. If you have a choice take Hendricks, but the class is extremely easy either way.

He is not a bad professor but it really showed that this was his first year teaching. Also, I don't understand how I got a 70% as my participation grade if I went to every single class and market games. Midterm/Final was easy and scored 90s on both. My business major groupmates must've sabotaged my participation grade so that they get a curve.

Don't take this class. Thought sustainability would be interesting, but it's impossible for it to be interesting when he constantly drowns you with lengthy assignments. The lectures are fairly boring, each class has a group assignment, and the homework each take like two hours and he grades them extremely harshly. He does love sustainability, tho!

He is liked and does everything right on the surface but I still absolutely hated the class. I care a lot about sustainability so this should be the most important class but I feel like I left the class without any real knowledge. He just gives you a million frameworks and makes you right 1 page docs every week applying them but its all BSed.

Chip is a really nice guy with a wealth of knowledge. My greatest challenge was contending with the flipped classroom format. He provides great overviews of the chapters to the point where I didn't even need to read the textbook (I watched the asynchronous and synchronous recordings). The group projects can be difficult.

Super nice guy. It is very easy to be successful in this class. It's true that he doesn't accept late work but I'm not sure why people are complaining about this. It's college, what do you expect? Final project takes some time but is built off homework assignments throughout the semester. Would definitely recommend taking this class

No attendance needed. Only about 1-2 hours per week for assignments, easy 70/70. Final project can be long, but very depending on some previous assignments. Take the course easily like some desserts and enjoy Chip's show. He's experienced and funny.
Ego maniac. Could not care less about his students. Avoid at all costs.

Such a chiller. No midterms or final, your grade is 70% homework and 30% a final project. Attendance is not mandatory but you should go because he is super insightful and the content is very useful. Final project is tedious but if you space it out it's not too bad. Chip is also such a nice guy and makes the lectures engaging.

I got pneumonia for a month in my first month of class for the semester. He refused to let me turn in anything late and ultimately wound up burning out. While the class itself was useful, the teacher was very uncompromising, and considering I had gone to the hospital twice, I expected some leeway or understanding. Unfortunately, none was given.

Professor Snively is an awesome dude. This class is honestly super easy but can also be super beneficial depending on your financial literacy status- which a lot of students lack in that subject matter. He is very lecture heavy and sometimes they drag, but show up and occasionally recieve and extra credit attendance point. Cool dude & good teacher.

Nice professor and interesting concepts, but the final was extremely unfair. Averages were in the low 60s, no one scored 100, and it counted heavily. The problems couldn't realistically be solved in the time given, making it impossible to answer all the questions.
Easy class, no attendance required, all assignments for completion. Long project for the final, but it is doable. I would take it again; he really does go over some useful stuff.

If you put in the work and effort, you can learn so much from Chip. His lectures are very informative and rather efficient, and having one online class a week that is prerecorded makes the class very flexible. The tests are really hard, but that's just how 408 is. He is great to talk to outside of class and really cares about his students.

BUSI 286 is super easy, would recommend if you need an elective. Only caveat is that you cannot by any reason turn anything late. Attendance to lectures is optional and unnecessary but gives you extra credit. Last project is tedious would start on that a week before but other than that super chill class. Professor not that chill of a guy however.

Easy A class if you stay engaged with the weekly homework. There are extra credit points available for attending class, but attendance is not actually required. Comprehensive, but doable, final project at the end. This course should be required as part of the general education curriculum at UNC, as the content is extremely useful for real life.
He is actually very helpful for personal finance if you're interested. Don't take the 8am or getting those extra cred points will be difficult.

Homework assignments are pretty much completion grades. Attendance isn't mandatory but you can get extra credit from it. Final project is a pretty long and tedious but there's a couple checkpoints along to way to help. Be careful because he apparently does not accept ANY late work. But I barely went to class and still got an A so I can't complain!
Easy A for sure....

Only one class a week with weekly hw (for completion) with two group projects (first one is really comprehensive) and they aren't graded harshly. Chip made lectures engaging and is knowledgable about finance. His tests are difficult with averages being 81 and 67 for MT/Final. He said he applied decent curve at the end of our class.

This class was very insightful! Chip is chill and has a lot of fun stories about finance.  Class consisted of many hw's and project.  Project's long 30% of grade, but not hard to complete.  HW's are simple/graded on completion/effort.  Attendance not required but can get EC on some days if you show up.  Great class if preparing for post-grad world.
Great nonmajor class for learning personal finance and not demanding at all. Snively is very approachable and makes learning easy!

People will complain about Chip, but if you really want to learn the basics of finance, he is the professor to take. The test are difficult but I felt well prepared with the lectures and provided material. I found his lectures very informative and interesting. I recommend his class if you are serious about finance.

If you have to take 408, do not take this class with Chip. He makes this class so much harder than necessary. Your grade is based on a midterm and final (worth 65% of the grade) and 2 group projects. There is homework every week (some taking several hours), but is graded for completion. He holds office hours but helps very little.
Great professor, good material.

Very nice professor, but you need to show up to class and actively participate to get participation points. Super nice and caring professor; the exams were moderate, so make sure to study. Very engaging class though! I learned a lot, even though I'm not a business major.

I really liked this class and enjoyed the content and he is a good lecturer that makes the class entertaining even as a morning class. Grading was standard and you can do discussion points to bump your grade. Group project was fine but time consuming, but less stressful class.

I highly recommend taking negotiations if you need 1.5 elective credits. The class was interesting and in-class group exercises kept lectures interesting. Petsko himself was quite nice, had clear grading criteria and was a good lecturer. He let you out early once done with lectures, but was kind of a tough grader. Overall good experience.

Nicest professor. Classes are super engaging. Had a final project and final exam which kinda sucked but takes weight off the final. Exams are tricky, multiple choice. Participation def matters but not hard to speak a few times each class.

Great guy, super nice. Content is easy (at least you think it is) but then the tests are somehow so hard. You are tested on motivation and things you already know but they make it impossible. Not much hw tho.

Dr. Petsko was an incredible professor who made lectures interesting and engaging. Provided tons of resources and clearly wants his students to succeed. Lectures and homework were easy, attendance is taken every day and participation matters. Tests were a lot harder than the general class, but the best professor you could take 405 with.

Professor Petsko is a fantastic professor. He makes a clear attempt to connect with his students and is super reasonable and accommodating. He gives lectures using slides and has an engaging activity planned for almost every class. I would absolutely recommend taking 405 with Petsko.

I got a B, unfortunately, but Dr. Petsko is clearly knowledgeable and a passionate professor that knows the topic well. I thoroughly enjoyed the lectures and in-class activities that applied to the workplace. The grading is clear. Make sure to participate a lot. Tests are tricky even with ample studying.

Great professor. You can tell he is passionate about the topic and cares for his students. The content itself isn't that difficult to understand, although I thought some of the exam questions were confusing. Must participate in class and he does take attendance every day. Overall good experience

Professor Petsko did an awesome job with this class. Even it was lecture-based, he found ways to include interesting activities and examples that demonstrated the topic and kept the class interesting. I went into the class with no expectations, but I actually really liked the material because of the way he taught it. Take 405 with him if you can!
Petsko is one of my favorite professors. He is passionate about what he is teaching and it makes going to class enjoyable. I would love to take a class with him again.

Petsko was absolutely fantastic. I've never been so engaged in a class and actually excited to learn class material, and all of the credit for that goes to him. Such an awesome guy who's very approachable and shows that he'd be down to talk about literally anything. Grading is very fair, just go to class and study for exams and you'll do well.

The most disorganized professor I've ever had. Already have had multiple assignments with due dates that weren't properly communicated or adjusted, even though she said they'd be moved. She's super entertaining, caring, and a fun person, but for someone teaching business communications, you'd think she would communicate more.

I honestly did not know how to rate Dr. Boyer; she's an incredible person who deeply cares for her students and is extremely reasonable. However, she is disorganized and often very behind in getting back grades to students, and in this particular class, grades are very harshly-like all other 401 professors. I would recommend taking it with her!

She's funny and makes classes engaging. Hard to get an A, her grading criteria is very unclear at times and the feedback is not great either - sometimes even contradictory. 401 kinda sucks in general, so among the options I think she's one of the best to at least have a fun time. Just accept you will prob get an A- even if you try really hard.

Despite her slightly disorganized nature, this is the second course I have taken with Dr. Boyer. Her grading criteria is unclear and assignment deadlines and metrics often are changed, but she is truly hilarious and a caring professor. If you are looking for a laugh and a genuine connection, and are willing to work with her, take the class!

Boyer's cool and a great lecturer who made class engaging. That being said, she is so nitpicky when it comes to grading. You can clearly do everything on the rubric but she'll take off ten points for no reason. I guess that's just 401. Also all her assignments are written/graded by AI which is pretty annoying since it leads to unclear guidelines.

Difficult to get an A, A- didn't require much effort, but that's honestly just BUSI 401. Discussion based class with lots of small group work and in-class activities that aren't graded. Assignments were applicable and didn't take too long. They're graded harshly, but again that's just 401. Interesting lecturer, and I actually enjoyed going to class

Fun class but disorganized and expectations are unclear. Assignment guidelines would change right before they were due which caused a lot of time to be wasted. Finished the mod a couple weeks ago and still haven't gotten any grades back. Seems like one of the easier electives though in terms of workload.
Impossible to get an A, also incredibly unresponsive to emails or feedback
SUPER hard grader, impossible to get an A in this class. Seems to be the same with all professors though. She was funny and each class was interesting. She did not provide clear rubrics or criteria.

She's really nice, but wow is she a harsh grader. This is an email writing and presentation class, and she will nitpick you on the smallest things. Honestly though, no 401 professor will hand out A's, so go ahead and take her.

Lori has a super over the top personality. She makes class fun and engaging. She does grade things tough but all the assignments were super easy so if you put a little bit of effort in you are guaranteed a B. Be prepared for class to be a big group discussion every day.

Professor Boyer is a very engaging and funny lecturer but as other people have said her grading is needlessly harsh. Her harsh grading made this class more stressful and difficult than it needed to be when looking at the actual subject matter. Good person, bad pedagogy.

This is the first teacher throughout my time at UNC I would 100% not recommend to any student. I'm certain Professor Boyer is a wonderful woman outside of academics, but I can't appreciate her grading. It takes weeks for her to give feedback and when I tried speaking with her about the criteria, she was always unwilling or unresponsive.

Dr. Boyer was hard to reach outside of class, but she was a very easy grader and the material was interesting. She cold calls a lot to facilitate discussion in the beginning of the semester. One discussion post, 2 presentations, a midterm, and an easy final assignment.

Professor Boyer is super nice and caring and can be really fun in class, but she is the absolute worst about grading criteria and giving back grades. The grades seem arbitrary with little feedback and they aren't given back for months. I didn't know my grade for this class until over 2 weeks after the class ended, and we didn't even have a final.

Grading is awful. She assigns so much busy work and then grades harshly. Takes forever to give feedback on assignments and will find the tiniest issues even if you followed the rubric closely. On projects she gave everyone the same grade. At times it felt like she had unrealistic expectations while simultaneously treating us like children.

You will breeze through this class all semester until the end. She gives everyone the same grade on everything until after evaluations are due. She went through and changed all my grades. I thought I was chilling, but then found out I was not. Harsh grader and unforgiving for mistakes. Seems like a cool person but will screw you over for no reason
Professor Boyer is a nice person, but she is unforgiving and a harsh grader. I would recommend taking BUSI 401 with someone else if you want a good grade.

Professor Boyer's only weakness is her lack of communication which is odd given that this is a communications class. He class is fun, and there is usually no homework but she will grade you harshly for things she never taught you.
She extremely energetic and fun loving, only downside is that she is a tough grader. But 401 has a bunch of filler assignments which helps you get a good grade. Would definitely take her.

Jeff was fine, but the class is a little annoying. The group project is a large portion of the grade and the criteria is vague. Assignments are a little unclear and exams are based largely off of accounting formulas and readings as opposed to what's covered in class.

BUSI100 is a fine class. If you read the short readings in-depth & really lean into the market games simulation, you'll be okay. Mittelstaedt's lectures are informative but can be a bit dry. Pay attention in class, as you are tested on random examples brought up. On your cheat sheet, put basic reading concepts & class examples and you'll be fine.

Professor Mittelstadt isn't bad, this is more a reflection of BUSI100 at UNC. Very unstructured class, weekly readings and assignments,  but lecture is confusing and doesn't make sense half the time. PAY ATTENTION IN LECTURE,  the midterm and final bring up random things talked about during lecture. Overall, just a mid class and professor.
Really nice guy, highly recommend.

Professor Mittelstaedt was great! His lectures were very interesting but be prepared to participate - participation in class counts towards your grade. The readings can be boring and he can move through math examples quickly in class but you get a one page cheat sheet for the midterm and final.

Super chill professor. HW assignments every week. Do the readings! worked in assigned groups over the semester for this thing called market games- an online simulation where you compete against other groups. Pay attention to what happens in class as it can be on the exams -the class slides aren't posted. However, you do get a handwritten cheatsheet

Course was easy, just do the readings and you'll be fine. Lectures were sometimes boring but were only once a week and were important for exams. You get a cheat sheet for both the midterm and final. A reading and an assignment are due every week before class. The readings can be hard to understand but questions about them are pretty easy.

If I'm not mistaken this is the first class he's ever taught. Given that, I think he did a phenomenal job. He showed from day one that he really cares about his students and that he wants all of us to succeed. That being said, especially in the beginning, he spoke very monotone which made it hard to listen but improved throughout the year.
She is a great person overall, but the class is very disorganized, and the quizzes are very ambiguous. Also our final exam was the same 10 questions repeated 5 times each...

Dr. Klevans is a tremendously kind individual who has a heart for teaching and all her students. While sometimes her explanations in class are somewhat difficult to understand, her quizzes in class are just applying the vocab from each selected chapter/section. The projects are not back-breaking, but don't get behind. Would take again!
Kinda didn't want to write anything. But she has been very accommodating when I was concerned about personal stuff. Don't love the quizzes, but class is fun.

Just got my grade. Did better than expected since I had heard she is a tough grader.
You need to know the material. It helps to get the textbook because she does not share her slides.

The good: real life examples, class activities
The bad: group projects.

Invited me to work on a project, so try to find out if there are other opportunities to do that.
Negative: lots of work.
Helped me get an internship!!!!!!

Follow the rubric. Otherwise she will find small details in your paper to deduct points.
She was willing to talk with me about other stuff, so she really cares.

Best: lots of activities
Worst: quizzes
But loved this teacher. She is fair.

I first reached out to Dr. Klevans after our first class. I was concerned about comments I had heard about class participation. Don't take this class if you don't like team activities or are kind of shy. I got an A but the hardest was to have to participate in class.
Dr. K. is kind and fair. Sometimes it is difficult to follow if you don't have the textbook. Does not share her slides. But loved her class activities.

Being a double major, comp sci, I was concerned about this class. Ended up with a better grade than I had thought. If you don't like participating in class, this is not a class for you. Lots of activities.

I am an older student. I appreciate all the knowledge Dr. CH K has. Her examples are based on her own experience, and that was refreshing. Not fond of tests, though. Very accommodating and  makes herself available to meet with students.

Class was not that hard. 
Took it on my senior year. Some concepts may be outdated. But in general, good class. The only negative is you won't have much time for quizzes.

Class is not that hard if you study the concepts.
I looked forward to this class every week. My best so far. I would take another class with Dr. Chrino
I am an international student and this was my first time studying abroad. This class made me realize I want to study in America! Loved Dr. Kelvans!

She goes above and beyond to make class engaging and fun. This was my first business class.
Quizzes are ok. Final assignment is an interview.
I disagree with all that someone wrote before this post. I think they must not have done well in the course. She is amazing and loved her course.

Loved the fun interactive activities we did in class; however, she grades kinda harshly with vague instructions. Gave many groups mid 70s-80s on the final group project, which didn't have a rubric. Class quizzes seemed easy, but turned out difficult for no reason. The final was recycled from past quizzes, so that was nice. try to participate

Ivonne is a nice person, but I agree with the review that said you can't disagree with her or she may take it personally. The course doesn't encourage grasping content but more-so just memorizing vocab. Silly in-class activities. Final project instructions were vague and the rubric she used to grade it was never given out.
she is a fairly liberal professor and the class content is just as much so. not sure if every 405 is taught this way, but hopefully not. definitely not my favorite class
One of the worst grading criteria for a professor that I've ever had. Don't expect to get a good grade in this class. Tests are very difficult for no reason

Professor Sonday is here to prepare you for the real world. She is fair, intense, and intelligent, and always ensures her teaching style reflects respect. She goes the extra mile to make sure her students are truly engaged and learning. Not to mention, she is super, super sweet and witty! One of the most well-rounded professors I have ever had!

Probably not the best choice when it comes to 405 professors. Grading is heavily weighted on a few items like group project, participation, and exams. Group project was not very interesting, in my opinion, and was graded harshly. Similar idea goes toward participation and the exams. Neither are easy to get a good grade on

not usually one to leave RMP reviews, but had to for Sonday. Hands down best professor I've had in recent memory, one of if not the best teacher at KFBS. Actually engaging, actually interesting content, and she cares about what she's teaching. One of those classes that reminds you why you actually go to school. 10/10

Prof Sonday is a nice, engaging professor, and her classes are fun to go to. No computers, but she shows evidence to justify it. The group project can be frustrating at times, but I enjoyed the class. 2 tests alongside the group project. Tough grader, as I felt I did better than the grade I got at times. Overall, I would take Professor Sonday again

Prof. Sonday is the best lecturer I've ever had. She is engaged with the class and excited about the material. While she does not allow electronics and requires paper notes, the material is very interesting. You do a semester long group project with assigned groups as well as take a midterm and final. No homework really other than readings.

Professor Sonday's lectures are less of a traditional lecture, and more representative of an interactive ted talk that feels far more interesting. The topics she discusses and the energy she brings is immaculate & her authenticity and transparency is refreshing. Midterms & Final are eh, with project graded a little harshly, but still a great class.

Professor Sonday is hands down the best professor I've had at UNC. She is extremely knowledgable and passionate about organizational behavior which is reflected in her lively lectures. Her exams are tough but fair, meant to test your application of the concepts rather than memorization. Her class is a great course in leadership across disciplines!

She is one of the most engaging + kind professors I've had at Carolina. No computers. Her lectures were great and she is really passionate. Not necessary to do most readings. Group project big part of grade, graded a little tough. Participation mattered. Worth it to take with her even if its a little more effort than other 405s.

Prof Sonday is goated. No electronics in lectures, but it makes content more engaging and exams easier. Readings/videos assigned before every class, but you can get participation points without doing them. Extremely transparent with how she grades. Final weighted same as the midterm and not cumulative. Favorite class/professor I've taken at KF!

Great prof, interesting classes. Mandatory attendance, participate 1x a week, do readings for class. Group proj worth a lot of the grade, with a paper and presentation to show your work. Midterm + final are 50 MC q. Absolutely phenomenal prof. Super great, interesting lectures + she's so kind.

She's great. You can tell she really likes teaching and cares for her students (very accessible outside of class). The exams were not bad if you study. Participation is big part of grade along with a group project that she really wanted students to go the extra mile on. Definitely a professor who you would want to take more classes with!

A fantastic and enthusiastic professor. Super passionate about OB that she makes you passionate. You can get a solid exam score just by attending class. You have to do readings to have any good input in-class participation. No computers but that's ok, you won't need it. Lectures were engaging. Highly recommend this professor.

Professor Sonday is genuinely one of the best teachers I've had at UNC. She is so nice to everyone, available for extra help, and communicates deadlines and course expectations well. The material isn't hard either but you do need to study and work hard on the group project to do well. Also, participation is very important if you want a good grade!

As senior, Laura Sonday is my favorite professor. She was passionate about the topics she taught, utilizing real-world and interesting examples. As an international student, I can feel her kindness and sincere. She is really nice and accessible outside classes. She made this class meaningful and fun. Love it!

Professor Sonday was by far my favorite at UNC.  She does not allow computers or tablets for note taking in class which was annoying at first, but I actually came to enjoy because it forced me to pay attention to her engaging lectures.  She moves quickly to constantly keep thing interesting and truly cares about her students.  Would take again!
Nicest professor I have had at UNC. You have to speak every day to get participation points which is dreadful, but shes a wonderful professor

Dr. Schlobohm is awesome, she is incredible caring and passionate. You do have to do work in this class, but its school so thats normal. It's never overbearing but it is work and thats okay. Overall she is awesome, and I would recommend taking her class.

Dr. Schlobohm was a charming professor and emphasized that her class was more about experimentation than getting things right. The class structure is centered around "if you put the work in, you'll get an A," which is a fantastic change of pace from traditional lectures, especially about personal branding. Plus, she loves feedback for the class!

Prof Scholbohm was a very nice professor and created a very fun and welcoming environment. I found the course content to be helpful in preparing for jobs. However, she's a slow grader and does not give out very many A's even though the assignments themselves are not hard at all.

Dr. Schlobohm is an amazing teacher and human being who truly cares for her students health. She is extremely charismatic and welcoming from the first day in her class. The biggest downside to her class is feedback a

Professor Schlobohm cares about her students, but has a strict attendance policy and takes a very long time to return feedback. Her grading scale is also very difficult, and considers a B in her class to be "very good". While she works to make classes engaging, it's hard to do well and gives only 1-2 students per class above 90 on each assignment.

Dr. Schlobohm's personality wasn't for me, but her class was fine. She's nice enough, cares about the content, and the work isn't hard because its very self-oriented, but she takes forever to grade and her scores seemed unfair. For our final presentation, the highest score she gave was a 90. Deceptively easy class.

Makes easy things unnecessarily tough. She has a very cheerful personality, but she grades you down for no reason. She also takes too long to grade, leaving no scope for students to learn from their errors.
One of the most confusing and vague profs I've ever had. If you are reading this comment, I fully recommend to stay away.

Prof. Schlobohm is my favorite professor at the b-school so far! She truly cares about her students and gives you everything you need to succeed. I learned a lot from the material and assignments. Her grading can be a bit on the tougher side, but she gives great feedback and if you put in the work youll do fine. 100% recommend taking her!

Dr. Schlobohm is an incredible professor. She makes writing and oral presentation material engaging and interesting and is receptive to feedback, even if critical. The classroom culture is kind and safe. Though she is a hard grader, her feedback is thorough and applicable. I can attest to the growth in hard and soft skills I've had because of her.

I didn't mesh well with Professor Schlobohm's personality. It seemed fake and strained, and I saw kids who disagreed get the brunt of that fakeness. The class itself was fine. Heavy on the homework for what seemed like no reason while two projects decided 80% of your grade. Honestly, the most useless class I've taken at Kenan-Flagler.
I would recommend seeking another professor. She is fine but I have heard anyone else is better.

Her team grades very harshly, and I feel they should learn more about giving feedback since it's usually so vague. I didn't enroll just for the TAs to give me feedback, but that's what happened. Your grade essentially depends on your teammates so keep praying.

The final grade is mainly determined by your placement on the case competitions, which can be difficult because of randomly assigned teams. Overall, such a great class to learn about consulting & be a great teammate. Teaches you more tangible things than most classes, especially slide deck creation & presentation skills.
