Really good for consulting.

Great class but hard and do not expect to get an A no matter what you normally get in classes. Anyone going into consulting or really anything should take this class and she teaches well and has you take in a lot of info. CSF "consulting" is a lot of making stuff up but still helpful. Grading can be hard and is based on winning case comps.
Really enjoyed this class and learned a lot of tangible business skills. Overall fun class! No exams which is nice all projects

I loved this class with Professor Cochran. She deeply cares about her students. I gained experience presenting recommendations to consultants and learned a lot. This class and the STAR program helped me realize that I want to pursue a career in consulting. Even though the workload demand is higher, the class was fun to work on with teams!

This class is challenging and the grading criteria is NOT clear; if you don't have a ton of experience in consulting, your grade may suffer. VERY competitive class, which can be awkward. Karin once had us do a "PollEv" in class to rank each team (the results were live and projected on the board), and assigned grades based off the rankings...

Karin Cochran is a terrible professor.  I tried to reach out to her multiple times to communicate about an assignment, but never received a definitive answer.  I did receive a very low grade, and she did not allow me to remedy the situation.  My assessment was that she did not care about student concerns.  I should have never taken her class.
Best professor at KF.
Great lectures, highly reccomend.

LOVE Tim. He was funny and relatable. On FDOC I thought he was a student after he offered me a celsius the second I walked in the room. Super cool guy, it would be a shame if you don't take his class.
Simply the goat

Tim is the goat. You'd imagine Ethics to be a boring class, but he makes every day so fun with all his little surprises. He clearly cares about the subject matter- goes above and beyond in every way. Grading is a little weird (bc it's j compared to peers - not specific criteria), but I feel like this is a B-school problem, not Tim problem
Quite literally one of the all time favorites within the business school. You should be doing everything in your power to have Tim as your professor.

Tim's class could be taught at 5 AM in the 7th circle of hell and I would still be there. I was genuinely excited to go to his class every day and have never heard a student say a bad word about him. Cannot recommend him enough.
Can confidently say Tim was the best professor I had at KF. Only class I've taken that I was actually excited to go to everyday. Enjoyed his class so much that I never used my skip.

Tim is an absolute star. Never had another professor in the b school who was so good at connecting the material to students. He's also incredibly self aware about the material and even though it's ethics it never feels like he's passing judgement on students for their views. Would recommend any student to take him if they have the chance

The best professor I've ever had. He made every class extremely entertaining and fun. If you take 404 with someone other than him, it would be a shame. He is extremely relatable and has amazing jokes / content in class.
Great professor, and connects with students and material super well. Couldn't recommend more!
I loved 404 with Kundro. He is engaging, accommodating, and his assignments are challenging but they really help you grasp the content. Definitely a fan favorite at the b school!

Kundro is an absolute gem and is probably one of the best professors I've had at Kenan-Flagler so far. He's got really engaging classes to the point that Lectures really flew by and I was sad when the Mod ended. It's clear that Tim cares about his students and is passionate about teaching. Would easily take a class with him again!

I truly believe  Hart is the best 408 professor at UNC by a long shot. She truly cares about the success of her students. The course is meant to be hard no matter who you take it with, but she puts in the effort to simplify conceptually. Exams are just like in class practice problems. You'll be fine as long as you pay attention and put in effort
An amazing professor! Be aware of group projects which she graded a little bit harsh. Median curve on the final. One midterm and final that composes 60 percent of the grade.

One of the best professors I've had here at Carolina. The course material can sometimes be difficult but she explains it SO well and has an abundance of opportunities to practice and get clarification through Office Hours. Great woman. Loved her.

Professor Hart is an incredible BUSI408 professor, and makes a daunting class a lot more approachable. Not easy content, but her teaching is great. Definitely recommend her to make a hard class more manageable!

Hart was awesome for 408! Homework prepares you super well for class/exams, and as long as you practice all semester she breaks things down pretty well. Group projects were graded a bit harshly, and, while approachable, she doesn't tend to regrade anything. Don't skip class because there are post class quizzes almost every day that add up.

Hart was a FANTASTIC busi 408 professor; the lectures were super engaging, and hw helped reinforce the material. Beware of end of end-of-class quizzes (they aren't hard it's always a question on something covered that day). There are 2 group projects, a midterm and a final. Learn to use EXCEL (way easier/quicker than your financial calculator)

Professor Hart is amazing. She really wants every student to understand the material and is willing to work with you outside of class to make sure you do. The work is pretty much standardized across all the 408 classes. She teaches the material in an engaging way and I looked forward to coming to class each day.

By far the best professor to take corporate finance with at UNC! She only teaches a couple of sections because she also teaches at State. 408 is hard no matter who you take it with but Melissa is a great professor and truly makes sure that you understand the information. 100% recommend 408 with her.

She really cares about students and will provide help and feedback in an understanding way! Good intro and walkthrough to data platforms in a short period of time, make sure your computer can run it bc be sure nothing on campus will. Honestly great intro, didn't like alteryx and found some of the work tedious but really fun assignments

Databases and Visualizations MOD class. Quite fast paced. We went through Alteryx, MySQL, and Tableau. Sometimes she moved too fast for us to follow along, but she slowed down and took time with us individually when we asked for help. At times when the class seemed hard and overwhelming, she made sure proactively check in and adjust accordingly.

Oh Prof Glaeser. Where is my H? Only a P?? Even then, you were great. 

Don't slack off at the end, make sure you know the scale. This class covers hard stats and technical software, which I hope I will need. Glad I learned them from Prof Glaeser, who, actually, cares about us.

So hard, she doesn't teach well.  She goes super fast with crazy excel formulas that you can't follow.  The only reason I gave her a 2 is that she is a really nice lady and really cares for her students.
410 is a hard course, but I highly recommend taking it from her! She really cares about her students and really knows her stuff.

Incredible professor! He explains concepts very methodically and ensures that everyone understands. His homework and tests are fair, and he provides so many resources on how his teachings can be applied to portfolios. Most "real-world applicable" class and professor I have taken. 10/10 would recommend if interested in finance.
Awesome prof

There's a very similar class in the econ department (ECON 425). But while 425 is VERY dry and just sticks to equations Gill's class is WAYYY more connected to actual applications and to news affairs. I felt I could actually do useful things to my dinky portfolio after 580. TAKE THIS VERSION of investments and then for "free" credit take 425....

I just took MBA792A in mod 3. I had no finance background and was quite intimidated about the class. It was inspiring to see how professor Gill connected our academic topics to things we can implement on our portfolios. Always cared if students are able to follow.
Really good if you want any kind of industry job, it's the most applicable class at kenan flagler

It was probably the best class I took at Kenan-Flagler, but the homeworks were difficult and the exam was tricky. Still the material is really eye opening and the discussion of current affairs is the main reason to take this class.
Very knowledgable. Always talks about recent events which makes the class practical and interesting.

She is vulnerable enough to make it clear that her classroom is a safe space that prioritizes learning, not manufactured rigor. Participate in class to really make the concepts stick; she makes many engaging real-world connections. Don't wait until the review sessions to ask your questions, bc everything builds on itself.

Dr. Annie Williams is by far one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. She taught extremely well, was transparent with her expectations, and gave significant autonomy to her students. She made the world of marketing something I am excited to continue to pursue. Always attend class, and don't rely heavily on the book for the exams. She's amazing.

Annie is SO nice & really wants us to do well. Takes feedback from students into account. class consists of 4 reflections, 2 group projects/presentations, midterm, & a 5-question handwritten short-answer response final, both open note. I genuinely loved learning & going to class. There were many readings, so be sure to take notes on them! must take

Professor Williams is great. She really cares about her students and has clear grading criteria and good feedback. She is accessible outside of class. Lectures are boring, but that's just 406. The projects are not too bad. Would highly recommend for 406.
Super nice and accessible, wish the lectures were more engaging - lots of repetition out of the book and make sure to follow guidelines on cases to get good grades

Williams is kind, funny, and receptive to feedback. She is easily accessible outside of class and values her officer hours time (she will not give general feedback on projects so you must go to office hours to talk about grading.) Grades are based on three cases (group), midterm, final, SONA research participation, and attendance. TAKE 406 WITH HER

Professor Williams is genuinely one of the kindest and most receptive professors I've had at UNC. She was able to acknowledge when things didn't go smoothly and took feedback very seriously. Exams were very straightforward, and the lectures were super engaging and made sure you were well prepared. Super chill elective and really interesting!
Brad is so nice. He's good at lecturing even when I found the content to be pretty boring. Hated market games though

Prof. Hendricks is a great lecturer and integrates readings into classes amazingly. Anything mentioned in class is free game for the midterm, so GO TO CLASS. Grading is done by TAs and is sometimes pretty unclear imo. I hated market games. BUSI100 is much harder than a 1.5 credit class should be. TA office hours were very helpful.

great professor, very good lecturer and really great guy. it was a different perspective on business than i had previously been taught and i enjoyed it a lot. there were a lot of readings, some may find them enjoyable and some may not. i personally enjoyed them a lot. this course asks for more than you would anticipate given its 1.5 credit value.

Each class would have a reading and a homework assignment due. More of a philosophy class than a business class. You are in small groups for the whole semester which can have a big affect on your final grade (2 of my group members never showed up to class or group meetings). If you read the assigned readings and do practice problems its an easy A.
He really cares about students. Market games are rough, don't go off of what previous students have done because variables change. Best professor for Busi100 by far and curve at the end helps.
for a 1.5 credit hour class, you will spend a lot more time that what you'd think. He likes to trick you in exams so be very specific when studying for them.

In short, Professor Hendricks is great. The class is lecture heavy, but broken up in topic and format enough for it to still be interesting. He is great at communicating, with detailed emails to the class and quick responses in individual correspondence. Rely on the TAs for help on assignments and Market Games.

Prof Hendricks is a fantastic teacher. The tests are not bad if you read and take notes in class. To do well in Market Games, check the math behind the year's targets to make sure it is mathematically possible to hit the goals, and analyze Year 1 results to see what patterns separated top teams from bottom teams and which factors influenced that.

I liked Professor Hendricks as a teacher and person, but market games was not fun. I studied A LOT for midterm and final which ended up being worth it, but definitely tricky. Way too much work for a 1.5 credit class.

As an international student, this class was challenging. The readings from the 1400s and 1500s were difficult, the midterm was tricky, and the accounting section can be hard if you forget the formulas.
Was a lot of work for a 1.5 credit class but Hendricks made sure it was worth your while. I learned so much from this class and can take away a lot of valuable material and mindset.

definitely  not a walk in the park, you need to really do well on market games. do not get a bad group. hard to get professors attention, so you should try to get close with TAs who imo are way more helpful

Ok class, inspiring professor. GO TO OFFICE HOURS FOR HELP. My biggest issue was market games until I went to the TAs for their tips. They grade fairly and provide their own advice. Overall, not bad just be sure to stay on top of your work

This class was fairly easy. The midterms and tests had some tricks, so its easy to misread and mess up. But, 1/2 of it are just repeated questions from quizlets. One thing that is tricky is the Market games, ..... I got A's on every single assignment and exams and still got an A- b/c we hit mercy (60s)... participation matters (average was an 80%)

Professor Hendricks is a great professor. Lectures are engaging, quick weekly assignments, and easy exams if you complete the short readings and study a couple hours. The only thing annoying about the course is market games, so hope you get a good group.
Prof Hendricks is a nice guy and good teacher.

Hendricks is a great guy and super caring of his students! Didn't know what I was expecting coming into this class but this wasn't it. Lots of readings, the math are easy, market game was horrible. I failed 2/3 rounds. Exams were easy. I'm sure I'll enjoy his teaching more if it were another class, just didn't like BUSI100 as a course.

Professor Hendricks is an amazing person, I love his lectures and his outlook on life. He emphasizes there's more to life than just work. That being said, I absolute HATE market games since I got such a bad group, and that really tanks your grade even though they cap it at 60%. Lots of readings, but overall easy class (esp if you get a good group).
Really nice guy cares about students despite the large size of his lectures

Excellent professor, even better person. Genuinely cares for his students success in class, but more so in life. Approachable, but lecture heavy so take notes and attend class. Lots of readings, but applicable to business and life. Minimal math, simply attend class, take notes, and stay on top of the readings to succeed. Highly recommend Hendricks!
Shimul is so cool and interesting. The best way I can describe the class is reflective but also BS at the same time. Easy work though.
Easy, enjoyable class. She is so sweet and cares about her students. Hard to reach via text and email to set up meetings, but overall really nice!

I am so thankful for the opportunity to take this class. Shimul is hands down the nicest professor I have met at UNC and I am so excited to work with her again in the future. If you are an assured admit you will look forward to this class each week. Participate and take in every in and out of class assignment, they all have meaning.
Show up do the work, you'll pass. She's an awesome person and loves to meet her students.

Shimul carefully chooses simulations & class activities that make the course material so much more engaging. She knows her material extremely well, and she facilitates such a comfortable environment for students to speak up in. Such a respected professor, and she gives you so many opportunities to do well. Exams aren't bad if you study well. 10/10!

Clutch professor, class was fun with group activities every day and assignments were graded relatively leniently. Curves up midterm and final scores. Ultimately comes through with the grade you want as long as you put in some effort and participated.

Extremely vague grading expectations and guidelines. While the class can be enriching and fun at times, the class can get overly repetitive with exercises and various simulations. Hard to reach by email for feedback, but definitely cares about her students.

She is so nice and loves the class. She tries to make every class a group activity but they are kinda dumb and I mean the whole class content is a joke. It is very much like a middle school class. Exams are just memorizing some random terms. Probably a good option for 405 but... eh...
Great online 407 class

Listen Wayne is a great guy. But online textbook is terrible, I had reading online textbooks, so i didnt read it for shit. Classwork has nothing to do with homework at times. BUT you wont find a professor as accessible outside of class as him, he is generally a very nice professor. Material is just as useful the appendix.

Wayne is a kind professor who wants to see you succeed. He can be a bit dry during lectures but is always available outside of class for questions or extra help. Drops your worst hw and quiz. Exam topics are clear and he gives tons of resources to prepare. Took student suggestions in the middle of the semester and improved based on them! Love him.

I wish all profs at UNC were like Professor McVeigh. He is simply the nicest person I have encountered EVER. Genuinely cares about every individual, wants his students to succeed and believes in their potential, is engaging and knowledgeable in lectures, and is by far the most accessible prof I've ever had. I just hope he knows how incredible he is
Superb

He is an incredible person and really cares about his students. He's always available to answer any questions and does his best to make sure everyone is understanding the material. On top of that, he is very knowledgeable on the subject and does a good job showing step by steps for longer problems. One of the best people in McColl
He is a great guy who cares about his students and keeps class interesting and engaging, one of my favorite teachers in the B school. Wouldn't take anyone else for 403.

This class is fine if you are not (ad-libs). I honestly had a hard time with the content and the structure of the course so figure out a way to study/be able to structure yourself to take the exam in class. There are a lot of resources and examples, he has a lot of knowledeg!! dont be afraid to ask

Oh Beeler where do I even begin. Ever since I met u on our first day I knew I was in for a great sem. Had me jumping for joy to come to class every day and put a smile on my face every time I saw u (shi I think i'm in love). I came in expecting spreadsheets and pain and I left with memories, laughs and a disturbing level of emotional attachment

Honestly the best class i've taken at KF. What a lad. Made me excited to come to class every day and spent the first 20 mins of class just yapping and telling jokes. Content for me was extremely enjoyable and all the exams are open note so extremely easy to do good on. Group project however is slightly annoying if u have incompetent group members.

If you are a decently social person who is not afraid to participate in class, big mike is your guy. Otherwise, take it with someone else. We start class with 10 minutes of jokes/talking about good things that happened. The material is easy and Beeler does not try to trick you on exams or homework.

Professor Beeler was by far the best teacher I've ever had. We spent the first 20 min of every class telling jokes, something good, etc before going into lecture which made learning and the class enviornment really enjoyable. He gives you literally every resource you need to succeed in the class and  made me lmao every day.

Prof. Beeler was a gem! We spent half of lecture time just chatting and telling jokes, and his class was super easy and fun.  Exams were easy, and you get an extra point if you put a joke on it! Attendance and participation were mandatory - I hated that I was forced to tell jokes/share something good with the class for credit. Regardless, take him

Participation based on whether or not you say something good or tell a joke. Unclear grading criteria for the final project with absolutely no feedback. Tests are pretty fair. I just did not enjoy this class.

I really enjoyed Beeler's class. To be honest, I was very depressed at the beginning of the semester, which is why I didn't do well on one of the exams because I could barely bring myself to study. But I think the class was well laid out, not too hard, and Beeler is always happy to answer questions. Remember to add a joke to your tests for EC!

Beeler is funny professor and his class material is relatively easy. However, his grading criterias are one of the worst that I've seen at KF. Your participation grades largely depends on the amount of jokes you tell in the class. Other thing is that some early mistakes in your Midterm can significantly lower your overall grade.

Very funny professor. This class is not very difficult as the test problems are very similar to the HWs and practice problems. You can only miss two classes though and participation does matter. Don't bother buying the textbook.
The best option for 403. Class is boring and easy. He is funny but the class is really so useless for our future it is hard to want to come to it. Has not updated class for a decade it looks like.

Great professor - approachable, entertaining, and doesn't take everything so seriously. The exams are open note, and he provides incredibly useful materials such as homework answers from previous years and spreadsheets to help you get your answers more quickly. The exams were a crunch for time, but use those spreadsheets and you'll be fine!

Honestly, he is a nice guy, but being real: why is my participation grade based on if I say a joke or not??? That actually makes no sense. There were very little opportunities to participate outside of telling a joke. Also you can only miss 2 classes and he isn't very understanding, even if you have a medical issue.
Beeler is my favorite teacher I have had at UNC. Made class enjoyable everyday and taught the material well.

Easy class with no exams. He spends the first 25 mins of class telling jokes then quickly reads off slides. He is not engaging and most people don't listen to the lectures. Make sure not to turn in things late. He can say some offensive things and can be a bit rude and unprofessional at times.

Funny but not serious. I sit in the first class with him and he was really good at vibing with the room but literally the second he hits actual materials his voice got so unconfident and brushed through everything. PPT is also boring and non-presentative.

Beeler has been my favorite professor at UNC so far. With that being said, I loved the content of this class but still found it a bit challenging. The two midterms were hard, but the final was much easier. He threw a curveball on one of the tests that ended up dropping my grade. Highly recommend overall but be prepared to study and practice.

Prof Beeler is a great choice for 403. He knows the material very well and does a good job relating concepts to everyday life. Grade breakdown: 66% - Tests, 14% - Participation, 10% - Homework, 10% - Project. Tests are open-note and directly tied to homework.  Class is a loose, fun, joke-filled atmosphere. If you study a little, you'll do well.

At times, I wished Prof. Beeler spent more time on the material. Could've gotten out even earlier if not for the 15 minutes to jokes to start each day. Appreciated, but inefficient. Beware- he is very tight on his attendance policy. Took some coaxing to make sure my grade was correct even through extreme circumstances. Overall, good option for 403.

Haugen is a very intelligent person who knows what she is talking about. However, she is overly particular about what she wants from students to the point where it is impossible to fulfill her standards. Best thing I can say is to get on her good side and make sure your first assignment is a good one cause that'll be the grade you get all semester.

Prof Haugen is very nice and caring, but runs a tough class. She is very strict on her criteria, which means you spend a lot of time on her projects. She teaches good information, which I still use today in my job. However, I felt she graded unneccessarily harshly and had slightly too high of standards. She is very nice and knowledgeable,.

- Extremely unclear directions on all assignments throughout the entirety of the course. Overly conceded. Nice and intelligent woman; however, I'm unsure how she can teach this class when her grading is based solely on personal bias, and over 40% of the assignments are intellectually useless for all students. Nice person, terrible class.
Very nice woman but directions are often unclear. Grading also appears arbitrary at times and students question how more effort can somehow correlate to worse grades. Tough.
Unclear directions, tough grader, and class just sucks in general. Got an 80 on every assignment.

Have her review your assignments before you submit. Don't use to-be verbs. Participate in class. Then you'll get an A.

Very time-consuming, assignment-heavy, class, but I walked away a stronger communicator.
take 401 with literally anyone else. super unclear directions and takes off points for no reason. what she teaches has no practical application to the real world. stay away.

Dr. Haugen was a great instructor! Class content itself isn't necessarily hard, but it is very valuable in learning how to communicate, especially in a corporate setting. I walked away from the class with greater confidence in my writing abilities.

Dr H is a great professor who definitely cares about her students. She brings energy to lectures and makes classes fun. The only thing is that she is definitely a tough grader about the smallest nit-picky details, so be prepared to put more hours/effort into the work for this BUSI 401 section than for sections with other professors.

I liked this class & thought Dr. H made it really fun. She's a tough grader & u have to put in a lot of work to get a good grade. There's a lot of nit picky stuff that she looks for in your writing. If u participate, pay attention, and don't procrastinate you'll be fine. She's very willing to answer questions. Try to get on her good side

This class actually made me worse at writing. Assignments are poorly explained and boring lectures. Don't even get me started on the grading. Be prepared to put in a ton of time doing busywork that doesn't help you write better. Blood, sweat and tears? Yeah, you can put those in too, but she's still going to give you a terrible grade.
Dr. H is one of the most caring profs at the b school. She grades tough but her feedback is super helpful and she genuinely wants all students to succeed. Highly recommend her for 401!
Don't listen to the previous comments. Dr. H is one of the best.

Dr. Haugen is a nice person and is very caring about her students. However, she grades super harshly and does not ever provide clear instructions on the assignment requirements. She made her students submit a 12 page solution proposal the second to last week of class. Also, a final presentation was required. Take another professor for BUSI 401.

He is a good and fair professor but he isn't equitable. Schedule and expectations are clear; the late policy is reasonable. BUT he doesn't drop any assignments or quizzes and he doesn't let students make up any assignment or quiz for any reason. The class is practical and I would take it again, but don't expect him to accommodate you - he won't.

Professor Day cares about helping students succeed and improve at using Excel. Very accessible outside of class over email. Happy to answer students' questions. Would recommend taking this class especially if you're an Excel beginner / have moderate Excel background. Might not be as helpful if you're highly proficient in Excel.
Great professor!

You complete assignments based on lectures recorded during COVID. It feels more like a formatting course with little real instruction rather than a high-level modeling course. There was little relevance for banking or high-level finance roles. Overall, gets you more comfortable with Excel, but a certification would have done the same.
Professor Day is a very enthusiastic and knowledgeable professor. The assignments can take a while, but class only meets once a week, and he's always available for extra help. Really useful class!
Travis is the best! This is the most useful class I've taken at the B School. The weekly assignments can take a while, but he gives clear instructions and feedback.
Travis is great. Take the class if you can it'll help you a lot. Pretty low-commitment too
Most useful class you'll take. Assignment+Quizz every week but it helps practice.
you learn so much, assignment directions are super clear and very manageable.
Professor Day is one of the best instructors I've had. He combines high standards with genuine support and clarity.
Great guy, funny, and cares about his students. Highly recommend as a MAC student or anyone using excel.

Professor Day runs a very well structured and formatted class. His notes files are very helpful, and he is very receptive to helping you out in class. The work is a lot and is challenging at times, but if you manage your time you will be ok. I learned a ton about Excel and recommend taking this class.

Note that the final is 50% of your grade.

Professor Day is an exceptional teacher. While the material was quite dense, his methodical approach to teaching made it easy to digest the information. 

In response to the comments about the final being heavily weighted, as long as you are diligent in completing the assignments, there should be no reason for you to not do well on the exam.

Final is weighed 50% of your grade and you cannot check your answers. Content is very useful but directions are often convoluted. 1-2 hrs of async that tbh could be 15 mins if edited down. Lots of overlap between lecture and async so its kinda boring. Grading is always quick and feedback is great. Useful and necessary class but needs some revision.

Great class - Professor Day makes things super accessible and assignments are clear. Content was very well organized and there was a lot of transparency surrounding expectations and grading. Class was held once a week online and was easy to fit into my schedule. Super useful content, highly recommend.
Professor Travis is an amazing professor and person, he made learning new things in excel fun and interesting. Really a good class to get an edge on excel modelling.
Practical course, good sense of humor, solid teaching and presentation skills, definitely recommend.
Has an extreme attention to detail in grading of assignments. Final exam is heavily weighted, which makes some of the assignments feel tedious in comparison. Professor is hilarious in class.
Prepare your mind ahead of time, as not everything will be taught in class.

Professor Day expects much but also gives you all the tools and knowledge you need to succeed. I found his teaching style and class format to be very informative--his notes were an excellent resource and the assignments helped to lock in that knowledge and skill. His enthusiasm for the material made it my favorite class this semester!

This guy is actually a beast. Best professor at Kenan Flagler by a mile. Pretty sure he only teaches 404 in Spring Semester, so, if you can, wait until then to take it with him. If I could take every class with him I would.
Seriously the GOAT- and my fav class at UNC. No other words- he had engaging lectures, passionate and serious discourse at times, but kept it light and a great time.
Best Professor at Kenan-Flagler hands down. Most engaging and inspirational dude ever. If you get the chance, definitely take 404 with him.

Wow -- what a great class and such a caring professor. Class is graded on a curve so its hard to earn an A but such great lectures and fun material. Really loved every lecture and each project. Very caring and inspirational when talking about how ethics interplay with business. Highly reccomend taking 404 with Kundro.

Great teacher! He really goes above and beyond to make class engaging and makes sure everyone is having a good time during lectures. He's super kind and genuinely cares about the topics he teaches.  Would definitely recommend taking 404 with him.
Tim is one of the best professors i've had at KF. If you participate and study for the quiz you'll be set. Class is unplugged which I actually liked. Wish he taught more undergrad classes.
The best. Super engaging. Best class/prof at KF.

Amazing professor, definitely take 404 with him. Unplugged classes with lots of fun participation activities makes the time fly by and helps you learn. Reading and homework is pretty minimal, but he's not a pushover. He's the funniest professor I've had so far and clearly makes an effort to make class entertaining. One of my favorite professors!
really nice prof, his projects are fun compared to other classes, quiz isn't bad and it reflects the lectures, class is unplugged which is really nice, the readings are also interesting.
what can i say about tim, hes the man! i looked forward to each class of his, he made learning fun. and its a plus that hes easy on the eyes. tim gets an A+ from me!!

Amazing class. Tim is super fun and I enjoyed his class everyday. Beware of one incredibly hard midterm that is a huge chunk of your grade. I got A's on every assignment and then did bad on the quiz and ended the class with a B. Other than he is a great teacher and deserves the world!

Tim is the boy. Best class I have taken at the B-school so far. Looked forward to each class because of how engaging Tim made them. He has your sanity in mind and does a great job of conveying concepts and teaching students without swamping you in unnecessary work. GOATED

Tim is the best professor I've had so far. He really cares about students and his grading is extremely fair. He made lectures really enjoyable and easy to pay attention. Group project heavy but he balances the class to evaluate in a variety of methods.

Not sure why these reviews are bad when PV is really chill. His lectures can devolve into him talking in circles for a while, but the classwork (a few canvas quizzes/discussion posts) and final are easy enough (open note/internet). Make sure to participate through talking in class or emailing him - he's interesting and truly cares a lot about VC.

PV is a really interesting guy who is very passionate about VC. His knowledge is a little outdated, and it's pretty clear that the VCs he brings in to talk to the class don't take him seriously, but love him anyway. Work is tedious, and your grade is dependent on who you pair up with for the projects. Heard this class is splitting into 2 classes.

Class is interesting if you choose an engaging start-up. I recommend double-checking with PV every single time you can because he will ALWAYS have his own "correct" way of looking at things. Pick competent group members! I don't care if you have friends in the class, you'll want them out of your group ASAP if they can't do the work well.

The work isn't hard... understanding what he expects is. Lectures are all over the place with long tangents. Asking him a question will lead to being interrupted by a response that goes in circles for 60 seconds without any helpful answer. HIGHLY recommend avoiding

PV doesn't know how to teach despite his "good" efforts. The content is decent despite the fact that he doesn't have any practical experiences with VC's.. Poor grading, decent presenting , bad teaching... PV I hardly pass do not take this joke of a "Teacher"...

Class was interesting with good guest speakers. PV has a big personality and can sometimes come across as rude but he is a good teacher. The assignments require a lot of time and to do super in-depth research and write papers on startups. The final was a 10 page paper but I think most people got good grades.

Tries to organize a course around VCs but doesn't have experience in VCs. He is quite arrogant which hinders what is enjoyable in the course. He is simply an OK teacher not any real added value has been added after I took this course, I would rather read a book on VCs / Growth Equity myself and learn more without having to good through him...

PV is a great guy. Some of the lectures got a bit dry from time to time. Grade is really dependent on who you partner up with for papers so pick someone good. Not hard to get an A if you put in time and effort.

PV is a hilarious guy that can talk venture capital for days. Has great Network to set you up in the sphere and organizes VC global competition. I have to say the class is a little tedious. You have to do a lot of due diligence and I wish there would be some prize for hard work rather than just complete grade.

Prof. PV was awesome! This class is very different from your conventional consulting ones so beware. Most of us were pretty lost throughout, which was "fun" since that replicated how startup founders feel. He really emphasized that we become owners of our startups so make sure you pick a good team! Also read his instructions - for participation!!!

Elad is a cheerful teacher, and the class is fairly enjoyable, but he crams WAY too much work into one weekend and gives you absolutely no feedback. Also wish the activities were a bit more creative since it's a creativity class (maybe a real-life Shark Tank as a team assignment). Overall, it was nice, but causes a ton of burnout and lacks support.

Nice person, but assigned an infeasible amount of work and relies on a group project format that simply doesn't work the majority of the time. Also is constantly interrupting his own students. Do not take this weekend class, and this is coming from someone who's taken almost all of the KF weekend classes.

Great weekend class. Interesting lectures and enjoyable activities made the weekend fly by. Fair amount of material to read in preparation for each day, but not unbearable by any means. If you need a weekend class, take this one

Elad is a good person and is engaging in class, but the amount of work he expects to be completed in such a short time is crazy. His grading criteria is extremely tough, he grades on tiers and for large assignments he will not give anyone higher than a 90.

Took creative thinking over the weekend. He's super engaging and makes the day go by faster. Only complaint is that the class is more like 9-9 than 9-5, but the grind is worth it and the material is fun. Worth it.

Great class, lectures were engaging, interesting, and had lots of activities to break up the long weekend. Knows the material very well. A lot of work outside class that weekend but doable. Grading is a little harsh for certain assignments but not too bad.
one of my favorite weekend classes. class is group work heavy, but pretty engaging.
My favorite professor at UNC
Really nice guy, not a ton of work but definitely fills your weekend. Not a ton of lecture, pretty fun activities
Awesome guy
final project is impossible and way harder than anything we're taught in the class. he's a nice guy but final project is brutal

Prof. Ringel's class was a really good intro to AI and DS in the business context. A lot of it was just high level code that was hard to understand, and we struggled a lot on our group projects. The quizzes and final were fair, but if you end up with a bad group then good luck! The CS students always carry the group, so be prepared to work if uk CS
The best class I have yet to take at UNC. It is very applicable to the real world. Dr. D does a great job explaining the complex concepts.

This class is driven by group projects. What you find is that one or two people lead the entire group, often time those who care to code, while the others coast off their lead. This class is unnecessarily extra, and for a class that applies data science in the real world, i can say with experience the real world is anything then the class projects.
his quizzes can be rough so just pay attention and you'll do well. a really funny professor and very passionate about tax probably the most interesting class i took at the b-school

I bombed first exam, hence the grade. Not an easy class but not hard either. Great lecturer and nice guy. Daily quizes that are just common knowledge, basically his way of taking attendence. Easy HW's, exams are similar to practice exam.

Dr. Hoopes is an absolute gem of the KF department, and I was so lucky to take his class. The 407 pre-req is entirely optional, and the energy he brings to class every day is the only reason why my trip to KF was worth it. The content is super interesting, and he's always flexible to talk about anything related to the class. Would take again 100%.

Jeff is probably the most passionate professor I have had in college. While it is true that taxes may not be the most appealing subject, his lectures are great and easy to understand. He calls exams "celebrations." As long as you keep up with the content, he will make sure you succeed.

I had Jeff for BUSI 574 (Taxes & Business Strategy). If you're planning on taking this class, make sure it's something you're genuinely interested in. His teaching is fast-paced and lecture-heavy. The class average on the midterm/final was pretty low (C- to C range). Nice and funny teacher overall, but not the easiest elective.

Professor Wilson is the perfect candidate to teach 404. She's very well read and experienced, helpful office hours, and pushes students to think further into hard questions. Everyone complaining in here wrongfully thought they could AI the readings and keep up in class discussions.

Dr. Wilson was a lively professor at the business school who expected her students to perform at a high level both academically and in participation. She is an understanding and kind professor, although you have to work very diligently and have to be dedicated to receive an A or A-. Her quizzes are fairly difficult and should not be taken lightly.

This class has a RIDICULOUS amount of work for a 1.5 credit hour class. Final paper, final exam, and final project for a business ethics class is insane. Boring lectures and relatively useless busywork. Only somewhat tolerable now because of AI.

This class was interesting and practical. Everyone who hates this class just hates anything qualitative. She isn't the most engaging professor, but our class discussions were interesting. Her other section said that she would trauma dump about her divorce in class, but I never experienced that. I have heard Tim is better, but she isn't bad.

While the other ratings are probably more reflective of how the course was previously, Dr. Wilson is really passionate about the course. While her expectations are a little high, she's extremely fair in terms of grading for the course, and is super willing to listen to feedback. Course is pretty discussion heavy but easier than past semesters. 8/10

She is strict with grading, don't mess around. Not an easy class, but she was willing to meet with me for feedback and seems passionate about teaching. Participation plays a part in your grade. Lots of reading, time heavy. Would take again, if possible.

hella assignments over thanksgiving break (async class you technically could do ahead of time, but it was a discussion post everyone else submitted on the due date on thanksgiving break, so not really lol), did not give a lot of time to do the final as peer review part doesn't unlock until finals week bc others have to submit their projects first

I know people have had bad experiences with P. Wilson, but for me the class was incredibly enjoyable. There was definitely a lot of work (the discussion posts were so long, but not difficult if you'd been paying attention in class), but the content itself and the method- meandering class discussion- was so interesting. Participation matters a LOT.

Did not stick to schedule on syllabus. Insane load of homework weekly - discussion boards take up hours and are graded harshly by TA's. Ineffective lectures; discussed the reading for an hour and flipped through the slides the last 15 minutes of class. Given an inadequate amount of time to complete the ending group project. Take with anyone else!

She is a very nice professor and I always looked forward to going to her classes. That being said, if you want an A you really have to go the extra mile. If you're not good at time management than the weekly discussion posts will run you over.

Wilson is one of KFs best professors. This class is not easy and the curve is reflective of that. An A is attainable if you are willing to work-- many discussion posts and participation matters.

Seniors, don't take this class if you are looking for an easy A. Sign up if you want to be challenged and learn from a brilliant and friendly professor.

I think Wilson is better than these reviews let on. The quizzes were sometimes challenging and the lectures were very fast-paced but the class wasn't impossible. The main thing I disliked about the course was that many due dates were on weekends, so you have to be motivated enough to do them ahead of time or do homework basically every Saturday.
One of the most difficult professors at the business school, the quizzes are tough and the discussion posts are almost impossible to get a 3 out of 3. The final exam is also extremely difficult.

In-class participation is weighed too heavily into final grades and accounts for 20-30%, when many students may be shy and have difficulties speaking up. There are frequent discussion posts that are graded very harshly and take an insane amount of time to complete. I would not recommend taking this course with this professor.

One or two questions on quizzes may be tricky, but I don't think they are hard at all. I also skimmed through the readings, which is sufficient for this class. Components that I absolutely hate: long discussion posts and final exam. Just ignore those that write 800-world essay for each discussion. There are more meaningful things in life to do...

Dr. Wilson is one of the smartest teachers I've met. Yes you have to do a discussion post for 9/11 classes, but it's directly based on what was discussed in class and you have 5 days after class to submit. People who complain just don't want to give effort and get bad grades as such. Engage with the material and get a good grade.

Discussion posts for every class, responses are usually 3-4 paragraphs and the average score is an 85 per post. A lot of readings outside of class, quizzes are multiple choice but the final is essays. She pushes you in class when you answer, which I get it's to make you question your reasoning but it feels like shes attacking you in front of class

Your grade comprises of two quizzes, one final, and is heavily weighted on participation. While Prof Wilson can be an engaging professor at times, she is very vague on her expectations, guidelines, and policies. Quizzes are difficult, expect to read more than 50+ pages per week, and discussion post grades can vary. Take another professor.
Take someone else
This class is awful, way too many assignments and readings.

Sweet professor who cares about his students. Only a couple of homework assignments throughout the semester that you can do in groups. Exams are heavily weighted but he curves a ton. Manageable if you can do practice problems and in-lecture practice. Confused by low ratings, he is such a nice guy who wants everyone in his classes to do well!

He is a nice guy but has no backbone. He made the exams but didn't grade anything (all grading done by his poor TA), so it took forever to get stuff back. Cheating was rampant on the final exam. You can tell he wants his students to like him, but he is an inefficient lecturer and bad with technology. He does allow cheat sheets and curves heavily.

Professor Shin really cares about his students' education. 408 has difficult material, but he does a great job explaining concepts. If you pay attention during lectures, you will do well and have a strong understanding of corporate finance outside of just the exams.

The class is just hard but he's cool and loves FRED. I don't know what type of voodoo witchcraft insane formula he curved the final using, but I thought I would finish with maybe a C if I was lucky and I got a B+. I am not like that. He maybe just didn't want us to hate him. One day he will buy that house!

I loved Professor Shin. Busi 408 is a difficult class, but he made the information digestible and less intimidating. All homework is done in groups, and there are plenty of practice problems for the midterm and final. Overall such a nice guy who clearly cares deeply about his students and the course topics.

I loved Professor Shin. Busi 408 is a challenging class, especially for me with no prior finance knowledge, but he made information digestible and less intimidating. Homework is group-based and there's lots of practice for midterm and final. Such a nice guy who obviously cares so much about the subject and his students.

I LOVE Dongwha. I was scared for this class because I'm not a fan of finance, but he really wants you to do well. Lectures are a little hard to follow and he can sometimes go on tangents. However, the expectations are very clear and he gives you all the materials you need to succeed. I highly recommend.

Not hard to earn good grade but class is disorganized. Little practice for concepts that need more than 2 problems to understand. Professor is sweet but if you want to deeply learn the material consider other instructor. Class is focused on applying concepts instead of learning equations, but if you want to take more advanced courses you need both.

Very weird class. Prof is chill but disorganized and prone to digressing, esp when the fratty finance bros ask random questions to flex their niche finance knowledge. Very unclear class and you basically self-study the whole thing, because lectures are not super relevant to exams. Still, very accomodating prof and overall a neutral experience.

Prof. Shin is super chill, obviously super passionate about crypto. He can get off-topic sometimes and can go on tangents on complex concepts that lose a number of ppl in the class. Class was interesting though and I enjoyed the final research project.

Professor Shin is the best!! 408 is hard, but I would 1000% recommend taking it with him. The final is hard and weighted heavy, but he curves a lot. Few long homeworks done in groups, but it's not too hard to do well on them. Real world examples make the content relevant and I always looked forward to class. His energy makes lectures fun!

Professor Shim is such a sweet professor. Those who are giving him bad reviews didn't put in enough time for this class. He even prefaced that he will push you more than other sections, so you can gain practical skills, representing yourself and Kenan in the workplace. As someone not going into finance, I was excited every day to go to class.
Confusing and unnecessarily difficult class. 45% of grade is final and spends the lecture before the final teaching new material. Surprised his rating is 4.5.

Professor Shin is a nice guy, BUT I wouldn't recommend! Although he assigns little homework, this means the class is EXTREMELY test-heavy. You also have to teach yourself everything because the lectures are so confusing. Also, from what I heard from other 408 students and tutors, he teaches different, more complex material than other classes.

He's a nice guy and in theory makes Corporate Finance interesting by bringing in current events. However, he puts practice problems on the board with the solutions on the same slide and many of his answer keys have basic arithmetic mistakes. Not the worst teacher by any means, but lacks basic diligence. Final average is 60 - would take someone else

408 is a hard class in general, but I recommend taking with Shin. He genuinely cares for students, is funny, and will help you out and provide additional resources if needed. Very test heavy but are graded or curved as needed. Not many HWs but they take a long time, but you can work with group. Most of work was studying before midterm and final
phenomenal prof, really vested in students. took him for two classes absolutely love the guy. if you have the opportunity to take a class with shin take him!!!!!
Excellent professor; goated

Prof Shin is the best 408 professor. He provides everyone with resources to succeed and is transparent about his expectations. He teaches challenging concepts in a way that everyone can understand. I highly recommend taking 408 with him.

He is THE BEST for 408, hands down. The content is hard and there is nothing you can do to change that, but he really listens to students feedback and will slow down if you ask him. Literally only half of the class shows up, but going is so worth it because the lectures are easier to follow in person. I love him! Wish I could stay in this class tbh
Everything is extremely fair, give feedback real quick. I am not a math person, but I did better than I thought in this class. My favorite professor!
She is definitely the best professor I have ever met at Kenan Flagler! Would love to take her class again!

She's a really good prof, the material is fairly easy and up until the final its pretty fair. The final was painful also she puts in grades extremely fast (same day we took the final) the final was really hard so just prep for that. I did not hence the grade (had an A all sem)

Dr. Xu truly cares about her students! She teaches at a very fast pace so we always get out of class early. She's very eager to answer questions and make sure students are successful. She also is open to helping students in non-class related things

Professor Xu is a fun and engaging professor. Her class covers all the content you need to know and I felt I had everything I needed to thrive. Class consists of problem sets, 2 midterms, a final, and a group project. the final was the hardest part of the class, but overall, I enjoyed this course and would take Professor Xu again.

Great teacher that clearly cares about her students. Class was pretty straightforward until the final which felt like it was trying to hurt our grades. Dropped a fair amount of people a full letter grade. Just be well prepared for an entirely different final and you're good

I'm so glad I took this class with Professor Xu! I've learned so much over the semester. She's super smart, but what really stands out is how inspiring and encouraging she is. She has this amazing way of making you feel confident and excited to learn, which makes the class even better!
Professor Xu is fantastic! Explains concepts super clearly, is always accessible for questions, and has very fair exams! Genuinely the sweetest professor!
Easy to understand everything. Awesome class.
Great class, take it if you can!
I love this class!

Professor Xu is the best professor I have ever had at KFBS. Materials and exams are hard, but still manageable if you spend a reasonable amount of time studying. She even replied to my question at 1 am!!! Would take any other courses that Xu teaches at KFBS!

Class was extremely misleading. HWs and midterm was quite easy but for some reason, she decided to make the final very difficult with no practice material being nearly as rigorous as the final. Would recommend taking with another professor. There are definitely other sections that are much easier.

Final was brutal given that both midterms were easy and that problem sets were also easy. Xu is really sweet and is a lovely person, but the final really felt like she was out to get us/bring down the class average.
Final absolutely screwed me over by a whole letter grade. Lectures I will say were very understandable, but holy cow, brace yourself for the final to see things beyond the scope of this class.

Yuqian is a great teacher and person, but I disagree with other reviews. Class is extremely test-heavy and the final was surprisingly difficult compared to other exams and course sections. Final dropped my final grade 3 thirds of a letter grade.

Professor Xu is attentive to student's needs and is genuinely just such a sweet professor. She's very fair with midterms and really cares about the wellbeing of students. Please take her class, it is worth your time, and I wished I did more to connect with her.
Xu was probably the best teacher I've had at KFBS. Such a positive person who would always smile and answer any questions I had. PLEASE take her if you have a chance
unbelievably easy class. the content is literally for middle schoolers. Xu is nice and cares a lot about teaching but the fact the class content is so easy makes it hard to rate her low

Professor Xu is an outstanding professor at KFBS. She is clear about her expectations and what she wants you to do to succeed in this course. I learned a lot from this class and her. She is also very understanding and caring. She doesn't make you stay for an entire lecture if it's not necessary. Review all slides and homeworks before exams

Amazing human being and professor. I don't believe there's anyone else you can take 410 (hard class) with that would be better. He is very understandable and tries to make 410 as easy as it can get for students (at a normal level, so study). Really great person if you get to meet him and also a big Man United fan who's very cool to talk to

Dr. Modaresi is a gem in the department. While BUSI 410 did feel like 408 in terms of content difficulty, he was incredibly supportive, passionate, and accessible throughout the semester. Exams are hard &  worth 60% of grade, but he gives past exams which are almost identical tbh. Fantastic prof and wouldn't have gotten an A with anyone else.

While many find the BUSI410 class to be a dread in their course load, Professor Modaresi is exactly the right person to guide you through it. He is incredibly good at explaining the subjects while still being mindful not to miss anyone's questions, even if they don't ask aloud. If you would like a good grade, the requirement is simple: follow along
awesome dude. 410 is not an easy class but he teaches well and is also just a great guy

Business Analytics is a difficult class, but Professor Modaresi does a great job of explaining the material and being accessible for questions. It is a good idea to make friends in this class to collaborate. Modaresi is empathetic and understanding. He sometimes runs through material quickly, but he is good at catching himself.
Pretty boring class with lots of busy work. Final exam is purposely worded to confuse you and trip you up. Avoid if possible

Professor Choi's teaching style made it hard to stay engaged. She didn't seem very invested in the content, and it was sometimes difficult to get in touch with her outside of class. Exam expectations were not always clear. She's fine if you have to take her but nothing special

I did not enjoy Professor Choi. I felt she was not passionate about what she was teaching. Lectures were hard to get through. She wasn't great at answering questions, concepts were ambiguous and wordy. Exams/quizzes were confusing, and multiple answers could've been debated as the correct answers.
The most boring professor at the b school. She sounds like she hates what she's talking about. I seriously could not pay attention in this class. 10/10 DO NOT RECOMMEND
Professor Choi is a great choice for 412.  The class is made up of Case Quizzes, Participation, Final and a Group Project.  She's kind and a good lecturer.  Overall I would recommend.

dont bother buying or reading the textbook. Memorizing the videos and vocab are what you need to succeed for the final and midterm. Group projects are a headache so get started early. Putting in decent effort into projects will get you at least an 85.

Get ready to be graded on random, arbitrary things often unrelated to marketing. I'm surprised some comments call her their second mom; she is pretty scary to me. It's going to be way harder than necessary for you to get a good grade in this class. Take a different prof.

Professor Malhotra is very knowledgable about marketing, and it makes lectures great. The flipped format is helpful for learning, and I find her, and her directions clear. My complaint would be the group cases, as I spent more time fixing others work and formatting rather than actually using marketing strategies. Grading is subjective and unclear.

Claudia is an incredible professor who clearly cares about her teachers and is very passionate about marketing. She always brought energy to the class and it was never boring. The class does have a lot of work and the case assignments can be tedious. The midterm I thought wasn't bad and final was harder. Both very heavy on memorization.

Amazing professor, cares so much about both her students and the material. Her passion and fun in class activities made this one of my favorite classes at UNC. Cases were a lot of work but graded fairly (loved new rubric system). Midterm/final surprisingly hard, definitely study and practice term definitions. Highly recommend, learned a lot!

30% of grade is 3 case studies she grades very tough and also includes an unrealistic page limit. For exams it's literally just hundreds of definitions, which is fine but she creates really niche arbitrary questions that I don't think trust ones true knowledge of Marketing. Very tough but also very nice at the same time. Would never take her again

Claudia is someone that was meant to be a teacher & it is so evident. She is so caring and understanding of her students & I genuinely appreciate her as a human being sooo much. Honestly, I won't say this class is easy, because I didn't find that to be the case. But taking her class was worth it because she is so knowledgable, passionate, & kind.

Claudia is so kind! There are a lot of chapters to get through but she does her best to cover them. I kind of did bad on the midterm & final, but looking back, there was def a way to do better. I recommend rewatching the lectures and using the sharpen app/website to help with vocab. The MC isn't bad, the written portion on exam is where it matters

Claudia is very passionate and knowledgable about marketing. She cares about her students' success inside and beyond the classroom. Group projects are pretty grueling - try and choose a good partner or group if possible. Exams are straightforward and fair. Lectures are lively, interactive, and include engaging in-class activities and guest speakers

Claudia is THE marketing professor. She is knowledgable, spirited, and kind. That being said this class is not an easy A. She lets you somewhat pick your own groups which was helpful and imo the cases weren't too bad. Exams are tough but fair, just study the vocab from the textbook. If you want a career in marketing take 406 with her.

F teacher. If you can apply the key terms (at the end of each chapter in the book), you will do well on exams. Meets once a week (watch all the pre-recordings done b4 class).Very dependent on Case Studies. Try to find hard-working people. You can do well if you do the work and meet with your team b4 the case studies are due.
Claudia is like your mom. She cares about you, your career and has very engaging lectures.

Claudia herself is amazing, but the 406 experience is tarnished by the risk of getting a group of incompetents to be stuck with through the course whose team work and evaluations will account towards at least 35% of your course grade. You can probably tell what sort of group I got. Great class besides that. Don't BS the class & you will have fun.

Claudia is a very kind professor. However, this class stripped me of any interest of marketing. Strangely difficult exams coupled with terrible group projects made this class a drag. Take this class with someone else.

Claudia clearly cares about her students and will do a lot to accommodate them. She genuinely is passionate about marketing and tries to make it as engaging is possible. The exams are extremely difficult and her grading regarding the case assignments is pretty inconsistent. I wish there was more room for growth in class.
This class is harder than you think it will be but she is very kind and good at teaching

Don't listen to the negative reviews! She is passionate about marketing and her students and makes every class fun. Watch the online videos and go through the in-class PowerPoint, you will be fine. Make her given corrections to each report (3 total) and study for the final!( had an A all semester, didn't study bc of easy midterm, ended with a B+).
Take with someone else

Heard a lot of negative things going into this class and heavily considered switching to another professor. Ended up staying in the class and really enjoyed it. Would highly recommend taking it. Claudia teaches the other professors so you might as well take it with her. Exams are challenging but fair, group cases require thinking outside the box.

Prof. Claudia was great! She lets you pick your team for the cases, but her feedback didn't really help us improve. Her exams were much harder than they were supposed to be, and she always tried to trick us on the multiple choice questions. You HAVE to read the textbook for the exams, and it's well over a 1000 pages long so get started early!!

This is a really fun class to take. Greg runs an interesting and engaging improv class, and it is easy to learn and have fun in. After this class, I'm taking away numerous life lessons that I will apply in my life.
Great class, lots of chances to participate, 3 pretty short papers over the course of the semester

This class is a must-take. Greg is great and you will learn more than you have in all the core classes combined. It will force you out of your comfort zone, but that comfort zone will be huge by the end of the semester. Fantastic course.

Amazing class and great experience. The business school would be a better place if all students were required to take improv. Creative, engaging, and unique course that truly helps you improve in ways you can't realize.
GOAT. Best teacher ever. Feels like you are just hanging out with him in class. Class is all participation. Class gets super close which is really fun. Greg is awesome.

If you can register for Improv, take it! While it's an easy A if you participate, you get a lot more than a GPA boost. It gave me something to look forward to each day and our class genuinely connected over the semester. I enjoyed the readings and learned a lot. Greg is a great professor and the reason Improv works so well, can't recommend enough!

This was one of the most challenging yet rewarding classes I've taken at Kenan-Flagler. It pushes you outside of your comfort zone in the best way possible, and you definitely get out of the class what you put in. Jim is also one of the best lectures at UNC with incredible stories to tell, and does a great job of rewarding effort.

Jim Kitchen is inspirational and savvy professor, who is accomplished in entrepreneurship and travel. Very nice person who wants all of his students to succeed and be happy. While I wish the class offered more lectures and technical information, I would absolutely recommend it.

Prof Kitchen is my all time favorite professor. He is wise but so humble and genuinely wants the best for his students. His class was one I looked forward to everyday, and I know I learned equally as much about life as I did about business. This class also gives you a taste of what giving back feels like through his emphasis on profit for purpose!

Professor Kitchen is fantastic and has stories for days, the guest lectures are extremely valuable, and the class projects show that "business planning" is an essential and learnable skill in the context of entrepreneurship.

Jim Kitchen truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He brings in so many guests that have gone through the entrepreneurial journey. Whole class is basically one big project that determines your entire grade.

Professor Kitchen's course was awesome. I enjoyed the hands-on experience as it allowed us to simulate running a business. 100% of the profits go to charity which is awesome. I would preface that the lectures were kind of lame and while it was cool he brought speakers, most of them just say things we already know.

Professor Kitchen is the most impactful professor I've had at UNC. He has a super interesting life that helps you gain perspective. The books in class teach valuable lessons, and the projects are easy to do well on as long as you work hard. HIGHLY recommend

This class was incredible! Professor Kitchen truly cares—he memorized all 70 students' names and held one-on-one meetings. His engaging, motivational lessons changed how I view business. You'll create a real mini-business, work on group projects, and gain hands-on experience. While time-consuming, it's rewarding. Highly recommend!

This class was super interesting because it uses a hands-on approach. While the content itself isn't hard, I realized if I put in the time I could get the grade I want. Other than learning a lot about myself and successful entrepreneurship strategies, the books we had to read were also very useful and are still something I think about to this day.
Amazing class with unique experiences.

BUSI 500H with Professor Kitchen is definitely my favorite course I've taken at Carolina. He does a great job at incorporating the readings and semester-long project to not only teach you about entrepreneurship but life lessons in general. This course is truly a rewarding experience and pushes you to be a creative and innovative thinker.

If you want a rewarding course that teaches real-world skills, take B500 with Prof. Kitchen. You'll gain hands-on experience creating and selling your own products, learning firsthand how to pitch, pivot, and persevere. You'll face lots of rejection—but that's where the real growth happens. Every aspect of this course is designed with intention.

Professor Kitchen is awesome. You will learn so much about entrepreneurship, relationships, and life that go way beyond the classroom. Much of class is hands-on, with projects that allow you to apply what you learned during class. This course requires a lot of time and effort, but if you put the work in you will be rewarded. It's also very fun.

Professor Kitchen is awesome. He's my favorite professor at UNC. I've never taken a class that teaches you more about business. There aren't any exams and grading is project based. You raise money for Make a Wish and it's easy to get an A in the class if you try on the project. You read 3 business books and 2 of them were really good.

Professor Jim Kitchen was by far one of the most influential professors I have had during my time at UNC. You truly get out what you put in and he wants to see you succeed. I loved this class so much and have gained so much from my experience. Cannot recommend enough- take this class!!

I loved this class. You get out what you put in. The readings provide valuable insights on persistence, entrepreneurship, and relationship-building, while projects help you apply them.

Professor Kitchen's passion for teaching and his students is clear. Take this class if you want to grow as a person, not for an easy A.

Jim Kitchen is an amazing professor who often interacts with the class and makes you apply what you learn to the real world. What you learn in this class will stick with you for the rest of your life. Highly recommend to take this course before you graduate.

One of the best classes I've ever taken at UNC. Actually prepares you for life with material in the class plus the readings he provides. It is no easy A but hard work and persistence really pay off. Couldn't recommend Jim more enough.

BUSI 500H and BUSI 500 are the same entirely. Aside from that, Professor Kitchen is an outstanding, spectacular professor, but be warned that his class isn't for everyone. It's truly experimental, where you're expected to put many hours outside of class, but he makes a substantial effort to have a lasting impact on his students, and it shows.
Unlike the other classes, you can actually learning something of entrepreneurship by doing project. Jim is the goat.
She is really nice and is prob the best option for 406. Final was tricky, don't underestimate it.
Professor Koch was great marketing professor and cares about the students while being a fair grader and enthusiastic lecturer.

TAKE KOCH FOR 406 and if she isn't available/her class is full, WAIT UNTIL NEXT SEMESTER TO TAKE 406. She is AMAZING. All other sections who didn't take Koch hated 406, but everyone in my class LOVED HER.

So fair and actually cares about us. LOVE her.

Cases were graded pretty harshly (pretty sure all sections are no matter the prof). Her lectures can be a bit heavy/boring depending on the chapter but she really does try to make the class interesting. She's really nice and midterm+final were fairly difficult. Definitely one of the best professors to take for 406.

She pulls straight from the textbook and so the content you need to know is very clear. You have to participate in class but she asks questions that are fun to answer. There are a couple of case assignments that you have to work in groups for but you can pick your team. One of the best professors I've had at Kenan-Flagler.

I LOVED PROF. KOCH! I was so nervous about taking this class (because I'd heard horror stories from the other sections) but I genuinely enjoyed my time with Professor Koch. She was SO clear on what to expect day-to-day and her lectures were extremely easy to understand.

I cannot stress this enough, GO WITH KOCH if you have the chance!

She was a very clear and to-the-point professor. She taught a ton of content each class but it was very digestible and easy to keep up. The group projects are graded very tough and midterm and final took a lot of studying to do well. She is such a sweet person in and out of the classroom and super encouraging.

There wasn't too much work outside of class, if you do decent on the midterm and try on the cases it should be an easy A/A-. The cases are graded pretty hard, but you get a lot of feedback on each one, and generally grades improve on each case. We also get class off to work on the cases. I really enjoyed Prof. Koch's lectures, always energetic.

While some do say his voice is a little monotone, he's clearly passionate about the subject and really cares. He revamped the curriculum this semester a lot to make it more accessible and interesting to students, and his willingness to change and tinker stuff shows he's super caring of students. Exams are open note and online, albeit a little hard.

Prof. Boysen is clearly very knowledgable about the world of corporate strategy. I really enjoyed the assigned cases and the in-class exercises - they really helped me grasp the course concepts. Prof. Boysen was also always willing to meet with students (even outside of his scheduled office hours). He has been one of my favorite proffesors at KF!
Professor Boysen was one of the kindest professors ever. He makes the class super manageable and I would 100% take another class with him. Definitely take him for BUSI 412!

I think 412 is overall j a boring class in general. But prof boysen is very respectful and knowledgeable in this field of study. He is also SOOO kind and often would bring small treats and gifts to class (which honestly makes my day)! Overall, choose a good project group, and you'll be fine

Professor Boysen is a kind and caring person who repeatedly emphasizes we prioritize our mental health before all else. His attendance policy is relaxed, and he is encouraging of us to schedule office hours for extra help. Reading-heavy with lots of cases and a discussion-based class. I enjoy his sense of dry humor. He loves his daughter! )

Such a good guy and understanding but extremely boring. All the quizzes and exams are online. There's a group project that is relatively easy but a big portion of the grade so choose your group wisely.

Boysen is such a great guy and wants everyone to succeed. The lectures are extremely boring though which is a bummer because it makes it hard to pay attention and learn. Choose a good group for the group project, my group screwed me over :/
Not a good teacher and is in the wrong line of work. Not sure who gave him this job or how he passed an interview to teach at KF. Take 412 with someone else.

The content was difficult to understand, but Prof Boysen is accessible outside of class and wants you to succeed. The weekly quizzes are difficult, but if you go to office hours, he will help you out. If you put forth any effort in the class, you will do fine. He is also funny and breaks up lecture with group activities/Pollev's version of Kahoot.
insanely boring but not hard to get an A if you try

He's definitely passionate and very knowledgeable about corporate strategy but its extremely difficult to understand his course material. His teaching style incorporates a lot of in-class group discussion, but often times the other people in the class were just as lost so it made it harder to learn this way.

Prof. Boysen is very knowledgeable about corporate strategy. However, he has trouble explaining these concepts to undergraduate students, and it boils down to students using his buzzwords without knowing what they actually mean. I believe he is better suited for research as other ratings say, but maybe he will improve in future semesters.

Dr. Boysen is extremely knowledgeable and knows a ton about corporate strategy and management. Classes are reading and case-based and the format is straightforward. Lectures can be long, but breakout groups split up lecture time and he is very supportive. He is really accessible outside of class for office hours and overall is an awesome professor!

Professor Boysen does a great job of making himself available outside of class. You can tell how much he cares about his students and spends a lot of time going over feedback to make his lectures better. He is a little bit shy at first, but is definitely one of my favorite UNC professors!
