Professor Boysen really cares about his students and makes a deliberate effort to be available for office hours and take students' feedback to make his class better. He definitely is monotone/the material is somewhat boring, but he really does his best to make the class as engaging as possible (PollEv activities, group breakouts).

Dr. Williams is super enthusiastic and really cares about her students, and it really shows in the support she provides in class. While the class itself is annoying (401 sucks as a concept), she's a really helpful, and inspiring teacher. Grading is a little strict but as long as you put in like a day for each assignment, it's p easy to get an A.

Yes she's a tough grader, but she GENUINELY wants us to succeed & grow. I learned A LOT in this class. If you truly want to learn something & put in the effort, take this class. Few in-class activities, 4 writing assignments, reading quizzes (3 tries), 3 pres. Final exam is just an evaluation report on your growth. Gives great feedback we can use!

I absolutely would not take this class with Kimberly-a harsh grader and most of her feedback doesn't make sense. Very condescending and chooses not to explain certain things fully to make the class material seem more challenging. Only way to do well is by meeting with her outside of class with her even though her feedback isn't ever really helpful.

TOUGH grader. Lecture heavy, and she does a bit of cold calling, some group work. Overall cool teacher. Class is very demanding though, be detailed with your papers and presentations. Has office hours often so she is available for help.

Harsh grading which is fine but what stood out the most is her general attitude towards students. She is very condescending and doesn't take feedback well. Not an enjoyable class. On the plus side, the grade is distributed over 7-10 smaller assignments instead of a midterm and final.

Very high quality professor, she would go above and beyond for you. She is very impressive. The class content is what it is, but she makes it great. Super nice, super sweet, but unless you are a sweat - you will get a B.

Dr. Williams is very knowledgable and passionate about corporate communication. Her goal is to form real-world business writing skills, so she is a tough grader throughout the course. She is an effective lecturer and is easily accessible out of the classroom. Dr. Williams' class is a great course across disciplines!

Rubric is very subjective
Grading is super loose and relative
Did not learn from lectures
Not very realistic
Somewhat harsh grader but willing to meet for personalized feedback. Assignments were a bit busy work-ish but overall useful information.
Approachable professor but very harsh grader. Very time consuming class for a supposedly easy core course.

Horrendous. Grades wildly unfairly and provides no feedback as to why. Does not round grades at all (89.999 is still a B+) and gives no class curve at all. Her class average sat at a low B. Zero knowledge about business communication and teaches objectively incorrect things. There are a bunch of 401 teachers, find one that won't mess up your GPA.
amazing personality, tough grader, gives great feedback, straightforward and accessible, I have genuinely learned a lot from this class.

Course is graded hard (come into it with this expectation), and she grades every assignment pretty thoroughly with feedback and notes to improve off. Pays to be detail-oriented and making sure you follow all the specific stuff needed in every assignment. Also, Dr. Williams cares about your improvement and is willing to work with you 1 on 1.

Dr. Williams is very knowledgeable, accessible, and outgoing. I had a great time in her class. She is a very harsh grader but is very clear about what she wants on assignments. You will always be able to figure out why you got points off even if at first, it seems like a lot. The class is more work than it seems on the surface with any professor!

He's a great professor. You can tell he really cares about what he teaches. He encourages talking in lecture, but it's very low-stakes. If you do the readings, graded annotations, and take notes in class, the essays will be no problem. He's pretty flexible with deadlines too. I'd say I learned a lot of fun and valuable things in 412 this semester.

The course code is listed wrong, it is supposed to be 412 not 312. The prof is chill and readings are mostly interesting. You're graded by three in class essays, weekly annotations plus a final project.
The most kind and passionate professor I've had at UNC in my 4 years!! He genuinely cares about his students and explaining difficult concepts.

I'm in one of the first classes Doctor Burç has given, and a very he's kind and engaging professor. His class is very reading-heavy with few assignments, and class discussion is suggested but not required. Lectures are interesting (if you enjoy learning about objects with cultural significance) and reading heavy.
Really thoughtful and caring. The readings can be dense, but lectures make things clearer. Grading is fair and not a ton of busywork. If you actually show up and engage, you'll learn a lot.

Class has pop reading quizzes that count towards grade (10%) for accuracy. They are not hard (mult-choice), but can be tricky. Each midterm is 25% and open note. Note that second midterm is on LDOC... You are given prompts and write two short essays. It's very manageable. Final paper is 40%. He grades fairly, but he can tell if you are bs-ing him.

Burç is actually the kindest professor I have ever had. He's super passionate about what he's doing. Expect about 2-3 dense readings per week but can get away with not doing them especially if you ask questions in class. Grades were made up of two essay exams, annotations, and a finals essay.

Great class, basically graded on readings and engaging group projects. Midterm was more than fair and generally a very good class, not difficult, attendance to lecture was not required, only to recitation. 100% recommend this prof for R&D Credit
Best teacher ever

Professor Shapiro is one of the few professors that doesn't require a purchased textbook, but instead provides us with PDFs of the material. He's very thorough and lectures are genuinely engaging. Attendance is mandatory for recitations, not for the lecture. He was very accommodating when I had to reschedule my midterm due to travel conflict.
Nicest professor I've ever had. Take his class for an easy A and interesting material. Super nice about late submissions and missing class.
** Correction to my last review, difficulty is NOT a 5.

Aaron was a gem!! I am a senior and took his Algorithms & Society class with little to no experience with interpreting data and he made sure that even the hardest readings were made understandable. He is so kind, understanding, and I genuinely learned so much in his class. 100% take this class you wont regret it

Took Comm 455: He genuinely cares about students and has an amazing response time to emails. You really don't have to go to class until you get to the end when everyone is giving presentations. There were 3 really easy assignments, a scavenger hunt, a short paper/video about a soundscape, and an essay on any sound topic for the final. 100% take him

Overall, I really liked prof. Shapiro, however if you don't have a background in algorithms/data science I think this class may be hard as just a comm major. It's not horrible and I'm looking to finish with an A or A- but a lot of the information we learned went over my head. I do like prof. Shapiro a lot and he is very knowledgeable.

Such a great guy and his classes were pretty organized. The reading responses were somewhat irritating but that was the hardest thing he really graded within the class. He was very easy to get in contact with and is very understanding. Would definitely take again.

It was cool to learn about algorithms. He is very nice. There are lots of readings but you do not need to do a heavy read on all of them and they are covered in class. You submit reading responses that are graded easily and then there are a bunch of group projects that he gives clear grading criteria and steps on.
The class consisted of 3 forum posts, a midterm, and a final exam, which are not hard at all if you pay attention. One of the most interesting professors at UNC.
The class is a super easy A if you sit through the lectures, midterm and final were both open book. Monje is a nice guy but has a tendency to ramble.

Very kind and knowledgeable, yet I don't feel like I've learned anything in this class which is weird as its a pre-req for many COMM courses. The few things that have been discussed more in-depth I've already learned in other COMM courses at UNC, making me wonder what I'm supposed to get out of this class as someone who is interested in the major.
Poorly prepared, regurgitated msnbc talking points. You can learn way more from just reading any book basically on media studies
Prof Monje the goat. He's so nice and is super understanding.

There were barely any assignments so most of the weight went on the exams, but the exams were open books and open notes, so it's really not a big deal. He tends to rant a lot, but he's really entertaining, and it kept me engaged.
incredibly easy A as long as you're willing to show up to and sit through the required lectures. midterm and final are both open-book. he has a tendency to ramble but he's a nice guy.
Class was easy but attendance is taken every day. The actual class isn't too hard but the lectures are kind of boring.
Nice guy. Lectures can be boring, but he's not a stickler about paying attention. The midterm and final are open-note take-home. No homework. Take this class for some easy hours.

Lecture based - somewhat interesting but can be boring sometimes. Tends to get sidetracked. Loses track of time a lot of the time. Class is graded by attendance (randomly taken), two forums post, a midterm, and a final. The midterm and final were take-home and open-note. Textbook was boring but the new readings he pivoted to were more interesting.

Dr. Monje was very knowledgable for the subject but he often went on long tangents during lecture, they were interesting but often he lost track of time. Grade comes from attendance, forum posts, and tests. Generally an easy grader, but if he detects and AI used you will get a 0.

COMM690: He lectures for the vast majority of class periods unless we are watching something. He does frequently go a bit over class time while he is talking so beware of that. He is not strict on attendance and participation, but by showing up to a good amount of the classes, you can get a 100 for that. Not many grades or clear rubrics-hard grader

David is a super caring guy, and very knowledgeable. The class is a bit lecture heavy but totally worth it, as there are rarely any assignments. Good, easy class for anyone interested in the topic or just needs the credit.
He's nice and makes the material in the textbook easier to understand in his lectures. Not much homework other than a couple assignments a semester, one quiz, and one final.

Dr. Monje is the best! The textbook was verbose but interesting, and the lectures were all about real-world application. Incredibly engaging and applicable to the modern world in nearly every respect. Dr. Monje is so kind and accessible; I found myself chatting with him for half an hour after every lecture. Lenient grader, too. TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

Monje does a great job at making his lectures relatable and easy to digest. There isn't much work, a few writing assignments and a couple reading checks, but as long as you can explain yourself and use applicable vocab you should be fine!
Certified yapper.

Dr. Monje is a very smart man with lots of fun facts up his sleeves. This class is very interesting and low stress. The two midterms and final are open book, open note, multiple choice exams on Canvas that you do from home on your own time. That being said it is a very easy A and a great GPA booster or gen-ed for COMM majors.

Dr, Monje is an amazing professor. He cares about his students and can work with you on any problem that you have. The class is very easy, but you do have to do work with a random partner. His lectures can be a bit boring, but he is very informative. I would take another class with him. Recitation is required and attendance is mandatory.

One of my favorite professors at UNC. he seems like he loves his job and this institution, unlike most professors at unc that act like someone forced them to be here. I 10000% recommend this professor. And for a class I was not actually interested in, he definitely did a good job making the material enjoyable to learn. 10/10
Class is very easy with there being very little work besides the speeches.

Great professor, but an even better person. Made sure to connect to students while also delivering content for the class. Although this content could get a little confusing, the class isn't too tough as long as you show up and participate, would recommend.
Dafna is a very great professor, grades fairly, and provides interesting lectures. Would definitely take again.

This relates to COMM 350. Dafna is the sweetest professor ever and she really cares about her students. The class is lecture only which can be boring at times-- the only critique I have for Dafna is to maybe make lectures more interactive and interesting. She covers material well, though, and I really enjoyed this class
Dafna is super sweet, I had her fall 2021 so my memory is failing me, but pick her if you have to take 170.

(COMM 140) Super sweet and very personable. Not the most engaging lecturer but that will come with experience. Extremely clear with grading standards and prompt with responses. Perfect teacher for gen ed classes.

140. Absolutely loved this class!! If you are a communications major and have to take 140 as one of the three prerecs, Dafna is 100% the best choice! She lectures off of PowerPoints and posts them after every class and the class is split up evenly between PowerPoints , quizzes ( 5 short quizzes throughout the semester) and her midterm and final.

Dafna is an amazing professor! I took COMM 140 with her (there's no option for 140 on rmp so i put down 120) & it was the easiest class I've ever taken. All her tests & exams are from her power points/lectures so you don't even need to read the textbook and she gives tons of extra credit opportunities. She's also such a sweetheart! V flexible too!
There wasn't an option for the COMM 140 course code on here, but I took her 140. She is a great professor and one of the nicest. Definitely wants you to succeed and overall just a great person.

Dafna is a real gem! She really cares about her students, patiently answers questions, and clearly explains hard rhetoric theories. Also nice powerpoints and understanding policies in her class. I would love to take her class again!

I took this class with ZERO experience in screenwriting and had a wonderful time. Professor Wattad is very passionate about screenwriting. He is kind and gives good feedback on your scripts. He does assign homework for each class, but it is easy as long as you do what he asks. No final exam, just a final script. Participation and attendance matter.

Take this class. Nizar was the most understanding professor I've ever had and I looked forward to going to his class everyday. It is a very lighthearted classroom environment, and the work really is not difficult at all, and it is really fun making scripts even if you are a beginner which I was.

I took this class bc I wanted to learn more about screenwriting, and it absolutely changed the way I write in all areas and also the way I think about stories in general. Every lecture was full of amazing advice. Prof Wattad is hardcore about the material, but it's def because he cares so much. And he really values his students! I miss his class!!

Favorite class this semester! He really opens my interest to screenwriting and is why I decided to pursue screenwriting more with the minor! The only thing is I wish he could gave feedbacks on final project, but I guess he had too many stuff to read!
Sweet professor and supportive. Cancelled class quite a bit due to some personal stuff I think. It's a beginner level course so she didn't have us do anything that felt like it was too much!
Great Professor, although we have to study and learn by ourselves sometimes on how to use the cutting means, but she is super caring and welling to help all the times. Warmest Prof I ever met in UNC.

Professor Hondros is the best! She is so fun and really cares about her students' success. 230 teaches you a lot about production and Hondros provides very supportive and in depth feedback of projects. There are 3 projects that require out of class work, but she often devotes a few classes to working on them too. Definitely take a class with her!

Hondros is one of the best in the department. She is very understanding and caring to her students. The class is very interesting and I feel like I was very productive even though it was an entry level comm class. As long as you do your work you'll be fine. Very clear expectations and easy to understand. I feel like I genuinely learned a lot.

Professor Hondros is an incredibly caring and supportive professor. She's always open to new ideas and gives good feedback without it coming off as personal criticism. She is genuinely one of the best professors you could have for COMM230 (shoutout Bree too). It's fairly easy to get an A so long as you put in effort, and she gives extensions!

Kristin is incredibly knowledgeable about the craft and also provides great insight about class registration in the COMM department. There are only about four graded assignments/projects, so ensure you put some effort into those assignments. However, she is not the toughest grader. Class is cancelled a lot, attendance was not mandatory.
Really helpful critiques, lots of new material and many short film projects

Avoid at all costs. While the material is fascinating and the projects are engaging, Professor Hondros is not. She cancelled more than 50% of our classes outright, barely communicated with students or TA's (who were forced to do most of the teaching), and never returned grades, single-handedly ruining what could have been a fantastic class.

I feel like I gained very little and put in a ton of effort to learn almost nothing. Way too abstract and convoluted assignments that are graded harshly and teach nothing about the subject. I was just constantly frustrated and bored.
Unmotivated lectures, pretentious assignments, and no clarity. Grades extremely tough.

If you are a stem major and don't have the mindset for creative thinking, unfortunately this is not the professor for you. Dr. I is very abstract and creative with her thought processes. To others, her guidelines appear to be vague and complex, but she wants to give you ideas and creative freedom. She is very caring and passionate.

Dr. I appears to be very caring and kind. However, I was very confused by her lectures. There are 3 major performances, but your TA gives good feedback on how to improve. This class was a nice brain break for me as a STEM major. I still didn't mind the class and would recommend it.

Gave multiple assignments over university mandated holidays, unclear assignment guidelines, excessive homework for a 100 level course. Currently have an A but not worth the effort. Professor is difficult to reach. TAs were the only saving grace for this course

her speech is very difficult to understand, and on top of the fact that the concepts are all very abstract makes her lectures very confusing. jumps between topics too quickly. the details of the performance requirements are usually incredibly vague and not fully explained until very close to the due date. take this class with literally anyone else.
Very strict on attendance
Way to much homework, think assignments class period everyday, mandatory attendance, and makes the class way harder than it needs to be. DO NOT TAKE

Her lectures can be very boring and convoluted, and she also has a thick accent which can make understanding her a bit difficult, especially in the mornings. Otherwise, you can tell she's very into performance and analysis and if you are too she'd be a great professor.

Easy A. I recommend Irina and Comm160. All TAs are great. Irina does talk quite a bit during lectures and expects student response. Very imaginative and gives feedback on our performances, but occasionally is vague on expectations. Very kind and laid back.

*comm 171* harshest grader ever when the criteria is not that clear. however, she is really passionate about students becoming better speakers/debaters. i thought she was nice, but others found her condescending.

Will give you mid/bad grades without giving clear criteria beforehand on how she will grade you. Like genuinely impossible to get a good grade on any assignment because she just wants to take points off randomly. It's literally a comms class and I've put more effort into this class than any of my STEM classes. Can't do well even if you do try.

Took her for COMM 113 (public speaking). Honestly was a pretty good class and probably one of the more applicable ones to the real world. She's kinda a hard grader and doesn't give out many 100s, but it's clear that she wants you to use the concepts she taught in class if you want a good grade. It would be hard to get an A but easy to get a B.

the class itself is not hard but she grades it like stem class. gives unneccessary b grades to everyone, be prepared to submit something and get a lot 0f 13/15 17/20 etc which over course makes an a impossible.

Dr. Fitz was honestly one of my better professors this semester. her lectures were thorough and to the point, and she was very fast paced. one negative about her is she is very condescending whenever you're not actively one of the all star student vibes, recently i was left out of a group so i joined a new one, and she said it was my issue? idk
Easy
Professor was straight forward, clear expectations and a good lecturer.

She seems generally out-of-touch with teaching college students, despite having lectured at other colleges. She assigned us a midterm over fall break and a group project over Thanksgiving break!! She also seems determined not to give people As unless their work is absolutely perfect. She'll take off points for things that aren't on the rubric.

DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES WITH HER. I feel like she truly does not want students to succeed. She is an extremely nitpicky grader and does not give clear expectations (contradicts herself often). I'd show her my work before it was due, she'd say it was perfect, then give me a C. She talks to us like we're 5-year-olds, which is extremely aggravating.

One of the harshest grading profs I've had. Her rubrics seem clear but she takes off points for absolutely no reason and doesn't explain her reasoning half the time. Super condescending and talks down to you although she tries really hard to seem sweet and understanding

She acts extremely nice and understanding in class but then grades extremely harshly and nitpicks everything you say or do. Her assignments were convoluted and not related or relevant to the course. Told the class numerous times she gave bad grades (60s/70s) on purpose because they were "only a small percentage of the final grade." girl what

Genuinely one of the most aggravating professors I've had here. Extremely specific and nitpicky when it came to grading, yet entirely unhelpful when you ask her what to do to fit that criteria. Condescending and honestly hard to be around because of the fake nice act she puts on. There are so many better profs in this dept, take them instead.

Honestly the worst professor I've ever had. She puts on this pick me front like she loves everyone but then will grade super hard behind closed doors. She also gives pop quizzes which were just hard and unnecessary. Literally when we had the sh**ting on campus she gave a pop quiz on the first day back in class. Like are you serious right now...

Megan was adjunct this semester. Took this class as a senior elective, but it ended up being more intensive than my 500-level major-specific classes. Her grading strategies are questionable... tries to preach to her understanding of students but it feels very fake.

Saw her ratings from other universities she was previously teaching at greatly varied, but to kick off the UNC one- not terrible, but not good. Lectures are unorganized & grading scale is strange, she'll take off 5pts from a paper bc of punctuation errors. She acts very caring but it seems performative, there's better profs to take if you can.
Really good professor.
uninspiring
Class could have used more depth.

Most classes involve him just standing and lecturing. He makes himself seem as if he is accessible outside of class, but its ironic that hes impossible to reach. He will post assignments last minute, take foreverrrrrrrrrrr to grade papers and give you only a day with feedback to write a new one, and doesn't respond to emails.

Caring professor that honestly has a lot of insight and commentary in various type of media research. Class was heavily based on readings and presentations by students but he was very engaging and led discussion as well. Final included a research project that we got to work on throughout the semester on a topic we choose that was media related.

Prof Palm is a great professor, especially for FYS like COMM 89. He's great at leading discussions so it's better to read the readings. He cares a lot for students and the subject. The grading is not harsh at all and he's very accessible to meet outside of class.

Professor Palm was a very caring professor and placed high importance on trying rather than being perfect which I greatly appreciated. He wanted to see everyone succeed and learn which made the course very enjoyable and less stressful than many other classes. He was very accessible and was kind to all students.
She was awesome! You can tell she really cares about your learning. Not an overly harsh grader and wants you to succeed.

One of my favorite professors at UNC. She is super accommodating and easy going. She explains the research process very well making it easy to understand. Would 100% recommend her class especially if you are looking for a research credit!

Professor Robertson is the best!!! She is truly so caring, flexible, and kind. The course is pretty easy, with some in-class reading quizzes that you honestly can do fine on without reading (common sense for the most part). Take a course with her for sure!!!

I haven't finished the course yet, but I'm almost finished with it. SUCH A GREAT COURSE! I'm taking it during a summer session, with daily readings, which are easy to comprehend and fit right into the final and unit quizzes. Such a sweet and caring professor, take a course with her.

Madalena was the TA for COMM 120, and we really had a fun connection this semester. I haven't ever had a connection with a TA like I did with Madalena,which was so fun for me. I was able to learn so much from her. The class had a major paper at the end of the semester, and she was so excited about my work, and was great encouragement. Love her!

I really enjoyed his lectures. He was pretty engaging and made confusing theories and concepts relatable and easy to understand. There is a good amount of reading and notes but I highly recommend doing them. Overall the class was pretty straightforward and a good start for the comm major.

Professor May is an amazing lecturer, people have a "just get it done" attitude in this class, and it is unfortunate. He makes difficult concepts easy to understand. He is extremely accessible outside of class, I once emailed him about the lecture slides, and he got back to me within the hour with the slides from that chapter and the one after.

Hereallycaresabout the topic butsometimes overexplainedwhatsomethingmeantmaking it a bit confusing. He hosted review sessions before the midterm and final as well as giving us a list of the topics that were going to appear. Youhavetoread a lot, but I gotawaywithnotbyjustpayingattentionto the lecturesandtakingnotesbecausehetalks about the readings.

Professor May is so passionate about communication, and he cares about students so much. He took every email, feedback after class, and students' needs seriously. The course itself may not be that difficult, and going to the review session is almost equal to an A on the test, super helpful!!! 100% recommend Prof. May

I think I lost brain cells during his lectures. Better off doing poppers. 2 essays, midterm, and final exam= entirety of your graded work. Very easy and only requires common sense; no reading of textbook is necessary. The recitations felt like I was at summer camp. Cannot believe this is a required college-level class, a 10-year-old could pass it.

Dr. May is very kind and passionate about communications! He is very knowledgeable and respectful of students. The class is lecture-heavy and can be boring, but you will learn a lot about theories of communication from this class. Midterm was tough but final was easier. Take class with Steve May!

Steve was phenomenal. You can tell he cares about his students and he gives professional help in office hours (cover letters, resumes, job connections, etc.). It's a two-person presentation, a paper, midterm, and final paper. He wrote the textbook and it's very well done, you just have to purchase. Interesting and engaging class!

Very easy class but repetitive (nonmandatory) lectures and unproductive (mandatory) recitations. Very easy class but graded on few things so make sure you put effort into the few papers/exams. He made the final open note/at home because some people didn't do as well as he intended on the midterm which was super nice. Very caring guy and gave EC.

He is knowledgeable and passionate about his teachings. Fairly easy class, note taking during lectures can be important as there is not much info on the slides to look back on. The nights before the midterm and final he hosted exam reviews which was very helpful as it was an opportunity to ask any questions we had which he would answer in detail.

Professor May is an awesome professor and he taught this class very well. Two lectures a week  (not mandatory attendance) and one recitation a week (mandatory). Only graded work we did all year was discussion form responses every other week and two four-page papers. Midterm is a mix of multiple-choice and T/F and final is four essay questions.

this class was easy and a good filler/elective credit. The professor is nice and the content isn't that hard. Sometimes we had guest lectures. Attendance to lecture is not mandatory but recitations are. Mainly just discussion posts about the reading but you only have to skim it. There were two papers that weren't hard but took a bit of effort.

I took COMM100 with him. He is a great professor, but I am not a communications major, so this class was soooo boring. 2 papers, a midterm, a final, and a few discussion posts. Super easy class though.

Professor May is amazing. He's kind and passionate about what he teaches, and he makes sure it's applicable to your future. Class time is group work discussing organizations through different metaphors and answering questions about entering the workforce. Midterm, final, and one ten page paper, each 30 pts w/ 10 pts for attendance. Take this class!

Steve May is the best professor I have had during my 4 years at UNC. He is incredibly educated and it shows in his discussion. He is also very caring and takes time in class for students to ask questions regarding jobs and interviews. If you get a chance to take one of his classes, do it.

Possibly best professor I have ever had. Perfect mix of professional and caring. Clear grading instructions, do them and it is hard to not get an A. First month is reading and lectures, but the rest is presentations - no mandatory HW after you present in your pair. One 5 page paper, short essay midterm, and the final is a 8 page paper. Not hard tho

Dr. May is so kind and extremely available. He will look over your resume, advise you in your career, and is very connected in the business world. 10/10 prof and I would take all of his classes! He is knowledgeable & reasonable, do speak up in class discussions for participation though. Material is based on ethical dilemma case studies.
Amazing professor, and more than willing to help with personal things outside of class. Top 5 professors i've had at UNC no doubt and the class is SO interesting!!
He was really nice and the class was interesting. You do not have to do much on the day to day but there's a few papers, a big presentation, and a couple small assignments.

Steve is the absolute best, so helpful and insightful. He is very well connected in the business world and you can always come to him for those types of questions or help. The class was based upon different case studies, done in partners which was fun and pretty easy. Would take this class AND professor again, 10/10.

He doesn't take attendance. Says participation matters but I showed up to 5 classes and spoke maybe 3 times and got a 93 for participation at the end of the semester. Midterm is multiple choice and based primarily on the textbook/readings/lectures he does. Final is a paper, papers are fairly easy. Overall pretty good and you can skip & still pass.

Victoria leaves extremely ambiguous and rather unnecessary comments on the assignments in this class. She repeatedly claims to not understand concepts that had been laid out throughout the assignment, and needed constant re-clarification to reduce the loss of points. It is hard to understand what she's looking for because it is constantly changing.

Attendance is very important, and you have to participate and talk each recitation. Her feedback for assignments is very vague but it is clear she is looking for something very specific which she does not always tell you. Once you understand what she wants the recitations are easier, but she doesn't make this very easily known.

Recitation instructor. RMP reviews had me worried, but she was a fair grader with exams and weekly participation (80% for showing up, full points for speaking at least once). She also created a great classroom environment by leading discussions on sensitive topics.

This is for COMM 450. She will give you grades well below what you should have gotten. She has no rubrics and incredibly vague guidelines for assignments. She will give little tangible feedback and the difference between getting an 85 or 78 is completely unknown. If it is possible, avoid this professor.

I took this course online, and to be as tough as a grader that she is, she gives ZERO feedback. I technically ended with an 87, but thankfully the final grade was curved. These assignments were dreadful and so unrewarding to get no help or feedback. I would not have done well on my final essay if it weren't for her not being the one to grade it.
I took her online, so we didn't interact much. But I will say she really did seem to care about her students.

This class was not the worst class ever, but the rubrics for the speeches can be a little unclear. Along with this, her office hours aren't always entirely helpful because she does not give specific feedback that goes from your speech specifically. Overall, not a bad class. I also never read the textbook ever even though it was required.

Greatest class I've ever taken. Most classes are just him telling stories about his life -- which is super interesting. The class is like an interactive stand-up comedy show that gives you a super easy A for very little work. (VERY little)

Mike Acosta is an incredible teacher. Class is never boring and he actually cares about each student. He has a wealth of knowledge and shares it in an understandable way. He emphasizes that the class is to grow, and you don't have to stress about turning in perfect work. You can genuinely learn. If you can take a class with Mike, do it.

He was by far the best professor I have EVER had at this school. I am a premed stem student and I took this class as my sanity class and it was the best decision. I enjoyed this class so much because of Dr. Acosta. The content and the class were enjoyable but it was Dr. Acosta who brought the class to life.

What a guy. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC. Acosta cares so much about his students. The man has lived three different lives and has countless hilarious stories he loves to share. He is so knowledgeable and inspirational, and he feels more like a friend than a professor. Cannot recommend him enough. Amazing final lecture too.

One of the best teachers I've had at UNC! Acosta tells hilarious stories that connect back to screenwriting and gives very good advice for life in general. He's very knowledgeable and truly cares for students and their education. Take this class if you can!!

Dr. Acosta has been the best professor I've had at UNC thus far. He is so funny and actually cares about us as students, which you don't see from the other professors at UNC. The lectures were so funny and he related it to screenwriting, which allowed me to learn in a way that I haven't in any other class in my life.

He has some of the most engaging lectures and every class he'll tell an incredible story. Assignments are graded for completion so as long as you submit them on time you'll get an A. He makes the group projects fun and I learned a lot over the course of the semester. Left the class with a new outlook on life.

Acosta rocks. He has lived a thousand lives and has the best anecdotes. As long as you really try in his class, it will pay off. If you're even slightly interested in screenwriting or movie production, take a class with him! He has a lot of valuable knowledge and advice about the industry, great guy!

Mike is and will probably continue to be the best professor I have had at UNC. While I am really bad at regularly attending my classes, this course is one I made sure to always go to. Not necessarily because I have to, but because I wanted to and looked forward to it. He is genuinely caring and pays attention. I could write so much more about him.
Professor Acosta is the best professor I have ever had. He is entertaining, funny, and knows what he is talking about. You must take his class if you get the chance!!
BEST PROFESSOR AT UNC!!!

Professor Acosta is one of the most influential and memorable professors at UNC. He has a plethora of knowledge about screenwriting and tells incredible stories in class. If you attend class and apply his notes/feedback, you will do good. I only hope I can take him again.

I truly believe Professor Acosta's classes have taught me more applicable knowledge than any of my others combined. Between learning how to screenwrite from scratch, to all the life skills he tries to instill in his students, I am thankful to have been a part of WSS and to have learned from him the past two years.
Mike is awesome. It's clear he cares greatly about his students. He is here because he actually loves teaching. He knows so much about screenwriting. Take this class.

Laid-back, witty, smart, cares deeply about film and his students. Some may dislike his blunt, old-school attitude but I appreciate that he always says exactly what he thinks. Cultivates a genuine connection with students and turns lectures into a conversation, making every class engaging and fun. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC.

Mike is the best professor I've had at UNC. He's hilarious, and his bluntness is never insensitive. He really cares about his students and treats them like the young adults they are. He's been a hugely influential mentor. He's not an Ivory Tower professor - he's pragmatic, no-BS, and empathetic. Take as many classes with him as you can.

One of my favorite professors I've ever had. That said, there's not much middle ground with Mike, I find that people either really vibe with him or they don't. He's got a really refreshing perspective on teaching and the industry as a whole and you'll learn a ton from him. He loves his students and wants them to succeed. Take a class with him!

Super hilarious and very knowledgable about the industry, I recommend this class for anyone who is interested in screenwriting, even if you don't plan on applying to the minor. Mike also makes it a point to give the class opportunities outside of school to gain industry experience. Class is not hard as long as you put in effort.

Professor Acosta is hilarious. Constantly made me enjoy my time in his classroom and was very caring when it came to students learning. He gave great feedback that helped me improve in screenwriting and even tried to give opportunities outside of class for students to expand their portfolios.

Professor Acosta is my favorite professor I've had at UNC so far! He was hilarious, encouraging, gave very applicable and useful lessons, and got the whole class excited about screenwriting. Assignments were very doable and graded for completion. I highly recommend taking a class with him if you get the chance.

His lectures are very funny and engaging, but he can go off track at times, which makes some concepts harder to follow. His presentations can also be difficult to study from. The class overall felt manageable, but much of the grading (including the midterm and final) was done by TAs, so your experience may depend on your TA.

Christian Lundberg was my favorite professor out of the 3 for IDST132L. The class, however, is very TA dependent as the midterm and final are graded by them. Very fun class to listen to, most of the readings you won't have to read, but there are a select few (they will make sure you know which) that you should read.

He's just a genuinely great guy, and super personable. I'm taking one of his classes next semester. Probably one of UNC's best profs. His lectures are really interesting too, he's a great public speaker. I had a great TA as well, and just thought it was a good class. I always attended his lectures, even with attendance not being mandatory.

Dense readings here and there, but he had the most interesting and applicable viewpoint. The midterm was to define terms, then recap a specific reading for each professor. You get to make an exam aid for the midterm and the final, and they give you the questions.
A very easy class to get an A. Don't have to go to lecture at all. End of semester quiz was really easy. He allowed us to have a take home final.

One of the easiest classes I've taken at Carolina. For lectures (1x week), either show up or just skim the textbook. For recitation (1x week), you give 3 speeches of your choice. Do these and you get an A!

Really great professor, I learned so much. Lectures were only once a week and recitation once a week. Easy to do well on all the speeches with a little bit of effort. One of my favorite classes this semester, I would def recommend taking more classes with him! Wonderful experience.

I took this for communication beyond Carolina credit, easiest class ever. Only 3 speeches graded by TA, and you pick the topic. Overall, I learned a lot and enjoyed this class! No homework other than preparing for speeches. The final was take-home and you write what you learned in the class. He also recommends his textbook but you don't need it.
Easiest class ever, if you can confidently speak for five minutes three times its an A. 100% would recommend.
Lundberg is very chill. He is one of the most eloquent people I have ever heard lecture. I had him for IDST 132 "Science in Hyperpartisan Times". Really interesting class, definitely recommend.

He was one of the professors in my triple I and he is actually amazing. His lectures were engaging, fun, and educational. I learned so much from him and it wasn't hard. Anyway, if you get a chance to take a class with him, I'd say do it.
Dr. Lundberg is a legend, his lectures are well developed and insightful. He's a reasonable guy and doesn't include all the waste of time bs that fills so many classes

He's moved to Wake Forest University. By FAR the worst Communications professor here. Like everyone said, he'll find any reason to miss class. Seemed possibly reasonable, like maybe a bad year, until I read other reviews. I've had about 3 classes with the guy in person. His lecture is so unnecessarily complicated it hurts. Avoid.

I saw a lot of bad ratings on Professor Watts and was a little worried going in but I took the class anyways. I didn't have trouble with him personally and he was a very nice person. He had to cancel class and send in recorded lectures instead often but he always had a valid excuse. I very much dislike subjects like this but I enjoyed his class.
Worst professor at UNC

Professor Watts is really nice and is passionate about the subject. Right from the start, he told us he's used to teaching 400+ level courses. The grading was completely decided by the TA you had, and there wasn't a specific structure they had, so it completely depended on the TA. if you work hard & go the extra mile (for a 100 level) you'll pass.

Professor Watts really is a nice guy but this class was extremely difficult. This class consists of three homework assignments and two exams. His lectures are consumed with him talking and the power points make no sense. The TAs take a very long time to grade assignments. The grading is also extremely harsh, would not recommend this class.

This guy flaunts his previous teaching accomplishments, but you'll wish a grad student was teaching instead. Horrible with grades and condescending if you ever ask a question. 3 homework assignments and 2 tests and you can't put grades in by end of semester? Lectures and info given is very vague, leaving you high and dry for tests. DO. NOT. TAKE.

Professor Watts is a genuinely kind person. However, he treats this intro REQUIRED course like an expert-level class. The material is complicated and confusing, there are very few grades, and he and the TAs are the harshest graders I've had at Carolina. I haven't spoken to anyone who feels differently. Save your GPA, and don't take this class.

One word if you are considering taking COMM 170. DON'T. Trust me. This class is terrible. Maybe COMM 170 would not be that bad with a different professor, but Eric Watts is not a good professor. His grading is very unclear. My TA was very hard to reach. Their grading was extremely tough. Teachers like this are what can ruin one's experience.

This guy is probably the worst teacher here. He may be a nice guy, but he is an awful professor. There are three homework assignments and two tests. The power points are extremely vague which makes the test extremely hard. He is also a ridiculous grader. If you are a COMM major, do not take COMM 170 as one of the requirements. Awful experience!!!!

I truly like Eric Watts as a person and enjoy his lectures, but the grading is terrible. There are only 3 assignments and 2 exams for the whole semester. There is less than a month left of school, and we do not have a single grade in the gradebook. This is unfair and I am probably going to have to pass fail. Avoid Watts in COMM 170 if you can!

I had him for my recitation and it seemed like he wasn't into the class or tired. He would talk in a monotone voice and we would have to do group assignments. Nothing particularly graded but just discussion in the class. At least it was chill and he would end class early in some occasions and for the last class we watched an episode of New Girl.

Great professor, classes were engaging and was mindful about not overloading with unnecessary information. Tuesdays were typically lectures and Thursdays group work/written project. Almost always got out of class early, some were on zoom. 4 in-class writings, 2 others that were longer, a group debate, micro-presentation. Overall easy and fun class.

He is a super chill guy. We usually had Fridays off and would get out early the other days. His lectures were very boring, but the class was easy overall, so it was worth it to take his class. Most people taking it are student athletes because it is an easy class.

Daniel was a really relaxed professor who placed an emphasis on growth during the course. As long as you put yourself outside your comfort zone and showed respect to your fellow presenters, you'll do well in this course.
He's a g

If you just want an easy grade, yeah, he's not the prof for you. Go take some pushover. But if you want to actually learn how to speak or write, he's helpful. He's very generous with his time outside of class, sometimes talking for over an hour if you need it.

Teaches nothing but the will to die. I CANNOT STRESS ENOUGH NOT TO TAKE HIS CLASSES. Unapproachable and rude. I consistently felt as though he was teaching a lot of nothing, then expecting an unattainable amount of work and careful thought with no content.
biased grader takes his hatred for life out on his students because he had an affair and a child and lost his pastor job at a church.
I had fun and learned a lot.

He is a great man! In my opinion, the lectures are very irrelevant to the final. Our entire grade was based on 2 papers, a final, a group project, and participation, which scared me. However, he was a very fair grader and even curved the final, which I found to be difficult. Not an easy A class, but good. The final is over 700 pages of the textbook

very easy class and material. for all projects and papers the criteria is clear but the prompts are very open to your own imagination. he's very funny and engaging and you could just sit back and listen to his lectures and fully grasp the course content without taking notes
Enjoyed and learned a lot! Would recommend. Curved the final and graded fairly.

Ian is one of the most friendly professors I've had. He engages students with class materials by asking relevant personal preference questions about pop culture. Plenty of opportunities to participate in class. 2 Essays, 1 group presentation, 1 exam. Essay and presentation topics were fairly open; he cares about what you're interested in and think.
Such interesting lectures and such a caring and fun guy!
Very nice professor - give clear instructions and care a lot about students

Ian is awesome - humble, hilarious, caring, and approachable. He deeply understands pop culture across generations and connects it to theories, inspiring us to think about the world through class concepts. He encourages discussion, grants lots of autonomy and extra credit opportunities. Genuinely cool prof who treats students as equal counterparts.

I had him for comms 89. He was good, he had to start halfway through the semester for my class so it wasn't his fault. I think he was scrambling just as much as the rest of us. But he is nice and gives good feedback. He just wasn't in his element.

She is a super nice professor and she will help you if you don't understand things. Workload was fairly light- the hw isn't always helpful but its always super easy. helpful to use chat to break it down when its confusing. Quizzes and exams were superrrrrr easy- she gives you a refrence guide telling you exactly what to know- so just know that!!

She's a great professor who genuinely cares about her students. There's alot of homework and the exams are tough, but she's always willing to help and makes sure you understand the material. When I needed accommodations after an accident, she was very supportive. She is very friendly, approachable, and fair—just be ready to participate and keep up.
The class is not easy but she makes sure everyone understands the material. Participation is important. She is a great professor but there is daily homework's
not a very friendly teacher, other friends in classes would get small cards to help them on quizzes and other exams like oral quizzes. Good teacher, but another teacher would definetely be better
Very fun class even if you don't enjoy Spanish. She makes sure everyone knows the material in class and is attentive to students needs. Homework is informative and good (but not fun) practice.

As a Latino myself, Tanner has literally been the most supportive person in my life when it comes to learning Spanish. He is literally like talking to a Tia and he does an incredible job being so charismatic and supportive. The department makes all the assignment guidelines, but he is very lenient with grading as long as you participate. TAKE HIM!

Tanner is genuinely my king. Do whatever is humanly possible to have him as your professor. He's super nice and funny and he makes class very engaging. Participation matters and he rarely gives out 100s, but he really wants his students to succeed so he's super lenient with deadlines and partial credit.
Amazing professor would definitely recommend!

Very passionate about languages and teaching! Makes class fun and is a chill grader. Slow grader for bigger assignments, but will always give you an extension to make up for it. Participate in class and turn in textbook homework on time and you'll be fine.

Take this man if you get him, honestly probably for whatever course he is teaching. Super caring and chill. Was very lenient when it came to turning things in a little late and honestly just there to see you succeed. Just participate in class! I hadn't taken a whole lot of spanish before but I felt fine and learned a lot in the end

(I was in SPAN261)

Tanner is a very easy professor. He's friendly, hilarious, and gives great feedback on your assignments. He is a bit harsh on grading and likes to give out 90s a lot, so your grade can drop to a B easily. In class, there's homework assignments pretty much every night, but they aren't too hard. He does grade participation.
Tanner (who may go by Joseph on Connect Carolina if you're confused) is the BEST. Take his class. I don't have a bad thing to say about him.

I LOVED Tanner! He made lectures exciting and funny, which made learning feel so much more engaging. He was always willing to help and would ask if we wanted to redirect the class to areas we struggled with to make sure we did well on quizzes and exams. I genuinely felt supported throughout the course. Highly recommend! Office hours are great too.

I loved French 102 with Mr Bourne, super funny and class went by so fast with jokes and made everything super interesting. Loved learning with him! 4 quizzes, final exam, and oral exam with some papers, more work than 102 but enjoyable.

Great teacher! Tanner is so energetic and passionate about languages, it makes coming to class much more enjoyable. He's very encouraging and will continue to explain things in different ways until the class understands it. Absolutely take this class with him if you get the chance!!

100% recommend! SO funny, caring, easy grader, and personable. The class is fully spoken in Spanish, but he truly does make it so easy to pick up on. Doesnt care if you mess up, just wants you to try. 3 exams graded easy, 1 oral interview (chill), and 1 composition + revisions. Fabulous teaching method. Approachable and caring. Take 203 with him!

Easy class for me just because I did most of the content already in HS. Amazing professor who made the lectures more fun and interesting. One of the best professors during my first year. Would 100% take his class if you could.

Tanner is energetic, funny, and clearly cares about his students. He showed up to class everyday ready to teach spanish and created a carefree class environment that made it easy to ask questions and mess up. Otherwise, the course load was minimal and the tests and quizzes were not bad. If your'e going to take 203 you want it to be with Tanner.

I had Tanner for SPAN203 and I would definitely take this class over again. Tanner is always energetic even at 9am and he made the lessons very engaging. He is very accessible outside of class and willing to work with you. Tanner is one of my favorite professors I've had so far. Definitely take his class.

Great guy and good professor; made things easy to understand. Only subbed for my Spanish class for about 6 weeks, but I would definitely take with him again. My only complaint was that he was practically impossible to reach by email.

If I could repeat this course again, I wouldn't even think twice about it. This class definitely made my semester as Tanner is absolutely hilarious and caring towards all his students. As long as you put the work in Tanner is more than happy to help you succeed.

I took Tanner for SPAN 203, and he deserves all this praise. I have taken Spanish for over six years; this was the first time I wanted to engage in class. He is hilarious and makes Spanish a concept that everyone can understand. Literally, show up, participate, complete the work, and you will be fine.

Take Tanner for Span 203!!! He is absolutely hilarious, and is one of the kindest people I've met. He makes the class as easy as he can, and uses fun activities to help teach the concepts. Homework is very manageable, and classes were always fun. Tanner is incredibly kind and down-to-earth, and is overall a fantastic professor!

I had Tanner for SPAN203 and it was the best decision! He is fun, caring, and not at all difficult. He understands that its a hard class (especially if you haven't taken spanish since high school like me). He helps out so that everyone does well! As long as you entertain him and get your point across you'll do great! Take Tanner's class!!!

I have tanner for 203 and he is one of the funniest people I have ever met, although its hard because every spanish 203 class is hard he makes it more enjoyable to go to class because he has good lectures. every spanish teacher has to make 5 quizzes for thier class and all of ours so far have been take home and very easy.
Dr. Shade makes spanish so fun, you have an oral interview, a composition and two exams. You should take her!!

Dr. Shade is the sweetest professor I have had at UNC. She makes everything super approachable and not intemidating at all. She was a little bit inaccessable outside of class but thats the only negative about her class. If you have the choice, take her, she is so kind and not a tough grader.

Professor Shade is a great educator. I learned so much in her class and felt comfortable participating. Her homework assignments are concise and help you learn a lot. Review the vocabulary regularly and you will do great in this course!

She's genuinely one of the nicest people I've ever met. I tried to get into her class for next semester but it filled up immediately. If you can take 101 with Prof. Shade, do it!! You will definitely not regret it.

She is the most caring and lenient professor ever. She really wants you to succeed. She is the sweetest person on Earth and would never make you feel bad for answering incorrectly. As long as you participate in the lectures, it is easy to get an A.

Take Dr. Shade! She made 105 such a breeze and made sure we were prepped for all of the exams. Super caring and wanted students to actually succeed. The class is light if you can keep track of the homework and have a good Spanish foundation, but you might have to grind if you don't.

Such a wonderful person and truly cares about her students. Made learning so much better, and does not make you feel bad if something is wrong but simply helps you correct it. As long as you participate in class and do the homework you'll be fine.

Take SPAN 101 with her if you can!! She is the most kind, funny, chill professor ever. Made Spanish significantly easier to learn and I suck at languages. Homework due weekly online as well as quizzes every once in a while but the textbook is so easy to follow. Loved this class with her.

Great professor. She not only cares about the subject, but genuinely cares about her students. During class we review and do lots of practice in groups. It is essential you learn the terms before you come to class to get the most out of it. A very fair grader tells you what you should expect. She doesn't respond fast to emails just ask in class.

Her study guides were very similar to the test and she is so sweet! However, the class is WAY too short and I was teaching myself Spanish every single week. Quizlet is your best friend because you don't do any learning in class, she also does not respond to emails very well.

She is a very sweet person and really cares about each student. But the class was super hard and she graded very strictly. Considering it was Spanish 101 she expected us to learn way too much. She also never responds to emails. Overall she is a good teacher but the class took me hours to study for and is very information-packed.
Great professor. Super sweet

Easily the sweetest professor I've ever had however not the best teacher. I found myself having to teach myself Spanish and all she did was go over briefly what we looked at in the textbook. She is also basically totally impossible to reach outside of class.

Very nice teacher but she makes you buy her textbook which costs $65 and is not that good and contains errors in it. maybe its different in the fall and spring but in the summer she does not respond to emails at all. Just not that good of an experience

So kind and helpful. Helped me when I kept mixing things up with french. Is super encouraging with trying to speak and is so supportive. Always there for help outside of class. I learned so so much. Try to get her class!! She is an angel, I wish all professors would teach like her. Cannot recommend enough !!

Pros:
- Easily the sweetest professor I've had
- Made Spanish fun
- Exams were online
- Lots of talking opportunities in class

Cons:
- Homework website was awful

How to study: Her study guides were goated. Also go to her office hours

Outstanding Professor! She makes learning another language fun and engaging. She does look for participation and attendance so keep that in mind. However, she is most definitely the easiest and best Professor to take for any Spanish classes!

She is super sweet. Everything is manageable. You only meet for 50 mins once a week which is tough. The only thing I don't like is that it takes forever for her to grade your stuff and she does not respond to emails. All tests, finals, and homework were online/zoom.
Not a hard class at all. Easy to reach. Easy exams. Homeworks are a little tough. Lots of assignments that creep up on you

This class overall wasn't bad. All my exams even final were online. She is so so sweet but is sometimes hard to reach outside of class. You have weekly videos and homework assignment which shouldn't take more than an hour.
Very kind professor who genuinely cares about her students. Teaches you about the language as well as events in Latin American countries. Would recommend to anyone who needs to take this course.
Paola is awesome, she explains grammar points very clearly and is understanding of mistakes.
Love her! Very sweet professor. She made me feel much more confident speaking Spanish. I don't like the way UNC structures Spanish courses AT ALL, but taking 203 with her is your best bet.

Prof. Pardo is absolutely great for Spanish! As long as you try, you will do fine; she gave me an A on our oral exam that I completely waffled through. Spanish curriculum is tough, with a lot of different assignment types, so don't fall behind, but Pardo tries to make the class as low-stress as possible. Lots of review material for tests.

100% take span203 with her if you can! Super helpful feedback given and clear about the concepts we learned. Very reasonable grading, fun class activities, and I greatly improved my speaking abilities this semester!

She is an incredible professor and is so so kind. I felt that grading was very reasonable and you did not have to spend a ton of time outside of class. She genuinely wants you to do well and will not embarrass you for making mistakes. I had heard horror stories about Spanish at UNC, but I absolutely loved taking it with her.

Great professor!! If you can take Spanish 203 with her, 100% do it. I am really bad at Spanish, and her class was not super challenging. She tries to help you succeed and wants everyone to end up with a good grade.

Sandra was so kind and understanding. SPAN 203 is a challenging class, that's not her fault though. All she cares about is that you try your best, even if it means speaking every other word in English (what I had to do but still got a 98 for participation). Homework can be kind of annoying but it's not overbearing.

Profe Pardo is my favorite professor at UNC thus far. So caring for her students and only wants them to improve in Spanish. Willing to provide relief grades-wise, and genuinely is so sweet to every student. I can't recommend her enough, and I am sad I won't be taking another class with her.

This class required meaningful participation, showing up isn't enough to get a good grade. 2 essays, round table talks, and a digital portfolio final project. The class wasn't hard but it definitely takes some interest and engagement to do well. No tests or quizzes, which I liked about her syllabus. Overall very nice professor.

I had Profe Pardo in the spring and absolutely loved her! The homework's are not hard but they are time consuming, doing the readings is important because you can tell who does them and who doesn't. She is big on participation!! But with that being said she will give you lots of opportunities to do so. 110% would take again!!

Was terrible at Spanish before this class. She made lectures interesting and used in class activities to facilitate learning. If you put in effort, you will be completely fine in this course. She is very understanding and genuinely wants you to do well. She is actually the best professor ever and deserves a major raise.
usually around 1 hr of podcasts to listen to before each class, participation is VERY important, but she's a very good professor who will work with you if you're having trouble

If you demonstrate effort, you will get an A. Profesora Cadena Pardo is so sweet and understands that college students have a lot on their plate. She's the kind of professor that you'd want to get to know outside of class because she is just super cool and down to earth. Love her!
Paola is super nice and caring. She knows a lot and is very good at helping students think deeply about literature. She's an easy grader and just wants to see students care and try.

She was VERY patient with me as I was going through some stuff. She cares more about us trying & practicing rather than grading very strictly. She gave pretty good feedback & was open to discussing any feedback/questions we had. A lot of VHL hw; only 2 papers, a midterm, a podcast project & a final.. seems like a lot but it's pretty spaced out.
Great professor if you're not great at spanish. She really just cares that you try youre best. The class was so fun and not a crazy amount of work.
Sweetest woman! Made me want to learn Spanish. Was also super accommodating!

Professor Cadena Pardo is awesome! So sweet and she put a lot of effort into making the lectures ones where it was fun to participate. She's a lenient grader who gives great feedback. I totally recommend her to anyone taking this class!

Paola is super kind and helpful. Participation is a part of your grade, but it's easy to answer a couple times a class. She let us do fun activities in class in addition to typical teaching methods. Doesn't make you feel dumb with mistakes and is always open to questions.

Prof. Martinez Franco is such a sweetie and clearly loves her students. She does grade somewhat harshly (I'm always getting A-s and never As :C ) and you have either a quiz or in-class essay to write every week, but she doesn't assign homework so it cancels out. Attendance is mandatory, but class is easy to go to.

Such a nice and caring professor. She really wants everyone to do well in the course and generally grades pretty easy. I am horrible at spanish and still passed 203 with B+ which was mostly due to sandra being my teacher. Great professor would highly recommend after hearing how hard spanish can be at UNC.
Professor Martinez was lovely! She is very understanding and genuinely wants to help you learn.

Ive heard nightmares about Spanish at UNC but Profe Martinez-franco was super sweet and did the best she could to make the content as understandable as possible. It's important to remember that for most of the stuff, she doesn't control what she has to assign us, it's the department.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. Dr Franco is a very nice person. But she only speaks in Spanish. This makes it extremely difficult to understand what is going on in class. Also isn't helpful for understanding the material when confused or lost. It was her first year at UNC, so Ill give her some slack. But I wouldn't do that again.

I was very intimidated by taking Spanish 203 in college as everyone was advising me to take Spanish online through community college instead, but Professor Martinez Franco is so kind, patient, and makes everything easy to understand. I feel like I learned more from her class than from five semesters of Spanish in high school.

The sweetest professor I've taken!! She cares so much about us as students and people in general. And even gave the class candy! Exams are hard, but that's for the whole Spanish department, so make sure to study!

The most absolutely caring professor I've had!! She's super nice and wants us to succeed, so if you don't understand a topic, she explains it super well. She's not a harsh grader at all, and even one time helped our class when we had a quiz. Take her class, you won't regret it !!

I really enjoyed Dr.Huesa's class. He is super funny and makes class pretty fun. Be ready to be cold-called throughout class. Spanish 102 is standardized under Dr.Shade's instruction, but he definitely added his own twists to the content to make it engaging. I learned a lot, but I wish he were more accessible outside of class. The exams are hard.

He is one of the most personable, funny, and caring professors I have ever met. He is a tough grader, but he is always understanding and gives great feedback to improve. The way he acts out words sometimes is so funny. He always tries to be a good professor, and he does great. I would take this class ten times over, he's so great.

Professor Huesa is super nice and explains class content very well. The class requires a good amount of effort and studying, but it's not too overwhelming. Class is very interactive, so I definitely recommend making it to as many classes as you can and participating a lot. He is also very accommodating and understanding if you have any issues.

Insane amount of homework, very harsh grader. He's a good lecturer, I had him twice but he was a lot harsher for this class. I would not take this class with him if I had known. Also seems to cater to native speakers so fair warning. He's very approachable and nice but as a professor I would not recommend to a friend.

Prof Huesa is really nice, and even though Basque was challenging, he did a great job breaking it down into digestible parts. He is a really harsh grader though and expects a lot from his students, so get ready to work. Not an easy course, but definitely doable and I learned a lot.
Very nice professor but sometimes wasn't the greatest at helping answer or clarify content-related questions. He does cold call and participation matters so be prepared for that if taking his class.

I  love this man as a person but unfortunately he is a rough professor. He isn't super knowledgable about certain topics and isn't super helpful with learning new materials. He also is a very very tough grader and there is no such thing as completion grades for this course.

Such a nice man and you can tell he cares about the class and students. He does cold call every class and tends to grade harshly, so prepare for that.
The Spanish department creates the tests/quizzes, NOT him, so sometimes we'd have ridiculously long tests and he'd do what he could to talk to the administrator and shorten them.

He is low key a bad teacher, but it's not really his fault. The Spanish curriculum is horribly designed. The course, and definitely the way he teaches it, is pedantic. He isn't very understanding, is a tough grader, and didn't really help us learn the language as much as he drilled in grammar rules and taught us irrelevant info for learning span.

He is the worst grader I have ever had at UNC. He takes off points in almost every single sentence, but when you try to talk to him he doesn't tell you how your fluency can be improved. He will make you laugh in class, but cry every night. Worst professor at the UNC spanish department, if you ask me, and I've had almost 8 professors at this point.

This professor refuses to take into account that his students are learning a new language. He grades as if we are fluent... and we are not. For the spanish major we have to have 261, and despite my love for learning spanish, I would NEVER take this class with him again - i don;t even know if Spanish is for me anymore because of him. DO NOT DO IT!!!

Did not give consistent feedback on the paper we wrote and when I asked for additional help outside of class he advised me to consult chat gpt. I found several problematic issues with the content in the book, which he authored, such as using slurs for LGBT individuals without clarifying they are slurs. Poor feedback and stubborn.

He is understanding and passionate about his work. If you are not sure about a question, he won't force you to answer. He is always happy/upbeat. If you need extra time on work, he will work with you. Readings/homework have to be done before class but it is all on VHL and not hard. Great experience for 1st foreign language class here at UNC.

IDK what professor these other people had, but pretty chill HE IS AN ABSOLUETLY IRRESPONSIBLE GRADER. He takes away points for random reasons and he never really explains why. He's incredibly pedantic, which to some is a benefit, but for me it's been very annoying. He's all right, can definitely make you laugh.

Professor Huesa is very kind and caring. His lectures are unfortunately very boring, as is the homework. This class goes at a fast pace and class is a review of the homework. He is a tough grader on the research paper but an easy grader on the exam and round table discussion. Class overall is a snooze, but he is a VERY nice professor.

PELLO IS AMAZING. Super easy to understand and I learned so much in his class. Genuinely the nicest person and he cares deeply about his students. SPAN 261 in general is a lot of work- but the grading is lenient. He is very engaging. 1000/10 recommend (:

If you want a Spanish professor that loves what he does take a SPAN class with him! I took both SPAN 204 and SPAN 261 with him and he truly cares about his students, and is a very passionate professor. Even though there is quite a bit of homework outside of class and he is a tough grader, it is all to benefit your learning. HE'S THE BEST!
Professor was awesome and the class was fairly easily if you participated. I recommend.

Super nice professor, a bit of a tough grader at times but completely fair. Cares a lot about students and wants everyone to learn - very good class environment. Homework on top of other materials can sometimes be a little tedious but still manageable.

Professor Huesa is pretty fun and understanding, however the course material is pretty boring. The classes were all very lecture heavy and there's a bunch of homework. He is one of the better Spanish teachers here, though he is a tough grader. If you study the grammar well for all exams and quizzes, you should be fine.
Nothing bad to say about her. She did her job exactly like how it should have been done. Not too serious not too relaxed. The definition of a balanced teacher.
She somehow made data literacy an engaging class, which is saying a lot. Props to her.

This class is pretty silly and I don't think it should be required, but since you do have to take it, you should take it with Prof Smith. She graded quickly and fairly and she was always kind in class.

Prof Smith is a lovely person, and it's clear she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. Class is very easy for the most part, and there are only six in-person meetings and you are allowed to skip up to two of them.

Great, easy-going professor. The Data Lit Lab is asynchronous and you can even skip up to 2 of the in-person classes if you do the module make-up work afterwards. Pretty simple assignments and she's a super lenient grader. As long you are aware of what's happening throughout the semester, this was a great class to take with her!

I had her for Data Literacy Lab, so it doesn't really matter but I found that she was condescending towards students (not only me) and did not have the very basic level of knowledge that is needed for teaching Data Literacy Lab.

Was rude in answering reasonable questions and unable to help with basic tech. issues when it was needed.

Profa. Smith is great. She speaks well and clearly, wants you to do well, and is willing to help you out. The material can be tough just jumping straight in but she emphasizes the important parts. Speaking and listening comprehension will be the hardest part, the rest she prepares you for very well.

Profesora Smith was nice and very helpful. She clearly wants her students to succeed but she does expect you to put in the work. There are many opportunities to bump your grade up but you still need to practice and put in the effort. This was my easiest class but the only thing that was poor was how they would prepare us for the oral quizzes.

Profe Smith is amazing! Intro to Yucatan Mayan is so interesting and an overall easy class! I'm taking this as a Spanish minor elective and she is very respectful, considerate, she is flexible, and if you put in effort you will do well. Study for maybe an hour or two a week and you're golden.
i love xka'ansaj smith. would recommend her class!!

Profa Smith is the BEST!! She definitely does her best to explain spanish to students, especially in ways that our generation can actually understand. She is funny, kind, caring, always wants students to succeed, and very open to talking about what you need. SPAN102 can be hard, but really, flashcards will help a LOT. Also kind ab missing homework

Profesora Smith is very accessible outside of the classroom as well as during class. She made learning Spanish fun for her students despite the very rushed curriculum of 105. I recommend using Quizlet and Conjuguemos to study for this class. Anyways, great professor!
I LOVED Profe Smith. She made the classroom environment comfortable and fun! She is a great teacher and always open to questions, she is also very understanding! Take Span with her!!!

Class is rushed but Profe Smith makes it more manageable. Most difficult class this semester but she doesn't have control over the curriculum and does her best. There's hw before every class and 2 midterms. Make sure you study vocab/grammar weekly. There are two midterms and a final (all tests end up being 65% of grade). Great option for any class.

Profesora Smith is a great professor. She keeps the mood light and is always willing to help. Span 105 is a hard class, but she makes it a lot more enjoyable and is willing to help and answer any questions. I would definitely  recommend taking her class!
