I definitely recommend 204 with Dra. Tolman! She's SO sweet, explains things well, and is a pretty lenient grader. The group podcast assignment is also actually really fun.
I definitely recommend 204 with Dra. Tolman! She's SO sweet and I thought she explained topics well. She's a pretty lenient grader and the group podcast assignment is actually really fun.

I enjoyed 204 with Dra. Tolman! She's SO sweet and I thought she explained topics well. She's a pretty lenient grader and the podcast group project is actually really fun. I definitely recommend taking 204 with her!

I really enjoyed 204 with Dra. Tolman! She's so sweet and made our class feel like a little community. Pretty lenient grader and the podcast project was really fun to do. I liked the activities we did in class, and she was really understanding and explained topics well. I definitely recommend!
I love this woman. She made me feel close with my classmates and I enjoyed her class. Weekly writings or quizzes, but all graded very fairly. She is so sweet and funny!

Weekly quizzes and/or graded writing assignments but were graded very fairly. Professor Tolman is very kind and caring. She is very accommodating to all students and answers any questions that students have. Would definitely recommend taking this class with Professor Tolman!

I don't feel like she actually taught us anything. She was incredibly nice, but I left class knowing exactly what I walked in knowing. We did a lot of slide activities, but the explanations were confusing, and I never knew if I was right or wrong. She rarely went over verb conjugations when that was what we were supposed to learn.
She's a good professor but I personally found the class kind of boring, it's all followed by the online textbook and I feel like classes got very repetitive.

Dr Tolman is so kind and willing to help. Span321 is a very interesting, informative class and Dr Tolman makes it fun and easy to learn/ask questions! I definitely recommend taking this class with her!

Professor Tolman was very kind and helpful. She is clear about what will be on quizzes and exams. She is not a tough grader and she is there to help you if needed! There is one group project and one essay which she grades very leniently. 10/10
She is super nice and makes SPAN 204 the best that it can be. Prepare for group projects/work and choose your groups carefully. Do the reading of the book ahead of class and you will do great.

Awesome professor! She is so kind and always looks out for her students. Do not be afraid to participate, she will not criticize you if you make mistakes. I learned a lot in this class and it was always a joy coming each day.

Profe Tolman has been my favorite professor at UNC by far. I took both 204 and 261 with her and she made me keep wanting to learn Spanish. Fair grader and gave excellent feedback. She really wants you to excel. Wish she taught higher levels, so I could take her again!

Professor Tolman is so sweet and an amazing Spanish teacher. I enjoyed her class so much, and she made it easy to do well. She gives lots of study tools and is clear about what will be on tests and grading criteria for other assignments. Highly recommend taking her class!

Profe Tolman is very kind, but I did not learn much in this class. It was easy and minimal homework, but my Spanish did not improve. She heavily relies on the textbook, literally every single activity in class comes from it. Boring and not a constructive use of class time. Does not really encourage students to always speak in Spanish.

Tolman was my fav teacher this semester. She understands when students go through things and won't take off late points if you just talk to her. She wasn't a hard grader and made the class fun. I would def take another class with her. Just study for the tests and quizzes and you'll be fine. Participation and attendance matters.

Super laid-back professor who always makes speaking Spanish in class comfortable. Activities in class to practice grammar are cool and fun. Tests and quizzes are straightforward. Would be surprised if less than 30% of the class got an A or A-. Cannot go wrong with this professor.

Best Spanish Instructor in the university! I was very scared to take this course initially, but Professor Tolman was amazing. Would highly recommend it, as long as you can keep up with homework and class slides before each class meeting you will be good. Also, try to participate a few times in class.

Profesora Tolman is probably the best Spanish professor at UNC. She is caring, speaks clearly, and genuinely wants you to learn. She also encourages her students to become friends and talk frequently. If you are taking SPAN 204 or 261, taking her is an absolute must.

Sra. Tolman is amazing! Her teaching style is very straightforward and easy to understand. She adds lots of pop culture references into her presentations and teaching material, which makes for fun classes! I also think she graded fairly, and was always there for us after class and during office hours to answer questions. 100% recommend!
Take span 203 with her! She is the best. All the spanish section are basically standardized, so it is very instructor dependent.

Professor Maqueda is absolutley delightful - she is not a harsh grader at all and truly just want people to enjoy Spanish and her courses. Absolutley recommend her! As someone who is worse at language courses I was anxious about taking 401 but she made it so approachable and un-stressful. She is so so sweet if you're taking Spanish def take her!

She always came to class with a smile, ready to teach. She treats the students as one of her own and you can tell she truly cares, she even rounded my grade when I needed it. Definitely take Spanish with her if you can!

By far the best teacher to take 102 with. The class is well-paced and was never overwhelming. She is extremely patient and makes students feel comfortable even if they're confused in class (she speaks in Spanish 99% of the time). Study purposely before exams and you'll do fine. She is very lenient with grading points for accents & small things.

She has a really good way of breaking down the information and making it digestible to her students. I found it really helpful that she was accessible outside of class and very interactive. She has a great sense of humor as well!

She's a great Spanish professor! Yes Spanish language courses are challenging at this school, but she explains things well and is super helpful. Make sure to participate in class, keep up with the homeworks and activly studying the vocab and grammar, and youll do fine!

She was very accurate and helpful, always teaching her classes in Spanish because her whole point is for us to be immersed in the language. I felt as though she explained things well and put them in different forms. I already know Spanish so I am a bit swayed, but going through her lectures, I see how she is able to teach people from scratch.
She's a pretty chill and understanding professor. She doesn't teach the language as well as other professors I've had- her teaching style isn't the best.

Professor Maqueda is probably the best professor to take SPAN 203 with. As long as you participate in class, read the textbook, and do the assignments, this class should be relatively easy. She gives a lot of partial credit and grades tests pretty leniently.

Prof. Maqueda can be quite awkward which makes the vibes of class a bit weird, but she's very sweet and well meaning, and the class is not too hard. Homework is short and relatively simple, and there are a lot of grades throughout the semester. The tests and final are pretty straightforward as well. Maqueda is a good prof to take 203 with.

If you have to take a Spanish credit, take it with Professor Maqueda! This class has a variety of assignments that all SPAN 203 courses have to do, but she is exceedingly nice when it comes to grading. She also always let us out of class early. This class is work, but if you put in the effort, she will most likely give you an A.

I love Prof Maqueda! She is super sweet when it comes to explaining and grading. Highly recommend for anyone curious about taking Spanish. There's homework every class, but it's textbook-based and not too long.

I loved taking this class! Professor Maqueda is one of the most caring and genuine professors you will get at UNC. She is willing to work with students about grades, and will take the time of day to help you with anything. I cannot recommend her class enough!

I absolutely love Professor Maqueda, she is extremely caring and genuine, she is understanding of her students and encourages us to attend upcoming events that are related to the language. Her class is always entertaining and she's really funny, she grades according to the curriculum, but if you just try, she'll make the class very enjoyable!

In my many years of Spanish, I have never had a better professor. Professora Maqueda is caring, understanding, sensible, hilarious, and overall the best teacher I've had at UNC thus far. If you do your work and study for exams, she will give you the best grade possible. 100% take all Spanish classes with Maqueda - she is AMAZING!

If you have any ability to take either 105 or 203 with her... DO IT!!! I had her for 105 in the fall and about half of my class moved up into her 203 because of how amazing she was. She cares about all her students and genuinely wants to help. She doesn't grade too harshly and is very understanding. One of the sweetest people on this planet.

She is the biggest sweetheart ever! 203 involves a lot of in-class Spanish speaking, and she is SO encouraging. She breaks down rules in ways that make sense. If you can, I highly recommend taking her class. She grades fairly and her quizzes are easy and reasonable. She is a very genuine person and cares about what her students have to say.

If you can take any Spanish class with this professor, DO IT. She is genuinely the sweetest and really cares about her students. Participation is important, but it's also ok to make mistakes and she is not judgemental at all!! She doesn't grade hard either, so as long as you do your work as best you can, you'll be fine.

She is, by far, the best Spanish professor I've had. Professor Maqueda is an incredibly fair grader, is accessible during office hours, and is exceptionally kind. I found the material to be difficult, but she made a clear effort to help all of her students understand. As someone who finds Spanish difficult, I could not recommend her more!
Take her class. She is kind, and really cares about you learning the language. She does not make you feel uncomfortable at all if you do not understand the content and is always willing to help.
Great professor and fun class. Just don't fall behind on readings or homework and come to every class prepared because she will call on you multiple times.
She was really funny and I enjoyed her class a lot. Cold calls but just pay attention to where you are in the book and you'll be fine. Sometimes gives extra credit. Don't fall behind.
She was really funny but expects a lot from a beginner language course. I liked her but she moves fast so don't fall behind.

I thought she was a pretty great professor. She's a super fast grader and one of the best 204 professors you can get. She's explains things pretty well. However, doing all the work before the class is crucial because she does cold call a lot and will base your participation grade off this. She truly just wants you to put effort in speaking.
She is very kind, and does her best to make the material understandable. Although the class itself is difficult, Professora Lee does her best! Definitely recommend!

Professor Lee is one of the best professors I've had at UNC! I love her and her teaching style and she makes class engaging and fun. She moves a bit fast but if you put in the effort, she's willing to work with you! Her face hours are so helpful and she is always willing to help. Take this class!
She's so nice and very funny. The tests are fair and exactly what you would expect but very content heavy. Not too much homework but she loves to cold call students

She cold calls a lot (not good for social anxiety) and doesn't really give opportunities for raising your hand, and it is unknown how she grades participation (everyone would get B's). She grades pretty quickly and gives enough feedback. She can be helpful but a bit scary. However, overall a good teacher. Reading the textbook matters!!

Professor Lee really forces you to learn the language, and that is something I learned to appreciate about her. She strictly cold-calls in class, and grades papers and quizzes very meticulously. She is an incredibly fast grader, and overall I enjoyed the class. I am taking 261 with her next semester. Be prepared for a LOT of work at first!

Profesora Lee is a great and caring professor. She is an INCREDIBLY fast grader and responder to emails. She is also understanding about makeup if you are sick or absent. She is a tough grader though, so pay attention and be thorough!

(203 not 204) Prof Lee is intimidating but a really good teacher. I learned the hard way to pay attention to instructions she gives in Spanish, and be prepared for each class. Lots of moving parts to keep up with, but not as bad as it seems! Get ready to be called on, which I ending up appreciating. Quick grader, glad I wasn't scared away by her.

Quick grader and sometimes funny in class, but overall very disorganized and made succeeding in the class difficult. Went through slides with dense material quickly and often without further explanation. Cold called the entire semester as well; never asked for volunteers during class - still not sure how we were graded for participation.

Unclear instructions for assignments and sometimes doesn't even give rubrics until the day before it's due. She says things in class that directly contradicts written instructions/rubric, but that's what she grades based on. Overall a nice person and helps you if you're stuck, but just be prepared for a very disorganized class and grading.
Gosia is a good professor, but slightly strange at times and very opinionated. She does assign a hefty amount of homework. Good class overall, extra credit opportunities were available.

(took Ital101) One of the best professors I've had at UNC. She is such an engaging and caring teacher and wants you to succeed.There is a lot of hw but it is usually average difficulty if you do it on time. She is a fast and fair grader and a very intelligent and funny person. I wish I could have her for Ital 102 but she does not teach that class.
Professor Lee is interesting and caring. Grades super quickly, often the same day or next day. Responds to emails quickly and is always ready to help.

Gosia Lee is an extremely caring professor and is very accessible outside of class. She grades papers and exams quickly so you will always know where you stand in the class. I am taking her again for 261 because she made 204 a great experience. Be sure to participate in class though!
Lovely woman, just wasnt ready for all the work outside of the classroom. when she says "watch *blank* movie" she really means it

She is a great person and a good professor! I do feel like she could elaborate more on the lessons in the textbook, but I enjoyed having her as my professor. She wasnt too harsh of a grader and she provided help when you needed it.

For me, this was one of those classes that made me really realize how much I really love learning spanish. Gosia Lee cold calls on everyone which can be scary, but its actually much less nerve racking than having to raise your hand to participate. She cares about her students and creates a great learning environment. Highly recommend!

SPAN 100: I loved her as a professor until I looked on canvas and saw that my grade was a 89.24 which is a B+ and a 89.50 is an A-. I sent a very kind email asking to round, and she said no. Girl I am a stem major PLEASE. Anyways she was chill before though, tough grader for participation, and oral interview. Just don't expect any rounding...
She was an easy grader and tried to make the class as stress-free as possible.

I had her for Spanish 203 this semester, and it was great! This class is very standardized, but she always brought tremendous energy to every lecture. She is very kind and always willing to help you outside of class. Would recommend her for any Spanish class you have.
The only way I can describe her is simply an angel on Earth. Most kind and caring person. She is so much fun and truly cares about students. I wish she could teach all of my Spanish classes

Prof. Gervasi is so genuine, caring, and wants to see her students succeed. She is lenient on grading and will help on any assignment if you ask. She is very patient and is a very thorough, hands on professor. As long as you try your best, you will succeed in this class. The material is a bit hard at the end, but Prof. Gervasi does her best to help

Professor Isabel (Maria) Silva cares more about her students understanding the material than she does grades and wants to see you succeed. Her lectures are set up with powerpoints that are clear and full of activities for practice. There are 2 midterms, a final, and pronunciation practice (graded leniently). Would highly recommend Professor Silva!!
Amazing professor made it as easy as she could for us. Good at explaning things and letting us go over the things we needed work on. Clearly cared about each student and was funny during lectures.

Prof Lopez is an amazing professor! He is very encouraging and kind and cares more about effort than accuracy. He will call on every student every class, so be ready to participate. Assignments are fair and he grades fairly as well. As long as you pay attention in class quizzes and exams are manageable. I totally recommend taking spanish with him!!
Fantastic professor. Sometimes a difficult grader on assignments, but will 100% help you learn to speak Spanish.

So sweet! SPAN203 was definitely hard for me, but he didn't create the tests, so it wasn't his fault (and the quizzes he did make for us were very fair.) He provided everything needed to succeed, and explained things super simply! Class was never boring, and even though I HATED Spanish as a subject, I never dreaded going to class.

Profesor Lopez Lopez is one of the best Spanish professors I have had here at UNC. He cares for his students and wants to see them all succeed. He was accessible outside of class and would be available to help you in any way that you would need. Sometimes there was a lot of homework, but it made me learn the concepts and material much better.

Spanish here is not an easy A, you have to put in effort to study and do work outside of class. However, Prof López is caring, funny, and good at explaining how grammar works. He always came to class full of joy and it made it easier to wake up and go to class. He tries to make Spanish engaging and related to college life.

Professor Lopez was one of the best professors i've had, definitely take him for Spanish 203! He was super funny and really seemed to care about his students. While the class overall was not easy he made sure to explain content very clearly and answer any questions we had. The tests are hard but they are not written by him and he helps you prepare.

I learned a decent amount in SPAN352 so far, but he grades harshly. Everything is graded hard with good criticisms, but it's unrealistic to get an A. NOT an easy A class like 351, youll prob get a B. Youll learn, but its heavy legal/medical focus. He should make hw completion while still giving feedback, but even that & attendance is graded hard.

Giovani Lopez Lopez was a wonderful teacher for 203. He was understanding to all students when they struggled, and helped them along their way. Attendance is very important and keeping up on work. He graded written sections fairly difficult with grammar, but provided extensive feedback for your mistakes.

Dr. Lopez is incredibly nice, understanding, and knowledgeable. Very fair grader. Definitely one of the better Spanish professors I have had. Exams are not written by him but are very straightforward for 203 at UNC.

Abel is a really nice and funny professor. Being a Spanish class, participation matters so much and is crucial. Otherwise, I think he is a very fair grader, not easy, but not harsh. Great class even though I realized Spanish isn't really for me.

i really enjoyed abel and took him for both 204 and 261. attendance and participation are key for him but if you make a good impression at the start and he likes you, he basically guarantees you an A. 204 was mega chill, 261 was a pain due to all the busy work.

Chill and understanding professor. Cares more about participation than perfection, make an effort to speak up in class and it'll go far, even if your Spanish isn't great. Communicate issues or a desire for an extension and he'll make it work for you, if he can tell that you care about the class.

To start, I had him for 355 (no option to select that on RMP) Abel is my favorite UNC profesor, this is the second class I've taken with him and 355 has been my favorite class by far. Reasonable workload, he is flexible, he is hilarious, class feels like a conversation, he made the entire class friends and I would talk to any of them outside10/10

He was super engaging in class and makes sure we had fun. Participation matters though and tests are very fair/no curveballs. He also plays a new spanish song at the beginning of class which was fun. Also he gives lots of extra credit opportunities.

This guy is the goat. I took him and can honestly say he was one of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. If you are a student you need to take him (like trust me). His lectures were fun, although the content is hard he makes it fun to learn, and really wants to see you succeed as a Spanish speaker and in the class.

Amazing class and professor. He cares a lot about his students and their success in the course, and he is very passionate about teaching. Grading, assignments, tests, and quizzes were very fair. My Spanish improved so much from this class, so if you are thinking about taking it, definitely take it with him!

I loved this man, very happy and go lucky, makes funny jokes. He makes class engaging and gives you a lot of freedom when it comes to your written work. Not a tough grader but expects participation in class. You can tell he has a passion for Spanish, teaching does not feel like a chore to him, cares about your learning. Reopened homeworks for me.

Abel was amazing as a professor and is extremely easy to reach outside of class. Participation is very important but if you talk a few times a day and engage, the participation grade wont be much of a problem. Essay was the hardest part of the class. 100% am looking for Abel as a professor in the future. He's also hilarious.

I felt like I learned a decent amount from this class and I liked the movies we watched, but this was probably the most disorganized class I've ever taken. I was constantly confused about deadlines and expectations. However, professor Munoz-Hermoso was very kind and easy to reach outside of class. There wasn't a ton of work for the summer class.

If you felt like SPAN203 was easy and you need FC-Create, I recommend taking SPAN204 with Abel. Similar to SPAN203, there is textbook homework, quizzes, midterms, a podcast project, and a final, so one bad grade can't ruin your final grade. Make sure to participate every class. Abel also begins every class with a song which is fun.

If you feel like you need help with learning, or have doubt about your Spanish, I would not recommend taking class with Abel. He made me dread coming to class, and on several occasions, even rolled his eyes and huffed at me when I did not know how to answer his questions. I\

Profe is very passionate about the course material, and he was really nice (he brought snacks for the final)! He's a somewhat tough grader for exams, the exam's covered a lot (info from lectures and readings) and they were essay formatted, but he wasn't a harsh grader for homework or the group project (you make your own groups).

Worked hard to engage all students and cultivate a positive learning environment. Participation matters, but doesn't hold you back if you are succeeding on tests and quizzes. Very straightforward with assignments and extremely considerate of other obligations. Definitely would take again, as many peers are taking him again next semester.

Really cares about participation and is honestly passive aggressive about it. He uses a flipped classroom model. The course has a good array of assignments. Overall a solid Spanish course, just make sure you participate.

Best Spanish professor I have had. He's kind, interactive with students, creates fun lectures, and overall I learned a lot in this class. Participation is expected, and he can be harsh when grading this, so do participate whenever possible. You don't have to be right, you just have to try. Information can be hard sometimes, but still manageable.

Do not take this class if you're looking for an easy A! The professor can come off extremely intimidating, but deep down he cares about his students learning Spanish. You are going to have to put in a lot of work to do well, but it's possible and there is room for error. If you truly work hard and let him know you're trying, you'll get through it.

Abel is an amazing Spanish professor. This is a difficult class and will be difficult regardless of the professor, but if you put in effort to learn the grammatical concepts and participate you'll be okay. He makes the material interesting and has fun class activities. Participation is important, but he won't dock points for mistakes when you talk.

Abel is a professor that you can tell really wants people to improve. His class is tough and there is a ton of very fast-paced content, but if you put in the work, go to office hours, do extra credit and participate you will do well. Participation is extremely important and you have to work through nervousness. Sometimes he is a little intimidating

Most arrogant professor I have had. Gives out broad feedback just criticizing your work that isn't helpful- just makes you feel bad. He's super rude to his students. Mistakes are not allowed in his class and you will get publicly embarrassed by him if you make one. My worst experience at this school, made me dread the days I had his class.

Incredibly caring prof with plenty of energy, grades fairly and conveys the information well. The class structure is poor due to how the department sets it up, but he works around it very well. Good for feedback in class, oral quiz, and office hours, but not too accessible as a remote teacher outside of them. 100 as a class sucks but he's fantastic

He walks into class with an alarming amount of energy. He's a character. His family is from Spain and he speaks with a Barcelona accent that is hard to understand. Spends more time on conversation and less on grammar bc you are expected to learn that by doing the VHL (VERY easy) and reading the textbook (who is reading the textbook? I never have).

Professor Walsh was very accessible outside of class through email and office hours. He was also willing to stay after class for any questions or discussions related to the course material. He provided thorough feedback for all projects, quizzes, and exams. I highly recommend taking Professor Walsh for SPAN 203.

Great professor! He's very understanding and helpful when you ask for extra help. The lecture style is a little basic and doesn't really teach you much, so I did have to do a lot of studying for the exams. I think 203 as a whole is easier than 105 though. We also tended to end class around 10 minutes early, which was nice.

Nice Guy, but very basic Lecture style that leads to me not really understanding concepts, a lot of the times we just read off a PowerPoint. Also, the 105 department as a whole is bad, with disconnects between us and the Admin, and extremely quick pacing of Spanish concepts for people that have not practiced in well over a year.

I loved Prof Walsh! This was a tough class but it was 100% the fault of the department-- for example, the department made an incredibly hard midterm, and Prof Walsh went to the department and tried to fight for us to get the grades overturned. He really cares about his students and wants you to succeed.
He's a caring professor, and all of the issues I had in this class were due to the way the Spanish department at UNC runs SPAN 105, not the professor himself. Would recommend.

Professor James is the best and I loved having him as a teacher. He is super sweet and very willing to help with any questions you may have. He is also very enthusiastic about teaching and loves to help you learn.
She's the best. Take this class.
Fantastic, engaging teacher. Very cool class projects and lots of vocab quizzes.

take her class!! shes a great professor, knowledgeable about the material, and cares about her students succeeding. the class itself is well structured, and she is the fastest grader ive ever seen. theres a semester long group project so make sure you choose solid groupmates at the beginning, as it will last. put in the effort and you will succed!

One of the best Spanish professors that I have had at UNC so far! She is encouraging, a fair grader, and wants every student to succeed. The class projects are also very fun and engaging to learn about businesses across Latin America.

Don't let other reviews fool you, this is NOT an easy A class. There are a handful of grammar quizzes throughout the semester that can tank your grade, the in-class essays that can be graded somewhat tough in terms of grammar, and the examsare fairly graded, but you have to study and be familar with the content.

Professor Aviles is hands down the best professor I have had at UNC so far. Although speaking in a different language can be daunting, she encourages practice and genuinely cares about whether or not you are learning. Participation matters to stay engaged, but class would fly by, as she's a great teacher and not a boring lecturer. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

Professor Aviles is amazing. Her lectures are interesting and engaging and she doesn't take herself too seriously. Her course load is made to challenge you and help you succeed (if you put in the work). She returns graded work so so fast. Seriously, she is the kind of professor that makes you happy you paid for college. Take her class.

One of the best professors I have had. She grades SO quickly (got my final exam grade back 6 minutes after the grading period had ended). She gives great feedback and does a good job of keeping everyone on track. There is a good amount of weekly homework, but its worth it and is helpful in understanding the class material. Really awesome Prof.

I took prof Avilés for span 344 and loved it! You will spend a lot of class time discussing readings, the lesson, etc with peers and I feel it really improved my speaking skills in a chill environment. The papers aren't hard and you can often take them in your own direction to keep it fresh. There is a group presentation but it isn't hard. Take it!
Very good teacher. There is a lot of homework in the class but it's pretty easy and helps you get better at the material. Highly recommend this teacher, one of my favorite professors at UNC.

Prof Avilés is an AMAZING spanish professor. For a school with a terrible foreign language curriculum, she makes it a lot better. Every class was structured and she prioritized practicing in class a ton to get speaking practice in. She was super responsive with emails and following through on grading issues. Super clear grader and tech savvy.
Prof Aviles was my favorite Spanish professor at UNC. While the approach to teaching language in American education is HORRIFIC, she made it bearable, and she is a great professor.

Professor Avilés is amazing! Her enthusiasm for the immigration-related content of the course was evident throughout lecture and engaged the class. She's a fair (and super fast!) grader and clearly outlined all criteria. Class consisted of 8 short written assignments, 6 grammar quizzes, 2 midterms, a group project, and a final.

With previous experience in Span, 203 will be easy, especially with Aviles who is a fantastic professor who genuinely cares about her students. The grading is fair and her quizzes are online, easy, and take about 15 minutes. If you just started Span, it may be difficult. You have to speak Spanish in class, but it isn't as daunting as it sounds.

Seriously a fantastic prof—knowledgeable, caring, and ridiculously organized (midterms graded in hours). Class is reading- and writing-heavy but very interesting. Grammar quizzes are no joke. Midterms are more of a time crunch than particularly difficult (but you have to know the readings). Besides HW, it's all discussions, so participate often!

Professora Avilés was genuinely the best Spanish professor I've had. You can tell that she really cares about her students. 

She creates exercise PDF's that we fill out in class, which help with studying for exams. Tests are not difficult at all and they follow the pre-posted study guides. 

TAKE HER CLASS!!!!

She is a great teacher and the class was good. Be aware of the out-of-class quizzes because they count for your grade. It's a lot of grammar review from previous courses if you've taken other Spanish classes. Also know participation matters but she tries to get you to participate.

Prof. Aviles was amazing. She was so caring and made Spanish so much better. While this class was very challenging, she made sure to help us understand with daily worksheets and practice. Best Spanish 203 prof!

Prof Aviles was very caring and helpful throughout the semester. While the class got repetitive at times, papers were graded mostly on grammar and workload was pretty light. One of the better professors in the Spanish department.
She is so sweet and genuinely wants her students to do well. I cannot recommend her enough and I have grown so much as a spanish speaker because of her!

Professor Garcia made Spanish 203 very interesting! It takes a little while to get used to a class taught entirely in Spanish, but overall, it's not that difficult if you spend enough time studying. My only complaint was the sheer speed at which the class moved, given how much material was covered. Get ready to study lots of vocab/grammar concepts!

This class had a very reasonable workload, with a quick grammar exercise after every class and one final project. I found the content interesting, but you may be bored if you aren't interested in linguistics. We got lots of good speaking practice every class. Profe. Ruiz Garcia was pleasant and made every class fun and engaging.

I had her for 203 this past semester (Fall 2025). She was extremely fair with grading and was very caring. The content wasn't hard as long as you put in the effort to actually be prepared for class. She is also willing to work with you on assignments/homework. Overall she was a great professor that really cares for her students.

I really enjoyed taking SPAN 300 with her! She is great at lecturing and explaining material, and I definitely learned a ton. It is important to keep up with the textbook so you have context for some of the class material, but it isn't particularly difficult or time consuming to read. I would definitely take classes with her again!

I loved Prof. Martha Ruiz-Garcia. Tried so hard to engage with our class, with songs and fun applications. Very easy to understand. Extremely fair - was late on getting our final project back and gave us 100s bc of that!

I loved class with Dra. Ruiz! I enjoyed her lectures and she was clear on what was going to be tested on exams. Each week we would have a song that we would sing and look at its grammar. She is an excellent choice for SPAN 300!

Really great professor, she cares about you, and from what I've heard, she's for sure one of the better 203 professors. The quizzes she gives are harder than some of the teachers, but fair level, if you study you should get an A.

This class was good.  I personally know I could've performed better if I studied a little more.  Take advantage of the practice resources from the book for homework and exams!  And always participate.  She can be a bit disorganized at times.  I will say the final was not supposed to be cumulative but she threw random things on there.

SPAN 376 is a know it or don't course, meaning that most of the course does require memorization of the API; however, Marta is good at giving ample opportunity in class to practice. Her homework is light and the test are fair. I would recommend taking the course with her!
Profesora Garcia is very clear about what is expected for homework, readings, and tests. As long as you read 5-10 pages the night before, you'll be prepared and will do well in class.

This class followed the textbook structure fairly rigidly, but it felt disorganized at times. Prof. Ruiz-Garcia covers the material by talking through it, sometimes with a PowerPoint and sometimes without, so paying attention in class is super important. We did a lot of review exercises in class. Overall, I learned a lot.

Data lit is pointless with lots of homework (the class is standardized across all of the idst111 sections so not the professors fault). Attendance is mandatory but 2 makeup assignments. She's an easy grader and let me change an assignment for full credit. The only negative I would say is that she didn't respond to my emails which was frustrating.

Prof. Loftus was a great professor for IDST 111L. She kept students engaged, and all projects were graded fairly. The attendance policy is very clear (standardized across the courses for IDST). She is very kind and approachable, and is always looking to help students. Clearly cares about the subject and provides awesome feedback.

She's a kind professor, generally very dry lectures, and her Spanish isn't THAT good, but awesome person. It is a pretty interactive class though so make sure you participate. If you do all the work she assigns, which can be a lot, you'll be good

Professor Loftus is really nice, but she is not the best professor in UNC's Spanish program. She does not know all that much about the class material, although she does speak good Spanish. She depends heavily on the textbook, so it is important to keep up with the readings. If you read and participate consistently, you should do well in the class.

She's very kind and accommodating. Expectations clear. You won't learn that much, as she has zero business/econ background and teaches out of the book. Lectures are relatively dry. But if you have to take her and show up to lecture it's not a hard class.

Professor Loftus is very flexible and understanding of her students. Lectures are clear, and class expectations are consistent from day 1. The content of the course can be dull, but participate in class and you'll be fine. This class is textbook-heavy so stay on top of the readings so you know what's going on.

The professor is super sweet and understanding; however, the course itself isn't set up well, and tests are a lot more difficult than quizzes/homework. The professor is sweet, but the class structure itself is hard to learn from.

Professor Lomas is very kind and accommodating. However, the class setup isn't great even for those with prior knowledge. You'll have to teach yourself all the information, most of which isn't reviewed in class but is still on the exam.

She is perhaps the most understanding human being known to mankind. I showed up for my interview not having realized there were sample questions on canvas, and she let me do the interview on Friday. I didn't even ask! In a world full of hate she is a shining beacon of understanding.

Very kind and wants students to ask questions. However, she takes an incredibly long time to grade and provides no feedback on assignments. The real issue with the SPA 100 class is the Zoom setup, which is beyond her control.

She is very kind and approachable. If you keep up with homework and attend class, you'll do well. Midterms and exams are fair with preparation. Oral interviews and video assignments are manageable. Chapter quizzes in the Alcanza textbook are strict and don't allow retakes, so double-check answers.

I thought the class was good for it being online. Obviously learning another language is challenging, but the instructor was VERY kind/open to questions and not a harsh grader at all. Assignments were a little annoying at times, but overall were very helpful for the final, which was not bad at all if you applied yourself

Those who have never taken Spanish before don't take this class or this teacher. She reads the slides and never actually teaches and the worst of all, she will only speak in Spanish never english. Half the time she doesn't even teach just tells us to read the textbook which doesn't help at all. Don't even get me started about conversating with her.

Amazing professor especially for an online course. She is very accessible and flexible, SPAN-100 was the easiest class I took at UNC. Just pay attention on the zoom calls and you will be perfectly fine, the study guides also outline exactly what will be on the exams.

The course is hard because of the structure (online once a week), but Dr. Lomas is a really great instructor. I appreciated how she put us in breakout rooms to practice. Make a Quizlet deck to keep up with all the vocab so you can practice. She is happy to answer questions and not a hard grader.

Lomas-Lozano is by far the best SPAN 100 professor you could ask for. Class content was straightforward. You would meet once a week on Zoom where she would go over basic content. Most learning occurs through the interactive, online "textbook." Consisted of basic assignments each week with unlimited attempts. Exams were taken online besides final.

If you get the chance to take a class with Professor Lomas, do it. She is incredibly helpful and easy to work with. Also fine with things being late you just have to ask her to reopen the assignment. My class was online and so easy, didn't expect you to be a perfect or native speaker.

Pretty good professor for such a difficult course to teach. Most of my complaints are about the course itself which is extremely difficult to work with considering it was once a week, online. Not a very teacher-heavy course but is willing to explain things if necessary. However, she varies with response time so contact her earlier.

She is a very sweet and understanding person and an amazing professor. You can tell she is genuinely passionate about Spanish and teaching. Always very kind to students and made the class enjoyable. Her exams were fair and reflected what we learned in class.

Would definitely take with her again! A very sweet lady that cares for her students. Homework can be a lot and the online tool used to auto-grade can be annoying as it manually grades to one correct answer. Lectures in class were much more useful to learn content and succeed on exams. Overall great class and professor.

Class was completely on zoom but she executed teaching very well. It's important to do the outside homework and reading but she explains very well and is very reasonable. Super nice teacher and I'm going to miss her

She's good professor who's understanding & gives good feeback. My issue is with course set-up. How do you expect me to learn if i'm not immersed & we only meet once a week online LOL? Essentially had to teach myself. Quizzes/interviews/tests are online & okay if you prepare. STUDY for the final since it's in person. There's a participation grade.

I absolutely loved this course. I was nervous about language classes at UNC but Professor Lomas made learning somewhat simple and very effective. She provided amazing feedback that really helped me make progress throughout the course and she was easy to talk to as well as work with.

This class had a lot of exercises and practices to do but they're all useful and won't take you that long. Dr. Lomas-Lozano is super helpful and understanding when you're struggling. She is always available via email or zoom. The exams are kind of hard but just study and get as many points on participation/other activities as you can.

taking the lowest level of spanish at UNC this is not what I expected. This class was once a week entirely on zoom and ABSOLUTLY sucked. you have to TEACH YOURSELF everything she will not teach you. the assignments are on myspanishlab, they are lengthy. after like 5 weeks she was talking nothing but spanish to us. DO NOT TAKE

Super sweet professor, always gave good feedback and really wanted to help. Responds to emails quickly. Really the only hard thing about the class is the in-person exams, but if you study a decent amount you'll be fine. Definitely recommend!

Carlos Lopez-Pari is a fantastic teacher who teaches SPAN 255 (conversational class) expertly well. He is a hard grader and the class is very writing heavy, but I have never felt more confident in my Spanish speaking/writing abilities and he is so kind.

Expectations were especially tough on heritage speakers, and grading was not consistent across students. Rubrics lacked clarity, and it was difficult to earn above an A- despite strong effort. Feedback was often blunt and support outside of class was limited.

Professor Lopez made this class so difficult and we were never taught anything in class. Lopez would laugh when you asked a question and would say to look in the textbook. He graded incredibly hard. Everyone was getting 50s and 60s on quizzes because he had 1 right answer in his mind, even though there were multiple right answers.

After taking 4 years of spanish in high school, I expected to do fairly well in span204. However, the class was extremely difficult and time consuming. Lopez basically just laughed in your face when you asked a clarifying question. The material would have been engaging if it was presented in a different manner by a different professor.

I hate an awful time in this section of span204. He spoke very little English, was very bad at explaining things- you would ask him a question (a question over half the class had) and he would just laugh it off and not give you ANYTHING clarifying. If you are taking span204, I would try to get it with Tolman.
He barely speaks English, and does not do a good job teaching the material! He is a very nice guy but just not a good professor.

Carlos is a great teacher and person. I had an A until the final exam which sucked. I don't think he was in charge of creating the exam, I think it was the same for each class which seemed unfair. I don't know why they have exams curated by someone who doesn't teach you. My friend took it a semester after and the exam was different for every class.

Carlos is probably the best Spanish teacher I've ever had. He cares about his students, takes feedback well, and really just wants everyone to succeed. I didn't find him to a be a difficult grader, and the feedback he gives is always very clear and concise. If you work hard, complete assignments, and come to class, you'll be just fine!

You can tell Carlos is passionate about his students. He frequently checks in on us. He gives great feedback and attempts to ensure students understand the course material. Take any class you can with Carlos. I love him!
Carlos was great! His class was small and engaging, and while difficult, really pushed me to get better at Spanish. I would 100% take Carlos again.

The GOAT. Pretty funny guy, and tries to make lectures as engaging as possible. You will definitely succeed as long as you put some effort into this class. I would definitely take him again. Tests weren't that hard too and he really goes out of his way to make sure you get the concepts. 10/10

Some of my classmates weren't big fans of Prof Cabrera -- but I liked him! While a little unorganized/inconsistent, Prof Cabrera clearly cared about his students and was a good and understanding grader. He has a great personality and elicits very interesting class discussions.

This class wasn't too bad. He cares about his students and tries his best to implement practices that help students in areas they are struggling. If you do the work and study for test you will be fine.

As someone who hadn't taken Spanish in years but was placed into 203, Cabrera was a great professor who truly cares about the success of his students and was very lenient. He was super chill and we had fun in his class, so definitely try to take a class with him, if available.
He is a great professor and definitely tries to make the class as enjoyable as possible I would highly recommend taking him, participating is so so important and he is funny
Great professor, the classes in span 203 were great and the homework wants too difficult. Make sure to study well for the tests and you will have a great time in the class!

Great guy and really kind. The only class this semester that I actually looked forward to going to. You can tell he really cares about his students, and he always brought a chill energy to class which was really nice. Explained Spanish in a simple way which was easy for me to understand :)

I had Juan Carlos for SPAN 363, disease in hispanic lit. He is indisputably the goat. Good amount of readings and 2 weekly forum posts + journaling, but readings are reasonable + very interesting. Class discussion is the core of this class so you must come prepared. The discussions are fantastic though, JC is an amazing lecturer. Take this class!

Juan Carlos has been my favorite Spanish professor at UNC so far! He is very clearly passionate about the subject matter and leads engaging discussions. His energy is unmatched and I looked forward to every class! He creates an environment where it is easy to participate and contribute to the discussion, even if your Spanish isn't always correct.

I loved JC! He cared so much about the material and subject matter and the class was super fun. I also appreciated how he was not a strict grader and cared more about the content of responses on homework as opposed to proper grammar.

Juan Carlos is such an engaging professor. He digs deep into the assigned readings and encourages students to participate. By fostering a welcoming class environment, I always feel welcome to share my thoughts and opinions. Homework was minimal. He's one of the best professors I've had so far-- take a course with him if you can!

I felt as if this class was a lot more difficult than expected. He was not easy to access via email outside of class and graded very difficult. At times, I felt like i was being graded more for my punctuation and not my writing in spanish (we were never taught grammar either). Take with another prof if possible.
she was very nice funny and helpful

Profesora Venegas was a great professor! She's super caring and made classes enjoyable. The SPAN 261 curriculum (at least when I took it in fall 2024) was standardized between all of the professors, so I can't really say anything about the course itself that applies to just her. I'd definitely take a class with her again though!

Professor Venegas clearly cared about the content shown in class in context to our heritages as students. She is super bubbly and provides a comfortable environment to discuss perspectives on the material provided. Gonna miss her and mis compañeros!

She is the most caring and understanding teacher I have ever had! There's homework for most class days but it doesn't take long at all. One midterm and one final exam and a project. I would highly recommend taking span 267 with her. She is not a harsh grader at all and gives helpful feedback.

She seems nice, but I was having a tough time understanding the concepts, and when I approached her during office hours, she refused to help. She also grades very strictly and gives few and unhelpful comments. The class as a whole is set up awfully, but that's the department's fault.
Very nice, but refuses to give 100's unless it's an online assignment because she believes "not everything is perfect". (I am a spanish speaker).

Profesora Venegas was super sweet and a great choice for SPAN 261. The Spanish department controls the content and grading for 261, but she was flexible when she could be and did her best setting our class up to succeed on the exams. 3
Great Spanish Professor- Super nice and caring. She is unfortunately constrained by the department's rules on teaching and examination.

Prof. Venegas is very caring, understanding, and excited to teach. She prioritizes learning language "the right way," so a lot of the class is based around partner discussion activities (very informal). Participation matters, but it's a very low judgement space. She is a pretty relaxed grader and understands that new speakers make mistakes!

Professora Venegas is a wonderful lecturer and a great Spanish teacher!! She is very sweet and understanding so never hesitate to go and talk to her. Her grading is also pretty chill and she will help you as much as she can. There's a lot of in-class participation and quite a few quizzes but just pay attention to deadlines and you'll be good.

Class is only graded by 2 exams and a participation grade, but Bruno makes it as easy as possible. He is very passionate about linguistics and wants us to talk to him in class (will cold call). No course schedule, just occasional reading homework to keep us engaged. Attendance is important, and he is sure to explain concepts clearly in class.

He is a very passionate teacher but very strict. Make sure you go to office hours. No computers/phones/ipads allowed in class-- all hand written. The class was also quite difficult for being an introductory course.
Lit teacher played Roblox all class and leveled up in adopt me hella take his class for an easy A
great class took it with the fellas and day traded the whole time I put bruno onto forex

I loved her so much, I am pretty sure any exams/assignments are not created by her but by the department she just grades them but they are relatively easy. Class participation is a grade and she cold calls a lot but is forgiving if you dont know it. Highly recommend!

Loved Monica, can safely say that she can write me a recommendation letter in the future! She is so kind and made me happy to walk into her class every single day; I could not have made this first semester without her.

She made what could have been a boring grammar pre-req fun and she pushed us a lot. Definitely an amazing Spanish professor. Tests were tough but she gave us a huge extra credit at the end which helped a lot.

Very very nice and helpful. She genuinely cared about you and your grade and was accommodating. She was not intimidating and would help if you were struggling. Try to do most of the readings before each class though so you don't get lost.

went to office hours for help, she implied she thought I wasn't trying or simply was not smart- offered no help to improve my understanding. I left feeling discouraged, the opposite of the purpose of office hours. She gave me a low participation grade even though I spoke 2-3+ times in every class, missing only 2 (both excused). absolutely absurd.

Don't be fooled by her kindness or her sarcasm. Tries to be funny but makes Spanish harder than it is. Participation is RNG, exams are 50%, and all papers and speaking is subjective to her harsh grading. Does not answer questions properly in class. Had to self study and learn to pass with a decent grade in the class. Take any other 203 professor.

Don't listen to the good reviews that say she is helpful, can teach, and is caring. She doesn't answer questions properly (literally said "I think that is the correct answer because it just is"), grades very harshly (points off for grammar), participation is biased and 10% of grade and not a free A. Take literally any other professor for 203.
Very nice and funny professor. Tries her best to make class interesting and engaging. Spanish 203 is not easy but I recommend her!!

Really great! I liked her a lot, she was super easy to talk to and was very excited about us learning! So sweet and make class very engaging and fun, we did a lot of great culture stuff too. Not difficult if you try and give it your best, just stay on top of the dates and you'll be a-okay!

Professor Alexander is super laid back and does not have heavy expectations. She doesn't expect you to be fluent in Spanish, and reviews a lot of key concepts. She grades very leniently, and she's very transparent about exam content. We spend most of class just working in groups; it's very low stakes, and casual. I would take her if you can!

Martha does come off as short or passive-aggressive to her students at times, but she does try to make class engaging and wants to see an engaging class having a lot of conversation during class. She's an understanding professor if you talk to her outside of class.

While she has received good ratings for lower level Spanish classes, I would avoid taking her class for anything higher than 204. She struggles to teach more complex gramatical structures and does not know any of the curriculum that the rest of the 261 students are being taught.
I love Señora Alexander. If you have to take 203, this is the most painless way to finish the language requirement. Be sure to participate and do the readings but she is funny and fair.

Spanish-only course but Prof. Alexander is easy to understand and kind! Easy grader overall, but make sure you participate in class because that's graded (not a free A). HW due before every class at 7:59AM. In my opinion course content is kind of all over the place, but that's common to all sections and Prof. Alexander tries to make it engaging.

I entered SPAN203 with zero confidence in my ability since it had been 3 years since I had last taken Spanish. She did a great job cultivating a comfortable environment so it was easy to participate. She is a kind grader and you can definitely get a good grade as long as you prepare for the exams, and she gives you the resources you need to succeed

Prof. Alexander is extermely nice. Class is taught fully in Spanish and feels more like a conversation than a lecture. Encourages a lot of participation from class. Great professor for understanding of the language.

I loved taking Professor Alexander. I enjoyed her lectures and she was always available after. I went from knowing virtually no Spanish grammar to bring conversational. She got frustrated when no one responded to her questions or did not engage so be conversational and if you're confused or don't understand something, just tell her (English is ok).

Hard class, tons of homework, but she is a really understanding teacher and genuinely caring person! Loved her attitude in class every day and she made going to Spanish 3 times a week much more bearable than it would have been otherwise. AMAZING!!!!!

Professor Alexander was defiantly my favorite teacher this semester and she made my days much better. She is a great teacher and gives very useful tips and is very funny. She made everyone in the class actually want to learn and engage with each other. Take her class if you can!

I honestly was afraid to take SPAN204 after a year of not taking Spanish, but Prof. Alexander made it a lot better! because I actually had a desire to learn! Super caring in my opinion and will try her best to cater to the class! She's an amazing option for SPAN204.

I really enjoyed taking SPAN203 with her. She was really great at teaching the material; she had good lecture slides, gave useful tips, and so on. She was also funny and nice. Also, she doesn't have a difficult-to-understand accent or anything like that, and the interview she gave that was part of the class was low-stress as well

Profe Alexander was definitely my favorite teacher this semester. She is so funny and cares a lot about her students. She is a fairly easy grader and pretty much as long as you participate in class and try on your assignments you will do well. If you're taking 204, try to have her. She is the best.

Professor Alexander is amazing. She teaches in a good manner and lets you participate in class. Participation is important in her class. She gives a lot of examples that can help you with quizzes, midterms, and the final. She cares about her students and helps them with anything you need. If you need to take a Spanish class she is the one to go to.

Dr. Alexander was a completely different professor in this class. Graded very harshly and without rubrics on papers. Made several comments about too many good grades making her look bad. Unhelpful and rude when asking clarifying questions. Everyone was shocked! I ended with a good grade, but it was difficult and took lots of effort outside class.

Very caring professor, she was approachable outside of class and understanding of personal circumstances without flat-out giving you the answers or just "handing out A's". Would absolutely recommend taking her class!
She's awesome. She teaches in a way that allowed me to quickly understand the material. I wouldn't recommend 203 with anyone else.

Take it from someone who struggles at Spanish: Professor Kohl is a really good professor. She encourages group discussion and participation, so make sure to read the textbook and know the material before class. She is easy to reach through email and office hours, and seems genuinely interested in knowing her students as people.

Always willing to help and very kind. Unbelievably approachable and knowledgeable on grammar. Definitely take Dra. Kohl if you can. In 204 I believe work is more or less the same across sections/professors, and it really didn't feel like too much.

Sweetest professor ever! This was my first ever class in first semester freshman year, Spanish 204 isn't the easiest to jump into (I did not take it the year before) but Dra. Kohl is always available to help! She makes class fun and engaging, genuinely cares about her students, and wants you to learn. If you can get Spanish with her do it!

Dra. Kohl is SO kind and helpful. she is so caring and also a great instructor. she knows her stuff and made every concept seem easy to understand. I have so much respect for this woman. she is so passionate about her job and makes learning fun. if you take span 204 DEFINITELY take it with Dra. Kohl!!!!!!!!

wonderful professor, super helpful and understanding and caring. very open to questions and encourages students to try their best. the class itself has a good bit of hw and the exams and quizzes are challenging. very grammar heavy course material. great professor though

Very funny, very kind, and a great teacher. Great at getting people to engage, content is clear, tests are very fair, and the overall grading criteria was very fair. Would absolutely recommend taking her for 102.

Lovely professor. Dra. Kohl really cares about connecting with students and giving feedback and helpful ways to actually learn the material. Very understanding and able to be reached outside of class fairly easily. I took the class for the gen-ed requirement, and don't need higher level spanish for my degree, but this was my most enjoyable class.

I loved taking Spanish 204 with Dr. Kohl. She cares a lot about the class and each individual student. As long as you put in effort, you will succeed in this class. She is so understanding and a great teacher. Highly highly recommend taking this class with Dr. Kohl!

Shes very chill and friendly. She is flexible with deadlines and doesn't put you on the spot; the class mostly talks and answers questions in groups. Super relaxed, but you need to study a bit and do the hw online (so not so bad). A few group projects, but she very easy and will respond quickly to emails. Attendance Mandatory.

Dr. Kohl is accessible, caring, and wants student success. Class activities are taken directly from the textbook, which can be boring, but she does her best to foster an interactive classroom environment. She is accessible at any time of the day, including weekends and provides ample resources to study from.

Dr. Kohl is the absolute best!!! Span 204 is by no means a cake walk but if you show up and put in the work you'll be fine. She is so caring and genuinely wants you to succeed, take her if you can! A very fair grader and easy to get a hold of outside of class

I absolutely adore Dra. Kohl! She has been one of the best and most understanding professors that I have had at UNC so far. She understands that her students may not know Spanish but trying is very valuable to her. She only speaks in Spanish but if there is a concept that needs clarity she will say so in English. Absolutely take her!!

SPAN 204 was pretty difficult for me, but Dra. Kohl's office hours really helped. Make sure to do the suggested reading and practice problems before each class and you should be fine. Not much graded homework, but you need to put in the work on your own in order to be able to participate in class. Kohl made our class feel like a family! Love her!

Dra. Kohl cares a lot about all of her students. She tries to make the class fun, is a pretty easy grader, and is flexible with deadlines. She's not a native Spanish speaker and explains in English when needed. SPAN 204 itself is pretty textbook heavy, but Dra. Kohl is great and makes it more interactive.

Dr. Kohl is an absolutely amazing professor and person. She cares about you as a student and a person and is always understanding and willing to be flexible. She really cares about your learning and comprehension of the material and is a very fair grader. I would 10000% take this course again with her as my professor.

Dr. Kohl is an amazing professor! I highly recommend her. She creates a comfortable and safe environment for her students. Although the course itself is hard, Dr. Kohl truly cares about the well-being of her students and makes sure no one is being left behind. She is the best!! Her grading is not tough but expects her students to do their best.

(SPAN 105) Doctora Kohl is my favorite professor! She really wants everyone to learn and enjoy Spanish. She is not strict and is flexible about turning in late assignments. There is ALOT of vocab, but as long as you know it and the grammar, you should be fine on tests. I thought this class was easy but it may be because I have taken Spanish before.

Professor Kohl has been my favorite professor at UNC by far. Not only is she an amazing professor, but I felt engaged during class. I never had to stress if I missed a deadline for homework, because she is extremely flexible with allowing people to turn things in late. She cares less about the deadline, and more about you learning something.

Definitely recommend him for span 101! Always available outside of class for questions, which was great with only meeting once a week. He was very gracious and encouraging, especially with learning a language for the first time. Did a good job of review and active learning/speaking practice in class. The class is tough but he makes it much better!

Jorge is amazing! Difficulty level 3.5 not because of anything about Jorge, but the content of Spanish 261 is just challenging in my opinion. But Jorge made class welcoming and enjoyable, even when the Spanish was challenging. He is a super nice guy, and I highly recommend taking a class with him!
Laid back, but obviously passionate. He really tries to make sure everyone's learning. I'm not much of a language person, but I really enjoyed his class.
Espinosa is very kind, funny and laid back. Class meetings are easy but the course is pretty difficult and textbook dependent. Only issue was the participation grade which felt arbitrary at times.

He's wonderful! Super fair grader, encourages participation, and really wants you to grow. Readings are manageable with short class questions, and he walks you through the final research paper step by step. Truly the sweetest professor—take Spanish with him!

Professor Espinosa is so kind and respectful of his students. SPAN 261 had a very manageable amount of homework-- just a reading with comprehension questions and some grammar to do before class. Can't recommend him enough!

Took for 261. Super caring and kept students engaged. I appreciated class structure and her was pretty organized. Consistent homework assignments on an online textbook, and one paper due at end of semester. 2 exams total, but weren't very difficult, and is a lenient grader.

Jorge is such a cool guy and a great professor, especially if you have never taken Spanish before. Spanish 101 is very much self taught outside of class with the textbook and less so through class lectures, but as long as you put in some time to memorize vocab, exams are chill. I am taking him again for Span102! Great option for Spanish.

The difficulty of a 4 is not Espinosa's fault, it is the course itself. The Spanish department here at UNC is ridiculous in how hard they make foreign language. 90% of students are taking these classes for gen eds, yet they make it one of your hardest classes. However, Espinosa is a good professor and fair grader.
Took in the fall. Great professor. Made it easy for beginners. Attendance is heavily required. Only one project, but I think everyone got a 100 for showing up. The online homework is really easy.

Super kind, caring, and easy to talk to about homework, tests, or material. Has a clear and simple teaching method, super chill class setting, and makes Span 105 easier than other professors would. Encourages but does not push for participation. Am finally actually learning Spanish. One of the most genuine professors I've had, definitely recommend!

Prof Espinosa is a caring professor who is willing to work with you to succeed. SPAN105 is a very dense flipped classroom, with lots of vocabulary and grammar being thrown at you on a daily basis. The class is taught with the same curriculum regardless of the professor, but Prof Espinosa was not a harsh grader and offered plenty of review in class.
Be prepared to be called on to participate each day. The class is a positive environment. You will learn a lot and actually retain the info.

Dr. Bruno is so sweet and super understanding. This class is an easy B and with a bit more effort you could definitely get an A. Homework isn't graded but theres a solid amount of participation grade assignments that help buffer your grade. Tests are fair and follow what you learn in class.

Dr. Bruno is very sweet and a fun professor. She cold calls on HW stuff in class but it's easy and she lets you go over it with other students before she calls so it's not so bad. Tests are very reasonable. Make friends in the class because there will be a couple group assignments (including a memorized 10-15min skit). Take her!

Professor Bruno has been one of the best Spanish professors I've had in my three years at Carolina. She cares for her students and will always love to talk with you about anything. She is accessible outside of class. Beware, she doesn't give too much specifics on the exams so you kind of have to study a lot. She will give good feedback though.

Listening to Dr. Bruno's accent all semester actually my Spanish worse. She is incredibly passive aggressive and cold calls on students every class. It was my least favorite Spanish class I've ever taken at Carolina. I did not feel comfortable making mistakes in this class which really hindered my growth.

Dr. Bruno is kind and always willing to meet with students / answer emails. As a non-humanities major, I found her class to be paper- and reading-heavy, and it was difficult to make above a 90 on said papers, with unclear grading criteria. Tests and quizzes require knowledge of textbook medical and cultural content.

She's a good professor. Her Spanish accent is a little annoying to have to listen to & she very rigid on grading especially for native speakers. Tests are crazy specific, be ready to have to answer something on her tests from a lecture you didn't think you needed to know.

I love Ms. Blanton. She is so kind and really cares about her students. I was afraid I would not learn much since it was an online class but Ms. Blanton made the zooms very interactive and easy to learn from. I learned a lot and I definitely recommend.

Professor Blanton is sweet and very helpful. I enjoyed her class even though I didn't know it was all online originally. Most of the work is done in the Alcanza textbook, while classes were spent reviewing and practicing the material. Would definitely take a class with her again!

Professor Blanton is a great instructor who truly cares about her students. The class was challenging for me since languages aren't my strength, but if you already know some Spanish, it should feel manageable. The assignments are easy, but the exams are tougher, so regular studying is helpful.

professor blanton was so knowledgable and passionate about spanish and clearly cared about helping her students succeed! she gave great feedback and was always kind when redirecting students during class and on assignments! the workload was completely manageable and she was a very fair grader! i would recommend her to anyone taking spanish!!

I would definitely take Span 100 with her again—she was so kind and the perfect teacher for learning a new language. Even if I made mistakes during my speaking exams, she was generous with grading as long as I stayed in Spanish.
Incredibly sweet and considerate. Really wants her students to succeed; participation is super important. You can tell she really cares about her language, too. Definitely take with her!

Profe Blanton was a phenomenal professor for SPAN 203 and I would recommend her to anyone who needs to take the class. Tests were a bit hard, but they are standard across all sections of the course. Blanton's homework assignments were not difficult and plenty of time was given to complete them.

Sarah ran our class with a lot of enthusiasm and humor which I appreciated. I missed quite a lot of classes and still pulled an 87% in participation, which is much higher than I deserved. SPAN 203 is a tough class, but I would recommend taking it with Sarah.

She's tough on her participation grading and I had her at 8am, so it was tough to do well on that. But she's a really good teacher and will always work with you if you need help with something. She wants her students to do well. Super nice and I'd take her class again at 8am rather than someone else's later in the day.

I really dreaded taking spanish and had to take the class for credit but Blanton was really enthusiastic and funny. She always welcomed mistakes and loves to talk to students. Participation really matters and I was bummed I ended with an A- but you will not regret taking her... one of my favorite profs.

Listen, taking Span for me has been difficult. But given the choice, I would gladly take 203 again if it is with Prof.Blanton. She made this class worth it and made learning Spanish enjoyable for me! It was tough (for me) but she clearly cares bout her students and is one of the kindest profs I know. Super approachable too. Please take her!

Prof Blanton was an absolute joy to have as a spanish 203 teacher. She made me want to go to class everyday, continuously brightening my day, welcomed mistakes, often let us out early, and made sure each of us felt valued in class. She always teaches with a smile, her energy is unmatched. Take 203 with her, you won't regret it.

I had confusion with expectations for written assignments but then went to office hours and he helped me and I got As from then on. Readings are tricky but you are not expected to know everything, just do your best. Also, utilize the extra credit assignment found on the syllabus, it was clutch.

He is super kind and very very understanding and accepting. I think the midterms were hard because there would be vocab on there we didn't know, but I don't think he is the one that creates them. He is super accessible and chill!

He's a nice professor but it was a lot of reading and he was a pretty tough grader for written assignments that didn't always make sense. I found the way literature was explained quite boring, and didn't understand many of the readings. I appreciated him taking our opinions into account for our participation grade though.

Really nice and chill guy. Requires participation and talking in Spanish with classmates which I really didn't enjoy but I survived. Didn't really rely on him to explain things to me I just utilized the Alcanza book and studying on my own. If you do the homework and go to class you will be totally fine TBH.

He is super kind, but if you're like me and hate participating, dont take his class. He expects you to participate at least a little, but also he isn't mad if you get it wrong or answer with broken spanish. He's a pretty chill guy and gives generous grade on the oral interviewHe also WILL check to see if you did the Alcanza "bring 2 class" ones.

Prof. Kim is well-intentioned and polite, but this class is unnecessarily difficult and workload heavy for 102. There was an absurd amount of vocabulary quizzes; the only way I could memorize all the terms was by writing down the words in a list, then translating them back and forth in Spanish and English about 10 times over.
Prof Kim is very kind and gives very in depth feedback about writing assignments. However, his explanations are often very confusing and I ended up watch YouTube videos for basically every concept

Javier has a scary rate my professor but I did not find it to all be true. His explanations certainly were more confusing than necessary but he was always willing to help me outside of class. He will show you grace as long as you show him that you are trying. He's smiley and happy to be there. As long as you study the textbook, you should do fine!

I'm a heritage speaker, but this class was a bit odd. The topics were explained in ways that made them unnecessarily hard. Javier isnt bad, but i'd take someone else if i could. Just read the textbook in detail & youll be ok. Participate in class too he will knock your points down if you speak English lmao. Learn subjunctive before starting class!
Horrible teacher, made concepts so hard to grasp and his lectures were impossible to follow. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM!!!

Was worried about taking 203 with a PHD student, but Javier was an amazing professor. He is very energetic during lectures and fairly good at explaining the concepts while speaking at a speed where he is not too difficult to follow along. He is a pretty fair grader and very accessible via email/office hours.

Not much to say other than Paulo may be the GOAT in terms of Portuguese professors in the nation, perhaps even the world. Really fun and interactive class, he really focuses on getting students to speak in Portuguese during classes, which is a lot more helpful than just listening to lectures and memorizing conjugations.
Felt like I learned less than with other portugese professors. Easier class. Maybe studied 2/3 hours for tests/oral projects.

If you ever have to take Portuguese, I 100% recommend Paulo. Makes class fun and interactive, where there is never a dull moment. I felt like I learned a lot, and he made it extremely achievable to do great on every quiz.
