Paulo is the best, if you can take PORT 102 with him you need yo or else you are missing out. Made the class fun and engaging and super approachable. He cares A LOT and will make sure that you understand all the content.

Professor Ferreira is probably one of the funniest profs I've ever had. It was extremely easy to do well, just show up, give an honest effort, and you'll do just fine. He was extremely forgiving when grading and you could tell he wanted all his students to succeed. Couldn't recommend him more.

Paulo is not only the best professor I have ever had, but the best human being I have ever encounter. He cares a lot for his students and makes Portuguese really fun. You HAVE to take Paulo for Portuguese, if not, you will regret never having the chance to meet an amazing person. Also it is unfortunate that you do not have a Jaylen in your class.
Paulo is actually the best Professor at UNC. Super chill class and a ton of fun

Paulo is perhaps the best professor I have encountered. He knows each of his students extremely well, gives the best feedback, and is understanding in a way that is rare among professors. On top of that, this is probably the most enjoyable class I have ever taken. I would crawl through a sea of broken glass and fight a pack of grey wolves for Paulo

I took Port 323 and Paulo is wonderful; you are lucky if you get to be in his class. He encouraged participation and made class a safe space to debate. I loved my experience in his class, and I looked forward to it even though it was at 9 am. Take class with him you won't regret it.
the GOAT also shoutout Jaylen

If you don't take a class with Paulo, what are you doing?! Taking his course after coming from another professor in the PORT department was a breath of fresh air. He is the best professor I have had at UNC and cares so much about his students and them doing well. While the content is not always easy, he makes it enjoyable...if you do your part.
By far one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Genuinely wants you to learn and is there to help you, extremely understanding and very funny. Not a heavy work load either.
I love paulo

Paulo is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. I took his class in the summer online and he made it feel like a real classroom environment and was very engaging. He really cares for his students! I cannot recommend Paulo enough, he is such an amazing professor. If you are taking PORT you 100% have to take it with him.

Legitimately my favorite professor ever! He is passionate about teaching the language and cares about all his students. You will learn a good amount and the class is quite easy. Just show up to class, participate and you will be fine. Dr. Paulo is 100% the best professor for PORT.
Paulo is such a great professor!! He is clearly passionate about teaching and does everything he can to help his students succeed. The class is an easy A as long as you put in effort.
One of the best professors I've ever had at UNC. He does assign a decent amount of homework but if you stay caught up and don't fall behind it isn't an issue.
Professor Paulo is my favorite professor I've had at UNC. He genuinely cares about every single one of his students and he made learning Portuguese fun. I enjoyed going to his class every week.
He's great, super nice and helpful. Take his class if you have the chance

HE'S THE BEST! We have 2 quizzes about movies, 2 papers, 2 online video presentations, and a final paper. I will say he does give low A's when grading but assignments are pretty easy and gives feedback. Always has me crackin' up with jokes, so sweet, and always attempts to keep the class engaged.
Take anything with him, attendance not required, but you will look forward to going to his lectures, which are awesome and an even better person.

The greatest professor at UNC and not even close, this dude freaking rocks, take anything with him. Lectures are very interesting, and he cracks jokes and really cares about his students. I wish every professor were like him. The GOAT
Easy, fun class. Recitations are required.
Goat. Take every class you can with him.
Very easy, good teacher

This guy's lectures man...they're actually so fantastic. By far the most engaging history class I've ever taken. He's always asking for participation, but never in a pressured way. It leads to a great learning environment. The content gave an amazing, all-encompassing view of the 1960s.

Every good thing you have heard about him is true. Best lectures I have ever attended and I was always genuinely excited to hear them. He is easily accessible outside of class and loves to get to know his students. Grading and recitations are up to the TAs, but the grading criteria is super clear for both essays and exams.

Wow. Professor Andrews was incredible! Coming from a stem major, I didn't think lectures could be so entertaining. The class is not an easy A. There are 3 papers that are graded harshly. Final was easier than the papers if you studied by the study guide. But class is worth it because of how great Professor Andrews was. Just enroll. You'll be fine.

His reviews say it all: Andrews is an incredible lecturer and a great person during office hours. He offered a full 2% extra credit on final grades, and the final was very fair if you reviewed some Quizlets or took good notes. The TA grading on papers could be tough, but not incredibly unfair.

Such a caring professor who has really interesting lectures!! Coursework was three essays and a final. The essays can be annoying if you have a bad TA, but go to office hours and work with them and you will be fine!! Extra credit opportunities give +2 points to your final grade so an A is very doable. Overall my favorite class this semester!

My favorite history professor at UNC! Dr. Andrews was my academic advisor for an internship as well. In both experiences he was such a caring, brilliant professor. He's well spoken and entertaining and makes his class content extremely relevant and interesting. Highly recommend. TAs grade everything, though, and they can be hit or miss.
Great professor, really cares about the class. Most of your grade is 2 essays and the final. TAs are super strict when grading. They'll always find ways to dock off points.

The lectures were very interesting however the final is based on knowing key concepts which are not made clear. Study guide mentions the structure of the exam, not what to study, so you are going into the exam not know what to expect regardless of your notes are. Grade in class is largely based on 3 papers which are graded by TAs who can be tough.

Amazing professor and great lectures, but the grading is honestly tough and since there are so few grades the final is stressful because you have to do well. Participation didn't matter but I always wanted to attend his class! Just go to your TA's office hours to get tips on how to do well on the essays. Also lots of readings.

Matt Andrews is a great person, and the lectures were interesting. However, for this class 67% of your grade is based on papers, and if you get a bad TA, as I did, you are SCREWED. I would not recommend taking a class with him if you can not pass fail it since this year he made his class significantly more difficult without the grading contract.
TAKE A CLASS WITH PROFESSOR ANDREWS IN YOUR TIME AT UNC. He is such a capitvating lecturer and the essays are not that difficult. Do it!!!!!! Olympics was so so cool.

Amazing professor and he's truly loved by his students. The course itself is so interesting, especially if you love basketball, and the grading structure is designed for success. Your effort and engagement with the content translates directly to your grade. The final exam is just an essay that you will be well-prepared to write.

I have but two regrets in life thus far: 
1) texting her at 3am
2) not taking Dr. A's classes sooner

Professor Andrews, as noted by many others, runs a fun, interesting class, where it is easy to thrive. Lectures are engaging, and you have two papers and a final, along with participation. He teaches interesting content, I recommend the class.
Goated professor, everyone should take atleast one of his classes.

DON'T TAKE. Makes you buy so many books, no tech in class, lectures are so hard to follow- no words on slides, theres no midterm so you have no idea what to expect going into the final. All assignments are graded ridiculously hard- they attack your grammar and prose beyond belief for a history class. Took for my create FC and seriously regret it
Forces all students to handwrite notes, then flies through lectures, which are needed for the assignments. Immense amounts of reading, expect to buy ~$200 worth of textbooks.

Professor Worthens "American Intellectual History" class is truly remarkable. If I were to point back to the transformational effect that college had on my values and judgement, it would be in that class. That said, the subject material is NOT INTUITIVE. Worthen is an accommodating professor but the writing assignments and material are difficult.

Professor Worthen both hadwith high expectations and was willing to work with and accommodate me as I went through a rough semester. Getting less than perfect scores from her pen felt in many ways more meaningful than the perfect scores I got in other classes, and I would recommend courses with her to anyone who wants to grow as a student.

Dr. Worthen is a very intelligent and engaging instructor. She is very intellectual and cares deeply about the content. However, I've never had an instructor grade as harshly as she does. Be aware that she wants near perfection on assignments and doesn't compromise on expectations. I took this class for fun and ended up with a C+ so be weary.

Lectures: dry with a bad aftertaste. Only talked about Christianity; on the one day we were supposed to talk about Buddhism, spent half the class talking about "New Atheism" wrt Christianity.
Don't take it, its horrid. You're graded on ~5 things, all graded harshly. Final question was "what is the meaning of life," answer imo is "not this class."

Dr. Worthen provides excellent feedback and constructs a class that challenges and greatly improves one's thinking and ability to communicate and write. Dr. Worthen was also extremely available and eager to talk with students about the class and general questions about life and the world. Dr. Worthen genuinely seeks the good of the students.

Prof Worthen clearly cares about her field and talks about it passionately. My main critiques are the lack of rubrics, tough grading (which is mostly on TAs), and the way she sometimes speaks condescendingly. I wouldn't take a course with her again, but I did feel I learned from her. I appreciated that she gave multiple extra credit opportunities.

She's is horribly condescending to students and most surprisingly the other professors. On multiple occasions, she has humiliated her colleagues in front of a class of 300+ students. Unnecessarily harsh grader and a rude person at best.

Dr. Worthen had really engaging and interesting lectures, but I wouldn't recommend taking IDST 122 for your Triple-I. It's an interesting enough course, but you're only graded on the midterms, paper, and final, and the expectations they have seem unrealistic for people fresh out of high school.

Whatever you do, do not take this as your Triple-I requirement. It is the hardest one by far. Grading is very subjective based on who reads it, and your TA can purposely take off points without giving clear reasons why. I attended every single lecture ready to learn and studied profusely for each exam, and never got higher than a 90.

Prof. Worthen is incredibly knowledgeable in her field, and I find her lectures engaging and easy to follow. IDST 122 requires a lot more work than I would expect of a first-year foundation, and it can be hard to earn a good grade. I personally find the class really interesting but would not recommend as a triple I due to the complexity.

Professor Molly Worthen was the singular worst choice for a Freshman Triple-I professor. Her level as a professor is far above what any freshman who is not an intended history major should be able to match. Yet, she expects you to match her level if not exceed it. She constantly degrades and condicends her students and fellow professors.

Ignore negative reviews. Prof. Worthen is a passionate and entertaining speaker. She comes prepared and expects you to pay attention and do your part. I think some give her low ratings because they don't want to do the readings and she gives some random easy quizzes for attendance, but if you came to learn, she is great. Engage and you will fine.

Among the most useless courses I have taken in my UNC career (which hasn't been very long, admittedly, but I should have spared myself from this back when I could). Drones on in her lectures, midterms were based on questions that barely reflected the lectures, busywork assignments. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE.

Dr. Worthen is super nice and extremely knowledgeable. I really enjoyed taking her class, but if you are looking for an easy A I would not recommend. To be successful, you have to pay attention and study names and general dates. Exams were difficult, but you will succeed if you put in effort. I would take this class again, it super interesting.
Absolutely wonderful professor and lecturer who is very passionate about her studies!

Her lectures were a bit hard to follow as her slides were more of a background than an aid, but overall I understood her lectures pretty well, she was a bit stricter than her colleagues who taught the class but still fine
While the class was challenging, Molly Worthen is a wonderful professor and lecturer. She is very passionate about her field of study and continuously encourages students to learn and grow.

Put in the work, engage yourself in her lectures, and be prepared to actually be a student in a college level course. All of Worthen's policies about note taking, tech, and class expectations are in your best interest. She's incredibly passionate, talented, and thoughtful. There are high standards, but she gives you every route to succeed.
I am taking a class on the Holocaust with Professor Auerbach this semester and it is interesting so far. Listens to students and she was helpful when I met with her about my essay.

Professor Auerbach is very caring and knowledgable, but the class is boring. The readings each night were very long and rarely talked about in class. She was very nice, but goes through the slides very fast and the slides barely have any actually notes to look back on. Guidelines for midterm and final were clearly posted before, which was nice.
The course was interesting, and Professor Auerbach is reasonable with grading and expectations. Class was engaging. There is a good amount of reading, but it is manageable.

Overall, I enjoyed this class, and it was definitely not difficult. Discussion post every week based on readings. Read a few books, and wrote short essays on 2 of them. The final and midterm were not that hard, I'd say, just remember your key terms. Grading came back late, but she is a fair grader.

The class was easy, and Professor Auerbach is very passionate about history. She gives you a study guide to prepare you for final and midterm. Overall, the class was pretty easy and lectures were hard to follow at times. You do have weekly readings and forums and two major papers that have to be done in class.

She is kind and was gracious to me when I was struggling, giving me extensions and hearing me out. She appreciates participation and will notice if you are active. The lectures are a hectic and hard to follow, but you can still do well if you can't pay that close attention to the material. Final was not hard; what was on it was what was expected.

I really enjoyed Professor Auerbach's class. She listened to students and I met with her at office hours a few times. Professor Auerbach is knowledgeable and she cares a lot about what she is teaching.

Prof Auerbach is very kind and knowledgeable but her lectures can be very confusing and hard to keep up with. Do the readings, they help with understanding the content and the quizzes so much. The TA I had was a tough grader. The final can be intimidating but if you did the reading it can help your grade a lot. Extra credit possible.

Everything said about this professor is true. While she is very kind and knowledgable about this topic, she is equally unorganized and her lectures are very hectic. Her quizzes are specific and detailed, make sure you truly understand the readings with dates/minor details before taking them. im halfway through the sem & only have one grade put in

I learned so much in this class. Professor Auerbach makes the lectures interesting and breaks things up with discussion. She helped me a lot when I went to talk with her about the essays. The exam is made up of short essays and terms, and she gives you a review sheet to study from.

BROOOO its been almost a week and a half and final grades are not out yet when there is a 72 hour rule super slow at grading but this is consistent with the rest of the semester often took weeks to give back essay grades

She is so passionate about what she teaches that her lectures are very unorganized. They are hard to sit through since, she keeps going back and forth on slides. The professor never answers emails but is very helpful if you attend her in person office hours. The class is also writing heavy and grading is based on TA.

Karen makes the history interesting if you pay attention, but lectures are dense and there is a lot of reading. She gives a review guide for the final exam. I went to her office hours several times and she helped me a lot with an essay assignment. This is the second class I have taken with her, and I would take another one if I could.

Karen is clearly knowledgable about the subject, but her ability to materialize knowledge into something her students can understand falls incredibly short. Boring unorganized lectures and slides making the readings the only way to truly learn. She is extremely unaccessible outside of class, often saying her email "isn't working" as an excuse.

Nice lady but lectures are really boring and repetitive. slides aren't organized the best. Very passionate about Holocaust. Don't really need to go to class except you gotta submit 5 discussion posts for participation. 2 3 page essays and 1 5-7 pg research paper graded fairly easily. final is blue book essay & vocab worth 25%

Professor Auerbach is super knowledgeable, and the content of this class was quite interesting and very important. However, lectures, while interesting content, were a little hard to sit through. I had to do a lot more work for this class than I feel like was necessary. I also really didn't feel like this class needed a recitation.

Professor Auerbach is a brilliant professor but sometimes her brilliance makes it inaccessible for students. Her lectures are interesting but it is hard to pay attention for the whole time. Grading criteria is clear but sometimes she is hard to reach and doesn't check her emails. I enjoyed this class but it was boring.

Overall, she is very knowledgeable about the topics for the class but the lectures are very very long and heavy. There are three books you have to read and 3 essays plus a research essay. Grades are very fair and she provides feedback and extra credit occasionally.

There was a lot of reading for this class than you had to write papers on. they were pretty interesting and led to good class discussions. No exams in the class, just 3 essays throughout the semester and a final research essay that professor Auerbach really helped you with if you asked. She is a little disorganized. she's a little disorganized.

There is a lot of reading for this class, but they were really interesting and we had great discussions. Participation definitely matters. Prof. Auerbach was very understanding with extensions. There is a research essay and she met with us individually to help guide with sources. Definitely recommend.

Super nice guy, chill professor. I took this class to satisfy a gen ed requirement but genuinely learned a lot. This class is very participation based, but its a smaller group so it is easy to get participation credit. Easy A, there is a lot of outside reading that content is based on but he cares more about reading a few pages than using AI lol.

Only reason I wouldn't take again is becuase no one really seems that interested, so he lectures for a long time. Otherwise, easy exams, short writing assignments, and he is very accessible outside of class. I think he should just teach higher level classes and not a 100-level class, maybe he would get more engagement.

Great professor, I loved his LTAM 101 class. Expect to have 20-45 page readings per class, but the lectures broke down all of the denser, more complex concepts into something that anyone can understand, so it truly wasn't bad at all. Definitely would recommend taking his class!
He gives students opportunities to come to their own conclusions, help them learn how to work collaboratively, would recommend this class and teacher to anyone interested in the subject

Dr. Walker is an incredibly nice guy and cares a lot about his students. He is newer as a prof but has his stuff together way more than any other prof I had this sem. He makes learning fun and approachable. Don't hesitate to take one of his classes

Professor O'Sullivan is a good professor, he cares about his students and wants you to learn the content that he is teaching in his class. His lecutres could be dry at times, but other than that I would recomond him.

He's the goat. Great lectures, easy enough readings (even though there are a lot of them), and the essays were not that bad to write. He also provides in-depth feedback on your essays, which makes you a genuinely better writer. The class itself was also exciting, and I always looked forward to going to it.

He is super awesome, engaging lecturer. Loves the material, class, and the students. Always available to help. BUT his canvas is very disorganized, many of the instructions for the class are only given in announcements, and if you miss those announcements, good luck!. Read all the material when he gives and the entire class will be fun and easy.

Dr. O'Sullivan is my favorite lecturer at UNC. He is passionate and pretty funny, although self-deprecating at times. I liked learning how history is still very relevant today in stuff like politics. Few assignments, and most are completion/effort. There is a lot of reading, but take the time to go thru everything to ace the midterm and final.

The only assignments were two 2-paged papers, a group presentation, and a final and a midterm that both consisted of two essays 4-5 pages long. Readings are really heavy, but you only need to know them for the essays. 
Dr. O'Sullivan is super kind and a gracious grader who gives great feedback. You can tell he loves what he does. Highly recommend!

Great professor for a fc-past class. Lectures can be a bit hard to follow, but the readings are what really matter when writing the midterm and final. Go to his office hours if you're confused, but the class is pretty low-effort to do well.

Dr. O'Sullivan is the best professor I have had at Carolina. He made the topic incredibly interesting. For HIST 339, we had two big assignments which were both papers for the midterm and final. He would proofread and help edit both, putting in the work as well and not just expecting you to. He also gave extensive feedback.

Dr. O'Sullivan is an amazing professor is who is passionate about what he teaches and is very kind to his students. providing great feedback to his students, he is very supporting and cares about his students' learning.

Professor O'Sullivan is the best; He's kind, caring, and ecstatic to meet with students outside of class and is always willing to engage student contributions. The class is interesting and so broad that you can absolutely focus on any particular thing you are more interested in and Professor O'Sullivan will encourage it. Absolutely take his class!

AMAZING professor! Attendance wasn't mandatory (except he did start using Pollev questions the second half of class, and I am not completely sure if that was factored into our participation grade), but I went to every lecture because they were honestly really interesting. The workload is also extremely manageable, with extra credit options as well.
Professor Gellman is the sweetest person and cares a lot for his students.

dr gellman is a great professor! he's extremely knowledgable and explains things clearly and makes things easy to understand without leaving out details / important things. your grade will really only depend on your TA, but dr gellman as a professor is great. this class isn't super work heavy either
Class is not mandatory, and lectures are easy. Only problem with the class is half your grade is five papers, and if you get a bad TA you are screwed like I was. Besides that class is easy
Lecture heavy, which I did not find engaging, but if you like worker history you'll like this class. 3-4 papers. the TA was fantastic.

Professor Gellman is very passionate about what he teaches. This class wasn't too hard and could be interesting. There are a few papers throughout the class and the only other grade is participation/attendance. Definitely take if you like history!
Gellman is amazing. Very interesting and very easy to get in contact with.
SUCH A GOOD CLASS it is easy and very interesting material

Professor Gellman is truly a gem at UNC. I loved taking HIST 128 with him, it was one of my favorite classes I've taken in my time at UNC. The class is graded by 3 papers, and the final was a take home 2 essays. I took it at 8 am but went to class every time just because of how interesting it was and how good Gellman made the lectures. Take this!!!

Lecture was not mandatory but even though this was an 8AM, I loved going to lecture! My TA was also excellent, and the grades/feedback were very straightforward. An A is easily attainable if you put in the work. I wish Prof Gellman offered more classes because I would sign up in a heartbeat.

Gellman is extremely knowledgeable on the subject matter and made having an 8 am really enjoyable. Your TA ultimately makes or breaks your grade but mine was phenomenal and could have honestly taught the class himself. While there are quite a few essays(5 including the two on the final) the prompts are quite easy to write about. No tests or midterm

Professor Gellman gives good lectures and is caring toward students, but I just wanted to say that for anyone considering this class as a gen ed, it is a lot of work. Depending on your TA, it might not even be that hard to get an A on papers, but nonetheless, 5 papers in a semester (2 for the final) can feel like a lot for a gen ed.

Professor Gellman is a great professor! His forte is American labor but his HIST 128 class was still very entertaining and informative. Lectures are not slide by slide but they are very vocally organized. The grades are based on 3 papers and a final paper, but they are graded by TAs. There are multiple extra credit opportunities in the class.

Dr. Gellman is a fantastic and understanding professor. He extends deadlines to help students and clearly cares about them. Lectures are informative and don't feel repetitive. Didn't like that the take-home final is 2 separate papers because there are already 3 others assigned throughout the semester. 5 papers feel excessive for a 100-level class.

Gellman is a solid lecturer and assigns thought-provoking readings. My only issue with the class was the somewhat vague essay prompts.

Would highly recommend

Dr. Gellman is awesome. I took him for Hist 128 and 365. Both great classes. He has done an incredible job making history class engaging, fun, and exciting. Assignments were a bit challenging, lots of papers, overall great class. The southern labor conference hosted this past fall was awesome. I would highly recommend taking his class.

Gellman is your typical liberal nerd history professor. I went every day and thought it made the papers easier but I know a couple of people who didn't show up once and still got a B or B+. My TA was the man

Dr. Gellman's HIST 365 course was incredibly enjoyable and well organized. There are 3 papers in the class and a paper final, but the class gives great resources for the prompts to the papers. The class teaches you a lot about American labor, and also helps improve your paper writing skills.

Professor Gellman was amazing. His lectures were informative and the class was graded through a series of smaller essays (3 pages double space each). My TA, Ben Fortune, was the best TA I've had in my time at Carolina. Couldn't recommend this class and Gellman enough.

professor gellman is one of the best professors i've had! i've taken both his hist128 class and his hist365 class. his lectures are incredibly easy to follow, his readings are interesting and engaging, and he's very kind and patient. participation is big, but he's awesome at setting up moments to ask q's. also, his TAs for this class were great!

Professor Gruber is an amazing lecturer and clearly loves what he is teaching. He makes jokes and keeps lectures light while also making sure to get through all the material efficiently. There are a lot of pop quizzes on the readings and lecture topics, but they're very easy if you pay attention in class.

Professor Gruber gave entertaining and informative lectures, and was otherwise approachable and willing to take questions. Grading may have been a little inconsistent-- it seemed that there was a lack of communication between him and his TA's about expectations. I prefer very specific guidelines for assignments but that isn't everyone.

Professor Gruber is a great lecturer and very nice professor. Make sure to come to class for attendance quizzes (very easy very hard to get wrong). There are 8 short papers, a presentation in recitation (very short), map quizzes, and a midterm and final. If you study the key terms and pay attention to the changes across periods, you should be set.

He is a great lecturer and very approachable.  There are several short essays, a presentation in recitation, and exams which are all pretty easy and fair.  If you go to class (which is required!) and put in any effort, you should be able to get an A.

Professor Gruber made ancient history the coolest subject ever! There are 6 short essays, all of which are pretty open-ended. Go to class for the great lectures and random attendance quizzes. Note the main changes across eras, as this is important for the midterm and final. There are drops and many chances at extra credit. Highly recommend.

Dr. Gruber is a fine professor. He is very knowledgeable about the material. This class was pretty easy, but the lectures can be bit boring if you aren't super into ancient history. There were 6 short papers graded by TA's. 1 presentation, 4 map quizzes and 2 tests. You have to come to class as in-class quizzes are a big portion of your grade.

Professor Gruber is really fun in lectures, but if you are not a history major I can understand why it can be boring. Grade is all dependent on papers so if you have a bad TA you're not going to do good in the class. Midterm and Final were harder than needed to be, but Gruber himself is super fun to have in class.

I absolutely loved HIST-226 with Professor Gruber! His lectures were fascinating and you can tell how passionate he is. The class is based on 4 papers and a final (all were relatively easy). Attendance is strongly recommended & there's lots of readings but it's fine to not read them all. I highly recommend this course and this professor.

I am a history major and I was bored in HIST 226. Dr. Gruber is a nice enough guy, and he was helpful outside of class. He tried to make lectures fun, but I didn't know what was going on half of the time because there was so much material (including the readings, which I didn't do). The rubrics for the four papers we wrote were vague.

Hes a very nice guy but only take this class if you are actually very interested in Rome. I took it as a history minor and I was so bored. I got As on my essays but a 50 on the final which tanked my 98 at the end. I didn't enjoy sitting in lecture at all so I stopped going. Every slideshow he has is paragraphs of text he reads directly off of

106 with Professor Gruber was great! He is a very skilled lecturer and succeeds in making lectures interesting even though it is not always the most exciting content. You may find it hard to pay attention if you are not interested in the topic of ancient civilizations. Tests involved long essay questions so understanding of concepts is important.

I really enjoyed this class!  I think his lectures were well put together and the assignment load was low.  3 essays throughout the whole semester and if you can write well and pick a good topic, you will easily make an A-B

First time teaching... He's nice but he struggles with the lecture format. Easy class but kind of boring if you're not already familiar with the material (but why would you take the class in then?) Only 3 papers but not hard if you have good writing skills. He would do better with more class participation. Not bad and could work but not for me.

A large portion of your grade is entirely dependent on showing up to class. Attendance quizzes happen almost every class worth a large bit of your grade which are free 100s. Weekly papers with readings attached but very fun lectures. My favorite history professor so far.
Professor Gruber is a super nice person and he is always trying to give us some extra credit which makes getting an A very easy. By the way his office hour is pretty worth going to.

We had weekly essays and two written answer exams in this class. Overall, the class was not very difficult and you should get a good grade if you put in enough effort. He was engaging and listened to his students' opinions on the way he designed the course.

Just don't take this class. Dr. Owre simply makes the class much harder than it needs to be by assigning lots of work. I'm generally very interested in History but couldn't engage at all with his lectures, especially since he refuses to teach in chronological order and answers at least 95% of questions with "I don't know, you should look that up."

I am someone who loves all of my history classes. However, this was unlike any course I have taken prior (of which there are many). Grand total of 2 assignments graded by LDOC, insanely tough grader (free write exams - 45 min only), and unclear grading criteria. I literally had nightmares about these exams and almost didn't make it out alive.
Really hard to understand. Heavy on tests, papers and hard grading.  Curious about his actual qualifications to teach.
Don't do it. Super TA dependent, lectures can get boring and tangential but if you skip them, you'll pay for it later with a bad grade.

Professor Owre is your standard, yet excellent history professor. The main class is a lecture and isn't too engaging, but the weekly recitation in which you discuss the homework assignment and that period of history is great. I do wish his class wasn't completely lectures and had more in class participation opportunities. Hope you get a good TA.

Weekly assignments, not to bad but are graded harshly. Good TAs. Lectures were engaging but hard to keep notes in. Overall it was awesome and I would take again. The assignments are graded harshly and give low A's on almost everything, but it was fair.

Fave prof at UNC. Caring, engaged. Super thoughtful lectures. I learned a vastly more complex and nuanced way of understanding history and current events. Only complaint is that if you want to learn the content, you have to be in lectures, and you have to be taking notes.

Professor Owre was definitely very nice but the damage that I think is about to occur to my GPA is a major thorn in my side. Although that is mostly due to me TA (who pains me even more), the way the class was structured didn't help much either. Essentially, unless you're purely interested in the topic, I wouldn't take this course.

I had to take other history classes the semester after to figure this out - Owre's courses are some of the most difficult you will probably take for 200-300 level history. Heavy reading, unclear slides, and very difficult handwritten essay exams. He's a nice guy but this class was far too difficult for a gen ed credit.

Prof. Owre is a kind, caring and engaged professor. Now, do not take this class if you are looking for a GPA boost or an easy one. Yes, it was interesting and I did learn a lot, but he is definitely a tough grader and you will have to work hard for a good grade. I recommend, but just be aware.
He had interesting lectures and was a cool dude. TA's are important though, as essays were an important part of the grade and my TA was extremely nitpicky.

This class was enjoyable for me and I looked forward to lectures and group discussions. He does grade slowly, though. If you're unsure about anything, definitely go to his office hours as he's very accessible. We had a variety of readings including memoirs and essays. The narrow focus on this class' topic made it dense but it was still interesting.

Professor Owre is a nice guy but as a history major I cannot recommend his class to anyone. I've taken difficult history courses but this one was completely unclear in its expectations and standards. The topic was interesting but the lecture was incredibly unfocused the entire semester. I unfortunately wish I had taken another course.

Genuinely one of the most frustrating classes I have ever been in. Changing deadlines, nothing posted on time, and unfocused lecturing. Also, grading criteria were super unclear for every assignment except one, and this guy has the harshest grading of anyone I've experienced in the history department. He's nice, but his class is so stressful.

I am so frustrated with this course and Professor Owre. This course was ten times more difficult and confusing than my other history courses during the semester. Owre is a nice person, but a terribly slow grader (we only had 3 grades out of 10+ assignments going into the final exam). Has the strangest methods for organizing/grading papers. 0/10.

This course was super confusing and not organized at all, plus the exams were really hard. It for sure isn't worth the GPA damage. Owre is nice, but as a teacher, I would never recommend him or take classes with him again.

Very nice professor, but the class is all over the place and not worth the hit to your GPA. Tons of readings, unclear criteria on assignments, very harsh grading on exams. If you aren't familiar with the content, would not recommend. Took thorough notes on every lecture, still none of it makes sense. Grades SO SLOWLY. One assignment graded by LDOC.

He is probably the nicest professor i've ever had. At the same time, I cannot give a good review. Lectures were boring, exams were extremely difficult, class was so unfocused. He never exactly explains what he wants on papers. As a history major, this class is not worth it. If one word could describe this class it's: CONFUSION.

Unless you have extensive background knowledge of Algeria, this class is super hard. Unclear grading and crazy difficult tests. Don't take unless you've already taken classes about Middle East. Not non-major friendly. Lots of books and discussion.

His classes are really tough. Homework tends to be pretty all over the place, and tests are weighted heavy and graded hard considering the time the class got to write them. Blue book, handwritten tests. IYKYK at this school. Lectures were okay but tended to be kind of unfocused on some days. I wouldn't take again, too tough.

Dr. Turk is extremely knowledgable and caring. She does a great job guiding you through the research and writing process. Even if her handwritten comments are nearly illegible, I still highly recommend any class of hers.

Lectures were very interesting, but your grade depends on your TA. Definitely go to your TA's office hours if you want a good grade. Be prepared to discuss a few readings each week, but there's a good variety. Take this class!

Her lectures were long and a bit boring at times, but she is very well versed in this topic. Your TA matters a lot and they do all the grading. There aren't a lot of assignments to be graded on. Overall easy class, but what is said in the lectures matter on the final exam.
Interesting material and a passionate professor.

Very nice, but lectures can be a drag. Lecture slides are provided but have little information on them. The recitations were helpful and great TA's. The class is graded mostly on papers but they start more lenient at the start of the semester.

if you care heavily about your gpa and can avoid this class, please do. i ended this course with a 89.94 and she refused to round to an 90, A-. so disappointed that as a chem major, this is the class that messes up my gpa.

great lectures, but they were scripted. accessible outside of class in office hours, but the TAs were the ones responsible for your entire grade. 3 short papers, midterm paper, participation, and a final comprised your entire grade; people complained about their grades from TA but I think they were fair and expected college level writing.

I didn't mind prof. Turk's lectures, although there is little to no information on the powerpoint slides so you really have to do your best taking notes. the main thing is that the TA grades every assignment in this course (final too). Even though the recitations were decent, it's like she refused to grade anything 100 (ex-4.8/5 participation)

She reads lectures from a script in an immersive, storytelling style. Barely any details on slideshows, so prepare to listen and take notes. TAs do the grading for the essays you write. It feels like the grading criteria were not clear. Prepare for boring essay prompts. The lectures are 2 days a week, and the recitation is once a week.

Turk is a good professor and accesible for office hours. Lectures were interesting as well as content. Although all of the assignmnets were short papers with such broad and confusing prompts. It felt like even though I knew exactly what the content we were learning was, my grade wasnt reflected because the essays were so difficult.

Material was simple and interesting, but lectures were read off a script. Prof. Turk isn't very involved outside of lecture. The reason the class was more difficult was due to the TAs. TAs consistently gave specific and harsh feedback, making it hard to do well on the 5 essays we were graded on. Recitation participation was the only other grade.

This class is incredibly easy. Lectures were sometimes interesting but mostly pretty boring. Turk is a very nice professor, but I felt I didn't learn much other than the social movements and presidents of the 1970s. Go to the recitations, participate, and put effort into your papers and this class is an easy A. Never once read the readings.

Professor Turk is a great lecturer and very engaging. There are few assignments, and TAs do all the grading. I had Skye, and a harsh, undeserved project grade hurt my final grade, even after a 97 on final. My recitation grade was 90 even after volunteering a lot. Tests aren't hard but fully written, so grading can be tough.

I loved Dr. Turks class! Her lectures were captivating and she was always willing to answer any lingering questions. The grades are dictated by the TA but I had Julia and she was amazing! As long as you go to class and do the readings an A is not difficult to obtain!

I had her for America in the 70s- she was great! She's an amazing lecturer and truly passionate about the subject. The class is very TA dictated, but they were great, so it was ok. No actual homework other than two short papers and one written lecture. I will say the lack of assignments can make one bad grade really matter but I'd still recommend!

HIST289 with Dr. Turk offers a lot of interesting perspectives on the US in the 1970s. Manageable workload though the final is weighted a bit heavy (35%, cumulative). Available outside of class for help if you need it. Kind and engaging professor.

REVIEW FOR HIST 289 - I loved America in the 1970s. It was a great class, I learned a lot. Professor Turk is a great human and professor. Her lectures are easy to understand. Most of the class was dictated by TAs but the TAs were all amazing. Highly recommend this class. Not terrible amount of work.

Dr. Turk genuinely knows so much about women's history and it is reflected in her lectures. She moves pretty fast and talks about A LOT in each lecture, so taking notes is essential. Attendance is require in recitation, but they aren't a drag to go to. Readings are required for recitation and 4 papers are written throughout the sem.

I really enjoyed this class with professor Turk, she was kind and made lectures easy to understand and fairly engaging. There is a mandatory recitation for this class, where attendance and participation matter. TA is more important when it comes to grade, because they are the ones grading the papers, but from what I could tell they're all great!

dr. turk talks very fast and can get a little monotonous, but the class is great overall! it's incredibly easy to do well if you do the readings (if you buy the online textbook, it has a read-aloud option) and participate in recitation. recitation was definitely the best part; we had a lot of interesting conversations!

Whalen is genuinely such a cool guy and made this class super interesting. Definitely not the easiest first-year seminar out there, and his grading was honestly a little frustrating in its vagueness. However, if you truly want to learn a lot about both film and the medieval world this is a super interesting and fun class.

Genuinely the best professor I've had here. He was very passionate about the material.  Short readings and watching films.  If you don't like participating in class discussions, this class isn't for you.  Take a class with him if you have the chance.

So many old, boring movies. Watched about 10 films, no color, silent, 3 hours long, and some in other languages, and most were not great. Had to read a chapter a week that barely related to move. There is a big group project, so hope for good group. MUST PARTICIPATE.
This introductory class was unnecessarily hard. Don't take it for the GenEd requirement.
Dr. Whalen is obviously incredibly passionate about the Medieval period and his students. Interacting with him is an excellent way to improve the uniqueness of his class.
Nice professor but unnecessarily tough grader with difficult exams. Not an easy gen ed. Don't take unless you really like medieval history.

Professor Whalen is really passionate about what he teaches and brings a lot of energy every class. The main assignments were group presentations and papers, which could be long. He is very considerate and flexible. He made learning enjoyable.

Cool teacher who cares a lot about history. The class was not hard at all. The only assignments we ever had were papers. There were 3 online papers and 3 papers were in-class "exams." All you have to do is read the textbook to do well in this class.

Super engaging lectures. You can hear his passion for medieval history. There are only 6 grades in this class but just have a clear thesis on your paper with info from the readings and you'll be fine. He also sneaks in extra credit on the final if you attend Friday lectures.

Amazing lecturer, however, doesn't take into account at all that this class is made of students fresh out of high school. Grades mainly consist of essays, participation, and presentations, which are graded fairly tough. There's definitely other professors who shape their first year launch better for freshmen, NOT an easy A by any means.

Dr. Whalen is a great professor who LOVES what he does and is always happy to give feedback on essays. The class was very interesting and discussion based, but NOT an easy A seminar. We watched a movie and read documents weekly outside of class. Part of your grade is from participation in discussions/group presentations and essays.

Choose another Gen-Ed. Professor Whalen is passionate, a great lecturer, and accessible, but the course is challenging. Grades only depend on papers, midterms, and finals, all graded harshly, expecting a historian's level of understanding. There are also daily readings which are long and boring. Class is also lecture heavy.

Professor Whalen is extremely passionate about medieval history, and that makes lecture interesting. However, the TA staff grades this introductory level history class as if students are writing a PhD dissertation, and getting an A on a paper required hours of my time. Love the professor, hate the grading -- if you want a Gen-Ed, look elsewhere.

From the format of the class, I thought it would be fairly easy. I was wrong, the essays were harshly graded as well as the midterm. I found most of the lectures uninteresting mainly because history is not my favorite. If you like history I recommend this professor. If you're looking for a gen-ed, I would look for a different class.

Very easy to approach professor, very passionate about the subject. Though the class is very Christianity-related, you may find some of the lectures boring if you are not interested in it (like me).
And about the papers, it heavily depends on your grader(TA). But everything else is fairly easy: open book quiz and cheatnote for tests.

Whalen is a very intelligent and caring guy. However, this class is unnecessarily hard for an introductory level course. I got A's on two out of three of my papers and an A on the midterm and yet i'm still on the precipice of getting a B+. The syllabus emphasizes it is introductory, however I feel like I'm in a 300 level course. Make it make sense
Professor Whalen is friendly and super passionate about the class content. However, the essays were graded extremely harshly I couldn't even get an A- in the class after getting an A on the midterm.

I took this class thinking it would be an easy gen ed and I was wrong. SO much reading and 3 big essays. The cheat sheet for the midterm did not help me whatsoever because I still failed. Professor Whalen is a great professor and passionate about his teaching, but do not take this class unless you are EXTREMELY interested in Medieval history.

Wonderful professor who cares a lot about his students and what he teaches. Definitely recommend if you're taking a lot of hard STEM classes to fill in a gen ed, his expectations are very reasonable and the class is very interesting.

Professor Whalen is super easy to get in contact with especially if you have any questions and he's relatively flexible. In this class, however, there were biweekly quizzes along with essays that were graded harshly, it's pretty hard to score above a B on the essays.

Took Fall '25. He is kind and knowledgeable but there are some hiccups. Lectures were all over the place, graded harshly, there were a ton of (long!) readings, and spent too much time talking about unimportant subject matters with students. Also, there were few women in the class & in his attempt to be inclusive he made things a bit awkward for us.

Took Fall 2025. McIntosh's classes require more active engagement than some others. His grading can be a struggle for some, but the curve is by no means harsh. He's always happy to research a question you have and get back to you next class. Monotone lecturer, but clearly in love with the subject and a funny guy. Not a blow-off, but I do recommend!

His grading style is unfair and puts too much work on students. Lectures are uninspired. He is rather hostile when a student challenges him, even if that student is correct (personal experience). He isn't really passionate about history or teaching.

"If you are wearing a sweater, sweatshirt, or something similar, you will need to take it off. Most importantly, if you plan to wear such a garment, please remember to wear an appropriate undergarment so that you can take off the garment without embarrassment" -McIntosh

Doesnt teach anything. His lectures are a bulletpoint style that only allows for vague descriptions yet his quizzes are all one essay based on the most in-depth things that were never covered in class. His lectures are not supplemented with reading material either. The only reason I did okay on his quizzes was because of prior historical knowledge.

Very boring lectures. Unless you're very interested in the subeject matter I dont reccomend. Attendance is required and if you show up you'll be fine, but he grades comparing students work to each other, so as the other students are saying if other people in the class are better than you you're not getting an A.

If you need a history course to fill out a prerequisite I do not recommend taking classes under McIntosh. He is quite rigorous and if you do not have evidence to support claims in your writing, it will show on your grade. On the other hand, if you want a nuanced understanding of the historical period and want grades based on writing, he is for you.

I enrolled in this class at the last minute and was almost scared away by the reviews - but I didn't have a choice. If you don't care about history, like me, prepare to be bored. BUT, this class really is not hard. He grades on a curve and compares your work to others in the class. His TA is nice and willing to help you with the papers.

If you like your sanity, stay away. Lectures are confusing and first half is ALWAYS a repeat of the last class. You will learn solely from the assigned (four) books. Books are read cover-to-cover, very dense and scholarly. Felt like I was being tested on memorizing the books. Three essay quizzes, four essays, final exam is timed essay. Slow grader.

His lectures are long, often off topic, and he is extremely disorganized. He's a nice man, but his grading is atrocious and his lecturing is worse. He shuts down students he disagrees with, and he even spent 3 classes talking about the inner functioning of pumps and machinery, only after saying it does not matter for the content of the class. Run

Lectures were entirely repeating what was said in the readings, and yet still felt disorganized. Quizzes are on broad topics with too little time to answer adequately. Additionally, you'll be waiting a month for you paper grades back.
His teaching style makes the interesting history disinteresting.

I love love love love Professor McIntosh! I took this class with my best friend, and neither of us are history majors, but we both love history and especially the Protestant Reformation, so it worked out very well! He was a wonderful professor, and I thought he was really funny. He also doesn't grade that harshly in my opinion. Best ever!

Early lectures were somewhat disorganized, dry, and reliant on the textbook, but all of this improved significantly over the course of the semester. Class requires a lot of books, which adds up in price. Reading recitation materials is crucial for the papers.The professor effectively grades everything himself, which gets fairly harsh and a bit slow

This class is the reason I am a history minor! Professor McIntosh is so knowledgeable and his lectures are honestly so great! He always takes time to answer questions and is so organized so you always know what's going on and what you need to do to succeed. He is one of my favorite professors and it is my honor to give him a 5/5!

Terence McIntosh does not have an interesting lecture style and teaches his lectures in a confusing order. He was way too harsh of a grader for a level 100 course, using a blind grading system in which he judges your work based off of others in your class. It was a challenge to stay awake during this class and to grasp what was going on at any time

Professor McIntosh is a highly intelligent and informative professor of German history. His class on the Thirty Years War was very comprehensive. However the class was hard and some of the papers were graded harshly, especially for a 200-level class. I feel that he wishes to mark all papers himself but he struggles with his marking workload.

Looking back, my review from March of 2022 for History 254 was inaccurate and crude. The lecturing isn't overtly entertaining, but it is very effective and professional. This professor is not a "bad" lecturer. 

Three Papers
Two Exams (Not open note/book) 

His grading is not unreasonable or hard, ignore the other reviews that claim otherwise.

Dr. McIntosh is an incredibly kind man. His knowledge of Medieval Europe is surprisingly thorough and impressive. However, you may not enjoy the course if you don't have an expressed interest in economics or medieval history. His lectures sometimes get discombobulated, but he can still deliver the information effectively.

Prof McIntosh definitely knows what he's talking about, but this class is so boring. He grades the 3 assigned papers throughout the semester so harshly for no reason. His lectures are also pretty disorganized. I've taken a lot of history classes at UNC and 225 has been my least favorite class/professor combination by far.

The class was interesting, but I found the lectures hard to follow. It's only graded off of a few things, and feedback takes forever to get back. We were tested less on the actual material of the class and more on our style of writing.

I had Caddell for Air Power, and I am currently enrolled in sea power. He had been fantastic in both classes! I especially recommend taking the classes with friends of possible, since lectures can be a bit long and are later in the day. Overall, if you can write well, the class isn't bad, but if you can't, then you will absolutely learn how!
Professor Caddell is a very engaging professor who communicates well with his students outside of class. My only complaint is that he grades based on 3-4 assignments with unclear grading criteria.
If you're in the major, Caddell's one of the best. Great lecturer, and covers all of the reading. Attendance not mandatory, but I recommend it.

Caddell is very knowledgeable and kind. The lectures weren't mandatory but they're good information for the exams. The lectures were definitely long and he takes forever to give back grades. Fairly easy class though despite the frustrating grade return length.

I really expected to enjoy this class more, given all the glowing reviews. While Professor Caddell is truly one-of-a-kind, this didn't always make the class enjoyable. Content moves super fast in lecture, the syllabus are super unstructured, and you're lucky to have a single grade back before the final. He can also be harsh with feedback.

The whole class is two papers, a midterm, and a final. If you are confident in your writing capabilities and are interested in the topic, I recommend this course. Professor Caddell is always willing to read your paper drafts, so take advantage of that. The class lectures are engaging and there is very little required reading.
4 graded assignments: thesis paper, midterm (includes paper), dialectic essay (10 pages), final exam (in class essay + IDs). Put in a relative amount of effort and you will receive an A.

One of those professors who really stands out because they're in it for the teaching. The class was a little disorganized and the lectures were super information heavy, but I learned so much from Dr. Caddell. He really enjoys getting to know students and is personable. If organization isn't a dealbreaker, I would definitely take a class with him!

Caddell is definitely unorthodox compared to other professors at UNC. He doesn't really use Canvas, syllabus is 100s of pages, grades slowly etc. BUT, Caddell is so knowledgeable, he is clear about his expectations for the few assignments in 488 and is very kind. He is one of the professors who wants to get to know you beyond the classroom.

Professor Caddell is one of the most interesting professors at UNC. I took both air and sea power, and he is knowledgable about both. Lots of notes, quick lecturing style, and writing, but you will learn a lot and he gives you all the info you need. I liked his courses.

Professor Caddell is a great guy and funny lecturer from a long military and academic career. Although attendance isn't mandatory, if you go to class and office hours it will be a manageable A. He reads drafts and if you give them to him it will be hard to do poorly in this class. Be there the class before fall break for some extra help.

Professor Caddell's class was great, although his lectures could drag on at certain points as he sometimes tends to ramble. The final exam was very easy, as he allows you to take one page of notes in to take the exam, ended up really helping my grade after harsh grading on the papers before it.

I really wanted to like this class, but I didn't. Lectures were often boring with him just reading off a powerpoint that was super repetitive had unnecessary information due to not being updated since the mid 2010s. Took 3 months to get back grades, and he's very particular about essays, which makes writing for this class a drag. :/
Sensational story-teller and extremely knowledgeable about all of the material.  Must take for history/lead majors, awesome guy. Three essays with a couple identification quizzes, and a final exam.

Joe Caddell is an extremely knowledgeable professor. I thoroughly enjoyed taking his class. You are graded by few things and he gives clear instructions on how he wants them completed. He grades harder than average for papers, but if you follow his instructions precisely and use "outstanding" sources, you will be fine. Lecture HEAVY, att. not mand.

Professor Caddell is an absolute legend. His grading criteria can be a little unclear, but please go and see him! His office hours or after class, he is very personable and clear once you can sit him down for a few minutes and after that all his courses are a breeze. If you like military history, do yourself a favor and take all his classes!
Tough grader for no reason. Slow grader too. Dont know your grade before pass fail deadline. Lecture heavy and lots of topics covered in short time period
Lectures were pretty dry and not mandatory. But he really cares about what he's teaching. Won't know your grade until the last week. 3 papers, 2 exams.

Dr. Caddell has not only historical knowledge but also experience in this field! His personal stories are hilarious and his lectured are engaging because of this. Even prolonged boring topics are made engaging because of this. Beware he DOES take a long time to grade. Papers are long with questionable criteria. Exams are hard but not impossible.

lectures can get boring and rambly, but his presentations don't have any words so make sure to pay attention and take good notes to use while studying for the final. you can tell professor brundage has done this for many years and is extremely knowledgable. however big chunk of grade is essays and depends on your TA.

Professor Brundage is definitely an expert in his field and could talk forever about class content, so lectures drag on sometimes. Presentations don't have any words so you'll want to rely on in-class notes and lecture outlines. Recitation discussions are good and helpful. Only two big essays TAs graded harshly. Overall a decent class for credit.

I took this class as an online summer course. Most of it was centered around a 15-page special topic essay. Professor Brundage was extremely helpful and engaged throughout the process, providing insightful feedback promptly. As I typed, I could see him reading every line of my essay to give feedback. He rambles a bit, but he is kind and cares.

Out of all the IDST121 Triple-I professors, he's the best. He rambles on a lot, but chill personality. Made us cornbread one day. You don't learn much from him (basic history/common sense). His assigned essay was weird, but not hard. Unless you're really interested in the South, only take if necessary. Other than the 3 essay assignments, no hw.

The class had 2 papers (40%), weekly posts, a final (35%), and participation. Grading is on a B-/B/B+/A-/A scale. Content was engaging, great if you like music history across genres. Worth taking, but your TA can really make or break your grade.

Super easy class, as long as you have a chill TA. 2 papers, weekly discussion posts, and a final, that's it. For one paper we got to pick a concert and write about it which I enjoyed! Only thing is lectures can be a bit boring and slides have no words, so you have to go to class and take notes to get the information. If you need credit, take this!

Professor Brundage was a really fun teacher because the content was something never taught before. His lectures can drone own a little bit but if you like history then you will like the class. The class is graded by two papers and a final. Get to know your TA because they make your grade.

the first couple of classes were interesting but then it became boring. there are no actual slides with notes just a prezi with pictures/videos and he never uploaded them. you have to go to class to make sure you don't miss any content and he talks kind of fast. the final had 3 parts: listening to two songs and comparing/contrasting, ids, essay

Very interesting lectures at times, but sometimes got boring. Attendance is not mandatory but I kinda regret how much I missed, def helps to have notes when studying for final. Grade is determined by weekly discussions, two papers, and a final. Spend a lot of time on the papers, they are important. Very nice prof, 5/5 for personality

Fitz was an awesome professor and genuinely nice guy. He often stays after class to chat with students. The class is two papers (graded by TAs), weekly Packback posts, and the final ICE. It's not difficult if you're interested. However, it is much more focused on the EARLY 20th century than later. Overall a great class, very interesting!

He is a good lecturer, but no keyterms on slides only pics/videos. So pay attention to what he is saying lol. Also the readings each week are pretty boring, but I enjoyed the packback assignments. Your TA grades all of your assignments so show up to recitation and show them respect.

The class is graded on two papers, a final, and weekly packback posts. That being said the amount of reading assigned every week ontop of the 1-2 hour movie every week is absurd. If you are taking for a gened just don't...

This class has so much potential, but I was ultimately left disappointed. The first 2-3 lectures are amazing, some of the best I've ever had, but soon it devolves into slow, monotone lectures with uninteresting content. My main issue is that the class isn't about pop music in 20th century, it's more like pop music 1840 - 1969.

Very interesting class if you like music and history. Prof. Brundage is very knowledgeable on the topics he discusses, and although some lectures were dry, he tries to make them engaging and interesting. Graded on weekly posts plus two essays that are graded by TAs, ask for help with them. Final is a lot of writing but not too bad.

Excellent professor who has an incredible depth of knowledge on a wide variety of subjects. Accessible outside of class and eager to help students. Lots of reading and his expectations are high, but you will learn a significant amount.

I took professor Morgan for my capstone course and 207. Having been immersed in his style of teaching both in lecture and seminar, there is no doubt he is an exceptional professor. His course load is rigorous, and his standards are high. He does not offer a free pass but something to aspire to. If you want a good humanities education, take him.
Dr. Morgan is an excellent professor and lecturer, so much so that, despite the sometimes ridiculous amounts of reading and the very demanding essays/exams, I absolutely loved his class.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The professor makes this elective class WAY too difficult. I recommend taking any other class. And he's Canadian to make it worse.

This class is VERY READING HEAVY. Weekly assignments range from 15 pgs to entire books. Prof Morgan is one of the best lecturers I've had at UNC and is incredibly knowledgeable about history and the Cold War. I would take this class if you're very passionate about the Cold War and have room in your schedule to devote a lot of time to the class.

I audited this course so can't comment on exams/grading but the lectures were fabulous. Riveting from start to finish and while they covered complex topics Prof Morgan delivered them in a easy-to-follow story that was compelling to hear. His command of the material was impressive and he is an enthusiastic and knowledgeable speaker.

Do not take this class if you are trying to do it for fun. Good lectures, horrible homework, especially if you are in other labor-intensive classes. Took this for my minor, wish I had not. 
Very nice guy though, highly intelligent. If the Cold War is of your interest, you may enjoy this more than I have. But LOTS of reading.
there is SO MUCH reading for this course, but dr. morgan is an incredible lecturer. grading is kinda tough but not impossible. overall, a really enjoyable class but not an easy A by any means.

Really interesting class but wouldn't recommend taking it for the fun of it. Tough grading and every answer on exams has to be specific. Interesting lectures but this class is too hard for what it should be.

ABSOLUTELY AMAZING lecturer. I never liked Cold War but somehow he made the lectures so enjoyable. 
Very heavy reading: 4 books, 200+ pages of documents/reading. However, you don't need to read all of them if you are paying attention during class and working hard.
The tests and paper were really hard, and each occupy very high proportion of the GPA

Professor Morgan is a great lecturer, I went into this class with no knowledge or interesting the Cold War and have found his lectures suck me into the story of it. He is knowledgeable and very passionate. On the bad side, this class had too much reading (5 books plus weekly chapters and documents) and the 10-page midterm essay killed my grade.

Very engaging lecturer, course is VERY heavy on reading. Most books on course reserves in Davis or online, I didn't have to buy any. Grading depends on what TA you get but generally if you do the readings and attend the lectures I imaging you would get a B or above. The exams are in-class blue book essays or ID tests and require a lot or prep.

Dr. Morgan was an awesome professor. He expects participation, so be sure to come prepared. He gives engaging lectures and thoughtful feedback. Office hours are very helpful. Not a harsh grader. Two 1000 word papers (10% each), participation (10%), final research paper (50%), and a few small assignments. He made me excited to come to class.

Morgan had an insanely extensive understanding of global history, Human rights, and philosophy. His knowledge of practically every country and all of their histories was outstanding. His lessons were discussion-based and extremely immersive, requiring participation and that you have done the reading.

The lectures were always interesting, but the slides are very sparse so lecture notes are essential. No technology is allowed in lecture so all your notes will be handwritten. The readings for homework are also quite long but if you take good notes in lecture, the reading isn't necessary. If you can, Marlon is the best TA!

Dr. Stieb is a really kind person, but PWAD 266 was frustrating mainly because of the course design. The final requires a lot of printing, and the scope of exams & quizzes is unclear. Grading is handled by TAs, but they tend to focus more on formatting than content, so the feedback isn't very helpful. Lectures also mostly just go through slides.

Take Professor Stieb's History of Modern American Class! Professor Stieb is both articulate and passionate in his lectures, while those lectures are information heavy they are engaging and enjoyable. The outside media is half readings and half muti-media helpful for younger students less accustom to readings. Excellent class, Excellent Professor

Dr. Stieb's lectures were well put together, interesting, and engaging. Through his class, I feel like I have gained a much better understanding about our current political situation and how we got to this point as a country. I think this class should be mandatory for all students, as the content is just so important and relevant.
Dr Stieb is a great Professor and really cares about his students - ensure you engage with the material and you will succeed! Would love to take another class!

I really enjoyed this class! Prof. Stieb's lectures are amazing, if a bit information-dense. He is clearly incredibly knowledgeable about recent American history. He answers questions and encourages coming to office hours (helpful). One of the few classes that has made me genuinely feel smarter and more informed about our world.

Take good notes!

Very knowledgeable and passionate about course content. However, he often used his opinion as fact and limited students ability to see the whole picture because of his personal political opinion. Also, he does not post slides or lecture materials online, so I recommend making friends with someone to help if you're absent. Does not allow laptops.

He is super knowledgeable and puts together good lectures. The majority of the final grade % is writing assignments, about half of them are take-home and he'll work with you and give feedback, but 3 are timed essays during midterm/final. No textbook but he assigns videos/papers to read, most are interesting.

Good class. Professor James is encouraging and answers emails quickly. Some of the readings are a little difficult, but none are that long and she covers everything you need to know in the lectures. Quizzes are open-book, and she gives you all the possible exam questions in advance. So if you study, you'll probably do well.

Very kind and encouraging prof, wants everyone to engage in discussions during class. Plenty of advance warning for in-class tests. Manageable amount of reading, never took more than 1-1.5 hours to prep for discussions. Go to office hours!

Prof. James is approachable and kind and gives good lectures. She's open to all perspectives and brings a sense of humor to class. She helped me improve as a writer. The reading load is completely manageable (~25 pages a class).

THE HARDEST A I'VE EVER HAD. I'm a dual stem major and this was way too much for a 100-lvl class. I really enjoyed the format and lectures but the workload/grading are par with my 400-lvl core classes. I did every reading (10hrs/wk) and studied 20hrs per exam, and BARELY managed to scrape up an A. Rating isn't lower bc problem is the class not her.

Professor James is incredibly kind. I honestly learned more than I expected in. I earned an A but this required an EXTREME amount of hours and effort. I would compare this 100 level class to a 300 level course at UNC. Feedback on midterm is only available via office hours and is largely based on the “vibe” of your writing rather than a rubric.
Nice professor, I really enjoyed

This NEW 100-level entry course only has 4 grades in the class: 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. There are no assignments, activities, slides, or lecture notes. Read 5-6 readings before each class. Her extremely harsh grading is only acceptable for a higher-level required class for SCLL students. I don't recommend this class at all.

Would not recommend at all. The professor is very kind and actually gives decent lectures. However, this is essentially an AP Gov/US history class with nonexistent grading criteria. Her midterm and paper grades are completely arbitrary with no clear explanation as to why she took off points. Otherwise known as "the vague B." Would avoid if possible
TA for HIST266. Very passionate about the subject but an extremely harsh grader.

Marlon is nice and genuinely passionate about the subject, but he grades quite harshly. His expectations sometimes reflect his own advanced level of expertise, which can be challenging for students taking the course. He was the grader and TA for the course. Was very accessible!

I enjoyed this class overall! Marlon is an excellent lecturer and it is clear he is very passionate about what he teaches. It is worth noting that 50% of your grade will be based on two papers which are graded very harshly. The final draws from the assigned readings and lecture material, so take good notes and read well!

Marlon is fantastic, but the class is challenging. Papers are easy but graded harshly, and quizzes vary in difficulty based on the material. The final exam is tough with three in-depth essay questions that require significant thought. I highly recommend this class because Marlon cares about his students and wants people to enjoy the material.
Marlon was a great TA, very dedicated and clear he wanted to help students in any way possible
Grades extremely fairly and wants to help

Marlon is the best TA Ive ever had. Hes engaging and really makes you want to learn the material. Great feedback and happy to help you with anything you need. Absolutely loved being in his recitation!

Professor K-L is awesome and one of the most personable and relatable instructors I've had at UNC! She truly cares about her students and the class is definitely manageable to be succesful in. Most of the grade comes out of group projects, with a fair amount of reading but she makes the class interactive and fun to attend.
Very caring professor. Would definitely recommend. The class was interesting and very easy to succeed in it.
Great professor and great class. I would highly recommend. Almost no work, just show up and take advantage of the class.

The lectures were extremely boring, with multiple long readings required and podcasts that were 30-1hr long. Quizzes were extremely niche, would ask what someone said in one of the articles you read weeks ago. No way to study for this class. TA's were awful. Had to make food w random ppl as a final group project.

Dr. K-L was a lovely, lighthearted lecturer. I recommend this class for anyone unsure about research but interested in academia. There's usually a small weekly assignment, and a group interview. It focused on career-building and thinking about research more broadly! The timing was unfortunately late, but most speakers were interesting.
Super kind professor who does great lectures! The pre-readings were often long but overall great professor and teaching style!!

Dr. KL is one of 3 teachers in FoF. I love the style of her lectures & the way she talks. Readings can be long, but I find them engaging; you MUST DO THEM and take good notes during lectures to do well on the 3 quizzes. There's a simple semester-long group project and final paper. Attendance not taken, but lectures aren't posted.

Dr. K-L is fantastic and I would reccomend her to anyone. I took her class her class focused on Research and she was great with giving advice to her students and being accessible to them as another research. She truly cares about her students' success.

One of those professors you will not forget. Genuine, engaged, passionate, and unreal intelligent. I feel really luck to have had Dr. Krome-Lukens.
