If you are at all interested in history, public policy, or just becoming more generally aware of how we got to where we are in America, PLCY 231 is the class.
ISDT 130 Futures of Food is mind-numbingly boring and the TAs were awful at grading. The lectures were pretty boring but I'm sure Dr KL is a better professor to take in her own respective department.

This course was not designed well at all. You have no idea what the syllabus is for the entire semester because they only release the schedule week by week. We were not told about a final until the last week of classes. The professors switched constantly and TAs graded terribly. There is no information on the slides to take notes on.

Dr KL is one of my favorite profs! Very caring but can be a tough grader. This is frustrating but she will review your drafts with you. Wants to know her students and encourages participation. We had a long paper due at the end and a small group presentation. Highly recommend Dr KL but I also acknowledge that she is tough. It is worth it though!

Dr. K-L was an amazing professor and friend. She was always friendly and lea the class in a very open and welcoming environment. While there was a number of writing assignments, her grading was concise and helpful. Participation matters especially as the class is very small.

Professor K-L is super great, and her class is very conversational. She can be a bit harsh when grading, but she leaves solid feedback. She really cares about her students, and she is well respected by students and staff. There are a lot of readings that can take a while, but they are necessary for class discussions.

class was interesting overall good, kind of harder grader, points off for little things; assignments: 6 reading pop quizzes w/ lowest dropped, 2-3pg faculty interview, 3 500-750 word policy journals, group plcy debate, 2pg proposal for plcy memo, 3-4 single space pg outline for plcy memo, 7-8pg plcy memo, oral presentation of memo

PLCY 231 was an annoying course to take. It was a lot of work for a 200-level policy course, and I'm still not 100% History does matter in public policy. That being said I did enjoy Professor Krome-Lukens, her classes were interesting and she did really care about her students. I would love to take her in a better course.
He should be fired. Unacceptable treatment of students.
very supportative of students! go to his office hours and he will love you. amazing professor. be prepared to read and talk in class
Interesting topic and good professor overall, but reading and writing was a little difficult (as expected). Lectures and discussions could be dull from time to time.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! Bull is a terrible professor. He speaks the whole time with no engagement. He sends out 5-paragraph emails daily. You're encouraged not use the restroom during class, you have to ask before going, no laptops. As a history major, avoid. He is also rude. Included a hard word on the final and refused to explain it to the class.

Marcus Bull is a very difficult grader and is not very clear on what he wants. I do not recommend taking this class for a gen ed, I did and I regret it. The classes are boring and the two essays were hard to write. If you have a deep interest in Elizabeth I go for it but if not take another class.

Professor Bull doesn't do much, the class for students is more dependent on the TAs. I unfortunately got a rough one. They can be really tough graders and the 3 essays are a large portion. There is no grading scale or rubric for the papers so the TAs just grade how they feel. The midterm is relatively easy tho.

I loved this class! Prof Bull is knowledgable and enthusiastic. Lectures are interesting and he posts an outline for each. Midterm was m/c & picture identification, final was the same + an essay(questions were posted 2 days before final). There were 3 papers which had slightly vague prompts. But, definitely take if you love early medieval history!!

Good lectures, very knowledgeable about the subject. VERY rude to his class, treats his students like middle schoolers. Throws a fit if people arrive a couple minutes late. Doesn't allow laptops in the lecture hall.  Midterms are not reflective of what we did in class. Take something else for your WB credit.

Incredibly boring and rude to students. Midterms consist of random facts and essays are graded very hard. Also given incredibly vague prompts for essays and then punished for not including things you could've had no idea knowing were necessary. Avoid this class if you actually want to enjoy learning

This class is very hit or miss. If you are not interested in the content, do not take the class. Lectures can feel disconnected and more like tangents than connected ideas, but there are times where content is interesting. Not the friendliest guy, but most interaction is with your TA anyways who also grade all of your papers. Reading is light.

Do not take this class for a gen ed unless you really like researching and writing and Queen Elizabeth! If I had more time to seriously divulge into the work, I think I would have enjoyed it more. He also doesn't want you to use double spacing which is super weird and makes it way harder than it should be. 30+ pages of reading before classes

Would not take this class again if given the chance. He is extremely inaccessible outside of class and not accommodating at all. Lectures for over an hour with no visuals, no notes, nothing but talking at you. Extremely strict about everything. It feels like he doesn't respect students or even want us in the class, teaching us seems like a chore.

This class caused me more stress than all my other classes combined. The lectures were unhelpful, full of vague, disconnected information and random pictures that you have to memorize for the tests. While he says history is not about memorizing facts, the test questions are very specific. The papers are difficult and time consuming. Not an easy A!

He has to be one of the worst professors I have ever had. The lectures were awful and the powerpoints were overall useless. They only contained pictures and no other information. This class completely destroyed my liking and passion for the subject of history. I really have no clue why his rating is so high, he was really terrible.

4pg source critique paper, 8pg main paper on anything you want, essay-based midterm and final. Wonderful guy, clearly knows and loves his stuff. As someone who's not a humanities major, I didn't know what to do with the papers but ended up doing pretty well on them anyways. Don't just fact-dump, analyze what things mean!

I absolutely loved this class. Prof Bull was clearly knowledgeable, interested, and engaging about everything he was teaching. He lectures without just reading from a powerpoint. Attendance is mandatory and you have to be prepared to take notes, but he provides outlines after class to fill in anything you missed.

He is very passionate about the topics and makes expectations about what will be on exams very clear.  Always post a schematic after class with the most important details that is perfect for studying.  Has a large emphasis on recognition of object but it is not difficult with a little review.

Professor Tasar is a wonderful professor who makes the lectures really engaging and enjoyable to attend, but he can sometimes go off on random tangents, and the course itself is a bit disorganized. Ultimately, I'd recommend the class if you need a gen-ed.

Fall 2025. Class of 240 ppl, and lectures were recorded and posted on Canvas, so attendance very much optional. Lectures fairly engaging, though the reading was a bit odd: a series of novels related to the content. Quizzes were sometimes on material not covered until the following week. Exams weren't bad, but grading heavily dependent on your TA.
Dr Tasar is the goat if you have the chance to take a class he's teaching do yourself a favor and take it

Lecture with optional attendance greatly appreciated (especially for a morning class!). Very personable professor who gave strong lectures and made a genuine effort to connect with students even in such a large lecture hall. Not an easy feat!

I love Professor Tasar! He was extremely engaging with some side tangents that I don't think I've ever been exposed to before which made his class very enjoyable. There is a ton of reading, but he prefaced the class by saying "If you don't like reading, don't take my class," but even then the reading was very interesting.

Dr. Tasar's 9/11 in World History class made me feel much more equipped to understand the world around me. Highly recommend to anyone, history major or otherwise. HIST511 is a seminar, so the class was primarily group discussion, with a mid-semester presentation and final paper. Take this course so you can tell your friends you have 9/11 class.

The lectures were nice, and the professor is very knowledgeable about the material. Attendence for lectures was not required, but the content being discussed was interesting. I did not get lucky with the TA, who was demanding and a harsh grader. Overall, the professor and course were great, but the TA was the only downside.

Professor Tasar is one of my favorite history professors! He clearly cares about the material he teaches and the success of his students. Lots of reading, but the books are generally engaging. While this class is called the history of 9/11, the first half of the course was dedicated to understanding Islam while the second half focused on terrorism.

Professor Tasar is very nice and if you like MENA and colonialism, he is a fascinating professor. He can go on tangents in lectures and get off topic, but we covered everything. Fairly easy gen ed class, and if you like studying the Middle East and colonialism, I'd recommend getting to know him - he loves lecturing and helping students out.

Professor Tasar was the best. For lectures you had the option to go in person, watch on zoom or watch a recording on your own time which was fantastic. Assignments aren't hard at all either. Only issue I had was I got unlucky with my TA assignment and he did everything he could to prevent me from getting an A but I still made it happen.

Great easy class for gen eds. Never have to show up to class except for first day. Most of your grade is a weekly online quiz which u can use chat to get 90+. Couple of easy essays and the final is a joke lmao. Class isn't really history after 1945. its a bunch of case studies where professor goes super in depth if u care about the stuff

He is a good teacher who knows his material and makes the class easy (I got a B+ because I suck at history classes). Class name was misleading as it wasn't really "The World After 1945" since a third of the class was before 1945 and we never talked about anything outside of Asia and Africa.

Dr. Tasar is a very good professor, who cares about the content. He doesn't make you go to lectures and posts a video of the lecture every class. Your grade is made up of 6 multiple choice quizzes, 2 five page papers, a final, and participation/recitation everything worth 10% of your grade. I would take it again
just by far the best history professor i've had

Professor Tasar is nice but the course was disorganized & he would often go off on tangents. Several papers to write, including midterm, final, and 2 event papers (which were both crammed at the very end of the semester). Rubrics for papers were unclear. However, a lot of your grade is open-note quizzes that test content directly from the lecture.

He is so funny and you will definitely learn a bunch, but everything is lowkey a bit disorganized. I also felt like he got a bit carried away at times, but it wasn't too bad. Do well on the quizzes (which all the answers will come from lectures most of the time) and you will do fine. Also make sure you know how to write an essay!

I enjoyed class with Dr. Tasar. He gives very engaging lectures and is super funny and kind. The only cons to his class is that he is a bit disorganized, which limited my learning as I am also a disorganized student. Essays are graded by a TA and also are unclear in the guidelines. Nonetheless, great class and a great professor.

Tasar is a good lecturer and he posts the recorded lectures so you don't have to show up. As someone who put this class on the backburner, I'd say this is an easy class to get an A- in but a tough class to get an A in. I elected to take it Pass/Fail after my TA graded my first (of three) papers, which is unfortunate.

Super easy class-- watched every lecture on my own time instead of going to class and did perfectly fine. Professor Tasar is really engaging and clearly cares a lot about the material he teaches. If you care, you'll learn a lot; if you don't, you can still finesse a good grade and easy gen ed.

Easiest class I've taken at UNC. 70% of your grade is quizzes which aren't very difficult. Depending on your TA they can be harsh on your essays. However, as long as you keep 100's on the quizzes and get above 80's on the essays you'll have an A.

I took this class to fulfill a requirement. Her classes are very lecture-heavy, but she wants everyone in the class to get an A. Grading is not tough, but she will not give perfect grades for surface-level analysis. Midterms and writing activities were easy, and the content was clear!
Extremely nice, wants all her students to do well, and is so accessible outside of class.
WORST TEACHER EVER. So extremely boring, and she expected us to write like professionals. We weren't in the class to learn, only to be judged.
This Professor expected you to write as if you were a PhD student in history. If you are not excellent at writing, do not take this class.

Professor Pennybacker is awesome! She is super understanding and caring. She is also very knowledgable about many things. We were really only graded on one paper and one presentation. She does lecture a lot, but its definitely a course to take.

Seminars with Professor Lee are a ton of fun, she keeps everyone engaged and interested. There is a graded assignment every class, so do the short readings and participate in conversation. She is also amazing about letting students make up work if they missed class. She's very kind, but deserves respect, so don't confuse her kindness with weakness.

Professor Lee is so passionate about what she teaches, and she made sure to guide our discussions and encourage us to share our perspectives. The course content and readings were very interesting, and Professor Lee was knowledgeable about all aspects of the course. She was always smiling and happy to talk after class, I highly recommend!

Dr Lee cares about student. You are guaranteed a B- on papers if you sign the no AI cert & she offered extra credit. But, there was so much ambiguity & confusion about her assignments. For ex, she only explained the final paper the last day of class/4 days before due date during exam week. Try writing a 2-3000 word paper when you have other exams.

Dr. Lee is very caring and approachable, and she offers generous extra-credit opportunities. The workload for this class is manageable, but the lectures are fast-paced, so it's important to stay focused and keep up. Everything is covered in the lecture, so attending class and taking good notes really helps.
Very knowledgeable. It really shows that Dr. Lee works hard preparing for her classes and she expects students to work hard as well.

Dr Lee is nice, but her class is so stressful & time consuming. There are 5 papers (ranging from 750 to 3000 words), 2 team presentations, quizzes, & a participation grade. Assignments are often vague and grading takes a long time w/ feedback being very high level. With 2 classes left, I have no idea where I stand since so few scores are in.

I personally love Dr. Lee, she's extremely kind and willing to listen to constructive feedback. This is NOT the class for you if you want an easy A, you actually have to pay attention to her lectures. The readings for recitation aren't too long and my TA Xinong was great. Dr. Lee also allows several cheat sheets on quizzes and on the midterm.

Dr. Lee is one of the best instructors that I've ever had. She is so friendly, intelligent, and loves to see her students learn. Dr. Lee talks pretty fast, but as long as you pay attention and take good notes, you'll understand the material. She allows cheat sheets on assessments, but you actually need to know what's going on to get a good grade.

The only reason not to get an A is not working hard enough, a fair amount of work for a college-level class. Nice to students, and very open to feedback. Lecture heavy, but all the information on the quiz and midterm is in the lecture. Give extra credit opportunities whenever she can. Dr. Lee is so friendly and easy to reach outside of class.

She means well, but her class is very disorganized. She changed the syllabus mid-semester, affecting the weighing of our assignments. Final grade is dependent upon your papers. Every class, we just talk about the reading we were assigned, so the format is very redundant. She is very nice and willing to help, but I wouldn't take the class again.

Prof. Lee does truly care about her students and wants to push them to become the best version of themself. While towards the beginning of the semester she was a very hard teacher, she adjusted as the course went along and takes feedback from the class to manipulate the style of the class. She is willing to help if you talk to her.

Y'all can't be serious guys, quality 1 is just completely unreasonable. Prof. Lee is a hard grader but she cares about her student and her class, and I personally learned a lot from her. Materials are boring sometimes, but just do the readings and participate you will be fine.

Dr Lee is a nice lady & responsive to emails. While the the class looked interesting (food+history), it has been super boring. We've spent a lot of time digging through library archives, have daily difficult quizzes, and tons of essays. Really slow grader so you have no idea where you stand. No tech allowed in class & all readings must be printed.
Do not take this class you will thank me.

Call me crazy but I love Professor Lee. Sure she's a harsh grader and assigns hefty readings but I really enjoy the class. I think about things that I wouldn't have thought of before and always leave inspired. As long as you're willing to talk in a seminar reliant course and can write a good essay, this class should be a breeze.

Prof Lee is a sweet lady who cares a lot about her class; however, she is completely and entirely unorganized. She changes assignments, class expectations, and even the syllabus as a whole on a nearly class by class basis, making it extremely difficult to keep up. Her course had so much potential to be great and was unfortunately a major let-down.

Am I taking a 100 level class or a 500 level class?? Only one midterm that consists of mainly open ended questions which are graded VERY HARSHLY. Almost weekly quizzes that you don't have time to finish and are designed to trip you up. I had high hopes for this class because Asian American history isn't taught enough but I can't wait to be done.

Dr. Grayson is extremely knowledgable in her field and is a very kind, understanding professor. Readings are done in class and she is not one to assign much homework. There are five total weekly essays that have to be submitted over the semester but she is a forgiving grader and does not ask for much besides attendance.

Got a 100 for everything, she is super sweet and understanding, put in a little bit of effort and you will be fine, you dont have to talk if you dont want to, very easy class, if you miss class you are literally more than okay, pls be nice to her, gives a lot of no classes bc of holidays so thats a W

Professor Grayson is one of the nicest professors you can have! She was very knowledgeable about a wide variety of subjects in the time frame (Middle Ages). The mapping project in the middle of the class was a little all over the place, but as long as you tried you got a good grade. She always made herself available for help outside of class.

Professor Grayson has been an amazing professor. She grades extremely easy and does not assign much reading for a history class. She makes you write a couple sentences about a reading before class, but it can be about anything and the readings aren't long. Exam questions given ahead of time. Lectures were reading off the slides, so sometimes boring

Dr Grayson is hands-down the easiest processor I've had at UNC. No textbook, just very light (a page or two) readings after every class. Aside from the midterm and final (study guide shows exactly what will be on the exam), there are 2 5-pg papers and she gives outlines of exactly what she wants. Incredibly, incredibly easy. Take for an easy A!

bad experience. Shields lectures only 20% of the time the rest are guest lectures, creating inconsistency in style and structure. Accent/lang barriers and frequent shifts make content hard to follow. Shields often misspeaks, and heavy Perusall/readings create an overwhelming, misaligned workload. 3 books to buy on top of that

I wish she was a bit more organized with the topics she taught. She was a kind woman regardless; I did feel a bit dismissed at times in class, but she was always very kind. She tried to teach political matters in a historical sense, which was a bit weird, kind of nonethelss though.

Professor Shields is really great. Lectures are interesting and there are often guest speakers. Most of your grade is dependent on a semester-long project. A nitpicky TA graded the first couple of things, but the other grades were pretty easy (including the final paper). Having to read a lot for every class is a bit annoying, but it's manageable.
Boring and repetitive class with too many readings on redundant topics.

I had her for HIST 62! She's a really awesome professor. Be prepared to write papers and do lots of readings, though. I feel like if I put in the slightest more effort, an A would be very easy in her class.

Interesting class but not taught chronologically which does throw you off. She uses a site called Perusall for hw which is a lot of reading and annotating but you don't have to read just put dumb responses and it counts. She was not always clear on the criteria for the midterm or final but was always available for an explanation also ask your TA.

I had Professor Shields for HIST62 and she was INCREDIBLE! She facilitated a respectful class discussion and allowed students to express their thoughts and discourse as long as it could be supported by the text. The final project was a breeze, with her providing excellent feedback before final submissions. There is a lot of reading though.

In HIST 62, Dr.Shields was very enthusiastic to learn and cared about her students. It felt like a lot of the things we did the first few weeks were unrelated to what our final projects needed to be. She was always willing to help us find sources or connect us to people within the libraries. Very few graded assignments and participation is big.

I did not enjoy Professor Shield's version of HIST 276. The class was not taught chronologically and Professor Shields seemed to assume that all the students had very high levels of prior knowledge. She assigned many readings, some of which were long books, that we never discussed in class or recitation. Easy assignments, confusing content.

Completely disorganized lectures and TAs that have to work overtime to clarify concepts & events. Seemed to hyperfocus on irrelevant details. Course not done chronologically, which I found intriguing, but only made it more chaotic. However, barely any readings and easy assignments made it an easy class. Completely checked out after a few weeks.

Biggest qualm is that I signed up for an in-person class and it was online. Even though we were told we would eventually go in-person we never did. She also seems to be easily irritated by students (ie. not turning cameras on, not doing reading early). TAs are amazing though and the class is easy so it was worth it.

Professor Jarvis is easily the best professor at UNC. I took her for both HIST279 and HIST340. She is extremely sweet, caring, accessible, and just a wonderful human being. Her grading criteria is extremely clear. Her lectures are engaging; she is clearly extremely knowledgeable and very passionate the material she teaches.

90% easy class, 10% harder during 3 key term check ins and final. No tech is annoying (I lost my notebook). Check ins don't actually test knowledge, just make u cram for 2 days and spit information. TA dependent, mine didn't use rubric which was aggravating and inconsistent. Lectures can be disjointed, overall good. Take for FC. 3 midterms +essay.

Professor Jarvis is incredible. Very lecture-heavy class, but she makes it interesting with a range of perspectives. Do the assigned readings; they make the final essay much easier. She cares so much about students and is accessible and funny, though the no-tech policy can be annoying. I could not recommend this class more.

This class was tech free for the first time. It made things a little difficult because she would change stuff based on how we did. In the course we had 3 key term check ins which were essentially our only grades besides the final (which was a timed handwritten essay). I think the course was very manageable and enjoyable. Also depends on your TA.

Genuinely learned so much in this class. Her lectures alone make this class worth taking. The assignments were tedious, but there were only three of them so it was not that bad. If you're interested in history and also need a class that isn't too stressful, take this one! There are also many extra credit opportunities if you're struggling.

She had a no tech policy which almost made me drop the class and I am so glad I did not. Dr.J makes the lectures super interesting and the class often flew by. She ensures you are prepared for the three check-ins throughout the semester, and they are graded generously. Only graded on a few items, 3 check-ins, participation, and final paper.

Dr. J is a very knowledgeable and passionate professor, engaging lectures that are a must attend to be successful. Show up to class, take thorough notes, and the 3 check-ins + final are very manageable. Plenty of extra credit opportunities. Very approachable and kind, but TAs heavily dictate your grade. Overall great course, highly recommend Dr. J!

Professor Jarvis is a very likable person and is very nice. She recently switched to a no-tech policy, so you have 3 check-ins and a final essay in class. Grade is really dependent on the TA; overall, not a bad class, but it can be tough with a bad TA. I would take her again as the check-ins seem to be manageable after the first one.

LJ was the BEST. The pre-work can be a lot, but it's all very intentional and helpful in class. As long as you interact with the material and pay attention during the lecture, the class is a breeze. The things she talks about are so applicable to real life and interesting. She is so kind and responsive. 10/10 take this with her

don't take this class if u want an easy gen ed. grade is very dependent on your ta. mine could barely speak english and my grade suffered. if you have a good ta it'll be a little easier. the final is a very long in class essay. she has a strict no technology policy. class would put me to sleep. only take if you're interested in history

Professor Jarvis is AMAZING! Tests were writing based and heavily weighed on how much information you knew about lecture and the ways you could connect them across the entire class! Readings are VERY important, but as long as you do them, come to the lectures and read over her slides (which she does post), and look over key terms, you are set!

Took her in the Spring of 2024, and so far probably the best prof I've had. Super kind and caring, lenient with deadlines, and overall just a good educator. Participation does matter, but she will never make you feel uncomfortable.

Really enjoyed this class for FC global. async maymester. A is a 93.5. 56% of grade comes from primary source analysis which are easy just make sure to be thorough. 18% each for midterm and final essays. last 8% are quizzes with unlimited attempts. super simple, fair grading, and interesting!! would recommend
Great professor and fair grader. Super accessible outside of class and really passionate about history. Take anything with her!

Dr. Jarvis is the reason I switched one of my majors to history. She knows SO much and gives everyone the space to ask questions and offer suggestions. Fair amount of reading but it's interesting subject matter. Small class environment makes for great group discussions. Learned so much from this class, Dr. Jarvis, and my peers.
Participation and going to class matters! Very kind and encouraged each student to give their thoughts during class. 3 major projects and a relaxed learning enviornment!

Decent lecturer, knows her stuff. The content is interesting. Multiple small extra credit opportunities and mostly flexible deadlines. Your grade for this course is dependent on the TA. However, the TA for this course (Thuney) is an OPP and a HATER!!!

Really great, interesting lectures. LOVED variety of lecture topics. Took as a major, but you can do well taking it as gen-ed. If you regularly participate and pay attention, you'll be successful. Three short papers, final is a group project, and there's a few VoiceThreads through the semester. Reading was reasonable and generally interesting.

This was an amazing class! Her lectures are captivating and she herself is absolutely amazing. Genuinely a fantastic professor. I took this class for my major but this would be a good class to get a focus capacity. There are three short papers and she weights the best grade the heaviest because she is the goat. Take this class.
An easy class as long as you put the work in. Material is not hard but make sure you attend class and do the assignments. Her lectures are amazing.

Professor Reid is very kind and encouraging. Although the class has a lot of reading (80-100 pages of reading due per class), I found the material fascinating. Classes are almost all discussion, so participation matters!

If I have one piece of advice, take HIST398 with Dr. Reid. He's so awesome at giving feedback, always checking in on us as people, built good community in class, and easy to reach outside of class. He made the paper feel less daunting. 1000/10 recommend one of my favorite professors at UNC!!!!!

The lectures aren't very engaging and you really have to pay attention to what he is saying because not all the material is on the slides. That being said, there aren't too many assignments. As long as you read the assigned material and participate in recitation you will be fine. It does mainly depend on the TA that you get and how hard they grade.
Reid is very knowledgeable, and is passionate about teaching students. Which TA you get can heavily influence your grade. I got a hard one, but was fortunate enough because they liked me.

Lectures aren't too engaging, but some content (eg Israel/Palestine, the environment, Apartheid) is very relevant, & the readings/films are interesting. You need to love history to enjoy the class, though, and 3-page essay limits can make it tough to say everything I want to (one required us to use 4 sources!). Worthwhile class for some but not all

We have 4 papers to write. The recitation was required, but the lecture was not. It was easy to learn if you didn't go to the lecture. Participation in the recitation was also required to count as present. We had 3 books we had to read, and would strongly suggest actually reading because you will write a paper on it in the future.

I absolutely loved Professor Reid and his course!! The material was heavy but extremely engaging nonetheless. There were two 6 page papers and a 6-8 pages final, all which were graded and returned extremely quickly. Dr. Reid gave incredible feedback and was extremely encouraging! I highly reccomend going to his office hours/talking to him 1 on 1!

291H: To succeed in his class, talk to him, do your readings, and PROOFREAD EVERYTHING. No tests or exams, but he's very into class participation and writing compositions as an alternative. I really enjoyed this class, it felt like just the right amount of challenging without being totally overwhelming. Very flexible about accommodations.
Nice guy. Decent amount of reading and movies you have to look at for recitations. Overall, solid professor.

I liked Professor Reid but my TA was awful. The TAs grade everything and mine was way too tough and gave mostly Bs (only 3 As total) for participation in the lecture even if you attend all classes and participate every time. There were 4 essays and the prompts were unclear and incredibly long.

This was a relatively easy, interesting class. Be aware Reid is often challenging to hear and rambles some. Attending lectures isn't mandatory, but attending the weekly recitation section is. These are NOT study sessions but seminars you need to prep for. Four three-page papers, recitation attendance, and the final paper are the only grades.

With one 2 1/2 hour class per week, you will be spending a lot of time reading novels for the class. In total we read 7 novels which sometimes necessitated us to read a full novel in one week. The assignments are not too bad, each week you'll submit a brief reflection on the assigned reading and there were 3 6-page essays (including the final.)

Unfortunately for me, attendance was not mandatory (so obviously I did not go). This led to me struggling immensely on the final because it was entirely based on lecture content. All papers/assignments are based on readings and films not covered in lecture so technically you could never go to class and do fine (until the final).

If you are interested in history, you will love Dr. Reid! He assigns really interesting readings and films that deepen your understanding of world history. Theres only 4 papers but they allowed for a lot of creativity and intepretation. His lectures can be long and a little dull to those not into history.

Professor Reid's lectures are boring, but the class isn't hard at all. Be prepared to read, write, and watch films often though. There is a recitation, but you just talk about what you read/watched. The final consists of writing an essay over a certain time period, but he doesn't tell you which time period you'll get before. TAs grade everything.

65% of his class are based on 4 essays. The essays are hard, boring, and they do not have a clear structure. The essays are graded by the TA's - they are graded very unfairly as they do not have a clear structure or requirements checklist and the grade only depends on the TA (better hope that u get a good one). Lot of reading and film watching.

Professor Reid is absolutely amazing! He is extremely caring, compassionate, & kind. He really cares about his students and wants us to succeed. He was very understanding with some extenuating circumstances I was dealing with & showed me so much kindness throughout. Truly a gem. Hes also very accessible! Take this class you will learn so much!
Great professor! Overall, she teaches very clearly and connects topics well. She gives good feedback on all assignments. Very calm environment with her!

She cares deeply about her students and is invested in our growth as people. Class is thoughtfully designed and really interesting. She took us to see Wilson Library's archives which was really cool. Great first-year seminar––interesting and fun but not overly difficult

She lectures very clearly. She grades written responses clearly and fairly, although there isn't a set rubric. Group presentations are fairly simple and she's very encouraging and respectful with her feedback. You are expected to do the readings, annotate, and participate in class.

I took LTAM314 with her. It was ok, wouldnt recommend. Topics felt random & irrelevant to modern law. It's graded by maybe 6 things total, so doing bad/ok on one of 2 in-class assignments will knock ur grade down bad. Most ppl didnt read before coming to class but plz do! Even if you like law like me, just take something else there's better classes

Prof. Silva was a delight to have as a professor. She was very kind and I loved that she incorporated different methods of getting participation points for people who may not have been comfortable speaking in front of the class. I loved the readings, and it's clear that she has a passion for the subject. One of my favorite classes of all time.

Heavy on the reading, but very entertaining lectures, talks as if he is telling a story and is easy to learn from. Easily accessible outside class, very kind and very understanding. Encourages people with no outside knowledge to take the class. Highly recommend.

Professor O'Sullivan gave detailed lectures and made sure to show every side of the various historical debates that we covered throughout the course. He provides good feedback on writing for history and is willing to talk and answer questions outside of class in general. He is very smart but also very down-to-earth, and kind to students.

Dr. O'Sullivan is my favorite lecturer at UNC. He is passionate and pretty funny, although self-deprecating at times. I liked learning how history is still very relevant today in stuff like politics. Few assignments, and most are completion/effort. There is a lot of reading, but take the time to go thru everything to ace the midterm and final.
Best professor I've had at UNC. 2 big assignments are midterm and final (both papers). He helps you with them before submission and provides great feedback.

Hard to take notes on his lectures, it's a LOT in a short class period. Very story telling adjacent, so he's fun to listen to if you enjoy the topics. Amusing, very caring, chill professor. Very understanding. Graded on midterm paper and final paper, and a few reader response. Lots of reading and one group presentation.

Professor O'Sullivan is so nice! The course is easy overall: 3 reader responses, a map quiz, a mid-term, and a final exam. Don't stress if you are struggling, go to his office hours and he's always willing to help. This course is reading heavy and quite fast paced, so make sure you do your readings or else you'll feel lost in class

Professor O'Sullivan is a very kind man who cares about his students, as long as you try to connect with the material you should be able to do well in this class. There are readings every week but he provides the material through PDFs. This class does not have many assignments so make sure to actually put effort into them.

He explains class topics really well, it makes class interesting. There are a lot of readings but nothing extremely hard. Also really important to take lots of notes in class for all quizzes and exams.

Very good class and experience with Prof Velasquez. I only took this class to satisfy some requirements but ended up finding it very interesting. He was also very nice outside of class and provides help with papers

So the class is history focused but on top of that you get other stuff. Basically lectures give you history overview and then the other assignments provide examples or let you dig deeper, like reading annotations on a website called Perusall. It was actually very interesting and the Prof was constantly engaging with us even though it was all online

Professor Velasquez challenged us to learn the course material on a deeper by giving us a variety of ways to interact with the content (movies, primary source document discussions, essays, podcasts, poems, music). He also presented historical events from many different perspectives, allowing us to have the full picture on topics we were discussing.

Prof Velasquez truly challenged my critical thinking. He would often provide feedback on our assignments which would help me improve my writing skills. Unlike any other professor, I have had I felt that I was able to learn while still being able to enjoy the material. You get used to the different format in Canvas.

A friend recommended I take this class in the summer with him and I enjoyed it a lot. FYI if you don't like writing papers, there are three in this class but you can pick which weeks you write them so you can see which week has more interesting sources

Prof. Velasquez is nice and knowledgeable. My first LTAM class, but I'm going to try to take more now since I enjoyed it. It's an overview kind of class but you kind of get a sense of what it's like in Latin America even if you haven't been because of all the media he uses. Take notes in lectures and post some comments to participate you'll be fine

The class goes from ancient times to the modern period in Latin America in short time, but you are just looking at the main themes century by century and it's actually cool to see things in that big picture way. He's flexible with due dates and friendly, just be sure to participate in the online discussions because you can't go back when they close

I liked Prof. Velasquez. It's not a hard class but it took more time than I expected. I took it in the summer so it was a short semester maybe that's why. But I learned a lot it's very interesting how connected the histories of Latin America and US are. There are papers but also weekly films, podcast, and short stories from literature that are fun

I took Intro to Latin America with Prof Velasquez because a friend recommended that I take it in summer with him. I was hesitant because it was an asynchronous class but it did not disappoint. He uses a lot of tools to make the class accessible and the readings and lectures are super interesting to see how connected Latin America was to US history

Prof. Velasquez was super nice and very knowledgeable. And he is very flexible with deadlines so long as you talk to him ahead of time. He just wants you to do well... I took this class Fall of my senior year, I was trying to get all my credits done to graduate and he was understanding. I learned a lot and wished I had taken another course with him

I really liked Daniel. I took him for LTAM 101 Fall 2022 because my original prof was experiencing health concerns. I wouldn't describe him as easy, but his feedback is super helpful and he has been incredibly accommodating; I would love to take another one of his classes in the future. Don't take him if you aren't serious about his class though!

Very passive-aggressive and tends to have an attitude with students at times. Needs to work on professionalism and should work on giving constructive criticism on papers. Very vague when responding to papers and does not provide exact prompts to help the writing process for response papers.
Prof Velasquez is super nice and knowledgeable

I took this class in summer so it was compressed, a lot going on, but the way the Prof structured it with a very specific schedule made it simple to know exactly what you needed to do, plus a lot of flexibility. The class was great, the prof is caring and knowledgeable and the lectures had pictures and stories from his own experiences in Latin Amer

Professor King is very knowledgeable in her topic and it shows in her lectures. She covers a lot of topic in a short time so it did feel rushed in some parts. The midterm and final was a lot of work and that really is my only complaint. Everything is graded by a TA so grade depends on them. Lectures were good and very organized.

Dr. King clearly knows her stuff when it comes to the subject matter and actively attempted to engage students in class. Unfortunately, I didn't personally enjoy many of our topics and felt our readings were pretty unorganized. Our final podcast project was a great experience though and fun to make. Just participate and do well on what's graded.

This course and professor King are fantastic. While she assigns A LOT of readings, the gist is more important than the exact details. Especially if you find yourself cramped for time/energy, broadly covering the books/readings helps. The assignments are specific in their criteria. However, do beware the midterm. It is VERY hard to complete in time.

Loved Dr. King, her lectures, and the TA, but not for everybody. Very intense, information-dense course. If you want to learn more about Chinese hist, this is the course to take. This is not an easy course to fulfill a requirement, though. Otherwise, Dr. King and TA are funny, inspirational, and very caring.

She is not inherently bad, but is boring. The class is graded by 1 paper, 1 podcast, 1 midterm, 2 discussions, the final, and attendance. Most of the grading is done by the TA, who is nice, but also is not a good teacher. I would only take this class if you know a lot about Chinese history beforehand, because the exams are extremely difficult.

There was basically a reading for every class we had but it wasn't too bad. I didn't like this class at first but really liked it by the end. Make friends in your class and help each other and it will be fine!
This is a good class for anyone interested in Chinese history. Professor King is very knowledgeable and always willing to help.

Lectures are a bit all over the place and hard to follow. Midterm and final make up the majority of your The final study guide has 160 terms and also includes the 90ish terms from the midterm. Will have to remember exact names and dates. Furthermore, you will have to read 3 full books on top of the weekly readings. Would not recommend at all.

This class wasn't too bad. I had a fun time taking it the homework is easy, participation is semi important. But we do have some papers and she can be tough at times. As well as a final project instead of an exam.

Lectures are super boring. She's a tough grader on papers (around 2). The midterm is impossible to fully complete without time running out. Stay away unless you are very familiar with Chinese History.
Would not recommend
King is so nice—I really enjoyed this class.

Not too many graded assignments so prepare to lock-in on your essays. As long as you somewhat attempt to participate during class discussion and skim the readings, you should be successful. She was super friendly and constantly open to revisions and new ideas.

The lectures were slow and there was no point in taking notes. Your grade is determined by 3 short papers and a 10 page research paper that you have over a month to work on. Not terribly difficult to get a good grade if you're a good writer, but I would suggest taking a more interesting seminar. Professor King is nice, but her class is boring.
Changed the syllabus four times during the semester
Just terrible

I desperately wanted to enjoy this class, but was disappointed. Lectures were incredibly slow and boring. Very long readings and the class is based completely off essay grades. Expected students to have graduate school level writing. Essays were graded pretty harshly with strict criteria. I recommend choosing an easier first year seminar.

Dr. King is nice and genuinely interested in the topic of this course, however she is extremely unorganized.  Readings were assigned the night before and quizzed on. Less than a week before a paper was due she was "not in the mindset to discuss it", not giving us instruction on a 5 page paper until the class before it was due.

The class was enjoyable, clear, and the papers and tests were all scored very fairly. There will be many things to memorize and read, but not overwhelming by any means. I learned a lot and had a good experience in the class.

MLS is as good as people say, if not better. Lectures are really engaging, and he is super nice and supportive. He's also pretty on top of communication and organization. Definitely recommend taking a class with him

Documentary-style lectures were really engaging and interesting (yet lengthy) readings. No required attendance, but come to class to be prepared for the midterms. The best part of the class is the historical video final project which was fun to write and film. Extra credit available for the best historical videos at an Oscar's-themed final class.

Dr. La Serna is an amazing professor. His lectures are "documentary style", not your typical lecture slides. This led to me enjoying every single lecture. The content is very important and I learned a lot of things I didn't previously know. Class is graded off of 2 exams (midterm, final), participation, & group project. Fun and interesting class!

The exams are graded fairly tough but both Professor La Serna and the TA were easy to get in touch with and work with. The lectures can sometimed be challenging to follow as he moves quickly and there are no words on the slides yet the subject material and the way in which it is presented makes for a very interesting (and important) history course

La Serna is an awesome dude! Lots of reading though… but I'm pretty sure most of the class didn't do them and it turned out fine. You might have to cram for the tests though if you go don't read them. There is a group video project you work on the whole semester (I guess your group defines your class experience). Such a fun class!!

Professor La Serna is a very engaging lecturer. He managed to convey a lot of information in a way that was "fun." He was also kind and accommodating. I think he really wants students to succeed, not just by passing the class but really gaining a better understanding of the history of Latin America- US relations and the modern day implications.

Hands down the best history professor I've had at Carolina so far, comparable only to some select TAs that were just as awesome.  You will not be disappointed by his lectures.  Highly recommend taking him.
I loved this class and professor. He is a great lecturer and almost feel like you are listening to him tell a story when he presents. Would highly recommend him.

Besides the TA grading, definitely the best lecturer I've had at UNC so far. His lectures were very engaging and provided many opportunities for students to earn participation credit in and outside of class. I would 100% him for history and non-history majors alike.

I enjoyed the class, and the professor delivered his lectures well. Interesting lectures to listen to, and the class itself didn't require much work outside of it. 65% of the grade consisted of 2 written exams that the TA grades, which were graded harshly. Wonderful class and a great professor who knows his stuff. The TA was the only downside.

amazing professor and his lectures were always super engaging. However, there aren't a lot of assignments that your grade is based on and lectures can tend to go kind of fast. Additionally, the TA was a particularly harsh grader, so unless you are confident in your ability to remember 50 IDs and 2 Essay prompts, an A isn't exactly easy.

Professor Miguel La Serna is super funny! His lectures are interesting, and the content is a lot of information but very interesting. There's a midterm, a group presentation and paper, and a final. Attendance is not mandatory but the more you go the more credit you get which goes toward your grade. The only issue is that his TA grades harshly.

This class was great! La Serna gave fast lectures and it was hard to keep up with him at times, but they were always entertaining. The midterm and final were not too difficult. There was a cool end of semester group project that raised my grade from an A- to an A cause you can get extra credit :)

He's great! I had him for my first year seminar and it was a really fun class. The class was pretty easy and discussions were fun. My only complaint was that I had to purchase like eight different books to do the readings (and they were sooo boring)

He is a great professor and very knowledgeable on his subject. You will end up loving him and the class environment he creates. However, if you disagree with him on his politics, some classes can be hard to get through as he does not seem to respect other political opinions.

PROF MLS IS AMAZING!!!! Taken for a FY-SEM, mls is the most personable professor ever. Very knowledgable and passionate about his subject. Amazing sense of humor; easy to access in office hours where you can talk abt class or life. Always finding ways to make class interesting. Lots of reading but you just have to focused on the main ideas.

A must-take if you're a history major. Lectures were documentary style which made every class feel like story-telling. Amazing professor and lectures that kept you wanting to go to class. No paper, but a long group-project for the final. Tests were difficult but definitely doable. Life-changing course.

Professor La Serna uses a "documentary style" lecture which is accompanied by audio and video. Some people may enjoy this, but I found it to be distracting and it made taking notes more difficult than it needed to be. No papers in this class and straightforward exams which was nice, the final was a group video project. Participation matters.

Prof La Serna used documentary style lectures for this class with audio/video playing while he was talking. This was off putting at first, but I enjoyed it overall. The 2 exams are straightforward if you study. There isn't a final. Instead, you have to make a group movie. Out of my comfort zone, but I'm grateful to not have another exam this week.

smart, obviously passionate, but in the most pretentious way. also assigns such insane, unnecessary work that even the TA doesn't know how to grade it. take if you're truly interested in the subject, but i definitely don't recommend.

I really enjoyed this class, and I learned a lot. I plan on taking another class with this professor. If you do the readings and take an hour to do the weekly journals, this class is super manageable. I came into this class with no prior knowledge. There are weekly journals and quizzes,and a final project, but no final though.

Prof Sweet is clearly enthusiastic about his subject matter, and his passion shows in every lecture. However, lectures drag on for what feels like forever. While the material itself is engaging, the lectures are boring and exhausting. The assigned readings are excessively long and often repetitive. Overall, I would not recommend this class.

Professor Sweet is an engaging lecturer but the content of the lectures are sometimes very traumatic with no trigger warnings EVER. The weekly reading journals are graded very harshly and there is no rubric. The TA gives no feedback on assignments and acts annoyed when asked any questions. I would not recommend.

I took this course last fall and a year later I still find myself drawing on knowledge from this class. Surprised to see so many negative reviews. Sweet is blunt but hilarious, and this was by far the most interesting class I've ever taken at UNC. If you have the time to do the readings/weekly discussion posts, I cannot recommend this class enough.

Dr. Sweet is super funny and knowledgeable about the topics he teaches. He does assign a lot of reading, but as the semester goes on, you figure out what is really necessary to read and you won't be reading every page assigned. The reading journals are kind of brutal. You do not need to print the readings even though he will tell you to.
horrid.

Dr. Sweet is a very intelligent professor and is passionate about his work. While there are weekly quizzes and reading journals, there is no midterm, and the final paper is 3-5 pages. You definitely have to put effort into the class, but it is not the worst.

Professor Sweet is an extremely knowledgeable lecturer as well as historian. The readings assigned are clearly carefully selected in order to reveal some of the most important and interesting developments throughout history. Professor Sweet is not always the most popular for his lack of sensitivity but he is truly an amazing historian.

Sweet was enthusiastic and knowledge about his work, but this class was a nightmare. Quizzes every Tuesday in class, reading journals everyday Thursday before class, with an in-class assignment to tell if you were present. 40+ pages of reading for every class, then 10 question quizzes about minor one-liners from the reading? Ridiculous.

Weekly scratch off-quizzes and reading journals, and he expects you to read the 30-40 page readings in entirety. He's rude, condescending, and insensitive. He covers some topics amazingly, but when it comes to racial topics he fails- makes insensitive jokes about slavery and racism. Although I loved the content of the class, he ruined it.

Mr. Sweet is a great professor to have. He really connected with my class. In the class there is sometimes a lot of reading, but it mostly isn't bad, and the work is easy. He is also not harsh on his grading. There are multiple field trips in the class, and you get to see what you are learning about in person and gain field work.

Dr. Sweet's lectures are interesting and he is great at teaching history of sex in America. There is a large amount of reading due each class and quizzes and short essays due each week. He was not empathetic when teaching Black history and made insensitive jokes. When students expressed that he offended them, he did not own up to his mistakes.

Professor Sweet is fun in an eccentric-esque way and the material for the course is very interesting. However, the workload is just absolutely unreasonable. We have 40-60 pages of weekly readings that you must go through in detail to score in weekly quizzes and reading journals. The stress wasn't worth it.

Professor Sweet does a fine job of teaching topics around sex. But what he significantly lacks is a sensitivity in dealing with racial concepts. When watching Birth of a Nation, he paused and asked the class if anyone had ever picked cotton. Not only is this comment inappropriate, but it lacks the necessary empathy needed to teach this content.

Sweet genuinely is one of my least favorite professors I've ever had. He is impatient, inappropriate, condescending, and a horrific grader. He makes you print 40-60 pages of assigned readings every class and is a distracted and un-engaging lecturer. Cannot stress how terrible this class is, do not take it.
No technology in class, weekly writing assignment, dry topics, difficult grader

This class was so interesting and I truly learned so much from it!!!!! An A is definitely attainable with a reasonable amount of effort, but you do need to try on the weekly reading assignments because the TA grades them pretty harshly. Grade is very much in your control but you do have to do the readings thoroughly.
Very difficult, does not respond to emails. He does not follow his own syllabus

I really enjoyed HIST236! I know people complain about his readings, and it's certainly important, but they're typically always relevant to the material at hand. The lectures themselves are not super structured, which at times bothered me but I got used to it over time. He is very knowledgeable about the subject at hand and pretty funny too.
266 is maybe my favorite course I've ever taken, the lectures are incredible and the prof knows how to capture the audience through excellent storytelling. TAs are usually pretty good too. 11/10.

The most interesting and intriguing lecturers I've ever listened to. Read the textbooks even if you can get by without. The final was one of the hardest I've taken because you need to have a deep understanding of many different aspects of the course, but it was so worth the work. Overall, one of the most academically rewarding classes I've taken.

It's jarring to see reviews dinging an excellent professor for assigning 10 (!?!) pages of reading per night. It's embarrassing that UNC students complain about having to read at the 8th-grade level and cry about their papers being held to a high academic standard. This is a top university, not a backwood high school. Lee is awesome. End of story.

Extremely difficult paper grading. One of the hardest classes I have taken at UNC, TA's will knock you down 10 points for something they said they didn't care about in recitation. Got low grades on paper's that would've been 95s in any other class. That being said, Professor Lee is fantastic, great lectures, engaging stuff, never skipped.

Don't be fooled by previous reviews; this class is DIFFICULT. Lee is a good professor, but he expects you to be a professional, and doesn't tolerate if you're not. Assignments are super comprehensive and graded harshly. 10+ pages of readings a night and lecture-heavy. Talks very fast and is hard to keep up with material. Would not recommend taking.

Wayne is one of the best lecturers at UNC and a foremost expert in his field. If lectures aren't your thing, he wrote the textbook to perfectly mirror class. Recitations are fine. Papers are a big part of the grade, and his TAs tend to be tough (sometimes unpredictable) graders. Hardest course in the PWAD core by content volume and academic rigor.

Probably my favorite class that I've taken at UNC so far. Wayne Lee is incredibly knowledgable and his lectures were always dynamic and engaging - plus he brings in a lot of cool ancient weapons to class! The TA's can be tough, especially when grading essays, so make sure to put in the work on the papers.

Dr. Lee was a really interesting an engaging lecturer, but if you are not all that interested in this topic off rip, definitely do not take this class. It is super hard to get into a lot of the material if you find this type of stuff boring. Although this class topic was not my favorite, I would definitely take a class with Dr Lee again

Wayne Lee is awesome! I'm in HIST266 right now and it is the best class I've taken at UNC. Dr. Lee is knowledgeable, has great stories, and brings traditional weapons to class. So cool. Research papers are intense but if you read the instructions you can do well. Attendance is important but not mandatory. Take this class if you like history/PWAD!

I had Lee for PWAD 250 and loved him. But I have him this sem for 266 and and this is absolutely the worst class I have taken at UNC. Biggest lovers to enemies trope ever. He is so all over the place during lectures he is impossible to follow. Unless you know everything about ancient warfare do not waste your time. DONT TAKE plssss im warning u

I thoroughly enjoyed the class I took with him and am taking another one this semester. The paper grades were tough for some people based on TAs, but I felt it was pretty fair grading. Make adjustments to the feedback you receive. Show up to listen to lectures to help with understanding themes for papers and the final.

Professor Lee's lectures are incredibly engaging and he truly is one of the best in his field. However, the TA's are extremely harsh graders considering this is a gateway course. Make sure to go to OH before the first paper to make sure they like what you're writing, since one paper grade can make it or break it in this class.

I wasn't a big fan of this class as it is a lot of lectures and the first half of the class was quite boring. It is just graded on 4 papers and the TAs are tough graders. You also need a 95% to get an A, it was too much reading, and I had to buy 3 textbooks. I wouldn't recommend this class unless you're very interested in the material.

Dr. Lee is a great lecturer! It almost seems as if he is overqualified to teach this intro-level course, he talks in-depth about things that don't match course material. Lots of readings, and you need to do them to do well in the class. 4 papers worth 80% of total grade & 20% participation. 1 TA is much harsher than the other. Its a lot of history!
Decent class, TA really screws you over in this course.
He is a dynamic and engaging lecturer. The class is reading heavy but ultimately worth it. He's just an incredible professor overall

He is the best lecturer I have had at UNC. Brings homemade crossbows and weapons into class. He is one of the leading experts in military warfare (wrote the textbook). The papers are challenging, but he makes it super clear what he is looking for.

Truly one of the best lecturers at UNC. Such a knowledgeable guy who makes lectures entertaining with personal anecdotes. Quizzes over the weekend (online). 2 research papers that are graded toughly by the TAs. Unfortunately, Lee definitely shows some liberal biases in his lectures but I would nonetheless definitely recommend taking his classes.

Amazing lectures, genuinely worth attending. You get the impression there isn't anything Lee hasn't done, he'll casually mention international archery competitions. Best way to get the FC-PAST, and not too hard if you listen in class.

Professor Lee is the best PWAD/History professor at UNC, hands down. Extremely knowledgeable, makes everything interesting, and the most complex topics understandable. He wants his students who put in the effort to do well
Interesting lectures, good class, tough grading but worth it.

Boittin's lectures are bone-dry, rambling, random, and occasionally border on offensive. My biggest gripe was our unit on terrorism, which Boittin devoted to justifying why the radical beliefs of those who murdered hundreds in Paris and Nice were not to blame for the events, but rather some abstract failing of European society. Just disappointing.

Class is alright but not very intersting. Quizzes are doable but don't have a clear rubric. If you try very hard in recitation you can get an 89/89 on participation which substantially boosts your grade so if you aren't willing to do that don't take this class.

Meh! That probably sums the class up well. Began interesting, but lost its intrigue as time went on. She is very knowledgable, yet this is quickly offset by her lackluster voice and seemingly disorganized lecture topics. Assignments were given at random and quizzes felt devoid of any lecture material. The recitations surprisingly saved this class.

The class really was not that bad. Many enjoyable movies and readings were assigned and watched during class. The professor and TA are clearly passionate about this topic. Only gripe, is that there is not really a clear rubric for any assignment and recitation participation can make or break your grade.
very difficult professor

No clear grading rubric. Quizzes were short answer style with little time to complete them. Feedback from TA's on quizzes would tell you to "add more detail" when you only had 10 minutes to handwrite an answer making it almost impossible to do so. Grade was essentially up to your TA. Unreasonably hard for a 100 level course. Would not recommend.

Boittin is very smart. Lectures were boring and nearly useless as quizzes were almost entirely on readings. Grades were pretty harsh, arbitrary and TA dependent. Recitation participation is very important.

There were 6 quizzes and there was no clear grading criteria for any of the quizzes. You will likely get the same score 3-4 times in a row with no explanation why. Also, there are no rubrics or anything, and the grading is based completely on the TA.
Very unclear rubric

I have never used RMP in my entire 4 years of college because I haven't felt the need to; the fact that I am writing this review should demonstrate how bad this class was. The grading was random, there is a no grade change policy, and classmates of mine got worse grades for the same quality work I did. Feedback makes no sense when given.
Boring lectures, readings were okay with a few movies thrown in. Grading is up to TA, which happened to be pretty harsh for a 100 level Gen Ed. Unclear grading criteria for participation and quizzes.

Do not take this class. Most assignments are graded harshly with no clear grading criteria. Lectures are very boring. Participation is 30% of the final grade and guidelines are not outlined in the syllabus. Seems almost impossible to get an A even though it is a 100 level gen ed.
Weird grading with no rubric - almost impossible to get an A, as the TA's grade harshly. The professor is nice, but the class format is frustrating in terms of grading.

I wouldn't recommend this class as a GenEd. Professor Boittin is fine, but lectures are slow and lack clear slides. Grading depends heavily on your TA and often feels subjective, with little feedback. Attendance is a major component of your grade, and participation doesn't guarantee an A.

Professor Boittin is a nice person and an engaging lecturer. My issue with the class lies more in her TA's. I was graded very harshly on
few assignments and was not given a clear rubric or instructions on how to improve. Participation makes up a large component of the grade and despite attending and participating full credit is not promised

Super tough grader. Grading is very arbitrary and all up to the TA. If you get a tough grading TA, you will get a bad grade. You only have 15 minutes for 5 quizzes throughout the semester, and participation takes the majority of the grade.

They grade everything with no clear criteria, mainly participation; attending all recitations with some talking isn't enough: the participation is arbitrary with no input. There is a harsh quiz grading system with 15 minutes to develop a full-fledged argument. Few assignments, but even history majors struggle with the quiz grading.

I like taking history classes as electives, but this class was not one to be careless about. Like it's too serious for a history class, with group projects and a bunch of movies and full books you have to read/watch, none in english. The grading is also too harsh, this class was annoying. not necessarily hard, but annoying.

An interesting course that seemingly got less interesting as time went on. The topics she discusses are clearly the ones she knows best, but that does mean it occasionally felt random. Some assignments were created as the semester went on which made it difficult to know what to expect each week, but all in all quite easy. Recitations were good fun!

Dr.Perez is an absolute genius and my favorite professor at UNC. His classes feel like high level academia, and they are subsequently not super easy. The class is mostly lectures where he just talks without slides or anything for the whole class. I loved it, but it probably isn't for everyone. His grading is harsh, but I think it's worth it!

There is no doubt Dr. Pérez is deeply knowledgeable of the Cuban Revolution, but most meetings consist of students fully reciting 5 page papers with unnecessary added context from Pérez. Take this course if interested in the Cuban Revolution and receiving mediocre writing feedback, but note there is little time for actual peer discussion.

This class is a weekly paper based on weekly readings of typically about 100 pages. Dr. Peréz is insanely knowledgable, but this was a tough class. We met once a week for 2.5 hours which was rough, and wrote a 5 page paper weekly. I improved as a student immensely, and absolutely plan on taking another class with him. He is a genius and loves it.

Dr. Perez is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had at UNC. His lectures are very entertaining and often feel like he's telling a story rather than teaching. This class was not easy at all, so make sure to take good in-class notes and you can side-step a lot of the assigned readings.

Prof. Perez is an amazing lecturer and a funny and genuine person. Only grades are three quizzes, midterm, and final. I would only suggest this class to history majors or anyone really interested in Cuba. Perez is a tough grader on the midterm and final. Read, take detailed notes, and engage with the professor and content and you'll be fine.

Prof Perez is amazing lecturer, harsh grader, and humorous presence in class. He is extremely engaging and I adored studying Cuban history in his class. Readings can be dense but be sure to note names of people mentioned for quizzes.

Amazing lecturer, teaches like he is telling a story- DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU FOCUS ON CUBA!!!!! Very strict grader, exams are horrible, grade determined by 3 quizzes, a midterm, and a final. I cried over this course and I would rather get hit by a bus than take a class for credit with this man again. But great lectures.

I love Dr.Goldmon, and I think she is a really cool woman. I want to be friends with her. The class is easy, and homework assignments and writings are short and not too complex. I thought some of the assignments she had us do were interesting, and recitation didn't meet every week which was nice. Can't say I really learned much, but fun class.

Professor Goldman is so nice and really doesn't give any homework at all. You're graded on only a few things, but if you do everything that's assigned, you should get a 100. It's barely any work, and recitations are only every other week.
Amazing professor, she really cares for her students and she is amazing at teaching. She always makes sure to figure out how to help her students when it comes to notetaking and lectures.

She is great, content was a bit boring, but overall, a good professor and is very caring for her students. Just a few assignments, but they are mainly straightforward and give you plenty of time and instructions to do them. Take her if you can I highly recommend.
Love her lecture! GOAT!
genuinely the easiest class I've taken in my life

Amazing professor; super kind and considerate. Her overall teaching style is very engaging, thought-provoking, and accessible. The assignments (the primary and secondary source analysis, book review, etc.) are very manageable and she offers plenty of guidance. I highly reccomend all History majors (and even non-majors) to take this course.

Dr. Goldmon was incredibly knowledgeable and caring. She knows what's going on and does a very good job lecturing. That being said, she knows how easy her class is. She makes attendance mandatory (through journal prompts every class), but if you go to class it will be very hard not to get an A. Absolutely take this class.
Dr. Goldmon was a very kind and respectful professor. Her class was a great overview of American history, and I would highly recommend taking this class if you need a gen-ed on the easier side.

Great professor and one of the easiest classes I've taken at UNC. Super chill, lectures aren't super intense, and your grade is based on a few short essays which are graded leniently. Goldmon knows the material well and is really nice (gives a lot of days off), so as long as you show up to class and recitation and turn stuff in, you'll do great.
Course was way too hard for a first year intro course, homework and test were obnoxiously hard for no reason.

You could tell he is very passionate about the course material, which helped make lectures relatively engaging. Quiz every class, but they were very straightforward and acted as a grade booster. TA grading made me ill, but besides that, I can't really complain.

I took a different class with Waterhouse and liked him much better in that one. He is so concerned about his students using AI that he makes his quiz questions impossibly specific and the human brain cant always remember the details hes asking for. Knowledgable about the subject but I spent multiple hours reading before every single class. Too much

Prof. Waterhouse is very respected in the field and I can see why. He explains historical concepts in a very easy-to-understand way to people who are not even history majors like me. There's quizzes (25 total, 5 dropped) based on assigned readings, and they're straightforward. You're allowed a double-sided sheet of notes for the midterm/final.

Listen, I do not like history. Like, it has never been my thing. That being said, I cannot get enough of Dr. Waterhouse's lectures. I didn't always do the assigned readings, and that probably wasn't the best choice, but his lectures were so engaging. This class was at 8 am, and he was the only professor that kept me awake.
Really awesome lecturer and personality.

Dr. Waterhouse is very knowledgeable about history. That being said, his lectures were often full of content and expected to be quickly understood (he mainly teaches 300-400 level classes). Ultimately, this class was hard for a first year class, however, I don't think that directly reflects him as a professor and moreover a learning experience.

Dr. Waterhouse is very knowledgeable in his field and was super interesting to listen to during lectures! The class was definitely tough, but I enjoyed learning from him. The readings are dense and often take a long time to fully understand. Homework was initially very difficult but gradually got better throughout the semester. Great professor!

Dr. Waterhouse is clearly very knowledgeable, but unfortunately is not a strong professor. His lectures were disorganized and hard to follow. Tests often featured questions based on random obscure comments he would make once with minimal relevancy to course concepts.

Dr. Waterhouse is so much fun to listen to and learn from -- he's extremely impressive and genuinely cares about students even in a large lecture. While this IDST class is difficult, I would definitely one of his classes again given his engaging and inspirational lectures. Everyone should listen to him talk about American politics

Dr. Waterhouse gave funny, interesting lectures and got everyone engaged. This class should not have been an 8 am, and was pretty brutal until they got the course reviews in mid-semester. The history sections can be dense, so give yourself some reading time, but he will cover most of it in class. Definitely take good notes.

Professor Waterhouse can occasionally get carried away with overly long descriptions of historical events that don't seem to matter as much as the course content that receives less attention. Nonetheless, the course was still very interesting and Waterhouse is a charismatic lecturer who absolutely keeps students engaged.

Focuses on the 80s up to recent American political history. Both Waterhouse and my TA were energetically invested in this topic, I found myself speaking with them after class on several occasions. Be friendly with your TA and let them know you care because they'll be grading all your papers. You can also bring a 1-sided page of notes for the exams.

Although I enjoyed the historical contextualization of this class, the grading was ridiculous. I took this as a gen-ed, but the TA's were overly critical and had excessive expectations for first and second year students. I got 90+ on both exams in this class and still ended with a B+. TA's are far too harsh on paper grading for the content.

Hist 129 was a really great class, and I had a lot of fun! The TA grading was not the fairest and way too picky for a low-level course. While I do not believe the grading was fully fair, the class is worth taking. The content is very important to understand, and the professor makes lectures so engaging. Waterhouse is very understanding!

for hist 129: professor Waterhouse is super kind and you can tell he cares a lot about his students. he is super knowledgeable and passionate about American history, and I genuinely learned so much about America's political climate and polarization. the class has a lot of readings and essays, but they are usually pretty simple and not too harsh.

(For HIST129!) Super engaging lectures and interesting subject matter. Attendance is graded through pop quizzes on the reading but they're pretty easy.
