My only complaint is that class always ran over by a few minutes, but never anything bad. Overall, this is a pretty easy gen-ed that I'd definitely recommend, and Dr. Waterhouse is a great professor

For 129! Solid lecturer and fair grader, and he cares about his students. There are two papers that aren't graded harshly, a midterm and final that are fairly easy, and pop quizzes on readings (of which there are a lot) that weren't tough. The material is also pretty interesting. If you put in a little effort, this course is an easy A.

For 129!!
This class is a pretty straightforward history class. If you put in the effort, it will be easy, and your TA's are there to help you. Professor Waterhouse is a good professor and really knows his stuff. The quizzes are fine if you understand the reading, but be ready to always stay a few minutes late in lecture, the reviews aren't lying.

THIS IS FOR HIST 129!!! It doesn't exist as a course on here yet. I thought he was really nice, the class was interesting, and the assignments were fair. If you need a history class but don't love history, this one is fairly interesting since it's America from 1984 to 2024. My TA was nice and your TA grades everything so make sure they like you.

Professor cohen was the absolute woat (worst of all time). I don't think I've ever hated ancient pottery more. You are expected to know everything found in a bunch of different archaeological sites. I thought this class would be fun and make me want to go to places in the Mediterranean, it was not fun and now I hate the Mediterranean

This was the most disappointing class I've taken at UNC. I had never taken a CLAR class before, but I decided to give it a chance, and that was a huge mistake. This class was extremely unrealistic & time consuming for a 100-level course, and Prof. Cohen was nice, but not helpful at all. Stay away at all costs.

Buried Alive like an artifact:
If the goal of this course was to make me empathize with an inanimate object buried under tons of sediment for centuries, then mission accomplished. I walked into this class a living, breathing student, and I walked out feeling like a fossilized relic crushed under the weight of ungodly expectations for a focus cap.

This professor was easily the worst professor I have taken in my academic career. Despite the grade I made in the class I tried to fully apply myself to the lectures and material given, and it still was not enough. Her tests are COMPLETELY written response, no multiple choice. I took this class out of interest for archaeology... never again.

Honestly an embarrassment to archaeology. She has me fighting to stay awake every class. She grades so harshly and expects we memorize everything. When you fail, she blames you for it, offering no real help. There's a reason why so many people dropped her class at the start of the semester. If you have her, drop it now.

Unreasonably difficult for an intro level course. Lectures were not helpful for tests, which were a majority of the grade. Had to memorize hundreds of slides that weren't thoroughly explained in class. Grading was harsh and unclear. Would not recommend this professor.

This class is a little difficult, but as long as you take good notes on the necessary monuments (use office hours to fill in the gaps) and use the study guide, you should be fine. She's very passionate, especially later in the course when you get to Italy, which I found really fun to listen to. Without a microphone it was hard to hear her though.

I honestly don't know what to say other than that there is nothing in this world worth taking this class for. You are expected to memorize every little thing she mentions in class, even if it's not included in the slideshow (>300 slides per exam btw!) It's genuinely hell like please there are much easier focus capacities for the same credit.
Bro is from pompeii or elsewhere, she speaks latin lmao. Take latin before this class
Just finished the final for the exam, and holy hell, words cannot explain how terrible and hard this exam was. I literally take STEM classes, and this shit was worse than my orgo chemistry classes.

Free-response exams make up 70 percent of your final grade. Professor grades this class like she has something to prove. It seems like she wants to show off how much she knows and how little you know. Don't take this class at all costs.
prepare to memorize latin and other wtf language names and to memorize 200 pictures of artifacts and buildings in order to pass

I can say with 100% sincerity that the only enjoyable thing about this class is reading the other reviews on this page. Feels like her whole goal in teaching this course was to flex on students with how much archaeology she knows and then fail everyone to make herself feel smart and special. Absolute waste of everyone's time.

If you are not a religious person, you'd better pick one and start praying because this course itself will make you start questioning your worth as a human being. I know seniors in the class who are FAILING because it's so hard. I'm literally failing this class, and it's not even funny. What a great way to end my first semester as a freshman.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS BY ANY MEANS. She teaches like she hates her life, and she will make you hate yours. This class is not set up in any way, shape, or form to make students succeed whatsoever. Gonna have to get straight A's after this just to make up for the shitty grade I received.

If I could travel back in time to the ancient cities myself, and have to go through the agonizing pain of finding the ancient artifacts just to never take the god-awful course, I would in a heartbeat. Take this class if you are genuinely an unhappy person. How worse could life get?

Legitimately the worst teacher I've ever had. I went into this class thinking it would be easy since it's a 120 class, but you are expected to know every tiny detail about a site we've talked about in class to get a good grade on the exams. She is an extremely tough grader and never explained what we got wrong on past exams. NEVER TAKE THIS CLASS!

Worst class I have ever taken, take this class if you want to be miserable. Harsh grader that will take points off and not give clear reasons. A class that does NOT have learning objectives, a clear schedule, structure, or enjoyment. Constantly confused due to bad set up to the content shes teaching. And acts as if youre dumb for asking questions.

I would rather live in ancient Babylonia then step foot near this class and this professor every again. Tests were unexplainably hard especially for a 100 level course. It is near impossible to get by on the exams with class material alone. Expectations were muddy if ever disclosed and getting any direction on an assignment was near impossible.

If archaeology is the study of the past, then this class made me wish I could go back in time and drop it. Truly, the most awful class ever. Even the TA's in office hours were typically of zero help. I came to class excited about archaeology, but now I'm just trying to piece together the remains of my GPA.

Overall a super passionate and nice guy! Class graded by 2 group projects, 13 7-question quizzes, attendance, and discussion boards. Disorganized canvas that made looking for things difficult. Available outside of class to meet. Pretty nice about grading but is very direct with project comments lol. Made me interested in urban planning!

He is very nice and very reachable outside of class hours but I think his canvas was a little confusing because there were old contents and information on it. Although you have 7 absences he gives you, there are 13 random quizzes and he usually tells you the lecture before.
Justin is a nice person and a good teacher, but beware of the 13 in-person quizzes!

This was the easiest class that I have ever taken at UNC. While class is optional attendance, he is very excited about the subject material making his lectures pretty engaging. Two papers and two online take home exams are the only grades in the class, but they are graded easily. Recitation is chill and gets out early. Take this class!!
Only 2 papers and 2 test. Wasn't a hard class, kind of boring. Overall easy way to get a focus capacity.

I liked this class! I didn't come to lecture often (optional attendance), but the lectures were interesting sometimes. Graded by two 5-page papers, a midterm, and a final. Good gen ed option to consider! I recommend going to recitations. Our midterm and final were taken at home. He's also really chill, used to be a high school teacher.

Information heavy slides make it so that purchasing the textbook isn't even necessary (like I don't recommend spending your money). Professor Nolan is a great guy but the lectures themselves are extremely fast-paced and monotonous. Your only grades in the class are two papers, a midterm and final but are all relatively easy.

I was unsure of Nolan at first bc this was his first year teaching the course, but my doubts quickly dissipated. Even for a optional attendance 3:30 that is far away from where I live, I made it to almost every lecture. Nolan cares about his students and is chill af

("City and Regional Planning" not "Architecture") Very funny, down to Earth, and kind. Fast-paced lectures. Detailed PPTs. Not much HW. Papers: 2x20% | Midterm: 25% | Final: 25% | Recitation Participation: 10%. Easy grading on papers. Vocab-oriented exams (there are hundreds of vocab terms so studying takes a long time). Good choice for a Gen-Ed.

This class is mostly readings, one essay-based midterm, a presentation or book report, and a final which has many different options. She is a very engaging lecturer and looks at animal studies from varying points of views and fields of study. Answers questions thoughtfully and is a fair grader. Definitely recommend!

I never really figured out what was going on. The lectures are very out there and so are the readings but the class is entertaining. There's three essays for the midterm and the you can volunteer at an animal farm instead of writing more for the final. Its and an easy A, just an insane class lol

Prof Holland is an amazing person, very caring towards her students and really wants her class to engage. The material... could be a lot better. Most of it is just her talking about her own life. Also, not very much animal talk in my animal studies class. Very much so an american studies class.
Good professor. Graded on few assignments, which made the class feel low-stress. Mostly consisted of readings and lectures, and expectations were clear and manageable.

easy class but lectures were dull. graded on 3 essays and a final project. there was literally no rubric for anything which was kind of annoying but they graded easy so it turned out fine. easy focus capacity.
Very inaccessible outside of class

For 255. The class was super easy and as long as you put in a little bit of effort you'll get an A. The content and Dr. Holland's lectures were super interesting but because the class was so disinterested it felt hard to be engaged.

I took the online summer course. Material should be interesting but lectures were long, hard to follow and confusing. Not clear grading expectations and grades somewhat harshly. Must be a good writer. Long readings. She is firm in her take on things and if a student disagrees, their point isnt always considered. Participation matters.

I took AMST 276. I wouldn't say she's a difficult instructor. However, if you're looking to learn something and not listen to anecdotes every lecture, then I wouldn't recommend. Assignment wise, you write three 3-page papers that have broad prompts and have a creative final project. Other than that, pretty easy.

This class was super easy and if attendance wasn't taken, I would've skipped every class and still gotten an A. She is a knowledgable professor but its a philosophical class so you'll leave it not knowing what you were taught (personal bias). My only advice is to take the discussion post seriously because its simple, but its a big part of grade

I took AMST 276. I absolutely loved the lectures she gave and how she would connect a lot of the material to real world problems. She is very kind and really wants you to learn the material. She is more than willing to help you with anything you need and always willing to meet with you. If you can take one of her classes I highly recommend it.

I took this for a PH credit & it's def worth it! There's readings for every class,1 forum post, 1 take home midterm. Participation is also part of your grade, but with a lot of students it was pretty easy to get full credit. Holland really knows her stuff & half of every class was a philosophical-type discussion. Overall would recommend!

I don't know how else to say this other than if you need a philosophy credit, take this class!!! There are hefty readings but we always discussed them in class. You get to choose what you do for the final and midterm was fine! Dr. Holland is amazing and so down to earth. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed.

Honestly a pretty solid class. In terms of positives, he was very passionate about the material, not that many assignments, gave great writing feedback and graded items relatively quickly. In terms of negatives, there's a fair bit of reading and his grading was tougher than similar classes I've taken. If you take it as a gen ed it's worth it.

Prof Marr is a nice guy, but his class is very unorganized and very hard to follow. No guidelines for essays; he grades based on his opinion. Huge final project as well as midterm and final. There's a reason there are seats open in class.
He is my favorite professor at UNC so far

Dr. Marr was very kind and knowledgeable. His lectures were long and had no structure. Rubrics were vague and confusing. TAs were confused too so had no one to get information but figure it out on my own. Very confusing but relatively easy class if you study.

While Prof. Marr is one of the sweetest professors I've had, the structure of this class made it difficult for me to enjoy. Super interesting concepts even if he is a bit long-winded. I didn't mind that but ALL of his assignments have lengthy, vague instructions with high expectations of content. I was constantly asking my TA for clarification.

Professor Marr is such a jolly, passionate fellow. We went out as a class to watch a documentary at 10pm on a Thursday. If you like reading, this class is for you. Class sessions were all discussion. 2 10-page research papers were basically 90% of our grade but he grades easy.

Professor Marr is incredibly intelligent and is knowledgeable about the lecture topics. However, the lectures can sometimes be boring and he rambles so for the final I recommend rewatching the recorded classes. Also, some assignments come out of no where and that feels overwhelming. He is a sweet guy but holds a higher standard than most100classes.

Has an unreasonable amount of reading due during the week, with very little actual directions on how to complete the annotations on them, and when to do them by. Lectures are impossible to take notes on because he just will put up one slide and ramble on for minutes on end. Other students and the TA's rarely had an idea about what was going on.

Professor Marr is a great instructor. There was a lot of reading material (first-year seminar), and the main assignments were two 8-10 page papers. He lead great discussions in class and cared abt his students. Would recommend taking this class if possible. We also went on a class field trip to the movie theater.

He is a professor who respects and cares for his students. You can reach him by email at any time, even on weekends. He loves his job and with responsibility. Although this course has a lot of reading, as long as you read the article or book he provided and think and discuss, then the essay and exam are not too much of a problem.

Honestly this class was a complete joke. The most absurdly whitewashed presentation of Islam in America. I'm not sure that Marr himself is an antisemite (also not sure that he isn't one) but the course is full of them, and Marr knows his audience. Embarrassing UNC has courses like this. He should go back to teaching Moby Dick or whatever.

Professor Marr was kind and enthusiastic about this class. All the assignments are SUPER easy and are graded very leniently. However, the class is reading heavy and you have to comment on lengthy readings before each class. Attendance is mandatory. The only hard aspect was the final. Nonetheless, super easy A.

Dr. Marr is kind and truly loves the material he teaches. However, his lectures are very hard to follow and it takes a while to get used to the new vocabulary. There are a ton of readings but most of them are actually relevant. The final also comes out of no where and is overwhelming. Still a very interesting class!

While he's a really sweet teacher, his lectures are all over the place and really hard to follow. I don't feel like i've learned anything coming out of this class and when he tells you what is on the final exam it is overwhelming, especially when the entire class is hard to follow. There are a TON of really long readings with annotations.

Dr Marr was amazing! His knowledge is astounding and he treats every student with respect and care. He also takes the time to get to know his students and even their interests. All in all, he is a sweet older man

I took him for AMST258 and he makes you read ALOT. Roughly 100 page readings due before class everyday. However, he was a nice, engaging professor and made the class enjoyable if you actually do the readings and participate in discussions. The readings and topics are interesting. Just a lot of work, but focuses on areas in history rarely discussed!

super nice,kind and understanding. if you have a chance to take a class with him, do it!! he holds office hours and helps you with any ideas you may have.  this was a PH credit so lots of readings but its just discussion based, you dont have to read the articles. 10 page research paper at the end with mini projects, not tedious at all

Professor Ferris was one of the kindest and most invested professors I have ever had. This class is so worth your time; there's a lot of reading. The love and passion she puts into this class is evident. She's referenced in most of the readings and has relationships with the authors who come to speak in class. 10/10 DO RECOMMEND!!!!

Professor Ferris is the kindest soul. Snacks & drinks for us every class, fabulous guest speakers, and truly the premier scholar in her field. Take a class, any class with her. You will not regret it.

MCF is FABULOUS. This class is easy if you show up and engage- super lowkey. Dr. Ferris LOVES her students and will return your energy 100%. Is it organized? No honestly not at all, but she if a preeminent scholar in this field whose class you will never forget. Maybe a little confusing if you know nothing about Judaism. Loved this class.

I love Professor Ferris. She knows so much about the topic and she brings in brilliant guest speakers. You have to do a lot of reading but they are not too bad. Class discussions were interesting. Class also starts slow at first but then picks up and becomes great. Assignments are fairly graded and she is always available if you have questions.

2-3 papers, take-home midterm & final. Lots of reading but not tested on & only requires notes of them. Lot of opportunities for outside involvement & she sometimes brings food related to the course materials. Sometimes the lectures/discussions can be bland but overall, she created an open environment for discussion, and I love her for that

Seth is awesome! There was only one assignment throughout the entire semester along with one midterm and final. He does take attendance but his lectures are always super interesting. If you can, definitely try to take a class with him at some point.

Dr. Kotch is such an interesting guy. This class is an easy A if you show up, listen, and do the work outside of class. The only assignments were one paper, the midterm, and the final. Definitely not a class you can use for other stuff. He takes attendance pretty seriously and he will dock points from you if he sees you on your phone a lot.

Dr. Kotch was great, interesting lectures (but you definitely have to dig for the deeper meaning). You have to pay attention in class, he will see if your not. Class is only one paper, participation, midterm and final. Extra credit opportunities are available. He's a little quirky but overall cool dude.

Dr. Kotch is a great lecturer who makes even boring topics interesting. His expectations were clearly laid out, and he can be a lenient grader. He offers a few extra credit opportunities that help you achieve the highest grade possible. He only requests that you complete the readings, come to class, and show everyone respect.
He's a nice guy. Tries to be funny. The class is a very easy A and he offers a lot of extra credit. If you're looking for an easy FC this is a great class, but it's very boring.

GENUINELY so easy but he's definitely GONNA piss you off. Tests are super easy but half the questions are fun facts. youll get a free 3 credit A+ but it definitely feels like a waste of time coming to class and doing the exams (he takes attendance sometimes). smart guy but also hella annoying and tries to be relatable by being edgy.

His goal is to help you apply what you learn and take a strong message about the teaching throughout the semester. I found that any homeworks and assignments assigned actually got me to think about the information in detail. He was very in tune with his students and very accessible outside of class.
Seth Kotch is the guy he cares for his students and he is very funny and the class is also very easy so take him.

He is a funny guy, the lectures are interesting but not always super relevant. A pretty easy A as long as you keep up with the lectures. Class is only a midterm, final, and one essay that is 4+ pages. Not hard at all. You get cheat sheets for the tests as well.

Professor Koch is amazing! Great, caring lecturer and genuinely wants students to learn. Always invited opposing perspectives and explained things in a clear, engaging way. He wrote the midterm (very fair) and even curved it when he noticed some ambiguous wording on his end. I learned a lot from this class and he always tried to make it fun. 10/10
Funny guy!! Really enjoyed his lectures and I don't know if it was just this specific class but the workload  was easy.

This triple I was pretty easy and honestly really interesting. Prof Kotch has a great lecturing style and is hilarious enough to keep students engaged. The class itself had a light work load. Our midterm was open note and the final is a group project.

Professor Kotch is hilarious. I hear they're getting rid of Triple I next year, but if you have to take one, I recommend this one. It was somewhat disorganized, but I hardly had to do any work for it. The topic was thought provoking. We had an open note midterm and a group project for the final.
I love Seth. Chill guy.

His lectures were the most engaging part of the course. I looked forward to them. Dr. Kotch had me laughing even while discussing serious topics. I love him, and this is the easiest triple I UNC offers.

This was an easy class. Lectures were interesting and he was always making jokes. Exams were open note and he posted lecture slides to study. A few readings were done each week for recitation, but nothing too overwhelming. There are only a few assignments you do have to do well on each one. Don't be on your phone during lecture he will call you out

The professor's lecture was excellent. But it is very difficult to get good grades. His teaching assistant is very strict and subjective when grading, and does not strictly follow the grading criteria. Secondly, it is puzzling how the attendance score is evaluated. Even if one follows his rules completely, it is not certain to get a full score.

Professor Kotch is such a fun guy! He is incredibly knowledgeable about both history and pop culture, interweaving the two together to form a stellar class. His jokes make the class laugh out loud and you will walk away learning a lot from a Kotch class. I definitely recommend taking a class with him!
Chill dude. Easy class. Cares about attendance. Recommend.

Professor Paduchowski was great! His style is part lecture, part interactive. You can choose a certain number of the assignments to complete. He doesn't do minus grades but does do plus grades. No mandatory attendance but he made going to class an easy decision as it was interesting.

Prof Paduchowski created a good learning environment and is understanding of scheduling issues. He is very knowledgable about the subjects and has real world experience. The final exam was done in a real courtroom, which was cool. The workload is average/lighter. If Prof Paduchowski teaches other classes in the future, I'm taking them.

An absolute must take for a prelaw student!!! Mike brings in phenomenal guest panels from a wide array of practice areas and the class felt like a must less stressful version of a law class. I learned so much while also having a lot of fun. Is an easy A if you turn things in and try(super flexible). Added bonus is that he is an actual attorney!

If you are interested in law school, definitely take this class! Prof Paduchowski structures the class to give students a stress-free introduction to the first year of law school. Our class even included guest lectures from local attorneys and judges! Amazing class.

The professor is an attorney who cares about the materials and that students get a glimpse into law school without the cold calls and a ton of work. The class had clear assignments, with 4 case briefs, a midterm project, and a final project (which the class voted on). He is very engaging and I highly recommend taking the class. Participate!

Dr. Robinson's class was not engaging. It was obvious she knew much about and was very passionate about the material. The material was interesting, but the lectures were disorganized, and it was hard to follow. The class required multiple readings per week.

Dr. Robinson is a good professor; she taught the material clearly. Assignments were graded fairly, and there was good feedback. Some concepts were taught in a politically biased manner; she was not always verbally politically neutral, which I did not appreciate.

Professor Robinson's lectures are extremely disorganized to put it lightly. The constant switch between lecture styles, accessibility of slideshows, and ability to use technology in class truly makes the course a train wreck at best. I would avoid taking this course with this professor if you value your sanity. Otherwise, it's a pretty easy A.
Her lectures are terrible. just reading off slides with a million words

If you want a class you don't want to attend lectures for and get A's on assignments and essays take this class. But, they added a final exam because no one attended class (because they genuinely don't make sense and this class is more black history than american history), and we all think we're screwed for it. But the exam is only worth 10%

Michelle is an okay professor and the class is pretty easy. She has a weird resentment towards the student's in her class who take it for a gen-ed instead of an actual love for American Studies (she came into my recitation once and scolded us about it!). Lectures aren't mandatory and you can easily skip all the readings.

Professor Robinson is a very nice person and cares about the course material. AMST 101 is an easy class with her but it's a little disorganized. Lectures can be all over the place but if you follow her instructions on assignments, you'll be fine.

Dr. Robinson is super funny and the content is very intriguing, but some definition-heavy lectures dragged. A few graded assignments, but the effort you put in is a pretty accurate reflection of both your assignment & final course grade. Performing stand-up to the class for the final exam is exhilarating btw.
I love Prof Robinson so so much!!! I would take any class by her again!

I LOVE PROF ROBINSON!! This class was one of my favorites this semester and she was a big reason for that. There are few assignments but the ones we did have were straight forward. Attendance was mandatory but the lectures were always interesting so it was fine. TAs were AMAZING too. 10/10 recommend this class!!

Professor Robinson did an amazing job connecting the course material to current events in a thoughtful and meaningful way. It was clear that she takes pride in her work and connected those sentiments to her lectures (which may become dense at times). The only poor grade I received in her class was a paper graded by a TA so beware of that.

This course has a lot of required readings, but you are never tested on them. You don't need to take notes in lectures, which can sometimes be boring. There are a few papers that determine most of your grade. There are also required out-of-class events that weren't particularly interesting. Almost everything is graded by TAs, mine graded harshly.

Professor Robinson made this class fun while still very informative. She is very accessible outside of class and her office hours are definitely worth attending. The class is graded on a few easy assignments, a multiple choice midterm, a final paper, and a final written exam for which we were allowed a typed reference sheet for. Overall easy gen ed
Super knowledgeable professor, her lectures were interesting if a bit hard to follow. Cool and interesting assignments that left a lot of freedom for interpretation.

Although sometimes she was vague about requirements, she graded us very kindly in the end while still giving good feedback. She knows a lot about the material and made the classroom a great environment for discussion and deep thinking. Her paper prompts encourage an artistic and thoughtful approach.

This class was interesting but very unorganized. The essay topics were vague and I felt like the lectures did not really help us. The TA's really make or break you as they grade everything and help you. The lectures are really hard to follow. I wouldn't say it's the easiest A but it is definitely doable.

Her lectures are pointless. I was able to manage a B+ average on the papers by making stuff up and looking at the slides; with extra credit and other things, I made an A in the class.  Bottom line, attend the lectures/recitations (and do other work in class), actually write decent papers, and do the extra credit. Do that, and you'll do just fine

Professor Robinson is a very no-nonsense kind of person. She's clearly passionate and knowledgeable about comedy, and the material is interesting enough. Beware of the essay prompts, they are VAGUE; I'd honestly only recommend this class to students confident in their writing skills or who like to think "philosophically".

It's physics 119. You know what you're getting. Dr. Zhang was a very kind and understanding studio instructor and lecturer and would frequently give points back on studio if we felt something was graded incorrectly. This class isn't as hard as most people say IMO, but it certainly requires a good bit of time.
Phys119 is a hard class. Sometimes it's a difficult lecture but it's really just content. Overall a good professor. Studio TAs can make or break it I guess.

All your homeworks and 100s of practice problems given are exactly like the exam. Lectures are explained really well and if you cant figure it out studios are just practice sessions and have amazing explanations. Just try and you'll do well. Plus she is so chill for labs. Literally gave me free credit when I needed it.

I had Prof Zhang for my Physics 118 studio and she was amazing. The class was very difficult but she explained everything in a clear and engaging way so it all made sense. The canvas was very helpful and she was always willing to walk you though any problems both in class and in office hours.
I had Muxin for my FY-LAUNCH lab professor, and she was great. Knows her stuff when it comes to physics and has quite the curated canvas page. Beware of a couple of difficult questions on exams.

Muxin was a very good professor; I had her for studio as well. She is super kind and always available outside of class if you need her. Her grading is very lenient for in-class work and gives a lot of partial credit on exams.

SHE IS THE BEST!!! She is super accessible, especially in office hours, and explains concepts extremely well. This class definitely requires some hard work, especially if you've never been in a college-level physics course before, but if you use your resources it is definitely doable.

Phy118 is hard and a fair amount of work, but completely doable. Course was organized really well. Dr. Zhang was my studio instructor, and she did a great job reinforcing difficult concepts taught in lecture. Class isn't super test heavy, either.

She was my studio instructor and course coordinator. Absolute gem of a person. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS. Phys 118 is hard but she tries her best to explain the concepts. Honestly I learned more from her studio than the lectures.

Prof. Zhang was my studio instructor for PHYS 118, and she was absolutely amazing. She was insanely good at answering questions and would always help you in any way she could. She was the course coordinator this semester, so she did not lecture for the full class. There is not a studio instructor I would rather have. Wholeheartedly recommend!

Physics is a hard class, it is work heavy and you will have to study for tests. This is intrinsic to first-level physics classes. However, Professor Zhang was great. If you have questions, she will understand your confusion and explain the answer clearly. Her office hours greatly helped my understanding of the course.

Really nice woman. Like the nicest professor ever. Actually cares. The other profs suck so bad and the class is so damn hard but at least she was nice. Exams and homework are everything. Studios help a lot but she is wonderful if u reach out to her!

Professor Zhang is very sweet, but this semester she was not teaching the class. The class was taught by Professor Dolan and Prof. Qiu and I only went to lecture for participation points. I used CramBetter to help me understand concepts from lecture and study for exams. I highly recommend using it!

Hard class with bad lecturers. I had Dolan and Yqiu who both are not competent at explaining high level concepts to other people. The tests are very difficult and meant to trick you. Do lots and lots of practice problems and be active in studio.
I took her for a 118 launch class. She was very kind and smart. She is always willing to help after class or in office hours.

For Fall 2024, Professor Zhang did not actually teach her own class. She had two Assistant Professors that taught under her and (with all due respect) provided low-quality instruction.

Yes, the job of a Physics Professor is difficult, but her absence from class provided a serious barrier to our learning.
good stuff!

Professor Zhang did a great job of teaching a hard subject in a beginner-friendly, but still thorough, way. Apparently, the physics department works hard to make their classes as helpful as possible, which is different from how a lot of other depts design their classes, but it was super helpful in this course!
The better of the lecturers since her background is in physics education. Tests were fair, assignments manageable, but you learn most from studio.

Took this course with Louise Dolan and her. Duane Deardorff is also listed as a professor but he doesn't teach. Dr. Dolan knows her stuff but doesn't teach well. Dr. Zhang is relatively much better at lecturing and explaining things. She sometimes lecture a bit fast, but you can ask her questions in class or go to office hours.

Rich is amazing, he was really passionate about all things APPL and BeAM. The entire class is group projects based but it is also extremely time consuming so beware of that. While lectures were long, the class was engaging and fun. Loves helping and talking to his students about anything and everything (especially plants).
Rich is super chill, funny, and knowledgeable about woodworking. There were very few assignments, but the grading was easy and they were typically quite fun.

Super awesome guy! Took him for APPL 60, and you can tell this guy really cares about his students. He invited the entire class to his house for a pizza party, and so he could talk about his woodworking. Class is mainly based around 2 papers (1 based on a gift that you build and the second a research paper), and making a GIF of a tree.

So this professor loves to be inspirational and is so sweet. Sometimes he gets passionate about things that few care deeply about, but I think that is a bit of the nature of the course. One can only have so much interest in different types of fasteners. Classes are graded by undergrad TA's of whom are easy graders.

Rich is super fun and a really good teacher for this class. While lectures could sometimes be a drag, the class was generally engaging and fun. He made us all cakes when the Eagles won the Superbowl. Knows a lot about designing and solving problems. Loves answering questions and helping you solve problems. Definitely recommend this class and Rich!

He cares about what he teaches. It might be a bit of work, but it's not that bad, especially if you're interested in design and making. This is a fun class and a super easy A if you do the work. Some people were tripping about the grading, which could be unclear at times, but everyone got an A in that class.

Rich is a super nice and caring professor and will work with you to help you out with what you need to improve. There were no tests, just 1 super long research paper and a bunch of little assignments. The only negative is that the class itself is a little boring at times, but he tries his best to make it interesting.

APPL 89 is now APPL 60! Rich is seriously one of the best teachers I have ever had. This class was so much fun, I looked forward to it every week. There was one long 12 page research paper but other than that all of the assignments are super creative and fun. Your final is to take two pictures of a tree each week and make a timelapse.

Rich is fun and caring. He loves what he does and wants to inspire more than anything. He is humble and admits when he doesn't know something. This class is hands on and creative, but requires a lot of time outside of class to do well. I absolutely would recommend this class and this professor to anyone!

He is literally perfect and adorable. Actually cares for his students and just a great teacher. He made this class so fun and not boring. We went on walks and did a lot fun stuff. Definitely take him if you have the chance. Can't say enough good things about him!!!

Professor Pegard is so funny, which makes his lectures fun and easy to follow. Lectures are short, and most of class is reserved for working on HW/coding assignments (make sure to go to office hours if the coding assignments are hard). Don't miss any assignments, even if the point total looks small, because of how final grades are structured.

This class is very heavy on the coding side of engineering. if you have no coding experience, you will have to mainly self teach, however he is very open to answering questions. the lectures are BORING and hard because he talks veery fast, is disorganized, and has a French accent. Would not recommend as an exploratory class into engineering.

If you have zero coding experience, the class will be difficult. Doesn't explain himself well and is pretty disorganized. For those truly exploring engineering, take APPL 110 instead with Goldberg. I didn't learn much other than how to complete the lengthy out-of-class coding assignments that were easy for ppl who can code and ppl who used chat.

This class is NOT an easy 100-level class. Dr. Pegard is very nice and knowledgeable, but it's hard to reach him outside of class. I emailed him probably 5 times this semester, and he responded twice. The class itself is very disorganized, and the grading criteria are not very well defined. DO NOT TAKE IF YOU HAVE NO CODING EXPERIENCE.

I love Dr. Pegard. Very funny, chaotic dude. Brought his delightful little daughter to class a few times. He values engagement and likes snarky people. I'm 80% sure he never reads the slides before presenting but he's very fun. The class is structured messily because a different person designed it, but if you've done any programming you'll be fine.

He's quite an amusing lecturer, and he explains things well. It's not his fault its a really boring class. If you actually participate you'll be fine. It's hard to teach the amount of coding you have to do in this class so you will probably teach yourself a lot, especially bc there's written quizzes after the coding assignments are due.
Good class, hard to learn stuff but i enjoyted it.
If your good with electronics, modeling in fusion etc take this class. If not it will not be easy but if you work for the A youll get it.

Professor Pegard is a really cool teacher! The class is based on projects which can be hard at first if you have never taken an engineering class before, but the TAs are very helpful and understanding when it comes to grading. You don't really get hw which is nice, however, you do have to spend time outside of class to work on the actual projects.

your grade basically depends on your TAs but they help you on assignments if you ask and are usually very lenient; pegard is pretty chill though, some assignments took more time then expected but weren't too difficult. overall easy A and a decent gen-ed

Professor Pegard seriously just wants you to learn a thing or two about design and prototyping. It's a fairly easy class although most assignments are group projects and I was lucky to have great group members every time. The projects are time consuming because you have to create things and travel to BeAM but it's fun and an easy VP credit.

Dr.  Becker is a nice person and clearly knowledgeable, but the way she responds to your answers was very disheartening to me--like an "okay...let's see if anyone else has a better thought." Long projects, homework was graded really harshly. Nice person and clearly knowledgeable though

Dr. Becker is a good professor and very knowledgeable about her area of study. The most important grades in the class are two projects that are very long and tedious but I would say she grades them fairly. The midterm and final were easy as long as you understand the content conceptually. Overall I thought this class was very interesting.

She is great at lecturing and encourages students to ask questions along the way. The topics were really interesting but I found it quite challenging. The two projects were extremely tedious and the exams were also difficult. Those three things are the main grades, but I mostly took the class to learn more about interesting topics, so I was happy.

The projects were relatively long and very tedious, including transcribing the phonetic symbols for a long recording of a child speaking and counting morphemes of hundreds of lines of child dialogue, both graded on accuracy. Overall though, the content of the class was very interesting, and the Professor also wrote the textbook for the class!

Lectures were easy to follow as she posted guides that you could follow along with. She was easily accessible outside of class as well as through email, and she clearly explains her expectations for tests. I would say that the expectations for the papers were somewhat blurry, but they were not graded harshly.

Misha was my favorite professor this past semester!  She had a great way of being able to break down the material and explain it in a way that was accessible.  She was happy to talk over anything in office hours if you encountered any issues. I would definitely recommend her if you are considering doing Ling 101.

I don't think I would recommend the class for non-majors/minors, just because there is a lot of content that you need to be familiar with to do well. That being said, Misha's lectures are interesting and engaging, and the grading for assignments is very lenient. There are not any major projects for the class, and three total exams.

The professor doesn't care about students mental health. She is confusing, she tells us to disregard what the textbook says and uses examples from the textbook in lecture slides and says that it is wrong. Her study guides are awful and tells us to review EVERYTHING and half the stuff she says to review is not on the exam. Awful course!

Syntax is overall just a difficult concept to grasp, but Brian is great at explaining! I love how clear his grading was and how helpful his response and resources are. He was overall great and I hope to take more classes with Brian.

He's funny. I came in wanting a linguistics minor and left not but would still recommend it! That being said, I only got an A by asking my TA for help. Skill-based is mid, but you'll get multiple chances. No final though!

This course made me change my major to hispanic linguistics from just linguistics linguistics. The grading system is horrendous. You will have so much anxiety throughout the semester about the amount of skills you have. If you get ONE LETTER or one thing wrong it's 0 for that skill. I saw the reviews and laughed. Don't make my mistake. Run.

Skill based grading is great, but I don't think I would have done as well if I didn't go to my TAs office hours, she was the greatest help to me getting my skills so if you take him, make sure to go to your TAs office hours for every HW because there's only 5 not including the final. Little mistakes are counted off for and mismark = 0 on skill.

The grading system that requires 100% accuracy per skill did not work well for me. I think I'd have had a higher grade with a raw accuracy percentage, as I'd often miss just one detail on a skill. very little feedback was given for mistakes. Loved the subject, and the lectures were great + funny. Would take it again, but with a different prof.

Lectures were great, and very funny, but very awkward. Lots of homework, grades on "skill based assessment" which basically means that if you don't get 100% of the content of a unit, you are not given credit for the entire unit. Fairly helpful.

grades are entirely based on skills from the homeworks, which can be annoying since they require 100% accuracy to get. lecture & recitations are completely optional, i never went and was able to complete skills purely through the uploaded slideshows, but that won't work for everyone.
Tries to pretend he's a nice guy but really just wants to tank your grade

grades using a skill-based grading system, wasn't the best for me. however, he responded to all emails quickly, if you take the class, be sure to go to office hours to understand the course better... also this is a far more in depth ling101 course than some other ones
BRIAN IS THE GOAT

His grading was all or nothing and based on achieving skills.  To get a skill, you had to get 100% of the skill correct on the homework assignment.  Tiny mistakes meant a zero for that skill.  While some sections of the homework had multiple skills, it was hard to tell which skills you got from the unclear red and green marks.
Once you study hard and put effort into the course materials, you'll definitely get nearly every skill and an A- at least.

Dr. Hsu is knowledgable about his field, & it shows. He grades based off of a skill system rather than traditional grading. So, once you gain a skill you don't have to do it again. Because lectures aren't mandatory, it's easy to get into the habit of skipping. Unless you have prior knowledge of ling, if you skip constantly, you'll probably fail.
Brian is a good guy, really enjoy his lecture, if you put some time in it, you will get A- at least.

Hsu has an interesting grading style that, in my opinion, makes it much easier to get an A in an already relatively easy course. He's a little awkward, but still a very kind professor who always wants to help. There are no exams except for the final, which is take-home, and very minimal homework. Really interesting course overall with little demand
Terrible course and terrible professor for sure.
Inconsiderate and not accommodating to students
Brian is a good guy, really enjoy his lecture, if you put some time in it, then it is a solid A.

Dr. Hsu was great! He grades on a skill-based system instead of a traditional system, so once you've mastered something you don't have to do it again. There were many opportunities to gain each skill throughout the semester and it was easy to get the skill on the second try. As a non-linguistics major, I would recommend!

Grading is insanely harsh and there are NEVER clear answers to questions. Keep asking follow up questions and the instructors will confuse themselves. Do not take this class. I am convinced that linguistics is not real.

Professor Terry is obviously passionate about linguistics. His readings are very engaging, and he is quite cool. The class is not difficult at all. I would recommend this one for your interdisciplinary credit. Midterms and the final exam are essentially all you are graded on.

Professor Terry is a good professor but his lectures were not engaging at all. I admire how much he enjoys teaching linguistics and how language is related to race even though I consistently found myself dozing off during class. He creates helpful slideshows which make studying his final exam material easy enough.

It's obvious he cares about linguistics, but it felt like he was just saying the same things over and over in class. I wouldn't say the content was difficult to understand, he just made it a bit boring to learn. He does assign readings but they aren't as long as one of the other professors, so it's manageable.

The linguistic side of this class was really interesting. He clearly knows what he's talking about, but that led to a lot of assumptions about prior knowledge. Without having taken LING 101, it'd be much harder to follow the lectures. That wasn't a prereq though, so it's hard to follow for most.

Professor Terry is very passionate about the subject and encourages students to explore linguistics. 
However, his lectures can be hard to follow and he tends to get sidetracked. If you do a good amount of studying outside of class you will be fine.
I appreciated this professor. The class wasn't difficult, he was accessible outside of class, and he was very accommodating.

Very interesting lectures and he's really nice. Conceptually the class is essentially set theory so if you took discrete or anything like that it's almost like review, wished we went more in depth with lambdas. However grading is really unclear since there was rarely any homework/practice so basically midterm and final decides everything.
The lectures are pretty boring and scattered. I wouldn't take this class if you don't have to.

Professor Terry was one of the best professors I had at UNC. The material he covers (beyond 101) is just tough in general, so don't expect an easy class, but he's accessible through office hours and personal appointments, and really wants to see his students succeed.

Dr Mora is very passionate about the topics he teaches, & while his lectures arent difficult to follow or comprehend, he is unorganized, consistently behind schedule in the curriculum, & his expectations on assignments, projects, etc. were pretty unclear. I wouldnt avoid a class if he was teaching it, but I do think his system could be improved.

See the syllabus? Look at it. Now ball it up and throw it out the window because he does not abide by it at all. Accessible outside of class, only on GroupMe. Issues with the final project because the atlas did not work how he said it did. Disorganized presentations with a sole focus on Maya. Often weeks behind from syllabus. Rubrics unclear/DNE

he is a really nice professor, but takes a while to grade. i didn't love this class it felt unnecessary and he had us try and actually decipher texts (like rosetta stone). the class is decently easy (had an A all semester) and he is very accommodating, let us meet on zoom if we couldn't go to class.

Professor Mora Marin is incredibly passionate about what he talks about (Mayan languages especially). However his lectures are repetitive at times. He does offer classes on zoom calls and is very reachable outside of class. He is slow to grade and regrades are even slower. Overall a super nice professor who cares about his students and his material

Dr. Mora-Marín is pretty disorganized and skips around a lot, but if you lock in the stuff he's discussing, is REALLY interesting. He's pretty slow at grading, so be prepared to wait. Also, get ready to learn a LOT about Mayan; he'll sneak it in there one way or another.

VERY disorganized. Class was behind on syllabus from week one and assignment instructions/deadlines were always unclear. Would spend weeks on certain slideshows and skip through others in one day. Was not an environment very conducive to learning.

Do not take him. The criteria was always unclear, we were always weeks behind the syllabus, and the information was so confusing. I did not learn anything from this class. There is a final project, paper, and exam. He harps on things that have nothing to do with the course while skimming over the important concepts. The class was too difficult.
LOVE this guy! Super fun and easy class! Super knowledgeable! Prof. Mora is the GOAT!
He is definitely a knowledgeable person and is enthusiastic about this topic. He cares about the students a lot. But a little bit terrible at organizing lectures and slides. Overall recommended.

Prof Mora-Marin is really knowledgeable in linguistics and is a very kind, considerate, and respectful professor, but as a professor in a gateway linguistics course, the experience wasn't great. The class was quite disorganized and the syllabus was pretty much irrelevant after a couple of weeks. The pacing for lectures could definitely be better.

Completely disheveled and unaware of the class pacing. Will spend 9 class days on one topic when there's a whole course to get through - and the final four weeks has us sprinting to the finish. Entirely inaccessible via email, but responds in minutes via groupme. Graded my final and then lowered the grade 2 days later. Take any other ling professor

Everything was okay in this class except the final project. Way too difficult and the dataset is extremely messy, they changed it 5+ times after releasing it and its just impossible to figure out what we are supposed to do. Too much highlighting, cross outs, and parenthesis that are used differently. This was very stressful as a graduating senior.

This class should really either have a linguistics prerequisite or be exclusively for non-ling majors. Prof. Mora-Marin is very nice, but he is also very disorganized. His lectures jump all over, and the syllabus was basically irrelevant by week 3. We all got assigned a language to present on, so that was basically the only one I learned about.

I didn't like her as much as other reviews. What made me mad is nothing was assigned in Canvas with specific dates so it was easy to forget due dates. Attendance is mandatory and you have to participate everyday.

Ellen is an amazing professor who makes it easy for students to succeed. She makes expectations clear with rubrics and grading criteria, and is a very fair grader. She leaves great feedback and resources for students to learn and improve. The exams were pretty easy and projects and in-class activities were fun and engaging. Overall great class!

Not sure how anyone could rate Professor Atterbury low, she is great! The class is pretty standardized for projects/tests but Atterbury prepares you well and encourages in-class group discussion which is super helpful if you actually want to learn the language. Midterms and final were easy if you just study a couple days before.
She was really amazing, we always know the expectations. She makes the class fun and educational!!

(Spanish 204) This class is pretty standardized for quizzes/tests and assignments but Professor Atterbury was super understanding all semester long and gave helpful feedback on assignments without being overly harsh. Make sure to talk in class and do your readings and you'll be fine!
She is a caring and lenient professor; does not listen to the 2-star review. SHE IS GOATED!!!
Miserable class to be frank. Type-A & overly strict grader. Super inexperienced in teaching. Be ready to devote all of your time to this class if you even want a B+ lol.

Mm. Meinke is a professor who ACTUALLY wants you to succeed and truly grasp french. He explains grammatical and tense formation clearly and points out common misconceptions/misunderstandings. Mm. Meinke also often brings out fun stories that relate to the course content!

hes super nice and I hear he's one of the best. the class is not too difficult. I just hate French and found I had to spend so much time on it in order to get a good grade. if u just stay on top of it u should be fine.

Monsieur Meinke is an amazing professor and is there to help you if you are struggling and need questions answered.  He explained things clearly so that people from an English background could understand how certain grammatical structures worked in French.  His grading is also very fair, I would 100% recommend taking 105 with him to anyone!

Monsieur Meinke always kept us engaged and made sure we knew what we were doing! His grading was pretty fair and he always made himself accessible outside of class if we had questions or wanted to discuss anything we were struggling with in class.

M. Meinke is a great teacher and I definitely learned the most I have ever learned from a french class with him. He wants you to succeed and gives great feedback on work. Most of the homework is on Mindtap and it is not too bad at all. M. Meinke is incredibly caring and I absolutely loved his class.

Monsieur Meinke was amazing. He is very caring about his students and genuinely wants them to succeed. His office hours are very helpful to get in depth feedback.There is a good amount of online homework before each class done through mindtap, but it is manageable. Everything is clearly labeled on the syllabus and straight forward.

Respectable teacher whom answers any and all questions. This is the first year where I feel like I learned something in French. There are quizzes and essays every once in a while, but participation is also a key factor. You should definitely take advantage of office hours to improve your essays and challenge test questions. Overall terrific class!

His lectures were tedious and a little boring to be completely honest, but the content was decently easy to understand as long as you kept up with vocabulary. I did not do all of the 'required reading' and did great on the midterms and finals, just keep up with the lectures.

Terry was nice but I wouldn't recommend if you can avoid taking this class as it was quite boring in my opinion. It seemed to create an issue out of nothing and the lectures feel SO long. If you pay attention and do the readings it's not hard to get a good grade (long readings but he is understanding and goes over it in class).

Professor Terry is very knowledgeable about his area of research but is not great at teaching/explaining it to those who are new to the topic. Expectations for exams were somewhat vague but his TA this year graded them in a pretty lenient manner. I felt like I had to teach myself a lot of this course.
His lectures are interesting and helpful, although they are very repetitive and could be 20 minutes long.

Terry was chill. I thought his lectures were boring sometimes but overall, he seems cool. In general, the workload wasn't crazy. There were 3 graded discussion posts, one longer graded essay, and just the midterm and final. For the tests, even if you didn't really pay attention, as long as you studied for a couple hours the day before its okay.

Sometimes his lectures were sometimes interesting, but not always. He seemed nice. Like all the professors, the homework was always reading. There are few graded assignments, and the work outside of class isn't that crazy. Make sure to take notes in the lectures as that is the only thing on the exam and is needed to study.
Terry's is boring, and his whole part of the triple I is a metaphor for race. Do not take this class !!!!!

Dr.Terry is a boring lecturer, he does try to connect his topic with the other professors but it comes off sloppy. Out of all three professors he probably gives the least amount of readings and is more helpful than Dr.Matute when it comes to lecture slides.

Professor Terry does seem to care about this course but clearly does not put enough effort into it. Only one of his lectures connected to the other fields. He is not an engaging lecturer although he does put together helpful slideshows.

If you are interested in European politics, you will love this class. She is an expert on the subject matter and all of the material is incredibly relevant and important for students in modern times. She is very kind and accommodating. 100% would take again.

Genuinely a great teacher and such an interesting class. The lectures were captivating, with a mixed style of group discussions and lecture, and minimal assignments. The class was tough at times but I learned so much! Definitely recommend!!

A truly mixed bag. She is expert in subject matter, but the class heavily focuses on her just as much as the subject matter. We totally skipped over Yugoslavia to go through her twitter bookmarks about Ukraine. She has a POV that is certainly backed up by evidence, but she has certain opinions that if you disagree with, she'll be dismissive.

MAV taught one of the more interesting classes I've taken at UNC. She is very passionate and knowledgeable about Europe. Class consists of 2 midterms and a final paper, and there are extra credit opportunities. Class could get off topic and rambles occurred, but they were always interesting and engaging. MAV is very nice, I'd take this class.

Prof. Vachudova is obviously a subject matter expert. Her lectures can go off on tangents sometimes, but the resources are all there to succeed. She is very accessible with many office hours times, and the paper assignment isn't too bad, and the class counts for the Research gen-ed. Sometimes slow to grade but always fair. Overall, I recommend.

Grades were entirely made up of two "midterms", one paper, and "participation" (which included attendance). On that note, we did not receive our grades for any assignment until the last day of the grading period, meaning if you didn't do well on one of those midterms, you had no idea if you were failing or not until there was nothing you could do.

Very disoriented + disorganized. Spends entire class time giving personal anecdotes, and doesn't cover material that we're then tested on. Doesn't follow syllabus schedule, creates lots of confusion. "Supplemental" readings are actually required. Probably one of the least impressive and engaging professors I've had at UNC. Don't take this class.

Terrible woman. Unfriendly and tries to intimidate you if you don't share her opinions. She obviously does not like to be challenged, which is ironic since the basic tenet of education is open discourse. The day she retires will be a great day for UNC students, past and present.

Dr. Vachudova is one of the only professors I have come across in my 2 years at UNC who 1) hates teaching, and 2) hates questions. Whether it was during office hours or over email, Dr. Vachudova made it pretty clear that she would much rather be doing something else.

Professor Vachudova is one of the most passionate professors at UNC. Unfortunately she seems quite disoriented, usually going over about 3 lecture slides in a powerpoint of 45 but are tested on even the things she didn't talk about in lecture but are on the slides. She loves talking about Europe but rambles. If you love Europe this is for you.

Dr. Vachudova is the best professor/teacher I have ever been taught by.  She always engages and prepares for class in an expert-like fashion. It is clear she knows what she is doing. Especially having to deal with students who never want to do the work, anything would be too hard for those looking for an easy A. 100% would recommend!

She is kind, a little disoriented, but wants to be there for her students. Has a lot of office hours and wants you to come. Very few grades so you have no idea where you stand until like the last week of class. Takes forever to get grades back as well. She did grade pretty leniently though. Lots and lots of reading for homework, so be prepared.

MAV is one of my favorite professors I've had - so funny, caring and kind! Her lectures are straight-forward, engaging and always include current events which keep the class up to date. 1 big research paper, 2 midterms, final exam and participation make up the grade. Not too hard to get an A, but you need to definitely put in effort!

Professor Vachudova is the best prof. I've had at UNC - coming from a Senior. She cares greatly about the subject matter, her students, and her students' success in and out of the classroom. She gives engaging lectures (participation in them a must for this course) and is easily available outside of lecture to talk about class or even just life.

Lectures were not productive as he would just repeat the textbook and go off on random tangents. Test average for the first exam was a 63% and he blamed the class for not paying attention during lectures.  If you really want to succeed in this class, then you would have to read all of the chapters assigned in the textbook--which mind you, is a lot.

would only really take this class if you are a political science major. i took this for the gen-ed credit and had a hard time. lectures are boring, Roberts moves through material super quick, and tests are relatively hard. you def can do well, but it requires A LOT of studying/work.

Class average on the first exam was a 63 and blamed it on us for not memorizing extremely obscure details. Class lectures are boring and unengaging and he often stops lectures to call people out for small talk.

I honestly learned more in recitation than in lecture. He is not very engaging and can sometimes come off rude. First exam had a 63% average in the class and did not suggest any changes on his end to help our performance. There is definitely a way to do well in this class, but it requires a lot of effort outside of class.

For a first year seminar, class was difficult for no reason. Graded by a few things, so messing up on the exams doesn't help your grade. You never really know what to expect on the exams, so they were difficult. Not reading heavy but lectures are boring. Professor is nice but any other first year seminar would be easier.
2 papers and 2 exams. For a 100 level class you genuinely have to lock in, and the papers are graded strictly and if you do bad on one exam then your grade is predetermined.

Overall, Roberts is a good/engaging teacher. He was very knowledgeable and kept class moving at a good rate. The exams were fairly hard but not cumulative and the papers were pretty easy if you utilize resources (TA and teacher). Do the reading to understand what he goes over in class and not have to worry as much about notes while he is talking.

The class was fine and uninteresting but not very hard if you read the textbook. Going to class was completely useless as he just repeats parts of the textbook you already read, but he takes attendance through quizzes. My TA was fantastic though and graded papers fairly. I just wish class time was more productive as I taught myself everything.

I was disappointed in this class because I was so excited to take it and knew it was going to be an easy A. Roberts was very all over the place during his lectures and got distracted most of the time. Most of the info on the exams was not talked about or just briefly skimmed over in the lecture. There's no way I should get a B- in a 100 level

Class is incredibly easy if you review the lecture slides and skim the textbook. The biggest issue would be the professor. Dr. Roberts, at times, had this aura of "I'm better than you" during his lectures. He would also use most of the class to just answer questions, without getting to the content. Overall, take it if you need an easy A.

This class is very lecture heavy so please please please pay attention during his lecture. Hie class his weighted on 3 exams, 2 papers, and participation in his class. READ THE TEXTBOOK! The most beneficial thing to do in his class is to read the textbook.
This class was based on 3 tests, which was unfair and not based on what we learned what so ever. He isn't a bad lecturer but they were not helpful. Would not recommend unless you want have to.

Professor Roberts is very easy to listen to and led very interesting lectures. However, his class is oriented around 3 exams and 2 papers. The exams are pretty tough, with a lot of trick questions. You have to read the textbook thoroughly and keep up with the lectures completely. The papers are slight. He does not curve exams.

Tests are hard for no reason. The second test (out of 3) had a 68 average. There are extra credit opportunities (to which I personally went to almost all of them) but not enough to come back from how bad the tests are. Normally an interesting lecture, but would not recommend.

For a 100-level class, this class is unnecessarily hard. The tests are hard to pass because it is based on the lecture slides and he words the exams so tricky. The average test scores were 70s and he does not curve them. Essays are easy but the exams will bring your grade down.
Definitely do not recommend.

Prof Roberts is very knowledgable, fair, and organized. He's not very flexible or accomodating, but the class is not too hard and the workload is reasonable. Totally fine professor and interesting class. Do the readings and you will be fine.

Class only consisted of three tests including final, two paper, recitation, and poll ev (had so many issues with poll ev technology).  Pretty chill class and getting a good grade is possible.  Keep up with readings and definitely study lecture slides for test.  Try to get Michael Greenberger for your TA; fair grader for papers.

roberts was very nice and a good professor, but he did pollev for attendance. the papers were graded easily, but the tests revolved around the lectures and sometimes included irrelevant and hard-to-remember information. for a 100 level class, however, it was easy and relatively laid back.

Overall, I enjoyed professor Roberts' course. The class grade revolves solely around tests and papers but the more you studied and listened to lectures, the better off you'll be. I would recommend him as he is clearly knowledgeable and engaged in politics, making it easier to not get bored.

Roberts had fairly interesting lectures, but the entire course is 3 tests and 2 papers, with participation taken through PollEv. Tests were extremely difficult and had many trick questions. Averages were in the 70s for all exams and he does not curve. TA's grade the papers, 3 and 7 pages in length.

This is an exceptional class that you should take if you're interested in the justice system at all. Attendance at evening speaker events is required. Now cotaught by Professor Johnson. The final was messed up this year, but other than that, it was great.
Awesome class, passionate professor, and super interesting. Highly recommend it regardless of major, super relevant issues discussed and have the privilege to hear from really unique voices,

Such a good class to take, the speaker series is what makes this class is amazing. I will say his lecture style can be a little boring and repetitive (when paired with the readings) but overall super informative. The final is basically a cumulation of all the reading quizzes plus an additional 10ish other questions

POLI-203 has been my favorite class I've taken at UNC. It's a pretty straightforward class in terms of expectations, and Dr. Baumgartner was incredibly knowledgeable. The speakers he brought in during the lecture series were amazing. The essays and papers are not graded stringently, and the final is a mix of old quiz questions. Take this class!

Frank is a really funny and nice professor who knows a lot about the death penatly and makes it exciting to learn about. Most people don't attend lecture, but they are interesting. Grade is mostly participation and attendance, including mandatory attendance at 8 guest lecturers. Probably one of the most impactful classes I've taken at UNC.

Phenomenal class and professor. This was an incredible experience; Dr. Baumgartner brings in a range of guest speakers and takes calls from death row in class while also covering relevant statistics about the death penalty. I left this class truly impacted from the testimonies I heard and inspired by his research. I cannot recommend enough.

Dr. Baumgartner is amazing, this class is so interesting! Everything I learned was so interesting and relevant, and the guest speakers were phenomenal. Everyone should take this class if they can.  TAs decide most of your paper grades and they can vary a lot so beware of that.

This class was so incredible! I would highly recommend it. It consisted of lectures, recitation, and an evening speaker series, and the speakers/call-ins during class really made the class. I will say that I felt like there was sometimes conflicting information given, but that didn't end up being an issue. Quizzes, reflections, term paper, final.

One of the most interesting classes I have ever had here and one of the best professors I have ever had here. Although speaker events are mandatory to attend, they are super interesting and necessary for the final.

This class was extraordinary!  Definitely one of the best classes to take at UNC!  Very eye-opening and inspiring.  Class was structured well.  Reading quizzes can be hit or miss, but they're open note and mostly easy.  Short essays were graded easily, and the final term paper was not bad.  Final exam was basically a mix of old reading quizzes.

Your grade is composed of weekly quizzes, recitation attendance and participation, attendance at speaker series (unc brought wrongfully convicted speakers for our class to hear) 4 short essays that were basically easy 100's, a final exam that was just the weekly quiz questions and a 7 page final paper. Overall 10/10 class, everyone should take it

I've loved my classes with Frank Baumgartner! He is super passionate about this class and cares more that we learn something rather than worrying about how to test us. Speaker series was interesting even though they were long and in the evening. His quizzes were exactly from the readings. TA grades papers and recitation attendance is mandatory.

Best class I've taken so far. The material is very important and Prof. Baumgartner delivers it well -- he really knows what he's talking about. And even though the subject matter is dark, it's still a fun class bc of his personality. There is an AMAZING guest speaker series w/ wrongfully convicted people. Homework isn't bad. 100% recommend!

Really committed and passionate professor about the wrongs of the death penalty, but due to the structure of the large lecture, taught mostly by slides which was not engaging. Not a hard class, graded by lots of things, material isn't hard at all.

Fbaum became a sort of cult legend in our class. He's funny, knowledgable, and structured. Some of the ideological bent did come through during the semester and little time is spent on victims or crimes, but the class was largely fascinating statistics and interesting anecdotes. A great way to get your US and SS credits. TAKE IT.

I was hesitant to take this class because I had no interest in poli sci, but this class is extremely interesting and illuminating about the death penalty in the US. It is one of the best classes you can take at Carolina. Baumgartner is an amazing professor as well. Take this!

Fbaum is awesome! I love this class and am learning so much. This class is awesome and will be unforgettable. I think everyone should take this class. I would take any classes taught by Fbaum. You can't go wrong here!

Life changing class and amazing professor. Important content that Frank makes very accessible to engage with, think about, and reflect. I recommend this class 1000% to any philosophy/political science major, or just any student in general who wants to dive into criminal justice.
Frank is the coolest guy ever. I have taken 2 of his classes and he is so awesome. I have really learned a lot from him.

Lecture is completely optional, 2 midterms are take home, 2 essays, and a take home final. Because of this, the class is not hard, but I recomend going to class and taking pretty good notes, especially when you know you are going to do the essay of that week (every week there is an essay and you do 2 of them).

Professor Bapat runs a good class. All lectures are recorded, attendance optional, midterm/final online. He's a good 150 professor, make sure you at least watch the lectures or go to class. Have 2 midterms, final, paper, and a few quizzes in your recitation. He's a good professor to have

The way he grades his papers makes absolutely no sense. He gives you a prompt and a specific outline of how he wants the paper written, but when you follow those exact instructions he still gives you a low grade and doesn't clarify why you got that grade... the papers are 60% of overall grade in the class, making it hard to recover from the papers

Super interesting lectures, respected our time! 2 unit exams and a cumulative final. 2 essays on diff prompts throughout the semester, overall a very doable workload. All exams were online and the lectures were always recorded. Go to recitaiton, participate there and you will be set. Paper grades were def harsher than other grades.

Attendance is not required, but his lectures were interesting and needed for tests/papers, so I just watched them through Panopto. 2 essays and 3 online exams. In each exam, theres an essay prompt, but no rubric is given. TAs have a checklist of terms and your grade depends on that. Not a fan of that because it makes grading subjective

This class was meh. Attendance wasn't mandatory except for recitation--and the grading felt artificial. The midterms and the final weren't difficult at all, just make sure you include stuff you learned from recitation and in class in your answers. The papers were okay, again, not hard if you include info from class. Overall not my fav poli class.
Don't request a paper regrade from him. He dropped my grade by 5 points causing me to get an A- in the class, seemed weird and a little vindictive for some reason.

Although attendance isn't required, I enjoyed his lectures and I think he's a super nice, entertaining guy. You get to pick which paper prompts you write and all exams are online, at home, open-note (don't need to read textbook, mostly covers lecture slides). Overall a very interesting class, he clearly cares a lot, and easy to do well.
