Great professor. Attendance isn't required, but take notes from the online presentations. two essays and three online exams.
Lectures were very interesting and attendance not required. Your grade really depends on your TA and there are not a lot of things to be graded on.

Professor Bapat was amazing! He was so knowledgeable and really cared about what he was teaching. His lectures were very interesting and the midterms were very attainable. Grades were combined of 2 papers (4-6 pages), 2 midterms, and a final. He encourages students to ask questions during lectures and has wonderful TAs!

POLI 150 with Prof. Bapat was super low maintenance. Attendance was optional, 3 exams including the final that are online and asynchronous, and you get to choose from 2 out of 10 papers to complete on your own time. I would take him for 150 if you can.
Overall basic & easy class. Worth taking

Bapat is a really engaging lecturer and very good prof! Even though I ended with an A, I'll say, didn't think I would esp. because the papers don't have super clear grading criteria. He posts lecture slides/recording, its really interesting, & he basically outlined what we needed to know/talk about in the final on the last day so can't complain

Bapat is amazing, very knowledgable and passionate about the topic which makes the lectures very engaging. Personally, the only problem was sometimes I found him to be a difficult grader- I would get points off for things that weren't mentioned in the rubric, so I didn't know to discuss them in my paper. Other than that definitely take this class!

Professor Bapat is incredibly knowledgeable and understanding. Attendance is not mandatory but he is such an amazing lecturer so I found myself going to every lecture. Grades are based on 2 paper, 1 policy brief, and 2 take home exams. Best POLI professor at UNC definitely take a class with him.

Great teaching format. Flexible attendance, not mandatory. The two papers carry 60% in the grading, but I believe every in-person lecture is worth attending. He has extensive knowledge, including current affairs. Grading is clear and timely. The syllabus, with information presented in an organized manner. He is my favorite professor at UNC.

LOVED this class w Bapat. First class with him so I was a little nervous but he is an amazing professor and really pushes students to engage with material. Lectures were interesting and organized— even though there was no attendance I loved going. Exams done in a very unique way that helps prepare you for the IC or other high stress jobs

Attendance not mandatory which was helpful and the content was very interesting and he is an engaging lecturer. But very hard to get an A. Frustrating because he has very specific criteria for papers which he does not share and just expects us to hit very specific concepts that he may have barely even touched on in class. Super frustrating.

Dr.  Bapat was a phenomenal lecturer and I greatly enjoyed his classes. He made me want to attend class! He was a very hard grader and did not give clear instructions on our papers that were worth 70% of our grade combined and expected us to know exactly what he wanted. If you want a good lecturer but hard grader, take the class.
Loved his energy. Great class!

Dr. Clark is a great man and a great professor as well. He is extremely knowledgeable about his field and his lectures are very engaging. I've spoken with him many times outside of class and he is very kind and approachable.

Professor Clark has been one of my favorite professors during my time at UNC! He is very engaging in lectures, is a fair grader, and is easy to reach if needed. Cannot recommend taking one of his classes enough.

Prof Clark is one of the most caring professors I've had at UNC. Although his classes are lecture-heavy, he throws in lots of engaging material (campaign ads, speeches, etc.) and plenty of jokes. Take a class with him if you can!!!

Amazing guy and very personable. Very easy A but as a southerner, I was really disappointed with the substance of the class. It was kind of structured as an orientalist view of the south through a northern microscope of awe which lowered my respect for the course. A southerner who understands southern culture and experience should teach the class.

Great professor, but lowkey not the easy A I thought it would be. Exam questions come from study guides. Essays were a time crunch since he tended to delay releasing prompts, but they were not too difficult. He has funny tangents in class. Great guy, make a lasting connection with him! Grades: 3 essays, 2 exams, participation (attendance)

Dr. Clark is a professor who will make you want to come to class on a snow day. From his vast knowledge of political theory to his desire to hear all students' opinions, he is extremely respected and beloved in the POLI department. He doesn't take himself too seriously and always has a fun anecdote-do yourself a service and take one of his classes.

Dr.Clark is a great professor! He is very passionate about the topics he discusses and it's obvious he cares for his students. A bit of a slow grader but he doesn't grade harshly. Would definitely recommend this course.
Great guy - super caring and an awesome personality. His lectures were entertaining and the midterm was not insanely difficult because of the resources he provided.

Clark is one of my favorite professors I have had at UNC. He is energetic, funny, and super engaging. He uses different media forms to teach like slides, ads, and discussion, and really cares about what students have to say. Papers and exams were straightforward and super easy if you review notes and ask for help when needed.  Take him if you can!

Dr. Clark was alright for IDST 128. He was the last professor so he was kind of in a time crunch. The pre-class materials were literally his papers he wrote so that was kind of weird. Didn't really teach enough about politics, more surrounding race which was odd. Easy class though, would take if you want an A!

The Triple-I format at UNC is undoubtedly poorly organized, and I think Dr. Clark would've been better in a smaller class format. That being said, his lectures had the tendency to be long-winded, and he tended to be slightly patronizing. Easy enough to do well, though.

He was the best professor in my triple-I. He is the only professor who could get all 300 students to speak. He knows what he is talking about and made me more interested in the topic. He shows fun videos that break up the length of the class. Discussion posts were a huge part of this class and there was no final- only a "hard conversation."

Professor Clark was one of the most entertaining and passionate professors I've had. He was so funny and welcomed student input a lot. It took some time to figure out how he wanted you to write, but overall he was a fair grader and inspirationally excited to teach what he did.

Professor Clark was overall really great this semester. He has an amazing personality and is certainly a funny guy. Class is very lecture heavy and readings are not required. Sometimes it was a bit unorganized, but I definitely learned a lot. Grade is based on participation, two papers, and two exams. Didn't find any of them too challenging.
One of my favorite professors ever. Dr. Clark knows his stuff and teaches with a passion.

Overall, I really enjoyed the class and topics. He is an amazing lecturer. I struggled getting responses via email during this semester. Additionally, I found the exam grading to be a bit picky about details when compared to the instructions. Just be sure to ask questions.

Dr. Clark was a great professor, he genuinely cares about what he teaches and for the well being of his students. Two papers, a midterm, and a final, and random attendance throughout the semester. You get a study guide for both exams covering everything that would be on them so it's an easy A. Readings not required, went over main points in class.

The class was rather straightforward. One midterm was easy with an hour of studying, two papers, a question, and a final group project. Not that much work. There was nightly reading but it was not mandatory and you can get away without reading it as long as you pay attention in class.

Great professor! He was really engaging, encouraged good class discussions, and was open to all students' ideas. Poli 204 was pretty easy when I took it - he gave us study guides for the exams and you can probably get by without doing all of the reading. Class attendance matters, so if you skip you're grade will be impacted.

Really nice, easy to do well in the class with effort. Class was 2 papers worth 25% each and a final paper and presentation worth 30%. Participation and attendance matters, but it is easy to participate. Lectures move fast

This semester, she wasn't very accessible outside office hours, but she's a good professor. She's caring and explains things well, though she can be a bit overbearing with coding and reporting students. Thankfully, her teaching makes it easy to follow. One downside was having both a final project and exam. Overall, 9.2/10.

I loved my 281 class with Prof Martin. She truly cares about her students and really wants them to succeed. While she doesn't necessarily lecture most class periods, it's helpful just to have time with R studio with ULA's and her walking around to help us. She is awesome in office hours and responds to emails and discussion posts quickly.

Flipped lecture, teaching yourself. For most the semester half the class is spent doing group work and trying to teach each other how to code in R. Go over basics as a class, hardly ever went over the answers to the group work. Assigned groups and seats for the semester. Nit-picky grading at times on assignments. TAs were nice. Valuable material.

Took her for 281 Spring semester. R is hard to learn but she teaches you the basics and knows that you may have no prior knowledge. Lectures are easy to track and Professor Martin is very nice and understanding.

Grades based on 5 coding assignments on R, 10%/each. Very easy to do well as long as you devote a couple of hours to it. A 30% final project and 20% participation. Very understanding professor who genuinely is looking out for you and the skills learned can be great for data analysis in the future.

I love her she is my favorite professor I've had so far. She teaches the course like you have never seen the material before (even though she has tutorials before class) and she makes this hard to digest subject seem not as scary. I knew nothing about coding before this class and now I feel very comfortable in R.

This class was challenging, but Professor Martin always did her best to help students grasp difficult concepts. I came into this class with no coding experience, but I learned so much by the end of the semester. I would highly recommend taking her class. She is also very lenient with grading and she is always available to help students.

Professor Martin made coding so much less scary than I thought it would be. I knew nothing coming in, and was able to complete a large scale project by the end of the semester. She is so patient and will always give help when you look for it. I cannot recommend her enough.

POLI281 is pretty difficult subject material, but Dr. Martin's lectures made it really easy to understand. You have a long time to work on the homework assignments and collaboration with other students is encouraged. As a major who wants to follow this career path, this was exactly what I was looking for from this class.

Dr. Martin is one of the best UNC professors if you have the chance to take her class do it!  The content was a bit difficult, but she gives students opportunities to ask for help when needed.  She is very caring and was willing to push several due dates back when needed.  I thought I'd hate the class bc it is coding but she made it really easy.
Professor Martin is super competent and makes learning coding easier than it should be. She is also super accessible outside of class if you are struggling along with the ULAs.
Lucy is a goat and any political science student at Carolina should be ashamed if they don't take a class with her.

Just okay. Final was absurd compared to the midterm and was not as fair. She is very sweet and very knowledgeable, but very hard to reach outside of class through email, so office hours are your best option. Participation grades didn't come with a rubric from someone who kept getting 90's and participated/raised my hand a lot during class.
Very sweet and fair grader. The subject is interesting and she leaves space in the syllabus to discuss whatever the class wants to.
Lots of required readings but her exams were always clear and easy to study for. Fair grader she was very open to feedback!!

Bella is an amazing professor! Poli-130 was by far my favorite class this semester. She made the class engaging, but there are readings due every class, with weekly quizzes. Some of the readings are pretty long and our final project was fairly difficult. Not an easy A, but Bella makes up for it with her awesome lectures and love for the class!

i absolutely adored poli130 with her! she's a very good teacher and her lectures are very engaging and she definitely knows what she's talking about. not an easy a and there's reading due for every class with quizzes but the reading helps and if you do it you won't struggle.

Definitely have to put in effort to get good results. Good lecturer and engaging. Does a great job of keeping up with the syllabus and all readings are available on Canvas so nothing to buy. Lots of quizzes but always straightforward w/ no trick questions. Kind and approachable. Loved Bella!
Bella is very friendly and clearly knowledgeable and passionate about political science! She grades fairly and gives good feedback on papers. Definitely recommend her as a TA!
Bella was my TA for POLI 130 and she was wonderful. She was very understanding and caring and encouraged participation even if no one knew the answer. I would definitely recommend having her as a TA.

She was my TA for Professor Anderson's POLI 130 course. She was helpful going over information and condensing the material to help students better understand the readings. There were 2 absences available for the recitation. Overall great TA/Professor and person. She is really understanding and nice!
She's the best TA, and does a phenomenal job of explaining the concepts of the class. She has clear criteria for how she grades your things, so no excuse not to do well.

Bella is an amazing TA! She made an overwhelming class a lot easier to digest. The course material is hard, but she is always available for office hours and answering questions. You can tell she is passionate about the subject and cares about her students' success.

A very solid TA for POLI 130! I looked forward to going to her recitation every week. I felt like the way she explained lecture concepts made them easier to understand. I really recommend going to office hours to discuss papers!

Good lecturer, funny, and engaging. Is able to explain concepts very well and make them easy to understand. Applies current events to lectures too. Class is easy and I never read the textbook and I was fine. Basically AP Gov. Take his class!!

Professor G. was great! Lectures were a bit dry during the first half of the class, mostly because you start off re-learning high school civics. The second half was much more interesting and incorporated many current events. Quizzes/tests required some prep, but were very fair. Take it at a reasonable hour (mandatory attendance).
Great professor! The class isn't difficult at all, nor did he make it difficult. There is a textbook that we had to read before classes, but it's not bad at all. Highly recommend him!

POLI 100 is a very introductory class and is very lecture heavy, so it can get a little boring. I did think Dr. Gebremichael did a good job trying to spice things up by incorporating current events. Attendance is mandatory and there is one midterm, one essay, 3 quizzes, and a final. Grading is very fair, and the class is really just not that hard.

Super fun guy with interesting lectures. You get 3 unexcused absences and my notes were just the slides copied down. didnt read the textbook and did fine. make sure to study for quizzes because if you bomb one you have to do really well on the midterm/final. He curves well though. Try to speak at least once every class as participation matters.

Attendance required, note taking required to do well, slides are posted tho, curved midterm and final (generous 10ish points) so that one person just did really bad, just talk in class and study, its a easy and interesting class

I really liked Professor Gebremichael's lectures and the group discussions! If you aren't comfortable speaking in front of the class, you may not score well in participation though. The material is very interesting and he often incorporated current politics into class. The exams were difficult but curved very generously (15% curve on the midterm).

Prof Gebremichael is extremely strict in attendance and participation, which altogether count as 25% of the total grades. He is also really strict in marking, not giving curves, and is not really helpful when you ask him about how to participate more in class. Would not recommend taking his course at all.

Professor Gebremichael was awesome. I had him for my African American Economics and Inequality FYS, and he had great content, excellent and funny lectures, and was an overall great professor. His grading is stricter for the final presentation and paper, but he gives you more than enough notice to complete them well in advance.

I enjoyed Prof. AG's sense of humor and how much he cared about our individual opinions in class discussions. Compared to other poli prof.'s, he is definitely more difficult. The class is graded on 3 five questions quizzes, a midterm, and the final. If you don't do well on all of the quizzes, it'll be very difficult to get your grade up. He curves!

Prof Gebremichael is down to earth and engaging during his lectures. We had very interesting discussions and his quizzes were super easy. Don't underestimate the tests though, they are pretty hard and have a detailed written portion. The exams were based on the lectures, so I never did the reading and did just fine. Definitely take this class!
nice lectures, interesting content, very interactive, but harsh grading. A is almost impossible

I honestly did not enjoy this class at all. It made me question if I enjoyed political science anymore, and my self-worth. For a 100-level course, it was incredibly difficult, and the professor didn't really provide much help other than lectures. I would not recommend taking this class with Professor Anderson, but good luck if you do!
Lots of reading but class material is interesting.

This class definitely felt a little harder for a 100-level course, compared to the other poli-sci courses i've taken here. Weekly quizzes were lowkey annoying, and readings were so long, but the class was okay and the lectures were good. Also hateeeee the fact that the exams are weighed 30% mcq and 70% essay, like dude, this is so ta biased.

no one cares that she went to Stanford and Harvard. this is a 100-level class. she's unaccommodating: i had to take weekly quizzes while hospitalized. grading feels TA-dependent, As are rare (94 = A, no rounding). i was docked for recitation participation despite university excused absences. not an easy A, and she acts like it's your only class.

Professor Anderson is a wonderful lecturer. It is very apparent in class that she is extremely knowledgeable. The class requires a lot of reading, which is important for exams and papers. The grading is very TA-dependent. It is difficult to receive an A unless you do super well on the papers, which again is TA-dependent.

She is an amazing lecturer, passionate about explaining political science. Readings complement her lectures, which cover core concepts effectively. The readings provide essential real-world examples, crucial for excelling on papers and midterms. The two papers are graded slightly harshly. Overall, a great class!

Ashley clearly knows a lot about the subject and cares about what she is teaching. Lectures were easy to follow but mostly conceptual so most of the examples you'll need for the exam essay come from the readings. She's kind of disorganized so be prepared for the syllabus to change. She also does not round grades so do the extra credit!!

Super interesting lecture and class material. Anderson is incredibly knowledgeable. None of the assignments are very difficult; however, almost impossible to get an A, given 80% of your grade comes from just 4 assignments (2 papers and a written midterm and final / have to really crush the papers) + extra credit assignments were really dumb imo.

The course was her just stating the blatantly obvious and she didn't really seem to portray her resume. This class being an honors class taught by an Ivy-Alum made me lose faith in Poli Sci and I dropped the major. Was geared towards how much surface level stuff you could learn as opposed to stimulating thought and depth into the Middle East.

I took POLI 130 with her, and she was pretty great! Informative lectures, clearly knows her subject matter, and encourages class participation. Readings are the main homework, and are necessary to know for the midterm and final. Additionally, I would recommend checking the lecture handouts for the key terms, because those will also be on the tests.

Very little homework for this class, just weekly quizzes that were online. She is a great teacher, very humble and real with her students. The most difficult part of the course is prepping for exams as there is such a large amount of information covered. Would definitely recommend for an intro poli class.

She's a little weird but all professors are. She talks very fast and makes really weird caricatures of different heads of state. I was doing well in her class until the final. The final bent me over and took everything. Study Study Study (I spent so many hours in Davis and it still wasn't enough).

Lectures are interesting, and the group project is fun, but the midterms are graded like English papers, not political science, which is hard with only 30 minutes. I didn't learn much comparative politics, did learn some more about the Middle East, and the class didn't feel like true comp politics.

Professor Anderson is disgustingly and dangerously educated. She makes lectures engaging and is very knowledgeable in pretty much everything she talks about. Attendance is required. There's weekly quizzes with five questions and two papers, along with the midterm and final that make up your grade. She challenges you, but an A is possible!
Loved her. Very intelligent, good prof. Fun class. Silly person! Made class enjoyable. Difficult assignments, but I learned from all of them and they all helped me improve.

Great class and professor overall, but didn't love the communication between professor and I. She's very nice but unavailable. I showed up to her office hours once, waited an hour and a half just to find out that she was in Europe and didn't notify her students. This was a week before finals. But everything other than that about the class was fine.
Incredibly knowledgable, caring, and well spoken professor. The class is huge but she manages to make it feel very personal. I'd take POLI 130 with her again in a heartbeat. (Also, great TAs)

Anderson is a very knowledgeable professor and makes the lectures more interesting than they probably should be. The essays and exams are more easy than they appear. Only drawback is that the Professor Anderson is not very accessible and the TAs will be your primary source of advice and communication.

Really informative course. Dr. Anderson's lectures were captivating and all the material was really interesting. You aren't graded on many things, which isn't ideal, but it isn't too hard to do well on her exams as long as you use relevant examples of what you learned in class in your essay.

The simulation is awesome, yet there were definitely times where the class wasn't super enjoyable. Nothing against Dr. Weidenfeld, but he can get disorganized at times and confuse you pretty easily. Material is pretty straightforward and overall a great experience.

Super cool professor, the class isn't too bad if you do the readings and attend lecture as the quizzes and exams are pretty straightforward. however, this class is extremely disorganized through and through, with last minute delays or last minute notices on exams and quizzes. nonetheless, not too hard to get an A if you do the work.

Weidenfeld creates an engaging class where I truly bonded with my classmates. He is also BY FAR the most DISORGANIZED prof I've ever had here. Completely inaccessible outside of class and doesn't answer emails. It wasn't ever serious and he grades leniently,but disorganization before quizzes and exams is definitely stressful, so keep that in mind.

Such an amazing and smart teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and doesn't grade harshly at all. Very engaging lectures and the simulation portion of the class if not too hard. The quizs are easy and sometimes even done in groups, exams are challenging but if you pay attention in class then you will be good. Take this class!!

He does a great job teaching and making topics understandable. As a non-poli major (took for the gen-ed credit) I found this course interesting and digestible, with a reasonable amount of work for a gen-ed.
Sometimes dawdling in lectures, but very kind person and passionate about the materials.
Great professor. Funny and just an overall good dude. The class was fun and engaging

Weidenfeld was great, I took poli 59 as my first year seminar and I am very thankful I did. He made the class a lot of fun and a nice way to spend the mornings. You get to know the people in your class and most quizzes and even exams are able to be done with classmates.

This class was so much fun and I would highly recommend you take it! It consisted of a speech, 6 quizzes (one dropped), 3 tests, participation, and a final discussion (10%) of grade. As long as you read the required pages listed in the study guide you will do well on the quizzes/tests, overall very fun class and a great way to get the theory credit

The Reacting to History format was engaging and fun, using a historical character to do a deep dive on different parts of political history. Mr. Weidenfeld was not often available over email/outside of class and the organization of the class was not great. Most of the benefit I got was from group collaboration and challenging my perspective.

Professor Weidenfeld is capable of being very engaging, but the class was incredibly disorganized. I learned almost nothing in the class and not challenged by anything other than keeping track of Weidenfeld's mess. Small classes or ones with no simulation component with him could be great but he can't manage a ~100 person simulation.
He is beyond unorganized and students suffer as a result.

Professor Weidenfeld is a great professor who demonstrates a deep passion for his field and is dedicated to helping students succeed. My only complaint is that he semi-frequently fails to communicate well (or at all) on assignments or class cancellations.

Weidenfield is a great lecturer as he is very engaging and truly knows the material. However, he is completely inaccessible outside of class, and his disorganization and bias in simulation made the course much more unenjoyable than it needed to be. I enjoyed this class, but you are pretty much on your own in the second half and grade is up to you.

He was entertaining but almost entirely inaccessible outside of class, so if you needed him for something, you better catch him before he scurried out of the room. As long as you did the necessary reading, you could make the class your own, i.e., you could play NYT Games during lecture/simulation. Unreal but definitely fun professor/class.

This class was one of my favorites! Lecture on political philosophy the first half, then simulation on the Constitutional Convention the second half. Weidenfeld creates an engaging environment and lets the class run the Convention. Only critic is that he never answers emails and is rarely available outside of class, but I overall recommend.

This is the most fun class I've ever taken. The first five weeks are content based with two quizzes and a midterm, but the rest of the semester is a simulation of the Constitutional Convention. Make sure to really play into your character and participate as much as possible. The midterms and quizzes were not super hard and they were graded fairly.

Weidenfeld is a great professor. His lectures are engaging and we have spent the last month or so doing a simulation based on the French Revolution. You can tell he is really passionate about the things he teaches. A lot of people are complaining about the quiz that "bombed" everyone's grade, but he let us use the readings. A bit Disorganized.

Dr. Weidenfeld is the goat. Really funny and very, very passionate about the topic. This course is a super unique format so you really have to buy into the whole thing but it's a lot of fun if you do. Quizzes and exams are on the harder side as it is an upper level course. Overall would recommend to anyone considering taking this class!

Nice guy and fun lectures but recent quizzes have been so difficult. Quiz 4 was literally impossible for everyone I know. Totally destroyed my grade and not sure what to do now. Again, fun lectures, but the quizzes feel super unreasonable :(

She is my favorite professo!! She is so sweet and you can tell she is very passionate about what she teaches. While she can be lecture heavy, her lectures are engaging if you are interested in the class. She has a great sense of humor, is incredibly intelligent, and will draw on her own personal life experience which I think is valuable. 10/10 imo.

She is super sweet and passionate about the material! The only thing is that she doesn't really grade anything throughout the semester, so you won't really know what your grade is until the end. The lectures aren't super discussion based, but mostly her just lecturing, but she explains concepts pretty well.

In the kindest way possible, CMG is very disorganized. She is very passionate about the topic however the whole class is confusing. Unclear grading criteria, putting incorrect answers on exams, etc. She is impossible to reach on email, and we don't even know what our grade is in the class. It sucks because she's a great person but not disciplined.

She's passionate and very sweet but very hard to reach outside of class. Your grade is hidden the whole semester and you can not even calculate your own grade most of the time because she never grades most of her things. Midterms can be tricky, just study your notes hard because some of the questions are really specific.

She is very passionate and kind but is not clear on grading criteria and refuses to open her email and respond to any questions. Only way to reach her is genuinely in class after the lecture. Super sweet but no sick days or absences so make sure you show up.

Interesting class, grade based mostly on low-stakes assignments. Do the readings/daily discussion questions, participate in class, and write a current event for basically half of your grade. The other half is a 5pg essay, group podcast, and 3 tests (multiple choice, short answer on final). She is super knowledgeable and made the class enjoyable!

She was a good professor who made the content and class interesting. However, if you like knowing what your grade is, don't take this class. She hasn't released any grades, and it's the day of the final exam. She also tends to make tests tricky, saying that there could be more than 1 right answer, but that she's looking for something specific.

She was going through some personal things this semester, so sometimes the class was erratic. In general, she is a good prof, but with all over-the-place lectures and focuses on things that fit her worldview, but which might not necessarily be the full story. Still, she's sweet and willing to work with you.

Professor Martinez-Gallardo could be all over the place sometimes in lectures, but it is strictly because she is passionate about the course material. I had a great time in this class. 55% of the grade is participation, so show up to class and pay attention to get a good grade. Basically, if you do the readings and discussions, you will succeed.

Poli 434 was a very easy class. 55% of the grade came from either attendance or assignments that were graded on completion. She takes attendance but does so randomly. As long as you show up to class and turn things in you will get an A or an A-.

She lectured a lot and would go off on tangents that meant we didn't cover all the material in class. Her lectures were also a little hard to follow at times. Overall tho, I learned a lot abt Mexican politics and feel informed enough to speak on current events. She gives lots of little low-stakes assignments. Its a lot of work but not too hard.
I absolutely loved profesora Martinez-Gallardo. She is so passionate about Latin American politics, and was so so kind. I'm taking her POLI-434 course this Spring, and I'm super excited!
Tedious lectures. Irresponsive professor. We didn't know any of our grades until right after the final. Pretty disorganized as well. Easy material, but the grading style was a little odd.

The absolute cutest. I love this woman. She's so caring, kind, and involved. Really stresses mental health and learning to learn, very flexible. Totally recommend her Poli 238 (latin america) or Poli 434 (mexico)!

Dr. Szypszak is knowledgeable and an interesting person to learn from. He has lots of legal experience. The discussions that we had in class to me were the best part. There is a reasonable amount of reading court cases and studying to do well on the exams, but I found it to be very manageable. Would definitely take again.

POLI 75 is a great course for anybody mildly interested in law, and Prof Szypszak is an incredible lecturer. Make sure you read before class, he cold calls and docks your participation if you can't demonstrate a basic understanding of the reading. 

One of those classes where it's more important to show that you're trying than it is to be correct.

Professor Szypszak is a fantastic lecturer and professor. He seems scary at first but he is super approachable if you want to talk to him after class. Just do the readings and pay attention in class and you will be fine!

Awesome professor! If you are interested in pre-law this class is a MUST. This course is mostly reading cases and lectures, a legal research exercise, a paper, and two exams. His lectures are highly engaging as he really understands the material and brings in anecdotes. Introduces the different fields of law and what being a lawyer is actually like

Prof. Szypszak is the goat. I thought he was scary at first but he rocks. You have to take notes during lectures and no electronics. He is so interesting and his past is crazy cool. He can be a tough grader but totally worth it. Learned all about American law, court cases, and the job of lawyers. Im def not cut out for law tho

This class is definitely more difficult than most of FYS, but Prof. Szypszak is a nice man who talks a lot about his experiences. This class exposes you to different fields of law, which is helpful for Pre-Law students. Grading is fair and you will end up knowing so much more about American law and what lawyers do after this class.

Absolutely my favorite professor of my first year. He is super experienced and knowledgeable, and every lecture was interesting and enlightening. There is a fair amount of reading, some of which is rather dry, that you need to do to be prepared for class, but it is worth it. Not much work outside of reading.

POLI 75 was an interesting class itself, but Professor Szypszak is a tough grader. He is vague with instructions for assignments that are worth a large percentage of your final grade. Be prepared to read a lot before every class and come to class prepared because participation is 20% of your final grade.

Professor Szypszak made this course really interesting. It was my favorite class of my first year and I highly recommend it to first-years who are remotely interested in law. The papers were really interesting to research and even though some of the assignments were fairly tough, he gave pretty clear instructions on how to do each assignment.

Professor Szypszak is very knowledgable about law and was great in answering questions. There are readings due for every class but most aren't over 6 pages. You should try to talk at least 1 or 2x a class since participation counts for 20%. Overall, his class was extremely helpful in learning about the different types of law and what lawyers do.

Professor is caring about his students and geniunely wants everyone to fully learn/appreciate the material. He's super passionate about law and answers all questions to the best of his ability. I enjoyed the seminar structure of the class and while readings are due every class, they aren't too long and most have a purpose for lecture. I recommend!

Professor Szypszak is an amazing professor. He comes off as a bit intimidating at first but he's super nice and will talk to you outside of class. His lectures were really great and it is clear he has a ton of experience in the law field. Reading wasn't too much, but class is graded on only a few assignments.

Professor Searing is a nice man who is willing to work with you. However, his lectures are extremely boring and unorganized. Additionally, there is about 100 pages of reading for every class. But, if you can understand a few main ideas from every reading you can do well on the exams and in the class.

Professor Searing is super knowledgeable and lectures, while long, are interesting. The readings are long and sometimes dense but you also don't always have to do them. Class is graded by few things. Exam and Midterm worth a lot. Debates in class are manageable with prep. Overall, not a bad class.

I greatly enjoyed the lectures. He does a good job of including students in his lectures, especially in the latter half of the class. This class is EXTREMELY reading heavy, so I would not recommend this class if you have many extracurriculars. There are few grades in the class, but he grades easily, so if you study it should not be a problem!

The three-hour seminar could be a slog, and Searing could be quiet and hard to listen to. The class is participation heavy with student-led debates and chapter discussions. Be prepared to voice your opinion on controversial topics, although Searing is a caring guy who treats the subject and students with respect and dignity. Overall, a good class.

He's a good professor, and the class feels more like a conversation between him and the students. If everyone participates, you'll enjoy it. It meets once a week, so don't miss class. He's clear about his expectations, just pay attention, and you'll do well. He's the good professor with bad reviews, but that's actually chill

Prof. Searing is very knowledgeable on the subject and I didn't consider his class very difficult, although other students had trouble. I got an A w/o doing any of the reading; just showed up to class, participated, did well on the assignments, and reviewed the key terms for the exams. Only complaint is he can be hard to understand bc he mumbles.

I loved 432 and 215. Searing is so knowledgeable and passionate about what he does, and the material and lectures are some of the most interesting I've taken at UNC. Bc its polisci people expect class to be easy and dont want to do the work but he grades easily if you just do the reading. HIGHLY recommend him. Very thought-provoking courses.

If you don't like reading 100+ pages a night don't take this class. Incredibly reading and lecture heavy, with no powerpoints or visual aids. He talks at you for the class period quietly mumbling. I would not take a class with him again. He grades on 3 grades: participation/group presentation, midterm, and final

Very knowledgeable, would recommend. The only things you are graded on are the tests and participation. You do have to do the readings (at least most of the time), but this course's material is easily digestible and interesting. Easy grader on the exams, and he gave me almost perfect participation even though I skipped several times. Good guy.

No slides. Talks TO us for entire lecture. Rambles. Unclear prompts for midterm and final essay (40% each). Due to him being late for finals, allowed us to copy our midterm grade to skip finals. I did.

He is very knowledgable and shares a lot of his experiences. I will say that he does not use powerpoints so it is hard to follow at times. He is a tough grader and the class requires a lot of readings. I have taken many poli classes before, but this one had the most readings.

If you are a minority or LGBTQ, I would advise strongly against this course. He came across as very transphobic and slightly racist in many lectures. It was a very difficult semester to have to sit through his lectures and him playing "devils advocate" in a way that invalidated the identity of many people (LGBTQ people primarily).

The class was not too hard, but I would not recommend skipping. Missing one class can throw you off in the course, and playing catch-up is not enjoyable. There is a lot of coding, but once you get a hang of it, the class becomes fun! Dr. Watson is a great professor and is always willing to help! I would greatly recommend taking the course with her!

I only received an A because a significant portion of the grade is the take-home assignments. There's a lot of coding, and it's all very fast-paced, so you have to understand things as you go. Missing one class absolutely took me out of the loop. She is a very supportive and caring professor, though.
She made R coding very approachable and while it's not an easy A class, it's not difficult if you put in the work

Dr. Watson was a great professor and flexible with deadlines. There is a lot of homework assignments, but they're all due at the end of the semester. This class doesn't relate to politics and it's almost all coding in R, but as someone who isn't coding or math savvy, it wasn't hard!

Watson taught the content very well and in an easy to understand way. Pretty easy A if you pay attention in lecture and do the homeworks. Also there are  extra credit opportunities for midterm/final. Useful skills to learn, but like the other comments mentioned, the slow pace kept class boring sometimes.

The reason the class is boring as other people say is because Dr. Watson has to move slowly to accommodate for the average tech-savy level of poli sci students (LOW). Teaches a very in-demand skill in a great way. Group project is dumb and heavily dependent on who you get paired up with, but I would reccomend taking this class 100%.

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS! If you're a POLI major, take POLI 209. Dr. Watson may act like she cares, but it doesn't really seem genuine. She often speaks in a soft, almost baby-like voice throughout class. There are five major assignments, and unless you're an R genius, you'll likely struggle with them. Also, her tests seem designed to trip you up.

Half the class is R and the other half is statistics. I had no experience with either, but I learned a ton and feel really confident that I'll be using these skills in the future. The class isn't super hard but you do need to study and ask for help if you start falling behind. Prof Watson was great and I only have good things to say abt this class
description of 281 was completely misleading- it's literally just incredibly boring coding the entire semester.
Lots of papers but she grades fairly leniently. Definitely the kindest professor I've had at UNC.

While the major part of your grade comes from essays they were not hard as long as you did the reading and took the time to actually write the paper. The papers are a lot of work! The class has a good bit of hard-to-digest reading while during class you have a lot of group work and participation. Professor Watson is very understanding.

The description and name of this course is deceiving. There's barley any politics, all coding. The prof is not very helpful, and the grades for assignments take forever (3 week average). Class was not engaged, and I don't think anyone I talked to in this class really liked it. Wouldn't recommend

Was not aware that this class was coding heavy when I signed up for it, so I hated it for the first few weeks as I was learning to code. Dr. Watson was very helpful though, along with her ULAs. While the lectures towards the end get boring if you don't like stats, she specifically is not a bad professor, in fact, she's pretty good.

The content of this class is interesting if you like data science, but the way it was presented in this course was very dry. The students in this class were never engaged and paid so little attention that by the time it got to the final project, nobody in my group knew how to use R. Unfortunately a disappointing course.

Dr. Watson is quite knowledgable and passionate about International Relations and Human Rights. While the course was interesting, you are required to teach yourself. Participation matters and a lot of the work you will do is for completion. For exams, they are all take home essays, that are strictly graded/not graded in a timely manner.

Dr. Watson is knowledgeable and kind, but the class relies heavily on self-teaching and feels repetitive. Each class includes lengthy readings with graded guides, group presentations summarizing the material, and her occasional input. Expect biweekly exam papers, slow grading, and a final Model UN sort of simulation. Ideal for self-learners.

Dr. Watson is an amazing professor. Though I started off really bad at coding, I learned so much through this class. Unless you have a sense of comfort in coding, prepare to be challenged at some point, but she is happy to work with you in office hours and is kind. The workload is very manageable and was the perfect amount for learning.
Prof. Andrews-Lee is by far one of the best professors at UNC! She is so smart and really cares about her students. The work is 100% manageable, the final and the midterm are very achievable.

Best polisci professor! So passionate about her work and super engaging. Almost too smart for us, so sometimes we leave her hanging when she asks us questions in class. Overall, highly recommend her class! 2 exams, 3 in-class writing assignments, and a final policy simulation. Meet with her in office hours if you want her to explain/help review.

Professor Andrews-Lee clearly cares for her students and their wellbeing both inside and outside of class. Lenient on attendance if you are sick, but make sure to show up as much as you can, as the exams are directly based on lecture slides and conversations held in class. Exams were easy if you studied the way she said. Lots of reading.

Prof Andrews-Lee is such a knowledgable professor on comparative politics and one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She truly wants her students to succeed and the assignments she chose for class are interesting. The midterms and finals are not too difficult and she makes her lectures really engaging! I would definitely recommend her class.

This course deals with Latin American politics, and it is clear that Professor Andrews-Lee is extremely knowledgeable about this topic. I also found it highly beneficial to speak with her during her office hours when I needed clarification on the course. She will suggest scheduling appointments so keep that in mind if you plan on speaking with her.

Prof. Andrews-Lee is one of the most kind and caring professors I've had. She is so great at making the material easily digestible. If I had any questions I found she was more than willing to answer them during office hours and over email, and often went the extra mile to help. If you review the slides before exams you should easily ace them.

Professor Andrews-Lee genuinely cares about her students and the topics she teaches. She's passionate and encourages students to participate regularly in discussions. No textbook, but there's still quite a bit of reading outside class. I learned so much, 10/10 would take again!

Professor Andrews-Lee is genuinely passionate about what she teaches, and she teaches in a way that's very easy to understand and relate to politics around the world. She's always open to answer questions and takes care to make sure everyone understands the material. Homework was very manageable.

Professor McGuire's lectures were always entertaining, and I felt like I received a very comprehensive overview of the Supreme Court's operations and the factors that influence it. Course structure is unusual for POLI courses, with three exams making up 84% of your grade, but once you figure out what you're expected to know they're pretty easy.

Professor McGuire is easily my favorite professor at UNC. He gives such amazing lectures that are so interesting, he really is one of a kind. The class is graded by 3 exams along with weekly discussion posts, but just go to class, study the slides, and don't put off the readings and you will do just fine. Great class, content, and professor.

McGuire is an incredibly funny and nice guy and I truly enjoyed his lectures and thought the content was engaging. However, as a MEJO major taking the class for the graduation requirement, I would not recommend it. There are much easier POLI classes to take instead, so unless you are very interested in the topic I would take something else.

Great professor and he is very knowledgeable. Most of your grade are the exams so be prepared to study for them AND you must read the books. 20 points of the exam are questions from the 3 books you are required to read so you must read them and the summary of the book is not enough. Lecture can get long but content is very interesting

Prof McGuire has a simple format, which I enjoyed. You talk and discuss cases during class until the midterms, when he asks you about them. You have to read, but he makes class interesting and worth going to in order to do well. There are 3 midterms and 10 discussion posts, that is it. Go to class and you will do well, I recommend the class.

I throughly enjoyed Dr. McGuires class! He is so good at explaining the cases and training your mind to look at cases through the lenses of the justices. Your grade is only based on three exams and a weekly discussion forum, but I found the exams to be extremely fair and as long as you study and come to class an A is definitely attainable!

Great professor, recommend him for anyone interested in Poli or on a pre-law track. Very clear expectations in the course, and it is very manageable. Midterms and the final were not too difficult, just ensure you study days ahead of time. Attendance isn't mandatory, but do make sure you go to class to do well in his class.

Professor McGuire is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He leads incredible class discussions that make understanding each case easy and memorable. On top of that he is hilarious, passionate, caring, and charismatic. You are graded by 3 exams that take up 80% of your grade, so start learning the cases early and you will do fine. 10/10 class.

Dr. McGuire is a great professor. He's very knowledgeable about what he teaches. He's also pretty funny in lectures. The class was structured in a very easy to understand way. 3 tests, and discussion board posts. If you attend class and study you will get a good grade. I'd highly recommend Dr. McGuire.

The guidelines for this class are very straightforward and easy to understand. The lectures are incredible and are not super difficult to follow. Attendance is not mandatory but it's hard to understand the point of the slides if you miss class. Mcquire is awesome and I would definitely take again. He's always available during office hours.

He is so witty and funny. He kept class interesting and I really enjoyed his lectures. Your grade consists of three exams and a discussion board. Personally, I loved this format. His exam questions and grading were super fair. He also puts in grades super fast even though the exams are all written! Go to class (& take notes) and you'll do good!
The class is very structured and easy to follow. As long as you know the cases and what they mean for the U.S. you will do fine.

McGuire is the goat. His class is super lecture heavy but attendance is not mandatory. It is still worth going because they are super interesting and he is a really entertaining guy. Exams make up the bulk of the grade but learning the cases and going to class make it easy to do well. If you are considering law school, I highly recommend his class.
Great Professor overall, grading could have been better.
The best Poli Sci prof at UNC by far. Take as many of his classes as you can!

Every week I feel like I learned something groundbreaking that changed my perspective on the foundations of government. McGuire's lectures are incredibly interesting and engaging, with lots of participation, as he likes to work through issues interactively and logically which is great. A few professors teach this course, but he is by far the best.

Professor McGuire is awesome, take his class if you have the chance. While the class is lecture-based, he makes it fun and engaging. The tests cover a lot of information and pull from both lecture and the textbook. The tests are 84% of the grade and forum posts are 16%. Overall I learned so much from this class - great for anyone interested in law!

One of the best lecturers I've had. Great at making tough subjects more understandable while engaging the students and keeping the mood light. IMO he tended to grade the three exams (which made up 84% of the grade) real harshly. But overall a super solid prof who I'd recommend to anyone interested in law.

I love this man, he is one of my favorite professors and I'm usually not a fan of lecture-heavy courses, but he did it in a way that I didn't find boring. Sometimes the content was dull, but that's not really his fault. Do the readings and understand them because that is where I always lost points. But he is fabulous and very funny.

The most amazing political science class. Truly an honor to have him as a professor. Every class was super exciting. Professor was incredibly funny. Participation is easy. Tests are difficult, but you just have to study and know your cases well. Made the most boring cases fun.

*SCLL 185* Dr. Hanagan is good professor, but definitely a tough grader(with little feedback regarding what was done wrong on certain grades). She values participation during class time along with group discussions. She does a good job of thoroughly covering class materials.

Took poli 280 for focus capacity as a freshman (not poli sci major).... but semi chill course. Prof hanagan is a very chill grader and clearly outlines all assignments + exams. I never got below an A- on anything. She basically hand feeds you what to argue in the group debate too, and graded that very leniently. There are 3 extra credit chances.

I like her a lot, she is very sweet and caring. Flexible with attendance if you have a genuine reason you can't be there. her lectures are sometimes quite dry. Class involves a lot of group discussion so do the readings.
This class was interesting and informative. Lots of in-class assignments, a big debate project, and quote identifications on the exams.

Prof Hanagan is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter, and she heavily encourages participation. She's a relatively tough grader as far as first year seminars go, but if you do the readings and put in some effort, you should be fine. The major grades are an in-class debate, short video, two reading analyses, and an oral exam.

I liked this class. Lots of reading some required for in class assignments. She's a great lecturer so it made a class I was worried about more digestible. There's a debate at the end of the semester you might be worried about but it was pretty easy. Not a harsh grader either

Awesome professor, not too difficult. HEAVY readings and has textbooks, but can probably get PDFs. Main grade is a debate which needs a fair amount of effort but she gives class time, groups are random but worked out pretty well for our class. Fair grader, just put effort into your papers and reflections and in class writings and you'll do fine.

Dr. Hanagan is incredibly knowledgeable about American political theory and delivers lectures in a way that make the content digestible. There is a significant amount of content covered, so I would recommend doing all the readings if you want an A. She is accessible and helpful in office hours. Overall, I learned a lot and improved as a writer.
Very harsh grader for a first year seminar…. You would definitely have an easier time getting an A in a different one. Lots of reading and lectures could be dry at times

Professor Hanagan was overall a really great professor. Her lectures could at times seem a bit monotone, but if you actually engage with the material outside of class and listen to what she's saying it's clear she has an abundance of knowledge on this topic. Pretty harsh grading compared to other FY seminar's, but very caring and accommodating.
This was honestly one of my favorite Poli Sci classes I have taken at UNC. Professor Hanagan is a genius and genuinely so nice. I would 100% recommend this class (and Prof. Hanagan) to anyone!

Prof. Hanagan was fine - she tried her best to make lectures engaging (which I personally found very boring). Only went to class for assignments that counted towards attendance, and never did a reading. Use the study guide wisely and be prepared to put some effort in for the papers and debate, and you'll be fine. Decent course overall.

Well, it's advisable to read before class if there's ever confusion. She was super good at demystifying information. Her exam study guides were actually goated, and you always knew what to expect from papers/exams.
This course was interesting and the class discussions were insightful. The professor was a fair grader, super understanding and caring, and overall a good professor.

Professor who knows her material well, offers extra credit opportunities and records all her lectures (which is awesome), and is a genuinely nice person. Grades relatively easily. Grade is 5% mini-assignments, 15% 2 short papers (500 words), 25% essay, 10% one midterm, 20% debate, and 25% final exam. However, an A is a 94 in this class.

Dr. Hanagan was truly one of the best professors of the semester. She's really engaged and as accommodating as possible. She didn't take attendance, but had surprise mini-assignments that counted for an attendance grade and THESE ADD UP so try to go. She's really great, just communicate your needs and stay on top of the work and it should be easy!

I liked Prof Hanagan's class and found her lectures to be very engaging. She's a very easy grader and the HW assignments are not hard. Even though she doesn't take attendance, she'll randomly have in-class assignments that are basically completion grades but you must be present to do them. There was a group debate, which I found frustrating.

As a senior lacking effort, this class was a struggle. Most of it is lectures that are not engaging and I played NYT games during it. Overall, got a good grade and it was relatively easy. Lots of readings but I barely did them and still got by. Few papers and a group debate. Just be aware it can be boring.

Professor Hanagan is a kind professor who really wants her students to succeed. If you put the effort into this class and attend office hours before the major writing assignments, you can improve. There were many readings throughout the semester which were sometimes very dense. The group project was interesting and a nice break from usual class.

Professor Hanagan is great. I took her food public policy class as a gen ed and loved how it was a discussion based, small class. There was a final and three papers, and this is one of the few classes where I actually learned something! She encouraged us to advocate for issues and discuss our opinions in conversations with the class. Love her.

This is the best class I've ever taken! I would look forward to it every day. Dr. Sebell is very intense and gets everyone in the class involved. This class made us ask hard questions and stretched the way we thought. The reading wasn't too heavy, and it was all super interesting. We worked really slowly through the texts and got a lot out of them.

Really enjoyed this class, favorite of the semester. I found Prof. Sebell's discussions engaging, even if they often trailed off a bit or lagged behind the readings. Don't take if you don't want to read or don't like engaging in in-class discussions. I found what brought me success was just staying engaged in class & actively participating.

Really interesting class. Attendance is mandatory but as long as you show up and do the readings it's an easy A. Pop quizzes here and there but short and not difficult. Participation encouraged but not required. 1 midterm, 2 papers, 1 final. Nice professor and fun class as long as you complete the readings and put some effort into the essays!

He lectured the entire class and was extremely disorganized, making it difficult to study my (paper) notes— no devices allowed. Lots of pop quizzes that make up a good bit of your grade (and were often given a whileee after the reading it was based on). Not a great environment to ask questions during class or ask peers for help.

Some of the topics were interesting but I feel like half the time the class was sidetracked so bad by some random kid saying something so irreverent. And then Sebell entertains it and before you know it the class is over and you're sitting there wondering what you even learned. The levels of disorganization in this class should be studied in a lab.

Tough class because it's the same thing every single day (reading books/writings and analyzing them). Gave pop quizzes so make sure you do the readings. He also gives extra credit opportunities by going to events, having perfect attendance, and participating class. Can be hard to participate and understand the key points sometimes.

Not a bad professor, just a boring class. But I am also not interested in the class topic at all. Beware of pop quizzes because lots of reading, and class consist one 1 exam, 2 papers, and a final. A reasonable grader, and easy to reach out to. I would recommend this class if you are interested in philosophy, but if not, I wouldn't take it.

This class wasn't awful but it was just so boring. Every day in class it was just us listening to him talk about the dense reading we were assigned. There are random pop quizzes throughout the semester. I just wish the class was more organized as the syllabus is a joke for staying on track. There were times Sebell didn't even know when break was

I really liked Professor Sebell - he brings up very interesting points about justice and how justice is defined (the class is listed as SCLL 103). I really don't understand the hate against him, especially considering how our class average is probably around the A/B range. Great lecturer, lots of discussions in class, and very quick with emails.

The worst professor experience I have had at UNC. Horrible, unorganized lectures and awful grading system. Absolutely no positives from taking his class, and I dreaded every day that I had his class. Painfully long and boring lectures. DO NOT take any of his classes by any means.

Lectures the whole class, line by line through dense readings. No participation, just him talking. Pure suffering - everyone hated it and struggled to stay awake, except that one reviewer. You haven't seen lifeless students until you've watched Sebell's class walk out at 10:45, and he noticed and didn't care at all.

In class, Prof. Sebell delivered incredible lectures on the basics of modern political theory. He is very knowledgable on the topics he teaches on, however his fatal flaw, funny enough, is that his lectures are often very long, because of his love for the material, so we did not get through all the expected readings. Overall, phenomenal professor.

Prof Weiler isn't super involved in the class itself. It's like 10 lectures (w/ cool speakers), pass/fail, your final grade is just based on an essay and attendance. Definitely have some previous knowledge about IR/poli sci beforehand, like maybe a few past classes, or you could easily get a bit lost in discussions. Liked the TAs.
He was nice and the class was pretty easy, would recommend.
Just amazing! One of the kindest professors on campus, but also absolutely brilliant. Is so invested in you as a student - get talking, and keep in touch with him throughout college.

This is more a plug for GLB 381 than a review of Professor Weiler, who was essential in organizing the course but did not interact substantially with students throughout. The course meets every Tuesday from 7-9ish for lectures of various IR-topics followed my a discussion-based recitation led by TAs. Applicable to all majors and a great experience.

Dr. Weiler is an engaging prof who facilitates class conversation well and offers thoughtful insights into the topics discussed. He is extremely accessible outside of class, and meeting with him made writing the papers and preparing for the final much easier. He cares about his students and genuinely wants them to enjoy this class and learn.

Dr. Weiler does a good job of breaking down large, complex topics and provides lots of material outside of lectures to ensure understanding. Readings are long and occasionally hard to read, but crucial to understanding course material. He is easily-reached outside of class. Not a super easy A (although doable), but rewarding nonetheless.
I have nothing positive to say. The fact I got an A- was a miracle. Worst experience ever. avoid at all costs.

You live by the test, you die by the test. I wish this class had more opportunities for students to demonstrate their knowledge on the law and court precedent. Instead 70% of the grade goes to two online tests with large multiple-choice sections. Unah is a very nice guy, but the laxity was too much. Class would begin far-later than scheduled.

I would recommend taking this class if you're pre-law. It's a great class and the assigned readings were actually interesting and not dense. Dr. Unah is a great professor and is an easy grader. The midterm and final exams are online.

I found the disorganization infuriating and he wasn't super accessible over email either. He is a very nice man but ultimately I did not like the class and even though I did all the work and read every textbook, still ended up with an unideal grade because of one assignment.

Dr. Unah is very knowledgeable and funny, despite his disorganization. You have to buy a lot of books and make sure you do the reading because all of his quizzes are based on the readings. Overall, not too difficult of a class but I learned a lot and would recommend it. The worst part is the paper, but you get a partner.

Dr Unah is a great professor. I think people need to give professors some grace. Unah is funny and caring. Definitely go to office hours and get to know him. He also has a lot of connections. If you're interested in law, take this. Easy A class - one midterm, 6 quizzes (drops lowest 2), a partner paper, and final. Exams are online which is nice

I love Dr. Unah! His style is not going to be for everyone, as you can tell from other reviews. However, if you can get past his high level of disorganization, his classes are really enjoyable. He has so much passion for his discipline, loves talking to students who are interested in law school, and is just a great guy overall. Would recommend!

Dr. Unah is a great professor. His lectures were engaging and he is funny. The class is fairly easy, and I would recommend to those needing a 400 level course. Class consist of online midterm, 6 easy quizzes, one 15-ish partner paper, and online final exam.  Readings were easy and not dense.  Would recommend this class for easy A / A- .

Great professor, is engaging, and passionate about what he teaches.  He is a lenient grader, lets you know what is going to be on the quizzes, and he pushed the midterm back 3 times because the class begged him to.  He is a bit disorganized which makes it hard to prepare before the class. He did show up to the final late because of Canvas issues.

Isaac Unah is the most disorganized professor that I have ever had, whether at a community college or at UNC. He shows up 7 to 10 minutes late to every class, and even showed up 20 minutes late on the Final test. At one point in the class, we were 5 to 6 weeks behind the syllabus, and he pushed the midterms back three times.  
Do not take

Unah is a man who clearly cares about the material that he teaches, and he is very knowledgeable. He is also the most disorganized professor I've ever had. He has delayed midterms and quizzes simply because he forgot they were happening. Material on quizzes and exams are barely covered in class. He is late to class every day. Beware taking him.

Unah is very engaging and makes the lectures interesting by adding in things that are happening in our world today. He really wants you to succeed and his grading is pretty lenient. The only thing I would say is that he is very disorganized and that can sometimes make the class more difficult than it needs to be.

Professor Unah was genuinely one of the best professors i've had at UNC. I had seen his reviews beforehand but was pleased to find he was nothing like what his rating on here would make him out to be. He cares so much for all his students and places a heavy emphasis on ensuring that his students come out of the class prepared for their future.

Dr. Unah is incredibly disorganized.  There are around six required textbooks needed for class, and the syllabus was unreliable to a crazy degree. The final paper for this class had unclear instructions that were contradicted by both the syllabus and in class lectures. Grade is based on three exams, a paper, and random quizzes.

Professor Unah is a little all over the place. If you go to class and actually pay attention, you can easily get a good grade. There are a ton of readings but the most important one is his own book. That one you definitely need to buy and read if you want to get good grades on the exam. Also you have to do data analysis so learn that.

Incredibly disorganized. No structure, long drone-y lectures. Quizzes in class, but would change quiz dates w/o updated the syllabus. Group project at the end w/ no clear instructions & confusing standards; he took points off for not finding evidence that wasn't there. He makes you buy 7 textbooks that you could get an A in the class w/o reading.

Unah is very caring, but his disorganization is insane- and made learning very difficult in his class. Additionally, the final project was a group project with incredibly unclear instructions on an extremely niche topic that didn't contribute to our learning about the U.S. Supreme Court at all- some groups also had a much harder topic than others
He is extremely passionate about the Supreme Court and Constitutions. Lectures are so intriguing! He gave us feedback on the homework to make sure we really understand important concepts.
Super nice and knowledgeable professor! Very interesting lectures and the project was fun!

Great Professor and overall human being. We had 6 quizzes but he told us when we would have them ahead of time. Lectures were detailed from the reading. Take notes of what he says in class and what is on the power points as this would be the info on the quizzes. Final and midterm were information from the quizzes. Term paper was with a partner.

Dr. Steiner is the kindest, most respectful, and passionate professor I have had at UNC. I went into this course anxious because of its description (heavy reading and light cold-calling), but I quickly adjusted and felt very comfortable in this class. Steiner encourages students to think critically about important subjects. I highly recommend!!

Dr. Steiner is great and really knowledgeable on the topics he teaches on. He genuinely cares about his students as people and wants to see them learn. Most of his grades are from essays, which he grades with a pretty high standard though. If you want an easy A, then he's not for you. But, if you want to learn, then definitely go with Dr Steiner!

Prof. Steiner is an amazing teacher, would definitely recommend taking a class with him! He's caring and passionate about the subject. It is a discussion based class, so come prepared. There is a lot of reading and material so definitely make sure to do it. The majority of the grade was in-class essays, with several small reflections and quizzes.

Seminar style class with short reading quizzes and discussion posts weekly, one group paper as well as in class essays for midterm and final. Steiner is a great professor who really does a good job of teaching the material while getting students involved. This class was so impactful to me and I cannot recommend it enough.

Steiner is an amazing professor, I'd recommend this class ten times over! He is very caring and genuinely wants his students to have a strong understanding of the content. Personally, I thought he was a fair grader, but it's crucial that you pay attention to the readings to make A's on essays and quizzes.

AMAZING class. Learned so much from Steiner and will actually apply it to real life. Lots of readings, but don't skip them because it will be evident in your work. Short reading quizzes and minimal cold calling, so come to class prepared. Group paper and 2 in-class essays for midterm and final. Do the work, be thoughtful, and you will be rewarded!

He is a super great guy and very passionate about the subject matter. He is, however, a harsh grader, and you have to write a lot in this class. Be ready for a lot of reading and writing, but classes are not mandatory, and they are discussion-based based which is super fun.

Prof. Steiner is a great guy. Gives good advice & clear feedback on writing. 

3 in-class essays & a group paper make up most of the grades, he also gives a lot of reading quizzes. Do the readings thoroughly & take lots of notes. Lots of writing, best tips are to cut the fluff & write a strong introduction. Participate in discussions & be present.

Steiner is the BEST professor at UNC. This is not an easy class, and he makes you very aware of that at the beginning of the semester. You can definitely get an A in this class, as long as you do the readings and think deeply about the concepts. This is the most impactful class I've taken at UNC.

This is the best class I have taken at UNC. Incredibly caring and kind Professor. The readings are long and dense but very interesting. Be ready to speak during class! It's a good environment to speak, so don't let that deter you. Grading is fair. Avoid any fluff in your writing. Just get to the point.

POLI 255 with Professor Steiner is discussion based so be prepared to participate in class. The topics are interesting and he cares about the students being able to engage with the content. Two take home papers, quizzes, and a group project, all of which are reasonable. I enjoyed this class but be ready to talk!

Graded by 3 equal papers but he is a TOUGH grader. I got a 91.5 on the first, which was the highest for the entire class. The class avg a B on papers, which is kind of crazy for a FY seminar. The content is interesting and he knows the subjects, but grades harsh on papers. Our group paper went to office hours, took his advise, and still got an 84.

Super engaging and interesting professor. Graded by 2 take-home exams and a group paper, plus some quizzes and discussion posts. Grading is done mostly by the TA. I found the grading to be a bit harsh.

POLI 255H is, hands down, the best class I have taken during my time at Carolina. Dr. Steiner is magnificent and the class is powerful, makes you want to be engaged. Readings are dense, but genuinely interesting and relevant to class content. He grades essays predominately for clarity and readability, don't waste time with flowery writing.

Professor Steiner is the best professor I have ever had throughout my academic career. His class opened up a respectful, comfortable space for students to have conversations about immigration. I could not recommend him enough. He is caring, funny, and an overall wise and knowledgeable professor! Show up to class and spend adequate time essays.

One of my favorite classes and professors. I truly learned so much about immigration in this class and really benefited from the discussion format of the class. Steiner created a safe and open environment to share your thoughts on the readings and topics. It's a decent amount of reading and writing, but super interesting and worth it. A must-take.

This class is very discussion based to be sure to participate. Dr. Steiner is very passionate about migration and very knowledgeable. Grades are based on pop quiz (that can be random) so be sure to do the readings and take notes. He is also somewhat a tough grader on the 3 major papers so be sure to go to his office hours and ask for help!

I highly recommend this class and Professor Steiner. He is very knowledgeable and helps you to dive deeper into the material. The readings are all very interesting and the 2.5 hour long feels short when you are there. I came in as a Business Major with no interest in immigration, and am leaving very interested due to Professor Steiner!!!

Dr. Steiner is an amazing lecturer - he is passionate about his work in Migration. His POLI77 class is very discussion-based. Readings aren't difficult as long as you manage your time well. Super kind, thoughtful, and trustworthy. He wants you to succeed in class, so being present in class and following directions is important.
His class is super interesting and engaging, but he's a pretty tough grader when it comes to papers.
Very easy for a 400 level class. The coding aspect was not as bad as I expected and he walks you through everything. Don't have to do the readings.

I thought it would be easy after PWAD 250 and Poli 130 and it was not. Overstudy for the midterm and the final was easier than the midterm. Very few grades that are weighed a lot. He's a good professor - very knowledgeable but the class is a bit hard, the TA this semester graded pretty harshly compared to the prof so fair warning.

Professor Pratt is super knowledgeable in international relations! I would highly recommend taking a class with him, he's super caring and wants his students to succeed. Lectures cover readings, and there are only a few assignments.

Professor Pratt is an underrated professor at UNC. He made a slightly boring topic, international organizations, interesting, and I learned a lot from his course. Class consists of a midterm, final, paper, and group project. Class is lecture heavy, but slides have plenty of notes to follow along, and he is engaging. I recommend taking the course.
