He is very passionate about the material of this class which makes his lectures very engaging. There is a lot of reading, but much of it is covered in class. The material is conceptually pretty mangageable. There is also several assignments that use R but you don't need experience to do them and he also gives practice and work days for these.

Professor Pratt is very knowledgeable and passionate about the content he teaches. There were only two exams in POLI252, a midterm and a final, and Professor Pratt covered everything on them in lecture so they weren't too bad. Overall, grading was fair, and the class was really interesting!

Dr. Ballard-Rosa is a great professor! If you're looking for a 400+ level POLI class or just are generally interested, take this class!! I loved it and wish I would have taken a class with CBR sooner.
CBR was an awesome professor. Really enjoyed this class. Lectures could be a little dry at times but interesting material.

Very kind and funny professor with great lectures. Recitations were just reviews that were unnecessary but attendance was mandatory. Pretty easy A but a lot depends on how your TA grades your essays. Don't buy the textbook you do not need to read it.

Magnificent lectures. Recitations were annoying and not needed, yet they record attendance. Other than that, there is nothing bad. Go to class, study material (the test are easy coming from a bad test taker), write quality essays, and it is an easy A.
I love love loved this class and CBR! He made lectures fun and it felt personalized despite the huge lecture. The grading really depends on your TA, some definitely grade harsher than others.

Dr. Ballard-Rosa is incredibly smart. The lectures were always so interesting and captivated my attention the entire time. However, your grade will heavily rely on your TA, so take that into account. The papers I thought were graded a bit harsh, but if you study for the exams, they are quite easy. I want to take another class with Dr. Ballard-Rosa.

Prof Ballard-Rosa is amazing, and his lectures are super interesting! Go to office hours - he is super knowledgeable and interesting to talk to! Your TA matters a lot (they grade papers, tests, & participation), and I got very lucky with Muhammet. He was accessible outside of class, funny, and made our recitations fun and helpful! Loved this class

CBR was an understanding professor and seemed genuinely interested in the course content. A lot of the content was straightforward but still interesting. There is weekly textbook reading (somewhat heavy), but you cankeep up with content without reading the textbook, since all of that material is covered in lectures/ recitation.

Professor Ballard Rosa is an amazing professor who is super knowledgeable about the subject he teaches! He is super kind, interesting, and really enjoyable to take class with! The only downside is the class is graded by 2 essays and a midterm and final, so if you screw one up, it's unlikely you will get an A!

Overall a great professor and a very engaging lecturer. The content of the class is very basic, introductory information for international relations, but is still pretty interesting. You may want to look over the textbook, but the lectures cover all the material from the textbook that you need to know for the tests and papers.

It's a very straightforward class. You don't really need to buy the textbook if you take good notes and get the terms down. The terms are given as a study guide prior to exam. Grades are 2 exams and 2 essays.

150's structure is essay-midterm-essay-final, so not a lot in the gradebook. 

CBR is a really engaging and passionate lecturer. He explains difficult concepts really clearly and although the class is pretty dense with a lot of content, he covers everything in detail. Nice and approachable guy in office hours or after class. Take 150 with him.

I looked forward to his class every day, his lectures were so interesting! He's also co-written some very interesting research papers. Course material is interesting, there's a textbook but you don't have to read it (he covers it all in his lectures), but you're only graded on 2 papers, a midterm, and a final, so make sure to study!
You have 2 writing assignments a midterm and a final. 20% of your grade is attendence. Dont need to read textbook. exams are pretty much just vocab tests. Take his class 100%
Awesome guy, awesome class. Did have to read a lot, but it's not entirely necessary if you show up and pay attention in class
As long as you attend class and follow up with the readings and go to recitation, you should be fine!

not much homework and the exams were easy. you did not need to read the textbook, only understand the slides so GO TO LECTURE if you want the class to be good. your grade is heavily determined by your TA since they grade your essays which are worth a lot!!

Grade is very reliant on your TA... exams aren't too bad, I recommend reading the textbook before class. He is very passionate about the subject and lectures are interesting. There are 2 papers, a midterm, and a non-cumulative final. If you put in the work it's not hard to do well on the exams.

One of my favorite professors, super interesting lectures. If you give your all on the papers, pay attention to every lecture, and you just study a lot of vocab before the exams, you will get an A. You don't even need to read the textbook, and there is very little day-to-day work, yet I learned so much.

Professor Ballard-Rosa's lectures were engrossing. He is passionate about his material, which makes it more interesting to listen to. Attendance is required, but they are big lectures, so attendance isn't taken; it is more about attendance and participation in recitation. The only grades in the class are two 5-page papers, a midterm, and a final.
Timothy is without a doubt, undoubtedly perchance

This course uses the textbook he wrote for the class, on which he gives pop quizzes. He could not explain the topics in a way that any human would understand, and he LOVES using AI-generated images. Half of the class grade was based on assignments, which aren't too hard, but the other half was the GROUP final project and 3 pop quizzes.

Textbook and required readings are written himself, some pop quizzes. He is tough to rate because I think he is funny and a very nice person and an extremely knowledgeable professor who definitely knows what he is talking about, but there is no forgiveness on late assignments or in general, feedback on everything but the final project is limited.
I would consistently not wear my seatbelt on the way to this class hoping that I wouldn't make it. Genuinely a top 3 worst professor I've had at UNC.

I took POLI 100H with TJR and it was honestly the most frustrating class. He told the class that he “doesn't give A's." Others reached out to me because they felt I was being singled out during conversations. I never explicitly shared my political views, but it sometimes felt like certain perspectives were treated less favorably in discussion.

TJR might be the worst professor on the east coast. He grades based on an algorithm that he does not share with students. Only about eight assignments/exams for the whole class and he provides little support and when combined with his extremely harsh grading, this is a hard class to get a good grade. Please, DO NOT take this class. It really sucks.
TJR is truly

Timothy Ryan is the worst professor I have ever had. He provided little feedback and EXTREMELY unfair grades on the few papers and exams we had. His grading is very inconsistent–he took points off my work for things that he did not for other students. He is VERY stuck up. Go ahead TJR, attach your "Course Evaluations" - they just prove my point.

Genuinely my hardest class as a PRE MED. Tougher grader than the chem department. All exams are open note, yet I never made higher than a 62. He will assign 50-70 pages of readings A DAY and will pop quiz you or call on you so watch out. He has no grading criteria or rubric and is just rude about you not understanding content other needing help.
He brings his dog to office hours... and that is enough for me (he's also pretty good at explaining complex topics).

Absolutely amazing lecturer, I learned a lot. As far as graded assignments, you play to an algorithm of what Professor Ryan wants to hear rather than memorizing or analyzing the concepts. Most arbitrary grading I've ever experienced. If he does not agree, -10-15 points. Not focused on learning, focused on his algorithm. Would not take again.

I would honestly not recommend this class. I found this class to be my hardest last semester and it was my only 100-level course. He is a tough grader and never has clear rubrics. Readings are long and time-consuming and if you do not take detailed notes, you will not do good in this course.

This class is amazing so long as you're actively engaged in the subject matter. You must prepare for class and take detailed notes, but that's to be expected in an honors course! His grading can be harsh at times on the amendment proposals, but his exams are lenient enough to make up for it. You should be fine if you read, engage, and study.

ABSOLUTELY DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I came into the class thinking it would be interesting and an easy A. I COULD NOT HAVE BEEN MORE WRONG. Exams and amendment proposals are graded on feelings. Readings are also very long. He seems like a nice guy, however he has a very vague rubric to when he is grading things.

Would not recommend this course! I took it hoping it would be an easy gen ed. It ended up being my hardest course and I'm a STEM major... He is a tough grader and participation is weighted heavily. It was way too difficult for a 100 level course. If you are an honors student I would honestly take the regular version.

I would not recommend this class. It was way too difficult for a 100 level course. I would honestly take the normal version if you are an honors student. The readings are insanely long and attendance is mandatory. His grading is confusing and harsh. Participation is weighted heavily. He seems like a nice guy but this class gave me anxiety.

Honestly, do not take this class as an honors student! He makes up grading rubrics as he goes and grades harshly for a 100-level course. If you need the credit, just take the normal version, which is 100 times easier than this class! Exams are all free-response, and he counts participation but will not call on you when you raise your hand ?!?!

Nice guy, but I found it hard to do well in his class. Two huge papers are amendment proposals, which he grades harshly with no clear rubric. Seemed as if he graded more on feelings than the quality of your writing. He is the type of professor who reserves 100's for students who go above and beyond. Loads of heavy reading and very lecture-heavy!

Knowledgeable on the subject and interesting material. class is not an easy 100 course as it should be. He is a tough, arbitrary grader. No clear rubric, and honestly, most students in the class felt their grades were unjust and unfair, with no good constructive feedback. be prepared to read a lot, and attendance is mandatory.

Dr Ryan might be the most stuck-up and pretentious person I have ever met. He is wholly in love with himself. He grades holistically and makes up grading criteria as he goes along. When you go to office hours, he only answers in riddles. I would rather stick my hand in a cheese grater than ever take another class with Dr Ryan again.

The professor was extremely kind and very knowledgeable. The entire course curriculum is based on his own research and political philosophy, so it's super interesting! All of the course notes were posted online ahead of time, and the reading/supplemental materials were easy to understand.

His material is super interesting and is very smart. The lectures cover all the readings so you normally don't have to do them. Your TA is what makes a difference in this class so make sure to get a good one, Jody was the best TA I have ever had.

Take this class! Professor Marks is an incredibly kind soul who really cares about the subject and about his students. I found the class genuinely helpful and interesting without being overly demanding in terms of content. His lectures are easy to follow, exams are very straightforward with good studying, and theres one essay thats graded nicely.
Great class and really great professor. He explains things very clearly and doesn't try to trick you on exams.

His subjects weren't personally my cup of tea so I kinda never went, but the class was easy enough. Just beware poli212 is focused on european government, not principles of poli sci overall like connect carolina suggests. how the class goes and the grade you get depends heavily on the TA

the kindest and best professor ever, genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about political science. a very very educated and wise professor. class isn't hard either 1 paper 25% final and midterm 25% and recitation participation 25%

Amazing professor and great first year seminar
Work outside of class was generally just to submit a question you want him to answer about the lectures
Final project essay, essay midterm 
Great lectures, he's super engaging and kind.

Dr. Marks is an intelligent and kind man and has so much background in European politics. He teaches half the time in Italy, so it is nice to know that he is here because he cares about teaching his courses which made me want to put more effort into class. Grades were 2 essays, a project, and discussions.

I really enjoyed this class! Some days, we were in person, and some were reading days. weekly discussion question. 1 group project where you work with a partner for a debate. There were three essays in total, 2 of which were take-home final essays, and 1 was about your debate topic. He was such a nice guy! I definitely recommend!

Professor Marks is super knowledgeable and passionate about the content of this course. I definitely enjoyed the class and would recommend it, but I did think it could be a little boring at times, and I wished there was a bit more diversity in the content. Other than that, it was great and Prof. Marks is super interesting!

Professor Marks was a pretty solid teacher. He was really passionate about the material and was willing to talk outside of class. The class itself wasn't very hard. Your grade comes from attendance/participation, a presentation or a debate (your choice), a final paper, and a midterm and final there were both take home. Attendance is mandatory.
Dr. Kroeger was a pleasure to have! She is very knowledgable, understanding, and caring.
Professor Kroeger is the sweetest professor I've had at UNC so far! She is always willing to meet during office hours and is truly enthusiastic about what she teaches!! Can't recommend enough

Prof Kroeger might be one of the kindest professors out there! She's so personable and cares about you in/out of the classroom. Lots of readings but you can skim them. Grade is really just a paper and exams but her grading is not overly harsh. There's occasionally an attendance sheet so if you consistently don't come, it'll prob affect your grade.

Professor Kroeger was very knowledgeable, open to discussion, and respectful to students. There were not a lot of opportunities for grades, and the ones that existed were all writing, so be ready for that. Kroeger was super helpful with feedback and had a quick return period for grades. For a higher level class, this was great!

Mary was a phenomenal professor for POLI 201. She is always available to help outside of class, and she actively wants to see her students succeed. She was one of the most caring professors I've had during my time at UNC!

Professor Kroeger was wonderful! Her lectures were engaging and she clearly wanted to see all her students succeed. She was accessible during office hours and offered frequent additional office hours, especially when we had larger assignments due. The subject matter was interesting and all readings were online, so no paying for a textbook!

Exams and expectations are pretty straight forward. You're gonna have to do a bit of reading for the class, and there's a 15 page paper you gotta do. Other than that, if you pay attention in class and do the readings you'll be fine. It's not the easiest A and she has expectations, but they're pretty reasonable.

Professor Kroeger was a delight to have. She expressed genuine passion and excitement about the material, is a fair and impartial grader, and has such a kind personality. Even if you are a non-major, you will get so much out of this class, as the bureaucracy affects virtually every aspect of life. Highly recommend!!

Mary was super sweet, caring, and understanding!  Her lectures can get a little plain at times, but overall great professor.  Willing to provide help outside of class.  Tests were open note just make sure to answer questions fully.  We had one 15 page research paper due at the end, but she makes sure we keep up by submitting topic and rough draft.

This class does have a lot of readings, but she makes it very easy to understand the readings by giving us questions we discuss in the class. She is probably the nicest professor I have had here, and I am a Junior. Nothing to pay for and not much work that is graded, but it is not hard to do well if you keep up with readings (I did not) :(.

Dr. Brew is a nice guy. This was his first time teaching the course. Lots of readings until the last month of the semester. Quizzes every class on readings. Exams are challenging,g but you can have a cheat sheet. Last month involved coding- so get ready for that.

Hes a Goat. Always made it so fun to show up and as a student who is the type to sit in the back and be on there phone I was front row always paying attention to him. He does expect effort, but with how engaging his teaching is its impossible not to put in effort. Chill grader, genuinely funny guy, and great political takes. Made me want an A

Incredible professor with true passion and inspiration for his students. Gave so much grace when I struggled due to personal reasons and let me take the midterm a week late. Such an incredible professor, take his classes!!!! So funny and attendance isn't graded (but it's important unless u look at the notes) No electronics but so interesting.
He is a great professor that is easily reached outside of class and cares about the success of his students. I highly recommend you take a class of his if possible.

brian was a pretty easy grader. one 10-12 page paper, a midterm, a final, and a couple of assignments that required you to go to office hours for a bit. he was pretty nice but he did go on random rants about primaries where he screamed for like 5 mins. there are lots of readings but you can just skim them enough to write the discussion posts
Brian was a great professor for POLI 208! His passion for the material is evident in his lectures and he genuinely cares about his students!

Brian was a good professor and loved teaching the material. He was funny in lectures, or at least tried to be. There's a ton of reading each week, but you'll be fine if you just skim. There are two papers and a midterm and final that he graded pretty easily. Attendance isn't required, but participation is part of the grade.

Brian is pretty great. He clearly loves political science, and that is shown in his lectures. He isn't a very harsh grader, and if you are interested in political science, you will enjoy his lectures. POLI 208 had two papers, a midterm and a final exam, and none of them were too difficult. It's a good class to learn in and not worry about grades!

Brian's class was AMAZING! Engaging lectures, and he's very funny.  Midterm's not bad if you study, and final was open book.  Major papers (2) are graded very fairly, and he gives great feedback.  Mini short papers (2) were easy 100s if you just did them and followed guidelines.  Also did mini simulation in class and earned EC.  Highly recommend!

Decent class and professor, although it becomes apparent that she favors certain topics more than others (esp. the Senate and court cases), so definitely put your energy more towards those areas when studying. Otherwise pretty standard as a poli prerec, do the readings and you'll be okay.
Great professor! Her class isn't hard todo well in as long as you go to lecture and do readings.

Great professor and lecturer but the amount of reading assigned for the course is insane. The TA's are awesome and helpful, so definitely use them to your advantage. Attending lectures is important because she covers so much content in a single class session.
Lectures were solid and materials were helpful. Exams were difficult and is a very reading heavy class.
Great lecturer, very light-hearted. Great time with interactions with the lecture hall and the extra credit chances were always hype.

Dr. Truel is the best professor I have had so far at UNC! She is a great lecturer, very kind, and really cares about her students. The tests are not too bad as long as you study and pay attention during lecture. The papers are graded somewhat harshly however. I would highly recommend taking her class, even if it is not required.
Professor Truel has great Lectures. Attendance is mandatory. Exams were not hard show up to lectures and do the readings and you will be fine .

Professor Truel was awesome. Her lectures were genuinely captivating and always kept me engaged. There is a fair bit of reading for this class, but it's definitely manageable. My biggest advice is to take notes and actually do the readings, as she tends to pull a bunch of her content from them. 10/10 would take her class again.

Lectures were boring at times, but she explained concepts well. Required textbook readings took awhile and sometimes felt unnecessary, but overall helpful. Grades consist of recitation, attendance/homework, 2 papers, and 3 exams (each aren't weighted very much). Overall, a decent amount of work for just a FC class but very manageable and enjoyable.
I would recommend this class. While I didn't do as well as I had hoped—that was on me—the lectures were very interesting, and she's funny. The TAs are also extremely helpful and very understanding.

The lectures are fast paced and dense, but Sarah makes them engaging and gets the information you need to know across. You need to study for the exams, but the material is straight forward. Would absolutely take again if my major reqs alligned.

Not too bad of a professor. Lectures typically follow with the syllabus' required readings, though there are times when the lecture lags behind the pre-class reading. There are 3 midterm exams and thankfully the final isn't cumulative like other classes. Papers are generally doable, just be detailed as possible. Beware of an ungraded pop quiz!

The class is way harder than it has to be and she made that clear that its on purpose. Her lectures arent related to the slides so if you dont show up, you miss a lot of what she actually goes over. We did well on one test so she made the second test harder with topics we didnt learn so the test average would be lower.

Dr. Truel was a great first experience in the Political Science department here. I personally really enjoyed what we were learning and she made her lectures engaging. Very straightforward class work wise as well.
It was such an interesting course but be aware of the amount of readings/work and the tricky questions on the test.

Professor Truel was one of my favorite professors last semester, and if you are willing to meet her during office hours, she is very accommodating. The course hit me by surprise for a 100-level and had me doing more reading than I ever had for a class (coming from a freshman). Read the textbook and recitation readings and review the lecture slides.

Tbh I thought this class would be easy bc I had taken AP gov in high school, and it really did FEEL easy, yet I ended with a B+. My TA, Audrey, was awesome, and the papers were easy, but the tests were designed to trick you. I couldn't understand how I felt so confident but did so badly on MCQ tests. Honestly way too hard for a 100-level class.

She was a reasonably engaging lecturer, but I could not understand how tricky an intro-level class was. This was my most challenging class the past semester, and I'm saying that as someone with some college experience (I think first-semester freshmen might have been scared out of the major). Just be prepared to work hard.

Sarah is an amazing professor! Her lectures are very enjoyable as she is passionate about the class. The exams are tricky, but manageable if you study content from recitation/textbook because it shows up on exams. There are 2 papers to write, both given out weeks in advance. She is very caring and always willing to help! Great class!!
The course consists of 4 heavily weighted exams; 2 papers typically require a great deal of detail and research (graded strictly). It is too difficult to be an intro-level course.

Prof. Wilson is awesome! Tests and writing assignments were easy, he prepared us well and gave insightful feedback. Felt like I learned and grew in my knowledge and writing abilities in his class. He genuinely wants to help his students succeed and treats everyone with grace and respect. Can't recommend him enough!

Allen is a great professor, genuinely nice person, and I really looked forward to his class. Poli 100 with Allen is a great way to meet the Values & Foundations of Democracy reqs. He clearly loves poli sci and works hard to make the topic engaging. He reads every written assignment himself and gives good feedback.

You can tell Allen cares about the material he is teaching and he was always open for discussion or any questions or concerns we had. He provided us with 3 grace days on every assignment with no late penalty INCLUDING THE FINAL PAPER! which was extremely helpful in times of stress. His exams were fairly easy if you studied the lecture slides.

Allen is great! He tries his best to make the class accessible to everyone. Very lenient grading criteria and grading. He gave us the FRQ prompt (worth 40% of exam grade) in advance, but some people used it to cheat, which he addressed in class, although he made clear that it was a very small minority. Person who rated him 1 was probably a cheater.

Allen is extremely down to Earth and deeply cares about the quality of what his students learn. He strives to make the grading policy as fair as possible, and as long as you pay attention in class, you will do fine. He even gave us the FRQ prompt for Test 2, but some people took advantage of that by cheating. :( This class is easy/fun with Allen!

LOVE Professor Wilson. He makes POLI100 super fun and enjoyable despite the heavy amount of content you have to learn. Such an entertaining teacher who is so so sweet. He is also very flexible about due dates and very understanding. Genuinely considering switching my major to polisci because of him.

Allen was one of my favorite teachers I've ever had ! I can't believe it was his first time teaching a course, he is such a talented teacher who cares about his students and pays great diligence to all the work that's submitted.
Great professor! Take POLI 100 with Allen!

Allen is the best! I had him as a TA for Poli 100 and then again as the professor for Poli 209! He is super engaging, funny, and willing to work with you around due dates or stress. He makes coming to class exciting instead of harrowing, and the work is thoughtful but not too difficult. Take anything you can with him!!
He was such a nice TA ! He gives good feedback and I don't think he's a tough grader. Clearly recommend

I have no idea what the other person is talking about, Allen has been the best TA I've ever had. Prepares you for the exams and helps guide you through the papers. Instantly responds to emails and gives great feedback. Recitation so good you'll be tempted to just skip the lectures.

DO NOT TAKE AS YOUR TA!! He will give you low grades on papers without much reasoning and then say to meet with him but cancel all office hours and not be able to find a time to meet. He also grades participation VERY harshly. I showed up to EVERY class, sat in the front, asked and answered questions. Also he doesn't appreciate joking or laughter.

Lectures were boring but not super important to pay attention to. Gave us time to complete our discussion boards in class. No final exam, just a big group project but he gives plenty of time to work on it.

Def recommend this class for anyone who needs poli credit. The R assignments were a bit tedious and lengthy at times, but def doable. Attendance was mandatory, so do make sure you go to each class. Besides that, the class itself was enjoyable, low-maintenance, and grading wasn't harsh. Group project was actually fun, just make sure you check in.

professor Steelman was easy to understand, his classes were a mix of lecture, practice in R, and group work. None of the assignments were too difficult or time consuming. The biggest grade in the class comes from a big group project that you work on during the second half of the semester.

Professor Steelman is a very laid back professor that makes getting an A very attainable and easy. 50% of the grade is a semester-long group polling project and 40% is attendance, so just show up to class and put in work and you'll get an A. I learned a lot about polling and as a political science major this was a very useful class. Great class!

This was the easiest class I've taken at UNC which also made it boring. Tyler grades very leniently which is nice and there's no final but most of your grade is from a group project where it was kind of a hassle to get everyone's work finished on time. Take it if you need a random credit for a major/minor/FC.

Don't take this class if you've never used R studio before. It was a nightmare for me to learn on the go in this class and caused me excess stress because it was never covered in class. Tyler is good to his students with deadlines/expectations but this class should only be offered to people with experience with R coding. I had to get outside help.

I think about this class all the time and I'm actually devastated he retired because I wanted to take another class with him. This class genuinely had me considering changing to be a poli sci major. That being said there was a lot of reading.... it's all pretty interesting though

Dr. Hartlyn is extremely knowledgable about his topics, and has a WEALTH of information to share. As long as you do the readings you'll do fine in the class. The readings aren't too extensive as long as you enjoy learning about Latin American politics/history, get ready to read! Overall caring professor who wants his students to succeed.

This class is actually very difficult for a first year seminar and there is a LOT of reading. However, Dr. Hartlyn is a really great guy and is clearly an expert in his field. He is a very interesting professor to take a first year seminar with, but I would only take the class if you like to read and are interested in Latin American politics.

Professor Hartlyn is very knowledgeable of the subject material and very kind. He is not the most engaging lecturer in terms of being entertaining, but if you listen actively and respond to questions you can gain a lot from the course.

Fantastic professor. Taking him in my first semester freshman year, and he has been fantastic, introducing me to college life. Lots of reading and lecture-heavy, so probably not the professor for non-history lovers

This is definitely a reading and discussion-heavy class that isn't for everyone, but if you are particularly interested in Latin American politics, it is a must-take class. Professor Hartlyn has a ridiculous amount of personal experience and knowledge about the region, and I found the content very interesting.

Really great professor, although lectures get boring sometimes, he facilitates really good discussions about the topic. Two readings per week that require deep comprehension. Very konwledgeable about the area and great professor to build connections with as a first year.

Professor Hartlyn is clearly interested in the content of this course, sometimes the lectures can get a little dense though. The grading criteria is kind of confusing so you don't actually know what your grade is until the last few days of class. If you do the readings and listen in class you should be okay though.

He is a very tough teacher but you will grow as a student! Come to class at least semi-prepared and participate a couple of times. He's very lecture-intense and it can be boring, but just stick with it. If poli sci/ social sciences really aren't your thing, pick a diff seminar!

This class was very hard to understand conceptually, and there was a LOT of reading and class discussion involved. Professor is very nice and clear he cares we did well in the class. However, a lot of class lectures are difficult to understand.

This was the most difficult class I took this semester. There are two readings assigned each week that are wordy and long. Hartlyn's lectures can also get boring. If you don't give him the right answer he can be very condescending. Assigned multiple essays and provided long yet unclear instructions. Find another first-year seminar.

Lots of reading outside of class, must be done to contribute to group and class discussions. Very long monotone lectures, minimal leniency with the course schedule, 30-minute commentaries, and rabbit holes about Latin America. Will not take another class with him or about the topic as a whole. There are plenty of other FYS to take.

Personal experience throughout Latin American countries' elections and political movements, scholar of the region, extremely concise and articulate. Interesting content and history, various viewpoints of analysis on political situations, opportunities to form analysis of our own on complex topics through project, term paper, classroom discussions.

Very difficult class for a first-year seminar. He teaches this class as if it were a 300 or higher level course. Many pages of reading are due every class period, and you must have a full understanding of the readings to contribute to the in-class discussions. Also, every lecture is very long and consists of him speaking for almost the whole period

Dr. Hartlyn puts a lot of effort into his reading guides and really makes it clear what you need to know for exams and whatnot. He offers an engaging class and really is knowledgeable. Also has an amazing curve on grades.

Prof. Hartlyn is a top dog when it comes to Latin American Political Science. This class is personalized for first-years, making it accessible and educational. Sometimes the lectures seem a little dense, but if you take this class, you will emerge with a good understanding of history, politics, and culture in Latin America.

This was a great class, and I learned a lot from it. She is an excellent professor who genuinely cares about her students' success. While there is a fair amount of in classroom tests, it's completely manageable with good planning. There are plenty of extra credit opportunities, and although attendance is encouraged, it's not mandatory.

Professor Bassi is a straightforward professor who keeps her course easy to follow. Assignments and tests are reasonable and not unnecessarily difficult, and the class doesn't feel mentally overwhelming. It's a great option for upperclassmen looking for a manageable workload, with no annoyingly hard projects and a flexible attendance policy.

Your grade is based upon only a few assignments, so you have to lock in for every single one. Lectures were often boring but the slides were full of information and easy to review if you needed to go back later.

Lectures are very important and its easy to get behind in this class if you dont attend. There is a textbook but the readings are not necessary. Material isn't too difficult if you pay attention. Extra credit and bonus questions will boost your grade. Bassi is very intelligent and answers questions clearly.

This class was very interesting, however I took it at 8am and each class felt like it was 4 years long. There were 3 assignments, worth 5% each, 2 tests worth 25% each and the final is worth 35% of you grade. There were also "pop quizzes" but they were ungraded. She was accessible out of class and responded to emails quickly. Would not take again

Professor Bassi's 288 is the start of Game Theory, and I really enjoyed the class. She teaches it in an intutive way, but you may need to do work outside of class. She answers a lot of questions, and is always willing to help out. Class consists of 2 midterms, a final, and 3 HW assigments. She is a good professor worth taking.

This class doesn't have to be hard but it will be if you don't continuously keep up with the new material. Attendance isn't mandatory but GO TO CLASS. If you don't it will be super hard. I was constantly in office hours and it was super helpful. She/ulas are very available.
Professor Bassi is amazing at explaining the concepts presented in a way that seems simple and easy. Her explanations made me feel more confident in my abilities to handle the information.

I really enjoyed this class! The first poli class that I've ended with an A. Lectures aren't mandatory but enjoyable and helpful. But you def don't need to read the textbooks at all. not much HW, clear grading, and def requires some studying, but the content was interesting. Contrary to the other reviews, I acc thought lectures got slow sometimes..

I thought Professor Bassi was a great professor overall and have few complaints. My main issue with the professor is that I sometimes felt she moved quickly through important class concepts that we would be tested on.

Professor Bassi is super smart and did a really great job of providing all the resources and practice material we needed. I wouldn't say this course is easy, but there is plenty of opportunity for extra credit and I ended the class with over 100%. I never did any of the readings, but you should definitely go to class if you want to be prepared.

Poli 288 was a great course and Professor Bassi was a star. She gives a lot of resources to prepare for the exams, which are challenging but doable with a bit of study. I just got the final exam score and it is 108/100!!!! She gives bonus questions in the tests!. It's failry easy to get an A if you just do every bonus/extra credit assignments.

I learned a lot of exciting things, and Dr Bassi taught the logic behind games/models very well so that I felt I understood concepts in–depth. Because Dr. Bassi placed much emphasis on knowing the intuition behind strategy ideas, I was able to complete more complicated problems than the class examples because I know how it works.

I really really appreciate Professor Bassi's availability to student needs. Whenever I had questions, she would always answer my emails in a very nice and respectful manner with tons of information. During class, whenever I asked a question, she made sure to go over it

I expect an A. Many extra credit opportunities that will bump mine grade up even if I did worse on the final, that was challenging but doable.
I loved Professor Bassi. She has no limitations as an instructor. Only recommendation would be slowing down the lecture. Sometimes it was too fast passed to understand.

Poli 288 is a fun class. I just had the final yesterday. It was tough but nothing unexpected. I expect an A given the many extra credit opportunities that she gave us during the semester.

Dr Bassi is so knowledgeable about the subject that it can be overwhelming for students. I think that is because she is just so familiar with the material.

I really enjoyed Anna as a lecturer. The course, focused on strategy and politics, didn't initially grab my interest, but her engaging teaching style won me over. She has an accent, but her use of PowerPoint makes her points very clear. The tests were very easy, while the assignments were more challenging, though they carried less weight.

Great teacher with lots of passion for her field. She's a little hard to access outside of class but the TA's are very easy to get into contact with. Her lectures are available on canvas. The exams are hard but nothing impossible especially if you attend class.

Bassi is an amazing prof who is super knowledgeable and passionate about game theory. That being said, her class was a lot of work. I think getting a good grade is attainable for anyone who puts in the work. Her lectures are effective.
Professor Bassi's lectures are entertaining and her TAs grade everything pretty fairly..

Professor Globetti is my favorite teacher here. She has fun, engaging lectures that relate to current events. There are a lot of readings, but no textbook so it's free! Not too Stata heavy, and there is one group project but it splits off into individual work for the end of the semester. I would 100% recommend Professor Globetti, she is amazing!

Prof. Globetti is absolutely the best professor! She is so kind, caring, and funny! The class material is interesting and not too hard. I got an A- cause I tried less than I should've on different homeworks and exam prep, but if you put in effort it's not hard to do well in. Take this class with Globetti!

5.0 rating for a reason -- Fully deserved. Professor Globetti is an amazing lecturer and she is super funny.  She gives good feedback on the homework and group work. She genuinely cares about her students-- learns everyone's names and sends weekly newsletters to the class. She is a kind, caring, and genuine professor. Also, exams are all online btw

Best professor in the Political Science department. Her lectures are funny and engaging. She is easy to reach outside of class and is easy to talk to.  No textbooks required as she provides all the readings on Canvas. The class work is easy to manage. Attendance is mandatory, but even if it wasn't, I wouldn't want to skip.  10/10 recommend.

Such a sweet professor. Truly wants her students to succeed. Course content is interesting and she makes it relevant to current events, does not just re-use lecture slides. Take this class if you are a poli major.

Professor Globetti is by far my favorite at UNC. This is now my second semester in her class, and I am sad that I cannot take more. She is the sweetest, and I go to her office hours just to talk. Take any of her classes!
I made an RMP account just to give Prof. Globetti a 5/5.

Professor Globetti teaches a very fun and engaging class regardless of how interested you are in the subject material. Some of the essays were graded a little tougher than expected but there were a few extra credit opportunities. Definitely recommend for any first year student even if you're a non-major

Prof Globetti is probably my favorite professor I've had so far at UNC. She's engaging and explains the content clearly and is just generally a super likable person. There's one paper and three exams that are open note and she pretty much tells you what will be on them. Readings before each class but they're short and you can skim them.

Prof. Globetti is the best professor I've taken at UNC! She learned the names of the entire class in the first week and has very engaging lectures. She clearly cares deeply about her students and is very accommodating. I felt like I learned a lot in the class, but the workload was incredibly manageable. Take this class!

Professor Globetti is the best! One of my favorite professors I've had at UNC so definitely take a class with her if you can! Grades are made up of one paper, 3 online take-home exams, and participation - as long as you go to class and pay attention you will do well.

Professor Globetti was always a joy during class and learned all our names within a week. It's clear how much she cares about her students. She's always available for questions and gives great feedback. She made otherwise boring and grueling information entertaining and interesting with interaction and creativity in her lectures.

I have taken many classes with Professor Globetti and she is awesome. She always makes lectures interesting and cares so much about her students. Prof. Globetti is also understanding, so if you can make certain deadlines, she always gives 2 extra days to complete her assignments beyond the deadline.

I had Dr. Globetti for my honors thesis course. She structured the class very well and gives step by step instructions on how to write an honors thesis and conduct statistical analysis. Dr. Globetti is gives amazing feedback and is super knowledgeable on how to conduct research.

Professor Globetti is kind, funny, and truly wants her students to do well. She went out of her way help whenever students had questions, especially when learning Stata and data analysis techniques. The class design (mixture of lecture, group projects, Stata, 2024 election discussions, and statistics) made 209 my favorite class of the semester.
Everything you heard is true. She is great. If you are a data science minor take this class, it'll take the edge off.

I absolutely love Globetti. I was pretty nervous to take this class because of the Stata element, but it ended up being my favorite class. Globetti is almost always accessible outside of class and gives the best feedback of any professor I've had. She has definitely been my favorite prof at UNC

Prof Globetti is a great person and teacher. She really cares about her students and works incredible hard to make sure we all understand and get the information we need. The material is tricky, especially if your not computer savvy, but she will work with you and is great.

A super caring professor. She will memorize every detail you wrote in the introduction. Professor Globetti gives amazing lectures, which are never boring. You will learn a lot from her lectures. If you don't miss the class before a holiday or a break, she will tell you the answer to the bonus question on your exams. So, don't miss her lectures!

Professor Globetti is incredibly kind, and very willing to be helpful to her students. She made the most of content that was not always that exciting, and went through the material logically and efficiently.

This professor was really great, absolutely loved his lectures, never fell asleep like he is super engaging.  However he grades way harsher than other reviews led on so really be warned. He also did not curve. I would take him again and probably will but I studied a lot and still did poorly so I would put all my effort into one of his classes.

Dr. Hetherington is the most enthusiastic and caring professor I've ever had at UNC. He is such a funny and laid-back professor and makes going to class enjoyable. His slideshows are vague, so you do have to pay attention to his lectures and attend class. Hetherington is a treasure to the UNC political science department and I recommend!
Great dude and really awesome class!

Prof. Hetherington is a good professor. He curves super well, although this class was a little bit harder than the reviews said. He tests on lecture content, so definitely go to his or the TA's office hours to get a better understanding of it. My con is that he does not post lecture slides until 2-3 days before exams, which makes it hard to study.

Great gen-ed. Two four-page papers but that's about it. He's a great lecturer but you can skip occasionally and still do well. Go to recitation and take notes on the Smith and you'll get an A, especially if you've taken high school government.

Great professor who clearly cares a lot about the subject matter. But this class is not easy by any means. You will have to do the readings and think critically. This class wasn't an easy A, but I appreciate that it made us think critically about such an important topic. Probably wouldn't recommend taking this for freshmen- wait till 2nd/3rd year.

Very easy if you took a government class in high school. 2 Short paper which my TA graded easy, three tests all semester which if you have an idea previously about the American government, class is very easy.
Class is more difficult than I imagined (particularly tests, but he curves) but he's a really nice guy and really funny.

Professor Hetherington was an amazing instructor. He made lectures very engaging and seemed to really care for his students. Tests were not too difficult but you definitely need to attend class and do some reading outside.
Dr. Hetherington is so awesome and funny. He wants his students to do well and his classes are interesting and fun. As long as you attend class and turn in assignments on time you will do well.
Class is harder than expected. The reviews are mostly untrue. This is a difficult course with very little to grade from. I would not recommend it. The professor is not helpful.

Hetherington is a great professor who is passionate about the course material. He doesn't use slides all the time, so you have to listen to what he says, but he makes the lectures entertaining so it isn't hard to pay attention. 3 tests worth 60% and two papers worth 25%, and the rest is recitation attendance. Great professor, okay class
I too was fooled by the reviews. This class is much harder than it should be. Grading is unclear and subjective. The teaching team was not very helpful.

Mr. Hetherington is genuinely the best teacher I've had in my whole schooling career. He's funny, empathetic, and engaging, and always begins class with a funny story to lighten the mood. You will love his class. Amazing person in general, and very knowledgable and widely respected as a political scientist.

Hetherington is the GOAT. Super funny, and does his best to keep the class attentive and entertained. You're only graded by a few things, but he's generally a generous grader at the end (he doesn't have a traditional grading scale). I've taken multiple classes with him, and they've all been great. Take him 100% if you can.
super wholesome professor and is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches. he assigns a lot of reading but you don't have to read it if you pay attention to his lectures.
Hetherington is a really good lecturer. He tries his hardest to keep class entertaining and the Exams and Papers are really easy if you pay attention in class and do the main textbook readings.

Marc was one of my favorite professors thus far. His lectures were interesting and he structured the class where everyone could easily succeed as long as you put in a bit of effort. There were only 3 tests and 2 papers. Super doable! Marc was super caring and clearly passionate about what he teaches.

Professor Hetherington's lectures were always funny, informative, and each class doesn't cover too much content. You're fine as long as you take notes, as he doesn't post lecture notes or powerpoints at all. Tests were a bit harder than expected, but they're curved. Not too difficult a class, but still harder than 100 level classes usually are.

Professor Hetherington is an excellent professor. His lectures are engaging and informative, and made POLI 100 a fun class to go to. He is very funny and his lectures are helpful, take notes. 2 papers, 3 exams are most your grade + recitation, show up, listen, take notes and you'll enjoy this class and get a good grade.

Professor Lemke is an extraordinarily warm individual who is an expert in her field. My only note is she definitely does have a worldview that, while by no means is out of the mainstream, she sticks to religiously, which does hinder her ability to present all material in class even-handedly.
Professor Lemke is super cool and very knowledgeable in her field. She makes euro gov very accessible to students. Would highly recommend this class.

Prof. Lemke is absolutely wonderful! She's extremely knowledgeable about the subject, and her lectures were always very interesting. She is also extremely kind and approachable! There was one midterm, all multiple choice, and a short individual presentation on a current event. The final is online and is a single short essay. Highly recommend!

Dr. Lemke is such a knowledgable professor with incredible experience in the world of European politics. Her midterm, final, and 2 papers were very straightforward. Her lectures are easy to grasp and she really knows her stuff. If you are interested and know anything about European politics please take this class. Great class overall.
Great professor. Her exams were easy if you attended class but the papers can be difficult. There is a presentation you do by yourself that counts towards your grade. Really recommend taking her.

I really enjoyed Professor Lemke. I thought she was adorable and very caring towards her students. One time on the midterm, I had a question on a certain term and she helped me out. Our final was asynchronous and was a written paper. I don't think that she was a very tough grader on the papers. I definitely recommend her because she was so sweet!

Very knowledgeable about her topic. However, she only gives letter grades, not numbered grades, and her feedback is not particularly helpful. Also, she made getting an A a 94, which is annoying. Her lectures are... decent, I would recommend reading the 50 pages of textbook a week in order to actually understand the topics being covered.

Prof. Lemke is an incredibly sweet, knowledgeable, and caring individual. She is a lenient grader who is always available for office hours when you need her. She is very kind and smart, and has led an impressive career (look her up!). I highly recommend her class for a fun, low stress learning experience.

She is very knowledgeable. The content is interesting, but the grading was not clear. There is a general guideline of what to follow, but a grade is assigned with little feedback and there are no real rubrics. She is a bit intimidating as well, very direct. 2 exams, 2 papers, and one class presentation make up your grade. Very overwhelming.

I think the course material wasn't exactly my "thing" per se so I had trouble paying attention- it's also so much information skimmed over and difficult to keep track of it all. It was not exactly the most interesting course. Dr. Lemke, however, is brilliant, fair, kind, extremely knowledgeable, and hilarious.

She was very understanding and gave a lot of feedback. she was flexible if need be and I learned a lot. Also very knowledgeable of the subject matter and would add in funny personal anecdotes. 10/10 would take again, but she is from Germany and only teaches 1 undergrad class when she's at UNC.

This was by far one of the best courses I have taken at UNC.Dr. Wiedekind is so knowledgeable and passionate about the subjects he teaches and truly wants his students to learn and think about these matters. He is very attentive to his students and is always willing to help in every way he can to ensure that they will succeed.

Prof. Wiedekind is the BEST! You cannot go wrong taking his classes, he will go above and beyond to help you learn the material and provides very detailed feedback that is implementable. If you get the opportunity to take a class with him, you should do it, you will not regret it!

UNC is really lucky to have Professor Wiedekind. He is very enthusiastic about EU policy and the transatlantic relationship, and he is excellent at eliciting that same enthusiasm from his students. He will also care about your interests beyond the scope of his class, offering advice whenever he can. Do yourself a favor and take one of his classes.

Professor Wiedekind is the best. He is super passionate about his research and designs his seminars to be very engaging. He cares about his students and wants you to excel. If you are interested in learning more about the EU on an interdisciplinary level, I definitely recommend taking this course.

Loved this class! Professor Wiedekind is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about his subject matter. His lectures are easy to follow, his readings are relevant, and the grading criteria is clear. Both papers let you write about your interests in the class, and Dr. Wiedekind gives you in-class opportunities for feedback before it's due.

The grading scale is difficult, but it's not impossible to get an A. There are 8 quizzes; two are dropped. You essentially need near-perfect scores on the remaining six, but she tells you what the questions will be in advance. The best advice for this class is to go to office hours for your papers to talk about them well in advance of the deadline.

Approaches philosophical materials in a strange way, mixing high school-level Engl, Philosophy, Polisci, and Classics but lacks depth in any. Extremely tough grader, focusing on trivial details. Avoid 270 if you dislike being disciplined - only by rewriting papers to her exact suggestions will you earn a decent grade. Tokens make little sense.

She's awesome, the only thing that sucks is her grading scale. It's almost impossible to get an A. She is so caring, engaging, etc. I thought I was going to hate everything about this class and I didn't, I actually kind of loved it. Seriously my ONLY issue is the grading scale, you have to get a perfect grade on almost everything to get an A.

She reduces grades when your interpretation is different than hers, even if you provide textual evidence. The class itself is insightful, though I don't think it reaches a philosophical level. The class material is philosophical but how we approach them is not. Grading is too tough and reading&writing is too much for a 200-level class.

Such a sweet and caring professor. Lots of writing in this class, and more centered on philosophy rather than politics, but was great overall. Assignments were well spaced out with lots of notice in advance. Some tough prompts for assignments but her feedback and office hours were helpful.

Professor Bickford is kind and knowledgable but her class is TOUGH. She's a very harsh grader and expects expert knowledge from her students. The amount of work that you have to do is not comparable to the grade you will get - it is next to impossible to get an A. If your GPA is important to you, take another political philosophy class for credit.

Professor Bickford is an amazing educator and you will realize that if you engage and put in the effort like she asks you to. She is a tough grader but there are opportunities to improve your grade via "tokens." She stresses attendance and you won't do well if you are absent and don't do the readings. Readings are manageable and worth your time.

Ugh, love her! Very respectful towards students. The class is mostly a philosophy seminar (see: participation!) with lots of assigned readings & quite a bit of writing assignments. That being said, she is very flexible & considerate. The final was a self designed project so we got to be a bit creative and dive in deeper to what we wanted to learn.

**EXSS 288 Ignore the reviews, this guy is great. Makes a so-so class very interesting and actually cares about his students/what's going on in their lives. Could not have been nicer. As long as you put in the work you'll be fine!

Don't know why his rating is so low on here. He is a super chill guy that tries to make the material (boring and a lot of it) bearable. I took 155 in the summer which made the class all about taking a lot of information in super fast but Justin made it a lot easier than what it had to be and made a good grade accessible.

Perhaps its a difference in classes, but I enjoyed his EXSS155 courses a lot—AND THIS WAS IN THE SUMMER! 

Despite us going at break-neck speeds, I was able to actually learn and do well in the class. He gave extra credit, explained everything well, answered emails quickly, AND he really seems to enjoy the subject taught! That's a 5 star for me.
I'm honestly convinced that Justin paid others to give him a good review. The only word I can use to describe him is terrible. He is the absolute WORST professor at UNC. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!!!

This is a hard class, but Justin does want you to succeed. He was really accessible to meet outside of class for extra help. He always tried to give real world examples when possible, and walks around when doing in class problems so people can ask questions. He also did a good job using the homework to prepare the class for the exams!

I don't get the bad reviews, Justin was great. I almost dropped the class early on, but after going to his office hours, I ended with an A. He's kind, helpful, and very accessible. I had a great experience and have zero complaints. The class is hard, but he WILL help you if you reach out. If I can do it, anyone can.

Justin truly is a good professor. The content in this class is hard no matter who your professor is and Justin has tried his hardest to talk about each topic in a way all his students will understand. Go to class, ask questions, and review your exams!! He is so helpful outside of class, don't be afraid to reach out to him if you do take him.

This class has hard content, Justin was helpful with questions & willing to meet for office hours. Posted practice problems when we asked & gave extra credit, points back, graded on a curve when needed. Don't know why he has such bad reviews in the past, he's a very nice guy. Helps to attend class even though attendance isn't mandatory.

Just finished my last semester exam in this class and know that I am going to fail. Justin has to be the worst professor I have ever encountered (been at 3 different universities.) Just don't take him, for you and your GPA's sake find any other offering of the course EXCEPT his.
This professor is by far the worst professor I have ever endured at this institution. Never take with this man, he has little to no empathy.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM!

He is the WORST professor I have ever had in my academic endeavors. He is a PhD student and doesn't know how to teach nor does he seem to care to put in the effort to attempt to do better. He wants you to fail. The slides are unhelpful and so is his attempt at teaching. Material is so difficult if you don't already know how to do physics.

He is an unqualified PhD student that has never taught in his life. Would not teach and provided no resources beyond lectures and homework. He is unapproachable, antagonistic and genuinely wants you to fail. Got a ratemyprofessor account simply to rate him because of how horrible he was.Take class with a REAL professor. DO NOT TAKE THIS WITH HIM.

I'll just say that the class is hard and the material is difficult. It's physics based mixed with EXSS concepts. Justin is super willing and helpful during office hours. I probably would take it again with him just because of the extra help he gives outside of the classroom. But he is a hard grader and doesn't give out enough practice problems.

He doesn't care about your success. he often refused to do any extra help. the class was made incredibly hard by how harshly he graded and poorly he taught. he talks in circles + doesn't explain. the only resources were him or his slides; neither of which made any sense. if your work wasn't exactly what he wanted you lost almost all of your points

Dr. Ondrak is a kind and fair professor, however the course weighs exams too heavily, which is unreasonable for students who aren't test takers and haven't taken an anatomy course. She gave great study tips however, sometimes they weren't enough. It really just comes down to memorization and I wish more physiology was incorporated.

Ondrak is the best! 256 is mainly physiology, but not necessarily harder or easier than 155, just depends on personal strengths. Class is half asynchronous and her and the TAs are great at answering questions. Exams have 2-4 short answer questions, but clear outline of what should be included. Makes learning anatomy easy and breaks up content well.
Very reasonable expectations, class is taught very well with one day online one day in person. Very test heavy but the tests are all multiple choice and it is strictly memorization.

Class is half async/online, half in person. Learning the content is entirely on you. It is hard to hold yourself accountable, but your grade will reflect the work you put into it. She clearly outlines exam content and the exams are fair. She's really nice and an engaging lecturer. You don't need to buy Visible Body, but it was very helpful.

This class is half async/online, half in person. This helps because learning the content is entirely on you to put in the work outside of class to memorize everything. She clearly outlines everything you need to know, and the exams are fair. She is also very nice and makes class engaging. Also, you don't necessarily need to buy Visible Body.
So sweet, such a good lecturer, and really wants her students to learn the content.

Ondrak was a good instructor considering the class size. Her exams are pretty straightforward, and do not try to trick you in any way. The class is extremely dense and there is so much to memorize. It was a difficult class, but she tried her best to make the class as supportive as possible. I would recommend Ondrak.

Exams were strictly memorization based but there is just A LOT of material in each exam. She is super helpful and wants you to talk to her if you need help, never be scared to reach out. There are small homework assignments and quizzes that are weekly/biweekly, if you do all of those it is a great grade boost.

She gives access to all the course content through digestible slides—it's on you to put in the time to memorize details on all of the body's muscles, bones, ligaments, nerves, etc. Don't learn content for the first time on the night before a test.

This class is definitely challenging due to the heavy memorization and test-heavy structure. The format is also different from typical UNC classes—it's mostly online, so if that's not your learning style, it may not be the best fit. That said, Professor Ondrak is kind and offers plenty of study tools to help you prepare for the exams.

truly such a wonderful teacher, the class is hard because of the level of memorization but she is an amazing teacher and makes it doable with mnemonics and acronyms. She is VERY realistic with how much she expects you to remember and her tests are well made. A little test heavy with 75% of the class being between the 3 total tests (including final)

Ondrak is great - this class is very standardized, so it's more about the content than the professor. However, Ondrak makes grading criteria very clear. This class is 100% memorization, and there is a LOT to memorize, but it is not too bad if you try. 2 midterms and a 30% cumulative final.

Ondrak is nice and not a bad professor, but I'm leaving the bad review because there's no reason that this class should only meet one day a week and have the other day be asynchronous. Do not take this class if you need structure to hold yourself accountable for work and studying. Class was already only one day and still canceled numerous times.

Professor Ondrak's anatomy class is challenging but engaging. Use Unstuck ai, Quizlet, and VisibleBody to supplement your studies - it really helps cement the content. Stay on top of the material and you'll do well.

Professor Ondrak was AMAZING and I genuinely enjoyed her lectures.This is a very difficult class with a LOT of information, but she has her own ways to help you understand and remember the information. My advice for this course is to STUDY because the grading is very exam-heav, but Ondrak is there to help!

Ondrak was a great professor for a hard class. The class is primarily organization and the only way to do well in the class is if you genuinely put effort into studying. It is hard to pass the class if you do not do the things she tells you to do in her lectures and on canvas. She gives great study tools for you to do outside of class.

Such a sweet professor who wants to help you succeed. Provided many ways to help memorize the material. The information was presented in PowerPoints that I found to be a little scattered. She makes the class asynchronous one of the days which made it more challenging. I put this class on the back burner too much, definitely study along the way!

Dr. Ondrak is a wonderful professor who truly cares about her students! She clearly wants to make content as engaging as possible for better retention and understanding and was very kind, including extra credit questions on exams and for completing the course survey for the final. There is a lot of information, so stay on top of coursework.

She is honestly a great lecturer and does a great job explaining the material, its just A LOT of material. The final was also a bit harder than expected because the questions she asked was not what I was expecting or what I felt she was emphasizing in class. But it is mostly memorization.

Ondrak is a very nice person and a great professor who really knows what shes teaching. The class is pretty much all lectures but because its hybrid its helpful to learn the lecture in person. The class is graded pretty much only on 2 exams and the final exam. Its a lot of memorization really but the exams aren't that bad. Definitely take Ondrak

Easiest class I've taken at Carolina. He is very kind and made a point to learn almost everyone's names, which was impressive given it was an 80 person class. There aren't too many assignments and they weren't super hard. Attendance is technically mandatory, but there weren't that many in class assignments second half of the semester.

TP is the man! 221 is a very simple class if u do the assigned readings and pay attention in class. The part I liked most was TP's accessibility outside of class and willingness to help us in our career path. He brought in several guest speakers during the year, each from a different sector of sport, who were very interesting. Take this class!

Genuinely the most impactful professor I've had here. This class inspired me to change my major. He supported me in finding opportunities within the field and was flexible when I was dealing with personal things. I can't recommend him enough. Cares so much about his students.

Professor Patterson is a great professor but I did not like this class. Attendance is optional but he likes those who show up to class. There are two group projects (but watch out because being in groups with athletes is brutal). Class was okay overall, easy A but boring

Tony is the goat! He is so fun, a great professor, and really knowledgeable about the subject he teaches! He wants all students to succeed and is so caring. The class environment is super chill and he makes it enjoyable to go to. I would take him over and over again if I could! The work is super easy as well, guaranteed A!
Great guy, even better class. Super easy material has a midterm and final, but both are online. Take this class, even if you don't have interest in sports field.

Great and engaging professor, but meh class (very boring material at times). All classes he teaches are graded by a total of 100 points, so just make sure to be on top of assignments. Exams are online and are pretty easy. Be careful about letting the little points missed add up and tank your grade, as it happened to multiple students.

Dr. Patterson is wonderful and gave me a lot of opportunities within the Sport Admin realm. I have test anxiety so I struggled on the midterm (which is to account for my A-), but if that's not a huge issue for you, the tests aren't hard, you just HAVE to read the textbook.

Very very easy class I took over the summer. Do the work and read the assigned chapters, you're guaranteed an A. I highly recommend anyone who needs it for a gen ed or just as an elective to boost gpa. Would take any class this man teaches if I need for credit or have room for extra classes to boost my gpa. A great class

Dr. Patterson is a very kind and understanding man. With my tough schedule this semester, this class was a breath of fresh air every day. This class was not hard at all and if you do your work you are pretty much guaranteed a good grade.  Dr. Patterson is very easygoing and you can tell he cares about his students.

Professor Patterson is an awesome hilarious guy who cares about all his students. He is super lenient on due dates and assignment criteria. He loves what he does and makes that clear. I 100% recommend taking his class.
Dr.Patterson is engaging and is positive when teaching. You learn a lot, while grading is so easy. All exams are online, individual and group activities, guest lectures, and more. Highly reccommend!
TP is the best, super cool guy. Easy and interesting class. Online midterms and a final paper and group project are most of grade. Take this class with him for sure

I enjoyed Dr. Pattersons class. He's very personable and willing to help wherever he can. Only negative I would say is that he's very lenient with group projects, and often times some put in more work than others. Overall easy A for a class

Awesome professor. He was very caring and clear in terms of grading, including extra credit opportunities, and the class overall didn't require me to spend too much time on it outside of class. He genuinely wants his students to succeed—one of the best professors I have had at UNC.
Take the class do the work and you'll pass.
My favorite teacher, take him if you can. Trust.

Professor Patterson is the absolute best. He is so kind and caring, but is still passionate about sports admin. He definitely reaffirmed my decision to be a sports admin major. If you get the chance to take his class, you should!

Dr. Patterson is amazing! He cares for his students and makes his lectures engaging and interactive. I probably opened the textbook 3 times max but you do need to read it to do well on the final. There is a group project at the end and a couple of homework assignments, but he gives enough time to complete everything without getting stressed.

Dr. Patterson is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He is there for his students and structures his class accordingly. As long as you take lecture notes and read the textbook, you will do great in his class.

Group project that is a good portion of your grade; she grades a little tough and gets a little tough if athletes won't help out. Cheat sheet on mid-term and final, attendance was required on some days, but overall not a bad class.

Professor Pratt is great! Lectures can be kinda boring and the two group projects being with athletes is unbearable sometimes. Midterm and Final are multiple choice with a cheat sheet. She lets you know which days are mandatory which is great but show up and she will love you.

This class is mainly centered around a group project with different assignments throughout the semester. The groups are random so be ready to make up for your groups lack or work. She is a pretty tough grader. 1 midterm and 1 final, both are allowed a 1 page cheat sheet which really helps (its straight from textbook). Most classes are optional!
Dr Pratt is an incredible professor, her lectures are always so insightful and if you follow the rubrics it is very easy to do well in this class.

Pratt is extremely kind in person, but is also an extremely stingy, tough grader. The course is group project heavy (all randomly assigned groups), so be prepared to put in overtime to make up for others' lack of work. Exams are straight from the book and can be challenging, but not impossible, as she allows a note page while you take it.

Dr. Pratt is an excellent support system to get you through this class. She is very compassionate, and genuinely wants her students to succeed. EXSS 493 is hard no matter which way you cut it (reaching the required hours is the hard part) but she gives very good feedback and is generally very understanding about any issues you might come across.
This class was very easy to do well in if you put in the work. Dr. Pratt was very engaging and helpful. Overall class was wonderful

Would not recommend, only take her if it's a last resort. Takes off way too many unnecessary points, grades way too hard, it's like she grades papers how she wants to see them, and doesn't understand that she can't grade by her biases. Like papers are subjective, keep your opinions to yourself??

I love Dr. Pratt! She is super kind and always wants to go out of her way to help students. There are many small assignments to balance your grade and there are many days that aren't mandatory. A great class if you work hard!

Same teaching style as 322, tests were difficult, lots of random information I don't remember reading. She's nice and def recommend going to office hours, but just beware of tests and group projects. Took last min to grade them! Also your group members rate you on you participation and communication (which isn't always fair).

She is very nice. I like the guest lectures! Only criticism I would give is that her tests are extremely hard. You get a cheat sheet but even then people were averaging 70's! Group projects are weighted heavily and got placed in a bad group which dropped my grade. You def will be needing the book!

Dr. Pratt is knowledge about her topics and is a nice person, I found it difficult to engage in her lectures and she is a relatively tough grader in comparison to my other exss classes. The group projects are easy but grades were not released which was frustrating. A few extra credit ops– take advantage Read the textbook chapters or fail the exams

Dr. Pratt is very knowledgable and is truly passionate about the content! The class relies heavily on in-person lectures and in-class activities so attendance is important. The class is also built to allow for guest speakers within the sports industry which was very insightful. She's very approachable and wants her students to succeed in her class
toughest grader in the entire department and the tests were not relevant to lecture material at all

The lectures were very boring. One midterm/one final. Barely any of the material from the textbook/lectures were on the exams and the average was the lowest I've seen for an EXSS class.Grades hard and posts the rubrics after due dates?Would not discuss grades for the semester, would only discuss them next semester when class would already be over

Dr. Monroe is a great professor. his tests are manageable as long as you study and they aren't worth that much. homework is common but easy. full semester group project but he is really helpful and not a strict grader at all. you can tell he really cares about research and wants to help his students. Put in the work and the class isn't bad at all!

Overall good professor who tries to make the content easy to understand. He is extremely into research and sometimes doesn't understand that the rest of the class does not have the experience he does. His tests are difficult, but totally doable if you watch the tutorials and do the activities in class, and they're worth like 15% total

Seems like he knows what he talks about but is extremely self absorbed. Extremely un engaging and boring lecturer. 4 tests composed of 15-20 questions in 30 minute time period most of which are tricky MC. So far have a A- cause tests aren't worth a lot but if you want a good professor and easy A take Kerr so more better and more caring as a person.

Do not take this professor. Exams are difficult and students are allowed only 30 minutes for 15 questions that are multiple choice AND written response.
