Big group project, graded heavy on and is very high level for an undergrad class. Also you turn in assignments through different platforms, and it can get very confusing. 
jh

Dr. Monroe made this class much harder and work heavy than it needed to be. Most of your grade is based off of a group project that has way too many complicated parts. He is very unorganized with the material in canvas and made it very confusing. Probably one of the worst classes I've taken at UNC.

Too much work for what should be an easier research class. Up to 3 group assignments due per week. Plus 2 tutorials to watch per week individually in addition to 2-3 canvas exercises plus homework assignment. Very pretentious professor seems like he thinks his class is the most important class we have.

Please just take this with someone else, you will thank yourself later. He makes this ridiculously complicated and way more complex than it needs to be. I can honestly say this class has made me NEVER want to do a research project again. Not worth it.

This class feels like there is a lot of information for not enough time. It is very exam heavy and has a group project. I feel like the class is unorganized and the profesor is not thorough with his instructions. It is hard to understand.

most of your grade is based on a group project; however, exams are given and only allow 30 minutes to take a 15-16 multiple choice AND written response exam. This was difficult for many students to even finish, not even considering their performance.

I took Professor Monroe during his first year here at UNC and he was very nice, but it didn't really translate to his organization with teaching. He had issues in the class such as not having a rubric on the first test, having material all over the place in canvas, and having due dates that were different than the course calendar.

He was very nice and tried his best. First semester at UNC but class felt very rushed and unorganized. Felt like there was way too much busy work that was unnecessary. Class isn't difficult but you need to check what you need to do every day. Most assignments are group work so if you have a bad group then good luck.

Prof Monroe is new at UNC & I really enjoyed his class, good person but also a great teacher. You have 5 exams (lowest dropped), a few hw assignments, class engagement points (attendance on PollEv), & a semester-long group research project. The class wasn't hard if you just paid attention but you need to attend class to do well on exams. Take him!

Pretty simple class and content, Dr.Murfree is very caring and helps you out with everything. Enjoyed the class and would take it again. All exams were open note and take-home, but overall a fun class, and I enjoyed coming every day.

Dr. Murfree was very nice and understanding. The exams were open-note, and there were multiple in-class assignments that were pretty relaxed. The only downside was that some assignments took a while to get graded, but I think that was because she was injured at the beginning of the semester.
horrible person horrrible teacher. Trust horrible horrible horrible.
Very engaging, all tests were open note, many small, easy assignments. Overall great class, loved Dr. Murfree. Would definitely recommend

Dr. Murfree is the absolute best! The way she teaches 323 is so engaging and I truly looked for this class every week. There is a good number of small assignments, and all exams were open note. Take this!!

Great professor who made the class interesting, so much that I actually enjoyed going to her class and listening to what she had to say. She is new at UNC but has teaching experience elsewhere and overall good class and good teacher, who is understanding that most of us are taking 4 other classes. Definitely recommend taking her classes!

I agree with someone saying the ULA's werent helpful. The tests are really hard and he just reads off the slides in class. The attendnace requirement is ridiculous as all of us can also read off the slides. Lots of random 1 point assignments that take a while. Not bad, but not great. Nice guy tho and very accessible outside of class

Dr. Defreese is a good professor, with the group project and assignments being pretty simple. However, his exams are OVERLY hard and stressful compared to how simple the material seems in class. I wouldn't bother taking this class if you have other options. Also, our TAs were disappointing, as their "study guides" weren't complete half the time.
Chill professor and doesn't grade too difficult. Not an easy A but cool class. Tests and quizzes were nitpicky but a good amount of it was common sense.
good professor to take, can always ask questions and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.

I liked this class and it definitely wasn't difficult, the only thing that was annoying was the group project. it's over the course of the semester and if you get put with a bad group it will make the class extremely annoying. overall the project isn't difficult but it can be if your group is bad. textbook not necessary tbh. take this class tho

lots of busy work and the lectures are hard to follow, exams are hard for no reason. attendance is graded heavily and the group project that goes across the whole semester is unorganized and not easy to follow.

Really nice prof. The lectures are really boring, but he really knows his stuff. Exams are trickier than you would think. I pulled out a B on the first one after starting studying the night before. There's a big group project and you're randomly assigned to groups, so as long as everyone does stuff you will be ok. Offers extra credit.
Gives extra credit which is nice, really boring lectures he just talks the whole time, strict attendance requirement, and just so much busy work

DeFreese's voice is the most monotone, boring voice ever. The content in this class is organized a little bit oddly and could be done better. It is just about a bunch of different theories you need to memorize. This class is one of worst classes I've taken at unc. Also, there is a big group project that is so busy work.
exams are trick questions and you must memorize every slide. average was a 65 for exam 1. he makes the class harder than it needs to be. dont take

JD is a really good professor. He's very understanding and responds quickly to emails. He also grades really quickly. Our exam grades were released the afternoon after we took the test. Class can be challenging and instructions aren't always the clearest for the big group project. Exams are fair but not the easiest.

Professor Defreese is so kind and a great professor! He is a quick grader and gives you feedback to improve on future assignments. Class was group project heavy, but if you get a good group you are fine and he is not too harsh on the group papers or presentation. Tests straightforward. Groups made doing class assignments easier. Take him!
One of the best professors in the department IMO. Definitely recommend!

I love Dr. DeFreese and would take another class with him. He is very understanding of students! Despite having a pretty tough attendance requirement, he really cares about the material he teaches and makes class engaging.
I really enjoyed his class. And he's just a nice guy.

Defreese is definitely one of the dryest lecturers I've had, but he knows what he's talking about. I just sometimes find it difficult to stay engaged. The class is broken into groups which honestly is helpful and I enjoyed talking to them. The semester long project is a bit of a pain, but not too hard, nor graded too harshly.

Quizzes are straightforward, with the answers coming from the textbook. The group project can be daunting but very manageable. The groups are randomly assigned. Exams are fair. For exams, make sure you understand the models discussed in the lecture well. Extra credit is offered. Dr.DeFreese is very understanding and patient, so reach out.

I liked 181, but be prepared to read the textbook and turn in an assignment before each class. There's also a semester long group project, which was frustrating at times. All exams given were fair in my opinion. He is an understanding individual and is willing to work with you to accommodate your needs outside of class or his office hours!

I loved Dr. Defreese, his lectures were straightforward and exams matched the material presented in them. Lots of low-stakes assignments that you pretty much will get credit for if completed. There is a big group project that is considerable for grades but if you have a good group (assigned) you'll be fine. Take with Defreese if you can!

Recommend taking this class with the other professor. If you are not a good test taker don't take this class. Test were made hard for no reason. I made a 100% on every quiz and most assignments outside of class besides a few and receive partial credit with no feedback. If you get a bad group for the semester long group project then good luck.

To be honest, the only bad thing about this class was the harsh grading. The exams were pretty chill, and the lowest scores get dropped. Professor Courtney, in my opinion, was chill, but the grading made her seem harsh. She also made us muffins for our last meeting.

Class consisted of an individual project and group project, each with 8-9 assignments. Not too difficult, but does take off points for minor things, so go to office hours and have her review assignments before submitting. Very sweet made muffins for an 8am Saturday final and always says hi when I see her outside of class. Dropped lowest of 5 tests.

I sort of agree with what others have said below, but she's not a bad person. She is nice to talk to in-person but a different animal when it comes to grading. She did bring us muffins for the final, and her exams are really easy. A lot of busy work and very harsh and unclear rubrics, and you do have to go into random neighborhoods for a walk audit

She was okay. I felt there was a lot of busy work and she grades really harshly. Her TA grades even more harshly which I didn't really understand. Read every single detail on the assignments because she will find a reason to take off points

Yall are crackin me up with your 1 star ratings—but stop scaring the future generations! Honestly she wasn't that bad. Yes there were lots of assignments and points for grammar, but her test isn't cumulative and she gives out muffins at the end. All in all communicate with your group members and ask her questions for the individual project.

The individual assignments took a good amount of time, and a lot of points could be taken off on the individual project if you weren't careful. The group project really depends on the people you're paired with. The exams were pretty easy as long as you study.

I have her at 8 in the morning, so not my favorite way to start the day. She will offer extra credit opportunities, but then says they don't actually count for your grade. Very very harsh grader and she will make you feel like you don't belong at UNC
random assignments built as busy work, makes you do an AI comparison....for what?
not much to say other than im not sure how she got this teaching position.
Go to a fortune teller to figure out what reasons she'll take off points for because it won't be stated on the rubric. Oh, also a billion points off for grammar. Take with someone else.

never hated myself more in this class. she assigns a lot of work each week and disregards the fact that we are students with other classes. she changes assignments halfway through the deadline, takes off loads of points for minor errors. I highly recommend taking a different professor if possible.
Took her a different semester and still haunts me. Busy work every week, very condescending, has favorites, seems like one to date a student ngl
Literally don't take her if you want to stay sane. And if you take her, be ready to lose 50 points without her giving any feedback on why
I had her in a past semester--she's just not very inviting or engaging. Lots of busy work, curses, and a really strict grader. Overall, my least favorite class at UNC

So many projects and short deadlines. Super strict grader (you WILL get loads of points off for grammar), makes you go into random communities to do a walk audit (almost attacked by homeless people), gets annoyed when you ask questions, and has a fetish for the baseball dudes.
Very spiteful person.

Dr. Courtney was great! She really values participation and a good relationship with her will only benefit you. She wants you to succeed and is always eager to answer questions and give feedback. The class itself is heavily centered around group work but it's not too terrible. She gave extra credit and saved my grade even after I bombed the final.

Very confusing professor, gets aggravated with students when they ask questions. She is quick to judge her students and will hold grudges against an individual when she feels they ask annoying questions or takes offense when a student tries to explain why they are struggling and seeks help. She takes it as an attack on her teaching. She also curses

I hate group projects but that's not on her. This class is an easy A and she wants you to learn a lot. There are occasional homeworks but can be pretty tedious. I feel like some people may find her confusing but thats on them for messing around during class. She's a great prof

Great professor! Would 1000% take any class with him. You can tell he really wants students to learn and is willing to help in any way possible. Class lectures were very interesting and cover everything on the exams.
Such a goat!! Awesome professor and engaging in class assignments

AWESOME PROFESSOR! I have taken him twice now. he is very personable, unlike other prof here, he tells you about his life and relates it to the course. i took 181 and 273 with him, but that wasn't an option. its common you will do fun things outside of the classroom  he even brought his dog raya in one day to hang during class!! material is easy
Literally the GOAT. Such a kind dude who really cares about what he teaches.

LOVEEEE HIMMM. My favorite prof at UNC. he is so encouraging. His lectures can be boring if you just want to learn the material and nothing else. He talks about real life and helps his students learn more than just by memorizing the work. I am not a great test taker but they aren't weighted too high so it ends up working out. 3 Free skips for class
King. Could not recommend him more. Favorite professor at Carolina. Easy A

such an engaging teacher even with slightly boring lectures. the tests seemed slightly unreasonable with details you needed to know, but tests arent weighted as high as you think! there are plenty of assignments that bring your grade up, as well as extra credit. would definitely reccomend!

Femi is such a fun lecturer, though sometimes he drags on about things, he really encourages conversations to happen in a fun way. By the way he teaches you can actually tell that he cares about the students and wants what is best for them.

Genuinely one of the best professors I have had. He makes it a point to allow you to learn from your mistakes rather than penalize you for them. There is a fair amount of written assignments, but they take the place of midterms and (in my opinion), teach you more about research than an exam could. Highly recommend Dr. Kerr!

Professor Kerr is the best professor! The content isn't always the best in 273, but he makes it so engaging. He is so supportive of students and is so willing to work with you on assignments, deadlines, and anything in life. There are also no exams! He is the best professor to take 273 with, but I would recommend taking any class you can with him!
So entertaining and honestly just the best ever

Literally the best professor here. Cares so much about his students and its evident. No exams, just projects. Weekly pre class and post class "quizzes" but he grades them on effort not accuracy. Super easy class and fun class. He's a chiller.

One of the best professors in EXSS. Constantly checks up on students and never overloads us with work. Opportunities for group work to be done in class and he would move due dates if we were stressed in our personal lives.
Highly recommend

Dr. Kerr is supportive and encouraging throughout the senior honors thesis process, and challenges you in the best way. Feedback is detailed and helpful, and time is always made to talk about challenges. Dr. Kerr clearly cares about student success as expectations are clear, communication is consistent, and support is always there. Highly rewarding

If you have the chance to take a class with Professor Kerr, take it. He is a phenomenal professor who is so understanding when it comes to his students and is willing to do whatever to help them out. He is so funny and makes going to class at 8 am worth it. You will not regret taking a class with him.

Dr. Kerr is one of the rare professors on campus who considers the fact that his students are people with lives outside of his class. He is very willing to be flexible as long as you are willing to demonstrate you are putting in effort to the class. Makes an otherwise really boring topic and 8 am class really enjoyable. I would highly recommend.
Data literacy is a very annoying class, but Dr. Kerr is awesome. He made a boring class as fun and easy as it could be. Could not recommend him more!
Zach is such a chill guy. He didn't make this (bs) class harder than it needed to be and understood the importance of it to students. If you still need to take IDST111L, take it with him.
Kerr's great. One of the best professors I've had up until this point. Super understanding of students lives but also does a fantastic job teaching and challenging students.

Zach is such a great professor. He seemed to really understand the point of Data Lit Lab and didn't make it more demanding than it needed to be. He was extremely engaging, understanding, and flexible with the class. Overall great guy.

Honest and understanding of students lives outside of classes, especially for a one credit course. Take this class with him if you can, it seemed he was able to be more flexible with the material than other professors because he helped create the course. Met six times throughout the semester, with biweekly online work and a final group project

Zack understood that the class was only a single credit hour, and only had us do what was necessary to learn the content. I had to meet with him for help with my final project, and I mentioned that I was looking for some good study spots on campus. He took the time after our meeting to send me a list of his favorite places to get work done.
Dr. Kerr is a great professor. He actually cares about his students and wants them to succeed. We had 2-3 assignments each week, but we didn't have any tests. Best professor I've had at UNC.
I wish every teacher were like him; he actually understands that we are college students.
Take this class with Professor Kerr!

Professor Kerr was one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes class entertaining and truly cares for his students. He is one of the most energetic and fun professors I have had at UNC, especially with his endless jokes and memes. His workload is VERY manageable, and he is very passionate about research. I would 100000% recommend!!

Dr. Kerr has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. I genuinely felt that he cared about his students and their success and well-being. No exams but 85% group work. He does grade assignments a little harder, but usually you can submit revisions and get points back. He's also extremely funny and entertaining. Worth taking 273 with Kerr.

Although the professor is kind, the exams are very challenging and account for 80% of the final grade. The PowerPoints are bland, making it difficult to learn the material without rewriting and reviewing notes outside of class. Homework is graded very specifically. Challenging for students without a physics background.

She is a great professor, while the material is hard, she did a great job communicating how to work through the problems. The first exam was a bit of a shock though as to how much was conceptual over mathematical.
Great professor that is always willing to meet with you! Very nice and a good sense of humor.

Unapproachable professor. Had to teach myself everything. Textbook homeworks + in-class quizzes you can't make up + 4 exams + 1 (easy) project. Always misgraded exams & hw. Would recommend taking pass/fail if you're not a physics buff.

I came into this class not having any physics background so I was super nervous, but both Dr. P & the ULAs were super helpful in office hours & class. Dr. P always made lectures relatable and super interesting. She does tend to overcomplicate concepts at times, so I recommend going to ULA office hours to uncomplicate things. I loved this class!

I enjoyed having Petschauer as a prof, shes hilarious and makes lecture less boring. The material for this class was very hard and I found it very difficult to study for the exams. Office hours were key but almost every exam, I felt like I was going into it blind. most of the class relies on exam and there was 1 or 2 quizzes & easy group project.

I loved taking this class with Dr. P! The class content was really hard at times, but Dr. P was very accessible outside of class and was always willing to provide explanations. This class had 3 paper exams, 2 open-note quizzes, a video project, and weekly homework problems. The exams are based on the slides, so if you study those you will be fine!

Very easy required class with Professor Petschauer. Lectures were sometimes long and drawn out, but that's expected. You do have to participate and complete some group work, but all required assignments are easy. If you do not get an A, you are not trying.

This was by far my favorite class this semester. Dr. P is so passionate and knowledgeable you can't help but be completely fascinated during every lecture. The workload was very manageable and she is a fair grader. She cares about her students and is there to help if you need it. I would 100% recommend this class and taking anything with Dr. P.

The most fun professor. She made class so much fun and really cares about her students. It was only a first year seminar so nothing too hard, but she encourages class participation and cares about what everyone has to say. 10/10 would totally take any class she teaches

We basically had to teach ourselves the problems in class. We came to class and she just gave us problems to do on the board in groups, we would do them and she would just go over them. It also took up the whole class period. As far as my group, one person knew how to do the work and the rest of us just sat there in confusion.

I love Dr. Davis DOWN. She is so kind, fun, and made earth science one of my new favorite subjects. She is literally my teacher crush this semester for looks AND personality. I adore this woman. Daniel is also a great TA. I wish I could take more EMES courses with her, even just to audit! Such a fun time and I've learned so much.
very possibly the best undergrad professor of all time bro makes me feel like im in middle school again love professor davis
Very sweet and willing to work with you!

I enjoyed EMES 101 so much, although I wasn't interested in the content because of Professor Davis; she is the absolute sweetest and genuinely loves what she does. She was also accessible outside of class and is very accommodating if you have any issues.

Dr. Davis was one of my favorite professors I've had at UNC. Just an incredible person. Kind, understanding, completely nonjudgemental and extremely flexible. Very easy to contact, and a very engaging lecturer. If you have a chance to take a class with her- DO IT.

Difficult for a supposedly beginner coding course. Lectures don't align with the homework/assignment content at all and you will probably be teaching yourself everything when it comes to assignments. Professor is overall a funny guy but not very helpful.

Truly one of the worst professors I have had at UNC so far. The assignments themselves are doable, no thanks to him. Everything you learn in this class will be things that you teach yourself outside of class. Attending lectures is purely a waste of time. Don't take a class with him if you can help it.
Not a good class or professor.

Professor Lees was very condescending. I went to office hours and he talked down to me and acted like I was dumb because I didn't know something about coding (we were never taught it) and made me cry. He gives 100% or 0s with no wiggle room. If you get 1 piece wrong you get a 0. The final was 40% of our grade and we didnt know until the week before

Took my grade from an A to a B because he decided to not grade one of my assignments for no reason. He also changed the weight of the grading scale that was in the syllabus the day he submit grades. Attendance wasn't mandatory but this class is certainly not for beginners. He takes pride in knowing more than his students, has an ego.

Submitting another review cuz this man didn't submit our final assignment grades on Canvas worth FOURTY percent of our grade, then gave me an A- when his grade scale on the syllabus said I had an A. Asked him about it, he ignored the final assignment question and said the syllabus scale was “just an example.” this man wants you to not succeed.

Lectures are boring and honestly not super helpful. I also don't think the course was organized super well. Most of your grade is weekly assignments and most of these weren't too hard but deciphering the instructions to figure out what you were expected was the hardest part.

He's so rude. He said students asking valid questions were just anxious. Asked a question and only got snarky remarks. There is no feedback on hw assignments. His lectures are so amazingly unhelpful. The only reason my grade is surviving is my TA. Truly the words I want to say aren't allowed on here. I think he puts students tears in his coffee.

Grade depends mostly on homework projects which are hard and time-consuming but manageable. Lectures are fine but somewhat gloss over the absolute basics of programming and don't show a good way to organize compsci-type notes, which may pose stumbling blocks at first.
Reviewing example code from lectures can be very helpful, don't ignore it.

Do NOT take this class if you dont have experience with R. This is NOT an intro to R class (even though its supposed to be) and you WILL be lost and confused. His motto is 'encouraging students to teach themselves' and best believe you will be teaching yourself everything. Weve done things in this class that my data analytics minor friends havent.

Boring, unnecessary lectures that often began with him bragging about the so-called worldwide praise he's received for his code. Disrespectful to students asking questions about the homework if he didn't immediately know the answer. Not an intro R class, take Geog 215 with Dr. Parr if that's what you're looking for. Rude guy.

No feedback on assignments, lectures were boring and really hard to follow. If you fall behind, too bad! Not mandatory lectures but material was hard and if you did anything wrong in an assignment you got an automatic 50%. No final exam only final project. Not an intro class.

The class itself was very straightforward, with the only assignments being weekly homework, but Dr. Lees was not a forgiving professor. He often made it very hard to ask questions and get a proper answer. This class was presented as an introductory class to R, but it absolutely was not and Lees was not very accomodating to those who did not know R
I cannot stress enough how hard it is to learn from him. Condescending and confusing are the main two words I would use to describe him.

I've only had him one week and he's awful. He acts really condescending about knowing how to do code, assuming it's "really easy" for everyone to learn. As a beginner, I'm very lost and confused. He keeps saying the best way to learn is to figure it out yourself, which I don't disagree with, but he gives you absolutely no starting point.
cool guy :)

Attendance is not mandatory; he posts online videos he posts after class. Weekly concept sketch and peer review, 3-4 easy problem sets, based on questions from class examples. Rewatch the lecture while you're doing concept sketches and the problem set. 2 tests NOT SIMPLE. The midterm was alright, but the final exam was very hard.

I started class thinking I would not enjoy it or do well in it, but it ended up being my favorite this semester! Some of the content is tricky, but if you go to class and office hours you will do well. Guidelines for assignments are clear, and grading is fair! Dr. Pavelsky is amazing, and truly wants you to succeed. I highly recommend this class!

Dr. Pavelsky is super nice and genuinely wants his students to do well - he boosted my grade at the end of the semester which he didn't have to do and is not opposed to curving tests when students struggle. His class was low pressure but very organized and straight forward! Def recommend.
Honestly a great class, tests are difficult, the final was awful. Overall you will pass the class even if you don't go.

Dr. Pavelsky is an amazing professor. EMES 324 turned out to be my favorite class this past semester! Dr. Pavelsky is super inspiring; he talks about his NASA conferences etc. during class which truly make me excited to be in this particular field. Some math, but none of it is too hard. Midterms and workload are manageable if you show up and study.

I wasn't particularly interested in the subject matter and was just taking this class for a major requirement, but Dr. Pavelsky did a good job making the content as interesting as he could. Math-heavy but not incredibly challenging. Attendance at lecture was not required.

LOVED Dr.Pavelsky. He was very knowledgable and excited to teach which made it so interesting to learn. He made the math simple and answered questions really well. I would 100% take him again. He is a joy to be taught by.

Dr. Pavelsky is a great guy! His lectures could get confusing at times, but he would do a good job of explaining as well as keeping the course fun. The course was more math heavy and overall more difficult than expected. However, he is very accessible outside of class and wants you to succeed.

Challenging course with more math than I anticipated. Midterm was difficult and lectures could be hard to follow, but Pavelsky posts everything and is very willing to help. You'll need to put in effort, but the resources and support make it manageable.

I found this course to be moderately difficult and sometimes the exam questions/problem sets didn't totally reflect the depth we covered in lecture. Overall, I think Prof. Pavelsky is very knowledgable and cares about his students. He can be a touch scatter-brained, very cool guy though!

One of the sweetest professors who is super joyful and kind and very passionate about hydrology. I would certainly recommend him as a professor however as a non-stem major the class was fairly difficult and more math heavy than expected. He is willing to help and a fair grader however which makes the class enjoyable.

Dr. Pavelsky is one of my favorite professors at this University. He is so passionate about what he teaches and is overall such a ray of sunshine. Overall, the class itself was not bad! Midterm was fairly difficult, but there are many grades throughout the semester and a lot of study resources.
The most unique thing about Professor Haskin's class is that she will make a third of your test grades be from a group portion. Most of the class did well as a result.

Dr. Haskin was a very organized class structure. A lot of pre-class work such as readings, videos, and quizzes. However, they help to understand the lectures better. Tests and quizzes aren't too hard if you pay attention. Overall, Dr. Haskin was very helpful and has her student's best interests in mind. Would definitely recommend.

Haskin's class was pretty easy to follow if you're paying attention to lectures. The material on exams was very lecture heavy, but she provided different methods of learning (videos, interactive websites) to aid in understanding. It's obvious that she cares about her students and makes an effort for everyone to have the best experience.

This class is easy if you go to lecture but most people don't. Exams are easier than the online quizzes and she gives a ton of extra credit. She is very passionate and the hardest part about this class is paying attention during lecture.

I absolutely loved Professor Haskin, and I don't really understand why she has such a bad rating on here. the course work is super straight forward and as long as you keep up with everything, you'll be fine. tests can be difficult, but you get a group at the beginning of the semester which helps a lot. she offers extra credit and drops low grades!
Haskin is a very nice professor but her tests are hard. you can do corrections in groups but they only help the grades a little.
AMAZING professor, she made me love geology. Please take her, she is so kind and understanding, and she explains things super super super well. I can see her passion and it makes me passionate

Really test heavy and for some reason I rlly bombed it but she does give extra credit and there is also a group exam right after the regular mid term which generally boosts your grade. Wouldn't take if you dont have to. Not super organized, she has the stuff but the fonts and aesthetics are a headache.

I liked her and thought she was a nice lady and good at what she teaches but just those tests were SO heavy. During lectures I would stay engaged and she'd say "great work in class!" and I thought I understood the material so well and study so much for the exams and then end up getting a 60. Group exams after make up a 1/3 so that helped.
i was told to take this class by my academic advisor and told it would be easy. it was not. nice professor but not for me.

Definitely an easier FC-Create gen-ed fulfillment, but be prepared for a boring and laborious semester. Haskin and the TAs are very unhelpful and unprofessional. Sitting through this class 3x a week is treacherous. The most boring lectures I have experienced in my life. The assignments are graded harsh, tho the material is middle school level.
If you put in the expected work to this class (reading, watching the video lectures, paying attention) then you should be able to succeed. She is super sweet and accomodating.
Haskin is actually chill and not really the problem, its the TA's who give the absolute worst advice and grade what are supposed to be easy assignments way too harsh

The class overall was very disorganized. Sometimes did not finish her lectures, which lead to another 45 minute video lecture for homework. Topics seemed to come out of nowhere, professors seemed consistently irritated at students without reason. She spent  about half her lecture time talking about nothing at all, and never explained concepts.

She is very sweet, but her lectures do not really teach much because she expects you to have done readings prior to class. She does a lot of stuff with small groups, including exams. She does not require attendance, but she does participation grades to make sure you are there. She does offer some extra credit. Overall, not that bad

Very clear with expectations/guidelines, gives lots of resources. 24 hr no-penalty late deadline, easy to cram for final if you miss lectures. Feels like a high school class, it's so guided. Group exams are a lifesaver, lots of groupwork with participation graded. Great NatSci and lab credit.

I HATED this class. She spends so much time talking about nothing. Expectations for this class were incredibly unclear. These professors were on completely different pages. Environmental concepts were way too in depth for a Triple I. the concepts could've been cool if executed well, but it wasn't. The final made no sense.

Not a great experience with Dr. Haskin. She was the main professor in my triple i class and was genuinely just...boring. I feel like she expects us to already have knowledge on complex environmental topics, which doesnt really seem fair considering this is a first year class.

Know what's expected of you and what needs to get done. Does group exams, honestly, a lifesaver. There are many resources to help with studying and any questions. Group participation is required, and attendance is counted by pollev. It is a great class for your natural science and lab requirement if you're not a chem or bio major.

Honestly, anyone who says this course was hard/boring/disconnected just didn't pay attention and then later complained that they didn't do well. In my opinion, Professor Haskin is a great lecturer, and she always provided her slides after class. Don't let the bad reviews fool you, if you study you'll do great. Quizzes and final were easy as pie.

Really caring professor. A lot of fun going through her personal collections in lectures. Midterms are take-home and final is clear and straight forward. Review slides and you will do well. Great class!

Dr. Surge is the best. Her lectures are engaging and entertaining and you can tell she really cares about what she's talking about. The class is not hard at all, but you can still learn a good amount. Would take again.
I really enjoyed this class! She was super nice, lectures could be kind of boring but she made it very easy to do well in this class!

This course is definitely more advanced, with many group critiques. However, I was able to learn so much and build up my knowledge. Having such a small class also allowed for Donna to become very friendly with everyone. She really showed that she cared!

Donna is one of my favorite professors at UNC. Her assignments are very writing-heavy, but the criteria are clear and she grades easily as long as the questions are answered. She is so charismatic, and made learning a topic I wasn't familiar with a joy! Her knowledge of geology shines through in this course, you can tell how much she loves teaching

She covers a lot of content in lectures but you can always refer to the slides outside of class. Exams were all take home over a week period and there were a few writing assignments. She's super passionate about what she teaches and excited to share with her students!

One of the least interesting and poor lecturers I've ever had. Doesn't seem to understand how to interact with people in a normal way, has high expectations but doesn't communicate them until the assignment is graded. I would never take another class with her.
dont do it

Dr. Cramer is a good professor who knows what she's talking about. If you watch Dr. Cramer's lecture videos and go through anki, you can at least score in the mid 70s range on exams and as long as you do well on the other assignments you can get a decent grade. She covers a lot of material but her tests reflect everything you go over in lectures.

MCRO 251 is the worst class at UNC. Dr. Cramer is disrespectful to students and says that you should've learned the topics "in elementary school", then immediately after tells you to take BIO 103 if you don't understand. She is condescending. MCRO is also just insanely difficult. I absolutely don't recommend.

This class is one of the hardest classes I've ever taken at UNC. However, getting a good grade in this class isn't completely un-obtainable. There's lots of content so although everything is reviewed in lecture, plan to do a lot of studying on your own. Overall, Dr. Cramer isn't a bad professor, she wants you to succeed, her class is just hard.

Dr. Cramer gets a lot of unnecessary hate! I really enjoyed her class and found her extremely knowledgeable on the content. It is not an easy course, no matter who teaches it. Expect to study weekly and put in work, but it is not impossible. Just don't fall behind! Exams are not super hard if you study-- she even hints on questions.

Cramer is one of the best professors I've had at UNC so far. You can tell she knows her stuff and while it's a hard class, its because there's just a lot of content, it's not her teaching. She isn't trying to trick you on tests and if you pay attention in class and actually study and put effort in, you will be fine.

Genuinely do not listen to any of the good ratings. This class is actually impossible. She is hilarious and I can tell she is passionate but she is the worst lecturer ever. She jumps from topic to topic, making her impossible to follow. Her slides have no information, just pictures. No matter how much I study it doesn't pay off.

content was disorganized and could have been given to students in a way that actually makes sense. Also exams are worth basically everything, so all the other assignments you do don't even matter. Cramer also likes to talk/yell at us during exams, which really messed with me. Overall, not the best class i've taken here.

She can be difficult to understand: jumps from topic to topic without care, difficult to follow, hits the ground running, everything said, looked at, and even lightly covered is important. DO THE ORGANISMS FROM DAY 1. DO ANKI. Look over everything everyday and make sure you understand it. Everything builds and she SUCKS at answering questions.

This professor is the worst professor at UNC. She is derogatory and does not care to see you genuinely succeed. Very awful, unclear, and unhelpful woman, she knows she is the only professor for this course and therefore does not care to help you even if you meet with her several times. I firmly believe UNC should fire this woman and replace her.

This class was one of the best classes I have taken at UNC. Dr. Cramer is hilarious and the tests were also easy if you studied and did everything she advised to do. There was a lot of work sometimes but if you review the Anki Cards, Organism Cards, and Lecture Notes, you should be able to do well on the exams. She curves too!

Dr. Cramer is amazing if you put in the effort she asks you to. Do the Anki every day, rewatch the lecture videos, and do the organisms cards. You will get an A if you do this, and she gives extra credit on every exam. My favorite STEM professor I have had at UNC, and don't be scared, she is very nice in person.

I was scared of this class because of the reviews too. But genuinely Dr. Cramer is super caring and yes her lecture can feel disorganized sometimes but she heavily emphasizes what will be tested. The topics were super interesting! Her exams were straightforward with no tricks. If you space out studying and memorize early on, you will be fine!

Don't take this class. The grade is based almost entirely on exams,required to write blog 3 page every week he exams require memorizing lectures, the textbook, and Anki material. No study guides.the teaching style made the course overwhelming and hard to understand. I would not recommend this class.

I love Dr. Cramer! Her lectures are engaging, there is a lot to remember, but she gives all the resources needed to do well and curves exams. Micro is just a hard class but it is super interesting and she is very passionate about it. She can come off as intimidating but she just really wants her students to learn and succeed. Best class I've taken!

Overall very nice and does want you to succeed. Biggest tip is rewatch all the lecture videos and put basically everything she says into an anki card. It sucks but it helps. Definitely easier than chem in my opinion. Exams are straightforward, there's just a lot to know which makes them difficult. Putting what she says into anki helps with this

On the first day of class, she told us her RMP ratings were inaccurate, and she wasn't a bad professor. This is a lie. She's a messy lecturer, bouncing around topics and mixing things up. In addition to this, she often shames the class on how awful the test scores are instead of taking accountability. So, prepare yourself for a 60% class average!
The content is super dense and the workload is heavy but it was interesting. She's very tough love but is a good lecturer (go back and rewatch lectures tho). DO THE ANKI AND STUDY!!

I don't mean to scare you because I know she is the only professor for this course, but she sucks. There were classes after an exam where all she would do was shame those who did not get a perfect score. She scribbles all over the slides and only uses them to help herself remember what to say. If you are going to survive this course, use the Anki!

The content is dense, as UNC requires her to condense three semesters of micro into one. The workload is a lot, but manageable: I learned a ton from the work she assigned. She's very upfront, which is nice when you need some tough love and motivation. You can tell she mostly teaches at the medical school, lol. Overall, a hilarious, awesome person.

I haven't even finished the semester and I can tell you Dr. He is easily the best professor I've ever had at Carolina. Her lectures are engaging, the readings (while sometimes long) are always interesting, and she's always available for questions. There are not enough good things I can say about her. I would recommend you take any class she offers.
Live, Laugh, Love Dr. He!!

Dr. He is so nice and smart, and the class was super interesting too! The work was very manageable, mostly weekly readings, one essay, and one project, and she always took into consideration our opinions and schedules. Highly recommend this class for a FYS and any other class she teaches!

I took my FYS with her and she is absolutely amazing! Dr. He is kind, funny, and very caring. She takes into consideration our busy shcedules when assigning work and is very chill. Her lectures are very interesting and I always looked forward to going to class. If you are wondering what to take for FYS, take her class!

Dr. He is one of the best! She is funny, encouraging, and accommodating, but most of all is clearly an expert in her field; lectures are very interesting and well designed, and I enjoyed every class meeting. She is accessible outside of class and gives multiple extra credit opportunities. I'd take any of her courses in a heartbeat.

Prof. He is one of the best professors I've ever had. She is SO knowledgeable, a great and interesting lecturer, funny, very understanding/accomodating, and engaging. Her expertise definitely shows. She offers multiple extra credit opportunities; the only tough grade is the critical essay. I would take any class she teaches in a heartbeat.

Professor He was very accommodating and understanding throughout the semester. The last lecture, she even took snacks to celebrate! Honestly, one of the best professors at UNC. Hopefully, I can take more of her courses!

Professor He is the best. I was always looking forward to her class every week. Her lectures were engaging and insightful. The critical thinking along with close-reading is good training for STEM majors. The assignments were challenging but not difficult. She gives useful, lengthy feedback on the critical essays.

Dr. He is honestly the best professor I've had so far and I am happy to have had her during my first semester here at UNC. She truly cares for all her students and goes above and beyond to ensure nobody is stressed out. I would love to take any of her classes during the upcoming semesters.
Dr. He's lectures are excellent. If you are interested in the course topic you will most likely find the class enjoyable.

Professer He is my favorite professor at UNC so far. She really cares about her students, and extends deadlines if she sees that people are busy. She also dedicated two separate weeks to giving her students a break and cancelled the final exam to take pressure off of us. The lectures are easy to follow, and the content is interesting as well.

Dr. He was wonderful. She was always moving our assignments around if she noticed the class struggling, and she gives really good feedback. Her lectures were very engaging and interesting. I enjoyed discussing the readings in class, and I always came away with a new understanding of the material. Take her class!

Dr. He is amazing! She is very fair and clearly cares about us. She's adjusted deadlines and such when she thought we were stressed and even canceled our final exam. Dr. He also gives a ton of feedback on papers and gives opportunities for revisions. The midterm was open note which was nice. There is a lot of reading but it's manageable.

Professor He is unbelievably thoughtful; she regularly adapts the material/schedule to fit students' needs. She is also incredibly knowledgable, and her lectures are engaging and informative. Although some readings can be lengthy, and some of the reading questions can be difficult, the class was great overall, and I would definitely recommend it.

Professor He was a fantastic professor and it was an honor of mine to have her for my fys! Her midterms are open notes and could be taken outside the classroom. Since we have essays throughout the semester (since all gen-eds require a total of 10 pages of writing), she canceled the final exam!!! Definitely have her during your time at Carolina!

professor dixon is the best! gives a bunch of extra credit and really wants to see you succeed in his class. you don't have to attend lecture to do well in the class, but watch out for pop quizzes. quiz questions can sometimes be confusing. take this for easy A!

This class would be better named Dixon101 instead of Japan162 because he made the entire course about himself.  His questions are built to trip you up, and it's more about reading the question carefully rather than the actual content.  Overall an easy A though.

Jap 162 is so easy, watch out for pop quizzes and your fine, there was a recitation but it was just a 1 five minute presentation, that's it. And you have to write some discussion posts and an essay. Take if you want an A
Very informative course. He sets up the course in a way where you are meant to succeed. Great instructor.
Dwayne is awesome. He is so passionate about his subject and was engaging even tho this is a gen ed for me.  Final was in person on lockdown browser, but only like 25 questions.
Do your bonus and you don't have to go to class. Respect for my GOAT professor
Very interesting lectures
Dixon is a great professor with interesting lectures! There are a lot of readings, some writing assignments, and a presentation but nothing too hard. Pretty easy class with an engaging professor.

Highly recommend taking Asia 150 with Dwayne. One of the best lecturers and provides generous extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Grade is made up of 3 discussion posts, 4 short quizzes, a paper, presentation, and the final.
Dwayne is the best teacher I've had so far at UNC and probably the nicest guy I have ever met. Take his class, you will not regret it!

The class is so chill, take home quizzes and short responses every so often. The final exam is online but its so hard. I recommend doing as much Extra Credit and get 100s and all the assignments so your final exam grade doesnt really matter.
GOAT! AMAZING!
He wants you to succeed. He really cares for us.

Overall, Professor Dixon is a very passionate and caring professor. But my issue with the class is that he assigns too many very lengthy readings, especially for a 100-level course. Like 1-3 40+ page readings before each MW class. Do not take this class if you have a busy schedule or hard classes and are looking for a chill class.
Dr. Dixon is amazing and incredibly passionate about his work. I really enjoyed his lectures and the class content, I definitely recommend this course to anyone especially with it's light workload.
Good prof, easy class
The goat, no more needed to be said.

One of the best professors I have ever had at UNC. He was extremely caring and very respectful of all students. It is evident he wants all of his students to succeed and is an invaluable member of the UNC community.
Dwayne is one of the most inspiring and talented individuals I've ever had the privilege to learn from.
Excellent human being and teacher.

This class was... awkward. The rating that said "twists history to make Hindus look like the main and only aggressors in South Asia, which is extremely inaccurate and problematic" was true in my experience, and I'm not even Hindu. It was also a bit odd how Mughal conquest was never mentioned as conquest and was only painted in a positive light.

He was extremely hard to access. Thank the gods that I have a bunch of prior knowledge in this class because of my background, or else I would have failed. He doesn't give any meaningful feedback. Like seriously some comments on my essays were "????????????". He also only uses WhatsApp to communicate, which felt kind of unprofessional.

Funny professor, but spends a lot of time in class going on tangents. Participation and attendance matter a lot, and his assignment rubrics are often unclear or nonexistent. He grades relatively easily, but he has a TA who grades very difficultly, so hope you get Taj. Also grades late, as of finals week, I only had one assignment graded out of ~15.

Dr. Taj is a really funny guy. He emphasizes participation. His course content is not strictly slide-driven, so you will have to do some more implying/rely on background knowledge. Overall, the class is fairly easy and enjoyable. If you pay attention and participate, you will be fine.

He is very enthusiastic and seems like a nice guy, but could not understand anything he said. Slides are all over the place and had to self teach. The final exam was difficult and practically only his portion of the course. Would not recommend.

The worst of the three professors. This class is awful but his lectures were incoherent and did not make any sense. His questions on the final were ridiculously hard like he was trying to make us fail. Do not take this triple I and if you do- study the most insignificant parts of his lectures because that will be on the exam!
The class was just terrible. I'm sure in a smaller setting he would be a better professor but I had to self-teach most of the unit because it was hard to hear.

He was the most enthusiastic prof I've worked with. He's clearly passionate about the material and seems like a really caring nice guy, however, I couldn't understand most of what he had to say. This could have been a combo of the big lecture hall, bad mic, and his accent, but I really struggled because of it. Great prof...as for the class, RUN.

Not very accessible outside class, took a lot of time to answer. Very unclear guidelines for homework and projects. Lecture heavy but many do not relate to direct topics. Participation is required. Does not grade anything until last minute.

Afroz Ji was a great professor! The class is lecture and conversation-heavy, but I enjoyed that. We had homework weekly but it wasn't difficult and he is flexible on due dates. Be aware there are 2 group presentations and a skit. He states that he never fails students and while they are a good amount of assignments, it isn't difficult.

SUCH A SWEET PROF. available for questions at literally 1am. Funny and engaging lecture. Homework 63% literally can't fail. Super flexible deadlines. Helps out students with everything! participation = A

Best prof I've ever taken@UNC. His Homeworks are super easy and worth 63% so you can't fail even if you want to lol, final is worth 20% and easy if you speak Hindi/Urdu and did the homeworks on time. Deadlines are super flexible and lectures were super easy to follow. He is also super accessible outside class(on WhatsApp not email) I'd say take it.

Professor Taj was interesting, but it was very hard to hear/understand him in such a large lecture hall. He was definitely the better of the 3 IDST 129 professors, but it isn't a class I would recommend. He did perform an original song and dance on the last day which was very cool, and he seems to be very passionate. Good teacher, bad class.

Prof. Taj is very engaging and wants students to have fun and learn. He gave us lots of readings/films and the ones I watched were super interesting. On the last day of class he performed a song he wrote for us which was great. Awesome guy, would definitely recommend him!

He cares a lot about what he's teaching and who he's teaching. Definitely not something I was interested in (took as a gen ed) but he's the GOAT. Readings were concise but he did expect us to watch a lot of movies which I personally didn't do (wasn't gonna put in 3 hours between classes for a gen ed). Don't take the class but take Afroz' classes
GOAT

I saw the complaints that there aren't clear grading criteria. The grading is quite simple tho, engage and have fun. That's it. Other than that, the prof is super sweet, caring, and funny. It's been a tough semester, and this class was the only class that I could breathe. You're not going to get a better professor than him.

No formal lectures, everything depends on class discussions. Lot of films to watch outside of class. You write a few papers, forum posts, quizzes, student presentations. Be engaged and keep up with discussions and you'll have a blast. Prof Taj is very entertaining!

There is no doubt that Dr. Bae is a very nice and highly competent person. These multiple-choice questions are a bit difficult, but overall they can still be handled. If you don't have a basic understanding of these topics, this course will be quite challenging because it requires reading the original materials that have been translated.

This instructor grades extremely harshly. Even with strong homework scores and near-perfect participation, earning an A is very difficult. The class has heavy reading after every session, and grading feels excessive. She also gives little flexibility for delayed final presentations. For a first-year “easy” course, this was unnecessarily stressful.

The class is easy as long as you participate and put in some effort. Theres readings every class and they can be a little boring. You have to speak at least once every class and pay attention to her lectures. I wasn't the biggest fan of her, she could be little rude and will call you out if you're on your phone or say something wrong.
Most projects are very subjective, and you will lose points in many unexpected places.

I think Proffesor Bae is very kind and incredibly smart. She really wants us to understand the content and works hard to teach it to us. The class isn't particularly hard. As long as you at least read a summary of the readings you should be fine in it. But project directions are vague and tests are written so watch out for those.

Reserved professor so sometimes hard to connect with personally. Overall challenged me to think a lot. Reading heavy and gives 5 random reading quizzes, but if you think about it, she gives them out very predictably. Instructions are vague which can be bad, but can also be very good since it gives you more leeway. Super nice, would take again!

Dr. Bae is a nice person, but she gives many long readings and always gives pop quizzes at the worst times and most if not all of the class does bad on them because they ask for the most random trivia questions. Although somewhat generous with grading, criteria is not clear. Overall it's an easy but not light class for a gen ed. Wouldn't take again

Smart and hard. I heard that she has revised the syllabus this year, and it's been made extremely complicated. If you have no background knowledge and are not good at writing in class, please do not take and  save yourself.
Dr. Kief genuinely cares about what he is teaching and will put in a lot of effort with giving feedback and ensuring that students grow. Overall very nice person.

Dr. Kief is an erudite scholar of Korean/East Asian history/culture/literature and a really nice guy. Although his classes are reading heavy, he's not a demanding grader and makes himself available to his students whenever he can. I thoroughly enjoyed taking his classes and would recommend him to anyone interested in studying Asian/Korean history.

Professor Kief is very knowledgeable about Korean history and passionate about what he's teaching. This class is reading-heavy, as half the class discusses the readings. However, he's very accessible outside of class and always willing to help. The final group project is with Makerspace, and he allows lots of flexibility on what the project is.

Professor Keef is nice but a bit awkward, and largely spends class at the board. Would have been nice to have more interaction in a small class size, but nonetheless it wasnt super demanding and he was lenient and available.

Kief's class has lots of readings, and the class is mainly focused on those. The 2 essays are tedious, but he gives feedback. Class is interesting if you enjoy the topic - otherwise, there are other seminars. He's passionate about what he talks about and I recommend him if you're into the humanities/history. Go to him with any questions you have!

Dr. Kief is an amazing professor and truly cares about your academic and personal well-being. There's once a week discussion posts, lots of readings, 2 long essays, 1 group project, and final. Overall, the grade you want is up to the work you put in. I am not good at discussion and writing essays, but he helped me greatly. Definitely recommend!
Extremely boring lecturer, I dont think even he enjoys the material he teaches. This dude is a talking textbook.
good professor, interesting seminar format, fairly easy grading as long as you write a cohesive paper
AMAZING!!!!

Super interesting class. Each class was basically a group discussion, so you have to attend and participate. Professor is really caring and shares her own personal experiences in Iran. So far my favorite class taken at unc. Super easy A; if you do the assignments, you will get a 100

I am writing this review as a Junior, but I took her class my first semester of freshman year. ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS I HAVE EVER HAD! She can be harsh and is a tough grader, but she cares about her students. Professor Yaghoobi is a super cool person and very knowledgeable. Her course shaped my undergraduate experience for the better.

Dr. Yaghoobi has an interesting way of commanding respect. For some reason I just really want her approval, it's kinda weird but iconic. Overall the class isn't too hard, but she has high expectations for you, and if you don't meet them you'll suffer.

I loved having classes with Dr. Y! She's super knowledgeable and graded very fairly in my opinion. It's telling that multiple of her students (including me) have taken multiple classes with her. She really cares about her student's understanding and development.

She did not really care about students and was very patronizing when answering questions. She also criticized participation but actively does not accept opinions other than hers so it makes it hard to participate. Most things are self taught or on your own.

I was really nervous to take this class but Dr. Y made this class enjoyable. I learned a lot about Persian Poetry from her experience. She was always willing to accommodate to fit your needs and help you understand this class. There is just discussions, so do the readings and watch the videos to understand. No finals, just two big papers.

I think that there can be another way to teach the course. There is no prereq, so it is likely that you would need to break down concepts, topics, and pronunciations rather than constantly getting mad at students. It was just a lot of heavy reading, but learning was not optimal. You do need to put in the work, but there are also other courses.

Dr. Y cares a lot about her students but you have to put in the work. Can't slack off in class and definitely have to participate a lot to get the grade. Do your work, talk in class, and meet with TA to get in her good graces. LOTS of reading, but honestly you can get away with not doing all of it, but still need to know what's going on.

This is not about grades because I think of you work hard, you can do well. But I do agree with the review below that there seems to be clear favoritism, shutting down opinions, sends uncomfortable emails to the entire class while not considering how it impacts the students who do their work. The class was overall a very bad experience.

Confusing, vague, and very hard to reach out to. Seems to antagonize anyone who isn't familiar with the content, and throws heavy reading at students. Doesn't seem to care about students beyond a select few. Previous reviews are NOT a reflection of how this professor is.

I LOVE HER! She's so nice! This class is definitely an easy A and it was actually interesting to learn about wars in the Middle East by reading 3 books. Her personal experience in Iran makes her the best to teach this class. 3 3page essays and a group project, grades really easily. The books that we have to read are interesting too! I def recommend

Awesome professor and awesome class. Gives tons of opportunities for extra credit and graded by three 2-page papers and an art project. The lectures are discussion based and all are current and interesting. HIGHLY recommend.

Helped me SO MUCH last semester. I had a rough semester and she was incredibly understanding and did everything she could to help me. She can come off kinda intimidating at first, but she's amazing! Her class was very interesting and wasn't an absurd amount of outside work. Participation is important, but the class environment was welcoming!

There was no hands-on material -- I was lied to! I thought there would be a lot more group work but it ended up being me by myself at night. Visual examples went a long way but could be more interactive.

Sensei is amazing and knows his boundaries (unlike other professors who creep up on their students).

This class and Professor Driscoll were awesome! Class content is super interesting, and Driscoll is hilarious. I will say, the class was very unorganized, which could be a bit stressful, but it doesn't really matter for your grade. Reflection papers, a presentation, midterm paper, and final paper aren't bad at all.

Really nice professor and nice course! Intriguing lectures, only 3 reading reflection papers, one midterm and one final essay with 3-4 pages each, and a group presentation — he even cancelled our final exam! You can definitely learn a lot if you're interested in the course materials.

Mark is incredibly intelligent and truly does want to hear from students. He can get pretty passionate in class but clearly cares so much about the course content. One mini presentation, two papers, and 3 reading responses and his grading is fairly easy. I totally recommend Mark if you want to learn beyond what is commonly taught in these classes.

Driscoll is a great professor but he does not believe in powerpoints. There are 3 reading summaries due throughout the semester, no midterm, a presentation and 2 short (3-4 page) papers. You touch on a different subject each class about whiteness and race. Overall pretty easy class and interesting!
This class is never boring. He is funny in lectures and goes on entertaining tangents. Lots of reading but not really too much. He usually cancels the final too. Will def take another class with him.
Awesome dude and very knowledgeable about Japan. Extremely funny in class and usually just cancels the final if you ask him.
Goated. This is the man you want if you really want to learn something and not just stay comfortable and boring.

Mark is highly unprofessional and completely incapable of separating his political biases from his lectures. He is the sort of person who lacks any nuance in their worldview and makes that worldview their entire identity. If you don't align with his socialist-going-on-communist position you are best served avoiding his class.
Professor Driscoll is such a fking good teacher. I think JAPN 277 is the best class I took throughout my undergrad 4 years. You won't regret for selecting this class.

PLEASEEEE TAKE HIS CLASS. Prof D is so amazing he is a total goof ball and very nice. He is very passionate about the topic. Classes are spent lecturing but he is so lenient. You have 3 400 word journals to complete through out the semester 1 paper midterm 1 paper final (4 pgs). slight work!

Driscoll was one of my best professors this semester. Had so much fun in this course. He always prioritized open and respectful discussion and brought interesting materials relevant to the course theme. One presentation, two papers, three reading reflections, ended up dropping the exam bc of circumstances this semester

Dr. Brodey is one of my favorite professors at UNC! I'm so glad I was able to be in her class my first semester. The class itself was very demanding, with ~150-page readings/long films to complete every class, but they're interesting/fun so it's not the worst. Brodey also is big on participation, so make sure you're comfortable with that. Love her!

Dr. Brodey was very kind, and invited the class over to her house for dinner a couple times. She was nice to talk to, and I enjoyed the class a lot. She offered good feedback on essays when asked. However, the workload was definitely overwhelming at times. We consistently read 150 pages of dense reading for each class, or watched long movies.
She is a really tough grader and rarely provides grading guidelines for rubrics. She also expects a ridiculous amount of effort for a freshman seminar.

professor brodey is knowlegeable, kind, and accessible. lots of reading, but to be expected for an english seminar, and definitely manageable. her grading criteria could be a bit unclear at times but she's always open to explaining! she even invited us over to her house for dinner, she's super sweet.
Professor Brodey is very kind and knowledgeable about Jane Austen. However, the course has an unreasonably heavy workload and her Canvas is both difficult to navigate and frequently wrong.

I would rather retake Gen Chem, pull out my anterior cerebral artery, and lasso a bear with it than take this class again. Expected full-length novels in a week and acted like we only had her class. Gives zero feedback on assignments but continues to grade extremely harshly.

Professor Brodey is very kind and passionate, but the workload is overwhelming. Full novels in under a week and long films in one night made the class feel unrealistic with other commitments. Creative final project, but I wouldn't recommend unless you have lots of free time.

As a Jane Austen fanatic, I was very disappointed. I feel like we did 85% of the teaching. We had group presentations where we taught parts of adaptations or extra readings. Also, lots of group discussion. We read 8 books, so you had 150+ pages due every class, which was impossible. No rubrics for anything. Brodey was very sweet, though.

This class was cool. Lots of reading that corresponds to journal entries, you do not have to read everything. Just get a general understanding of what its about. Essays that are easy, but she never gives a grade on anything. Had no idea where my grade was at the end of the semester, but it felt like I was easily getting an A.

Get ready to read a ton of Jane Austen! However, assignments are very easy and straight-forward (mostly just weekly short forum posts on the reading). The teacher is incredibly kind and understanding, and there are typically chill class discussions every day on the reading.

I took CMPL 130 which I think is listed as 134 on here, but I thoroughly enjoyed this class, however, it was very reading heavy, at times we had to read 300 pages a week. Doesn't give much feedback on essays but is willing to discuss further if you schedule office hours. I enjoyed the diverse selected readings and felt that I learned a lot!

Ms. Brodey is by far my best and favorite teacher this semester. You can tell she cares about each one of her students. The course is heavy on reading but if you don't have time to complete the readings before class, you can choose to simply listen to discussions rather than adding to them. There are no tests or quizzes.

She is easily one of the nicest and best professors I have ever had so far at Carolina. She is so patient in class and so enthusiastic to help students learn. Definitely take Lu Laoshi for Chinese if you get the chance!!!

One of the nicest professors I've ever had, I've enjoyed the class very much! She was very helpful when reading, as if you didn't know the characters, she would help you. The only aspect that's not as good is how slow the assignments were graded.
She is very caring and will help you understand t

Takes a while to put grades in and had some assignments we never discussed, but otherwise she is so kind. She wants to see you succeed and is willing to help for your assignments and projects. Class was chill because we just went over vocab, read the textbook, or did some writing practice. Quiz days are spent reviewing for the quiz, hw is mad light

She's the best. Chinese is a hard language to learn, but she does her best on aiming for personal growth. Being honest, I didn't really deserve an A, as my skill level was lower than my peers. However, I felt that the final grade was based mostly on participation and effort. Definitely take Chinese with her!
She is very helpful and nice. Super caring teacher and very helpful during lectures and reading the passages. I really looked forward to the class on days, but she does take a while to grade.
Lu Laoshi is so sweet and funny. Take this class with her!
Pretty easy if you try like at all. NO HANDWRITING in 305 or 306 on exams. Very nice. I think this class could honestly benefit from more difficulty lol.

周老师 like all UNC Chinese profs is great. 305 felt like it lacked some structure compared to 101-204 but still felt like I learned enough. Anyway, she's sweet, grading is fair and quick, hard to complain.

I really enjoyed class with Zhou laoshi! The lectures were fun, informative, and prepared me for the tests. Zhou laoshi is hilarious and really sweet. She wants all her students to succeed. Also there is barely any homework for most of the semester which is really nice.

she's not bad, but i don't feel like i learned that much in her class. not sure if it's the content or the structure of the class but i feel like my chinese regressed. idek how i got an A it was a miracle or something. quizzes and exams are pretty reflective of the material, except the final, which was garbage, but overall not a bad class

This was my third teacher I've had in the Chinese language department, and I think Zhou Lao Shi did an okay job. I definitely feel like the structure of the class was strange. I didn't feel like I learned from her lectures. I feel like she might be a bit burned out as a teacher, and she didn't feel very personable.

Very relaxed and happy environment. The material is very practical, so no time is wasted. Practice the vocabulary and phrase structures often, and you will be well-prepared for the quizzes. Exams are just a longer version of that. Fun final project presentation.

Zhou Laoshi is caring, alleviates stress off of her students whenever possible, and always makes class enjoyable. Participation matters, as with every language course, but she is accommodating and aware that not every student comes from the same background. The course is practical and tests are straightforward. I'll take a course from her again!

Professor Zhou is one of the kindest professors at UNC, she really wants you to participate and seek feedback on your assignments. In general, her main goal is for your Chinese to improve. Her class is engaging and she is very kind to everyone. I will miss her class!

Zhou Laoshi has a very blunt, but she's really sweet! You will learn a lot. She grades you based on your individual progress, so as long as you work hard its an A. As a heritage speaker, this class was really easy for me, but I still learned a lot! It's so nice to have a teacher that cares about your learning and doesn't want you to stress. TAKE IT

I absolutely love Zhou laoshi. She is so sweet and amazing at engaging the class, very clearly cares about all of her students! She is always encouraging of students attending office hours if they need help and the assignments given to us were all helpful to developing language skills. You are lucky to have her as a teacher!
Zhou Laoshi is literally the best professor I've had at UNC.

Make sure to attend and participate in discussions. Your participation grade starts at an 80. You will have to watch a 1-2 hour film each week and be prepared to talk about it in class. Quizzes are based on the films.
Profe L. was amazing!!! I really recommend her if you want a chill class and great discussions! However, be aware participation REALLY DOES MATTER, so come to class but speak up too!
She should review her way to create engaging ways for people to participate. Some of the questions she proposes are limitated and don't explore as much the materials.

run. did not learn a single thing, and going to class felt like a burden. she's awkward, has unclear expectations, is afraid of giving 100s on assignments, and doesn't even facilitate conversation in the classroom well. all topics feel haphazard, and you won't be able to breeze by this class if that's what you expect.

You'll have to read a lot to even stay up to pace with the class. She has a perception of what is "correct" for documents and if you don't align with that, you'll lose points or get stuck with a somewhat rude answer. For the bigger projects, you also won't have any idea what she wants. She doesn't give rubrics or anything else to go off of.

She said attendance didn't matter but still harshly graded our participation points. Lectures were useless since they were merely discussions among the students, and I saw no value in going to class. She is a very harsh grader on the papers and got confused and gave me someone else's participation points (much lower than I deserved).  Don't.

The class was pretty easy, but I didn't enjoy the content or discussions.  The films were so boring, misogynistic, and inaccurate.  Graded on 5 film responses (pretty easy, can drop one) and 2 papers, no exams.  Attendance doesn't really matter, but participation is graded so take that as you will.  Lots of reading but doesn't really matter.

There are lots of readings, but as long as you skim them or read most of them, you'll do pretty well on the extremely easy quizzes she gives. There are two sort of long essay assignments (and essays on the final) but she grades pretty generously. Overall a good class, definitely take it if you're interested in the subject.
Readings are humongous. Although she is kind, Prof L does not really engage the class in any way. Content is made confusing by her teaching style.

Prof. Lothspeich is a nice professor, but, her class was hard to follow. Her lectures are all over the place and don't make much sense. Two papers and an essay final, with quizzes throughout the semester which are super easy. Would be an interesting class if the subject interest you. Easy if you do the readings and are a good writer for the essays.

Not super clear grading criteria. Her and the TA often didn't know answers to questions. The A cutoff was a 95. Not too difficult if you try and keep up with the readings or find summaries. Worth the effort for the three gen eds though.
