Pamela is by far the most caring professor I've ever had at UNC, although sometimes she can drag on to her lecture, the material itself was interesting but some of it was hard.

Professor Lothspeich is the nicest professor I've had at UNC. The content itself is very interesting and her papers, and other portions of the grade are all very clear, fair, and not too difficult. Sometimes lectures can be a little jumbled and drag on but she is definitely a great choice for classes, especially gen ed requirements.

Professor Lothspeich is a genuinely caring person and an ok professor. ASIA61 was an easy, yet super interesting class. You basically just watch about one film a week and then spend class time discussing it. FYS so no exams, just two papers and weekly reflections. Participation matters.
It's such a pity that I knew him in my senior year. I really wish I can study Japanese with him from freshman

I had his class at 9AM everyday, and I was excited to come to JAPN 101 everyday. Sawamura-sensei is a really good teacher. Like really. There is work to do everyday and his grading might not be the easiest. However, if you keep up with what's assigned by the monthly schedule, you will be guaranteed a good grade in the course. Take Japanese with him
Best teacher ever. You can tell he's really passionate about his job and tries really hard to make every student succeed!

Sawamura-sensei is hands down the best language teacher I've ever had! His lectures are engaging and hilarious, and I found myself excited to come to class each day. As long as you stay on top of the homework, and study for the quizzes (there are a lot!), it's easy to do well in this class. Also, take advantage of the extra credit opportunities!

Don't slack off, keep up, and you shouldn't have trouble making an A in this class. The professor is really kind and funny, but he is on the harsher end when it comes to grading. Make sure your handwriting is legible. Other than that it's a very fun class and think I learned a lot in this class. Highly recommend this class with Sawamura-sensei.

Just do what he tells you and study a bit every week, you'll be guaranteed an A. The quizzes and midterms aren't too hard, and there is a fun group project near the end of the course which helps with your final grade. The final was a little harder than then quizzes and midterms, but they definitely weren't too bad. Would recommend JAPN 101 with him

Oh my goodness I love Sawamura-sensi, and also loved this course. The first month of the course felt really quick, but everything will be fine once you get used to everything. There are lots of quizzes and homework, but they're easy if you just review everything. You'll get full credit for the homework if you submit them on time. Take it!

Great introductory class to Japanese. The class might feel like a lot of work in the beginning, but it really isn't. Study for the quizzes and do the daily homework, after a semester, your Japanese will be completely different after taking this course for a semester. Sawamura sensei is very hilarious and accommodating.

I loved having Sawamura sensei! Be prepared for a lot of homework and weekly quizzes. They arent difficult, but they can be a lot if you don't keep up. Review the material a little bit every day if you can. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities and Sawamura is very helpful. He makes class very fun but be prepared to participate a lot.

Sawamura Sensei made going to my 9am worth it. He's very personable and hilarious. Overall, the class had a lot of work & quizzes almost daily, but if you study you'll be fine. If you are scared of participating, I encourage you to take this class anyways, he's super understanding & helpful. Lots of pair work, so make friends & form study groups!

Sawamura Sensei is just as good a language teacher you can find on this campus, as long as you study and come to class every day following the classroom rules, you will get an A. I've learned a great deal of not only the language, but the culture from after-class conversations with him as well. Very sad that he's not teaching second year Japanese.

I took professor Sawamura in my first year of college, this class is very time consuming I will not lie, it was not hard as long as you did the work, but it can be a lot to handle. Overall, I learned a lot in this class, and I am planning on continuing with japanese, it was very fun and enjoyable and it makes you love the language.

Is Japanese a hard class? Absolutely. That being said, Sawamura Sensei is one of the best language teachers I've ever had. Also, the Japanese dept. at UNC can be really inflexible but is never unfair with exams or quizzes. You do have a ton of in-class quizzes and hw, though. They give out plenty of EC as well so be sure to take advantage of that.

Took his JAPN101 class, amazing as always. JAPN102's class work was a bit more difficult tho. Attendance is optional, but you'll miss a lot of stuff in class. Lots of quizzes, but the schedule he gives you at the beginning will tell you what's due throughout the semester, so it's really your fault if you forget there's a quiz.

I had 101 and 102 with Sawamura-sensei, and this was by far my favorite class. He made learning Japanese fun and engaging. As long as you make sure you study for quizzes and exams, you will do fine. Lots of opportunities for extra credit. I will definitely miss taking Japanese with Sawamura-sensei.

I took Sawamura-sensei for both JAPN 101 and 102, and he is a terrific professor. He is funny, kind, and has a lot of enthusiasm for teaching Japanese. A lot of quizzes (and homework), but they are extremely straight-forward and fair. JAPN 102 grammar is harder than 101, so study! The best language professor I've taken to date, strongly recommend!

Sawamura sensei completely made my freshman year at UNC. I was astonished at how well I absorbed information when it was taught in a fun and engaging way. Genuinely such a kind soul that loves to see his students succeed. If you were to take a language here I would recommend taking as many Japanese levels as you can with Sawamura sensei.

Sawamura Sensei  10/10. Super kind, funny, sensible, gets the job done & then some. He's so awesome and his classes have such a positive vibe. The daily/every other day quizzes kind of killed my grade, but only because my attendance was spotty. He's a gem of a language instructor!

The class environment was great; everyone always seemed to enjoy class, every time. There were roughly 2-3 quizzes every week, but if you studied, they were easy. I even once asked Sawamura Sensei if I could do office hours outside of the usual time, and he agreed and I asked him questions for half an hour straight, all because he made time for it
Overall, this class was ok. I felt like the workload was manageable and easy to get a good grade. However, I didn't like the attendance policy with only a single absence for the entire semester.

Dr Bergeton clearly cares a lot about the content but his lectures were not very captivating as someone who didn't already have a passion for the topic. I did enjoy the freedom in the final paper which allowed me to dive into really any aspect of Qin and Han history/culture. If you already know you love the topic, you'll enjoy this more than I did.
hard course but he is a nice guy.the materials are hard though, i don't know the stories in the slides even though I'm a Chinese
Good professor take his class
uffe is so nice in class and is really gentle during lectures, but the grading is absolutely horrible. TA also grades really irresponsibly.
He is a tough grader. His lecture is really boring. He never check his email and always be busy during his office hours.

Dr. Bergeton explained things very well, and I have learned a lot from him. 

Although the course was challenging, I have learned a lot from him, and I will 100% take a course taught by him again. 

Thank you Dr. Bergeton!

There are quite a lot of readings, but they all relate in a way and most of the readings are online. 2 essays, one being the midterm, and the final being a 10pg paper along with a 5 min presentation. He is a very generous grader and the lectures were pretty interesting. He holds office hours for essay critique so you can score better on the essays.

Overall, decently easy gen-ed. If you're familiar with some Chinese history, this class shouldn't be difficult at all. There were a lot of readings and this class was very performance-based (90% of grade based on tests and papers). Tests were fairly easy but get ready to do some timed-writing

Yes, he is one of the smartest professors; yes, he is old-fashioned; yes, he is so very slow with grading; yes, the lectures get dry; yes, you will get an A if you put some effort into reading and throwing in a few of his vocab into the essays.
Great professor. He learns China a lot, if you follow his instruction you can get good grade. be prepared to read Chinese classics (in english)

Professor Bergeron is really sweet! A lot of people didn't like his lectures and assignments but he just really cares about the material and you can tell. There was a LOT of reading. Few papers but he expected them to be done very well. Overall the class was not too bad but definitely a lot of work towards the middle and end.

Though I did learn a lot I would NEVER recommend this professor. He never answered emails and would cut me off in office hours. He said he wanted students to participate but when people did, he seemed annoyed. The workload was pretty light, but the class got extremely boring after a while. He is passionate about the subject but very condescending.

He is very passionate about the class and its material but he lectured for most of the class period every day and they were incoherent lectures that didn't make sense. He assigned long readings and then didn't use them during class. He is a VERY slow grader. In general, he seemed very unprepared for class every day.

Very enthusiastic and clear lecture style, though occasionally erring on the side of restating some points too much. Not a harsh grader, but reading the course materials makes a lot of difference for the assignments. Great class for anyone interested in the topic.

He was a decent professor. Readings were assigned but not used in class. He graded on 3 essay papers. He definitely has his point of view and if you disagree he makes it pretty clear he doesn't agree, but overall the class was pretty easy. His Powerpoints are pretty unorganized and not really used in the class.

The class itself was interesting, but Bergeton is a lecturer who stood and spoke with a slideshow for 1h30m each day. The readings were required, but I never did them and got an A in the class so don't let that scare you. Overall, an alright class but not a lot of room for discussion or disagreement because if you do, he can become condescending.

He never answers emails. He teaches in such a dry manner. He does not care about students at all. He is frankly rude to students. He is super unclear about dates and randomly changes the syllabus and assignment dates. He changed class from in person to online within an hour of class FIVE times this semester.

He may teach but he is not a teacher.

Pretty nice dude and interesting to talk to outside of class, but his lectures were pretty boring. He brought insight into what we read, but he was pretty monotone throughout the entire class. His exams and papers were a little difficult, but going to see him about it and studying a little more than normal and you'll do fine.

Exams test super-detailed stuff from the readings. Lectures are boring and dry. Never respond to emails. Recitations are not helpful at all. Paper grading is super vague and not lenient. Doesn't provide a rubric.

I took this class for a gen ed having no prior knowledge about Japan, and it ended up being my favorite class I took this semester. Dr. Pitelka is SO kind, SO caring, and you can see how passionate he is about what he teaches. I could not recommend this class and this professor enough! and almost no homework is a plus (worksheets are done in class)

Understands the text that he teaches, but overall an incredibly text level professor. Has an impressive resume with accolades like a Watson Fellowship and various grants, but his teaching style left a lot to be desired. If you're looking for mentorship, it might be better to check out his published work instead of relying on his class for guidance.

TAKE FIRST YEAR SEMINAR W/ HIM!!! So kind, genuinely fascinating guy. He will be on sabbatical next fall but will be back in 2025. Reading discussion posts once a week, no tests, easy group project as final. He made a healthy environment where everyone was comfortable with each other quickly! There's one week where you play samurai video games!

Dr. Pitelka is an incredible instructor. He is very passionate about what he teaches, his grading is clearly outlined and fair, and the course is not difficult as long as you participate in class. He is also so supportive of his students and is very accessible outside of class. I would take another Asian studies course just to have him again!!

Mr. Pitelka was an amazing teacher, and its evident he also loves what he teaches. Genuinely cares for his students and makes a history intensive class not difficult. Will take one of his classes again.

Professor Pitelka is a very nice person and very knowledgeable in Japanese history. He knows what he's talking about and is passionate about this subject. The class itself is very interesting but doesn't really relate to the homework or the exams (its fully based on the assigned reading). Be aware that the exams weigh 45% which is very heavy.

Some people were born to do things in this world. Dr. Pitelka was born to teach Japanese History. This class was awesome and he is extremely knowledgeable on the subject. He has spent years in Japan and answers any question you might have on the time period. He is also very accessible outside of class. Great guy and great class.

He is a really good professor, at times the lecture could feel like it was dragging on but that could also be because I have 3 classes before this one. You can tell he knows what he is talking about and he values student connections. I'm excited to take the second half of the course!

Professor Pitelka is one of those professors who you should go out of your way to take a class with. He is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about what he is teaching that it rubs off on students. His lectures are great! He also grades very fairly. I definitely wouldn't say it's an easy A, but if you do what he asks, you will get an A.

Proffesor Yaqub put together interesting readings, but was not a great lecturer. She often goes off topic and doesn't get into the meat of her lecture. She also will try and keep you after class is over to continue her lecture if she got off topic. I wish she was a better lecturer because what she has to say is often very interesting.

These classes are not easy, it is very reading heavy and she is a harsh grader. But she really cares about students and is very understanding of any outside circumstances you might have, which can't always be said for other proffessors at UNC. I was very grateful that she was so understanding.

I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Yaqub is very knowledgeable and approaches the subject very well. She is a little disorganized, and the class is reading heavy, especially for the first two exams. Other than that, I enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

Super interesting and intelligent professor! I loved the Palestinian literature and films that we read/watched during this class. I gained a lot of important knowledge. She probably would be better in a smaller class though.
Not recommended. she is always unprepared to class which makes it hard to follow

Lectures can be pretty hard to follow. The test relies too much on lectures and ppt slides. If you find lost with study guides or how to prepare for the test, just approach the TAs. Some might be unwelcoming or not very enthusiastic but the one I usually had the review sessions was superb.

20% of your grade for the class is the test. She harshly shuts down people's opinions if they don't match her own. Big classes are not her forte, maybe she would be better in a small class. The content is interesting but she rarely stays on topic. Test is class attendance heavy.

This class is really not that bad. It's interesting and I learned a lot. That being said, Nadia was not a good lecturer. She's clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches, but she just doesn't do a good job teaching to such a large body of students. Students should know that her unit focuses on the Israel-Palestine conflict.

She seems to not be open to students perspectives. She quickly shuts down peoples opinons and judges people harshly. She does not stick to her PowerPoints, and instead will go off on tangents that do not relate to the test material. She is hard to follow and does not seem like a genuine, caring, person. I would not take another class with her.

Her lectures and exam were centered around multiple readings and videos during the weeks she taught so as long you do those, you will be perfectly fine. She cares a lot about her content which is very apparent during her lectures. Overall good lecturer.
interesting readings, lectures can be confusing. the tests are not bad if you pay attention in lecture and review the slides

I had Nadia for Borders and Boundaries and she honestly just could not lead a clear lecture well. Everything felt very frazzled and the way that she presented her content was a bit unclear. Overall I would probably not take this class if I had another option, the tests were graded very harshly and randomly by TAs.
She's a caring teacher she's just all over the dang place and it seems like she can't control her own thoughts, not the best lecturer

Lots of reading and movie-watching, with boring lectures. Is not a good lecturer, but tries her best and is very nice. She was hampered by the other 2 professors, overall not awful, but would be better in a smaller class.

I took my first-year seminar with Dr. Yaqub and absolutely loved it. She was a very caring teacher and really encouraged the class to participate. Expect daily homework in this class, but nothing over the top.

This class had a homework assignment every day but none were graded until the end of the semester when they were looped into one cumulative grade. The final project is a group project, and all the groups have very different prompts. There are a lot of readings and films to watch. However, I could tell she was really passionate about the material.
average. wasn't a good lecturer for a big class, but wasn't the hardest prof for the course.

Professor Yaqub is a great person and is passionate about her work. However, in the new course setting she was often hard to hear during lectures. She assigned lots of reading but reading quizzes were moderate difficulty. Even though she's great, don't sign up for this class, it will be too much on your work load for a gen ed.

Generally a fine instructor, she was helpful in office hours and helped me understand what I needed to study for the midterm. She assigned SO MANY MOVIES. And books. This class has a quiz for every class meeting and the questions are very specific. I wouldn't take a class with her again but she's not the worst B&B professor.

Her lectures were somewhat boring and often more about artistic interpretation than borders, etc. When she isn't talking about a book or a movie she is actually pretty interesting. This class isn't hard at all if you just put in the base amount of effort, but Yaqub could have been better. She also has a notable bias towards Palestine.

Took Arab 407 with Prof. Doria and currently in Arab 408. The topics are interesting and the class is easy. She's very caring and lenient but gives a lot of work. The work amount is justified since the class is just a conversation. You must do the reading or watch the movie in order to participate. If you speak Arabic, give it a try.

Doria is very sweet and caring and is always willing to take additional time to explain the language and Arab history and culture; she also has easy tests. That being said, the class isn't too enjoyable because of the heaps of HW (1-2 hours/night) and unclear class calendar. Just make sure you show up and don't fall behind on HW or it'll be tough.

Doria means well, but it's hard to do well in her class. She constantly talks about how she's sad students are stressed, but grades on unclear guidelines & doesn't teach grammar. I did corrections AND extra credit, and she told me she wouldn't give me the points back because I already had a "good enough" grade. I wish someone else was teaching 204.

Professor Doria is the sweetest person. She gives a good amount of homework that is crucial to learning the material, so it is for good cause. She is very lenient with due dates if you speak with her about it and she is not at all a tough grader. If you want to learn Arabic and are excited about doing so, you should have no trouble in her class.

Ustaaza Doria really emphasizes language immersion and speaks only in Arabic for nearly the entire class period. She also has a lot of cultural knowledge and is eager to share it with students. The homework was excessive, usually amounting to 3-4 hours of homework a day, but she tried to be flexible with everyone and sometimes accepted late work.

Dr. Shemer's lectures are interesting. If you don't know a lot about Jerusalem, sometimes it can be difficult to follow some of the concepts he talks about, but he's always willing to answer questions and clarify when needed. Great person!

If you're taking it for the Gen-Ed, be aware that it's a decent amount of work, & unless you're really interested in film, you probably won't enjoy it. Dr. Shemer is very caring and a generous grader, but lectures can be mind-numbing. If you do the readings, watch the films, and participate, you WILL get an A, but don't expect a fun class.

Seems like a nice guy but I dreaded going to class. Drones on and on and I had a hard time following. On tests and essays he wanted me to parrot back what he taught, didn't appreciate me putting in my own perspective on things. A deep dive into Middle Eastern Cinema, but I came out of it still not understanding why that was important.

Highly recommend Professor Shemer. A lot of readings but interesting content, especially if you are interested in film studies. Class is almost entirely discussion, he values people who are vocal & do the readings. He is kind and invested in his student's success.

Professor Shemer was obviously deeply knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter. While I personally do not even remotely care about Israeli cinema and psychoanalysis, his sheer enthusiasm was enough to get me through the lectures. He offers generous extra credit opportunities, so you should be able to succeed by virtue of showing up.

He gave me an 86.99 on purpose and wouldn't round to an 87, even though I was deserving of an A in the class by his own grading. The whole semester he was giving me A's until I said in class I disagree with him. The entire class is pro-Palestinian propaganda under the disguise of an Israeli class, and an absolute shame to the Israeli community.

Prof Shemer is a great professor who is able to convey information about the complexity of culture by analyzing several facets of the lived experience. He sometimes goes on tangents but overall I really enjoy the class discussions we have and the media we get to watch. Overall, I think he is a really great professor.

I love Prof Shemer. ASIA 425 (Beyond Hostilities: Collaborations in Culture between Israelis and Palestinians) was an incredible course. There are a lot of readings but he is a fair grader. Sometimes, he can go on tangents but the material was really fascinating and I could not recommend this class more.

The professor is great! He really made me think of Israeli cinema on a deeper level and the films watched were very interesting. There is not too much work to be done outside of class; as long as you at least scan the reading for the lecture/discussion you will be fine. He grades work very fairly and he wants you to succeed. Wonderful course!
I found the class not having enough of the Palestinian perspective or very diluted. He also took away the Zoom option and was not flexible with problem going through circumstances.
Yaron Shemer is a horrendous professor.

Cai 老师 was genuinely such an amazing professor! She was so sweet and caring and really made it super fun to learn Chinese. Attendance is part of your grade and she will cold call on you during class but its all part of learning. I made so many friends in this class simply because of the way she encourages you to talk with those around you. TAKE HER

Very engaging class, but makes the tough language exciting to learn! Lots of homework and tests but very manageable and helpful. She is very understanding and gives great feedback, I would recommend to take her class if you can!

She is a very nice person, very good teacher, and wants all students to learn. I have no clue how you would do well in 101 if you have not taken before. It isn't necessarily the hardest course, but just a lot of work everyday.
Tough language but great teacher for the subject, she is super kind and helpful!
amazing kind professor, very lenient with grading and will give you answers/hints during tests.

Cai Laoshi very nice and friendly. She is by far one of the nicest, if not the nicest, professor I've had at UNC. If you're scared of Chinese because of its reputation ofor being a hard language, don't be and take it with her. She is very caring, and this class is very beginner friendly. Just do what she asks, and this class will be an easy A.

Cai Lao Shi is a very caring and understanding instructor. She's SO sweet and actually wants you to learn the language. Since the class itself is a 4 credit class, it is assignment and quiz heavy! Make sure to divide your work up and you should be fine. I would 100% take her again!!

Cai Laoshi is genuinely such an amazing and caring professor. I look forward to attending class and even though Chinese is hard, she is great at teaching. Easy to get an A as long as you do homework and study for tests

I had no experience with Chinese before Cai Laoshi's class but she is an amazing teacher. On tests, she'll give us little "hints" which is also super helpful. There is a $100 textbook but majority of the learning is done in class. As long as you review vocab and grammar, you'll do well in her class

Great teacher. Makes you really learn Chinese. Go to class and study before quizzes and tests and you'll get a good grade. I probably averaged about 4-5 hours of chinese work per week -- which might sound like a lot, but its not tough work. Overall awesome experience and I highly recommend her.

Chinese is a hard language, but I feel you have to TRY to fail Cai Laoshi's class. Even if you never study, you're still set up for success on any unit exam as long as you participate in class and do the lesson homework.

Cai Laoshi is such a sweetheart! So nice and helps make the difficult topics clearer. She really wants you to practice speaking in class but it's low pressure. Graded on hw, vocab quizzes, character writing, 6 tests, and a final. The difficult part is learning the language; she doesn't make it harder than it already is. TAKE HER!!!
Great lecturer. Class meets often and homework was very manageable. Continuing with Chinese!
So good! Had her for 101 as well, stellar professor.
Caring, friendly, and accessible! Her office hours are a great chance to practice speaking, go visit her!!

Amazing professor and class. If you're nervous about taking Chinese with her, don't be. It will be your favorite class. So sweet and caring. You will get called on to speak multiple times a class but it's low pressure and she'll help you if you aren't sure what's going on lol. She's the best! TAKE THIS CLASS.

Cai Laoshi is the best professor I've had at UNC. I was nervous about taking Chinese, but she made it such a great experience. She is incredibly patient, non-judgmental, and caring when it comes to learning the language. The class is well-structured, interactive, and so much fun! Looking forward to CHIN-102 in the Spring.
Professor Cai is so sweet and a wonderful teacher! The more you can speak with her, the better.

Cai Laoshi is one of my favorite Professors at UNC, and is an amazing choice for CHIN 101!! The class has a great format, she provides many resources to succeed, super kind and caring, and is always available outside of class. Highly recommend taking CHIN with her!

Good prof for a relatively easy course. Honestly, it was an ok class - the readings were helpful but you would discuss them in class in small groups so keep that in mind - lectures tended to be one reading behind. Grade was made up of 'participation', assignments (really easy papers), midterm, final, and oral history project
Don't take this course unless you have a strong interest in the subject matter. Harsh grader and very dry.

Enjoyed the class overall. It did have some readings, but if you pay attention to the lectures, the readings do not matter as much. She is very nice and accessible outside of class, but she does require you to know very niche details from the slides on the exams, so just be aware of that.

Worst class I ever took.
1. Four 2-page reflection papers but have to write at least 4-page research papers to get above B.
2. Dry and meaningless lecture, random group discussion. 
3. Extremely harsh grading on tests. It asks for every detail and is unable to finish on time. 
Just watching great YouTube videos for Korean history is much better.

I took this class for a gen-ed. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ARE NOT INTERESTED IN IT. The class consists of four main papers, a midterm, and a final. The test are extremely difficult and specific. The professor is very nice and provides lots of extra credit opportunities, but again DO NOT take if you are not interested in Korean History.

Dr. Jo's class was not that bad. For Fall 2022, our grades were based on 4 film reviews, a midterm, and a final exam. In class, she focused a lot on group discussions and the exams were straight from the ppts. I suggest following the study guide she gives out. Only thing was that the papers were slightly hard bc her grading criteria was unclear.

She wasn’t my favorite. Every time I go to her office hours she has a condescending tone about her. I’d ask for help with something & she’d always point out what I was doing wrong. Her expectations are extremely high. The class would be more enjoyable if taught by someone who appreciated their students efforts learning new material.

Her tests are incredibly difficult, and large portions of your grade rely on group projects. I HATE the way she organizes her canvas. Arguably the most engaging and easy to understand class of the semester was the day our TA taught the lesson. Also 2 points are taken off your semester grade for every class you miss starting day one. Good otherwise.

2 tests, 4 individual assignments, and 4 group assignments ending with the final research project. Tests were moderately difficult; use flashcards for vocab and practice quizzes for question style. Focused mostly on application. No final, just comment on other projects. Great instructor, super experienced and friendly if you showed you cared.

Prof. Entwisle is nice, but she will get mad if ur on ur phone. The class is okay, basically one big group project the whole semester and the grading criteria for it is unclear, and if u miss a class its 2 pts off ur overall grade. It was not hard to get a B+ or an A, but only take this if ur interested in the subject, or ur gonna be really bored.

Barbara is VERY knowledgeable, but she occasionally was condescending when speaking to students. Her feedback was great and fair, but sometimes grading was harsh. Overall not bad, but I wouldn't choose to take her again.

Barbara is amazing and clearly knows what she's talking about. The class was pretty easy, there were clear rubrics for everything, and you learn a lot about research processes. Exams were a bit tricky with vague study guides, but its fine cause you can ace everything else. Lots of group work, so depending on your group you may have more work.

Prof Entwisle can be a good prof at times but sometimes it feels like she has 0 humanity. There were several times people expressed concerns and she seemed like she couldn't care less. We had two tests that were less than 10% of our grade and I failed both and still got out with a B. Easy B to pass but no one felt great about tests.

Professor Entwisle was very knowledgeable about the subject. The individual assignments were easy and graded fairly, but the semester-long group project was somewhat difficult and graded harshly. Also, the multiple choice questions on the tests were unnecessary difficult.

It is evident that Dr. Entwisle knows her stuff and is passionate about the course. TA gave very vague feedback which was frustrating. Odd grade scale (ex. a test is 8 points). Tests are difficult. She is very understanding about attendance as long as you communicate. The course is tough but Barbara really cares.

Assignments were generally easy to complete and the material wasn't hard but the exams felt like you were set up to fail. There wasn't any one I spoke to who felt confident about the exams so no matter how much you study, its not going to work out. Also the group projects felt repetitive.

Prof Entwisle makes class easy enough, but the big project we worked on all semester was broken into small assignments that felt repetitive. No tests or quizzes though, just open-note in-class assessments, which was great.

FAVORITE PROFESSOR. Prof Caren is funny and his lectures are intriguing. Participation is counted through PollEv, be in class. Class is built off many assignments and lots of things to boost average. Exams had some very difficult questions but were overall ok! He had movie days to help you understand content, must partipation on slack for credit.

Professor Caren is a great person and teacher. Super straight forward with exams and assignments a seems like he wants students to succeed. The 2 midterms and final exam weren't overly difficult. The assignments and homeworks were actually pretty interesting and engaging. Overall highly recommend SOCI 101 with prof Caren.

Prof Caren is such an amazing professor, even in a 300 person lecture. He keeps it interesting and interactive, he will always humor you. You watch films in which you expected to participate in a chat group. Overall a pretty light class. The tests are very application based so it really comes down to how well you understand the material.
Take SOCI with Caren. Research Assignments can be a decent amount of work but exams are easy if you study. One of the best teachers ive had at UNC

Overall a great professor and class (boring sometimes), very understanding, gave tons of opportunities for EC, so go to class! Only 3 exams total and he makes everything very enjoyable. 10 Research Assignments that can be fun but also a good bit of work, but he offers regrades, so do them and get a 100. Overall totally recommend, he's awesome

Lowk chill asf class. Lectures can get quite boring at times, but you have to attend them since you are graded on participation from an active polling throughout lecture. Exam midterms avg 70 questions and final 130ish mcq. I didn't use the textbook since it is just vocab and appliance based so I just studied the term definitions & did practice q.
Cool guy, easy class, sometimes boring but I'd take boring over evil any day.
Exams are tough, but the overall class grade is determined by a lot of different things.  RA projects help to boost the grade as long as you put effort into them. Textbook reading is long
Great guy, great professor, and so interesting.
This dude is amazing. Fantastic professor. Ethnography can be a bit time consuming.

This was one of my most favorite classes I've taken at UNC. While you do have to put work in in reading, getting to know your character, and writing and memorizing speeches, this class truly helps you become a better public speaker. There is no judgement and the more you engage with the material and design of the class, the more fun it is.

Professor Caren is an amazing professor with such a welcoming personality. I took this course to fulfill my minor, and it was a great class with wonderful people in it as well. We have speeches to give, but the process leading up to the speeches is structured so well that you truly shouldn't feel scared. Take his class, you'll love it!

He is so funny and I would retake his class. Although my friends who had other professors for Soci 101 said their exams were easy, which is the downside to taking his, I found his exams to be challenging after spending days studying to prepare. However, if you follow the criteria for the homework, you get a 100, so it's a pretty easy course.
One of the best professors at UNC. Take Soci 101 with Professor Caren, you won't regret it.
Great guy -- gave everyone a free 100% on a midterm!

This is the goat of Sociology 101. We all got 100s on our last mideterm since more than 60% of the class didn't take it(He stated if more than 60% of students get a question wrong it will be given full points). Not much work other than Research Apllications and Inquizzitives. Pollev is used for attendance. Overall show up and it's an easy A.

Neal Caren is THE SWEETEST prof you will ever take at UNC. Everyday, he arrives so excited to teach and engage with students. He is extremely knowledgeable and makes his course engaging with online polls and halftime quiz games (i got to play soci family feud on LDOC). Easy homework, bi weekly assignments, 1 midterm exam, 1 final exam.

Wow. One of the funniest and nicest professors of all time. Tons of easy extra credit. The only downside is having to write about 3600 words of "research applications" throughout the semester. But even as someone who hates writing, take this class.The exams are easy and he made a custom quiz website so you can study for the exams in no time at all.

I love Prof. Caren.  His lectures are sometimes boring but more often than not fun.  The assignments are very easy, and you don't have to read the textbook.  There are 2 midterms and a final but he'll replace your midterm with the final if you do better.  I would highly recommend him to everyone!
The BEST professor. He's amazing, I love his class.

Dr. Cai is clearly an expert, but cannot teach. Flipped classroom model for a math and computer science heavy course with an unhelpful textbook. Excelled at statistics and still found this course dehumanizing. Everyone I know is teaching themselves and struggling horribly. Stay away or take the formerly required SOCI251 counterpart first.

Such a nice guy who is really passionate about what he teaches. The lectures can get boring at times but in general the content is interesting, and the workload is pretty light. There's one midterm and he gives a very comprehensive study guide, 6 homework assignments that don't take too long, and a few short pop-quizzes that are also very chill.

Dr. Cai is a great professor. Only two exams (1 midterm and a final). Other than that the only assignments are homework. He does say he will give pop quizzes at times, but they arent scary and only a few questions (i only took 2).  The homework grade depends on ur TA. he provides the readings. he is sweet and is passionate about what he teaches!
dont listen to the othre reviews that he is bad. yes, his lectures are dry, but he is actually such a sweetheart and funny. he gave a study guide before midterm. 6 hw's, 1 midterm, 1 final.

Don't listen to the review that says he's the worst prof at UNC. Dr. Cai genuinely cares about his students. While his explanations can be a bit confusing at times, the course content isn't too difficult and he let us do make-up quizzes for our second midterm since the average was in the 60s. Content is similar to STOR155 (stats), plus you learn R

WORST PROFESSOR AT UNC-DO NOT TAKE!!! Textbook and lectures are from a free online website-he doesn't make his own materials and when students as questions he doesn't know how to explain any of it. No rubrics given for anything, no practice exams, and no realistic expectations. He gets frustrated easily, not helpful if struggling. Taught myself.

Professor Cai is a brilliant instructor who deeply cares about his students. The material in this class is very straightforward, and Professor Cai does an excellent job making his lectures engaging. The tests were easy and there is only 1 homework assignment every week.

Dr. Cai is the sweetest professor. His grading system is extremely fair, with hw/extra credit to balance the exams. There is no reason for you not to get an A. He does open-note exams, and again, they are very accessible if you put in a little effort. I technically didn't need his class for my major, but it was a wonderful elective.

Professor Yong is a very kind, lighthearted and funny professor. I wish his class was more organized because he is clearly very passionate about his lectures but most students use the time as a study hall practically. You end up teaching yourself...

It's clear that Professor Cai cares about his students and is very knowledgeable about research. However, he has difficulty explaining the concepts in a way for students to understand. His lectures confused me more than I was. The textbook is more of a workbook and explains no concepts. Be ready to teach yourself. No clear rubrics for anything.

Professor Cai isn't the best lecturer but as long as you read the book and teach the majority of the information to yourself you will be fine. Grades consisted of weekly Homework and Labs, occasional quizzes, and three exams. Difficult questions unless you study. Not an impossible course, learn R as well.

Stat was really hard and confusing. Nothing was that hard just confusing and weird. Prof Cai has a thick accent so if that is distracting for you I wouldn't recommend because lectures are so helpful in understanding the content. Midterm and final were hard.

Professor Cai is incredibly out of touch with his students. He lectures all class long (boring lectures) and does not interact with us, and then gives us exams that over half the class fails because they are way too long and test us on content most of us don't understand. Pretty sure he doesn't know any of our names. Not sure how I will pass...

She's the most incredible professor I have ever seen by far. Her grading was really clear and fair, but the class as a whole demanded a lot since we had short essays due almost every week. If you need to take soci101, def take it with her!!
This was my favorite class I have taken this semester! She is a great professor and I recommend everyone take this class.
So Free. Literally Take notes and do ur work for a guaranteed A. ZERO flexibility on missing assignments or turning in late tho, so if you do that even once you might be cooked.

She is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Her lectures are very information heavy but it you pay attention and take notes then everything is easy for her exams. She knows how to keep people engaged and is very funny. Def recommend her for everyone!!!

Dr. Guzzo is such an amazing woman and professor. Genuinely hilarious, cares about the subject, and tests are very straightforward and easy if you go to class. If you need to take Soci 101, take it with her for sure. Hardest part of the class is remembering to do the reading responses.

Allow me the honor of telling you how AMAZING Professor Guzzo was. Funny, intriguing, and passionate, Professor Guzzo was always available and open during class. Her slideshows were easy to follow and informative, the readings were chill, and the hardest parts were the reading response papers, which you could easily forget about.

He's not a bad guy, but he takes forever to grade. Put everything into studying for the exams as they are the vast majority of your grade. He will frequently cancel class due to various reasons, but I see that as a positive. All in all, he teaches a fine class, but I would recommend another sociology instructor due to the amount of work required.
just save your GPA and avoid this guy. hopefully he gets laid off soon!
never posted grading criteria, told me id get an A if i got above 90%, gave me an A- for a 92

Professor Lammers is a great guy, very understanding, nice, and leads a good lecture. The class itself is suuuuper easy. Two papers, two midterms, pop quizzes, and a non-cumulative final. Exams are solely vocab. Point-based grading scale, which makes exams very heavy, make sure not to fall behind because of them. Takes forever to grade anything.

I tell everyone to take this class as an easy focus capacity. That being said, it is easy if you are good at memorization and able to remember definitions very well. Exams are fair and he gives a study guide with all the terms you need to know. He is definitely funny and I enjoyed his lectures.

Not an easy focus capacity as expected. Grades are based mostly on two midterms and a final, so one bad exam can hurt a lot. Pop quizzes exist but don't count much. Lecture slides aren't posted, and study guides aren't very helpful. Limited support overall.

Lammers is a great professor, especially if you talk to him outside of class. I do think the exams were graded too heavily and unfairly and he never responded to emails. I still enjoyed the class and would recommend to anyone, however I do wish he listened to feedback. He is very knowledgeable and he made the lectures interesting and fun.

Take a different professor. He's dry and convinced he's a sociology genius. Class was boring and he doesn't post the slides. It's not awful, if you're a good enough student you won't need to pay attention. but it's still a drag. I never did a single reading and did okay.
take any other sociology 101 professor. you'll have a much easier time.

The class itself isn't difficult, but the teacher makes the class leagues harder than it needs to be. He doesn't post his lecture slides, which he goes through very fast, and the study guides he does post don't prepare you enough for the exam material. If you have him pls take pictures of the slides, or you won't have any study material for exams.

This guy is chill, but wants you to fail. He doesn't post any lecture slides, and he moves way too fast, so you're struggling to write everything down. He doesn't give a clear explanation, mostly just definitions and scrambled thoughts. Also, he will not work with you if you miss a quiz; he clearly does not care.

He can be nice but DO NOT TAKE HIS COURSE AT ALL! I literally and begging you all to not listen to the comments other this one, even if it's your last hope. This prof will not give you your grades until last day or any feedback. His classes are not worth it, choose any other professor. I am praying you to listen because I and others wished we did.

Amazing professor. I have taken all three of his classes and have enjoyed them all greatly. He is fun, the readings are interesting, and the exams are directly based off the practice exams. Expectations are clear and the class is enjoyable. Attendance is NOT mandatory.

He cannot be reached outside of class, besides office hours.

Lammers is awesome, if you need a chill class you should definately take something with him. His exams are very straightforward, and there aren't very many assignments. Just know he is completely unreachable outside of class.

Not sure why Professor Lammers has such a low rating. Attendance is not mandatory, but there are occasional once question quizzes that he even posts the prompts to so you can prepare for them in advance. His lectures can get boring and you need to be in class to know the material for the three exams. But, if you study, the class is pretty easy.

You can tell he's a nice guy, but he doesn't care about teaching this class. Pretty disorganized and has to cancel a lot because of health issues. Tests are fair, but quizzes and assignments are worth very few points so almost all of your grade is dependent on the two midterms and final.

If you want to take a class where the prof doesn't teach, cancel class often, no feedback on work, and post grades only on the last day of class. This is an easy class, but honestly, the most boring and useless prof. Will not respond to contact info and the TA also sucks

He is absolutely hilarious, but we had like 5-6 primary assignments, there were a couple of pop quizzes based on readings, but they were straight-forward he is a tad unorganized but overall this is not a hard class and all tests are purely vocab if you pay attention and come to class (or have a friend in class willing to share notes) you'll be fine

Definitely come to lectures or you won't know what's going on. Springs a lot of pop quizzes on you, and this semester he saved all of them till the very end of the semester. Exams are weird and kind of confusing. Definitely make sure you read, too.

Prof. Lammers is one of those professors who, if you come lecture, you'll be fine. There are two exams + a final + 2 papers. The two exams are basically vocabulary exams, which you can find on Quizlet, and you'll be fine. The only downside is that there are "pop quizzes", which come from the assigned readings, SUPER EASY! The papers are super easy!

Professor Gonzalez, if you are reading this, I would just like you to know that was one of the most unfair final exams I've ever taken. For someone who understood every single of the concepts we went over on the exam review, and who understood all of the definitions of everything, I should not be getting a 68. You tricked us on half of the question

The class content wasn't difficult and it was really interesting! With that, Prof. Gonzalez did not give clear instructions, lectures were awkward & structured around talking with your "families," changed classrooms and never sent an announcement about it, showed up late to class often, and doesn't post slides/goes through content incredibly fast.

Attendance was technically not mandatory but basically was to get notes and to know about in-class assignments. Never posted any information on assignments, so it was really hard to know what was expected. Readings were incredibly long. Also does not believe in posting slides for students, which makes studying hard even if you took good notes.

Although the class was not difficult, I would not recommend it. Dr. Gonzalez had a bad attitude and seemed to dislike their students. They were strict on due dates, yet showed up late to every class and was even a no show once. They were pushy to get the class to participate and it made lectures full of awkward silences and uncomfortable tension.

The content was interesting but I wouldn't take again. Attendance isn't mandatory but you can't make up assignments and slides aren't posted, so you have to go. LONG readings. Sometimes unclear instructions on assignments because they aren't posted anywhere. Bare minimum Canvas. No rubric given before the in class essay midterm.
doesn't accept doctors notes? says attendance doesn't matter but can't make anything up
If you miss class she won't let you make up assignments even if you have a doctors note from the school and also doesn't follow the UAAO rules. BAD TEACHER DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!
Doesn't really accept late work and very strict on assignments and the way she grades is kind of like we are taking a Phd class.

This is a boring class, especially if you're a STEM student who's just taking it for the gen ed. That being said, it's also ridiculously easy to get an A in. Professor Gonzalez is a nice person, but not the most organized or clear when it comes to grading policies. Take this class if you want an easy A and don't mind mind-numbing lectures.

this is for her first year seminar, soci 89. she is actually the coolest person ever and so chill. has a genuine interest in sociology and cares so much about the well being of her students. my favorite class I took all semester. I hope to take another class with her again sometime!! very easy grader and just wants to see you try.

There is so much reading and the points from the readings are unclear. The lectures (?) are boring - it's mostly just her having you discuss with your group for 8-10 minutes at a time. Expectations for assignments are unclear. The material is pretty easy but the structure and her attitude are just so bad.

This class consists of lots of readings for homework that are quite long. In class, participation is expected, and she will wait for a group to answer if nobody is. There are two exams which are pretty easy if you learn the topics and generally what each reading is about. The class activities are engaging, and the graded homeworks are easy.

There was a lot of reading for the class. The class was a lot of effort, considering its a 100 lvl course. The exams were based off the lectures, so take good notes and study those notes. Usually all multiple choice, around 40-50 questions. 4 exams. If you study the lectures you should be able to get A or B.

Such a great professor! I was actually interested in the material we learned and she was genuinely passionate about what she was teaching. Easy class to take for a gen-ed. I highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Malone Gonzalez!

The class is very interesting and is super easy if you've ever taken a sociology class before. There's a good amount of homework with the readings but I didn't do any of the readings and got Bs on the midterms and full credit on all homework and in-class activities. You can def half-a this class and get a good grade.

Shannon was great, super sweet and provided a lot of extra credit for exams. The exams themselves were crazy easy, I didn't do a single reading, just looked at the slides before exams and came out with an A. Great soci class to knock out that gen ed.
Pretty easy class for the most part. Study a little for the exams and you will do okay.

Such an interesting and thought provoking class! There are many assignments that are based on your own experiences and analyzing your own life, which makes the course much more relatable. There's many readings, but she goes over them in class and they're generally interesting. Take her class is you can!!

Professor Malone Gonzalez has been by far the best professor Ive had at UNC. There are readings to do before every class but shes very real and open to what she expects out of every student and truly wants every student to succeed in her class. She has an awesome personality and its truly a great lecturer. Exams were also pretty easy.

Prof Gonzalez is really caring and actually has a personality- unlike many professors. There are only a couple exams and homeworks that make up your grade, however she is super accommodating and wants students to get A's. Definitely recommend!

AVOID AVOID AVOID! This class was brutal for absolutely no reason. Like so many others said, if you do poorly on one assignment (with vague directions and feedback) it is difficult to make a comeback! Exams weren't terrible but some questions are written purposely to trick you using vague language. Lots of reading. Condescending. Beware.

So many negatives about Fitzgerald: a poor lecturer, fuzzy requirements for a final paper, no criteria for evaluation, tests designed to "catch" you, the "textbook" is not academically published, a bunch of essays, no alternative perspectives, no theories, no inspiration, no intellectual depth. She is sick, abusive and should be fired.

The SOCI122 was super easy, and she didn't seem rude to our class at all. Overall, a great teacher/lecturer. The class was very discussion-based. I only skimmed the texts/textbook after receiving the study guides for the midterm/final. HIGHLY recommend doing and STUDYING the study guide, it will save your grade.

The positive reviews here are so far from true. There is no way these are accurate. Midterm and exam which are really the only grades (plus 1 paper and 2 small quizzes) are SO hard and designed to trick you. Genuinely was so hard and barely scraped out a B. Unsure why she tries to make class impossible and students miserable. Steer VERY clear.

VERY reading and lecture heavy. won't get a good grade unless you read the textbook, be prepared to read. Class is based on few grades, kinda hard to pull your grade up.  shes a bit passive aggressive but is sweet and passionate about sociology. Just follow her criteria and expectations. Don't take class if you don't wanna read. There's easier FCs

DO NOT TAKE! The instructor with a tunnel vision abuses her power in this class. She does not understand how to organize discussions, contradictory about the paper requirements, her one page requires one thing, but she actually does not want that in the paper! She is unfit to teach as many said here. I like the textbook from which I learned a lot.

Was nervous about her at first but ended up loving Dr. F. She will push back/question your thoughts but not if they're opinions (like these ratings say), only if you misinterpreted something or are simply wrong. Graded on few things but midterm and quizzes are easy as long as you do the reading. I barely studied for them and did fine.

Confused by the harsh ratings on here as Dr. Fitzgerald's class was my favorite all semester. Yes, a lot of reading but that's all you have to do to do well in this class—read the assigned pages, show up to class, and take good notes. She's not condescending, she just won't let people take up class time to talk about irrelevant things! Great class.

DO NOT TAKE, unrealistic amounts of reading for the semester, class is awful with the "facts" you are graded upon being almost straight opinion, some of which can be disproved with a blatant google search. Extremely rude to all students, extremely vague outline for final paper which is 20% of grade, I would rather get the chem dpt from yikyak again

DO NOT ever take Dr. Fitzgerald.  The most rude and condescending prof I have had at UNC.  She does not seem to have any respect for her students.  Her exams and quizzes are designed to trick you, and there are so few grades that it is hard to bounce back from a single bad grade. I would steer FAR away from any of her classes if you can.

Overall, the professor was okay. I felt like it was difficult to express opinions bc she would push back if she didn't agree. Exams were worded in a way to be intentionally tricky. Most of her lectures were info directly from textbook. Course wasn't terrible and it wasn't hw heavy.

This class overall felt like a waste of time. The tests are easy as long as you use the study guide, but the lectures themselves felt pointless since she just reiterates what's in the textbook (not everything though-you still need to read it). The best thing about this class was reading Defectors by Paula Ramos which you could do in your own time.

I loved this class. Dr. Fitzgerald is clearly passionate about sociology and reparative justice. She is strict about attendance but, other than that, I disagree with the negative reviews. Take this class to learn, not for an easy A. She is clear about her expectations and sticks to the syllabus. She just wants students to genuinely participate.

Having her as one of my professors for my first semester at unc lowered my expectations for the rest of my professors in the future. I have never experienced a teacher so rude. She was mean to everyone exept for the people that were similar to her. Do not take this class unless you want to get yelled at for sharing your thoughts.

This class feels like it should be 5 credit hours. Dr. Fitzgerald often assigns up to 90 pages of reading in between class periods and with the service-learning requirement this class can be difficult to manage. She is also the most condescending professor I've had at UNC. Lectures are very interesting and midterm was easy with some studying

Every single question is worded in a way to trick you, often making one word off and so the whole thing is wrong. She claims all subject matter is science when 100% of the time, the statistics are sketchy, incomplete, or skewed. Very condescending, rude, and often passive aggressive. DO NOT TAKE!

Do not take this class especially for a FC. It is way more difficult than it should be. Unrealistic amounts of reading due throughout the semester, then test questions designed to trick you. She is mean to the students and consistently talks in rude and passive aggressive tones. If you don't agree with her politically, you will not get a good grade

Save your time and effort for other classes, especially if this one is for a FC. Dr. Fitzgerald is very rude to all students and says backhanded comments to every question asked. the course content is manageable but she makes it 10x more difficult than it is. The midterm was hard and questions that are designed to trick you.

Save yourself the time and the effort. The teacher is very rude and will say backhanded comments. You are only graded by a few things, a hard midterm, 2 quizzes and a final paper. Mid-term is really hard, tricky questions and doesn't really explain things, only in her point of view. If you go against  her opinion, get ready for an augment.

I am currently enrolled in SOCI 130. Doing badly on this midterm basically ruined my grade for the semester because there are only 2 quizzes, a midterm, a final, a paper, and attendance grades, which are all graded very heavily. I would NOT recommend it if you are not the best test taker. This class is also VERY reading/lecture heavy.

There is very little graded in actually participation which goes against the idea of a "seminar" class. Most grades comes from out of work readings. She grades very vaguely and harshly. Even if you were to follow the rubric word for word, the chances are you will get a grade much below what you are expecting.
Unclear grading scale and changed the syllabus multiple times throughout the semester. Weaponized sarcasm during lectures.

Her lectures are funny, but she is generally a very passive-aggressive and not very understanding professor. Was very disrespectful during Creativity Relay presentations. My group had an issue because a student wasn't doing any work, and she was not very understanding or helpful. The class is easy, but she tries to make it unnecessarily difficult.

Took SOCI89. She can be sassy, and her lectures are somewhat interesting. Her homework is structured oddly, due the morning on the day before class, and the homework was often 25+ pages of readings. However, she is really nice and rounded up our grades at the end of the semester; a big part of our grades is based on projects.

Sassy but somewhat entertaining in lecture. Everything online except for one group project (lowkey she was annoying about these). The kind of class you do other homework during- only took attendance twice in the semester

She makes her lectures entertaining, however she is really rude and passive aggressive during the creativity relay presentations, obviously aggravated and corrects the content students share immediately after their presentations. Grading is really harsh, its not a difficult class however the grading style makes it hard to get a good grade in class.

I took SOCI 89. She's an extremely harsh grader, gives passive aggressive feedback, and doesn't provide good instruction on what she's looking for. Homework due before every class which includes multiple readings that can each be 25+ pages. Her lectures are somewhat interesting and sometimes she shares funny stories, but overall not worth it.

Painfully unfunny. Sent the syllabus for the group project AFTER we had completed and presented it and graded us based on it which dropped my grade down to a B. Everything else is just quizzes and take home exams with questions that she lazily pulls from quizlet. Unaccommodating/Only professor I've ever had a grudge against. Dont buy her book
funny but sassy. everything is online. attendance is spot-checked. never opened the book once other than the group project. definitely take for an easy A

If you just want to get your A and be done with it than this class is a good one to take. However I honestly think she is extremely rude. Would make rude comments in class and tell us that she would not bother to respond to emails if she thought our email was not worth replying to. The exams were all online and she did take random attendance.

There was a group project that wasn't hard and is pretty expected for a 101 class; however, the grading criteria was not fully available and then she wanted to grade heavy. It is clear she knows what she's talking about and cares about students, but sometimes her comments can rub people the wrong way. For credit though, this class was easy.

Unprofessional, out of pocket, unorganized professor. She was condescending, and never gave clear directions/expectations for the course/assignments. She was funny at times & the content was interesting, but it doesn't make up for the fact that she made the course way harder than it needed to be. She did not set up the class to succeed at all.

She tries really hard to be engaging & is funny most of the time (some jokes just don't land). The group project is annoying, but if your group is on top of it a good grade is doable. The TA grades just about everything so as long as you have a good TA it's fine. There are small responses due at the beginning of each class based on the reading.

She's really passionate about sociology and tries to make lectures fun. Bottom line: the material is not hard and you don't need to attend class at all. Grades are based on weekly quizzes and a few tests and papers; easy to get an A.

Honestly yes sometimes the lectures are a bit dry, but if you have a solid TA, the class will be a breeze. If you do the readings and take notes you'll get extra credit at the end of the semester just for doing them. I recommend her if you can get her, attendance is mandatory but also not at the same time. Midterms and final were pretty easy too.

In one lecture she had twenty students come to the front of the lecture hall and line up by skin color in some backwards way of trying to make a point. She is well-intentioned but tone deaf and just misses the mark. Required attendance (even though lecture is large), made us read her own book even though it wasn't relevant to the course content.

Dr. Ravenelle is really funny and her lectures are enjoyable. Although I agree with some of the comments saying that the group project was frustrating, I wouldn't let it stop you from taking the class as you can learn a lot from it! The grading was very fair and the readings were also really interesting.

Dr. Ravenelle's class was not too bad. Readings were not dense but you need to do the daily participation assignments. Both the midterm and final were online, essay-based. About a month and a half is centered around a group project that was a frustrating experience. We were trained to use a coding platform that was not very helpful. TA was great!

She was ok.  Her lectures could be hard to sit through.  She tries to be funny/snarky, and it often doesn't really work out.  Pretty easy class, though.  I wouldn't say I recommend her, but I also didn't absolutely hate her.
She had really entertaing lectures and all of the homework/ tests were very easy.

Ted is awesome. Class content is super interesting and current events based. The class is graded on daily reading questions that are due before class each day (very easy), participation, 4 in class essays (again very easy and he allows a cheat sheet), and a final (2 page cheat sheet). Highly recommend this class it is easy to do well.

He does a good job of teaching this course and is understanding. I really like him and what the course was about. SOCI 412 focuses a lot on meritocracy and what it means. Interesting course and wasn't terribly difficult.

Such a fun and nice prof! Class is graded on attendance, participation, 5 in-class essays, final, and reading notes for each class. He was flexible with our class and super personable. He does cold call so be prepared for that.

Ted is the funniest professor I've had at UNC. He's very flexible w/ the class schedule, and passionate about the course. The lectures are all discussion based in groups, with a few essays and pre class assignments.The course concepts can be hard at times, but Ted does a good job at simplifying the content. I looked forward to this class, take him!

Professor Mouw is one of my favorite professors! It is very discussion based but it makes class fun and engaging, and the topics we discuss are insightful and cause you to think outside the box. He cold calls but you are able to say "pass" if you don't want to speak. We have in class essays, but he prepares us so well. He is so sweet & caring!

This is my third class with Ted, so you can guess that I'd take more if I weren't graduating! The work load is above average, but the readings are typically interesting which helps a lot. You get to explore some unique topics as well. Class is discussion-based, so if you don't prefer this format, it's not the class for you.

Sarah is extremely caring and concerned that students learn and succeed in the class. It's a really easy class; you have to do some reading but it's not too much and you can get away with skimming. The exams are very easy to prepare for because they're based on class warm-ups and discussions.

One of my favorite classes I have taken. Class is not demanding and has warm-ups that are self-graded, and four tests that are all open note, and then a final presentation that is only worth 10% of your grade. Professor Brown is super caring and always willing to work with you, highly reccomend this class.

Honestly, the easiest class I've taken at UNC. Sarah is so nice and obviously cares about her students. The class was a mix of lectures, discussions, and small group work. 50% of your grade is warm-up "quizzes" that are self-graded and based on the readings. Tests were open note, and a bank of possible questions was given. Take this class!
She's a really good professor, she is caring and makes you feel listened. The content of the course is not that hard and you can get a good grade if you understood the readings. Clearly recommend.

She's very sweet and caring but honestly the class has way too much work than its worth, especially for a 100 level class. The content is extremely good and thought-provoking, but the readings were anywhere from 30-80 pages a night, and you have to do them because there's a 5 question quiz at the beginning of every class. The final is a project.

I overall liked the class and it was pretty interesting. But I have to say- we turned in our final projects on May 3 and it's May 13 and still, none of us have final project grades or final grades at all... She did not communicate with the class about any delays which is pretty frustrating. We shouldn't have to wait this long for our grades.
Do the readings. Show up. Write down what he says. Review these notes before the quiz.

every minute you spend listening to this prof try (and fail) to explain his own material is a minute you will be wishing u were anywhere else. rly grating professor, and don't you Dare ask him any questions or he will issue a retort. i watched him talk down to students who just wanted to understand the material better so many times. bad all around

Good guy but a weird class. Always came in unprepared, lecture notes were made during class as topics were brought up. Expected an essay and hours of reading before EVERY class. Often started teaching before the posted time and kept going several minutes after it ended. Not hard to get a decent grade but would definitely recommend a different prof.

Decent professor, but much room for improvement. Ruy required readiness quizzes, which were sporadic and often not available until a couple days before due date. Also expected a great deal from us, but did not hold the same standards for himself as a lot of work was not graded until a week or two before final grades were due. Would not take again.

He is a bit of a tough grader and there are reading quizzes before every class. But he is very respectful and cares about all his students. Class was tough but feel like I learned a lot and nothing ever felt unfair in terms of workload or grades. He also doesn't force you to participate during lectures. 2 tests, 1 paper, a few group assignments.

Worst Professor I have ever had! He doesn't respond to emails and when you ask questions and trying to participate in class he makes you feel belittled. There are a lot of readings and he basically wants you to write an essay each day before coming to class. Grading is horrible and unfair. He changes % after assignments have already been submitted.

Assigns "readiness quizzes" before every class. They take about 2 hours each and he does not bother to keep up with grading them. When he does, he will take 10-20 percentage points off for minimal mistakes or missing content, even though the assignment says to use your own words in simplified terms. 2 months behind on grading. Terrible class.

People who did not understand the course simply just didn't read or didn't pay attention. So many people in class were sitting on their phones instead of taking notes & asked questions that were answered clearly in the readings. Professor was a bit disorganized and was frequently late, but he cared a lot about his students and was very lenient.

Ruy is a good person, but he is horrible at time management and he is so unorganized, frequently late to class. We really didn't learn but if you really wanted to you could teach yourself. We had to use UNCCheckin attendance but it wasn't on syllabus. He wants u to make a good grade he isn't that bad of a grader. You work w a group, kinda easy A

Jacob Conley is a great teacher! He makes lectures very entertaining and insightful. The course material was very interesting. The assignments were very easy as well. I will truly miss taking a course with him. His class would genuinely make my day better because he would consistently make me laugh during class! I would highly recommend!

Jacob is very kind and knowledgable. I don't enjoy sociology, but he made this class bearable. Even when the assignments weren't my favorite topics, his feedback was exceptional and motivational. Don't abuse his generosity. He is very smart and funny! And his submission comments always make my day. Thank you Jacob! :)

Jacob cares more about our well-being as students than how much output we can produce. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about sociology. His lectures are intriguing, clear, and includes fun class discussions. He makes social theories easy to understand and helps us connect them to our own experiences. He's very understanding about absences.

Jacob was a great professor, he was super funny and always did great lectures. He makes class easy to engage in which makes learning the theories much easier. He gives good feedback on assignments. You do have to read for every class but its not a crazy amount.
He was very caring and respectful of students, but the lectures were very dry and boring

Jacob cares for his students and is approachable after classes. However, his lectures are dry and hard to focus. He always reads slides and rarely interacts with students. But overall, the course is easy. If you just want to earn credit, take his class. But if you're interested in the class content and are keen to learn, he's not a good lecturer.

Truly one of the best at UNC! Jacob is so kind, accommodating, generous, and flexible, and he works hard to make class not stressful. He even went so far as to always say hello when he saw me outside of class and was honestly just a joy! He is so knowledgeable and makes course content interesting, always tying it to real life. Would 110% recommend!
Jacob is an amazing professor! Super chill and is great at explaining difficult concepts. We do have a good bit of small assignments, but they're all easy.

Genuinely one of the best instructors I have ever had the pleasure of having. Yes, attendance is mandatory, but he builds in some free absences already and is very understanding with outside commitments and pushing back deadlines if necessary. If you can finagle yourself a spot into one of his classes, consider that an honor.
Jacob is okay. He gives excessive amounts of work. 3 assignments and a quiz every week. More papers throughout the semester and a final. Participation matters as well.

If you have even the smallest chances of getting into one of jacobs classes, try as hard as you can! He is super caring and understanding. Attendance is mandatory, but you are given a few unexcused misses and easy to make up the points with 2 weekly 150 work responses and weekly quizzes. Final paper and exam. Content is all found in the lectures.

Jacob is an amazing professor even though he is still working on his PhD at the same time. Very sweet and understanding person that cares deeply about what he teaches and his students. 3 attendance skips are allowed, reading responses are not bad, a weekly quiz that he allows corrections for. He is perfect in every way

Jacob is a true gem at UNC I took him for 411 and am now retaking his class for soci 420. He is very understanding and you are truly missing out if you don't take a class with him. All I will say is that you will have to submit reading reflections before your classes but as long as you are prepared his classes should be a breeze.

Jacob is an amazing professor. Although he is still a grad student, he has been one of the most caring and kind professors I have ever had at UNC. He cares about his students and makes the material so understandable. Reading reflections are due before each class, but he mentioned cutting down to two a week. No midterm, just a paper and a final
I had Jacob as a TA for this class and he was great! He was super helpful and approachable! He only lead a few lectures but he was super prepared and I really enjoyed them!

The professor is caring and supportive of students. Communication is clear and responsive, and she is open to questions. Grading is fair and reflects the effort put into the course. I would recommend this class. 5/5

There are quizzes for every unit (every 1-2 weeks) but she does review right beforehand and touches on everything that will be on the quiz so PAY ATTENTION! She canceled/moved class online a few times. Notes came from slides and from things she would show on the board like BLS statistics. Current events discussions involve some participation.

Jordan's very laid back, gives lots of remote quizzes and class off days. There was some frustration with varying quiz difficulty and varying harshness of grading on assignments. Not work-heavy, but quiz-heavy with questions pulled from niche things she said like one time in class. She's a bit of a lazy professor but it was a chill class overall.

Unpredictable and unorganized. She seems very chill, but she's a harsh grader and never really has a schedule.
