Thankfully it's not work heavy, but it's all about memorization of random stats for short quizzes, which is tough. Also it's week 13 and we haven't been given any information about the final project.

She was an amazing professor. She was very knowledgeable about the information, but also paired everything with detailed slides that would represent what was on the weekly quizzes. The quizzes were easy if you looked over the notes from the class before and she is very chill.

This class was an easy A for me, but I think that's because I sat in the front row and Professor Young knew my name and we talked a good bit. If you participate and she knows you, this class is a breeze. Not hard content, but some of my friends that never showed up were in danger of B's. lots of online (easy) quizzes, group project, final.
Easy class to do well in.
This is my second class with Professor Young. Super low-maintenance class, content is interesting, and she's really understanding. Ended with a high A in both classes I've taken with her.

Didn't attend any lectures and also didn't do most of the readings (because there was A LOT), but still learned a good bit tbh. Grade heavily determined by TA for recitation, and I got lucky with mine.

Unless this class is required for your major, I wouldn't recommend taking it. Dr. Huerta-Bapat's lectures are very boring, and your grade is based on two papers, two tests, and participation in recitations. TA will determine your entire grade, so make sure you get a good one. Overall, not a terrible class, but I don't think I would take it again.

I would not fully recommend Professor Huerta Bapat, as she is all over the place and just reads directly off her slides. Participation matters in recitation, and your TA solely decides your grade in the class, so if you have a TA who grades harshly, good luck! Two papers and two exams, along with participation, make up your entire grade.

Bapat had heavy readings that were not super necessary for the class besides a bit in recitation. Attendance not required in lecture but her lectures are very boring and she just reads off the slides. Grading all depends on your TA, which is very hit or miss but the midterm and final were take home online.

She is passionate about what she teaches and the course material was pretty interesting. The group projects were a little much and made up a huge chunk of the grade. Also she expected us to read about 30 pages for every class. Was pretty disorganized at times and didn't make an effort to learn names either.

Carmen's class was definitely an experience. It was pretty heavy on readings and the grades were pretty much all reliant on group projects, however, the final and the midterm were super easy. Although this class was somewhat disorganized at times, I think it was interesting and she definitely cares about what she's teaching.

Carmen's class is an easy A, the midterm and final are pretty easy if you take some time to study beforehand, but it's also a lot of group work which can be challenging if you get assigned a bad group. That being said the class was pretty disorganized, she was also kinda rude didn't learn any names in a 30 person class.

I'm someone who always does class readings. This is hard to do when your professor is unreliable. Lecture content contradicts test questions and she also put in grades the night before the final. That being said, exams are memorization-based, so if you're good at that you'll do fine. It's just not enjoyable. She never learned names either.

GLBL 221 is reading heavy and the readings are dense even if you're interested in the topic. Carmen is funny but can be a picky grader. Learn how to read her and you'll be fine. Participate often and at least have some idea of what the reading was about so you can be involved. Group projects are manageable with the right group. She is unique fs!

This class is super interesting and Dr. Bapat is very passionate about it! Long readings but super interesting information. The group projects are a little intense and work heavy, but the information is cool!

The class itself was pretty boring- a saving grace was Carmen sharing personal stories. Both exams were online and TAs are super helpful with writing the papers. Attendance isn't mandatory, but she gives out a lot of exam essay questions and multiple choice answers (write them down). Also, TAs heavily imply other questions. Overall, should be an A.
Do not take as a summer course. Very subjective grading and very vague feedback. Regardless of whether you follow all instructions on the rubric, she will grade poorly. Avoid.

If you take this class over the summer, don't. There are no TAs to grade your essays objectively. Her recorded lectures seem condescending and disorganized, and there's no use in following essay rubrics since her grading is very subjective. Avoid this professor.

This professor is extremely rude to students and TAs. She is not organized which shows through her lectures. The class is made up of recitation attendance, 2 exams, and 2 essays. The TAs grade everything so your grade will be based off of that but TAs are very caring and understanding. She says readings are crucial to passing but I didn't do any.

Prof is rude to TAs & students. Class is chill! Do not do the readings - she goes over the ones in class that are important. Graded off of recitation attendance, 2 exams, and 2 papers. Exams were on canvas & easy. Papers/written exam portions graded by TAs, so meet with them and they will help you. Shout out to my TA Ella who was amazing!!

She is incredibly disorganized. Her actual lectures and slides are not closely related to the readings. Also her lectures were very personal and did not seem to be that important. All the readings were long and often irrelevant. She's snappy to the TAs and not very friendly. Her TAs were amazing and looked out for you. Avoid taking if possible.

She put maybe 30% effort into this class. Managed to make every single lecture about herself and her experiences. Horribly disorganized, the TAs even agreed and would express that to students. Tons of reading, lectures were just tangents half the time. Pray that your TA will clear things up for you. I'd take a different GLBL professor for this.

This professor demonstrated how inept in all ways she was when it came to the material, technology, and lecturing. Lectures were sometimes irrelevant to readings, and tended to go on tangents, and constant tech issues. TA even agreed this was their least favorite iteration of this class. The professor ruins the class by putting 50% effort into it.

Professor Huerta-Bapat knows her stuff and is really passionate about what she teaches. That said, her class is very lecture heavy and she expects you to do 30+ pages of reading for each class. The readings are very technical and lengthy, but she does a good job of summarizing the main ideas in class. Project guidelines can be a bit unclear though
Professor Franklyn is an amazing professor and person in general! I have loved the multiple classes I have taken with them and would recommend taking any and all of their classes.

Grace Franklyn is the most passionate and insightful professor I have ever had at UNC. Grace had great lectures, amazing grading criteria, and very well organized canvas. I would take every class she offers if possible!
Grace is a gem of a teacher. So incredibly caring yet passionate about the subject matter. Really made me care about health and society in news ways! Couldn't recommend her more.

I loved loved loved this class. Grace is such an amazing professor, she made all the lectures very interesting and easy to understand. I genuinely learned so much from her class. The exams are open note and there is one final paper, but other than that there are just two assignments each week. Would definitely recommend this class!
Grace is awesome! I had a great experience in her class and think everyone should try to take her class before she graduates from Carolina's program.

boring lecture and attendance not required so you can get away with not going. tests were pretty easy as long as you complete the study guide. tests were mcq, true/false, fill in the blank, and frq. has review days before exam where you can earn extra credit for the midterm. overall p easy class

For the semester long project, everything is peer-reviewed until the final research brief meaning that it could fail to meet her standards when it's worth the largest portion of your grade. Extremely strict on grading for exams and provides no flexibility in answers. Lost an entire point out of 30 for using a synonym instead of the actual word.

Horrible class, harsh grader, way too specific on her test for no reason, class was all done in lecture and a waste of time to go to, her in class assignments did nothing to reinforce the class content.

Tests were horrible. She grades very strict and the questions are too broad. She gives barely any material to study and grades so specifically. Other than the tests the class is fine but the tests make it awful. You can skim the readings that are assigned every day. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

I enjoyed this class! She is very particular when it comes to grading exams, specifically the essay portions but as long as you complete the study guides you will do just fine in the class. Attendance is preferred but you can get by skipping if you need it. Easy A if you complete all the study guides!

The grading for the exams were ridiculous. Averaging low Cs on material that is straight forward. It wasn't very clear how she wanted the short responses and it made a lot of people lose points. Other than that is fine, but grading should not be so hard.

Loveddd Prof. Mitchell. The class itself was not that bad, as long as you follow the exam review sheets you'll do solid on the exams. You'll get a good grade if you follow the rubric for the papers. Prof. Mitchell was good at breaking down complex topics into something digestible. Take her!!!

Overall, this was a good class. Mitchell can grade strictly on exams and you need to know the material well, but it's not impossible as it's not that much material. The guidelines for assignments were pretty straightforward.

Denise was a good professor but very picky when grading. There are assigned readings for every class but you can get away with skimming them. The final presentation is fair and I think she has a lot of potential as a professor.
Great teacher who involves the whole class, provides new perspectives, great for first years

I really recommend this class for FYS, she is really nice and even speak French Fluently.
However the case studies were really long to read and boring for me.
The Final project is a little intimidating but easy if you break down works and start early.(You will have to interview someone in STEM and present it to the class) also write 10 pages final.

I really love this class. It opened my eyes to a lot of the realities of being a woman in science. Lots of reading but the book and studies you read are mostly interesting. No exams, there are 5-6 short essays. Final is doing an interview with a woman in S.T.E.M. and you write a paper about everyones interviews. Definitely reccomend this as a FYS.

Such an amazing and intelligent professor! You need to take one of her classes; it will truly change your life. Captivating lectures and very important content. This class inspired me to minor in sociology.

I took SOCI 101 because I thought it would be easy A. This class definately wasn't that. It's a lot of reading and you to study a LOT for the exams. I would not recommend this class if you the rest of your schedule is a heavy workload. That said I learned a lot and the professor is very knowledgable on the topics.

Dr. Valentino is an incredible lecturer. She gives clear, thorough lectures that prepare you well for the exams. She's very accessible and caring, and she does some fascinating research. This class is doable as long as you attend the lectures and read the assignments. Make sure to actually pay attention to everything covered though!

For a SOCI 101 class, her exams were difficult. I thought this would be am easy A class, but she asks for very specific info on her exams. She is super nice, but lectures are boring. Graded by in-class assignments, attendance, and exams.

I strongly recommend avoiding Professor Valentino's class. Her exams are unnecessarily difficult, and the study guides are practically useless, they barely cover what's actually on the test. She doesn't explain things clearly and makes the class way more frustrating than it needs to be. Easily one of the worst teaching experiences I've had.

SOCI 101 is a very easy class and Dr. Valentino is a good professor. Her midterms are not hard at all and are based on exactly what we did in class and read in the readings (never any longer than 25 pages and you can skim). If you need a free A, take this class. :)
Dr Valentino is the best. She asks great questions in class and really helps us think about things in a new way. Really eye opening!
Amazing prof!! Take a class with her! She's great at making you really think about things in a totally new way. Really interesting class!!

Dr. Valentino is genuinely one of the best professors you'll ever have. The content I learned from her class will stick with me for the rest of my life. She used various mediums to keep the class engaged and provided the most detailed feedback I've ever seen. You would be doing a disservice to yourself by not taking one of her classes.

Dr. Valentino was my favorite professor this semester! She is truly so intelligent. Her lectures are very interesting, and the way she structured the course was very organized. I feel like I learned the most from her this semester. I could not recommend a better first year seminar or professor at UNC.

Professor Frankenberg is really nice and warm-spirited. She loves talking to students after class. This class is pretty reading-heavy, but she also goes over it during lectures. 1 mid-term + final and other assignments.

dr. frankenberg's lectures were usually lengthy and unengaging, but the content was straight-forward and fairly interesting. she spontaneously does in-class assignments and her writing assignments were pretty manageable. her exams were easy if you paid attention in class or reviewed lecture slides, and she allowed cheat sheets on both.

From the moment class starts til the moment it ends, she talks with a white screen, black text PowerPoint behind her. It is so boring and very hard to stay interested in her lectures. Gives random in-class assignments, so be sure you show up to class so that you get those points. The midterm and final were pretty tough, even with the "cheat sheet"

Very nice professor, caring and kind, but her lectures are boring and her readings are quite long. You do get a 2 sided cheat sheet for midterms and the final, tests are not necessarily hard but there is quite a bit of niche details. Attendance is basically mandatory because of random exit tickets. Study lecture vigorously and do the readings.

I wouldn't take this class just to fulfill a gen ed. You can't cram for it unless you took notes... she tests random details from slides and lectures. About 50% of the exam is fill-in-the-blank with no word bank, sometimes on totally random phrases, so it's extremely frustrating. But she's genuinely one of the nicest and most helpful professors.

Very passionate, and it shows in her lectures; she will go very in-depth. It may be a little boring, but she covers everything for exams in class. Attendance is measured through random in-class exercises, so you need to show up. Large readings, but she covers them. Very fair grader, and will give 100s if you do the work. Take this class!

Genuinely one of the kindest and most supportive professors at UNC. The lectures are long and a bit tiring, but the studies she goes over are super interesting and WILL be on the tests. The tests are straightforward and easy, so just go through the slides/readings beforehand. Also, go to office hours she's actually amazing!!

She knows her field well, but her lectures are not engaging. Lectures were boring, and many people used this class to do other work. There's 2 mini papers, 2 prob sets, 6 class exercises, a midterm and a final. The material is fairly easy and the class is tolerable, but I would not recommend her unless if it's required. Not bad, but there's better.

Somewhat interesting. The lectures were unengaging, so when I studied for exams, I basically retaught myself with lectures she posted on Canvas. She is clearly passionate and nice, but includes niche reading/lecture facts on exams (which were hard) so be prepared. Honestly, I wouldn't take this for an FC unless you're interested in the content.

This class was so much reading and I found the lectures pretty boring. The tests were pretty hard because she asked very specific questions from the reading. You were allowed a cheat sheet on exams but it still didn't help me that much. I would only recommend taking this class if you can devote a decent chunk of your time to it.

Don't take this professor unless you're extremely good at exams. She doesn't teach the topics well, she just assumes you already know base knowledge. The exams are worth more than half of your final grade, and although attendance isn't mandatory, I would recommend not missing a single class because of in-class assignments.

The material is really interesting, especially for premed students. The workload is light: one midterm, four 1-2 page assignments, and a final. If you're consistent in attending lectures and reviewing slides, it's an Easy A where you can learn valuable concepts pertaining to issues of population health and disparities. Love the professor.

Really good class and an enthusiastic professor! There are a couple of problem sets and papers. Follow the rubrics and you will be fine. Random attendance quizzes so just go to class lol. Exams are thorough, but you can bring a cheat sheet. Go thru all the slides since everything is fair game. There is extra credit on everything. Highly recommend!

She is so sweet and is passionate about what she is talking about, but her lectures can be quite lengthy sometimes. I don't know my final grade yet, but I would say overall this class is easily passible.

Worst lecturer ever. Will not answer student questions and rambles about things unrelated to lecture. The tests are worth a huge chunk of your grade and reference really niche topics from the readings as well as covering a huge wealth of information. Coming to lecture will teach you nothing but you have to go anyway because of the attendance.

in-class exercises count as attendance and she makes you turn it in on paper. 

exams aren't hard, but there's so much information. allowed a cheat sheet. she will throw in really specific questions from readings so make sure you at least skim the 40+ pages she gives you every two days.

She seem very genuinely interested in many of the topics she discusses but often times 50% of the slides are just going over the lengthy readings from the night before. The summaries of these readings are important but tune in to what she is saying because it's easy to understand but it can get boring throughout the hour and 15 min.

We go through 40-50 page slideshows every class that she reads directly off of. You can tell she is interested in what she teaches but does not know how to make it engaging for students. When trying to figure out what to study for the midterm, no matter who you contact, you aren't given a response because they haven't taken the course at UNC

Took for the global engagement gen-ed, stayed for the engaging lectures and relevant content. Very nice professor, exams were fair, midterm had test corrections, almost all exams and HW have extra credit possible. Recommend!

Very good professor for sociology 180. Just took it for the global engagement focus capacity but ended up really enjoying the course. Grading is quite easy in my experience, extra credit available on most HW and midterm and final.

I have no idea why Jorge has a low rating. He was so funny and genuinely a nice guy. He wants to see you succeed. Very accessible through email and his midterms were so easy IF you did the review sheets. Would totally take him again.

I thought this class was very easy. His lectures can be a bit boring especially if you have background in what he is talking about but he makes understanding the material very easy so its good if you need extra help! Definitely better than some of the other professors that teach this class. I found the tests to be pretty easy.

It wasn't a hard class for me as a data science major. Very light workload. But Jorge is not the best professor, I would've had a tougher time if I wasn't familiar with statistics. Extra credit saved me in the end cause the final was tough.

It's like he wants you to fail the tests and he doesn't let you see them afterward. Which is weird because problem sets are pretty easy. Participation heavy, boring lectures and not very helpful when you have questions. I liked learning the R code and applying in context but that's about it.
Teacher was not good at lecturing and was very boring. Participation matters and test heavy.

Good content, low stress class besides the tests. But very dry, serious teaching style, and had to give extra credit because his midterm went terribly. Poorly worded questions intended to throw you off and expects too much precision. I didn't really enjoy him as a teacher and thought he was way too critical.

Very interesting and worthwhile class overall.
Pros: problem sets are short, textbook is helpful but not necessary. Not too difficult or heavy on coding, but still a good intro to R.
Cons: Jorge is a pretty dry lecturer and his test questions are bad; the midterm average was 70 despite the content being pretty easy. Attendance is important!
He is a fun professor, pretty good lecturer. The material was pretty wishi-washi, so be careful about writing down what you want to study, becuase looking back at the slides won't help.
Victor was a fantastic teacher. As long as you listen and work hard, you should do well in the class.

Victor is an amazing and funny guy. There are two things you should be prepared for: You'll do a lot of group work and Victor loves to do karate moves in class. Overall the class was a fun time and I recommend Victor as a professor.

RELI 109: I really enjoyed this class and felt that I learned a lot. We even referred to him as "Mr. Cool" because of how enjoyable the class was and how much we learned. Participation is important for earning a high participation grade. The tests aren't too difficult if you study, and the two papers are manageable in length.

RELI 109: "Mr Cool" is the GOAT! Whether or not you are interested in religious studies, you learn a lot, and the teacher is engaging. The lectures are interesting, and the tests aren't bad as long as you go to class and study what's in the study guide. He is one of the best RELI professors I have had, and I will be taking classes from him again.

He is super chill and informative. Not overbearing on work and a fun guy to get to know. Content is pretty cool as well. He is surely passionate about the subject and is kind of a walking encyclopedia on religion. Would take again for sure.

Victor made it fun to be in the class, he has a great sense of humor.  The material can be heavy and you can expect to do some reading for the class, but Victor makes it relevant and interesting.  I'm glad I took this class with Victor as the professor!

Had fun in his class, even if it was at 8am! Tons of reading, but class was discussion heavy. Mr. Knight used alot of worksheets and small groups to talk about ancient texts, some of which were surprisingly interesting.
Good professor overall. Lots of reading, but he would sometimes tell us which ones to focus on and even cut some out a few times. Class was mostly discussion based with not a lot of lecturing.
Way too much reading.

Class isn't hard but lots of readings assigned and the material is very scattered. I found the class to be boring and it can be difficult to keep track of what you need to know on test from things mentioned very briefly in lecture.

This class is only interesting if you are very interested in the topic of the Ancient Near East. It is a lot of reading on topics I had a hard time understanding. Class was not graded hard until the final paper and final exam.

What can I say? Victor mf Knight is the MAN. We learned a lot about the ancient near east and it's actually pretty interesting material. Assignments are clearly outlined and reading quizzes are straightforward (reading can be long-ish). Provides useful study guides for tests. Take any class w him
Quizzes are super easy as long as you pay attention half the time. He makes sure to review before big tests and is honestly a good professor.

Victor is awesome! Despite the class being an 8 am, he always brought a good attitude and started off every class with music. He also included a mixture of lectures and fun group activities that were low-pressure and didn't require anyone to turn in anything. The assignments were very straightforward, and it's an easy A if you put in *some* effort!

Victor is a great professor. He is super down to earth and chill, which is reflected in his teaching. I've never met someone more passionate about their area of study, he has so much knowledge on the ancient Near East. Grading/class is manageable and he is a very fair grader, just a TON of reading to do.

Just lots of reading but he does take in feedback and cuts most of it. Really easy class you just have to participate and understand a gist of what's going on. Overall, amazing was very understanding of different circumstances and situations that arose out of nowhere. TAKE HIS CLASS!!

Victor is a super funny and nice guy. He is very lenient and very caring if you have a personal issue come up. His lectures and classes were always extremely entertaining and I enjoyed the group. There were only two papers and two exams. Just be prepared to read a LOT.
He was great, accessible outside of class, and made instructions clear on all assignments.

Victor is a wonderful TA and is very passionate about the subjects he teaches! Quite a lot of reading, but it will be worth it if you are interested in the topic. He is very knowledgeable and has fun teaching. He also grades papers/assignments very fairly and and is easily accessible outside of the classroom.

Professor Styers is super knowledgeable and passionate about the course content! He is a bit of a tough grader and has high expectations for his students. The course was very heavy on readings, and many people found the midterm difficult, but it is definitely doable if you pay attention in class and take notes.

Oh boy. Dr. Styers is an absolute unit of a professor. He's passionate about what he does and is very intelligent and knowledgeable. Him and the TA were the best part of the course. The course itself was hard though: tons of readings, and tons of information to know. Get ready to write a lot of essays because that's what most exams consisted of.

Interesting perspectives and comparisons of the afterlife, mostly about Christianity though. Styers isn't scared to dive into all aspects of religion and allow students to question and explore. You can tell he is passionate, sometimes lectures were boring but there were definitely some amazing ones too! Midterm was hard, but final was a take home.

Very interesting class! 2 very easy essays, but midterm & final are HARD. Not the easiest gen-ed, but A or B is possible. Beware all notes are paper and he doesn't post slides, so make a friend. Weekly readings for discussion posts don't make sense but are for participation. Take if you're fascinated by afterlife or want to question religion.

I signed up for this course thinking I could get a better religious understanding. Dr.Styers never answers class questions from students, talks for the entire lecture time, doesn't allow technology for note taking, & doesn't have any notes for lecture. Dr.Stylers leaves grading to his TA's; very selective in grading & doesn't give grades above 85.

It was a fun class if you're interested in religion. The mid term and final was tough to study for because there was so much material that could've been on the test. Pay attention in lecture any little detail could be on the exam. Overall, a great guy.

Took this class for a credit, and it was easy. No electronics allowed in lectures which honestly helped, listen attentively. I studied for the exams and did well on every assignment. However, I still ended up with an A- which makes no sense. I felt like my final grade didn't justify how well I did in the course, and they didn't see that.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS, for it to be a general ed class, 100 level it is NOT worth the workload, you have heavy 70-100 page readings due every Sunday which don't really come together or click until after the week is over. There's so much content you don't know what to study for, it's never clear what your glade is in the class, not worth it?

Dr. Styers is super knowledgeable about this topic. His lectures move really fast and he doesn't allow laptops, so listening is really important. Recitation attendance is required. There are weekly discussion posts about the readings, but hardly any other assignments outside of that. The final exam was take-home and just essays. He was great though

Take notes of every bit of information, as it might come on the mid term. Ask for the midterm format sample at the first day of class, so you can take notes accordingly. Tell professor to record class lectures and ask professor to give you the recordings later on. This way you can take notes at home, because the lecture is very fast.

Dr. Styers is a very respected and caring professor. Highly, highly recommend attending office hours. The class is reading heavy - you have to read and then write a forum post each week. The midterms are challenging, but take good notes and attend the lectures/recitations and you'll be fine.

I LOVE DR STYERS! My favorite prof I've had, see him in office hours, he loves to get to know students and is a great reference to have. I did not have interest in reli, but loved this class. Def a good bit of work, but keep up with organizing notes after lectures and you'll be fine. 2 midterms, 1 final, and forum posts which are easy.

Lectures are hard to sit through, there's a lot of dense reading, and we felt extremely unprepared for our midterms because of how much material could have been on it with no idea what exactly to study. For most of us to have taken this as a gen ed, the workload was pretty heavy. The content was interesting, though (kind of).

Readings and forum posts before every class. Readings are somewhat lengthy but fair. Students lead class discussion in groups twice. Three essays: first essay, midterm essay, and final essay. Class discussion was engaging. Only qualm is that the class was centered almost entirely on a single book "The Dawn of Everything" which felt tiring at times.

He's a chill dude! This specific class was rough for me, just because I didn't really vibe w the material, but Styers is a great prof and genuinely cares about the class. He's a lenient grader and assigns relatively little work outside of the readings. Readings are long but skimmable, and a reasonable trade-off for an otherwise light class.

He is a nice guy and is very knowledgeable. His lectures are super hard to sit through sometimes, especially because he doesn't allow technology for anything, not even note taking. It was an interesting class and I am glad I took it but it was definitely a lot of reading and discussion posts.

Great lecturer, a lot of extra credit, and just a really great choice for your required interdisciplinary. His personal beliefs were obviously reflected in his response to student questions/debate sometimes which was frustrating, but interesting guy.
Loved him! This class was great and his lectures were super interesting.

Dr. Bayne is a great lecturer and helped me to understand a lot about the course materials. I am excited to take more of his classes in the future. He is extremely knowledgeable about his field and is a great guy to have a conversation with.
Not bad Just do the work and you will be fine.

this class was a gen ed for me but i loved this class. prof and TA are awesome and i learned a lot. not a lot of hw for the class, probably an 1-2 each week but readings are required and they do notebook checks. exams were easy and theres xtra assignments to pad out ur grade. overall a super nice guy who wants to see students succeed!

I LOVED this class and the teacher. He is a great lecturer and I was never bored in his class. He is very clear on his assignments and exams. If you put in the work, this is a very easy class to get an A in. he gives and adequate amount of work. There is a lot of readings but they are enjoyable. He also made us food for the exam.
Lots of reading to do with the required book. Honestly, most of it can be overlooked by the lecture and recitation. Very knowledgable about the content and created a light hearted atmosphere.

This was my favorite course so far at Carolina. It made me reflect on my own faith and consider ways we could be doing better. Professor Bayne is super knowledgeable about both Christianity and Native history. Sometimes it was tough to confront so many difficult moments, but he always gave us helpful context and led creative group discussions.

Dr. Bayne and Carla were amazing this semester. The classroom environment is very engaging and interesting, and both are very caring. As long as you pay attention and study the exam guides, an A is nearly guaranteed. The best professor and TA duo I have had at UNC so far.

Lots of reading and lecture notes, if you pay attention and show up you should be ok. Tests can be challenging if you dont show up but you create a study guide together so no reason to do bad. Overall interesting class.

Prof. Bayne is amazing! He is very passionate about what he's talking about and is very nice! definitely not overwhelming! LOVE Carla(TA), although I believe she will be leaving next semester, so hopefully the next one will be good too! Def recommend!

Dr. Bayne is a great professor who knows so much about what he talks about. This course was very discussion based but it was very enjoyable and easy to take part in if you did the readings. It involved also going to plays of UNC arts performances and all assignments were given plenty of notice ahead of time. Overall a great course, would recommend

Dr. Bayne is super nice and really knowledgeable! All of the projects and assignments we did helped me think more deeply about the topics we were discussing and helped me explore lots of arts forms I had never been interested in before. I really enjoyed the class and would definitely recommend to someone looking for FC-AESTH credit.

Bayne and his TA were very nice and incredibly understanding. The class has a lot of work, but the work itself is pretty easy. The readings are very long and boring but you can get around doing them except for when it comes to discussion posts. Make sure to attend class and take notes, as the slides are very vague and mostly consist of pictures.

I enjoyed Prof. Bayne's class this semester. There is a lot of reading and you need to be prepared to discuss it at length in class. The work wasn't too bad though - discussion posts and responses, 2 quizzes, 1 paper, and a final project (no exam!) He wasn't good at keeping up with grading though. Overall very nice guy who wants you to succeed.

The class itself wasn't that much work: 10 discussion posts and replies, 2 quizzes, 1 midterm paper and a final project. But Bayne had no rubrics, barely any guidelines for assignments, and grading was random and subjective. He also didn't grade the majority of our assignments until the last week of class which was stressful and frustrating.

Disscussion posts were graded easily, but the readings are such a drab, and some are quite long. He started out quite nice, but became super jaded as the semster went on. Lectures are helpful for the essay portion of the exam, but referring to the slides to study is useless, there is nothing helpful on them.

This class is just made up of discussion posts throughout the semester, book review paper, 1 midterm and 1 final. Super easy. Caring teachers, and a nice environment. Would recommend to take for a gen end. Easy A.
Great guy, very organized. Made his midterm very fair and explained exactly what students needed to do. Material could be dry at some times.

I really enjoyed taking IDST128 with professor Bayne. He made the lectures interesting and the use of Jonathan Haidt's book was very informative and compelling. IDST128 is overall a great class when choosing a triple I.

Dr. Ariel is fantastic! His classes can be hard to follow and he interrupts presentations. BUT! He is a wealth of knowledge and I have never had a professor be more complimentary and supportive of my passion. He can take a joke, is willing to be (respectfully) challenged by students, and brought food to share at the beginning of class. He is great!
Great professor, gets to know his students, very personable. Would recommend him to anyone.

Great professor. Provided clear expectations for exams and opportunities to help prepare the class. Would highly recommend any class with Dr. Ariel. Honestly, a gem of a human. 

The topic of 242 (New Religious Movements) was unlike anything else I've ever learned and broadened my understanding of other faith communities.

I LOVED this class. Favorite professor and favorite class and i'm about to graduate. I would take any class he teaches. It's not hard if you try and are thoughtful. I really enjoyed the topics and Dr. Ariel always brought snacks, which was super kind. For the class, we got to visit churches and write about our experiences visiting them.

Dr. Ariel was the best professor of the three. He kept the class engaged through clips, texts, and slides. His essays were the easiest of the three, if you listened to him for 5 mins you could easily score an A. Plus, he gave you hints ahead of time. Great professor, especially if you are a history buff.
Professor Ariel is not engaging. The slides were all over the place and very boring class overall. Would not recommend.
horrible class. ariel is mid.

Yaakov was a bit eccentric, but always kind and caring. The class isn't difficult at all as long as you show up and participate in lecture. Grading criteria can be unclear at times, but contacting him via email/outside of class is easy.

Professor Ariel is an extremely genuine and passionate teacher. There were just a few church observation papers due throughout the semester that he graded pretty easily, and you could observe online. He brought snacks to every class, which always made my day. Readings were assigned but never mattered for class.

Semester consisted of four written assignments plus a comparative midterm assignment. Classes were very lecture heavy and at times a bit boring. Professor Ariel's feedback was not always super clear but he does offer regrades and wants everyone to succeed. Be prepared to put in a moderate effort to secure the grade you want.

I don't think he was a bad professor. The class just sucks and the location was not helping me learn. The microphones in the Stone Center were always hard to listen to and honestly I never could understand what either of the professors were saying. Yaakov definetely was the funniest one and liked to make a spectacle of students.

You can sit in the back row and avoid eye contact and he will still make you stand up in front of the class and say something. He's really funny and definitely a great personality but he doesn't really teach as much as he tries to facilitate discussion. This is a terrible class (mostly the TAs and UNCs faults) but Dr. Ariel is a great teacher

His assignments are broad, but he expects specific criteria in writing. It gets frustrating when trying to do assignments since his instruction is so broad and is usually only discussed in class rather than posting guidelines. Nice guy and occasionally gives second chances.

This class requires a lot of writing: there are four reflections on online church videos, at least two reviews, and an essay midterm, all of which are graded somewhat toughly. He let us write the midterm in advance and gave us all the terms that were going to be on the final, though. There's also a lot of reading, but you can get by not doing it.

I recommend both this class and Professor Ariel. He is an understanding professor that gives clear, precise feedback. You are graded on multiple papers (at least 6), but he offers extra credit in the form of redoing your papers for a better grade. Attend class! Lectures were slow and boring at times, but this class is an easy Gen-ed to knock out!

This class was super interesting to me, but often the lectures were hard to follow. Papers were graded harshly, but many opportunities were available to improve upon your work. Professor Ariel and his TA were easy to work with and wanted us to do well.
Prof. Ariel is personable and understanding. If you're a self-starter and remain engaged, the courseload is pretty manageable.
the guy is a jerk and the material is so boring and hard. worst class i have EVER taken (I am a senior)

Do not take a class with him. The most unorganized professor I've had. Syllabus was so confusing which caused problems for everyone in the class. Lectures hardly made sense because he went off on so many tangents. I feel liked I barely learned anything because I was confused the whole time. I'm a RELI major but I dreaded this class.

Professor Ariel is kind, but classes with him feel like they cover 20 minutes of content in a 70 minute session. He doesn't teach to the textbook. The only graded assignments are digital church visits and film/book reviews. He asks questions on the material before he teaches it, so if you have no background knowledge, you won't have answers.

She gives great feedback and is always available outside of class through email. She is very kind and welcoming of questions. As long as you do the work correctly and participate during class, grading is extremely fair. I would highly recommend her, especially to students who want to improve their writing and critical thinking skills.

Professor Boon is great! This class is heavily part participation and there is a lot of reading prior to class, but Boon keeps class super interesting. I would really recommend this class because it not that hard, but you do have to put effort in. There is a good bit of writing, but Boon is super helpful in and out of class.

A great professor. The things that UNC students write on here really devalue the degrees from this school.  Who's more qualified to say what level of work is appropriate for a 100- or 200-class? A professional with years of experience, or a teenager fresh out of high school? Stop crying about having to work hard. You're at a top college.

I took this as a fully asych Maymester and was honestly surprised by how harshly she graded for how few assignments there were. Her comments were brief and unhelpful even for low scores, so you never know what you need to work on next time. She always required "more analysis" despite putting strict word limits on writing assignments. DO NOT TAKE!

The directions for the discussion assignments are always so straightforward with word counts all under 200. Yet, no matter how much detail and connection and out-of-the-box thinking you do, she always wants something more. It doesn't seem possible to do so without surpassing 500 words, yet it is never enough. The grading is so arbitrary.

Dr. Boon is really nice and clearly very knowledgable, but an extremely hard grader for a 200 level religion course. She is nitpicky- you can definitely pass doing what she tells you to do but only going out of the box/beyond her expectations will get you an A. Overall, content was set up great for an online class and I enjoyed it!

TOUGH grader. Expects you to be at a "ready to graduate" level of writing. Their feedback is cosmetic and while they teach great theological content their instruction lacks in knowing how to connect to the student and guide them to a finish line that allows for ideas to grow from said feedback. She will embarrassingly make an example out of you.

Pretty easy PH credit. I' feel like she makes it so that most people get good grades because I don't think I deserved an A tbh. There are 2 papers, a midterm and a final. Content is sometimes boring but sometimes interesting. I would def recommend for a gen ed class. Especially if Bryce is the TA, he's really great.

This class was great overall! Professor Boon is very knowledgeable about the material and the structure of the class works well! Bryce was our TA for the semester and was awesome! Class participation does make up your grade, but it is not overly strict (3 unexcused absences). Definitely recommend!

This class is a decent PH gen ed. There are a several papers and journals due but they aren't graded too harshly. You do need to do some of the reading to complete those assignments but it's not bad. She provides the essay questions for the exams in advance so you can prepare beforehand.

Professor Boon is an amazing lecturer. She presents the information so well and is very good at explaining incredibly complex philosophical and theological concepts in terms that everyone understands. This makes her class that much more interesting, because it is clear that she is very knowledgeable aboutthe subject without being too obscure.

Lectures could sometimes be a bit boring and the required reading was intense sometimes. But like other comments have said a lot of grades were participation. She is a bit of a tough critic for essays, but overall she's a great professor.

Prof. Boon was VERY knowledgeable about course material.  Lectures were engaging and material pertained to contemporary events.  There were lots of projects/assignments that were graded for participation which helped keep grades high and Prof. Boon rounds at the 0.5 (92.5 = A).  My only complaint is that there were a LOT of required readings.

Lots of reading and writing and the contents feel super boring and dense, and the gradings are exteremly unforgiving. Plus, this class has high threshold (95%) for getting an A. Overall, exhauative class and waste my time. Take this class if you truly enjoy religion. If not, please AVOID it at all cost.
Professor Ochoa is very kind but his class is extremely hard and the gradings of the rubrics very unclear. The class contents are super boring.
Very nice and helps everyone

Todd was great for RELI 121, lectures were mostly discussion based and centered around groups of 4. You should really do the readings if you are going to have any hope of understanding the class, but if you buy into it it will be top their!

Professor Ochoa is a very kind man and assumes excellence in students. You have a discussion board and a short writing assignment every week(allowed to skip 3). From my understanding these assignments were graded based on completion and you just had 2 longer papers graded by TAs. I took notes in class and had no trouble writing them.

Passionate and caring professor. The small group oriented lessons implemented for this semester were a miss (especially if you're anxious speaking in a massive class hall). Class attendance is graded but may be *ahem* bypassed relatively easily with the check-in beacon system. Lots of homework is assigned, but was ungraded and therefore optional.

Awesome professor. Really knows what he's talking about is my favorite type of nerd/geek. He really does make the class engaging and provides nice discussions in class. There is a lot of material you need to read, however Ochoa does clarify ideas and concepts from them in his lectures. I would highly suggest taking this professor.

Grade is mostly made up of two papers (a midterm and a final), while the rest of your grade is just attendance and doing the required work for recitation. Lots of reading but Dr Ochoa does a great job explaining them during lecture, and making intentional time to review the text before beginning lecture. Ochoa is a fascinating man.

Ochoa is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Lectures were amazing and extremely interesting, class was fun and interactive. He makes very deep topics about religion and society very accessible to people of all backgrounds. I'm a CS major and Todd made me want to add a RELI minor. Not that hard if you just do the work and skim the readings.

I liked the setup where we were in groups and would always discuss the readings in class, although that meant it was a flipped classroom. He is a great, funny guy and he manages to make the theories of religion fun and interesting while being fair in grading and assignments.

I love love love Todd. He makes abstract topics and learning as a whole really personal. I'd describe RELI 121 as an introduction to the philosophy of religion class and I found it to be really interesting. Todd is realistic and understanding. You could get a good grade with little work, but I really loved engaging with both Todd and the material.

Cannot recommend prof Ochoa more. He was able to make deeply complex topics interesting, understandable, and relevant, and is able to make you feel important and heard in a large lecture class. There was a decent amount of weekly hw, but it was not too difficult, and the only major grades were 2 papers. Great prof, caring, def would take again.
Sometimes his lectures were a bit confusing but recitations helped a lot. Easy class though for gen ed credit!

TAKE THIS CLASS!! I never would have thought I would enjoy a gen ed but this one was entertaining, very lecture heavy but interactive with peers, no quizzes or tests just a midterm paper and final paper. Recitation grade is worth a lot so easy to get a high grade in the class as long as you show up. highly recommend todd is the goat

TAKE. THIS. CLASS. TAKEITTAKEITTAKEIT!! Todd is an amazing prof. I've never been so engaged during lectures. Recitations and discussion posts are the only grades besides attendance and midterm and final papers which are graded super easy. Class is super open ended and engaging and content is fascinating. Don't do the readings, just watch the videos

The content is super engaging Professor Ochoa is the most engaging "lecturers" that I have had. I put that in quotes because his lectures are more group discussions than lecture. Your own thoughts about the content are important. There are very helpful videos that explain the reading content.

This class is interesting- it's honestly more of a philosophy class than a religion class. Lots of very philosophical readings and concepts. Attendance is important (20% of grade), and then weekly reading responses, midterm (20% of grade), and final (30% of grade). Class is overall not a ton of work, Prof Ochoa is also a lovely guy, kooky but nice!

The class was a pretty easy A. Showing up to class/recitation and weekly forum posts were worth half of your grade. The other half was 2 papers which took a lot of time, but even with my low-quality papers, I got an A on both. However, Todd doesn't grade these, it's your TA. So choose Arpan to be your TA if given the choice.

This class was super interesting; I'd never taken a religion class before (though I took philosophy in high school), but Prof Ochoa made the material as accessible as possible. Every lecture was so informative and interesting. He's also just a lovely guy; he's caring and funny. He cares a lot about this class, so he wants you to care too. 10/10!!

So far, Ochoa's reading assignments are incredibly philosophical rather than on the topic of Religious Things. If you're into roundabout ways of overcomplicating simple concepts (philosophy), then this would be fine, but as a RELI major this isn't what I signed up for. Plus, he has a weird pedagogy which leads to him not really teaching any content

Professor Mendez was a great lecturer, I really enjoyed this class. Felt that recitation participation was biased as I participated in every class but still got 4/5 for participation. The class is not HW heavy at all, exams consisted of essays and vocab, but he provides a study guide. I do feel like the essays take up a lot of studying time though.
Best lecturer I've ever had, extremely passionate

Hugo is one of the best lecturers at UNC. He is obviously passionate about the subject and while he will admit he is Catholic he teaches from a totally unbiased, historical perspective. As a Christian, I was not expecting RELI 104 to challenge my faith but it certainly did. However this is something that I think ever Christian should experience.

I took this class for an interesting, and relatively simple introductory focus capacity. It has not been what I was expecting. The tests are graded ridiculously harsh. I was talking to a friend with a different TA and they were getting 2 points off for things that I got 5 points taken off of. Just very frustrating

Doesn't teach anything from the textbook that he wrote, but still tests all vocabulary from it. Exams are way too difficult and harshly graded for an introductory level class. Spent more time studying for this class than for any of my biology or math classes, it was unnecessarily time consuming and difficult
I loved this class. I learned a lot and Dr. Mendez was passionate about what he taught. The tests however were graded hard, so I didn't do as well as I wanted to.

If you get the opportunity to take a class with Dr. Mendez, take it! He made going to a 9am easy. His lectures are entertaining. He is also an incredibly kind professor and wants to see his students succeed. Now, the class is quite test heavy with three exams making up 68% of your grade. However, he gives a detailed study guide that is cumulative.

Prof. Mendez was one of my favorite professors I have ever had at UNC. He kept lectures engaging, attendance was mandatory but he made them fun. Workload was one 6-8 sentence reflection from each class and one 8-10 sentence paragraph from a prompt a week. Exams were very fair and study guide was super helpful. LOVED this class and this professor!

Wonderful professor, great lectures, and such a nice guy. Midterms count for a good amount of your grade, but they are pretty easy and you can do well if you use his study guides. Overall really enjoyed this class and would definitely recommend him as a professor.

Great professor and cares a lot about the material! Unbiased, and easily accessible. Definitions on tests can be oddly specific and meant to trick you, but everything is in the slides from class. Made attendance required halfway through the semester because everyone stopped showing up. Hard to bring your grade back up if you do bad on a midterm.

He is one of the best professors I've ever had! He truly cares about each and every student. For each test, he gives a detailed study guide with all the possible questions he could give. Have multiple assignments that also help your grade, as they are basically just a completion grade. Lectures are very interesting.
the absolute goat. if you can take his class do it. easy A. gives you the test questions to study. so nice and very knowledgable.

I loved Dr. Mendez. I took him for 416 cult of the Saints (not an option), he is a sweetheart and cares so much. Class was a few discussion posts, in-class talks, a martyrs feast, and one big paper broken up to keep you on track 100/10 recommend

Amazing class. Took online during maymester. Second class with Mendez. Super flexible. Low effort. Gives 100s for almost everything. Open book quizzes and exams. Don't buy the textbook, you can find it online for free. I wouldn't even read it honestly, just use it to find answers for the quizzes.

Took this class over maymester for a gen ed and recommend to anyone who needs it for a gen ed or even as an elective. The ideal workload for what you'd expect from a gen ed. Discussion posts and daily quizzes to do everyday with a midterm and final. Professor Mendez is easily accessible outside of class, very caring, and responds to emails quickly.
Hugo was a great teacher, gave study guides, and attendance wasnt necessarily mandatory. however, my TA was very unreasonable and kind of screwed me over.

Dr. Mendez is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Down to Earth, kind, and comprehensible/interesting lectures. Teaches Christianity from an unbiased, academic perspective; very respectful of all beliefs. Such a fabulous professor, could not recommend him more.

Dr. Mendez has been my favorite professor at UNC. He's funny and is responsible. He made an error in one recitation's exam and gave everyone a 100% to make it fair. His lectures are very interesting and you can tell he knows what he's talking about. Study guides are clear and exams are easy if you know the vocab and study the free response answers.

I took 2 RELI classes with prof Mendez and both were awesome. He is kind, funny, and loves what he does. Exams are very straightforward and memorization heavy, which I enjoyed. Daily reflections are helpful for keeping up with the information and lecture material in the class. Definitely take one of his classes!!

Professor Mendez has been one of my favorite professors at UNC. He's obviously very knowledgable about what he's teaching and cares about his students. He is understanding when things come up and will take responsibility if he makes a mistake, which happened with one of our exams. I would definitely take him if given the chance.

Class is straightforward and easy for the most part. However, be cautious on the final book report as grading may not reflect your effort if your views differ from the professor's. Emailing about grades may go unanswered for days with no resolution. Lay low, avoid controversial opinions, and you will be fine.

easy class, tbf she was going through a lot this semester so i think thats why it was easy. all the grades were purely off our journal reflections and participation. lecture heavy so def take notes. besides it being easy, she knows her stuff and doesn't make u feel stupid (im not muslim so that helped a lot).

Very interesting class and feminist insight! Also, very easy. My class didn't have pop quizzes they dropped all of them which was nice. Journals are easy and you don't have to do them all. Great course!

Great Professor and really cares about her students. You have weekly 500 words journals that aren't difficult just do some of the readings, not all it's a lot, and take notes in class and you're fine. Book review, an Art project with a write-up, 3 papers for final. The overall class was not that hard and she made learning fun.

Dr. Hammer is awesome! She truly cares about creating as "safe" a space as possible within the classroom. She's lenient on deadlines as well so if you need an extra day or so as long as you communicate with her she's cool. Learned so much with her and my classmates! Please participate!! She wants to create discussion and learn from students!

Dr. Hammer is one of the most brilliant professors at UNC. She is an easy and accommodating grader who truly cares about her students and just wants them to succeed. Yes she is opinionated, but also so smart and makes you read a variety of voices that challenge normative ideas. Do your readings, go to class, and you'll do great and learn a ton!

She is the EASIEST professor ever from a grading perspective. Made our class essentially pass/fail and everyone who passed got an A. However, you need to share her beliefs, or she will look down on you. Very opinionated. Like so much. For the grade, it was worth it to stick it out but I probably wouldn't take a class from her again.

I think that the teaching is very ineffective in the sense that it is not teaching, but telling students what they should think by quickly shutting down other opinions. I did not really grow much from this course and I would not take it again.

I think you are better off teaching yourself and formulating your own opinions or taking other courses.
Creates an uncomfortable learning environment to share thoughts and my peers dropped this class due to that reason
Dismissive and condescending attitudes towards interpretations of Islam that do not align with her thinking

Dr. Hammer TRULY cares. She prioritizes teaching and learning over grades, and it takes off a lot of the pressure - the only thing I cared about in that class was learning. Readings can be a lot, but a fast read through and paying attention in class was enough for me. She is an amazing human and professor.

Take this class for credit! Hammer is a lenient grader and lets you turn in assignments whenever you can. Very understanding. Assignments were easy, readings not really mandatory, no tests or quizzes. The entire class is basically being lectured which is sometimes boring but not bad, attendance is mandatory and part of grades.

Dr. Hammer is the best prof I've had! This is my 2nd class with her, and she is one of the most intelligent and caring people I have ever met. I have struggled a lot this semester, and she went out of way to accommodate and check on me. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed no matter what, and the material is eye opening/fun!
Nice person, but can be dismissive towards other opinions.

This class was great. Dr. Nester was very prompt in grading assignments and giving ample feedback. Class discussions were stimulating and thought provoking, and I always felt comfortable speaking in class.
Flexible with assignment deadlines and very responsive.

Prof. Nester is very nice and enthusiastic about what she teaches. She really cares about students understanding the materials. The lectures were very informative and engaging and the class discussions were interesting. Homework assignments were straightforward and most of the time she gave the answers already in class before we had to submit.

I really enjoyed Dr. Nester's class! The lectures were very engaging and the assignments were manageable. She was very clear about what is expected in the assignments and exams and gave very detailed and helpful feedback.

The class was very interesting and the lectures were well-organized with really helpful slides that made studying for the exams much more manageable. Prof. Nester is very nice and accommodating. She encouraged participation in class and gave a lot of helpful feedback on the homework assignments.
She was very attentive to students' needs and was flexible with assignments. The lectures were super interesting and you could see Dr. Nester is passionate about the subject.

Dr. Nester was a very kind and understanding professor. She assigned lots of extremely lengthy readings which were the only things covered in lecture. Her exams were what you make of them, she is very clear with what will be on the exam, you just have to make sure to prepare for them well because she is a tough grader in my opinion.

Professor Nester's class was wonderful. We read engaging texts from diverse perspectives, creating a rich and meaningful learning experience. Discussions were consistently thoughtful and in-depth. Exams were fair, and she clearly reviewed key material and how to prepare. Highly recommended.

I enjoyed this class! You can tell Nester is very passionate about the subjects, which sometimes led to going over time with lectures and getting off schedule. She really wants to help her students, she gave plenty of feedback on assignments and offered extra credit. She can be a little bit of a tough grader, but is clear with her expectations.

She is very kind but grades extremely harsh. Make sure you go to her office hours before the analytic paper. The group project was very annoying. In the assignments you need to be as specific as possible to her questions. Midterm and final are doable they require a ton of studying

She was vague about her expectations and did not teach much- she just expected you to know how to analyze texts in the way she wanted you to. The class was mostly just open-ended discussions. Graded harshly considering she gave so little guidance. I would steer clear of taking this class with her if you have the choice.

Dr. Nester is a great professor. The class had a ton of readings, and sometimes her lectures were slightly difficult to follow. But she is very approachable and always ready to answer any questions you have. Very passionate about the course topics. Not a very tough grader but you will have to work hard to get an A. Would recommend.

The class itself was of reasonable difficulty since it is a 300-level class. The grammar wasn't that hard but had to write a few essays that were challenging. No warning about graphic content for the films we had to watch. The final consists of the usual quiz questions but also an ESSAY! Took me the entire 3h to finish, still shaky.

Professor Nester is very nice and is passionate about the topic of antisemitism. I felt this class is very lackluster, it drags on slowly. The texts we read are somewhat confusing but philosophical. Maybe my class is just a dull group of students but don't take this course if you don't like to read. I like her as a person and she is very caring.
Super disorganized and terrible teacher. Felt my German got worse after taking this class.

This class was super unorganized and Professor Nester assigned some questionable material. Many of the mandatory films contained scenes with graphic sexual violence that I was not prepared for because she attached no trigger warnings. Aside from this, the readings are boring, and "lecture" is just her rambling about random stuff. Fell asleep daily
GSLL 56 was an extremely interesting first year seminar. Grading was fair, and the lectures were highly interactive.

I took GERM/GSLL 56 in spring semester of 2021 and it was a very interesting class. Dr. Nester was very nice and understanding and was always interested in her students' wellbeing, good professor and taught the class well

Dr. Rose is really passionate about what she teaches and she sets you up well for success in this class. Lectures could be dry and hard to engage with, but great option to get FC-CREATE credit. She is a kind grader.

Great prof, extremely knowledgeable. Lectures are very articulate and interesting, however if you are not interested in the subject matter, you might not like them. Feedback can take a while and be nitpicky, but if you participate in class and try, you will get a good grade.

Class was quite boring, assignments had gone ungraded for half of the semester +, tough grader on subjective matters, it is hard to communicate and evaluate effort and assignment grades when grades do not come out until the day final grades are due. 

Every class period was rushed and there was a lack of communication and transparency.

Prof Rose is very nice, and did her best with this class. However, it was quite boring, and I felt the lectures would go on and on. You make a film for your final and use editing software, which must be planned out, but she outlines it well. Its an easy class, but not the most interesting class.

GSLL 273. Nice person. Easy to get an A-, hard to get an A since everything is graded subjectively, it's like she'll take points off for something even though it was never clear that was what she was looking for. Can't really complain though because I put very little effort into work outside of class and during class.

Extremely sweet, understanding, and intelligent professor. A real gem. I've probably had classes that I enjoyed more but she was my favorite professor easily. Don't be intimidated by the difficulty of the readings, the class isn't hard. I'd rate it like a 2.8/5. Interesting too.

She is very kind and understanding. she has in class assignments that you cannot make up if you miss class but if you miss a day that does that contain one, then it won't hurt you to miss. she drops a lot of grades and it is an easy A class. Only thing is some of the material is sexual and concerning to talk about if not exposed before hand.

Dr. Rose is so kind and knowledgeable. Get ready for the unexpected- because this class is not what you're thinking! I loved participating in class and engaging in discussions with her. You are expected to do a lot of reading and film watching, which is interesting but a ton of work. Overall it's manageable, and meeting Dr. Rose makes it worth it!

I did not really know what to expect when I enrolled in 287, but I ended up really enjoying the class. At first I struggled on assignments, but then I worked with Professor Rose to address my mistakes. She is very accessible outside of class and wants her students to succeed.

Probably my favorite professor at UNC, inspired me to pick up a minor for GSLL, she's amazing. If you're ever reading reviews and wondering whether you should take a class with her, you have to do it!!!

Dr. Rose is wonderful! She is so enthusiastic about her topic and always ready to help talk through tricky concepts. She was very real with us about the workload and gave us extra days when we needed them to talk through stuff. If you're a good writer and try, this will be an easy A and a FUN easy A!

Dr. Rose is an absolute gem! She makes her criteria clear. The assignments are relatively easy (minus average-toughness midterm and final research paper). The readings are quite manageable and she is very understanding if you're struggling. Do the readings, visit office hours once, pay attention in class and you should get an A

Dr. Rose is simply a fantastic professor. She cares about her students and the material greatly. Although this course is graded by few things, she is accessible to students outside of class and is willing to help set you up for success. The course material itself is also just very interesting. Unbeatable class if you have background interest.

Dr. Rose is incredibly well-spoken and her lectures were so fascinating to me. She truly cares about her students and the readings were interesting. She does not grade quickly and there are only a few assignments that factored into your final grade but if you pay attention, go to office hours once or twice and do the readings you'll get an A.
She slays. Leads great discussions about interesting readings and films. Loved this class, great way to get EE credit.
Shes great

GSLL 481
Professor Rose is amazing. Lectures are in-depth and you can tell she is really passionate about the topic. She grades anonymously to make it fair for all the students. She also is not a tough grader at all. There are only a few grades for this class. Course ontent is only as engaging as you make it.

Professor Prica was nice, however I did not enjoy this class. It was INCREDIBLY reading heavy. Some of the readings that took hours were covered for maybe 10 minutes and other than that totally wasted. Classes were very disorganized, and no study guides for exams which were all tiny details and dates. Also she graded all of our essays with AI.

Dr. Prica is one of the best professors I have had here at UNC. She is very lenient with deadlines and gives great feedback on all homework and essays. You basically have a 10-15 minute homework assignment due before each class, but it is very easy and helps a lot for the tests. She is very down-to-earth and engaging in her lectures as well!

Very sweet, funny teacher who is interested in the topic and wants to hear her students' various opinions. As long as you did the readings and actively listened in class, the class was really fun and has been my favorite in my time at UNC. The writing assignments helped me try some new styles I might not explore in a STEM-heavy major.
Very interesting course content. Graded on a few papers, simple post-reading questions, and participation. Reading the texts is important but participating was easy enough.
Most caring professor. Makes participating easy! Thoroughly enjoyed this class.
Goated. She is very passionate about the topics in class and the only thing she expects is adequate participation in class.

Dr. Prica is very humble and kind! She gave us grace with due dates and was in tune with her students' needs/feedback. The course is structured on five easy papers and in-class participation/discussion.

Professor Prica is extremely smart, brilliant, and funny. You can tell she cares so much about her students and is always open to discuss grades and gives excellent feedback. Assignments are very creative and thought-provoking, and she always leads very interesting discussions in class.

Lots of reading. Class time is spent with some lecturing but mainly discussion. She occasionally gets off-topic, but her side comments are mostly interesting and I almost always learn something. She does care about you and wants to help you succeed. Very kind and willing to help with assignments if you go to office hours.

Dr. Prica is very kind, but her lectures are incredibly boring and disorganized. The tests are pure regurgitation of specific details and don't really involve any critical thinking. If you can't memorize 100 random facts, you're pretty much screwed. Also not really a GOT class.

Dr Prica's lectures were very well thought-out and prepped, and if you took good notes, doing well this class was very achievable. She cares about the content and the students being involved with the material, however might have overestimated how much students would care about the medieval history behind GoT. I still really enjoyed the course.

Easy seminar. Long readings (~2/wk) but the quizzes are fairly doable. If you miss one talk to her and she'll let you do it late and give full credit. There's a separate participation grade that can lower your grade a lot if bad, so speak in class. Most classes begin with a lecture followed by a ~15 min group activity. Extra credit is given.

The course had on average two readings and a movie per week. Overall, she was an easy-grader and the material was fair. The midterm was only difficult due to not enough time given to complete it. You can tell that she is interested in the material and has a passion for it.
She was such an easy teacher. She is such an easy grader, but the amount of work the class has is crazy. U should usually be fine not doing any of the work but regardless the class was super easy

Dr. Layne is a good professor and is knowledgable in her area of expertise. While the class is pretty easy, there is quite a bit of work which include readings, films, papers, and other random assignments. I would recommend this class if you are interested in the topic, as the class may not be that engaging if you are not interested.
I had Professor Layne for the 2025 summer abroad course, the Weaponization of Knowledge. She was so amazing, enthusiastic, and caring! I would absolutely recommend this course to any major.

Dr. Layne was one of the three professors in my triple I (science fiction) course. She was my favorite professor out of the three, and I honestly wish she had more lectures. She is super passionate about what she teaches, and her lectures are engaging and interesting.

Dr. Layne was one of three professors in my triple-I. I wish she got to speak more because her lectures were so incredibly interesting!! While sometimes the content felt like a reach, and it was easy to get lost in all of the information, Dr. Layne is clearly passionate about her studies and was always interested in engaging with her students.
I took her for my Triple-I class (there was no IDST tag, sorry!), and she is a very kind woman. I genuinely enjoyed her lectures, her part of the class made the whole thing very enjoyable!

Dr. Layne is very understanding and caring of her students. She does build a connection with students in class and cares about what she teaches. It does not seem though that she follows her own grading scale. By her record I should have an A, but instead put an A- on connect.

GSLL 288 was one of my favorite classes I've taken at UNC. Dr. Layne is so sweet and a little awkward but incredible at getting you to analyze texts. Can't complain much about reading comic books for homework! Very short responses to readings due every week, if you try you'll get an A, and learn a lot about chronic illness and disability.
I really enjoyed this class. I felt like I learned a lot and the class was super interactive. Prof. Layne is super understanding and helpful. Assignments and tests/ exams are not hard.

Professor Layne is one of the kindest professors I have had at UNC. However, I gained very little from this course and did not learn much in class. I feel like anything that I learned is what I taught myself. We would do grammar exercises in class from the homework, but they were not taught or explained. I do not suggest taking this class.

Some professors can take a topic I don't find interesting and make it interesting through the class. This was not the case for Hitler in Hollywood. All of the assignments were manageable (though the amount was sometimes annoying), but I just don't love WWII as a topic. Dr. Layne didn't seem super enthusiastic about a lot of it either.

I loved this class & highly recommend it! Sure, a few films were a bit boring but overall it was a very good selection, and if you're taking this class then you know what you're getting into film-wise. Extremely fair homework load, and steady course structure each week. She grades very fairly. Her lectures were very interesting and engaging! 10/10

I found his class very engaging, he seemed to make an effort to include some sort of interactive every class. Watch out because some of the assignments are posted on Canvas but not in the syllabus and he won't take them late. Overall I liked his class, would recommend, the material is interesting.

Major dislike of the “professor discretion” portion of the grade. There is an attendance policy, test and other grades, and then 15% of your final grade is left up to “discretion”. Had I gotten a higher discretion grade, I would have ended with an A. Not saying he is biased, but feels unfair. DO NOT TAKE

he was completely insensitive, said he did not care about our mental health and not to come crying to him about anything, told us that he purposely made the midterm too long so we would not finish, and was then replaced halfway through the semester by the department.

I would never take a class taught by him again. For every class period you miss, you must write a 1-2 page single-spaced paper based on the readings. 25 percent of your grade is labeled "professor discretion".

20% of grade was professor discretion. participated, did well, didn't miss any classes and still got an 85% for some reason
lots of readings and some hard to understand 
final project was reforming a school...expected you to know very minute details about the behind the scenes that were not taught in class and hard to find online

Not a fan of lauen. There's a ton of extra readings and assignments that confuse the topic. the class is unnecessarily burdensome as the content itself doesn't have to be so complicated. dreaded class of the policy major bc of it
