Halfway through the semester, Prof. Lauen was removed from the class as a professor due to many student complaints and questionable teaching choices. On day one, he called someone out for having to retake the class. He told us no one would do well or finish the midterm and not to come crying to him. This is not the first time this has happened.

Professor Lauen made a difficult subject, even MORE difficult. Lectures were long and often not applicable to the assignments due at the end of the week. Throughout the semester there were numerous instances where Professor Lauen made inappropriate comments to students. Needless to say if you have to take PLCY 460 wait until Moulton teaches.

I honestly loved him. I know he has bad reviews, but this semester has been great. The class is obviously difficult, but students blame the teacher for not doing well when they aren't trying. He was very caring and understanding, especially with the group project. Also, I thought he was really funny and very much so enjoyed his music taste.

Professor, Lauen was very unforthcoming about what he wanted for literally everything. We were graded on three assignments, two essays and a final group project. All of his comments on all of them were vague at best. 
OVERALL I HATED THIS CLASS.

This class had no clear grading criteria, vague projects/essays, and very little teacher instruction. Assignments were given with little time to complete them and Professor Lauen was not willing to listen to student conflicts with deadlines. No rubrics for the class and feedback is unhelpful, so you will lose points and likely never understand why.

Rubric has two items ("content & clarity") which he would not elaborate on. Rude to students when they have different opinions. Unorganized: didn't describe project worth 30% of grade until 2 weeks before due, and then changed project every class period until 5 days before due. & more, but I don't have enough characters. DON'T TAKE THIS PROF.

Overall, this class was an absolute mess from the very beginning! The pop quizzes are just bad, there are exercises to do, and lab videos to watch along with recitations and readings. Lauen is terrible in lectures and was often rude, but is okay one on one. He should really stick to small classes as it seems large lectures are not his strong suit.

Professor Lauen was a pretty solid professor. Super knowledgeable and assigned super interesting readings. He's kind of a tough grader and made his expectations confusing at times, but overall I was never extremely lost. Grade is based on two papers, a project, and participation. Make sure to contribute to discussion. Overall learned a lot.

His course sounded very excited, but I was quickly disappointed with the lack of room I had to grow in the course and the inadequate feedback given weeks after assignments were submitted. Standards for grading were always met by the same answer of "content" and "clarity" with no further details or rubrics, especially with the final project.

I found the class to be pretty disorganized (quizzes announced the night before, grading criteria not very specific or clear). The class covers a lot of material, too: both coding and statistics. If you're like me and don't understand stats, take a stats/coding class first. The TA's kept me afloat, but the class was stressful. Wouldn't take again.

He's by no means my favorite professor in the world but I do think other people are a bit harsh. It's really hard to get an A but if you actually show up to class, put in the work, and find people to study with you should be able to pass. He was always helpful to me and my group when we went to office hours but no he's not always the kindest.

Doug Lauen does not care about his students. He repeatedly violated ARS accommodations and humiliated students by cold calling them to the front. He mocked stressed students before our midterm by blasting "Under Pressure" as students cried. He was slow to respond to emails and responded bluntly with little compassion, if he responded at all.

It is true that this is a hard class, but I have taken many hard policy classes and this guy is not only an awful person but an awful professor. He likes to make fun of his students in front of everyone, provides no constructive feedback, and I feel I have learned nothing from this course. Take this class with another professor I beg you.

Truly one of the worst professors Ive taken at this school, dont understand how people defend him. He's been rude to students in lectures, rude to students over email, and will rake you over the coals in front of the class. He gives vague & unhelpful feedback & does not coordinate with the TAs at all. The TAs are the only reason people are passing.

Prof. Sasser is very sweet and accommodating. This class was a seminar so she encourages group conversation as much as possible. There are no tests/finals but instead 3 in class writing assignments based on homework readings and lectures as well as an essay worth 25% of your grade. She gives great feedback and not a tough grader.

Professor Sasser is a difficult professor to work with. She would often grade deliverables using her own interpretations of “professionalism” rather than the actual rubric. She took 2 weeks to grade our final deliverable but gave us a 48 hour turn around for the final version. If you get her as your instructor just drop the class, save yourself.

Pretty basic class with not too much new info if you took APES, but in class discussions and assignments are interesting. Went on a few field trips and had many guest speakers which were super exciting. Prof. Sasser is super sweet and responds quickly, but didn't grade anything until exams started and 1 assignment chain is 50% of your grade.

I loved this class. Mrs. Sasser is one of my favorite teachers, she's so passionate and actually helpful when it comes to career advice and seems to genuinely care. I will say I had many papers where I had points taken off with no explanation and there were a few where I missed one mark on the rubric and received an 80, 20 points seemed harsh.

Easy in class lecture, but constantly had unclear AND unreasonable expectations. She is kind and very accessible, but no matter how good your work is, she'll take off points just because she can. I've received feedback that says no more than "--, excellent work!" but then my actual grade is poor and she won't explain why. Makes success unattainable

This instructor is sweet, BUT plcy 51 as a class is not amazing. The class is all over the place and her grading is so unclear. She deducts points for everything and honestly grades like you are supposed to be a FLAWLESS human. Elizabeth is an AMAZING person, but a frustrating and disliked prof. I believe she will get better since she is new.

Loved Prof Sasser. She's super sweet and helpful, but grading was confusing and took off for criteria never clearly stated in rubric. Usually gave detailed feedback but sometimes gave positive feedback on papers with no criticism, then took points off with no explanation. Very frustrating but overall super easy class, can skim readings and be fine

Very entertaining lecturer and very passionate/knowledgeable about his subject matter. Although the class is exam heavy, it isn't hard at all to do well on the exams so long as you've done the readings for the semester. Would absolutely recommend to anyone in the plcy major to take at least one course with preiss before they graduate!
Great Lecturer and very great in office hours. The class is very reading and exam heavy but is manageable

Professor Preiss is a very engaging lecturer. He is also very understanding and even took away the quizzes at the beginning of class after a week because he felt that they were unfair. Make sure to study for the exams though–moderate difficulty but midterm is 40% of your grade and final is 40% of your grade so study and understand readings.

The GOAT. Super chill and funny during lectures, even if the readings were a bit much at times. Also very receptive to student feedback; he abolished reading quizzes (attendance) because he didn't like the "vibe" they brought. Two easy exams worth 40% each and a few group essays are your grade, and both are graded leniently. Definitely take him.

I really learned a lot from Dr. Preiss, but his class was not my favorite. The midterm and final were both 40% meaning 80% in exams. I can't decide how easily they grade the exams because I did really well on one but poor on the other. He also asigns 40 pages of reading a class and the whole class is based on those readings. Hes super stylish tho.

He is an amazing lecturer who loves to try to engage not only through the content, but with his dad humor. He's super accessible and amenable to looking over grades if you believe the TA wasn't fair. Favorite lecturer I have had in the PLCY department and my only gripe is the class consisted of 2 40% exams which were fair, but the weight is scary

Dr. Preiss was a great lecturer and pretty funny. The course is graded on 2 exams and 4 group essays (easy A's). Tests were heavy on just showing what you know from the readings (he covers the main ideas of each text in class).

I really enjoyed Dr Goldsmith and the class. While it can seem like he makes things unnecessarily hard, all this class really comes down to is putting in the time. Put real effort into your assignments and projects, and you should do fine. The ten page policy brief is very manageable, as it consists of assignments completed throughout the term.

I had some preconceived notion about him going into the class from hearing it would be a lot of work and difficult. Guys, come on. The reading is really manageable. I have genuinely never had a professor offer so much extra credit. He is super compassionate, it is not hard if you try. Definitely too smart to be teaching a 101 class though.

Dr. Goldsmith selects good readings and has interesting topics to lecture on but he relies too much on audience participation. He uses class time to get student opinions, and often doesn't even adress the questions he poses. I found it hard to study for tests because he rarley provides definitions for terms, yet he grades in a very specific manor.
Course was way too hard for a first year intro course, homework and test were obnoxiously hard for no reason.

Such an understanding and knowledgeable professor. Probably the smartest and most well-informed professor I've had at UNC thus far. Semester long paper, wasn't too bad. Before and after class assignments as attendance. Reading heavy but it wasn't too strenuous. Take him, if you have a slight interest in public policy or PPE you won't regret it.

There's nothing wrong with this professor, but I wasn't a fan. This class was at 8 am, and I had enough trouble staying awake without his lectures lulling me to sleep. He graded fairly, but we just didn't click.

Dr. Goldsmith is the goat. He assigned a lot of readings, but I didn't do any and did fine in the class. He really cared about his students and public policy. As long as you put a little bit of effort into the class and study for the midterm/final you'll be fine. He's an awesome professor.

Very knowledgeable about policy, and it definitely shows in this class. He clearly puts a lot of effort into each lecture, but there is also a lot of reading before each class. Very kind, nice to speak with in and outside of class, and gives so many opportunities to improve your grade. You will need to put effort in, but you will get a lot out.

Goldsmith is a really caring person, but this class itself should not have been so hard for a first year requirement. The grading criteria is extremely vague and frustrating. Homework takes hours nearly every week and you are expected to do a lot of pre-class reading. Great professor, but disorganized and unnecessarily difficult class.

Dr. Goldsmith is one of the most passionate and caring professors I have met on this campus. Although he is strict in his syllabus, he is open to listening about problems you see with it, allowing for compromise. However, even with that being said, I feel that he gives too much pre-class work, assigning more than he should for a first year class.

Goldsmith is AMAZING! However, he did not have the grade calculator on for the entire semester. The class focuses on your final brief, so pick a topic you are interested in, most of your grade will depend on it (even part of your final). You get a cheat sheet for exams! I learned a lot and always wanted to attend classes. Take this class!
Kind of boring, but nice guy.

Dr. Goldsmith had no respect for students in IDST 131 and brushed off concerns about unfair grading in the class. His lectures were dry and disorganized. He was not helpful when asked questions about course content. IDST 131, more broadly, is a difficult, unorganized class with lots of work, unclear grading, and unhelpful TAs.

I loved this class! Very smart guy and you can tell he really cares. The main assignment is a 10 page final policy brief with assignments before that help you write it. If you do the work and go to office hours (he's very accessible for help) you can get the grade you want. Would recommend to anyone who is interested in learning about public policy

Great intro course for public policy. A little dry at times but rlly interesting to take during an election year. You learn applicable content I've alr used as a pub pol major. Final and midterm (you get cheat sheets) that are writing intense with a long policy brief assignment and presentation at the end, but useful for the future.

He was a good professor, just don't EVER take this class if you wish to maintain your mental health. You are given so much homework that is worth a big portion of your grade but after they grade it…they don't tell you the correct answers so in the class you'll never really know what the exact answer should have been. Spare yourself and don't do it.

This class was very difficult for a first year foundation course, I would not recommend it to anyone. 3 tests and a final presentation with a paper. Professor Goldsmith is an amazing person on his own, but I would not take a class from him again. Does not matter how much time you spend, the TAs grade homework extremely harsh with vague questions.

Though this Triple-I is not a fun time, Dr. Goldsmith is an awesome lecturer and does make me more interested in public policy. You have to actually pay attention though when he lectures because his slides don't contain much information. Though I would never wish this triple-I on my worst enemy, I would definitely take Goldsmith again

Dr. Goldsmith lectures the most in this class. Public policy is dry, but he does a very good job of giving detail. Take this class only if you're actually interested! The homework and tests are a bit intense, but the subject matter is fascinating and detailed. Dr. Goldsmith can feel challenging, but he genuinely wants his students to thrive.

Loved Dr. Goldmith! He's passionate about what he teaches, and he's very accessible outside of class. He's very understanding and doesn't want anyone to stress about grades, but he still gives good feedback on the policy brief. He's a little funky, but also funny and kind. Classes were interesting, despite the decent amount of readings.

Just drones on and lectures are very boring. Sweet lady but not too hard to succeed and low effort level. Not too much work and you don't really need to do the readings if you can lock in for the 4 exams.

These reviews are very harsh and unfair. Professor Addo is a very nice lady, and this class is not difficult at all. The midterm was fairly simple; just study the slides and you won't have a problem. She responds to emails quickly and makes herself very accessible to her students outside of class. Classes are interactive. Take the honors version!

Bad lecturer. Graded by 5 assignments and 4 exams which are both easy with sufficient studying from study guide and research on picked policy topic. TA's were not too harsh on grading and their feedback was helpful.

I feel that some of the negative reviews of Prof. Addo are exaggerated. She is one of the most caring and supportive professors I've had at UNC. She truly wants her students to succeed, is approachable outside of class, and takes the time to explain material when you're confused. If you put in the effort, she will absolutely meet you halfway.

Very nice person and is willing to help you outside of class, but isn't always good at answering questions. We had three midterm exams and one final exam with 5 policy assignments throughout the semester, which felt like a lot, but if you study the lecture content well you're fine. She reads straight off the slides which isn't helpful.

Professor Addo cares a lot and is knowledgable but her lectures were verbatim off the slides. She was not great at answering student questions in lecture either. 4 exams throughout the semester which was a lot but if you study the guide she gives then you should do well on them. Easy class and interesting content but unhelpful lectures.

When she lectures she often does not answer student questions well, or at all. The course was very disorganzied but easy. The TA's are lenient with the grading of the decontructed policy brief. Overall if you go to class and are willing to do some of the readings you are fine.

Dr. Addo seems like a very nice person, but she has very poor lecturing skills. No one in the class listened because she was reading the slides verbatim. This class was also so disorganized. I wouldn't take her if there is another professor avaliable. Her class was still easy, it was the last of my concerns and I did well.

Dr. Addo is a wonderful person and you can tell she has a lot of passion for her field. However, lectures were rather dry and I do not feel I gained a whole lot from the class. Still, assignments weren't too hard, nor were exams. Attendance is technically required but often not enforced.

lectures were boring and pointless since she mostly reads off the slides, the content is also boring, tests are more about memorization with a little application, I didn't pay attention but got >95 on every test and assignment

This class was extremely repetitive with the same content in every single module. Prof. Addo does NOT know how to lecture in any way shape or form. She needs to take a workshop on lecturing. The class itself was boring, tests were fine, just study the review that she posts. Application based. Our assignments were easy 100's. I skipped class a lot.

She is clearly smart but such a bad lecturer. She gets confused by her own slides, mostly just reads off them anyway, and struggles to answer student questions. She also weirdly giggles so much and it makes me so angry. Exams weren't too hard though and out of class assignments were easy 100s

I found her class frustrating. She is condescending and fails to answer questions beyond the content of her lecture slides. The content is manageable, but lectures are poorly organized. My biggest issue with her class was the volume of tests. A policy innovation and analysis course should focus on research and writing, not multiple choice exams.

These reviews over-exaggerate what Dr. Addo's class is like. While she is not an engaging lecturer (she mostly reads off her slides), she is clearly knowledgeable in her field. If you do the few readings assigned and put in a decent amount of effort on the problem sets, you'll be just fine. This class was my last priority and I ended with an A.

I don't think I learned a lot from this class and I found Professor Addo confusing in general (how she explained things), but I didn't feel that this affected my ability to succeed in the course. She was very helpful outside of class and seemed to care a lot about students. Grading didn't feel nitpicky and the workload was relatively light.

Professor Addo is a really nice person, but I think that they need to work on their lecture skills. It is really hard to pay attention. Majority of the time I had no idea what was going on. Available outside of class and just so nice, but the class needs to be restructured and they need to go to a lecture/public speaking workshop.

There were multiple occasions where the teacher or TA could not answer a question posed by a student in the class. Not gonna lie, I didn't even know if the teacher knew what was being taught. The tests aren't terribly hard but they grade hard for no reason. If you could pick another professor for 210 probably would do that. Gonna end with a B.

Probably one of the worst classes I have taken at UNC. The professor and TA's grade super hard for no reason and give no feedback. They don't even seem to understand the material themselves and just take off points randomly. They give you 8th grade level exams and then grade them super harshly for no reason. I might get a B in this class.
She's a robot reading slides and exams are poorly designed and graded. Don't take her if you can avoid it.

She does nothing to engage students while lecturing. While she seems to know a lot about the subject, she does not teach it well at all and you many leave lectures more confused than when you entered. She talks in circles and does not give straight answers. Impossible to reach outside of class and you're better off asking a TA.

Dr. Mehdi's lectures are hard to follow, so most learning comes from homework and the textbook. The class is 75% homework, with one drop and a retake option. Participation is just completing textbook sections. I didn't learn much from the lecture, but still got an A. Focus on homework and study for the final. He is super kind and gave us cookies.

The class itself is easy since you don't need to understand the concepts. You have 3 attempts on each homework and can drop one. Attendance can be done from home since lectures are boring. The final was open-note and open-textbook. Medhi really cares about his students. He brought these gluten-free Oreos to every class that I would definitely buy.

Not sure why his reviews are so bad! He is really funny and often brings stuffed animals in to class to make students laugh. The material is pretty boring but homework is like 90% of your grade and it is easy.
The lectures were SO boring but the homework assignments made up most of the grade (online, 3 submissions for each question). Almost no work but so hard to pay attention in class to.

Do not believe the bad reviews! This class was very easy to get an A in. Homework is 75% of your grade, the final is 15% (just show up to most of the classes), and participation is 10%. Mehdi brought cookies to class every day and cared deeply about each student's success in the class. He also did a great job connecting the topics to public policy.
Homework is 75% of your grade and is online. Professor is very nice and lenient.

Mehdi was one of the kindest, most caring professors I have had at UNC. Not only was the class very easy ( 75% HW grades, 10% attendance, 15% final which is open note) but he brought us snacks most classes, was kind and patient, and always connected the dry econ notes to policy like SNAP, Taxes, etc. He is a gem & the class w him is super easy!

I did not enjoy Mehdi by any means, but I also don't believe that he deserves such low ratings. He is clearly a smart guy and he certainly isn't afraid to cold-call people. He gets easily frustrated with students (one of his biggest faults), but if you put in the effort you will do very well. Our class really liked to complain.

Medhi got a really bad rep this semester, but I do not think he deserved it. Lectures were not the most helpful to me, but the homework is more than doable if you read the textbook before working on it. The class was 72% homework, 13% attendance, and 15% final. He wants you to succeed. 50% of the class got above A-, 90% got above B-.

Homie misspelled "week" on the syllabus as "weak," which is not very helpful for this but I found it humorous. The course is very difficult and lectures can be intimidating, but it can be done with a lot of focus on the readings.

Class is hard work and fast, but I don't think the prof deserves such low ratings. Assignments make up majority of your grade and you have two weeks for each. They are directly tied to the textbook so read! and watch the graphing videos in the textbook. An extension of econ 101 topics in the context of policy. Gets easier as the semester goes on

Genuinely the worst class I have ever taken at UNC. His lectures are useless just go to them and if he calls on you say you don't know. Read the book, it is infinitely more help, it sucks but you just have to teach yourself the material. he will get mad that you don't understand concepts, and tries to assign work over spring break.
Super awesome professor. Passionate about the subject and has fun, interactive lectures.
So so kind and caring and made it feel easy to talk in class!
Super passionate and does really fascinating work - also an easy A

Dr. Davis is an amazing professor! She truly cares about each of her students and is willing to accommodate everyone. She isn't strict on grading, but cares more about whether students actually understand the material. She is passionate about what she teaches and is willing to modify the syllabus if students want to dive into tangential topics.
Amazing lectures!

If you are looking for a first year seminar and you like to discuss inequalities at the time, this is the class for you. Dr. Davis has a very different approach in that she takes feedback more seriously than the syllabus, she will hear you out and gladly move a due date. Easy and fun A. She has relationships with everyone.

Dr. Davis is really passionate about addressing inequality across America. She intentionally makes the grading extremely easy, while diving deep into content during class and via readings (she goes on a lot of tangents!). She herself admits that this is an "easy A". Take this class for your seminar with Dr. Davis!

Professor Davis is a great professor. PLCY 75 is not meant to be a lecture-based class, but more of a discussion-based class. We had interesting and nuanced discussions, and Professor Davis will give you an A as long as you participate and write your papers.

Lots of space for discussion about difficult topics and helped us connect to the readings. Lots of leeway and consideration. Wasn't exceptionally hard at all. She definitely cares about her students and is perfectly fine with straying from the plans if it is more beneficial for the students. Take this class.

Dr. Davis is so knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. There are a few easy, structured assignments throughout the course, but the class is largely discussion based, allowing students to take the conversation in whatever direction they find most interesting/beneficial. This is a class you will never have to worry about your grade in!

I took this class and I feel like we were taking about the same issue the whole semester. You do not learn a lot from her class. If you want the class for an easy credit and don't care about you knowledge and it's growing, then take it. She also don't give a detailed instructions on essays. A 10 paper page have a 1 paragraph instructions.

Dr. Davis is genuinely one of the best professors I have had so far. She cares about the material and explains it very well in a manner that actually helps students understand. There are only 5 assignments in the class, one being a final paper, and the rest are group work. Managing this class was very easy and would take any class with her again!
Professor Davis is truly a great professor. I had her for my freshman year seminar and an intro to my major. She does such cool work outside of being a professor and is super knowledgable.
She is an awesome professor. Graded kindly, and the assignments were straightforward. Had to stand up in front of class 3 times for presentations.

Dr. Davis is an amazing professor and I thoroughly enjoyed her class. I learned so much and had a lot of fun doing it. The class is very discussion based so you do need to do the readings to be able to participate but the readings are not bad and usually very interesting. I would highly highly recommend!!

Dr. Davis is an AMAZING professor! She's so smart & creates a comfortable space to discuss these topics. A discussion-based class, but she directs conversation & introduces intriguing points. She cares more about learning than grades, but we had to read a lot before class. I'd 100% recommend this class to anyone who wants to learn about inequality!

A LOT of reading/work for a FYS, sometimes 50+ pages after each class. He's a tough grader so be prepared to work hard if you want an A. Other than that, he is extremely knowledgeable in global health policy, and his classes are super fun to attend. Participation matters, so try to talk at least once every class or every other class. Great guy!

Super knowledgeable and entertaining professor, and really cares to get to know his students. Participation matters and you will be expected to talk at least 1x a class. I would say he's a relatively harsh grader but his feedback makes sense and is helpful, so it's definitely easy to improve in his class.

If you want an easy A first-year seminar, do not take PLCY-76H. However, if you want to work hard, truly enjoy the history of health policy, and enjoy reading at least 20+ pages of reading each class, then do take this class. Professor Meier is very knowledgeable and really cares about his students, but his class is hard for a FYS.

dr. meier's class is unlike any other class i've taken, he is an amazing professor who cares so deeply about his students and global health. i look forward to coming to class everyday. his class is one you listen and retain information from. he is such an engaging lecturer and would take another one of his classes in a heartbeat.

Meier was entertaining, but in retrospect I was a bit disappointed with the content in the course as he elected to touch on Ukraine and Russia, but not Palestine — a much more pertinent issue. To be fair, this wouldn't have sat well with the board, but to not acknowledge it in any capacity for a class called ‘Justice in Public Policy' is odd.

Dr. Meier is incredible. This class has been by far my favorite class I have taken at UNC. The class has been so fulfilling and I have learned so much. The class is not for the light -- it is a lot of work and constant readings but i can ensure you will never take a class where you will learn more. would recommend and he is very kind/understanding

this class is incredible and Meier is amazing! all students must take this class and it is accessible for both undergraduates and graduates. it is a class thats challenging but not overwhelming. AMAZING PROFESSOR

This class does a beautiful job of turning complicated subjects into something discussable and accessible without removing the importance of them. Dr. Meier is the most passionate professor I have ever met and he cares so deeply about his students. He will know everyone's name before you even walk into the classroom that day. This class is a must.

Dr. Meier deeply cares about his students and makes them all feel at home! I've been in his class for a few weeks now and would say it is already one of my favorite classes at UNC. super interesting material and engaging lectures! a solid amount of reading, but it is not overwhelming. definitely recommend
incredible professor and inspired me to pursue a degree in public health! Everyone must take a class with Meier, it will change your UNC experience.
must take class, extremely interesting content and fun interactions with students. learned a ton and would completely recommend. great professor and he is extremely passionate

Extremely engaging and absolutely incredible class. Material is interesting and open my eyes to the world of global health. Even if you are not studying public health I seriously recommend! Both the professor and content make this class incredible. A definite take at UNC

Took this class last semester and I will miss being in class with him!! Incredible content, professor, lecture style! Every student of any major should take!! So happy I took it!! I didn't feel overwhelmed but also felt I gained a ton from the class!! it was a perfect class and also very flexible to student feedback. you feel very cared about!

I RECOMMEND. Dr. Meier is funny and uses current events to engage with students -- he is never afraid to belt a tune and is also the kindest professor I have met at UNC. He makes you welcomed and heard in his class! The material is interesting and extremely relevant! There are not exams, but rather papers which he provides accessible material for!

LOVE THIS CLASS!! incredible professor, learn a ton, solid amount of readings but not too much that it is unbearable. anyone can take it -- provides foundational understanding of global health! SO applicable to current events/other majors/etc. U HAVE TO TAKE!!!

MUST TAKE: I have gained so much knowledge about global health!! This class will leave you fulfilled and fascinated. Meier is incredible -- using songs to interact with students and truly cares about his students. He goes beyond being supportive in class and always has a door open to be there for any student. I always look forward to class!!

He is clear and answers questions. He engages with the material and is an amazing lecturer-- it is impossible to be bored in his class. He provides room for students to engage with other students and engage in larger class setting. You will learn tons from the class! You cannot graduate UNC without taking a class with Meier and this one is a MUST.

Incredible professor and fascinating material! Both undergraduates and graduates will learn A LOT from the class. Good amount of reading, but not too much that it feels unmanageable. Very understanding professor and kind human. This class is a must take! If you are not passionate about global health before it, you will be after!!!

I came into university not considering global health, now it is my major. The person I attribute this to is Dr. Meier. During a time when global health is under attack, we need more Meier's and more students to learn from him. Everyone should take this class. Also, it is an appropriate workload allowing students to learn but not overwhelming.

Dr Meier's class has been my favorite class I have taken at UNC. He brings an energy into the class that engages each and everyone of his students and he connects with them personally. Dr. Meier provides a foundational understanding of global health that is accessible for both undergraduates and graduates. I couldn't recommend his class more!!!

Hands down the best professor at UNC! He is kind, thoughtful, compassionate, and an exceptional mentor who cares about your perspective and success. As a senior now, who took this class as a freshman, Dr. Gitterman is the best professor I've ever had. His classes are engaging, preparing you for the real world in politics, policy, or life itself.
Easy A class and great professor!
Absolutely Amazing

Gitterman's a nice, funny guy and a good professor. There are only a few assignments, and they're not graded hard at all. He tells you word for word what's going to be on the exams, and all the answers are straight from the readings.
Gitterman is a great prof, very in touch with students and knowledgeable. Class if difficult but also getting an A is attainable.

Lowkey all grades will depend on your TA, but I know Gitterman gives them specific answers for the midterm and final. He assigns readings, but as long as you stay in class and skim the readings for examples: you will do fine on the midterm & final. Your other main grade is your policy brief, which is long but very simple. Easiest 101 class.

The goat. Really cared about his students as people. I had a disagreement with him about the way he broached a difficult topic and he took the time to meet with me and hear about my perspective. Absolutely loved the class. Super easy but valuable nonetheless.

This was a great class, and Professor Gitterman genuinely cares about his students! Class was based on a few papers, attendance, a midterm, and a final. The assignments had a clear grading criteria and were designed to build toward the final paper. The midterm and final were both based off a top 10 list he provided so it was clear what to study.
He is the goat. I loved coming to the lectures, he was very lax and communicated well.

Take this class if you're interested in Policy or need a focus capacity. Gitterman is super chill, and all of the TAs are chill as well. There's a policy brief, midterm, and final, and they're all fairly simple. Gitterman gives clear directions too. Class is actually interesting as well so that's a plus.

Professor Gitterman is very passionate about the content and lectures are always interesting. He is so sweet, brought in donuts to class and even the Cleffhangers one day. Gman rocks. The class is not hard at all and he gives you a study guide for midterm/final telling exactly what will be on the exams. 1000000/10 recommend he is the best
Professor Gitterman is super knowledgable and experienced with policy and you can tell how much he cares! Genuinely loved his lectures.
Super easy A and hes genuinely an awesome person

Really just depends on your TA, as they grade everything (which is only about 4/5 things for an entire semester). Very clear outline for the midterm and final exams. Lectures get a little dry, but he's a very understanding guy outside of class.

would HIGHLY recommend taking PLCY 101 with Gitterman in the fall. He is funny and caring and wants his students to succeed and have a good time with the class. There is a lot of reading, but if you pay attention in lectures you can get away with not doing it. The mid-term and final are based off a list of topics he the lecture before the test day.

Professor Gitterman is the best, he genuinely cares about his students and lectures were really enjoyable to go to. Policy brief was biggest component of grade and midterm/final were given a study guide that was close to exam. Take him at UNC he's awesome!
Professor Gitterman has been my favorite professor so far at UNC. He's funny, knowledgeable, and very accommodating. Take a class with Gman if you can!!
genuinely made going to class interesting and his lectures were never boring.

I loved Dr. Gitterman and couldn't recommend him enough! He has such a kind heart and genuinely cares about the well-being of each of his students. Class was also very versatile: "game-show" style activities, watching short films, hearing from guest speakers, etc. He even brought in the Clefhangers one class. So awesome.
He is an amazing professor that cares about his students. A few assignments and a midterm and final exam but as long as you take notes during lectures you will be fine.

One of the best professors. Extremely nice and really cared about the well-being (academically, mentally, etc.) of his students. This class was extremely interesting, and the majority of the content is backed by his own research and publications, which made it more relevant and digestible.

Professor Moulton is the best, if you have to take PLCY460, take him! I was worried about this class because I was not comfortable with statistics or coding, but he made the material digestible. The grading was very fair, if you work hard in this class, it's possible to get an A. Prof Moulton wants his students to achieve and he cares about you.

Prof. Moulton is by far the best professor for PLCY 460. He is amazing at teaching the material and makes it very easy to do well in his class. There is a learning curve with Stata and statistics in general, but his grading scheme is very forgiving. He usually only teaches it in the fall, so make sure to plan your schedule so you can take it then!

Professor Moulton was very interactive with the way he taught Stata programming language. Much of the information comes from the slides and then applied, with quizzes testing knowledge during recitation. As long as you keep up with the notes, understand the material, you can finish the course easily with a passing grade, would take again!

An excellent professor. I came into the class with no Stata experience but this class was designed to accommodate that. As a consequence, however, you won't actually become really good at Stata. The class focuses more on statistical interpretation. Also, Moulton rocks.
He made difficult topics easier to understand. He also sees students as real people and genuinely cares. He gives plenty of opportunities to ask questions and get help. Great guy.

I was really scared to take this class because of Stata and actually using data on our own, but Moulton is a great guy. Really tries to go through the lesson with the class and make it understandable. Plus, the TA's were great. The final was curved and instead of just passing the class I ended with an A minuss

I LOVED taking 460 with Prof Moulton this semester. While 460 can be a challenging class, he made the difficult concepts easy to understand during lectures, and group work/open note quizzes in recitation each week helped to make sure students understood the material and asked questions. Also, shoutout to Joonho for being the best TA ever!!!

Prof. Moulton made a class with challenging material much more attainable. The class was set up with lecture on Tuesday, group work on Thursday, and a quiz on Friday. We were able to continuously see and practice the material, which made studying for the final much easier. Moulton was great and tried his best to make the class entertaining.

We had our professor take a leave of absence halfway through the semester, and Prof. Moulton stepped in for the remainder of the class. He was incredibly helpful and made the transition much easier than it could have been. His grading policy was very considerate of the circumstances and he was more than willing to help students and TA's out.

Moulton made 460 not terrible. his slides were very clear guides to completing group work and he was a fair and understanding grader. highly recommend taking 460 with him if possible!! no unnecessary assignments he's very straightforward.

Professor Moulton was an incredible professor who made what seemed like a hard subject very understandable and reading with clear grading, weekly open note quizzes, a group project, and an open note final. Highly recommend 460 with him.

Committed to his students' success, but doesn't take himself too seriously. Made complex concepts accessible and always tried his best to keep us engaged. I really liked the structure of lecture T, group work TH, and a quiz in recitation to take the pressure off of a midterm. Quizzes/final were open note and he/TAs were accessible for office hours.

Dr. Moulton is a king! He made coding, a daunting topic for most policy majors, easy to understand and was incredibly accommodating. This class is by no means an easy A (or B) but if you put work into the class and study for the quizzes you will do well. Lecture and recitation is not mandatory, but make sure to go to Thursday classes for groupwork.

This was a tough class I won't lie, but Professor Moulton did a great job teaching the materials. His class was structured super well, with a nice blend of lectures and group work. Cares about his students too. He moved the final online to accommodate for the ACC Championship Games. He's a real one for that.

Professor Moulton is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He really wants his students to succeed in his class, and he is incredibly flexible to meet outside of classtime. 460 is a difficult class, but if you pay attention during lectures and do some extra coding practice here and there, you will definitely do well! 1000% recommend taking him!

Prof. Moulton was an amazing professor, I was in a TTH class, and TU were for lectures and TH were for group work. Group work was turned in individually and prof Moulton was always really helpful. The group project wasn't that difficult, you just have to put in effort. Overall, an amazing professor!

Amazing professor. Clear lectures, grading criteria for assignments, and class structure. Every week there was an assignment and fair quiz used to test that week's material, and there is only one exam. Left the class learning a lot. He is also really nice and approachable.

I genuinely could not recommend a class more than this one. If you have the chance to take it, please do. The material of this course is enriching and Shai conveys it in a way that is both powerful but easy to understand. Be prepared to step out of your comfort zone and being vocal and vulnerable. Seriously, the is THE best class ever.

I would highly recommend this class to anyone who is able to take it. Shai is a wonderful professor. This class is very easy in terms of workload, but in order to do well, it definitely requires that you be willing to open up and be vulnerable.

Shai is an amazing professor, I can not stress how much I loved this course. You will do a lot of speaking in this class, everyone does but it's not scary at all. There are three journals and one final paper, but so easy to write and not stressful at all. I love this class and if I could take it again I would! TAKE IT!!!

I love Shai so much! I was in the first PWAD480 class and it rlly help you to get out of your comfort zone. There were a few journal assignments and the final is a paper that isn't graded harshly if you put in effort. The class has really cool speakers and you get to work hands on with the Chapel Hill community. If you can get into a class, do it!!

don't take this class if you are not willing to be vulnerable, reflect on yourself, and oveall understand people better. this is my favorite class I have taken at UNC. it was so meaningful and Shai was so caring and great. wish i could take it again.

Shai is incredible and this class is such a good class to take just to learn how to better interact with other humans. Not a lot of work in terms of academic "homework" but can be a bit mentally/emotionally taxing at times- totally worth taking though!

I cannot recommend taking PLCY 581 with Professor Gutierrez enough. It's an engaging class and she is very understanding of student circumstances. You can turn assignments in over a week late with no penalty applied.

Follow the instructions, you will get an A. Professor Gutierrez lectures very well, and the content is interesting and relevant. You don't necessarily need to take notes, and I enjoyed being able to just listen and learn. Readings were interesting, which I normally would not say. Each assignment is engaging and fun.

Professor is very kind and really likeable. Grading is super generous and there is essentially free extra credit for all students as well. If you're looking for an easy A with minimal work and on/off attendance, this is your class. If you want to learn this topic well or are passionate about research design, I would suggest a different teacher.

Highly recommend taking this class with professor Gutierrez. Definitely one of the easiest classes I have taken at UNC and all you have to do is complete the assignments. There are some in class assignments that count as attendance but you are told what days they are. The lectures aren't too bad and she is honestly amazing.

Professor Gutierrez was a very enjoyable professor, engaging and easy to follow lectures. Nothing too difficult and assignments within the class was informative and followed material. Would recommend to anyone!

Class did not feel like a valuable use of time. There was little new information beyond other PLCY core courses and minimal application of concepts. Grading was a little unpredictable but there was so much extra credit it didn't really matter. Easy class, take it and get the A, but don't expect much more.

This class was easy and I enjoyed the lecture style- a 30-40 min lecture, rest of time applying what you did to in-class work with a group. The lectures were fast sometimes and the assignments (4) and quizzes (2) were time consuming, but made me think critically. She provides many resources and supplements if you missed class/need more clarity.
361 is a great easy policy elective. Semester long group project and only a few mandatory classes. Professor Gutierrez is super nice

Prof Gutierrez is very understanding and the only out of class work is a group podcast (with segmented assignments) and a group presentation on an assigned reading. There is also no midterm or final for Plcy 361. Very few lectures have attendance required and she lets you know well in advance. Only critique is that the lectures can be a bit fast.

Easy class and flexible to student needs, but once she did answer a question in class (about the material we would be graded on) with "let's ruminate on the uncertainty" instead of saying she didn't know/would get back to us, which was absolutely insane and has lived in my mind ever since.
Dr. Gutierrez is my favorite professor I've had for a public policy class. she cares a lot about mental health and made the content very easy (although this isn't really a hard class anyways)

Professor Gutierrez's class was very easy. There is one group presentation but it was graded easily. There are lots of long readings but they aren't necessary to always do and class attendance wasn't mandatory. Overall, Professor Gutierrez is very accommodating and flexible. Open note midterm and final.

Prof Gutierrez has few assignments. The midterm and final were take home and open book/note. There are 4 quizzes that are also take home and one group presentation. She grades fairly easy and attendance is not mandatory. Class is simple as long as you do the work. Plenty of EC opportunities. Requires a book but I didn't buy it and did fine.
For PLCY 581, Dr.Gutierrez was super flexible with assignment deadlines and grading. Not the most interesting content in my opinion but she did her best to make it an easy class for us.
She was very fair and took her student's mental health into consideration. We had a few short papers, class discussions, and a group project. Just make sure to read the syllabus carefully!

This professor shows she cares about her students in the way she teaches and grades. There were no tests in the class and the final was a group project worked on all semester producing a podcast at the end. Also, she gave us mental health days. The class was straightforward and she was always respectful. However, she was very hard to reach by email

Love ashu!! Very willing to help outside of class, lots of jokes throughout lecture to keep us engaged, and lots of step by step help to make sure we are really following what we are doing! TAs were great as well. Loved the treats ashu brought in (though wish we got to try his brownie recipe). If you can take a Class with ashu, do it!
TA Laraib Kamal has anger issues.

Professor Ashu is an amazing. He's incredibly engaging, bakes cookies for his students, is clearly passionate about the material, and makes his expectations/what we need to know for exams very clear. If you attend the lectures, utilize your recitation TA's and their office hours, and take good notes you won't have a problem in this class!

Ashu is super nice—he brought us cookies/cupcakes and even gifts when he traveled for research. The class itself isn't super hard, and the curves were also really generous. As long as you come to the class, do the problem sets, and attend review sessions, you will do fine. Favorite class & professor—definitely + highly recommended!!!

Professor Ashu is a really caring professor (he baked us treats often and got us gifts when he travelled)! He doesn't provide powerpoints for his class, so attending his classes would be really helpful. And the exams are hard and he's tough grader, but his exam grades and the overall grades are curved generously, so it's not too bad.

The class was very clear in terms of expectations for assignments and the lectures themselves. The group discussions were interesting. A lot of midterms but she drops one which is very nice. She was very kind and caring about us doing well in the class!

Dr. Alinor is a caring professor and wants everyone to do well in her course! Instead of having exams, we had 5 take home quizzes that were a little tricky, but they were open note. She's a somewhat tough grader for assignments, but she gives great feedback so it's easy to make changes and do well on future assignments.
Wonderful prof and I think her 581 class is the gold standard from what I hear. Super personable and very smart. Class is fun and always something to look forward to.

Dr. Alinor is nice and if you email her she will respond. My biggest issue is how vague the rubric is yet how everything is graded harshly. Definitely go to office hours and get feedback or else you probably will not hit the points they want you to. Quizzes are based on lectures (20- 25 minutes, remote). An A is 93.5, so do the extra credit!

Dr. Alinor is very knowledgeable in sociology/public policy, kind, and accessible outside of class. Her lectures are great, yet occasionally hard to follow. There is one large policy research project that makes up a large portion of grading. However, her grading criteria is vague and the timeline is rushed, so start early. Overall, good professor!

Truly a national treasure! She is so caring and offers good feedback on assignments handed out. She is extremely renowned in her field yet able to explain difficult concepts in an accessible way. Lectures sometimes felt too sped up for me but she was nice enough to let us out of class early multiple times. Also enjoyed the group work!

Lectures weren't mandatory and based on information from the posted slides. The midterm and exam were all  short answers and one essay (same format/length) but easy to get an A if you paid attention. Had to do 10/14 reading quizzes (3 mcq with lowest quizzes being dropped) and three news reflections all semester. Light workload and relevant class.

PLCY 220 is an easy A if you have any interest in government or have picked up a newspaper in the last year. Dr. Kreitzer is very nice and means well, but should probably not be employed. Midterms and Finals took forever to grade despite being very basic, expectations were confusing and not helpful, and I can confidently say I learned nothing.

Literally never posted the final exam. Like... just did not post one. Went ghost after LDOC & now we are all getting Not Reported grades. Also, never graded anything. She posted the midterm a month after the syllabus said. It goes so far that I feel bad for her. We all quit showing up to class after a while, but she seems like a nice person. Weird.

It was easy to get an A in PLCY 220. She records her lectures and will send them to you on request. The course topics were interesting, and I showed up to lectures almost always. The final grade is based mostly on two writing-based exams worth 33% each and other busywork. If you do the readings and show up to lectures, the tests will be simple.

Very nice person and super educated but struggled a lot with the assignments aspect of being a professor. Had some insanely conflicting expectations, but she will just end up giving you an A. If you want to learn about interesting things and do well, I would recommend. I think the course would have been more effective with more clear expectations.

I took this class from 5:05-6:20 on M/W. maybe that's why it was so difficult to pay attention, but this class is SO boring. boring lectures every day, she's so unorganized and takes forever to grade, almost impossible to reach over email. was easy enough to get good grades in, but I have no idea where i stand with my grade right now

Kreitzer was an amazing down to earth prof. Please note that she emphasizes that she is Autistic and ADHD, so her class can be chaotic at times. However, overall it was a great course and deadlines were usually pushed back if anything went array. Awesome teacher and person. Take a class with her!

Prof Kreitzer regularly begins class by apologizing for her latest disorganization.She is a nice person and definitely knows about the subject, but also the least organized professor I have ever had the misfortune of taking. Reading quizzes are very easy but often have wrong due dates. Final grades were submitted 2 weeks after the exam.

Just to reiterate what other people are saying - she takes forever to grade. Other than that though, the content is incredibly detailed and is decently based on memorization. She seems like a really nice person but her class made me fall asleep and I skipped it often. Don't take unless you are very passionate about politics.

Class was easy, I attended lecture (though not necessary) but the content was relatively common knowledge. Nice person, terribly disorganized. Took a week to return final exam grades, constantly changed deadlines, and abused the freedoms of having a syllabus she likes to refer to as a "living document." Easy class, but wouln't recommend.

didn't really care for her lectures, the reading quizzes are a lot but her grading of them is good. honestly an easy class and attendance isn't even mandatory, the tests were simple and it was one of the easier courses I've taken. she takes a lot of time to grade the exams though which I didn't like.

PLCY 220 is an interesting course, and I found Professor Kreitzer's lectures to be engaging. However, the experience was soured by the fact that midterm grades took well over a month to come back, and final grades were returned a week and half past the 72-hour deadline. Accessibility outside class was another issue.

Professor Kreitzer is an amazing professor and lecturer. My only complaint is that she does grade very slowly. It took well over a month for us to have our midterm exams released and well over two weeks for our final exams to be released. However, she does grade this in a very fair manner.

Class was a joke. Attended every day hoping to eventually learn something, but no. Content was boring, basic information. Would be fine if this was the only issue. However, there is a much more serious issue in her severe disorganization. She took a month or longer to grade, and we still have no final grade resulting in a NR being reported.

Prof. Kreitzer is such an interesting lecturer and kind person! Most of the grade comes from a midterm and final but the class also includes some small, easy assignments to help your grade. As much as I liked her as a person, this class was really disorganized, which is why I wouldn't take a class with her again. However, not difficult to do well!

Amazing professor. All the content is super relevant and helpful and you will walk away from each class learning something. The exams were kind of annoying because she stresses not focusing on memorization but exams are closed note, but overall not too bad. Also records lectures so you can watch later which is super helpful.

Professor Kreitzer was a pretty good professor. She was really nice and sat down to answer my questions. She was a bit unorganized and she takes forever to grade, due to the exams being all written response. Content information was too much for only 2 exams. Other than that, the class was decent.

Professor Kreitzer is a very nice person, and does a good job explaining things in class. For me, class moved too quickly and Professor Kreitzer was a little bit unorganized. Overall pretty easy class.

One of my favorite professors. Her lectures are fascinating, and she gives many opportunities to improve your grade. Does not use textbooks, instead, she provides reading articles each week. Grading did take longer, but midterm was open ended so understood. Grades were provided back in timely manner, and grading criteria was fair. Very personable

Professor Kreitzer went through a lot of content quickly so sometimes it was hard to keep up. However I felt that she graded exams somewhat leniently to make up for this. She took a while to grade and was a little disorganized overall but she was very nice and knowledgeable on content. The lectures themselves were interesting and relevant.
Nice guy and seemed to know the material. However, lectures were hard to follow and exams were harsh and long. Everyone in the class struggled and I have never studied harder for a final exam.

Josh is new and has room to grow, but the class improved a lot throughout the semester. The midterm was tough but he took accountability and allowed test corrections and provided extra practice materials. Allowed us to submit a draft paper for feedback, and exams had EC. Keep up with the readings and participate and you'll be fine. Nice guy.

Josh seems nice and could be a good professor, but he made PLCY 581 way harder than normal. We had two harshly-graded papers and a hard midterm. Josh did give chances for corrections on midterm, but paper grades were unnecessarily nitpicky and unclear. This class ended my 4.0, and I never really felt like I had a real chance of getting an A.

Trying to succeed in his class felt truly Sisyphean. You can go to office hours, read the textbook, pages and pages of the readings he assigned, and still not feel confident for his assignments. He was such a discouraging instructor. His syllabus said that effort does not mean success and boy was that true. Take anyone else for 581.

I think with more experience he could be really good professor because he knows the material well, was accommodating, and quick to answer emails and questions. However, I know from working in pairs with different people throughout the semesters that most people found his lectures hard to follow, which was the main issue.

You should immediately consider taking anyone else. His grading was unfair, harsh, & inconsistent. He also offers no actual assistance be it office hours or online. He made the notoriously manageable core PLCY class absolute hell, and ever other section had it much easier which was really unfair and disheartening. Not kind, capable, or helpful.

Go to the lectures and record them bc the slides aren't helpful but a lot of exam questions are based on random topics that she would lightly mention. If you're not interested in public policy don't take this course!! Find another gen ed

She grades nothing, so pray for a good TA. Feedback on papers is almost nonexistent. You are expected to read her mind at times. Everything is said during lecture, and the slides she gives are unhelpful. Go to class, write down literally everything she says, and maybe you'll do well, though that depends on the TA.

Dr. Sullivan was nice, but our grades depended on our TA. She doesn't include a lot of info on her slides, so make sure you are writing down what she says in lecture, and do the readings. A lot of that info will be tested on exams! Go to office hours, especially for clarification on the papers and assignments at the end of the semester.

I do not understand how she is the Chair of the Department of Public Policy. Her lectures are lowkeniuley so boring, but if you do not pay take notes, you finna fail. She puts random examples on the exams. She said in class, You cannot receive a 100 because it's not 'publish-worthy' work. God forbid you need help with grading or understanding.

Pretty easy class if you do the work, but grading is tough, and feedback isn't very clear. Lectures were very boring, but the material was easy to grasp if you reviewed it. All of the work will be graded by the TAs.
The professor was very nice and welcoming. As long as you do your work and actually read the books you will be just fine. She's very flexible with assignments due dates.

Prof Sullivan gave clear and super interesting lectures- I cite this class as some of the coolest things I've learned here. She really explores from wide perspectives and shifted my viewpoint. I would absolutely recommend this class for the content. Tests were straightforward what she emphasized in class, and readings were interesting and short.

I loved Dr. Sullivan's course as an intro to the public policy field. It's clear that she cares a lot about the subject. I would say the first half of the semester was pretty reading-heavy, but the second half was more like 2-3 articles per week. Not a very difficult class but interesting and I would definitely take a class again with Dr. Sullivan.

Don'y take this class if you are not interested in public policy or it isn't your major. As a poli sci major, I thought I would enjoy this class but I found it boring. She doesn't upload slides and doesn't like when students take pictures of it either. The papers we had in class were fairly easy but I recommened to donall readings.

Relatively easy course overall as long as you take notes during lectures. Attendance isn't required (though it is for recitations), but Professor Sullivan does not post slides, so definitely don't miss the lectures. Grade depends largely on the midterm and final (both super easy). Make sure to do the readings just to have examples for essays.

There are many readings, but completing them makes the online quizzes easy grade boosters. The professor doesn't post slides, so attendance and note-taking are not required but necessary. Recitations are relaxed and mainly based on participation. While the lectures were a bit boring, Dr. Sullivan was understanding and passionate.

Her lectures are pretty clear, although she doesnt allow students to take pics of lecture slides and she doesn't post them on canvas either. She explains each concept thoroughly. She doesn't do much of any grading, mostly her TAs do that. Pay attention to lectures because there will be quizzes on tiny things from lectures and readings.

The TAs grade everything, I don't think she's ever graded anything tbh... just pray you have a good TA. the class was quite easy, workload was very light, and the tests were fairly easy, however, she doesn't round grades and I was only 0.4 away from an A but did no get one so... eh

Dr. Sullivan is a super understanding professor and was always willing to meet her student's needs! I thoroughly enjoyed the class and thought her lectures were interesting, although a little long at times. Class is extremely manageable as well. Just make sure you do well on both exams and the final paper! For sure take Dr. Sullivan if you can!

Sullivan's class was fine. I am not sure I would recommend this class to anyone not interested in policy. There were weekly quizzes with niche lecture content in them. The professor graded finals and midterms harshly and included specific questions from lectures and readings. However, the project receives a very lenient grading.

Dr. Sullivan is a great lecturer. You definitely need to attend class to do well on the weekly quizzes. I recommend doing all the readings, cause they show up on the quizzes, midterm and final. She doesn't post the lectures or slides, but if you show up to class and pay attention you'll be fine. Midterm and final are relatively straight forward.

Sullivan is a good lecturer and makes it very clear what needs to be done to succeed in her class. There are weekly quizzes, a final and a midterm, and a final research project that's a bit difficult. Recitations are required but you don't learn anything in them. Good intro into Public Policy.

Professor Sullivan was a knowledgeable, engaging lecturer. Graded based on weekly quizzes (as long as you take notes in lecture you will be fine, plus the lowest 2 are dropped), midterm, research paper, and final. The research paper was daunting but plenty of time and feedback was given. You have to attend lectures and read to succeed.

Prof Sullivan is a kind person and clearly knows her stuff. However, this class was unnecessarily hard as resources weren't posted online and small lecture details were on exams. The final project was daunting given the lack of instruction, took hours, and got no feedback. Recitation grades seemed arbitrary but overall the class was interesting!
Attendance not recorded, but slides are not posted online so going to every lecture is required. Tests were fair. Recitations were worth 20% of the final grade. Interesting lectures tho.
IDST111 is never a fun class, but he does the best he can with it. Super accessible outside of class, and obviously a super light grader. This class is a waste of time, but an easy A+.

IDST 111L is a boring class no matter what, and just by doing the assignments well enough, this was an easy 100. However, Prof Alvarez did not explain the guidelines or teach well at all, and I didn't learn anything. I heard other profs walked students through the Excel skills more. We were left to figure it out alone, meaning I learned nothing.

The class was easy, but the professor is an awful communicator, sending out no updates about class cancellations and schedule changes. When I approached him with questions, he lied and then attempted to gaslight me about my attendance.

I recommend going to office hours or participating in class to help him get to know you.  Professor Alvarez is super accessible outside of class and loves questions. He did a horrible job communicating with his TA though which caused a lot of issues with grades/communication/clarity/learning. Material isn't hard

He has a pretty thick Spanish accent, which is difficult to understand sometimes, but it shouldn't inhibit your learning. The course has some interesting topics but focuses on very specific neo-liberal global policies. There is a huge 10+ page paper you have to put together with a partner by the end of the semester.

A wonderful TA and very open for questions and office hours appointments. Very experienced in the global policy field and clearly is passionate about the course content. He appreciates participation during recitation, so try your best to contribute! Not too difficult and I really enjoyed this class.
Class was way too stressful for no reason. What grade you get depends on what TA you get. Really interesting material but the way the class taught it was pretty mid.

Professor Alvarez was very middle of the road, not terribly engaging but not terribly difficult. There are quizzes in recitation and you can attend class on Zoom but he could never figure out the sound for it. It's not a bad class, but it's definitely not my favorite.

Dr. Thomas is a very caring professor. The class involves several papers throughout the semester, some due within the same week. One big group project at the end, including a paper and a recorded presentation (Not bad). Also, an in-person final completely separate from the project. Will push her political agenda; other than that, no complaints.

Dr. Thomas is extremely kind and very knowledgeable about planning. The grading criteria is pretty straightforward and the assignments actually felt meaningful. My only complaint is that the class felt pretty disorganized at times and lectures often ended 15-20 minutes ahead of time.

She's definitely passionate and knowledgeable about the material which makes her lectures very meaningful. Tests aren't very hard, but she isn't the best about getting grades in quickly and it feels like she and her TAs take points off at random. She even said herself she feels that only the top of the top will get an A in her course.

GOOD PROFESSOR FOR PLANNING!!!! DO NOT take it if you want an easy A. Exams are straight from the reading quizzes. Very dense material and a good amount of reading. Two papers- an op ed and a group paper. Very clear on deadlines. Quizzes are for completion. Lectures were heavy but interesting and required attendance. MAKE FRIENDS.

Dr. Thomas is very sweet and clear about her commitment to student success. If you need an extension or you're unclear on an assignment, she will help when asked. There are a lot of readings but you can just skim them. Good study guides for the midterm and final. As long as you pay attention, it's pretty easy (I'm not a planning major or minor).
idk it was ok but honestly more work than the class deserved, a lot of exams for a class most people were taking as a gen-ed, not a major requirement
Test heavy, essay heavy

do not understand these bad ratings. tests are extremely easy, follow the study guide and she uses the same exact questions. lectures are well prepared and interesting.did not do the readings ever got an A with minimal effort. she grades the essays harsh i would say. easy and doable. for context i was a freshman and with no background on this class

The lectures were pretty engaging, but it was pretty difficult to follow what was going on. Most of what I learned I did outside of class, and the recitations were useless. Your grade in this class is 50% determined by which TA ends up grading a single paper (with less than 1000 words) and the other 50% is the cumulative final exam.

The content of this course is really easy. The lectures are boring at best and a waste of time at their worst. The exams are fair and she is pretty clear about how she formats them. However, Prof. Thomas comes off as incredibly rude and unprofessional towards her students and seems to direct her TA's to grade assignments against her own rubrics.
Late and badly organized

Allie Thomas is a formidable foe. There is absolutely nothing wrong with the content of this course. The work is more than manageable, and I enjoyed the content. Thats as far as my praise goes. Assessment was a mysterious ritual, with grades assigned as if they were divine decrees rather than earned through any logical or transparent criteria.

It's not worth it. She is not super accseable out of class and is extremley disorganized. There are better seminars out there. The majorty of your grade is a research paper and then a podcast about a certian topic at the 1939 New York World's Fair. Grading is also not helpful and she doesn't provide much feedback.

The material was pretty boring for me. She didn't give informative feedback for assignments and took a long time to grade the bigger assignments. The final assignments are worth your entire grade, and the entire course is set up to work on them the entire time. Peer reviews are the main source of reviews for assignments. Not awful, but not great

Overall, this was an easy A. The two major grades are two final projects that Thomas basically holds your hand through. Lectures weren't extremely informative, but at the beginning of November basically every class was cancelled for the rest of the year! I learned A LOT about research as a freshman who hadn't done any. Thomas is VERY hard to reach.

The content is not bad, but the way she lectures and grades was not good. The recitation is a complete waste of time and they assign you middle-schooler busy work, such as taking pictures of crosswalks and sitting at them for an hour "watching the pedestrians." Good luck if you take this class thinking it is an easy A, cause unfortunately it is not

I wanted to like this class so badly, but professor Thomas has flaws that are difficult to overlook. She directs the TAs to grade the essays harshly, her lectures are quite disorganized, expectations for test questions and essays are cryptic at best, and canvas was a mess. The content in the class is great, but it gets buried under these issues.

Easily the worst professor I've had at UNC. While I'm genuinely interested in the topics covered in class, the material is presented poorly. The class is the most unorganized I've ever taken, and the teaching style is completely disconnected from the level of the tests. The recitation sessions were a total waste of time.
Interesting professor, sometimes felt disorganized but the class was definitely informational. I thought the assignments were creative. Not a difficult class.

Didn't seem happy to be there or interested in what she was teaching. Seemed irritated by questions about grades, even though most of the grading was done by TAs. Useless readings while minute details from lectures were on tests. Unclear grading criteria on one major assignment and "participation" (random assignments that accounted for attendance.

He seems like an econ guy trying to teach a policy course. I think he wanted to go deeper into the subjects, but the class was not ready for that. He was respectful of this and didn't go too deep into the topics. Class was not hard, assignments and exams were straight forward enough. USE THE GROUPME, he loves when you use the groupme.

Professor used AI to give essay feedback and big portion of grade based on a group project policy brief paper. Class is very disorganized and I struggled to understand what exactly he was trying to teach.  Seemed like he prioritized other commitments over teaching. For an essay worth 20% of grade due in Sept did not receive grade until Dec.

Rubalcaba was very inaccessible outside of class, and his materials did not follow any schedule. The course began the first few weeks using the syllabus, but by mid-semester he had scrapped the whole thing. 90% sure he used AI to grade our assignments. Very knowledgeable, but not a great educator.

This class is easy, but prof. Rubalcaba often has long talks on one topic in class which makes us get behind. The discussions can be helpful, but if you are someone who needs a more structured course then I would choose a different professor. Exams are open note, but you have to study to pass. Note that he is not that reachable outside of class.

Dr. Rubalcaba's class was by far my easiest this semester. If you can grasp the main concepts from ECON 101, you will be fine. He really wants students to be successful and has open-note exams. He often rambles, so some classes felt useless, but overall he's a great option for 310.

By far the easiest class I've taken here. Prof. Rubalcaba is very passionate, but his lectures lack focus bc of tangents that may not adhere specifically to content you'll be tested on. That being said, every test is open note and he'll cover everything you'll need to know in lecture. His lecture notes are GREAT! Loved this class.

Professor Rubalcaba genuinely cares about student success and fully commits to helping students understand economics. The class was approachable, and the material was thoughtfully connected to real issues in North Carolina, which made it both relevant and engaging. I learned so much and truly appreciated his dedication.

Gives periodic pop quizzes for attendance, so just show up to class, and you're good. Prof Rubalcaba is pretty chill and picks interesting cases to discuss in class. Go to office hours if you want a better explanation than lectures. 3 tests (open note), 7~ pop quizzes, 3 practice problem sets. Do your work and you'll be fine

He is super goofy and makes a pretty boring topic interesting most of the time. If you did well in Econ 101 this class will be super easy, the tests are open note and the problem sets are intuitive. He does have some random attendance quizzes and tests are graded out of few points so be careful. Overall, a good professor and a good class.

Professor Rubalcaba was great! He had very interesting lectures and he definitely cared about his students. He was very understanding and genuinely wanted us to succeed. It is not too hard to do well as long as you use the materials and past assignments to study. The tests were also open note which was a huge plus!

Professor Rubalcaba was such an interesting man. The only word I can use to describe him is a Goober.
