The other positive reviews are very accurate with the class not being very difficult at all, but I did absolutely learn a great deal. Professor Rubalcaba is such a funny man and always made me laugh, though he absolutely did not try to be funny.

Don't get me wrong, Dr. Rubalcaba is a cool person. But I didn't learn a single thing in this course that wasn't covered in ECON 101. The grading was also incredibly delayed, and the class overall was remarkably disorganized. All in all, I wish I had taken ECON 410 instead and learned something.

Rubalcaba was great! He was really accommodating given everything that happened this semester and he was very straightforward about what was required for tests, homeworks, and has good lectures. The tests are only 15 questions (including the final) so one mistake counts a lot. Do not be intimidated by this class, pretty much everyone does well.

Professor Rubalcaba was overall a strong professor with mainly fair grading and open note everything. Only negative thing was that he graded the last assignment harshly with no explanation after not teaching the unit super well (barely providing adequate notes/lecture)

He's a nice guy and a pretty decent lecturer. Don't expect responses to emails and he will forget to upload content a lot. My best advice is to reach out to the TA. With that being said, tests are open note and not bad (not nearly as bad as ECON 101). The exercises are pretty similar to the exam and you're allowed to work with other people.

The other reviews are odd considering that he was very accomodating, energetic, and kind. He cares about this students and brought bagels before the final exam. His lecture notes outline what is tested on the exam. His lectures can be disorganized, but they are engaging, and he takes time to respond to emails but he is overall a good professor.

I had an amazing time in this course and with Prof Gifford. He draws a lot on the board, so you'll have to come to class to get the material; if you show up to class and read through your notes the night before a quiz you'll be fine (+no midterms). He loves what he teaches and it makes you enjoy it too, I would highly recommend him!

I feel like I got a lot out of this class! Dr. Gifford gave us weekly/biweekly quizzes, which really helped me stay engaged with the material as it built upon itself. He is super intelligent and it shows that he cares about his students learning.

I really liked Dr. Gifford. It was a smaller class and he wrote his notes on the board and it was easier to learn that way. The grades are based on quizzes and projects and then the final exam. I loved the weekly quizzes instead of midterms, it helps with studying and learning more. Take him if you have the opportunity.

I really enjoyed Dr. Gifford! The course was formatted with weekly quizzes instead of a midterm, a group project, and a final exam. The quizzes were straight from the lecture and required you to redraw diagrams he drew on the whiteboard in class. Take good notes, and study them the night before the quiz and you'll be fine.

Writes his lectures on the white board and imagery heavy. post study guides for lecture with an audio, but come to class to get the images he drew out. Quizzes instead of midterms, they were directly from the lecture. one group project/presentation that wasn't too bad. assigned readings each week. study lecture notes and you'll be fine.
Professor Gifford is amazing!  His quizzes are straightforward and based off class material.
He is a king!! Take this class if you want to have a good biology experience!

I'm not a science major, so I took this class as a gen ed and the material was a little difficult for me, some topics/lessons were harder than others... Professor Gifford is really nice though, so if I had to take this class again I would take it with him!

I really liked this course, but be aware that it is pretty difficult. You cover so much information in class from a wide range of subjects and are tested on all of it. The TA makes and grades the assignments and tests which were always very challenging. If you are looking for a easy gen-ed this is not for you, but it's an interesting class anyways.

My biggest complaint is you don't talk about marine life (animals) until mid-April. Most of the class is atmospheric and ocean interactions, which is cool too but not what I was looking forward to. 
I think the TA's are really hard graders for no reason, so not an easy A. I learned a lot and went to all the lectures, but I am barely pulling a B

The professor is nice and the TA is helpful, but the exams in this class are pretty hard, and there are some assignments as well that can help boost your grade, but not by much. This is one of my gen eds and its the class I'm struggling with the most. If you can, or unless you love this topic, refrain from taking this class.

He wanted quiz answers to be exactly from the textbook and wanted us to memorize textbook definitions of vocab terms. Assigned whole entire units to read each week, but never asked questions on material outside of lecture, so it's a complete waste of time to read. Gave us an EC assignment that curved grades by about 4% at the end of the course.

I have mixed feelings about him. For one test question he took off points because I "could have drawn the image bigger." And for two of the MC questions he admitted that the answer I chose was correct, but just not the main point. He never gave back points and I stayed after class almost every single day. However, it all worked out in the end.

perfect class. Tests and quizzes were always clearly derived from the textbook and what he said in class, he really did a good job of making me feel prepared for assessments with the information he delivered. Everything was well-organized and distributed across the semester, and he delivered a manageable amount of info. And SO NICE!

He was fine, he just really gave us an information overload and would test us on things he mentioned once in passing. The class is easy if you attend, but don't expect to get quick replies from him outside of class.

Nice guy who gives decent lectures but regularly gave unclear answers to questions, admitted to not knowing answers about his own material, or even gave incorrect or inconsistent responses to students. He was not particularly receptive to student concerns about grading and exams.The material isn't too difficult but there was very little support.

A pretty good lecturer, and tried to engage students in discussion. TA's were very harsh, and the short assignment required a lot of detail which was not always gone over in class. It's doable, but be prepared to work for a good grade.
He does not know anything he is talking about. Most of questions asked were answered with "IDK". Boring lecture, don't take if you don't have to.

Dr. Gifford was a great lecturer who tried to engage the class well. His tests were relatively fair considering the amount of material covered. However the TA's were harsh graders. The short answer assignments due about every other week were only 4 questions but required lots of detail. Many of them weren't discussed in class and not in the textbk.

Marine microbial genomics with Scott was an absolute pleasure, definitely my favorite class in a while. He is clearly passionate about the course material, and while it can be difficult, you will get a thorough understanding of metagenomics, get involved with research in his lab, and make some new friends if you keep up. 10/10!

Extremely nice professor.   Let's you redo homework for higher grade.   One midterm and no final.  Had year end presentation.   Always available and holds consistent office hours.  This is great teacher with interesting lectures.  Offers extra credit.

Marc is an extremely kind professor, but unfortunately his lectures tend to not make any sense so matter how hard you try to follow along. He tends to contradict himself. I walked out of this class more confused than I walked in. he also doesn't put in ANY grades until after finals which I found to be extremely stressful.

Nicest personality, ruthless homework and tests. Graded very easily though.
Lectures are fun if you like the course material. Overall, I think his great personality wins over questionable assignment arrangements.

Dr. Alperin was great! He is one of the kindest and nicest professors that I have ever had while at UNC. He was very well spoken, always quick to respond to emails, and gave good feedback. He did take a very long time to grade, but his exams were not very hard and if you put the effort in, you will do well.

As a person Marc has been my favorite professor at UNC. Very down to earth and genuinely caring guy; super approachable. Lots of hw and he does not grade ANYTHING, but if you submit your work you WILL get a good grade. If I rated him mid semester it would be a 3 max, but coming out with a dubiously deserved A I have to reevaluate

Marc is a CHILL GUY, ok. You won't get a grade back until the final, but probably because he wants to just pass everyone. Work with friends on the problem sets and try your best on the tests and you will do fine. This is an interesting class but not a walk in the park.

His lectures are 60+ slides with ONLY pictures and no words. He doesn't make sense when he lectures and the information that is on lectures contradicts with his test. His test are extremely difficult especially since you can't study the slides since theirs no information on them. Also, you won't know your grade in class until the semester is over.

Very friendly and chill professor, definitely not the best lecturer but is very passionate about what he's teaching and very approachable outside class. A little old-fashioned in the format of assignments but I'm okay with that.

Marc is very passionate about what he teaches, but he is not a good professor. He talks the entire class period and doesn't explain things well. His tests are extremely difficult and his problem sets don't make sense half of the time. He claims you don't need prior experience with Matlab but I disagree. Beware, math and coding heavy!

Class was intense and several hours long and the daily hw took even longer. Trip to IMS was awesome! Be familiar with excel; he wants things done in specific ways. He also wants everything printed. Any STEM person would definitely do well here but it wasn't an easy A. He never graded anything until after the final. Definitely recommend though!

Professor Alperin is extremely intelligent on the subject and is passionate about what he lectures on. He is extremely kind and really is more than willing to help if you make an effort. He is not the fastest grader, so if that's something that would bother you you should avoid him. This class is extremely interesting and I'd take it over a math.

this man takes everything so literally. there's a rule you have to write 10 pages of writing for a gen ed class but i was unaware this also applied to science classes, and despite having written 1.5 pages for homework each week, he sprung a 10 page research paper on us the week before the final. And we were in our final for the entire 3 hours.

I took this for the QI credit and while it was definitely worth it to take this over a math class, it was still the worst first year seminar. He's a really great guy and offers tons of corrections on homework, however don't expect to get a SINGLE grade for anything until a week after the final. Also everything is on paper bc he can't work computers

If you take Professor Alperin, get a folder. All your assignments he wants turned in on paper, and he's quite fond of paper handouts. Lectures are kind of boring, but he's a nice guy, obviously cares a lot about the subject, and offers corrections on homework assignments.

This class should take that much work considering it is a first year seminar. The class is heavy on lecture and you have homework and readings basically every week. If you are looking for an easy credit definitely do not take this class! However, Prof Alperin is a nice guy and very understanding
the man is MAD thicc, but is a terrible professor. I mean sir, this was a Marine Sciences class and we didn't watch Finding Nemo ONCE! i consider this course a waste of time. he als0 stole my girl:((

I took this instead of a math class for my QI credit. I think it was a better alternative, but make sure you know what you're getting yourself into if you want to take this. There's a LOT of homework assignments (reading and math) and he doesn't do a good job of teaching the material. However, you get the opportunity to make up work.

Professor Alperin, is my favorite professor that I have had at UNC. He is extremely passionate about his work, enjoys bonding with each student, and provides helpful knowledge to students. If you're an environmental science kid, you will love this class! The exams and problem sets are very tough, but Professor Alperin is a very kind grader.
Way too much work assigned for a first-year seminar! Also, way too high of a math level. He is also not the best at teaching concepts.
Lots of homework with way too high a math level for a first year seminar. This is not what a first year seminar should look like. Do not recommend this class.

Seim is always ready to help if you are willing to ask. With around 8 homework assignments and the rest tests determining your grade, it can be difficult to bring up what you have because barely anything is given to you. Quite challenging tests because you need to remember very specific numbers. Lectures and slides are decent, but helpful.

Dr. Seim is SUPER kind and wants us to succeed. I am a biology major (took this as allied science) and HIGHLY recommend. Tests are straight from class and a study guide is provided. Homework is slightly difficult sometimes, but it's made by the TA. Content is interesting and I have learned a lot!

Prof. Seim is a good lecturer and he is really knowledgeable. The TA grades most of the work and helps make the homework and tests. Most of the testing material is pulled from the homework and the free textbook.

He is super nice and super invested in what he teaches. I learned a lot of interesting material. "Weekly" homework is easy, and tests are very straightforward. If you study the study guide and attend class the exams will be easy. The lectures sometimes felt like they were dragging or long, but overall easy class with a very nice professor.

Dr. Seim is SO sweet and his class was very interesting. I am an EMES major so that's why I found it fun, the lab is even better. Make a quizlet of the study guides and as long as you know the answers you will be fine. Take the homeworks seriously because they weigh a lot.

There's only one homework assignment a week, which are very manageable if you review the lecture slides and skim the textbook. The tests are manageable as well, he provides a study guide with the exact questions that are going to be on the test. Attendance is required and lectures drag, but Professor Seim is very knowledgeable of his subject.

Nice guy but class was all auditorium lectures and graded nearly entirely by exams that were 100% fill-in-the-blank on very specific things. Very difficult tests for a 101 class. I did well bc I had prior knowledge but I certainly would not recommend this class to anyone looking for GenEds. If you're STEM take 401 instead and if not don't take this

Professor Seim was very knowledgable about the subject matter, but at times the material was too complex to be adequately explained in the timeframe of a 101 class. Most of the grade was made up of 3 exams which was challenging, but it was not hard to do well once you learned the style of the exam.

I ended up doing pretty well in this class but very many did not. I did not enjoy the test format: all fill in the blank questions of random, arbitrary facts and numbers that must be memorized. The tests are also worth 80% of your final grade, and there was never any feedback on the tests or the homework except grades. There was a curve though

Dr. Seim does his best to make lectures enjoyable, and he let class out early many times. 80% of your grade comes from the midterms/final, but detailed study guides are provided. Attendance is mandatory, but if you're willing to show up to class, do the homework, and study, you'll be fine.

Dr. Seim runs the most complex intro classes I have ever taken. Grade is determined by exams that are 100% fill in the blank and are far too detailed for non-majors. This class feels impossible to pass unless you already have marine science experience and lectures do not help. Would never recommend this class to anyone. Look for a different option

Good professor with a lot of knowledge and exprience in his field, but do not take if you're just trying to fulfill a Gen Ed or other requirement. Tests make up 80% of your grade with the final being 40%. Tests are almost completely short answer and they aren't short either.

Tony is great! Lectures were engaging, good amount of info on slides but not too much. Exams were mostly vocab-based with some application questions. Homeworks were easy and the TA helped out a ton! A good amount of reading, but he goes over the important stuff in classes so attendance is a good idea. Great class and great material

Tony is an extremely nice and genuine guy and I could have done much better if I would have paid more attention and studied harder. Grading is only on two midterms, a final, and weekly homeworks but the homework is a small chunk. Found the lectures very, very information heavy and hard to pay attention to and exams hard to study for.

Super enthusiastic about marine science. Presentations are pretty good, although not always great for individual review. Homeworks are weekly but don't take up much time each week. He can be a little disorganized, but nothing bad.

Textbook chapters are incredibly long and you likely won't have time to read all of them. Two midterms, a final, and homeworks are the grades in this class, and if you stumble once it's over because you need a 95 to get an A. Tony's a nice guy and the material isn't complex, but I wouldn't recommend for just a focus capacity.

Tony is one of the sweetest human beings alive. He genuinely cares about each one of his students. I was not super interested in sed strat at first, but his excitement and teaching made me enjoy the class way more than I thought I would. I wish he taught more classes b/c I would 100% take another class with him.

An A was a 95, Dr. Castillo is a very passionate professor, but his lectures were quite long and fast paced. No textbook, only slides, and each slide deck was anywhere from 40-70 slides, each class. The tests were a lot harder than I expected (took this class for an upper bio). Lot's of extra credit though, he wants you to succeed.

GROUP PROJECTS (4). COIL makes class feel like 2 classes. Doesn't communicate well. Exams are niche and questions are worded poorly. Lectures are boring. Cold calls. Loved him for 490. Highly disappointed and frustrated with 441. Quizzes every class. Feels like he doesn't care about students and only wants to do his personal research.
This class was about corals and it was so interesting. There is a project, but the topic can be chosen for wahtever you want. As long as you try, you will succeed.

Dr. Castillo is a passionate speaker. He is insightful and holds office hours and will work to make sure his class succeeds. I have taken 4 classes with him so far and plan to take more! There are also extra credit opportunities if you go to class.

Dr. Castillo really cares about his students' learning the material. There are quizzes in every class but they're open note. Even though there were weekly assignments, I didn't feel like they were busy work. He is very clear on grading and the class is well organized. I would recommend this class if you're interested in the material

Professor Castillo was a good professor. He made it clear he was more concerned about us learning than about grades. Your overall grade came from in-class quizzes (given randomly), assignments and exams. It was relatively easy to get an A even if you didn't do well in the exams as the other assignments made up for it.

Professor Castillo is extremely intimidating and belittles students in class. He called out a girl for being on her phone in front of an entire class of at least 80 people. His lectures don't help at all and he pulls from a textbook that's simply too much to read for an entry level course. He is extremely unforgiving with grading/late work.

Dr. Nowlan is really nice but I just did not like the way the class was organized - made interesting content pretty boring. The group work felt pointless most of the time, and grading took forever. The CREATE method project is annoying but not difficult. Exams were easy to study for since lectures are recorded and she gives learning objectives.

I really liked Nowlan, if you understand the material well and re-do the quiz questions you will do well on the exams. The CREATE Method was a little annoying but if you have a group and stay on top of work you'll be fine.

I really didn't enjoy the CREATE (group) assignment. A huge percentage of your grade is dependent on group work. The lecture content felt random throughout the semester. However, studying for the final was actually fun because everything finally connected together. Midterms/final were super fair but only worth 39% of your final grade
inconsistent grading that takes 40 years, unclear directions

Dr. Nowlan is sweet! Lots of group work and huge project, mildly difficult exams but study and you'll be fine. Often didn't finish lectures in time so we had to spend the next class finishing them, and the cycle would continue. She's very caring though, and she was helpful during office hours
Huge group project, but this class is super interesting and as long as you read you will do well.

Dr. Nowlan is really nice and caring, and she's very open to talking about the intersection of neuroscience and humanities. I learned a lot from this class but she would run out of time in pretty much every lecture. Don't need to read the textbook, all exam questions come from the lectures. Hated the CREATE method project though, very boring.

Dr. Nowlan is very supportive and there are a lot of built-in drops and extra credit. Exams test comprehension on pretty complex research papers, so take time to understand them well a few days before. The Makerspace project is a lot, but by the end you become super informed on a specific drug and receptor. We had a cool field trip as well.

Dr. Nowlan is an amazing professor. Her lectures are primarily open-discussion, so it is important to come to class to participate. She gives many extra credit opportunities. She heavily uses Gradescope and gives a one-day grace period for a lot of her assignments. It is important to stay ahead on deadlines and give max effort on assignments.

I liked 405 with Dr. Nowlan, but I am pre–PhD. If you don't like reading scientific papers, I wouldn't recommend, but it is cool to use the Makerspace to make a receptor model. Be sure you are ready to work, but Dr. Nowlan cares about her students and will work with you to make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Reading some of the NSCI 221 reviews I was worried bc I didn't get NSCI 222 or 225, but after a semester with other challenging stem classes, it honestly wasn't bad. Her lectures are recorded, (big plus), her exams are crammable, and CREATE is tedious, but doable with a good group. And with extra credit - you'll be fine!

People are hating on Dr. Nowlan, but she's the best. If you actually read and do the pre-class work, which is not more than any other NSCI class at UNC, you will learn a lot more pharmacology than you learned in 221 and you will vastly improve your ability to read a dense scientific paper. Don't be a lazy bum and you'll be fine. Exams are easy.

Professor Nowlan seems new; however, her class structure is not as bad as many make it out to be. The slides have everything you need to succeed. The CREATE project, though tedious and honestly lengthy for the content learned, is not bad as long as you don't procrastinate. Her class was fair, and she genuinely wants you to succeed.
Prof Nowlan was excellent!

I liked Dr Nowlan in 221 so I wanted to take 405 with her but this class isn't what I expected it to be. She is super sweet but the class itself isn't fun and I feel like I haven't learned that much about neuropharmacology but more just about research papers. Feels difficult balancing the semester long project in between all the paper assignments.

This class was not what I was expecting at all! There are assignments due before every single class and in class assignments every single class for attendance. There is not really a lot of learning in this class, but more so work towards a larger semester long project. The assignments are not helpful for the project as a whole. DO NOT TAKE!

DO NOT TAKE. entire class is a huge group project with minimal guidelines. takes FOREVER to grade things (over a month & hasn't graded 1st exam) in class assignment everyday for attendance. journal club everyday but on the same paper for a month. boring lecturer & never knows answers to any questions. class has no actual content learned nothing

Group project thats graded pretty harshly and feels kinda pointless, exams are pretty much straight memorization from lecture or textbook. her lectures are pretty boring as she just reads off the slides and doesnt really explain, also waited till end of the semester to put a lot of grades in

I liked Dr. Nowlan's attitude a lot. She's obviously a very new professor, but I wish she would discover her own teaching style instead of teaching the class like it has been in the past. CREATE Method project was miserable, but everything else (exams, assignments, pre-class work) is up to you to do well on. Nowlan was always sweet and helpful!

Dr. Nowlan is an okay lecturer. She's nice and funny, but lectures are always behind and can be disorganized. The CREATE method project, worth a huge portion of the grade, is harshly graded, SO MUCH WORK, and at the end of it, I didn't learn much. The rest of the content was interesting, and the exams are reasonably easy.
Be ready to retake this course!
There is no review material offered to students to prepare them for exams. Exams are confusing and nothing like the lectures.

Bad BAD BAD professor. Exams poorly written class incredibly disorganized and no practice problems were available the ones that were had no similarity to exams. He honestly seems like a nice guy  but seriously avoid it if you want a good grade.
The easiest class I've ever taken. I just took the final and it was so free.

Great person, not the best lecturer. Most of the test content is not discussed in class. Seemingly not equipped to handle a large class size, and there were tons of tech mishaps that set back classes. Grading criteria is confusing (I've given up trying to understand it). I'm sure he's a better professor in higher-level classes.

Great dude - not a great teacher. Most of the slides he posts don't have the answer to the problems on them so there is no study material other than ULA made questions (lots of mistakes). Assignments posted and due randomly (saturdays sometimes??). Tests have material he never lectured on. Not tech savvy - lots of tech errors - but lovely person!
There are no practice materials written by the professor for the exams. There is very little practice/homework to engage with and understand content. The exams are written poorly.
Very disorganized, and exams are written very poorly. He is a nice guy, but I would recommend taking 220 with anyone else.

Dr. Matera seems like a great person and likely a strong PI, but the course is very disorganized. Canvas is hard to navigate, assignments are posted unpredictably, and many aren't graded, so I don't know where I stand. Lectures and exams are unclear, and practice exams are often inaccurate.

Prof. Matera clearly understands the material that he is teaching but does not seem well equipped to teach it to a class this size. Formatting and online materials are not his strong suit either: poorly made tests and Canvas, no access to exams after the fact, runs into issues during lectures, etc. Would recommend looking elsewhere for this course.

So, he's such a nice guy. And he DOES know what he's talking about, he's very smart. He does not know how to teach, especially this class. Does not know how to explain things in a simple or really coherent way at all. Exams were very poorly written and the spread of content covered felt unfair at times. Prob a great PI, don't take 220 with him.

Class is extremely unorganized, your grade is almost fully comprised of exams, and exams are very poorly written. Definitely would've had more success with another professor. Very obvious he hasn't taught this class before. Also said students rely too much on grades and unwilling to curve an exam with a median of a 65. Do not take. Nice guy though

This was his first semester teaching BIOL 220 (usually teaches 400-level). Easy to see how much he loves the subject, as he's very knowledgeable. I will say grading and structure are a bit unclear at times, but exams are not overly difficult and come from his class slides. You have to attend class to write down things he mentions. Super nice guy!
Super nice and funny guy. 3/10 lecturer. Makes content more confusing that it needs to be. Exams are extremely difficult and poorly written. Tests on content that he covered for

Dr. Matera is a great professor! Definitely one of the best research professors to take in the bio department. His exams are fair and he's really engaged with the lectures. The more you engage with his lectures the more you will learn. Not a lot of study resources like other sections but not bad for anyone experienced in bio classes at UNC.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Basically your entire grade is comprised of exams. You can study for weeks for the exams and it is absolutely pointless because nothing covered in class is going to be on the exam. He writes the exams very very poorly and they cover topics you will have never heard of.

Do not take BIOL220 with Dr. Matera if you want to ensure a high grade in this course. The exams are written extremely poorly and it genuinely does not matter how much you study as you will be tested on things that were not covered whatsoever. I promise that it would be easier to obtain an A in Organic Chemistry.

Professor Matera is an expert on molecular biology, and he is great at explaining the details. The class focuses solely on analyzing research papers, but background is provided and Dr. Matera is happy to help. Tests focus on interpreting scientific figures and applying mechanisms. Video project was a nice break and spaced out well.

Professor Matera structures his class around research papers relevant to advancements and discovery in molecular biology. While this may be overwhelming at first, he does a wonderful job explaining the papers and the science. He has a clear passion for the topic which made lectures extremely engaging and learning easy.

Super nice! This class is common sense but she did a good job explaining regardless. There is a book you have to read (your choice) but she doesn't use the textbook more than once. The group project is not bad but lowkey confusing but she didn't grade too harshly. The exams are easy and basically ask specific questions about what the slides say.

Dr. Nedimyer is great and very accessible, she wants to help you understand her material! You are given random attendance grades so show up to all classes. Lecture/slide based. 1 group project and book club, that has multiple assignments. Is a difficult grader but criteria is pretty clear. Exams are extremely specific so and all multiple choice.

Dr. Nedimyer is super caring, accessible, and wants the best for you! She is a harsh grader at times, specifically in the group project, which is a randomly assigned group based on what book you choose to read for book club. Tests are relatively fair. She requires a course pack for this course, but we honestly did not use it more than 3 times.

She was a nice professor who seemed to care about her students. The material is easy but its a lot of busy work and readings that aren't necessary. I had to buy a coursepack for this class that we didn't use much. I did like the book club portion and the group project is relatively easy. Her exams are really detailed and she can be a harsh grader.

I loved Dr. Nedimyer. She is a great person. She is passionate about the course. She didnt grade tough unless it was the group project assignments. It was one big project broken up into like 3 parts. Her exams are REALLY SPECIFIC so study every little thing in the powerpoints.

The content of the class was very easy but there is A LOT of busy work that was not at all helpful. The semester long group project seemed fairly easy but she was a harsh grader and sometimes did not elaborate on what you did wrong. Overall, she was nice but the class itself, the busy work, and grading techniques were just annoying.

Dr. Nedimyer is really nice but she treats her students like high schoolers. The class content is super easy and pretty much common sense. There is a lot of group work but it wasn't hard, it was just graded harshly. Attendance is pretty much mandatory because of mandatory group meetings each week.

She's incredibly nice, and this class is by no means hard, BUT she treats you like high schoolers. Don't expect to learn anything revolutionary in this class. There's lots of busy work that is more overwhelming than helpful. Drink some caffeine before class and come prepared to feel like you're wasting an hour.

I liked Dr. Nedimyer for what this class was. A lot of the material is common sense and she can grade a bit harsh, overall it isn't a hard class. Exams are easy to prepare for and the group project isn't that bad, coming from someone who didn't get the best groupmates. I think this was her 2nd semester with this course and it will only get better

Professor Nedimyer is an amazing person who cares about the topics of her lectures and tries to make class enjoyable. Although there are lots of readings for homework, the course is fairly easy itself, also by the help of Prof. Nedimyer. There is a lot of group work but nothing horrible, coming from a person who hates group stuff. Would recommend.

The course itself is a lot of common sense but she grades a little hard. A lot of group work and busy work but its required for my major. I like Nedimyer a lot though so although the class feels like a waste of time, she is a good option for it. I think this was her first year teaching the course I thought she did a good job.
Attendance is graded; just come and listen. Only 1 essay is graded at the end of the course. Gives you directions for every paragraph that needs to be on there.

Dr. Greg is great, I heavily recommend this class for anyone even slightly interested in public health! We just met once a week briefly on zoom with mandatory attendance, but Dr. Greg is very understanding and offers alternative options if something comes up for you. The only grade is the final paper and he wasn't a tough grader at all.
super chill class. once a week class online and attendance was mandatory. had to have camera on. only assignment was a 800 word paper. learned a lot about how to get a health career.
Love Dr. Greg! Great class if you're pre-med or pre-nutrition. Mandatory attendance on Zoom once a week and class ends spring break. One 1000 word paper is the only assignment.
Dr. Greg is a really cool guy and this class with him was both extremely easy and enjoyable
Had a great time listening to all the lecturers come in and talk about their studies!

Your grade in the course consists of attendance and a final paper. The class is what you make it: if you are passionate about public health and interact with a guest speakers, you will probably get more out of the class. It's pretty easy to get an A, just show up and write a paper.
Greg is awesome, classes are super interesting, easy A and very informative if you're interested in behavioral health or public health in general.

I have no interest in Public Health but took this class because I needed one more hour to graduate. It ended up being really interesting! You do have to attend class with your camera on, but the lectures are engaging. I would recommend it (especially if you are actually interested in Public Health).

She is an absolutely amazing person. College thriving is the most boring and useless class on Earth, but she really tries to make the lectures engaging. She always has fun games and a prize box full of stuff. She is so kind and enthusiastic about what she does. Definitely recommend for college thriving.
She was super sweet and tried her best to make the class engaging for us. All the assignments are easy and some are actually pretty fun to do. Definitely a great professor for College Thriving.

She was so kind!! No one likes to trudge their way to college thriving, but Melanie tried her hardest to make it entertaining. I actually made a few friends in the class because she made it so open and welcoming. Definitely try to take CT with her! Assignments are busy work, but so easy.
LOVED her! So kind and caring, tried her hardest to make classes fun and engaging. Even had a cutie little prize box. Take with her 100%.

Not much to say about this class, it's very easy to pass and it's the same for every student. Professor Goss is very sweet and she definitely cares about her students. Grading is very clear and she's pretty lenient so I'd recommend her.

She is so sweet and really cares for all her students. This class is very pointless and dumb but she tried to make it more fun. Most of the assignments are written reflections and she grades them all really well. Definitely recommend her for college thriving.

Dr. Goss was super duper sweet and made a mandatory class very enjoyable. The weekly assignments can be a pain but that is just the class, doesn't matter what professor you have. That being said, Dr. Goss was very accomodating and brought a fun energy to every class! I'd 100% choose her for this class if you have the choice!!

so kind and caring. I am taking my third class with him and he is probably the best professor I have taken at UNC. His classes are discussion based and the material is interesting. You can tell he truly cares about his students.

Very engaging classes and lectures. Lots of discussion and group activities. He is easy to work with. You are graded on very few things so messing up one hurts. Final is on the harder side and feedback isn't given so grading criteria is unclear.

Genuinely the best prof I have ever had. He is SO caring and wholesome. He is willing to work with students who are anxious about giving an oral report, which is so kind. He also is very clear about expectations and is an easy grader. His campus tours are the best- he truly cares about learning rather than making the course difficult.

Best professor I have ever had. I did his AAAD 231 summer course on Zoom. Three grades: participation, journal, and final. Super lenient with deadlines and the journal is so much better than any paper/essay assignment I have done. He is super intelligent and is so interesting to listen to. Highly recommend taking a class with him if you can.

Dr. Porter is an incredible teacher. He will meet you where you're at, provide make-up opportunities, and challenge you to speak off-the-cuff in front of the class. I thoroughly enjoyed this class and the rich discussion that was included. He does have a tendency to interrupt, which can be frustrating at times, but I highly recommend this class.

Professor Porter is one of the kindest, most passionate professors here at UNC. You can tell he cares about his students and the content he teaches. The class is discussion/lecture heavy, you'll read about five books, lots of writing assignments, 2 presentations. He was willing to accommodate so long as you communicate. Engage and you'll be fine.

You will never meet a more passionate and knowledgeable professor (in any department) than Porter. His classes are reading heavy, but what do you expect from humanities? Do not listen to any review giving this man less than 5 stars. Just go to class, pay attention and participate in lecture, and go to the library for projects and you'll do well!

I have never written a review on a professor in 4 years at UNC but I could write essays about how much I love Porter. I have taken 2 classes with him & I wish I could take 20 more. He truly cares about his students & wants you to succeed. Pay attention in class & go to the library for projects, you will get an A! TAKE EVERY CLASS YOU CAN WITH HIM!!
this prof is goated. I've taken 130, 252, and 254 with him. Can't reccomend enough

Professor Porter is truly awesome! He's so kind and easy to talk to – he never made anyone feel bad for not knowing something and is a very supportive instructor. I can truly say he is the most caring professor I've had during my time at UNC. Course content is heavy, but important to learn about! Classes are discussion-based.
Porter is a great professor who cares about you. As long as your request is reasonable, he'll work with you on any requirements.
FAV UNC PROFESSOR. Very interesting readings and class discussions. Lots of group discussions as well.

Profressor Porter is a great profressor who really is really passionate about the subjects he talks about. Although 252 is really reading heavy, he is an understanding professor and a fair grader, just make sure to participate in class discussions.

Porter is a great professor. In class, he gives questions that you & and a group discuss. Reading the textbook is helpful, but just make sure you know a little about the topic. Grade is made of 4 assignments (2 oral reports [3-5 min presentation] a 5500 word journal and the final). Caring man who cares about the subject and talks about himself.

He uses subjective grading.He does not give feedback on any of your speeches or journal. He also does not provide students with any review of the exam material.Only 4 assignments, so must do great on each one.He spends most of the class telling students who to vote for in the next election.Sadly, no positivity or good vibes in a 3 hour class.
Way too many readings that are super academic in nature

I learned nothing new in this class & feel extremely unprepared for the final (which is worth 45% of the grade) with what info I have obtained. Very unorganized in terms of dates & class logistics. Rarely answers emails. I have emailed him twice about my attendance bc I was sick (he specifically stated to stay home if you're sick) and no response.

I took Professor Porter over the summer, and he was terrific! While only me and two others participated in the class, Porter held great conversations with us. The only two things graded were our journal and the final, which was an essay. He has super clear grading criteria and, overall, just a fantastic professor!

The reading is less. There is a journal writing (minimum 7500 words) based on readings and the visiting of historical sites. 3 oral reports and a final exam. Take notes on class lecture/discussion to do well on the final exam. You will learn a lot. Professor Porter is awesome and I felt like he was my favorite after taking the course.
Professor Porter is very passionate and knowledgeable on the subject matter. He wants to make sure every student learns and succeeds in his course.
Great class, I don't want it to end
I absolutely LOVED this class
Really good intro to art history overall. I'm learning a lot and hope to take more art history in the future.
This is a really cool class, like a menu of different art history courses.Levine's lectures are really good too
What an amazing class. Professor Levine is one of the best, and this was one of my favorite classes at UNC. I learned so much about art and beyond.
Interesting easy class with guest lectures. Professor Levine is really good at connecting the lectures to big themes and ideas
The course is straightforward, and with interesting guest lectures on all kinds of art, it's a fantastic way to learn without feeling overwhelmed
The class is pretty easy, and the guest lectures on various periods keep things fresh and engaging.
This is a wonderful class. The guest lectures touch on various art movements, and Levine connects each topic back to historical events, making it all resonate.
I really got a lot from this class. Professor Levine connects contemporary art to today's issues, and his classes are always interesting. Loved the discussions
Dr Levine's passion for  contemporary art is contagious, and he really makes you think about the artists and their worlds.
Professor Levine is amazing! His lectures are super fun, and he makes art history feel relevant. I actually looked forward to class every week!
Amazing class, amazing professor. Try to take a class with him

The class is unusual because it's mostly guest lectures, but I really enjoyed Professor Levine's sessions and am planning to take his class next semester. ARTH 150 is a pretty easy class that's interesting
Such a good class. Professor Levine challenges students to really think. Lectures are loose with time for discussion. He really cares about the students and their learning.
Loved it and look forward to taking more classes with Levine
I really enjoyed the class. Professor Levine was excellent and Christina the TA was too.
This is a fun, pretty easy class with lots of guest lectures. Levine ties it all together nicely and is super nice and easygoing and helpful. I highly recommend

As someone who has taken other art classes that focus on gender/female anatomy with no issue, I feel like Prof Levine really put an uncomfortable emphasis on certain topics. He was also condescending / seemed annoyed with certain questions. The only good thing about him beating strange topics into the ground is that it sticks with you for exams.

this guy literally belittles his students and clearly has a big ego. the class itself was very poorly run, but his section was horrible because the slides itself included no notes, just images of the paintings. if you didn't attend class or get the notes from someone else on the paintings, you were screwed. easy A tho.

She's extremely passionate, but unfortunately I had a very difficult time paying attention. She writes solely on the chalkboard, and I can't write and listen at the same time. Concepts were made to be more difficult than they actually were. Don't fall behind in this class because I ended up teaching myself everything in a week before the final.

Lectures are easy to follow and include both formulas and examples. Always posts lecture notes and slides. Grades exams within 1-2 weeks and generous with partial credit. Passionate about stats, wants students to succeed, offers lots of extra credit. Don't listen to the bad reviews, which are mostly from her first sem here. She has improved a lot!

I think fall '25 was her first sem teaching, she was much better in the spring than what I read in her reviews from the fall. She's fixed her problem with taking a long time grading exams. Just pay attention in lecture and actually do homework and you'll be fine.

The content is boring but I really like the way she structures the class. You barely need to go for attendance, and she gives a lot of extra points. If you put a reasonable amount of time into studying, not very hard.

Dr. Bergland is a great professor who knows the content like the back of her hand, and she truly cares for her students - she is accessible at office hours/via Piazza, asks for questions frequently every lecture, and provides ample extra credit on exams. Convinced bad reviews are from non-stem majors, because this class is truly not difficult.

She's really kind, accessible and does want the best for her students. She's very available on piazza & in office hours. Homework's & textbook are not reflective of exams after midterm 1. Final exam was cumulative but heavier in just learned content learned in days leading up to LDOC which made it HARD. Would benefit from a recitation & TAs.

I honestly believe she really cares about her students, but the lectures are boring and difficult to follow. The midterms are not unreasonable, but are definitely challenging, and preparing for them is not always straightforward. While she is enthusiastic, she tends to lose many students during lectures and is not particularly effective at teaching

I struggled to pay attention in Professor Bergland's lectures. While she is passionate about statistics, her lectures are often difficult to follow and somewhat boring. Her tests are also very difficult and do not typically reflect the homework. I would try to take STOR 155 with another professor if possible.

Honestly, a nice person, but she is so boring, and it is extremely hard to pay attention to her in class. She tries to teach and honestly does an ok job if you can stay attentive. Does allow a cheat sheet at least. Just do yourself a favor: stay away from taking her class, or just take Data 110 if you're just doing business.
NO COMMENT BUT...

these reviews are way too harsh... there are professors genuinely so much worse than her, and they still have a better rating. it seemed like she struggled a lot with anxiety and felt disorganized often times, but she was passionate and tried her best. her exams were very hard, as the other comments suggest, but it was not anything impossible.
Does not curve. Final exam was extremely hard.

GOOD PROFESSOR. She's good at teaching. I understood everything. Don't skip class and pay attention. You will be fine. Tests were pretty light, similar to practice tests. She's really kind. Don't be scared to take her class. Just study and review. There's too much hate on Bergland.

Pros: passionate, partial credit on exams (68% of course grade), final replaces lowest exam, exam format fair (potential +4% bonuses), active on Piazza, awesome in office hours, encourages participation
Cons: very slow to return grades, homework is super lengthy, seeks pity from students, assigns unnecessary group work, not a confident lecturer

Dr. Bergland is genuinely passionate about Statistics, and she knows her stuff. However, her lectures were not very engaging (had to self-teach outside of class) and practice questions were not effectively integrated into the class. She is available and helpful via office hours. Need to be VERY self-motivated. Definitely sit up front (no mic.)

DO NOT TAKE STOR 155 WITH HER. The midterms were way too hard and the questions cannot be completed in the allotted exam time. Even after students gave her feedback on the midterms, she still made the final insanely long and tough. She also refused to curve the final exam or our final grades when most of the class was in the 50-60% range.

Worst professor i've ever had at UNC. She literally walked into exams with them messed up everytime. She takes forever to grade. Isn't good at teaching the material to students. Didn't keep her word on credit with exams either. I understand it was her first year teaching but even a TA could have done better with the class. Nice lady but  wow.

Rated her 2 (not 1) bc she does genuinely have a passion and it shows in her good lectures. HOWEVER, she is not meant to be a professor. Harsh/rigid grading and closed-note tests aren't sensible for a coding class, and tests (that she made) not graded for 1-2 months. She tries to do too much then penalizes the students when she finds out she can't.

She is nice and extremely accessible. However, she often made topics more complicated than they were, failed to explain them in class (better explanations in office hours), and graded extremely slowly. We didn't have an accurate final grade until a few days ago. The 2 midterms did have revisions and homework is 28% of your grade.
Final was taken a week ago and we are still missing a homework grade from October and the final exam grade. So frustrating.

Dr. Jia is genuinely the sweetest guy of all time. I took this class as my statistics credit for pre-business and learned little to no statistics because most of the class is coding on Python. I had never coded before and hate coding but he always said to use AI for help. Him and the TAs were always super responsive, easy to reach, and helpful.

AWESOME, gem of a human being. he is perfect in every way. most understanding, accommodating professor/teacher i have ever had. he wants you to succeed and provides many resources to do so. practice exams are very helpful, homeworks and labs are tedious though. he is so caring about all of his students, and wants the best for all. funny too
he's an amazing teacher and genuinely cares about his students and their success.

Dr. Jia is the sweetest! He's a super caring person that just wants you to succeed. Labs, homework, and exams were all easy, and he set aside time for review sessions which really helped. The final was a group project/poster presentation. Lectures were a bit confusing, but all slides were posted and Dr. Jia was always willing to clarify or meet.

Dr. Jia was awesome! Attendance isn't exactly necessary, but his lectures are straightforward and always posted. Exams are extremely easy if you review, which he sets aside time for. Labs are easy, but homework will take a lot of time. Grading criteria for everything are extremely detailed. Super nice guy overall, take DATA110 with him!!

Dr. Jia was an incredible teacher and extremely generous with his grading. All it takes to succeed in this class is showing up, listening to lectures (all the slides are posted anyways), and doing the practice exams. A- class average on exams all three exams. HWs were pretty challenging, especially if you left them to the last day.

Dr. Jia is a great professor that genuinely cares about his students! While assignments are relatively straightforward, the homework can be difficult, so it is important to give yourself time. He is very accessible outside of class and is very responsive to emails. He truly wants the best for his students and is very patient!

Jia is a really nice professor who really wants you to succeed. There are three tests and a group final project, as well as homework and weekly recitation labs. There's an exam review before all exams, and they're super helpful. Homework in Data 110 can be really challenging, so be prepared for that. Drops 1 lab and HW, extra credit for attendance!

Dr. Jia is the best! He is very patient and wants you do to well. The homework assignments can be a bit much at times, but the exams and labs are extremely straightforward. Would definitely recommend!
Super sweet and genuinely wants you to get an A! Tests are fairly easy and he will review them the class prior.
The good thing of taking this class is that you will never feel any other class (at the undergrad level) hard. Still, Dr. Seeger is very patient and willing to help.

Dr. Seeger is a sweet guy. Lectures were slow and a little boring (though I'd also learned most of the basics in previous courses), but Dr. Seeger explains things thoroughly and clearly. Homeworks weren't bad. Midterms were a joke, and the final wasn't too hard—though it was significantly harder than the midterms and caught some people off guard.

I really loved Professor Seeger! He understandably explains difficult math concepts and is very patient and helpful if you talk to him one-on-one. Discrete math is a very difficult course, but I really feel like with Seeger I learned so much and understood the concepts well. Exams were hard, but they are also graded extremely fairly.

Professor Seeger was very kind and loved to talk about his pet bunnies. Attendance was not required and lecture slides with notes were posted after class. Big weekly homeworks from the textbook but reasonable grading.

The class proceeds at a slow and friendly pace. It's fine to take this class in your freshman or sophomore year if you meet the prerequisites. There are no mathematically difficult parts. The homework is very heavy. All lecture content is immediately available online, which is great for review.

Professor Seeger spends a good amount of time on each topic for this class and has notes provided for each lecture. The textbook is a good resource and all the homework comes from that. Make sure you stay along with the class and understand the material. Final wasn't as hard as midterms and it replaces lowest midterm, so that's good.

Prof Seeger clearly wants his students to succeed, but this class is a little weird. I liked the class's overall layout, but I wish we had longer than 15 minutes for the quizzes. Final was super generous compared to midterms and quizzes, so that's a plus!

Professor Seeger is so sweet and genuinely cares about his students. Very clear lectures and explanations but could get boring at times. Provides clear and accomodating explanations in office hours and really make sures you understand the material. Would love to take him again.

Professor Seeger is very kind and genuinely cares about his students. I do not, however, believe that he should have taught this class. Discrete, as a whole, is very difficult and Seeger understood that, but he was not good at teaching the material. Instead, he only showed examples which made doing others confusing. Very kind and chill guy tho.

Mr. Fuchs is a good band director but sometimes has lapses in memory or makes comments during instruction which are outdated and mildly uncomfortable. The most frustrating part of working with Mr. Fuchs is when he we are learning drill and he forgets the instruction he told you five minutes ago or changes it between every rep.
He's great. Sometimes comes off a little rude but I promise he means well

Decent band director. He may have high expectations at times or come off as stern, but he just wants the best for everyone. Show up to everything or communicate clearly for absences and you'll get an easy A.

Dr. Scott is an incredible professor. For anyone considering the Athletic Bands, working with Dr. Scott is a great experience. She is very caring of her students and makes an effort to get to know everyone regardless of their involvement with the music department. Absolutely would take again.

Dr.Scott is actually the GOAT!  She is extremely caring and very student-oriented, it is clear that she only wants the best for her students.  I went through something terrible the last semester that I was with her and she showed me nothing but grace and kindness.  Cannot recommend her enough!

I had Dr Scott for both marching/pep band and symphony band, and I loved her for both. She really cares about her students and is constantly asking for feedback. She always had a plan for rehearsal so we knew what to expect as well.

Dr. Scott is a kind woman who wants the best from everyone. She loves what she's doing, and it shows. Everyone in band with her has something good to say, and rehearsal is a safe place no matter where you come from.

Dr. Scott is an amazing professor! Her rehearsals are super efficient, and cover important stuff very well. She is clearly very passionate about music and I am super excited to take more classes with her as time allows it in the coming years.
A little obsessed with Taylor Swift. But super kind, motivating, and when she pushed you to do more, she always tells you how great you are doing after. Literally love her.

Dr. Scott has elevated the entire music department since her arrival and I truly can not say enough good things about her. She is very caring and good at her job, plain and simple. No matter the class, if you have the opportunity to learn from her TAKE IT. You will not regret it.

Dr. Scott is the best! Her rehearsals are always so efficient, and we get a lot done with little time. She's very understanding towards her students, extremely nice, and clearly passionate about what she does. I think our band has gotten better as a result of her direction.

I'm a singer and this version of teaching music theory I think appeals to Dr. Neal's skillset so much more. I learned so much in this class and Dr. Neal had such enthusiasm and excitement to teach every student. I did horribly for most of the sem, but going to office hours and showing improvement and effort earned me my A.

Professor Neal's class had unclear assignment instructions and grading. While enthusiastic, her lectures lacked substance. However, unstuckstudy was a helpful study tool to prepare for the vague assessments.

For context, I am a published songwriter. The class follows a model-practice structure by lecturing material and having you go home and write a song using those tools. The class covers song elements, song structures like blues and AABA, Nashville numbers, figurative language, and rhyme. If you can't play an instrument, you will likely struggle.

One of the three most narcissistic faculty at UNC, through and through. Suffers from insecurity and fear of being 'found out.'

Tread lightly, retribution is her middle name. Avoid and you won't regret the time lost.
she likes taylor swift a lot...somebody who studied and teaches music...i think that's all I need to say

Professor is very knowledgable but could be unhelpful at times. The structure of the class was lecture heavy and didn't facilitate music making. Felt like class content could be covered more briefly and more emphasis put on listening and making music. Poor at giving feedback. Overall it just had so much potential that it didn't live up to.

Assignment instructions were impossible to understand (felt like she just threw a bunch of buzz words in there) and her grading made no sense on the papers. Encouraged us to go into more detail, but had a very low word count. Condescending attitude, and her lectures were boring. Do not take!!

The three assignments were poorly written and it was unclear what she wanted. She also chastised the class for not making concise arguments and then proceeded to lecture about Elvis for 75 minutes without making a single substantial point. All triple I classes seem bad, but avoiding Professor Neal is in your best interest.

Every assignment she made was so vaguely worded that you had no idea how to prepare for it or what was expected of you. She made compelling arguments about the music and encouraged interesting analyses but if you don't care dig deep into music then don't take IDST 121. A huge chunk of southern music was simply left out for no good reason as well.

Professor Neal is unlike any other professor I've had at UNC. She is VERY enthusiastic about the subject matter which can take a while to get used to, but I learned the most from her compared to the other instructors and she made going to class fun and interesting. IDK what her music theory classes are like, but I liked her in my Triple-I.

Unclear grading criteria. Gave very low word count and was then upset that we didn't go into more detail. Lectures consisted of obsessing over Elvis instead of making any actual arguments. Very condescending. Avoid if possible.

Professor Neal gets a bad rep because music theory isn't an easy subject, but she is an amazing lecturer.  She's extremely knowledgeable about the subject and she always comes prepared in order to make the lecture fun and engaging.

This professor WILL double down on you for participation and attendance no matter what your circumstances. Just make sure to go to class and talk. It's easy to get on her bad side. Knowledgeable but condescending when she speaks to students, and is definitely on a power trip.

I truly don't understand the negative reviews. If you don't enjoy music theory, then Neal's strong enthusiasm might drive you away a bit, but she is a great professor nonetheless. Incredibly dedicated to teaching and helping students. I wish I could have her for Theory III.
Would not recommend.

Music theory courses are going to be difficult no matter the professor, but Joce Neal does nothing to make it easier for students to learn. Homework is fair but the midterms and finals are unnecessarily difficult and are graded ridiculously. I learned so much from this course, but the final was graded so that no matter how much you studied you fail

The only reason I'm taking MUSC 132 next semester is to sit in her class again. She plans her lectures well, so all the theatrical timing that belongs in education is there. If you're new to music theory, you might have a hard time, but she's incredibly helpful in office hours and if you sit up front and engage then you can't help but learn.

I get why people say she's a bit intimidating, but she explains everything in a very clear and helpful way. The one time I went in for office hours for the final project, she was super helpful and went above and beyond my initial questions and made the whole project leagues better. You definitely want some music knowledge going into it, though.

Absolutely terrible. She is an okay person but just makes music theory much harder and more complex than it ever should be. The workload is manageable but honestly, unless you want to be a professional musician or an educator, do not even waste your time.

This is a 5-star prof if there ever existed one. Excellent lectures, fair exams and workload, great pacing, quick email response time, well-organized, etc. Very knowledgeable/passionate about theory and super friendly/helpful during office hours. A skosh intimidating and a little tough on grading, but she still makes an A 100% doable. She's a gem.

She's really sweet and enthusiastic, but unless you're really passionate about music, the lecture is a bore. You get to listen to interesting music though. I didn't get much out of the lectures, yet I still did fine on the assignments. A lot is group work and the essays aren't hard. Just do your work, and you should be fine.

Professor André is a caring and passionate professor that makes every student feel welcome regardless of their background or musical knowledge. There are readings, but you can usually get away with not reading them. In class, you will either be listening to music, discussing a reading, or listening to André lecture. The class is relaxing too!

Professor André is amazing! She is so passionate about drama and cares about every student in the class. She truly wanna make the class more than a class, forming a sense of community, so there would be many group works. Feedback on each assignment is also detailed and personalized. Try this class no matter you are good at music or not!!

Naomi is an angel! She is passionate about the subject she teaches and so caring for her students! She wants everyone to succeed and encourages collaboration and discussion in the classroom. There are minimal assignments that are graded harshly, so if you don't know music at all, it may be kinda difficult, but she is so helpful and understanding!

Dr. André is a great professor and she is very knowledgable. There are only 3 assignments, and they are all papers. They are about 2 pages either double/single spaced. The class is very lecture heaver, but there are a few guest speakers. This class is super easy and it's a focus capacity.

Dr. Andre is an amazing professor - she cares about all of her students very deeply and strives to make the class interesting for all. She's also such a talented and knowledgable musician, and it was incredible being able to learn from someone like her. Even though MUSC 120 itself wasn't my favorite class overall, Dr. Andre made it so much better!

Dr. Andre was so amazing, she was so sweet and personal. The class was a first year seminar so students are encouraged to participate however joining into the conversations were not difficult at all. There are group projects but they are easy. She assigned readings, however I got away with not doing them. Be prepared to talk A LOT about opera.

Dr. Andre was an amazing professor with not only an endless amount of knowledge about the class, but her passion and genuine excitement about the subjects she teaches will make you feel inspired about the content. She is an easy grader, gives really helpful criticism and feedback, and has the most caring personality. Best class in my schedule.

Dull. She's sweet and caring as can be but boy is this class a snooze (literally!) So little of the material covered in lecture is necessary for the assignments, it just becomes hard to care. Do the assignments and you'll get an A though!

She is kind and does genuinely care about each of her students, she is not the best lecturer in my opinion. She tends to get off topic very easily and rambles about a lot of things. There is a very vague outline for the actual class so she kind of gets to do whatever she wants, so be prepared for a lot of Opera. She grades participation harshly.

Dr. Andre is one of the most caring professors at UNC. She gives great feedback on your writing, her deadlines are flexible, and she assigns most work in groups. She has a lot of control over the curriculum and lectures a lot about opera but it's actually interesting since that's her area of expertise. Would highly recommend taking her.

Dr. Feldman is such a caring professor and always makes the class fun! This is one of the classes that I felt like I really left with a good community of friends, and I felt like the professor really played a big role in that. He also gives lots of feedback, is clear in his expectations for the course, and class is always interesting!

Main focus of class is a volunteer project you do with an organization, and we do two presentations on it as well as a final paper. We have minor assignments throughout the course as well. Class is heavily discussion based and Dr Feldman is very good at facilitating conversation and asking questions. He is funny and interesting, class was fun.

Dr. Feldman is the best. If you go to UNC and are serious about a wind instrument or percussion, you gotta do wind ensemble with him at least once before you graduate. He picks some hard stuff fall semester but spring is a lot more challenging (judging off last spring especially). It's worth it every step of the way.

Took this for my EE credit. The course itself was great with interesting content. The professor was so horribly inaccessible outside of class that it made me absolutely hate attending. Responses would take 5-8 business days even with follow-ups and prompting after class. Easy A, but terrible professor. He did not seem to care.

Class itself is just fine - the professor however was very passive aggressive and unresponsive to feedback. I found it difficult to communicate any issues or struggles I had throughout the semester with her. Do not recommend taking her.

Dr. Bohlman clearly has a passion and interest in her lectures. She looks forward to participation, reading over the short assignments, and gives great feedback on the midterm. She takes students' workloads into account when scheduling her big deadlines/midterm, clearly showing empathy for her students.

Prof. Bohlman's passion for music is evident taking this class and she really just wants students to find their musical passions. The two papers require a lot of thought, though the final project I felt was easier than these papers. This course will challenge you to think abstractly and let go of your preconceived notions about music.

Andrea is very knowledgeable in her subject areas. That being said, I had no interest in basically all of what she had to teach about (which is maybe more the music department's fault than hers), but it felt like a high school class where it was just fluff that had no impact on what I am going to be doing in my professional career.

I beg the UNC Music department to do away with this new curriculum. Dr. Bohlman was fantastic and clear but the material she was given to work with was nearly nonexistent. This course caused multiple people to DROP the music major because they have decided to stop teaching anything useful. The dumbing down of the music major at UNC is sad to see.

The main issue with this course was the course itself, not the professor. Bohlman is a zealous, involved professor who will help you with anything-- academic or personal. That said, I didn't learn a lot in this course. The lectures tended to be all over the place and slightly unrelated to each other. Homework is not required, tho assigned.

Andrea is alright; no more, no less. Similar to my experience with her MUSC 120, we learned absolute nonsense the whole semester. We basically studied music through unguided interpretation. Andrea has a knack for calling on students but not really caring for their responses & for giving unclear essay criteria, but overall this class is an easy A.

Andrea is fantastic. I would happily take another class with her. I would also give her a 5 if this class wasn't pure fluff. This is more beneficial than music history? The curriculum is disjointed nonsense and the final project was a show and tell of everyone's musical interests. I think music conservatories would laugh if they observed MUSC270.

Andrea is great, I've loved her in every class I've taken with her. Unsure about the other review for 270 -- this class was totally fair and each assignment's instructions took you through baby steps to complete. Lectures were diverse and required critical thinking. Being the first semester of this course, some bumps in the road were to be expected

Course was very badly structured and not well taught. Assignments lacked guidelines and grading was tough considering how vague the instructions were. Lectures were incredibly tedious on topics that were totally unrelated. Bohlman was completely useless when you asked for help, and gave feedback that resulted in bad grades. Do not take.

Music 120 was an interesting class to be sure, it would be hard for me to summarize exactly what we learned as it was a bit all over the place. Lacking in structure. HOWEVER Professor Bohlman was fantastic. She took the time to be personable, tried to get to know each of her students and was open to differing opinions.

MUSC 120 was a frustratingly disorganized class but this was much more due to the curriculum than the instructor-- Bohlman did her best to teach us useful material and some classes were very enjoyable. Participate & put some time into bigger assignments and you can get an A. Take advantage of her office hours to get to know her outside of class!

Very caring and understanding professor. The course structure felt a bit disorganized and we only found out we were getting a final 2 weeks before the final, but it is very easy to get an A in this class. It is genuinely challenging not to get an A if you show up and hand in all the work.
She is super nice and the class is very though provoking. Class is all about participation in class discussions and presentations. She is super understanding and just wants to see everyone succeed.
I had a wonderful time in this course due in no small part to Professor Rivers. She is very passionate about the material covered in class which creates a great learning environment.
I genuinely loved her class and I am literally going to find any class that fits my degree just so I can take a course with her again. My favorite professor at Carolina.

She is my favorite professor I've ever had at UNC, she's so incredibly passionate and cares more about her students actually gaining knowledge and understanding of the natural world, than she does about numerical grades. She's the type of professor every student wants to have. No matter how much you put in you will leave a smarter person

Professor Rivers teaches a very interesting course. I learned a lot about Africa and found myself wanting to learn more outside of class. There are 2 major projects, 2 quizzes, and various in class activities. My TA was very fair on grading, as was Professor Rivers. This course is very informative and interesting, and I'd 100% recommend taking it.

Professor Rivers is my favorite professor I have had during my time at UNC. She is so kind and passionate about what she teaches- and though I am not a GEOG major, I gleaned so much from this class that will prove valuable for life. If you have the chance to take GEOG 294, do so because it is an incredible, rewarding experience.

Professor Rivers is a great teacher and is very passionate about her work. The class is easy, graded by short papers, simple in-class assignments, 3 main projects, and 3 presentations. Light grading, simple content, and you get good feedback on everything you submit. Mandatory attendance, and expect some lecture and presentation days to be boring.
Best teacher. I wish I could take this class again.

Professor Rivers is great, you can tell she cares about her students and what she's teaching them! She wants to make a difference in our lives. The readings are super interesting and very meaningful. There are two big projects that you can use a lot of creativity for and I would definitely recommend taking a class with her if you can!

She knows her stuff, and her lectures are fantastic in inspiring critical thinking about Africa! Group project was a bit of work, but it's graded individually and has a fun creative component at the end. Several papers graded easily and three memory quizzes take a bit of studying for! Attendance is graded harshly BTW. Shout out to the amazing TA!

Professor Rivers is a great teacher who makes it very clear what she expects on every assignment. There are two papers, two group projects, and a few short assignments. There is reading for every class but you do not really need to do it. Overall very easy class for a gen ed.

SO, SO passionate about what she teaches, I loved this class as it really gave me a profound perspective! Some assignments are more free-write since she asks what/how much we know about a topic and then to reflect on it. Big group project for a lot of pts but it was graded individually! 3 quizzes-basically straight from the study guide.

She is the best professor I've had! She's very respectful and the class was interesting and engaging. I would encourage anyone to take this class! She's a very kind person, and the work was minimal and easy. A few projects, short essays, and readings were the only homework. Class was very discussion based. 100% recommend her and this class!

I LOVE PROF NDAKILO. I took her for GEOG 294 and I LOVED IT. Learned so much, had amazing conversations, and VERY minimal outside work aside from some interesting readings (that weren't super long). If you have the chance take this class!!

This class was very inspiring and changed my perspective for the better. Prof. Ndaliko is kind, accessible, and her first hand experiences were extremely valuable to learn about in relation to the lecture material. The assignments and readings were very straightforward and interesting. You will definitely walk away from this class a better person!

One of the most valuable classes I have taken at UNC, Professor Ndaliko is wonderful and her first-hand experiences intertwined into the course are great. The three quizzes require some dedicated studying, and there is weekly reading for the first 3/4s of the class. A final group project rather than a final exam.

GEOG 480 has been hands down the most meaningful course I have taken at UNC so far.
