The theory is dense, but Ndaliko's class structure, projects, and thought exercises encourage a thorough understanding of how systems of violence work by finding intersections within our own lived experience. This class was like therapy for me :,)

He doesn't seem to understand college students, but very interested in a forum for his life stories. He's a nice guy, might be fun over coffee, but the grading is very arbitrary, his lectures are completely focused on him, there's no rubric or understanding of grading or expectations.  Repetitive. Boring.

Worst professor I have had at UNC, grading had no rubrics and is entirely opinion based. As someone who had perfect attendance I would recommend this class to no one. All comments were contradicting on assignments for the same venture and lectures consisted of ramblings. The only thing I learned was patience. This was a joke of the shufford program

Avoid this shuford track course and take a different one. Grading feels arbitrary and based on personal biases. The entire class is a group project and there isn't a peer review at the end. Attendance is 100% mandatory and there are no excuses. 

The lectures were boring, random, and useless. Find another class.

I recommend this class to no one. He is extremely disorganized and lectures are boring and repetitive. I genuinely can say that I did not learn a single thing in this class- coming from someone who attends every class. His grading is random and I found myself worrying about my grade in this class more than I do in my upper level Economics courses.

I wanted to give the benefit of the doubt and took the class even after hearing all the horrible stories and that was a mistake. He makes no sense, grades on nothing but what he's feeling that day and doesn't teach anything. He made many incredibly belittling comments directly to me multiple times no matter what I did. Save yourself honestly.
Great class. Needs some direction but overall I truly enjoyed it
He gives great lectures, offers a lot of great anecdotal stuff. A little disorganized, but overall a class I really enjoyed and learned a lot from.

He is a nice guy but he doesn't know how to teach. All of his classes are just the same conversations over and over again where he only listens to students if they tell him exactly what he wants to hear. It is an easy class to do well in if you use all the buzzwords he want you to in your assignments but I don't think I learned anything at all.

I feel SO BAD rating him low because he seems passionate about teaching. BUT I don't recommend this course AT ALL. Its SO unorganized, grading isn't clear, & a semester long group project, a pain. Class convos are random & boring, you will get called on a lot. Engage in hopes of getting an A. You'll be left confused & aggravated. Save yourself pls.
He's the most incompetent educator I've ever had. Nice guy so I feel bad but he has no idea what he's talking about, and he's guessing with your grade.

The number 1 worst professor I have been taught by. Classes are completely unproductive, his grading is completely arbitrary. You can literally not do anything about your grade. He will give you whatever he wants to give you. His explanations will never make sense, and eventually you just realize hes not very smart, but tries to seem like he is.

The professor talks about his life stories, which are interesting. But that life story is supposed to be how our assignments are written. No clear grading criteria. He claims there are no right and wrong answers, but at the same time the grading we received tells us a different story. He should feel lucky RMP limits ratings to 350 since I have more

Still not really sure what I learned and what he graded on. Every class he would just tell us random stories and give us assignments to do in our groups. Then he would grade super tough and it oftentimes made no sense.

MUSC 150, not MUSC 89 THE GOAT, please take at least one class with him!!!! He is really really kind, knowledgeable, and an amazing human being! Any class you take with him will be very chill, but also informative and DEF worth the time!

MUSC 150: Dr. Livingston is a great professor and I would recommend him to anyone! He is very clearly passionate about the subject matter and is an excellent instructor. One of my favorite classes I've taken at UNC.
Not MUSC 89, but MUSC 150 Intro to Hip Hop is the best class I've taken at UNC. So chill but I have learned a lot from the class. He's great and I would highly recommend you take it for FC-AESTH
Super chill guy and very cool -he's a rapper and poet. He really cares about his students and its truly a free class
Not sure if IDST 101 can even be hard, but Dr. Livingston was such a nice professor. You can tell he loves his job.

He is very kind and you can tell he loves his jobs and students. Grading criteria was unclear at some points so points would be deducted by surprised. He was not the most accessible by email, but you shouldn't need to contact him if you submit assignments and go to class.
Had for college thriving - super sweet and open. Definitely wants to know all of his students. Highly recommend!

Dr. Livingston is one of if not the best professor I will ever have. He is truly a great guy and is super caring for everyone that he teaches. He will talk with you after class about topics that you are interested in and genuinely wants to help in any way he can.

I LOVE Professor Livingston!! The best guy, both inside and outside the classroom. I don't think you can choose who you get for college thriving, but if you get him, thank your lucky stars—the nicest, most caring guy ever who truly wants you to succeed. I genuinely feel better about myself every time I leave that class.
Hes awesome everyone should take a class of his

He has lots of knowledge on hip-hop and the history around higher education. His class is very engaging and fun. It took me out of my comfort zone but it was probably the best class I have ever taken.

Dr. Livingston is the most down to earth, kind hearted, selfless professor there is. He was my first ever professor and genuinely the best one I think I will have. Very clear grading scale, a lot of emphasis on growth, and very understanding of situations students have outside the classroom.

Genuinely the most down to earth kind hearted professor I've ever had. He is so obviously caring about his students and really helped us be successful throughout the tough times of freshman year. The man never stops smiling and it's contagious, I didn't think IDST 101 would actually help me thrive in college but it really did with him.

AMAZING prof for idst101, super cool guy, let me miss class for a family emergency and was SO kind about it. He won't cold call on you, he is incredibly respectful and genuinely an interesting person. IDST 101 is a drag of a class, but he makes it lowkey kind of fun.
Dr. Martin is just the GOAT and I would take a million classes with her.
I love Dr. Martin so much! Her class was a breath of fresh air and she is kind and welcoming to singers of all talent levels! Can't wait to take more classes with her.

Fantastic professor. She is no-nonsense but also extremely caring and encouraging. It's hard getting out of your shell and singing in front of everybody, but she makes it a lot easier. I will say, it's a decent amount of energy for only 1 credit, but it's such a fun class.

This class has a lot of homework and one midterm as well as a final exam; they are both on the lockdown response browser, and the grading is very nice, because you automatically get 25% for one of the essays out of the 3; you choose 2. However, Professor Bri has high expectations and isn't very understanding when it comes to work questions.

I hated this class. Bri was mean to all of us, spoke condescendingly, and didn't seem like she wanted us there, and tbh we didn't want to be there either. Just not a fun class with her. TAs are what determine your grade, and rubrics were not clear, with some TAs being "oh let me text her and back to you."

She made this class a snooze fest. Every lecture took a year off my life. Redeeming quality: you don't need to go to class at all. Class only helps with the midterm and final which we're free. There were 4 papers, had nothing to do with the lecture, and your grade solely depended on which TA you got. Regardless should be an easy A

I went to maybe 5 lectures the whole semester, so if you want a class you can skip this is it. However, there are about 5 major assignments, and the TAs seem to grade more harshly as the semester goes on. midterm and exam are EXTREMLY easy and identical to the study guide, which is amazing (I "studied" 2 days before both and got a 96 and 97)
Professor Nave really tried to make the class engaging, the assignments just didn't do a great job of supplementing learning within the class.

Pretty boring, especially considering that its a jazz class. not sure how that happened. feels like she doesn't like students or something like that. its an easy A but was probably a waste of money to take. maybe went to 3 classes total throughout the semester.

This class is so buns holy. Every lecture is so boring and I now hate jazz which I didn't know was possible. The TAs are on a power trip taxing you for stuff for the love of the game, and the assignments take so long and don't even correlate to the class lectures. All in all, please avoid this teacher, prob would've been a fun class without her.

Nave was okay, lecture was boring. Getting a good TA was gambling, only Mick A. knew what they were doing. I lost all interest in this class due to the constant passive aggressiveness from a certain TA and how all assignments were just busy work. Don't take this class.

Briana is very knowledgeable on this subject, but this is a lecture-heavy course. I enjoyed the class because of how passionate she is about the topic. I will say that some of the assignments seemed like busywork, and your grade depends on the TA you get. Mick Anderson is amazing and was the only one who provided feedback. I enjoyed this class!
Briana Nave was not the best teacher. Very condescending and didn't really enjoy going to the lecture. Grade is really dependent on the TA. If you get Mick Anderson, you are in good hands.

Many of the assignments she created for the class felt unfair and far too long for what should be required of an intro to jazz course. Nave often gave off a vibe that she feels she is better than you simply because she is pursuing a PhD. Unfortunately I am limited by space on this site, but in short: don't take her class.

Interesting material and class. Professor is knowledgeable, kind personally and clearly cares, but low-energy for a jazz course. Lectures solid but repetitive. Interesting perspectives and engaging guest speakers. Assignments felt overly long and not always relevant. TAs were bad except for Mick A. Learned a lot about jazz culture and history.

Briana very obviously cares about what she is teaching, and I would say the content was engaging. As someone who knew next to nothing about jazz culture and history going into this class, I can say I am pretty knowledgeable now. Some assignments seemed like busywork, but the content of them was interesting. Very TA dependent, some grades confusing.

She clearly knows what she's talking about and puts together decent lectures. Buuuuuuuuut, class is quite boring, I'm not too sure she likes students, and you never know what you're gonna get with the grading.

Briana is really passionate about jazz, but the class itself is pretty challenging. You have to put a good amount of effort into the papers if you want an A, and the last assignment took way longer than expected. The exams weren't too bad, though. Memorize a few paragraphs, and you're good.
Acted like we don't know how to write and made us use only the UNC library and JSTOR resources for our Lesson Plan assignment. Effectively doubles our research and wastes your precious hours.
Made jazz so boring. Assignments were too long and didn't feel a value add. TAs were random with grading.

I signed up for the class because it was supposed to be taught by my guy Stephen Anderson, and I got stuck with a teacher who makes jazz so boring. Lectures suck and she somehow makes learning jazz terrible, and I grew up playing in a jazz band. The TAs other than the homie Mick are all doing too much, and every assignment makes me tweak crazily.
Professor boring. Terrible assignments that don't add to the course. Horribly rude TA's.

Absolute waste of time and energy. The grading in this class is a joke. The TAs themself don't even know what they're doing. They take off points for things that are never mentioned in the rubric for assignments. Ms. Nave speaks to her students condescendingly as if undergraduates don't know what they're doing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
Pablo is absolutely the best professor! Super awesome and so gifted!

The classes were not organized very well. His feedback on assignments was often limited to only 2 words. Assignments should have been more hands on instead of watching him read off a doc for an hour. Obvious this is just a paycheck for him, but an easy grader.

Pablo is an incredible teacher. I took this class fall of 2024, and he canceled class a lot - this has since changed in later classes. For the final project, we recorded and mixed a live performance, and we only had 2 analysis papers and 2 music projects, plus 2 quizzes. He takes a while to return grades but pushing back our due dates as a 'sorry'.

Professor Vega is extremely knowledgable. can't really teach. I could have learned so much from him except that we barely got through any material. Cancelled class all the time, didn't grade anything till the last week, but did give feedback on assignments.

Pablo was super nice and the class work was not super hard. There was an online quiz that i missed as I had work and it brought my grade down to a B- from and A. I was not allowed to take it with a penalty or anything, just lost the points. This was frustrating as the class was not supposed to hurt my gpa and inevitably did.

Pablo is awesome. He is a great teacher and will work with you personally on anything you have trouble with. He is incredibly expereienced in the field of mixing and is great at passing that knoweldge on to others. There are two projects you have to work on and some quizzes that he gives you a study guide for.

Hands down the best professor at UNC. He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate. He's super accessible if you need help and he truly cares about his students and their well-being. Best professor I've ever had, and the best in the music department. If you want to learn the ins and outs of music and production, the best possible way is thru Vega!

Professor Vega was an awesome resource in further developing my skills in music production. His class was mainly project focused which was perfect for a class of this type. Professor Vega was always willing to help give advice on personal projects and class projects and has tremendous industry experience himself. Field trip was my favorite part!

Dr. Figueroa is clearly knowledgeable, but the class focused almost entirely on musical ethnographies rather than music theory or history. Most classes involved discussing readings in a lecture of about 100 students. There were only four graded items (midterm, final, and two projects). The class is easy overall, but I found it very boring.

The class and professor were extremely easy, and earning an A required minimal effort. However, the material itself was very boring, which made attending class feel unnecessary and frustrating, but attendance was mandatory and graded. The readings were not required to succeed, and I did not feel that I learned anything meaningful from the course.

easiest class ever, but since it isn't fulfilling any requirements for me and it wasn't that engaging it really felt tedious to show up. Focuses on readings during lectures, but doesn't go that far in depth to ever feel obligated to read them. There were a few interesting lectures, but those were a minority for sure.

Like many of the other musicology classes, this class was loosely defined as a concept. Dr. Figueroa didn't seem particularly interested in reading our work or giving us feedback, and a lot of our time was wasted with him trying to figure out what to do. I'm almost sure that he didn't read our final papers before grading them.

Great professor. Didn't take attendance but syllabus mentions participation so still go to class. Very supportive during the research process and wants you to succeed. I wish he would have given more feedback throughout the semester since his feedback was super helpful. The final paper is super manageable if you make steady progress on it.

Dr. Figueroa is wonderful and very smart. If you genuinely care about music, this class is great. However, if you are taking this for the requirement, you must show up. Attendance is the biggest thing in the course. I loved it, but I can see how someone who doesn't have good attendance would not be able to pass the course.

Figueroa is caring and knows a lot, however he made attendance mandatory for a class where nothing in class actually contributed. Whole class is based around writing one paper, and yet I barely got feedback through the drafting process. Easy A if you complete assignments, not a whole lot of work on a day to day.

Dr. Figueroa is very nice and caring, but the class time itself was often wasted in "writing workshops" or empty discussions on how to write or edit a paper. Late & minimal feedback & no clear assignment instructions. I enjoyed researching a unique topic, and I did learn, but mostly from my own research rather than from the professor. Easy grader.

Overall a kind and respectful professor. However the course was a learning void: empty Canvas modules or a single link, vague paper instructions with no rubric, and an absent professor during "writing workshops". Feedback arrived at least a month late, assignment extensions were frequent, and learning was nonexistent. Wouldn't recommend this course

Prof. Figueroa is a super kind and encouraging professor. The content of this class is kind of difficult, but he grades very easily as long as you are willing to try. Very participation heavy, but not like you have to volunteer every class. Great professor and class!

Professor Figueroa is the best professor I have had at UNC. He is so obviously passionate about what he teaches and he really instills that passion in his students. The assignments are relatively easy but are relevant to the material and are truly engaging. Absolute BEST choice for VP credit (or just for fun and learning).

Professor Figueroa is one of the best professors I have had. Lectures are interesting with cool music being played and just 5 projects for the class that basically everyone did well in. There is no better option for a VP credit at all.

Great professor and TAs; Very easy class and interesting; there are low stakes quizzes each week in recitation and 5 projects; people often don't participate in class which makes me feel bad since Prof Fig is awesome and clearly excited about the topics so pls participate if you can!

Probably one of the easiest classes you could take. Super nice guy and the TA I had graded extremely easily and was also super nice. Main assignments are 5 projects (1 per unit) which take no almost time and 3 out of 5 are group projects.
Take this for an Easy A/Gen eds. lots of group projects, attendance and readings aren't necessary. grade based upon five projects and a final paper which are graded by TA's.

Overall an interesting professor, knows a lot about course content, and invited a lot of super cool guest lecturers! Just pay attention to lectures, and use slides combined with your own knowledge on graded writings. Midterm, final, and journals are take-home open-note.

Katz brought guests to class ranging from US foreign ambassadors to musicians from across the world. Super cool class and a lot of interesting guest speakers There were no clear rubrics and I had to reach out to my TA to get feedback on my graded assignments. Also did not have a single grade in the gradebook until the last day of class.

Dr. Katz is the best!! This class offered so much insight into the criminal justice system. Class is a welcoming environment, and Dr. Katz is genuinely so kind and hilarious. Take this class if you can!!

Professor Katz is a very passionate professor! If you participate and do journals well, you're set! However, he's a tough grader, and your final grade is based on very few things. I would also argue that he was verbally indirectly politically biased, which I did not appreciate. We would have guests in class, which was an interesting experience!

Great teacher who cares about the student experience in his class. Great speakers were brought in, even if the actual lecture days were a little meandering. Grading felt a little bit arbitrary sometimes, with any grade for a fully and well completed assignment falling between a 95-96 for every. single. assignment. Hey. I'm not complaining though.

Dr. Katz is very passionate about this class. However, he spent a lot of time talking about his own experiences rather than teaching. He also initially said we'd have 3 quizzes, but he took those away, so we were only graded on 4 things: midterm, final, journal entries, and attendance. His grading criteria was not clear at all. I wouldn't take it.
Great proffesor and super kind and compassionate towards students. Covered so many cool topics and brought in speakers. Decent bit of writing but nothing crazy. Great class for FC-AESTHETIC

A IS A 94 AND I GOT A 93 THINKING IT WAS AN A WHICH PMO but I guess I should've seen this coming...make sure to do your diary entries early/on time because he TOOK OFF POINTS FOR SUBMITTING THE DIARY ENTRIES LATE WHEN HE SAID HE DIDN'T CARE AND IT WAS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN AN A AND A-. Great class though - show up half the time and it's an A.

Very nice and passionate prof. Cares about student's opinions in class discussion. Not a lot of substance or rigor to the material but it's always pretty interesting. Do your journals during lecture and the class will be a breeze.
What a king

Dr. Katz's section of MUSC120 was generally easy. Your final grade is dependent on a midterm and final exam, engagement points, journal entries, and an interview assignment. Attendance isn't required, but some journal entries are only accepted if completed during the lecture. Grading wasn't stringent but was vague (points removed, no explanation).

Easy, but sometimes boring, class that requires very little effort to get an A. Attendance isn't mandatory but missing too many "special classes" could make writing your journal entrees more difficult. Just show up to class and take notes on the big ideas and you should be fine on the exams and journals.

Generally the course and professor are good. No music background needed, but DO NOT take this class if you are not good at writing. Attendance is not mandatory and your grade mostly comes from essays. The grader is tough, sometimes criteria is vague and inconsistent, but a B or higher is still guaranteed.
Professor Katz was okay, I think it was TA's that made grading so much harder. The assignments were not hard just beware of the grading as in my opinion was inconsistent sometimes.

Review below for 291 sounds like student had personal issues with Prof. Grading scales, while not always super clear didn't seem arbitrary (+consider that this is a music class). He makes it pretty clear what he wants to see (no AI, use class readings in essays). Class can be boring sometimes, but artist performances & interviews were always great.
DO NOT TAKE. He is lowk annoying to listen to and he is so arbitrary in his grading. His class wasn't that substantive and he just talks and talks. Take a different class for you FC-AEST.

Katz is a kind and brilliant guy. This class was easy and grading was harsher than it should have been. Midterm and final are take-home essays, and most of your grade is based on those and 10 journal entries. Class had both interesting and boring moments. Attendance was not required so I went probably 1/2 times a week. Nice guy with some hard TAs.
Professor Katz was good, his lectures were entertaining but sometimes his deadlines were not clear so it was hard to keep track of due dates.

I didn't learn anything of substance in 272, but we had a couple of interesting lectures. Katz has you go to music events outside of class instead of counting attendance. Quite a bit of writing, but he's an easy grader on everything if you put in some effort. Overall, a cool person and a good lecturer. Would recommend for any musicology-type class.

Mark Katz is a really interesting professor. I really enjoyed the guest speakers who he brought in over the semester. There is often reading to do before classes but not a ton. The classes did end up feeling really long because they were a bit lecture heavy. No multiple choice tests. A few essays, big writing midterm and final. TAs make your grade.

Understanding of not being well versed in music theory. Lectures were heavy on deeply analyzing scores, which can be frustrating without thorough theory knowledge. However, your own compositions don't need to be strictly done. As long as you write as best you can, you'll be graded fairly. Very nice and understanding guy, and cares about all music.

Prof Weisert is knowledgeable about composing and gives great feedback on projects. Required individual meetings with Prof are very beneficial for your grade and for your learning. In class, teaches new concepts well and facilitates good discussion among students. Would take again.

Prof. Weisert is very knowledgeable and helpful with composition. I appreciated his individual meetings and his investment in every student's composition, regardless of skill level. A basic level of knowledge of instruments and music notation is required, but I would highly recommend this class to anyone in the music department.
Don't take this as a gen ed, especially if you have no music background. There is a lot of information and the study guide doesn't cover the material on the test.

a fairly easy seminar. be prepared to be creative as you draw out sound art concepts you make yourself. also beware that you have to present once in this class. the papers can be long and tedious but he isn't too harsh of a grader. the classes in the beginning of the semester were boring, but got better throughout! prof. weisert is a great person.

Passionate about the materials, but some lectures felt like they digressed into material that really just wasn't useful for music technology. It's good to know about music significant to the history, but it should be much more important to spend time on technology itself and how to use it. Course prepares you well for a fun final project in Logic.

Lee is the man. Took the internship class with him and it was extremely relaxed. I've also taken 239 with him and it was a pleasant experience. 100% take a class with him if you get the chance, he's super knowledgeable and seems like a great guy.

Prof Weisert is a great guy. A bit dry, sure, but he clearly cares about music and student's success. Class wasn't hard at all and was very informative - all in all a good experience. As long as you have a pulse you should be fine.

Professor Weisert is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subjects that he teaches. That being said, the midterm was one of the hardest tests I've ever taken. I also think that, in a music technology class, knowledge of the music technology should be the #1 priority, not knowledge of specific instances of music that he plays in the class.
He's pretty good. I took it as a FC, and it wasn't too bad. The lectures can be confusing, and the exams aren't the easiest, but its not that bad.

A fun class but very lecture heavy. Learned a TON. Weisert can seem unapproachable but is very caring. Genuinely wants his students have a good time, cares about the subject. Lectures are very detailed and can get boring, some of the assignments are busy work. Wished we could do more workshops.
Easy class, just do the homework.
Weisert's great! Highly knowledgeable, intelligent guy with a great sense of humor and a down-to-earth personality. MUSC130 was very doable and he made it enjoyable and low-stress.

Kicked-back, respectful, and very fun class. Professor Lee is a very fair grader and lays out all expectations beforehand, while also being very forgiving if the situation calls for it. Be prepared for the first 1/2 of the semester to have homework after every class, but most of it is simple half-hour assignments.
Nice and genuine guy. Pretty easy class, literally just practicing sight reading and transcription. I also had a great TA, Ken Ge, who graded easy. Chill and helpful.
Very interesting class and was pretty easy to do well in. Lots of hands on learning.

Very easy grader, not a lot of homework or assignments. If you show up to class, participate, and submit your assignments, you will get an easy A. She is also very nice, approachable, and accessible. Take this course with her if you can. She is also a very good fiddler.

This class often felt like a waste of time or mind-numbing, but that wasn't the professor's fault. Prof. Hargreaves is a caring professor and a great fiddler, and does her best to engage the class. The workload is very light and assignments are graded for completion. If you have to take MUSC 128 do it with Prof. Hargreaves.

Dr. Hargreaves is accepting of all skill levels of musicians. The class can be awkward at times because it is just you sitting in a room and making random noise with whatever instrument you do or don't have, but Hargreaves knows how to push through it and fill the space. Since improv is subjective, grading is lenient, so it's an easy A!

This class is a little goofy in nature. It is pretty much sitting in a circle and making noises together... However, Hargreaves is a phenomenal fiddler, which honestly kept me entertained during compositions. The class is easy and in my opinion not needed for the Music major, but take it with this prof! I still learned a bit and she is very nice!

This class could have been terrible but Hargreaves made it great. Didn't assign too much homework, super caring, wanted to help us learn but understanding it's a 1 credit class. If you don't miss class you should get an A, and have some fun along the way.

Overall, the course was pretty easy. I don't think Dr. Pittman was very involved, but I also wouldn't hold that against her since it is an online course. It's an easy A, coursework isn't unmanageable and it's nice being able to do everything in your own time.
Class was pretty easy. An A is a 95 though so be careful.

She is a great professor! This course is all online so sometimes it could be a little disorganized with things showing up late or being pushed back last minute. She is very kind and caring, and really cares about inclusivity. The class was easy (everything was open note and open book, even the exams) and I learned a lot from the class!
Such a goat

The class is completely online. I found it helpful that you could complete the work all on your own time and at your own pace. Dr. Pittman was always very generous with granting extensions as long as you let her know ahead of time. The only thing that sucked was you need to get a 95% in the class for an A.

This is an easy A class with all assignments, labs and quizzes/tests online and open note. The exams are straightforward and one is dropped. As long as you stay on top of due dates this class is very manageable and provides a good foundation of biochem. The instructor is nice but does not reply to emails so be prepared to only communicate with TA.

Great professor! There are many opportunities for extra credit. The exams can be a little tricky, but they're open-note. Everything else was very fair and easy to get an "A" on. It's important to watch the lectures and use the lecture outlines to take notes (a way to get exam extra credit), but I found her lectures really engaging.

Fully online class, exams and all. Exams are open note with 3 hours to complete. I have taken Pittman for BIOC107 and 108, and she's been great. I 100% recommend taking this over chem if you can. will save you from a world of hurt. 4 exams, daily assignments but all easy (discussion posts, responses, etc.)

This is a great sci class if you need an allied sci. Class was online/asynchronous. All assignments were easy and the tests were fair.  Everything's open book. You do need to get a 95 for an A, but it's doable. Definitely do the extra credit! Dr. Pittman seemed very kind and welcoming.

There is a lot of work for this class but everything is pretty straight forward and easy. Because it is an online class it is hard to have a deep understanding of the concepts. However, this class provides extra credit and every exam and assignment is open note. And there is a automatic extension for any late work and one exam gets dropped.

She was on maternity leave this semester but her recorded lecture videos are detailed and very well done! It's so obvious she cares about her students with labs and with the extra credit assignments. Participation wasn't graded this semester so grading was based on quizzes (open-note, unlimited attempts), exams, and labs. I would recommend taking!

As someone not heading into pre health, I thought this class was accessible for those needing a lab credit and overall, I felt like I could succeed. Overall, I think Dr. Pittman's lectures were easy to follow and while the labs and exams were really challenging, it felt doable. My only qualm with the complete lack of feedback on quizzes and labs

I took 107 and 108 with Pittman, and I received an A- in both simply because you have to make a 95% to get an A. Other than that, the class is fairly easy. She drops the lowest exam grade, gives extra credit for almost every exam, exams are open note, and the class is pretty much self-paced (within reason). I love Pittman and highly recommend!

Dr. Pittman was very knowledgeable about biochem. It helped that the class was all online. She puts out video lectures 3 times a week with embedded participation questions (but there aren't many). Exams are all open note and she often gives extra credit opportunities.

Dr Pittman is amazing! I took BIOC107 and 108 with her, and she is incredibly kind and understanding, as well as flexible with deadlines. The course is asynchronous so it is important to stay caught up with work and watch all of the lectures, and you do have to get a 95 to get an A, but I still managed and would 100% take this course again!

This was an asynchronous class so I didn't interact with the professor much but she's very caring. There is an automatic 48 hour extension on everything and all quizzes and exams were open note. You do need to make a 95 to get an A but besides that, this is class was pretty simple for a STEM class.

Professor Shea is great. I have taken multiple classes with him; attendance isn't mandatory, and he usually posts his lectures. I've taken 244 & 270, he always posts a study guide before exams and if you literally read it like twice before any exam you will be fine.

Dr. Shea is a really good professor, super funny and engaging. There are reading for every class and some of them can be 30+ pages, so get ready to read because you will discuss in groups than as a class about the readings and they help on the exams. Other than that super easy and interesting class.

I had Prof. Shea for CLAR492 (new class so wasn't an option) and he was fantastic. Constantly asked us for feedback as he developed the class and genuinely cared. Funny and super knowledgeable, he makes you WANT to listen lectures. Clear assignments while letting you go your own direction and encourages thinking outside the box with great feedback.

I took this last semester, but Shea is a delight!! I am not a Classics or CLAR major, but I loved this class. He was very encouraging and one of the most motivating professors that I've ever taken a class with. Even if you're not a classics person, I think this class could be enjoyable for anyone. He really challenged us to think outside the box.

This was a really great class. Grade determined by 3 short papers, one exam, and a final paper. The lectures were really interesting and Professor Shea is a great professor. Attendance is not required, but it makes the class better if you attend and participate.

I actually had him for CLAR/RELI 375, but that wasn't an option. Anyway, he was fantastic! Such a sweet person, and clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about archaeology. There were only a few papers (and no tests), but I still learned a lot in this class! I cannot recommend him enough!
Very chill class. Only consisted of three mini essays and one final take-home essay.  Grading was mostly fair.  Definitely recommend this class for VP/Art credit.

Shea is so knowledgable about the subject matter, which in this class was Greek Archeology. He always tried to attack each subject from a new angle and was genuinely interested in our ideas about it. We were graded by a few very short essays and the final exam was an essay.

Dr. Gates-Foster is clearly very knowledgeable about Roman history and archaeology, and she seemed very nice. However, I found the lectures to be somewhat repetitive. Grading was fair, and was half determined by her and half by a TA. Turn in the work and read at least some of the required readings and you'll be fine.

class structure wasn't my favorite but project based which was nice. weekly check ins were often confusing and drew questions from more abstract concepts. simple enough but easy to fall out of A territory if you're looking for an easy gen ed.

Could probably lecture about paint drying and make it at least somewhat interesting, she grades fairly although the TA might not be as fair (50% chance the TA grades your stuff I believe), and hope you get lucky with your group members for the project worth 20% of your grade.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Tests on the smallest details said in class even though she claims otherwise. Crap ton of reading. 2 exams and the first one is 15% even though historically students don't do well on it and she's aware of that. Weekly quizzes and weekly attendance. Barely lenient. Not your easy gen ed please skip out and save yourself

Professor Gates-Foster is a passionate lecturer, though can come across as distant at times. The class is manageable with a focus on lecture slides and attendance. unstuckstudy proved helpful for preparing for exams.

Controlled, calm and engaging lectures are brilliant. Dr. Gates-Foster does an excellent job at making this material accessible to people outside the department, but there is a lot of reading involved so it's not easy. Tests are 95% from the lectures and she does not post notes, so you have to attend and pay attention. Easily one of my top 3 profs

worst IDST123 prof by far. She cares way too much about making her subject of interest seem like the most challenging/important subject in the class. She talks down to students and seems to think she is generally better than everyone else in the room.
in my opinion, her lectures are the most interesting and easy to follow. The test is almost entirely based on lectures and ppt even though readings are assigned for every lecture.

The test is completely based on slideshows AND information discussed in class. She is a good lecturer but not great outside of being your teacher. Information on the tests is pretty straight forward if you came to class and did the readings. Read the text for examples you can use on the test, not for understanding.

Borders & Boundaries is not that bad. The readings can be long, but there's not a ton of work and it's really not difficult. Jen was definitely my favorite of the three lecturers, although she also assigned the most reading. I actually really enjoyed her lectures. Archaeology wasn't something I expected to enjoy, but she made it interesting.

I had her for B&B and out the three teachers, she was the best lecturer. However, her exam was the hardest. To do well in the class, you must attend lectures so you can get credit for the in class assignments and study for the  exams - that's it. Study guides are helpful but TA's and teachers will not help you with your grade or even respond.

Professor Gates-Foster cares a lot about her area of study. Her lectures were very entertaining even if you did not care too much about archaeology. She assigns a lot of readings but as long as you review what is on the slides and take notes during her lectures you should be okay. Would definitely take another class with her again.
not very approachable & passive aggressive. assigns lots of super long readings but you don't need them for the tests, just review the lecture stuff

Prof. Foster was an amazing lecturer. The exam was difficult with no study guide and just a "read the slides" for advice, but overall it wasn't too hard. I wasn't too interested in the material, but Prof. Foster lectured in a way that didn't make it boring. There are readings every class, but reading them isn't necessary

Lengthy readings every night, but in all honestly they're not necessary to do well on exams. Didn't read any and did very well on the exam. Her lectures cover all the material you need to know, and everything on the exam is laid out very clearly and explicitly. She's understanding and lays out expectations well. Would highly recommend!

Very organized and efficient compared to other triple-I instructors. Clearly very knowledgeable, slightly sassy, and expects a lot from you on a topic most students were not interested in unfortunately

Fine as a lecturer but very condescending and rude to students. Will ask students questions and then belittle them for answering, even if they answer correctly. Often walks around the lecture hall to hawk students when she isn't lecturing. Generally seen as a pretty mean and disrespectful professor. However, she is knowledgable in her field.

Professor Gates-Foster in Borders and Boundaries was an interesting lecturer, but the class overall was poor. The constant shifting in topics was confusing, and TAs determine your entire grade. The professors were unprepared for such a large class. I would not recommend this class.

If you are taking this for a gen ed, don't. She is a great professor but unless you have a background in this content it is extremely difficult and the format of exams make it very challenging to do well. I am typically an A student and this class killed me even to get a C+. Very lecture heavy and tests weigh a lot.

Dr. Gates-Foster is one of the best professors I've taken a class with so far at UNC! Her lectures are excelllent, and super fascinatingl; this is a great class to learn about Ancient Egypt in-depth, but may not be a good choice for anyone looking for an easy gen ed credit. 

You HAVE to go to her lectures; otherwise, you definitely won't do well.

I really enjoyed this class! Although Dr. Lye assigns a lot of weekly tasks and it might get overwhelming to keep track of them, she's lenient on deadlines and wants to make sure you pass her class. The content was interesting and comprised different yet intertwined topics. The assignments themselves were pretty easy.

An incredible amount of work. If you do all the readings, maybe 10 hours a week. Do not do them. Dr. Lye is an extremely lenient grader and it is easy to get an A. She cares very much for her students, though and the class was generally interesting. The group project was my favorite part.

So much reading and work outside of class. Didn't know our grades in the class going into the final exam. She is very knowledgable and cares about us doing well but she just covers so much information it's hard to follow.
This class is far too work intensive for a 100 level course. Dr. Lye is very knowledgeable but this class is too much reading in my opinion

Professor Lye was passionate about the topic, and I highly recommend this class if you grew up liking Percy Jackson or any other mythological-inspired series. Unless you're in the honors section, the TAs grade all of your work, so you will be fine as long as you set up a good relationship with them and submit weekly assignments on time.

dr. lye is very passionate about mythology which made the classes interesting, but if you have interest at all in mythology, it may be boring. A LOT of reading and homework (discussion board). her tests are really easy just make sure you pay attention in class and at least know some parts of the myths. only thing is you literally can't see ur grade

She is very caring and passionate about mythology, so it makes the lectures more engaging. However, the class is A LOT of reading and busy work (multiple discussion posts every week), and grades are unavailable for the whole semester. Exams are pretty easy if you go through all the lectures and readings.

Great professor! I honestly can't believe she doesn't have a perfect rating. If you like mythology you should absolutely take this class. It was a lot of reading but if you find this stuff interesting is totally manageable. Highly recommend.

I'm not sure why she has so many bad reviews. There's a lot of reading, but if you pay attention in class, you never have to read. I haven't opened a single assigned book in this class and I got a 101 on the midterm. Her lectures are engaging and she's very nice. This class isn't hard if you pay attention and don't treat it like an easy A.

Dr. Lye is an exceptional professor who genuinely cares about her students' success and is always ready to provide help. Lectures are fascinating and engaging while also contextualizing reading done outside of class. Readings may seem daunting, but they are very manageable, primarily as the course teaches you proper time management. Highly suggest!
She told me that my disability (severe hearing loss) was fake and that I needed to learn to listen better. She refused to meet any of my university required accommodations.

This class was disorganized, but the exams are easy enough if you go through the lectures and the (very long) readings. There was no feedback for grades until they were official! Make sure to do the discussion posts/replies on time. Be aware there's a LOT of busy work. The lectures were fairly boring, but she's passionate about the topic.

There are a lot of assignments in this class, however, none are very difficult. Professor Lye is an incredible lecturer, and I personally always loved her discussions. Exams are not too bad, just make sure to review presentations closely. If you do not enjoy reading I also would not take lol. Pretty fun class!

It is said that Heracles once battled a course called CLAS 131. Every time an assignment was completed, two more would grow in its place. The directions for these assignments were unclear and his grades not released for weeks. He had no way to know or estimate his grade leading into the final, as the 21 page syllabus was incredibly cryptic.

Professor Lye is so smart and knowledgable and I was really excited to take this class. That being said, the actual process of taking this class has been chaotic. I have NO idea what my grade is, none. and yet we have had upwards of 5 graded assignments a week, 10+ hours of reading, with no connection between the lectures and the reading.

I was given so much work that was so pointless ALL the time. I wanted an easy gen ed class for focus capacities and this was not one. It was easy but so pointless, not that bad sometimes but super annoying and too much stupid work. It was not the worse class but I would not take again

I took this class hoping for an interesting and easy gen-ed, but I was terribly wrong. This class took up more time than my 400 and 500 level classes this semester. She swamps you with readings weekly which she doesn't cover in class until 2-3 weeks later. There is an extreme amount of busy work. If you are looking for an easy GenEd this is NOT it.
She was lowkey passive aggressive and her exams were hard. Although attendance isn't mandatory there is still a lot of stuff you have to do for the class... way more than I expected.

I took this class for fun as a senior but it was definitely a mistake. A lot of the class is geared toward freshman (adding multiple unneeded assignments before projects). Expect at least 10+ hours of reading and unclear busy work every week. With little guidance and the expectation to memorize everything from the texts and lectures, for exams

Prof. Lye is sweet and passionate, but this course is miserable. She drowns you in readings and movies to watch, and it's SO overwhelming. There are weekly discussion posts, quizzes on readings, and TONS of mini-projects and assignments. Grades aren't even disclosed, so it's difficult to gauge whether or not you're doing well in the class.
Not difficult but not interesting.  Don't take unless you're passionate about greek history.  Lots of reading expected for a gen-ed.  Not graded harshly, but only a few things were graded.
Very interesting and passionate, easy grader and cares about students.

Prof. Baragwanath is very knowledgeable and passionate about the course. Decent amount of reading and writing, but as long as you pay attention and stay on top of the readings you'll be fine. Really enjoyed this course.

She is an amazing lecturer, but most of the grading is from the TAs; they are really sweet too though. You def need to do your readings to be up to date with the class and prepared, and there are a good bit of written assignments, but as long as you read and listen you will be perfectly fine
Dr. B is such a kind, interesting person and SO knowledgeable. Loved this class & she is a very generous grader. Cares more about learning than grades

Prof. B truly was amazing. She is extremely passionate about the classics and she is so personable that I would invite her to my wedding. The course is extremely reading heavy so my only setbacks in the class were if I did not do all of the readings. If you engage, you will do well. Assignments are given in the syllabus so no surprises.

Professor Baragwanath is amazing! Her energy during lectures is infectious. I took this class not expecting much but I've ended up loving it. There's a fair amount of reading, but not too much and it's all interesting. It's not completely an easy A, but if you participate and put in a little work you should be fine. Highly recommend!

Had zero interest in classics but absolutely loved the class & professor. Have never seen a prof so passionate about their subject! Her energy was infectious. Very fair grader and appreciated genuine effort & participation. Overall great person. Tempted to take another classics class with her even though it has nothing to do with my major.

Emily is incredibly personable, happy, and caring. She expects and values participation in her classes, of which I have taken three. She even organizes her lectures into a tiered system of pods, and passed around a microphone among our hundred. You will do well if you do the readings; she just wants you to think and participate.

There are specific versions of Greek Tragedies you need to read (they are listed in the syllabus). The free-write in class is doable as long as you understand the general plot. The essay is relatively straightforward and you can also go to office hours. The midterm was a bit difficult but with other grades it balances out. Final was group project.

Baroud seems really intense at first but honestly he is one of the most inspirational and passionate professors I've had. I took CLAS122 for the focus capacities and loved it so much I ended up taking 241 too. Classes are action packed and I always left feeling I learned something. Readings are manageable and exams are fine.

CLAS241*. He does NOT give you the full time to take written exams. Also, it seems he wants students to give 120%, but in terms of being helpful and accommodating for students, it feels he only gives 70%. if he likes you, yay! if he doesn't, go ahead and drop.
Professor Baroud is an amazing storyteller and professor. I got a B and still would take the class again because of how well he taught the course.

Prof. Baroud is easily one of my favorite professors. His class was immensely difficult (300 pages of dry, dense reading each week; could not bullshit your way through exams), but his grading was fair and he forces you to grow as a thinker/reader. He's scary (and maybe a bit snarky) at first, but he is super approachable in office hours.

Don't take this class if you want to sit by, skip the readings, and hope you'll get a good grade. Professor Baroud is an amazing professor, extremely intelligent, and loves the Roman Empire. Highly recommend going to office hours, as he wants to know every student personally. If you are willing to go a little crazy, then this is the class for you.

Quite literally the most engaging and thought provoking lectures I've ever heard. He's an incredibly knowledgable and charismatic professor. Main downside of the class are the reading assignments, almost too lengthy to handle. If you show up to all the lectures, do the readings, and ask questions, you'll do well. I wish I could take CLAS122 again.

Prof is very passionate, intelligent and gives good lectures. I wouldn't recommend this class as a gen ed unless you actually like the Romans and classics. Readings are long and confusing ~150-200 pages a week but he explains the readings in class. Tests were graded kinda harsh but office hours helped me improve.
Maintaining a GPA of 4.0 for four years and screwed up in this class. Thank you Prof.
DO NOT take this class for gen ed. If you are a stem dude like me, your GPA will plummet pretty soon.

***THIS REVIEW IS FOR CLAS-122***

Dr. Baroud is one of the most intelligent and insightful professors I have had here at UNC. While the readings can be long, and the exams difficult, his amazing lectures make it all worth it. He is a passionate and charismatic professor who is never terribly unreasonable, and he knows his stuff.

**this review is for WGST/CLAS 241** Prof Baroud was truly one of my favorite professors I've ever had. I was nervous about taking a women's studies class with a male teacher but he exceeded all my expectations. He is so ntelligent and cares about the material. He values students' questions/opinions. His exams were not too difficult if you studied.

Read his other reviews at NYC -> they are aptly complimentary. 
Baroud has been my favourite prof in nearly 3 years of university. His lecturing/teaching is incredibly good, he clearly has a natural interest in the work. My Ancient Roman Empire class with him was incredibly enjoyable. Check out his office hours; interesting in conversation.
good class, good professor, tests were fair and so were essays
Attendance isn't mandatory but such an easy class if you go. 6 participation in class writing assignments, a midterm, final, and a few essays. She's very understanding, highly recommend.

She was very sweet and very passionate about Pompeii. Very easy tests and assignments, just make sure to put some effort into the 2 essays. Almost completely homework free, and prioritizes your learning over your grade. Unexpectedly interesting, easy, and professor Valladares is awesome. I would recommend this class to anyone
Dr. Valladares is well established in this field and if you have any interest in Pompeii or the Roman Empire, you should take this class! It's an easy gen ed, but lectures can be pretty boring.
took as a gen ed and learned a lot! definitely take if you are interested in Pompeii/Rome. lectures are long but it's a T/Th class so it's to be expected

No required attendance in lecture unless you are worried about missing the notes. She is knowledgeable about her field and is an amazing class if you are interested in classics. As a non-history major got kinda boring. Easy grades, graded by a few in class writings, 2 papers, a midterm and a final. Midterm and final are nothing to stress over.

I loved this class. It was so incredibly chill; they just want you to learn. They send all test material out beforehand. Valladares was so kind. Her lectures could be a little boring, but it wasn't her fault; it's just that it was a Tu/Th class, and it loses your attention at some point. Overall, would definitely recommend for an easy gen ed.

Rarely showed up, attendance not mandatory and really not necessary. Exams were super easy and lenient grader. 2 papers, midterm, final, in class assignments (completion grade). Easy double gen ed class if you can put in just a bit of work.

Super easy class, lectures are long and dull but 90% of the information in the lecture is in the Cengage textbook. Attendance non-mandatory and I didn't feel like I missed anything when I skipped. Exams are easy and study materials include everything covered. Professor is knowledgeable but seems (unintentionally) condescending at times.

Professor Valladares is incredibly knowledgable and know A LOT about antiquity. Some people had a hard time with the exams, but overall I thought the class was pretty interesting and easy. She really cares about her students, however the lectures can be a bit boring at times.

I'm honestly surprised by some of the lower ratings here! Yes she is lecture heavy, however she is one of the most knowledgeable people in the world when it comes to anything antiquity. She's also super caring and considerate. I've taken two classes with her now, and she has personal connections with her students and knows the answer to everything.

Loved this class! Prof Valladares is so nice and her lectures were amazing and fascinating. Our museum based projects were interesting and also relatively simple. For both the midterm and final she posted all of the information we would need to study beforehand. Definitely take this class if you like Pompeii or Roman history in general!!

Professor Valladares is so sweet and knowledgeable! She is also very flexible and adapted the course in light of a difficult start to the semester. I would 100% take one of her classes again! Just make sure to go to lectures because even though they are not required, you will miss out on a lot of information that the slides alone don't cover.

Professor Valladares was a great professor! She is extremely caring and gives clear instructions for any assignments we have. Quizes are counted for participation and she prepares you for midterm and final beforehand. Lectures can sometime be boring but other than that it was a great class!!

Great lecturer and super interesting. This class was very easy, there were two museum papers and quizzes that counted only for participating, and then a midterm and a final. If you look over the material from class, you will be totally fine for the exams. She emphasizes learning over stressing about grades and the TAs were super easy graders.

Professor Valladares is a wonderful professor. I've taken 2 of her classes. Her lectures are very interesting. She makes the exams super easy and just wants you to understand the material rather than stress for exams. I love Professor Valladares and would recommend her to anybody especially if you're interested in archaeology and classics.
Outstanding classics professor! Engaging lectures, deep knowledge, and passionate about the subject. Highly recommended for any classics enthusiast.

DO NOT take this class unless you are at the bottom of the bucket. Not only is this teacher extremely boring, but you will fall asleep and lose track of everything very quickly, especially because there is no supplemental material to refer back to! Also, she only speaks subjectively (her opinions) and uses no words on powerpoint slides.

Professor Valladares was awesome! We had 3 papers and two presentations (the final one was a group project and she deleted the third paper from the syllabus) and she was very understanding the whole semester with all the students. She was very encouraging and lovely to work with. I highly recommend her class, specifically the CLAR/ARTH465!

I learned a lot from this class. Prof and TAs are sweet. But the exams are really hard and tricky. She went through lectures so fast. You rarely have enough time to write things down. And the little details that you missed could potentially be on the exams. I learned a lot but the exams are unnecessarily tricky.

English 105I was amazing with Professor Lang. 1 individual project, 2 group projects, no midterm nor final. All the projects were writing wikipedia pages on topics you choose. You can only miss two classes, but he's very understanding if you explain absences. Super easy grader, and a B is the lowest you can get if you complete all the work.
He's very chill and super kind. Just make sure to turn in the homework on time and you'll get an A. Also, go to his office hours, he is very knowledgeable on classics (lowkey cool)!

An amazing teacher and my favorite professor this semester. Every assignment we did was marked based on completion. I loved how his areas of expertise (I believe it was Latin or Roman linguistics) seeped into the way he taught class. What you learn and get out of this class is based on what you put into it. There was one group project.

Prof. Lang is a great choice for ENGL 105I (Natural Sciences). The writing assignments were all interesting and relevant. They're caring and will work with you on deadlines if you communicate. You'll have homework each class, but as long as you show effort and turn everything in you'll get an A. Make sure to have some scientific topic in mind.

Prof. Lang was caring, kind, well-organized, and overall a really great teacher. Assignments were fairly easy but engaging and had lots of room for creative touches. Good incorporation of individual and personal work. Engaging lectures. Grade was mostly completion and attendance. Would highly recommend taking his class.

I loved english 105 with this professor. The class was extremely well-organized and setup, and was not hard at all to get an A. This professor grades off of a 'completion' grading scale, so as long as you do all the work for the class, you are guaranteed a B. If I could take another class under this professor I would.

I had Anna for 203. She's a really nice person and gives a ton of grace. There are translations for homework for every class, but they're very manageable. She's disorganized, but she also was recovering from a TBI.

I will say that you'll get out of this class what you put into it. Prepare the translations and pay attention and you'll learn.

Though Anna is genuinely such a sweet and kind person, this class (LATN 203) has sadly not been a good experience. She is extremely disorganized and class is always very chaotic. I would consider myself extremely Latin-savvy and even I have trouble keeping up with her pace, she rushes through the translation in a very chaotic, confusing way.

102/203-Anna gives a TON of grace & will give partial credit, this is needed bc quizzes are hard & contain a ridiculous amount of material. If you get lost in class, youll stay lost, she moves quick & stays at a pace that is with the most advanced students. Is extremly unorganized w/ class, takes forever to return/grade, will show up to class late

(LATN 203) Anna is a very nice professor and gives a lot of grace in terms of attendance/make-ups but her class is extremely disorganized. She rushes through the slides and expects us to get everything she says. There was lots of grammar we never learned in 102 that she just expected us to know.

literally the best Latin instructor ever, if you get the chance to take her please do. she gives tons of extra credit on quizzes and is extremely lenient about makeup quizzes, homework, and attendance. super friendly and loves to talk. definitely definitely definitely take every Latin class you can with her 🤞🤞🤞🤞🤞🤞

Lectures were easy to comprehend and she showed us how to use all of the platforms needed for projects in class. The bulk of the class is a group research project, but she meets with you to give advice before deadlines and provides feedback as you go. Professor Zhao is very caring and just an overall pleasant person to learn from!

idk what these reviews are about! she was awesome to us, lectures were pointless sometimes but she's really sweet and talks about her dog all the time. a lot of classes were virtual work days which was nice and she meets with your group before the assignment is due to go over it and give feedback AND lets you resubmit one thing to be re-graded!!

I would recommend taking ad/pr research with Eva. She is super nice and accessible and is very passionate about research. She is willing to help you and the class is very manageable (with little assignments). Just participate in class!

One of the worst MEJO professors. She gave NO FEEDBACK. Doesn't believe in giving 100s. She told us we did great but the max she gave someone was a 94. This isn't supposed to be a difficult class, but is when she doesn't give any feedback other than a good job, and quickly goes through the slides. We have only done group work all year. DO NOT TAKE!
Take this class with this professor if you want to feel terrible about yourself and want to have your work picked apart to shreds. AKA don't take it.

Professor Reid was a great professor for media law. The class is super content heavy but participation is graded on a panel basis. There is plenty of room for extra credit. Her tests used to be open note but they no longer are so just study hard and pay attention. 2 midterms and one final along with quizzes and discussion posts regularly.

Professor Reid is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Media Law is a lot of content, and she moves fast, but she makes lectures engaging and interesting. The exams were a bit challenging, but the lectures prepared us well for them. I would definitely take Media Law with her if you can!

Professor Reid was so down-to-earth and understanding. Take this class when you have space on your plate for it. If you aren't very interested in law, you're gonna need to lock in and learn how to make space for it. Expectations are very clear from day one and lectures are engaging. Panel based participation system. Extra credit. Open note exams.
One of my favorite professors at UNC!! You can tell she is so passionate about law and she does such a great job teaching. Midterms and final are open note!
The best professor I have had at Hussman
Honestly the goat

Tough course with a LOT of material that goes by kind of fast, but she lays out the info really well! The quizzes/discussion posts are helpful and the midterms+final are open note and not too difficult if you study. She offered us extra credit as well.

I am a HUGE fan of professor Amanda Reid. This class is very content heavy and it's a lot to study, but she teaches this class so well that it is 100% worth taking with her. It is definitely a hard class, but she taught it very well.
Media law gets a bad reputation, but Dr. Reid makes the class fun. She provides a lot of memorable snippets that will help you on the exam and in your life as you come across these topics.

Literally, stop what you're doing and sign up for this class. Dr. Reid is an extraordinary professor who is passionate and funny in lectures. She is so smart and does an amazing job of drilling information into your head without it ever being dull. Her class is so entertaining and she really encourages participation and discussion about the law.

Hands down, the BEST professor that I have had at UNC. She made one of the most dreaded classes in the  MEJO school one that I absolutely loved. She simplified complex topics into understandable language and was always available to help. The class is difficult, and you must stay on top of things, but take this class with Dr. Reid!!!
Her class is tough, but she is an excellent professor!

Dr. Reid was great. Provided tons of resources to help study. Sakai site is well designed. Lectures were recorded and slides are posted. Super accessible through email and office hours. Material is hard and complex but if you just put some effort towards the class you'll be fine.
Professor Reid is the best professor I've ever had, she makes media law so engaging, and she is very organized and on top of everything. She is very passionate and an amazing instructor.

For MEJO 390: Really great professor!! Teaches material in a very digestible way and walks you through everything. If you have a question, don't be afraid to speak up in class because he will answer without making you feel bad + also very accessible outside of class to help with homework.

Extremely unclear and constantly changing grading criteria. I swear he grades based on his mood. Feels like he is always on a power trip and will take away points as much as he possibly can. Far too strict for being a level 100 course, considering over half the class is AD PR, not a journalism major.

Prof. Thornburg is a tough grader, but his comments are very helpful and definitely improved my writing throughout the semester. The more you practice, the more natural those changes become, and Thornburg gives a lot of opportunities to practice writing stories in this class. Not flexible with late/missed work, but many chances for extra credit.

Thornburg gives lots of feedback and can be a tough grader, but is so helpful in improving your writing. 
If you finish your assignments on time, apply his feedback, and take advantage of his office hours you will be totally fine!! He made this class so enjoyable and was my favorite professor this semester! TAKE HIM!

Thornberg was the first professor I had in the Hussman school and was amazing. He is a tough grader but if you do the work then its not hard. He also will provide feedback on articles before you turn them in which was a huge help. Super nice and very approachable too.

Prof. Thornburg is one of the best professors at Hussman. Coding and understanding how to work with data can be very intimidating but Pro. Thornburg is great at breaking things down and making them understandable. He cares about everyone is makes himself available outside of class. There's a lot of homework, but do your best and you'll be fine.

Thornburg is super accessible, great to talk to about the class and journalism in general. Decent amount of homework but not hard, just takes a little bit of time. If you put in the effort it's easy to get an A in this class. I loved being in his class and would definitely recommend! +EC if you do extra or point out something wrong on an assignment

Ryan is goated. I'm a MEJO major and am a good writer so I did really well in the class, but lots of my classmates struggled to get an A. If you make a fact error in your writing the highest you can get is a 50% on that assignment. He's tough but totally helps your writing so much. Really knowledgable too and wants to get to know you. I recommend

I enjoyed him as a professor and often thought that I did a lot better on assignments than I actually did. He would grill me and rip me to shreds on every assignment I turned in, and I don't know if I ever made any improvements to my grade even towards the end of the semester. Cool guy and would love to pick his brain on so many things.

Ryan is a great guy who made really helped a semester that got off to a pretty poor start. He explains R very well, the labs and homework were very to learning and can always be referenced pretty easily. A great mix of journalism and code, with a very approachable and kind professor who truly just wants you to learn.
Dr. Thornburg helped me improve my journalistic writing in a crazy-short amount of time. He's a tough grader, but I am thankful for it because I couldn't have improved without his feedback.

Ryan Thornburg is great especially if you get to know him and go to office hours. The class is obviously on the more difficult side if you struggle with grammar, but Ryan helped me out a lot and helped me to improve over the semester. If you have to take this class strongly recommend to take it with him.

Professor Thornburg was easily one of my favorite professors this year. He can be a bit strict with grading, but that's beneficial because he makes you such a better writer. He does require a lot of textbook reading, but there was nothing that I felt was busywork. He was accessible outside class as well. An A is doable if you put in the effort.

As a MEJO course, it is reading heavy but the content really does help with writing prompts that are assigned as homework. Dr.Thornburg was always willing to talk through a grade or question. His feedback is helpful and made me a better writer. He also facilitated a positive and welcoming classroom environment.
Ryan is awesome. I learned so much in his data journalism class, without having any prior coding experience. He listens to student feedback and will work with you through any problems.

Professor Thornburg was so kind. He can be a tough grader but he grades like how the real world would critique you so it is super helpful. He is great to meet outside of class with students, gives feedback, and will sometimes boost grades when you review an assignment with him. I learned so much from his class! One of my favorite prof. yet.

I absolutely loved MEJO 340 with Professor Dancy. Her lectures are engaging & fun, and I always looked forward to coming to class. She tells you exactly what she's looking for on the exams and truly wants her students to succeed. She also offers extra credit! This class was my favorite class I've taken at UNC so far!

The sweetest and kindest professor I've had at UNC! I'd heard horror stories about Media Law, but she made it engaging and clear. Learned so much helpful legal info that is applicable in real-world journalism. If you come to class and listen, it is an easy A.

Literally the sweetest person and most supportive professor ever! Shelvia was always willing to help her students and I actually ended up enjoying the course and learned so much. There are a few assignments that feel like a lot at once in the most intense part of the semester, but nothing any of us couldn't handle.

BEST MEJO 340 PROF EVER!!!! You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and the topic. Lots of reading, but exams were easy, and she offered extra credit. Grade is based on midterms, participation, a couple of engaging case brief assignments, and reading quizzes. If you need to take 340, take it with her. You will absolutely not regret it.

This class with Professor Dancy was the easiest class I've taken at UNC. Don't get me wrong though, it was very helpful. I learned a lot about how to speak more clearly. She doesn't necessarily teach you how to have a standard reporter voice, but she helps you polish it. She gives a normal number of assignments and they're all super easy.

Professor Dancy is one of the kindest professors at UNC. She is passionate and a seasoned reporter and really knows what she's teaching. The assignments are time consuming, but she is just trying to prepare you for the real world. As long as you put in the work and ask questions, you'll do fine. Interesting lectures, too!

Professor Dancy, so far, has been one of the best teachers I have had in the Hussman School. I had her for MEJO340, and she was very clear and responsive with questions, well aligned with her rubric, and extremely knowledgeable in the content she teaches.

Best class ever, best professor ever! There is such a stigma going into this class, but it genuinely couldn't have been more interesting and easy. Professor dancy breaks it down so clearly, and her tests replicate word-for-word what she tells you to study in class. Her lecture keeps me engaged the entire time, and she offers a ton of extra credit!

MEJO 421 can be hard but entirely manageable. Reporting isn't an easy job, but if you give it the time and effort it deserves it's very easy to succeed in this course!  Professor Dancy is such a great tool and mentor, who is accessible to breakdown any aspect of the class. She is one of the best at UNC, and I recommend taking time to work with her.

Professor Dancy was one of my favorite professors I have had at UNC so far! She went to law school, making learning even more interesting. The discussion posts and quizzes helped summarize information, and she gave great feedback on all assignments. The class consists of readings, discussion posts, quizzes, a midterm, case briefs, and a final.

This is an easy class, but Prof. Dancy does a lot to make sure it isn't boring, even if you don't want to go into broadcast which this class is aimed towards. Her lectures are engaging, the textbook readings are extremely manageable, and you will definitely learn something new about your voice!

425 is an extremely easy class, but I still felt like I learned a lot about my voice! Professor Dancy is incredibly kind and encourages you to put your own spin on your projects. Her expectations of classroom conduct are high but perfectly reasonable. She readily encourages participation, and being in the front row of her class is so fun!

The ONLY negative thing I could ever say about Professor Dancy is that she is a really textbook-heavy professor. Besides that, this woman is an angel. She really cares about everyone, will give you time and effort if you put it back in to her, and will do anything to ensure your success. I thought Media Law would be terrible, it was the opposite.

Professor Dancy is a kindhearted person who wants to see her students succeed. While MEJO 421 is difficult and she expects quality, deadline-meeting work, she will meet you more than halfway if you put in the effort. Go to office hours with a shell of an idea, and you will leave with a story. I really love Professor Dancy and she is one of my favs.

I really like Professor Dancy, but I am not sure I like this class. The class is super easy but its not super interesting. I think other reviewers are mistaking her when they say she is difficult. Professor Dancy can be stern and upfront which could turn away some students but she is actually very kind and enjoys talking to her students.

At a high level school like UNC this class seemed like a waste of my time. All we did was practice saying letters and breathing. Just a free social period. The "lectures" were just what was in the book. Half of the information made no sense at all and I really learned nothing from this class. Easy, but a total waste of time.

Ms. Dancy was not the professor for me. In a hands on, learn as you do the work class, her expectations were SO high. She expects perfection as we are learning and has no grace. She is rude and not willing to work with students. It is impossible to ask questions unless you go to office hours, no matter what the question is. Do NOT take this class.

Simply put she makes your life 10x harder than it has to be. Her criteria for what she accepts as news for this class is extremely narrow: It must take place less than 4 days before the due date, you must be able to find info not reported on by news orgs, and she has to think its news. How does she tell you to find stuff? LOOK ON MAJOR NEWS ORGS!

For a class I heard so many scary things about, Media Law w/ Prof Dancy was actually enjoyable.
