Ryan really made what could have been a boring class feel fun and interesting. As long as you do the reading, this is a fairly easy class. He treats everyone with respect and encourages asking questions. He also gave lots of great movie/tv recommendations. Overall great guy and awesome professor!
If you can handle ADHD rambling you will love him. Very informative and a genuine guy. Only 2 grades in the class, midterm and final, but open note and online.

I LOVE PROF. TUCK!!!!!! He makes a potentially miserable class interesting and engaging. He is witty, generous, and committed to his students' success. Easily one of the best instructors I've had at Carolina. Be prepared to read most of a 400 pg. textbook.

One of the best professors I have had at UNC. Super engaging and inspirational lectures. You will learn so much in this class and become a much better feature writer and writer in general. Graded on three long-form feature stories and much of the work had to be done outside of class.

Professor Crothers keeps class very interesting and has a lot of experience in journalism, and it shows! He has high expectations, but as long as you put in the work (and double- and triple-check your AP stylebook), you'll do well. 153 has a heavy workload, but he keeps it very reasonable. Ask him about Queen of Katwe sometime!

This is a one of a kind class. It's entirely guest lectures with notable people in the sports media field, with short weekly assignments and two papers at the end of the semester. Prof. Crothers repeated that if you take this class for a grade, that's the wrong reason. He's right, this is networking and insider info galore. Take this class!

Professor Crothers is the most influential professor I've had at UNC so far. The feedback he gives on papers is also super helpful. The only reason I didn't rank 5/5 is the lack of a Sakai page, canvas site, or even a specific syllabus. This made it difficult to keep up with my grade or what we were doing in class.

(For MEJO 153) Professer Crothers is the most outstanding professor I have taken. His real world experience shines through in a way that makes you feel that you are truly learning. Not only do I feel I have become a much better writer, but I also feel that I am leaving the class a much smarter person, overall. Definitely will take again!

Professor Crothers is elite. J455 was one of the coolest experiences to be a part of, especially as someone who is really into sports. Really caring and understanding professor, couldn't recommend more! There is no way of checking your grade throughout the semester, so that was tough at times. Other than that, he's amazing! Take 455 if you can!!

Crothers is nice but he doesn't teach the class, he finds guest speakers that come in every week. If you are interested in what the life of sports media people looks like this class is great. Adds little stress and is interesting to know more about the journalism profession.
MEJO137, no Sakai site so it made it hard to know my grade at the end

(For MEJO153-Intro to Writing and Reporting**) 

Tim Crothers is an amazing professor and I would 100% recommend you take a class with him if given the option to. He has valuable life experience which translates into his teaching. He gives good feedback on papers, and he genuinely cares about his students. Made me a better writer.

She is kind as a person but she is an extremely tough grader and everything is extremely subjective. Her rubric is completely inconsistent and changes each assignment. Nice lady but take the class with anyone else tbh.

Professor Thorpe is very demanding in terms of grading. However, she makes her expectations/requirements very clear, is lovely person, and is very understanding and accommodating. There is also not a ton of homework for the class.

A late grader as the others have said with not so welcoming attitude as a first year course instructor. Also said to have multiple jobs other than teaching, the efficiency of replying to works submitted or emails or texts would be coming as late as drake's iceman album. This is literally a writing class and you need absolutely updated reflections.
Was scared to even raise my hand in this class. Scary professor who will shred whatever you turn in. I realize this is a hard class but there are much much better options.

I liked her as a person; she cares about students and her lectures were helpful and engaging. However, I would try to take the class with someone else. Her grading is tough, which is expected, but also inconsistent and late. It was hard to improve when some grades took over a month to come in, and it felt like her grading was heavily subjective.

Absolutely amazing. Very nice but a strict grader. She really wants her students to improve as writers and sometimes gives tough love, but its all with our interests in mind. Walked away from this class as a much better student because she has such an accesible way of teaching and grading

This class made me fall in love with reporting. After the very first day knew I was where I belonged. I was working for a real newspaper at the same time as I was taking this course, and what I learned was genuinely so helpful to me in the job. Najuma was always willing to answer my questions and offer advice after class.

She is so great! A little bit of a strict grader but she clearly cares for her students and is passionate about the material. Wonderful wonderful professor! And it doesn't hurt that the exams are all virtual.

Possibly one of the hardest Mejo professors at UNC. I took her my sophomore year and was not impressed by how she structured her classroom. Arrogant person who doesn't like the underdog. I was in a zoom meeting with her 1 on 1 in the middle of the semester, where she had her camera off the entire time and honestly made me feel bad about myself.

A lot of people give her crap for being a touch grader but I really loved her. I only got one or two shocking grades before I knew what I was doing and then easily succeeded in the rest of the class. She is super kind, but blunt, and really easy to access outside of class (on text). Do not be scared to take 153 with her, she will make you great!

I learned lots but only at the expense of poor grades. Thorpe was reasonable and seemed nice at first but was very passive aggressive. She sometimes would just assign something you were completely unfamiliar with and then give you a horrible score. She has a poor final grading system in which she can choose to add -/+. I wouldn't recommend.

Clay was an absolute joy the entire semester. Deadlines and grading criteria are super clear, and you have an automatic two-day grace period for every assignment. Not sure what he's teaching now, but whatever it is, take it!

considering his first time teaching, did a not bad job! do expect assignments to kind of hit at the same time, but they aren't hard to complete and there are options to rework for a better grade. definitely got to take away a decent amount of skills!

Clay is so awesome! He is super funny, kind, and a great professor! He really wants to help his students succeed and creates a very easygoing, fun learning environment in the classroom! The work is straightforward, and it's extremely likely you will get an A! Would take his class over and over again if I could!

Professor Williams is honestly one of the best professors I have had. There are quite a lot of assignments in the course, but I always felt prepared. Clay gives incredible feedback and cares so much about your success. I truly feel like I'm a better creative person because of this class.
Take 121 with Clay if you can!!! He's super chill, funny, and wants everyone to succeed. His feedback on assignments is super detailed and helpful. Absolutely loved this class

Clay is one of the best professors I've had. He is super charismatic, cares about his students, and super accessible outside of class. The feedback given on assignments is so valuable. The class moves fast with assignments almost every week, but it's very manageable. I would hands down take another class with him in a heartbeat!

if you want to actually become a better writer, take his 153. i have also now started to enjoy writing again and he gives helpful feedback, fair grading and always gives room for you to improve/make up assignments you didn't do well on!
Take Belichick's $50 million and give it to this guy.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER PLS TAKE HIM! Kindest teacher and genuinely cares about you and your learning. Gives thorough feedback and is so understanding. I love going to his class!
Professor Howlett is so good. If he has other classes I'll definite take it with him. Interesting lectures and meaningful assignments. Clear feedback too. Love him.

I can not recommend someone better or more kind than Prof Howlett. He is truly such a caring and personable guy. 

He always checks up on his students, provides great feedback on assignments, and keeps class interesting. I have never felt that my time in his class was wasted. Take him for MEJO 153. Even if it is in the evening. Take him.
He is genuinely the best professor I had at UNC. He really cares for his students and wants everyone to do well. He is always there to help and listen. I learned a lot from his class.
Prof. Howlett is so amazing I cannot even attempt to write it all here. Whatever you do, take this class with him.

Professor Howlett truly is the best instructor you'll ever take. He increased my writing confidence astronomically. I had his class at  5 p.m., and it's the only class I never skipped. I was excited for class even. He has such knowledge, and makes writing so fun. You might struggle at first, but you'll learn and excel so mcuh!

Prof. Howlett was one of the best professors I've had at my time at UNC. He is caring and genuinely engages with students. His grading provides constructive criticism, making me a better writer at UNC. He is enthusiastic and lively, never making class boring. Class feels very short with him!
I loved Prof Howlett so much! Although this class was challenging initially, he gave great feedback and genuinely wanted all his students to succeed. I would recommend him to anyone.

Professor Howlett is awesome! He provides thorough, helpful feedback on every assignment and tells you where deductions come from, which is super great for improving your writing. It's also evident that he cares for his students success and well-being. Take his 153 class if you get a chance!

Professor Howlett is one of the BEST professor's at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. His class is great but he's a tough grader. He is SO caring and understanding. He makes the class fun. His class made me a better writer and gives great feedback. If you need to take MEJO-153 PLEASE pick Professor Howlett as your professor.

If you have the chance to take Mejo 153 with Prof. Howlett DO IT. He's one of the best professors I've had at UNC. His extensive feedback on every paper was so helpful and I'm a better writer because of it. The class does have a lot of papers, but Howlett does his best to make every assignment interesting and a learning opportunity. He's awesome!

Best prof I've ever had. Despite a late class period, he has tons of energy for his lectures and is extremely enthusiastic. He's very knowledgable and loves to talk with the students. The grading criteria appears hard but he makes the course very easy to get an A if you pay attention in class.

The best professor I have ever had!! He is so kind, really cares about each student individually, and gives the best and most extensive feedback! We also had some awesome guest speakers and learned so much. This class made me want to be a journalist! Take 153 with Prof. Howlett!

By far the best professor I have had at UNC! Prof. Howlett is an amazing teacher who made a generally tough course very enjoyable! There is a decent amount of writing, but it is very manageable. The lectures are super informative and are very helpful in becoming a better writer. Above all, he is super caring for his students and is very genuine!
She's really nice… but not a great professor. She's incredibly unorganized, very little in-class practice before exams, and no clear rubric to grade by. I don't feel like I learned much.

One of the sweetest professors you will ever have! I had an assignment where I used my grandpa as a source and she personally reached out to him to thank him for participating. Very lecture heavy but very generous on grading. Midterm and final were pretty easy. Quick grader and good feedback. Couldn't recommend her enough!

She wants to be a nice teacher and brings her students snacks and little gifts, but she's unorganized and unresponsive and very dismissive of anyone whose views differ slightly from hers. I do love her laugh though.

The grading is super confusing. She put in the syllabus that graduate students' grade is based on attendance, presentations, and other assignments, however, after the final, she said that it is only based on the final paper. She then never replied to our emails about our grading components. She is arbitrary, and we didn't feel respected at all.

Dr. Friedman is the best and most caring professor I've had so far in all my time at UNC. She is extremely accessible outside of class and genuinely cares about her student's mental health/wellbeing. She is super knowledgeable about journalism and puts in a lot of effort to bring in real life examples to class and make it fun. Take her if you can!

Dr. Friedman was one of the sweetest professors I've ever had. She cares a lot about her students and would bring us cookies and candy for class. She has incredible experience and insight, but sometimes her grading was a bit tough. If you meet with her and listen to her feedback, getting an A is possible

Dr. Friedman is one of the kindest professors I've had the privilege of meeting. While some of the papers can seem intimidating, she always gives the best feedback and works with you and your needs. I 100% recommend her to anyone who needs to take MEJO 153!

Dr. Freideman is very caring and helpful in meeting any of your accommodations. The grading can be frustrating because points are taken off for small grammatical or wording errors, but she works with you to fix them in the future. The lectures are pretty boring, but it is not necessary to fully listen to do well in the class. Take class with her!

Dr. Friedman is truly one of the most caring professors I've ever had the privilege to have. I had PTSD regarding a topic she went over, and she went out of her way to accommodate my needs. She also gives fair work in comparison to lectures and homework. I highly recommend her for anyone needing to take 153!

Dr. Friedman is my favorite professor I've had. She cares so much about her students and gives really good feedback. She bakes us cookies and brings candy to her office hours. Her grading criteria is very clear, and you can use the AP Stylebook on every test and quiz. I would definitely recommend taking MEJO 153 with her!

Dr. Friedman was such a great professor, she gave interesting lectures and was very fair with assignments and projects as far as the amount of work expected and the grade she gave. She was also very available as a professor and just a genuinely lovely person. Take her if you can!!

Awesome dude with so much experience in the field, but not a great teacher. He has funny stories and lectures, but I do not think I learned anything new. I turned in a few things late, or not at all, with no explanation, and it never affected my grade. Attendance is not mandatory. If you want a challenging class to learn in, do not take this one.

Professor Kenney is a fun person and cares a lot about his students. However, I felt like I learned nothing from this class. Very disorganized, unclear rubric, vague feedback. You cannot reach him outside of class. Definitely not a hard class, but also don't take it with him if you want to actually learn something.
Best MEJO 153 professor definitely. He is an awesome guy who really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well.

I thought he was a great professor! Super chill and never cared about attendance. Absolutely impossible to reach outside of class (never responded to any of my emails) but if I spoke to him in person, he would always be super understanding and helpful. One thing I really appreciated was how much he connected with students and joked with them.
Easy A, but very hard to reach him outside of class.

After the first class I thought it was going to be amazing, but it took a dark turn quick. He only lectures about stuff he wrote about 10+ years ago. He is very political. We only talked about elections and made it very hard to share other perspectives. We were never given a syllabus. The only feedback I ever received was "well done".

You need to do the readings for this class since they're not covered in lectures, but the lectures are fun, engaging, and insightful. I learned a lot about journalism and life, and it's clear Kenney genuinely cares about his students. He is such an amazing professor and I can't overstate how compassionate he is.

Professor Kenney had great lectures on current events - he always had eye-opening perspectives. 

That being said, I had to self-study most of the content because it was disorganized and unclear. Assignments are not hard once you get the hang of it, but it was stressful figuring out what was expected or what I needed to know for exams and papers.

This class was a really cool concept, but I feel like it was pretty unorganized. You really have to take control of this class yourself because not much (if any) guidance is provided. If you go in knowing that, it would make the class better

I love Professor Kenney!! He is such a genuine guy and very down to earth. He cares more about practical experience than memorizing tons of facts, so I definitely recommend. There are a good number of assignments, several of which are to be done and turned in within one class period, but if you work hard and ask questions you'll be fine!

Professor Kenney was really kind and super experienced in journalism, but his class (MEJO 459) was not super organized and could sometimes be a big source of stress for me. However, I learned a lot about community journalism in this class and appreciated the freedom he allowed his students. Super lenient on deadlines.

I took this course in the fall semester of 2022. This course had no clear structure and an overpriced textbook that was not used. Grading was always unclear and opinionated. There was no guidance, no resources and no assistance. I do not recommend enrolling in this course, there are better options. I was constantly set up for failure. Terrible.

While he was a great and fun professor lectures-wise, the structure of the class was stressful and lacked transparency. Very few of the assignments completed were used for the final grade despite his promises of dropping grades and such. Also didn't communicate with the students concerning final exam procedures and left many confused.

This professor was nice all semester and gave solid feedback. In the last two weeks of class, he refused to meet with students after saying he would, only included random grades (different from the grading structure he had said previously), and didn't even show up for the final. Don't take a class from him.

Such a great professor! Learned a lot more about real world journalism than if I were to take a different teacher. Cares more about actual journalism experience than learning all the basic facts. Grades were a little hard since his grading system was more for our improvement than our GPA (although he did give some freebies). Super fun also!

obviously interested in what he talks about but I found the lectures to be extremely confusing and often uninteresting. Simple enough for a gen ed, although the midterm was graded overly harshly in my opinion.

This class was amazing! The work all happens in the recitation, but the TAs are understanding and not very tough graders. Lectures are posted online and attendance isn't mandatory, but classes are quite interesting so I often went to class. One midterm and one final that are open ended and all come from the lectures. Great class overall, recommend!

Dr. Gangi is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. If you are concerned about building your network, he's your guy. He also sat and had lunch with us every Wednesday. If you take his class and he offers it, DO IT. Conversations with him are some of the most interesting conversations ive had in my life. what r u waiting for ENROLL!!

He was a good professor, just a bit hard to follow in lecture, and a bit boring. Just beware of the recitation for this class, the group projects are brutal. Midterm wasn't bad, the projects are so much worse.

Taking notes on the lecture before AND in class will almost guarantee you the information for an A. I slipped a little at the end, but the grading is not as difficult as most say and the material I found to be extremely interesting. Gangi is super knowledgeable and willing to know and help students, just a little intimidating to start.

His lectures are borderline excrutiating to listen to, but the material is easy to digest if you're interested in the material. The class itself is not hard to pass if you go to recitation and put a little effort into the assignments. Gangi is great for providing connections in the energy industry if you reach out to him.

Gangi is a really smart guy, and the content is pretty interesting if you can get past Gangi's monotone voice. The class is project/presentation heavy but is graded lightly. Gangi has a great load of connections and does a good job connecting with students by offering to get lunch with them. That all being said, the class is very disorganized.

Really pretty terrible lecturer, jumps from topic to topic so fast. LOTS of outside work he wants you to do, though it isn't really required. Recitation is helpful, though. TAs are generally good, easy class to pass and attendance is not counted.

Class was very boring, and I found the way he taught to be very boring as well. There was very little engagement during class, but there was also very little work. There is a midterm and final, and I got 100 on both with very little studying. If you're interested in the topic and want a relatively easy class, take it.

Gangi is well-known in the industry and among faculty, so if you get to know him through office hours, he can get you some nice connections. His lectures are monotone and long, often unnecessary when the final/midterm tests only 1 or 2 topics. Most of the assignments are through recitation, but as long as you do the work, you should be fine.

Professor Gangi is a nice guy, but his in-person lectures are unnecessary. He has Zoom lectures posted that cover all the content he discusses in class. Grading all depends on the TA. I had a more challenging TA, and all I heard was how less challenging everyone else's TAs were.

Dr. Gangi is a great person, but a pretty disorganized professor. Don't recommend taking this class if you're not interested in environmental policy and law. He uses a flipped classroom, but it's really a double lecture. Honestly, this class would have been way better if it weren't a giant lecture hall class. I recommend going to his lunch hours!

He does not seem to prepare for any of his lectures, does not post slides either. Invite guest lecturers coming out of nowhere and all contents are tested. Close note essays for final which is nightmare. All homework done in recitation. (edit: TA really tried her best to save our grades by giving a 99 percent to final paper)

Prof. Gangi is a cool prof, held office hours during his lunch, knowledgeable, willing to answer questions. His lectures are sketchy, no PP slides posted probably for that reason. Heavily relies on guest speakers who don't stick to his curriculum. His TA's run recitation hours & grade the work, don't qualify for the job--shallow and arrogant. Run!

Professor Gangi is one of the best lecturers I've ever had! If you can get past his monotone delivery, he has so many interesting things to say and really gets you thinking about the material. Come to class though and take notes — the exams are hard and are worth a lot of your grade! Join him for lunch after class if you can — he's a cool guy.

Not sure why theres so much bad feedback. If your any env related major take this! Yes, online lectures are annoying but get they get shorter. Did not put any work into this class and got a 97. Very fun guy and has LOTS of connections if you need it. Theres also not much work in recitation, one group project and then main paper. 10/10 recommend.
Amazing classic archetype professor, but keeps up with current events and vibes. Cannot recommend Greg enough.

Gangi's lectures can be hit-or-miss, but the recitation is where the real learning happens. Attend faithfully and supplement with resources like unstuckstudy - that combo should set you up for success in this manageable course.

Dr. Greg teaches diverse topics centering on sustainability. I learned a lot from his lecture. However, this course is only graded by TA. The exams and group projects are hard and intense. I put much effort and time but the grade was not reflected. Need to do reading/watch lectures/take notes forehand. Overall, still learned a lot from Dr. Greg.

This class was okay, attendance in recitation and putting in the work there really matters to get a good grade. Even as an environmental major, I find Professor Gangi to be pretty insufferable as a lecturer and person in general, even though he is very well connected. Although a manageable A, I wouldn't say this class is an easy A.

Professor Hatcher is THE BEST. I will be enrolling in every single class he will teach at UNC. This class offers good finance basics that everyone should know and Professor Hatcher does an amazing job going over them. Attendance is part of your grade, but it really is not hard to show up to this class. All assignments are basically group projects.

He is AMAZING!!!! Truly cares about his students, which you don't find much of here!!! 3 take-home assignments, which are easy A's, and he leaves you an optional question to check in with him on each one- genuinely so nice. Please take this class, David Hatcher is awesome!!!!!!!!!!!

Professor Hatcher is probably the most caring professor at UNC. Sweetest dude and really cares about what he is teaching. He is very accessible and is always willing to help! Highly recommend if you want an easy A and to have a professor who is willing to help you; classes are also very interesting.

Professor Hatch is amazing. He has no exams and very little readings/homework. Still, I learned a ton. His experience working for Duke Energy made his lectures especially interesting. He broke down big concepts in a great way, allowing me to understand concepts that I otherwise definitely wouldn't. Love him! Great guy, great teacher.

Professor Hatcher is the most caring professor you will find and wants you to come to him with questions and will always accommodate your needs. His class is mostly lectures which are sometimes hard to follow as there is not a clear outline of what the class is about. However there is very little work but a few group projects (graded fairly easy).

Highly recommend! Very easy course. Dr. Hatcher cares about his students and wants them to do well. Overall, I am not someone who cares about energy, but I learned a lot. He assigned 4 take-home assignments and 4 group projects + presentations. He definitely goes on tangents in his lectures, but participation matters in this class and was an easy A
One the most knowledgeable and caring professors I've ever had at UNC. Take this class.

307 is my first class at UNC that's actually an easy A. I learned a good bit and the class had zero pressure. Hatcher is great person and cares about teaching, the class is a little slow but I think it will continue to get better. He gives great feedback, no busy work and he just wants you to learn.
Caring professor who has lots of real-world experience and has interesting lectures. Also brought cookies to the final, which was awesome. Take him if you get the chance.

Professor Hatcher is by far one of my favorite professors at UNC. He is extremely kind, encouraging and passionate. His class was a little disorganized at times, but it was his first semester teaching so I'm sure it will improve. He is always willing to help and has great insight into the energy sector! TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!

This was Professor Hatcher's first semester and I think he did great! He's such a caring guy and is always willing to help you with his course. As for assignments, he didn't grade anything super harshly and a lot of it was group based.
Take this class

He's a new professor so his organization was a little all over the place but he was a great professor! He's clearly passionate about what he's teaching and truly wants everyone to get something out of the class. A lot of group work but not too bad. 3 take-home assignments, 4 group projects (including a midterm w/ a paper), and a final policy brief

Professor Hatcher was incredible! This was his first semester teaching, and though he was still getting the hang of it, he was visibly excited to be there and made the students excited as well. There was a lot of group work and opportunity to work on independent projects tuned to students specific interests. Wonderful addition to the ENEC team!

Professor Hatcher was an awesome professor! He cared about his students and always sought to help them in any way he could. The class gives a good broad overview of energy through the lens of CARE (clean, affordable, reliable, enough). It was also a very easy class (3 hw assignments and 3 group projects including the midterm and final).
He is the Goat

COIL aspect of the course was not well executed. Kept content locked and we had to remind him to unlock it. Due dates didn't align with syllabus. Quizzes every class and two ungraded mandatory presentations. He seems like a really passionate guy but did not utilize Canvas very well. Expects previous knowledge of marine bio.

Total of 4(?) group projects, he keeps randomly adding them. Forgets to unlock canvas files. Doesn't answer emails. Exams have niche questions. Questions are worded poorly. Cold calls in class. Lectures are boring. With COIL, this class feels like 2 classes worth of work. Loved him for 490; I dread attending 442. Quiz every class. I'm frustrated.
This class was about corals and it was so interesting. There is a project, but the topic can be chosen for wahtever you want. As long as you try, you will succeed.

Dr. Castillo is a passionate speaker. He is insightful and holds office hours and will work to make sure his class succeeds. I have taken 4 classes with him so far and plan to take more! There are also extra credit opportunities if you go to class.

Bio 457/EMES 442. Long tangent filled lectures. Super unclear exams, that aren't application based & are random facts from one-off slides. This class was sooo easy but when it came to exam time, people lost a lot of points because of how stupid the questions were. Would not take a class from him again.

The professor is very lecture heavy, which are not very clear, and always gives pop quizzes. He has a very intricate and unclear grading system. Throughout the semester he promises that if you do all the extra credit you will be moved up a letter grade but after the final exam he claimed that no extra credit will be given or contribute to grades.

Dr.Castillo is a very passionate professor, he'd rather you actually know the material and isn't too big on heavy grading. Lectures are long but I loved learning about the marine environment. Very accessible outside of the class! Does have a different grading scale but it is more to your benefit.

Do not take his class. Lectures are hard to follow and awful to understand, he is one of the least caring professors I have encountered at UNC. He's quite rude when people ask questions, and his tests are extremely hard. Half the time I have no idea what content we are talking about or why. He goes on 30 minute rants about not sending him emails
Cooke is unorganized, but I've never learned so much from a class. She has passion for agriculture, not for grading. Attendance quizzes are the difference between an A and a B. Loved this class tbh.

If you want to literally never even know your grade in a class then take this class. She makes it a grade to go to office hours and then complains when you go because she is hungry. Every exam is not graded until 1 class before the next exam, most unorganized, rude, procrastinating professor ever and 100% has favorites.

Dr. Cooke is unorganized at best. I found her lectures extremely hard to follow and the criteria for many or her assignments unclear. Her tests are not super hard, but she grades them with little explanation and isn't generous. She is a chronic complainer, grades slowly and will change her mind about test dates and course policies.

Dr. Cooke is very passionate about agriculture and time in the classroom goes by quickly. She is very funny and encourages asking questions, even if she doesn't immediately know the answer. The class itself is very vocab heavy. If you pay attention in the class, you'll pass with at least a B-.

Dr. Cooke is one of my fav UNC professors. Highly recommend ENEC325; truly a class that will make you think and write about complex, important, and relevant world problems related to water accessibility and its implications for humanity. Also, such a funny, loving, passionate, and intelligent person who makes lectures feel like conversations.

I enjoyed Dr. Cooke's lectures and thought this class was interesting overall. The class was a little bit disorganized and communicating with Dr. Cooke outside of class wasn't always easy. Attendance was taken in the form of a pop quiz in almost every class.
Uses class time to rant about her personal life and tries to put her problems on the students. Disorganized & passive agressive

Cooke is unorganized and unclear--not worth the stress. Content was interesting and uncomplicated, the hardest thing is Cooke. She goes on random tangents for the majority of class and then it's somehow on the students that she is behind. Changed Feb midterm grade the last week of the semester and 50% of grade came from assignments in last week.

She is very passionate about the subject and will sometimes get off track in lectures but was an entertaining class to be a part of. Pop quizzes were a little annoying but they got easier as the semester progressed and basically became participation credit.

Professor Cooke is kind and gives interesting lectures if you like this topic. However, she was a little disorganized and sometimes loses her train of thought. She gives pop quizzes and exams that require that you to do the readings and pay attention. There are two group projects and some short papers. This class requires decent effort to do well.

I was going to give her a 4/5 but I am giving her a 5/5 because she's hilarious, nice, and deserves way higher of a rating average than a 3.4 overall. Super knowledgable and helpful if you're struggling.

Dr.Cooke is unprofessional and likes to use class as a time to rant about her personal problems. Personality aside, this class was easy for an upper-level ENEC class. It did, however, take over a month for us to receive grades on our first exam, and some of the grading is questionable. Overall, if you focus on the lecture material, it's not bad.

If this class had been better organized, I would have loved it. Professor Cooke will have favorites, so make sure you are one of them- go to office hours and try to laugh along with her jokes. HOWEVER she will repeatedly talk about her time in the Peace Corps and make disrespectful comments about the cultures she experienced in Kenya and Tanzania.

This class has so much potential as the content is very eye-opening, but unfortunately, Dr. Cooke does not foster a nurturing environment for students. She has her favorites and makes it obvious. She expects the most from students but doesn't provide rubrics for assignments and grades very harshly. I wish she cared about students more :(

Dr Cooke is incredibly knowledgeable, but also very disorganized. She grades far too harshly for the amount of clarity she gives for assignments, and tests are harder than you think they will be. I like how she designed the class, but the lack of organization made me too stressed to enjoy it.

Dr. Cooke is a very caring person but is not a good professor. The class material is somewhat interesting, she paces well and has realistic expectations. That said, she is very unorganized, is almost never reachable outside of class, takes an extremely long time to grade and often does not come to class with a good attitude.

Dr. Cooke is obviously very smart/knowledgable but she has a rly bad attitude and can be so condescending and snappy. She is unorganized and quizzes us on readings regularly but doesn't make clear what readings are required. She is also a reallllly slow grader and is just not very pleasant to be around bc she is soo complainy, it's a little odd

Is very unorganized with lectures and grades unfairly based on her performance as a professor. Will frequently complain about her workload and vent to her students in a very unprofessional manner. She is very knowledgable about the subject matter but has a pessimistic personality and will snap at students.

Dr. Cooke cares a lot about the topic, but oftentimes is scatter-brained and difficult to get in touch with. It took over a month for her to grade our first exam, and since this course is graded by few things, with 40% being exams and 30% being two group projects, it is easy to not know what your grade will be. She is very funny and kind.

She is so knowledgeable, which is awesome, but is quite unclear about the extent of things you should know for tests. The best thing to do on her tests is just write everything you know, even if it's tangentially related to the prompt. Use all the space and you'll be fine. She's so cool though and made for a fun in-class experience.
I did not enjoy this class; it felt all over the place and I spent hours searching for evidence that didn't exist. The way some assignments were graded were frusturating. Exams were written poorly.

sphg 351 is such a useless class and the instructors do a very poor job teaching it and often contradict themselves. the TAs are what make the class successful. it is an easy class and mostly common sense, but the professors try their hardest to make it as difficult as they can for you. the exams often have so many errors that need to be corrected.

I made an 89.98 in the class and they refused to round up. Would take off points constantly for things that weren't in the rubric. The professors disagreed on course material and never gave clear answers to questions. Straight up almost dropped my public health major because of how bs this class was.

The current rating is accurate. The instructions are extremely unclear for every single assignment, and the exams are very subjective, including the final. Overall, an extremely negative experience, and, unfortunately, it is a required course. Keep this in mind when taking it.

Exams somehow turn simple material into complex questions designed to trip you up. Assignment instructions are unclear and require an impossible amount of information and transitions to fit in the strict word count. TAs will say one thing and then grade differently. Nice prof and lecturer but unfortunately this class is too demanding for its scope.

I've spent most college taking high-commitment, conceptually demanding STEM courses. This class somehow managed to be even more confusing, time-consuming, and mismanaged than those. It's required for Public Health majors, so I can't recommend "avoiding" this professor, but keep this in mind when starting the class. Felt like a hazing ritual.

This class is run like a circus. Northcross contradicts the textbook and other instructors, assignment guidelines are all over the place, and exams are super subjective and insanely hard. She treats it like a STEM weed-out course and demands respect without giving any. TAs were honestly the only thing keeping it from falling apart.

She somehow finds a way to make common sense difficult. Every question on each exam never had a clear answer choice, she was very contradictory in class, and made me want to be a public health major a little less. If it wasn't a required class and she was the only professor, I would NOT take it.
I'd explain my rating further, but all I can really say is that it's nuanced.

The material in this class is not difficult, but:
- Multiple-choice exams with questions that were subjective
- Final exam had incomprehensible sections that were AI-generated with careless typos and errors
- Prof routinely belittles students in class
- Can't answer questions, just says "it's nuanced"
- profs. contradict each other and the textbook

she is nice and i honestly enjoyed her as a prof and tbh the exam she wrote was not that bad, though a lot of people struggled. i think it was bc of little details/multiple potential answers that /could/ be right, but regardless she curved mega for exam 1. sphg 351 just has an absurd amount of work
While the overall course could use improvement, I think that Dr. Northcross is engaged and wants to interact with students. She is super knowledgeable about public health.
Do not take this class.

Class is spent with the first few weeks giving background on environmental health, with the second half of the class spent doing a group project. You can pick basically any topic, so choose something your group is passionate about. Professor-wise, very unorganized- make sure to keep communicating with her. Grade- not too hard to get an A.

Dr. Northcross is a wonderful person, passionate about her work, and wants students to succeed. My main issue was lack of clear instructions for some assignments and some disorganization.  It's mostly a group research project, which can be stressful but also very rewarding. Not an easy FYS, but if you put in the work you'll get a lot out of it.

While I do like Dr. Northcross and think that she's a very knowledgeable professor, I think that ENVR 89 is a very disorganized class. You're basically told to do a research project of your choice and they just let you go at it with little instruction on how you can go about doing this, and the assignments don't have very specific rubrics.

This class is very time-consuming. Dr. Northcross provided little support, leaving me to search for non-existent data on Google for hours. Assignments and grading criteria were confusing, and instructors often suggested restarting projects instead of offering guidance. My advice: attend TA office hours. Good luck!

Grade is composed of assignments that have unclear criteria and grading is very TA dependent. It would often be impossible to find the specific info asked. Felt like attending your TAs office hours every week was required to succeed in this class, effectively turning it into 4 credit hours. This course made me lose my passion for public health.
Seems nice. Grading is harsh and criteria is unclear. Profs and TAs often contradict each other. Just try not to get frustrated and start assignments well in advance.

I thank this class for making me regret gillings and for singlehandedly destroying my interest in public health. Assignments extremely time consuming and grading criteria arbitrary. The teaching team seems to forget that students have other commitments beyond this class and therefore can't spend all their time doing assignments or in office hours!

I'm so glad I took this course. Dr. Banu is an extremely caring professor, and wants all students to feel welcome. She relayed first-hand anecdotes of Middle Eastern culture as she is from Turkey herself, which enhanced my class experience. You are expected to read then discuss the readings in class, but they are pretty interesting.

As a more STEM-related student, I really like her. I honestly have no notes or qualms, just that there are a good bit of assigned readings. 3 online exams throughout the semester but no cumulative final, only a project. Overall an interesting class

Banu is so kind, understanding, and incredibly intelligent. Her lectures were by far my favorite in this course and I feel I learned a lot from her. Doing her readings is pretty important even though sometimes they can be dense and a bit dry. Whenever I felt confused or needed guidance with essays, she was very helpful. Loved learning from her

Out of the three professors for this class, Professor G was the best. She was super engaged with the content and the students and was sure to make sure everyone understood what was going on. The content of the readings and reading quizzes were difficult, but not too bad. She's great, but don't take IDST190.
She was the best of the worst in B&B, her lectures were generally pretty interesting and she wrote clear test questions.

Despite this being a 300 person lecture, Banu was always willing to meet with me and I could tell she was genuinely invested in what she was teaching. Her readings were always easily understood, interesting, and to the point.

Class structure is Professor Martin reading off of slides or having table discussions. A bit of a boring lecturer, graded out of only a few things that aren't worth many points so you have to do well. Very sweet person but the class itself felt like a waste of potential
Easy A, felt a little disorganized

Dr. Martin is a really boring professor and I found her class incredibly disengaging. Most of the work was done outside the class. In class time was almost always spent lecturing. Her grading criteria were unclear and feedback was unnecessarily harsh. However, she cares about the subject. Would not recommend.

Dr. Martin is a jolly good lady, but her lectures can feel a bit stale at times. The coursework and exams are relatively easy though and the required readings are skimmable. Overall I'd recommend the course if you're a geography major or need a gen-ed.

Lectures were boring, but I think if you have a fun, engaging class that wants to converse, it has potential. 1 presentation, 5 500-word journals, and 2 exams. Not an easy A, but if you enjoy learning about experience, cities,  gentrification, and sociology, you would enjoy this course.

This was a really interesting class with clear expectations and a well laid-out syllabus. Her personality might take a little bit of getting used to but she's funny and makes sometimes boring lectures enjoyable. Easy class, but particiption is important for final grade.
Good class for the geography major/minor. Coursework is relatively easy, exams include handwritten essays in which it was useful to be up to date on the readings and course themes.

Nina is an amazing person to talk to, however I don't think she's a good lecturer. I usually do work from other classes in the class and tune in every so often. The class isn't hard, but grading turnaround is long so you don't know if you're doing the assignments correctly for the awhile. She did change the midterm format when we complained though
How has no one here mentioned that she was the bass player in Plumtree!

This class was really intresting and minimal work. There were 10 forum posts opportunities but we only had to do 5. The midterm covers a lot of material but the questions were fair and covered topics covered throughly in lecture. Nina is super sweet and loves new ideas. Participation is 10% but the content provides lots of room for discussion
A class I took to fulfill a gen ed it was very easy, the workload was very light and the lectures were actually interesting. If you are looking for a class to fulfill certain gen eds take it!

Prof Martin is SO funny and I really enjoyed this class. It was very manageable, and didn't require much time or effort at all. Pre-class readings can be skimmed and the grading wasn't harsh. Would strongly recommend this course.

Very easy and interesting class. No technology allowed but also no homework. That alone makes it less stressful than 99% of classes, and it's a bonus that the content is pretty interesting and useful as well. He's a very funny guy as well, super kind. Absolutely recommend any class he teaches.
Insanely easy. All assignments were in class. Very easy exams. Surprisingly interesting content, I often would have preferred to keep listening to a lecture than complete the in class assignments

As a STEM major I loved this gen ed, one of my favorite classes I've taken at UNC. Adrian is funny, honest, and super caring to all his students. The class is composed of "commonplace books" which are quick, not graded harshly at all, and kind of fun. The midterm was easy as well. You should try to do at least 30% of the reading.

Dr. Drummond-Cole is one of my favourite professors! He made a large class feel like a seminar by making space for discussions and creating really engaging participation exercises. The readings were super interesting and assignments were very doable. Just keep on top of the work and stay engaged in class.

Super easygoing and knowledgeable guy -- on the quirky side but he's very genuine. Assignments can get annoying at times but class was okay, grading was clear, but a lot of it is subjective, so you have to make sure you establish you work hard early so he grades you well. Solid class; fairly easy B+/A- but definitely a hard A given grading criteria
Would recommend as a gen ed class!

This is the second class I've had with him and Ben, his TA. They are both wonderful! Prof. is a great lecturer. There are three 500-750 words essay, 2, 3 slide presentations, a midterm, a final, and 10 participation assignments. The essays are graded pretty harshly, but feedback is clear. The participation assignments are easy 100s. Great prof!

Professor Drummond-Cole was an excellent professor to have during my first semester of college. I appreciate how passionate he was about the topics we covered in class. We wrote several short essays, worked through a cumulative blue book assignment, & had a MCQ/FRQ midterm and final. Graded mostly on terms but there were a fair number of readings.
This was the easiest class I've taken at UNC. The quizzes are take-home and the journal entries are simple. Twice a week you have a group quiz/worksheet that is super simple and easy.

Easy class, take it with Adrian. Honestly you are just graded by low amount of assignments and he gives you insane opportunities to get extra credit. Got a grade beyond 100, if that tells u anything. TAKE HIM

Professor Adrian is a great professor! The lectures can be a little boring sometimes but they go over the readings so you can skip those. Attendance is only really mandatory on Fridays, where we do connection reflections(really short in-class assignment). There were 2 group projects that were super simple and 4 papers(350-500 words) in this class.

Absolutely loved ADC but seemed to heavily dock points for presentations (2). Attendance wasn't necessary but I attended and thought his lectures were engaging with passion for the subject. Thought TA was fair, but never gave full pts on papers (4) even when given no feedback on how to improve. The Connection Reflections (10) every Friday were easy

Great professor!!! He really tries to make the class interesting and is always cracking jokes. It's an easy gen ed consisting of 4 short papers (300-500 words), 10 in class participation assignments, 2 group presentations, a midterm and a final. He really wants student to participate in class but never forces you to. Would definitely take again!

This class was really easy but so easy to do bad in if you missed one friday of class or something. Do not expect him to be lenient either, even if it is a university permitted absence (I had COVID and he didnt let me redo an assignment). Otherwise this class is an easy gened to just knock out.

Highly recommend for an easy gen ed, grades are based on 4 super short essays, 2 group projects, midterm, final, and weekly participation grades (really only have to show up on Fridays). Super caring professor who will work with you if you are sick/need an extension, etc. Couldn't recommend more.

GEOG 121 is a great gen ed to take, light workload & fair grading. Adrian sets up class to be easy to succeed. Participation grades, only have to go to class then (Friday), 4 short essays plus midterm & final where you have graded group presentations to review. Lot of readings but can get by w/o doing them. Class was enjoyable & learned a good bit
A really great guy. Caring professor and super easy. 2 group projects with 2 opportunities for +1% on your final grade. Would definitely take again.

(review for 120, not 121)
Adrian has been one of my favorite professors here so far. His class is easy and interesting and important! There is a lot to be learned from his lectures and this class is honestly one of the first times I have looked forward to the reading. TA's were great. The class challenged my view of what geography is. 10/10

Adrian is by far my favorite professor I've had at UNC. I took him for two classes, GEOG 121 and GEOG 460. Adrian truly does everything he can to make sure you get an A in his class, while making his classes enjoyable and meaningful. For one of the two classes, I was sick for an extended period of time, and he helped me as much as possible.

Adrian was one of the nicest professors I had during my freshman year, and you can tell by his lectures that he really cares about the material. There is a lot of reading along with 4 essays, a midterm, and a final. Studying can seem overwhelming given the amount of material covered, but I learned a lot about inequality across the world.

Knowledgeable and kind professor, but the course structure is odd. Heavy weekly reading, 10 TA graded essays with no feedback, and 2 presentations with vague grading. Half your grade comes from very specific open-note quizzes. No way to miss a class without losing points. Interesting class and cool guy, but not the best FYS by any means.

final presentation was a 4-minute 4-slide with three sentences for instruction. no rubric. graded extremely harshly for a professor who barely paid attention, with points taken off for the smallest things. in some cases, students weren't told what they did wrong, yet got deducted many points. promised a few point generous curve, didn't happen.

Way too much work for a FY FC/Launch. Weekly quizzes required a lot of reading and studying, there were weekly essays. Overall he lacked accommodating student needs, would give you a 0 if you missed a quiz for travel/family emergency with actually zero help or sympathy. I would avoid this class if you could. Rude in emails, super subjective grading
Pretty hard, but is managable if you put in the time

stay away. STAY AWAY. professor does not want students to succeed, nor the TA. no feedback, no clear grading criteria. so much extra work. lowkey rude. long lectures with no text on slides, so you need to pay attention for every miniscule detail he says. cannot miss a single class because you lose points regardless. do NOT take for a focus capacity

Professor seems very nice, but the grading isn't very clear. He likes to give 90's instead of 100's on most assignments even if you don't do anything wrong, saying you have to really impress him to get a 100. Most quizzes are also kind of confusing. Not a bad professor but I would avoid the class if you can.

Lab assignments were pretty easy, but point penalties for tiny mistakes were large at times. Our reading quizzes were pretty challenging, but doable. He is very accommodating, and provides plenty of opportunities to make up points for late assignments. Overall, he is a great professor and this was a very interesting class!
had weekly quizzes, really nice guy, would definitely take it again

Extremely picky about grading papers/labs and would take off points for the tiniest things. Also had extremely specific weekly quizzes that were closed note and based off of multiple readings that were laughably long. Kind of nice, sometimes? Kind of also passive agressive.
Pretty straightforward class, interesting (but lengthy) readings and complicated quizzes. Grading was pretty inconsistent, but fair ins ome cases. He did not  fw me but was pretty chill to others.

Do not take this class if you are not good at weekly quizzes on lengthy papers. The quizzes are hyper specific and they are not open note making them quite tricky as they are a large part of your grade. The work wasn't necessarily bad, but Dr. Gray is not accommodating or flexible on any assignments.
Love Professor Gray as a teacher. However, if you are not good at weekly quizzes, DO NOT TAKE. You will regret it and be very sad.

I love Clark! He's so sweet and teaches the class material in a very easy-to-understand way. Lectures were straightforward and you had weekly quizzes (they're easy if you did the readings/or paid attention to ppl presenting the week's readings) and a super quick and easy final presentation. I learned a good amount! Very nice gen ed.

Super chill guy, really liked him. The setup of the class was a little weird- basically every semester he has students write their own variation of the exact same research paper and you work on this all semester. We used Stata but didn't actually write any code. I like how the work was spaced out though, nothing ever piled up or stressed me out.
Geog450/451 was super easy and manageable! you could easily get ahead on the papers and then vibe for the rest of the semester

I'm pretty sure this class is GEOG 451, not 450, but I loved this class! Dr. Gray is a great professor and definitely cares about the material and his students. There are lots of hefty journal articles that we were quizzed on, but if you pay attention to the class presentations on them you get the picture. Easy assignments and open notes quizzes!

This is the most caring professor I've had! I struggled getting labs turned in and he reached out to make sure everything was OK and allowed me to turn them in with limited late penalties. Quizzes were hard but don't majorly affect your grade. Final is a paper which he has you turn in sections throughout the semester. All around just a great guy!
Great class and great professor! Grading criteria is very clear and fair. Always willing to work with you if you have questions and is great at explaining material.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO!!!!!!!!!!!!! SHE IS ON A POWER TRIP

I passed/failed this course and still felt the need to note how bad it was. There were no quizzes or midterms, but the final was 20% with no review session. It was all written responses, and the workload for a 200-level class was excessive. Avoid this class unless the curriculum changes or the professor does better.

Dr. Combs has limitless expectations and seems to be allergic to "handing out" A's. Same with her TA's, who seem to be grading off of vibes and not their rubric. In general, this class is overly serious even though it's basically an exact repetition of PLAN 247. Also, raise your hand in class or Dr. Combs will hate you lol

I enjoyed her for 655! If you do the readings and attend lectures (graded) you'll no doubt do well. The biggest assignments are a group project and a final policy memo, the rest are smaller things (reflections and graded drafts). She has some peculiar requests for submissions so make sure to carefully read the instructions.
Don't take this class if you don't have to.
DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER
She was absolutely awful. Please don't take her unless you need to, she was completely unfair to my group and gave awful grading when there is no rubric provided
absolutely awful. only take if you need the class for the major. yikes

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU HAVE TO! The semester long project is organized terribly. There is so little instruction and absolutely no feedback on the drafts you submit throughout the semester, and of course, there is no rubric for the project. About to take the final (first assessment of the class) however the 3 other assignments are easy.

Dr. Combs was usually an understanding professor, however, if you end up in a group with members who do not care about the class you WILL end up with a bad grade. Dr. Combs was not as understanding as she could've been. Also, group projects are graded harshly when rubrics for the papers and final paper are NOT included and she does not make clear

Dr. Combs is very knowledgable about the subject, but her communication and organization are severely lackluster. For semester long paper, we were never given feedback on milestones and have no idea where to improve, despite this promise being made. Does not make enough use out of the TAs, has a lot on her plate and makes it everyones problem.

I adore Dr. Combs and her classes. She is passionate about what she teaches, and I highly recommend getting to know her outside of class as she's super caring and funny. The course is difficult and she's a tough grader, but you walk away from it having learned so much! I definitely recommend her Complete Streets course if you liked this one!!

She is a knowledgable professor and cares a lot; genuinely sweet. Terrible class. Do not take this class unless you have to. SO SO much work for a 200-level class. Semester-long project was so much work. She gives very little guidance on projects. class is heavily controlled, super detailed for the big size

Extremely boring lectures with a large amount of readings throughout the entire course. A 20-page paper done throughout the course is only 25% of your grade. The exam took three hours had a minimum of 23 paragraphs with other questions and was labeled as a "stress-free process" for the students. She then left before half the exam time had finished

The lectures are boring. There is a lot of reading but I haven't done any of it yet and I've been find. There is a group project with 25% which 2 days before the exam still isn't graded. 3 essays are worth 45% but they were easy. The final will be very content and detail heavy which could be bad.

DO NOT take this class unless you actually want to be an urban planner. So many readings, so much content on the final exam, and recitation is a waste of time. Dr. Combs herself isn't that bad, but her lectures are boring and I don't think she realizes that the amount of work is ridiculous for a 200 level class.

I fully believe Professor Combs had the best intentions but her students were assigned a 20 page paper which was only given feedback on a week before it was due. The guidelines are extremely unclear and only 30% of the class is graded when final grades will be in in two weeks. 20-40 pages of dense reading are assigned before every class.

I enjoyed this class and ultimately learned a lot, but the class did feel disorganized at times. The Canvas page was confusing and work was returned weeks/months after we turned it in. However, for someone interested in GIS, I would recommend this class, as it covered a lot, and Professor Delvecchia was very  helpful and accessible outside of class

Gave many basic assignments, did them all well. Graded 2 months after assigned, I got 7/9 8/12 etc. Couldn't change my strategy for doing those because it was end of year. She gave surprise grade # of perusall comments we made. Never told us to write comments on all but 2. Got a 14/30 on it dropped my grade by 7% got me a B. Super unfair ridiculous
wouldnt take again. Lectures were hard to follow. Everyone completed activities at a different pace. Grading criteria for quizzes was unclear. Not enough guidance

Dr. DelVecchia is sweet but her class is disorganized and her grading criteria is unclear. There's no way to know what she will decide deduct points for in written assignments. 591 needs a recitation to justify the amount of labs. The pacing and structure is nonexistent, and she is unavailable outside of her office hour.

Dr. DelVecchia is the best professor at UNC hands down! She genuinely cares for her students and wants to help them achieve their goals. She will work with you to find what you want to do then help you figure out how to get there. I haven't has a professor as influential as Dr. DelVecchia in my four years at UNC
She is super approachable and passionate. She sticks to policies in the syllabus and doesn't give extensions as much as other professors have because she wants to keep the course consistent.

Professor DelVecchia was very enthusiastic about the content she lectured about. I sometimes felt lost in the class, but I did fine. She prepares you for quizzes and normally offers some extra credit questions. She also drops your lowest quiz grade. There aren't any tests or a final exam, but rather a project. I enjoyed it and would recommend it.
Respectful teacher, really nice. Probably easier first-year seminars based on the course content but she made the class very easy for us.
There are probably better FY seminars to take.

Awesome professor that respects each student! You can tell she really cares about what she's teaching. The class only has a few assignments and a final exam consisting of a paper and a presentation. It's a fun and easy class that I recommend to anyone seeking to fill out a gen ed requirement.

I took this class my first semester and was by far the best class taken at UNC. Not because I have any interest in freshwater ecology-- but rather because I think so highly of Dr. Delvecchia. She is an amazing professor-- cares about her students, is passionate about what she teaches, and grades timely. Take her class if you get a chance!

Dr. DelVelcchia is a kind and enthusiastic professor. GEO 89 is a stress-free class (aside for a 2k final paper) that I always enjoy.

Lectures are interesting if you are invested in the subject matter.
GEO 89 might not be the best class for those with neither a background nor interest in hydrology/freshwater ecology/environmental science.

She is very sweet and caring about her students and is very passionate about what she does which makes it more interesting to learn. The class structure changed throughout the course which made the class seem unorganized. I enjoyed this class this semester.

Prof. DelVecchia's class is one that many people are auto-assigned to and it's not the most interesting class. However, she is clearly very passionate about teaching and she cares about her students. The class could be organized better though.

GEOG115 is a fun class overall. Dr. Cardwell definitely tries to get you interested in the material and is pretty funny. I think this class attracts a weird mix of students who are taking it as a requirement not because they're interested. Most other students seemed pretty checked out but she definitely did her best to keep engagement up.
the class is okay, but the final project is really weird. also lecture itself is not that interesting.

Good and passionate prof. Attendance is random but you could expect it'll be taken at least once a week. Lots of classwork and projects, and lectures can be super boring, but the class is really easy. You don't design maps until the final month of the semester, and for this all you do is follow her guide and watch videos on how to use GIS software.

Dr.Cardwell is great. You do HAVE to show up to class. Pop quizzes for attendance. She never makes you do the group projects at home only in class, so you have to be there. The assignments are not difficult. If you go to class and do the assignments, you will get an A. Also if you don't get a good grade on the assignments, she lets you redo it.

GEOG 370 is a hard class, and Dr. Cardwell's grading system is kind of weird. Once you understand it, though, it is pretty straightforward. If you don't understand something, Dr. Cardwell and TAs are always available outside of class and able to explain stuff in more depth.

Amazing professor, very open to feedback from students, which makes up for some disorganization. Very accessible in and outside of class, and open to helping you troubleshoot. Class consisted of a test, some labs and a final project, manageable as long as you dedicate some effort.
Great teacher, will be taking another class taught by her in the spring. Also took geog 115 with her and she is funny, passionate and makes sure you do not fall behind.

Dr. Cardwell is fair, clear, and engaging. I saw the world differently after her class, and I enjoyed the combination of thoughtful instruction, collaboration with others, and patience from Dr. Cardwell. I'd highly recommend her class and hope I can take another.

Dr. Fuhrmann is extremely kind, knowledgeable and approachable. You definitely need to know your stuff for the exams and come to lectures because you'll miss a lot otherwise (not too many words on slideshows) but he's very open to providing help.

Nice professor, attendance required sometimes for in-class activities. Very lecture heavy & slides are pictures so not much to look back on if confused. Would not take if you want an easy A filler class. Too much work for a 100 level intro class. Does provide study guides for exams.

Good class overall. Attendance isn't required but highly recommended because his slides are mainly images that he explains in class. For a 100-level class, there is a lot that is covered in each lecture, but as long as you ask questions, go to class, and find a good study method, you'll be okay!

Awesome professor, he's so wonderful and passionate, but his class is so incredibly difficult. He's super accessible and gives great pointers for studying, like providing study guides, but the topics are difficult to grasp because there's so much to consider.

He is a good person, and he is so passionate about his subject, he is a big nerd really. He can show it through the lectures. However, be sure to study. He is lecture-heavy and the exams are a significant percentage of your final grade. For a 100 level, this was difficult.

For a 100 level class, it was harder than expected. Exams are 40 mc questions with a extra credit questions. Slides mainly pictures-hard to go back and review if you didn't get to write anything down. Quizzes, easy but ended up missing one bc lecture wasn't finished but yet he posted the quiz anyway and it is due before class the next day.
he was great

I liked Dr. Fuhrmann but woww this was a tough class to grasp, especially for being 100-level. Every little thing he says in lecture is important, and he puts almost nothing on the slides besides images, so if you miss one class you miss a TON. Majority of class was not confident about the final or final project (which was also quite confusing).

Nice professor, attendance required sometimes for in-class activities. Very lecture heavy & slides are pictures so not much to look back on if confused. Would not take if you want an easy A filler class. Too much work for a 100 level intro class. Does provide study guides for exams.

Wonderful professor, but the material was pretty complicated for a 100-level class. He gives study guides, but please be careful and just study all the slides; don't rely on them entirely. The slides also don't give much information, so make sure you go to lectures even though attendance isn't required.

This class was such a breeze! Not only was Professor Fuhrmann an amazing lecturer, the content was interesting and exams are straightforward. He is overall just a cool guy. The one drawback is that he often 'begins' his lectures with a review of last class content, but it gets repetitive and half the class becomes review from just a day or two ago.

Love Professor Fuhrmann and highly recommend him for C&I 1 and 2. The class is not necessarily easy but if you genuinely like ancient culture (greeks, romans, etc), you will do great in this class. Prof Fuhrmann is also the funniest teacher I have had so far in college and he gives good feedback on papers. You wont regret taking his class!

Cool guy and very knowledgeable in the field. This class could be hard at points, but the study guides are handy and extra credit questions are on every exam. Graded on 4 exams, in-class activities, open-book quizzes, and a project. The project criteria was a bit confusing but ended up getting cleared up. Make sure to pay attention in lecture.

The instructions for the weather project (and the weather project itself, really) suck, but that's not a reflection of Dr. Furhmann (I just don't think the department realizes it sucks). A lot of what Dr. Furhmann says isn't written down anywhere on the slides so you've got to really be paying attention. Helpful study guides and review before exams

Dr. Olson is incredible. I took this course twice to conduct two different independent studies and they will forever be the highlight of my college experience. She cares so unc about her students, is open to learning from your perspective, and is an incredibly wise person. Take her classes and get to know her; you won't be disappointed!

Dr. Olson was my far my favorite professor this semester. She is incredibly intelligent, yet has such a gentle and kind manner and is always so encouraging. Geog 130 isn't necessarily an "easy A," but with some work and participation (definitely go to class every day), it's not bad at all. Would highly recommend Dr. Olson!

Olson made every lecture interesting and engaging! She is truly someone who cares about her work and knows what she is talking about. Her work and exams are fairly easy, and she always gives feedback. She will tell you this, but make sure you listen and participate in class and it will help A LOT for exams! Listen to all of her key concepts!!!!

*Review for IDST-116 (Gender)* Overall, Professor Olson is great. You can tell she cares about her students learning the material and succeeding. There are a lot of reading and essays, and geography isn't my favorite, but she really helps you understand geography on another level and is really great.

This rating is for IDST116 - Gender.  Just take another Triple-I if you can.  It's not Prof. Olson's fault necessarily, it's just a slog of a class.  Do not take if you have trouble focusing.  As a teacher, she was pretty engaging and talked about interesting topics, just be ready for conceptually-difficult readings and discussions.

I took GBL 700 as a graduate student with Dr. Olson (class not listed on ratemyprofessor), and I have to say that I cannot recommend this course to a serious academic. The class should have been titled "Globalization Through the Lens of Critical Social Theory", as our readings regularly came from a subjective emotional bias and poor methodology.

IDST 116 Gender: Professor Olson was the best of the three Gender Triple-I professors in my opinion. I wasn't a fan of the class, but Olson herself was very invested in how students were holding up mentally, and was passionate when giving lectures. She's a nice woman who, if you're interested in gender studies or geography, you'd love even more.

Gender 116.001 Triple I. Prof Olson was the best out of the 3 gender profs. She was caring and always asked how we (a 300+ person lecture class) were doing. She remains calm even when Levine interrupts and talks over her. She is wonderful - would not recommend Gender 116.001 Triple I but would recommend her as a professor and person.

Gender 116.001 Triple I. I enjoyed this course, learned loads, interesting topics. Olson was very knowledgable, and nice. Students were able to speak with her after class if needed. Most grading and questions for this class do go through TAs though so my personal interactions with her are limited. Lots of assignments but clear instructions.

I found Prof. Olson's content and lectures for the Gender Triple-I Course to be extremely interesting, and she is highly interested in engaging with students. Although the class overall was challenging, her geography section was really good. I am also conducting an independent research study with her. Do not hesitate to take a class with her!!

Do NOT take gender. Prof olson is rude to answer questions and she and the other gender profs do not listen to any suggestions or critiques, even though this class and the way it's built are awful, and so many students have tried to offer advice. So much reading, so much memorization, and very little help or guidance from any of the profs.

In my first semester, Professor Olson had such a great impact on me. She was by far my favorite teacher and I always looked forward to her class, yes the material is a bit unconventional and some people may see it as boring, but her passion when it came to the class made it so enjoyable and interesting. Take any class she's teaching, she's the best

Professor Taillie is upbeat and passionate but I found GEOG212 to be pointless. Occasional attendance, assignments graded on completion, and exams that took 3-5 minutes to complete felt made it difficult to find the will to commute to an 8am class. Not for the kind of person who needs to be engaged and challenged to enjoy something.

The most unorganized professor ever. He takes forever to respond to emails, doesn't give clear instructions or feedback, and then gets annoyed that the work isn't perfect. Lectures are very long and boring and seem pointless, but attendance is required.

This class was very easy and basic. There are reading assignments and peer-graded essays that make for an easy grade boost. You get a cheat sheet for all quizzes and exams, they tend to have some really out there example questions but, other than that, they're not that hard. There's a textbook but you really do not need it.
Class is not hard, group projects were necessary and worth majority of grade. He is a little disorganized sometimes but I found it never harmed the student.

Really caring, knowledgeable professor. Very easy going and very easy to talk to outside of class. Exams and quizzes can be a bit tough at times but you're allowed to bring a cheat sheet (even for the final) and Dr. Taillie offers several easy opportunities (reading/writing assignments) to bump up your grade.

Professor Taillie is easy-going, funny, and kind. If you talk to him, he is understanding, helpful, and considerate. His lectures are heavy, though... So study. He gives ample opportunities to bring up your grade, and you also get to bring a reference sheet for quizzes and exams. If you take this class, have some interest in the topic, it helps.

Professor Taillie himself isn't bad, very kind. The class and the grading are the issue. A lot of work that often seems insignificant. Cheat sheet for quizzes and tests, but don't always match what was covered in class. Deadlines can also change unexpectedly. Stressful class for no reason

So unorganized. Schedule was inaccurate for a lot of the course readings and some assignments, gave out the wrong midterm study guide and changed it less than 48 hours before the exam, quizzes not accurate on the course schedule.

I went to this class 4 times, never coded anything a day in my life, and I was fine. Prof. Taillie used really intuitive textbooks and assignments, and you were always allowed to refer to them in assignments and exams.
