The final project was fun, and I appreciated the freedom to explore a topic of my own interest. Just stay on top of the homework.

Don't take this class without a basic coding background. I came in expecting for it to be a solid replacement for COMP 110 but we only used Rstudio and focused on maps the whole time. Long droning lectures, moves super fast on examples. Easy class assignment wise, just difficult when asking questions/rude.
He was awesome but if you are not familiar with coding know GEOG 215 will be a lot of work, he is always willing to help but it is easy to get scared if you do not stay on top of things. :)

Prof Callie wasn't bad himself. The class can get quite boring at times, but attendance was not required. The homework's were graded off completion. The tests and quizzes were based off of random things in class at times, but you do get to bring a cheat sheet for all quizzes and exams, even the final.

This is a pretty fun, very laid back class. You have 3 tests, worth 20% in total. The rest is all group project work or individual assignments that are graded kindly. I feel like you learn a lot in this class, but as long as you try and even slightly study, this is a very low stakes class. Great guy, very understanding, and really passionate!

the content of this class isn't difficult to understand, but the quizzes and exams are ridiculous. most of the time, exam content is pulled from passive mentioning during lectures, and the textbook rarely helps in preparation. there are opportunities to raise your grade (reading and writing assignments), but dr. taillie doesn't offer extra credit

Super passionate and makes lectures easy to follow! Readings for each class but the questions on them are for completion. Group project that's worth 30% but lots of small grades associated with it. Exams and final is 25 - 35 questions multiple choice and fill in the blank. Show up to class and put in a little bit of effort and its an easy A.

Really laid back guy, cares about his students. Class is easy but unstructured - do NOT take it for granted. Can skip class but studying after is tricky since slides are mostly just pictures/summaries . Chill group project, exams can be specific with a small # of questions, which can hurt you if you're not careful. Good gen ed to take in any case.

Taillie is super chill, but the exam and quiz prep took a lot of time. For being a level 100 class there was so much that went into it. He would go on tangent's and have random questions on the exams about things mentioned in passing. That being said, there are a ton of opportunities for grades to boost. Also, he records lectures which is nice.
Taillie cares alot about his students and is extremely chill. Easiest class I've ever taken at UNC, lectures are a bit boring but tests and projects were pretty easy.

Dr. Taillie is kind and smart, however he is not the best prof. I left lectures feeling confused and overwhelmed by his explanations. Slides had little/no information and mostly just pictures. I agree with the other reviews saying that he changed the grading scale. If you're seeking a stress-free gen ed/elective I would seriously look elsewhere.

Changed the grading scale multiple times, sometimes without telling us, said the grade differences were negligible (negligible being 2 pts on final grades). Weekly quizzes were so hard that the cheat sheet didn't help. Several questions on 1 exam were on topics we hadn't learned. Refuses to round, doesn't believe in extra credit,DONT TAKE HIS CLASS
incredibly nice and enthusiastic, assignments are clear and concise, sometimes they take forever though so be prepared. he teaches 491 with QGIS if that's important to anyone
Dr. D is honestly one of my favorite GEOG professors! He explains concepts super well and actually seems to care and want to connect with his students. His class is pretty laid back and fun.

Comes off as a pleasant and understanding person but your first conversation with him outside of class will make you change your mind immediately. He's so incredibly condescending and rude when you ask questions in office hours and doesn't actually care about helping you -- instead he just belittles. The TAs were the only redeemable part of him.

This was my first time really working with R, and Dr. D made it super approachable. Everything we did on a "major" grade assignment (hw or project) came straight from an in-class assignment or demo that we had access to. Very easy to do well if you take the time to pay attention to the coding. I thought the class was fun, and Dr. D is a good prof.

I love Dr. D and this class! I learned so much (you learn R) & he was really helpful with feedback & responding to emails & discussion posts. There's a semester-long final project, many coding assignments, demos, and in-class exercises. It's a lot but if you pay attention to his (sometimes boring) lectures and do everything on time you'll get an A.

This class is INCREDIBLY organized and you learn R which is great but the lectures are beyond boring and Dr. D is honestly rly condescending which can create barriers when you need to ask for help. There are in class assignments for "attendance" but on canvas and you can do them from home. Exams are easy and its rly easy to do well in his class

My biggest problem with this class is that he waited till last minute to tell us problems he had with a semester long project. His class is not too hard and very organized which I appreciated. Attendance was not mandatory but there are in class activities (you can do these outside of class). You do learn R by the end though!

This isn't an easy A, but manageable. The class has a ton of assignments and two midterms, no final though. You definitely learn to code R and there's a class website which details all of the content and assignments. However, this guy is condescending and rude. Not a huge problem, but be aware. Overall decent class but I did not like the professor.

While there is nothing wrong with the course content, Delameter is very disrespectful and condescending in his feedback and when students ask questions. Never have felt scared to talk in a class before. For a class about technology, no question is a dumb question. Consider a student might be struggling with serious issues before you berate them.
GEOG 215 might be the most organized class I've ever taken. Everything was very clear and there were several examples given before we were expected to do stuff on our own.

I really connected with Dr. Delamater, and he ended up being my favorite professor. I had no coding experience coming into GEOG215, but picked it up really quickly. The TAs are super helpful too if you get confused. Material is easy to learn, just pay attention and do your work and you'll get an A.
Easy class. Straightforward directions. Can be condescending and assigns a lot of busy work.

Mostly graded by tasks that have very detailed instructions so its easy to do well but the lectures were super boring and frankly unnecessary. I skipped half the classes and got an A. Don't mistake this for an easy class though. Even tho the assignments were handed to you, they took several hours to complete. Learned R but did not enjoy the class

This class was so unnecessarily stressful and Dr. D is the most condescending person ever, he's so mean and degrades you if you ask questions, don't go to his office hours. Lectures are so painfully boring and participation in this class is so obscure. This class would have been more enjoyable if he wasn't teaching it. You do learn R though!

Dr. D is a great lecturer. He is very structured, organized, and transparent about what can be expected in assignments and exams. You will learn a lot about data science and R. My only complaint is that he has the tendency to be condescending and harsh toward students. If you have extenuating circumstances, please don't rely on his understanding.

Cool class. Great professor. Definitely recommend it.  Class is made up of many assignments that are easy to complete with the detailed instructions given. The final Project is a little difficult for me but that was only because my topic was weird. Just pick something simple. The participation grade is weird too, but it's only 5%. Awesome class!

We had 7 assignments, a (pretty simple) semester-long project, & 2 tests. Super easy to get a high grade if you follow the assnmt instructions & study a bit for the tests. He also provides many resources for success with writing the code. The lectures could get boring, but having an easy & semi-fun workload made up for it imo. Take this!

I honestly had no idea what I was signing up for when I registered for this class, I mostly used it to fill hours, but I ended up loving it so much! Dr. D was seriously great in every aspect. The lectures could get slightly boring from time to time, but you could tell just how passionate he was about the content. No coding experience required!

He is very knowledgeable and interested in the topic of the class, with many stories and personal experiences to share. The lectures focused on big picture ideas and were very enjoyable. I would highly recommend the class if you are interested in anthropology.
He is very knowledgeable and clearly cares about the topics he discusses, just overall a boring class and not worth the work.

Great lecturer, I was very engaged even in a longer T/TH block. He expects you to read but he also covers important topics from the readings during lecture. 2 group presentations (can't pick group); some had issue with lack of detail in his rubrics/instructions. He gives off the impression that he wants us to succeed. Sometimes takes roll.

I had Dr. Lentz in spring 25. Coursework was light but I would not take this to fulfill a focus capacity. He had no grading criteria or rubrics, so that allowed TAs to grade arbitrarily. When I asked for specific feedback and which criteria I had points docked from, my TA gave vague answers and was adamant that her grading was correct.
Doctor Lentz

Professor Lentz was a good professor and was available to help with course content. The material was fairly easy, but expectations for the quiz, midterm, and final were unclear, and his advice focused on big-picture themes, while the tests asked about specific details. The papers lacked rubrics, which can impact your grade.
Very few assignments but feedback was delayed. Course content is not difficult. Lectures could sometimes be dull, but not unbearable.

Content isn't hard, but grading is vague and based on just a few assignments with no real guidance. Despite full participation and strong work, I got a B+. Prof disappears for multiple lectures (trips to Singapore, etc.), returns feedback too late, and doesn't put in any grades until they are finalized (likely to avoid receiving complaints).
Only had 5 graded assignments for semester. TAs did most the grading.  Lectures were boring.  He was approachable.   Left halfway through semester to go to Singapore for 2 weeks.

Professor Lentz is probably one of the best professors I have had at UNC. As someone whose major is not geography, his lectures are beyond fascinating. There are two papers, one quiz, and one midterm. There are also readings to do before each class, but he covers the important parts of these readings in class lectures.

Professor Lentz is easily one of the best profs I've ever had at UNC. He is a natural teacher. Very knowledgeable/passionate about SE Asia, genuinely cares, and keeps class fresh with field trips, museum exhibits, and group work. Two short papers + two quizzes; readings are hefty but fascinating. You'll stay engaged and actually learn a lot.

Dr. Lentz is truly a gem. He is so passionate about teaching and incredibly accessible outside of class. Ask him about his research! Get to know him outside of class! Highly recommend for any course of his.

One of the most informative classes I've taken! The quiz, midterm, and final are all multiple choice, papers are graded very leniently. Attendance is not mandatory and if you go, you get extra credit for EVERY time you attend. Uses slides for terms, but most of the information is given orally. You can do very well if you put in a little effort.
Dr. Lentz is very knowledgeable about Southeast Asia and very passionate about teaching it. I found this class very engaging and fascinating.

I really enjoyed the content of Professor Lentz's class, and always found him incredibly helpful outside of class. Go to class and take notes, the lecture content is what he will test you on. The class grade is based on attendance, 2 quizzes, 2 papers, and a final. There is NO 'busy work' which is GREAT!

graded by 2 quizzes short ppr final ppr participation final exam. NEVER uploaded quizzes participation final exam grades.Entered total grades w/o letting us know our exam grade. Rude over email& dismissed my concerns about grades not being entered properly. NOT student-friendly. DONT TAKE. inappropriately calculated grades Not a person of integrity
Don't know your grade until the end of the semester, and is graded by too less things.

This class was very reading based, but if u go to class n pay attention you'll do good. I was reluctant to take this class but it turned out to be so interesting and I actually enjoyed going. Professor Lentz is great and really inspiring, its cool bc u learn and think differently about food and the world around you. 10/10 class. recommend.
You won't know your grade until the end of the semester when they are submitted to ConnectCarolina and unclear grading criteria. not a bad class but not an easy A.
Rude and condescending. Do not recommend.

Dr. Parr is one of the best professors I have had at UNC - he is very caring, and genuinely just wants his students to learn. This is really exemplified with his 'unique' grading scale he has in place - it makes the class less stressful because it's a lot easier to get an A and you can focus more on course content and work than fighting over points

Dr. Parr is a great teacher and a jolly, caring guy. The class was easy but uninteresting. The grading is this random letter scale he made up, but he outlines it very clearly so you know what you need for an A or whatever. If you are taking GEOG 115 he is a great option.

Dr. Parr is the goat. The grading criteria are clear, and he prioritizes the students' learning over exams. With how the class is set up, getting an "A" is achievable as long as you're not lazy. All the resources are there, and the lectures are engaging. Dr. Parr is a cool professor who is willing to help a student learn and grow in the class.
Dr. Parr is the best data science related professor I've had as a data science student. He is incredibly caring, funny, and incredibly engaging in lectures due to his personality.
Dr Parr is so amazing! He makes this class super fun and the content is super interesting.

Dr Parr is a wonderful individual who genuinely makes an effort to get to know each and every student. The class is perfectly structured and the grading criteria is very clear. As long as you do the work and make an effort you can set yourself up for an A rather easily.

LOVE DR.PARR! Took both 215 and 370 with him. You definitely need to learn the concepts because you need to code yourself in the assignments, but 90% of them you copy and paste from his example. His exams come straight from the assessments. Definitely an easy A, but you need to put a little work in. Please be nice and engage in class- he cares.

Amazing, wonderful and intelligent professor. He was so caring for his students and obviously passionate about teaching, which is rare in a lot of professors at UNC. He always makes sure his students understand what is going on and feel comfortable.

Really good grading scheme that made it low-stakes and extremely easy to get an A. If you get an 80% cumulative avg b/w the 2 exams, complete 8/9 assignments, complete 3 small projects, and deliver 1 presentation, you will be guaranteed an A in the class basically. As a teacher, Dr. Parr is accessible and really understands how to teach new coders.
Super sweet guy, absolutely loved his class! He made spatial data science easy for a non-STEM major, which is saying something. 10/10 guy, and I learned a lot from the class.

This class is an easy A IF you do the work. The final project was interesting, the final exam was easy if you come to class throughout the semester, and the lectures were straightforward. I respect Dr. Parr immensely for emphasizing learning over grades in today's academic system. I actually remember everything I learned in this class!

Dr. Parr planned this class and executed it in an organized structure that makes it incredibly easy to succeed and actually learn the material. Assignments are clear and well thought-out, & the course feels planned and perfected. He is also incredibly caring and kind, and makes himself very available to students in and out of class. 100% recommend.

Dr. Parr was one of the most caring professors I've ever had. He is a very clear professor, who genuinely cares for his students and has all the motivations that make a great professor. The TA's I had were amazing too, they and Dr. Parr were always willing to help outside class and never make you feel discouraged. Made me like R!

Dr. Parr's criteria grading system made it very easy to set yourself up for an A in this class. I enjoyed the assignment's in this class, but the lectures could be a bit dry (as GIS lectures tend to be). Dr. Parr seemed very kind, and there was plenty of support offered so that students could succeed in this class.

Grading policy makes it clear what is needed for each grade and helps with stress. Very approachable and office hours are helpful. Beware of pop quizzes though, that is the attendance mechanism. Projects are interesting and the final isn't bad.

The grading criteria make securing an "A" in the class manageable. I enjoyed the class, and overall, he's a nice and chill professor. He cares about your success and is willing to help if you're having issues with software or assignments. It was cool to learn about QGIS, and overall, the class was pretty light.

He is super nice and caring, and his lectures and in class activities are engaging. He used a different grading criteria that made it easy to get an A if you wanted to. There were a lot of quizzes, some of them pop quizzes, but you only need 70/100 points between the quizzes and final for an A. No midterms.

*FOR GEOG 370*
Dr. Parr is one of the best professors in the Geography department, he knows what he's talking about and is willing to answer any questions you have. There were 10 quizzes in this class, some announced and some not (we had 2 in one week once). Grading criteria is different, but it's not hard to get an A.
Literally nicest professor I've ever had. Was honestly unsure of the class before I took it, but he's awesome and the class is awesome.
This class is literally so easy. Great guy. Teaches so well and the assignments are a breeze.

The class wasn't too difficult, but the assignments often felt surface level to me, and group projects were a big part of the grade. I didn't love the lectures, which often felt dry. However, Professor Song was caring and went out of his way to help students succeed.

The material and midterms aren't horrible, but Song is very pedantic in his grading; my biggest gripe though is that he docks 6% of your grade for only missing two classes, which is beyond unreasonable. Avoid if you're looking for a fun, easy A course.

Very easy class if you pay attention to the lectures and professor Song is great. Pretty test heavy with 3 midterms 7 quizzes and an exam but there is no homework besides the group debate project that is too much work and is pretty fun. Professor Song is very nice and a pretty decent lecture so if you take good notes as you go it can be a breeze.

Don't take this class unless you're looking for an extremely mundane course that requires you to memorize minuscule details on weekly quizzes that make up 20% of your grade and exams. Avoid if you're looking for an easy A!

I didn't take GEOG 477, which is a recommended prereq for this class, so I was nervous about this class' difficulty, but it wasn't bad. Just make sure you study for the tests and go to office hours before you get too confused. I'm not sure if this is normal, but he did give us a couple opportunities for extra credit, which was really helpful.

Prof. Song is a great person and lecturer! I learned a lot from his class and really enjoyed the course.  The tests would occasionally include questions on super minor details, but other than that were pretty easy to do well on, especially if you go to class regularly.  Very few assignments outside of tests.  A super nice guy and a 10/10 course!

Incredibly sweet, understanding, and caring. I missed several days due to graduate school interviews and/or mental health reasons and he was so accomodating. The lectures are alright and the class is moderately easy/difficult.

You could tell Purifoy was a knowledgeable professor, but she spent too much time trying to force group discussions in a big lecture hall. I wish she would have just lectured and used recitations for group discussions. She generally picked interesting readings to assign for homework.

This class is just not structured well. Very lecture heavy and no activities, yet prof was confused at the lack of participation and discussion. Topics were somewhat interesting but were repetitive and I never felt engaged. On the bright side there were only a few assignments. Prof just needs to find ways to make class more engaging and interesting

DP is knowledgeable and inclusive of all thoughts, but their class is so dry sometimes. I think the class covers some really interesting topics, but between the extensive reading for class and conversations that are dragged out, it can be hard to stay engaged. Grading is pretty lax- online midterm and no final.

DP was okay. They pretty much only lectured for all of the classes and never left appropriate time for discussion. You are graded on four assignments, two of which are group assignments, and the other two are papers/midterm. DP is a great person with lots of experience but they made an interesting class so dull with endless and redundant lectures.

This class is super easy. We were only graded on 4 things (a reading presentation, an art project/paper, a midterm, and a final group project). Participation is not required. A ton of reading assigned, I only did the readings a few times, and skimmed them before the midterm. Lectures were tedious. An easy A, but I wasn't interested in the material.

I enjoyed the content of the lectures, but after a few weeks it became extremely repetitive. They are very knowledgable, but I found my engagement decreasing as the weeks went on due to repeated topics and 'nuances'. Overall great class topics but a little boring! She's super understanding and great professor to have despite all.

DP is an awesome person and super passionate about EJ but the class can be pretty dull even with cool topics. They lecture at you for the whole class, easy to zone out. It's not required to attend class, but I went to most anyway. Only a few assignments, but easily graded if you know what's going on & put in work. Go to the field trip, it's fun!

I really wanted to like this class, but it is just so boring. Dr. Purifoy is super nice and super accommodating, but this class can seem very repetitive, especially if people don't participate. You're only graded on 2 forums, a midterm, a project, and a final project.

Some people adored this class, and I understand why. It just wasn't my favorite. I'm not a huge fan of the way they lectured, and the forums felt kind of redundant with a load of groupwork (sucks cause no one wants to respond) and your grade is heavily dependent on that. If you go with friends and can do work that way I could see myself liking it.

Although Professor Purifoy is really smart and respect, the class was honestly a little boring though really easy. The class consisted of constant lectures where the students didn't really discuss any of the topics, meaning that I didn't learn that much.
She's just professional and cares about students. She made things more flexible for students even during a hard time. I got more feedback than I expected as a junior. I will say take her class again!

She's the nicest professor I've ever met at UNC! She hopes students can learn from the course and makes the course as easy as possible. The topic is interesting and we have lots of case study about different worldwide cities, such as Chicago, Beijing, etc. She is very reachable after class. I will definitely take her class again.

She cared about her students and was very enthusiastic about teaching. Attendance was not taken and the class was graded by 7 short open-note quizzes, a presentation, two papers, and a final. All were very easy.
She's very kind and sweet, and always willing to help her students with anything.

She was always available to help and had the best, most welcoming attitude. She tried to make learning the material fun and enjoyable, and I believe she succeeded. One of the best professors I have ever had. She cares so much about her students and her field.

The class wasn't hard but him and Professor Havice weren't the greatest instructors in my opinion. I appreciated their passion for Geography but a lot of time they were both borderline rude and made the class kinda uncomfortable sometimes when they'd call out students publicly or make snarky comments.

This class was so unbearable. Everybody was taking this as either a focus capacity or to fulfill their data science minor. They wanted us to be so dedicated to the topic so bad but no one cared. Such a boring class and attendance matters. Started picking on me for no reason towards the end of the semester in a 200 person class. Don't recommend.

Seems like a chill guy, but lots of condescending comments. Blamed wifi. Expect you to devote your life to geography in a 100 level class for data science majors. THE WORLD DOESNT REVOLVE AROUND GEOGRAPHY. Expect you to come to class having done the readings but not doing that. So i just didn't go a lot of times. easy class though

Honestly I dreaded going to this class. Professor was passive agressive and randomly called on us. The lectures were a bit boring to me. Definitely requires some studying for the exams as the material is pretty dense, but making a good grade in the class overall isn't too difficult. Most exams were very similar to the practice ones he posted.

Dr. Riveros-Iregui is so friendly and a very engaging professor. You can tell he wants his students to succeed in class and he'd specify on slides where they would be important in an exam. He gets upset when students don't focus in class or are distracted on their devices, and you get more out of class when you pay attention in lectures.

Big class (~150), but this professor makes a boring subject interesting with his genuine passion and animated lectures. He asks lots of questions, so stay alert or he'll call you out. Tons of material, but his energy and lively teaching make it manageable. He's one of two instructors, and he clearly loves what he teaches. Great engaging instructor

For a 100 level class the coursework was way too involved. For multiple assessments we were split up into small groups with randomly assigned people in a 200 person class, which ofc turned into chaos where nobody could get any work done. Profs were very stubborn to get any real feedback and scolded multiple people during lecture for not listening.
back handed comments, blamed students for the wifi problem, honestly felt like i was in middle school again.

Diego is one of the real gems of Carolina. If you aren't interested in his class topics, I'm sure it may seem boring. But, if you are interested in environmental science (particularly the kind of hands-on science the ENEC department brushes over in favor of more conceptual/political environmental education) you will love geography.

He is a kind person but for a first year seminar I think he was disappointed in the lack of initial interest in geography. He does not do much to spark interest in the topic. Project grading criteria is often unclear. He may be better in a higher level class.

He likes what he teaches, but he's very passive aggressive. The class is a bunch of seniors and it's been clear they don't really care about what they're learning. If he doesn't get an answer to a question, he will call on someone random and saying "I don't know" isn't an option. Exams are all multiple choice and a couple essays every so often.

this class kinda felt like a waste of time, and other students would agree as the attendance of the class dropped so much to the point that they had to do random attendance checks. other than that, the lectures were super boring and felt pointless. class was graded by few things and graded by the ta and was super lenient with grading.

I did not like this class. I felt like the assignments were unnecessarily time consuming and required readings were often long and not posted until the night before class. Grading, however, was extremely generous.

Dr. Riveros-Iregui is a nice person who had great experience and insights into physical geography issues that he shared with students through lectures. However, he did not give off a friendly vibe, and was condescending to students when giving directions or answering their questions.
A lot better than Havice. He did cold call in a 200 person class though. Easy A and was more tolerable

His lectures were harder to learn from as it's mainly graphs, not info. Also tended to cold call more in class which was always stressful. Seems like a nice guy, and the content wasn't awful, but it was hard to retain with the structure. Class is just ok, honestly hated it more because of Dr. Havice, who teaches it with him. Be cautious lol

I thought Prof. Diego was a great teacher! His class may be a little boring but he seems to really enjoy what he teaches which is great. The assignments were pretty easy but this is just an intro class and I am a junior. There were 3 exams, in-class participation, and 3 essays. Overall, I would take him again for sure!

Overall, I really wanted to like this class and like Professor Riveros-Iregui. He's a very nice guy, but his lectures make little sense and his slides are full of confusing graphs. For this class, Professor Havice's lectures are great but I always dread his lectures. Overall, this class is boring and confusingly structured but has potential.

Diego seems nice and that he cares, however, he is not the best lecturer. I got bored a lot in this class and found it hard to pay attention. They also altered the class structure so its more difficult now for no reason. I don't enjoy the class much, don't know anyone that really does.

I literally never showed up and got an A. Really nice guy and passionate about the material. this can be a throwaway class if you want it to be, or a really good class if you're a GEOG major. 3 essays based on articles (not class material) and online exams. TA's were responsible for grading the essays but mine were really easy graders.
LOVE HER. The kindest prof

TAKE HER CLASSES!!!! I absolutely LOVE Dr. Smith! She is the easiest grader ever and is the sweetest person known. The class was a little all over the place but it was so fun and was but far my favorite class. There were no tests or quizzes and had to do some group presentations and two VERY short essays and I got a 100 on both of them.

Sweetest caring teacher ever. I never did readings but still learned soooo much,, seriously a great professor. Group work but manageable and fun. Their was a lot of walking tours which was a bit annoying but it was a great class and 10/10 recommend.
Do not recommend

The class is very easy, and it is even easier if you do the readings. She is a pretty entertaining lecturer and invites a lot of participation. Her class is easy and you will learn a thing or two along the way.

Professor Smith was a fantastic professor. In every lecture, she brings the most enthusiastic energy to students. She consistently makes an effort to ensure that everyone is heard and comfortable and that the topics in the class are applicable and interesting. This seminar is a must-take for the professor alone and made my semester that much better
You will get an A if you put a little bit of effort. Take this class.
Sara was such an amazing teacher! all of her assignments were easy and fun and I enjoyed the content. She gives very good feedback at office hours so I would highly recommend going.
Professor Smith is insanely caring and the course material is interesting as well. Grade is mainly based on only a few papers and group projects which are graded nicely. Take this course with Sara!!!

Professor Smith is the definition of a great first-year teacher. She cared so much about her students and was very flexible with project and paper grades. Lectures can be a little boring at times, but definitely take this class if you are looking for an easy FYS.

Do yourself a favor and snatch an easy A from this first year seminar. If you're not interested in geography it may be boringgg, but if you're looking for an easy GPA booster to fulfill this first year foundation this it. Grades based on three papers and some group work.

I loved Sara, she is probably one of my favorite professors here, she was so sweet, incredibly inclusive, and open to everyones thoughts and opinions. Even if politics aren't your thing, this is a great first year seminar with light course work; only 2 papers and 1 group project. 10/10 recommend this course and prof.
Not a hard class, but there's a lot of work and she is SOOO nitpicky about the smallest details.

Prof. Wise is very strict on her policies and is not flexible with her grades either. She gives out low grades if you don't follow everything to a T. Also, has a bad attitude overall, which is seen through her making faces and leaving cold remarks. She also does not teach much; most of the class is a mix of useless activities and presentations.

She moves too fast, and the class seems like a jumble of weird parts that never truly come together. She tries to incorporate too many different forms of data analysis, so it's hard to keep track of what you're doing and what the purpose of it is. She's mostly nice but the class was frustrating, and I feel like I learned nothing

Dr. Wise is one of favorite professors I've taken a course with at UNC (as a senior). I didn't come into this class with a ton of enviro sci background, but have learned so much through the projects she set up. She has very specific expectations for the many presentations in class but provides clear examples with sound reasoning.
DONT TAKE HER CLASS.

For GEOG416. A lot of presentations. Dr. Wise only accept slides with picture or less than 10 words, so you can't read over the slides. Extremely fast paced as non-geog major. Teammates aren't even helpful, people just work on their own things and said you did nothing in the end. DON'T take this for data science minor elective.

Doctor Wise was extremely kind and her class was so helpful for me! This class is genuinely one of the best classes I've ever taken, and it shows in my improved presenting skills! She is caring and allows for students to grow throughout every class meeting. Would 100% recommend for 415!

Dr. Wise was a very caring professor and was always respectful to her students. I took this class because I heard it was easy to fulfill one of the STEM focus capacities, but it wasn't. The tests were long and had lots of open-ended questions. You have 4 tests, 3 papers, and 3 Storymap assignments on ArcGIS which are honestly a pain to complete.

Professor Wise is super friendly, but she isn't a great teacher. Her lectures are her speaking at you for an hour and are followed by a few poll-everywhere questions. The content isn't explained well and all of the assignments done outside of class don't help. It's a lot of busy work that doesn't prepare you for the exams. TAs are harsh graders

She is a sweet lady don't get me wrong. But she is here for research and it is reflected in her class. The assignments felt like busy work and did not help me prepare for exams. She never mentioned that the assignments and exams would grow in weight as the course progressed. Do not take for an easy Gen ed.

She is so kind and you can tell she cares about her students! The assignments on the other hand just seem like busy work, and the TAs are very harsh graders. This class is overall somewhat enjoyable, but I am only taking it for the Geography Major, not because I am interested in physical geography lol. I'd prob take another one of her classes tho!!

Erika is super nice and if you're interested in climate change/env science, take this class. If not, it is super boring. Tests are kind of difficult and the project was super boring. I took this for the PL credit and there are definitely better classes to take to fulfill this requirement.

I was not personally a fan of the grading scale in this class. Projects felt like inconsequential busy work. Exams were overly specific and difficult. Lectures felt long, boring, and almost never focused on the information that was most important for grades.

***This review is for GEOG110**
I just took this class for credit but was surprised by how much I liked it. It could be boring sometimes, but Professor Wise is a knowledgeable lecturer who tries to keep the class engaging. This semester there were four big assignments that were annoying and long but weren't too hard.

Dr. Wise is very nice and knowledgeable, and the class structure itself was very organized. She returns grades back pretty quickly and normally gives pretty good feedback. The only thing that bothered me is her assignment instructions sometimes seemed vaque, but she grades fairly so it wasn't too much of an issue.

Dr. Wise is so kind and caring. She's extremely passionate about the course material and puts a lot of thought into class lessons and assignments. Each class is different and you always feel like you learn something.
He's the best. My favorite professor this semester!

Cyrus was an amazing teacher. Unfortunately it looks like he won't be back next semester but he made the class so engaging and enjoyable. Everyone I talked to also loved the course. If you ever have an opportunity to take a class with him do it!!!
Quite literally the goat. Super interesting class, and very chill.
Sweetest guy ever, and a ridiculously easy class. Think I will get a 102 as my final grade. Take it
so chill, hes the goat,

Cyrus is absolutely the best professor I've ever had! He cares so much about his students and it's clear that he truly loves what he does. I especially like how he takes the time to get to know students and goes above and beyond to make the course relevant and interesting for everyone. Additionally, if you pay attention in class, you'll do well!
Easy class, take it if you need the credit

Nicest professor ever. Cares so much about his students and their success and is very passionate about the topics he teaches. Not a lot of work assigned, 1 assignment and reading reflection per week and only 1 midterm and final which you can use a one pager on each. Would recommend him to anyone. Take his class!!

Cyrus is the absolute goat. He is willing to work with you on extensions, late work, anything you need. the man would probably donate a kidney if I needed a transplant. homework is extremely light since my class voted to move half the assignments to be optional. extremely easy tests: 1-pagers allowed, hard questions dropped, you can get points back
I haven't finished the class yet, but i dont need to. It was that easy. I already got an A+ and its September.
Made the class as easy as possible. Never studied a single bit, too bad he's leaving

Cyrus's lectures were easy to understand and very informative. Expectations for exams were clear and grading was pretty straightforward. He allows one-pagers on exams and as long as you pay attention to lectures/participate in the class activities you'll get a good grade. Class activities were helpful in understanding the course material.

Cyrus is an awesome professor. He is very knowledgeable and has many anecdotes and stories from his past experiences that make the class engaging. Very accommodating and understanding if you communicate with him about any questions or need help. I learned a lot from this class. We did focus more on sub-Saharan Africa than on other regions, though.
Very respectable and understanding professor. Very clear expectations if you want to succeed in this course. Would highly recommend IMO. Interesting material too.

I liked Kirsch - I could see how you could view his lectures as boring, but if you're at all interested in our modern interconnected world, there's a lot of interesting material. Often relates in-class regions to his own global travels. Quizzes are multiple choice and can be on fine details, but if you take thorough notes, the class is really easy.

Get ready to pay attention to this class, and don't be fooled by earlier reviews, since he grades harshly, covers very broad content with little depth but lectures are incredibly boring. Syllabus and readings are only guidelines and you really cannot predict what is required. Not an easy A if you need it for Global Studies

There are nothing important on the slides, and he NO LONGER RECORDS COURSES. He doesn't provide practice problems so prepare to lose many points in Quizzes. 2 xtra credit opportunities directly added to final grade. Despite these he focuses on Asia (Phillippines) and is a quite interesting guy to talk with.

Knowledgeable about the material but can ramble at times. The quizzes ask very specific questions; past slides are accessible but mostly contain pictures, the questions require good notes from what he says during lecture. Essays and other assignments are pretty straightforward, if you attend class regularly you'll be fine.

Prof. Kirsch was so funny, I was always giggling up a storm in his lectures. His quizzes are quite tricky with wording; however, if you take detailed notes on what he's *SAYING* in class, and take notes on the actual slide's material outside of class, I can guarantee you an A. (P.S. The final is easier than the other quizzes!)

Dr. Kirsch honestly made me interested in Geography. He is a great professor with a keen sense of dad humor that keeps the lectures bearable on early Monday mornings. I enjoyed this class and found it practical to be forced to view and understand other's perspectives from all over the world.

Scott is an incredibly funny (dry humor) professor who cares about his topics and students. Even though he can be a bit monotone or boring at times, he also is incredibly funny and if you put the effort in you will receive a good grade.
Boring and has favorite students

He's super chill and cracks a lot of dad jokes. Lectures can be very boring (took as a gen ed) but he tries to keep students entertained. A few in-class assignments, and quizzes (50% of grade) are based on specific details from lecture (slides are mainly for talking points and pictures) but if you go to class and take good notes, you'll do fine.

He is a really chill and funny professor, but inherently, the lectures are a bit boring. The quizzes were more difficult than I expected because they were based on specific details from the lecture. You'll be fine if you go to class and write good notes. Overall, it was an easy gen ed with a great professor.
His lectures are mumbling and reading through his prepared lecture draft sentence by sentence. Monotone and lack of emotions and interactions, which makes you feel exhausted and hard to follow.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS unless you feel confident about history, religion, and culture. 
The course blends all these things and compresses them into fast-paced lectures. When you review and remember all of the things and take the tests, you feel betrayed and cheated because he tests on small and detailed things not covered. Tests worth 50%.

Pretty boring and not a great lecturer. He does not take any late work for partial but 20% of the grade is easy mapping assignments/participation stuff. The quizzes and final are very specific and go into minute details about readings and lectures so be aware of that as well.

Lectures are extremely and mind-numbingly boring. Gives a ton of information and drops very niche, unimportant-sounding facts in lecture that end up on the exams. I don't feel like the exam questions are at all a fair representation of what the material covered in the class was. Don't feel like I actually learned much from this class either.

Professor Kirsch tries to make lectures interesting, and they are about 70% of the time if you like geography. Assignments are easy, but quizzes are based on lectures and readings, and can have some tricky questions. I loved that lectures were recorded- this alone makes me respect him so much more and made the class less stressful if you're absent

Professor Kirsch is a very chill professor, his lectures are relatively boring and his lecture slides also have little to no words and there are a lot of photos on them which makes it semi-difficult to study for the quizzes. But he does record his lectures so you can go back to them to prepare for the quizzes since he asks for specific things.

The most mind-numbingly boring class I've ever taken. But, it is not too difficult, and there are a lot of easy "free 100s" assignments. Your grades on his tests pretty much rely on whether you took good notes in class, because he'll test on very specific things talked about in lecture, so pay attention and show up.

Super chill dude but your grade really depends on the TA and if you actually take decent notes. He records class but the quizzes have really random/specific info from the notes and readings so just be careful.
Scott is great and has a quirky sense of humor. He's not as boring as people say as long as you are somewhat into geography and the course material. Good guy and nice to talk to outside of class

Prof. Kirsch is an interesting guy.  To be frank, the course material wasn't interesting to me, but he did a good job presenting information in an interesting way.  If I cared at all, I would have enjoyed the course.  Regardless, it was a very easy class, as evidenced by all the athletes taking the class.  Take if you need an easy gen ed/GPA boost.

I liked Prof Lawton (although idk if she liked me). She starts every class with games and time for us to talk about our weeks. She's also very funny and loves gossip. She did give us maybe 1-3 assignments per week, but I think that's fair for a class that only meets once a week. We also had to write our own plays as a group, which was a lot of fun.

Professor Lawton is the kindest professor I have had at UNC, and she is also so funny and personable. Class is basically just a gossip session with your friends and sharing all your opinions on the reading for the week. It is such an easy A, but also a class that you'll look forward to every week!

TAKE THIS CLASS! Prof Lawton is AMAZING. She cares so much for her students and her grading policy allows for basically unlimited extra time on assignments and you can still get an A. The assignments are graded for completion and a lot of class time is spent playing games!

Professor Lawton can best be described as angel. She is one of the kindest individuals I have ever met. Her passion for addressing intersectionality through drama comes from a deep seated passion for the topics. This class will force you to think and learn, but will be one of the most inclusive and nurturing environments you will find at unc.

Definitely take this class if you can! Professor Lawton is energetic and caring. She always accepts late work and only takes 10 points off no matter how late it is, which was a lifesaver during this course. None of the work is too difficult (you'll get an A if you do it) and the plays are interesting to read. I highly recommend.

Be prepared to read 12 play scripts, write 12 play responses and 12 production assignments, watch 2 plays in theater and write corresponding play critiques. Easy A if you complete all homework, but the amount of assignments can be overwhelming.

Professor Lawton is amazing. She is incredibly kind and caring and extremely knowledgeable! If you have a chance to take a class with her, it is an absolute must. This is a chance to learn from an expert who is SO NICE.
Full of athletes, easiest class I've had at UNC. You just have to go to a few interesting plays and show up to class.

I had a difficult time with this professor. I am retaking since I failed the first time from mental health struggles, and this time I have been struggling with physical health. She has been very ableist and not understanding of my needs, even reprimanding me for being disabled and facing ableism in class. DO NOT TAKE HER.
This was a focus capacity class that was graded extremely harshly. Do not take it if you want an A

Professor Snowden is great! Made the class really fun and entertaining. Definitely need to enjoy theatre to some extent to take this class. Sometimes lectures weren't the most entertaining, but it was fun getting to read the plays and dissect them afterwards. A lot of group work was involved. Overall a good class, great for a focus capacity.

Class was alright, some of the plays we had to see in person were somewhat interesting but overall not too fun of a class. You could tell Snowden felt that her students didn't seem to care too much about her class and she combatted this with 8 mandatory attendance checks which were annoying.

Tons of assignments and can get unlucky with TA grading. Snowden is a knowledgeable professor who loves drama but makes the class difficult. Wouldn't recommend that highly for a focus capacity anymore.

Take DRAM 116 for a focus capacity. Class often ended early, assignments are easy worst part is reading the plays. Graded on attendance, midterm and final (both take home), in class group assignments, and quizzes on plays. Extra credit opportunities. Beware won't round your grade.

This class is a breeze if you put in some effort. Attendance is mandatory, but the workload is light - just weekly reading quizzes and a few papers. Unstuck study was super helpful for prepping for the exams. Overall, an easy A.

Some of the lectures were interesting while others were not at all. Grading is mostly chill except for one review paper, which was heavily weighted and mine was graded by a pretty rude TA that dropped my grade a good bit. There is some group work for attendance that sucks. You have to buy many extra books but you don't really need the textbook.

I wouldn't call the class an easy A, mostly because your grade is HEAVILY dependent on your TA. Some are fine, but others are extremely stingy. The paper was graded harshly, but most of the other assignments weren't too difficult.

Don't listen to these other reviews…people are just lazy. Do the work, you'll get an A. Snowden clearly marks when you need to come to class on the syllabus which is nice. You have to see a few plays at Playmakers. She clearly cares a lot about the course material and is easily reachable after class/by email.

Should be an easy A or A- for any student at UNC. Never went to class other than the few mandatory days. Had to go to a play outside of class which sucked, but other than that, it was chill. Didn't interact with her too much because I was never in class, but when I did she seemed nice. Lots of athletes in there, so you know that is a good sign.

I am writing this as I wait for this class to start (late, as per usual). The papers are graded harshly, the lectures are super duper boring, there is no point in taking this class unless you hate yourself. Seriously trust me on this. (I did get an A though, I just hated it the entire time. Warning, wasn't easy though.)

The class was easy, but Professor Snowden was rude. Reached out to my TA about grades but Professor Snowden went through one of my assignments, left rude comments about what I did wrong, then emailed me back and say my TA was "generous" in grading it. Both the TA and prof held a grudge against me when grading my remaining assignments in the class.

Snowden is so fun and very passionate about drama! The class has a give or take 1 play a week to read, but they are short. There are a few group assignments to be present for, otherwise attendance is optional. You have to attend 2 plays and write only a few papers, otherwise the class is laid back and an easy pass as long as you keep up with notes.

This class was super easy.  If you do all of the assignments with even the smallest amount of effort, you'll get an A.  You must come to class to do the participation assignments and you must see three plays at playmakers throughout the semester.

This class is extremely easy, but also enjoyable. Super light workload, tons of athletes. Simple reading quizzes every week, no need to read in depth (ctrl F will do the job if needed), one paper, multiple choice online final exam, have to go see 3 plays but they are usually really good and fun to watch, it's easy to not miss attendance days.
SO BAD PROFESSOR, DO NOT TAKE HER COURSE ANY MORE!

You dont rlly have to go to class but there are a few participation things that if you miss your grade will drop significantly. Grading depends on your TA. The TA Jack Roark grades extremely harshly on papers and will not accept regrade requests. I wouldn't take another drama class instead.
she was fine and i got a decent grade but if u miss one participation assignment ur grade will tank significantly
LOVE Kathy. She's amazing and cares so much about the department. She can be a little disorganized, and sometimes her grading doesn't match the feedback she gives you, but otherwise she's excellent.

Professor Williams is very passionate about what she teaches and above all wanted students to learn and consider new perspectives. She was an interesting lecturer and didn't assign much work, but when she did it was meaningful and she was more than happy to clarify/provide feedback. I learned a lot from this class and would recommend her 100%.

Professor Williams is just what you want out of a dramatic arts teacher. She is theatrical, fun, and very supportive of her students. For IDST, she lectured about theater as an expressive outlet for incarcerated people and the lectures were always engaging and emotional. She frequently showed the class videos and brought in guest speakers too.
Super smart guy, super fun class. I'd recommend you take it. Dr. Perry is incredibly smart, he knows theatre like the back of his hand. I'd recommend for anyone looking for a FC or not.
idk why I got an A- lol he looks like a chill guy

Mr. Perry is so cool! He is super nice and understanding and patient. You can tell he is super knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches, and it makes the class interesting and fun. Also you learn a TON about analysis. Would 100% recommend, especially as a freshman launch, even if you're not that into theatre, it's interesting.

I absolutely ADORE Mark! This is genuinely the best first year seminar you can take. Even if you don't love drama, the class is very accessible and fun. My class was made of athletes and frat guys, but we all had a great time. Most days we just meditated or had group discussions. Very few readings!
He is really nice and makes class fun and engaging if you read the plays! But OMG, there is so much homework it's crazy. He does allow late work, though, but it is too much homework for a gen ed.
he is so awesome!

Mark Perry is an incredible teacher. If you're interested in the theatre, I highly recommend you take his class. That being said, be prepared for a LOT of work. You'll have to read a couple of plays, buy a pricey textbook (though you could potentially get through class without it), and do a lot of assignments, but class discussions were top tier!

Great as an FYS. It's not a traditional theatre class by any means, and a lot of class is dedicated to community building and reflecting about the world in general through topics like meditation, so if that's up your alleyway (it was for me, but definitely not for everyone), definitely give the class a try. Even if it's not, Mark's a great guy.

Super nice guy. Seems like a genuinely great person. However, this class was a bit disorganized. I went in expecting to learn more about theater and acting and performing plays, but we did a lot of random talking and activities. Like we spent time talking about "mindfulness" and writing journals. Not what I signed up for. Again, great guy though.
Overall pretty easy class, not much structure though. The only real assignments are to journal and thats about it. Just go to most classes and you will be fine.

Nice guy and class is chill. Class doesn't really have much structure, lots of group work and group discussions. Typically only homework is to journal and see shows at Playmakers - when there's other work, you get little warning and syllabus is super vague. He does a good job creating community in class though and it's an easy FYS to take.

Professor is nice and the plays analyzed are interesting, but the way he wants us to analyze is far too prescriptive and there's way too much unnecessary work. Would not recommend as a gen ed. A very late grader with little feedback, and sometimes takes points off for seemingly no reason. I came out of this class never wanting to read a play again.

I wouldn't recommend taking this as a get ed. Not necessarily the easiest, nor the funnest. Lots of reading, lots of homework. He's a cool guy, definitely cares about his job and students, however, if you're not into drama and plays, spare yourself and find another gen ed.

Mark Perry is super nice and funny, however, this class was so much more work than it needed to be for a gen ed. Assumed everyone was a drama major and gave so much homework. Graded assignments harshly and never put in grades, so it was a mystery till the end. Wouldn't really recommend for STEM people, didn't have enough time for this class.

do not take this class. The amount of work given is insane. either have to read a whole boring play and write a response on it or complete 5 assignments before every class which is so excessive for an intro gened. textbook is $80 and then you have to pay $30 to watch 3 plays throughout the semester. grading on profile binders is so unclear
So much homework for a drama class. For the people taking this strictly for gen eds this felt like a massive waste of time.

Genuinely, Mark Perry is an angel. If you ever get the chance to take a class with him, take it. You won't regret it. I learned so much from him in such a short amount of time and honestly it was an honor to get to learn from someone who is so incredibly talented and insightful.

Wonderful professor! Kind of disorganized, but he is so kind and cares about theatre and his students so much. Creates meaningful conversation and watches the metal health of his students. Very passionate and caring. Take Mark's class!

TAKE THIS CLASS. Mark is super caring and kind, he really wants the best for everyone (helped me through a rough moment). I made really close friends + core memories (to this day) because of this class, and class made me feel home at Carolina. Lot of games, group discussions, therapy, and bonding. Truly the best class to start UNC with in 2021.

Everyone in our class bonded this semester through our acting activities, games, and class discussions. The workload was more than manageable so I never had any negative feelings about this class, and our in-class time was always worth showing up for. PLEASE take this class!! It is so much fun, you will never regret it!!

Professor Schwinke was incredibly kind! When reading her reviews I was a bit scared as I am generally a sensitive person, but she did her best to make everyone feel as comfortable as possible. There were many opportunities to collaborate with my classmates, which I feel added to the good energy. I will be taking her again for voice training 2! :)

Professor Gwendolyn was the kindest and most supportive professor I had during my four years of college. The coursework was manageable, consisting of just three short projects (a poem, a speech, and a monologue) throughout the entire semester. All works are done in class. You'll get an A as long as you attend class.

I have no clue why Professor Schwinke has low reviews. She is an excellent teacher who provides an energetic approach to sort of "black and white" topics. This class is not difficult at all. She is a tough grader but if you follow the rubrics for the essays you have nothing to worry about!

Super kind and energetic!! This is a theatre class so PARTICIPATE. Don't be afraid to be/act silly during class -- both your grade and speaking ability will improve if you go along with it. Take this class !!!!!

Gwendolyn is divisive. Some people found her fun, others found her condescending and stressful. Be prepared for her to call on you and kind of pick on you in class. Again, some found it funny, others would get upset. It's an easy class but a strange one! This review is for 154, Performer's Awareness (wasn't available as a class code.)
Very kind and well-respected within the department. The class is fun and I learned a lot. Tia is hilarious

This is by far one of the best DRAM classes that I have taken at UNC. Tia was kind, understanding, and not to mention incredibly talented. I equate her to the raise your yayaya lady because she is a magic worker with her notes and direction. Would 10000% take again.

Such an amazing artist, performer, and mentor. She only asks that you come to class and put forth the effort, so there's not that much required of you time-wise, but you will learn so much! I left this class feeling fulfilled and with skills that I will always remember. Tia is wonderful.
Tia is such a wonderful person and teacher. I loved getting to participate in this class and I found it super rewarding.
Literally the best professor and mentor. Tia is so caring and creates a classroom that feels like a family. I learned and grew so much in this class. One of my favorite classes at UNC by far.
He assigned a lot of reading but the quizzes and tests were all pretty easy.

Professor Bray is an amazing guy! I found all of his lectures super interesting. He is very approachable. There is a lot of reading for the class, but I found all of the plays to be super fun to read and discuss in class. The biggest thing you can do to succeed in this course is just go to class! He highlights everything you need to know!

Prof. Bray is awesome -- nice guy and talented actor. Textbook + plays + slides can be a lot of content, but if you GO TO CLASS he highlights exactly what is important and should be noted. You go see 2 plays IRL and write papers on each. You read several plays throughout the year, all very fun to read + gave lots of time to finish. GO. TO. CLASS.

Jim Bray has compassion for his students. Very easy to access via email. The class can get heavy on the reading; however, if you just attend the lectures and take notes, it's not a hard class. Quizzes are take-home, and the papers aren't too difficult. You will have to go see 2 plays, but they are pretty fun.
Super nice and funny guy. Definitely recommend reading the plays and going to class if you want to do well, but overall an easy class and a great professor.

He's very sweet and the class itself is pretty easy. If you read and understand the plays and the supplemental material you should be set. Quizzes, tests, and papers are all done at home. Midterm was supposed to be in person but that was also tale home. We get a cheat sheet for the in person final. Papers are very easily graded. Great class

Took for DRAM150 (not an option). Jim is a great professor who clearly cares a lot about acting. You will have to get outside your comfort zone and read a full book over the course of the semester. Lots of memorization (it is still an acting class). Be prepared to show up, as you're only allotted 2 absences through the semester. Great feedback.
hes chill. you dont need to show up to class, read the plays, read the textbook or anything. All tests/midterm is takehome, final is in person but its chill.

Professor Bray made classes very fun. Although attendance is optional, it is important to go to class in order to get an A. The class is a little reading-heavy, but every piece given has value. He promoted inclusivity and made sure we experienced readings from many different perspectives and points in time.

Took DRAM115 to fill a capacity, and though I was hesitant at first I came to enjoy this class. Attendance wasn't mandatory but it definitely made tests easier and Professor Bray's energetic personality/passion made me continue wanting to go regardless. No extra credit or late work accepted but that's reasonable given the timelines for assignments!

I took this class to fill my focus capacity and I think I made the right choice. There are a good amount of plays that you're expected to read/watch throughout the semester, but it's nothing unreasonable. Attendance isn't taken but I tried to go to every class anyways because it helped when taking the quizzes. But overall it's a nice easy A class.

Professor Bray clearly cares about the topic and class, but his lectures are truly useless for the grade you get and material. He seems like he wants his students to succeed, and honestly, this class is as easy an A as you can get so shoutout to him. Quizzes/Tests are all online, Papers are basically auto 100s. Had to go to 2 plays but were CLE.

Professor Bray is super funny and kind! I would totally recommend him (and DRAM115) if you need an easy FC-AESTH. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are "pop group assignments" so just come to the lectures. You definitely need to put in the work (going to see the plays, do the readings), but overall an easy class if you do what's assigned.

Professor Bray is easily one of the best professors I've had at UNC. His lectures and slides are easy to follow and understand and his content delivery is very engaging. To do well, you just have to show up and read the plays. Most people take this class expecting it to be an easy A but it won't be if you don't put in the minimum effort.

don't take this class expecting to get an easy A. gave us 6-7 papers this year compared to 2 last semester. Although the papers are an easy 100, In person midterms and final asked the most specific questions about every single little detail about the 14 plays we read, on top of slides material on history. Quizzes every once in a while too worth 10%

Ton of material cramped into a super short time. Had unrealistic expectations about students theater background and ability to comprehend theater. Papers were an easy 100, about plays seen at PlayMakers. Exams included overly specific questions about several plays read across the semester, hard to keep exact details straight with so much content.
professor bray is amazing. he is very kind and thoughtful person and very accommdating. i would recommend taking his class its very easy.
lowkey yeah, its a good car like I would prefer the Mazda but I want a manual with an old suspension.

Prof. Bray is super funny lol. I'm not a fan of watching all the plays from the Playmakers place and having to write a 5-7 page paper after each of them, but he is really funny and definitely cares about his students.
It's the easiest A for GE ever, take him!

Dr Magness is a nice person who teaches well. I have little critiques about her teaching, just the class was unnecessarily hard. INSANE amount of reading, like one or more entire chapters to read for every class. The tests remind me of state testing in HS, so strict. 3 profs, so u have to learn the content of essentially 3 diff classes.

Prof. Magness is really engaging, and her lectures are very interesting for someone who didn't know alot about Jerusalem. She is knowledgeable, but she doesn't post her slides, so make sure to go to class. Also, the reading is ALOT for an IDST. Overall, this Triple I isn't that bad, but having interest in Jerusalem or history would be helpful.

She is really an expert in the content however the lecture is really boring; I slept most of the time in that class. The Midterms and Final were a little tricky but overall, it was decent. You will do good if you know how to takes notes while she's talking and ask questions.
Take this class if you want to learn about past stories of the Bible.

She is really an amazing person as well as the most knowledgable professor in her area of expertise I have ever seen. Class is not an "Easy A" FYS, but not extremely difficult, not difficult at all actually ,but due to her grading system there is a very low margin for error so make sure you never miss class or an assignment.

If you pay attention to her lectures, you will get an A, but she doesn't put notes on the board or post lectures (which also have like three slides), so you actually have to listen to her the entire class time and take good notes. But grading-wise, it was always a TA who was also amazing, a very caring teacher, you have to go to class!

Jodi Magness is super knowledgeable but the lectures are very hard to stay engaged with. She wrote the textbook that the whole class is about, so her slides have no info, it is just pictures with her talking about it, Tests are lots of memorization of details about pictures. Cool class but honestly very boring.

she cool 
the discussions were fun and she was passionate about the stuff she taught about
invited us for pizza at the end of the semester 
we had to write a paragraph before each class about the stuff we were gonna talk about, which was work but it was interesting to think about

Old-school professor; lectures, textbook readings, and exams. Not that I mind; she gives an entertaining, detailed, secular narrative of definitely-not-secular stuff. You need to be interested in the content to enjoy the class (for me, it's to learn about my religion). Still, great, easy-to-read textbook and simple exams; study hard, play hard

This was such a great fy seminar class, it wasn't something I ever thought I would be interested in but Dr. Magness knew so much about the subject she made the class entertaining. Super easy class overall, there is a 200-250 word essay/paragraph due at the beginning of each class but you can knock it out in an hour or less and the professor is nice

Dr. Magness is mad cool. The tests are fair you just have to study for sure. First semester she allowed kids to use technology in class. 1 page papers throughout semester, 2 midterms and a final. Lots of different things to remember but She was so awesome and her computer background is her with Morgan Freeman on a show

While most of this class was based on tests, if you went to class and listened it was very easy to do well on them as they were written quite fairly. She does not post her slides, but had review sessions in class before all exams so it was easy to still get all of the information. She is genuinely very interesting to listen to.

I highly recommend it, even if you're not interested in religious studies or archeology. The homework was not difficult, and the prompts were usually pretty interesting. You can't turn the homework in late, however, so if you're absent, it is an automatic zero. Professor Magness has an awesome attitude and makes the class really fun.

She was THE BEST professor I had this semester and I would 100% take her class again, she is really knowledgeable about her subject and is very caring for her students (even brought a bowl of candy to class every day). Had 200-250 word essay due every class but wasn't really a lot of work since her questions were very clear.

Took this just for gen ed credit but genuinely one of the most interesting classes I've ever taken. You just come to class and listen to her lecture the whole time but the lectures are so interesting that time flies! She's super knowledgeable and wish I could take more classes with her. Definitely worth taking and not hard if you go to class

Awesome professor, clearly knows her stuff. Graded by few things and doesn't post lectures, so if you skip class you won't do well. Three midterms and a term paper, challenging but not impossible with studying.

Dr. Magness is probably THE best professor I have had at unc thus far (and this is coming from a stem major). She is an incredibly engaging lecturer, makes content easy for anyone to understand, and is a really friendly and helpful professor overall. The class is only 4 tests and a paper, but she gives out all of the test questions beforehand!

She is clearly an expert in her field, although at times is a little showy in my opinion. Long dry lectures. You will not get slides so read the textbook and notes for answers to the provided test questions. It is a lot to memorize but if you are good at memorizing you will do ok. She is not interested in interacting with students, unfortunately.

I love Dr. Magness. She is an INCREDIBLE lecturer. I've never taken a reli class and I was dreading it but it was one of my fav classes I've ever taken. She doesn't allow electronics (I promise its not bad, kinda nice) but you do have to go to class for the notes but exams are very fair and if you have Victor as your TA you chillin, he's the goat.

I can't believe she teaches at UNC...there's a reason she flew off to Dubai this fall and speaks at ivy league conferences on the regular. Such a unique personality and respected academic. MINIMAL Canvas usage and not transparent on grading at all---I genuinely didn't know my grade until it was on my transcript. No hw and easy FYSem.

Dr. Magness is an amazing lecturer. She is strict about no phones/technology during class but that honestly helped me pay attention the entire class period and actually absorb what she was teaching. Didn't love that she doesn't post lecture materials (ie slides) after classes, so it is absolutely necessary to take good notes during class.
Dr. Hansen is a really great lecturer, he explains topics really well, and is always eager to answer questions we might have.
Dr. Hansen is very nice and he is open to questions. He makes understanding physics easier, I highly recommend.
Physics is hard. Hansen makes it a little easier. He's great, does a good job in lecture, cares about students, fun guy.
Hansen is so nice and explains stuff so well! Super open to take questions, very understanding
Take this 114 with Hansen; he's the legend among men in the UNC physics department!
My GOATT!!!!!!

Dr. Hansen was great! He made physics easier to understand for such a hard and standardized class. He co-taught my section and did an amazing job. He was accessible, caring, and took questions well. Highly recommend taking physics with him

Physics is co taught and pretty standardized, but Dr Hansen is very fair and understanding. He is also easy to talk to and get to know and seems like he cares about his students. If you truly understand the material his tests are socreable, especially in comparison to tests written mainly under other professors.

Nice person, but not good at teaching. Instructions for assignments are unclear, and grading feels pretty nitpicky. I lost points on a 3D puzzle assignment even though I made six pieces because she said they weren't “distinct enough.” Also be prepared for random pop quizzes on stuff if she thinks people aren't paying attention during lecture.

Do not take this class for a focus capacity. Easy A, but way too much work to justify a gen ed. It is the work of two classes combined. It is very based on group work, and the grading criteria is slightly unclear. Dr. Gillmore is really nice, and is an understanding professor that wants you to succeed but the structure of the class is not worth it.

Unless you really like building things, I would not recommend taking APPL 110 to satisfy the focus capacity. Nothing you do is very difficult, but it all takes a ton of time. Prof. Gillmore is an energetic lecturer and generally amiable, but grading is inconsistent. TAs grade leniently, but she doesn't. You don't know who is grading what either.

Dr. Gillmore is a lovely person, and largely very fair. The assignments did have some confusing guidelines, because the class is taught by multiple professors with countering philosophies. Even with hellish partners in the two major group projects, this class was fairly easy. Start assignments ASAP and have fun in the makerspace.

She doesn't communicate with her TAs at all. They say my design is fine, then she claims it doesn't meet expectations. No clear grading criteria, completely inconsistent. She's passive-aggressive when you ask questions and dismisses your effort by saying it looks “too easy,” so it doesn't count the day before the due date.  This course sucks.
RUN

She is not a great teacher, but she knows her stuff very well. She will answer questions well, but won't explain it properly the first time. It doesn't help that her subject is vast and complex, covering a lot linear algebra, python, and some stats. She is nice deep down, but very protective against students who she thinks are trying to cheat.

she seems to enjoy making her students feel small too much. she bought candy on the last day and walked up to the desks selectively gave them to students who hit some attendance %, she calls on people to answer and will make a passive aggressive remark and embarrass u in front on the entire class, unless u already know python+linear you're cooked

Homework is the biggest difficulty of this course---you actually must know how to code before going into this class. The first 3 HW's will be really bad, but it gets easier from there (coding). The tests are pretty identical to the lecture and are not that hard. While she may seem unapproachable, if you ask questions, she will answer them. Great!

She's not THAT bad. Yes, she can be quite patronizing, just try not to let it bother you. Tests are very similar to the practice tests, which makes it easy to do well if you study enough. Homeworks are LONG, start early and work in groups. She is mostly nice, and clearly wants students to do well.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!

This person is more difficult to deal with than any Physics you would ever encounter.

Professor comes off as patronizing and unapproachable. At that same time, one of the few professors who routinely makes mistakes during lectures. Class is graded very harshly and is honestly not worth the effort (this is probably true regardless of professor). Avoid.

While it's clear that Professor Oldenburg wants to help students, her teaching style can be very condescending at times, which makes it difficult to feel comfortable asking questions. Her explanations are often unclear or unhelpful. If possible, I would recommend taking this class with a different instructor.

Very knowledgeable, but not the best at teaching. She seems a bit rude at times, though is trying to help her students. My main concern was that timely feedback was not available. 50% of the grade is based on a few lab reports and we didn't recieve feedback until the class wrote 3 lab reports (which everyone got around 70%). Avoid her if possible.
