do not take this class if you can avoid it habibi. if you get a lame lab partner you're cooked, if you turn in 5 min late you're cooked (20% pen), weekly lab reports which would be fine if they weren't so harshly graded, super late at grading so my grade was 3 reports behind when i decided to P/F. she's always trying to pick you apart, it gets old.

I signed up for rate my professor solely to write this review. Worst class I have ever taken. She is extremely rude to students and has no empathy. Grading is insanely harsh. Twice worked for 3 days straight to receive D-. I got As in phys118,119, 331, math233 and 383, but this was the worst. If you have to take PHYS281L, avoid her at all costs.

If you are someone who requires additional clarification, don't take this class with Dr. Oldenburg. She will get flustered if you ask her questions and will go off on a tangent about racing. Pick a studio with a TA, not her.

Dr. Oldenburg is very knowledgable and willing to help in studios if you need it. The class in general is a lot of work and studios are long, but they are really useful for understanding 118 and getting a good grade.

Dr. Oldenburg is very smart but if you ask her a question she will not help you. She expects students that have never taken a physics course to already know the content. Take your studio with a TA not Oldenburg.

If this is your first time taking physics, be prepared to never know what is going on. She refuses to actually teach or answer questions. She's quick to point out mistakes in work, but will walk away before you can ask where it went wrong or what to do about it. She will just say "I'm not sure about that" then leave.

Dr. Oldenburg was a good studio instructor. She was very knowledgeable and I enjoyed what she brought to the table. I would definitely describe her as a 'cool' professor; she has cool hobbies and her background is also very impressive. As for the course content, Dr. Oldenburg did a satisfactory job teaching Dr. Jeglinski's materials.

100% recommend taking a class with Lightning. He is an overall great guy who makes a boring class fun and engaging. No homework or out of class work just a few easy quizzes and exams. Brings his dog into class sometimes which is a plus!

MEJO341 is a boring class but Lightning made it so much fun! There's no homework, and quizzes and exams are fairly easy, just be prepared to read. Only downside is it's an 8 AM but it lowkey doesn't feel like that sometimes (+ attendance technically isn't mandatory, he does give extra credits if you come though).

Lightning is the best! Goes out of the way to be accessible during office hours and help with assignments as much as you need. Gives great lectures as well and is very engaging. I wish I could take more classes with him, he's one of the best Hussman professors I've had.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Media Law is not the easiest class, but Lightning makes it so much better. Three exams + five quizzes + participation. As long as you do your readings, you'll be fine. He also curves the grade and offers extra credit, so don't worry if you didn't do well initially.

I had the pleasure of taking Lightning for Mejo-341. He made law material understandable and digestible for someone who has no background knowledge of it. He had great communication, was open to questions, and quickly gave us our grades back. You can tell when someone is meant to be a professor---and Lightning is one of those gems!

MEJO341 is no joke, so do yourself a favor and take it with Lightening. Grades consisted of four quizzes, three exams, and some extra credit. Awesome person - super smart, caring, and engaging. Brings dog to class!

I've never rated a professor on here but I MUST rate Lightning. IF I COULD TAKE EVERY CLASS WITH HIM I WOULD. He makes the information so digestible, holds exam review sessions before each exam that basically tell you what to study and genuinely cares about the success of his students so. much. his dog Bert is adorable and he brings him to class.

I loveeee Lightning!!! HANDS DOWN BEST professor at the j school. He let us color in class, got us all starbucks gift cards and always brought his dog to class ALL WHILE teaching us the material in the most knowledgable and engaging way. I LOVE YOU LIGHTNING!!

If you have the opportunity to take this Maymester course in South Korea with Lightning, don't miss it! He is hilarious and organizes fascinating industry visits to a wide array of Korean companies. Getting credit while traveling with such a fun professor makes this the best class in the Hussman School.

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! 10000% recommend. Not only are the lectures engaging, but Professor Czabovsky really cares about his students and puts in the effort to get to know each of them. We only had two papers the whole semester; they took a lot of time and detail, but they were so worth it in the end.
Lightening was awesome. I will for sure take another class of his. He is super caring and makes things interesting. He really cares about his students.
I could write an essay on how incredible he is. I LOVE YOU LIGHTNING

Lightning is one of the kindest most compassionate professors in the entire world. He cares SO MUCH about his students and wants the best for everyone. He gives extra credit all the time and brings snacks and has pizza parties. So qualified and smart, I adore him more than anything ever. Not a hard grader

Joe is one of the best professor at Hussman school who really cares about his students. He devotes himself in office hours with any kind of concerns or helps that students have. He grades fairly and has a clear criteria on grading. So don't worry so much about your grade and just try to have fun and learn something from his classes.

Joe is incredible. Cares about his students in and out of the classroom! Makes himself available for questions and is so helpful with feedback on assignments. Wants to help you succeed! Bonus points for humor.
A lovely man who wants everyone to do well. I recommend him and the class in general

Joe is a great professor! His exams are straight-forward and he is very accessible outside of class. I'm taking MEJO 340 over the summer with him and he has made the course load manageable. There is required reading (~25 pages per night) but he expands on/explains the readings in class. I would definitely recommend him for MEJO 340.

Joe is the best. If you do not take a class with him then you are making a mistake. This class focused on media in Asia and it was so interesting. I learned so much about another part of the world. The work is not too difficult but you need to stay on top of it. Best professor at UNC.

Rebecca is easily one of the best professors at UNC. I learned so much in her healthcare capstone (MEJO 669) that I can use in post-grad. She's incredibly helpful when chatting about internship and job searches, a great lecturer, and provides the most detailed feedback by any professor at Hussman. I would 110% take a class with her again.
This is a tough class, but very important. I am getting the most real-world experience that I can in a class.

Dr. Fish is one of the most impressive and inspirational professors I've had. She cares deeply about each of her students and all of her assignments and exams are written to cause the least amount of confusion possible. Her exams are very fair and the few assignments we have are also not bad. She brings in cool guests lecturers sometimes too.

Prof. Fish is the reason why I decided to do the focus area in healthcare comms! Her lectures were SO interesting and tests were fair. She truly cares about her students learning what they need in class and in post grad. You actually learn content you'll use in life instead of doing meaningless busy work. I couldn't recommend her enough!!

Professor Fish is hands-down one of the best professors I've had at UNC. I took her for Healthcare Communications, and she made the class super engaging and actually taught skills that are super useful for getting a job. She really knows her stuff and genuinely cares about her students.

Prof. Fish is so caring and she really wants you to succeed! I recommend going to her Office Hours.
The tests go beyond her test review and you will be tested on some specific examples in her slide so make sure to go to class and pay attention to the details.

My favorite professor at UNC!!! I wish I knew about her sooner to take more classes with her. If you come to class and pay attention and study, the class will be easy. You can tell she cares about her students and what she teachers

Prof. Fish is a great teacher and has tons of experience in the healthcare sector. Her lectures are interesting and she really cares about her students and wants them to succeed post grad. Her exams  only covered big topics which were on the slides and readings. If you listen in class and study a little for the exams, its an easy A!
Most impactful professor I have had here at UNC! I highly suggest meeting with her outside of class as she is very interested in each of her students and helping them succeed school/career wise.

This was actually the best class I've ever taken at UNC. I feel like you learn SO many important things that you can really see how you'd use outside of the classroom. Her exams are very fair and always focus on big picture ideas, barely any homework, the most entertaining lectures I've ever had. Take her if you get the chance she's amazing!!!
I love Professor Fish so much. She is a fantastic lecturer and teacher. She cares about her students, and the class is exciting. I wish I could take this class again.

This class was very interesting, and the lab is a good complement to the course. Dr. Goldberg is willing to work through problems in detail, but I found him to be a bit frustrating. He is unwilling to shift the pace of each module with difficulty or student interest. The homework, labs, and quizzes were fairly reasonable.

Dr. Goldberg is willing to work with students and seems to genuinely enjoy teaching. He doesn't allow laptops to be used in class unless he assigns work during class time. He is willing to help if you ask and is overall a very fair instructor.

good enough prof for the class. the class is just really tedious so i wouldnt take it unless youre doing the minor or major or like simulations. hellps if you have a cs background or if you like writing reports

Unbelievably condescending, he WILL find a way to make you feel dumb about something in the class. His lectures are SO boring and there is so. much. busywork. Also, if you don't know how to work MATLAB he won't teach you how to do it, he will just expect you to know -- again, condescending. Take this class with the other professor, not Goldberg.

Not sure why he gets such a low rating - All you have to do is show up to class and ask the TAs or himself for help on the projects. I will say this though, the projects are confusing and difficult if you have little experience with MATLAB. Very group-heavy class as well!

Dr. Goldberg was a little condescending at times. Lectures are practically useless and take up time that students could use to work. Grading criteria is sometimes unclear and projects are very time consuming. Be prepared to live at the makerspaces. I had fun sometimes but overall this class stressed me out. I would recommend a different professor
Liked the class, but the lectures were too long and unhelpful. If you take this class I would recommend taking it with a different professor.

Dr. Goldberg gave heavy coding assignments but did not give enough time in class to work on them. His class lectures were not very useful and often too long. The structure of the class was disorganized and this class is more time-consuming than you would think.

Condescending and unorganized, felt like a bad high school class. Not difficult in the end, but much more work than you'd hope/expect. Lectures serve little purpose but he won't let anyone open their computer to do actual work. Rubrics were atrocious and the even the TAs were confused by the criteria. Fun class in principle but not in practice.

This class was terrible. It took a ridiculous amount of time out of class trying to figure out what he was asking for. The class was an easy A, but take it with one of the other two professors unless you need the gen ed credit.

Goldberg is an OK professor, nothing more, nothing less. He gives unclear grading criteria and deducts points arbitrarily, however, it relatively easy to get an A. Additionally, APPL110 requires a lot of work outside of class (lots of time in BeAM). Take this course if the other two professors are unavailable or you really need the FC-create credit

Goldberg was a fantastic professor. He is a good lecturer, and the class is not too difficult (time-consuming, though). He is occasionally insensitive (as the other comments touched on), but I never saw it in a mean-spirited way, and it never bothered me. He does not take BS though, so he will crack down on you if you try making excuses.

Definitely takes a decent amount of work, especially if you don't have much experience coding, but there are lots of opportunities to get help and guidance on assignments. Highly recommend taking the time to get to know Dr. Goldberg- he's awesome once you get to know him!

He is condescending, and not very good at explaining questions you may have. The class itself takes A LOT of your time so be prepared to work a lot outside of class. There are clear rubrics so you know exactly what grade you will get based on the requirements. I'm not going to say it is hard but it is very annoying

This professor is so rude and does not care about students. He enjoys making teenagers cry and he treats his TA's terribly. Be ware he doesnt teach many necessary things in the course and expects the students to find them on their own.

Great professor. Goldberg cares about his students and is easy to work with. There is a good amount of coding in this class which was a bit challenging without previous experience. Therefore assignment took time but he allows you to work on them in class so you can get support from TA's and classmates. Found this class useful and not to hard.

Goldberg is condescending and gives unnecessarily long, useless lectures. Very specific about what he wants without clear instructions. He decided to assign us a group AND individual LC project despite there being only 4 laser cutters on campus. Easy A, but I recommend taking this class from someone else and ONLY as a freshman/sophomore.
The whole class was made up of individual and group projects. As long as you follow the guidelines and work well in your groups, you will do well. The class was usually half lecture, half group work.

He was an ok professor, but he was vague on his requirements for projects/assignments. It wasn't hard to get an A, but he demands specificity from vague guidelines and even after you have asked him questions, he still takes points off for things. He takes up too much class time with lectures, rather than letting us work on necessary assignments.

Professor Goldberg is extremely nice and seems to enjoy what he does but is just not a good teacher. I had no coding experience and felt I learned nothing from the MATLAB simulations we were forced into. He spends half the class talking about information that could be looked up then gives us less than 20 minutes to do our work.

Dr. Ceballos is a great professor and makes 207 super easy to understand while also teaching you a lot of useful information. Exams are very fair and are designed "for a bad day", so she makes it very easy to do well in the class. Homeworks can get a little tedious but you work in groups, and they prepare you well for the exams too.

She is a great lecturer and takes the time to review everything you need for the class. Exams are very straightforward with lots of partial credit given just for attempting. Super caring and seemed to actually enjoy teaching.

Dr. Ceballos is an enthusiastic professor and helpful professor. Her notes are always organized and well-explained. Her homeworks prepare you extremely well for her exams, since her exams are always easier than the homework. There are times when she goes over her notes too quickly during class, but she posts them online in a timely manner.

She's so nice and genuinely cares about her students. The material can be hard sometimes but thankfully, the homework overprepares you for the midterms and final too. Labs aren't too bad either, are graded leniently. Homeworks are long though so start on those early if you can.

I had her for both BMME 207 (circuits) & 365 (systems & signaling). She is an amazing professor that understands that the topics can be hard. Because of this, homework can sometimes be on the heavy side, but is always worth while and amazing test prep. Never grades harshly and always is clear for dates of tests or due dates.

I had Dr. Ceballos for BMME 207 and she was amazing! I was really scared about the class going in but she took the time to explain the basics really well. She had amazing methods for solving circuits which I had never seen before in other classes. The exams are based off of the homework she provides. I can't recommend this class enough!!!

Dr. Johnson is a very nice woman and interested in helping you if you talk to her. After the first midterm, I attended this class twice and will be easily making an A, although grading is TA-dependent. Midterm and Final setup is very straightforward, essay prompts are clear. Only graded on 3 weekly discussion posts, 2 exams and 2 essays.

Assigns 80-100 pages of dense, philisophical, and academic writing each week. In fact, the readings are so dense that she spends the entirety of class having to break them down for us. Little attempt to make the material relateable or exciting. In recitations, we sometimes sit in silence for over 30 minutes. Shocked at how high her ratings are.

I took Dr. Johnson's class last year FA'24. This class was very interesting and honestly the heavy reading was worth it because she would go over them in class. You should take notes though so you can review for the midterms and final. The midterm exam was a little harshly graded (all of the grades depend on TA) , but otherwise, good class.

I took Professor Johnson last semester and she was very engaging as a lecturer. The readings were always interesting too. My TA was also great, so it definitely helped matters as they are the ones who will grade most of your assignments. Overall, definitely recommend

Good class- interesting and straightforward. Grading dependent on TA, but professor Johnson is willing to work with students in need and available outside the classroom. Wish this class were a bit smaller and more engaging in recitation, but overall a positive experience.

I loved Dr. Johnson! She is very kind and cares about her students. Your TA generally decides grading, but all of them were so awesome! There was heavy reading, but it was usually recapped/worked into class discussion. I truly loved this class and Dr. Johnson and will definitely be looking to take more classes with her.

Honestly, this class was not enjoyable. The writing style for the essays is unintuitive. Instead of making our own arguments, we're forced to base everything we write on the sources given in class. There is a LOT of reading, but you can just skim them, she goes over them in depth during lectures. The lectures about economics were sooo boring.

Took this class for FC-Global and I'd recommend y'all do the same. Understanding, responsive, and kind professor who grades easily. TA who led recitation was chill. Only 2 papers and 2 exams. Content is easy to keep up with.

Paid so little attention I had to look up this prof' name to review. And still got an A. The lectures are a direct repeat of reading: there is no new information. Don't skip the reading, it's more important and detailed than lecture. A few times we watch movie in lecture, ATTEND. Only hard part is midterm.  Easy A, just actually go to recitation.

Dr Johnson is a caring prof but this class was not my fav even as a global studies major. It's organized well but the way it's taught was very vague/broad, which could be an issue of the course itself. She's a fair grader and most of the test is from the readings she assigns - which is a lot so keep up w/ them. There are disc q's and 2 essays.

Dr. Johnson is a such kind professor. She truly cares about her students and her lectures are quite engaging. The essays and exams are fairly easy, and if you keep up with the readings you should be fine. Overall, this was a very enjoyable class.

Dr. Johnson was so amazing... I took this class only to fulfill a focus capacity but it was really interesting. She was so helpful and gave amazing feedback. Not too much work and pretty flexible grader. Only struggle was keeping up with the readings, but overall was a 10/10 class with Dr. Johnson.

The worst part about this class was the slides. They lacked detail so you pay attention in class, which is difficult because discussion can get unorganized. Otherwise, this class is fairly easy, and paying attention almost guarantees you an A. 2 essays, 2 exams, and discussion post assignments. Focus on key terms and the reading assignments.

I really enjoyed having Professor Johnson. She is kind and graded fairly easily. There are a lot of readings and material to get through and it is a lecture-heavy class. There are also 3 discussion posts weekly, but it is easy to do well on it. Overall, I recommend the class but be aware that it is dense and you have to work for an A.

Prof. Johnson was awesome! Really engaging, open to random conversation/questions and lectures are really interesting. We used the textbook a couple times but its on Anna's Archive so just do that or go w/o. Take lecture notes because there's not tons written on the slides - she's super helpful though (answers any Qs and happy to help with papers).

Really kind and understanding professor, probably my favorite I've ever had. Lectures are genuinely interesting and although there are a lot of readings, the majority of them are not boring at all. She breaks down concepts to make it really easy to understand, and is a very fair grader. I would recommend taking this class with her, you learn a lot

Very sweet professor. She cares about students and is lenient with deadlines. Lectures are basically a review and discussion of readings. She says the textbook is required, but I only used it twice, and I could have gone without it, I recommend not buying.

Dr. Berry is very blunt and often comes off as rude, but if you do what is asked of you and show her you care she will treat you fairly. There are a lot of readings, but the quizzes are very easy. There are a few big assignments throughout the semester but if you space them out right it will not be overwhelming.

Super easy class and easy A. However, Prof Berry is extremely unorganized and you never know when you walk in what she is going to choose to ramble on about for well over half the class. I quite literally have never felt like going to class was more of a waste because we often learned nothing substantive. Take for easy A, but you will be frustrated

Fulfills the creative expression gen ed. You must not be afraid to dance in front of others because you will be dancing in every class! First half of class was for lecture, the other for dancing. 2 papers, weekly discussions, 1 presentation. The only true "final" was performing our last dance. You must participate in class or she will call you out!

Class is spectacular. Requires you to get out of your comfort zone and dance, but truly pretty fair grading wise. Just a group presentation, weekly journals, two papers, LOTS of long but decently interesting readings, and a final dance showcase. Really a memorable teacher who cares about passing on her wisdom about Afro Cuban dance.

Professor Berry is very kind but can come off as condescending. If you write to appeal to her opinions and thoughts you'll get an A. Two weekly discussion posts that are chill. Two projects (one about a historical figure and one "study guide"). One essay that she can grade harshly but all you need to do is appeal to her thoughts.

Class is mainly discussion posts, there's two essays and a group project at the end. Most of the readings and work are really interesting and easy. She can be passive aggressive at times and work needs to be precise on her criteria, so just be aware of that, but other than that she's a great professor and I advise you to take this class.

*AAAD89* This is a pretty easy class and was pretty low effort, as long as you follow the directions and try you will get a good grade. 2 extra credit opportunities and many ways to makeup a grade. Sometimes rubrics are not clear though. 2 discussions a week w/ responses, group study guide + essay, 4-5 pg paper, and a final group project.

This class is super easy and chill. Don't really trust low ratings, since this was literally was of my easiest classes at unc and she gives you all of the tools to succeed. If you do the work and follow her rubrics, you would literally have to try to not get an A. She's an expert in the field, and while a little harsh, its just cause she cares tbh.

Dr. Berry doesn't create a safe space to ask questions. She can be rude and off-putting if she thinks your question is dumb. Participation is weighed a lot so unless you love public speaking I don't recommend this class. She is passionate about topics but I always found myself nervous in her class.

She's great because she cares about all her students, but she's a VERY harsh grader I found myself fighting for my life. She does very little in the teaching parts, It's entirely class presentation groups that teach the class. You can't do anything to fix your grade if you mess up, don't take this as a gen-ed unless ur AAAD major/have essay brains.

Firstly, this is a DANCE class. unfortunately, i was unaware of that. i am not good at dancing, so it was difficult to get out of my comfort zone. you dance and learn abt afro-cuba. 2 Group presentations, 2 papers with rubric that was (imo) vague, weekly journals. Dr. Berry herself is great & wants u to have fun, but this class wasnt for me.

AAAD 89. After the rough beginning of the fall semester, she was very understanding of where students were in the recovery process. All of the readings assigned were unique and interesting. She was welcoming to the students in the first-year seminar. We had one paper that she gave us a chance to revise for a better grade. Take a course with her!

For AAAD-89* (FYS), NOT 130. 
Dr. Berry is a great professor!! She really encouraged deep discussions in class and invited us to connect the course readings to our own experience. Expect weekly blog posts on readings, a few essays, and a group project.

FOR AAAD 89*
Professer Berry is honestly a great professor. You can really tell that she cares about her students and teaching. There were no tests for this class as she focuses on readings and written assignments. We had a few essays and some forum posts throughout the semester, as well as some group work.

THIS IS FOR AAAD89.  Dr. Berry was such an amazing Professor. very kind and respectful to all students. She loves participation and group discussion. Class consisted of weekly forum posts, 1 essay and 2 group projects, no final. If you show her you're making an effort its not hard to get an A. 11/10 would recommend.

I really enjoyed this class. Dr. Berry is knowledgable and personable. The structure of the class is paired project presentations and online open-note reading quizzes. I regularly attended but most people did not. There are a few big assignments but expectations are thoroughly communicated. This professor is awesome, take a class with her.

Maya Berry is probably one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She understood that we were not only students but people with lives, struggles, and hardships. She showed students a lot of grace and promoted an engaging learning environment. The course was discussion heavy, and I learned so much about the intersections of Cuban activism.

Dr. Berry is super passionate about AAAD, and her lectures are interesting and inspirational. Grading rubrics are clear. You will get a good grade soon as you show your understanding of the course materials and readings. Extra credit can be obtained if you finish the optional paper. For the final presentation, remember to stick to the topic!

Dr. Berry was such a kind professor! She obviously is so incredibly passionate about what she teaches, which is very motivational. Dr. Berry's class is easy, simply put. I would say that the most difficult part of the class are the reading quizzes, but as long as you read then you are fine! Definitely recommend you take her course.

Dr.Monroe truly was a great professor. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches. While the class comes with a lot of readings, they are always discussed in class. She can be particular about writing however she typically won't take off more than 5-10 points so class exam averages were typically around a 90%!
She definitely focuses on lectures, participation is important. You can get away without reading EVERYTHING but you should read. She's not too tough on grading so just be present.

This class was pretty stress free as long as you keep up with the assignments. Either she grades super generously or is strangely picky. She cares a lot about the subject and she expects students also care a lot, which can be annoying. Definitely likes icebreakers and says "colleagues" a lot.

Dr. Monroe is a really sweet lady; you can tell she is passionate about what she teaches. There are a lot of readings and long documentary-style videos that you should read/scan and watch (in 2x speed) to help prepare you for lectures/quizzes. Most assignments were due the last 4-5 weeks of the semester, definitely could've been spaced out better.

Doctor Monroe is passionate about what she teaches and that is clear in class. Everything I learned in this class was super interesting and connected to each other well. The only really difficult thing about this class was the amount of reading. While some of the articles are really long, reading them is necessary. Little homework.

Dr. Monroe was very passionate. The readings in 286 were lengthy, you can survive with summaries. All quizzes were open note, open book, directly from her slideshows so they aren't hard to get a 100. On other little assignments grading was a little tedious. The midterm and final are very easy to score high if you prepare well.
She does not follow a grading rubric, only basing her grading off if she likes you, and lowkey is annoying. She was horrible and gave horrible feedback on something I corrected multiple times. AAAD89

The readings/assignments aren't necessarily "hard," they just take a bit of time and grading is strict. Also, she tends to be a bit of a talker and is strangely obsessed with the idea of "bonding"
 and getting to know your "colleagues"... erm, anyway. Nice woman otherwise, I just had a hard time connecting sometimes.

Good professor, assigns a lot of long readings but they are discussed in class so even if you don't make it through all of them you'll be able to keep up. quizzes are open book and online with plenty of time to take them, exams were in class essays. Gives a lot of good feedback especially on writing but isn't a harsh grader

Professor Monroe is a teacher who is extremely passionate about the subject she is teaching! She encourages the class to discuss readings in class so I would advise anyone who enrolled to at least skim through and get the basic idea of the assigned readings. Very generous grader if you show that you are engaging with the content presented.

I took AAAD89 and she was a great professor in that class! She was not the best lecturer but encouraged class discussions. There is a good amount of reading outside the class. VERY easy grader and overall nice lady. If you can take this as your first year seminar I would definently recommend!

* i actually took AAAD89

i was so scared to take this class because of the reviews but i honestly had a good time! either her instruction drastically improved, or you guys were being extremely dramatic lol. 

still lots of readings to do, but it's manageable! she's nice and grades fairly. does asynchronous reading days. tons of group discussions

Professor Monroe isn't really a difficult teacher, but much of what she says makes no sense. She assigns extremely long readings, that often aren't even mentioned in class discussion. She's nice in class, but answers questions in an extremely weird way. Quizzes were open note, but exam questions were unpredictable and not previously discussed.

Dr. Monroe has very high expectations for assignments, which will either push you to your best or frustrate you beyond belief. She also tends to answer the question she is expecting to hear rather than the question you actually ask, so you may need to clarify 2-3 times to get the answer you need. Overall good class, but read. the. syllabus.

This teacher has assignments due at bizarre times of day which is most evident in that the midterm was due April 9th (Saturday) at 7pm. I am very anxious about turning in assignments despite the fact I've always been told I'm a good writer because she will critique small mistakes or even creativity.

Professor Monroe doesn't use a rubric and when she grades you harshly, it is impossible to tell where you lose points. She gives absolutely no positive feedback and fails to summarize feedback.This teacher makes me feel horrifically conscious and anxious about my writing. Pretty much expects you to have a private editor.

Professor Monroe is a organized, provides clear deadlines, and sends assignment reminders. She can be a strict grader but there are not many assignments. Quizzes are super straightforward if you do the reading. She is also easy to get in touch with if you have questions. This is my second course with her, she has improved as a professor.

All classes are important because they teach you something, and this class is not an exception. This class taught me to distrust the system, that teachers do not care for your well-being, and that adults will not respect or value you as an individual.

I will be honest, I forgot to check the rate my professor profile for this teacher, and I sorely regret it. I hope that you do not make the same mistake that I did, as it has cost me greatly. I have never struggled so much in a class and learned so little while also being interested in the content.
Nice prof. but constantly canceled class, took forever to grade, and was extremely inflexible.

This was a very interesting subject, and the professor was very nice; however, there were barely any lectures, and the exams were very detailed on things we never covered. There were a lot of readings and movies, and the homework was a lot of writing. For a gen ed class its not worth all the work he assigns and never holds class.

Barely ever has class, doesn't grade assignments until right before the semester is open. Expects you to learn everything at home and then come in and take a long exam. Super nice guy but so unorganized and clearly unfocused.

for aaad356. pretty brutal. does not grade anything. assigns 50+ pages per night and hours of films and documentaries weekly. has long, wordy, discussion posts that he does not grade, and constantly cancels classes and throws off the entire semester schedule, so you never know what is due, when you are presenting, or when your exam is.

Does not grade anything, midterm exams are incredibly nitpicky, and gives 60 pages of reading before each class + 1-2 movies per week. Ridiculous amount of work and not physically possible to do everything he wants for a gen ed.

Relatively easy class, but awful prof. It was clear this class was very low on his priority list. He constantly was late for class, never responded to emails, and regularly posted assignments late. He wasn't there for the final and also never posted a study guide for it. I'd like to think it was just a particularly demanding sem for him, but idk

This class is 1 paper, 2 quiz and 1 grp prjct. Quizzes are hard but some online. Paper is graded lightly, and group project is also fine as long as you try. The topic was interesting to learn about, however doing the discussion posts was a little time consuming so just don't do nothing for the class.

Lots of readings, but can be skimmed. Tests are very similar to study guides. Be sure to actually participate in class. You will get an A if you just do your assignments on time, memorize the study guides, and participate in class.
I thought the class was really interesting! He is very knowledgeable and a nice guy. A lot of reading but homework isn't hard. Highly recommend this class!!

The class was really nice. My class had like 11 people in it. The class consists of two quizzes, one final paper, attendance, discussion posts and a presentation. Everything is easy except the two quizzes and the final paper. Study his slides a lot, like every detail for the quizes. There are questions he asks in class but don't count for anything.

Dr. Camara is a caring professor and engaging lecturer, though he seldom answered emails. The readings are heavy, and there are ten 500 word discussion posts required, along with a group presentation and a final paper which he graded pretty leniently. I made the mistake of thinking this would be an easy gen ed, but I did really learn a lot.

Prof. Camara was amazing and you can tell that he really cares about his students & course material. Released a study guide before the midterms that went over pretty much all the exact questions that would be on it. Required one group presentation mid sem and had a 7-10 pg research paper at the end. Really values class participation, reading heavy
Prof. Camara is actually the GOAT, as long as you do your readings you're gonna get an A in this class. This class gave me no stress whatsoever, if you need an easy gen ed, take this.
Real ah mf

Prof Camara was a very kind professor.This is a VERY easy gen-ed. Two midterms where he gives study guides that are exactly like the exam. The final sadly does not have a study guide. No quizzes. Weekly discussions where you answer two questions and respond to one peer. One group project where you make a presentation and "teach" the class.
If you need a gen ed. Take this one. It is interesting enough and not going to steal your focus from your major classes.

AAAD 303 pretty easy, exams were not too tough, and class topics were interesting and taught a lot about Africa and Islam. Pretty easy A, however lots of readings. Camara is extremely nice, flexible, would recommend him and AAAD 303 if looking for a gen ed.

Dr. Camara was great! Lecture was based off of him reading off of slides and some class discussion. Attendance is mandatory, if you have 3+ unexecuted days, you will get points taken off (like a lot). Other than that, this class is very manageable. You can get away with skimming the long readings as the quizzes pertain to the PowerPoint slides.

Dr. Camara's course was very clearly laid out with an excellent schedule to pace out all the assignments and quizzes throughout the course. He was very accessible outside of class, willing to help clear up topics during office hours, and knowledgeable about his material. Definitely recommend this class for an enjoyable gen-ed!

Professor Camara's lectures are straight-forward and easy to understand. The midterms are based off of past quizzes and the quizzes are from content from the class slides and the assigned readings. He does assign a lot of readings but they are manageable. I highly recommend this class for those whose are interested in fulfilling a gen-ed!

Dr. Sahle is an incredible professor. While the class was reading-heavy, you will be fine as long as you keep up and participate in discussions. I feel like my reading comprehension skills have improved dramatically in this class, as well as my ability to synthesize arguments from different sources. Highly recommend AAAD 403.

Dr. Sahle is methodical and thorough, and expects her students to be the same. She has a deep knowledge of Africa. There are a lot of readings, but they are very interesting. I learned a lot in this class and really appreciate her perspective.

Dr. Regester is very knowledgable about African History! The class is very lecture heavy and does not have any slides, so going to class is important. Grading policies can be unclear at times. I found the topics to be very interesting and I learned so many  things about the African Diaspora.
She is so kind but one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. The tests are incredibly specific and hard to study for.
Such a sweet and knowledgeable person but such a hard class. I really wish I did not take it even though at times it's been interesting.

Dr. Regester teaches you what you must know for exams, but you cannot miss class. All notes are spoken and you will not get them if you do not attend. The paper guidelines are unclear as she gave me an underserved grade because she did not like my word choice and had no comments on my thesis or supporting arguments. Find another gen ed to take.

I loved taking her class (Fall 2023). I will say that taking good notes is required, as the test questions come straight from the topics she puts on her slides...and her slides were not available outside of class. So attendance was required. I loved her class though, all I needed to do was make in depth flash cards and I was good to go on exams.

There is no clear outline for what we will do each day, so you won't know if we are taking notes or watching a movie that day. If you miss a day of notes, you could do really poorly on the exams. She is a very tough grader and doesnt give study guides, which makes the tests really difficult no matter how much you prepare. Lots of athletes in class

Dr. Regester is an overall nice lady and compelling speaker, however, she doesn't prepare students well for exams. Attendance is MANDATORY because if you miss a single lecture it could be potentially detrimental to your performance on the exams. She has no class slides, so when taking notes, you must listen and copy every word she says verbatim.

DO NOT TAKE. THERE ARE MUCH EASIER GEN EDs. She grades the papers and exams EXTREMELY harshly. All the class content is also given orally, with no slides or notes to look on if you're sick and miss class. Overall, this class is very boring, and the grading is unbelievably unreasonable, with points being deducted for the most miniscule things.

Rarely ever showed up and passed. All assignments are papers, which she graded unnecessarily harsh for movie reviews. It's hard to achieve her analytical standards. All of class was spent watching movies or popcorn reading the readings that had been assigned. Find another AAAD/FYS class that you may actually learn something from. Waste of time.

Everything on the tests are from lectures and there is nowhere to find what was on each lecture other than being there and trying to catch every little thing she says in your notes. Attendance and paying attention to every word that comes out of her mouth is pretty much mandatory to pass.

She was very unclear on assignment due dates and grading guidelines. Extremely hard to get in touch with you outside of class. I will never take another course with her. No extra credit and the entire grade is based on 3 papers. EXTREMELY hard grader.
Enjoyed the class content, but your grade is based off of three papers and the feedback is very vague.

She is a great Proffesor but the grading is very harsh. Not an easy A, but a very intersting class. 
If you like writing papers- I reccomend!

super chill and actually very interesting class. you get 7 unexcused absences and your entire grade is just a bunch of little discussion posts. there is a group project but its not hard at all. you would literally have to try mega hard to not end with an A. Professor Samuel was incredibly kind and engaging.

Dr. Samuel is an amazing professor. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. Everything she assigns is discussed in class, so you do not forget. I enjoyed how every topic was discussed in class, making it easier to understand the concepts being taught. I 100% recommend her and would take another class with her.
No exams which is amazing. You are allowed to miss up to 7 classes with no penalty so super lenient. 2 group projects and mini reading quizzes. super easy class and sweetest professor.

Dr. Samuel is an incredible professor! I truly looked forward to her classes every week. The content was very intentional and well-planned out. Her instructions were always clear and she was very accessible in person or via email. I would highly recommend taking a class with her if you can! 10/10 recommend!

Dr. Samuel genuinely made the class enjoyable and always valued student feedback, especially regarding the minimal homework assigned. She is incredibly understanding about absences or the need for extensions. As long as you communicate with her, her class is fantastic, engaging, and highly informative!
She was great! Her instructions were clear and she is very understanding. Just make sure to go to class and use your absences wisely.

Genuinely Dr. Samuel made class great and really cared about student feedback for her course when it came to the low amount of homework that was assigned. She is really understanding when it comes to being absent or needing to use an extension. As long as you communicate with her, her class is great and very interesting/informative!
Dr. Samuel is really caring and gives great lectures! Holds several extra credits at the end of the semester. She also gives 7 absence absence credits so you can literally take one or two weeks off!

I absolutely adore Professor Samuels and this was my second class with her. I would definitely say that I prefer 388 and feel like I didn't learn as much as I hoped in this class. It was very heavy on group presentations which weren't the most interesting but the books were great and I appreciated the space to discuss decoloniality.

Incredibly kind and intelligent professor who cares a lot about her subject and her students. Generous absence and extension policy. Readings were fascinating, class discussions were engaging, and she encouraged participating outside of class. Final is a group project. One paper during the semester, not hard because she gives you tools to succeed.

I loved this class and Dr. Samuel. Class was very discussion based. A lot of reading but it was all really interesting and engaging so I didn't mind it. Grades pretty leniently and gives a lot of absence credits and late work credits. Cannot recommend this class and Dr. Samuel more!

This class was a very pleasant surprise! I was not expecting to get much out of it, because I was not a AAAD major or minor, however it was one of my favorite classes. There are not enough good words for Dr. Samuel, and many times I noticed myself looking at things in a way I never had. The content was also just overall very interesting.

Professor Samuel was amazing! Class was discussion-based with reading quizzes (open book/ no time limit). We had 2 media analysis papers due (3 pages double spaced) and the final project was a mini syllabus in which you can work in a group. Professor Samuel values student feedback and will incorporate that into class. However, she is a slow grader.

Absolutely one of the best professors!! Relatively manageable class!!! Classes are discussion based and Professor Samuel is so understanding and accommodating. We had readings each week, reading quizzes occasionally (which is open book and used to guide reading), two media analysis papers and our final was a project. 10/10 would recommend!

AAAD130 Review: She was an amazing professor super understanding, inspirational, kind, and made a safe place for students to talk about difficult topics. This class makes me want to get a AAAD minor the way that she speaks so eloquently and brilliantly. Built in absences that require no explanation and she is so nice. My favorite professor at unc.

Dr. Samuel has been one of my very best professors at UNC. She has such a way with words that I was hooked to her lectures every class. She values peer input and often bases the discussion on her students. Although she wants everyone to speak, she doesn't cold call or make anyone feel uncomfortable. Can't wait for my next course with Dr. Samuel!

She's an amazing professor and is so sweet! She's full of wisdom and really cares about her students! I took the class last year but still have coffee chats with her! Would totally recommend this course--I learned a lot!
Very caring! No exams, just a longer course paper and final paper and other things. Super nice and accommodating. Lots of lectures
She is the best!! I recommend this class to anyone, it was so interesting and she is very flexible with deadlines.

She genuinely loves what she teaches and is very accommodating if you ever need an extension or have to miss a class. All we had to do was write a discussion post each week and create one final paper. There was also a short presentation, but it was only graded by whether you did it or not.

Super manageable class! The only assignments we had were 250 word discussions due at the end of each week, and one 10 page paper due near the end of the semester. There were also 2 quizzes, but as long as you read, you would be fine. Prof. Hudani is super understanding, and wants her students to pass and do well in her class. 100% recommend.

Professor Hudani was great! Very nice! The class covers interesting topics I wouldn't have learned as a biology major. But she allows one unexcused absence, then penalty for further absences. Lots of reading and class is a lecture about the reading and then discussion. She loves to hear from EVERYONE so will have to share something. But recommend!

Hudani is very passionate about her class and is a great lecturer. Her classes are always engaging, and she takes time to know every student. She gives great feedback and fosters a lot of intriguing conversation in class. There is a lot of reading, so be prepared to at least skim the texts before class.

I took Dr. Hudani for AAAD as a freshman fall semester of my freshman year, and at first I was intimidated by the class. There are a lot of readings that are unrealistically lengthy but she does a great job at breaking them down in the lectures, so it's okay to skim. She is also by far the most caring professor I've had at UNC, especially for MH.

This is the sweetest lady ever, and you can tell that she really wants you to do well. She loves when people ask questions and engage with the content. There is a fair amount of reading each week, but the quizzes on the readings are always open note and open text. Her lectures are interesting, and it feels like a seminar style class.

Prof. Hudani is the sweetest! She is very understanding, gives high quality feedback on every single thing we submit, and is not a difficult grader. She's super accessible and really wants people to succeed - the assignments are not difficult although there can be some dense readings. I would absolutely take another one of her classes!! 10/10
Sweetest and kindest teacher

THIS IS A REVIEW FOR PLAN 576: Her wealth of knowledge seems almost limitless. If you read and engage with the texts and answer her equally interesting discussion questions, you will learn something new every class. She is an incredibly sweet person and will always go the extra mile when you ask a question.

Dr. Hudani was wonderful. I learned so much in her class, it was pretty engaging! The readings could sometimes be dense, but she was understandable. She also receives criticism and feedback very well. All it takes is a meeting or quick conversation with her.
I learned a great deal from this class! There was a lot of reading, but she did her best to be understanding and responded to our feedback, including about the quizzes. Would definitely recommend.

At one point she assigned over 80 pages of reading for one class period. Quizzes entirely based on the readings (not classes) and focused on specific details rather than main ideas. She ended up dropping the lower quiz grade when we complained, but it soured me on her class. She seems nice otherwise and class was ultimately easy, but be aware.

Caring teacher that is seriously invested in student wellbeing. Won't cold call and if no one raises their hands to answer a question, moves on. Kind of a pushover in that way? No huge penalty to not doing the readings; I would have gotten more out of the class if weekly forum posts required me to skim readings and not just answer from lecture.

Professor Pier is extraordinarily proficient in his field. His readings for the class were always eye-opening and radical, which I loved. He is definitely my favorite of the three professors who teach this course. I recommended this class for your interdisciplinary credit. Midterms and final exams are essentially all that you are graded on. 10/10.

HOKAY so Pier is GOOD, while the other professors need to get some teaching reps in. When it comes to the other professors they gotta work on just about everything but they are good at stealing your points ON THE TEST as they throw some zingers. I've tried any several classes with Pier ON PURPOSE so you could say I built it class by class with him.

His lectures were the most interesting in the course, he very obviously is knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. He also makes it very clear in his lectures what he is looking for on the exam.
Out of all other IDST professors, he was the best. Easy readings, good lectures and slides and easy exam questions. Nothing special, he was just an easy professor.

Pier was very nice but I wouldn't recommend if you can avoid taking this class as it was quite boring in my opinion. Some of it was fun but for the most part I had a hard time enjoying it. If you pay attention and do the readings it's not hard to get a good grade (long and hard readings but he is understanding and goes over it in class).

Honestly think he should have better reviews. His lectures can get boring, but as long as you go to most you should get an A. Readings are interesting and discussion posts don't take long. Good class to take for credit. He is caring, does lectures in a unique way instead of typing up notes for the slides beforehand, does during class.

He was a very caring professor. He doesn't bump but he does provide extra credit opportunities so I would strongly encourage taking use of them. His readings are somewhat long and are needed to be read in order to know what to do for mid-term but he doesn't assign many readings. Just 3 papers, 1 midterm, 1 final so not much work.

Professor Pier was the best of the IDST113 professors. His lectures on the history/sociology of race were by far the most interesting and his slideshows were comprehensive and great for final exam review. He was always the professor to make clarifying announcements in Canvas and seemed like the professor who cared the most about the course.

Honestly take this class, I only attended three lectures overall and still got an A. Do the first three discussions and you can skip the rest. I didn't did about four readings and nothing else. Mr. Pier definitely had the best lecture slides (I didn't have notes so this was how I studied for the final), the rest are slightly incomprehensible.

The class is very poorly structured, with grades based on three discussion posts, a paper, a midterm, and a final. However, it's easy if you stay on top of the work, though there's no curve. Pier, in particular, is the best out of the three professors—his slides are clear, his portion of the final isn't cumulative, and he's very generous.
High school level class. Do not take

I think that IDST 113 is structured poorly but Pier was definitely the best professor by far. If you missed class the slides were easy to understand the point he was trying to get across. He also gave a summary of his thoughts of the other professors lectures which was very helpful and made his part of the final non-cumulative. goat professor.

His portion of the class is slightly reading-heavy, but his lectures have great information which was super helpful for the midterm + final, especially as compared to the other 2 Triple-I profs, who had tough slides to understand and super dense readings. Overall a kind professor who definitely cares about his work + wants students to do well.
I really enjoyed his lectures and he was relatable.

Pier definitely has the best lecture slides which he posts on the syllabus, all of which are very detailed and easy to study. Pier's content was more interesting compared to other topics and his test questions were reasonable. The midterm and final were overall pretty easy with MCQ + open response being vocabulary questions + one longer question.

Prof. Pier was great and made his material accessible! Unfortunately would not recommend taking this triple-I due to the overall structure of this class and inconsistency between the way the three disciplines were taught.

Pier carried idst113 even when the other two professors didn't have clear plans. He tried to clarify other professors' lectures and provide review material for himself and others. He had clear slides that were easy to review, and his lectures were logically progressive. There are only a few assignments, but they are easy and low effort.

Out of the three professors he was my favorite. His lectures were often the most interesting and he was kind. Like all the professors, the homework was always reading. There are few graded assignments and the work outside of class isn't that crazy. Make sure to take notes in the lectures as that is the only thing on the exam and is needed to study.

Prof.Pier is the nicest instructor among the three instructors in this triple-i course. He provides detailed slides that cover basically everything he mentioned in class. He made the exams as easy as possible by not taking cumulative tests and providing review slides/direct instructions on memorization.

I think Dr.Pier is the best professor in the IDST 113. He provided his own insights on what the other professors were talking about in relation to his field which was helpful. The triple I is just not well organized and when we did a review session the midterm had not even been created yet.

Best professor and class at UNC. Amazing guy with great experience and stories he frequently references in class,  which helps the material stick. Understands different learning styles and tailors his lectures to help as many as possible. Very helpful in office hours for class or post-grad advice. Could not recommend more.

Favorite prof at Carolina. Class is so engaging and fun. He has many stories from his AT days. If you study you will get an A. That said I'm not done with the class but I have a 99 rn. Very accessible and so kind. You have learning checks and exit tickets that you get the dates for, so don't miss those classes. Such a fun class so show up.

Really enjoyable class, he teaches things multiple ways to accommodate different styles of learning, and is always happy to answer questions and hear what students are struggling with. Class is very centered around the needs of the students, and his learning checks and exams are written very fairly and do not try to trick you. Take his class!!

EXSS 265! Have nothing but great things to say about this professor. He is so accommodating and noticed the needs of the students grades and offered extra credit. He has personal experience from being an AT, which was interesting to hear different stories. I would take this class and highly recommend and class with him!

(FOR 265) Prof Aguilar is very funny and understanding. The class is QUIZ HEAVY and it makes up most of your grade. They can easily be tricky so keep up with ULA reviews, go to class, take notes and ask questions. Hes very accessible to help you out and offered extra credit that rlly helps ur grade.
Unorganized and unfair. Not consistent between semesters and many exam questions are worded esoterically and he expects you to read his mind. Not as lenient and fair as he tries to let on.
Very fun class. He's hilarious and I would recommend the class for anyone who may be interested.

Took 265 with him. He was a very entertaining lecturer which made things easy to understand and remember. Class is very chill and easy. He's the type of professor who is happy if everyone gets an A. He has lots of stories from personal experience which are fun. He also keeps standing on top of his desk for no reason which is funny

I took 265 with him. Dr. Aguilar is probably the best professor I've had at UNC so far. His lectures are engaging, and he really cares about what he is teaching which makes everything so much more engaging.

Alain is nice and very accommodating. He tries to be very understanding. I just found lectures to be a bit boring and I did not like his use of nearpod. The course was also pretty unorganized and I'm sure it will become better with experience. Felt like our class were the guinea pigs a bit. The test format is very strange. I took 265 with him.

I loved 408 with Alain. He is a super chill, kind guy with a lot of knowledge about strength training and exercise in general. Some classes are hands-on (going to Ram's, using foam rollers), which I enjoyed a lot. Grade is based on a few assignments, class attendance, an exam and two projects. Great for lifters who want to learn more!

Love professor Aguilar, he might be my favorite at UNC! Only 1 exam which is take home and like 12 questions. You will learn so much and Aguilar is so insanely nice. His class is engaging and often you participate in the exercises you learn about which can be fun. This is a great class for aspiring fitness/rehab personnel, I recommend it!

Dr. Aguilar is my favorite professor I have had at Carolina. His classes are relatively easy, but I learned so much. Alain has a way of making everything interesting and engaging. I have never written a review on RMP, but thought he was deserving of one. Dr. Aguilar was kind, compassionate, and made me want to come to every class.

Professor Aguilar is one of my favorite professors to have had at UNC (I'm graduating and specifically came back to his page to recommend him). The class is interesting and very applicable to people that go to the gym and enjoy working out. Aguilar is incredibly kind, approachable outside of class, and all-round a great teacher. Take Alain!

I love Prof. Aguilar! Probably the best professor I have ever taken. He's super funny, kind, understanding, and knows his stuff. Never makes you feel dumb for asking a question. I wish I could take him again!

Dr. Hanson is one of my favorite professors I've had at UNC. His class isn't too difficult, I would say it's one of the harder ones in the EXSS major but certainly doable. He is hilarious, gives great lectures, and really understands the subject matter deeply.

The course structure felt inconsistent. One of the biggest challenges was the inconsistency with due dates. The syllabus stated when assignments would typically be due, but the due dates were often not posted on Canvas, and deadlines were occasionally changed. This made it very easy to miss assignments unintentionally.

Dr. Hanson is a fun professor that is a clear lecturer and his class isn't too hard. There is a group project (debate) but if you participate in preparation and in the debate you'll do fine. Exams matched the lectures and there were few, very easy, assignments outside of class. Hanson is very understanding and super nice, take with him!

Where do I start- Erik Hanson is a cool cat who teaches a very hard class. The material is a lot and tests are 55% of your grade so if you mess up on one, then you are screwed for that A in the class. The lab is a big help though because it is pretty easy if you do the work and is worth 25% of your grade. The class is v hard
Just bad. Do not take this class.

Ryan was a great professor who made class fun and engaging. His class was very dependent on group work with very high expectations of working with randomly assigned people. I learned a lot in his class and enjoyed his lectures.

This class was super easy and fulfilled IDST and Communication Beyond Carolina requirements. Lectures are a bit scattered, and recitations are not super helpful, but I did learn more about leadership and feedback, which will be helpful in the future, and I had fun. Your grade is VERY group-dependent. Grading is a bit random but easy overall.
Very bad class, not organized, and oddly difficult

Relational leadership was a disorganized class. However, when Ryan led interactive and engaging class activities, it worked. The three teachers for this class had great ideas but couldn't quite execute them. If Ryan is teaching another class, don't let these reviews dissuade you from taking it. He will try his best to make it fun and valuable.

This professor is terrible at teaching material, and does not explain his stories well. The Taste are tough graders, and they show very little partiality even though they don't help. Would not take any class he teaches!!

Ryan was super respectful and kind. The issue is with the course structure, not Ryan. IDST 190 was completely disorganized and had no real purpose. Ryan made the class as interesting as he could considering there wasn't really a relevant goal with the actual course. Would love to have Ryan as a professor again, not the class.

DO NOT TAKE. Take any other triple I, this one is horribly organized and has no clear instructions. Lots of group work and the final is worth 30%. Also it's totally focused on healthcare or higher ed so if you don't like those you'll be bored. Also wouldn't say what was on the final and when we asked questions he would just say I can't answer it.

The class (Relational Leadership) was bad, but Ryan was ok. There's not much to say as I'm not sure this class will be taught again, but Ryan was much less of a problem than the TAs and was one of the better people to have giving the lectures in class.

He seems like a great guy and a nice person. However, this was not a good class at all. Extremely disorganized, harsh grading from the TA's, and overall the content was quite irrelevant and boring. Very inapplicable to the real world, and you won't learn anything. Genuinely wasted my time, didn't gain any knowledge.

Very rude, does not like answering questions, huge ego, hard to pay attention to. Awful class-Do NOT take. Lots of readings, project-based class with random students who don't do their part, MCQ final exam. Disorganized, lots of people fall asleep during class, super boring, everything takes so much time. TA Jillian was great, the rest were awful.

Ryan is incredibly rude and dismissive when asked questions. When I asked for help, he said, "I don't answer content-based questions; you should know this already if you did the hw." Additionally, the course had a mcq final despite being project-based all semester, which made no sense and was unnecessarily difficult for such a pointless class.

Disregard these comments on Ryan, they are mad at the class. Ryan was the best part of IDST190. He was kind and didn't grade the work (the TAs did). His lectures were the most interesting of all the professors. This class's grading is harsh; the group projects are a large part of the grade and are vague. However, Ryan makes the class interesting.

The class is graded off of a couple group projects and a final. The projects were grading harshly and did not have a clear rubric on any of them. Ryan seems to have an ego when discussing grades and is not personable. Overall, this class is way to difficulty graded to be a triple i. Do not take it or Ryan
This guy is very obnoxious and rude to students. Do not take. Grading is not explained well and the class is taught very poorly.

Grading was always extreme for no apparent reason. Sought out pieces in assignments that they gave no information on but was still weighted heavily. Refuse to give A to A+ on most papers even if lots of work and thinking was put into it and it was clearly well based and established. Just overall unnecessarily difficult.

If you have a chance to take her for college thriving DO IT! She is really nice, understanding and made sure we knew about important information about classes. You could definitely confine in her and she made sure to make everyone feel comfortable in the class. Good mood and encouraged us to talk with each otherplus she cancelled class a few times.

Gabby is fantastic! She genuinely cares about students' success and always offers support in any way she can. The class mostly consists of busy work (not her fault, by the way), but she tries to make it engaging, and she is very flexible and kind!
Super easy class basically just busy work. She is a very sweet lovely lady, cares about you, and wants to help anyway she can.
i don't care for this class at all but she was an amazing teacher. very kind and understanding. there were even times when she decided not to have class that week!
The best!!!!!!
Mrs. Rios was incredibly kind and understanding throughout the course. College Thriving is a requirement and an incredibly easy class itself, but still having Mrs. Rios made it even easier.

This class is the definition of a thorn in your side. The work is busy work and can be easily done, but I saw no value in it. Mrs. Rios though is a very caring and sweet professor and is the only reason that class was tolerable.
While I firmly love the class, this class should not be an one level class

Please do not take this class if you are looking for an easy gen ed. I worked so incredibly hard for the B+ that I go. Professor Bauer is kind, but her lectures are incredibly disorganized and the amount of material included on midterms is insane. Get ready to study and memorize your heart out if you take this class.

Very difficult considering it is an introductory level class. Her lectures go incredibly fast and are very disorganized to the point where I had to reorganize all my notes after every lecture. Midterms and exams are written only and require very dense knowledge about the structures covered and memorization of terms, dates, and architects.
This is a great professor and a great course to take some time here at UNC. Made learning more about the art styles in movies very entertaining and had good commentary on the aspects of movies.

This class was a lot of fun! I think this class is one that you can take regardless of your level of interest in film, because the movies were all very good and the lectures were extremely interesting! Just get ready to write a few papers, but overall the work is very manageable and the professor is so nice and accommodating!

JJ is one of the best professors I've had at UNC so far. This was a rough semester, but JJ's class was a bright spot. I'm not an art major and have never been the creative type, but the material in the lectures was pretty interesting and she is good at grasping students' attention. Great class and great prof

I am not an artsy person but was invested in Dr. Bauer's classes because of how she presented these buildings. She tells you about architecture as if she was there when every building was built, and it is genuinely so engaging. The paper prompts were unclear in parts, so work closely with your TA on how they will be grading essay formatting.

Amazing class! Every subject was not only interesting, but my favorite part is that Dr. JJ Bauer wears shirts every lecture that coincides with what you were supposed to watch before that class. Overall, it is a writing-heavy class, but nothing not manageable. Her pacing is perfect and recitations are interesting as well. Highly recommend.

I took this class for a VP credit and it was honestly pretty interesting. Im not an art person but I enjoyed Prof Bauers lectures and connections to history. The tests are relatively easy and she made them open note, but her lectures move really fast, so it's difficult to keep up. There are also 3 3-4 page papers but they're pretty simple

paper and assignment criteria is usually v unclear, usually its outdated. there are not 1 but 2 midterms in her classes. yeah, 2. on top of the 2 midterms, theres like 3 papers & a final, & post to a forum for 5 of the weeks. usually a recitation on fridays & made us write a 6pg paper in the span of 3 days only knowing the prompt on the 1st day.

Awesome professor, very passionate about his field and very chill. Not graded on many things but one bad test grade isn't going to hurt you too bad, he is also a very generous grader. Always down for a conversation :)
Engaging and interesting lectures. Really knows his stuff. Not too much work. Pretty easy work. Very understanding guy. Best professor I've ever had!!

Pretty vague on what my grade was until it was finalized, but a chill dude who is clearly very passionate and respected in his field. Very niche topics but you don't have to memorize as much as other ARTH electives I've taken (only like 20-30 things per exam) and attendance didn't matter.

Prof Turner was a great, he was understanding and didn't mind absences (don't abuse this). He graded papers for completion and the 'term paper' on accuracy. His exams aren't bad but you must memorize a lot (took me 2-3 hr w/flashcards). I rec if you have a busy schedule bc he has no homework, but exams are weighed heavily but graded forgivingly.

Lectures can be boring, but overall it is a chill class with interesting content and teacher. What started off as a filler class eventually became a fav. He doesn't grade harshly, and focuses more on conceptualization than gpa. He said before the final. “I'm not here to tank your gpa.” Not much work outside of the classroom, few assignments.

Prof Turner is very knowledgeable and passionate about his work and that shows in his lectures. The content is quite interesting, but the lectures themselves can drag on and feel boring at times. Final grade is determined by 3 assignments and 2 exams which kind of sucks, but he is a pretty forgiving grader.

Super interesting class, especially if you're interested in art history! I definitely wouldn't take it if you're looking for a gen ed to skip out on and still get a good grade, as concepts will be very hard to find/grasp outside of lecture. But I learned so much! Go to class!!!

Great professor. Very lecture heavy class, going to class helps. Everything was graded by TAs, I had a great TA so as long as you followed the rubric clearly and used what you learned in class lectures it's fine. Final and midterm criteria was posted so you know what you're in for, as long as you study the material from class, you'll get an A.

I find that she made an already boring course more difficult by slow lectures and few assignments that determined your final grade. Although she was accessible outside of class and kind, she was very harsh on grading, giving unhelpful feedback. An absolute bore to sit through with long readings and pointless in class assignments.

Professor Cao's lectures were very interesting. Attendance was only mandatory for recitations, but I don't see how you could get in-class content without actually going, since her slides only had images. The TAs didn't grade harshly at all, but there was no way to know what they were looking for, and they seemed mildly disorganized.

Love art but still this is a frustrating class, super picky graders on midterms but then don't care about other assignments. You can still do well, just expect vague feedback, unclear expectations, and the confusing lectures. I was taking an 200 art and it was easier than this. also the ta judged me a little and did not care to help much.

If you show up to the lectures, take notes, and pay attention you will be fine in the class. For me, the lectures were interesting and fun to learn about. No textbook, but posted readings which I always did before class (some are longer than others). Not many assignments throughout the semester, but they aren't difficult to complete.

Super frusterating class. Lectures are insanely boring and their is a certain social narratives that run as an undertone in the class that Cao seems to perpetuate. Aside from that the TA's are sporadic graders with some assignments getting 100% stamped on and others being scrutinized to the T, but you never know which is which.

It's a pretty easy class if you attend the lectures consistently, there are not much assignments to do. Though it would be better if the TAs provided rubrics for the assignments and projects as they're the ones that grade everything.

The TAs grade everything and they are usually pretty tough graders. What sucks most is that they don't give you a rubric yet will take off random points. With that being said it is not a hard day-to-day class, it is just frustrating at times and I would not recommend it if this is not in your major. Choose another class for focus capacities.

She is extremely knowledgable in the topics she teaches, but is not very engaging. We were graded on a few things---a paper, a project, and maybe two assignments. She graded extremely harshly, taking points off for small things. She is accessible after class, but I wouldn't say it is any more enjoyable than hearing her lecture.

Reviewing for ARTH557-- The best class I have ever taken at UNC! She is so smart. Small group, very discussion based and I learned so much. Not a harsh grader, and assignments never felt like busy work. Lots of readings, which had to be printed out, but the material was always so interesting.

Professor Cao is super knowledgeable and engaging, but the TAs in this class make everything way harder than it needs to be. They are unhelpful, slow to respond to emails, and grade inconsistently. It feels like they don't even understand the material sometimes, and when you ask for clarification they are bad.

I cannot wait to take another class with her, it was an incredible semester and I loved every lecture. I will day that while attendance was technically not mandatory, I don't see how people could succeed without attending them because there are no recordings and the slides don't have any of the important information on them. 
\
just don't

Maggie Cao is a really good and inspiring professor. Every lecture, she expands on the reading materials she gives during the weekends. You can always learn more perspectives of America and art history through her course. T I do have three Ras this semester, but overall I get good grades. You do need to respond to the prompt precisely.

Recommend avoiding this class unless you're passionate about art history and happen to satisfy the preferences of three different TAs (for one recitation section) throughout the course of the semester. Professor Cao is sweet but her grading should be for more advanced classes or actual art history majors. I liked the most of the material, though.

Quite easily the worst professor at UNC. Tests were next to impossible, treated us as Art major students even though its just an elective class, and lied to us about a curve.
