Lectures were terrible, wouldn't excuse my absence even though I was in critical condition, and had a terrible personality (hated when asking questions). AVOID THIS CLASS!!!!!

The professor isn't bad, but genuily one of the worst classes I've taken. Don't take this class if you want an easy gen ed. The TAs give awful feedback, and don't even explain in depth what you got wrong. Do not take this class if you think it will be an easy gen ed.

Very knowledgeable and passionate, with engaging lectures. Great survey class, with diverse artists and contemporary debates included. Homework readings weren't too difficult. The midterm and final suck, and I thought the midterm was graded excessively harshly (having taken multiple ARTH classes), but assignments were otherwise pretty easy.

Professor Cao's passion for her subject is very clear; however this does tend to most of the salient information (i.e. stuff on the tests) to be said by her and not really on slides. The TAs grade tough even though most ARTH 100 level courses are meant to fufill focus capacities. Overall if you are looking for an easy A it might not be here.

She is passionate and knowledgable but won't let you use the bathroom during class, no taking notes on laptops.She really wants engaged students, so make sure to participate. While she can be intimidating, she is funny and really wants you to learn. Take if you like ARTH or need the credit, but prepare to work. I like her, but not for everyone.

Her expectations for undergrads are like asking a fish to climb a tree-unrealistic and downright absurd. The only masterpiece in her class is the art of making students want to gouge their eyes out. Dims the lights at 9:30, but God forbid you actually nod off, she'll unleash a storm of pretentious wrath. Save yourself! This class is BORING!
There is no clear rubric for grading essays, boring lectures, and many readings for each class.

3 papers are 80% of your grade, but Prof. String is willing to meet outside of class to help you with them. The lectures are boring, and even though this is supposed to be a seminar it's her talking almost the whole time. I would only recommend it if you're really into art history. Overall, boring, but not too difficult.

She is pretentious and expects you to write a certain way without telling you. She marked off points for using words like, "showcasing" and "based off of" when describing art and her explanation was she doesn't like those words. 80% of the class is scored from 3 papers. do not recommend taking it unless you love art history

She encourages office hours help and her lectures are very thorough but they are redundant and it is difficult to get an A as her grading can be harsh and subjective. Many negative comments are prob from people getting bad grades but doing well is definitely manageable if you put in the work and are able to think critically. Attendance is very key!

Prof String is nice on the surface but classist, elitist, pretentious, and frankly rude to some of her students. I have yet to be targeted but have watched others take hits for not knowing a minute detail or simply being late to her 9 am. Worst Art H prof I've had at UNC. Don't take.

Dr. String was an amazing person but she teaches in an interesting manner. She expects her students to know all the information and artists' names on quickly when most of the students aren't in the art field. Her grading is harsh as well and sometimes she makes you feel dumb for not understanding. Nice person, okay professor.

The course content was interesting. Her approach to teaching, however, left a lot to be desired. She had weird tendencies about things that caused me to lose interest quickly; I didn't feel I got the most out of the course. I didn't enjoy the humiliation tactics she employed, even if someone was just a few minutes late. Good course, bad professor.

This was one of the more interesting classes I have taken at UNC and Prof String was super knowledgeable about the course content. She isn't a super tough grader in all honesty, especially on the papers. There was a lot of reading in the first half of the semester but there is a significant decrease after the first midterm.

She may be good to undergrads, but her conduct with grads is unprofessional at best. Disrespectful, undermining, and expectations that shift arbitrarily. Classist and ableist. Does not care about graduate student growth, only about posturing. Otherwise fascinating course content fully obscured by this.

Tons of memorization and annoying class discussions (more than most other ARTH classes I've taken), lots of heavy reading. But Professor Sherman is really interesting and funny and I definitely learned a ton.

You (and every other student in the course) will never make a grade higher than a B on any essay or exam. Be prepared for that. A bit condescending, lectures were often dry, and he really Really loves to talk solely about France-- to the overall detriment of the course, because this wasn't listed as a course specifically about French art history.

Grades based on his own opinion. In essays you could back up your argument extremely well and still get several points docked because he does not agree with the argument. Super time consuming. DO NOT take unless you absolutely have to.
Tough grader, grades everyone in the B range no matter how detailed. Brutally sarcastic. Midterm and final are pure memorization and essays. Good luck.

He is knowledgeable about the material, however the manner which it is delivered is un-encouraging and passive aggressive. He interrupts you, corrects you on tedious things and the atmosphere of the classroom is fear over saying something wrong. He will talk about the art but not the social movements surrounding it, which is a big component of ARTH
does not provide clear grading criteria. Grades more on feeling rather than a specific rubric

Professor Sherman is definitely a challenging professor, but equips his students with the resources needed to succeed. I wouldn't recommend his class unless you're passionate about art history, but if you are the course is a blast and you'll learn a lot regarding academic and art research and connecting a work to the history it was created within.

Professor Sherman is awesome! I loved taking ARTH54H with him even though I'm a STEM Major and had no experience in a college-level history class before. He is somewhat of a tough grader but if you are a good writer you should have no problem making an A. He does care about grammar, tone, and conventions a lot more than you would expect

majority of final grade consists of how well u do on papers. he grades them toughly but provides very specific feedback. the readings were rly heavy but u can skim them before class and be ok. he gives lots of opportunities for participation. the course was harder than expected for a gen-ed, but overall good learning experience.
Professor Sherman clearly was knowledgeable about all of the topics in the course, funny too. The majority of the grade relied on papers which were graded toughly, but he gave thorough feedback.
Amazing! I do not like German at all and I have no interest in it but I would take it again if I could have her. Super accessible out of the class and clearly wants everyone to succeed.
Amazing professor. I actually hate German but I would take it again if she was my professor. Extremely caring to all her students! She wants to make sure everyone succeeds and it is very obvious.

Elena is a super chill professor that really wants you to succeed. She's compassionate, good at explaining, and is really understanding. German 102 isn't as hard compared to 101, but it's much more grammar based. Would a 100% recommend the course and professor. This was the best course I had this sem. Also, go to review sessions and kaffeestunde!

Elena was by far the best language teacher I have ever had! She was amazing at explaining concepts and coming up with ways to make class fun. I would absolutely take another class with her and I hope to in the future.

Elena is absolutely amazing! Possibly the nicest and greatest professor I've had. She has the experience of having learned the language, and that really comes out in how well she teaches it! definitely take her!
Simply amazing!

It is very clear that Professor Petron cares about her students. She is very dedicated to explaining the grammatical and cultural concepts required for this course. It was very easy to get conceptual questions or inquiries about assignments answered via office hours or email. This course built on and reviewed concepts from 101.
Easy enough, but required lectures don't go beyond the slides.

She is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Her lectures are always engaging and her insight is invaluable and brilliant. Accommodating with deadlines if you reach out. She encourages participation and creates a fun laid back yet stimulating classroom. Highly recommend taking a class with her!
This class was so much reading but was truly one of the best classes I've taken at UNC!

She is passionate about global cinema and assigns us to watch some interesting films and some that are eh. If you are into film I would definitely recommend, her lectures sometimes do drag a little but your grade is entirely determined by your TA.

Pollmann was passionate about what she was teaching and an engaging lecturer, but the format of the course was lacking. Lots of films to watch and unnecessary readings that were assigned that never amounted to anything you needed for exams and papers. Textbook was helpful for papers, that was it. Grading is entirely TA-dependent.

She comes across as very snobby. Everything is graded is actually graded by the TA (so find their RMP). Readings are not relevant. I would only recommend this course if you are into "film" and need to fufill the FC-AESTH requirement. She also has a terrible attendance policy where if you miss more than 3 lectures your grade goes down by a +/-

There was definitely a lot of material that had to be covered in the curriculum, but Dr. Pollmann always kept up with the syllabus and made sure that even on lecture heavy days that it was will interesting and entertaining. 2 films a week, 3 papers, a written midterm, and a written final (both in person). Grading is pretty tough though!!

German 303 was not difficult at all and the course is not super time consuming. I am not the best at German and still did very well in the class. Dr. Pollmann was a very lenient grader on all assignments including the midterms. She is just a bit hard to get in contact with over email.
Kind and knowledgeable about the content. Very fair grader. Homework is incredibly easy. Forgiving attendance policy. Lectures would drag a bit. Two big papers worth a large chunk of your grade.

She's very passionate about the topic of film and has a way of describing films that makes you think about them in ways you never did before. I really enjoyed her class and learned a lot about how to analyze films and a lot about German society during the Weimar period.

I liked her lectures. Pretty interesting content. Didn't do the readings -- don't worry about getting the textbook. Mostly decent to good movies. 3 papers and writing-intensive midterm and final.  Otherwise an easy class.

I took this class for the VP credit but I did find this class to be pretty interesting. She covers a lot of the homework (movies and readings) in class so I rarely did either of those unless I was preparing for the test or papers and I was fine. You don't interact with the professor much and your grade solely relies on your TA.

When I took CMPL-143 in Spring 22, there was minimal interaction with the professor. A few lectures were cancelled. You'll have to watch all the movies on your own. the textbook is largely irrelevant to the course. Your grade largely depends on your TA. If you're interested in film history and art movements (art cinema) its a good class.

Was shocked by the amount of work for a low level course. It was interesting if you are a movie fanatic, yet beware not many modern movies were shown. I personally didn't interact with prof. Pollmann at all... only my TA.

Dr Pollmann's lectures were always interesting and she made tough concepts understandable. However, essay prompts were always very complicated + hard to unpack and readings for the class were not always relevant. This class is probably more work than you would expect, but if you enjoy learning about different types of movies I would recommend it.

Professor Pollmann's class was enjoyable and informative, with a heavy focus on group discussion and papers. Each week before class we were expected to watch the week's selected movie, each of which were made by German director Max Ophuls. This narrow focus allowed us to take a rare deep dive into the director's unique style.

Dr. Aksin has designed a brilliant class to merge German and the FC-CREATE credit. Super fun and interesting, we spent the first chunk of the semester reading a play (which feels really cool to say!) and then made movies of our own reinterpretations. Tests were fair, we were well prepared, and she truly wanted us all to succeed!

Dr. Aksin is fantastic! Very nice and understanding, easy grader, and my favorite professor at UNC so far. I never felt like I had to be perfect to answer questions, and she never made learning feel like a chore. Some homework outside of class, but never anything crazy. Overall, very happy with Dr. Aksin, and am excited to take 204 with her!

My German made leaps and bounds under Dr.Askin. She learned German in middle school and as a result better understands the many struggles people learning German experience. She's able to break down complex German topics and make it easy to understand. Also very understanding, clearly hates to grade and doesn't put a lot of emphasis on it.
Dr. Aksin was amazing! I greatly enjoyed GSLL 89 and would take it again if i could! Her lectures were great and I loved the class participation.

This is for GSLL 89 FYS. Dr. Aksin is amazing!!! She picks the most interesting literature/movies and gives fantastic lectures on super interesting topics. We think about language in a totally new way, and she has unique perspectives because of her background in Germany and Turkey. Highly recommend her seminar, and getting to know her as a person!

This is for GSLL 89, FYS. It was such an interesting course and I loved it, it was so easy. She's an amazing teacher and such an easy grader. If you are interested in the holocaust or anything this is the course you should take. Yes, you read a lot but its so fun!

THIS IS FOR 203. Great professor, her lectures make learning a language easier, totally understanding and flexible, The entire class taught in German but makes sure to keep students in the loop and focused. Grading structure is favorable and encourages you to just come to class and learn. Would recommend to anyone trying to learn German

This seminar was really fun - small class size and pretty much all grades were very creative assignments (presentations and essays). Dr. Aksin speaks with no accent, and she does a lot to keep class topics interesting. This was the best type of environment to learn German in, and my favorite out of all of the German courses I've taken here so far.

This was Professor Aksin's first semester teaching at @UNC. She's a generous grader, an active listener, and has been my fav prof this fall. Class grade depended on 3 large presentations, 2 (5-10pg) essays, and a paper final exam. Very manageable homework load. Small class size too.

This is a pretty difficult class if you are still not confident in your German. She talks very fast and expects you to already have a good understanding of difficult concepts. Other than that, she is very sweet and accommodating.

Probably the sweetest and most caring professor I have had at UNC! Definitely cares about her students and loves her job! Her feedback and grading criteria aren't always the most clear at times but she is very willing to meet with you outside of class and office hours!

Ruth von Bernuth is the best prof I've had here yet. She's so knowledgeable and passionate. I came in struggling with grammar and I've seen a big improvement in my writing now. She was a little slow with grading but the assignments were fair and doable. She's caring and wants to get to know each of her students. Her office hours are helpful!

This class is interesting and fun. I didn't expect to like it when I first signed up, but I did. The professor is great, but she's not good at keeping up with grading. Only two group projects and two essays throughout this course, but this class is reading-heavy.

She is so sweet and SO passionate about what she teaches. I had her for Fairytale class and it was so sweet watching her speak and lecture about the content. Attendance IS mandatory (I made the mistake of not going to like 4 class periods thinking attendance didn't matter) but honestly the class is so interesting that I never dread going.

She knows so much about every concept brought up in class, and she's such a sweet person. The class was mostly lectures and discussions, but you'l be fine as long as you skim the readings. The exams are not difficult as long as you pay attention in class. She cares less about the grade and more just that you're learning something. I loved her!

Professor Ruth von Bernuth was great! She kept the lectures interesting and made sure to involve everyone in discussions and class projects. At one point, Professor Von Bernuth baked the class German pastries! The class itself could be difficult to people not familiar with Christianity or European history.

Kable is retiring this year but I can't not leave this rating-- he was truly the best. So fun, incredibly easy grader. Our final exam was to write three things that made life worth living... so I regret spending time studying. But love love love him!

His last semester here at UNC so I am so sad for him to go. He is the absolute best, his classes are relaxing and inspiring. He made a non-theatre major like me even decide if I want to do a major/minor in dramatic arts or not lol.

Professor Kable is genuinely interested in his students (he learned everyone's name in my 40-person class). I enjoyed his selection of plays, and most reading was done in class. He is funny, invested, and very professional.
Prof. Kable is very respectable. I love his choice of drama and play, as they are representative and thought-provoking.
Attendance matters.

This class was probably the easiest I've ever taken, and Dr. Kable is so funny, caring, and supportive. Literally 75% of your grade comes from three journal entries that he grades super leniently on. The rest is participation and one "scene panel" that is a really simple acting project.

Class was very straight forward and very fun! I enjoyed his class a lot during this semester, as it is basically watching musicals based on the era we were learning about! I highly recommend taking this course as it is an easy A.

IF YOU ARE A FIRST YEAR HONORS STUDENT TAKE THIS CLASS!! super duper easy to get an A - literally just show up, submit the 3 assignments (only 3.), and give an ounce of effort when you do your scene panel. in class we just watched movies and read aloud scenes and chatted, but most ppl were just doing homework from other classes. highly recommend!

Kable is such an amazing professor! You'll read a lot of plays, but as long as you show up to class, occasionally participate, and think about the material, it's an easy A. He's a generous grader and clearly knows a ton about the subject material. Take any and all of his classes!!
He's just the best. I've taken him twice now and he's so smart and cares so much about his classes. I hear rumors he's retiring soon so take a class with him while you still can.
I am taking as many classes as I can with him.  He is absolutely amazing and one of my favorite professors.

Took this class fully asynchronous over the summer. 
Take it! I learned a lot about American musicals. Kable is a very fast and lenient grader.

DRAM120 was the perfect AES focus capacity. The whole class is graded on two exams, an 8-page paper, and 10% participation. As long as you show up to class and read parts/answer questions occasionally, you'll be good. He chose really interesting plays, and I got good scores on the tests without doing much reading outside of class time. Loved Kable!

While participation isn't required its so much easier to comprehend if you go to class. There are two exams and one 8-page paper total with no other homework. Be careful to look out for smaller details before exams, but overall the class is wonderful and I would take it again.

Favorite professor ever! He was so kind, caring, and passionate about the subject. As long as you participate, the class is very easy, and you will get a good grade -- it helps if you actually enjoy theatre. His class was a delight every day and I would love to take another class by him in the future.
I would die for this man.

I will ALWAYS recommend prof Kable. Ample opportunities for participation, and tries to make lectures as engaging as possible, even though it may be difficult for some because of content. Easy grader and passionate about the subject.

Kable is an amazing professor who only wants his students to succeed and learn about Drama. The class is based on 3 assignments, each worth 30%, and participation is 10%. Get ready to read a lot of plays but he makes it fun and grades pretty easily.

Amazing professor!! Read lots of plays but if you stay on top of the work then you're fine. Only had three journal entries to write and they were just diary style on your opinions of the play. No midterm, no final! For group project you act out a scene from a play - but it's low stakes and as long as you commit, you'll get a good grade. Take this!!

Okay, so I skipped class three weeks in a row and got 66 on my first exam but I managed to bounce back and get straight 100's and extra credit. The professor is a little boring but DRAM 115 is totally a GPA buffer if you actually have the willpower to show up to class.
Professor Marienberg is very engaging and knowledgeable. Class is not difficult if you do the readings/discussion posts ahead of time.

Class was a lot of work, but its very easy. Takes a lot of time but all grades are easy As. If you put a little effort into studying, the tests (1 midterm 1 final, both writing) are pretty easy. Would reccomend only taking this class if you are genuinely interested in the topic, as you'll be learning a lot about it and spending a lot of time on it.

(Fall 2025) Loved this class. Marienberg can be a bit of a character (in a good way!). Absolutely hilarious guy, great stories, and still gets you immersed in the content. Grading was very easy: mostly completion-based, and what wasn't was fine if you skimmed the reading and paid attention. Loved the course and professor. Will take him again.

Dr. Evyatar has a wealth of knowledge and shares it enthusiastically. He's honestly a funny guy and shows videos in class, along with bringing in prayer shawls. Classwork is easy, you just write a discussion post before each class based on the readings.

Prof Marienberg is super funny and a great guy! His classes are lectures, but he is very funny and adds videos and time to discuss the topics with your classmates, which helps break up the lectures. He is very accessible and helpful outside of class. Great class!
As long as you pay attention in class. You will be fine! Take Dr. Marienberg because he's super fun and nice.

Not sure why the ratings are so low, I had a great experience with Professor Marienberg. He's very understanding and his lectures were very engaging. There is often a good amount of reading per week and a discussion post or quiz for every class. The midterm and final were relatively easy as long as you studied the concepts and reading material.
Dr. Marienberg is so funny and so kind! I really enjoyed this class and hope I will get to take another with him in the future.

Nice man, though he was difficult to reach. Class content consists of readings and discussion posts due every class which, if done well, will take multiple hours each. The lectures are basically a recap of these. Exams contain very specific knowledge, but if you actually do the readings (and not just put them in ChatGBT), they're very manageable.
Nice in person. Not nice on email. But SUPER funny. Love this guy. Be prepared to read.

He is a very chill dude and lovely professor. Probably my favorite professor at UNC so far. He just wants you to understand the basic concepts and occasionally talk about what you think in class. As long as you do the 1-2 hour homework every week you will do well. Would very much recommend the class and professor.

As long as you keep up with the discussion posts and readings, this class is not too difficult. Dr. Marienberg is a caring guy who genuinely wants his students to succeed. Would recommend for anyone interested in taking an intro level RELI course.

Truly one of the best professors and nicest people I've met. Maymester is already a VERY condensed class but due to personal reasons I fell behind. Not only was he accessible outside of class, not only was he accommodating, but he acknowledged that as humans these things happen.100% recommend this class and his book and am grateful to have met him.

Professor Marienberg is an exceptional professor who deeply cares about his students. He is passionate about what he teaches, and knows enough to tell you what he does and does not know. He encourages you to participate, but you don't have to if you don't want to. Would 100% take a class with him again.

Be ready to read for his classes! He can be a bit strong headed at times, but never once stopped a student from expressing their views. He is very open about what he will talk about, and gave anyone the chance to step out of the room. Overall a great professor!
Great professor! Highly recommended!
Wonderful man and amazing professor.  Knows a lot about his field and really cares for the students.

Only take this class if you like to read! Aside from that, this was a fantastic class, and the Professor has a way of keeping the class engaging at all times. I can't recommend his classes enough, a true gem!
Awful

Professor Marienberg was a great professor and I highly recommend his class! It is true that there can be some larger reading assignments, but given that there are generally just two forum posts due each week. The exams weren't too bad if you pay attention in class and skim the readings.

This class was really entertaining and Professor Thornton was a great teacher. Mostly discussion based with some lecture. A lot of good content that gets you thinking. Four short essays scattered throughout, mostly self-paced, slightly harshly graded but hard to do too bad on. Relatively easy midterm/final. Great class!
Grading was a bit tough, but overall the class was interesting and involved concepts that are unique to UNC.  If I needed more gen ed courses I would definitely take another class with him.
Amazing professor! Learned many things during his course. Highly recommend!

Wish there was a 3.5 rating. Thornton is a great guy and genuinely cares for his students. RELI 247 with him was challenging because there are so few opportunities for grades. The class relies almost entirely on group discussion. Grading felt arbitrary. I would only recommend taking if you are a very strong writer. Interesting class, otherwise.

Excellent professor! Creates an environment that promotes critical thinking, open dialogue, and a cohesive class. He encourages us to learn not just from him, but from each other. The readings are engaging and thought provoking and the topic is fascinating. I really enjoyed his class.

Professor Thorton's class on evil was amazing and thoroughly interesting. He has a unique sense of humor and views his students as equals. He is uniquely qualified, which will help cultivate a different perspective for you. Very awesome class!

Do not take this class. This is your warning. This man will literally stress you out for no reason. If you have mental health needs or go to ARS he cares nothing for any of that. Between the creepy demeanor and lack of email responses do

He was a really casual and funny professor and I genuinely enjoyed laughing at his lectures! His content is so easy- just term memorization and connections to broader themes in the course. Five 1-2 page papers for the whole semester were graded leniently. He provides study guides for the midterm and final. My TA was so fun to talk to! Very easy A!

Mr. Thorton's class was such a bad experience I had to leave my first review. He often gets critical facts wrong (Men at Jewish weddings break glass to symbolize taking the bride's virginity, the husband stitch is false) and is often gratuitous with gory content to try to be contrarian and shocking. After the third dead baby joke it's exhausting.

Thornton is an interesting fella. He is not funny, grades very harshly, and does not care much for his students. He made the final exam shorter than the midterm because he wanted less reading. I think he cares more about his trips to Trinidad than teaching as we just read and watched the most boring controversial material. His lectures were boring

Dr. Brendan is a really nice guy! This class was super interesting. Just get ready to read... a lot. Some of the readings were interesting, but the majority were kind of boring. he has a great personality, but he loses it during his lectures & it becomes really boring. I do like Dr. Brendan views his students as equals, and his genuinely cares.

I took spirit possession with Prof. Thornton and I loved it! He is super knowledgeable about the material and very funny and engaging. He was lenient with the midterms and the final is an essay, with a group project at the end. He expects you to show up and do the readings, but it wasn't hard and all of them were interesting!

She's sooo nice, and this class is genuinely interesting. Most of the readings, if not all, are assigned on Canvas, and there's no homework. There are 3 writing quizzes and a midterm and final, but she explains everything multiple times so everyone understands. Great class that isn't too difficult, highly recommend!

Prof. Cooper is delightful, and you can tell she cares a lot about the topics. You have a lot of reading but if you like ethics, culture, or religion, then you be in for a treat. Grades depend on in class writing, participation, discussion board and exams. But it's all very manageable if you pay attention to lectures and take notes. I learned a lot

This was an enjoyable class I learned a lot in. There are three 3-page papers to write, but they weren't graded harshly and the tests were open note. The lectures were usually interesting though sometimes they ran over into the next class, or were a bit scattered. This is a solid class for a gen ed.

This was a fine class. As a Jewish student, I can't say I learned much. Cooper was solid, made content relatable, class had three short papers a midterm and a final, I would say a solid gen ed and interesting content

I took Reli 123 with Professor Cooper to fill one of my focus capacities. This course was a little harder than I anticipated, but I feel like I learned a lot. The TA graded all of the work, which seemed fair throughout the semester. Lectures were a little boring at sometimes, but participation points are easy to get.

Lectures are information dense, but somewhat middlebrow. We almost never got through the entire lecture. This would result in the next lecture going over the previous day's lecture, making that day's lecture be incomplete. This cycle persisted throughout the semester. Readings were interesting, but lectures really just went over the readings.

Dr. Cooper is a very caring and sweet person. She truly cares about the material and actively tries to integrate better treatment toward animals in her everyday life. While most of the grading are done by the TA's, she goes over the readings very well, which is helpful since it is unrealistic to assume you'll be able to do all of the many readings.

Dr. Cooper is really sweat and interesting in class. BUT this class DEPENDS A LOT on the TA you have. If you unfortunately gets a TA that get points deducted for no reason but just don't want people to succeed, then this class is a total trauma. almost 100% of grades is decided by your TA. BE CAREFUL in selecting sections.

Professor Cooper was great. I ended up taking her Judaism class because it fit into my schedule. I left the class wondering if I should convert. If I was Jewish, this class would inspire me to go to synagogue a lot more. I appreciated lectures were recorded, and the TA (shoutout Vinna!) was always available for office hours if I had any questions.

Dr. Cooper made this class as informative and as stress-free as possible. Grading criteria is very fair, and she listens to the students and their suggestions. A great class to take as a gen-ed: you have to do a very reasonable amount of work, but you get a lot out of it in my opinion.

Professor Cooper was fantastic this semester. Very insightful lectures and I always left having learned something new. The class is graded off of 5 response papers (lowest dropped), a midterm, a final, and participation. Response papers were at times frustrating because of vague directions, but overall everything was graded fairly.
this guy bruh. unbelievable. idek what to say about him.

one of the meanest professors I've ever had. one of my best friends & I took this class together, and she got low-key persecuted the whole class by the professor. He was unbelievably rude to her & conveyed no respect over emails. He will say criticisms in the most unnecessarily condescending ways. also, 0 structure, no curves, & interrupts you.

Z-man is a great man and scholar, but an awful teacher. His disorganized teaching style, combined with the esoteric/incomprehensible subject material makes for an absolutely baffling class. He doesn't post grades until the last week, gives rubrics for nothing, and will never assign anything normally on canvas -- only through announcements.

This guy looks nice but turns out to be MEAN. He never released the grades during the semester, and he sent me sarcastic email when I argued about my grades and asked for grade breakdown during the final weeks. He is also not responsive to emails and not helpful during the semester.

Z-man is the goat, without a doubt the best professor I had at UNC. He is an amazing lecturer and super funny. With that said, this class is a lot of work. Weekly one-page writeups on the readings (which are very long), one in-class presentation, a midterm, term paper, and final exam. The midterm and final have hard passage ID sections.

Z-man is super nice but there is a ton of content and a lot of reading. One-page papers are required weekly (on readings) and there is a term paper. The midterm was hard but graded fairly. Both the final and midterm have a lot of information on it. I would not take this class if you are not a religion major.

Overall a great guy and you can tell he cares about his students. I had difficulty in this class not because of him, but because I could not comprehend the content. If you genuinely enjoy philosophy you will do fine in this class. He made sure to help us review and prepare for exams/papers and genuinely put in time to create resources to help us.

Z-Man is a nice person and very knowledgeable in the subject. The readings and curriculum is VERY difficult for a first year seminar. His comments on your work will be harsh, and sometimes mean, but I believe he means well. He's a very tough grader but can be reasoned with. Take another class unless you're up for the challenge.
The rudest professor I've ever seen. Very passive aggressive.

Z-Man was such an amazing professor. While his class requires a lot of reading and studying, if you go to class and keep up on readings, you will be fine. Plus, it helps that Z-Man is funny, caring, passionate, and helpful. He really cares about teaching and getting to know students which is why I'm taking another class of his next semester.

Z-Man is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. A lot of people in this class know a lot of information on Christianity going in, but I knew nothing and was still able to do well, but probably just with more effort. He is a very passionate and fun guy, just make sure to pay attention in lecture and write down all the important stuff.

I am graduating this semester; this was the best class I took at UNC. Z-man was amazing. I took this class to fulfill a WB credit and became so interested in the topic. Course topics are engaging and class discussions are respectful but truthful. He is also world-renowned for his research, I ended up citing him in my final essay.

Zlatko seemed nice, but put us in uncomfortable situations in class. The readings were complicated and often very long, so when asked to recall info during class, people obviously had a hard time. He took it personally and got super intense and accused students of not reading. He was also a bit passive aggressive and was a terribly hard grader.

Prof. Plese is a very intense teacher and gets really annoyed when people don't do the reading, which there is way too much for this class in my opinion. I got overwhelmed and basically stopped doing the reading halfway through and then just crammed for the midterms and the final. I still found it a pretty interesting and fun class though.

Loved Z-man, but the class was much harder than I expected. I'm pretty sure the amount of reading/writing is supposed to be standardized across all the FYS though. It is a lot of work and not always easy to understand. Z-man is very engaging and cares about his students, but his grading scale was not clear at all

For someone who is not a religion major, Z-man was great. He helps ease you into material and makes it accessible. The lectures are a little all over the place but if you pay attention you will be able to do fine on the exams and on the paper. The midterm was tough but if you understand the structure you will do well on the final.

Z-man is the MAN. Awesome professor, nice, funny and makes the content extremely engaging. Not a completely give me A, and you do need to attend class, but not a difficult class. Engage in lectures and study for exams and you will do well. Exams were graded a little tough.

Z-Man was such a joy to have this semester. His lectures were extremely animated. He playfully yelled at the class when we didn't know the answer - not because he was mad, but because he wanted us to engage and understand. The write-ups are super easy if you read the passages, as well as the term paper. The midterm and final exam were also easy.

Z-Man was a great professor and he was a very interesting person. I enjoyed taking his class and the topic of the seminar. However, I will say that you don't know what your grade will end up being until the day grades are due and he's a tough grader. But he really wants the best for the students and teaches you to think critically about everything!

I took this class as a seminar credit, and although I learned a lot and was challenged in a positive way, I wouldn't recommend if you want an easy first year seminar credit. Z-man is a really interesting guy, but beware of all of the readings, it would take hours. I would recommend if you are very intrigued by philosophy and can grasp it.

For Ohio Wesleyan University; Hebrew Bible class. Her class is difficult, but it was one of the most rewarding classes I have taken. She is also incredibly kind and understanding, allows late work when needed. Didn't use textbook, still passed. If you're willing to buckle down and study, take good notes, and write fast, then definitely recommend.

This is for Ohio Wesleyan's REL111 class, Dr. Rassalle Lectures for the whole 1 hour and 20 minute class period, and is rarely interactive with the class with activities. 2 page essay duefor every class, and readings that can possibly take up to 3-4 hours to complete each class. Midterms are so much information it is nearly impossible. Do not take

RELI 101 ended up being one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at UNC. Professor Tsoulouhas gives amazing lectures and makes complicated ideas easy to understand with real-world case studies. I would definitely take a class with her again!
Professor Tsoulouhas is very organized with her Canvas being extremely accessible and all of her rubrics/deadlines being very clear. This class has a lot of group work and class discussions.

I took RELI-101 with professor Tsoulouhas this semester and it ended up being by far my favorite course I took. Prof. Tsoulouhas is very kind and displays a good knowledge of subject matters present in the course. She is not difficult to reach outside of class and you can tell student success is a priority. I would take class again with her.

An interesting course. I learned a lot while investing a reasonable amount of time. Discussions were also worthwhile. Quick aside: Students at a school as prestigious as this one shouldn't lash out because the professor prohibits plagiarism, or because they assign college-level amounts of reading. It makes us all look bad and devalues our degrees.
Be prepared to read.. Make sure you cite every quote. Not a fun class

Professor Leve is incredibly knowledgable and passionate about what she teaches. I learned so much in this class! However, this class would've been a lot better if she were more organized. There were a handful of assignments that had really quick turnarounds as a result. Overall, good class but surprising amount of work. Maybe take a different FYS.

Dr. Leve is an amazing person and a pretty engaging professor. Towards the beginning, I found her to be a bit disorganized and slow, but it got better as the semester went on. The class is a bit of work for a FYS, especially the final project and weekly readings. I did do well even without too much effort though so take that as you will.

She's super nice and knowledgeable about what she teaches. I enjoyed the readings and class discussions. The final project is a lot of work, but she's not a harsh grader. She's disorganized and often unclear about assignment timelines and requirements, but she wants her students to succeed and I learned a lot.

She is a great person, very nice and smart. But, DO NOT take this as a First Year Seminar, she makes it way harder than it needs to be. There are 2 weekly readings and analysis due before class, group papers and presentations, and a hefty final project. It's just too much for a FYS honestly, this class was more work than my STEM classes.

It's true that Leve is unorganized, but if you do the readings and put forth a bit of effort to understand the content you will do well. Lectures sometimes drag but Leve usually finds a way to make them funny and engaging.

I loved Leve as a person, but as a professor, she was hard to keep up with. The tests are full of Sanskrit terms, so it felt like we were just learning Sanskrit. That being said, it truly wasn't THAT hard, and as long as you memorize the terms and skim the readings, you can do fine. Don't take if you don't have time to read though

Dr. Leve is so nice and experienced! Readings are meant to be paired with lectures (occasional pop quizzes), and Dr. Leve does a great job making them cohesive yet still abstract (not disorganized). 
The study guide is usually posted a week before the midterm, so it's a bit hard to find gaps in your notes until then. Overall, great class!

Dr. Leve was very kind, so I feel kind of bad for saying that I didn't love this class. It was paced very slowly and it often got bogged down in the particulars such as memorizing words rather than understanding concepts. The grading criteria were kind of murky with respect to reading memos. Huge hippie vibes if you're into that.

never had such an unorganized professor in my life. rewrote the syllabus multiple times because she could not manage to keep up with her own pace. often rambles and goes on tangents about odd things, including children touching their genitals and the sexuality of young people. would not recommend anyone to take a class taught by leve ever.

I ended up getting an A in the end as I had stacked up on all the extra credit opportunities and came through with the final paper and exam, but the actual discussion posts were graded quite harshly at times, stressing me out initially. I liked the structured nature of the class and was quite easy other than that.

Nice + knowledgable but teaching style is very discourse heavy and lectures can really drag on. Nonetheless, material is interesting and beneficial to anyone. Workload not bad - journals graded by TA, the exams are a lot of writing though not too difficult/graded too harshly.

While Dr Leve is a kind professor, she often goes on rants and never finishes the material. I liked the topics but we never properly got to learn about it. The class is not difficult but you do have to remember a lot of material. Overall I recommend if you want an easier class but be aware that the lectures are very boring.

leve is great. kind, caring, and wants everyone to succeed. teaching style not be for everyone but i found it easy to follow. not too much work. no papers, just forum posts which i really appreciated. reading was manageable. exams chill. what i have learned from this class has truly helped me in my own life. highly recommend for a gen ed.

Dr.Leve is such an amazing person I really enjoy talking to her one on one but in a class setting she does get really behind on grading. She begin grading assignments 1 week before the last day of class. The extra credit that she does provide you must put in the work to do the readings and questions before class each day. Overall I did learn a lot!

She is very nice and very knowledgable, but she is super scattered and will spend an entire lecture on one slide. She goes off on tangents and answers unrelated student questions for significant chunks of class time. She then expects you to know a bunch of sankrit terms that she maybe mentioned once or twice in passing.
Very knowledgeable teacher but extremely disorganized

If you like the subject, you'll probably like the class. Although Prof. Leve was pretty disorganized, gave very ramble-y lectures, and spent a lot of time on the same topics, causing us to be way behind, the class was very interesting, the readings were short and manageable, and her grading policies were generally pretty fair and lenient.

Lectures can be unorganized and difficult to follow. Lessons fell behind schedule, so the syllabus was modified frequently. Long reading assignments, I'd recommend at least brushing over them and lightly annotating so that you aren't playing catch-up before the exam. TA was tough on grading, but if you go to office hours, your grades will improve.
nice person but class was deeply unorganized. maybe she had an off semester?

I did learn a lot about Hinduism, but she made a first year seminar more difficult than needed. I spent a lot of additional time on this class. Rubric was constantly changing and she would post assignments the day of/day before they were due. Although she was extremely unorganized, she was very nice, available, and knowledgeable on Hinduism.
Interesting class but so much work

Yoooo bart is a certified chiller. Tough grader though, it is really hard to get A's. You can know everything about the material and give full right answers and still get a B. Chopped. Lectures are cool though talked about anti-semitism too much imo. More about gnostic texts than about actual early christianity.

Dr. Ehrman is one of the most influential professors at UNC and this class was the most interesting class I have ever taken, even if you are not deep into Christianity. He does expect his students to put in the work (lots of readings), but overall, its not difficult to get an A. If you come into the class with an open mind, you won't regret it.

He's goated. If you're interested in Christianity this is a good class to take. He is a tough grader and doesn't give much feedback, but it was a fun class. Lots of reading though but you can get away with not reading it all.

From the moment I knew I was going to attend UNC, I knew I had to take a class with Dr. Ehrman. He's one of the most knowledgeable people I have ever met, cares about his students, and is funny, witty, and passionate. If you are interested in religion, take one of his classes. If you aren't interested, take him anyway, he will make you interested.
He's goated

I love Dr. Ehrman, he is by far my favorite professor here at UNC. His class even convinced me to add a religious studies minor. However, I will say the quizzes do seem to be graded unfairly. I overall for my quizzes received an average of around a A- however, there was no apparent pattern seen as to what he is grading for. Overall great!!

Out of all the classes I've taken in college, I regret this one the most. If you need the PH credit take a philosophy course instead. Class will not be an easy A, he is egotistical and makes it very clear on his personal beliefs which makes class an uncomfortable environment if you don't agree with him. He is way too harsh for a 100 level course.

Dr. Ehrman's grading is unclear and unfair. You can spend hours working on this course and not receive a grade that reflects it. He primarily uses his own books, articles, and podcasts, leading to a course that seems very one sided. Dr. Ehrman does not value or respect his students and makes his classroom an extremely unwelcoming environment.

He runs his classroom like a police state with TAs patrolling the isles harassing students trying to take notes, one even brought a spyglass to the final exam. He has three midterms one a week before the final. How is that a midterm. You can only get a B no matter how hard you work, this is a 100 level course keep on mind. He is a bit egotistical

Do not take this class. Bart makes his TA's grade on a completely arbitrary basis, like almost randomly assigning grades for written portions of tests. The content is just rote memorization of Bart's textbook. Also he expects you to memorize bible verses?? I got an A but learned absolutely nothing and hated every second of it.

This is by far the worst class I have taken at UNC. There are 2 pg essays every week, 3 midterms that no feedback was given for, and a harshly graded final worth 40%. Grades were not put in until the last day - after the 72 hour exam period, and the TA and professor were extremely unhelpful when questions were asked. Please PLEASE avoid this class.

Although the workload was decently heavy, I would recommend Professor Ehrman to anyone. Easily one of my favorite professors at UNC. He is a great lecturer, very charismatic, super knowledgeable, and you can tell he cares strongly about his subject.

here are weekly 2 page essays and a lot of reading. The discussions are interesting. The main issue was that he gave little feedback on essays throughout the year and the finals (2 essays worth 20% each) he grades very harshly. There were also 5 quizzes through the year that even he admitted to grading them harsley (no one in class was doing well).

Please. PLEASE. Listen. If you are not a RELI major, and you do not live, breathe, eat, and sleep the New Testament, do not take this class. I understand, it's a Philosophy credit, it's a 100 level class, and people say it's interesting. All three of these things are true. It is too hard and not worth it. Find another.
Very disorganized and not clear with what he wants. Far from an easy A. Final is a ton of info.

I enjoyed Dr. Ehrman's lectures but the work you have to put into this class is excessive. 2 pg papers every week and the grading is wack- it's based on how well your classmates write. I tried really hard but couldn't get the grade i wanted. The final is worth 40%. Take a different class, you will weep and gnash your teeth in this one.
DONT take Reli 104- it is so hard

Bart Ehrman gives unnecessary expectations for a 100-level class. My final exam is tomorrow (worth 40% of my grade) and I currently only have 2 grades in my grade book. 70% of your grade is determined by a little over 4 hours of testing and the other 30%, which is mostly participation, we haven't even received yet. I do not recommend this class.

Loved his lectures,but awful. A 2 pg paper due every week even with exams. Exams are 20 minute essays graded based on your peers; may not get the grade you deserve because someone else wrote better than you. No feedback on exams, last one not graded before the final. No recitation grade before the final. Interesting class, the structure is so bad.
So nice!!!!!! Sweetest professor ever and a very easy A. Don't have to even show up. I'm a senior and haven't had such an easy A at UNC here.

Loved this class. Abelardo is such a great professor and he cares so much about what he teaches. I took this for a Gen Ed credit but honestly found this to be a super interesting class. He is very lenient with grading, he just wants you to learn. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Nicest professor and one of the easiest classes I've taken. Each class has a reading assignment with a summary, but he grades very leniently. There's one midterm, a group presentation, and a final 10-page partner essay. Overall, it's a very easy class, and he genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about the material.

Professor De La Cruz is so kind and caring, he tries his best to remember student names even in such a large lecture hall. There are a lot of readings for this class but very little assignments, the biggest ones being a group project and 10-page final essay. He is an easy and fair grader, and I found the class material very interesting.
Literally the nicest professor ever. So knowledgeable and such a great class.

He's extremely nice and I am very glad I took his class. He was caring and careful in his discussions, speaking from his personal studies and experience in the field. One of the few teachers that actually loves doing what he does.

Dr. Abelardo is by far one of the best professors I have gotten to experience at this school. He is excited about teaching and his enthusiasm makes the course interesting and insightful. In addition to this, he offers lots of insight on first hand experiences, allowing students to get a more comprehensive idea of Indigenous communities.

Abelardo is very passionate about what he teaches and a very lenient grader. I learned a lot from his RELI 138 class and can genuinely say I enjoyed writing the very few papers and assignments he gave us.

I was actually in Reli89 (Wasn't an option?), but Prof Abelardo was so funny, caring, and the class was super easy. He cares about his students and wants them to just succeed and be passionate about what he is teaching. I'd take him again, super easy class and great prof.
Nicest Professor Ive had at UNC. Very easy A if you do all the work. Would recommend him to anyone.

I would definitely recommend taking this professor. I thoroughly enjoyed making it to her lectures- she was funny and she made the content super interesting. The main assignments are write-ups for the reading, but she grades very fairly.
she was super nice and engaging! there were a lot of readings but it was interesting to learn and her midterms and finals weren't too difficult either

Carter was an amazing professor! She provided clear examples in her lectures to help aid my understanding of complex topics. Her commentary kept me engaged and entertained.

I would recommend this class to anyone interested in religion, society, or death studies!

Gives very thorough and individualized feedback. Weekly journals instead of essays. Gives term list for exams. Lectures are sometimes monotonous, but she is very intelligent and has some funny one-liners. Overall highly suggest taking this for a gen-ed.
caring and helpful feedback.

RELI 220 was a great experience. This class is mostly lectures, but there were group discussion days. My class was graded based on 20 journal entries (typically two a week), attendance/participation, a midterm, and a final (with 5 opportunities of extra credit!). I recommend this class because it was interesting and with effort it was easy.

Overall, I absolutely loved RELI220 with Carter. She is kind, realistic, and extremely funny. The topic is very interesting, and her lectures really draw you in. Going to class is important, as the notes you take matter for the exams. Overall, if you need a class to take, as long as you pay attention and study, it is a great class!

I love Carter so much! She's so amazing and so knowledgeable. The terms can become a little overwhelming, but quizlet is your best friend. Her lectures are very similar to each other. She's one of the most funny and understanding and instructors, and make difficult dense topics easy to understand. There is a lot of reading, but it's all helpful!

Long readings, annoying weekly assignments, and mandatory attendance. Carter was reasonable as a grader and instructor, but the workload for this class was a lot for a gen ed. If you are really interested in learning about religion (I am not), and you are willing to do the work (I was not), you should take her. If not, this is awful; stay far away.

She was amazing!!! Very kind and passionate about what she teaches. I took this class as a gen-ed not expecting much, but now I am trying to take similar classes because of how much I enjoyed it. I hope my future professors will be like Carter. RELI220 is my favorite class taken at UNC so far, thanks to the classroom environment Carter created.

Carter is the absolute best! This is the first religion course I have ever taken, and it has inspired me to take more. She is funny, kind, and incredibly knowledgeable about the subjects she teaches about. She handles difficult subjects carefully & challenged us to think about our own perspectives & biases. Can't recommend taking her class enough.

(RELI 64)
Dr. Carter is a pretty laid-back guy who is passionate about teaching Islam and niche topics within the religion. Although some of his lectures I found boring, others were very interesting, and I definitely learned a lot. He also brought in cupcakes for us one time!
He is very knowledgeable and you are graded on completion and just showing up. He is an amazing man!
Just show up, listen, and do your work for an A if you care about an A. If you care about learning would not necessarily recommend unless you know close to 0 on this topic.
Good guy and easy class for sure take if you want an easy A. Lectures sometimes can be pretty boring.

Most days in this class we didn't have homework, and the few assignments we did have were easy and generously graded. The biggest problem was the lectures, which were often ramble-y and at times a bit boring. But Prof. Carter is super knowledgeable and if you're interested in the subject there will probably be some stuff you find interesting.

Professor Carter gives out few assignments and grades the ones he does pretty leniently. However, his lectures are very dull and he often goes off on tangents that are confusing/difficult to follow. I find myself not learning much from his lectures. Overall an easy class to take, but the lectures make it almost not worth it.

RELI 345 Reading every class (some readings are hard to get through), Dr. Carter lectures on the topic. Few assignments, a couple papers and a group project, but as long as you turn it in on time, you should get a good grade. This isn't a hard class content or grade wise but it can become boring with Dr. Carter lecturing the whole time every class
Enjoyable first year seminar but long lectures seemingly without direction. Easy A and knowledgeable about his topic, but not super intentional and memorable lectures.
Dr. Hynes is genuinely the best. I had so much fun in this class and learned so much with the group projects. super easy A, the best FC-create ever

This was probably one of the most fun classes I have taken. We did lots of group activities and games which made the class enjoyable and distinct from other UNC courses. One con is that we'd often be let out late which was a problem for many people trying to get to other classes or ride the bus. Even with this, her teaching was overall amazing.
Very nice professor, and for the most part good at teaching public speaking, but assigns SO much homework, especially for a gen ed class.

Incredible class and professor. Extremely supportive environment if you're nervous about public speaking, very fun social/theatrical games with classmates, fairly easy assignments with useful feedback.

LOVE Prof. Hynes! The class is very fun. I learned skills I will forever carry with me thanks to her. She is very helpful and wants her students to succeed. I 100% recommend this class for the gen-ed. Just put in efforts to the speech and you will be fine! TAKE IT

This class was so so much fun, but at times, it was unnecessarily stressful. Speeches and reflections were graded based on what felt like tiny mistakes, and the grading criteria were often unclear. But it is because Professor Hynes wants her students to succeed. Go to office hours to practice speeches, and it will be fine. Enjoy the class!
a LOT of work for a focus capacity. not clear grading and gives barely any time to get assignments done. class is fun though

Rachel is a very caring teacher. She writes in-depth feedback for all big assignments. Class is pretty fun. Lots of busy work towards the beginning of the semester. I feel that most speeches were graded based on how much effort you put in, so seeing her during office hours is super helpful.

Rachel is an incredible actress and professor. She is incredibly knowledgeable about the craft and gives great feedback. Participation matters (obviously, it's an acting class), but she is very understanding of injuries and health issues.

If you are interested in acting, I highly recommend taking a class with her -- you will learn a lot!

I LOVED THIS COURSE AND PROFESSOR HYNES! Attendance DOES MATTER, but the class moves by quickly. You must participate, but the class is so small that it comes naturally! If you need a public speaking credit, take this course! Just don't buy the textbook, it's on the Canvas page!

Rachel is an amazing professor. I had her for movement for the actor and the class was by far my favorite class of my four years at UNC. She is very good at getting students to get out of their heads and into their bodies. 100% take a class with her! Just be prepared to participate every class and perform.

Rachel is absolutely wonderful. She made this class so accessible and exciting for both drama majors and non majors alike. She is incredibly caring, personable, and an expert at her craft. I learned so much this year and I strongly encourage you to take this course, or any course with her, if given the opportunity.

AMAZING!!!!! Jeff was awesome, the class was awesome. As long as you lay it all out there and give it your absolute best you'll do very well. Probably my favorite class I'll take in college. Highly recommend!

Loved this class! We learned 3 scenes in this class, and all of them were with partners. Scene 1 had 4 lines, Scene 3 had ~1/2-1 page of lines, and Scene 4 was ~2-3 pages of lines to memorize. Jeff is a really nice guy and really made us all feel welcome, even when we were doing more silly things in class. Totally recommend this class!

TAKE THIS CLASS. If you need an FC-Create and you're thinking to yourself, "I'm not creative" (like I did) -- this class is for you. It'll push you outside your comfort zone, you will have a TON of fun, and as long as you really try your best, you will do well. Very minimal homework that you will honestly probably enjoy.
Inspirational
Overall a great course

If you are a drama major, taking a class with Jeff Cornell is a must for you. He is an extremely thoughtful and caring professor, and the first professor to ever fully take the stress off of grades and place it on our journey and personal growth. This man really deserves the entire world.

Where to start? He's just a joy to learn from. So knowledgable about the craft, and all about the process. He'll challenge you to consider different approaches to a scene, and you will undoubtedly become a better actor. Wonderful classes and a wonderful human being. Could go on and on.
He is awesome, take this class as a gen ed. Not only is it easy, but you actually learn lots of neat things and get to see him perform!

I LOVE Prof. Cornell! He is so passionate about the learning material that it really captivates you during lectures. Everything was graded pretty leniantly, and I loved seeing him perform in a few of the required plays we had to see!

Jeff is one of the best professors here at UNC. He is caring, loves to talk to you, and has some amazing lectures. He is very passionate about theatre. He actually helped me get into one of the plays at UNC, so thanks for that Jeff! He did assign some essays but they weren't bad and he definitely just loves seeing students engage in theatre at UNC.

Great guy and great professor. Made the lectures and material really interesting. The workload was not bad at all and was not a harsh grader. Made me excited to come to class and it's a great gen ed to take.

Cornell is by far the most passionate professor I have seen at UNC. His lectures are extremely engaging and his charisma has you wanting to attend class. I didn't really care about the subject matter but seeing someone else so invested in something was very inspiring. [The class is an easy A]

I have taken 3-4 classes with Jeffrey Cornell and he is by far the best professor I have ever had. He cares about his students and is good at giving criticism while also motivating you to improve. Genuinely he made me enjoy school a lot more.
Great guy. I literally sparks-noted the quizzes and never came to class and made it out with an A+. Great gen-ed to take to raise GPA. Cannot recommend this man enough.

Highly recommend 115 for LA and NA credits. Cornell is a great professor for those who enjoy the content but also understands that not everyone is there for that reason, which makes it a fantastic and easy course for gen eds. If you have room in your schedule, take it, whether it be because you like theater, for gen eds, or even just credit hours.

Take this for an easy entertaining class for the LA gen ed or to balance a hard semester. Attendance is not required. Class grade consists of two papers and 4 quizzes that are exam grades. These are all done on Sakai outside of class. Highly recommend

I LOVED Professor Cornell's DRAM115 class! Whether that's the theatre kid in me speaking or not, I found his lectures and selection of plays to be super interesting. He's a great guy who is super cool to talk to about theatre, UNC, and life in general!

The class was overall pretty easy, but, I would recommend watching or reading the plays in order to do well. There were 2 major papers and you did have to go see one live, but the grading was fair. Overall, the class was interesting and I watched way more plays with a deeper understanding of theatre as a whole.

She was friendly and class was decently easy.Most assignments revolved around the semester group project. Which wasn't too bad as long as you got a good group. There were peer reviews for groupmates if they suck. Canvas page was messy and everything just thrown into files. You can have full-page cheatsheet on midterm and final is open-note/canvas.

An incredibly dry lecturer, and she literally cannot organize Canvas. Virtually impossible to follow her lectures. Assignments throughout the semester are just glorified busy work that she proceeds to grade unfairly.
I would take 273 with her if you can—great professor, clear expectations, and straightforward grading.

Takes attendance randomly. 30% of your grade comes from the group research project, and groups are randomly assigned. Willing to help and gives extensions. The first exam was a little hard, but we were allowed a cheat sheet. The final was open note. She does grade the group project pretty strictly, so follow the rubric closely. Great prof!

She is a good person but the class sucks. Its a lot of material that she does not really explain well. She will answer questions about it after though. She does allow extensions on a lot of the assignments. She is a tough grader especially on the one big project that is spread out over the semester. She is REALLY SPECIFIC about the grading for it

Dr. Kucera is an awesome professor who truly wants her students to succeed! She is very flexible with deadlines. Your experience in this class will HEAVILY depend on the group you are randomly assigned to work with for the semester (as this is a huge project worth a huge chunk of your grade). Ask questions when you're confused and you'll be fine.

Awesome, kind and very helpful professor. I met with her many times during office hours to get help with the group project. If you are assigned a good group then you'll be fine in this class. The first exam was a little difficult but we did get a cheat sheet. Second exam was take home. Took attendance one time the day before spring break.

Dr. Cramer is amazing! She's very knowledgeable about her stuff, and always responds to questions after class or on Piazza. This class is very content heavy, and that does not mean that Dr. Cramer is a hard teacher; she's a fair teacher for a hard class. That being said, it is very doable in terms of getting a high grade.

Dr. Cramer is caring but lecture heavy professor, I took this as a junior and thought it was comparable to bio 103 and 220 level of difficult. She always curves 4-5 points on exams at least. Very fair exams. Study organisms the most and rewatch lectures in depth! go to her office hours to review exams. do GLQs but hunt and gather for answers.

Dr. Cramer is overall a very sweet and funny professor. We did fall behind in class sometimes, but the exams were easy as long as you studied everything that was gone over in the lecture. She tells you what you need to know for the exams and the Anki and Organism Cards are good resources to study. It was also very nice that she curved.

This class was crazy hard, but Dr. Cramer always seemed to make an effort to make it a little easier. Every exam is curved by like 5 pts. The content and lab are super interesting, but there is a LOT of content. Lectures can be hectic, we fell behind a lot, but she took content we didn't get to off the exam. Stay engaged, you'll do fine!

Dr Cramer is great professor but her class is definitely hard! Beware there is a lot of information and it is easy to fall behind. Keep up with readings, Anki, and make sure to pay attention in class, she hints what will be on the exam sometimes. Exams are mainly memorization and covers every single thing she gives you. The lab is fun too!

If you want to succeed in this class you have to WORK for it. MCRO is VERY difficult and requires a lot of discipline if you want to do well. DO ANKI EVERYDAY!! It will help you A LOT. Anyways, overall, the class was good and Dr. Cramer cares a lot about her students.

Dr. Cramer is one of the best professors I have had at UNC! Mirro is content-heavy, but not as difficult as people say. The exams are primarily based on simple memorization and consist of multiple-choice, select-all, and fill-in-the-blank questions. As long as you keep up with the assignments (which there are a lot of) you will be fine!
I fully wished I had been hit by a car on the way to her classes. Not a single thing she said would be on the exams, were on the exam.

This is a HARD class, but an A/A- is obtainable. It really is just all memorization, but it is A LOT of information, so keep up with Anki, organism cards, and go to SI sessions! I LOVE Cramer and she really does care about what she's teaching, but honestly, she can be a bit frazzled at times. Still, the resources are there for you to succeed.

Her exams are EXTREMELY memorization based. I love a good application based test and these are not that so they were very difficult for me. ANKI is your best friend. And so is Dr. Cramer. So sweet in office hours, will give you fist bumps for questions you got right on the exam, etc. MCRO is hard, and needs a LOT of time but it is worth it.

MCRO is a difficult class, you need to listen to lectures and study to do well but I believe I was given more than enough resources to be successful. I personally found the lectures super interesting which helped. I also found the content to be pretty basic - there is just A LOT of it. Do not be afraid of Dr. Cramer! She was awesome!

Don't listen to the bad reviews. Dr. Cramer is the absolute best STEM professor at UNC. Yes, this class is a lot of information, and it requires a LOT of studying. But you can tell Dr. Cramer cares about her students and wants them to do well. Go to her office hours and STUDY!

This professor is hilarious, sure, sometimes she is a little disorganized and maybe a little insane, but I enjoyed her class. She made every lecture fun, and I could tell she really cared about the material and wanted us to do well.

Professor Cramer is an engaging lecturer who makes the material interesting. While the exams are challenging, completing the guided learning questions and using Anki and Unstuck AI for study prep can help you succeed. Overall, it's a tough but worthwhile class.

This class was interesting, and I learned a lot in the end. But this class is HARD, especially if you take it with other challenging STEM classes. Your grade is based purely on exams 2 Midterms, each 24%, and a Final that is 24%. These tests are DIFFICULT, but you can do well if you study at least 2 weeks in advance, DO THE ANKI, and meet with her!

I was scared going into this class because of her other reviews but I can truly say that she is an amazing professor and if you study and stay on top of the material you can definitely get an A. I have struggled in other science classes at UNC but Dr. Cramer does a good job on explaining content in a clear way. I would definitely recommend her!

She does care deeply for her students and you get that sense when you come into her office hours. She is a funny lecturer. The best way to stay on top of the class is to stay on top of your GLQs and rewatch the lectures!! After class print out the blank GLQ & treat it like a quiz to refresh your memory. She & her TAs are accessible through Piazza.

Professor Cramer genuinely cares about you and wants you to succeed. Compared to my other STEM classes, I really enjoyed this one, despite being scared to take it from the reviews on here. She is a very good lecturer and is very passionate about the material she is teaching. She curved all of our tests as well.

Dr. Cramer is very funny during lecture, and makes an hour and 15 minute lecture very engaging. The course is exam heavy as the three exams (2 exams and final exam) are worth 72% of your final grade. If you complete your guided learning questions, take good notes, and do anki, you will do fine in this class.

Dr. Cramer is one of my favorite professors at UNC! She is so sweet and really cares about her students and wants you to succeed. I highly suggest going to office hours and the SI sessions!! Although, the class is still hard and moves pretty fast. There is a TON of information to know. But getting a good grade is still doable!

Dr. Aliaga was a kind person, but not the best professor in my opinion. Her lectures were very boring and unengaging. Her class was very dependent on group work, so prepare to be stuck with random people who could potentially bring your grade down. The class was helpful, but felt very repetitive at times.

This class was super easy and fulfilled IDST and Communication Beyond Carolina requirements. Lectures are a bit scattered, and recitations are not super helpful, but I did learn more about leadership and feedback, which will be helpful in the future, and I had fun. Your grade is VERY group-dependent. Grading is a bit random but easy overall.
The class is not just a free A at all, dolly hard but nothing crazy. I think you just learn not much about being a leader, much more theoretical, most of grade is group project dependent
Class is thought be 3 professors and is extremely boring and oddly difficult for a gen-ed.

(I took iDST136) This class was taught by 3 professors, and Sofia was my least favorite as far as teaching style. Her lectures usually are a list of questions she asks the class, so there were many times it was awkward silence. Example could be our Midterm Q & A session. Someone asks something but instead of answering, she asks the class to reply.
Sofia Aliaga was able to connect concepts the best with outside experience. This class was just super hard for no reason and if you need to take a triple I chose something else.

She was the best professor and seemed to generally care about us but the class is very difficult and I would not take it again. It's very group heavy and I didn't get a good group. Also they never had clear instructions and were VERY disorganized. Final is worth a lot and very confusing. All the grading is done by the TA's and is pretty harsh.

Absolutely loved Dr. Aliaga, she is an amazing voice in relational leadership. I'm giving it 3/5 however because the class was rough. It was very disorganized and the lectures overlapped frequently which made it feel as if nothing new was being taught. Other Triple I classes are definitely easier and more enjoyable. Absolutely no hate to Sofia :)

Out of all the professors, she was definitely the kindest; she should not be blamed for how the other professors and TA's managed the course. Not a good class at all though. Extremely disorganized, harsh grading from the TA's, and overall the content was quite irrelevant and boring. You won't learn anything useful.

Caring and helped with issues. Fun to listen to her lectures. Awful class-Do NOT take. Lots of readings, project-based class with random students who don't do their part, MCQ final exam. Extremely disorganized, lots of people fall asleep during class, super boring, everything takes so much time. TA Jillian was great, the rest were awful.

This class is highly disorganized, with confusing lectures and inconsistent grading. Sofia was the nicest of the three instructors, but the group lacked cohesion and seemed unprepared. Also, her mouth sounds were distracting and annoying. Overall, it was a very frustrating experience. Save your sanity and avoid this class as much as possible.

Sofia was nice and shouldn't be blamed for unfair grading as that is all TAs, but DO NOT TAKE THIS TRIPLE-I. If you are assigned it like I was, SWITCH. OUT. The grading was ridiculous, the TAs do NOT hear you out, and the quizzes are impossible unless you were paying attention to every word in lectures. Lectures are very hard to follow.

Dr. Lapushin is the best! He is clearly passionate about what he does and makes learning fun. You are graded by few things, but he is willing to work with you to make sure you are receiving the best grade possible. I would 100000% take this class again if I could.
