Really sweet and caring guy! He gets very into the stories and is clearly passionate. You can get away with not doing the readings. He doesn't grade anything besides the midterm until the very end, but does so leniently.

Prof. Lapushin is amazing. I took his class in Fall 2024 and he was a warm welcome to UNC. He is a very sweet and sincere man. The class is easy: just a decent amount of reading each week, a short paper, an easy solo presentation, and two in-person written exams. I found the readings to be enjoyable, and you'll love the class if you like animals.

2nd time taking a class with Professor Lapushin. His classes are very engaging and the course material is usually pretty easy to understand and read. His midterms and finals are easy if you have read the texts, and he gives good feedback on the final paper as well. Definitely would recommend any of his classes, especially Chekov.

2nd time taking dr.lapushin. he is the absolute sweetest and goes so far out of his way to help. accessible and helps on the final paper (read and edited drafts). it was a class i never had to stress about and could always enjoy!

Dr. Lapushin is awesome and really cares about Russian Literature. The readings are great and for the most part really short. I learned some cool stuff about Chekhov and did not have to stress about grades, would definitely recommend.

AMAZING professor and amazing class. So caring, insightful, and considerate, not to mention extremely passionate about his field. Definitely a lot of reading but it is so worth it. Highly recommend a class with Professor Lapushin

Radislav was great professor. Only a few canvas discussions about the reading and a midterm and final, both which were essay. There is a bit a reading that you have to do every day before class, but you weren't forced to discuss in class. He is a great guy who cares a lot about what he teaches.

I love this man. He is very soft spoken and has a lot of personal knowledge about Soviet Russia, which was interesting to listen to. I missed 3-4 classes but was not marked down. There is a decent amount of reading, but it is all fiction. Super easy and love this professor.

he is the best. most students who take him once will take him again. he is so knowledgable and so understanding. the class is set up like a book club (you don't have to speak, and there are never grades to check if you did the readings). he's very accessible and willing to help with the final paper. reading can be a lot (~200 pgs/week). take him!

Such a sweet guy. If you have the opportunity to take this class DO IT. Short readings before every class  that are talked about in class but if you pay attention and do the small amount of work you will get an A!

Loved Lapushin! He was really funny and loved it when we asked questions and discussed in class. We did have a lot of reading for this class and it was a bit difficult to keep track of the 20+ stories. We had 1 midterm and final all online. We had 2 papers.

Prof. Lapushin is definitely the most passionate and kindest professor I've had so far! This class isn't really difficult to do well in, you just have to keep up with the readings for each class, but to be fair there are a lot and they got longer later in the sem. (up to ~40 pages). Midterm/final have short essays, discussion posts every few weeks.

Lapushin is an amazing professor who loves what he does! There is a good amount of reading, so be prepared! Participation is required as the class is discussion-based. There is a midterm, a paper, and a final -- all very manageable. Tip: you have to buy many books & it can get expensive, but I got them from Davis or you can try to find them online.

One of the best profs I've had at UNC. Such a kind and understanding professor who truly cares about the subject material and his students. He asks thought-provoking questions in class but relies on students for discussion, but many participate so the classroom dynamic is great. Would recommend 10/10 to take a class w/ Lapushin if you can!

He is an amazing professor, genuinely cares about literature. There is a lot of reading but the selections are all great. Discussions in class were enjoyable and there was good participation from everyone

Professor Lapushin is so great! He's sweet and animated with his lectures. The class is fully discussion based so you have to do the readings for credit (i found most of the books through online sources). There is one midterm with clear criteria and a final paper that's broad and more complicated. the vast majority of your grade is this final paper

FOR RUSS/WGST 486 - Lapushin is the kindest and most passionate professor at UNC. I had never read any Russian lit and was completely fine in the class. Class is very interactive and you do need to do the reading. Reading is heavy, but it is a lit class. If you need an extension on anything, he will give it if you send an email. Love Lapushin!

ACTUALLY FOR RUSS486. for some reason it won't let me add a new class. lapushin is a true performer, his lectures are truly an act. this class is something he is very passionate about and it is extremely evident. the readings are very interesting and i definitely recommend if you need a gen ed

Although participation is required, Lapushin works hard to make his class feel more like a bookclub than a lecture hall. The content is easy to analyze and any confusion will definitely be cleared up in class. Not a lot of homework + easy grader. Plus he is the sweetest!
Lectures were kind of hard to follow but interesting. I really liked most of material we covered, could be boring at times. Opportunity to earn points back at end of semester.

I really enjoyed taking Stas and this course! The structure of the lectures was different than what I was familiar with, but it made class interesting. We used lectures to discuss a piece of media we were assigned to read/watch on our own time each week. The discussions genuinely improved my critical thinking. He is also very kind and accessible!

Professor Shvabrin was incredibly enthusiastic and charismatic. I loved his style of teaching, and the class discussions over novels we read were insightful. I definitely recommend GSLL84 to those genuinely interested in Russian history and literature, but to those who are not, this class can be reading-heavy and take up a lot of time.

Professor Shvabrin is an extremely passionate instructor, and this course was very insightful. Lectures were rather abstract, but I was able to learn a lot even on days when I had a really hard time following along. He didn't put any grades in Canvas, which was frustrating, but my final grade was posted on the Student Center on time anyway.

Dr. Shvabrin was very invested in the topic personally and invited students to contribute their opinions and experiences. There was a lot of reading in the first few weeks, but most of the course is watching films. Taking notes during lectures is crucial to understanding this class. Good for a humanities gen-ed. Big final paper, though.

A very good professor teaching an extremely interesting class. I was kind of shocked to see that students at an elite school like UNC complain about reading "five books" (GASP!) a semester--especially in a literature class. These are not serious people and should probably be attending a less selective school. The books are great; so's the class.

stas is so intelligent that @1st i felt nervous to ask for help. however, he is the kindest & most uplifting prof so dont be afraid to meet w him outside of class or ask for help. has become my absolute fav class & completely changed my views on “lolita” & nabokov. 4 book quizzes (missed q's on these become the final), 2 written papers, final.

Stas is very kind, knowledgable and accessible outside of class. However, be aware that this is one of the toughest literature classes I have taken as an English major. Lectures were rlly confusing and it was difficult to get concrete takeaways. Quizzes were tough but you earn can back points with the final, and the books we read were great.

Dr. Shvabrin's Nabokov course comes highly, highly recommended; as a graduating senior, it's easily a top 3 class I've taken at UNC. I emerged from the class a certified Nabokov fan but, more importantly, a more astute reader and erudite thinker. Dr. Shvabrin's lectures are among the best I've come across and make coming to class a joy. Take him!

This is my second class with Stas. Some ppl don't like the way he teaches, but you have to reframe it as an illusive performance! I love being in his classes. The books were really interesting. We had quizzes for each book. The midterm was just a regular book quiz. The final was just the questions that you missed on your book quizzes. 1 long paper.

He is truly passionate about what he teaches, always willing to answer questions and guide you through any assignment. You can tell he genuinely wants his students to learn and succeed. I would definitely take his class again!

He's the worst professor I've ever had. During class he invites everyone to participate but if you don't say exactly what he wants on tests he'll take multiple points off without explaining why. He's extremely condescending and rude and won't help you with anything. I went to him for office hours but he didn't help at all. Avoid him!

I'm a senior, and among all the courses I have taken this is in my top 5. His teaching style encourages critical thinking. He fostered a safe and encouraging environment while we dealt with difficult subjects. As a 400 lvl course, it is challenging, but worth it. By the end, I recognized growth in myself. You get what you put into the course.

He's a passionate and kind person, but a tough professor. His lecture style can be confusing and I often left class more confused than when I came in. It felt like he talked in riddles and tried to lead us to a point in lectures, but never told us the point if we didn't come to it. Tests were very fair. Didn't address Nabokov's misogyny.

Great professor and very passionate about what he teaches. However, I took this class to fulfill a focus capacity and didn't really know what I was getting myself into. There is a lot of reading, and if you can't keep up it's difficult to participate in class, which is a factor in your grade. Overall, only take if you can really commit to reading.

I LOVED this class! It was my favorite course this semester. Shvabrin was funny and always encouraged group discussion. We wrote 2 papers. The second paper could be a revised version of your first one. We had a midterm and a cumulative final. We read and watched really interesting materials like 'Rocky IV'. Take this class!

I wouldn't advise taking 280 for the gen ed. He is very unclear about grading criteria and speaks almost completely in metaphors, lectures are incredibly wishy washy. However, I thought I was for sure going to end up with a B- at most and finished with an A because of how many points were available to earn back on the final. Fine, but not great.

I wouldn't wish this class on my worst enemy. He never made expectations clear, graded with extremely harsh comments, yet I still haven't received my actual grade. He speaks in riddles, gives far too much hw, clearly wants us to get to some point in class discussions but just isn't capable of leading us there. He shouldn't work as a professor.

harshest feedback I have ever seen on an essay, criticism borderlines on personal. I would never have expected how harsh he was. Comes off as a cool and passionate guy, but when he's mean, he's really mean. Do NOT take his class as a Gen ed, he had us read 5 full length books. I regret signing up for this class, although I did learn a lot.

Professor Shvabrin is one of the best professors at UNC, he was super chill and obviously cares about teaching the material. The class was very fun, especially if you like Russian history and movies and it was overall very easy, take this class.

Prof Whitaker is great, class has writing assignments, 1 midterm exam, final is group policy brief. Attendance is not monitored, but midterm is lecture based so go to class. Prof is very passionate and wants to help you. Gives clear grading criteria on writing assignments. Semester long war sim., unclear grading for this, EXTREMELY time consuming.

Professor Whitaker is a great professor. However, for PWAD250 you must be prepared for her grading. She is very reasonable but also very strict. Follow her syllabus, rubrics, and announcements diligently. One point on an assignment is equal to one percent on your grade. There aren't many assignments-bring your best to each. She also doesn't round.
Prof. Whitaker is a great professor. I just did not enjoy the class material. She has very clear grading criteria; if you genuinely focus in class and on homework, you will get an easy A.

Make sure to participate each class, participation is a big part of her grading. Your grade will be fine if you follow her rubric exactly and pay attention to in class directions, for each assignment. No final exam, did a debate at the end of the semester, was not graded harshly.

PWAD 89 was my favorite class from this semester, and I loved Professor Whitaker's teaching method. I will say there are a lot of readings, but the class gets easier with time. Each assignment has a relatively low point value, which means everything matters. I would totally recommend taking a course with her!

Her courses have been a boon to my GPA despite excelling on the actual writing and policy assignments. If you are quiet or struggle with participation do not take her. This page is dominated by her FY seminar for a reason. Wait until Wayne Lee is teaching PWAD250, guest lectures and working at the CIA does not mean you will learn more.

One of my favorite professors and loved this course! She is very engaging and her field experience really shines through, Participation is very important so make you understand the readings and relate them in class. A few papers and solid amount of group work but nothing over the top. Excited to take 250 with her next semester!

The class has a fairly light workload, and papers shouldn't be too difficult if you wrote a decent amount in higher level high school courses. Participation counts for 15% of your grade, so be prepared to talk in class and do (or at least skim) the readings beforehand. Lots of group work, but it's generally pretty easy to divide up.

Prof Whitaker is great, definitely very knowledgable in her field. While she is pretty strict with her grading, there is a lot of leeway built into the syllabus, and she is willing to grant a one time extension if you just reach out to her. Will be taking another class with her next semester.

By far one of the most informative classes I have taken at UNC! Prof. Whitaker is extremely knowledgable and her power points were extremely digestible and easy to go back and reference when needed. The final is a group policy brief which I loved. I definitely plan on taking another class with her!

Professor Whitaker is a great professor, her class felt like home from the beginning. She was by far my favorite professor in my first semester at UNC. She is very knowledgeable on her topics and is very easy to talk to. I would highly recommend her she just isn't any old professor.

Professor Whitaker was fantastic. I took my first year seminar with her and was moved by how effectively she taught the class, connected with her students, and let her students connect with one another. She's really smart and a great professor. I would absolutely recommend this class.

Whitaker is so kind, smart, and interesting! She gives great lectures and really wants you to engage in the class. For reflections and assignments, don't be afraid to show up with your real questions, and she loves helping students understand the security system.

Professor Whitaker is incredible. Definitely take a class with her. She cares about feedback and improving your experience. She can be a tough grader but her rubrics are very clear. There's no final exam in PWAD 250 but there is a group discussion almost every week and a big group assignment.

PWAD89 was one of my favorite classes ever! Professor Whitaker is so knowledgeable and well versed in her subject, it is so enjoyable listening to her lecture. Class was ready heavy and discussion based, but super manageable. As a freshman, I could not recommend a teacher more! She was very kind during office hours and very understanding.

If you are a freshman looking for a seminar at UNC take PWAD 89! I am not a PWAD major but I absolutely loved this class. Professor Whitaker is extremely knowledgable and engaging. She brought in amazing guest lecturers who shared their experience in the intelligence industry, which made the course even more interesting. Highly recommend!

Prof. Whitaker might be the best teacher I've ever had! She is caring, respectful, and really cares that you learn the content. She is the reason I added my PWAD major, and I hope to take more classes with her in the future. Class is reasonably reading heavy, but nothing unmanageable. Take her!

Professor Whitaker is a dream and very refreshing Professor. Having worked for many years in the IC, she brings an expertise and understanding of the world that is rare in academia. Many peers scored low on her participation grade, but if you make sure to attend class regularly and talk whenever you are there, participation should not be an issue.

Tough grader for a first-year seminar, ESPECIALLY with papers (10 points off for one sentence), but the final debate was graded surprisingly leniently. Could redo paper for up to half the points back. She would cold call and the readings were tedious but interesting. Lots of guest speakers and fun in-class assignments! Overall, hard but manageable.

Professor Whitaker is a great professor in the PWAD department. She is very understanding and caring. She really values feedback and will give you feedback on your papers which is really helpful. I found her class extremely engaging and useful.
Was the most caring and amazing Professor

Few people can say they've impacted lives like Andy has, whether it be in his time at USAID or inspiring students at UNC. Andy has enormous compassion and the utmost care and respect for his students, and would look forward to class on the weekends. I wouldn't have skipped this class in a hurricane, snowstorm, or outbreak of the bubonic plague.

Andy is one of the best professors I've had here. He is dedicated to helping the next generation handle the world's issues and it shows. If you have the chance to, take his class, or if you don't, swing by his office hours to chat.

Andy is certainly one of the most caring professors I've had during my time at UNC. As the creator of this class, he wants the opportunity to engage in discussion with his students and give them opportunities to see if a career in the foreign service is a good fit. Very thoughtful, super wise, and full of anecdotes, I cannot recommend Andy enough!

One of my favorite professors here while at UNC. Andy is a wonderful person and an excellent teacher. He has so many stories and is extremely knowledgable. I would love to take a class with him again!

Osborne is a great professor, and really knows and cares about what she teaches. Some topics can be a little boring, and she's a little monotone for the first couple of chapters, but if you interact, she's a great instructor. The class isn't hard, as it is graded purely on online quizzes, which are easy as long as you follow along in class.

Overall, a good professor but the class material is boring, it's based around a lot of readings and court cases, so she can only make it so interesting. The quizzes online for each chapter can be difficult but are not too hard if you go to class and pay attention. Quizzes could probably be done w/o going to class but would definitely be harder.
Not an easy course, but with 100% online quizzes you can do well on them. Attendance is optional and overall just boring lectures.

You will not regret taking Professor Osborne! She is hands down one of the best professors I have ever had the privilege of taking. I highly recommend her course and she will always do whatever it takes to make you successful in the course. She definitely cares about her students. The course has challenging aspects of it as it is a law class.

Took this as asynchronous during Summer I. Grade was completely based on 12 quizzes. I enjoyed the class overall, and Prof Osborne was super available to answer any questions, or just chat during office hours.

Professor McCormack was great. You can tell she cares a lot about her students and their success. Overall, the class wasn't very difficult, and I learned a lot. There are some confusing topics, but she answers questions well.

Assignments and tests were very fair and not graded harshly. She clearly loves teaching and really wants her students to succeed. I learned a lot about how to use R, run regression models, and analyze results from this class. A class all BIOS majors should look forward too.

Amazing professor. I've never taken a biostats class before, and she made it very doable. Grading on homework and labs was generous. The exams were not terrible, and even though exam 2 was a little more difficult, she gave us points back for questions she thought were unfair. She really cares about every student, and it shows. Very kind person.

She really wants you to succeed, like how she simply gave everyone a 100% for an entire exam problem because she didn't specify a formula, although we did it in class before. She is a nice grader and very accessible for extra help, and will do a lot of extra things to help whenever she can.

If you can, you should absolutely take BIOS 600 with her. She is kind, caring, and lets way more slide than she should while also being understanding and lenient. 8:00am class was tough since her voice is a little drone-esque, but she is funny, and lenient grader, and will go out of her way for you the student. 10/10 take this class with her.
she doesnt know how to plan course scheduling, disregarding student needs in terms of randomly overloading us w assignments

I have no idea how Dr. Monaco is so highly reviewed on here because she is, by far, the most overwhelming professor I have had with the most ridiculous expectations. She wants EVERY DOCUMENT AND ASSIGNMENT printed out, even though it's an online class. She also talks so quickly and never really finishes a sentence, so trying to understand is hard.

Homework is graded for participation, not accuracy, yet feedback is extremely particular and micromanaged, focusing on formatting, wording, and presentation. Expectations are scattered across a long syllabus, FAQs, Q&A documents, and constant announcements. Lectures are unhelpful. High stress, low clarity.

Dr. Monaco was very sweet and ran a very fair class. I loved how accommodating and reasonable she was with due dates and assignment lengths. She was very clear about what would be tested, and I would definitely take a class with her again.

She's so kind, made time to talk with me outside of class about general concerns I was having with the public health major (cough cough SPHG 351). She clearly cares about her students and this class is a layup if you just do the work and go to class.
Very mean. Not focused on teaching.

The nicest professor ever! I would highly recommend taking a class with her if you can. BIOS 500 is very easy as long as you turn your things by the due date. The flipped classroom is a bit bothersome, but you'll get used to it over time. Again, don't sweat it, you'll do great, especially with so much support from Dr. Monaco and the TAs.

Genuinely the most caring professor I've ever had. If you can buy into the flipped classroom it will boost your understanding a lot. She focuses on truly understanding the content which is awesome for the public health context. Has been teaching for a long time, well-known but still so kind. Take her!!

Dr. Monaco is super passionate about the field of biostatics. Very caring and kind professor. HW, tests, and assignments directly relate to lectures/videos and teach you the content effectively. Lots of good feedback on assignments and doesnt penalize you for trying. If you put effort into the HWs you will learn some neat stuff and get a good grade

Just the sweetest professor - always available to meet outside of class to talk about plans and get help. The course itself isn't too challenging, but she always made sure to give us time to practice with SAS and other statistics problems in class (class work was required but you didn't turn anything in so it was more free to do at your leisure)

She's great. It's easy to hate on the flipped classroom but I only realized towards the end that it was very helpful. Yes, a lot of busy work, but she prepares you well for any HW/exams and future biostats courses. Very inspirational and understanding of students. Gave us multiple free 100s + extensions.
Great professor! In-class final and midterm are fair but manageable to study for especially with a flashcard as a cheat sheet.
She's a queen! Absolutely adore her

Dr. Monaco is one of the most caring, enthusiastic professors I've ever had. Other complaints about the flipped setup are exaggerated--the videos were never that long and she always reiterated everything in class. Tests were fair, and while homework assignments were long, she graded them leniently and was flexible with deadlines.

Not a great professor, but kinda the only option. I think she needs to rethink the flipped classroom style a bit. Easy A though so don't worry. Just prepare for the most unnecessary work of your life.

dr. monaco is the best, the flipped classroom environment was honestly not that bad imo, you just have to make sure to keep up with it, the class itself and the info can be tough at times but it's like any other class and studying will get you an A or A-. 100% recommend taking this class with dr. monaco!

this course singlehandedly forced me to drop out of the biostatistics major at UNC. the flipped classroom setup was not conducive to learning especially having to watch videos all the time. the concepts were difficult and were poorly explained in class. sas is not intuitive and oftentimes a struggle.
Having a final project and a final exam in which the final project takes away time from studying and makes it so you have less time to study for the exam wow what a brilliant idea.

LOVED having Dr. Monaco as a professor, I was a prospective student and she was so encouraging and helped me out so much! She is genuinely one of the kindest professors I have ever interacted with and is so sweet and interested in helping us with respect to personal / career-related ambitions. I loved the class and learned so much from her!

In reality, I think Monaco is more like a 4/5, however the amount of hate she's been getting by people rating her for this last semester, in my opinion, makes no sense. She was passive aggressive at times, and the lectures were chaotic, but she was a kind, accessible, caring professor who wanted the best for us. An A was a 92.5.

Mid prof that uses flipped learning style. Emailed us after semester was over and asked us to rate her positively on RMP which is ironic for a stats professor. Curious what made her reach out: neg. reviews from this semester are pretty fair, pos. reviews (from Jan after her email) are pretty biased.

Would not recommend this professor. He is very nice and passionate about data science, however, his lectures are hard to follow and consistently cover topics beyond the scope of the class. Focuses on theory and not actual coding practice. Kinda a professor is too smart to teach situation. Ur better off watching yt videos if your goal is to learn R.

No syllabus or structure, essentially just practice for people who already know everything about R and AI-related topics. Absolutely not suited to beginners. Worst class I've taken in college or grad school.

The professor is very knowledgeable about data science. However, this class is not appropriate for beginners and lacks organization & structure. R was only taught for a couple of lectures, then expected to be understood after that. This class should be an advanced graduate-level course rather than an intro course; people are quickly left behind

It's an easy A, but not suited for beginners. Prof Toups is brilliant, but not suited for an entry level R class. No syllabus/grading was posted. Class was expected to know all of R by lecture 2. Lectures are dominated by 30-min rants and tangents. Discussion is discouraging. You'll need supplemental learning for basics. Avoid if you like structure

Imagine you need to water your garden but instead of using a watering can, you use a fire hose. That's this class. 

You'll do best if you have prior experience with R, Python, Bash, Docker, Git, & Make. I will say Vincent is very helpful in office hours and generous with grading. However, HW due dates change a lot and are sometimes during breaks.

All-time great 1hr15min lecturer. 4-6 page midterm; 8-10 page final; two 2.5-4 page essays (prompts given more than a month in advance). ~3 readings a week, summarized in class, so not required, but interesting nevertheless. 15 films, most from the 21st-century. Lectures are insightful and extensive, which makes it a bit hard to participate.

Dr. Warner had interesting lectures and great film recommendations. You definitely don't have to do the readings. Course is graded by a few papers, but just put some time into them and show him you care about your grade. Try not to miss lectures, they're super chill anyway.

Great Professor, not a hard class just really time consuming especially in the first half of the semester when you have to write notes for each film. Although you have time because they are turned in for a midterm grade in the middle of the semester. Great class!

Professor Warner had great lectures which really expanded my knowledge on films and the components that go with creating a good film! Grade depends on your TA, make sure to show up for lectures and have your laptop and phone put away during class.

Dr. Warner was an excellent professor that incorporated a good blend of classic, modern, and underground artsy films into the syllabus. He is very clear about his expectations regarding assignments. The homework was usually watching a film and reading an accompanying article/essay. Would recommend to anyone interested in film.

Dr. Warner is truly an expert in his field. I've always loved film, but his lectures made me interested to the point that I've decided to pursue the Global Cinema Minor. He is knowledgeable and engaging. That being said, your grade is entirely determined by TAs in this course, but mine was awesome, so no complaints there.

Good class, good professor. Lots of movies to watch but he picks good ones. 3 papers handled by TAs, fairly self explanatory. Recommend for a gen ed class. Lectures are interesting, but you have to show up. Attendance is taken.

Dr. Warner is incredible! Class is very lecture-heavy but it is always a joy to hear Dr. Warner's passion for and knowledge of film. 2 papers + 2 mini papers for final exam, lots of writing but graded leniently. Gives great, detailed feedback on essays. Extra credit by writing short papers about films. A true expert in his field and it shows.

Rick is the GOAT of UNC film studies and probably the entire English department. Get ready to unlock new dimensions of the cinema as Rick invites you to ponder the artistic medium with a whole new mindset. His got a bit of quirkyness that usually translates into rehearsed or off-the-cuff jokes that land most of the time.

Professor Warner is incredibly kind and chill. He obviously LOVES movies and centers the class around the film watched for homework. The class is lecture heavy but he makes the talks engaging and always asks students to offer their thoughts. 2 papers and 1 quiz and 1 final exam. A great class if you want an easygoing course or love movies!

Makes boring movies interesting, that's the biggest complement I can give. Engaging, makes complex film theory accessible, seriously knows his stuff. The class gets way into the weeds on film theory, but if you're into movies you'll learn a lot and be able to speak about them in a much more educated way. Definitely a prof worth checking out.

Rick was an interesting professor, and the class is super interesting and fun. Learned a lot about film and how to more deeply appreciate the artistic aspects of whatever film I'm watching. At the same time, I sometimes felt like I was taking my TA's class more than Rick's, as the course is large and recitation can be more important than lecture.

He's a bit awkward but he genuinely loves what he does and the content that he teaches. My TA was phenomenal and graded really fairly but others weren't as lucky. I loved how many different films we watched and Rick's background knowledge makes his lectures so interesting. Learned so much and really enjoyed this class.

The TA you have will determine the grade you get, but I really enjoyed Rick's lectures and enjoyed most of the movies that we had to watch. This semester we were able to go view some of them at the Varsity Theater and I would highly recommend to go if future classes get this chance it made the viewing experience 10 times better!

Be sure to get a good TA for this class as they grade papers. Lots of extra credit here even though he might say that he won't give any more. He also dropped a paper which helps, but don't count on it. Movies are super interesting, but sometimes really long. You don't have to watch all of them to get a good grade (if you aren't writing about them).
Funny, sweet, and caring. Warner clearly loves cinema and he put a lot of great screenings on the syllabus. Papers are graded toughly, and there's a lot of writing. 95 for an A is a challenge.

Rick is Good, Rick is Great. The syllabus is super interesting, a good range of all things horror. Participate! There are 3 papers, but Rick is super accessible and will literally give you so many ideas. Highly Recommend!

-Another review talked about 50 page readings and 2 movies a week, thats cap. Watching movies for homework is pretty chill.

I went into this class for a gen ed, and overall enjoyed the content. Good selection of films, feel like I learned a lot. We produced 20 pages of writing for the midterm, final paper, and final exam. Participation is graded by how much you speak in class and the paper's are graded kind of harsh. An A is a 95 also, whomp whomp. Nice guy tho.

Really enjoyed this class! Rick is so knowledgable about films, specifically horror for this class, and he has a great sense of humor. The class is more paper heavy but you can choose to do a creative project instead of a final paper. I've walked away with a new-found appreciation for horror films -- highly recommend taking a class with Rick!

Probably the best and most interesting class that I've taken at UNC.  Dr. Warner is so kind and funny and his lectures are very interesting.  He doesn't take himself too seriously.  Overall, it was just an amazing class.  Would definitely recommend it to anyone who needs to fulfill a Gen Ed.  If you can take a class with rick do it

Dr. Urquhart exercises alot of patience when dealing with some students. Gladly, I was not one of those students. Sometimes he can be long-winded, but he does provide valuable real-world experience.  Overall, it is a strong class and a great opportunity to build your portfolio.

I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Urquhart is very approachable. In particular, I appreciate his honestly and real world examples. I could tell that he really cares, although some students wanted to blame him for their lack of responsibility. He was always available to meet after class and would even assign extra credit. The key is to come to class.

Dr. Urquhart is a great prof who won't shy away from sharing his real-world experience with the class. Teaching-wise, he's very direct and has been using the same assignments since forever, so there are clear expectations. However, since the semester project is a group one, you better pray for good teammates. Good class and great portfolio booster.

This class was a huge waste of time. I heard that 382 with other professors is actually really helpful but I feel like I didn't learn anything. he was not clear at all on what he wanted and graded harshly. Didn't learn much he seems like a nice guy but takes himself too serious and doesn't teach any material. You have to cheat on quizzes due to ts
Boring 2.5 hour lectures.

Super student‑focused. He invited feedback throughout the term and actually used it. His real‑world examples helped the material stick, and he made sure everyone participated. Would definitely take his class again. To stay in the loop, you must come to class.

Loved the class. He checked in often, adjusted based on our feedback, and used real‑life examples that made the content practical. Lots of participation, but low‑pressure. I'd absolutely take another class with him.

Amazing professor. If you're struggling in this class, it's not on him it's on you. He's tough, blunt, and expects you to act like an adult. People who complain are just soft and not ready for real expectations. If you can "handle" honesty and want to actually learn, take his class. Highly recommend.

The other reviews aren't wrong, he definitely gets cross with the class sometimes. However, he did a good job of putting us in an entrepreneurial mindset and I got more out of this class than I was expecting. He also offered to write us a LoR for grad school which was unprecedented. Was he my favorite prof? No, but he far exceeded my expectations.
Horrible professor and grader. Did not give me any reasons for the grades he gave me so I had to drop the class. Changing majors because of him.

Switched directions a lot in the class during the semester, never made full use of the lecture time and would go on random tangents and impassioned lectures. Very funny and approachable, but unsure what the point of the lecture was. Semester long project also felt purposeless, could have been completed within a week.

I read the comments and had some apprehension coming into the class. I was amazed about how the comments were totally wrong. I'm a Jr and many of the ppl were Sr. who were complaining. All you had to do was come to class, complete the assignments. He was always available to meet via zoom, b4 or after class. Don't pay attn to the crybaby comments

This class is a joke and not worth my time or money, but it's mandatory and easy so whatever. Prof randomly gave us a pop quiz one day and no one even knew what it would be on since we weren't learning anything...

He spends most of the lecture telling stories that are not relevant to the course work -- also a very subjective grader. He is "against rubrics" so he will give you the grade he feels like giving you and you cannot dispute it utilizing a rubric.

The class is fairly easy, though. He is upset that it is considered an "easy A" class.

Just a horrible professor who does not respond to emails at all and gives really long and boring lectures. But you are pretty much on your own because he will not respond to any sort of communication so if you have any questions about your assignments you are on your own.
This class is super easy if u just show up. Literally all you need is common sense and like attempt to make a decent thing and he will give you a good grade

He started out very nice, but halfway through the semester he got mad at the class and suddenly everything was graded harder. He changed due dates, directions were not very clear, and he had no office hours on his syllabus. Grading seemed subjective as well. Hes not a bad guy, but he definitely needs to create rubrics for his assignments.
Ryan was all over the place. I could not tell you what I learned in this class and I went every time. He changed criteria for grading and never gave good feedback. It was an easy class.

This class is composed of four easy quizzes, a presentation and a project. Each week there is a lecture and recitation but attendance isn't taken. Prof Urquhart is a cool guy and you can get whatever you want out of the class. Probably the easiest class I've taken at UNC.

A low-stress class that was very manageable. Just follow instructions and you'll do fine. Sometimes they can be vague so you just have to ask questions but overall the class was really reasonable. Prof. Urquhart was very nice and generally cared about the students. Grades mostly come from 1-2 quizzes, article pres., and a semester group project.

An extremely unorganized and average professor. Winget's mandatory class consisted of reading off of a slideshow and then having 'group work' or brainstorming from previous weeks. She is typically unhelpful and vague about all of her assignments and gives surface level feedback.

Teacher has an attitude so not comfortable sharing a dissenting opinion. Was rather passive-aggressive.
Final project for 777 is actually decent but the other class is tedious

Wignet is a condescending, rude, and absent professor. I often thought she thought very little of us as people, and was not above scoffing in my face. She's taking all of Melanie Feinberg's presentations, and doing a botched job of them, with not being able to facilitate discussion, and sat back in class to do her duolingo. Granted, an easy class.

Literally saw/heard her violate ADA by questioning a student's legally mandated accommodations. I hope that student reported it especially since she was approached discreetly but replied loud enough and bluntly enough everyone heard the conversation. She's very passive aggressive and she was constantly rude.

Professor Winget is alright. This course was online and she required cameras on. I turned mine off for 15 seconds to pull my pants up and she requested i turn it back on, which was kind of irritating. Kind of sassy, a little condescending, but still cares about students if you email her and you're having any problems.

Since it was online, she was very particular about having your camera on & participating every session. If you didn't do both of these things, she'd mark you absent. The group work was challenging, since we weren't in person. But overall, its an easy class and she's mostly fine attitude wise.
Everything was so bad that I don't even know how to explain it. Her attitude was terrible every time.

This class is basically a semester-long group project, and the instructor barely teaches. The final is a project presentation, and she scheduled “group work weeks” with no class. Then, a week before, she suddenly required a pre-presentation, even though many of us already had plans that day. Also, she's always on her phone during class.

Very unapproachable. Seems kind, but it doesn't seem genuine. There's a lot of lack of guidance in her class. I understand this class is supposed to be us putting our skills to the test, but it genuinely feels like a class led by a substitute. She is also very pessimistic. I don't find the class itself stressful, it's her and her way of teaching.

If you need to take the Info Sci capstone take it with her. She makes things very clear and pretty easy. She gives pretty clear cut feedback just makes sure to work with your groupmates with everything. There's tons of group work

I took Winget for INLS-777 but it wouldn't let me select that as an option. She is pretty callous and doesn't really care about the students, and when we were put in groups for class activities or discussions you could hear her watching TikTok. Very rude and insensitive about international students, and overall I would not recommend.

She's a good teacher I suppose, but this class is the biggest waste of time. Since it's a required class, you have to endure it. I know she tries to makes things easy which they are, but each class feels like another pointless group activity for team building or something. But if you have to take this class, she's a fine teacher to take it with.

Although the material was often hard and confusing, he really did try his best to make it make sense. He would also try to make it engaging despite the large class size. Professor Capra was also quite understanding of external situations so long as you have a UAA.

Mr. Capra def cares about his students and the questions they ask. I normally just read rate my professor but i know he's the type of professor to read these. The material isn't the most entertaining but the way he talks and conducts class is awesome and keeps me engaged. I haven't had an exam yet but normal day to day class is a treat. Recommend

I thought the class was taught very well. All assignments, homeworks, and tests were very reasonable with what was taught in class and never felt overwhelming. He definitely reads his reviews as he addressed a lot of the previous year's feedback and worked to improve.
Honest to god you will learn and he does his best, but makes the class harder than really needed. If I had to take this class again I would try another Professor.

Capra is a solid teacher but sometimes lectures could be a lil rushed. 3 exams weighted 15% ea, similar to the practice exam and you'll be fine if you practice extensively (mcq, t/f, diagram-drawing). For our final, he posted the practice exam w/o an answer key which sucked and tested items from Exams 1/2, though he said it wasn't cumulative.

People that complain about this class are probably not the brightest. This class was definitely easier than COMP110 in my opinion. It is more conceptual based than computational skills. Capra is definitely a great teacher and he knows what he is talking about. You'll be fine as long as you attend lecture and pay attention

It is a chill class. Two midterms that are 15% each and also a final that is also 15%. Attendance is graded but graded in a way where you can miss a certain amount of classes and still get a 100% for it. Also get 3 late passes that you can use at once or however much you want on every assignment. Exams were pretty simple and not too hard.
Never respond to emails.
I went this whole class thinking that a 90+ was an A because his syllabus said 90-100 A and 80-89 B, but he changed it after the class was over to give out +/- without telling anyone???? screw him
He did not follow his own syllabus for grading and he is very hard compared to the other INLS 523 professors. But not following his syllabus for the grade range is crazy
Chiller for real for real

I really enjoyed this class and professor Capra. His lectures are clear and he tries to have fun. He took participation with poll everywhere. Reading quizzes and homeworks were not too difficult. Pay attention in class and it will be a lot easier in the long run. Overall great guy and very helpful.

My favorite class here at UNC. Rob is a clear lecturer, and topics are very easy to follow. The midterms are long, but as long as you go to class, they are easy! He makes topics interesting to learn about. He is funny and positive. The TAs give helpful comments on assignments too. Had so much fun!
He's a great professor and takes the time to explain hard concepts. But the grading distribution is hard and the assignments and tests are hard with averages of 75. Put in work for an A!!!
Quite a bit of work, but she is very flexible and understanding as a teacher.

Fei is a very passionate teacher. She was always communicative and understanding, so long as you communicate first. The class was organized as one major group-project with various smaller projects and quizzes sprinkled throughout. I would've liked to see shake-ups in team composition so you could interact with more students.

I have never rated a professor before but I felt like it had to be done for Professor Fei Yu. She is one of the most unorganized teachers I have ever had. She assigns a lot of little projects that have quick turn around so we never really have time to understand the material. I feel like I waste my time in her class and wish I had a different teach

I didn't learn much from 718 as the flipped classroom & virtual format puts the full burden of learning on the student. Class time was not utilized well. We'd sometimes use 45+ mins to talk logistics/rubrics & skim over actual content. I will say that Yu responds to emails/feedback readily, isn't a harsh grader, and does games on Zoom though.

DON'T TAKE 718 W/ YU! I have taken other UX classes and was very excited to learn more in this class. Instead, I felt like each week hours were wasted of my life. Class was so DULL! She was never helpful at office hours and she didn't give clear instructions on the HW. Also didn't hesitate to call ppl out in class. MEJO 581 with Ruel was better!
Dr. Fei Yu is a great professor and one of my favorites in the program.  If anything were confusing, she would always be happy to clarify and genuinely cares about her student's success.
He is very knowledgeable but doesn't really teach in a way that promotes comprehension. His lectures are long and dull and he assigned a lot of readings that we never really discussed.

If you can take this class with someone else besides cal, you should. He's an incredibly pleasant professor, and I gained a lot from his course. Elliot is such an amazing professor. He is passionate about his students and what he teaches. He is very personable, has engaging lectures, and assigns projects that are impactful!
Attendance is a must! I missed a few classes over the limit was penalized. But he is a great prof who cares about his students success.

Dr. Kuecker is literally the best professor I've ever had. He builds incredibly well-organized online classes, so there is no excuse to miss an assignment--you can work ahead which is so nice. He also is just one of the nicest people you will meet and clearly cares about his students. If you show up and do the work, you will learn so much from him!

An awesome professor. He really cares about 1) what he's teaching and 2) his students. The assignments are fun and engaging, as are the in-class discussions. Assigned readings average at about 3 per week. He also likes to share relevant events and employment/internship/award opportunities, which is a plus. Again, great professor!

Professor Kuecker has a great reputation at UNC SILS as being of the few professors who not only teaches real-world skills but is approachable, friendly, and helpful. He goes above and beyond for the students, and everyone would benefit by taking as many of his classes as possible. 20/10 DO recommend.
Mike is awesome but sometimes he poses really specific questions to the class that only he knows the “correct” answer to. But he is such a character and a good professor.

Took the idea of AI with Professor Fox, one of the most thought-provoking classes I've taken at UNC. We talked about many contemporary AI ethics issues, and the discussions felt very current and intellectually stimulating. The atmosphere is excellent. He is also a generous grader. Really hope he teaches more courses in SILS in the future.

Class was asynchronous, and our lectures were videos. Michael was available for questions when something stumped me on assignments. The grading criteria is very clear with sample outputs provided for the programs you write. Very informative class!

Professor Fox was a fantastic, incredibly accommodating professor. The class is async, and you get what you put into the class. The content is interesting, however it does get complicated at times, yet he's very reasonable in his expectations. His office hours are flexible, and he's always very happy to meet with students to talk about whatever!

Extraordinary experience!  The discussion-based format was particularly engaging. Fortunate enough to have access to personalized feedback on written assignments, which allowed us to make necessary improvements. The only downside was the substantial amount of philosophical papers we had to read, which were rather rigorous.

Ron is a gem! He genuinely cares for his students and is passionate about information science. He has a lot of experience, both in teaching and in the field, that makes his content interesting! His grading and work are extremely lenient and he just wants you to learn and engage with the material! I also took 161 with him and he is the best!

Definitely one of the most understanding professors and is always just so kind and willing to help students. He has a lot of experience that he draws on and tells stories to supplement his teaching. Sometimes assignments would feel daunting, but he'd always give positive and constructive feedback and grade lightly.
The lectures really weren't that important, as they had next to nothing to do with the homework and project assignments. Really easy class to take for even non-Info Science majors.
My third class under this goat, and never disappoints and always a new learning experience. Take him!
Class was so easy, you do pretty much everything in recitation so can skip the lectures at 8. You will learn as much as you put into this class but it's an easy a

Love Professor Bergquist. He genuinely cares about his students' learning and he makes all assignment expectations crystal clear. I took both 161 and 385 with him, both of which were a cakewalk. Just to note 385 has group work and lectures focus a lot on military/historical concepts. He also gives great feedback

Bergquist is such an accomplished individual, and it definitely shows through in his class. Very useful content, but with a focus on military contexts rather than corporate America. If you don't mind that, I'd definitely recommend. Couple papers, optional attendance, group presentations that are recorded, and super light grading overall.
Take every information science class you can with him! He is great, very understanding, and is passionate about what he is teaching. 10/10!
One of the best professor ever! Very patient and have appropriate teaching pace, and you are always welcomed to pull up to office hours to ask any question related to this class or area

Prof. Bergquist is hands-down one of the best teachers at the school. He's been here forever and everyone loves him. The class itself is super easy and the website walks you through everything. Easy A, great teacher.
Very easy class with a professor who emphasizes learning without the stress of test-taking. Learn by a learn-by-doing approach for the assignments.

Professor Bergquist is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. He really cares for his students and wants to see them succeed. He is a professor who truly cares that you learn rather than causing students stress to do good on an exam. Has a lot of fun life stories and I think you can learn a lot from him. He's great!
Amazing professor. Truly cares for his students!

Initially was confused about this class but was able to learn very much thanks to Professor Bergquist. Great teacher overall however some of the grading and assignments could have been better implemented. Good luck.

Dr. Bergquist was awesome for an introduction into the information science major. The lectures were pretty interesting and the only grades in the class are discussion boards and four projects. The projects involve working with HTML, Word, Excel, and Powerpoint. It was pretty easy but the information was very useful. Great professor.

Sweet is a word that truly describes him. He is kind, approachable. Based past positive reviews, it's clear his class is easy. However, I strongly urge anyone reading this not to just attend class and then get distracted by your computers. Please take the time to listen to his lectures and his content is genuinely enlightening and inspiring.

Dr. Bergquist is one of the best professors at UNC. He is super kind towards the students and wants to see you succeed. His has very obtainable office hours and lets you easily schedule zooms with him. All of the answers are easily findable in his lecture slides. If he has open seats in his class, take the class even if it's just for an elective.
Ron is wonderful. He is very knowledgeable about the topics he talks about. He is really sweet and will make the class as easy as possible, literally all the assignments are so easy.

Prof Bergquist is just the sweetest man! It is very easy to fall behind in this class and skip (given the lecture and most recitations are either 8 or 9AM), but it is just as easy to catch up, and he is extremely flexible with deadlines and regrading things if you communicate with him. This was a very valuable class, would reccomend!

Dr. Bergquist is truly an amazingly understandable professor. His class was an interesting way to expand on some of the skills we thought we previously knew. He's really flexible with deadlines and overall a really kind person. He follows the rubric strictly and if you can't get something to work, meet with him in office hours and you'll be fine.

I think Professor Kelly was great; however, the class had like a million readings for every class and we learned a lot of the content through readings which were supplemented by lectures, rather than the other way around. There is a lot of grade padding and she was very reasonable (and generous) with curves. So many readings though.

I'm pretty sure people expected an easy course (as it used to be). The curriculum has been redesigned, so maybe thats why some assignments were graded a bit nit-picky at first. Later, they made efforts to improve our grades with extra credit and making the tests essay-based rather than MCQ. 2 exams, 1 final, mandatory attendance, in-class quizzes.

Not the most engaging professors - but the information is honestly common sense and just explained further. Graded by participation/attendance, quizzes, homework, two midterms, and a final. Honestly really easy class, quizzes were just on the reading and for the homeworks just don't LLM them and you'll be fine
The class itself isn't bad, but the professor's grading is excessively strict. Exams aren't hard, but they are short response and there are weekly reading quizzes, so stay on top of the readings.

She was so boring, but also so easy. I went to every single class, but was locked for maybe 20 minutes all semester. As long as you look at the slides the day before the test you are fine. This is such an easy class, but she is nitpicky about some of the homeworks which may be the reason for the bad reviews. The tests are the easiest things ever.
Really nitpicky grading from the professor. The class is relatively easy; it's just that the professor will point out every little thing "wrong" in your work and grade extremely subjectively.

This class was only difficult because of the professor. The information taught is genuinely interesting, but the way the professor is so hard on clarity/punctuation when forcing students to write in a time crunch is asinine. Would only take if interested in the INLS major/minor. Really hope she changes how she approaches this class.

Professor Diane is honestly such a good professors, the learning environment is fun and interactive which is helpful because the course is a little difficult but she makes it easy to do. Exams are open notes from your previous readings, attendance is mandatory and you will get extra credit. I would honestly take her again, she loves what she does

Worst class i have ever taken at UNC., This woman single-handedly made me hate Information Science. INLS 201 was a nitpicky, terrible and useless course, She refuses to accommodate students, and seems to pride herself all the time. DO NOT TAKE!!!!

The exams are based on really nitpicky concepts. Her lectures are boring. I hate the quizzes that start in the first 5 mins and just close, plus you never know when you will have a quiz. Lots of reading and just too much work

It was incredibly frustrating. I've never encountered such a ruthless professor at UNC. You can't get a good grade even though u put efforts already. She spent so much time on formalism that I felt like I wasn't learning anything useful. This class is incredibly difficult for an prerequisite, totally disaster

I feel bad writing this but I had a miserable time in 560. He's a very nice guy, but I learned absolutely nothing in this class, given how he doesn't even understand the material.

Had Jones for recitation and he's AMAZING!!! His instructions are so clear for each assignment, and he also walks you through the assignment to make sure you understand the material. If you ever need help, just shoot him an email and he will reply right away or set up a Zoom meeting. Cannot recommend having Jones for INLS recitation enough!!

Loved this guy so much; he's definitely a favorite in the program. Super chill, clear about the material / feedback, etc.  He's always open to giving second chances to students, and you will come out of his recitations learning something. My only tip: show up. He likes seeing students actually put in the effort.
The man the myth and legend. Lawrence is godsend and can teach anyone. Take him if you want to learn and enjoy this class. Jones for the W.

Mr. Jones is one of the best here at UNC! Anytime I was struggling with something, he was always helpful and understanding. Due dates are not strict, but it easier to stay on top of assignments as the class gets busier towards the end of the semester. Loved this class!

He is seriously one of the kindest professors I've had so far! He gives excellent feedback and none of his assignments are difficult. I took this class over the summer and highly recommend you do so as well. As long as you put in the work, this class will be a breeze.

I had Professor Jones for 161 recitation and would recommend him again and again. He was clear about the grading material and had a separate page with detailed steps on completing every task accurately. When I missed a few marks on an assignment, he helped me fix them and even let me resubmit for full credit. NO tests or in person final either!

He is a really nice professor, and he understands his students very well. He tries to be brief in lectures and give you meaningful projects so that you will understand how to use Python in different areas.
I'm a slow learner with technology and I also didn't have great attendance, but still easily got an A. Jones is incredibly kind and is always willing to help.

Highly recommend taking a course with Mr. Jones! I only had him for recitation, but he is super approachable and enjoys making sure his students succeed. He made it clear from day 1 that if we got the work done he didn't care about attendance. 161 is really easy, the grading for assignments is outlined in the course website.
GOAT

Really nice guy, cares about the students and their wellbeing. Very clear instructions and grading criteria. Very accessible class. Everything is recorded and posted online. Zoom calls if you can't be there in person, soft deadlines, allows resubmissions. Would definitely recommend him!

I had Mr. Jones for spring 2022 and he was truly the best. He was always willing to help with assignments and provide feedback/assistance outside of class. He was very flexible with deadlines and allowed for resubmissions as well. He really cares about the students and wants what is best for them. Extremely understanding and compassionate.

Summer class, Jones is a great prof. Class was easy so long as you stayed on top of your work. If you came to class, you could generally finish an assignment along side him and not have much to do outside of class. I would recommend this class for anyone wanting to learn more tech skills.  Final is a recorded presentation which helped with anxiety

Mr. Jones is so helpful. He is clear about his expectations, and it makes the work really easy. I had attendance issues, but I still made an A in the class because he cares more about the work quality than the attendance. I would recommend for anyone who wants an overview of some different tech projects.
Had for recitation; great professor that has clear grading criteria and wants you to succeed. "You are the only thing in the way of you getting an A."

Mr.Jones is a stellar professor. He was so kind and patient and gives great feedback on your errors. He also allows multiple resubmissions. He is an amazing professor and I wish more teachers were as kind, patient, accessible, and understanding as him. Easy A, take this class!

Clearly cares about her students & the material she teaches. Do not listen to the bad ratings. Her "tangents" substantiate course material. She gives fair grades. If you do bad in class, it's most likely because you didn't do the readings.

Dr. Booth is truly an amazing professor and human. You get out of her course exactly what you put into it. She is a lecturer who challenges you to think and especially encourages discussion, so get ready to talk.This is a collaborative learning class, so group and individual participation is ESSENTIAL. She is also WONDERFUL in office hours.

This was an amazing class! Prof B did a great job at explaining the main components of reproductive justice and she created a good environment for meaningful discussion. There is a semester long project but it was broken down into check points with feedback along the way.

Prof B. is a great professor! She is very knowledgeable and is able to teach a wide variety of topics. This is a survey course so there is a lot of material to go over but Professor Booth does a great job at explaining the nuances of all of them. There is a semester long research project but it broken up into manageable segments with feedback.

The class has assigned reading assignments followed up by in class discussion and pop quizzes. Talking with other students definitely helps with better understanding different experiences in the community. Overall I think this class is definitely worthwhile!

I was worried to take a class with Prof B due to her poor rating but I found her class pleasant. She can be a bit old school but I feel her class is accessible to disabled students and she's incredibly understanding. I also felt the class material and assignments were understandable/doable. Prof Booth is also a good resource for WGST majors.

I've taken and enjoyed two classes with Booth. This class emphasizes participation b/c it is a discussion-based class. Yes, Prof. Booth talks a lot, but I think she is insightful. Idk why there are so many bad ratings. Everyone who actually tried/cared about the class seemed to do really well. She's so understanding and will work with you if you go to office hours.

IGNORE THE POOR RATINGS. They were in my class and literally didn't put effort into it/care abt it at all. They're just offended their grade actually reflected the quality of their work lol. Prof B is the sweetest. If you actually care abt social justice and you try in class, you'll be golden. Unfortunately those who liked the class didn't rate her

I highly recommend taking this class with professor booth. She is so knowledgeable of reproductive care around the world and you will learn a great amount in this class. This is the second class I have taken with her, and I will be looking for more classes to take with her in the future.

Professor booth is an amazing professor and I loved having multiple classes with her. I have taken 2 classes with her now and loved both of them. She is extremely caring for every student in her class and is very knowledgeable of every topic she teaches. She is an amazing person and I will be looking for classes to take with her in the future.

I was hesitant to enroll because of the ratings, but I'm so so glad I took her class. Professor Booth is kind, knowledgeable, and truly cares about her students. Discussions are open and respectful, and different opinions are welcomed. I would absolutely take another class with this amazing professor!!!

Do not let the other reviews lie to you. Professor Booth is extremely knowledgeable, down-to-earth, open-minded, and caring. Grading rubrics are somewhat tedious, but mundane compared to what college students should realistically be expected of. The class is quite elementary. Readings are simple and straightforward, as are class assignments. 10/10.

This was the first time that she taught the class. There were a lot of pre-class readings that were being discussed about during class, which participation mattered a lot.

unclear grading criteria and was late/disorganized with many assignments and their rubrics, cared about the class as a whole but made some portions unnecessarily difficult. research project was main part of grade

Solid class, but instruction was just plain boring sometimes. Dr. Booth has a very interesting collection of  personal research and ideas that reflects in this class, but she is not very engaging. Lectures are long and boring. She was constantly late releasing rubrics for the final paper. She only calls on a few students that she knows will agree with her even if others have their hands up.

She is very opinionated and her thinking is the only way of thinking. Very simple class but the professor does not do it justice for the materials since she wants to project only her opinions and not hear anyone elses.

Lectures were boring sometimes, but not terrible. TAs graded all assignments. We had a semester-long paper to write in multiple steps, one campus engagement assignment, and a midterm and final. Not a difficult class, but felt tedious at times. In-class discussions were very interesting, and I learned a lot.

- Extremely tough grader. If you don't say exactly what she wants, how you want, as if she wrote it herself, you will not get a good grade
- Not good a critiquing things. She has quoted my work and criticized the quotes... except.. the quotes she used to criticize and explain why my grade was bad were quotes I NEVER USED IN MY ASSIGNMENTS EVER. So

Dr. Hinderliter is a great professor who is clearly very passionate about what she teaches! The class was not super difficult, and she gave thorough feedback on all writing assignments. She also gave a few extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Would definitely take again!
She is very passionate about what she teaches! I loved her class despite it being an 8 am, definitely worth taking. The assigned readings were also interesting and relevant to the lectures.

I thought Prof. H was a great professor who cares a lot about the class. She lectures a lot, but also opens up the floor for discussion, so it's not all sitting there and listening. I thought the content was interesting too. She's a fair grader, a passionate professor, and just a caring person. I met a lot of friends in this class too.

Dr. Hinderliter is amazing!! I took both her 202 and 330 classes, and she is so knowledgeable and passionate about both. There were a lot of readings but they are skimable. The class was a mix of lecture, discussion, documentary/media viewing, and a trip to the archives. Highly recommend her as a prof!

I really enjoyed taking a class with Professor Hinderliter! She presents material in a very interesting and thought-provoking way, and she encourages participation and discussion whenever she can. The work she assigns never feels like busy work, and I always felt like I could approach her if I had questions or concerns. Take a class with her!

I enjoyed this class. It was relatively pretty easy. Lectures are super interesting. There are a lot of papers so beware. It is also a 95 and above to get an A. Dr. Hinderliter never gave me higher than a 90 on any assignment. I got a 94 in the class which is an A-, beware

Dr. Hinderliter is one of the best professors I've ever had. She is caring, flexible, and understanding. She is truly an expert and so knowledgeable. All assignments are useful to better understanding the material and she gives very good feedback and fair grading. I wish I could take a million classes with her as I could not recommend her enough!

Dr. H is amazing and arguably one of the best professors I have had here. She is very flexible and understanding with assignments. There are two projects with ample time to work on them and peer review. There are four writing assignments based on your assigned readings but you decide when to do them. Great verbal and written feedback on everything.

Dr. Hinderliter is amazing! She cares about students and is open to working with you. Lectures are dense but interesting. Casual discussions every class were always fun. Grades based on attendance, participation, and papers. Fair amount of reading but I really enjoyed materials. Feels very do-able! YOU choose when and which assignments to write.

The class is super super interesting but somehow she made most of the lectures boring. Not really a discussion based class as she lectures the whole time. Some student discussion leading but grades mainly focused on papers and reading journals. Attendance mandatory.

Dr. Hinderliter teaches an amazing class that is interesting for people who may not be interested in the topic. She always leaves room for discussion and will ask and engage questions to help everyone gain a better understanding. She is so sweet and legitimately cares about her students. There are some papers but they are easy to manage.

Dr. H is super caring and passionate about her work. Pretty easy/short readings, clear expectations, and not too much work (short essays, final project, discussion leading). Super lecture heavy, but if you're paying attention and keeping up with the readings the lectures are interesting. She expects class participation but isn't too harsh.

Dr. Hinderliter is knowledgeable and sweet. Reading is heavy, with on average 20-30 pages before each class, but many of these were pretty interesting. Decent amount of writing, with two 2-page papers, a 4-page,a 5-page, as well as an essay final, but she is a very reasonable grader. I would recommend esp if interested in Jewish or women's studies.

Dr. H was a sweet professor throughout a difficult semester, however, her lectures were fairly uninteresting, despite a seemingly interesting course topic. The course itself isn't too difficult, but the amount of reading is above average for a gen-ed class.

Dr. Hinderliter is clearly extremely knowledgeable, passionate, and delivers very interesting lectures. Attendance is mandatory, readings are helpful to do before class but she only checks them through occasional at-home reading quizzes. There are a couple of two page reading responses, and two longer essays. Overall, would recommend!
She makes the lectures interesting and is very understanding as long as you communicate. Love her as a professor, I highly recommend!

If you're taking this for a Gen-ed, I recommend! She was very nice and the class was pretty easy. Lectures could be kinda boring and readings were long, but she went over them. She gives a clear study guide over the midterm, 3 essays with clear rubrics, and weekly reading quizzes. Just wish the TA gave more feedback on assignments.

Super caring professor! Easy class, just don't be rude and occasionally add something to conversations. The tests were pretty easy, essay-style but she gives you some possible prompt beforehand so you can prepare. Recitations were basically just a rant sesh about the current state of feminism and women so honestly super fun class
Professor Bloesch is a great professor who clearly cares about her students and their success. I would take another class with her.

great intro to the wgst dept!! very very lovely prof, very well spoken, extremely kind. class itself has many readings but she goes over important info from them in class. very easy gen-ed and very enjoyable. only holds lecture once a week too.

I enjoyed this class Professor Bloesch is great and very knowledgeable. She prepares you very well for all the assignments she expects of you. There is a lot of reading but you can get away without doing it because she goes over it during class. There is a recitation which is mandatory but not too much work overall.

Attendance in class isn't mandatory but recitations are. They were pretty interesting though. Bloesch is a good professor and her lectures pretty much some up the readings. Although, if you do the readings there's not much to pay attention to in class. Exams were easy too as long as you did the readings.

She was very kind, accommodating, and interesting. There were 2 short papers, a midterm, a final (multiple choice), and weekly ten-question reading quizzes (take-home, open note). In addition attendance and participation in recitation were taken.

Professor Sarah Bloesch is an outstanding educator! Her Sexuality and Salvation class in Women and Gender Studies was engaging, thought-provoking, and eye-opening. She fosters an inclusive environment and encourages deep discussions on complex topics. Her teaching style is clear, passionate, and approachable. One of the best professors I've had!

She is an incredibly understanding and flexible professor. The only mandatory attendance was for recitation. She only had lecture once a week as well. I only did the readings for the exams and for the recitations and did fine, there were no time limits on the weekly chapter quizzes.

She's a great professor and teaches very well. Attendance is only mandatory for recitation and she ends up dropping the Thursday class. Midterm and final were easy if you studied well and the essay project was pretty easy too. I had Jacob as my TA and he was great too. This class is a great GPA booster and pretty interesting too.

Overall, good class and professor. She seems to care a lot about her students and this class. In my opinion, the lectures were nothing crazy or extremely helpful, she basically reads off the slides. There is a good amount of reading. Attendance is mandatory, but only for recitation; she also dropped the Thursday class, which was great.

Dr. Bloesch is INCREDIBLE! All lectures were engaging, and she was always willing to answer questions and have conversations. Participation matters, but is self graded . Bloesch did a great job breaking readings down and helping us understand the concepts. My class was almost in tears when it was over, the course, and Dr. Bloesch were excellent!

The class was pretty straight forward and discussion heavy. No tests/ quizzes which is nice, instead you're graded on a semester long research paper split into 7-8 ish different parts.
