Professor Bloesch was caring but was terrible with time management. The class is one long essay with each step needed to be graded to do the next but she never graded quickly, making the class fall behind really quickly. The work wasn't terribly difficult but her lack of organization made a class that had the potential to be intersting miserable.

I loved Dr. Bloesch. She is so passionate about the subject and very open to everything students have to say. The readings were long, but they were easy to skim and honestly really interesting. Class conversations were always interesting. Would highly recommend this class.

There were 2 papers and a few small assignments. Dr. Bloesch is an amazing professor!! I wish I could take all my classes with her. The only thing is that she doesn't give above a 97 on anything, so you're "100" is a 97. If you're a perfectionist it can be discouraging. We read a LOT, but the readings were engaging and fairly straight to the point.

Amazing prof who cares about her students. Readings are required for class if you want to grasp the material but most readings are relatively short. Took this to fill a FC requirement and have no knowledge of WGST and did pretty good. Class involves a lot of group analysis and discussion and participation is part of your grade. No exams either

This class felt like a massive waste of time and I wouldn't have gone if I hadn't been required to for the major. I really don't feel like the teacher actually shared any true knowledge and also, we didn't read or discuss any of the foundational feminist thought readings?

The class is one drawn own essay that feels drawn out for no good reason. The rubric was incredibly unclear, and I had no idea what I was supposed to be writing, and the instructions we did have made my work worse. She was incredibly nitpicky and just overall hard to talk to when I did discuss my frustration.
*WGST 270 Women and Sport. Good lectures and discussion about modern topics. I have no interest in sports but learned a lot from this class.

Dr. Ashley is wonderful! We had a group book club project, which was really interesting and something I haven't seen before in a class at UNC yet. She clearly cares about her students and makes sure everyone feels comfortable and safe. Her feedback on assignments is great, and she tells you exactly what to fix and why you got points off.

*wgst 340* Professor Ashley's decent. You can tell she cares about the material. LOTS of reading and weekly journals that are pretty tedious and boring. The material was interesting if you are interested in the topic l. Has barely graded all semester so no idea what my grade will be. Service learning for apples was the best part of the class!

If you are interested in the content you will love this class. class is split into lecture, activity, and discussion. You can miss 3 of each. She covers a wide range of topics and truly wants you to enjoy the class. Exams are online with clear feedback for how to improve. One of my favorite WGST classes at UNC!
This class was great, and prof Ashley was super kind and definitely very knowledgeable. Class can be boring if you dont care about the content but still very engaging.

Dr. Ashley is such an amazing professor! She is so understanding and really cares for the wellbeing of her students. I actually had her for WGST 340 and had a lot of readings, but she is very knowledgeable in a plethora of topics, so I highly recommend taking a WGST class with her.

I loved Dr.Ashley's class. super interesting but you def have to do the readings. She had a lecture, activity, discussion setup for her MWF class which I really enjoyed. Had to read a book for a book club but it was engaging and not overly strenuous. You will learn a lot and should get an A if you do your work and participate.
Wonderful professor, very understanding and super lenient. 100% take this class if possible

Everyone can tell that Amalia puts so much hard work into her lectures. She seems genuinely interested in what she's teaching and is happy to provide additional resources if anyone has questions. Amalia is a very understanding person and allows the lowest grades to be dropped. She's very engaging and loves to learn from her students.

Deb is an amazing professor, and you can tell he genuinely cares about his students. There are few assignments, but he lays out the directions very clearly, which makes it easy to get a good grade. I would definitely recommend him for this course!

Super energetic and passionate about the subject. Assignments provide a clear rubric and grading generally isn't harsh, granted that good effort is shown. Lectures aren't super helpful but all test material goes along with the readings and slides he provides. Very fun class.

Deb's class is not challenging if you show up to lectures (attendance is mandatory) and follow assignments' requirements (his grading is very clear). The content is not difficult and you do not have to deeply understand it to succeed in the class, knowing the terms/events discussed in class and their impact on media is sufficient.

Deb is SUPER nice and the tests are very easy- mostly common sense and based on all of the readings he gives us. There were a few projects, all of which were graded easy as long as you follow directions. The lectures weren't ever helpful (it's mostly Deb asking if anyone has any questions), but overall would recommend- Deb's a great guy!
Deb is a great professor! I took MEJO 141 over the summer online, and it was pretty easy. He was always available outside of class for help on the very few assignments we had.

Deb is very but, but he's all talk and not much knowledge or teaching. He really pushed us to give good evaluations, which is outa hand. I don't dislike him but I also didn't really learn anything. You don't have to do much to pass.

Deb is really cool. He ALWAYS will answer whatever question you have. He wants questions. But just a APA citations project, easy presentation, midterm, more citations and final. He cares a lot about the kids and participation not graded but participate -- it'll make him happy. Nice old Indian guy

I had this class from 5:45-7:00, but Deb was always so positive and uplifting. The content of this course was very manageable, going to class and participating in lectures made it MUCH more engaging. Highly suggest MEJO 141 with him!

This class was a 7:15PM, but he brought the energy every single time. He is nothing short of a phenomenal professor, who keeps lectures interesting. If you need credits or a good grade and want to enjoy the class, take Deb. He is an amazing guy and a great yet understanding teacher.

Deb is kind, fair, and loveable. While not very tech-savvy, he always provides space for student questions and suggestions. His syllabus and grading criteria were the most well-organized and clear that I have ever seen. Most people I know got high A's in this class just by participating and following directions.

He is a very nice professor, but does not teach much. I was often confused about the material on the tests because most of it we had to learn on our own. He constantly is asking the class if they have any questions and gets annoyed when no one does. That's the majority of the class. But it is easy, most of the tests and projects are common sense

Professor Aikat is incredibly kind, and it's clear he wants his students to get a high grade. Expectations and grading criteria couldn't be clearer, and he spends a lot of time (maybe too much) answering questions about assignments. All of the assignments are easy, just a bit tedious at times. Even though an A starts at 95, it's still doable.

Deb is an amazing and extremely caring professor. He is there to answer any and all questions that you may have about his course as well as help you outside of his course in any way he possibly can. MEJO 101 was a class that I always looked forward to going to.

Took off points because I used a citation machine and then took off 3 points for the letter not being capitalized in the citation when that's how the title was written. There's like 5 grades in this class so not very confident going through. Takes off a bunch of points for trivial things.
Deb's class was fun, and really gives a good foundation for the field of journalism, and even touches on the basics of Advertising and PR.

Super energetic and cares about his students. You can tell he's really passionate about the class too. I thought this class was easy but an A is a 95 which is kinda high. Diff professors from the MEJO school come guest lecture for every class. You take a couple of open note quizzes, a take-home exam, and the final exam.

Deb is extremely knowledgeable, sweet, and caring. Even with a class period starting at 7:15 p.m., his humor and personality made it worth going to class. Deb is one of the best professors I've had at UNC and even if you aren't a MEJO major, 141 is enjoyable and interactive if you take it with Deb. The assignments aren't hard, just time-consuming.

This course is awesome. Many guest speakers from different Media and Journalism areas introduce the basic knowledge about their teaching field. Deb is very strict with the deadline, but overall friendly. The quiz and exams are pretty easy.

Only take this class if you want to get to know the BASIC concepts of MEJO and some of the professors. You will not learn much. Deb is interesting but unclear. They test on readings and concepts but also just specific things that lecturers and the readings say.

does not answer emails, always has excuses, went off on personal tangents, wasted so much of my time by calling us into class and then letting us go, did not put grades into Canvas. I believed I had an A+ the whole semester then he plugged in a B+ without explanation ruining my GPA. very upset, do not take his class.

Mike is a very nice guy but his lectures can be painful to sit through. He only graded us on a midterm, final, and final paper. He knows what he's talking about but can get sidetracked sometimes. It helps to engage with him during and after class to understand his view of the subject, as the material can be very subjective.

He talks a lot in lectures and can be boring but he's the sweetest professor and really cares about his research. this class was super interesting and I enjoyed working in groups! I've taken him twice and plan on it again
So nice and caring and have taken multiple classes with him. Very understanding, lenient and kind!

Mike knows his stuff and loves what he teaches. Lectures are chatty so u have pay attention, slides are just keep him on track. All essays, kinda like philosophy. He connects ideas between his classes well. Some ppl zone out on laptops which sucks bc he's too nice to say anything. But if you're into that lecture style, totally worth taking!
Very kind man who truly cares about the content of his courses and his students! He never lectures for the full period and sometimes his le

Loved him! This class was sooo interesting. Class was really lecture heavy for the first half of the semester for the exam (that wasnt too hard, def study though) but dropped off after that. Group and final projects were kinda long but worth it to me, so fun! He grades so easy. I think his lectures were long but captivating, and hes so caring!

Dr. Waltman is very knowledgeable in the topic of social/collective memory, and he definitely wants to engage the class and is kind.  However, he is not a very concise or interesting lecturer. We had 3 grades: a ~15 page midterm paper, a similar final, and participation/attendance (def try to attend every lecture). He graded pretty leniently.

DOES NOT ANSWER EMAILS!!! Professor Waltman is a very kind man, but his class is rough, he seems to struggle to teach a bit. Your grade is decided based on 4 total things: a paper, midterm, final, and 3 recitation quizzes - so you have to do really well on each of them to do well in the class. The 2 exams are online which is nice.

Prof Waltman is a very sweet guy - he is just obviosuly not use to teaching intro level courses. Lectures and paper/test grading criteria were very vague, and the class seemed to be disorganized. Nonetheless, the class was easy and attendence was not mandatory. I will say the most difficult part about the class was the unclear grading parameters.

Prof. Waltman is a kind individual, but it was evident that he would have preferred teaching a higher level course. Lectures seemed to cover nothing but common sense; I do not feel that I took anything away from this course. Very vague instructions all year and poorly written final exam.

Graded super ambiguously and made tests very vague. For an intro-level communications course, he should have communicated way better. This class really depended on your TA, and honestly if I didn't have mine I don't think I would've stayed in this class. Super monotone lectures and an insane grading scale for an intro class

The final exam was poorly written. Lectures are dull, and he does not care about this class. There are about 4 assignments in the class, a final paper, and a final exam, which gave very few things to be graded on mixed with harsh grading. Success varies from TA. My TA is a wonderful individual and took the brunt of the work for this course.

If you have to take it and you're good at BSing a 6-page paper, he's fine. Very very boring though. I think I got lucky with my TA for recitation being a saint and basically handing out quiz answers and giving a group doc to fill out the final study guide together. Without that I might've been in trouble. I went to class maybe 5 times and got an A.

Nice guy but rambled during lectures and stated multiples times he doesn't usually teach intro courses like this. Paper on movie was 30% of grade (kinda random and depends how harsh your TA grades it). Take home, open note midterm and final make it very attainable to get an A.

Monotone and boring, obvious did not care about this intro level class. Easy class, but every single class feels like a chore to show up to. His one module on hate speech was interesting! There were moments where I could see that he is a good professor, but I think it's just this class.

Professor Waltman is a great professor and he's really nice.  The class is fairly easy and is composed of 2 exams and one paper on a movie we watched in class.  Be sure to take notes in class and read the textbook.  The readings are short and easy.  I highly recommend this class.

Whereas Dr. Waltman was by no means an awful professor. His exams and teaching styles differed heavily, and I am one to study lectures and study guides profusely. One thing I really did not agree with for this course was that his TA (a wonderful person) graded half of the classes midterm, papers and final, which resulted in differing grades.

Professor Waltman is a really nice guy, but his lectures can be very boring. The midterm was a 20 page paper, which sounds kind of extreme for an undergrad course, but he's a very lenient grader. I didn't mind him as a professor, but I wouldn't take a class with him again

He hadn't taught this class many times, so it was a little rough around the edges. There were two grades (2, 15+ page papers) for the entire class, which was a good and bad thing. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he does go more into depth than the book which is helpful. Has a dry sense of humor and goes off on tangents but it could be so much worse

Not even a studio art class, just philosophical assignments with one thing that could be considered art. Unclear expectations, my classmates and I would ask questions in class about the assignments, only to be left with more questions. She has also come in late multiple times to class, sending out a delay announcement once we're already in class.

Gave very vague instruction and would often change up what she wanted from you. Never ask her for advice on a project because she will most likely dismiss all of it and tell you you did the entire thing wrong. The class material would be interesting, but lectures drag on and are boring. Some of the projects were fun.
this professor was not kind or understanding, nor accommodating. class was incredibly boring too.

It has been a week since LDOC, and she has not submitted any grades so far. When you ask for feedback on a project, she is very vague and not helpful. There are better first-year seminars than this course. It is very lecture-heavy and boring when not completing projects. The professor is kind, but does not grade on time.

The worst professor I've ever had at UNC. Her class was so unorganized and nothing was made clear. Would get mad and snap at students. Spent the first 5 weeks going over the same 20 page powerpoint and just read off her notes the entire time. Multiple people dropped the course and I wish I could have. I would never take a class with her again

Roxana is my fave professor at UNC. I understand the low rate bc a lot of my ppl disliked her teaching style. But as a professor and artist, she's great to learn from. Her class is not easy, it challenges you, and she doesn't take nonsense. You have to be willing & engage. She was my only professor who accommodated my predicament with genuine care.

Took class Spring 2022 and was skeptical because these reviews are horrendous!!! The class was very enjoyable and it was nice to make tangible things by hand. Project deadlines based on class progression. 3 very simple review papers. Small final presentation on assigned sculptor. Overall grades on effort & at least coming to class. Highly recommend

PM gave me a 2nd chance after threatening to fail me, so credit where due. She also disrespected me when I tried to explain my situation, and it genuinely hurt my feelings. PM goes on bizarre, biased tangents in class. She actually gets offended if you miss class. We used Dropbox and Flipsnack instead of Sakai, and blamed us for issues. PM aint P.

Fall 2025 ARTH 453. Manageable class. Lectures were a bit redundant and was usually confused on what was being taught. Deeply appreciate Prof. Magee's drive in this class though. Grading can be a bit harsh

Class wasn't graded super hard and she's really nice. But unless you are really interested in the very niche topics, it's hard to feign interest in all semester and there are definitely more useful electives. Super small class so you must be engaged and present at all times, and she grades participation harshly.

Dr. Magee is an expert in her field and her class was rather enjoyable, however her grading scheme is rather unforgiving and many of the grades seem arbitrary. Expectations are laid out clearly but she seemingly doesn't give out grades >95.

This was a really unique interdisciplinary class that combined art history with Feldenkrais movement lessons. Sometimes it was hard to make the link between the readings and lessons, but overall fascinating. She is definitely a tough grader—the more "meta" and detailed you can get with your analysis the better.
tough grader and has her favorites. not much else to say

Graded things very last minute, didn't know my grade until the end of semester and it was sent to connect Carolina. Many times her rubric is very unclear and she takes off points for no reason very very tough grader. Participation counted a lot and needed and projects. Don't recommend this class to anyone!

I'm rating her for ARTH280 (not listed). Prof. Magee is very kind and enthusiastic about what she teaches, and she explains things well for those that don't know a lot about art. I thoroughly enjoyed the class and would take her again. The class is graded by a lot of different things, so there's no assignments that are particularly heavy.

ARTS 290 was very frustrating and complete waste of time. The professor was dismissive when students asked questions about new software and often seemed annoyed instead of helpful. Grading criteria and expectations were unclear. Class time felt unproductive (we once spent 2 hours talking about chairs). Absolutely do not recommend—avoid if possible.

This was a digital drawing course. Mario is knowledgeable about the topic and gave decent feedback, but classroom structure and vibes were so awkward that I wish I could've taken a different class. During workdays, he plays music quietly on his phone and we sit in silently; he discourages talking. Wish he let us give peer feedback more.

Nice guy and very interesting mix of information 
This was a fun class but a lot of work 
Having some experience with Wordpress or blogging in general would be really helpful
poorly planned due dates and no rubrics, slow demos, not enough critics and not enough time for last few assignments. take only if ur extremely interested or confident in the topic
one of the easiest classes ive taken at unc, would highly reccomend
Take this class!!! Easy A! Prof. Bond is absolutely amazing!
Prof Bond is a fabulous woman! Very inspiring, funny and nice. Easy grader, too.
Very disorganized and we didn't get much done, but she is a lovely person.  Do the assignments, and you'll be fine.

Pamela Bond is such an incredible teacher and even better person. She's super understanding and clearly cares more about you learning than busy work. Would recommend you take her classes, but if you do, please give her the respect and attention she deserves!! Top tier teacher!

Professor Bond made learning a joy. She is by far the most kind and energizing professor that I have experienced. She always showed up to class with a smile and was the highlight of my day. Her assignments consisted of reflective essays, designing our own sustainable fashion piece, etc. I learned a lot and had a bunch of fun in the process!

Professor Bond is the best teacher I have had at UNC so far. She genuinely cares for all her students and she gives you the confidence to participate. She is hilarious and  I always leave class feeling so much better than I did walking in. All the assignments are easy but interesting and you learn so much from her style of teaching!

Professor Bond was one of the best professors I have ever had in college. She was so caring and made class so engaging and fun. She genuinely sparked interest and inspired me every single day. I cannot emphasize enough how awesome she is and how awesome this class is. Shes truly the best.

She was literally the nicest professor out there. She is so funny and cares so much about each student. I 100% recommend taking this course, the assignments were easy and super fun. We had to create a piece of clothing out of scrap materials, and it was very entertaining.

Professor Bond is probably one of the (if not the) best teacher I have ever had. Not only will you leave her class laughing, but you also feel as if you have a genuine friendship with her. Her lectures are very interesting and taught in a very entertaining way. You will not regret taking her class.
No one could ever hate this woman. Best professor I have ever had. If you ever have the opportunity to take a class with her, take it immediately. You will not regret it.

I enjoyed Pamela Bond's class so much! It was a morning class, but because of how enjoyable she made her classes I was excited about going. This was a really relaxing class and helped me also learn more about myself in a clothing sense.

I love Professor Bond and DRAM 80! This class is definitely the easiest I've taken in my life. Professor Bond has an infectious energy that keeps class entertaining. We had a few assignments/projects throughout the semester but mostly just talked about the textbook content. Great way to get the FC-Global and Seminar requirement out of the way!

Prof. Bond made DRAM80 an extremely easy class. The final is almost identical to the quizzes where the questions come directly from the slides. Attend lectures and put effort into your projects and it's an easy GPA booster. Not to mention the content is also interesting. Would definitely recommend it.

Pamela Bond made the class Psychology of Clothing probably the easiest First Year Seminar. The class is graded by the final, two quizzes, a presentation, and a group project, and you don't need to do ANYTHING outside of the class. She is super flexible and repeatedly moved deadlines back if most of the class asked for it.
Dr. Fokina is so nice and funny. She likes for students to participate, so don't be afraid to! She is a super fair grader, so just show up and pay attention to lectures, and you'll be golden!
She wants you to succeed. Great lecture and course material. Attend lecture and you'll be good.

I honestly don't know why other people dislike her, she is truly such a good professor, who when you ask for clarification will help you understand complex concepts better. She is really funny and always made attending class enjoyable. Definetly would take her for 225, HW is not that bad and exams are pretty fair.

She was fine and a funny lecturer, a lot of the material/hw/slides did seem written by chat gpt which is a little disheartening but the class was pretty easy and exams weren't too hard if you practiced with the poll everywhere questions. HW load is light and attendance policy is forgiving

Dr. Fokina is truly the kindest professor I've had the pleasure of learning from. I know so many people who can say the same about her kindness and genius. She understands time constraints and the under load of an undergraduate, which not many professors do. Above all though, she teaches with compassion and intention. I highly recommend taking her.

Only reason why I got a good grade in this class because I studied on my own. Her slides are not clear and very hard to study from, especially if you miss a class. She also just does not teach effectively and is bad at explaining so it's not really of use to go to class anyway. Would not recommend taking it with Fokina

Professor Fokina is not a good teacher. She does not explain things well and everything I learned in this class was taught on my own. She made a topic that could've been really interesting incredibly difficult and hard to understand. Don't take this class if you want to learn everything yourself.

I personally really enjoyed this class. All assignments were pretty easy and the only thing you have to study for are two midterms and a final, which weren't that hard. The class was also interesting and we often did demos in class.

Dr Snider is really caring, his lectures are great, and provides good slides. WA helped me understand the content though they can be time consuming. I wouldn't take the class if I didn't have the time to study for it, but the content is super interesting. He likes questions at the end of class, feedback from students and is open to improvements.

Probably my favorite prof ive ever had. Easily the most knowledgeable. I didn't apply myself to the fullest extent and got the grade I deserved because of that. You can get an A if you try hard for an A. Very very smart and cares about his students a lot! Love him

Dr. Snider is very knowledgeable and covers many aspects of the systems neuroscience field in an up-to-date way which I loved. The exams were fairly written. He often speeds through lecture slides so be prepared to review after class. I would recommend taking this class if you're looking for a challenging but rewarding class.

Dr. Snider is great - he genuinely cares about getting to know his students. The course material is super relevant to emerging research in neuroscience but is challenging. The tests are most
of the grade and are detailed, but are very fair and if you study the powerpoints you'll do fine. Attendance isn't scored but participation in discussions is

Currently as a research tech in neurobiology, I think this class was the most useful class in undergrad. If you want to do any type of wet lab neuroscience research such a great course to do so. Yes the class is hard, but it's by far the most relevant and up to date class I've taken that teaches you about systems neuroscience.

If you want to continue to pursue the field of neuroscience or psychology, do NOT take this professor. He only gives you lecture slides to study, nothing else, and he doesn't let you see review past exams at all. The class is supposed to be PRINCIPLES of brain circuits and he expects you to know every intricacy of every circuit. I despise this man.

This prof is not accommodating to people with ARS. Other than that, he really isn't that bad. His exams are very detailed and you need to know almost everything that's in the slides. But if you study well the tests are very doable. He curves every exam so that the average is ~85%, so some people end up with over 100. Papers are straightforward too.

Baffled by the good reviews. Most of my interactions with him were nice, but for 1/3 tests he printed off the wrong one, noticed before class, lectures instead, and did NOT tell students at ARS. We took the test 2 days before the main class with no notice or effort to make up for the non-accommodation students getting the benefit of more study time

Cannot imagine taking this course with any other professor - Dr. Snider is the GOAT!  Dr. Snider is extremely knowledgeable about his field and truly makes an effort to get to know every student well! Be ready to work really hard to get a good grade in this course though, as LOTS of very challenging concepts are covered throughout the semester.

I'd describe him as the Neuroscience department's Tiani. Not the friendliest, but you accept it because easier tests. Other reviews exaggerate his difficulty.

Dr. Snider is a very caring professor, & he will go out of his way to personally ask how to support and help you succeed. But the course material is TOUGH & requires a lot of time. I don't recommend if you already have heavy STEM course load for the semester. Dr. Snider is great and knows the material in and out, but not a light class by any means.

Nicest professor ever! He relates concepts to the current world and genuinely just wants you to learn. Very kind with grading and problem sets. Brought in some awesome guest speakers and is willing to help you. The best!
this professor was genuinely the nicest person ever. the class itself was also pretty easy

This professor was absolutely amazing. He has to be the best professor I have ever had. He had fun, engaging lectures and made occasional jokes that I enjoyed. Reading quizzes were all completion grades. No exams in the entire course. Final project was a group project that was very fair and they helped a lot with it. Please take this professor.
He wants to give you an A, so let him

Outstanding professor with entertaining lectures! He did as much as he could to make every group's final project as fair as possible. I really enjoyed the class and made a lot of friends along the way!
The original computa. Derek can do whatever you put your mind to. Congrats bud, you've been Derek'd
He "touched" me
Every class he encouraged us to get "snug" with our classmates. He would then pretend to be a classmate.
Wow, Derek!!!!!
Derek is just a stand up man. His lectures are VERY "hands-on" and I find you learn a lot that way. Highly recommend, but be prepared to "break a sweat" to get good grades in this class.
He really cooked my goose with his stiff grading system. However, his stiff grading system opened my eyes to the world of "responsible" "research".

The class was mainly focused on Dr. Butler going through slideshows and discussing readings in groups. It's not the most organized, but as long as you somewhat pay attention, the class wasn't hard. If you commit some time to the readings or oral histories, getting an A is very doable. That said, you could get away with skimming the readings.

If you're looking for an easy or filler class, do not take this course. It is graded on around six different components, making it more demanding than expected. Dr. Butler is a good person, but the lectures and assignment details were very unorganized. The exams were also poorly structured and much longer than they should have been.
Do not take this course if you're just looking for an easy filler. Dr. Butler is very kind, but the lectures are often unorganized and the exams are much longer than they need to be.
Really great professor. Very accessible. LOTS of work. You will discuss the readings in class, so you have to actually do them. Learned a lot though.
I love Dr. Butler. She's amazing, grade very lightly and super understanding.

There are a decent amount of readings. There is a group interview, and a final paper along with a 10min presentation. There are only 2-3 homework assignments, and there were about 3-4 tests, all being online, including the final. The class was decently heavy on participation but it was always fun and usually was discussing the reading with someone.

I wish I dropped his class when I saw it was only a couple of students. I should have paid attention to the reviews, but I didn't, and it was a huge mistake. I am a straight-A student and received a B in his class for no reason other than he is a tough grader. Run ! Do not take his courses!

Dr. Jordan is very knowledgable and passionate about his work. But his teaching style is very unorganized! His slides were all jumbled into one large powerpoint (100+ slides). He would announce mandatory/extra credit opportunities days before, not considering students who work. And he barely followed his syllabus schedule. Avoid if you can!

The beginning of the course was very interesting. As time passed, you can tell he does not want to teach. Very subjective in grading everyone's paper.. has one PowerPoint with 130 slides.. feel like I learned absolutely nothing.. exam has questions that pertain NOTHING on the syllasbus. AVOID!

Dr. Rizvi is a very talented researcher and clearly has a lot of passion for the material he teaches. While his lectures sometimes seem a little out of order or repetitive, he covers most of the material he says he will at the start of the year, and his exams are very fair. One of the most passionate and easy to talk to professors.
Dr Rizvi is obviously very knowledgeable and incredibly passionate. He is my favorite BME professor I have had!
The best. He really organizes the class to ensure student's success. Truly passionate about the subject,  one of my favorite professors at UNC.

Dr. Rizvi is very knowledgeable about the subject. My main issue with the class is the lab reports, about half of them being full-length. I recommend going to office hours while doing them as the TA's will always find some points to deduct otherwise. Exams (including the final) are not bad, study diagrams and lecture slides and you're good.
my idol!!

I really enjoyed this class. He is very knowledgable and truly cares about the class's understanding. The only issue is that the class is somewhat disorganized with timing of assignments, and grading for labs doesn't seem standardized with TA's. If you don't pay attention, read the textbook instead. Tests are not impactful, and an A is 95+, not 93.
Skip all the lectures, watch a few of the lecture videos, do all of your work in recitation, A+

the lectures were really boring to sit through especially because he's very monotone and his slides are typically bland. however the recitation is very helpful grade wise—i bombed the midterm but ended up doing well on the final without watching the lecture videos!

Overall, Dr. Gangi is a really interesting guy, his lectures can be so boring though. He jumps from topic to topic during them, and can be hard to follow. But, he posts the lectures in Canvas, so if you watch them before class ur good. Recitation is the only part you actually have to do work for, but it's definitely not bad at all.

Really pretty terrible lecturer, jumps from topic to topic so fast. LOTS of outside work he wants you to do, though it isn't really required. Recitation is helpful, though. TAs are generally good, easy class to pass and attendance is not counted.

Recitation was the only thing you actually had to do work in/show up for. Grade on that really depends on the TA you get. Gangi is chill, knowledgeable, and experienced. Lectures can be kind of boring, even when the content itself is interesting. Overall, he's a decent professor. Either watch the videos or show up and take notes during lectures.

Professor Gangi is a nice guy, but his in-person lectures are unnecessary. He has Zoom lectures posted that cover all the content he discusses in class. Grading all depends on the TA. I had a more challenging TA, and all I heard was how less challenging everyone else's TAs were.

You won't learn much from his lectures, and he has you to watch online versions of them before each class. The recitation was the hardest part, but still easy. The midterm and final are both written, essay based assignments, but the midterm was online. Your grade will depend on which TA you have.

It gets a little scientific, which may be over your head without the background. The course focuses a lot on clean energy and sustainable practices, and it's kinda boring. It didn't cover the relationship between society and the environment as much as I expected and was more about how we can shift toward clean energy alternatives under capitalism.

This class is an easy prerequisite, it is some work and depends on your TA/group for the essay. A lot of the online lectures and articles are not entirely necessary, I just looked at the topics and taught myself them, Greg kinda just yaps (in a great way if you are interested!!) Greg is awesome, sweet guy with tons of opinions. Take this!!

Gregs lectures are tough to get through. The first half of the semester I didn't know what was going on. Just watch all of his online videos, and understand that there are 3 huge assignments for this class. What messed me up was how hard of a grader my TA was. Greg is a respectable guy though, very smart.

This class's lectures is mostly discussions on general topics or trends in the world of environmentalism, with your textbook and recitation being the brunt of the workload. The grading criteria isn't all that clear, but the lectures are interesting and you will learn something from taking this class.

gangi is a giant in the clean tech space definitely a great resource. in terms of the hnrs section, i wish i took regular bc in hnrs every single class students present but i would rather have listened to him talk bc he has so much to say. the final exam was ridiculous imo. way to specific abt random things. but i should have skipped less.

Gangi is a great guy, knowledgeable, and has a ton of connections in the Cleantech space (happy to introduce you too!). Class is interesting, but there is a long group essay. A little unorganized/chaotic, but that's how these problems/solutions tend to be since its big system problems. Not easy gen ed, but worth it! Changed how I see the world

If you are an environmental major, this is the class for you (if not maybe take something else). Greg is definitely a character, but very respectable, knowledgeable, and has a lot of good connections. The lecture videos are really helpful for taking notes even though he repeats most of it in class. Show up and watch the videos and you will do fine.

Your grade totally depends on your TA and the group you get assigned to. If you are looking for an easy gen-ed, I don't recommend it. Greg is a great lecturer, but his lectures have little to no connection to the material and tests. 
Overall, the class is not well-structured and doesn't have transparent grading.

Dr. Gangi is very knowledgeable in his field and well connected to many in the sustainability industry. His seminar lectures were interesting, but he sometimes had a tendency to go off on tangets (although they were interesting!) Just make sure you take notes, pay attention, and study since the class is only graded by a few things.

Dr. Gangi is a great resource. He is very well-connected and knowledgeable. He genuinely wants students to succeed, not just in class but professionally. He will connect you to people in the field you're interested in and is great about providing internship opportunities. Highly recommend.

Prof Gangi's class was my favorite of the semester. He is very knowledgeable about all topics discussed and loves student input. He brings in exciting guest speakers and has many connections so students can get a real idea of what they could do in the field. Although I will say the recitation can be difficult because of the extensive group paper.

If "unclear grading criteria" was a tag I would choose it. Recitation was most valuable. Frustrated by grading breakdown, huge recitation projects count for very little, final is about 35% of entire grade (2 essay and 4 short answer). Midterm - take home BUT final - closed note in person and graded on obscure topics - should focus on big ideas.

Dr Gangi is a solid professor and great guy. Lectures were good, but it was difficult to motivate myself to watch the prerecorded lectures before class as they related to the same topic. Group paper in recitation is annoying, and only one open note midterm means it's hard to know what you should know for the final. Overall, you out what you put it.

I really like her as a person, she was very approachable and you can tell she knows what she is talking about. However, lectures were pretty uninspiring and the tests were horrendously written. Good news is about half of the questions on her exams are free points, but the others were often very ambiguous and did not focus on core concepts.

Dr. Bustamante-Marin is a GENIUS in the field and is very knowledgeable. She's the sweetest person if you take the time to actually talk to her. That said, she is a tough grader with exams with tricky wording (which she will not give points back on), and omg the lectures are so fast with sometimes 100s of slides. you learn a lot! DONT CRAM!!

Though Dr. Marin may seem strict, she is genuinely really nice! Class content is difficult and requires a lot of memorization to be prepared on tests, so definitely do not study last min! But it is really interesting to learn if you are interested in nutrition. Her office hours were pretty helpful to go over exams or any content related questions!

unclear guest lectures. exams questions not released for review. course flow doesn't make sense. homework doesn't impact class grade. often quizzed before lecture on the topic. bar for an a is too high (94). overall her lectures were unclear. difficult to anticipate exam qs. she is somewhat nice but i wish she would've cared more.

Dr. Marin a little more on the serious side and she goes through slideshows fast. There's LOADS of information and cramming will not do you any good. BUT Dr. Marin DOES care about you. If you're not doing well, she will personally reach out to you to chat. She's understanding and wants you to do well. But don't take this class unless you need it.

I think Professor Bustamante-Marin. While the class was difficult, it was not as bad as it sounds. If you make sure to review the lecture slides and take notes on the textbook, you should do fine on exams. This class is not as hard as others at UNC, but I would not recommend taking if not required for your major.

Dr. Marin is overhated. Just study the slides thoroughly and they align pretty well with the exams, tho some questions on the exams were pretty tricky + I didn't find the textbook to really be of use. Dr. Marin was very helpful and accessible to me in and out of class and really did want the best for me. She comes off blunt but is truly caring

Horrible class. Lectures make no sense, she reads off the slides word for word with no explanation. Test style is horrible. Practice exam answer key was wrong ALL the time, so do not even waste your time. Practice exams looked nothing like the real exam. This class is straight memorization and is very content heavy. She is also very rude.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken, mostly self-study. The professor is smart but just reads off the slides. Exams are entirely based on the slides, so skip the textbook—just memorize the slides, including wordless images. Her exams are extremely tough. You have no option tho she the only profressor and her accent does not help.

This professor is very knowledgable about the subject but fails to transfer that knowledge to her students. She is very blunt and if you don't know the information inside and out she gets frustrated with you which makes it difficult to ask questions. I dedicated so much time and effort to this course and was barely scraping by with a B.

very few grades were put in the grade book (2 midterms, 20ish quizzes, recitation, & final). average for the midterms (worth 40% of our grade) was a c. the midterms were incredibly hard and very detail heavy & based on like 5 30-40 slide ppt so lots of memorization. also, lectures were just her reading of the slides (so hard to learn based on that)

Dr. Marin is a sweetheart, but at times her lectures seemed very rushed and lack luster as she read word-for-word from slideshows. She is very knowledgeable though! I wish she were able to translate that knowledge better for us. Very caring lady and funny. This course overall was challenging for me, even though I've taken upper level chem and biol.

Dr. Marin is caring, but exams are difficult, and you need to memorize EVERYTHING from slides. She read off the slides and moved SUPER fast in lecture, so I needed to spend lots of time outside class. Make sure to do the EC. Only 1 section, so don't take it if you don't need to, but also don't let it stop you from applying to the Nutrition major.

Nice person but genuinly the hardest grader at UNC. When I took this class, I was surprised at the fact that it easily surpassed the horrors of the chem department. 
The class, hard as is, tests on biochemical metabolic reactions without us given background information how they work. Also, get ready to be tested on the most minute details possible.

Seems like a nice person, and very knowledgable at the subject, but for your own sake take with another professor! Genuinely one of the most difficult classes I've taken at UNC, and I've taken a good amount of chem and bio.

TAKE NUTR 240 WITH SOMEONE ELSE. Dr. Marin seems incredibly smart, but intelligence does not equal good at teaching. Her exams are insanely difficult, and when the class average was a C for BOTH midterms, she placed the blame on the students. Her expectations of us were far too high for the quality of teaching she provided. 0/10

Her exams are insanely difficult, and when the class average was a C for BOTH midterms, she placed the blame on the students. Her expectations of us were far too high for the quality of teaching she provided. 0/10

Her teaching style involves reading off the slides. She expected her students to know everything in the PowerPoint and the textbook. She would not give hints about what we were expected to know. This class is a big time commitment, and homework is not a part of your grade. Her exam questions are sometimes confusing.

Her lectures are boring. They only go over a small part of the assigned readings, so you are basically teaching yourself. If you read the chapters you could skip the lectures. Exams are hard. Multiple select questions. For example, the choices would be A; B; C; A & B; or A , B, & C. Over half of the test consist of question in this format.

Genuinely worst course I've taken at this university. I am in orgo at the same time and am even doing better in that class. She reads off the slides, tests are unbearably hard, and I have had a medical emergency, and she refuses to even take that into consideration or even respond to emails regarding the situation in terms of points.

Sturgill without a doubt is an amazing lecturer. If you take his class in OS, you will understand so much after. My main gripe with this class is the tests. If you ever tell yourself "this won't be on the test". You're wrong. There's some questions you can guess with be on the test. But every single topic could be on the test, so be prepared.

Dr. Sturgill is a very miserly, nitpicky, and unaccommodating professor. He expects you to know the content after hearing it once. On exams, he asks overly specific questions and will deduct more points during regrade requests. He takes an eternity to write and grade HWs and will not respond to Ed posts. Do not be fooled by his happy demeanor. -HY
very stubborn. Don't understand any kind of issue he will just go with his opinion. If it is possible please don't take him. Trust me by taking him you will loose your mental peace.

He don't care about his students. It doesn't matter if your GPA gets affect and class average is really low for all the exams he will stick to his " I don't believe in free points so I won't curve" and not open to accept any alternative or extra credit. Grades everything so hard. Sometimes he do negative grading too. Please avoid him!!

I enjoyed Operating Systems with Dr. Sturgill. The course is challenging and he holds his students to a high standard, but I never felt unprepared. He is an excellent and knowledgeable lecturer. I recommend this course if you want a rigorous OS experience and are ready for the time commitment. You will leave feeling like you mastered the material.

For an exercise I put down (example only) 1100 1111 instead of 11001111 and got no credits for it. Asked him for a regrade since it is otherwise identical answer and clearly showed that I understood the concept. He looked into it and said he won't give credits. Don't bother wasting your time with him. Dude doesn't care about his students.

Doesn't reply to students emails or discussion board questions - what's the point of a professor if we are not given the teaching support we are paying for (all the material can be learned easier, more stress free, and affordable on YouTube)!!!

Positive reviews mean they had nothing else to do all semester. He explains very well, and that's a good thing, but for averages to be a borderline 60 and refuse to add any curve is ridiculous. Very difficult tests, and he loves to ask questions, so hidden, you'll never expect them to come on the tests. Good for understanding, bad for your GPA.
Nice satire below me. Go take OS with McLeod if the hardcore exams aren't for you. Everyone has their preferences, so don't shame whether they pick.

Sturgill is an average lecturer who primarily relies on (posted) slides. The course itself was very disorganized, with several assignments/projects being released late. Additionally, their instructions were abysmally unclear, often more difficult to decipher than the coding itself. An A is possible, but requires more effort than a 3-credit should.

Tests were absolutely insane and pulled questions from topics he talked about for 2 picoseconds. Daily quizzes were also disgusting too, because some days you don't get enough sleep and aren't paying enough attention to minute details from the slides.

He decided the best way to "help" students after the averages on the first two tests were in the low 60s was to shift the weight from those tests to the final, which also had an average in the low 60s. He genuinely doesn't care that his class affects GPA, grad school, scholarships, and mental well being. Avoid at all costs

The positive reviews are either from him or from masochists. The tests are impossible, he takes forever to grade homework, and he gives little to no leniency. He somehow has a PhD but can't make the connection that if the test average is a 60, his tests are probably too hard or he just doesn't care (probably the latter).

Sturgill gives great lectures and assigns homework that does a good job of applying what's learned in class. His tests can be fairly tough, but if you actually take the time to understand the material you'll be fine. If you're interested the content, you'll like Sturgill.

If you want to learn OS, take Sturgill. If you only care about your GPA, go with the other prof. My biggest gripe throughout the semester was the exams, which I still do believe are too difficult at times, but at the end of the day, I learned. And as somebody who took another prof for 230, I can't say the same there.

Sturgill's CSC246 is very tough but rewarding if you're interested in the material and willing to put in the work. The learning potential is off the charts for anyone who wants to understand operating systems, and the lectures are engaging. He holds students to high standards, but it's silly to interpret that as not wanting them to succeed.

He's an excellent lecturer who knows his stuff. Answers lots of questions in class. Quizzes and exams are tough but put in effort and you can succeed. Clearly makes an effort to help students succeed, using an elongated grading scale, shifting exam weights, and communicating with class to see how he can help. Take these 1 stars with a grain of salt

This guy is insane. His tests are made for you to fail because he enjoys watching students fail.  I joined in for an office hour one day and this guy is lounging on the couch like he is at home? If you want to fail a course, take this section.
He takes IMMENSE JOY in lowering grades as much as they can for students. Just look at his past gradients and you will see what I mean.

Absolutely ridiculous standards for students and grading. Posted a major project write up a month late, cutting a month out of the time for completion. Exam questions require photographic memory. He will dance around questions.  This is the kind of class that will force you into mental distress and have you calculating minimum passing grades. 0/10

I don't know what y'all did to him last semester but it made him turn CSC230 into a weed out class. You'll get tested on the most minute details said once in class and that goes for the quizzes you get after each lecture too. Very disorganized class.

CSC 230 w Sturgill has the potential to be a great class. However, lack of support (no email response except 1 TA), unrealistic deadlines, not returning grades/feedback on time, and tests which ask meaninglessly specific questions (no technical interview will ask), all make it to be a poor experience. Severe disconnect between professor & students.

So heres the TLDR on what happened. CSC 230 under went restructuring. That kinda made a lot of chaos. His exams are still equivalent to the Great Wall of China. The 1 big new project we get this semester was released late with less time to do it. Also, to celebrate Thanksgiving, he took away points because of errors in the auto grader. TYVM

Saw a quote the other day summing up this class - "if a professor cannot lecture without notes/slides, how can students be expected to remember EVERYTHING"? Obviously a bit far-fetched as the point of college is learning material and all, but the man makes his tests SO DIFFICULTLY SPECIFIC on purpose. He gets a sense of joy from doing so.

He has a massive disconnect between his students and the coursework. He boasts how he made his tests harder recently. He doesn't respect human life as he will include every little arbitrary term from the hundreds of slides for several fill in the blank questions for as much credit on the tests as writing entire algorithms in C. Ruined my major.

Take him if you want to be miserable and lower your GPA! You get a pop quiz after every lecture and if you aren't able to memorize everything after 75 minutes of lecturing you will do bad on it. For tests you either have to memorize every slide from the class or hope you get lucky enough that the stuff you remember is on the test.

Don't know what this guy's problem is, but he seems to enjoy making the class as hard as possible. Test avg was in the low 60s with no curve. He goes out of his way to make things harder, and if you need flexibility, he'll ignore you or give a non-answer. He's reminds me of an evil robot that's sole purpose is to make students suffer. Start praying

I understand this class is not meant to be easy, but god forbid you don't have a photographic memory and can't memorize every word he says in lecture. Too much emphasis on small details rather than general topics. On bright side, projects are worth decent part of your grade and those are not terribly difficult. Tests and daily quizzes are HORRIBLE.

Would tell us that things would be graded by a specific day, and they would be graded a month later. Not good time management, and for our final semester project we got less time on it because HE DIDN'T FINISH THE WRITE UP IN TIME. Student's penalized for his lack of organization. Also tests VERY difficult. No curve. Say goodbye to your perfect GPA
Never seen a professor's RMP rating drop so much in 1 semester... so I'd like to pitch in for the fun of it!
I was depressed so to distract myself I started studying for this class. Then I realized this is the reason why I was depressed.
Ignores student questions via email or discussion form. Course is overall disorganized and very badly paced. Designed to fail as many as possible :)

I will agree the CSC department has some ruthless professors (whose sole purpose is to weed out students). Sometimes, a challenge is appropriate (take CSC 316 with Dr King for instance) which is a great one. But this guy pushes the limits on ruthlessness and sole ability to not care at all about student success, student grades, and amount of work.

Decides the best way to “help” the class is shift 4% weightage from midterm to final exam which will already be extremely hard and lot of material rather than address the fact that his exams are just bad with a 60 average, standard deviation 20!!!!

Thousands of lecture slides. Make sure you know every single term that was never used in code, it will be on the test. Takes a month to grade homework, goes back a week after grading to take more points off. Literally refused to give assignment grades back and was reprimanded. Daily quizzes meant to take your grade down that sometimes are hard.

I have always been academically strong and ready to tackle an academic challenge. This class made me lose faith in myself let alone my ability to learn. If you have always been a straight-A student, this class will make you start calculating minimum grade to pass and stuff like that. PLEASE, I beg you take with another professor.

The exam average is in the 60s. Exams are "That one term listed once on slide 47 from 5 weeks ago". I studied 2 weeks in advance for exams and still struggled. HW grades come out late so you lose points you couldve fixed on the next HWs. On the DAY of Thanksgiving he even LOWERED grades on HW that came out a MONTH ago instead of just letting it go

Absolutely awful at teaching, only reads off the sides and dances around questions. Shows no effort to help students succeed. All projects were delivered late (a semester long project was 2 weeks late) without pushing back the deadlines, while the instructions were confusing and full of mistakes (both in spelling and classification of material).

He rates himself. Read the 5 start reviews and it's obvious which ones are him. My honest review is that he tries to do too much, bottlenecks the grading until the last week of the semester (no exaggeration), provides overly complicated assignments and focuses on weird details that are covered in

His goal: Make the class as difficult as possible without getting in trouble. He enjoys making things unnecessarily difficult and enjoys watching students squirm. 

Other instructors can't even decipher his own projects, let alone help because of how complicated his assignments are.

HE DOESNT CARE ABOUT YOUR GPA! DO NOT TAKE! AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!

Happy Thanksgiving! He is "grateful" for his students. To demonstrate this, professor spent Thanksgiving day regrading homework and trying to squeeze out as many point deductions as possible. States very casually that his exam average was a 60 without any shame not realizing his class has an impact on GPA, grad school, scholarships, and well being.

Pro: Knows C. Cons (a lot): Takes forever to return grade and feedback of major assignments, impossible tests (be ready to remember obscure definitions),complained that students make him do extra work yet he never assigns anything on time, never reply to emails / barely answer questions on ed.  DONT TAKE HIM, he's NIGHTMARE FUEL.

Worst professor of my life. He will give you outrageously hard assignments. also make sure you know your spelling or you will lose points for forgetting one letter. He doesn't seem to have the ability to write a decent set of instructions for any assignment to the point the other professors are confused by his write ups. DONT TAKE AWFUL!!!!!!!!!!!!

Way too much material. Attempts to cram 100 sides worth of information in a single sitting. Finishes your question yet somehow manages to not answer it. Finds ways to dock points on HW, so obtaining that beautiful green checkmark in Jenkins means nothing. If you don't memorize a term from slide 28 out of 600, it's sayonara to your test grade.

Plz don't choose! Especially u r NOT learned enough about C before this class. To be honest, his lectures are interesting BUT exams and grades are more important for us as CS students. Exams are really hard that require u to remember nearly all stuff. He gave lots of extra credits but still didn't help exams.

"HW will be returned next week" ... proceeds to take 2 months. "Exam will be returned tomorrow" ... proceeds to take a month. "Will release the assignment tomorrow" ... proceeds to release 2 weeks later providing us only a week to complete assignment that should take 3 weeks. Grading, planning, workload and timing is just utter ridiculous. AVOID!!!

Stupid lecture quizzes end up hurting you. Finds ways to dock points from HW. Tests are oddly specific such that even after hours of studying your grade is destroyed Take any other 230/246 professor. The 5 star reviews here do not represent the reality of this class. If anything the series of 1 stars as seen in Fall 2025 on RMP should be a warning.

Traps are set so that you get points taken off on the "Homework" and Projects. We've had to put in 5+ hours outside of class to watch out of class lecture for an in person section because of how much material there is. "I shouldn't have to answer that, you should already know". He's intolerant if you don't immediately understand it.

Ended up dropping. He has definitions in his slides that he defines half the time verbally during lecture. He is the type of person who will put more effort in a non-answer than the actual answer. He holds the belief that if you are not incredibly gifted, you should NOT do computer science. I reject him and his high-minded belief. Avoid at all cost

Imagine having 5+ TA and still delaying grade returns because he insists on re-checking everything to prevent students from getting extra points. He holds up homework and projects long after TAs finish, and the support vs work is totally out of balance because of him. Will not debug during office hours, will not answer questions directly, awful

Please, please listen to me. For your own mental health, for your own sanity, DO NOT TAKE HIM! This class is a classic example of academia being academia. Just because you can write it in one line, doesn't mean you should. Readability is important. C will make you a better programmer, but his class will just make you frustrated. Take someone else.

Just don't. Tests are probably some of the most difficult ones I have taken in my entire CSC degree (and he makes them difficult on purpose). He doesn't care even if half the class fails. They also don't grade things on time. Assignments from September have still not been graded in November causing students to repeat old mistakes and lose points.

Sturgill is an amazing lecturer, but classes are packed full with information and you will be in class until the last 5 minutes when he hands out the end of class quiz. You have to be absolutely locked in the whole time to do well on quizzes. Tests cover a large amount of information, but study guides and terms lists are provided.

Dr. Sturgill is one of the most interesting professors I've had. While I agree with the general population that he's a hard professor, he believes in his students and their abilities. He loves the work that he does, which can be both his strength and weakness, as it can be overwhelming with him at times.

Had him for 230 as well, by far the best professor for 246. Lectures are clear and concise, homework has some extra credit available, and I've never seen him fail to answer a student's question. His section uses a modified grading scale, so anything >= 87 is considered an A-, which is much appreciated due to the difficulty of this course.

Everything in this class is so much better than his CSC230, from projects to course content.  246 is a lot of work, but it's information worth knowing, and Sturgill is by far the best lecturer of the 246 teachers.  His exams are hard, but if you put in the hours, you should do well enough.  He uses an adjusted grading scale, doing well is possible.

I had him for 230 and 246. He does not make the hard classes he teaches any easier. I would not recommend him, but he is supposed to be the better of the professors that teach his classes. Good luck...

230 is awful no matter what, but Sturgill does make it more challenging w quizzes after every class and tests that cover every topic no matter how minor. Start projects as soon as you get them, they can take excruciatingly long but you can also earn a lot of extra credit on them. Got A's on both midterms by starting my studying a week before

Dr. Sturgill is knowledgeable in his field but scares away students with his ridiculously hard tests. Quizzes are unreasonable as remembering every detail he says in a 1hour 15 minutes lecture heavy class is hard. His tests have to be the worst and he doesn't give any sample paper or questions, just study guide with every topic mentioned in class.

His lectures are very engaging, and he's honestly a fun guy. The class is kind of a lot, and if you want to take good notes be ready to have your hand on fire, but overall everything was very fair, and incredibly interesting. I thought his tests were pretty challenging, but fair. You have to study a lot, but it could be worse. He's pretty great!

If you want an "easier" 230 class, don't take Sturgill. If you want someone who is very knowledgeable and will teach you C better than the other professors, take him.  While his exams are harder, he has the best lectures and can provide the best answers to project questions.  I did hate his end of class quizzes though, they always felt too hard.

Sturgill is an amazing professor. In my time at NC State he has been the best lecturer I have ever had. It's evident that he is extremely knowledgeable in the subject. He writes his tests well and I feel that they are very reflective of how much you know. 230 was significantly more work in my opinion.

Several reviews claim his tests are more difficult; having had friends in other sections, it seems there is a pool of similar questions, and each test is a subset. After-class quizzes (covering content from the lecture) are easy and a grade booster. Generous extra credit on some of the projects. The class is very similar to 116. Very good lecturer!

He pedantically grades short answer questions on tests. Most of the tests are taken up by simple non impactful and random regurgitation which leaves no time for the actual coding parts, let alone to give a detailed short answer question.

I took him for 230 as well and found this class to be ever so slightly easier, and more interesting overall. I would definitely recommend taking him over another OS professor as his lectures are engaging and he really knows the course content. Additionally, he stretches the grading scale for this course so there's no reason not to get a good grade.

Sturgill is an amazing lecturer. He's detailed, clear, and will answer questions during class. There are in-class quizzes for attendance, but they aren't tough and end up boosting your grade. His only downside is that his tests are significantly harder than the other 230 profs. If you want to learn and don't mind a lower grade, Sturgill is great!

Very nice happy guy. We did 100+ page slides and would still have catch up lectures frequently. With 1k+ of slides, its hard to retain the information. The tests were unstudiable- the study guide is a list of every single idea. The vocab section was random specific words. Needs less content and make the tests about what we actually practiced/used.

Sturgill is a brilliant professor who knows a lot about the material he is teaching and exactly how to teach it. If you take 246 at all you will have to take his difficult tests no matter what, so I highly recommend taking Sturgill for the wealth of knowledge he provides. Though he is very slow on emails though which makes regrades frustrating.

CSC 246 is a hard class, but Sturgill is very passionate about the course and it is evident in his lectures. Lectures are mandatory because there are small quizzes at the end of them. Outside of that, you'll have 1-2 small coding exercises a week and then a larger homework assignment due every 2-3 weeks. Exams are tough, but not impossible.

After taking CSC246 with Sturgill, I regret not doing the same for 230. People told me not to take him because he graded harsher / harder tests than Balik, but I honestly disagree after seeing it for myself. Sturgill is a MUCH better professor, way more knowledgeable, I enjoy attending his lectures versus Balik's were absolutely worth skipping.

Sturgill is heavy on the lectures and while attendance isn't technically required he provides daily quizzes at the end of the lecture which forces you to attend. Exams are hard and detailed. To give credit where credit is due he does try to make the course doable. But he provides very little help if you are stuck and will not help debug anything.

Class is well organized and informative. It moves very quickly and covers a lot of material so you need to show up and pay attention. Tests are very difficult and require lots of studying, but it's curved pretty fairly. Projects aren't too bad. You can tell he cares about you understanding things. Overall, pretty good.

He actually seems to enjoy the material and teaching. Curriculum and projects are well-designed, and he has several office hours a week for questions.

Leave more time for debugging in C than with Java, but generally his grading seems reasonable. Anything I missed on an exam was something I probably should have known (but I did have to study).
Great professor, and very enthusiastic about a class at 8:30 AM. Harder tests than the other professors, but by far the best lecturer. Make sure to start projects early, there are 6 of them.

Yes, if you take Sturgill's sections for C and Software Tools you will likely get a lower grade. This is irrelevant. The class was engaging all the way through, and it is clear that he knows both the course content and the inner workings of C significantly better than the other professors. Project heavy -duh. Get started early and you'll be fine.

One of the best lecturers I've ever had. VERY knowledgable about what he's talking about, and tries to be engaging/entertaining in lectures. His tests are hard, but I studied really hard and was able to score above the average for both midterms. If you take him and put in effort, you can leave with a good grade and a lot of knowledge.
This is a difficult class, but worth your while if CS is your major.  There's a lot of work, but if you do it you'll come out knowing your stuff.

Great lecturer however some of the technical aspects of the course were quite lacking. Jenkins feedback was not available for the first half of the projects, and he was very behind on regrade requests. Has end of lecture quizzes that cannot be done online or made up. Tests are very difficult but Sturgill is also very good at teaching the content.
NGL, Sturgill is harder than the other professors who teach this class. He's also better. Take his classes if you really want to learn.

Quizzes are very hard sometimes and he forces you to go to his classes by having quizzes. Exams are insanely hard too. He makes the materials not fun or enjoyable by asking you very tricky questions on exams.

Difficult class. Do not take with Sturgill if you want a good GPA. He is very hard but I still respect him since he is intelligent and knows what he is talking about. It just feels unfair taking it with him since its so much easier with other professors, so I will not in the future.

Great teacher, great at teaching but super heavy workflow, he will not give u answer but hint in office hour, get early at lease a week early to do the project. it is super charllenge, but you learn a lot, like a lot!!

Dr. Sturgill is an awesome lecturer. He expects a lot, but almost everything he explains is something that you will end up seeing in the professional world. Tests are difficult but manageable with a good study routine. The homework requires some thought but is fair. I would rather take a B in a Sturgill class than get an A in a different section.

Dr. Sturgill is a good guy and he knows the material very well. Lectures can get boring, but the content is very important (CSC 230 is a grind). He assigns handout quizzes at the end of every lecture which can be annoying if you miss class, and his tests are really tough. Doing well on the projects can help you stay on track in the course.
Awful, wasn't accommodating to extenuating circumstances, and even yelled at the class. Very unprofessional.

Sturgill knows his stuff. He is willing to help students outside of class and even holds night office hours sometimes. You have to pay attention in class and the tests are very tough, but you come out really knowing what you are doing.

The weekly projects take a lot of time to complete but aren't necessarily super difficult. Prof Heckman is a solid lecturer and I felt like I learned a ton in this class. Just stay on top of project deadlines and you'll do very well in this class. Exams are relatively easy and offer lots of partial credit.
She is a really nice professor. However, the exams are hard and projects take a very long time, so make sure you actually lock in and study.

She seems nice, but I do not like the lectures. Fast-paced, lots of info presented, and not getting enough from them. Projects take a lot of time, and they have components with deadlines during exam week. I wish I had started P1 sooner. Thankfully, we were allowed a partner for the final project.

If you go to every class and take good notes then you can stay on top but if you miss even one class be prepared to do a lot of work to catch back up. The projects are not hard but the instructions are unclear, so you will often spend many hours rewriting code, because the instructions and the staff test code expectations can be different.

Easy class with two lab projects constituting bulk of the grade. Midterm and final were each 15% only. Dr. Heckman lectures a lot with several participation activities in class. Attendance is mandatory.

Dr. Heckman is a good lecturer but she moves really fast. However, the class is really just hard. There's project milestones and lab deadlines on the same week as an exam.

Project directions also contain typos, confusing language, and broken links. And not to mention the MILLION research studies they keep hounding you to participate in.

The course has been difficult to follow because the lectures rarely align with the lab work, leaving many concepts unclear. The instructor's explanations feel scattered, and her interactions with students often come across as curt, which makes the class atmosphere uncomfortable and discouraging.

The instructor's lectures are poorly structured and don't connect to the labs, leaving students confused. Her teaching style is unhelpful, and she is often rude and dismissive when students ask questions. This has created a frustrating learning environment and makes understanding the material difficult.
Solid lecturer but nothing exceptional. Go to class and don't wait until the last minute to start the projects, and you will succeed.

Dr. Heckman is overall a great teacher. Lectures are very fast-paced, so be prepared to spend time outside of class looking over old slides. Projects make up 50+ percent of your grade, but are very good coding practice. Overall, not an easy class, but Dr. Heckman made it a bit easier with her enthusiasm and knowledge!

Dr. Heckman was very knowledgeable and a great lecturer. She went over notes and information in lectures and gave us tips for how to do things more efficiently. The projects take a long time, so start early! The projects will usually take longer than the projected time she gives. The class is time-intensive, but Dr. Heckman makes it bearable.

Dr. Heckman is a great lecturer and very enthusiastic, but the class overall is rough + fast-paced. The exams are more difficult than they should be, especially the final (too much writing code by hand). The projects take up lots of your time but are great at giving a hands-on experience, unlike the slides. Beware of the min grade requirement!! -HY

She loves teaching and is passionate about computer science. Tests are fair and it is easy to do well in her class if you stay on top of project deadlines, go to office hours when necessary, and study well. All in all, a great 216 experience and prepared us well for 316. Will surely take her again if given the chance!
216 is awful. Tons of work and long hours. Dr. H made it much more bearable with her helpful TAs and great digestable lectures. I still suffered greatly in this class but Im glad it wasnt worse.
Amazing teacher, absolutely loved her. Would take her class 10 times over again. You can tell she really loves computer science and it shows in her lectures.

The best CS professor I have had, you don't need to attend the lectures to do well but attendance matters. Class overall is pretty easy but start the projects early because they can take a lot of time.

Dr. Heckman is the best professor you can take for 216. She is really passionate about Java data structures and techniques (especially iterators), and prepares you the best she can for the numerous projects and coding assignments. Start Part 2 of the projects as soon as you can--you will spend more time than you expect debugging.

Dr. Heckman is a good lecturer with fair tests and projects. The projects are important and take a long time so start early! Tests could be difficult and involved a lot of writing code by hand but are graded fairly. Dr. Heckman also makes sure there is a lot of help available to students at most days/times.

She is a good lecturer and a nice professor. Majority of the grade is projects which were great for working with the concepts covered and enjoyable to work on as well. They do take a while so start early. Tests were fair, got to bring a note sheet for the midterms. Have to hand write a lot of code on exams which I didn't like.

Dr. Heckman is one of the best professors I've had so far in CSC. She is very approachable and knowledgeable. It's clear she wants us to understand how to write good code for industry. If you're taking her for CSC216 make sure you start on the projects early and study lots for the tests. The final has lots of code writing on it.
