She's fine - your options are limited in this course anyways. Attendance not mandatory. Tests trivial, vast majority of grading focused on projects. Soooo boring though. I skipped at least 30% of class towards the end. Lots of focus on practice, processes, etc. They assume you can code at this point.

Dr. Heckman does an outstanding job of explaining everything needed in a way that is clear and understandable. Not only is she one of the most approachable and nicest professors I have ever taken a class with, but she also doesn't put an effort to fail students. If you're taking CSC216 in the future, START PROJECTS EARLY, INCLUDING THE GUIDED ONES!

Once again a hallmark class by one of the well respected professors in the Computer Science Department. Class was a clear demonstration of what a typical software engineering job would look like. Very much a team based class so pick the right group of people. Exams were fairly easy as a notesheet is allowed. Very project heavy but not too difficult

She's super nice and her lectures are very appropriate. Cares about the course and the students. Tests are super straightforward and a very fair class. Projects are a massive pain and headache I would say (mainly that first one). SO if you start early and work hard for the work heavy class you will do great. Material is pretty enjoyable :)

Dr. Heckman is a great professor who knows what she's talking about. Her teaching style is definitely one that a hands-on learner may not do well with though but she's knowledgeable about it so you do end up learning a bit about the concept. Watch out though for Project 1, that one can take a toll on you, it did for me even starting it early.

Heckman's CSC 326 not only assumes that everybody wants/needs full-stack engineering skills, but grades you based on superficial criteria that doesn't apply to the work itself. Too much emphasis was put on "process" which took away from the engineering side of the class.

Great lectures and a well structured course that gives lots of practical experience in software engineering. The class is a lot of work, but it all feels relevant for the most part. Heckman is a great lecturer who clearly cares about her students and gives lots of real world context to the material.

Make sure you have good group members.

She's a great lecturer, but I thought that CSC326 was a huge waste of time (and she has the control over making it mandatory as the director). I do appreciate that the class let me realize I have no desire whatsoever to get into Software Engineering.

Dr. Heckman was nice but the class is fairly boring and mainly just depends on doing the lab and projects. I rarely went to class as you don't have to physically attend lectures to be counted a present.

Dr. Heckman is incredibly relaxed teacher with student-focused grading policies. However, the material covered in the lectures are not always related to what is covered in lab, so be sure to spend extra time learning lab concepts on your own.

Dr. Heckman is a very knowledgeable and capable instructor.  The course concepts can be hard, but she does a great job explaining them, and she knows what she's talking about.  A lot of the grade, however, is left up to your performance on projects--start earlier than you'd typically do, because they will take up dozens of hours usually.

Great professor. Engaging lectures and fun projects. She doesn't have the ability to connect one-on-one with students due to the class size, so she does the best she can through the TAs. Would take again in a heartbeat.

SE was a blast with Heckman, incredible lecturer. The course project has switched from previous years and is a fresh new experience. Evident that lots of care has gone in to make 326 a great course. Definitely take lab sections with people you know, though, as you'll be working on a project with them all semester.
She is a fine professor, but the professor you take for this class doesn't really matter that much. It's more about doing the work. I did find her to be a bit overly enthusiastic at times...

I rarely asked the professor for help on assignments since I usually received help from TAs. But Dr. Heckman is a great professor. She teaches the material well. For projects, start them early. Usually you will be debugging code errors. If you know you're going to need help, go to office hours ASAP. They get filled up quickly near the deadlines.
A great lecturer who explained concepts very effectively and enthusiastically. You will need to start working on projects early or else it is very easy to fall behind.

If you are taking CSC216, she is not a bad option. She does tend to speak pretty fast during lectures but she is knowledgeable in what she is talking about. Expect to spend a lot of time for this class, and definitely start the projects early. Also try to get help from TAs whenever you can.

I failed 216. I love Dr.Heckman though. Her lectures are by far the best I have taken at NCSU. Be ready for a lot of work in projects (especially project 1). For lecture test, I would recommend doing a lot of practice-it problems. Lots of the data structure test answers are from the lab so Make sure you know them by heart.

Heckman has very organized lectures and is overall a great instructor. CSC216; is NOT a cakewalk. Start projects as early as possible, and seek help when needed; or it's very likely you could fail. Expect to spend around 10+ hrs a week on 216, IF you're not a gifted programmer.

In CSC326 basically the only contact you will have from Dr. Heckman is the lectures. She clearly cares about students and does her best to make the very dry material from software engineering engaging. A solid pick for 326

Balik provides everything you need to be successful in this course and it's clear she genuinely wants everyone to do well. The only downside is that the lecture is a bit slow and dry but if you make sure you are caffeinated she moves at the perfect pace for you to take notes and actually absorb information during lecture.

lectures are required but its so hard to learn from them, she is unorganized, doesnt record the lectures, and makes the slides impossible to study. 
waits until last minute to grade big projects so theres nothing you can do for your grade if it drops. confusing and unorganized project requirements. exam two is a GIANT jump of topics after the first
She just sucks as a teacher and person. do not take her class and nc state should of fired her 500 years ago
I didn't wear a seatbelt on my way to class. If you can infer what I mean.

The lectures were dry but fortunately the class itself is pretty easy so it doesn't really matter. Tons of homework and a mandatory online textbook. Cares a lot about her students but the tests/projects are graded really harsh. I would recommend Balik if you are new to Java, but if you are already familiar you'll be very bored.

If you haven't taken Java/coded before she may not be for you,bc it's mostly powerpoints: great for reviewing java, but not learning it.However, if you have, she's a much easier time than other csc116 professors, with hw and tests being pretty straightforward, and her group project is simpler than other profs.'.Focus on projects, they take time!

Despite providing practice tests, her tests, which require you to HANDWRITE CODE WITH PAPER AND PENCIL, are horrible. I went into this course with previous Java knowledge and 3 weeks to the end, I BARELY have a 90. The lectures are useless, but attendance is graded. The class is way too difficult for an intro level course.

Dr. Balik knows her stuff, but she teaches class as if it's a review, since for a lot of students, it is. If you're new to programming do not take her. The review feel of her class makes it very hard for a beginner to learn the material. Otherwise, a good teacher. She gave practice tests that looked just like the test, and helps when you ask for it

Dr. Balik gets a lot of hate, but I had a good semester with her. Yes, lectures are boring, but you're forced to complete an online interactive textbook which helped me learn everything needed. Her tests are also VERY similar to the practice tests, so just start projects early and always maintain high quality in them as this class is very demanding

Alright, listen. Yes, lectures are dry, name tags for attendance is a bit weird, but the slides are great and you should come to class anyway. Just pay attention. She's kind and wants you to do well, put the laptop away and synthesize what she's saying. Ask questions. There's no reason to avoid her, she will support you if you put in the effort.

Do you want a college professor that treats you like a middle schooler? If so take this class. We had name tags for attendance and we had to get them one at a time to ensure that no one "cheated the attendance system". Lectures are dry but the tests weren't awful.

Lectures weren't very interesting or insightful. The only benefit of class time was to ask her and the TA's potential questions. zyBook was the homework and I found it to be pretty redundant. Grade was comprised of coding activities, homeworks, projcets, and tests.

I found coming to class useless, slides were read with no added given context / personality. Self studied, ended up with an A- with not too much effort. She seems to have good intentions, seems like a really nice person... I just wish she'd take into account feedback from her students.

Just read the slides as is in class with a lot of information that isn't conveyed in a manner that is not easy to understand or intuitive. it's just unfortunate that this class is difficult and is coupled with a professor who shouldn't have the responsibility and doesn't have the competency to educate students.

She reads off the slides so her lectures arent necessary but attendance is graded. She is passive aggressive if lecture is interrupted but better than past classes from what I heard. Gives time at the end of every lecture to work. Project heavy: start early because these are long. TAs are nice and helpful for projects GO TO OFFICE HRS!

Absolutely terrible teacher. She is a good person but should not be teaching. This was my first programming class, and I will never take one again. The projects caused me migraines and took up weeks' worth of my time. I only ended with a good grade b/c I got help from the TAs and spent extensive time outside the class getting help. Not worth it...

If you have experience with Java or coding in general and can organize a schedule well, you should be able to do well. Anyone else who is new will need to self-study hard from the Zybook textbook and projects/daily exercises since her lectures are meaningless. Lots of work but at least gives some extensions for projects and better due dates

One of the worst professors I've had at NCSU. I don't think I learned anything from the lectures because she reads only what is on the slides and adds very limited context to the information. She never even opened an IDE to show us how the code works, and has the TAs do most of the work. You might as well not go to class and learn it on your own.
The final is so hard, but the exams are easier than Sturgill's.

Dr.Balik is not a good lecturer. She reads through her slides without giving you any context of the topic. She talks slowly but somehow she is able to finish most of her lectures in 30-40mins(It is a 75 mins lecture) because she does not lecture you but reads the slides for you. Overall, she seems like a good person but not a good professor.

Balik is rude and lacks connection with her students. Her lectures are very boring and fast-paced. She lacks empathy and acknowledgement of college student feelings and struggles. I am very interested in Computer Science but after her class I feel bitter about the subject. I would recommend not taking Balik for CSC 116 if you can avoid it.
She gives a lot of homework and overall is not a very thorough good teacher.
Arbitrarily difficult and tedious sums up this entire class. You would genuinely be better off in every way going to a coding boot camp.

I did not enjoy Balik's lecture style at all. It is extremely boring and non-interactive. However, she does cover all the necessary concepts and provides decent powerpoint slides. DO NOT take Balik if you are planning to pursue Computer Science. She does not teach or implement GitHub or allow you to use an IDE.

12 Weekly coding workshops will take anywhere from ~2-5hrs. Very straightforward instructions. His slides are good for studying. Tests are very similar to workshop-written activities. I struggled initially, but got the hang of it. Semester project (proposal, coding, reflection), but it is spread out nicely. He is a cool dude who uses Kahoot a lot.

Dr. King is a caring professor teaching a challenging course, and student frustration with the material is sometimes unfairly directed at him. While his lecture style wasn't my personal preference, he is a good professor who puts real effort into making DSA engaging. This is an important course, and the effort you put into it will pay off.

Dr. King is a solid lecturer and provides recordings of all the lectures so you can watch them at any time. The workshops can be a lot of work but are manageable and helpful for studying. The class moves quickly, so it's important to stay on top of the assignments. The tests are long for the amount of time given, so you need to work efficiently.

Dr. King is a good lecturer and very knowledgeable, but is overly strict especially about academic integrity. The class is very fast-paced with lots of content to learn. Exams have too much content and not enough time, so memorization is key. Workshops will take up time but will be your best friend. Beware of the MGR and form good study groups. -HY

Very fair professor, knows we have an insane amount of content and does give a lot of work. But the assignments aren't super hard and aren't strictly graded. And we get late penalty waivers. Tests not too hard and they are fair. Great class organization. You must put in a lot of work, and I caution taking with CSC 230. But King is great for 316.

Dr. King makes the best out of an extremely vast and complex course. His lectures are interactive (although some topics can be boring), and he's very responsive on Ed. The course is tough, however he (and the TAs/textbook) offer plenty of help with the material. The exams are a time crunch, so focus on the point-heavy questions first!
King makes good lecture slides and weekly workshops. He makes it very easy to skip lecture, read the slides, do the workshop in a few hours, and come away with a strong grasp of the material.

CSC 316 is a challenging course. You have to put the work in to get the results. Dr. King's lectures and explanations make data structures and algorithms interesting and easy to understand. Weekly coding and written workshop assignments (5 - 6 hours/week). Exams are dense, but fair. I ended up enjoying this class quite a bit!

Best teacher I have ever had. Made data structures an enjoyable class which is insane. Tests are extremely reasonable and test you on knowledge rather than trick questions like other teachers. 10000/10
The GOAT of 316 🐐

CSC316 is a theory class (no new Java) but also has weekly coding assignments that take 3-7 hours and have clear instructions. The tests are open-note, but they move so fast that you NEED to have most of the material memorized or be able to find it almost instantly. Drawing and visualizing the steps of the algorithms and tree operations is vital.

His class is manageable if it's your only CS class, yes, that's how much time you'll spend on it. Beware of the midterms + final, they're open-note, and that's why they're way too long. The exams are also much more difficult than what you normally see. In general, you need to keep up with his pace for success. He's also super responsive online.

Dr. King taught this class well. The class is organized and structured quite well which is nice because you know what to expect each week and lecture. He gives late penalty waivers to allow you to submit assignments 2 days later with no requirements which allowed me to balance my classes way better. Just get ready to study and do a lot of work.

I love Dr. King! His lectures are some of the best I've ever attended. This class is a LOT of work, and Dr. King knows it. If you keep pace with the work, start early, and prepare well for exams, you will do great! This course is extremely important to the field of computer science, and Dr. King is a fantastic teacher of these tricky topics.

Terrible lecturer, way too rushed. Assigns a lot of work that has surprisingly little semblance to real world work. Cares more about overly strict rules & artificially hard policies on cheating than improving the course. Zero help inside or outside of class, which hurts for how needless & hard the workload is. Rly wish there was another 316 prof.

Dr. King is a totally fine professor. He isn't the most enthusiastic by any means, but he lectures well and does his best to make the material entertaining (it's just not the most exciting class). The workload is a lot, but he posts deadlines in advance and he clearly puts a lot of thought into this. Be ready for a lot of work, but don't be afraid!

Hes a good teacher who really cares. His lectures are very well put together and organized, but you have to pay attention. If you slack off for even a little bit, you might get behind, but that's not his fault, it would be yours.

He's a great teacher if you actually apply yourself and lock in.
now, is not his falt as the collage requirt him to teach so many thing in one class, and too many student at once.

he has the best slide and class. As a student who has been in ncsu for both undergrade and grade, I have to go back to see his slide when i take OS for my master. Don't blame him on no helpful on out side of class, as there too many student and too few TA, and school is reciving too much student for money, but not hire enough teacher as they should

This class is a LOT of work and can be very hard.  That being said, King makes it well known in advance when stuff is due, and he is also very responsive on Ed.  He's not the most engaging lecturer but his slides are good and it's worth going in-person to class.  Everything is well planned; this class just requires you to be on top of things.

Good lecturer, but there is a lot of content throughout the semester. Make sure you study the content the entire time, otherwise final review will be a lot. The tests are open note. Very serious about academic integrity. lectures are online and in person, with small quizzes for the topics.

Genuinely unhelpful outside of class. Will take hours to respond to even the most basic questions and is not willing to make any adjustments. Will not mention deadlines in class, the students are left to check every little thing themselves.

For the difficult class it is, he does a good job teaching, especially in-person. Attendance is optional, but I suggest going to class as the default. He explains concepts well, the slides are well-made, but his questions he asks mid-lecture are often confusing and a bit awkward. He's also incredibly specific when describing terms. Pretty solid.
Dr King is a nice guy and he tries to make this class easier but 316 is just very difficult. The lectures were somewhat helpful but you need to put in effort outside of class to do well.

This was my favorite class last semester; he cares about what he does and is passionate teaching. Couldn't have asked for more. Does set tough standards, but if you put in effort it's a piece of cake.
Great professor for a very hard class, was very enthusiastic about the material and is clear about what is required to succeed in the class.

Engaging lectures with online option. Has review kahoots in beginning of class. Theres lecture questions but theyre reviewed in class. He checks Ed online forum for questions everyday so he responds very quickly. Coding workshops can be long but easy for most part, can collab on written questions. Exams are online and open note. Would recommend!

Dr. King really is a pretty good professor, the class gets a bad reputation due to the workload. This is mostly unavoidable for King though, as the class and content is important (seriously!). The lectures are engaging if YOU engage. Don't just sit there and look at the lecture slides. Overall a fine class albeit dense.

Great professor, I never personally had any issues with him or his teaching. The lectures can sometimes be a bit boring but that is also just how the material is. Just be aware that this course is VERY time consuming, I took this course w/CSC 230 and at only 12 credits I felt like I was working constantly on projects and assignments.

I took CSC316 with Dr. King. He is a really good lecturer and he can explain material well, but god forbid you go to his office hours if you are stuck on a piece of code (at least he makes this known). King also is an extremist about academic integrity violations making many people retake. Exams are long and difficult. LOTS of homework each week.

Class is pretty standard, but exams are quite long. Projects/workshops are easy, but the class is too focused on tree data structures to be of any value for the average student. You don't really cover DP, greedy algorithms, or really any competitive programming topic aside from the basics of tree traversals.

King is a good lecturer and very organized. This course is interesting and very useful. It's set up well for EOL - Moodle is fully utilized, everything is available on time, group work, open note online exams, etc. My only gripe is there is a bit of a "witch hunt" mentality when it comes to academic integrity violations. Overall difficult but fair.

Dr. King does not teach, he just talks. Most of my classes were extremely difficult because this class took so much time to do anything. Be careful what classes you take along with this class, and don't take 230 along with it if you can help it. Expect to take twice as long on any given assignment and you'll be okay

You aren't allowed to go to office hours for help. The average response time is largely inaccurate and posts get resolved with the "help" being one of three 1) generic/pasted answer from a different q 2) threat of ban due to asking public/private pair questions 3) an actual response?! -usually short and nondescriptive or refers to a different post.
Sometimes I wonder if King is sponsored by red bull because you will need one to make it through lectures and absorb everything

Her class is flipped class style which I personally do not like but she is a good professor. Especially if you have any background with coding, you'll be just fine throughout the course. Projects took some time and there was weekly quizzes but overall it was an easy class.

This class was more time consuming than it was difficult. Weekly labs are very long and can require further work outside of class. Its a partially flipped class so she puts a lot of the learning on you. Content still gets covered in class and is explained well. It feels like a lot of work for a 3 credit class, but it is conceptually fairly easy.

The flipped style of the classroom renders the excruciatingly long and boring lecture period for the class to be entirely unnecessary. No one pays attention during lecture. Also, in our class, Dr. Battestilli wasnt great with technology aside from Matlab.

Dr. B genuinely cares about her students. The lectures are long and labs are longer, but the work given is good practice and prepares you for exams. It is helpful to come in with previous coding knowledge, but is not necessary. The exams were fair, labs and weekly "graders" were helpful, and projects were difficult but you can work with partners.

She loves to say that flipped classrooms help the students learn, but all the material she gave us was pointless. The labs and the TAs were the only reason I understood the class at all. She tries to be motivational, but no one pays attention during lectures because they get nothing out of it other than participation. Attend the online section.

Dr. B truly cares about her students and has awesome TAs. The labs are long and boring, but they're relatively easy. Projects are significantly harder, but you can work with partners if you want. With it being such a big class, it takes a long time to get grades back, but that's not a huge deal to me. Lectures are boring and not too helpful to me.

I have no personal issues with Dr. B, however the class setup for CSC113 is egregiously mind-numbing. Despite it being a 3 credit hour class, the amount of work you have to do outside of class (projects, online learning, mini coding work) takes up your whole week. Projects are long and can be hard. I feel she expects too much for a beginner class.
Lectures are absolutely mind-numbing. Attend the lectures online via zoom if possible. Class is saturated with micro-assignments that consume quite a bit of time but are worth nearly nothing.

She assigns way too much work for the course. Projects are due and expected to be done while you are still learning the material that you need to know for the project. She treats it like a hybrid class even though it's purely in person and is NOT hybrid AT ALL in the enrollment wizard. I recommend going to lectures on Zoom as well.

Every lecture: 
30 x "are you with me?"

While I respect Dr. B, I found her lectures to be pretty boring. Her personality is very calm, which can be pretty numbing at times. I have more gripes with the course than Dr. B herself. 

Unless you enjoy Comp Sci, the course feels very long. The Tuesday lectures approach 2 hours, and the weekly labs can last up to 3 hours.

A kind professor who is very accessible through office hours (even though I never went to one). To succeed in the class, I would study the function reference sheet that's provided for each cycle. She gives opportunities for test retakes if you didn't do well. My only gripe is that class time kinda feels redundant (it's a flipped class)

Dr. Battestilli is a great professor. She makes it very easy for students to get the help they need outside of lectures by keeping a calendar for office hours and holding office hours all throughout the week. It did bother me, however, that we would be asked to watch online lectures at the beginning of each week to learn the material before class.

Overall a pretty easy 3 credit hour class if you pay attention and study. The content is not hard, the tests are not hard. Her class is very well structured and organized, it is easy to see what you need to complete and when. You don't have to go to lecture because they stream it to zoom. I came in with minimal coding experience and had no problem.

Dr. B is the only instructor to teach CSC 113 as of today's date. She has long lectures that I didn't find too useful since most of the learning was online before lecture, but the test review lectures that are in-person only are worth going to. The lab sections are great if your TA is passionate about MATLAB, I learned more from my labs tbh.
The class isn't very hard. For the projects do them early for free points. For the tests just do the practice problems and you will be fine.
Excellent professor for Senior Design.

Pre-class lectures = comprehension questions, goes over material again in lecture w/ more explanation and practice. I barely knew coding going it, but even if I didn't I would've been fine. Labs have 5-6 problems, TAs are great, good test prep, and I left in 1-2 hours. Lots of extra test practice. Projects are easy w/ early submission extra credit

The lectures are genuinely useless since all of the material is recorded online and mandatory to watch the night before, but attendance is mandatory. The labs are well done but time-consuming and at annoying time slots. The class is a good intro to coding and not overly difficult. Just find something to keep yourself busy during the lectures.

I did not like Dr. B or this class very much. It has a lot to it, and requires a good amount of time and effort. The lectures are pretty useless - the most useful resources were the TopHat videos (recorded lectures) and projects, whereas the labs and graders felt tough and easy to neglect. Keep track of deadlines, make friends. You can do it!

I had her for "Well-Being Strategies for College and Life". I personally learned a lot, and if you take the assignments seriously, you will definitely find something that sticks with you. Dr. Battestilli clearly cares a lot about her students and has done lots of research to create this course as a great intro to practical strategies for wellbeing.

Good professor. She cares about making the class perfect. The tests allow you to use the MatLab grader to do it which allows for the tests to actually test your knowledge. The lectures aren't super helpful, but you should still go. The lab portion is honestly perfectly designed. Overall a good class and professor.

I appreciate how Dr. B gives real-world advice to her students. She may not be the most personable, hundreds of students are being funneled through her class, but she leaves little easter eggs of wisdom which I think are nice and speak to how she does care about her students. She tells students to believe in themselves, and that's key.

The lectures are futile, frankly. One time she took a poll to see if the students wanted to do "breakout rooms" on zoom, it was a unanimous no. She sits there.. "hmmm I don't know I think I kind of like break-out rooms" ? We all just said no? Makes you wonder if she takes into account the substance in the hundreds of surveys she pushes.

The class followed a flipped classroom style, so lectures were just three hours of examples.  Lectures were very difficult to get through, but the content wasn't too difficult to learn with some effort.  The labs were very engaging, and the projects never took too long to complete.

Reverse classroom, 2 hour lecture, and 3 hour lab for a 3 credit class is absolutely brutal. Lectures felt useless because you learned everything prior, but there were some good examples. 3 projects, 3-5 weekly homework problems, 2 hours reverse classroom, 3 exams, no final. Lot's of time needed for this class but it's easy and enjoyable

The class is a reverse classroom, where you learn the material outside the course with a few practice problems and then during lectures, she would review the material and dive deeper into practice problems. Lectures were boring though. 3 projects, pretty easy and fun. If needed, she would explain concepts differently to get students to understand.

I hated coding before this class but it was my favorite to take; she really caters her teaching style to what is best for the students. She uses a flipped classroom which I initially hated but the way she does it is so helpful, I rarely struggled and when I did both she and all the TAs were extremely helpful. Love Dr. B!

Labs and projects are great. The weekly lectures are a snooze-fest and felt like a waste of time since the TopHat questions are so basic, and she asks for questions for 5 minutes after everyone understood the code. The class itself is very easy. If you've coded at all before, MATLAB has a rather frictionless transition into grasping its syntax.

Her lectures are insanely boring and almost completely unnecessary since she makes you learn everything outside of class anyway. She really only goes over examples in class and doesn't actually really teach anything. I'd say this class is heavily self taught, just zoom the lectures and go to lab. Do the work and you'll be fine.

This is one of the only sections that requires you to buy the $100 textbook for your grade. If you're shooting for an A+, you need to buy the textbook. Getting an A without the textbook is doable, but I strongly recommend finding a different section.
Very useless class. Very easy though. Nothing against the professor that much, she and Dr. Adams were occasionally funny. But just work on other assignments during the lectures.

This class was really good. And you will learn a lot about DSA that is directly relevant to LeetCode problem-solving. He provides generous grading and curving. Best of all, he teaches really well, and if you follow the class (no mandatory attendance policy), you should be able to get an A grade easily.

Extremely high-quality class and one of the best professors at NCSU. The tests make up most of the grade and they are definitely not easy but with curving and generous grading its more than fair.  Take thorough notes, especially when he steps through an algo in class and be familiar with algebra and simplifying terms like 2^log_2(n)

The professor is very passionate about the subject, and extremely clear about the grading, homework, quizes and final exam. It's an interesting and scoring subject if you study regularly. The professor even gives mock exam papers with solutions before mid term and final exams, so the students can prepare and have an idea on what to expect in exam.

Prof Heber is really passionate about the subject which can be seen through his enthusiasm and teaching style. Would definitely recommend taking CSC 505 under him in the Fall semester (some other prof teaches it in the Spring semester).

He Included a lot of mathematics in the course that was kinda unnecessary but overall really helped clear some of the basic concepts for CSC505 and liked his teaching style, also liked the fact that attendance was not mandatory and I could just watch the recordings.

Great lectures. Study throughout the semester and pay attention to quizzes and assignments. Exams are easy. Professor loves this subject and can be seen by the way he delivers it. Worth attending lectures!

Very good lecturer, but the homework assignments are just the worst. Be prepared to write 10-20 pages of proofs and explanations on multiple algorithms for each assignment. Tests are also very difficult and have so much you need to review but he curves generously and gave a 5% flat curve at the end of the semester as well.

One of the best instructors I've had. Lectures are very easy to follow and provides nice visualizations of algorithms. The lecture content is quite abstract, but Dr. Heber presents it in such a way that it is very easy to grasp. Course could be improved through more ungraded problem sets, but would recommend to anyone. Exams are not difficult.
great professor he put  a lot of effor on the slide.

we have question so we went up to him after class,he pack his stuff, after that he said follow him, we following him all the way to the next class and he just gave start putting his stuff and giving lecture? How hard to just f**k said I don't have time so we don't have to follow you all the way to another building and sav our time?

The professor works hard to make lessons easy to understand. Tests are quite simple and follow examples given by the teacher. Grades are curved at the end of the semester. I really liked how the teacher taught, even though it focused more on theory than solving problems.

Terrible.More like a math class rather than one centered around algorithms. The grading system is quite stringent, with graders focused only on deducting points. Abundance of homework and quizzes with very little contribution to the total grade. Midterms and finals, coupled with the limited time provided for comprehensive question-solving.

This professor makes algorithms a frustrating experience with excessive testing, tough exams, and memory-based assessments. Consider taking the course with a different professor for a better learning experience.Students score well by solving previous year papers and not from what he teaches in the lecture. Disappointed.

Prof Heber offers very thorough lectures that are useful for anyone entering algorithms with any prior skill level. If you truly pay attention to what he is teaching, you will have a good time in this course. He offers generously graded quizzes for practice problems and makes sure you are given all the information you need before a test. 10/10

The course includes group projects and homework requiring consistent effort. Grading policies are strict, including penalties for unsuccessful regrade requests. Lecture style may not be engaging for all students

Her strict "no partial credit" policy is frustrating - she probably thinks wrong answers mean you don't understand, but I was swamped with other coursework, even making presentations the night before exams with little sleep. While generally decent, this harsh grading dropped my letter grade penalizing me juggling multiple commitments.

Dr. Chi is a kind person and good lecturer, but I cannot emphasize enough how terrible the TAs are. Regardless of how many times a question is asked, the TAs reply: "find it in the lectures somewhere," even if the question cannot be answered by the lectures. This would be a great class if the TAs would bother providing the slightest bit of help.

Professor is very knowledgeable, but a tough grader. This is not the hardest class I took in my Masters, but it is the lowest grade I've gotten. TA's fairly useless, telling people to "check the lecture" on questions where people confirmed they already checked. Grading is all-or-nothing. One rounding error I made in a homework lost me 30 points.

Dr. Chi's class is entirely group oriented, except, conveniently, the exams. All your grades, apart from exams, will be shared with your group despite supposedly half the presentation being graded on how well you presented as an individual. Professor is also profoundly lazy when it comes to grading, specifically pertaining to how she grades.
wonderful lectures, amazing graders, would definitely take again!

One of the hardest but most rewarding classes I've taken. This class is a LOT of work but she teaches all the content very well and you'll definitely come out of it with a better understanding of the subject. The midterm was a lot like the given practice exam and you can do homework in teams as well as have a few free late days which is very nice.

The lectures were a bit dull and basically repeated what was on the slides. However, the course layout and syllabus were well thought out. There's no partial credit given for homework or tests. The mid-term exam followed the same format as given provided by the professor. It would have been better if the teacher had made the lectures more engaging.

Dr. Chi is a good lecturer and does cover everything you need to know...however there is a major flaw. She (and the TAs) will NOT answer your questions, they will answer the same thing to every question --> "It's in the lecture videos, not sure which one, but find it". That is not helpful

Hate is a strong word, and as a child of God, I really try not to use it toward anyone, but this woman tested every bit of that restraint. She is completely disorganized and barely teaches. This class was an absolute waste of a semester and a total waste of my time.

Many students take Prof. Kemafor's class only to fulfill credit requirements, not because she's a  great professor. She lacks teaching skills and professionalism. I even heard she once asked a student for a picture of her medicine bottle and purchase receipt, even though she already provided a work note. This is privacy violation! Such a shame.

Worst professor. Always unprepared, unresponsive, and doesn't seem to care about her students. Instead of focusing on teaching well and making the course enjoyable and rewarding, she's more concerned with questioning students integrity. She even scans students' exam paper to compare what they wrote before and after restroom break during exam.

Class consisted of 10 hws, 3 tests and a final. Given an online book and lectures given from 2+ years ago. Tests are all written response. Not a terribly hard class but given so little material, resources, and grading criteria. It makes it 2x to 3x harder and more time consuming than a normal discrete class. Doable if you put in the time and effort

Very little learning material is provided.  Don't expect any ideas to be explained well. You will lose (many) points on assignments for unspecified requirements. If you ask a question, expect ridiculous non-answers. It doesn't matter how reasonable or polite you are, his return communication is always rude, weird, and immature.

Save yourself the struggle and wait until the Fall. I just lost 60% of the last HW grade because I formatted my program wrong (it worked fine). Not the hardest class I've ever taken, but definitely the one where I've had the worst grades.

The first homework had incorrect references to the textbook and asked questions about things we would not cover until after the second test, so I knew this class would be bad. Prepare for prolific typos in official communication, blatant coding errors in assignments, and a refusal to explain questionable test and HW grading. Rubric has secret reqs.

Single worst professor I have been unfortunate enough to encounter here. His lectures are meandering and poor, he mostly just reads the slides—except for when he goes on lengthy and irrelevant tangents. Grading is ridiculous, the entire class has lost points for hidden requirements on HW assignments and tests, and he refused to regrade or explain.

He gives very little effort even for an online class. Homework is long and basically busy work. No clear grading outline/feedback for homework and tests. I learned from the textbook and did his examples as practice for the tests. He explains easy concepts poorly. This class is definitely easier during the semester with another professor.
Terrible professor, borderline hostile to questions. Will ruin your summer

It is very hard to do well in a class when the instructions and grading criteria are not clear. Especially for tests, the instructions in the questions are not clear, so get ready to lose a lot of points even if you get the answers correct.
This test questions are super vague and then he grades them WAY too hard.

Dr. Tim is very kind and made a strong effort to make the course accessible for students. He provided multiple opportunities for extra credit and was quite accommodating. Lectures could feel somewhat disorganized at times, likely due to ongoing course restructuring. Overall, it was a relaxed course with manageable deadlines and workload.

Definitely one of the more knowledgable professors at NC State. The lectures are a bit erratic, but if you listen to what he says you can learn a lot. Most of his lectures regard his experiences during industry. Most bad reviews on this site come from very lazy students who never went to class to begin with.

Prereq for 515, 519, 710, and 712, but I can't recommend it unless absolutely necessary. Lectures were rambling and unstructured—I stopped attending after week 4. Heavy, poorly organized group work. Not very hard, but tedious and frustrating. Redundant if you had a serious undergraduate software engineering course. One midterm - optional final.

His teaching is poor. Lectures are chaotic; attendance alone won't help with exams. Heavy workload: weekly assignments first half, then lit review. Extremely strict grading; final paper needs near-publication quality. Requires in-person group meetings and discusses grades only face-to-face. Hinted at curve before finals but never followed through.

I took ASE under him. He doesn't know how to teach, and is very much full of himself.  
He cites himself, jumps from one concept to another. Doesn't teach but mentions new concepts as if we should know them. Neither are his notes any useful. 
Never take his class unless you know what he is teaching and are only doing it for the grade.

You really wouldn't learn anything from this course. He does absolutely nothing in class nothing useful in class. Take this class if you just want a high grade. But if you do not do somethings specified in the rubric sheet (which are basically a lot of things), you will definitely lose marks. Your grade depends on who your TA is for grading.

he is a nice guy? He asks the whole class to bring their poster at their cost(even seiner design classes don't), so how do 300 students is going to stare at the tiny poster in the class? He says he talk randomly or just reads the page, always no saying the whole sentence, can't understand what he talking about sometime.

He is a nice guy but he is bad at teaching, organiz the class, material sometimes missing, he is not forcus on the class, always jumping around the concept, the material is no been update since 2018, he will randomly talking about stuff, you are no going to learning any technical stuff, u learn how to make repo pretty and concept,

Class he taught did not match the description at all, was more of a Data Mining class. It was a class of 100, he taught so horribly and singled out students for no reason. Was graded mostly by homeworks, which he gave us lua files and output and asked us to convert to another language... I got a perfect score but didn't learn

His teaching style involves talking about his experience in the industry. You never feel you are being lectured. You grasp the concept. He provides you with material from each class and kind of questions he might ask from midterm or final perspective. His goal seems to make one learn rather than fail someone. I wish there were more prof like him.

This is less a warning about Menzies and more about CSC510: don't take it! It is not worth it. You can get a better software engineer learning experience from an internship, this class is only for those with loads of free time who like doing work they'll be doing for the rest of their lives for free w/ no superior support like a real job would give

Perfectly fine lecturer, does things flipped so classes are mostly just time to work on stuff, and you watch lecture videos at home. He's a very very nice and fun guy, knows what he's talking about. If you like coding and are interested in games, this class is amazing. Projects are tricky but fun and satisfying. Expectations are clear.
Good course and professor.
The class is not heavy, but u need to learn some stuff yourself, but he is a really nice guy and willing to help student, I love this guy, projects are super fun 2

Don't expect to learn new things from lectures. The programming assignments are nicely set up and not too difficult. It would've been better if the lecturer actually taught something in class. The grading is also pretty lenient.

Dr. Watson's class may feel a bit unorganized at times but I found the work he assigns to be reasonable and fullfilling and the material overall is presented well. He is a very caring professor and gives plenty of oppotunity to go above and beyond or earn extra credit.

Dr. Price is one of the best professors I've had at NCSU. This is one of the best courses I've taken. Lectures are detailed and well-organized.

The guided projects with milestones made learning ML really smooth. Practice problems on Tophat and homework -  helpful to grasp the theory. He's also very considerate. Wish I could give more than 5 stars!
The class was pretty easy, the way he graded things was great, it was very lenient, and with tons of extra credit and easy-to-follow instructions for labs. I highly recommend taking it

Really enjoyed this class, convinced me to minor in Compsci! Dr Price is so nice and so obviously cares about this topic! He uses a flipped classroom model which I really enjoy. Most work is with a partner so be ready for that. The final project was a bit harder then I think it should've been and I had some grade issues with TAs but no other issues

As someone who is helpless with technology I was scared to take this class but Dr. Price was great. Every class period him and the TA's would walk around and help us with any questions. There are 2 big partner projects that make up the midterm and final, also 4 quizzes dispersed throughout that he will warn you about.

Classroom environment doesn't feel welcoming for questions/confusion -- responses come across as dismissive. Exam solutions aren't provided and grading criteria is super unclear. I put significant effort into this course just to receive some of the harshest grades of my college career, which felt disproportionate to the work I put in.

Difficult to make an A in this class, but very well-structured course and Dr. Chirkova is a great professor. Strict and old-school teaching style which made the course clear and easy to follow. You will definitely learn a lot. Zero tolerance for dishonest students unlike others profs, which I appreciated.

A solid teacher & I liked the class, but it felt as though you were given a bunch of information every week with little in the way to apply it; just partially through big projects & discussion papers. Then the exams don't quite test what you spend so much time learning and studying. That and it takes a long time to hear back on grades.
The teaching is great also reasonable HW, I learn a lot in the class

Wonderful professor! He's very clear about what's expected on tests and homework assignments and gives you ample time to do them. He's super engaging during class and makes difficult networking concepts easy to understand. Would take again in a heartbeat!

One of the better professors I've had. I'm not very interested in security but he did a great job keeping the lectures interesting, and it's not too much work outside of class. Always very transparent about whats expected on tests, and will go over homework/questions in class the lecture before the test. Very conceptual class, no big projects.

Great lectures, very concerned with making sure students understand the material. Tests weren't easy but weren't unfair, he not only has a review day before the test, he reviews the test after its been graded and its accepting of regrades. HomeWorks were involved but involved either material to prepare you for the test or practical applications.

Software Security is a really fun class if you're interested in cybersecurity. Dr. Williams does a great job of making sure everyone understands the concepts, and the workshops/projects are very interesting. Its a great introductory way to learn about cybersecurity, especially if you don't have too much background knowledge.

Someone said this class teaches practical skills - I disagree, the course focuses a lot on how to test and use tools and databases, but it doesn't go into actually resolving security issues at all.  As a software engineer you will mostly focus on resolution.  Finding is trivial - a security team or static analysis tool will be responsible for this.

Painfully tedious and time-consuming projects, basically spending entire semester analyzing a codebase for vulnerabilities which has potential but it's very repetitive and time consuming.  It would be much better if the requirements were more reasonable, and the work could be divided so that everyone learned something, but it's just too much.

She isn't that bad. She's pretty nice, and her lectures are decent, but her exams have ambiguous or trick questions, and the instructions for the projects are either outdated or need external sources to help keep up. I don't recommend taking her since she isn't clear on some instructions. You learn practical skills at least for cybersec

Very boring lectures last only about 30 minutes and is primarily group projects and discussions.  Very disorganized and vague projects and exams, for example an exam question might be: list 3 attributes about X only for points to be marked off for not explaining or going into details.  Generally unresponsive and doesn't read or answer questions.

CSC 515 was bad
1) Often unclear or incorrect instructions
2) Tough grader, class midterm avg was like 77. Answer isn't an identical match to answer key? You lose points
3) Doesn't respond to simple questions or show up to office hours
4) No guidance on exams, no learning objections, no recommendations, sample midterms useless 
5) TAs unhelpful

One of the few instances where a flipped class was beneficial. Great at answering questions comprehensively and is extremely open about how the class operates. The class felt like a disproportionately high amount of work at first, but it smoothed out over the course of the semester.

Knowledgeable professor who gave fairly interesting lectures and improved my knowledge of the subject. Ill-equipped to help with homework, stripped from a previous year's student's assignment submissions. Office hours completely useless. Interesting but challenging course project - if you can DIY, the course will be worth it despite the challenges.

Lectures were pretty monotonous and all over the place but the course itself required minimal work. A few homework assignments (coding/writing) and a group project. Very little guidance or help when it came to the group project (LLVM) which is notoriously difficult and undocumented so beware of that. Didn't get a lot out of this course.

The course was made very difficult not because of the syllabus but because of the inadequate information provided. The lectures were also pretty boring with little to no interaction between the professor and students. I hope I still had an option to drop the course but sadly there isn't.

The HWs and Proj are hard but they are graded very generously. Do HWs and review solutions for HWs, and then you won't have any problems with the one midterm(No final exam). Lack of instructions for the project(LLVM setup). Collaboration between students for the project. Dr. Shen cared about how to make the course more comfortable for students.

Very good class, but there is a lot of information to cover before tests (hundreds of slides' worth of material). Grading tends to benefit the student, and the projects are challenging yet very interesting.

Dr. Singh is a very experienced and distinguished professor. His lectures, though, are very dry. He prints out the powerpoint slides and marks them up on the doc cam. The topics (for 455/555 at least) are frequently very dry. There is a relationship between the topic and computer science, but Dr. Singh does not attempt to highlight these.

Overall enjoyed this class. The lecture topics seemed to be a bit far apart from each other but I guess that's just how the course is structured. There are short word limits for written assignments and a few interesting coding assignments. He does ask lots of questions and calls on people so some may not enjoy that.
DO NOT TAKE HIS CSC520

He is a very good professor. Communicates and teaches well, has a lot of knowledge in this field. But the first assignment was really bad, he could've asked us to do the same thing with a better network simulation tool or could've just given some other useful assignment. The exams have questions about stuff not really taught or solved in class.
His mental status is not good.

I will never take his class.
His pronunciation was really bad, and even his speech rate was so fast.
Also, he never checks the course website or his e-mail.
Not only that, he always starts his class late, and end it early. The original time for a class is 75 min, but I think his average lecture time is 60 mins.

I am paying for an education, not to be told, "This homework is 25% of your grade. Good luck." Class content is important, but you might as well watch YouTube videos if THIS is the instruction. Take anyone else's class.

Very knowledgeable professor, but a bit hard to access outside of class. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I HEAVILY recommend going each day. Lots of students didn't show up and then suffered greatly for it. "Homeworks" are very hard if you don't have a background in security already--I spent >30 hours on each. It is possible to do well though.

I absolutely adore Professor Alex! He is good-natured, funny, and extremely talented in the field of computer security. Three "homeworks" (really projects) for 25%, and participation in HackPack CTF at the end of the semester for 25% make up your grade. Start early, ask for help, and it's an easy A!

Other reviews are too harsh. There are no midterms, and the final is an open-note cybersecurity competition, making it very low-pressure. The course also teaches a lot of skills not covered in other classes. While the homework is time-consuming, it's the only graded component, and putting in the effort virtually guarantees an A.
Dr. Kuttal is a great professor! She is also very nice and truly cares about her students' success. I personally really enjoyed her class and would definitely recommend.

Dr. Kuttal is knowledgeable, and the other reviews that harp on her behavior in class are not fair, as the class did in fact, have behavioral problems that interfered with her ability to teach. The class is mainly based on a group project, so choose carefully. The tests were not that bad if you attended class and read over the powerpoints.

Kuttal is fine. Her lectures were a bit mundane. The class usually did not have exams, but this was the first semester where they implemented them, which really sucked. Overall I would not take the class again. The grading criteria for the assignments was nonexistent so you were pretty much in the dark about what to do or how they were grading it.

The instructor has been annoyed with anyone. The instructor spends too much time. The instructor goes around the classroom to check what people are doing and 
scolds people for talking or smiling in class. The irony is that the instructor points out that the 
class is too quiet, yet she does not want people to talk.

This review is for Programmer Centered Design/Research. It was a nice class, focused on reading and understanding major research papers in the field especially considering Human-Computer Interaction, and UI/UX design. One semester project focused on interface design and user study - it will really help you understand how to conduct such studies.

The course was an interesting overview of HCI, focused primarily on completing one large group project. Dr. Kuttal gave interesting lectures and I overall found the course good, though there were times where there was some ambiguity on how to fulfill the requirements of the assignment/project milestone. I do recommend her and this class, though.

Software product management was a great class that taught me more about user facing jobs related to software and what they look like. Work was mainly listening to podcasts from industry leaders and completing two group projects focused on evaluating and improving software products. No coding. Dr. Stolee is a caring teacher and well liked.

IDK why people are saying she was a bad lecturer, imo she's one of the best in the dept. I found her consistently engaging & I learned a lot. Also v understanding, if you show some effort & reach out she'll generally be quite helpful.  She makes sure her classes aren't artificially hard even if they're naturally hard. I took 492 & 408 with her too.

Dr. Stolee is not a bad option for Software Engineering as most of the learning is done in the lab section or group projects. That being said, she is not an engaging lecturer and often confuses/contradicts herself in class. Clear answers to questions are few and far between and the quality of teaching feels monotonous. The grading is clear and fair

Extremely disappointed with the performance of Kathryn Stolee. Her teaching was disorganized, lacking clarity, and left me feeling confused throughout the course. Moreover, her grading seemed arbitrary and inconsistent, making it difficult to gauge my progress or understand the basis for my grades.

Easy and amazing prof. No tests all just hw, which are very comprehensive but doable and he gives a lot of time to complete them. Also gives extensions for anyone who needs it. Lectures are a little boring for students who aren't very interested in the content but describes the content very well. Highly recommend taking this professor.

If you're looking for an easy class, this isn't it. 40% of your grade is four homework assignments, each taking about a week. The other 60% is two closed-note midterms and a closed-note final. Unless you really enjoy networking theory and the lower OSI layers, consider another professor or wait for an easier section.

This is a theory-heavy system class that has no programming assignments. There are four homework assignments each worth 10%, two midterms (15% each) and a final (30%).  Wouldn't recommend you take this course with this teacher unless you have to, there are better courses. teacher isn't great.

He includes a lot of unnecessarily convoluted explanations to things that could be a lot more simple. Goes back and forth quite a bit and can be difficult to follow. I think he gets impatient with students who are not catching on and can sometimes end up leaving them behind
He's pretty good

Dr. Guo is one of those rare cases of a professor who is not only extremely knowledgeable in his field, but is also incredibly adept at actually conveying that knowledge to students. I have never seen someone sum up the intuition behind otherwise dense and complex concepts as quickly and concisely as he does.

Incredible lecturer, v knowledgeable about the field and explains it in a very clear & in-depth way. Balanced levels of work. V disorganized tho, messed up two exams of three. Not always v empathetic. Generally p good and its an easy enough class, not much to say.

He's a kind guy, knows his stuff, receptive out of class, asks when we want things due. But, not a great lecturer. Assignments often have confusing ambiguities, or questions that ask you to do things and the correct answer is "that's not possible", which is lame & frustrating. Graded by few things, but not graded too harsh. Cool material, though.

Not bad but not great. Most of the hate she gets is undeserved. Lectures are pretty clear and easy to understand, and she takes questions and answers them pretty well. Homework is pretty light, it's just a 10-20 minute video to watch before each lecture as well as a couple hw questions after most lectures. Final exam can replace midterm grades.
I wouldn't wear a seatbelt on the way to her class.

Dr. Schmidt is a good person and does care about her students. However, the flipped classroom approach is not for everyone and the labs and project deadlines can overwhelm you if you're not careful with your time management. Also, this class is very test heavy, but the final exam replacement policy helps a lot.

I did not like this professor for 116, but honestly she's pretty good for 226. I mean discrete's not easy and it's overwhelming at the start, but honestly the harsh ratings are strange. She lectured clearly, the exams were not super easy, this class is fine, not easy, but overall decently fair. I used a lot of office hours, so I put the work in.

RUN!! do not take this class with Schmidt like your life depends on it. Genuinely one of the worst professors ever. Lectures are mundane and a waste of time, homework's don't really match the exams, and she is barely accessible outside of class. Her passive aggressiveness is frustrating, and exams are unnecessarily hard and difficult to prepare for

Horrible professor. HW and labs are easy but tedious, don't lose points. Has a passion for teaching but not a great person. Attendance is helpful, the problems in class are similar to the tests. Tests are mostly hard, the MCQ can be tricky, and small errors can lead to points off in FRQ's. Try to take Card. Doesn't record lectures, study a lot.

Idk why everyone's giving bad reviews about Dr. Schmidt, she is actually not that bad. Her lectures are great, HW is not really difficult and the midterms are easy. Even though the labs are difficult and very long, you can get a 100% if you complete them. The final was kind of difficult, but she's definitely better than the other professor though.

Mentioned so many times during the semester about the final exam replacement policy, and then proceeds to make the final exam super difficult by adding some difficult proofs worth lots of points. If you can avoid taking her class, do it, but options are limited. Anyways, good riddance.

Class structure 4
Explanations 2
Attendance policy 1
Labs 4 (2 long labs but you get 100% if you complete them).
Generous final exam replacement policy 5
Final exam difficulty 2 (some way too difficult problems there).
Zybooks is a waste of money and time. You do not need it.
Overall rating 3. 
Just glad to be done with this. Good luck!

She misleadingly suggests that attendance is graded and required, even though it is neither. Her consistently passive aggressive communication, combined with a flipped classroom approach, makes the class far more challenging than it should be. Both the lectures and the videos offer very little value. If you can avoid her, you should.

Utilizes a flipped classroom. Lecture videos are unclear and confusing, while also not being comprehensive. The homework itself is not terrible, however inputting answers and the useability of WebWork is sometimes rough. The Labs however are truly the worse assignments I have ever experienced. Genuinely made me reconsider all my life choices.

The mirrored class structure feels like an uphill battle; attendance mandatory yet feels useless about 80% of the time if you don't understand the videos. If they absolutely insist on enforcing "practice" on students through practice problem examples, why not hold problem sessions like lots of other classes do in addition to a lecture session?

Attendance is "mandatory" in the sense that if you skip too much she sends you a strongly worded email, which is good cuz lectures are a waste of time. She just dully does problems with unhelpful explanations. Zybooks isn't required anymore but all the actual learning is done with pre-class videos. She gives bad vibes in a way that's hard to place.

Sat in the front during exam 1, pulled out a 4-function calculator after mishearing her instructions. I begged her to just fail the exam, but she decided to fail me for the entire class in my final semester of my senior year. I needed a job for health insurance this spring, and now need to stay in school another semester.

Flipped classroom, so the lectures are basically useless (just practice problems). The lecture videos and ZyBooks participation activities are completely redundant, and half of the (required) topics in the online textbook were not assessed on the tests or homework at all. RUNNNNN! if you have the option to not take her, don't. Literally so petty, strict, and passive aggressive for no reason. "Good morning let's try that again, good morning!" are words that haunt me. The deadline situation is sometimes crazy with exams and projects, especially the final project had me crying. Dr. Schmidt is by far one of the worst professors I've taken at NCSU. Yes, she is knowledgeable and her lectures are decent. Hard tests, no lecture recordings, and lots of homework. If you want to be miserable for a semester then this is the class for you. On a personal level I don't think Schmidt is too bad, but it seems like she enjoys making the class as difficult as possible.

Not great, not terrible. Mostly terrible though.

Mean, petty, and strict for no reason. Makes your life miserable. Enjoys failing students for fun! Dr. Schmidt is a nice person, but not a great professor.  She doesn't upload recorded lectures, so unless you go to all lectures, good luck teaching yourself these tough subjects. I liked Dr. Schmidt contrary to most people. She wasn't exceptional or anything, but she taught me what she needed to without going too fast or being unclear. Does upload slides but does not upload them with her teaching on them so they're basically useless blank slides. "Records" her lectures but does not even upload them. Should I go on? I think you get the point. She's incompetent and doesn't put any effort.
