Easily the most time consuming class in the ECE department. You will learn a ton and struggle a ton but he is very helpful for working through issues. My biggest complaint is the class is pure chaos.

Carlson is the goat. You'll do fine on the tests if you go to/watch lecture, he basically tells you what's gonna be on the test. There are 10 projects and they start off simple, but be ready to spend your semester in the lab as the class ramps up. Easily the most time consuming class I've had at state, but it was also the most rewarding.
Best professor in ECE.

350 characters is not enough to explain how great Carlson is. This has been by far my favorite ECE class at NC State. You will learn so much, and genuinely have fun the whole time. Carlson is available virtually around the clock. Definitely the most passionate professor I have had. It's a lot of work, but not actually too hard, just time consuming

Carlson is extremely straightforward and knows what he is talking about. 306 is a rough class because of the amount of work. If you put in the time and get the work done as early as possible you will be fine. By far my favorite ECE class and Professor I have taken.

This will be one of the hardest classes you will take at State. It will also be one of the most rewarding. I feel like I learned more in one semester with Carlson than I did in several years with other professors. He loves talking with students and is always accessible outside class.

Absolute legend. The class is very time consuming and very stress inducing. Nothing is too hard (until you get a little later into the semester) but you always have to keep up with your work. Honestly your experience is almost completely dependent on your TAs because mine carried me so hard in the lab. Making the car is sick.

Dr. C is a great explainer, I was able to understand almost everything being covered in the class just by attending lecture. If anyone is planning on taking ECE 109, I would recommend checking out the puzzle game Turing Complete, as the content covered in this class is VERY similar.
Amazing professor, not only is he a great lecturer, but he cares a lot about the students and goes through a lot of efforts to make sure that we succeed.

Dr.C is the GOAT. He's by far one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are interesting and he does a good job at explaining complex topics and breaking them down. There are big 3 projects and weekly labs with mandatory lab reports. It's a time consuming class but not hard and he's always willing to work with students and have office hours.

Dare I say he rivals Bob Evans GOAT status? The best prof Ive had here in ECE. Lots of opportunity to succeed (like extra credit). He does give a lot of work out but generally it isnt too bad. You learn a lot from this course. Grading rubric is clear and it is quite easy to get a good grade in this class as long as you try.

Dr. C is easily one of the best professors for ECE. I wish I had him for 109. Probably the most understanding and kind professor I've had. He is very accommodating; he's always willing to extend deadlines if you need them. He gives an absurd amount of extra credit throughout the semester. This class is a lot of work, but it is not hard to do well.
Great professor. Second half of the class is a bit harder, but he's very open and helpful. Definitely recommend taking him for 109.

Genuinely best ECE professor at state, very easy going, as long as you email him he will give you extensions. Gives out tons of extra credit. Explains material really well, gives good feedback and has always helps in explaining things. Only one midterm and one final, both are decently easy and he's a very nice grader. Lots of partial credit.

Dr. C is an excellent professor! While I don't intend to major in computer engineering, his ECE 109 was quite fun despite having to write code in an Assembly language. He is incredibly passionate about computer engineering and explains concepts concisely. If you have the chance to take a class with him, take it!

He honestly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. If you show that you are trying and actually engage in your studies. He will help you with whatever you need. The exams are easy. No tricky questions just straight up from HW, Reviews, and practice test he gives. You understand those you'll A's his class. You must put in time to study.

Nothing but respect for Dr. Cutitaru! Very transparent about expectations and grading criteria.  

Downside: his lectures are sometimes not the clearest, and he doesn't use a textbook, meaning if there is a challenging topic you have to research it on your own (not really that hard though).

Get ready for a lot of work in ECE310, but a fun class!

Great Class! There is a decent amount of work, but you learn a lot in this class, and the grading is very fair if you do your work. Dr. C is also very knowledgeable and is easily accessible outside of class.

Cutitaru is by far my favorite professor I have had so far at state. He is a fantastic lecturer and makes the class very engaging. The exams effectively cover the content and are a perfect level of difficultly. He provides plenty of practice questions and the LC3 programs are actually pretty fun. 100000% TAKE CUTITARU FOR 109! :)
Goated professor
The goat of NCSU ECE. If you have to take a class, and he's a professor, take him.

A really interesting guy, but very intent on making the class simple and fun. Very engaging with class and really cares. Lots of projects and the projects aren't easy, especially the reports, but overall a great class with a great instructor
It was a rocky start for me, but I came to realize how leinient and understanding the professor is. He is also very FAIR!
Dr. C is a great professor, and you know he wants to see you succeed. He always made himself available for questions or concerns. So far differently one of my favorite professors at NCSU.

Very passionate and fair professor. Does his best to help each student learn. I took it over the summer, so I got more 1 on 1 time so if its during the fall u gotta reach out first ( especially with coding ). Two tests, two coding assignments (not bad), final was fair. Learned a lot and was not stressed at all. Would recc. Does not round!

Dr. C was great! He tended to go through material pretty fast, but was always open to explaining more. The second half requires a lot more time for the programs, so be sure to start the programs as early as possible!!
Had him for 109 last semester and it was great! Already in 212 this summer and hoping it's just as good.

Didn't take his class but many at Lehigh University know about his Title 9 violations. So please be careful ladies and talk to people who have taken his class.

Use your discretion & please proceed with caution half of these good reviews could be from him.

I loved having him! He was great with deadlines and he gave really good feedback. He understood that this is an introductory class and explained very well. He does go fast so do not fall behind and you will be just fine. The second half of the class is harder so take your time on the programs.

Dr. C is a wonderful professor, but he does go through material very fast. Don't fall behind and you'll be fine. It's very difficult to find practice problems for 109, though. Most of the examples posted on Moodle are filled with mistakes. Dr. C often goes over things in class that directly conflict with the textbook. Ask for clarification.

Very solid professor. I recommend going to his lectures, as you can't speed up the online recordings because he is just that fast. Most of the class is projects, which can take time. The homework was meh, and the labs were a good way to learn. He is very caring and allows a lot of flexibility. Constantly pushed back due dates. Much better than 212.

Dr. C knows his stuff and can answer any question you have. The 2nd half of the class itself is difficult, but he does a solid job teaching the tough material. His lectures are also very worth it. Take his class if you can.

Great professor, especially compared to past profs for this course. If you need to take 109, he's your guy. Beginning of the semester he moves fast, but slows down towards the end. He explains things well and tries his best to make himself available to students who need help. My only complaint is that he doesn't work through many examples in class.

He has very clear lectures and cares for his students. He reminds people of due dates and accommodates for different problems. It seems like he wants his students to pass the class. He gives lots of partial credit if you put work on tests.

Although lectures were recorded, I attended the 8:30 am section anyway, because his lectures are awesome. He is very communicative in and outside of class. The homeworks are very easy, but are still great study tools. Tests are appropriately difficult, and the three programs are not mindless slogs. I would totally take Dr. Cutitaru again.

Dr.C is the best professor that I had. He genuinely cares about the students' success. He always offers extra office hours to help with the programs, he would literally host office hours till 8:00 pm so he can help as many students as he can. Definitely take his class if you can.

Loved Dr. C's class! Lectures are recorded and he clearly cares about his students! Makes time to explain difficult concepts in an easy to understand way. The class was hard, but there are curves for the places students struggled the most.

Dr C. is a great professor. He makes the content quite easy to understand and is always willing to explain concepts covered in a previous class again. My one minor complaint would be that he should allow students to take the second test and then choose to void it if its not in your favor instead of the current system.

He was a great professor in ECE109, while his lectures could be a bit boring at times, he offered a lot of time outside of class to get help, whether it was through office hours or problem sessions. He also very clearly cares for the success of every student, and is willing to support them near deadlines.

Class was a little disorganized and tough at times, but Dr. C really cares about his students and is very accesible outside of class for help and gives many opportunities for extra credit. Lectures were good, except a little fast and unclear sometimes. Overall, Dr. C is a great guy and the class turned out to be enjoyable because of that.
Good professor. Lectures are kind of boring. Chill guy, very understanding. Class isn't that hard, just verilog.

Dr. C is very understanding of the student experience and is willing to work with students on deadlines. Homework isn't too bad, just a short assignment and lab every week. I really enjoyed his lectures and the material, but he can be fast and the class can feel a little disjointed at times. Only one midterm. Overall Dr. C is an incredible guy.

Professor Aysu is passionate and fair. He encourages AI use for HW/projects, but AI is not perfect, so you must understand the material, check its work, and correct mistakes. Exams are straightforward with few curveballs. Pay attention, learn the concepts, and the class is very doable.

Decent professor but design project sucks. No TA office hours the week of, doesn't provide support, they are extremely difficult to get right. Other professors teaching this course are a much better choice.

Easier than some 1 credit classes. He introduces a topic, then does practice problems. Mediocre handwriting isn't an issue since his slides are on Moodle. He gives a week for HW and often pushes deadlines back if the class has a heavy exam week. Highly recommend if you want a professor who works with your schedule. Encourages AI use to check HW.

I took Logic Design at another college and got an A-, here I am looking at a C.  During lecture his writing is very hard to read making it hard to follow after class looking at lecture notes. Also, homeworks are posted by random, projects appear abruptly, no exam schedule to go off of. No communication, only TAs. You will always feel unprepared.
Go to class and pay attention and you'll do great. Loved his teaching style and the exams were very similar to lecture content.

Very nice, and chill professor, definitely the better option for 212. If you're having trouble he will listen and help as much as he can (also if you ask for extensions for the projects he will probably say yes). Start the project early!!!  Grading does take a while, but they are usually easy graders. worst part is how much money you have to drop.
Dr. Aysu is a very passionate teacher and is clearly very knowledgeable. Take 212 with him if you get the chance.
Likes Elden Ring.

Professor Aysu is a GEM! He is a great teacher and is extremely understanding. He seems to really enjoy his job and his work and enjoys talking to students. He will extend projects and tests if the class asks him to which is awesome. He has been one of the best prof's I've had in ECE by far!

Dr Aysu is a very caring professor, the class was just very unorganized and many assignments were given to us with multiple errors in them. I also felt woefully unprepared for the design projects (which were both assigned at the two busiest/worst times of the semester) and wish the actual hardware aspect was covered more in class.

Dr. Aysu is the best professor I have ever had. His lectures are wonderful. Dr. Aysu is also very understanding. He gave us for Design Project 2. He understands the struggles of being a college student studying engineering. Dr. Aysu cares so much for each of his students and manages to teach us so much while upholding very reasonable expectations.
Had a dream he pushed the project/tests back, woke up it was real. 10/10

Amazing professor! Great lectures. Exams are straightforward if you do the homework's. Extremely helpful in office hours. Very respectful when speaking to students. Overall, highly recommend his class, he makes ECE enjoyable and allows undergrad to help with his research!!

I don't think it's possible to dislike Dr. Aysu, he is extremely caring of students and lenient. There are two exams which are similar to examples in class, and a take home final. There are also three (if time allows) design projects that are a little challenging so give yourself time on them.

Amazing professor. Very lenient and caring. Loves to crack jokes in class, making it that much more entertaining to attend. Only two tests and one take-home final. Two major projects which both take a while but were super fun so it didn't actually feel like a chore to do. Understands his students and how they are feeling during stressful times.

Dr. Aysu is one of the best professors I've had thus far in my two years at NC State. His lectures are enthusiastic and engaging. He is very accommodating and helpful, and shows a lot of care and respect towards his students.  The tests were not too bad as long as you paid attention to the lectures and did the coursework, and projects were fun.

Aysu is a great professor. He acknowledges his content is kinda repetitive and boring but does his best to make it interesting. eHW portion of the course was interesting and actually helped my knowledge of logic design. Only two exams the whole course which was really cool. Best professor I had this semester, wasn't really a great contest though.

Dr. Aysu is one of the best professors I have ever had. He has great informative as well as engaging lectures. He takes breaks in the middle and he has the highest attendance percentage of any class I have ever seen where attendance is not graded. Tests were fair and we were well prepared for them in the lectures. He is also flexible on due dates.

Great prof, keeps things fun and will give 2 min breaks in the middle of long lectures. Conveys concepts well and clearly, homeworks quite helpful to understand those concepts better, and tests are fine as long as you kind of pay attention to what is going on in class. The design projects were very fun for me.

Literally the best professor I've had at NC State. One of the few classes I've taken where I've wanted to go to lectures every time. He genuinely cares about students learning, and grading can be quite flexible. Take Aysu!

Dr. Becchi is a really great ECE prof. Yes she has an accent, but it doesn't impede on being able to understand topics. Her lectures are thorough and tests reflect what is covered in class and the homework. She is very knowledgeable and is always willing to re-explain stuff. The course is conceptually difficult, but she makes it easy to do well.

The operating systems class (now ece565) that Dr. Becchi teaches is probably the most important class i have taken here. In every single low level programming interview I've ever had, that information taught to you in that class has covered about 80% of them. Concepts of scheduling, mutexes, semaphores, and virtual memory are incredibly important

If you want to maintain a good gpa just don't take Becchi. Her accent was definetly tough to understand which sucks because you definetly should attend or watch the lectures to get a good understanding of the material. Tests dates are honestly really annoying and the tests themselves are much harder than Carlson.

Becchi is a really nice person but I would not at all recommend taking her class. I've had teachers with bad accents before, but I could barely understand her, and you definetly have to attend classes to get a good understanding of the material. Highly dont recommend, please take byrd or really anyone else.

I hate writing this review because Becchi is a pretty nice person, but her class is pretty terrible. Shes a good lecturer and you should definetly attend lectures, but programming assignments and exams are straight up unfair. No extra credit and schedules exams at the same times as other ece classes like 211 and 200.

First teacher with actual un-understandable accent. Have had Indian and Korean accents but they were understandable, she is not. This was my first experience in coding and I pretty much had to learn myself because her lectures are worthless. If you can take Carlson, or Byrd, do. I'm pretty convinced her 5 review from May 12 is fake because no way.

Great teacher for C. The course consisted of 4 tests, 3 projects, 6 labs, and weekly homework. For most students, the main challenge was the tests, but Becchi gave out LOTS of partial credit and MASSIVE flat curves, so getting an A+ isn't too difficult. Overall, if you came to college to learn, take it with Becchi; otherwise, take Carlson.
Exams and programming assignments are spaced very horribly, knowingly schedules them at the time of the ece 211 exams. Very harsh grader, if you can take someone other than Byrd or Becci, please do.

Make sure you attend class, the lectures are very important since Becci is very harsh with grading and has hard tests. Her accent is pretty thick, so I could never really understand her, but make sure you at least understand the lecture slides. start the programming assignments EARLY, she makes them due at very inconvenient times.

I have taken several programming classes before, and thought it would be safe for me to attempt to test out of 209. Dr. Becchi was extremely helpful throughout the entire process, working overtime in order to ensure that I was making the right decision and providing numerous extensions so that I could eventually gain credit for the class.

Becci has a thick accent so its pretty hard to understand her lectures. Make sure to do the programming assignments way before hand, she makes them due very inconveinetly, right before the test week. Also a very tough grader.

Dr. Becchi is one of the best microarchitecture lecturer I ever met. The course covers from basic 5 stages pipeline, w. scoreboard, tomasulo with reorder buffer to cache organization. It might be hard for students not familiar with computer organization but you will definitely learn a lot and be able to crack interviews. Hope this message helps

Thick accent. Lectures are fine once you get used to it. Homeworks are challenging, tests are more challenging, and projects are extreme. If you had Lakew for 209, you will struggle with the projects (35% of grade). She does changing the grading scale depending on how students perform, though.

OS Design, this course builds your fundamental knowledge of operating systems right from the hardware level. The instructor provides excellent lectures, readily addresses questions, and offers dedicated office hours and lectures to assist with projects.
One of a kind course. It goes into the depths of the working of an operating system. It strengthened my fundamental knowledge of operating systems. Very difficult but worth it!

Very interesting subject that can strengthen your concepts of operating system fundamentals. One of the few OS courses that works with low level assembly code. However the exams are quite brutal and can seriously lower your grade
Good and interesting projects but extremely brutal exams that lower your grade.

The projects, although very interesting are quite heavy and still doable. However the exams are extremely difficult and barely have anything to do with that was taught in class, and the professor is quite rude towards some students.
One of the better professors in the ECE department. The course is fast-paced, but if you enjoy analog design and reference the books, you'll do well.

I've tried to like Prof Floyd as he really does seem like a great guy, but I can't get past the fact that he is a terrible lecturer. He will go out of his way to help, answering questions, meeting outside of class, additional office hours, but I just can't stand how this professor teaches. I constantly felt on the back foot in the class.
My manager knew him. He was saying he was not good at integrated circuits and IBM laid off him. I think he was right because I didn't learnt much after taking his course.

He's okay with a few first lectures if you have passed other analog circuit courses, but he has no idea about analog design. I studied a book myself otherwise I was similar to other classmates that failed more advanced courses that 511 was their prerequisites.
I think he has some mental issues. He was looking at me angrily during the lectures.

Dr. Floyd is a phenomenal instructor who willingly works with students to help them understand the course material no matter their background. His lectures do a great job conveying information and prepare you well for job interviews. He provides ample test prep material to be successful. Solve all of the practice tests for an A on each test.
Tough grader.  If you're struggling on assignments in the class, well good luck!

Dr. Gupta is way nicer than people give her credit for. She will tell you the truth about exactly how much your project sucks in the early stages, and she's doing it for your sake, there's no point in being offended. She is very fair, and nice if you can accept criticism (and she does only criticize when it's deserved).

Both Rachana and Jeremy are terrible at double standards, and it shows in both their grading and lectures. The structure of the class lives inside spreadsheets, deadlines are very unclear, and Moodle is never used. Though rubrics are given for all presentations, they are never followed and assignments are graded on no basis with no way to appeal.

SO mean, I don't think she has any respect for the students. She'd basically yell at us for not doing enough, like two weeks into class. I think I only got above an 80, like twice; everything else was 60-70s with feedback like "it was lacking." She'd interrupt presentations, to ask/yell about things that'd be answered later on in the presentation

I don't think she has any respect for her students. Every time I tried to talk to her, she cut me in the middle of my sentence by saying "My time is out.", I do not find that respectful or professional at all. She is also unavailable to her students outside of the class and has very few office hours.
Didn't go to class other than for tests bc his "lectures" are essentially online learning modules. Easy class, but not a particularly great teacher just an easy one which is fine with me.

The only reason Tuck has good reviews is because his classes are easy. He "teaches" with a flipped format using videos that were made 8+ years ago. During class he sits there unless someone asks him a question, occasionally working through practice problems. Don't expect to have anything graded until after LDOC or get a fast response on Piazza.

This professor was very mid. I didn't really learn much in the class, but I did well on the exams because they weren't that hard. If you want to learn C++, you're going to have to teach yourself or use Zybooks. As of now, you can find all of Dr. Tuck's lecture videos on YouTube and those are very helpful for explaining the same slides but better.

However, he was really difficult to understand and was honestly horrible at explaining the material. I had to teach myself almost everything. He gave no preparation at all for the exams, and they were all strange exams. Very mid professor

Very mid course. His lectures were pretty useless. His exams didnt really make any sense but were generally easy. He will decide if he does a final project or exam near the end of the semester. Overall, if you want to learn C++, get ready to teach it to yourself.

Used all of James Tuck's material but gave his own exams. The point distribution was pretty annoying but I think the content was fair. Zybooks and written homeworks are not hard. It's his first time teaching 309 so I'll cut him some slack. Maybe he'll curve the overall grade too.

Super tough grader when it comes to exams and gives awful preparation for them. Failed the final after feeling really good about it and doing well on exam two. Gives extra credit and bonus points. Tests were hard to prepare for but I think if he made his own slides, the class would've been better. They switched the professor right before the semester started.
Very intelligent. Nice guy. Exams are strange. He was thrown in at last second.

Very poor lectures. He'll write down a topic, ask ChatGPT to create an example and then poorly explain what is going on. Super tough grader on exams with horrendous point distribution. I disliked this course mainly due to the professor. Signals and systems is interesting, but it was made hard to understand. Homework are timed Moodle quizzes. She is by far one of the worst professors I had. I had a low grade on an exam and she took further points off amid regrade request. DO NOT TAKE HER! I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE HER!

She is a nice and caring teacher but ultimately she does very few examples in class and skips through a lot of steps when solving the math. It is very hard to follow and the tests are very difficult, we are allowed a cheat sheet for an exam but honestly its of no use. Avoid is possible!

I tried a different professor for this class previously but Dr. Gurbuz was much better. A caring professor, making herself available to questions and providing many study resources. ECE331 is a difficult class as it is a lot of new content for non-EE students. Although the class was a rushed at the end, I think it will get better with time.

All these other ratings are wack. I took this junior level class as a freshman and got a B, while taking other engineering classes. It was very well taught, the professor speaks well and gives lots of extra credit. She is very knowledgeable about the material and expects us to understand it. Tests are fair and very well made to prove your knowledge

Bro what a waste of a semester. Easily the worst class I've taken yet. Stay away if you're not an ECE major. She's not helpful in the slightest, I sent her an email in early February and got a response around the time of the final in April. She doesn't explain anything well and the tests suck. Avoid her for your own sake.

She was genuinely awful. She took way too long to grade tests and they were already extremely difficult. She's one of those professors who's super into their topic and fails to explain basic concepts of the material. The practice tests and the real exams didn't line up either. Not good for non ECE majors.
Tests did not line up with practice exams. Grading is extremely harsh with no curving and little partial credit.

Absolutely the most caring professor ever. Wants us to do well and gives up so much of her own time to try and help us. Was great for the first 2/3 of the class but the end content felt rushed and it was so friken difficult. It wasn't intentional but her final exam was BRUTAL compared to everything else.

Absolutely terrible professor. Do not take ECE 331 with her. She did not explain the basics, or anything well for that matter. Most of the class was going over theory instead of actual examples. Takes FOREVER to grade tests.

She didn't really explain things well. As a non-electrical major, I need ECE dumbed down a bit for me, but she went very quickly and didn't always stop to explain things. She really likes ECE, but that didn't always help us for in-class success. The last class was spent learning about motors which weren't covered on any HW or the final exam.

This course is quite difficult. It's even harder to understand conceptually - it's 2 semesters of EE coursework in one.

Dr. Gurbuz dramatically lowers this difficulty by being great at explaining course concepts. She cares about students in a way no other professor I've met here does, and she cares deeply about helping her students learn.
A great professor who offered lots of extra credit. Would say she is very smart and sometimes forgot to explain basic concepts expecting us to know it but overall she did her best.

Dr. Pantic is the nicest man you'll ever meet, but not a great professor. He makes lots of mistakes in his example problems, he gets to exams late, he flies through material but also can go off on tangents during lectures. He's great for office hours but be prepared to study a lot if you take him for this class.

The grading breakdown makes no sense. 81% of your grade is dedicated to exams that have an average grade below 70%. A project, that requires you to present for 10 minutes, 5 minutes to answer questions, and 5 page report is only worth 9% of your grade.
This professor just won't answer emails. Incredibly frustrating that I have to attend his office hours that are far from campus merely to receive his attention for 5 minutes.

Do not be too scared of the bad reviews, Dr. Pantic is good at explaining the material and cares about students understanding. However the class does feel very disorganized and he changed several things about the grading(albeit to make it easier) mid semester. Overall he is a good teacher and I wouldn't mind taking him again, but there are problems
He took 3 weeks to give scores back on exams, and wouldn't even let us bring them home.

This professor is not good. He makes every test problem and HW problem WAY HARDER than it has to be. He gives problems that require you to solve multiple steps that take hours by themselves before even being able to solve for the actual focus of the problem. If he is the only available prof. during registration, take ECE 331 next semester!

Violated FERPA. Failed almost all his students with no partial credit or curves. A class of about 90 students with an average way below 70%. He doesn't go over your mistakes and if you fail, just study harder he says.

This class is exceptionally difficult. 26 students received below a 50 on the first test, and the average was well below 70. The professor took no responsibility for this, and only told us to study harder.
Professor arrived to the exam 18 minutes late, and then expected us to remain seated for the last 20 minutes to not disturb anyone else. Made me late for my next class. It was quite rude.
Testing Testing

Very passionate about the subject. Group Labs take HOURS to do on top of indiv. hw and quiz. Exams match hw. lowest quiz, hw, and lab get dropped. For hw he gives a practice hw with solutions to help with concepts. Extra credit for showing up to class. Posts all annotated slides after each unit. Subject for me was very interesting.

Zeljko was passionable about what he taught, but the way he went about it wasn't great. He didn't post the annotated lecture notes online as a way to force people to attend his lectures. Homework and lab assignments took a lot of time to complete but were similar to the practice problems he posted. The exams were similar to the practice exams.

Dr. Franzon is very knowledgeable on the topic and quite funny, but his lectures are disorganized. Quizzes and exams are multiple choice and can be very tricky, plus there were mistakes in both the questions and the grading that made it a bad experience. The project was challenging and very fun, that was the best part.

Prof. Paul Franzon is one of the better professors I have faced at NCSU. His industry experience is helpful and he's often helping students find work. His quizzes and exams are worded poorly and multiple choice is everywhere--which makes the class more difficult than it needs to be. Still, the assignments are fun. I recommend despite the challenge.

I actually liked Dr. Gu and how she would write stuff down with the class. She is very nice and doesn't deserve all the bad rep. Everyone always says take Titus, but it doesn't matter, everyone who hasnt had Titus tells you to take him. Then, you take him and find out that you're not doing too much better. Rewatch lectures, that's why Titus helps.

The only thing saving Dr. Gu is that you become institutionalized to the communist community which is the physics department. Dr. Gu is a very nice lady, but does not make the lectures the slightest bit interesting or enjoyable. Use Dr. Cox's lectures to study for the exams and you should be fine.

Dr. Gu isn't horrible, it sucks that your only graded on the best of 2/3 exams that are worth 40% of your grade. HW graded on completion not accuracy worth 10%, and an oral presentation another 10%. The way she conducts lectures matches how i best receive information so i thought it was fine. This course is basically PY208 w/ calculus 3 that's it.
Not ready for her lectures
Dr. Gu is really nice but her lectures are pretty much straight from the textbook, and the book isn't good. If you understand the hw you will do fine on the tests.

Gu is not a lecturer. Gu is a textbook being regurgitated onto paper under a document camera. And it's a really bad textbook. No other study resources are provided; practice problems come from the textbook, and homework problems come from an additional instructor's supplement to the textbook. Garbage experience, felt like I learned nothing.

Yes, she does mostly do textbook examples and derivations in class, however I felt like that was all we needed to succeed. We were able to make our own formula sheet, so if you do the practice problems she recommends and make a good formula sheet then you will be fine.

Qing Gu is a nice lady that tries her best to lecture, but with that said, I would not recommend taking her for PY 208. Her lecture style involves writing down stuff from the notebook and not providing relevant examples. She does not write the tests and because of that she often under emphasizes the stuff on the test. Take Titus if possible.

What is given in lecture does not match what is given on tests. I attended every single lecture and did every homework and did poorly on exams. She is more thorough during office hours, but lectures are effectively useless unless you're actually interested in the math behind EM wave propagation. She ended the class with a 10 point final curve.

Dr. Baron is a great professor and excels in a small classroom setting. However, he does not provide any digital notes, and some aspects of the course do not map to a specific section of either of the two textbooks he uses. Due to this, you will need to take diligent notes to understand the material.

This is for the Quantum Computing Special Topics course. Prof Baron is great, he cares about making sure everyone has an enjoyable and productive experience in class. His lectures aren't so exciting, but he tries to be engaging. The class had short weekly homeworks and quizzes that weren't too intense. Not a harsh grader, and very flexible.

It's a free A but you likely won't learn a thing from this class because he is an extremely smart/knowledgeable guy but can't explain concepts to us without excess jargon/formulas (u have to build up to it cannot just have every slide be a bunch of scary math functions). Ur grade is mostly peer reviews + some coding HWs nothing too bad work wise.

Great lectures, though a lot of intricate math on slides is difficult to follow.  Good mix of assignments including quizzes, homework and individual and group projects with easy going grading.  End of semester got overloaded with overlapping projects, but overall, excellent class.
This course is an easy A+, but you won't gain any meaningful knowledge. It's a waste of money and feels like a scam.

In-class lectures are poor and often confusing.  Misunderstands simple questions, leaving students even more confused.  Is generally condescending to students.  Lectures are not representative of homework/exam questions.  Be prepared to read Pozar's Microwave Engineering textbook, as it provides much better explanations than are offered in class.

Professor seems to constantly misunderstand student questions, making errors, or furthering confusion. Even if he does answer your question, prepare to be treated like you're stupid. His excessively long tests are comprised of a mix of basic questions, to random trivia that wasn't in lecture. Prepare to read the whole textbook. Avoid if possible!!!
The professor is incredibly discouraging, and his behavior is excessively strict. I've never felt so utterly frustrated with myself. I strongly advise steering clear of this professor.

I regret taking this seminar/class. Maybe he is just inexperienced, being somewhat new, but it was a waste of time. The other reviews here about awful communication are true, though he tries and is available outside of class.

There are much better options in the department. This guy clearly likes his subject but is just horrible at explaining things. He drones on a lot with useless stories. He means well but my time would have been better spent elsewhere.
Posted a review that was taken down. Take him if you have no other options.
Awful communicator. Avoid him if possible. Negative reviews are removed, so don't know how long this will be up.

Dr. White is nice and funny, and gives extensions when it's reasonable. He does his lectures while handwriting, which means there's a good pace, but his handwriting is hard to read, and the lectures can get really boring. He doesn't really give any time to think about it, it's just write along as he goes, no breaks. Easy exams and homework.

One of the best professors I've had in my whole college career, not because he "made the class easy", but because he very clearly laid out what we needed to know, made the material make perfect sense, and approached each subject from a real world perspective. Exams were open book/notes because "that's how it is in real life."

The homework and exams are a bit challenging, but he gives you everything you need to succeed in this class. He posts old exams and the exams he gives you are for the most part problems ripped out of old exams. The exams are online, and you have 72 hours to complete each one once they open. Fairly easy class, but the homeworks can be long.

Dr. White is a breath of fresh air when it comes to professors. He has engaging lectures, a great sense of humor, and is always receptive to questions or feedback. His exams are take home, but are still very difficult. He provides a lot of study material and makes a very difficult course a little easier.

Lectures are recorded and posted immediately so attendance is not required. Professor posts his notes too and homework is tough but not incredibly impossible since he provides so much information to help (textbook reading, notes, lectures). I definitely love the subject matter so far.

Dr. Wu demonstrated deep knowledge and he was very helpful in office hours, but there is too much material to cover with sufficient depth to really understand it from the lectures, so they can feel rushed.

This guy is a solid professor. The homework is tougher than the tests and quizzes, so if you do them to mastery, you will be fine. He has good lectures as well, but he has rather poor handwriting and needs to work on organization. He is very slow in responding to emails. He allows you to waive the final exam, which is very appreciated.

Professor Lukic really cares about students learning, and he is very easy to talk to if you just ask. His exams are graded very nicely, you just need to pay attention in class and study the practice exams well. The final exam was optional, with the option to have both exams be 35% each instead or they can be weighed less if you take the final.

Dr. Lukic is a kind guy, and he knows the material well. However, the class is very unorganized, and he is not the best at communicating outside of lecture. In class, all notes were done on a legal pad and (mostly) scanned into Moodle. The material itself is not that hard, and if you are good at learning on your own you will do ok in the class.

Very nice guy, however class is disorganized which made it really hard for me to keep up. I'm sure he will get better, but he really needs to evaluate the class content itself to pick what will be covered. He also says he will post additional solutions, but forgets.

First of all, I want to acknowledge that Professor Lukic hasn't taught at NC State for long, so I am trying to be understanding, and he genuinely is a nice guy. However, his exams and prep are lacking and needs to be worked on. He doesn't typically answer emails and the whole class was pretty unorganized to say the least.

Dr. Gurbuz was a fantastic teacher for 220, but for 301 he was a lot more theoretical than practical with the content of the class. We would go over the uses of certain topics as well as general descriptions, and the only way to practice was through HWs and other teachers exams (which weren't like his). He does give EC and is very nice.

Dr. Gurbuz is a generous person overall. A lot of people in class got a question wrong on test 1, so he gave us a curve. We were asked in class if we wanted a difficult topic to be on test 2, and when majority of the class said no, he just avoided it on the test. Class is not hard, but need to spend time to remember a lot of content. (cheat sheet)
He is a very nice person. He can go a little quick on the slides

He sounds like Khabib and has some funny pronunciations. He's a good professor. I honestly think he'd be better in more advanced courses. His tests were very similar to past tests, which makes them easier to study for. Fantastic notes, and the lectures were fine. He also took Bob Evans office which makes me sad.

He isn't a great lecturer but that's fine because his slides have everything you need. Homework problems come straight from the textbook and you get plenty of time to do them. The exams aren't too far from the practice tests he gives you.
Very laid back guy, very chill class. He posts his powerpoints so you can probably get away with just looking over them and taking notes. The practice exams are very helpful

He is an alright professor. He did not seem to care about the class after receiving a failing average on a test; he laughed it off. I would say the best way to prepare for this test would be to study the homework and the notes, and you will for sure pass the class. I do, however, like how he drops an exam, including the final.

Dr. Bandodkar is a nice and funny professor, and explains the material well during lectures. However, exams are very fast-paced, and usually more than half of the class is still in the room when time runs out. Also, exams are 80% of the grade (but lowest out of four gets dropped). For exams, I recommend studying the HWs and extra practice problems.

The lectures are very poorly structured (especially compared to Veety). Does not go over any examples in class except for the simplest scenario that is possible, and then gives the most unnecessarily complicated problems on exams. Be prepared to spend 95% of your time doing useless complex algebra.

Dr. Cui cares about his students and really wants to make sure they understand the material. He is easily accessible outside of class and does his best to try and break down lectures and hard concepts. I took him for ECE 211, which is a tough course, but I couldn't recommend a better professor besides Veety to take it with.
Difficult class but Dr. Farfurnik is an enthusiastic professor who wants to help you learn the material. Very fair exams and curving.
Less painful than it could have been

She was hilarious and really encouraged participation by giving out chocolate every lecture! If you take advantage of this class, you will come out with a lot of good skills (matlab, excel, power flow, etc). The group project is medium difficulty (ask for help). Overall - such a great, positive, and encouraging professor. I wish she taught more :(

Her easygoing attitude and sense of humor made lectures interesting. Homeworks and the midterms have solutions provided and the final doesn't have as much impact on your grade as it seems. The project takes time but she's willing to help you when you need it. Her class had a laid back environment, which was nice considering my other classes.

Horrible Professor. Goes on way too many tangents, His homeworks and quizes are vastly different. 
Doesn't clear doubts. He's knowledgable no doubt but he has no idea how to teach a class.

Dr. Marley is the best! She is so friendly and loves chatting with students outside of class. She does an amazing job teaching, and she really tries to make sure every student succeeds. She interacts with students in class and keeps the lectures engaging. As long as you put in effort to learn, this class is nothing to be scared of.
